en: The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, Volume Thirty-Four.
Compiled by the monk (Chao Yong), Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple in the Capital;
proofread by the monk (Chao Kui), Abbot of Gu Huayan Temple in the Capital. Presented for Imperial Review.
Presented below is the tenth generation of the Yunmen school under Mount Heng.
Chan Master Tianyi Yihuai of Yuezhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xuedou Xian.
He was a native of the Chen family of Leqing, Yongjia. By profession, his family had been fishermen for generations.

His mother dreamed that a star fell upon her house before she conceived him; at the time of his birth, there were many auspicious signs. When he was a child, he sat at the stern of a boat while his father...

He caught a fish and presented it to his master, who skewered it. The master could not bear it and secretly threw it into the river. His father became angry and whipped him, yet the master remained as placid as before.
He traveled far to the capital, where he relied on Jingde Temple to serve as a novice monk during the Tiānshèng era of Emperor Rénzōng of the Sòng dynasty.
He passed the scriptural examinations to receive ordination and visited Jinluan Shan at Xian County, where he received the seal of approval from both masters.
He then traveled from Luoyang to Longmen and subsequently returned to the capital, desiring to continue the ancestral tradition, yet his mind remained undecided.
Suddenly, he encountered Yan Fahua in the marketplace, who patted his master’s back and said, "Yunmen and Linji have departed. Upon arriving in Gusu, he paid homage to Mingjue at Cui...
Feng asked, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Yihuai. Feng said, "Why do you not name yourself Huaiyi (Holding Righteousness)?
The Master said, "That would have been appropriate at the time. Feng said, "Who gave you your name? The Master replied, "It has been ten years since I received the precepts.

Feng said, "In traveling the roads, how many pairs of straw sandals must you have worn out? The Master said, "Master, please do not deceive people. Feng said, [laughing]... (the text here implies a further exchange).
"I have no measure of my own offenses; you have no measure of your offenses either. What do you say to this? The Master remained silent.
Jue struck him and said, "You hollow liar! Get out! Later, as the Master entered the room, Jue said, "It is not so, yet it is not otherwise.
It is neither so nor otherwise—none of these are acceptable. As the Master hesitated, Jue struck him out once more.
This happened four times in succession. Jue was then appointed as the head of the water supply. While drawing water, his carrying pole suddenly broke, and he attained sudden enlightenment.

He composed an "ad-hoc verse" (touji ge) which said: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Standing alone on one foot atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak, He snatches the bright pearl from beneath the chin of the black dragon.
With a single word, he exposes Vimalakīrti. Juewen patted the table and praised him, saying, "Excellent! Later, he sat upon the site of enlightenment (the bodhimaṇḍa) seven times.

He traveled throughout the land spreading the Dharma, and those who inherited his teaching were very numerous. After he had settled there, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Spreading his hair to cover the mud;
lying across the ground. The monk asked, "What is the underlying meaning? The Master said, "Even Pāpīyān would have to knit his brows.
The monk said, "If that is so, then I thank you for your instruction. The Master said, "India and this land. [The monk] asked, "How about for a student? The Master said, "..."
[The Master] ascended the hall. He requested the Master to preach the Dharma. The Master said: "The birds chirp in the forest; the fish swim beneath the water. Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"On the summit of Mount Sumeru, the golden bell is not struck. Within the Pipphala Cave, no one gathers. This mountain monk rides backward upon the Buddha Hall;
everyone puts on their straw sandals backward. In the morning they roam Mount Tandi; in the evening they arrive at Mount Luofu. The staff is a needle-case."
The Master entered the hall. "Monks of the patch-robed school speak horizontally and vertically, yet they do not yet know the eye upon the crown of the head.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the eye upon the crown of the head? The Master said, "The robe is worn through and the bare bones are exposed;

the roof is broken and one sleeps watching the stars. He entered the hall again. When the assembly had gathered and settled, he said, "To say 'Not well' (*fǔxǐn*) at the outset can dissolve ten thousand [delusions]."
"Two pieces of gold. [The Master] then stepped down from the seat and said, "Take care. This is sufficient to receive the offerings of the four continents.

If you try to understand this as a discourse on the Buddha-dharma, even a drop of water will be difficult to digest. If you try to deliberate upon it as a matter of non-action, it is like putting grit in your eye.
But what, then, is it? After a long silence, he said, "Do you understand? Take care! [Later,] while ascending the hall, he said: "To be a master of our school, one must indeed..."
To drive away the oxen of the plowman; to snatch the food from the hungry man. To make the lowly noble when encountered, and the noble lowly when encountered.
By driving away the oxen of the plowman, one causes the crops of others to flourish; by snatching the food from the hungry man, one ensures that others shall forever be free from hunger and thirst.
When meeting the lowly, one treats them as noble; grasping soil, one turns it into gold. When meeting the noble, one treats them as lowly; transforming gold, one turns it into soil.
This old monk neither drives the plowman’s ox, nor does he snatch the hungry man’s food.
Why is this? What use have I for the plowman’s ox? What food have I to eat? I do not grasp soil to turn it into gold, nor do I transform [gold].
Gold is above. Why? Gold is gold; earth is earth; jade is jade; stone is stone; the monastic is the monastic; the layperson is the layperson.

From antiquity to the present, the heavens and earth; from antiquity to the present, the sun and moon; from antiquity to the present, the mountains and rivers; from antiquity to the present, the human relations.
Although it is thus, how many have broken through the Great San Pass? "Meeting Bodhidharma while Lost" [is the title]. Entering the Hall: "The Wild Geese Fly Over the Long..."
Emptiness. A reflection sinks into cold water; the wild geese have no intention of leaving a trace, and the water has no mind to retain the reflection.

If one can act thus, only then will one understand how to walk among the heterodox classes. There is no need to lengthen the ducks or shorten the cranes, nor to fill the mountains and valleys with the ordinary.
When let go, there are a hundred uglinesses and a thousand clumsinesses; when gathered in, there is a clutching and a grasping. If used, one dares to rival the Eight Great Dragons.
The King competed in wealth; he would not accept even half a coin that was not brought from the capital. [He] ascended the hall and said: "The skull-bone constantly engages with the world;
the nostrils touch upon the family style. When the banana tree hears thunder, it blooms; when the sunflower faces the sun, it turns.
O worthy ones, when the banana tree hears thunder and blooms, does it have ears? When the sunflower follows the sun and turns, does it have eyes? If..."
One will also attain it. The Western Heaven is this very land. If you do not understand, then seven times nine is sixty-three.

[The Master] ascends the hall: "The spiritual source is devoid of traces; the form-body manifests everywhere. The Dharma is free from the extremes of annihilation and permanence; existence and non-existence cannot be demonstrated. Therefore it is said:

'In every speck of dust one does not see the Buddha; in every world-system one does not hear the sutras. If you wish to understand the personal transmission of the prediction at Vulture Peak, look at the day."
Day and night he observed the stars. After a long while, he said: "If you travel to various regions, do not err in your conduct. [He] ascended the hall for the formal lecture.
"Last night the cold frost was piercing; the Yellow River was frozen solid. The Iron Ox of Shanzhou broke at its waist.

Everyone says that Nüwa melted stones to patch the heavens, yet how could they prevent the northwestern corner from remaining deficient? Now, if I wish to patch it for them, I fear it will cause the great earth to collapse."
People have no place to breathe out; let this single aperture remain for all people of the great earth to breathe out from. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Empty clarity illuminates itself;
there is no need to exert mental effort. When those of superior capacity see it, it is like a ghost's meal. Those of middling and inferior capacity attain it."
The deranged mind is suddenly stilled. Furthermore, there is one person: "By all means, do not speak of it. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Light penetrates the sun and moon;

brightness and darkness cannot contain it. Wisdom transcends the holy and the ordinary; the worthy and the ignorant do not traverse it. Therefore it is said: 'There is no need to lower the head and ponder, for it is difficult to obtain.
After a long silence, he asked: 'What is it? Ascending the hall, [he said]: "The green vine entwines itself, climbing straight up the cold pine."
The summit. White clouds, thin and translucent, appear and disappear within the vast void. How is this different from "clouds rising on the southern mountain, rain falling on the northern mountain"?
If you can understand this, the sweet melon is sweet all the way to its stem; if you do not understand, the bitter gourd is bitter down to its roots. [Ascending the hall:
"The realms of infinite lands are not separated by a hair’s breadth between self and other. Now tell me: does the world of Wondrous Joy not...?
Dong Rulai said: "What Dharma do you preach? Throughout the ten ages of past and present, beginning and end do not depart from the present moment.
As for the first assembly of the Buddha King of Awesome Voice—how many people did he deliver? If you are one who has penetrated the Way, try to say something on this.
After a long silence, he said: "Difficult is the road, difficult is the road; atop the ten-thousand-fathom peak, look for yourself. (End)
Hall: "The withered mulberry tree knows the wind of heaven; the sea water knows the cold of heaven. The golden-hued dhūta’s perception of his location was not true;
he remained in Mount Kukkuṭapāda to guard the robes and bowl for others. The three thousand major parables and eight hundred minor parables are much like washing clods of earth in the mud.
Throughout the forty-nine years and over three hundred and sixty assemblies in the kingdom of Magadha, it still falls short.
"A mere trifle. Though Deshan and Linji were indeed men of stature, how could they compare to the King of Kaśmīra, who cut them in two with a single stroke?
"If there were someone here today whose nostrils reach to the heavens, where would this mountain monk’s life be?

After a long silence, he said: "Peace was originally brought about by the generals; it is not permitted for the generals to witness peace. He gave a shout and descended from his seat. [Question: "..."
"Heaven cannot cover him; earth cannot support him. I do not know who this person is. The Master said, "Dig a deep hole and bury him.
[The monk] asked, "Does this person still accept arrangements? The Master said, "Add more mud upon the soil.

[The monk] asked, "What was it like before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "The Long River has no sixth month. [The monk] asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said—
He said: "Once a year there is spring. He questioned the monks in his quarters: "A handless man can perform a fist-punch; a tongueless man understands speech.
Suddenly, the handless man strikes the tongueless man—what does the tongueless man say?
He further said: "The soul of Shu cries out through the night; the quail and the owl wail all night long. The Gate of Perfect Penetration stands wide open—why is it obscured by clouds?"
In his later years, [the Master] lived at Shanshan Hermitage in Chiyang due to illness. His disciple Zhicai was residing at Furi Temple in Linping;
he invited the Master back to serve him. While Zhicai was still in Suzhou and had not yet returned, the Master urged him to come back. When Zhicai finally arrived at the gate, the Master said:
The Master told him, "The time has come; I am going. Xuefeng Cai asked, "What words do you have to instruct your disciples?
The Master then spoke this verse: "The red sun shines upon Fusang; Cold clouds seal Mount Hua. At the third watch, he passes through the Iron Ring Mountains, Crushing the horns of the black dragon.
Cai then asked, "The egg-shaped stupa is already completed; what is the ultimate matter? The Master raised his fist to show him, and then passed away.

He passed away peacefully while reclining on his pillow. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the plain east of the temple. During the Chongning era of Emperor Huizong’s reign, an imperial edict posthumously conferred upon him the title Chan Master Zhenzong.
In Yuezhou, Chan Master Shengzong of Chengxin Monastery was asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied: [The text here indicates a response follows].

A traveler was thinking about the road. The Master said, "I do not understand. The traveler said, "Tie your straw sandals tight. Ascending the hall, the Master said, "The seed of the Buddha arises from conditions;
therefore, the One Vehicle is taught. He held up his staff and said, "This staff is the condition. Which one is the seed of the Buddha?"
"The staff is the Dharma of the One Vehicle. What is the condition? Here, having seen the Old Śākyamuni, you must go out to travel wearing straw sandals;
you must not pass through the gate of a patch-robed monk [without being challenged], for I shall break your waist.
But tell me, upon what does the patch-robed monk rely? After a long silence, he said, "Thirty years hence, do not let people down. He struck the ground with his staff and descended.
[The Master] was seated.
A monk asked Zen Master Chuanzong of Chengtian in Quanzhou, "When the Great Function manifests before one, and no rules or regulations remain—how is it then?
The Master said, "Today at Chengtian, we hoist the banner of surrender high. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "A descendant of Linji!"
The monk shouted again. The Master struck him. A monk asked, "What is the essence of prajñā? The Master said, "Blue peaks shrouded by clouds.
He asked, "What is the function of prajñā? The Master said, "The moon in a clear pond."
A monk asked Chan Master Mingri Shen of Chuzhou, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said, "The reflections of water and sky merge into azure. The monk asked, "Ultimately, are they the same or different? The Master said, "The sounds of pines and bamboos share a coldness."
A monk asked Chan Master Fanzong of Touzi in Shuzhou, "What is the家风 (household style) of the Way?
The Master said, "A *kāṣāya* wrapped around straw sandals. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Barefoot, one goes to Tongcheng."
A monk asked Chan Master Yun of Tiantai Shixiang-yun, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "Majestic and imposing, over eight feet tall.
Chan Master Xiansheng of Mount Junshan in Yuezhou ascended the hall and said: "The Great Square has no exterior; it encompasses the ten voids. The ultimate principle..."

Formless, it is perfectly interfused throughout the three periods of time; transcending names and appearances, its wondrous essence is fully manifest. Standing far beyond past and present, the true mechanism is uniquely revealed.
Grasping the dragon pearl, one reflects all things, and every phenomenon radiates brilliance; casting away the jewel, one brandishes the sword through the void, and the void itself leaves no trace.
To hold fast is like Mahākāśyapa’s closing of his room or Vimalakīrti’s silence; to let go is like Shide shaking his head.

Hanshan clapped his hands and said, "Tell me, whose realm is this? He took up his staff, struck it once, and said, "At the moment of a blink of an eye or a raising of an eyebrow, rely on you to look closely."
Huijin, the steward (diànzuò) of Shuǐyuè Temple in Píngjiāng Prefecture, followed Míngjué at Xuědòu. Upon hearing the discourse on the "Mount Sumeru" koan, he attained silent resonance with it.
One day, wishing to go and inquire further, he encountered Jué in the corridor of the hall. Jué asked, "What is your name?"
He said, "Master Huìjīn gave me some gold. Jue asked, "Who gave you the gold? He replied, "I intend to go to the abbot’s quarters shortly to express my thanks.
Jue said, "What about right now? He replied, "In this place, even a monk like you cannot remain."
Chan Master Zuyin Zhifu of Changlu in Yizhen, Yangzhou, was the son of the Xia family of Jiangzhou. He studied under Xuedou and suddenly realized the meaning of the patriarchs.
His practice of the Way, his talent, and his wisdom were remarkably transcendent. Having entered the world at Changlu, he ascended the hall.

A monk asked, "What is it like when the precious sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard? The Master said, "Rough. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has emerged? The Master said, "Sharp. [The monk] asked again.
"What is the first pivot? The Master said, "It is not for the sake of a house mouse that one sets a trap.

The monk asked, "Is there no skillful means? The Master said, "'Svāhā' in a quiet place. He then said, "The question lies where the answer is; the answer lies where the question is. Let everyone nod their heads as they please.
But if the question does not lie where the answer is, and the answer does not lie where the question is, how will you go about grasping it?"
Spreading his two hands, he said: "Without leaving out even a single thread or hair; everything is entrusted at once.
Chan Master Huìyuán of Dōngshān in Ruìzhōu studied under Xuědòu during his youth and immediately attained the essential meaning. His reputation soon became widely renowned.
Later, he relied upon Kāishān Xiān, who, when Dōngshān was short of personnel, recommended him to fill the position. He subsequently entered the world [as a public teacher]. Above.
The Hall. My learning is not derived from antiquity, and my realization of the Way falls short of the present age. Having no door through which to enter, I have followed the will of the assembly.

As the ancients said: "When there is nothing to do, go up the mountain and take a turn; ask the people of the time, do they understand? It is just as when this mountain monk and you all came from Mount Lu:
meeting night, we stayed; meeting dawn, we traveled; and so we have come directly to this place, with one foot already [inside].
One foot is ahead, the other behind. Now, everyone hangs up their alms-bag and sets aside their staff; what further matter remains?
Nevertheless, if one does not ascend the tower to look out, how can one know the depth of the vast ocean?
Master Zhongqing of Fengxi in Fengyang ascended the hall for the formal discourse. A monk asked, "When ancient Buddhas appeared in the world, it was for the sake of the one great matter;
for what purpose have you, Reverend, appeared in the world? The Master opened his mouth and extended his tongue to show him, saying, "It is just this;
is there anything else? He then said, "Three thousand in the morning, eight hundred in the evening. He continued, "Majestic and dignified, the three realms..."
Peerless. Monumental and expansive. The ten directions are vast and empty. To deliberate is to lose one's body and life;
to ponder is to fall into a thousand errors and ten thousand mistakes. (He lets out a shout. He descends from his seat.
Chan Master Zhichuan of Longxing Temple in Changsha was asked by a monk: "Having resided in the Lake and Xiang regions for a long time, I intend to pose a question;
will you answer me, Master? The Master said, "Why do you drag along mud and water? The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "A burst of rain, a burst of coolness.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "There is a beginning but no end. He passed away during the Zhiping era of Emperor Yingzong of the Song dynasty. Ping...

Wherever he was born, walked, stood, sat, or lay down, śarīra relics emerged everywhere. When the practitioners of meditation proclaimed that they had obtained robes and other requisites, the śarīras appeared daily.
For those who sought them before the true image with utmost sincerity, the relics manifested in accordance with their thoughts.
The monk asked Chan Master Ninggan Mingze, "What is the Sea-Seal Samādhi? The Master said, "Simply seek it within yourself.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Do not seek it from others. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "A pure breeze arises in the azure void. [The monk] asked, "What is the underlying principle? The Master said, "The bright moon reflects."
Changjiang. Chan Master Qianming of Changde ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?
The Master said, "Supporting heaven and propping up earth. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after it has emerged? The Master said, "Filling the valleys and filling the ditches. He then said:
When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up the mat. Fire moves and smoke arises; clouds lift the hue of rain. Presented face-to-face—how lightly it is cast aside!
A heavy reward is three thousand; a light recompense is eight hundred.
Chan Master Yunfeng Yuanyi of Nanyue in Hengzhou was asked by Li Linzong: "I desire to transcend the mundane world, yet I have not yet done so.
I request that the Master resolve my doubts this very day. The Master said, "What is the matter of transcending the mundane?
Li was perplexed. The Master said, "Do you understand? Li suddenly attained realization and presented a verse, saying: "The mirror of the mind has always been luminous; the great river..."
Originally it was deep. It was only because of the Master’s question afterward that the sand and stone turned into gold. The Master said, "You are heading straight for hell.
Li said, "When there is no mark of self or other, why is there hell? The Master said, "Where are you now? Li said, "Face-to-face, yet I do not recognize you.
The Master said, "This very thing is golden."
The editor, Layman Zenghui, had lived in the same quarters as Mingjue since childhood; however, upon reaching adulthood, they took different paths.
During the Tianxi era, while the official was serving as the governor of Chizhou, the two met one day at Jingde Temple.

The official then cited the *Zhongyong* and the *Daxue*, incorporating passages from the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and the sayings of the Chan school to question Mingjue. Mingjue said, "This [teaching] does not even accord with the scriptural vehicles (jiao-cheng), let alone..."

"Is this the *Zhongyong* or the *Daxue*? Scholar, you must understand this matter through a direct and swift path. Thereupon, [the Master] snapped his fingers once and said, "Just realize it in this way.

The official understood the meaning beneath these words. At the beginning of the Tianxing era, while the official was governing Siming, he sent letters and gifts to welcome the Master and appointed him to Xuedou.
Once the Master had arrived, the official said, "Recently, I discussed Zhaozhou with Elder Qing."
Regarding the story of the examination of the old woman: I do not know for certain whether there was a point where he was truly tested and seen through.
Jue said, "What did Elder Qing say? Gong said, "He went off in that way again. Jue said, "Let us let Elder Qing off with one stroke."

"Scholar, do you know that the monks of the world cannot escape the snare of this old woman? The Duke said, "There is another way to approach this. If Zhaozhou had not exposed her, the old woman would have suffered a lifelong injustice. Jue said: *Note:
The character [袖-由+貴] (xiù-guì) is a variant or scribal error for 套 (tào), meaning "snare" or "trap. Thus, the phrase means "cannot escape the snare of this old woman."*
"I have seen through it," he said, and the Master laughed heartily.

Chan Master Juzhe Zuyin of Lushan Yuan Tong was a descendant of Chan Master Yanqing Rong; his secular surname was Jian, and he was born in Zizhou. From birth, he was exceptionally brilliant. He studied...

He could recite from memory any text he read upon a single glance. At the age of eleven, he left the household life; at seventeen, he passed the examination on the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and received ordination.

After receiving full precepts, he pursued his studies at lecture halls, where the senior monks looked down upon him. Later, when a practitioner of meditation returned from a southern journey, he earnestly exhorted him to practice. Thereupon—
He traveled extensively throughout the Jing and Chu regions, yet until then he had attained nothing. Upon reaching Dongshan in Xiangzhou, he remained there for ten years;

while reading the *Huayan lun* (Treatise on the Avatamsaka Sutra), he experienced a profound realization. Later, he traveled to Mount Lu, where his reputation as a teacher grew daily. He moved from Guizong to Yuancong.
Emperor Renzong of the Song dynasty heard of his reputation. At the beginning of the Huangyou era, he issued an imperial decree for him to reside at the Jinyin Chan Monastery of the Ten Directions.

The Master claimed that due to eye ailments, he was unable to comply with the decree. An edict was issued stating that someone must be recommended to serve as his successor; consequently, the Master recommended Dajue Liaoyan to respond to the summons.

When Liaoyan was brought before the Emperor for an audience, he was questioned on the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma and satisfied the Emperor’s expectations. Thus, the world recognized the Master as a virtuous teacher who truly knew men. A monk asked: "The ancestral monastery is being restored..."

"How was it when you first aroused [the aspiration for enlightenment]? The Master said, "The man was on Mount Pòtóu. [The questioner] said, "What about when power is in one's hand? The Master then struck him.
One day, he suddenly went to take leave of the Governor of Jiangzhou, Lord Liú, and returned home. He bathed, sat upright, and manifested parinirvāṇa.
This was on the sixteenth day of the third month of the Xīníng era, the *xīnhài* year of Emperor Shénzōng. He was sixty-two years of age and forty-five years since his ordination. [Tea.]
Within the *vī* fire-flame, white vapor ascends and pierces the sun. Ou-yang Wen-chung Kung held him in particularly high esteem.

Zen Master Hui-yin Huai-hsiang of Huiyin Monastery in Lin’an, a successor in the Dharma lineage of Zen Master Baizhang Ying, ascended the hall and said: "The Southern Mountain is high, the Northern Mountain is low; the sun rises in the east."
When night falls in the west, the white ox climbs a tree but cannot be found; the black chicken enters the water, and everyone knows it.
But tell me: what is it like after it has been found? After a long silence, he said: "What can it possibly be used for?"
A monk asked Chan Master Yining of Huilin Temple in Lin’an Prefecture, “How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?
The Master said, “Queen Māyā. The monk asked, “How was it after he appeared in the world? The Master said, “Prince Siddhārtha.”
Chan Master Xinghua Yanqing of Qizhou, successor to Chan Master Nanhua Yuan, ascended the hall and said: "If you gain realization before words, you betray your lifelong practice;

if you apply yourself to the meaning after the phrase, you completely miss the essence of the Way. Apart from these two paths, how was it under the gate of our ancestors? (He sat in silence for a long while.)"
It is said: "The pupil in the eye blows the wooden flute.
On a winter day at Nanhua, Chan Master Baoshou Xingde of Shaoyou received an invitation and addressed the assembly, saying: "A new winter for a new Baoshou;
these words are the same as those of old. If you would understand the meaning of the Westward Journey, it is like a Persian boarding a ship."
A monk asked Chan Master Shoucheng of White Tiger Mountain in Shaoyang, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Having eyes but no nostrils.
A monk asked Chan Master Chongqin of Buddha’s Footprint Mountain in Shaoyang, “What is the single phrase for directly benefiting people?”
The Master struck with his whisk and asked, “Do you understand? The monk said, “I do not. The Master said, “When you meet someone, do not speak of this in error.
A monk asked Chan Master Faning of Yanxiang in Shaoyou, “What was it like before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?

The Master said, “The staff. The monk asked, “What was it like after he saw him? The Master struck him. The monk said, “Today I have personally seen the Master. The Master [said], “...[you] have seen me.”
It is said: "A second offense will not be tolerated.
A monk asked Chan Master Huibao of Shunfeng in Shaoyou Province, "What is it like when one ascends higher with every step? The Master said, "Perilous."
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when there is neither advancing nor retreating? The Master said, "Loss. [The monk] asked, "How is this so?
The Master said, "Suru suru.
[He was a successor of Chan Master Xian of Beichen.]
Chan Master Xinghua Shaoyan of Tanzhou ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "The entire Tripitaka is but used-up toilet paper.
Discourse that transcends Buddhas and Patriarchs is but a deception for the common folk. As for the gate of the patch-robed monks, not even a single point is of any use.
What, then, is the matter within the gate of the patch-robed monks? After a long silence, he said:
"Much emptiness is not as good as a little reality. [The Master] struck the incense stand and descended from his seat.
Zen Master Yiyu of Fachang in Hongzhou was the son of the Lin family of Zhangzhou. In his youth, he left home and received the full precepts at Chongfu Monastery in the prefecture.
Possessing great ambition, he traveled to various regions after his ordination and became renowned in monastic circles. Fushan Yuan once said:
A person said, "This is the model for the conduct of a student on pilgrimage. He went to visit Beichan. Chan asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The Master replied, "Fuyan. Chan asked, "How much longer is Sita’s nostrils? The Master replied, "They are exactly as they were when you first saw them, Reverend.
Chan asked, "Tell me, how long were they when I saw them? The Master replied, "The Reverend seems almost not to have seen them at all."
Once he went to Fuyan. Chan said, "You are just a fellow who parrots words. He asked again, "When you arrived, was Master Ma well?

Thus, it becomes like a flawless iron hammer—water cannot splash upon it, and wind cannot penetrate it."
Tell me, does Fachang have any way to benefit others? After a long silence, he said: "A sharp blade may cut the flesh, yet the wound eventually heals;

A single dream of Nuo has just reached its full measure. Carrying my staff, I stride out through the pines; everywhere the peach blossoms are fragrant and rich. Reflecting on this...

Even if you were to understand with such distinct clarity, should you encounter Linji or Deshan, your forehead would still strike the ground.
Tell me, what excellence does he possess? After a long silence, he said: "Having once crossed the great ocean, do not boast."

The waters freeze and the fish move with difficulty; the forests thin and the birds find it hard to roost. Already the severity of the frost is heavy;

how can one endure the traveler’s single-layered robe? Cease thinking of the thousand peaks of the mountains along the purple road; for now, embrace the fire of the red brazier. Set down the *ju-yu* (dogwood) and let it rest.

Calculated, this is truly groundless. *Chan* (Investigate!). One day, while the Master was in his room with his disciples, the Layman东坡 (Dongpo) arrived.
The Master said, "There is no seat here; what do you intend to do by coming here? The Layman replied, "I shall temporarily borrow the Buddha..."

if you cannot answer it, you must forfeit the jade belt at your waist. The Layman joyfully replied, "Please ask.

A traveler’s pavilion: props for the door and supports for the frame. But tell me, when it is in the hands of this mountain monk, what is it used for? Do you wish to understand?
Sometimes I pace upon the eastern lake, pointing at the distant green mountains with a monk. Striking the meditation seat, he descended from the high seat and entered the hall, saying:
"I remember when I was seven years old, at a village schoolhouse, I obtained a Dharma gate that transcends [all others]."

The essence is free from views; it is most wondrous and most profound. From the time it first permeated my spirit over sixty years ago, I have kept it hidden. Today, I bring it forth to announce it universally to the great assembly.

If you wish to receive and uphold it, you should listen with careful attention. He then said: "The plowing and sowing on the cold fields are finished; I lead the calf home, carrying firewood upon my back.
This night, a single brazier’s fire Is the clothing for the entire family. "O practitioners of Zen, when meeting people, you must not..."

A Misplaced Citation. Entering the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'Receiving beings and benefiting life is most exquisite. But an outsider like myself is ultimately unworthy. His own descendants will surely come;
when they arrive, their application will be perfectly suited. "O Zen practitioners, do you understand? When the garden wall collapses, it is rebuilt only in the sun;
when the fence of the guesthouse is pierced, it is repaired after the rain has passed. When the temple buildings leak, they are mended as best one can. As for the children..."
Sun Daoshao’s Great and Small Exhaustion of Wind and Flow. Entering the hall, he raised the case of Master Xian, who said: "Cold, cold! The hearth fire is warm;
sitting idly upon the *pútán*, one says that Kāśyapa was not right and speaks of Bodhidharma as being groundless.
This and that—surely they are of one kind. The Master called to the assembly, saying: "In what way was Kāśyapa not right? In what respect was Bodhidharma groundless? If..."
If you can examine this and discern it, those two elders will have met with a total embarrassment.
If you cannot discern it, do not say later on, after thirty years, that you were not deceived. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "I have this one move. It is chewed by everyone’s mouth.
Those who can chew it through must quickly spit it out; those who cannot chew it through turn it into poison. He then called to the assembly.
"Zen Virtue," [the Master said], "what flavor is there? Try to tell me. After a long silence, he said: "The King of Physicians is not without prescriptions;
the fragrance of the Su-herb from a thousand li does not turn back the elephant. A Daoist asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The dragon roars in the golden cauldron;
the tiger sighs in the elixir field. [The Daoist] asked, "What is one who walks the Way? The Master said, "Exhaling the old and inhaling the new. [The Daoist] asked again. The Master said: "..."
"How far apart are the Way and those who dwell within the Way? The Master said: "A crane caught in a snare atop a precipice; soaring toward the heavens, one is oblivious to the common folk.
A monk asked Chan Master Yuanchu Baoyue of Tianzhang in Yuezhou: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master [replied]: [text fragment]
[A monk] asked, "There are three hundred and sixty days in a year. [The Master] said, "If you understand it in this way, what then? The Master said, "Ten thousand miles away is not far.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The drumbeats fall in succession; the mountain colors are majestic. Since the source itself does not exist,"
"From where have you come? After a long silence, he said, "Keep your eyes open.
Chan Master Wanshan Shanshuang of Mount Lu in Nankang ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Wanshan?"
The Master said, "Ten thousand pine trees below, a thousand fathoms of bamboo. He asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm?

The Master said, "I, the old monk, stand with my hands folded facing you, O Kalyāṇamitra. He asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A man from Kunlun wears the peak of Mount Hua upon his head.
Then he said, "The ancient is the present; the present is the ancient. Beneath the windows of every house dwell the Patriarchs. Mañjuśrī reveals them."
The mountains and rivers are fully manifest; yet from this time on, people have failed to understand and awaken. The assembly, tell me: what is it that they awaken to?
(He lets out a shout.
This is the lineage of Chan Master Qinshan Qun.
A monk asked Chan Master Yuanying of Liangshan in Dingzhou, "What is the discourse that transcends the Buddhas and surpasses the Patriarchs?
The Master said, "Eating porridge, eating rice.
[He was] a successor of Chan Master Yungai Peng.
Chan Master Tan of Zhongshan Bao’en Temple in Zhuji, Shaoxing, ascended the hall and said: "The Dharma-body has no form; it manifests its shape in response to things.
Zen masters, how would you explain this principle of manifesting form in response to things? He held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying:
"The World-Honored One was sixteen feet tall; this staff is also sixteen feet tall. Maitreya’s body..."
It is a thousand cubits long; this staff is also a thousand cubits long. Square or round, it conforms to whatever vessel it meets; hidden or manifest, it follows others.

It encompasses heaven and earth in its vastness, yet enters into a single speck of dust in its subtlety. Like a donkey looking into a well, like a well looking at a donkey—those who attain it direct strategy from within the tent and hold fast the vital ford;
those who lose it drift in obscurity and confusion, living in vain and dying in delusion. Such is gain and loss.
"Let go of both paths at once. I dare ask you all: tell me, how long is this mountain monk’s staff?
After a long silence, he said: 'Laughing, I point: from where does the guest come? He struck the incense table once."
Zen Master Weijue of Jingguang Temple in Wenzhou, a successor of Zen Master Ji of Yandang, ascended the hall and said: "This is the azure temple of Jingguang, an ancient Buddha’s Jeta Grove.

Those who hear its name find their worldly minds instantly stilled; those who behold it with their own eyes feel as if they have ascended to heaven. It faces the city walls before us and leans against forests and springs behind."
Everywhere people sing the praises of the Emperor’s transformation; why need one further expound the subtle and discourse on the ultimate? As for that "one opening above"—how is it?
Suddenly grasping his staff, he struck it once and said: "The embroidered mandarin ducks are displayed for you to behold;
I do not hand over the golden needle to anyone. He then descended from the seat.

Chan Master Baoji Xiong of Caoshan in Fuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Heshan Cui, ascended the hall for formal instruction. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A cold cat does not catch mice.
[The monk] asked, "It is said that 'every speck of dust is a Buddha-land; every leaf is a Śākyamuni. How should a student apply this?"

[The monk] said, "Sufficient. The Master said, "The grass on the great earth spreads vast and wide. [The monk] said, "I thank the Master for his reply. The Master said, "It is difficult to deceive one with clear eyes.
[The monk] said, "Let the assembly take note all at once. The Master said, "Today Cao Shan has suffered a loss. He asked, "The Dharma-thunder resounds once more."
"Dragons and elephants come from the four quarters; how does the Master issue his commands? The Master said, "The clear breeze does not understand my intent;
it blows away the white clouds, which fly about in disarray. [The student] asked, "Does the student have a place to settle the body and establish one's life, or not? The Master said:
Standing firmly on solid ground, he said: "Skillfully responding to all quarters, ten thousand matters converge. When meeting face-to-face, I do not ask;
why is it that when you pick up the spoon and grasp the chopsticks, you cannot speak? After a long silence, he said: "Cao Shan has lost today. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The mountains are not green, the waters are not blue; north, south, east, and west—there is nowhere to set foot. A single fragment of white cloud..."
Soaring from one peak, he returns at night to nestle within the reeds. Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "A thousand rivers compete to converge; ten thousand streams share a single source.

The precious moon rises in radiance, its light dividing across the myriad worlds. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—bright and dark are each distinct. Whether sitting, reclining, walking, or standing, in whose sphere do these activities reside?
Among you, is there not a monk for whom words and paths are severed, whose realization is like a box and its lid perfectly fitting?"
"Sammo! Come forth and meet Cao Shan. At that time, a monk came forward and was about to prostrate when the Master said, "Great assembly, take these words of this monk clearly to heart."

Chan Master Fahuai Faquan of Jingshan in Jinling, a successor in the eleventh generation under Yunju Shun Chan Master of Nanyue, was the son of the Shi family of Suizhou. A monk asked: "The ancients said..."
“It does not reach there. Please, Master, explain. The Master said: “When the Master of the School entered the Grand Ancestral Temple, he said, ‘I do not yet understand.

The Master said: “In the warmth of spring, the willow branches turn green. [The student] asked: “What is the one phrase that is most urgent? The Master said: “Fire burning the eyebrows. [The student] asked:
“As for the meaning of the Patriarch facing the wall—what is its intent? The Master said: “Supporting the heavens and propping up the earth. [The student] said: “If it is just like this...”
“How is it when departing? The Master said, “Seven down, eight down. “Question: Regarding the Second Patriarch standing in the snow with his waist level to it—what is the meaning?
The Master said, “Every three years there is an intercalary month. “Question: Why was the Dharma transmitted and the robe bestowed?
The Master said, “Village wine is sufficient for those who buy it. “Question: How is it when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water? The Master said, “Aparagoyānī.”
[The monk] asked, "What is it like after emerging from the water? The Master said, "The Great Sage of Sizhou. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Long hair; a monk's face is ugly. [The monk] asked, "I do not understand the intent of this. The Master said, "Shutting the door for fear of the cold.
[The monk] asked, "When the summer retreat is held at Nan Chan, why is it instead concluded at Jiangshan? The Master said, "The assembly."
The current flows until it meets the end of the sea. [A monk] said, "If that is so, then matters are like one family. The Master said, "In a dream, one arrives at one's hometown.
He ascended the hall and said: "Coming? Not coming. Leaving? Not leaving. Beneath one’s feet is Mount Sumeru; behind one’s head is the Pillar that Supports Heaven.
The Great Canon cannot proclaim it; the Buddha-eye cannot behold it. O Zen practitioners, as you grow old and encounter spring, you know how to cherish it. Last night..."
Flowers fall in countless numbers. [The Master] ascends the hall, draws a single circle, and with his hand pushes it upward, saying:
"Virtuous ones, do you see it? Round and round it leaves the coastal peaks; gradually it emerges from the cloudy heights.
If you have not yet seen it, do not say that Old Man Nanming merely recites a poem about the mid-autumn moon while seated upon the Treasure Flower King’s Throne.
If you can see it, then this night the single orb is full; where is its clear light not present? [Ascending the hall:
"Where you wish to go, you cannot go; where you wish to stay, you cannot stay. Break through the Great San Pass and cast off your birth-clothes. O worthy ones!
"When the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month arrives, tell me: what will you use? After a long silence, he said:
"Willow catkins follow the wind, drifting west and east. Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients were thus; Nan Chan is not thus.
The ancients were not thus; Nan Chan is indeed thus. Does the assembly understand? Wang Po’s robe is short; Li Si’s hat..."
Yanchang’s Ascending the Hall for the Imperial Birthday: Holding up his staff, he struck the Dharma seat once and said, "By this merit, may the Emperor's life be prolonged.
He then descended from the seat. Ascending the Hall: "If people wish to know the path to Nan Chan, there is a tall pine tree before the gate.
It is clearly right under one's feet, not by much; yet alas, travelers go about in such a manner. Do not do so!"
Turning back in haste, one looks upon the towers and pavilions shrouded in mist where the bells toll. Because of the snow, he ascends the hall and calls to the assembly, saying:
"Is there anyone who can pass through this color? After a long silence, he says: "Mañjuśrī laughs; Samantabhadra is angry. Those with no sinews in their eyes are poor for a lifetime.
Everyone they meet says, 'I am retiring from office,' but not a single person has ever been seen beneath the forest trees. [End of Text]
The Hall. A single word from a man of talent is like a lash to a swift horse. If your eyes still flicker and move, you cannot avoid being wrapped in paper and bound with hempen rope.
Underfoot is the earth; above your head is the sky. If you do not believe this, simply look at the eighth and ninth months, when yellow leaves fall in profusion across the mountains and rivers.
Later in life, the Master received an imperial decree and resided at Zhaihaimen Chan Temple in Daxiangguo. He asked the assembly: "I have gone to..."
Zhikai remained at Jiangshan. When asked, "Which course of action—staying or leaving—is correct? the assembly could offer no reply. The Master then took up his brush and wrote a verse:
"Not Buddha, not mind—merely idle conjecture; Obtaining the skin or the marrow—all in vain deliberation. As I depart, take care, O fellow practitioners of Zen."
Outside the gate, a thousand mountains bask in the setting sun.

Having finished writing, he sat and passed away. A monk asked Zen Master Dànjiāo of Tiantóng in Míngzhōu: "The Lin-yún Pavilion soars and the Taibái Peak is high. Having arrived here, how does one advance further?
The Master said: "Simply seek the edge of the wild weeds; do not ask how deep the white clouds are. The monk asked: "I do not yet understand."
"How can one speak of this? The Master said, "When Hanshan meets Shide, the two of them are both deluded at once.
[The monk asked: "As for the supreme vehicle of the patriarchal tradition, how can it be proclaimed? The Master said, "The former words do not reach the latter speech.
Ascending the hall, he said: "How very marvelous! How very mistaken! Of ten fingers, eight have gaps. From the beginning, it has been quite clear; there is no need to bore through it."
"The turtle strikes the tile. He then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Yu of Chongfan in Jianzhou asked a monk: "Linji’s shout rarely meets with one who understands; Deshan’s staff is difficult to encounter for a true master.
How will you act today, Preceptor? The Master said: "Because of your question, I am driven to such a state that—"
He stepped back three paces, his back drenched in sweat, and said, "A master of the school has been encountered today.
The Master replied, "A single word that wounds a person stirs a thousand knives in the belly. The monk drew a line in the air with his hand and said, "What can be done about this?
The Master said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated. A monk asked, "Do you receive those who come in such a manner? The Master replied, "A solitary peak."
"There are no overnight guests. [A monk] asked, "What about one who does not come in such a way? Do you still receive him? The Master said, "The rapids are so steep that they do not detain a boat.
[The monk] said, "Setting aside for a moment 'such' and 'not such,' how is it with the phrase that pierces through the skull?
The Master said, "It is laughable, yet it is also pitiable. [One day] he ascended the hall and said: "You must grasp it while the black bean has not yet sprouted."
After a long silence, he summoned the great assembly and said: "The sword has gone far away.
Chan Master Xiuhui Yuanzhao of Ciyun Monastery in Chuzhou ascended the hall and said: "A sliver of moon reflects in the cold pond; a faint cloud fills the azure sky.
For one who has attained the Way, this is a truly excellent message. Is there anyone here who has attained the Way? He paused. Then he continued: "Faint..."
Clouds pass through your skull; a sliver of moon touches your nostrils. Take care!
A monk asked Master Ziliang of Nanshan in Hangzhou: "What is it like during the time of rest in the sixth month?"
The Master said, "When one has retired from office while still at home, what should be done when a guest suddenly arrives? He asked, "How should one receive and attend to them?

The Master said, "Chew the pure breeze thoroughly and eat the bright moon to satiety. He asked, "Does the student have a share in this? The Master said, "There is no place for the mouth to enter. Then he said:
The oriole sings among the green willows; the magpie caws upon the flowering branches. If one can realize this here and now, there is radiance everywhere. Yet there is yet another principle:
to prevent the sprout and stop the gradual, to contemplate danger while dwelling in peace. What words are these?
Chan Master Jianning Kaiyuan Ying ascended the hall. "There is a mirror hung everywhere; neither ordinary beings nor sages come before it. Who is above? Who is below?
He then took up his staff and said, "This is the staff. Which one is the mirror?

After a long silence, he said, "The moon in the empty expanse of the azure pool through all eternity—only after repeatedly stirring and searching will you finally know. He ascended the hall again. Suddenly—
Suddenly, suddenly! Rising in the east and sinking in the west, without harm and without injury, it pierces skin and penetrates bone.
It is the universal application; neither mind nor Buddha. It strikes through the face; what thing is this? The ancients, for no reason, called it a hawk from the distant heavens.
Let those without eyes look at Li Kou Xi! *Duh duh duh!* (He strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and descends.)
A monk asked Chan Master Huītong of Guizong on Mount Lu, a successor of Chan Master Daomou of Dàméng, "What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth? The Master said:
"His mouth opens in the east and his teeth fall in the west. [A monk] asked, "What is the phrase that cuts off all streams? The Master said, "An iron mountain lies across the road.
[The monk] asked, "What is the phrase that follows the waves and drifts with the current? The Master said, "The boatman sets sail for Yangzhou.
[A monk] asked, "What is the samādhi of every dust mote? The Master said, "Ashes fly and flames rage. [A monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "..."
The general meaning of the Dharma. A student asked: "The Yellow River water flows from the peak of Mount Kunlun.
The Master said: "An iron ox walks upon spring grass. A student asked: "When returning to the West in a single shoe, what was the purpose?
The Master said: "Because one finds joy where conditions arise; it is not out of loathing for a foreign land. A student asked: "What is the matter right before one's face? The Master said: [Silence].

With his nose hanging down from his eyes, he ascended the hall. When the mind follows after appearances, one perceives the arising of defilements; when one clearly perceives the fundamental mind, one knows that the mind is without marks.
Thus, throughout the oceans of lands in the ten directions, every thought-moment is perfectly luminous; within the infinite Dharma gates, every moment of mind is all-pervasive.
For one who is thus, what need is there to go to the eastern outskirts of the City of Enlightenment to meet Mañjuśrī? Only when the gate of the pavilion opens...
He approached Maitreya. Thus he said: "The inexhaustible ocean of all dharma-gates converges within the single dharma of the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
Raising his staff, he said: "This is the one dharma; which is the site of enlightenment? This is the site of enlightenment."
"What is that one dharma? After a long silence, he said, "Look! Look! This staff pierces through everyone's skulls; Mount Sumeru crushes everyone's nostrils.
He struck the incense stand once and said, "For now, understand it right here.
Entering from non-existence into existence is easy; entering from existence into non-existence is difficult. At the point where both existence and non-existence are exhausted—do not [seek further].
From the very beginning, it has been vast and open. Look up! Hanshan and Shide pay homage to Fenggan.
Chan Master Hui Xian of Dajian Xingjiao Monastery in Anzhou ascends the hall and says: "I have a staff; with what can I usually compare it?
It was not gathered from the Southern Mountains, nor is it from the western cliffs of Mount Kunlun. When picked up, it fills the eyes."
Light arises. Let go; it is like a black dragon contracting its neck. If you, my fellow students, would borrow a look at this, you will stand preeminent among men.
He struck the incense stand and descended from his seat.
Zen Master Qingya of Chongfu in Raoyou was asked by a monk, "What is the realm of Chongfu? The Master said, "The sounding of the chime."
A cold night moon; incense smoke like white clouds at dawn. [A monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm?

The Master said, "The monastic is a monastic; the layperson is a layperson. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything more extraordinary beyond this? The Master said, "The golden crown atop the head of Lubi.
[The monk] said, "Layer upon layer you have granted me instruction; for a thousand ages it shall be transmitted. The Master said, "It will make all bystanders laugh to death."
A monk asked Chan Master Jìnghuì Jièbǐ of Fórì Monastery in Lín'ān, a successor of Chan Master Yùwáng Lián, "What is the seal of Vairocana?
The Master said, "Wearing straw sandals while treading through snow. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Every step leaves its trace."
Chan Master Shenhui of Tiantong Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "The eighty-four thousand gates of the *pāramitās* stand perpetually open.
Within this trichiliocosm, as numerous as motes of dust, every Buddha preaches the Dharma—neither speaking of existence nor speaking of non-existence."

It is not said to be non-existent, nor is it said to be existent; it is not said to be both existent and non-existent. Why? Because it transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.
Meeting face-to-face, few recognize it when their eyes meet. Last night the frosty wind leaked its secret: the plum blossoms still cling to the cold branches as before.
A monk asked Chan Master Wuyue Weilin of Mount Jing in Hangzhou: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? The Master said:
"It is not before the time of Dīpaṃkara, nor is it after Śākyamuni. The monk asked: "Does this mean you are a descendant of Yewang?
The Master said: "The peaks of Shen’e are high; at the tail-end, the waters are swift. [The monk] asked: "What is harmony?"
[The monk] continued the family tradition. The Master said, "The divine phoenix sits with brows raised atop its head; the yellow crane strides with its neck held high within the mountain ravines.

[The monk] asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "If you understand, then you understand. What meaning are you looking for? The monk said, "I take my leave," and departed.
The Master said, "Listen to a verse: 'The firewood is spent, white ashes fly; the old monk’s body is as white as snow.'"
Snow. Sitting in meditation by the earthen stove, no one knows. A gray monkey cries out to the bright moon on the western mountains.
Master Zishengyin of Linping, Hangzhou, ascended the hall for the assembly. A monk asked, "Enlightenment cannot be attained through the mind."

"From where did the Master obtain it? The Teacher said, "You blockhead! He then continued, "If one discusses this matter, it is like the sun and moon adorning the heavens, universally illuminating the eight directions.
That the blind do not see it and those beneath a basin do not know it is not because the sun and moon are not bright; rather, it is due to the obstructions of the person themselves.
According to the current standard of the Patriarchs, if you entertain even a single deliberation, there will be a thousand differences. You must strike right through the golden lock."
Barrier. Let the wondrous function unfold freely in all directions.
One day, the abbot of Mida Temple in Wenzhou, Zhengyan, went to visit Xuedou Liang.

Liang asked, "Are you a novice with a master, or a novice without a master? The Master replied, "Setting aside for a moment whether there is or is not, are you, Preceptor, a Chan master with a master, or one without?"
Master Chan said, "Zhang Luang, you are like one who has turned his gourd upside down and wrapped it in climbing vines. Luang asked, "What did you say?
As Luang was about to respond, the Master shook out his sleeves and departed, saying, "Seeing the person is not as good as hearing of their reputation. Luang laughed heartily.
Chan Master Yuanming Zhengtong of Lingyin in Lin’an Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Zhilin. A monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "When walking at night, do not step on white. The monk asked, "Who is the person on the Way? The Master said, "Huang Zhangsan and He Lisi."

Chan Master Liyuan of Zhizhe Mountain in Wuzhou, successor to Chan Master Jiantian of Chengtian, ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "When the Great Function manifests, no rules or regulations remain.
A single point toward the east, and heaven and earth are solemn and still; a single point toward the west, and all things crumble like ice melting away. South...
One finger toward the south: the Southern Dipper flees. One finger toward the north: the Northern Dipper hides away. One finger toward the zenith:
it strikes the nostrils of Śakra. One finger toward the nadir: it pierces through the adamantine waters.
One finger before you all—what kind of matter does this accomplish? After a long silence, he struck the ground once and said: "Pointing at the fleeing deer on the road; before the gate..."
Beating the Dog.
Zen Master Yinzhuang of Ruian, Wenzhou, ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the essence-body of the Dharma?
The Master said, "A large head and small ears. The monk asked, "What is the function of the Dharma-body? The Master said, "The one from Nanyuan has finished plowing and is leading his calf away."
Carrying firewood on his back, he returned and said, "If that is so, then the three bodies are not distinct. The Master said, "A tiger looks at a water mill.
Then he said, "To ask the Buddha with the mind is as far as heaven; to seek the mind through the Buddha makes the Way all the more remote.

If one encounters Yunmen exercising his true authority, he will surely distinguish the dragon from the snake beneath the blow of the staff. After a long silence, he said, "Let those with eyes see for themselves! (Song Shen)
On the thirteenth day of the ninth month in the Ding-si year of the Xining era, Zong bathed, changed his robes, and spoke this verse:

"The spirit-sword leaning in space glows with cold radiance; Buddhas, patriarchs, and demonic armies are gathered by a single stroke. With the moon upon it, it roars through the wind and returns to the precious scabbard;
The iron oxen are startled and scattered at the head of the Qu River. Having finished speaking, he passed away. When his body was cremated and his bones collected, five-colored śarīra were obtained.

Chan Master Zu Jing of Daming, whose secular surname was Zhang and who hailed from the same prefecture, was a dharma heir of Chan Master Shao of Jiufeng. Having renounced Confucian studies, he passed the scriptural examinations and received ordination.

He practiced the exposition of the teachings at Yanqing Monastery. Whenever those of established virtue were stumped by points of doctrinal study, they would invariably question the Master; the Master, however, would simply let his words flow freely.

He distinguished himself and was revered by the assembly. Suddenly, he remarked, "Names and forms are circuitous; how could they be what I take as my primary principle? He then went to study under Jiufeng, who recognized his potential.

When Jiufeng spoke with him, it was as if they had long been together in the monastic community; consequently, he probed him with intense, incisive questions. The Master grasped the essential meaning, and from then on, he gained renown.
Later, while presiding over a hall, he ascended the seat and said: "The beginning of the thirty-six decades; the start of the seventy-two seasonal signs."
Setting aside the final phrase for a moment, how would you express the very first phrase?

[The Master] picks up his staff and says: "On New Year’s Day, one grasps the brush; all matters are auspicious. Act with haste, as required by the decree. "O Assembly, when I, this mountain monk, proclaim it in this way, tell me:
does it still contain the meaning of the Patriarchs? After a long silence, he says: "I remember the black plums of East Village."
4. Every year he personally wrote [this] at his door. (He stood with his staff and descended from the seat.

At the beginning of the Xuande era of Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty, an imperial edict was issued for all monks and nuns to become "virtuous scholars" (*de-shi*). Although the masters of the Dharma deliberated together, not a single word could turn the Emperor’s mind.

The Master composed a commentary on the *Laozi* with a free hand and presented it for the Emperor’s perusal. The Emperor remarked to his close ministers, "Faying’s commentary on the *Daodejing* is concise in expression and profound in principle;
nothing like it has existed since antiquity. It should be granted entry into the Daoist Canon for circulation. He further bestowed upon the Master a ceremonial cap, sash, altar insignia, and edict.

Those who did not understand the Master’s intent often regarded these honors as mere flattery. In the autumn of the following year, an imperial decree was issued to restore the [Daoist] Heavenly... (text fragmentary).

The lower-ranking monk Nisengshi alone did not alter his resolve. When the early years of Emperor Gaozong’s Xianxing era arrived, he rose at dawn wearing a birch-bark hat, donning a crane-feather cloak, holding an ivory tablet, and wearing vermilion shoes.
He had the drums beaten to assemble the congregation and ascended the seat, addressing the multitude, saying:

Orchids flourish in spring valleys; chrysanthemums bloom at autumn fences. All things must undergo growth and decay, each in its own season. Formerly, monks and nuns were disparaged as they devoted themselves exclusively to the Way of the Daoists.
Later, when the Daoist flatterers were suppressed, the status of monks and nuns was restored. Now tell me: what are the physical forms of monks and nuns like?
