The Head Seat of Jingzhong Monastery in Yuezhou addressed the assembly in the vernacular. He cited the words of National Teacher Nanyang:
"If one teaches the Dharma with something to be gained, this is the howling of a jackal; if one teaches the Dharma with nothing to be gained, this is called the lion’s roar. The Master said:

"The National Teacher speaking thus is very much like covering one's ears while stealing a bell. Why? Whether speaking of 'existence' or 'non-existence,' it is all merely the howling of a jackal. All.
"Do you people know the lion’s roar?
*Pah!* Chan Master Chonghui Yuanzhi of Sanzu in Shuzhou Guishan, a native of Lin’an, was asked on his first day opening the hall:
'What is the primary truth? The Master said, 'A hundred pieces, all shattered. [The monk] said, 'If so, then Baochan's one...'"
[The assembly] assembled. [It was] no different from Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa. The Master said: "Bring me the dustpan and broom. Question:

"When you ascend the precious throne, you stand like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high; when the true command is being exercised, you cut off the ten directions. I wonder, by what means do you benefit people? The Master said: "A crossbow with a thousand-jun capacity.
[The assembly] said: "The great assembly receives your grace. The Master said: "Appointing to office according to one's talent. Question: "Although the principle is realized all at once..."
When his temporary illness gradually subsided, he no longer questioned [the Master]. He asked, "What is the principle of sudden awakening?
The Master said, "There is an echo within words. He asked, "And what of it, if one simply acts thus? The Master said, "A golden-maned lion.
[The student] asked, "Birth is like putting on a shirt; death is likewise like taking off trousers. I do not yet understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "It is like this:"
A monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "While walking, it does not hinder one from swinging one's arms.
A monk asked, "What is heaven? The Master said, "It is far too distant. He asked, "What is hell? The Master said, "I cannot let you go.
He asked, "How far apart are heaven and hell? The Master said, "Seven and eight scattered about. A monk asked, "At the place where white clouds unfold..."
The gate to the pavilion opened. Why did Sudhana enter from the outside? The Master said, "To open one's eyes is to go blind.
[Sudhana] asked, "I do not understand; where does he fall? The Master said, "Filling the ditches and blocking the ravines. Question: "What is the Immovable Honored One (Acalanātha)?
The Master said, "A thousand miles in every step."
A monk asked Zen Master Jie of Zishou Monastery in Quanzhou, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "An iron ox gives birth from a stone egg. The monk asked, "What is the phrase for receiving people? The Master said, "Joining one's palms before the main gate.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase for the great function? The Master said, "The crown of the head touches the ground. The monk asked, "What is the phrase of non-action? The Master said:
He was sleeping across the main road. A monk asked, "What is the extraordinary phrase? The Master said, "The exact.
Chan Master Quan of Guanyin in Hongzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The pines grow long and the cypresses grow short. The monk asked, "What is the underlying principle? The Master said, "When the leaves fall, they return to the root."
A monk asked Zen Master Yuanshan of Tianzhang in Yuezhou, "The great has no exterior; the small has no interior. Since there is neither interior nor exterior, what exactly is this thing?
The Master said, "Open your mouth and you see my gallbladder. The monk said, "I do not yet understand. The Master said, "The bitterest of bitternesses.

The monk said, "Exerting one's full strength for the sake of the assembly, yet disaster arises from one’s own private door. The Master struck him, saying, "When told to stop, you refuse to stop; you must [suffer the consequences]."
While waiting for the rain to soak his head, [a monk] asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "Bring me the last phrase. The monk asked, "Why is it so?
The Master said, "The one who sets out first does not arrive. The monk said, "Entering the water, one sees the tall man. The Master said, "Qin Huang struck the jar. Ascending the hall, he said:
"You ask about the meaning of the Westward Transmission; Master Ma [Damo] trampled through the waters of Liaobu. If you recognize but a single hair..."
Head! When has it ever known right from wrong? As soon as the kalpa-fire blazes forth, the deluded seek dry grass.
How could they know that those with clear eyes have long been vexed on your behalf?
Chan Master Yuanjian Taiming of Changlu in Zhenzhou ascended the hall. Looking to his left, he said, "The lion’s throne—how can it avoid its growls?
Looking to his right, he said, "The majesty of the elephant king—how could it forget its backward glance? To take this and flee that—how could a superior man endure such a thing?
To recognize change and discern the opportune moment? At the den of the wild fox, one must know that there is the ordinary here.
The Sage does not traverse these places; they are places that have never been reached by those of antiquity or the present. [The Master] said, "Tell me, what kind of person can walk here?
After a long silence, he said, "A man of spirit naturally possesses the will to charge toward the heavens; do not come from the path where the Tathāgata has trod."
Chan Master Zhizhi of Kaiyuan Temple in Tingzhou ascended the hall and said: "For the family of patch-robed monks, hiding one’s body within the eye of a needle is somewhat spacious;
galloping a horse across the great ocean is extremely narrow. If the general does not mount the drawbridge, the brave warrior’s donning of armor is but a weary labor."
"By day he travels three thousand [li], by night eight hundred. This was not questioned. How would you say it regarding the phrase "without moving a step"?
If you can say it, Guanyin, Shizhi, Mañjuśrī, and Samantabhadra are right before your eyes.
If you cannot say it, you must immediately pull up your skirt, tighten your straw sandals, and investigate! Ascending the hall, he said: "The cold sky is vast and empty; the great earth..."
Vast and boundless. Clouds arise from the mouths of caves; water flows from the high plains. If you hold fast, the ten directions of the world become a blur;
if you let go, east, west, south, and north are all level and plain. Throughout the vast and empty universe there are countless people, each and every one with nostrils reaching to the heavens.
Now I ask you: is it holding fast, or is it letting go? Is there anyone who...?
Can anyone cut it off? If no one can cut it off, there are two great men outside the three gates:
one with knitted brows grasping a sword, and one with glaring eyes brandishing a fist. Study this!
A monk asked Zen Master Huiji of Chengzhao in Pingjiang Prefecture, "If there is nothing at all to be attained, why is the sky so high and the earth so vast?
The Master said, "Narrow. He ascended the hall for formal instruction: "If we discuss this matter, to even lower one's eyebrows is already to have missed it.
How much more so to step forward and demand that this old monk explain it further for you? Now it has been explained; do you understand?"
Do you understand? Yesterday it rained; today it is clear.
A monk asked Chan Master Fayu Huiyuan of Lin’an Prefecture, “What is the very first phrase? The Master said:
King Liang did not understand and asked, "What is the final phrase? The Master said, "Bodhidharma crossing the river.
Chan Master Zhicheng of Shimen in Xiuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Presented face-to-face, there is nothing else. If it were like this, would it not be most excellent?
This mountain monk, however, has no choice but to bend for your sakes. If you turn toward the patch-robed monk..."
"There is not even a single point before one that can be grasped. All you Zen practitioners, tell me: what can possibly be said before a patch-robed monk? After a long silence, he said:
"In the deep autumn, a thousand homes share the rain behind the curtains; at sunset, a single flute accompanies the wind atop the towers."
At Qiyin Monastery in Quanzhou, there was Chan Master Ping. A monk asked, "What is the ordinary way?
The Master said, "The monk bows with palms joined; the Daoist holds his fists aloft. A monk asked, "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, how should one proceed?
The Master said, "Put on your clothes and eat your food. The monk asked, "Is there anything else besides this? The Master said, "Yes. The monk asked, "What is it? The Master said, "The midday meal."
He further requested another bowl of tea.
A monk asked Chan Master Yun of Dinghui in Pingjiang Prefecture, "What is the single phrase for benefiting others? The Master said, "If you see it and do not seize it.
The monk said, "I do not yet understand. The Master said, "It is lost by a thousand miles."
A monk asked Chan Master Wang of Dading Tongyuan Monastery in Jianning Prefecture, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, “A tortoise entering the market. The monk asked, “What is the intent of this? The Master said, “When it is time to withdraw the head, one simply withdraws the head.”
A monk asked Chan Master Wujun Tiefo, "What is the master’s house style? The Master said, "A single fathom of withered trees stand as neighbors;
three matters of autumn clouds—who else recognizes them? The monk said, "I have received your instruction on the master’s house style;
what is the message for others? The Master said, "The new moon has its night of fullness; the human heart never knows when it is satisfied."
Chan Master Faben of Anjingshou was the son of the Lu family from Qiantang. A monk asked, "The talk that leaves nothing to be sung about cuts off people’s mouths.
What is the phrase that cuts off people’s mouths? The Master struck him and said, "If it were so, then one phrase would circulate, and devas and humans would prick up their ears.
The Master continued, "I only fear it is not jade; even if it were jade, it is still large."
Qichu said, "I am solely intent on circulating [the teachings]. The Master said, "Let them speak nonsense as they please.
When Tianyi was invited to ascend the hall, he was summoned by Shengshou of Wujiang to serve as abbot; feeling at a loss whether to accept or decline, he simply followed his karmic conditions.
All of this was due to the Abbot’s guidance and instruction, and his encouragement from beginning to end. If one were to act according to the true mandate of today, it would be appropriate to do so.
"A single blow of the staff would have killed him; how could he be allowed to stand before the seat? Nevertheless, it is said: 'Only by raising a child does one see a father's kindness.
Master Qichan of Kaisheng Temple in Hezhou, upon ascending the hall, delivered this statement: 'The field for selecting Buddhas has opened; humans and devas are gathered everywhere.'"
[The Master] said, "There is no one who has long experienced the field of awakening. Let any guest who has finished their Zen practice come forward to meet me.

At that time, a monk stepped forward. The Master said, "A true practitioner! A true practitioner! The monk replied, "Do not be in such a hurry. The Master said, "It seems you are not a true practitioner after all.
The monk held up his sitting cloth and said, "Look! Look! In the kingdom of Magadha, this decree was personally enacted. The Master asked, "What are you doing right now?"

[The monk] was born. The assembly prostrated. The Master said, "A dragon’s head and a snake’s tail. [The monk] asked, "When one cannot distinguish east from west nor differentiate north from south, a student comes before you;
I beg the Master for a reception. The Master said, "I do not receive you. [The monk] asked, "Why do you not receive me? The Master said, [silence].
"You cannot distinguish east from west; you cannot tell north from south. [The monk] said, "I thought the red-bearded one was a barbarian, yet here is a barbarian with a red beard.
The Master said, "Sulu sulu. [The monk] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "I give you thirty blows."
[The monk] asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "Murder may be forgiven; rudeness is difficult to tolerate.
He ascended the hall, took up his staff, and said, "Great assembly, look quickly with your eyes! With a single stroke, Mount Sumeru is shattered into a hundred fragments.
With one blow of the staff, Jambudvīpa tilts to the east and leans to the west, leaving no escape. Yet, I keep it within the hands of Kaisheng, and let him..."
Unable to exhale, he struck the ground once.
Zen Master Weili of Mount Heng in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "If one discusses this matter, it is difficult to clarify directly.
The Three Worthies cannot fathom it; the Ten Sages do not know it. Reaching this point, one must loftily uphold the Patriarchal Command and lay across the sword of Mohe. When a Buddha..."
If not a single speck of dust remains, how can anything be established? I shall simply cause Mount Sumeru to be pulverized and the great ocean to wither away.
I will open up a narrow path for you all to deliberate upon. But tell me, what is it that you are deliberating? After a long silence, he said: "Salt is expensive; rice is cheap."
A monk asked Chan Master Xianming Shanzu of Beishan in Lin’an Prefecture, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, “For nine years he sat blankly facing the wall; now he has returned to the West again. The monk asked, “Why is it so?
The Master said, “Fine food does not satisfy one who is already full. The monk asked, “What is the Dharma-preaching of the insentient? The Master said, “The lamp.”
A hanging lantern was suspended from a pillar. [The Master] asked, "Who can hear this? The Master said, "Walls and tiles have ears.
Chan Master Simian of Qixia in Mingzhou was asked by a monk, "All Buddhas appear in the world for the sake of sentient beings. For whose sake do you, Venerable Sir, appear in the world?
The Master said, "Not for you, Dharma brother. The monk said, "If that is so, then the pond is deep and the waves are surging."
[The Master] was silent. The student spoke at length with a low voice. The Master said, "A dragon is not formed by striking it with a staff.
Chan Master Lingkan of Yunmen in Yuezhou was asked by a monk, "How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said:

While burning incense in the Buddha Hall, a student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Joining palms at the main gate. Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Defilements have not yet been shattered;
when encountering objects, a thousand differences arise. Yet the mirror of the mind is perfectly luminous, with not a single hair’s breadth of obstruction. The numinous light shines brightly."
It stands alone, revealed before you; past and present are both forgotten, and the paths of sage and ordinary being are severed.

Only upon reaching this point can one exercise mastery in rolling up or spreading out, applying oneself without deficiency, appearing and disappearing, coming and going, whether among humans or in the heavens.
O Great Assembly, although it is thus, suppose someone were to seize you by the collar and ask: "Where do you place this staff? How would you respond?
"Is there anyone who can speak? Come forward and speak! The assembly remained silent. He then struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Zen Master Yuantan of Taiping on Mount Tiantai ascended the hall and said: "This Dharma has no fixed school; it is established according to conditions.

Sound and form, movement and stillness—perception and hearing are never obscured. Its applications vary in a thousand ways, like a bell waiting to be struck. If you can realize this, then for now, follow along."
At that time, he put on his robes and ate his meal. Had this been Deshan or Linji, one would have had to strike out on foot wearing straw sandals to seek instruction.
A monk asked Zen Master Furi Wenzu of Lin’an Prefecture, “Please grant us an indication of your sublime and steep mechanism.
The Master said, “Standing with eight characters at the crossroads. The monk asked, “As for a boat sailing on the bottom of the great ocean, what about Mount Sumeru?”
[The monk] said, "A horse gallops upward. How about that? The Master said, "A tortoise facing the fire.
[The monk] said, "In that case, one can ride the tiger’s head and skillfully grasp its tail. The Master struck him once with his staff and said, "Prostrate yourself!"
A monk asked Chan Master Zong of Wangxian Mountain in Yizhou, "I do not ask about the four seasons and the eight seasonal festivals;
how is it with the single phrase of everyday life? The Master said, "Heyishan beats the drum. The monk asked, "Is this not where the student should apply effort?"
The Master said, "Guizong drags a stone. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "A true patch-robed monk indeed.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Southern Terrace black-odor root; Northern Sea *tianma*; Xinyu *fuzi*; Chenshi cinnabar.
[Pausing for a long while] Do you all understand? [He remained standing for a long time. Ascending the hall, he said: 'Do you all consent to let go? If you do not let go, then... "
"Carry it away. He then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Yongji of Jingjue Monastery at Wufeng in Ruizhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "One cannot step upon it even in the middle of the crossroads. The monk asked, "If one goes in this very manner, what then? The Master said, "For now, proceed slowly."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Qingping crosses the water; Touzi sells oil. Of the three hundred and sixty days in a year, there is no need to seek them repeatedly within the count.
Striking the meditation seat with his whisk, he descended from the seat.
A monk asked Chan Master Xiang of Wujun Army Buddha’s Footprint: “What is the essence of *prajñā*?
The Master said, “A cold lamp hidden within a lapis lazuli palace. The monk asked, “What is the function of *prajñā*? The Master said, “Vividly alive.
The monk asked, “Regarding that which is of a single color and without change—calling it a white ox on open ground—is this truly definitive? The Master said, “Its head...”
[The monk] asked, "What about when the horns have not yet grown? The Master said, "Do not trespass upon the crops.
Chan Master Huiyun of Mingyin, in Pingjiang Prefecture, ascended the hall and, holding his staff horizontally across his chest, said:

"If one proceeds in this manner, it results in a state where there are no two suns in the sky and no two kings in the land; even the Elder Śākyamuni must suppress his breath and swallow his voice. A great... [text fragment ends].
The teachings of the Treasuries are like wood gnawed by insects; even if one drills and probes them from above, they are nothing but a holeless iron hammer.
Even if one were to pick them up with a confident hand, they would still be mere leftover dregs and stale food. Only by spitting them all out at once does one attain a slight degree of resonance.
Thus one falls into empty oblivion; it remains nothing more than the livelihood of the realm of ghosts. Do you understand? Only after the rain does one know the verdant hue of the mountain colors;
only when faced with difficulty does one see the mind of a true man. (He plants his staff and descends from the seat.)
Chan Master Bian of Xinghua County’s Xitai Monastery ascended the hall and cited the words of Linji regarding the "True Person of No Rank.
He then called to the assembly, saying: "The old fellow Linji usually had a backbone as hard as iron;
yet when he reached this point, it was as if he were lost in the midday sun or seeing flowers in the air. Even if one were to say that the True Person of No Rank is..."
"A dried-up dung pellet. This is truly like a mud-turtle dragging its tail; that monk knew only the extreme heat of late summer, but did not know the bitter cold of mid-winter.
According to what was appropriate for that time, what words could he have used? He has effectively blocked the tongues of all people in the world.
Xitai simply leaves it at that; yet, seeing that "out of sight is out of mind" is not enough, he cannot help but extend a hand and let things fall into disorder.
Linji’s burden and Xitai’s heap—one burden, one heap—to whom shall they be entrusted?
"Following the teaching, it is scattered in all directions; it brings laughter to the ancient masters of yore.
Master Zizhen of Yongtai in Chuzhou ascended the hall and said: "The golden wind begins to fan; pines and bamboos cast their interlacing shadows.
The moon in the water is clear and distinct, yet the patch-robed monks are at a loss. Do you understand? If there is one who understands, come forth and convey a message. The mountain...
The Monk gave him proof. After a long silence, he said: "A chisel in a cloth bag—those who do not poke their heads out are the true masters.

Chan Master Fayan of Yenan in Wuning, Nanchang, was the son of the Xu family of Linchuan. In his youth, he served at Chengtian Monastery in his home prefecture and left the household life out of a longing for seclusion.
At the age of twenty, he received full ordination through his mastery of the sutras. He traveled to various regions to visit Xuedou Xian. Xuedou...

Upon his death, he followed the teachings of Tianyi Huai and again traveled extensively throughout all directions, claiming to be one who had "fully participated" in the training. He returned to Linchuan and resided at Ruyi Yuan on Huang Mountain.
Before ten years had passed, the halls and pavilions were like a *pūranakalpa* city; he then abandoned them and, with staff and alms bowl, went to Shanglan in Nanchang.
Later, he resided at Yan’en Temple in Wuning. His dwelling consisted of only a few wooden pillars for a thatched cottage, with dilapidated beds and broken storage jars;

the Master took pleasure in this. The county magistrate, seeking to rectify the local elite, plotted to renovate the temple into something entirely new. The Master smiled and said, "The Dharma of the donors is fundamentally intended to deliver sentient beings.

To force this upon them now when they have not yet awakened their resolve is called 'worldly labor,' not 'Buddhist activity. He firmly declined the offer. He remained there in retirement for ten years.
Thus the monastic community was established. The Master and Fayun Xiu were brothers. Xiu once sent a letter inviting the Master; upon reading it, the Master simply smiled.
When someone asked him the reason for this, the Master said, "When I first saw Xiu, he possessed a brilliant spirit, and I thought he could be spoken to regarding the Way.
But from this day forward, I know his folly. A foolish person is precisely one with whom it is impossible to speak. The questioner—
[The Emperor] asked, "What is this? The Master replied, "It is the law of a bhikṣu to travel through the four directions carrying only a single bowl.
Since Xiu cannot do this, yet builds a large house at a major crossroads to beg for food from others and support several hundred idle men—is this not folly?"
The Master frequently said to people, "All matters follow conditions; this is the Dharma of peace and happiness.

On the first day of the eighth month in the Jiazi year of the Yuanfeng era of Emperor Shenzong of the Song dynasty, he entered parinirvāṇa. He had lived for sixty-one years and had spent forty-one summer retreats in meditation.

The layman Yang Jie of the Ministry of Rites, whose courtesy name was Cigong and style name was Wuweizhe, traveled extensively to study under various renowned masters before following Tianyi Huikong later in life.
Huikong frequently cited the kōans and sayings of the elder Pang, urging him to investigate them deeply and reach profound realization.

Later, while serving as a ritual official at Mount Tai, one day at the crowing of a cock, he beheld the sun rising like a great platter; he suddenly attained great enlightenment. Thereupon, he took no further notice of his son’s marriage or his daughter’s betrothal.
The verse on not marrying says: "When a man grows old, he must marry; when a woman grows old, she must wed. What leisure do we have to further discuss talk of non-arising?
He wrote this and sent it with his robe. The recipient praised it as excellent. Later, he met Fuyong Kai.

The Master asked, "How many years has it been since we parted? Fuyong said, "Seven years. The Master asked, "Have you been studying the Way? Have you been practicing Zen? Fuyong said, "I am not hitting [the mark]."
Regarding this drum and flute, the Master said, "If that is so, then you are merely wandering through mountains and waters, capable of nothing at all.
Rong replied, "It has not been long since we parted, yet you are well able to discern with lofty insight. The Master laughed heartily. The Master had a verse for departing from the world which said:
"There is nothing to be attached to, And nothing to be abandoned. In the great void of space, There are only 'zhi-hu-ye-zhe. Taking what is mistaken as correct, I go to the Western Pure Land."
Joy. Master Zong of Chengxin was a successor of Zen Master Yao of Huirì in Pengzhou.
A monk asked: "The ancients said, 'I have a phrase; wait for the tongueless person.'"
[The monk] understood the words. He then said to the Master, "I do not yet understand; what is the meaning? The Master replied, "One may deliberate well beneath the shadowless tree.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "The tiles shatter and the ice melts away."
Chan Master Kezun of Zhongji in Fuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Baoben Lan, ascended the hall and said: "Pucker up! Pucker up! Pucker up! What is that chirping at the bottom of the well?"
"Even if it were the three thousand great chiliocosms, it would still be nothing but a ghost cave. *Pfft!* Ascending the hall: "Last night at the fourth watch I arose;
I laughed and laughed without ceasing. Fortunately, I had been enjoying a good sleep. A frost bell strikes and is split in two.
Ascending the hall: "Heishan and Puhua suddenly went mad; they beat drums and shook bells for a theatrical performance. The kalpa-fire blazes through..."
However, it is fitting to brew tea. A great mountain breeze blows; enjoy the coolness. Four snakes in a single basket—watch them wriggle. Two rats gnawing at a vine—how lacking in self-awareness!
Where does the moon go when the vast ocean is bright? In the palace of Guanghan lies a bed of white silver. *Du!* [He] ascends the hall.
"The eighty-four thousand profound Dharma gates—each gate has a path that gives rise to heaven and earth. What about this one?"
This one cannot be stepped upon; it is simply because there are too many legs on the centipede. Not only are there many legs, but there are also many mouths;

a nailed beak and an iron tongue only serve to increase its ugliness. Picking up the mallet, raising the whisk, washing the mud, and casting up the eyebrows or blinking the eyes—these are like chickens in a coop.
If you wish to know the place where Buddhas and Patriarchs do not reach: the door is closed, fallen flowers lie scattered, and spring birds sing.
The *upādhyāya* Faming of Kaiyuan Monastery in Xingzhou relied upon the *Benmo* (Fundamental) teachings. Not long after, he attained profound *dharmakṣānti*.

Later, he returned to his hometown, where his conduct became dissolute; he was fond of wine and gambling, and whenever he was heavily intoxicated, he would sing several stanzas of Liu Yuxi’s lyrics as his daily routine.

The local villagers treated him with contempt; when summoned for a vegetarian feast, he would refuse, but when summoned for wine, he would comply. This continued for more than ten years, until everyone pointed at him and called him "Drunk Monk.
One day, he said to the assembly of monks in the temple, "I shall depart tomorrow morning. Do not go elsewhere."
The assembly laughed at him in secret. At dawn the next day, he adjusted his robes, took his seat, and called out loudly, "I am departing!
Listen to one verse from me! When the assembly heard this, they rushed to see him. The Master then said: "A lifetime spent stumbling in intoxication, Yet even in intoxication there was discernment.

Where shall I be when the wine is clear tonight? Willows by the riverbank, the morning breeze, and the waning moon. Having finished speaking, he became silent. They shook him, but he had already passed away.
[The previous master] has shed his skin.

Master Guangji of Shanglan Monastery in Hongzhou, a successor of Chan Master Chengxinming, ascended the hall. Holding his staff horizontally across his chest, he called to the assembly, saying: "Do you still..."

"Do you recognize this old fellow from Shanglan? His eyes are like wooden pegs; his mouth is like a flat carrying-pole. He knows nothing of fine or coarse, nor does he distinguish between salt and vinegar.
To preside over a monastery in such a manner is a hundred thousand offenses. Do any of you, venerable Chan practitioners, have anything to offer by way of repentance for this mountain monk?
After a long silence, he said, "This is driving me to my wit's end! He struck the ground with his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Miaofeng Ruchan of Fuzhou, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Guangyin Yao, ascended the hall and said: "Today is the anniversary of the Tathāgata’s birth.
Monastics throughout the land all use fragrant water to bathe him, together repaying his vast kindness. Why is it that, in the teachings, [it is otherwise]?"
The Way: The Tathāgata comes from nowhere. Since he comes from nowhere, one does not know who it is that has descended to be born.
Please try to speak on this for me; if you can speak it, your debt of gratitude will be repaid.
If you cannot speak it, on the eighth day of the fourth month next year, I shall still pour water over your head.
A monk asked Chan Master Jingwu of Qingshan Monastery at Baizhang in Lin’an, a successor of Chan Master Yunju Yuan, "What is the Buddha? The Master said:
He asked, "Who? The monk replied, "I am specifically asking the Master. The Master said, "A hawk flies over Silla. Ascending the hall, he said:
"To speak is to move the lips; to act is to move the feet. Even if one neither speaks nor acts, it is still a mistake, a mistake! He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.
Chan Master Huitai of Shanguan in Changzhou ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas appeared in the world to extensively expound the Three Vehicles;

Bodhidharma came from the West to secretly transmit the Great Matter. Those of superior capacity transcend [delusion] instantaneously upon hearing a single word; those of middling or inferior capacity must gradually clarify the ground of their own minds.

Turning the light back upon itself, one suddenly illuminates oneself. How is this different from the crimson sun in the sky, moving alone without partiality, or the bright pearl in a bowl, turning spontaneously without being pushed?
Nevertheless, although it is thus, this is only for beginners; as for the higher mechanism, they have not yet stepped upon it.
Furthermore, tell me: what is the upward-moving pivot? After a long silence, he said: "Looking up at the sky, one does not see the sky.
Chan Master Jingming Fayin of Chang'an in Luzhou ascended the hall and said: "In the heavens the moon is full; in the human world it is half-moon."
"Seven or eight" is a number; the actual matter is difficult to calculate. Let us set aside for now the failure to distinguish between the hidden and the manifest.
As for the phrase "before black and white are distinguished," how do you speak? After a long silence, he said: "Meeting within the autumn colors, conversing together under the bright moon.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The wondrous secret of the Patriarchs has nothing else to be said. Even with a beak of nails and an iron tongue, one cannot avoid turning cleverness into a failure."
How clumsy! Vimalakīrti has already let slip his celestial mechanism.
Chan Master Shouchu of Fuyan on Mount Fucha in Luzhou ascends the hall. A monk asks, "What is the samādhi of utilization?
The Master says, "Picking up the spoon and setting down the chopsticks. The monk asks, "What is the single path of straightforwardness? The Master says, "It cannot be stepped upon."
[The Master] said, "Having stepped upon it, what then? The teacher replied, "In all four directions and eight points. He then said, "If one discusses this matter:
if one lets go, the moon is bright and the wind is clear on the path of Caoxi; if one holds fast, the clouds are gathered and the mist has rolled away before the peak of Shaoshi.
Such discourse already involves many paths; it can only be believed through the resonance of a single thought-moment, and does not come from others."

"Attained! But tell me, Great Assembly, attained from where? After a long silence, he said: "The flowing water has always been in the sea; the setting moon does not leave the sky. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The characteristic of the very nature is a single expanse of clear sky; the nature of the very characteristic is a thousand waves rising in competition.
If you penetrate the source, the clear current flows without obstruction. Therefore, in raising a single thought, the dharma-gates as numerous as dust motes and sands appear."
Suddenly revealed: by picking up a single hair, the realms of boundless lands are manifested all at once. But tell me, where are Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra?
Not running downhill, such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter. Thereupon he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Deshan Renhui of Dingzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Venerable One of Immovability? The Master said, "A thousand come, ten thousand go.
The monk said, "If that is so, then one's heels do not even touch the ground. The Master said, "In fact, it is you who understand.

He ascended the hall for a discourse: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes picking and choosing. Just do not harbor hatred or love, and it will be transparently clear. As for this mountain monk..."
Not so. The ultimate Way is most difficult; it requires discernment. If there is neither aversion nor attachment, how could one fail to see its clarity?
Chan Master Yongmin of Xiangji Monastery at Shengshou Temple in Liuzhou ascended the hall and said: "The wooden horse breaks through the path of a thousand riders;
the iron ox penetrates ten thousand layers of barriers. Where are the wooden horse and the iron ox right now? After a long silence, he said: "Startled!"
"Geese on the sands rise toward the evening sky; two or three rows slant away toward the sea-gate.
Chan Master Rixiangzi Lai of Ruizhou ascended the hall and, looking over the assembly, said: "As a patriarch of our school, one must take up the guiding thread wherever one is.
Responding to stimuli through question and answer, one kills or gives life according to the moment. With the eye of mind sharp and clear, how can there be room for demons? If..."
Realization is attained at the tip of the staff; one takes responsibility upon the shout. To bury the ancestral style and feel shame for the deeds of those who came before is a failure.
The single path of turning the body lies beyond hesitation. When a single breath does not return, one is no different from a dead man. O Great Assembly, even if you reach such a state—
These words remain buried; there is as yet no path for breakthrough. I dare ask you all: what is this path of breakthrough? Is there anyone who can say it?
If not, this mountain monk cannot help but reveal it for you. After a long silence, he said:
"The jade leaves the Jingshou Mountains, its cold radiance stirring; The sword emerges from Fengcheng, its purple vapor sweeping across."
Chan Master Congyi of Luzhou ascended the hall. "The mirror of mind is bright and unimpeded.
He then picked up his staff and said, "To call this a 'staff' is an obstruction; not to call it a 'staff' is also an obstruction.
Apart from these two, how is it ultimately? Do you wish to understand? Whether obstructed or unobstructed—who is there to oppose it? The great earth, the mountains, and the rivers."
Utterly shattered and pulverized.
Chan Master Guang of Qianming on Fenghuang Mountain in Xiangzhou ascended the hall and said: "The sun rises from the east; the moon sets in the west.
Coming and going as swift as a shuttle, it drives people to become white bones. I, this mountain monk, have a Dharma that can serve as a protection."
The Art of Life: Birth and death do not interfere with one another. Smash the cave of the vital spirit! *Du du*—what thing is this?
It is neither a sentient being nor a Buddha. Investigate!
Chan Master Daolin Guanghui Baolin of Changsha was a native of Suzhou. In his youth, he studied the sutras and śāstras;
having visited Yuantong, he realized the ancestral intent. Lord Wang Jinggong invited him to take up the abbacy at Xingjiao in Guangde, and subsequently he moved to Jingde in Chiyang.
At Wanshan of Mount Lu and Daolin of Tanzhou, [the Master] ascended the hall and said: "The clouds have withdrawn from the face of the peaks; the sun rises over Fusang.
A chilling wind blows, and withered leaves fall in profusion. Within the Xiang River, white waves surge to the heavens; before the gate of Guanghui, the ground is as level as the palm of a hand.
If you are a monk who knows this, you sit securely in peace and stability. If it is not yet so, you cannot avoid [the consequences]."
Reaching for heaven and groping on the ground—ascending the hall. Today is the fifth day of the fifth month. Among the myriad plants and sprouts, who does not behold them?
When Sudhana gathered medicinal herbs with Mañjuśrī, they acted as master and attendant to one another, killing or giving life according to the occasion.
You followers of Zen, do not be reckless! Raise your eyebrows and look well! Picking it up at random with the hand—do you know it or not? The sweet is sweet, and the bitter is bitter.
A monk asked Master Guicaizhi of Fengyang Shouzhou Huoqiu, "What is the patriarchs' secret, hidden meaning?
The Master said, "Even the Buddha-eye cannot see it. The monk asked, "Why can it not be seen? The Master said, "Because it is the secret, hidden meaning.

The monk asked, "When a single word is spoken and there is mutual accord, what then? The Master said, "The crimson sky is revealed. The monk asked, "What about when no word is used? The Master said, [Silence].
"How is it? The Master said, "Carrying water, dragging mud. [Question: "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what is it like?
The Master said, "The eyebrows are three feet long.
Chan Master Xinzhin Zhixun of Kaishan on Mount Lu in Nankang was a native of Ruzhou. He went to Yuan Tong to seek awakening and attained realization there.
Initially he resided at Yanchang; subsequently he moved to Kaixian Foguo. He petitioned for a purple robe and a return to the capital.
Marshal Zhang memorialized that he be granted the master title "Seal of the Mind. [The Master] ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Zhaozhou employs three grades of reception for people;

"What is the fundamental matter? The Master said, "Receive the hook; do not fixate on its meaning.

When Panxing asked Subhūti to chant, "The Way is manifested through non-explanation," he further inquired, "I wonder, Master, by what means do you manifest the Way? The Master replied, "This mountain monk is simply like iron.

To deliberate further and engage in more discussion would only result in another manifest proclamation. Having stood for a long time, he returns to the hall; let us go drink tea. At dawn, during the hour of Yin (3–5 a.m.):
When the sun rises over Mount Fūsang, who is it that it illuminates? Within this, those who have not yet attained understanding rush north and south;

Ascending the hall, he struck the drum and said: "Everyone who comes up here sees that all phenomena are manifest before them; there is no need for further refinement.
All you practitioners of Zen, why is this so? Each and every one of these great men shall, for your sake, open up a single thread."

Chan Master Chongsheng Yizhi of Beitianwang Monastery in Luzhou ascended the hall and said: "The ancestral command of the Zen school has long been stifled by those who merely sit with their mouths sealed shut.
The wondrous peak spans the universe; yet here, one must find a way to emerge. After a long silence, he said:

The abbot of Qixian, Zhirou, of Nan’gang, studied under Yuan Tong and attained realization. He then offered this verse of karmic resonance:
"For twenty years I have traveled on pilgrimage, Wandering through all of Eastern and Western Luoyang. Now I have arrived at Qixian;
Not a single step has been moved."
A monk asked Zen Master Zongyong Huiyan of Tianxi in Jinling, "What was the purpose of facing the wall for nine years?

During the Tianxi era, the true-body śarīra of Śākyamuni Buddha was reinterred there; the tomb faced south (yi) and looked toward the west (xin), with the Yue King’s Terrace serving as the front desk.

After a long silence, he struck the ground once and said: “It reaches the high; it reaches the low.”

He said: "It has been penetrated. He ascended the hall and said: "The dragon soars through the azure heavens; its transformations are boundless. The phoenix flies through the clear sky; who knows its traces?

Therefore it is said: 'It cannot be grasped; it cannot be relinquished. Within that which cannot be obtained, it is simply thus obtained.'"
Furthermore, tell me: what have you attained? After a long silence, he said: "Do not engage in false conceptualization.

[The student] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "All things emerge from this very place."

When Su Shi was stationed in Weiyang, the Master sent an attendant to submit a petition to resign from his office and return to his old hermitage by West Lake.

Su Shi, together with his subordinates, went to the Stone Pagoda, beat the drum to assemble the congregation, and produced a memorial from his sleeve, instructing Chao Wujiu to read it aloud. The text read as follows: [The memorial follows.]
Venerable Jigong, you have opened the gate of non-duality and bestowed an inexhaustible treasury. To reflect upon our long separation by West Lake is also a matter of chance;
yet, to stay for a short while for the sake of Dongpo is nothing that cannot be done. For a moment we bow our heads, once again awaiting the striking of the mallet.
The ferry boat returns to the crossing; the colors of the clouds and mountains remain as they were. With the arrival of autumn and the passing rain, the sound of the bells and drums is renewed.
At this point, the Master’s fame was preeminent throughout his time.
Chan Master Dao Rong Jue Yin of Xuedou in Mingzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Changlu Fu. He was the son of the Chen family of the local prefecture.
A monk asked, "What is it like when Hanshan meets Shigede? The Master said, "Raising an eyebrow, flashing lightning. The monk asked, "Is there anything further? The Master said, "Open [your eyes]."
A ray of light issued from his mouth, and he asked, "What is the path that leads upward? The Master replied, "Seven, six, eight.
Chan Master Zongze Cijue of Changlu in Zhenzhou was the son of the Sun family of Luozhou. He was born during the Yuanfeng era.

His father encouraged him to leave the household life, so he went to Changlu to seek ordination under Yuantong Xiu. After Xiu departed, Guangzhao succeeded him; Zongze subsequently studied under Guangzhao.
One day, while ascending the steps, he attained enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "Raising my feet to step upon the brick stairs, Clearly there is no other dharma.
Beside the yellow-waxwood tree, I laugh heartily; Ten thousand miles of blue sky, a single moon. Zhaoke and Yang Gongwei requested him to appear in the world. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
"When Bodhidharma sat facing the wall, what was the principle of this? The Master remained silent for a long time. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Today, having been questioned by this monk, I am left speechless. He then continued: "From the winter solstice to Cold Food Festival, there are one hundred and five days.
Upon the road for the living, the dead are countless. They thrust their heads into thorn-bushes, imagining the suffering of sentient beings.
As for the matter of visiting graves: they merely add earth to a heap of bones. Only those who have left the household life do not tread upon the path of non-arising."
The Road. The assembly, tell me: where does it go? Do you understand? To South Tiantai; to North Wutai. Entering the Hall: New Korea has no secret formula.
When speaking, one does not shrink from having one's tongue cut out. If one can only achieve the correspondence between mind and mouth, one will not have fully realized its utility for a lifetime.
Now tell me: what is the phrase that corresponds between mind and mouth? (He remains silent for a long while.)
He said, "A scorched brick strikes the frozen ground to its very depths. [Case closed. Question: "When the six gates have not yet ceased their activity, what is it like?
The Master said, "Incense is burned inside the nostrils. The student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A drum is beaten inside the ears.
Question: "What is the merit of meritless merit? The Master said, "The clay ox does not move its feet; throughout the world there are no fallow fields. [The student said,] "In that case..."
"Is it not then the case that one's efforts have not been exerted in vain? The Master said, "Though his great supernatural powers were vast, he could not avoid meeting this 'penetrating staff.
He ascended the hall and said: "Though gold dust is precious, if it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract. Once the gold dust is removed, where is the eye?
If you are like this, you have not yet emerged from the thicket of brambles. To seek realization at the tip of the staff, or to take responsibility under a shout—this is precisely [the trap]."
Ascending the hall at Jinfengke: "Beyond the pavilion, the colors of Mount Zijin are exquisite; before the gate, the sound of the Amṛta waters is cold.
Beneath the shade of ancient locust trees and amidst the clear breeze, let me point it out once more for you all. He held up his staff and said:
"Do you see? He struck the incense table and said, "Do you hear? He leaned his staff against it and said, "If the eyes and ears are unobstructed, one is sufficient wherever one is;
the sound of water and the colors of mountains flow on of their own accord."
Chan Master Huiri Zhijue Guangdeng of Pingjiang Prefecture was the son of the Mei family of that same district. Entering the hall, he sat for a long while and then said:
"Rest! Rest! Rest! All in vain, drifting aimlessly. The fishing pole remains firmly in hand; the fish are cold and do not swallow the hook. He gave a shout.
The master descended from his seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Zongchu of Langye Mountain in Chuzhou, "What is the realm of Langye?
The master said, "The red sun shines upon the golden realm; autumn mists dye it with azure lapis lazuli. The monk asked, "What is the person within the realm?"
The Master said: "Lifting one's head, ten thousand peaks; in hand, a single staff.
A monk asked Chan Master Daocheng of Mount Panlong in Chuzhou: "I have heard that you have already attained the essential meaning of Huangmei.
How do you instruct people regarding the Great Dharma? The Master said: "A thousand flowers bloom in splendor; a single breeze stirs the cold of the river. [The monk] said: "Lean bamboo..."

He possessed high principles; like drifting clouds, his traces were不定 (indeterminate). The Master said: "A single verse of Chu-gē is enough to kill the sorrow. Entering the hall for instruction, he said:
"Picked up at random from the hand, there is no such thing as a 'mysterious function. The nature of numinous awareness is ever thus throughout kalpas. Movement and stillness follow conditions."
It is like a valley responding to an echo; manifesting ten billion bodies, he follows the myriad beings in their various ways so that they all return to the Ultimate Way.
Serene through past and present, you must further rouse your spirit and look clearly. "Do you all see? After a long silence, he said:
"A single pool of autumn water, its bottom always visible; a thousand-foot mountain pine, never growing branches."
Chan Master Lingquan Ziling of Jia Shan in Liuzhou was a successor of Chan Master Furu Cai.
He was the son of the Zhou family of Changzhou. A monk asked: "The golden rooster pecks through the lapis lazuli shell;
the jade hare pushes open the gates of the azure sea. These are but shadows and lights of the human world. What is [the reality] beyond them?"
The Master said, "The patriarch’s pivot is such that a needle cannot pierce it. The monk asked, "What about before the first sign has even arisen?
The Master raised his whisk. The monk asked, "How should one comprehend this? The Master said, "Gazing upward with bared brows toward the rising sun.
The monk asked, "What was it like before the primordial chaos was divided? The Master said, "The spring breeze blows gently. The monk asked, "And what is it like after it has been divided?"
The Master said, "The spring days are long and leisurely. A monk asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "There are three hundred and sixty days in a year.
Ascending the hall, after a long silence, he looked at the assembly and said, "A golden crow runs through the moon;
who says there is nothing at all? On the eastern wall of Zhaozhou hangs a large gourd. Examine this! Ascending the hall, after a long silence, he struck [the meditation seat] once.
Yuanxiang said: "O Great Assembly! Five thousand scrolls cannot fully explain it; the Buddhas of the three periods have not been able to praise it sufficiently.
This makes one recall the oil-seller who, in a flurry of haste, descended from his rope-bed and stood there. [He] entered the hall.

Yet, even as he remained silent with his contrivances forgotten, he was already preempted by the Golden Grain (Kanakamuni). Should he wish to deploy the sharp edge of his rhetoric, he would fall into the trap of Gautama."
Afterwards, having departed from these two paths, what is this single road through which a patch-robed monk attains liberation? After a long silence, he said:
"It is truly laughable where Nanquan brought it up: the sickle for cutting grass is curved and bent. *Chan*.
Chan Master Qingman of Yuanfeng Monastery in Wei Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Tianbo Yuan.

“When one cannot speak, what then? The Master said, “A mute person eating honey. “When one speaks but does not know [the truth], what then?
The Master said, “A parrot calling out to people. The monk bowed. The Master rebuked him, saying, “You mere messenger!
Who is it that you ask who is not swallowed by impermanence? The Master said, “I only fear he has no place to put his beak. [The monk] said, “If that is so, then...”
A single thought penetrates the primordial arrow; the three *śi* demons lose their guile. The Master said, "If you have even one thought, you will surely be swallowed up by them.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when there is not a single thought? The Master said, "I have caught you, *ācārya*. Ascending the hall, he said: An ancient said, "Endure, endure!
From this, the Tathāgatas of the three periods are exhausted. Yield, yield! From this, ten thousand calamities and a thousand misfortunes are extinguished. Be silent."
[The Master] remained silent. "Unsurpassed Bodhi is attained from this. The Master said, "Once you have understood these three kinds of speech, you will see what a truly joyless fellow you are!
This mountain monk simply takes a bull from one person and returns a horse to another; he splashes water and spits upon others, thrusting his beak and cursing them back.
He struck his staff and said, "Even-handed! Even-handed! Ascending the hall, [he asked: "From which mountain does the cloud arise? From where does the wind come?"
Born from a deep ravine—what a fine place to enter! "The official road has few travelers. Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "It is not an objective realm, nor is it the mind.
To call it 'Buddha' is already to sink into the mud. Within this, there is fundamentally no hierarchy; one must strictly avoid seeking within that which is without hierarchy.
If you do not seek at all, the error is even deeper. Only by smashing Yunmen’s rice-bag will you finally know the truth."
The earth is yellow gold. Tuo!
Chan Master Ruigui of Wanshou Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture, a native of the Wei clan of Jian’ning, was asked on the day he ascended the hall:
“What is the environment of Suta? The Master replied: “Mountains rise in the beauty of lions; waters join the clarity of Lake Tai. He said:
"What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "After the imperial attire of the Great Song, before the ritual and music of the Great Zhou.
Whenever the Master saw a monk, he would invariably ask, "How have you been lately? As soon as the monk attempted to respond, the Master would pat him on the back and say, "Inconceivable!"
As he was about to pass away, the assembly gathered. He spoke once more, saying, "Inconceivable," and then, with palms joined, he passed into extinction.
Chan Master Tianyi Ruzhe of Yuezhou’s native village is unknown. After retiring from his monastic seat, he resided at Wanshou Monastery in Pingjiang.
He ate and drank without discrimination, and many people mocked him. Someone asked him about the koan regarding calling out to the "host" at Ruiyan.
The Master answered with a verse: "Ruigan constantly calls out to the 'Lord of the House. He stands out prominently atop the highest peak of Mount Sumeru.
The great earth is overturned, yet there is no place to find him— A single melody of flute and song resounds within the painted pavilion. One day he said, "I am going."
He ordered his bamboo sedan chair to be wiped clean, then wrote a verse to address the assembly, saying: "The Way lies in the place of activity; the Way is used in the place of death.
People of this age merely preoccupy themselves with craving pleasure and refuse to study non-action (*wuwei*).
Having recounted his past inquiries and exhorting the assembly to advance in their cultivation, he suddenly raised his fist and said: 'Everyone, tell me: where does this fall? The assembly—"
[The Master] was without opposition. The Master struck the desk once and said, "All at once, it is entrusted to the autumn wind. He then entered his carriage and passed away while sitting upright.
Zen Master Fachuang of Zhizhe in Wuzhou ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to strike the profound pivot, you must possess integrity and fortitude. To an extreme...
Magnanimous! Only one who can sever the nails and cut through the iron—a man of unyielding resolve—can truly attain this.

As for those who hide behind their blades and dodge arrows, mere mediocre fellows, they may have a share in this upon merely looking. [He strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and descends from the seat.]
Chan Master Zhine Miaokong of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture was the son of the Xia family of Xiuzhou. He first resided at Tianting Monastery in Huai.

At the beginning of the Jianyan era, Empress Cisheng of Lingyin bestowed upon him the title "Buddha-Ocean" (Fohai). Han Shizhong submitted a memorial requesting that Lingyan Monastery be established as a merit cloister and appointed the Master to preside over it.
In total, he occupied the Dharma seat on five occasions. A monk asked: "Before Niu Tou [attained enlightenment]..."
"How was it when you saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Sitting for too long leads to fatigue. [The questioner] asked, "How was it after you saw him?
The Master said, "It does not hinder my walking east or west. In the *dingchou* year of the Shaoxing era during the Song dynasty (1137), the Master arrived at Huating.

A man surnamed Zhu invited the Master to a vegetarian feast. On the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month, he went to Zhu’s residence and sat upon the seat to preach the Dharma to the monastics and laypeople.

When they had all assembled, a monk stepped forward and asked, "What is the root of birth and death? Before the Master had finished responding, he raised his whisk, struck the meditation platform once, and passed away.
He was eighty years old, with sixty-seven years of monastic seniority. He was buried at the Baiyun Hermitage within the monastery.
Chan Master Jue Ran Baoyue of Ba’en Monastery in Changzhou was a successor of Chan Master Jinshan Hui. He was the son of the Zheng family of Yuezhou. One day he ascended the hall and said:
"Students who speak empty words while having no realization must seek wondrous awakening. If one has wondrous awakening yet speaks empty words, it is like chasing after a foul odor. Thus it was said.
"Even so, those who pierce their ears are rarely encountered; those who mark the boat are many.
One day he said to the assembly, "Worldly conditions are easily defiled, but the work of the Way is difficult to accomplish. You all must exert yourselves. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
Chan Master Shaoxian of Zhiye Monastery in Wuzhou was a successor of Chan Master Fayun.
He was a native of Tanzhou. Once, he ascended the hall and said: "The sense organs and their objects share the same source; bondage and liberation are not two.
With every movement, even the slightest, one plays throughout the ten directions. Though the dog of Zihu is fierce, how can it compare to the turtle of the South Mountain?"
Bi then raised his voice and said: "Great assembly, look beneath your feet! He ascended the hall and said: "It cannot be gathered into a ball;
it cannot be dispersed by a brush. Sunlight cannot dry it; water cannot rot it. It hangs casually within the great void, leaving others at liberty to gaze upon it with cold indifference."
Chan Master Zhongyi of Fusheng Monastery on Mount Ma’an in Yizhou ascended the hall and said: “One, two, three, four, five. Ascending the hall, the Dharma drum is struck.
Crowds gather and come forward together; one by one, we face each other. The autumn colors fill the empty courtyard; the autumn wind stirs the universe.
If you ask further about the Zen of the Patriarchs—when Xuefeng arrived at Touzi, he gave a shout: ‘Tut!’”
A monk asked Zen Master Huihai Yueyin of Huilin Temple in Tokyo: "Whose song does the Master sing? To whom does the lineage of the patriarchal style succeed?
The Master said: "A jade pavilion upon a golden ground. The monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said: "In the third month, the people of Luoyang wear flowers. Entering the hall, he said: "Upon the ground of pure gold, those with true eyes are unwilling to settle;
within the thicket of thorns, the one who abides in his own fundamental nature cannot be detained. As for departing from these two paths—"
"What is the place where a patch-robed monk walks? After a long silence, he said: "Lifting one's head amidst the mist and clouds, one sees the home mountain faintly.
He then ascended the hall, looked over the assembly, struck the meditation seat once, and said, "This briefly expresses that it is not empty," and then descended from the seat.
Chan Master Jianlong Yuan of Yangzhou was the son of the Xia family of Gusu. One day, he ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said:
"Buying a hat to fit the head; following a mold to draw a pattern. Let the rustic old man frown as he pleases; Master Zhi did not come here as a mere ordinary monk."
Zhuo struck his staff and descended from the seat.

Chan Master Fojian Weizhong of Jingshan in Zhenjiang was a native of Tingzhou. He traveled to Mount Lu and journeyed through the Huai and Zhejiang regions, visiting and questioning masters of the school at every turn.
Upon reaching Guishan, he studied under Foguo; during one session of entering the inner room for instruction, he heard the master raise the "Pine Tree" koan, and he attained sudden enlightenment.

He attained realization. Later, he went to Huiguo at Cizhou to leave the world. Subsequently, by imperial decree, he resided at Fayun Monastery in Dongjing. The Master served as the head of the First Seat.

In the Gengchen year of the Yuanfu era of the Song dynasty, Emperor Zhezong passed away. On the fifth or seventh day [after his death], the Emperor summoned the Master to enter the palace to preach the Dharma.
The Emperor bestowed upon the Master the Dharma-name Fojian. In the *Xinsi* year of the Jiàzhòng Jìngguó era under Emperor Huizong, he resided as abbot at Mount Jinshan.
The Empress sent an imperial messenger with incense to offer prayers for the longevity of the state. Entering the hall, a monk asked: "Today, the Field for Selecting Buddhas is opened."
The Emperor asked, "With what Dharma will you repay the Imperial Grace? The Master said, "The Ten-Thousand-Year Pine stands atop Mount Zhurong.
The Emperor asked, "But when the Great Inspector presides over the banquet, how can one repay his kindness? The Master said, "Fishermen and woodcutters rejoice in peace from a thousand miles away.

The Emperor said, "The fresh rain and dew have drifted here, washing clean the ancient towers and pavilions. The Master said, "You speak with great reason," and then added, "Yet the Dharma is fundamentally beyond words."

Responding to circumstances according to their capacities, the mind is fundamentally formless; yet it manifests immediately upon encountering conditions. This has been so throughout antiquity and the present; ordinary beings and sages follow the same path.

It is simply that sentient beings, through delusion and ignorance, fail to realize this and thus undergo the cycle of birth and death. Therefore, the Buddha Śākyamuni suddenly forgot all emotional attachments and views, thoroughly comprehending the fundamental source.
He did not seek it from without, nor was it obtained from within. For this reason, Buddha after Buddha handed down the torch, and patriarch after patriarch transmitted the lineage.
Establishing the lineage’s tradition, each spreads their own mat; encompassing the myriad phenomena and embracing the great chiliocosm. In profound stillness, there is no confusion;
amidst the vast expanse of form and sound, how could speech and silence interfere? To hold fast is to sever the ten directions, like a tiger crouching and a dragon coiling;
to let go is for the thousand sages to arise, like wind passing through grass that bends. May you assist the benevolent governance of the Yao-like Emperor and extend his sagely reign.
Extending like a great swan, he subdues the myriad māras and brings universal benefit to all beings. Nevertheless, this still involves traversing a path;
rather, the true command must now be enacted—how can it be discussed through mere theory? He then struck his whisk and said: "The One Breath speaks not, yet it contains all forms;
where could the myriad spirits go to thank its impartiality?"
A monk asked Chan Master Qianming Yong of Baicheng Mountain in Hanzhong: "Changing the Vinaya for Chan is not without its reason.
As a student who has come here, I beg the Master to speak directly. The Master said: "A single phrase, perfectly clear, yet even those who have realized it remain deluded.
The monk said: "The waters of the Han River must surely flow to the sea; the lunar disc ascends straight to the highest peak. The Master said: "That will suffice for now."
**Linghua:** "The World-Honored One appeared in the world and golden lotuses sprang up from the earth. When you, Master, appear in the world, what auspicious signs are there?
**The Master:** "Yesterday it rained; today it is sunny. **Linghua:** "Is there anything further beyond this? **The Master:** "East, west, south, north;
above, below, and the four intermediate directions."
Chan Master Shengyin Chongkai of Huai’an ascended the hall. A monk asked, “When a Bodhisattva perceives their nature, it is like seeing the sun by day;
when a Śrāvaka perceives their nature, it is like seeing the moon at night. I wonder, how does the Master perceive your own nature? The Master said:
He struck it through with a single stroke and asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master replied, "Ten thousand miles of cloudless sky; a thousand peaks standing like walls.

He then said, "The Patriarch’s true command is fully upheld from ancient times to the present. It encompasses heaven and earth, secures the world, and causes the celestial wheel to turn left and the terrestrial axis to spin right.
The night moon flows with light, the morning sun shines with brilliance; the four quarters are radiant and the eight directions are clear."

Gazing out, all is vast and expansive; not even a hair’s breadth is concealed, nor is a speck of dust left behind. The mountains are green and the waters are azure; the cranes are white and the crows are black.
Mist rises over the plains, and dragons roar at the city walls; wind stirs beyond the balustrades, and tigers howl before the pavilions.
The Wooden Boy reveals the hidden pass, and the Stone Woman splits open the golden lock. As for Shigong’s bow and Bimozha’s trident—one must simply let them go; so too with Deshan’s staff.
Linji’s shout leaves no ground for display; why need one beat the drum or carry mud? There is no use for rolling the ball or dragging the stone.

Within this, all principles are exhausted, yet there is not a trace of the "nose-ring" (the essential pivot). Nevertheless, as for that matter which transcends the school and surpasses the standard—how is it so?
After a long silence, he said: "The great earth cannot bear it up; even heaven and earth find it difficult to contain."
Chan Master Dajue Faying of Kaifeng first resided at Puzhao Monastery in Sizhou, later moved to Shaoshi Mountain, and subsequently lived in Dongjing.
While his attendant was reading the *Record of Dongshan*, the Master remarked, "This is a place for the foolish and deluded. The attendant said, "The ancients were truly extraordinary.
The Master replied, "After I pass away, you may call out to them; if they can return, it will be through my spiritual power (*mārgabala*)."
Later, when the time for his final passing arrived, he composed a verse, saying: "On the fifth day of the fifth month of this year, the four elements shall depart from their original master.
My white bones shall fly away with the wind; do not occupy the land of the donor. Thereupon, he completely distributed his clothing and possessions to provide a meal for the monks.
Having heard the sound of the midnight bell, he sat and passed away. His attendant called out to him as they had agreed. The Master responded, "What is it?
The attendant said, "Why have you departed, Master, so naked and barefoot? The Master said, "What did you have when you came? The attendant wished to forcibly dress him, but the Master said, "Stop;
leave this for later generations. The attendant asked, "At such a moment as this, what is it like? The Master said, "It is just like this."
He further wrote another verse, saying: "Seventy-three years have passed like a flash of lightning; as I depart, I shall open a single thread for you.

The iron ox leaps across Silla, shattering the void into seven or eight pieces. He then passed away in solemn stillness on the fifth day of the fifth month in the Guihai year of the Shaoxing era of Emperor Gaozong of the Song dynasty.
Chan Master Wuishang of Guangfu Monastery in Lin’an, a dharma heir of Chan Master Baoning Ying, first visited Jueyin. He asked, "What was the meaning of Nanquan’s act of slaying the cat?
Jueyin replied, "One must be Nanquan to do so. Jueyin then challenged the Master with his previous words. The Master...

Proceed. If this is not yet so, strictly avoid wandering about in confusion. [The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Chan Master Shanyou of Luozhou Luohan Monastery ascended the hall and said: "In a single breath, there is no speaking, yet the myriad flowers compete to bloom.
