A grave. Half of these are people who have come to wail for the past year. Let us set this matter aside for a moment. "What is the Way? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!
[The student] said, "I have come specifically to ask this question. The Master said, "Blowing a flute at the crossroads;
drinking two or three rounds of sour, cold wine in the village. Question: "If there were even a single dharma, Vimalakīrti would fall into the rank of an ordinary person."
"If the myriad dharmas were non-existent, Samantabhadra would lose his realm. Setting aside these two paths, I beg the Master for a definitive resolution.
The Master said, "Turmeric and licorice. [The student] said, "This is still a point of doubt for a student. The Master said, "Let it cool, then look at it. [The student] asked about the path beyond:

"The path beyond, which not a thousand sages have transmitted—how can one know what this path beyond is? The Master said: *Note: The dialogue regarding "turmeric and licorice" (dà huáng gān cǎo) is a classic example of the Master’s pedagogical method of using mundane, medicinal substances to point toward the ineffable, as they are neither "existent" nor "non-existent," yet are necessary for healing.*
"Traveling until the end of the mountain, sitting to watch the clouds arise. He asked, "Why is this not transmitted? The Master said, "Every house has a road leading to Chang'an.
He asked, "As for the gate of the patch-robed monks, what is it ultimately like? The Master said, "I give you thirty blows!
Ascending the hall, he said: "Five times nine is forty-five. The Sage acts and all things behold him. It was so in the time of Qin..."
The carriage wheel crushes the sharp point of the drill. Fan Kuai was enraged before the hall of the Han Founder. I have heard of the Yellow Crane Tower; Cui Hao composed a poem upon its summit:
"The clear river stretches on, with the trees of Hanyang clearly visible; the fragrant grasses grow lushly upon the Yingwu Isle.

One must know the rites. The gentleman applies himself to the root. When the root is established, the Way arises. From the Way arises the One; from the One arise the Two; from the Two arise the Three.
"Three things give birth to the myriad things. [The Master] suddenly grasps his staff, rises, and says, "Venerable assembly, how does Baofeng compare to Confucius?
After a long silence, he says, "When wine meets a kindred spirit, it is drunk; when a poem meets one who understands, it is recited. He strikes the ground with his staff and descends from the seat.

[Ascending the hall: Announcement. It has rained continuously for many days without clearing. It is such that at the summit of the Five Elders Peak, dark clouds gather and swirl, and within Lake Dongting...
White waves surge to the heavens. Great Master Yunmen, unable to restrain his impatience, burns incense within the Buddha Hall and joins his palms at the main gate to offer prayers and vows:
"May the Stone Woman of Huangmei give birth to a son, and may mother and child be reunited;
may the hornless iron ox of Shaoshi always find sweet water and grass. With a shout, he asks: "What connection is there? He looks at the assembly and says: 'No.'"
Because Yang Deyi recommended him, Ma Xiangru vied for an audience with the Emperor. Ascending the hall: before the Primordial Unity had yet divided, the One Qi was profound and still;
there was no hearing of heaven and earth, the primal yellow, the vastness of the universe, the waxing and waning of the sun and moon, or the harvesting in autumn and storing in winter.
At such a time as this, it is indeed a fine occasion. Yet one cannot bear that old fellow Xuefeng, who instead [seeks] within the void...
He drove in stakes and rolled three wooden balls until the person behind could no longer reach them. Then one sees the water-buffalo of Mount Mui, who has always been bold and coarse;
and the tiger of Changsha, who bites the pigs and dogs of every household wherever he goes.
Nevertheless, such rudeness is difficult to tolerate, yet for now I shall let this matter pass. The Preface to the *Xiaojing* says: "I have heard that in ancient times..."
A Brief Note from Fengbo: Yao Min Xie Yuan, Scholar of the First Rank from before the Mountains, sends his greetings. I am pleased to learn that you are in good health and well-being.
*Ascending the Hall:* Today is the tenth day of the twelfth month; last night the heavens sent down snow. From every vantage point, the myriad peaks appear white from top to bottom;
it is difficult to distinguish the green bamboo from the dark pines. Surely next year’s silkworms and wheat will ripen, and both Mr. Zhang and Mr. Li will rejoice. They all rejoice.
Delighted, he beats his belly, singing and laughing without ceasing. Grasping a cloud-flute, he blows it in a wild, disordered manner;
it appears vaguely like a willow staff. Unconsciously, he finds himself dancing with his hands and stamping with his feet, moving left and right.
He shouts: "When Zen travelers meet, they simply snap their fingers; how many can truly know this mind? Ascending the hall, he said: "Under the Gate of the Great Sun..."
Day after day, three autumns pass; before the Hall of the Bright Moon, moment after moment, nine summers elapse. Master Dongshan only knew how to catch the black chicken at midnight;
he did not realize that he startled the neighbors from their sleep. Baofeng, sitting at the same table, beat the rhythm of the game and said to all you Zen adepts:
"It would be well to place a torch in a cold spot. *Pah!* He ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'Do not read the sutras, do not recite mantras...'"
The Buddha said: "What is this that one contemplates while reading the sutras? Since I have recognized the person who turns the sutras, he held up his whisk and said:

'The sages of the Dragon Canon are all swept away by a single stroke of this whisk. With the whisk, he made a sweeping motion and said: 'O virtuous Chan practitioners, at such a time as this, tell me:
where does the local guardian deity of Yunyan establish his dwelling and sustain his life? He then threw down the whisk."
Clenching both hands into fists and knocking his teeth together, he said: "Ten thousand spirits, a thousand sages; a thousand sages, ten thousand spirits. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
"The scriptures state that if there is one person who awakens to the truth and returns to the source, the voids of the ten directions will all vanish away.
I wonder, what is the principle behind this? The Master then opened his palms and pointed his fingers, saying: "Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao; Chen, Si, Wu, Wei."
One is Mars, two is Earth, three is Water, four is Metal, five is the Sun, six is the Moon, and seven is Ketu. Today, the star Ketu enters the house of Cancer.
Baofeng does not beat this drum or blow this flute—[he] then descends from his seat. Entering the hall: The Great Way runs lengthwise and crosswise;
in every encounter, it is fully manifest. The clouds part and the sun rises; the waters are green and the mountains are blue. [He] takes up his staff and strikes once.
The junior monk said, "Master Yunmen has arrived! He says that Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva uses money to buy sesame cakes;
as soon as he lets go of his hand, it turns out to be a steamed bun. "Great assembly, Yunmen saw only the sharpness of the chisel's tip, but did not see the squareness of the chisel's handle.
Baofeng is not like this," [the Master] said, throwing down his staff and adding, "Do not let matters of the Empty King hinder you on the way; spur yourself forward!"
"Zhàng must return to his native village. Yesterday someone came from Huainan;
he had no news from Fujian, but instead said, 'The Great Image of Jiazhou has swallowed the Iron Ox of Shanfu. [Yunju] gave a shout and said, 'What kind of talk is that?
It would make even the local deity of Yunju fall over laughing! He ascended the hall and said: "The pivot of the Patriarchs' gate is hidden in mystery, known by few. It is not..."
Regarding those who have awakened to the mind: how can one present this to them? [The Master] gave a shout and said, "What kind of talk is this?

If things were always like this, the entire school of Bodhidharma would be wiped out like dust. Therefore, when the Great Awakened World-Honored One first realized this matter, he immediately opened the gate of expedient means to reveal the true reality, universally causing it to reach everywhere—north, south, east, west, above, below, and in every direction. [He then called out,] "Guo Da!"
Li Er, Deng Si, and Zhang San all clearly understand this matter. Today, Yunyan cannot help but follow the example of the ancients.
[He strikes the whisk and says: "The gate of skillful means has opened; what, then, is the true mark? After a long silence, he says:
"Eighteen, nineteen—the fool runs off at night. Addressing the assembly, he takes up his staff and says: "For the practitioner-monk, the staff and wooden pole follow as they may."
The body encounters the stage and performs a play; held upside down or grasped crosswise, it possesses its own inherent meaning. Thus, in the past, Yaoshan asked Yunyan:
"I have heard that you understand how to play the lion; is this true? Yunyan replied, "It is. Yaoshan asked, "How many performances have you played?"
Yunyan said, "I can play it six times. Dayuan said, "I, this old monk, also know how to play it. Yunyan asked, "How many times can you play it, Preceptor?
Dayuan said, "I, this old monk, can only play it once. Yunyan said, "One is six; six is one. Dayuan then ceased speaking. "O Great Assembly!
Yaoshan and Yunyan have thoroughly confounded people. These two sons and their father played with a single lion."
He could not bring it forth. If it were Master Zhun, he would have needed only to perform it himself;
having dragged it out, he would have reversed head and tail, rolled his two golden eyes, and extended his iron claws.

With a single roar, he would have caused all fierce beasts within a hundred li to hide their tracks and all birds in the sky to fall in disarray. Yet Master Zhun had not yet performed the lion’s dance.
Please, everyone, look up with clear vision. First, let us establish the scene. Throwing down his staff, he said: "As for this message within, how many people can truly know it?
When the Master returned from Zhejiang to Lestam, he went to visit [Master] Shen. Shen immediately ordered him to share the seat [of teaching].

There was an attendant named Wengu who, upon seeing the remains of the cooking utensils thrown down by the Master, attained realization. He went to the abbot’s quarters to communicate his awakening to Shen. Shen—
He shouted, "Come out! Because he had lost his resolve, [Wu] committed suicide behind the latrine in the Yanshou Hall. He appeared and disappeared without a fixed time, and the assembly feared him.
When the Master heard of this, he went there specifically at midnight. Just as [Wu] was climbing onto the toilet and beginning to undress, Wuzhuo immediately arrived carrying pure water.

The Master said, "Wait for me to finish undressing. After he had finished undressing, Wuzhuo arrived again. Shortly thereafter, Wuzhuo offered him a tally-stick (chouzi). Once the Master had washed himself clean, he summoned him forward to receive him.
As he was taking away the clean bucket, Wuzhuo just happened to meet him. The Master took hold of his hand and asked, "Are you Wuzhuo, the attendant?
Wuzhuo replied, "Yes. The Master said, "Was there a moment of awakening for you back then when you saw the burning matchhead in the guest prefect's quarters?
In Zen practice and the study of the Way, one seeks only to know where one’s own *benming yuanchen* (original source of life) falls. You have gone about it all wrong."
Regarding this coming and going: when you were in the treasury hall, did you not move the head seat’s sandals—was that not something you realized at that time?
Furthermore, when you were in the guest prefect’s quarters, did you not move his pillow—was that not something you realized at that time?
Every night you have been here fetching water and passing out counting sticks—was that not something you realized at that time? For what reason do you not [realize it now]?
Knowing his end was near, he remained right here to disturb the assembly. The Master pushed him violently; he collapsed lifelessly like a stack of bricks.
From that time on, no one saw him again. During the summer of the *wuyi* year of the Zhenghe era of Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty, the Master lay ill.
When those administering medicine were ordered to avoid toxic substances, the Master did not comply. When asked the reason for this, the Master said: "Does illness have an inherent nature?
They replied, "Illness has no inherent nature. The Master said: "Since it has no inherent nature, how could toxic substances possibly possess a mind?
To receive emptiness with emptiness—this I have never done in a perverted way. How is it that you all are so utterly deluded? On the twentieth day of the tenth month, he further...
He preached verses while wearing his robes to convert others. After his cremation, śarīra were obtained, crystalline, perfectly round, and lustrous; his eyes, teeth, and rosary remained unharmed.
He was enshrined in a stupa on the southern slope of the South Mountain. His age at death was fifty-five, and his years of ordination were thirty-five.
Jing-shan Gaofeng invited Chancellor Zhang Shangying to compose an inscription for his stele of religious practice.
On the day Chan Master Huiji Wenya of Mount Lu was invited [to take up residence], a monk asked, "I beg the Master not to be parsimonious regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school.

The Master said, "The staff is now officially opening its seal. The monk said, "A small emergence meets with a great encounter. The Master said, "If I let this pass, it will not do," and he struck him.
Chan Master Fanyan of Dongshan in Ruizhou was a native of Taiping Prefecture. He ascended the hall. Two monks came forth together;

one monk prostrated, while the other asked, "When you employ what is appropriate for the occasion, how is it? The Master said, "The *ilan* tree becomes a sandalwood tree. [The monk] said, "When there is spirit, add to that spirit;

where there is no elegance, there too lies elegance. The Master said: *Note: The term "伊蘭" (Yīlán) refers to the *ilāñjana* tree, a fragrant plant often used in Buddhist metaphors to represent the transformation of the base into the sublime.*
Amrita is but a garden of thorns. Entering the hall: "My mind is like the autumn moon; it is as clear and bright as a deep pool.
There is nothing that can be compared to it—how am I to describe it? Han Shan Zi has labored in vain. Furthermore, Shi De says:
"If you do not recognize this meaning, your practice will be in vain, though bitter and arduous. To speak in such a manner is to fail to save even oneself.
Understood. Ordinarily, picking up a dung basket or grasping a broom, acting like a madman—this is still somewhat better.
Even if Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra were to appear once more, upon reaching the gate of Dongshan, they would all be assigned to the steward:

those who tend the fire shall tend the fire, and those who sweep the floor shall sweep the floor. Whether in the front corridor or the back eaves, one must strictly avoid interfering with the spoons or the chopsticks. Abundant!
I shall say no more to this old man. After the formal session, tea was served; then he ascended the hall for the discourse: "One gives birth to two; two give birth to three.
Unable to be suppressed, it pervades the entire dharma-realm. De-yun ascends directly to the Wondrous Peak, while Shancai enters the pavilion."

"The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. The mountains are green and the waters are blue; the peach blossoms are red and the plum blossoms are white. In every speck of dust is a Buddha-land;
in every leaf is a Śākyamuni. Then, with palms joined, he said: "I trust that all you sons of the Buddha are well this morning?"
The late spring is extremely warm. I hope you are light and well in your daily activities and that you are living in peace and happiness.

I shall come specifically to pay my respects shortly. Please do not trouble yourself by standing for long. Ascending the Dharma Hall: On the twentieth day of the twelfth month, as the year draws to a close, there are those who have not yet returned from ten thousand miles.
The entire assembly here are guests from foreign lands; is there anyone among you who has returned to the source and restored the origin? (He strikes the whisk.)
The Master said: "The remaining snow before the gate is melted by the sun; who shall sweep away the red dust within the room?
Chan Master Wenshu Xuan from De’an Prefecture was asked by a monk, "What is the Lamp of the Patriarchs?
The Master replied, "It illuminates all four modes of birth; let you behold this single point. Ascending the hall, he said: "Shigong’s arrow, Bimao’s staff—directly beneath!"
To realize that the flowers in one's eye are empty is something both pitiable and laughable for the guests of Shaolin, who secretly carried a single sandal across the desert sands.
Chan Master Shanzu of Shouning in Guizhou ascended the hall and said: "If we discuss this matter, it is like a crow pecking at an iron ox;
there is no place to drop the beak, no place to apply the mind. If you further seek it within words or contemplate it beneath phrases, even if you were to divine..."

To attempt to deliver others is merely to engage in the peripheral matters of frivolous proliferation (*prapañca*). One simply fails to realize that from the very beginning all is fully complete and directly manifest.
Neither Buddha nor sentient beings can be established in the slightest degree. I constantly tell people: ordinary beings are fully endowed with the state of the sages.

The Dharma is such that ordinary beings do not know it, yet the sages fully possess the dharmas of ordinary beings; the sages do not "realize" them, for if the sages were to realize them, they would be identical to ordinary beings.
If ordinary beings were to know them, they would be sages. Thus, ordinary beings and sages are one and the same in name and designation.

They speak to one another, yet they do not recognize the original source and remain deluded regarding true awakening. Consequently, they chase after objects to give rise to thoughts and follow their emotions while clinging to things.

If you can, for even a single thought-moment, forget these emotions, the true and eternal essence will naturally be revealed. After a long silence, he said: "I invite you all to realize this immediately.
While monasteries everywhere hold formal audiences once every five days, Shouning ascends the seat every day. Do not take offense at my repeating these verses.
The fault lies with Bodhidharma from the West. Those of superior capacity encounter him everywhere; those who have recently begun their studies miss him at every turn.
But tell me, where does this one missed step fall? Raising his whisk, he said: "A single moon rises over the sea;
how many families ascend the tower?"
Chan Master Huihe of Shangfeng on Mount Zhurong at Nanyue in Hengzhou ascended the hall.

Before he had even mounted this seat, all the people throughout the great earth had already completed their attainment of Buddhahood; what further Dharma could there be to preach? What further beings could there be to benefit?
How much more so regarding enlightenment and afflictions, which are fundamentally quiescent from the start; birth-and-death and nirvana are like a dream from yesterday.

The arrangements of the gate and courtyard are but deceptions to lure children; when the gates of expedient means are opened, they form intricate patterns and knots that become mere illusions before the eyes of a monk.
Tell me, what excellence does a monk possess? Raising his staff, he said: "The solitary root has its own [strength]."
A posture that supports the heavens; it is not like an ordinary curved branch. He planted his staff upright and descended from the seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Jingjue Ben of Wufeng in Ruizhou, "When voices respond to one another, what then? The Master said:
A pigeon cries upon a tree. [A monk] asks: "When it is said that 'like-kind seeks like-kind,' what is the meaning? The Master says: "A fierce tiger roars before the cliff. [The monk] asks:
"When it is said 'one advances and one retreats,' what is the meaning? The Master says: "Your feet are beneath your belly. [The monk] asks: "What is the Venerable One of Immovability?
The Master says: "Walking, standing, sitting, and lying down. [The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks: "Since you have ascended the precious throne, we wish to hear your teaching."
[The Master] sang: "The plum blossoms bloom amidst the snow; the fire blooms within the flames. [A monk] asked, "Is this not the very point of benefiting others?
The Master said, "Red dust has already risen to fill the sky at the bottom of the well. He then said, "It cannot be thus, nor can it be otherwise.
It cannot be both thus and otherwise, nor can it be neither. How do you all understand this? If you can understand it directly, then..."

Do not obstruct the extraordinary. Furthermore, whether using needles or awls—whether in the Western Heavens or this land—when ascending the hall, the house style of Wufeng is to go north, south, east, or west;
when needed, it is used immediately. To drive a wedge into space! *Du!* (A shout).
Chan Master Taiping of Yongzhou ascended the hall and said: "Whether there is profit or no profit, do not leave the marketplace. Radishes in Zhenzhou are extremely expensive;
rice prices in Luling are very cheap. How can these compare to Taiping? Here, the times are prosperous and the Way is peaceful; merchants and traders throng together.
White rice sells for four cash per sheng, and radishes cost one cash per bundle. There is no need to buy from the north."
"Inexpensive at the western end, yet sold at a high price. Natural objects and the four modes of birth naturally provide the resources for the king’s transformation of the world.
Furthermore, how can one speak of the principles of the Buddha-dharma? After a long silence, he said: "I urge you not to carve upon a stubborn stone;
on the road, the traveler's mouth is like a monument."
Chan Master Baoji Jin Ying of Tanzhou was the son of the Luo family of Taihe in Jizhou.

He received the full precepts at the age of eighteen and, after completing the mourning period for his mother, went to see Yun’an. Yun’an had been received by Huangbo as Linji’s successor and had been received by Yunmen;

it was through these karmic conditions that the master’s potential was awakened. Upon this, the master attained a sudden and great enlightenment. He once served as the attendant to Foyin, who called him "Iron Beak. Initially, he began his teaching career at Baoji.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "I do not ask about having traveled the long road; as for the single phrase of arriving home, how is it?
The Master said: "Snow fills the vast sky. The monk said: "This is still something known by people of the present age. What about the other path for turning the body?"
The Master gave a shout and said, "Baoci has a public case that has never been settled by any quarters.
Fortunately, meeting this new day, I bring it forth. Each of you, please look with eyes wide open. He then kicked down a shoe and said, "Do you know this news or not?
When Bodhidharma returned to the West, he carried it by his side. [He] ascended the hall and spoke thus.
"Come! A fierce tiger emerges from the forest. As he went down like this, "a startled snake enters the grass. Neither up nor down, "the sun’s orb shines brightly. He let out a shout and said:
"The waters of the Xiao and Xiang rivers are clear and deep; once you step out the door, you are on the road to Chang'an.
He then threw down his staff, called to the assembly, and said: "The staff has swallowed the Patriarchs! He then gave the instruction: [To teach...]
"Who speaks of Chan? Is there anyone who can save themselves? He let out a shout. Entering the hall, he suddenly took up his staff and said:
"All Buddhas of the three periods of time have entered this same pitfall. Monks call it a 'hawk soaring in the heavens.'"

Zhuo struck his staff once. Later, he traveled to Tainan, where he returned to establish a hermitage at Liangshan. During the Jiawu year of the Zhenghe era of Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty, he resided at Tianning Temple in Huayao.
In the winter of the Xinchou year of the Xuande era, he returned to his hermitage at Liangshan.
The following year, in the twelfth lunar month, he passed away.
Chan Master Zhigan of Dongshan in Ruizhou ascended the hall. "Dongshan does not know how to talk about Chan; he does not know how to speak of the Way.
He simply eats when hungry and sleeps when tired. You all surely must have some other special skill;
try coming forward and uttering a single phrase with all your might. Is there one? Is there one? After a long silence, he said, "Muzhou’s bottom line."
Chan Master Fohui Pujian of Baohua Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture was the son of the Zhou family of that same region. From his youth, he abstained from meat and pungent roots.

He received the tonsure under Qingzhi of Jingde Monastery. At the age of seventeen, he began his travels to seek teachers. Initially, he visited Jueyin Ying, but there was no accord; he then went to call upon Zhenjing.
One day, Zhenjing raised the story of Shishuang Qian’s attendant to question him, and [Pujian] attained a clear and complete realization.
Wu composed a verse, saying: "Blighted trees bear no flowers through many autumns; Severed clouds still hang from the treetops.
Since I broke the horns of the clay ox, To this very day, the waters flow backward. Jingken approved of this and appointed him to attend his robes and bowl.

Later, following the wishes of the assembly, he opened the Dharma-treasury at Fahua. Subsequently, he moved to Gaofeng and ascended the hall, saying: "In the study of Chan, there is nothing particularly marvelous; it is simply..."
One must indeed sever the life-root of human existence and shed all doubt; then the thousand eyes will open instantaneously.

It is like a wheel rolling across the bottom of the great ocean, or the brilliant sun ascending through the heavenly gate, illuminating everything beneath the four heavens. All myriad distinctions and a thousand variations will be clearly understood at once.
Thus, one can grasp the precious sword of the Vajra King, leaping freely in every direction with sovereign mastery. Is this not joyful?

Alas! Should one’s vision of the Truth be insincere, with images appearing only as faint reflections, merely following words and chasing phrases while being led by others—how could one ever attain liberation, even in a donkey’s lifetime?
It would be better to cast away all worldly attachments, straighten the backbone, and summon a bit of true spirit.

Having thoroughly investigated the teachings until they were penetrated from every angle and mastered with complete certainty, you may dwell by the waterside or beneath the forest trees to nurture the holy embryo;
thus, you will not have received the offerings of devas and humans in vain. Nevertheless, beneath the Gate of Sleeping Amidst the Clouds, there is an iron threshold.
"You must exert even greater vigor; only by leaping over can you succeed. In the mere interval of hesitation, one falls into a pit or a ditch.

[The Master] struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "O Full Moon, I respectfully wish that the Buddhas of the three periods, the house cats, and the white oxen—each and every one—enjoy ten thousand blessings in their daily activities.
At this time, our provisions are meager and there is nothing to offer as hospitality; I earnestly hope you will be patient and compassionate toward this old man."

The water buffalo has recently fallen ill and been plagued by many troubles. Finding no pleasure in water or grass, as soon as it encounters a warm day and a gentle breeze, it immediately collapses with its whole body.
When one tries to make it pull the plow or drag the harrow, it simply shakes its head and tosses its brain. Alas!
Ten thousand acres of fertile fields have all at once turned into overgrown weeds.
When Chan Master Xiu Guang of Jiufeng in Ruizhou was traveling to seek instruction, he visited Yungai Zhi. He asked, "What was the meaning behind Xinghua beating Kebin?
Zhi descended from his meditation seat, extended both hands, and stuck out his tongue to show him. The Master struck a single blow with his sitting mat.
Zhi said, "This is merely turned by the force of the wind. He then questioned Shishuang Lin, who said, "What do you think?"
"How is it? The Master also struck his meditation mat once. Lin said, "A fine meditation mat, but one does not know where its fall lies.
He then asked Zhenjing. Zhenjing said, "What is your intention? The Master again struck his meditation mat once. Zhenjing said, "He strikes, and you strike too.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Zhenjing subsequently had a verse which said: "A man of spirit should cut off..."
He cut himself short. Xinghua was a man who had reached the ultimate; hereafter, let his eyes open through the teaching. [Xinghua] was caned, fined, and expelled from the monastery.

Later, he resided at Jiufeng, where the assembly of monks looked up to him with reverence. Once, King Jieyao invited him to ascend the hall. Jie stepped forward and asked, "What is the realm of Jiufeng?
The Master said, "The waters of the two gullies flow on and on; the nine layers of mountains stand tall and vast."
[The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within the environment? The Master said, "The tall are simply tall; the short are simply short.

[The monk] asked, "I have already received your instruction regarding persons and environments; as for the ultimate vehicle of the patriarchal lineage, what of it? The Master said, "Have you even finished eating the staff-blows? [The monk] withdrew in shame.
The Master turned to his attendant and asked, "What was the occasion for ascending the seat just now? The attendant replied, "Jie Yaowang (Medicine King Jie) made the request.
The Master said, "A golden-maned lion cub roars as soon as it leaves its den. But tell me, who is this golden-maned lion cub?
After a long silence, he said, "It is none other than Jie Yaowang this very morning," and then descended from the seat. That evening, the Master again [spoke] with Zuo Tong.

Master Menfu’s virtue was deeper than that of Letan. One snowy night, he and Fu were sitting around a brazier; after they had conversed for a long time, Fu secretly sent someone to remove the Master’s bedding.
When it was time for bed, the Master went to sleep without questioning him. In a short while, he fell into a deep sleep, his snoring like thunder.
Such was his state of forgetting both things and self.
Chan Master Daoquan of Huangbo in Ruizhou was a native of the Wang family of Luoyang. Initially, he pursued the study of the commentaries on the sutras.
Encouraged by Lord Dong, he abandoned that path to follow at Ganlu; subsequently, he followed Xiu of Qixian for seven years. Later, he served Zhenjing for five years.
One day, he informed Zhenjing of his realization, saying: "With a single blow of the mallet, I have penetrated through the inexhaustible treasury; all precious treasures are now mine."
There was one named Jingke. He went out to reside on the Stone Platform in Qingliang, and subsequently moved to Huangbo.
Entering the hall, he struck the meditation seat with his whisk and said: "With a single blow, one pierces through the inexhaustible treasury; all manner of precious treasures I possess.
Taking them up, I universally relieve the poor and destitute, so as to spare them from wandering the roads of Pāṭaliputra. He then shouted: "Who is the poor and destitute one?"

On the day of Yichou in the twelfth month of the Jiazi year of the Yuanfeng era of Emperor Shenzong of the Song dynasty, he took his leave of the assembly and passed away while seated. His body was fragrant and supple.
Upon cremation, countless śarīras were produced. He was interred in a stupa at Duanji. To the right of the stupa, Su Che inscribed a memorial.
He was forty-nine years of age and thirty years since his ordination.
Chan Master Juefan Huihong of Qingliang in Ruizhou was the son of the Peng family of that prefecture.
At the age of fourteen, both his parents passed away; he then became a novice under Sanfeng Qingsheng, memorizing several thousand words daily and reading nearly the entirety of the various classics.
He refined his vessels [of character]. At nineteen, he underwent the *jìng* examination at Tiantáng Monastery in the Eastern Capital and received full ordination.

He followed Xuānmì to lecture on the *Satyasiddhi-śāstra* and the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra* for over four years. Later, he left them to visit Zhēnjìng at Guīzōng. When Zhēnjìng moved to Shímén, the Master followed him there.

Zhēnjìng was concerned that his profound learning had led to a decline in his practice; thus, he frequently cited the words of Xuánshā regarding "not yet having reached the ultimate" to provoke his doubts. In all matters...
When there was someone responding [to his questions], Jing said, "Are you again expounding upon principles? One day, he suddenly cast off all his doubts and composed a verse, saying:

"Once Lingyun saw it, he did not see it again; On every branch, red and white, no flowers cling. I cannot bear this guest on the fishing boat, Who comes back to the level ground to scoop up fish and shrimp.
Upon seeing this, Jing expressed his joy for him and appointed him as the Record Keeper (*jishi*). Not long after, he departed to pay his respects to [Master] Yuanwu.

All the elders were honored by his enlightened discourse; thus, his reputation resounded throughout the monastic community. Master Zhu Yanxian, whose courtesy name was Xianmu, invited him to open a Dharma seat at Jingde Temple in northern Fuzhou.
Later, he resided at Qingliang Temple. Addressing the assembly, he cited the *Śūraṃgama Sūtra*, where the Tathāgata said to Ānanda:
"You should smell this sandalwood in the incense burner. Suppose this fragrance were instead burned in a single *śroṇa* chamber..."
Within a distance of forty li from the city of Raṭṭhapura, the scent was perceived simultaneously. What do you think?

Does this fragrance arise from the sandalwood tree, or does it arise from your nose, or does it arise from space? Ānanda, if this fragrance were to arise from your nose, [how could it reach those who are forty li away?]
If it is said that [the fragrance] is produced by the nose, it should emerge from the nose; yet the nose is not sandalwood—how then could there be the scent of sandalwood within the nose?

To say that you "smell the fragrance" implies it enters through the nose and the fragrance emerges from within the nose; thus, to speak of "smelling" is illogical. If [the fragrance] were produced in empty space, [it would have no relation to the nose].
If emptiness were eternal, then fragrance should also be eternally present. Why then rely upon burning this withered wood in an incense burner?

If the fragrance were produced from the wood, then as the substance of the wood is burned to become smoke, the nose that perceives it ought to be affected by the scent of that smoke. As the smoke rises into the air, [the fragrance would vanish].

It has not yet reached a great distance; within forty *li*, how can it already be smelled? Therefore, one should know that the nose and the smelling, as well as the fragrance and the act of smelling, are both devoid of a fixed location.
Both are fundamentally illusory; they are neither produced by causes and conditions nor do they possess an inherent nature.

The Master said: "Entering this practice of nose-observation (*niguan*), one personally realizes the unarisen (*anutpāda*). Furthermore, the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* asks: "How does the hearer hear?
Is it heard by the ear-faculty (*śrotra-indriya*)? Or is it heard by the ear-consciousness (*śrotra-vijñāna*)? Or is it heard by the mental consciousness (*mano-vijñāna*)?

If it were heard by the ear-faculty, the ear-faculty lacks sentience or cognition, and therefore cannot hear. If it were heard by the ear-consciousness, the ear-consciousness lasts for only a single moment."
It cannot discern. It should not hear. If it were the mental consciousness (*manovijñāna*) to hear, the mental consciousness likewise could not hear. Why?
Because first the five consciousnesses cognize the five objects, and only thereafter does the mental consciousness cognize; the mental consciousness cannot cognize the five present objects.

If, according to the doctrine of Consciousness-Only, the mental consciousness (*manovijñāna*) can cognize the five sense objects of the present, then blind and deaf people should also be able to cognize sounds. Why?
Because the mental consciousness is not impaired. The Master said: "Examine this object of hearing."

Thus, one accords with the original wondrousness. Having realized non-arising, one again accords with the original wondrousness. After a long silence, he asked: "What kind of realm is this ultimately? After a long while, he said:

"The white monkey has already called out as the evening falls over a thousand crags; the first blue threads are laid across the ten-thousand-character incense burner. This was during his residence at Jingde Temple.
A monk asked, "In the south there is Jingde; in the north there is Jingde. I do not ask about 'De' (Virtue); what is 'Jing' (Splendor)?
The Master said, "On the left side of the neck. During the *kaiming* year of Kaiming (1083) of Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty, at Shanxi in Xia, he met Zhang Wujin.
Zhang had once claimed that he had attained the "final phrase" of Yuanzhao of Longan; the monastic community feared to speak with him. Consequently, they conversed during the night.
He reached him and said, "It is a pity that Yun’an did not know this matter. The Master asked, "Why?

Zhang replied, "Shangying recently moved from the post of wine official in Jinling to serve as Prefect of Yuzhang. On my way there, I visited Guizong and saw him, wishing to provide him with a breakthrough.
Just as I was beginning to explain the final phrase, the old man became furious and cursed me, saying: 'This spittle-spitting shaveling! You are a liar and a deceiver!'"
He could not believe what he had heard. Having seen his intense anger, [the Master] did not wish to explain it further.
The Master smiled and said, "Your Excellency knows only the final phrase transmitted orally by Longan, yet you cannot discern the true medicine when it appears before you.
Zhang was greatly startled, rose, and took the Master’s hand, saying, "Does the Master truly have this intention? [The Master] replied, "If you doubt, seek elsewhere; then take it from home."

He prostrated himself before the portrait of Changyun An and composed a eulogy, which he inscribed and presented to the Master. The words said: "The fundamental principle of Yun'an is capable of both function and illumination;
like the rare sound of a celestial drum, it does not fall into the ordinary mode. With a cold countenance and stern eyes, his divine radiance shines alone."
Who could transmit his true essence? To behold him face-to-face was to see his likeness. Before there was Yue, and after Hong; like Daorong and Daoshao, he stood among the great sages.

During the day when Dahui dwelt among the assembly, he once personally relied upon him and constantly marveled at his wondrous realization and eloquent wisdom. In the fifth month of the Wushen year of the Jianyan era of Emperor Gaozong—
He entered parinirvāṇa at Tong’an. The Grand Marshal, Duke Guo Tianmin, submitted a memorial requesting the bestowal of the title Baojue Yuanming (Treasure-Awakening Perfectly Enlightened).

The Master authored the *Línjiàn lù* (Forest Records), the *Sēngbǎo zhuàn* (Biographies of the Jewel of Monks), the *Gāosēng zhuàn* (Biographies of Eminent Monks), the *Zhìzhèng zhuàn* (Biographies of Realized Wisdom), the *Zhìlín* (Forest of Will), and the *Lěngzāi yèhuà* (Night Talks from the Cold Studio).
The *Tianchu Jinluan* (Forbidden Selections from the Celestial Kitchen) and the *Shimen Wenzici* (Stone Gate Zen of Words and Letters) both circulate in the world.

When Chan Master Chao-hua Jing of Quzhou ascended the hall, he said: "To recognize it before the sound already involves entanglement; to take it up after the phrase still makes one a dull-witted fellow.
Even lightning striking a stone or a spark from flint remains within the realm of hesitation. If you do not respond when the point is struck, you will lie dead across ten thousand [miles]."
After a long silence, he said, "What use is there? He gave a shout.
Nanyue Shitou Huairang, the Hermit of Mount Shitou, was the son of the Wu family of Wuzhou. At the age of fourteen, he relied upon Master Zhizhe Cheng.
Twenty-second: He underwent the tonsure examination for his studies. For twelve years he lectured extensively; senior scholars revered and admired him.
He once intended to synthesize the various schools and rectify the temporal teachings of a single era. A Chan practitioner asked: "Du Shun was the patriarch of the Xianshou school.
When discussing the *dharmakāya*, he said: 'The ox in Huai Prefecture eats the grain; the horse in Yizhou has a bloated belly. Does this verse accord [with the truth]?"
"What is the meaning of returning to Tiantai? The Master had no reply and immediately departed to travel abroad. Later, he arrived at Dongshan and paid his respects to Zhenjing.
He asked, "Regarding the ancient's single shout, which does not function as a single shout—what is its intent? Zhenjing rebuked him. The Master hurried out.

Jingxiao called out to him, saying, "Young man from Zhejiang, it would be well for you to go sightseeing after your midday meal. At these words, the Master suddenly attained enlightenment. After some time, he took his leave.

Jingxiao said, "Although your realization is of an extraordinary caliber, I regret that your karmic conditions are not yet sufficient. He thus understood the Master's intent. Thereafter, various quarters exerted great effort to urge him to appear in the world, but the Master declined them.
He lived in seclusion in a hermitage for twenty years, never interacting with the world, even when literati and officials came knocking at his door.

He ignored it briefly. There is a verse that says: All myriad affairs brought to rest, entrusted to the simple and the foolish; My traces allow wild deer to occasionally join me. Without shedding my hempen robe, I make my fist a pillow;
For many lifetimes, my dreams have remained in the Ivy-covered Hermitage. Someone asked, "Having lived on the mountain for many years, what is the purpose of this?
The Master said, "I dwell in the mountains; with the wooden gate closed alone, there is no other pursuit. Three pieces of firewood...

The "Tou-pinzi" Incense Burner. Without needing to wield the brush, its literary brilliance is revealed. In the winter of the first year of the Chongning era (Renzi), the first year of the Northern Song dynasty, I took up my staff and went to Long’an;
no one could detain me. On the final day of the sixth month of the following year, I asked an attendant monk:
At dawn and dusk, [the Master] would say, "It is already evening. He then would smile and say, "We have met within a dream; I have already awakened from my sleep.
You need only not fail the monastic community, and that is how you repay the Buddha's kindness. Having spoken thus, he entered nirvana at the Zui-le Hall.
His remains were collected through cremation and enshrined in a stupa beneath Ru Peak.
The Head Seat Yin of Shuangxi in Wuzhou had personally seen Zhenjing and thoroughly realized the principles of the school.
He retired to Shuangxi, where one day he happened to write: "The broken-legged cauldron smolders in vain; After meals, I am always sitting there in a heap.
Since my livelihood has grown clumsy these days, The hundred birds have carried off the flowers and do not return. Because his robe was worn through and tattered, he composed this verse:
It is said: "Only when not a single thread hangs upon you is one truly free from cold; why needlessly dangle a long fishing pole?
Now, as things fall away one by one, where can the names of the Seven Buddhas be placed?"
Chan Master Huian Huiyuan of Fengxin in Longxing was a man from the north. He was solitary and firm in his self-reliance. Having studied under Huitang for a long time, he attained realization;
subsequently, he studied under Zhenjing, where he remained submerged among the multitude, unknown to anyone. The Huian Monastery stood by the side of the road;
among the monks traveling between Letan, Huanglong, Dongshan, and Huangbo, there were none who did not pass through it. One day, by chance—
The Dharma seat was vacant. At that time, Zhenjing was at Baofeng; the Prefect sent a letter ordering him to select a person to occupy it.
The assembly all feared the journey, but the Master said to Zhenjing, "Huiyuan, would you be able to go? Zhenjing said joyfully, "You may go."
Thereupon, he again wrote a letter recommending the Master. The Head Seat, Tanzang, asked the Master, "How will you manage as abbot when you go? The Master replied, "Huiyuan has no merit;
I shall simply create karmic connections for all people by carrying a wicker basket on my shoulder to beg through the streets for the sake of the assembly."
Zantang said, "It must be you, my elder brother, who can do this. He then composed a verse to see him off. When the Master arrived, he went out every day to solicit alms.
Whenever anyone arrived for a short visit, Zantang would invite them back to stay overnight at the monastery, saying, "Please allow me to return and prepare offerings.
In this manner, for thirty-five years, he never faltered despite wind and rain; the monastic buildings were completely renovated, and everything necessary for a forest monastery was provided.
As for those who possess [such qualities], they are all fully present here. When Sīxīn first stayed at Huánglóng, he went to visit him.
The Master said, "New Elder, you have always loved to use a single 'point' of hidden intelligence to brush people aside.
For tonight, stay here and let us discuss some subtle and great Dharma gates. Sīxīn was intimidated by this and said to his attendant, "This fellow truly understands the principle..."
As for those who understand the essence [of the Dharma], they cannot compete with him in piercing teeth and splitting jaws;

it is better to leave and rest. Without staying overnight, he departed. Later, the Master passed away at Huian. During his cremation, three of his six sense organs remained unimpaired, and countless śarīra relics were obtained.

A wondrous fragrance filled the chamber, continuing without ceasing for many months. After the establishment of the new capital, the area suffered from military fires; everything was destroyed and nothing remained, except for Huian.
The various halls stand majestic and alone; this is surely due to the fulfillment of vows and the protection of divine beings.
(From *Wudeng Quanshu*, Volume 38 and Volume 39)
Compiled by the Abbot (Your Servant) Monk Chao Yong of Shenggan Chan Temple, Kyoto;
reviewed by the Abbot (Your Servant) Monk Chao Kui of Gu Huayan Temple, Kyoto; presented for imperial inspection.
Dharma heir of Chan Master Yunju You of the Thirteenth Generation under Nanyue in the Linji School.

Luo Han Yuan of Mount Lu was Chan Master Nan, whose secular surname was Zhang and who hailed from Tingzhou. Initially, he studied under Master Daoyou at Daolin Monastery and received his formal certification (*jibie*).

He subsequently moved to Luo Han Monastery, where he served as the Hall Director (*zhangtangsi*) and was immediately assigned a seat to receive monastics. Later, when Daoyou relocated to Yunju, [Nan followed him].
Succeeding to his master’s seat, he drew scholars to him. According to the family lineage, Huanglong was his great-grandfather;
as their names were identical and his reputation for the Way rivaled that of his ancestor, people called him "Little Nanyuan. He ascended the hall and said: "Zen is not Zen; the Way is not the Way.
This three-inch tongue sweeps through chaos. Last night, the sun's orb shed its cassia blossoms; this morning, in the moon's cave, magical fungi have sprouted."
A-ha-ha! Ten thousand taels of gold cannot be found anywhere; from the very beginning, there has been no conceptualization. All phenomena do not distinguish one another.

When the Master was about to pass into nirvana, he ascended the seat and addressed the assembly, saying: "Today the Arhat rides an iron horse backward, ascending Mount Sumeru and trampling through space, leaving behind not even a trace.
He then returned to his quarters and passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. He had remained in the world for... [years].
Forty-five.
Zen Master Yanlong of Ciyun in Tanzhou ascended the hall and said, citing Xuansha’s instruction to the assembly:
"The entire great earth is, after all, but a single bright pearl. At that time, a monk asked: "Since it is but a single bright pearl, why is it that practitioners..."
“I do not know. The Sandalwood Monk said, “The whole body is the pearl; who else could you ask to recognize it?
He replied, “Even though the whole body is the pearl, what can be done about the fact that the student does not recognize it? The Sandalwood Monk said, “Ask your own eyes.

The Master said, “All you Zen practitioners, this koan is called ‘feeding a child with chewed rice’—reaching out one’s hand and then giving them a staff. Do you understand? If you have not yet understood, you must go and knock [on the door].”
Furthermore, one must seek the direct and the true; one must not speak recklessly or pursue the empty, for that would merely result in a life spent in vain and a death lived in delusion.
A monk asked Chan Master Ziyu of Mount Ziling in Yingzhou, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas?
The Master said, "Barefoot, treading through mud, cold as ice. The monk asked, "I do not understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "Do not bother to drag along the mud and water."
Shui asked, “For what reason did the Great Sage of Sizhou appear in Yangzhou? The Master said, “Karma lies within it. Shui asked, “What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, “The honorable descends to accord with the lowly. Shui said, “Thank you, Preceptor, for your answer.
The Master said, “The thief is a petty person, yet his cunning surpasses that of a gentleman.”
Chan Master Jingfu Shengyue of Dongshan in Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Throughout the twelve hours of the day, limping and dragging along, we simply pass the time like this.
Great assembly, where does the point of profit or loss lie? After a long silence, he said, "Listen and let the various quarters pass judgment.
He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.
Chan Master Baizao Qingyan of Bozhou was a native of Xinzhou. A monk asked, “Yang Guang lost his camel; nowhere was anyone able to see it.
I wonder what kind of person could have seen it? The Master beckoned with his whisk and said, “Step back, step back!
Do not obstruct others from asking. The monk asked, “Ultimately, where does it fall? The Master said, “It is utterly [unfathomable].”
Recognizing his fondness for [the scripture], he struck him.
Zen Master Yuan of Baoxiang in Taizhou was asked by a monk:
"It is said that all Buddhas and the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* of all Buddhas emerge from this sutra. What is this sutra? The Master replied: "Recite it constantly."

It does not cease; it is neither meaning nor sound. [The student] asked, "How then should one receive and uphold it? The Master said, "If you wish to receive and uphold it, you must listen with your eyes."
The abbot of Eiju-an in Yongfeng, Xinzhou, was the son of the Qiu family of that same prefecture. He entered the monastic life at the age of seven and received full ordination at Mingxin Temple.

Having attained spiritual resonance with Yunju, he traveled extensively through the regions of Xiang and Han. Upon returning to his native village, he resided sometimes in mountain valleys and sometimes in market towns.
He led the local people to address him as "Master Uncle Qiu. Whenever anyone questioned him, he would answer with the words, "I do not know."
Suddenly he said to the people of the village, "I shall depart on foot tomorrow; you may come to see me off.
Thereupon, those who wished to provide him with travel provisions gathered in full. The Master laughed incessantly. When the crowd asked for the reason, he immediately wrote this verse:
"Master Qiu does not understand: Silent and still, bright and clear. At midday, the third watch is struck; Who can strike it through? Having set down his brush, he passed away.
Master Yongcheng of Nanfeng in Quanzhou addressed the assembly: "From Jifeng, the flame was continued; from Shaoshi, the fragrance flowed.
The clouds of compassion were widely spread, and the sun of wisdom was grandly opened. The teachings were divided into the Three Pitakas, yet they directly point to the One Mind.

Sometimes the staff and the shout are applied together in their full presentation; sometimes taking and giving are employed as guest and host alternate. Sometimes the Vajra presses its sword; sometimes the Lion..."

A turnabout! Whether it be like a clap of thunder in its application or a flash of lightning in its sharpness, it is nothing other than the excision of deviant delusions and the opening up of the primordial subtlety.
Directly clarifying the fundamental source and reaching the ground of reality—O virtuous ones, only upon reaching this point may you be granted the "single thread" path.
I shall discuss this with you. If it were otherwise, to interpret everything solely according to one's teacher would be incorrect.
Zen Master Foyin Zhiqing of Zhikai in Dongjing, a native of the Ye family of Tong’an in Quanzhou, left the household life under Huiru of Luyuan.
After traveling extensively to study under various masters, he finally realized the mind-ground at Mount Gui. He first appeared in the world at Wuzu, where he received the Dharma succession.
By imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Zhikai Monastery. On the day of the opening of the hall, Emperor Zhezong of the Song dynasty dispatched an imperial messenger to bestow incense.

After the Master had ascended the seat and finished the exchange of questions and answers, he took up his whisk and called to the assembly, saying: "Do you see? Layer upon layer, for your sakes I emit a hundred kinds of jewel-light.
He then struck the meditation platform and said: "Do you hear? Sentence after sentence, for your sakes I expound the definitive meaning of the One Vehicle. All...
If a person attains awakening here and now, they will immediately see that the Eye of the True Dharma on Vulture Peak is brilliantly manifest before their eyes,

and the wondrous mind of Nirvana at Shaoshi is radiantly revealed throughout their entire being. Just as Yajñadatta realized that the face in the mirror was originally nothing other than his own head,
and the wrestler obtained the pearl upon his forehead which, in the end, could not have been gained from another— it is exactly like this.

"Then immeasurable supernormal powers and samādhis are, in every atom, primordially and perfectly accomplished. The dharma-gates of the Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, are fully present in every thought-moment.
O worthy ones, is there anyone capable of grasping it in this very way? After a long silence, he said:
The single breath speaks not, yet it contains all forms; where do the myriad spirits go to repay this impartiality? In the *genji* year of the *gengchen* cycle, Emperor Zhezong passed away.
One hundred days later, the Master was summoned into the palace and bestowed with the title Chan Master Foyin. In the second month of the following year, the Empress Dowager passed away.
On the fifteenth day of the fifth week after her death, he received an imperial decree to expound the Dharma in the Cide Hall.
A monk asked Chan Master Shouchong of Baiyun Haihui in Anqing: "Everyone praises Yaoshan’s single phrase; how is it with the teaching of Baiyun?
The Master said: "It fills the void. The monk asked: "Who knows that today, within the bright moon, Shucheng is locked?
The Master said: "Gazing upward, one awaits the rising sun. [Another monk] asked: "A single drop from Caoxi universally moistens the great thousandfold world."
"White clouds emerge from the mountains; how do they benefit sentient beings? The Master said, "Clouds hang across the mouth of the cave; returning birds lose their nests.
[The monk] asked, "What about the single path pointed out by the compass? The Master said, "An iron snake stands across the great road, its entire body black as smoke."
Chan Master Zuquan of Daomiao, Tanzhou, successor to Chan Master Daomiao Xiu of Fuzhou, was a native of the Wu clan. A monk asked, "What is the house style of Daomiao?
The Master said, "Bamboo has joints above and below; pines are green now and forever. The monk asked, "I do not understand what is drunk therein."
"What do you eat? The Master said, "When hungry, I eat the noble lord’s fine white rice; when thirsty, I drink the tea from before the Divine Transport Granary.
Entering the hall, he said: "The Way has no fixed disorder; the Dharma is free from seeing and knowing. When words and phrases coincide, there is no fixed definition at all.
From antiquity, the Dragon Gate has had no overnight guests; to this day, the Bird Path is devoid of tracks. If you wish to understand the essential meaning within this, [it is like] fire..."
The mole cricket swallows the great tiger. *Du!* [He] ascends the hall. Rain falls and the steps are wet; when dry and sunny, the water does not flow.
Bird nests are at the bottom of the vast ocean; fish leap from the tops of rocky mountains. Among the assembly, there is much deliberation regarding the first two lines.
These are words of plain reality. The final two lines are talk beyond the ordinary. If you understand it thus, you will see only jagged rocks and not the falling of jade.
Only when you see the falling of jade do you finally know the vast expanse. Heh!
Chan Master Wenyuan of Fuyan on Mount Nanyue was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master spat directly in his face. He then ascended the hall and said:
"Wild flowers have fallen away to the roots of the ancient city; Gradually the cicadas sing across the banks of the Xiang River.
Fine drizzling plum rain sprinkles the high heavens; Gentle, fragrant breezes fill the courtyard and chambers. The thirty-three [deities] and the ancient adept— The elephant turns, the dragon..."
What was once hidden has now been revealed; as soon as it is revealed, it becomes a stain. I respectfully inform those who investigate the profound mysteries: do not let your time be spent in vain.
On the day Master Yunggong of Nan’ge and Nantai opened the hall for formal preaching, he ascended the seat and said: "Rarely encountered and difficult to meet—this is precisely the moment.
Why say that Śākyamuni has already passed away and Maitreya has not yet been born? [He] took up his whisk and said: 'Right at this very day, the Buddha...'"
The Dharma is entirely contained within the tip of this whisk. To let go or to hold fast—everything depends on the moment.

When letting go, it is like the wind blowing and the grass bending; even shards of tile and pebbles emit light, and Shi-de and Han-shan nod their heads and clap their hands. When holding fast, there is no leakage;
even refined gold loses its luster, and De-shan and Lin-chi swallow their breath and silence. At such a time, let go.
"Practice is it. Grasping it is it. After a long silence, he said, "Look again in five days.
At the Fangguang Temple in the Rear Cave of Mount Heng in Nanhua, State of Hengzhou, Chan Master Da ascended the hall.

Holding up his staff, he said, "Virtuous Chan practitioners, extend your unobstructed hands; pluck it from amidst the clouds and bring it here with the snow. Present it before the assembly and gaze upon it."
Sufficient. There is more than enough to play with. He then drew a line and said: "Sooner or later, it shall disperse as rain, nourishing the grasses and trees throughout the world.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Departing from the four propositions and severing the hundred negations, one thus brings the frantic mind to rest.

If the faculty does not turn in this way, doubt persists. Apart from this, by what principle can one rely? 'Zhaozhou’s East and West'—do you understand this thoroughly? The radish of Zhenzhou exists."
The Flavor. (He gives a shout.
Chan Master Shaojue Chunbai of Zhaojue Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture, a dharma heir of Chan Master Huangbo Xing, was the son of the Zhi clan from Feiwu in Zizhou. He possessed [past]...
Dongshan Guifeng. While crossing a stream, he attained a realization. He subsequently went to Mount Emei to leave the household life and receive full ordination.
His first teacher was Taiping Huijun; next, he studied under Huangbo Xianyan. He stayed for over a year, yet Huangbo never once looked at him.

The Master served him with increasing diligence. One day, Huangbo raised his eyes and gazed at him intently. The Master exclaimed, "Why does this old fellow fail to hold himself? Huangbo laughed heartily. Thereupon—
This was for the purpose of certification. At the end of the Yuanfeng era of Emperor Shenzong of the Song dynasty, Prince Nankang invited Ba to the capital. The Master accompanied him on the journey.
Not long after, some students of the Imperial Academy submitted a memorial accusing a *boshi* (Confucian scholar-official), and the discourse implicated Ba.

By imperial decree, he returned to Shu, where his disciples dispersed like stars; the Master alone remained to attend upon him. It happened that the military governor of Chengdu changed the status of Zhaojue Monastery to a *shifang* (public monastery).
The Master responded to this. Having taken charge of the monastery, he lived according to the Vinaya: when it was cold, he would warm himself by the fire; when it was hot, he would fan himself;

when hungry, he would eat; when weary, he would sleep. Thus, the cypress before Zhaozhou’s courtyard and the pine behind Xiangyan’s ridge were planted for no other purpose than to usher in the pure breeze. But tell me, what is the ultimate point? [Seal] (Jia)
The Zi year, Yi-chou, is the Metal of the Sea; Bing-yin and Ding-mao are the Fire of the Furnace. He entered nirvana and, with a verse, entrusted his small disciple Zongxian, saying:
"The wind is high and the moon is cold; the waters are distant and the heavens are long. When one leaves the gate, there is no shadow—every which way."
He passed away with a serene countenance. His age was fifty-nine; his years since ordination were thirty-four.
He was interred in a stupa at his home mountain.
A monk asked Chan Master Daoying of Jianfu in Raozhou, a successor of Chan Master Kaiyuan Qi: "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master replied: "Lapis lazuli."
[The Master] said, "A crystal vase holding flowers. [The monk] asked, "What about after you have left this world? The Master said, "An agate bowl filled with fruit.
[The monk] asked, "I do not know, Master, whether today is the same as before or different. The Master said, "Kicking over the vase is better than knocking over the bowl.

He ascended the hall and said, "Speaking in accordance with reality, speaking is not permitted, and silence is not permitted. Even if one were to forget both speech and silence, there would still be no point of connection."
Shè. Why is there no path within the phrase? The meaning lies within the phrase; it is neither intention nor non-intention, and it is beyond the reach of calculation.
If one is struck directly on the head and the eye opens wide at the crown of the skull, then there is indeed a swift realization here.
If one lowers the head and seeks it beneath the roots of thought, one will ultimately fail to grasp it. Thus one knows that [the myriad things...]
The Dharma has no root. Those who seek to exhaust it err; its single source leaves no trace. Those who seek to return are lost. Behold:
the radiance of the ancient Buddhas and the refined spirit of the former worthies—each and every one manifests from within the state of desirelessness and non-reliance.

At times they are solitary, steep, and towering, ultimately impossible to grasp; at other times they are harmonious, inclusive, and all-pervasive, such that nothing at all can be seen. In the end, not a single thing is fixed.
It abides nowhere, nor is it bound by either extreme. There is neither "is" nor "is not," neither "non-is" nor "non-non-is.
In gain there is nothing gained; in loss there is nothing lost. It has never been separated by even a hair’s breadth, nor has it ever been altered by so much as a strand of silk.

This luminous ancient path does not belong to the subtle or the minute. To encounter it is to hold it forth; in a fleeting glance, one passes right through it. It does not dwell in the position of correctness—how could it?
Falling into deviant paths, one does not tread upon the Great Way, but instead rushes along narrow trails. Drifting and dazed, where does one dwell?
What is one doing? Turning back, nothing is encountered; looking around, there is no counterpart. To contemplate universally with a single thought, all is vast, empty, and still.
This essential point has not been transmitted by the thousand sages; to understand it directly and thoroughly is to transcend at this very moment. Thus, in this state of bare radiance, it is thus:
It is easy. In the place where things are clearly manifest, it is thus difficult. One must not allow for any sticking or staining; one must directly strip away and clear them all.
If you let go with your original hands and feet, there is nothing that cannot be gathered back. Each and every thing emits light and manifests auspicious signs.
Each and every trace is erased, every vestige cut off. Upon the pivot, there is no lingering; within the words, nothing can be revealed.
Thoroughly stirred, it does not become turbid; struck through and through, the whole body does not shatter. Tell me, after all, what is this?
How can it be so penetratingly intelligent, so extraordinary, and so steadfast? Friends, do not seek to recognize its face; there is no need.
Do not fixate on their names, nor seek out where they dwell. Why? Because they have no location, they have no names, and they have no countenances.
Were one to give rise to even a single thought of seeking them, however minute it may be—like a speck of dust—one would immediately be separated from them by ten or five lifetimes.

I further intended to take charge [of my own mind], but as I contemplated it, I saw only increasing confusion and entanglement. It would be better to let it go for a long time, allowing it to be free and at ease.
When it wishes to arise, it arises; when it wishes to abide, it abides. It is the natural and yet not the natural; it is suchness and yet not suchness;
it is profound stillness and yet not profound stillness; it is decay and yet not decay. There is no attachment to birth and no fear of death.

There is no Buddha to seek; there is no Māra to fear. One does not associate with bodhi, nor does one dwell together with afflictions. One does not accept a single dharma, nor does one reject a single dharma.
There is neither being-present nor being-absent; it is neither separate nor not separate. If one can perceive and attain it in this way, [one has realized it].
Śākyamuni is Śākyamuni; Dharma is Dharma. It makes me feel like a worn-out wooden bowl.

To speak in such a manner—when scrutinized within the school of the patch-robed monks—even those with hempen skirts and straw sandals cannot avoid getting a bit of mud and water on them, let alone you all.
Furthermore, you say, "I believe this is a statement of ultimate reality," while that is merely a gate of differentiation.
The courtyard. This is the crucial pivot; this is the root of the Way and the sensory objects.
They are taught and practiced to one another like the passing of a secret word from house to house in a village of seven households. What connection is there? There is nothing to do; take care.
Lecturer Zunseng Youpeng of Quanzhou was the son of the Jiang family of that prefecture. At the age of seven, he took the scriptural examination and was selected;

he subsequently shaved his head and studied extensively at various monastic academies. He once composed commentaries on such sutras as the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi* and the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa*, and scholars revered him.

Yet, he often harbored doubts regarding the path of the Patriarchs’ direct pointing, and thus frequently associated with Chan monks. One day, he went to visit Kaiyuan Monastery; before he had even reached the threshold, he encountered [the Master].
His mind was suddenly enlightened. Yuanchu then asked, "Master, what have you come for? The Master replied, "I dare not hold my ears high while disparaging my eyes.
Yuanchu said, "You are already old and venerable; why must you be like this? The Master said, "He who considers himself superior does not grow.
Yuanchu said, "I do not ask about your morning study of the *Avataṃsaka* and your night reading of the *Prajñāpāramitā*. What is that one phrase for the present moment? The Master—
[The Master] said, "The sun is exactly at noon. Yuan said, "Idle talk. Speak further. The Master said, "Throughout my life I have relied on loyalty and trust;
today I leave myself to the winds and waves. Although it is so, what connection is there between this and the Master speaking thus?
One must have the new precept-holder’s straw sandals worn through. Yuan said, "I will let you pass here for now. But should you encounter Bodhidharma..."
The questioner asked, "How would you say it? The Master then gave a shout. Yuan said, "This lecturer, meeting the old monk today, has his spirit piercing the Ox and Dipper constellations.
The Master said, "A second offense will not be tolerated. Yuan clapped his hands and laughed loudly.
Chan Master Yun Guang of Shuangxi Baoyan on Mount Lu in Nankang ascended the hall and said:
"A-he-he! How truly marvelous! Without rolling up the curtain, one sees the whole world. 'Shenguang obtained the marrow'—who says so? Bodhidharma never came to the land of the East.
It is easy to dry up the Western River with a single gulp, but the supreme treasure of the Central Plains is difficult to price. How truly marvelous! It causes people..."
Recalling Old Xinghua, he gave a shout.
Zen Master Shan-sui of Longwang Mountain in Tanzhou, successor to Zen Master Weiyang, was asked by a monk: "What is the realm of the Dragon King? The Master said: "Water."
"In the Crystal Palace. [The monk asked: "What is the wish-fulfilling jewel of the Dragon King? The Master said, "In the topknot upon his head.
The monk prostrated. The Master said, "Do not say it is not as you wish. Very well."
A monk asked Zen Master Yongtai of Shiyuan on Mount Huangbo in Ruizhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Cast of iron. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him and said, "Do you understand? The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Why did you not realize it sooner?"
Chan Master Huiri of Mount Lu ascended the hall and said: "There is no need to seek the Truth; one must only cease all views.
Although the Great Master of the Third Patriarch avoided the golden hook, he was unaware that he had already swallowed the red line. Huiri, however, is not like this.
There is no need to seek the Truth nor to cease all views; riding backward upon the ox, one enters the Buddha Hall. With a single blast from the herdsman’s flute, heaven and earth are vast and wide.
I bow my head to Gautama—the true Yellow-Faced One.
A monk asked Chan Master Jingxian of Guyin in Xiangyang, "I do not ask about 'one arrow piercing the three barriers.
But when practitioners meet one another, what then? The Master said, "The thief’s own body has already been exposed. He ascended the hall and said: "Today is the fifth day of the first month.
Everyone, look clearly! To add heat to fire; to add bitterness to suffering. It is truly laughable that Guyin is so lacking in..."
End. A riddle flows before the crags of the empty valley. [The Master] gives a shout.
Chan Master Fada Baoyan of Yuyang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Gancheng of Fuyan, was a native of the Yu clan of Ruzhou. A monk asked: "Without falling into..."
At Jie-chu, he requested instruction from the Master. The Master said, "A wax figure facing a fire. He asked, "What is it ultimately like?

The Master said, "The thin spot pierces first. Ascending the hall, [the Master] held up a flower to show the assembly. [Vimalakīrti] merely patted his own chest; [the Buddha] broke into a smile. Both fell into the secondary moon.
Śāṇavāsa faced the wall at Shaolin as if no one were there; at midnight crossing the river, he was too eager to reach his destination. Furthermore—

To speak of Buddhas and patriarchs is to place a head upon a head; to expound the wondrous and discourse on the true is to wash soil with soil. To gather flowers and cluster brocades is for the mouth to be a gate of calamity.
To remain in stillness without action is to wait for a rabbit by a stump. None of these are as it truly is: it is an unperforated iron hammer.
For one who practices the Way, how could this be so? Do you understand? Though white clouds are mindless things, in the end they remain attached to the green mountains.
Chan Master Faru of Daochang Monastery in Anji Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yungai Zhi.
He was the son of the Xu family of Quzhou. Having studied under Yungai, he attained enlightenment through the saying of Fenyang, "The Ten Wisdoms are Identical with Reality.
Because he frequently spoke of these "Ten Wisdoms Being Identical with Reality," the monastic community called him "Ru-shi" (Like the Ten).
The same applies to Shuian and Yuanji; both relied upon him. Ji once praised him, saying: "A face of cast iron is difficult to approach; in an ordinary step, he moves heaven and earth.
Playfully taking up the 'Ten Wisdoms as One Reality' talk, he does not fail the true-bone grandson of Huanglong.
Ascending the hall, [he said: "When knowledge and views establish further knowing, this is the root of ignorance. When knowledge and views are without seeing, this is Nirvana."
The *paryaṅka* is untainted, truly pure. How could anything else be admitted within it? Śākyamuni, the Old Man, has collapsed with his whole body;
how shall his descendants of later generations receive and continue him? Do you wish to understand? The Penetrating Mystery is not the world of men;
where can one seek the green mountains that fill the eyes?
Chan Master Baoshou Zuile of Fuzhou was a native of Gutian. He ascended the hall and said: “The Buddhas are not real, yet they preach the Dharma to deliver all living beings.
The Bodhisattvas possess wisdom, yet their vision of nature is not clear. White clouds have no intentionality, yet they shed rain upon the world.
The great earth has no sentimentality, yet it can cause all grasses and trees to grow. If you can understand this, you still harbor a lingering consciousness.”
If you understand, well and good; if you do not, you fall into the state of the indeterminate (*avyākṛta*). How can one be identical to this while departing from these two paths?
The sea is so vast it cannot hide the moon; the mountains are so deep they are exceptionally cold.
A monk asked Chan Master Hui-ming of Shifo in Shaoxing Prefecture, “What is the realm of the Precious Mark?
The Master said, “Carved out over three lifetimes. The monk asked, “Who is within the realm? The Master said, “One Buddha and two Bodhisattvas.”

Chan Master Guanghui Daga of Fuzhou, successor to Chan Master Wenzhu of Xuansha, ascended the hall and said: "The Buddha awakens through a mindless state; the mind becomes deluded because of the existence of a Buddha."
In the place where the Buddha-mind is pure, wild monkeys cry beyond the clouds.
One day, Chan Master Yongyuan of Sizhou in Pingjiang Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Jianlong, asked Jianlong: "When Linji was at Huangbo, three..."
He returned to inquire about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, but was struck three times. What was the intent? Before he had even finished speaking, he was struck once more with the whisk.
The Master suddenly realized the essential principle. On the day of his formal opening of the hall, a monk asked: "The fourfold assembly has gathered like clouds;

we pray that the Master will preach the Dharma. The Master said: "Having eyes but no ears, sitting by the fire in the sixth month. [The monk] said: "A single phrase cuts off the flow; ten thousand..."

The student’s mental activity suddenly ceased. The Master said, "When you do not listen properly, you call a bell a water jar. The student asked, "From morning attendance to evening requests, what kind of business is this accomplishing?
The Master said, "I only want you to come to rest. The student said, "Had I known earlier that the lamp was fire, the meal would have been ready long ago.
The Master said, "Why is it that your nostrils are pierced by this staff? The student said, "It is twisted and crooked."
"Even if one acts with straightforwardness, how can one possibly win? The Master said, "For now, let him vent his anger. He ascended the hall and said:
"One, two, three, four, five—within the fire, a cricket swallows a tiger. Six, seven, eight, nine, ten—under the water, a clay ox stands upon the waves.

Day and night, the rain falls incessantly; an unperforated iron hammer cannot be soaked through. If it cannot be soaked through, the urgency of those who have reached the core is such that the hundred rivers [flow back]."
The surging waves and Mount Sumeru are towering; the eight-armed Nātha comes crashing out. He bows his head and praises, saying, "It is difficult to reach.
*Ei!* [He] ascends the hall. Holding his staff crosswise, he looks at the assembly and says, "Today, one tumbles on level ground," and then descends from the seat.
