[End. The Chan Master Yuanzheng Chuandeng of Chengtian Yong’an in Pingjiang Prefecture, a dharma successor of Chan Master Baoben Yuan, was the son of the Zheng family of Yanzhou. [He] contemplated the cypress.
Shuzi had a sudden realization. He then composed a verse, saying: "Zhaozhou’s Cypress Tree—few know its coming and going.
Casting aside the sweet peach tree, he seeks the mountains to pluck sour pears. He presented this to Yuan, who approved it. Later, Yuan ordered him to reside at this temple.
A monk asked, "A wooden man and a stone woman converse about the Truth. I do not ask about the conversation; what is the Truth? The Master said, "On the mountain peak..."
The plum blossoms are white; by the stream, the willows are green. Entering the hall [the Master said]: "All classes of beings, including devas and humans, receive this power of grace.
Great assembly, suppose someone were to say: 'I do not receive the power of the Buddha's grace; I do not dwell within the three realms; I do not belong to the five elements.
Even the Patriarchs would dare not settle his case, and even the Buddhas of the past would dare not bestow a name upon him. But tell me, what kind of person is he?"
A person stood for a long while and said: "Leaning against the stone cliff, one burns the iron bowl; hanging from the pine branches, one suspends the copper pitcher.
This was the Dharma successor of Chan Master Longqing Xian:
Chan Master Wen'i of Qineng at Anhua, Tanzhou, ascending the hall [to preach]. He said: "Picking up the flower and smiling was a vain exertion of effort. Standing—
"Snow reaching the waist is a waste of effort. How does it compare to Old Lu, who had no use for such things? Yet he transmitted the robe and bowl to stir up the true wind.
The assembly, tell me: which is the robe and bowl transmitted by Old Lu? Is it the one that Daoshou struck his head with and could not lift?
Tell me, is this not "mistaking the zero-point on the scale"? [With the whisk, he strikes the meditation seat and descends.]

Chan Master Weishuang of Kuangxiao Temple in Ningguo Prefecture, a dharma heir of Chan Master Sanzong, ascended the hall and said: "Today is the first day of the sixth month; already half the year has passed.
I announce this to those who study the Source: recognize your mother’s birth-face! Whether you recognize your mother’s birth-face or not—look, the egret flies!"
Amidst the waves of human life, one shakes out a ball of silver embroidery thread.

Zen Master Qi Tian of Falun Monastery on Mount Nanyue, a successor of Zen Master Ying of Letan, was asked by a monk: "I, a student, have come before you; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said:
"Did you hear the sound of the drum just now? The monk replied, "I heard it. The Master said, "Give me back the head of the phrase.
The monk bowed in prostration. The Master said, "This makes people wonder. Ascending the hall, he gave a shout and said, "The lion’s roar!
He gave another shout and said, "The elephant king’s snort! He gave another shout and said, "A mad dog chasing a clod of earth! He gave another shout and said, "A shrimp!"
Unable to leap out of the measuring bucket, he said: "Of these four shouts, there is one shout capable of serving as a teacher for the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Let the monks try to discern it. If you cannot discern it, you are much like one lost in the middle of the day. Ascending the hall, he remained silent for a long while, then shouted once, saying:
"When the nature is still, the emotions are at ease; when the mind is stirred, the spirit grows weary. He then looked to his left and right and said: [The text ends here.]

"Guarding the truth, one's resolve becomes full. Holding up his staff, he said, "When the mind follows external objects, it is led astray. He suddenly called out to the assembly, "If you do not find strange things strange, the strangeness will vanish of itself.
He leaned the staff against [the wall] and descended from the seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Yun of Huiming in Quanzhou, “How do you guide people within the ocean of Prajñā?
The Master said, “The clouds part; the Milky Way stretches far. The monk asked, “Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, “Blood appears at the tip of the staff.
A monk asked, “Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind upon it long ago, yet until this very day he has not attained the wondrous. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, “Ugly and clumsy.”
Capable of bearing it.
Chan Master You’en of Yangshan in Yuanzhou ascended the hall and struck the meditation seat with his staff, saying:

"The Buddha's command and the Patriarchs' command have crumbled like tiles and melted like ice. The half-words and full-words are ten thousand mountains and ten thousand rivers. Under the gate of the patch-robed monks, the grass bows before the wind."

[He] walked about. Nevertheless, "The official gate does not admit a needle, yet private paths allow for carriages and horses. There is one extraordinary cause and condition; I shall present it to the great assembly.
After a long silence, he struck the ground once with his staff and said: "Dharmatrāta sat in vain against the wall for nine years; returning west, he was ashamed to face the people of Luoyang."
Chan Master Da Miao Qi Xun of Changsha ascended the hall and said: "When the horns have not yet grown, if you can recognize [the ox], you have already trespassed upon the crops.
If you wait until it has raised its head and wears its horns, coming from among the heterodox species—giving birth to a calf and raising it—how could one possibly endure that?
Have you not seen how Yangshan said: 'Each time it enters the grass, each time he pulls it by the nose'? Although it is thus..."
"May they spare the crops of the farmers. Now tell me, how can one avoid offending them? After a long silence, he said:
"The iron ox does not eat the grass by the fence; it climbs straight up to the summit of Mount Sumeru to sleep. Ascending the hall, he said: "Layered green mountains, vast and boundless waters;
the monkeys love the fragrant ripening fruits on the cliffs. There is yet another thing worthy of admiration: deep in the night, the bright moon shines upon the mountain hall."
Chan Master Wujue Jingtan of Yuyang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture was a Dharma heir of Chan Master Baoning Ji. He was a native of Jiahe and later returned to Fahui Monastery in Qiantang.
One day he ascended the hall and said: "Originally I lay among the white clouds in the deep mountains; by chance, I have come here to lodge my idle body. Do not...
Someone came to ask me about Chan and the Way. I am but a man who eats rice and defecates.

In the summer of the Bingyin year of Emperor Gaozong’s Shaoxing era, he took his leave of the nobility to return home and entrusted the affairs of the monastery to others. As the fourfold assembly crowded around to watch, he fanned himself for a long time and then wrote this verse:
"This fellow has never had a crack or flaw. For fifty-six years he has established his reputation as a master of speech.

Today he dies and meets King Yama; the Sword-Trees and Knife-Mountains strike fear into men. He then drew a circle and said, "Aha! Let the various quarters do as they please—drilling tortoises and striking tiles.
He withdrew his legs and passed away. After the cremation, the *śarīra* (relics) fell like fine snow. His disciples took the bones and returned them to Aśoka.
Mount Wang: Construction of a Stupa.
Chan Master Jiexiang of Zhenru Temple in Taizhou, a native of the Lin clan of Xinghua, ascended the hall and said: "At the break of dawn in early winter, the sky is cold;
leaves fall and return to their root, revealing the distant mountains. This is not a phenomenon of seeing, hearing, arising, or ceasing—do not treat it as such right before you."
Seeing, hearing, and observing.
A monk asked Chan Master Chushi Ching of Nanyuya Shousheng in Qizhou, successor to Chan Master Wuzu Fanchan: "When a deceased monk undergoes transformation, where does he go?"
[The monk] departed. The Master said, "At Lingfeng, the water is swift. [The monk] said, "In that case, there is no birth? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!
On the ninth day, Chan Master Dàlún of Yánfú at Yuèdǐng in Qízhōu ascended the hall and said: "What thing can offer hospitality on the Double Ninth Festival?"

At home, every branch of the hedge chrysanthemums has burst into bloom. Rather than acting like the former Marquis who merely accompanied others for wine, I shall brew a full cup of Zhaozhou tea for you.
With this single cup alone, one awakens from the great dream; Lu Tong’s boast of seven bowls is but empty vanity. After a long silence, he said, “I request it now,” and struck his staff once.
Ascending the hall, he said: “The seasonal rains have passed frequently, and the northern eaves are cool. In the wild fields, the insects and shells are all gone.”
Radiating light, the Chan master lies high in repose with no other concerns; he has won the long resonance of the chime from the treetops.

At such a moment as this, who is the one who understands? After a long silence, he said: "Since the passing of Ziqi, a thousand years have been in vain; the moon rises over the azure cliffs as the mountain stream flows cold."
Zen Master Weigu of Baizhang in Ruizhou, successor to Zen Master Huanglong Su, ascended the hall.
Once the assembly had gathered and settled, he held up his staff and showed it to the crowd, saying:
"Much emptiness is not as good as a little reality.
*He struck once and immediately rose.* The monks of Zen Master Zu Jian "Moon-Jewel" of Jiading Prefecture requested the Master’s essential words for their records. The Master said:

"When Bodhidharma came from the West, he transmitted the mind-seal alone. The Sixth Patriarch of Caoxi could not recognize a single character. Today, the words used by those appearing in the world everywhere..."
[He] spoke this verse: "Like a mountain already heavy, one adds further ropes. Then, striking the meditation seat, he said: "If you can realize it here, you are still of dull faculties.
If you have not yet done so, sleep as you please in the depths of the white clouds; just do not let the cold monkeys wail at midnight."
Chan Master Qingjian of Yangshan in Yuanzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The matter is clear beneath Mount Jiyun; I ask the Master to hand over the four rattan canes.
The Master said, "Zhaozhou was eighty years old before he began his travels. The monk said, "How could you be so unaware of the proper timing?
The Master said, "Once you have traveled as far as Nanquan, you may simply rest. He then said, "Having newly arrived at this eminent assembly, I am truly comforted."
The spiritual breast: amidst the arrayed peaks and ridges, the local style of one’s own house is ever revealed; the green pines lining the path lead straight through to the Great Road of Chang’an.
Where mist and clouds span the wilds and palace halls soar above the void, without shifting a single step, one suddenly enters the Flower Treasury World (*Kusumagarbha-loka*).
Looking left and right, he said: "The assembly has entered, indeed; but do you see Sudhana? Thereupon, he lowered [his hand].
The First Ancestor said: "Those of long-standing practice who are superior men already know where they must return.
As for those who have newly arrived as practitioners of Chan, it does no harm to strive to grasp it.
A monk asked Master Zongshi, the Abbot of Jingzhao An in Dingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Shilang Lin: "Who is the master of this hermitage? The Master [replied]: [Silence].
The Master said, "I have never granted permission from the beginning. When the monk hesitated, the Master said, "If you understand, then you understand; you must not settle upon names or characters.
As the monk was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him with his staff. In the Master’s quarters, he would constantly hold up his whisk for the assembly, saying:
If you call it a whisk, it is still not it. If you do not call it a whisk, you are willfully ignorant of it. What do you call it?
In response to a monk’s request for instruction, the Master answered with this verse: I have a single whisk; in its use, there is no other artifice.
Sometimes it hangs from a pine branch, letting its head droop while its horn remains exposed.
Master Nian of Wanshou Monastery in Chenzhou was a successor of Master Gong of Huayao. A monk asked, "The auspicious assembly of the Dragon Flower has commenced this morning;
I wonder where the World-Honored One Maitreya currently resides? The Master said, "On the head of the pork stall. The monk said, "If that is the World-Honored One Maitreya..."
"Why are you at the pork stall? The Master said, "If you are not one who can play in the tide, do not enter the surging waves.
[The student] asked, "Ultimately, what then is the matter? The Master said, "The barbarian does not tie his sash. On New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall and said:
"Going and returning are boundless; movement and stillness are of one source. Containing virtue, it returns to emptiness; transcending the selfless, it is utterly remote."
The sun of yesterday and the sun of today: their illumination is not dual. The wind of yesterday and the wind of today: its blowing is not dual.
The rain of yesterday and the rain of today: its moistening is not dual. Within this, one seeks the marks of coming and going, yet they cannot be found. Why?
When the minds of self and other arise, there is no trace at the place of arising; when the mind of self is forgotten, that forgetting is without cessation.
The Trace. If the great assembly can understand it here, you will share the same root as heaven and earth and be of one body with the myriad things.
If you have not yet attained clarity, this mountain monk shall chant it for you verse by verse. First Verse of the New Year: The ancient Buddha’s house style emerges from this;
No need to labor further upward. Throughout kalpas, how has it ever differed from today? Second Verse of the New Year:
"Silent, desolate, and cold—there is no flavor. Zhaozhou calls out, 'Come, let us drink tea. Raise your eyebrows and you must see through it at once.

On the third day of the New Year, I prostrate and offer my greetings to all who have come above. If you ask about the matters within Mount Xiangshan, the stream of Lingyuan flows on, as blue as indigo.
He then gave a shout and descended from his seat.
The lay practitioner Su Che (style name Ziyou), who served as a Minister of State, was a successor of Chan Master Shun of Shanglan.

In the third year of the Yuanfeng era, while serving as an official in Suiyang, he was demoted to the post of salt and liquor tax collector in Ruizhou. At that time, Shun of Shanglan in Hongzhou was with his father, Lord Xun of Wen’an.

There was a man named Chunsu. [Zhaozhou] went to visit him, and they were immediately filled with great joy. The Master [Zhaozhou] inquired about the Dharma of the mind, and Chunsu showed him the karmic conditions regarding the "pinching of the nose.
Thereupon, Zhaozhou attained realization and presented a verse, saying: "In middle age I heard the Way and realized my former errors; By chance we have met, Master Chunsu, the aged one.
Pinching the nose, I directly entered upon the true countenance; Shaking my head, I will not accept any other tongs or hammers. [The verse continues: "The withered vine is broken..."
What business has this patch-robed monk? "White wine and green salt—who am I? I feel ashamed before the waning moon rising over the eastern eaves;
a single cup of nectar, as smooth as honey.
[This is] the Dharma heir of Master Jicui Yong’an.
Master Chujin of Qingping in Luling, Jixian, ascended the hall for the formal discourse. Striking once with his staff, he said: "The bell has just ceased; the drum thuds on.
I have specially ascended this hall to speak of the Patriarchs' wind. A thousand explanations and ten thousand metaphors turn into falsehoods.
To distinguish the black from the white—who would communicate with them? My mountain monk’s staff probes and investigates minutely: how many [will understand] thirty years hence?"
Bai-tou-weng leaned on his staff and said, "Take care.

Chan Master Ding of Longxing Temple in Changsha, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Foyin Ming, was asked by a monk: "What is the realm of Xiao and Xiang? The Master replied: "When the monkeys arrive..."
Deep into the night, he cried out from the foot of Mount Lu: "Tell me, what is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said: "When we meet, we do not dismount;
each must hasten on his own journey. Ascending the hall, he said: "The autumn wind has blown for several nights and the cold gradually increases;

the patch-robed monks have already begun to feel their bodies shivering. They stay awake all night long, brooding over their impatience. The Patriarchs ran about in confusion without realizing it; Śākyamuni appeared in the world, yet they missed him."
"Step by step, Maitreya descends to be born. How regrettable! One’s own divine light remains dim throughout the day until the hour of You (the sixth watch).
Brothers, how would you describe this 'own divine light'? After a long silence, he said: "A single bright moon shines upon the Xiao and Xiang rivers.
With a shout, he struck.
Chan Master Chaozong Huifang of Heishan in Jizhou,
a successor of Chan Master Huanglong Xin of the fourteenth generation under Nanyue, was the son of the Gong family of Linjiang. He ascended the hall and raised his whisk.
It is said: Look, look! It is simply this. In Linji, illumination and function proceed together; in Yunmen, principle and phenomenon are both complete;
in Caodong, the partial and the correct harmonize and penetrate; in Weishan, the hidden mechanism is perfectly integrated;
and in Fayan, how could it be merely "mind-only"? Nevertheless, while each of these five houses has its own distinct pedagogical methods and institutional arrangements, even if one were to...

To argue with such boldness and clarity is still merely a matter of chasing after shadows and reflections. If you wish to resist and overcome birth and death, there is a world of difference between the two.
As for the single phrase that transcends birth and death—how would you say it? After a long silence, he said:
"I have nearly provided a mistaken footnote."
Chan Master Chongjue Fakong of Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Gushu. He ascended the hall and said: "The ten directions have no walls;
the four sides likewise have no gates. Pure and bare, clear and naked—there is nothing to grasp. He then raised his whisk and said:
"The old fellow Guǎngxī flaunted his elegance on the crossroads, peddling his cleverness by saying, 'I know how to string pearls; I know how to string pearls.'"

Jade tablets are disordered; silk scrolls and rolls of gauze are scattered. In brothels and wine shops, among the commoners and servants gathered like broken tiles, within tiger dens and demonic palaces, Nanda and Kumbhakarṇa display their fury.
Encountering King Wen, they promote ritual and music; meeting Jie and Zhou, they brandish weapons and war.
Today, having been spotted by Chongjue, they are utterly humiliated. The Master’s verse on the "Wild Fox" story says: Spitting blood at others, one first soils oneself.
His mouth was like that of a wild fox; he had lost his head and was running madly, when suddenly he was called back and performed a somersault.
The Master was a man of stubborn integrity. Having served Sīxin for a long time, one day he took his leave. Sīxin said, "Your merit is thin; you should simply nourish yourself through the Way.
Qing Caotang also sent him off with a verse, which began: "Ten years we gathered at Longfeng Temple; once awakened to the Truth..."
"The myriad realms are empty and at rest; from now on, I shall follow conditions and remain in high seclusion. Do not let my name fall among the people of the world.

Later, when he appeared in the world at Chongjue Monastery, the temple was destroyed by fire within less than a month. The Master sighed and said, "I have failed to follow the words of my former teacher."
This was why he had come to this point. There was a wealthy man who wished to host a vegetarian feast for himself alone and had a three-gated hall constructed for it.
The Master said, "Your Excellency gives wealth to invite blessings; these are not gifts for an Elder to receive. If you command me to eat apart from the assembly, that is something I do not desire.
When Caotang Qing once sent a monk carrying robes to visit him, disciples arrived upon hearing the news. The Master was already old, yet he passed away at last.
At Mount Ben, Chan Master Zu Xiufeng of Tanzhou, a native of the He family of Changde Prefecture, ascended the hall and said: "Before the cliff of the withered tree, the night-blooming flower opens;
the iron ox still lies in the misty sands. I now once again brandish the shadow of the whip. He struck his whisk.
He said, "A single thought turning back brings one home. He then gave a shout and descended from his seat.
Zen Master Jixing Huiquan of Jiuding in Jiading Prefecture was a native of the Zhang family in Chengdu. A monk asked, "When the mind is deluded, the *Lotus Sūtra* revolves;
when the mind awakens, it revolves the *Lotus Sūtra*. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The wind is warm and the birds sing."
[The sound] *sui*. "The sun rises high, the flower's shadow deep. Entering the hall: "In the past, Yunmen had three phrases:
the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth, the phrase that cuts off all streams, and the phrase that follows the waves and rides the currents. Today, Jiuding also has three phrases."
These are what are called: "When hunger comes, eat; when cold, face the fire; when weary, sleep.
If one judges this by the Buddha-dharma, then Jiuding is standing directly downwind from Yunmen. If one judges it by worldly convention, then Yunmen is standing directly downwind from Jiuding.
Since these two statements contradict one another, how is it so? It is because of Jiuding.
The Hermit Xingkong Miaopu of Huating, Xuzhou: A native of Hanzhou, he long relied upon Siji (Sicixin) to attain realization.
He subsequently traveled to Xiushui, where he followed the legacy of Chuanshi (Chuanzi). He thatched a hut in the wilds of Qinglong and amused himself by blowing an iron flute.

He composed many poems and verses, which those who obtained them invariably treasured. Regarding his mountain dwelling, he wrote: "When both mind and dharmas are forgotten, one is still separated by delusion;
When form and emptiness are non-dual, a trace of dust remains. The hundred birds do not come and spring passes once more; I know not who is the person dwelling in this hermitage.
Furthermore, he warned the assembly, saying: "Studying the Way is like guarding a forbidden city: By day, ward off the six thieves; by night, remain alert."
The Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army can carry out his orders; without moving a blade of grass or a grain of dust, he brings about Great Peace. It is also said:

"Eating without plowing and wearing clothes without silkworms—tranquil and at leisure beyond the mundane world, one finds fulfillment in this sagely age. Yet, if you have not yet penetrated the pivot of the Patriarch’s gate, you must still maintain your intent and apply yourself with skillful means.
It is further said: "In the twelve hours of the day, do not let your work cease; exhaust it, exhaust it until there is nothing left to exhaust."
One must directly penetrate to the bottomless depths. Tread down the highest peak of Mount Sumeru. At the beginning of the Jianyan era of the Song dynasty’s Gaozong, Xu Ming rebelled.
His army passed through Wuzhen, where they carried out widespread slaughter; many of the local people fled. The Master alone went forth carrying his staff.
When the rebels saw his imposing and extraordinary appearance, they suspected he was a hidden spy and questioned him about his purpose. The Master said, "I am a Chan practitioner. He wished—
Upon arriving at Mijin Temple, the bandits were enraged and intended to execute him. The Master said, "A man of great character:
if you want my head, simply chop it off. Why be angry? My death is certain; I only wish to have one meal as a parting offering. The bandits served him meat and grain.

After the Master had finished his usual midday meal and performed the ritual for the deceased, he asked, "Who shall compose a literary inscription for me to offer in sacrifice? The bandits laughed and did not respond.
Answer: The Master asked for a brush and wrote in large characters: "Alas! O Spirit, that you weary me with life is the fault of the Great Mass;
that you employ me with longevity is the error of Yin and Yang; that you deprive me of wealth is the irregularity of the Five Elements;
that you constrain me with fate is the inauspiciousness of the time and day. How lamentable! How ultimate! Fortunately, there is the Way that transcends the mundane, which has awakened me."
As for its nature and its wondrous mind—what could possibly be its neighbor? Above, it accords with the true transformation of all Buddhas; below, it merges with the ignorance of ordinary beings.
Not a speck of dust moves; it is primordially and perfectly accomplished. How wondrous! How wondrous! The sun and moon are not sufficient to represent its brilliance;
heaven and earth are not sufficient to represent its vastness. It is磊磊落落 (leilei luoluo)—unimpeded, unobstructed, and free from attachment.
Unobstructed and free from entanglements for over sixty years, he blended his light with the mundane world. At forty-two *lǎ* (years of ordination), he wandered at ease and in sovereign freedom;
he rejoiced upon meeting people, yet did not bow before the Buddha. How joyful! How joyful! A pity for this young man—his refined elegance was so radiant.
He returns with composure to entrust himself to the spring breeze; his body is like empty space, ultimately indestructible. May you enjoy this offering. Thus it was said.

He raised his chopsticks and ate heartily. The bandits laughed loudly. When he had finished eating, he said again, "Since we have encountered these times of calamity and chaos, I am a man of great vigor and joy.
Now is precisely the right time to seize the opportunity; let me please cut you into two pieces with a single stroke. He then shouted, "Chop! Chop!

Only then did the bandits realize they were in the presence of a marvel; they bowed their heads in apology for their transgression and ordered guards to escort him out. Thus, the houses of Wuzhen were spared from burning.

This was truly the kindness of the Master. When both monastics and laypeople heard of this, they revered him all the more. There was a monk who saw the Master prostrating before a Buddha image and not bowing;
he went against the grain and asked, "Since you have seen the Buddha, why do you not bow? The Master struck him with his palm and said, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand.
The Master struck him again with his palm and said, "There are no two masters in one house. In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Xiangshi era, he fashioned a large basin and bored a hole in it.
He sealed [the coffin]. He wrote a letter and sent it to Xuedou Chihui, saying: "I am about to undergo a water burial. In the year of Renxu, Chihui arrived and saw that [Xingkong] was still alive.
He composed a verse to mock him, saying: "Alas, old Xingkong! You stubbornly insist on feeding fish and turtles. If you were going, you would have gone with your true nature;
Instead, you merely continue to speak to others. The Master read the verse and laughed, saying: "I wait for my brother to arrive so that he may bear witness. He then...
He announced to the fourfold assembly, and when they had gathered, the Master preached the essentials of the Dharma for them, further reciting this verse:
"To die while seated or standing is not as good as water burial; it saves on firewood for cremation and avoids the digging of graves. To cast off one's hands and depart is truly free and unimpeded.
Who is the one who understands? The Boatman Monk. His noble wind is hard to follow after a thousand years; of his single song of fishing, few have heard."
He sang: "I shall now sit cross-legged within this basin and follow the tide downstream. The assembly all followed him to the seashore, gazing until their eyes nearly failed them.
The Master took up a scoop to bale out the water and turned back; the crowd pressed forward to watch, but the water had no way to enter.

He then rode the current away once more, singing: "The Boatman of old returned to his native land; where his traces vanished, his wondrousness is immeasurable. His true wind is sent everywhere for those who know."
As for the sound: he played a transverse iron flute as the assembly dispersed. For a moment, the sound of the flute was plaintive;

then, amidst the vast expanse, he was seen casting the flute into the air and vanishing. The multitude wailed in longing and worshipped his image. Three days later, he appeared sitting cross-legged upon the sand as if alive.
Monastics and laypeople vied with one another to go and welcome him. He remained there for five days, after which he was cremated, and *śarīra* relics as large as beans were found.
Do not take account of it. Two cranes circled in the air and only departed once the fire was extinguished. The assembly enshrined the sacred relics and constructed a stupa at Qinglong.
The head seat Daolong of Zhongshan Temple in Yanzhou was the son of the Dong family of Tonglu; he received ordination at Zhongshan Temple. From—

He traveled extensively, and wherever he went, the venerable elders all held him in high esteem. In his later years, he arrived at Huanglong, where Sisi invited him to serve as the head of the assembly (*zuoyuan*).

Upon Sisi’s passing, he retired to live in seclusion on Mount Zhong. Admiring the world-transcending character of the elder master Chen, he bolted the door of his retreat and withdrew from worldly affairs.
He would sell his yarn several times a day for his own pleasure, and no one recognized him. He always wore a single sock on his hand.
Whenever a Chan practitioner arrived, he would hold it up and show it to them, saying, "I have worn this old monk’s sock for thirty years now. A temple monk once asked him jokingly:
"What is the Samādhi of Non-contention? The Master then struck him with his palm.
The Head Seat Qi Mi of Yangzhou was a native of that same prefecture; Si Xin called him a "thorough practitioner.
Although various scholars repeatedly invited him to renowned mountains, he would not go. Later, he manifested his passing at Gushan in Tan. His miraculous traces were numerous. His disciples once...
He had his portrait painted and requested a colophon for it. I wrote this: "This fellow, with his head turned to ash and face covered in dust, usually does not wish to reveal himself.
Now that he has been drawn out before people, it is much like shooting an arrow at empty space—how grievous, how regrettable! On a bolt of silk three feet long from the human world."
The Chan Master Zhìtōng Wéijǐu of Xīzhú Nunnery in Sūzhōu was also known as the "Hermitess of the Empty Chamber. She was the daughter of Fàn Xún, a Grand Councilor of the Longtú Academy.
Intelligent and wise from childhood, she grew up to marry Tí, the grandson of the Chancellor Sū Sòng. Not long after, she grew weary of worldly phenomena.

He returned home to request ordination, but his father disapproved. He subsequently devoted himself to pure cultivation and, upon contemplating the *Dharmadhātu-vipaśyanā*, attained sudden enlightenment.

He composed two successive verses to express his realization. The first says: "In the vast expanse of dust and defilement, the essence is suchness; Transverse and longitudinal, intermingling, they seal Vairocana.
The entire wave is water, yet the wave is not water; The entire water forms waves, yet water and waves are distinct. The second says: "Objects and self are fundamentally..."

There is no difference; the myriad phenomena of the universe are identical. Clearly and brilliantly, they transcend both the primary and the secondary; lucidly and thoroughly, they penetrate the true void.
A single essence contains manifold dharmas, interlacing within the Indra’s Net. In this place of infinite layers, movement and stillness are entirely perfect and pervasive.

Later, when his parents had both passed away, his elder brother Jian took up the post of Magistrate of Fening. Tong accompanied him on the journey. Hearing that the reputation of Sishi was great, he went to visit him. Sishi—
Seeing that he had attained realization, [Zhaozhou] asked, "Sadāprarudita Bodhisattva sold his heart and liver;
whom did he teach to study Prajñā? Tong said, "If you have no mind, I too shall rest. [Zhaozhou] asked again, "When nourished by a single rain, the roots and sprouts differ;
on ground where neither yin nor yang exists, what grows there? Tong said, "A flower with five petals. [Zhaozhou] asked further, "Throughout the twelve hours of the day..."
"Where shall you find a place to settle your body and establish your life? Tong replied, "Venerable Sir, spare your eyebrows; you have struck with a kind heart.
[The Master] said, "This woman is creating disorder. Tong bowed, and Xinyuan approved of him. Thereupon, his reputation for the Way became widespread.
During the Zhenghe era of Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty, he resided in Jinling. He once established a bathhouse at Baoning Temple and posted a notice on its gate that read: "One..."
Objects have no washing. What is this "a speck of dust"? If it arises, from where does it come? Speak a single phrase! Only then can you all enter the bath.
Guling only knew how to scrub backs; Kaishi had never clarified the mind.

When one wishes to realize the Stage of Freedom from Defilement, one must break into a sweat throughout the entire body. Everyone says that water can wash away dirt, but who knows that water [itself]...?
This, too, is a defilement. Even if the impurities of water are suddenly removed, one must still wash this away upon reaching such a state. Later, she became a nun with the name Weijiu.
She hung her monk’s staff at Xizhu in Gusu, where she received inquiries from lay and ordained practitioners day and night;

many attained the Way through her. Suddenly, manifesting illness, she wrote a verse and passed away while sitting in the lotus posture. Her *Mingxin lu* (Record of Illuminating the Mind) circulates in the world.
Chan Master Focin Benchai of Shangfeng in Tanzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Huanglong Qing.
He was the son of the Yao family of Fuzhou. Having received the tonsure in his youth, he received full ordination and traveled to study under various masters.
During the Dazhong era, he relied upon Haiyin Long and studied with the elder master Dadao, who was reading a sutra; they came across the passage: "A single hair..."
On the head of a lion, ten billion heads appear simultaneously. The Master pointed at it and asked, "How does a single head on a lion's mane come to manifest ten billion heads all at once?
Da replied, "You have only just entered the forest; how could you possibly fathom such a matter yet?

The Master was thus struck with doubt and subsequently resolved to cultivate his mind. He took up the post of *jingtou* (sanitation officer), and one night, while he was sweeping and cleaning, [he encountered the following...]

Yin arrived for the evening session; upon his arrival, he encountered the conclusion of the assembly. Throwing down his staff, [the Master] said, "When realized, even the tip of a hair swallows the vast ocean;
only then does one know that the great earth is but a single mote of dust. At these words, the Master attained a sudden awakening.

Later, when he departed from Min and traveled to Yuzhang to visit Huanglong Xin, their spiritual resonance did not harmonize. He then went to visit Lingyuan. Whenever he entered the inner quarters and emerged, he would invariably shed tears and reproach himself, saying: "This..."

"I have seen this matter very clearly; it is simply that when the moment arrives, I cannot bring myself to speak it. What can be done? Lingyuan, knowing the Master’s diligent devotion, told him that he must achieve a great penetration (*dàchè*) before he could attain mastery. Not long after, Lingyuan happened to observe a monk at the neighboring desk reading the *Extensive Record of the Caodong School*. It reached the passage where, upon returning from gathering firewood, Yaoshan was asked by a monk, "Where have you come from? Yaoshan replied, "I have come from carrying firewood. The monk asked, "What is the price of firewood these days? Yaoshan said, "Three cents per load. The monk asked, "Who will buy it? Yaoshan said, "If you don't buy it, I'll give it to you for free. The monk said, "I don't need it. Yaoshan said, "I don't want it either. At this point, the Master suddenly attained great enlightenment. He went to Lingyuan and said, "I have attained it. Lingyuan asked, "What have you attained? The Master replied, "The ten thousand phenomena are all within me. Lingyuan said, "How do you understand this? The Master said, "It is like a person with a hundred thousand pounds of gold walking through a marketplace. Lingyuan said, "You have attained the skin and flesh, but not yet the marrow. The Master said, "Please, Master, do not withhold the marrow from me. Lingyuan said, "If you wish to know the marrow, you must go to Mount Dongshan. The Master then went to Dongshan. One day, while sitting in meditation, he suddenly heard a dog bark and attained even greater realization. He returned to Lingyuan and said, "I have attained it.
