[Daowu] said, “I have come to investigate Chai. The monk pointed to the sword at his waist and asked, “What is this ‘míng bōbō’?
Daowu drew the sword and made a motion as if to strike. The Master suddenly became joyful; he slapped the monk on the table next to him with one palm, pulled back the curtain, and hurried out.

As he went, he spoke a verse impulsively: “Thorough! Thorough! The great ocean dries up, Space shatters apart. In the four directions and eight points there is no obstruction; Ten thousand [things]...”
The elephant-like forest of phenomena was simultaneously revealed; later, he shared his seat within the True Vehicle and emerged to respond to the highest honors.

Having moved repeatedly among famous monasteries, on the day he resided at Qianyuan, he ascended the hall and said: "The gates of hundreds of thousands of samādhis and the treasuries of immeasurable merit—when let go, they are like opening a military armory, with weapons scattered and reflecting light;
when held fast, they are like snow covering reeds, such that one cannot distinguish the whole body."
Those who see it must spring up and go; those who hear it must enter directly with a single blade. Each one possesses the true eye atop the head;
every person hangs the efficacious talisman behind the elbow. They sweep away the views and knowledge of Buddhas and Patriarchs, acting as a calamity and harm to the monastic groves.
I recall the day Bao-shou opened the hall: San-seng pushed forward a monk, and Bao-shou struck him. San-seng said, "With..."
How can one act for the sake of others? One would blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou!

Yet, as for my opening the hall today at Ganyuan, if any monk comes forward, I shall strike them as well. Not only will this story spread far and wide, but I also intend to open the eyes of the entire city of Fuzhou.
Why? Because "the sword leaves its precious scabbard because of injustice; medicine is used because of the need to save the sick."

Producing a Golden Pitcher. Entering the hall: Before Bodhidharma had yet come to this eastern land, everyone harbored the pearl from the Maitreya Pond, and every individual cradled the raw jade of Mount Jing.
This could truly be called standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
Yet, once the Second Patriarch had performed his three prostrations, each one went south to seek out friends and north to pay homage to Mañjuśrī. How unmanly! Or perhaps there was someone...
One and a half. Not seeking from the sages; not valuing one’s own spirit. A lone horse and a single spear, casting the blade into the void—how unimpeded and exhilarating!
Is there anyone like this today? "Since I have not returned, when I do return, I shall find it; who can compete for the misty scenery of the Five Lakes? Ascending the hall, he said:
"The proclamation of the Dharma-lineage is wondrous beyond words. A single phrase encompasses all; heaven..."
The Kun (Earth) contains and covers all; upright, it resembles the central eye of Śiva; vertically extended, it projects from the face like the three dots of the *triśūla*.
Horizontally, it encompasses the entire Dharma-realm. Then, striking his staff, he said: "If you can attain clarity beneath this very point, leaving the body may still be easy."

"Transcending the body, the Way is difficult to fathom. Again, striking the meditation staff, he said: "If you can realize it beneath the second dot, you will traverse back and forth beyond the three realms;
your hidden and manifest bodies will pervade the ten directions. Again, striking the staff, he said:

"If you can realize it beneath the third dot, the fish and dragons will lock their doors and the Buddhas and Patriarchs will conceal their tracks. Otherwise, let one move pass by, and there is, according to one's lot, a single branch of spring color."
The Third and Fourth Flowers. Entering the Hall: A single Dharma has form that encompasses all things moving and still; the hundred rivers rush and surge, competing to flow toward the source.
The Zao-琴 (zither) is not struck, and the heavens are serene and vast. One might imagine the old, ailing elder of Vaiśālī.
When Vimalakīrti is ill, then Shangfeng is ill; when Shangfeng is ill, then the staff is ill; when the staff is ill, then the myriad phenomena of the universe are ill. The myriad phenomena...
The myriad phenomena are ill; thus, both the ordinary and the sage are ill. Do you all perceive where the root of this illness arises?

If you do perceive it, then the sentient and the insentient are of one and the same substance, and every place is identical to the true Dharma-realm. Should this not yet be so, then as the saying goes:
"The sweet melon is sweet to its very stem; the bitter gourd is bitter to its very root."
Chan Master Tongzhao Defeng of Huanglong in Longxing Prefecture was the son of the Hu family of Jing’an in the commandery.

He was born with thick eyebrows. At the age of seventeen, he received the tonsure under Master Jin of Shanglan and subsequently went to rely upon Lingyuan. Upon hearing the profound meaning [of the teaching], he ascended the hall;
when the Master raised the dialogue concerning Jia Shan’s realm, the Master said: "Fayan merely has these words, yet he did not realize that Jia Shan..."
This old fellow was so lightly pressed by this monk that he was left with no place to stand, neither before nor behind.
Even if one does not interpret this as a "contextual statement" (jinghua), one cannot help but remain halfway there.
Chan Master Fajian Yingduan of Tanzhou was the son of the Xu family of Nanchang. In his youth, he relied upon Huayu’s Shanyue;

having shaved his head and received full ordination, he went to visit Zhenjing Wen. His faculties did not harmonize with Wen’s, so he proceeded to Yunju. There, he encountered Lingyuan, who was presiding as the seat-holder for the assembly and inspiring them with fervor.
The Master inquired into the essence of his teaching; however, he prided himself on his subtle mastery of the various sutras. Lingyuan once severely rebuked him for this. The Master...
He then cited the pivotal dialogues of Mazu and Baizhang, as well as the fundamental tenets of the Avatamsaka Sūtra, as his credentials.
Yunmen laughed and said, "Mazu and Baizhang were certainly mistaken; however, the tenets of the Avatamsaka have no connection whatsoever to this matter.

The Master was indignant and wished to leave, so he requested leave to depart. As he pulled back the curtain, he suddenly attained great enlightenment, and sweat poured down his back. Seeing this, Yunmen said, "Duan..."
"You recognize good and evil. Mazu and Baizhang—Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra—were nearly brought to ruin by you.
From this point on, his reputation spread in all directions, and though scholars vied with one another to entreat him to appear in the world, he declined them all.

Toward the end of the Zhenghe era, Grand Preceptor Zhang Sicheng insisted that Baizhang firmly appoint him to propagate the Dharma. Having no choice, the Master finally complied. He ascended the hall and, citing the Great...
The conversation ended as the fires of the kalpa of the Sui dynasty blazed forth. He then said: "The six realms of existence overturn and come crashing against my face;

for a moment I don a coarse hempen robe to mingle with the dust. That the wind fans the fire is but a trivial matter, yet it draws wandering travelers who refuse to turn back. Is it destroyed, or not?"

Whether following or not following, you merely take what you have heard and seen to force a needle or an awl [where there is none]. Thirty-six thousand acres of Taihu Lake—the moon in the heart of the waves—whom does it speak to?
A monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, "Wearing straw sandals and carrying a bamboo staff, one wanders through the red dust.
[The monk] asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Meeting the Patriarch at the crossroads. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
“What is the guest within the host? The Master said, “The golden whip that governs the horses mingles with the four classes of people.

“How is it the host within the host? The Master said, “At the golden gate, who would dare lift their eyes to look? “I have already received the Master’s instruction on guest and host; as for the supreme vehicle beyond this, what is it like?
The Master said, “Last night the frost wind scraped the earth with its cold; the old monkey on the ridge cried out until the last.”
Month.
Zen Master Shouzhuo Changling of Tiantong Monastery in Tokyo, a native of the Zhuang family of Quanzhou, ascended the hall and said:
"Among three thousand swordsmen, only Zhuang Zhou was permitted [to enter]. Why could he not leap out? When a skilled physician’s door is thronged with patients, for what reason?"

This does not require even a single note. For those who have already passed through the barrier, I ask you further to examine it with discernment. Entering the hall: It is like the faculty of the eye not seeing itself;
the nature of the eye is inherently equal. When there is no one to whom equality applies, then go thus: an iron hammer without a hole.
For the time being, let it rest. It is simply a matter of entering the forest without stirring the grass, or entering the water without disturbing the waves;

this is a provisional expedient for the duration of one’s life. If, however, the bamboo shoots within the fence emerge as sprouts outside the fence, and the flowers on the east side of the stream bloom as red as those on the west side—then wait until I have finished my investigation, and I shall strike you!
A monk asked: "When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, why did the temple master's eyebrows and beard fall off?"
[The monk] dropped [the whisk]. The Master said, "A cat can climb a tree. [The monk] said, "Had I known it would be thus earlier, I would never have let it be so.
The Master said, "Spare your eyebrows. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said, "The heavens are parched; I grieve for the people.

[The monk] asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said, "Not a hair's breadth, not a speck of dust. [The monk] asked, "And after he appeared in the world? The Master said, [the same].

The Master said, "Filling the ditches and blocking the ravines. [A monk] asked, "Between 'having emerged' and 'not yet having emerged,' how much difference is there? The Master said, "When a person is level, they do not speak;
when water is level, it does not flow. Ascending the hall, he said: "Leveling the high and conforming to the low invites thieves to ruin the house; cutting through iron and chopping off nails."
The fox is attached to its den; it is never like this. How should one act? Therefore it is said: "To personally let go at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff—one must be such a person.
As for holding the almsbowl in the Land of Fragrant Accumulation—how do you say it in a single phrase?
After a long silence, he said: "Be careful not to let the wind blow it into another tune. Ascending the hall, he said: "Śākyamuni’s closing his room was an offense that fills the heavens.
Vimalakīrti’s refusal to speak could not save himself. How is this? How is this? The gateway of the mouth is simply too small.

On the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month of the *guimao* year of the Song Xuanhe era, he suddenly manifested his passing into stillness. On the day of his cremation, Emperor Huizong dispatched an imperial messenger.
The envoy was granted incense. Holding a golden platter, he sought to obtain śarīra relics. When the burning of the incense was finished, there was a metallic clinking sound within the platter.
Upon examining it, he found several five-colored grains, each as large as a bean. The envoy carried them back; when the Emperor saw them, he was greatly delighted.
Chan Master Wuyin Zijing of Boshan in Xinzhou ascended the hall on the first day of the year and said: "A harmonious breath arises from withered stumps;
cold clouds disperse across the distant outskirts. The wooden man divines an auspicious omen; at midnight, the hexagram lines of the tortoise shell are revealed.

All you venerable Chan practitioners, where the tortoise’s lines are revealed, the patterns are already manifest. Thus one sees the twelve months of the year, month after month remaining thus; in a single day, there are twelve [hours]."
At that time, it is always thus, resembling itself from moment to moment. Upon reaching this point, it is exactly like the yellow of gold and the whiteness of white jade;
since the beginning of vast kalpas, it has never been of a different color. Do you see it?
If not yet, then for now let Zhang San follow the seasonal changes, and let Li Si’s hair turn grey and ragged.

Baizhang of Longxing Prefecture said that Qichan, a native of Xinghua, once ascended the hall and said: "When Kāśyapa Mātanga entered the Han and Bodhidharma came to the Liang, the tracks were already established;
yet the descendants of later generations open their eyes and lose their way. If you are one who is truly alert and discerning..."
In the end, one never picks flowers from the sky or grasps the moon in the waves; such efforts are but a waste of heart and mind—what purpose do they serve?
Today, I, this mountain monk, have already raised a heap of bones upon level ground. As you all walk along, each of you must look with full alertness.
Chan Master Guangxiao Dezhou was the son of the Qu family from Xinzhou. He received the tonsure at Zunseng Monastery in Jingde.
Having pursued the Way for many years, he later went to Huanglong. Upon hearing the teaching on the wall-gazing of Shaolin, he attained sudden enlightenment and composed two verses to present to him.
Huanglong approved them. After taking up residence there, he ascended the hall and said: "The whole body is revealed, majestic and grand; throughout the ten directions, there is no obstruction."
A thousand sages could not transmit it; ten thousand spirits hold it upon their crowns. If you wish to deliberate upon it together, open your mouth and it shatters into a hundred pieces.
But how is it before the mouth has even opened? *Pah!* Ascending the hall, he said: "Mutual accommodation or no mutual accommodation—look and there is nothing to be seen.
Having penetrated the barrier of the Patriarchs, one tramples the path of gods and men. A-he-he! Realization or no realization?"
"Where do the falling flowers and flowing waters go?
The temple attendant, Layman Dai Daochun, whose courtesy name is Fuzhong, questioned Lingyuan until one day he attained realization. He then presented this verse:
'In the realm of the total function at the bottom of the profound source, a single petal of the mind-flower reveals its imprinted patterns. I know this must have been so for many lifetimes.'"
He had once made offerings [to former Buddhas]. From time to time, he would smile, causing clouds of fragrance to stir.
Chan Master Tang Daozhen of Huanglong Mountain in Longxing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Letan Qing; he was the son of Zhao of Jinling. In his youth, he relied upon Jueyin.

Ying was a youth. He moved his residence to Puzhao Temple in Si. It happened that the Consort Shu was selecting candidates for ordination as novice monks (*śrāmaṇera*), and the Master obtained full ordination (*upasampadā*).
After some time, he took leave to visit Danxia Chun. One day, while discussing the fundamental tenets of the Dongshan school, the Master presented this verse:
"White clouds deeply shroud the ancient, cold cliff; Strange grasses and numinous flowers are carried by the colored phoenix. At midnight, the sun rises in the sky."

At noon, he was riding a cow with his back turned, wearing boots and a shirt. Chūn (Huangbo) esteemed him; the Master himself considered it an obstacle and abandoned him to rely on Caotang. Upon meeting him, they were immediately in accord.
One evening, hearing the drum for the late assembly, he stepped out from the sutra hall and looked up at the moon; thereupon, he attained great enlightenment.
He hurried to the abbot’s quarters, where Caotang saw him from afar and immediately granted him formal certification (*inka*). He first resided at Caoshan, and subsequently moved to Guang.
Shou Huanglong ascended the hall and said: "I cite an ancient precedent to question you, kalyāṇamitras.
You must not interpret it according to antiquity; if you do so, you lose the eye right before your face. I cite a present-day precedent to question you, kalyāṇamitras."
"Ācārya, you must not engage in this present convention. If you engage in this present convention, it will obstruct your original eye.
Even if you do not lose it or obstruct it, being neither ancient nor modern, it is still merely the mutual treatment of medicine and illness—a teaching for silencing a child’s crying.
As for that single phrase of transcendence, can you say it, Ācārya? If you cannot say it, wait until you reach Luohan Peak."
[The Master] nodded his head and said, "I shall tell you. He ascended the hall. Sitting in cold seclusion at Shaolin, the disciples each propounded divergent views;
it was much like a group of blind men feeling an elephant. When Shen Guang performed three prostrations and stood in his place, Bodhidharma said, "You have obtained my marrow.
This dark-faced Brahmin has not even touched the ground with his heels. [The Master] ascended the hall. A stone man asked:
A withered stump. When will you blossom? A withered stump and an angry stone man—how can they chatter away?
The stone man laughs aloud; the withered stump emits wondrous blossoms. Red clouds illuminate the jade elephant; white jade grinds against golden sand.
I ask the master who has penetrated the profound: who is it that does not arrive home?
Chan Master Fayi Xuechao of Wanan in Taizhou was the great-great-grandson of Li Yonghe, the Grand Preceptor and Duke of Xiangyang.

His family had resided for generations in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng. When his mother dreamed of an elderly monk arriving, she gave birth to him. At the age of seventeen, he sat for the imperial examinations at the Upper School (Shangxiang) and passed.
His paternal great-uncle held office in Huainan and wished to appoint him to an official post, but he declined. He was about to renounce worldly affairs and become a monk.
Cijue’s maternal grandfather, Ci, disapproved. His mother said, "This child must have been a śramaṇa in a previous life; I pray you do not thwart his resolve.

Not long after, Cijue passed away. In the first year of the Daoguan era of Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty, he visited Lingyan Temple to take the vow, shaved his head, and received full ordination.
In accordance with his vow, he remained for ten years, yet he was bewildered and unable to enter [the state of realization]. He visited Yuanwu at Jiangshan;

when Yuanwu was summoned by imperial decree to move to Tianning in the capital, the Master accompanied him in his service. During the Jingkang era, he sought out Caotang at Shushan, and upon hearing a single word regarding the Great Dharma, he attained sudden enlightenment.
In the Ding-si year of the Shaoxing era of Emperor Gaozong, Liu Yanxiu, the Governor of Quan, invited him to reside at Yanfu. Four years later...

Moving to the great monastery, he ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "This staff, at times, acts as a dragon emerging from the water, with clouds and mist stretching unbroken for ten thousand miles.
At times, it acts as a lion crouching on the ground, causing all manner of century-old monsters to vanish their tracks.
At times, mind and phenomena are both forgotten, and it stands alone, illuminating its own essence. At times, illumination and function occur simultaneously, with host and guest interacting freely."
He struck the ground with his staff and said: "Under the Gate of Yanfu, nothing at all is employed. Tell me, what does Yanfu usually use?
He planted the staff in the ground, gave a shout, and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "Looking up, one does not see the sky; looking down, one does not see the earth.
Before the ancient sword and the skull, the great ocean’s waves boil. [He] retired from Changlu and returned to Tiantai.
At Wanyuan Guanyin Monastery, [Dongshan] suddenly manifested a slight illness. He wrote a verse, saying: "This year I am seventy-five; returning, I shall become the master of this hermitage.
Be careful, Avalokiteśvara! A clay snake swallows a stone tiger. He sat cross-legged in his coffin and passed away.
Chan Master Dongshan Huikong of Xuefeng in Fuzhou was the son of the Chen family of that prefecture.

At fourteen, he shaved his head and immediately traveled to various regions, visiting many veteran masters. In his later years, he attained realization at Caotang. This was in the Guiyou year of the Shaoxing era of Emperor Gaozong of the Song dynasty.
On the day Kaifang Xuefeng accepted his invitation, he ascended the hall and said: "Those who are quick-witted are enlightened by a single word and immediately set off;
those who are dull and obtuse cannot be moved even by being pushed and pulled. When they set off, everyone rejoices; when they do not move, everyone feels resentment.
I, this mountain monk, shall now turn this dullness into a swift departure. He snapped his fingers once and said, "All that was previously pushed and pulled!"
He did not appear before, yet he appears now. Previously he did not dwell in a monastery, yet he dwells in one now. Previously he detested being a Buddha and would not be one;

now he is one. Previously he detested the Dharma and would not preach it; now he preaches it. Setting aside for a moment the questions of appearing or not appearing, dwelling or not dwelling, I dare ask you all:
what kind of Buddha is it that he has become? Is it Vairocana (Empty King) Buddha? Is it Dīpaṃkara Buddha? Is it Śākyamuni?
"Is it Kāśyapa Buddha? Is it Maitreya Buddha? What dharma is this that you speak? Is it the fundamental dharma? Is it the dharma of non-arising?
Is it a worldly dharma? Is it a supramundane dharma? Is there anyone in this assembly who can realize it?
If you can, my work in appearing in the world is finished. If not, do not misrepresent it when you meet people. [He] gave a shout.
"Ho! [The Master] descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he raised the case: Yunmen once addressed the assembly, saying, "This very thing brings suffering upon people.
The Master said: "Yunmen’s usual bearing was like that of a king; yet to speak in such a way is much like a poor man lamenting that he has too many bodies.
This mountain monk is not so: this very thing brings joy to people. Why? Because only when the heavy rain has ended does one return to the shelter of the roof."
Sitting inside. Blown by the winds of karma, it circles back around the mountain. Even so, this is like a beggar seeing small profit.
Furthermore, regarding the phrase "not harming the principle of things," how would you say it? Ascending the hall, he said: With one punch, I knock down Yellow Crane Tower;
With one kick, I overturn Parrot Isle. When there is spirit, add more spirit; Even where there is no elegance, [there is still spirit].
How elegant! How brilliant! What joy! What joy! He is just like a nineteen-year-old imperial scholar.
Who cares for heaven? Who cares for earth? When the sovereign mind does not stir falsely, the six realms are simultaneously penetrated.
Lay aside the three-foot sword; cease playing with the bow. Free and easy, free and easy—just like a seventeen- or eighteen-year-old.
Ten old men acting as ministers is like this: the wind blows in season, the rain falls in season, the five grains flourish, and the myriad people are at peace.
[The Master] raises his staff and says: "O Great Assembly! These two, together with my own staff, can be made into one.
When a monk arrives at the gate of Xuefeng, he simply knows to follow the custom and eat his fill; he may even obtain three coins for it."
[The Master] held up his straw sandals, gave a shout, struck the ground with his staff, and descended from the seat. A monk asked, "What was it like before the Master had seen Caotang?
The Master said, "It is present in Jiangnan. The monk asked, "What is it like after having seen him? The Master said, "It is absent in Jiangbei."
Chan Master Yetao Puchong of Yuwang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of that same region. Addressing the assembly, he raised the case of Ba Ling, who said:
"It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving. If it is neither the wind nor the banner, where else can one place it?
If anyone were to come forward to speak on behalf of the Patriarch and meet with Ba Ling, Xuedou would say: "The wind moves, the banner moves. Since...
"This wind and banner—where else could they be placed? Someone came forward to speak on behalf of Baling, meeting with Xuedou.
The Master said: "Neither wind nor banner, there is nowhere to place them; it is the banner and it is the wind, yet there is no place for attachment.
The soaring falcon in the vast heavens loses its tracks; the golden-haired lion crouching on the ground is likewise disoriented. A-he-he! Whether you awaken or not, this is the command.
A Great Turning of Mind: A Parting Verse for Sanlang. "A single thread of line, fishing alone in the cold river rain.

A monk asked Chan Master Huan of Liangshan in Tanzhou, a successor of Chan Master Xinxin of Qingyuan: "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; we pray that the Master will grant us an instruction. The Master said: "Furthermore..."
"In stillness, one knows not where the clouds have gone; because the ground is cold, the snow remains for a long time. The student said, "I do not yet understand the fundamental words;
I beg the Master to grant me another expedient means. The Master said, "Behind one mountain range, there is another person."
Chan Master Ximing of Zhengfa Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture was a native of Hanzhou. On the occasion of the lifting of the retreat restrictions, he ascended the hall and said:
"Leaves fall in profusion from the forest; heaven and earth announce the early autumn. This is clearly the intent of the Western Patriarch; what need is there for further seeking?

If you can understand it in this way, you will finally believe that the Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is fundamentally level and even, and that the Great Gate of Liberation has never had a lock or key. Mii...
It permeates the universe and fills the void; its measure is inexhaustible and its wisdom unfathomable.

If one has not yet clarified this principle and does not understand its source, then even if one cultivates merit for a hundred kalpas and refines one’s conduct through a thousand lifetimes, it will be nothing but self-exhausting toil, with no connection whatsoever [to the ultimate truth].

If one deeply clarifies this principle and penetrates its source, one will then realize that all movement and stillness, as well as every action and practice, [are but manifestations of this single essence].

Whether sitting or reclining, every movement accords with the Way; every thought aspires toward the source. Did not the Patriarch say: "Delusion gives rise to stillness and turmoil; awakening is free from likes and dislikes.
Let gain and loss, right and wrong, be cast off all at once. If this is so, who is deluded and who is awakened? Who is right and who is wrong?

It is simply that you people alone give rise to divergent views—observing the great and the small, clinging to existence and clinging to non-existence, while your own spiritual luminosity remains solitary.

The radiance refuses to be accepted; the solitary fullness of the moon in the mind naturally gives rise to opposition. How is this different from abandoning one’s father within the home or forgetting the pearl within one’s clothing?
It causes thorns to form a forest upon the path to Bodhi, and misty clouds to obscure the sun in the sky of liberation.

Fortunately, on this day, I, this mountain monk, encounter the *pravāraṇā* ceremony of the assembly of monks, as the fundraising master returns to the mountain, and all you virtuous ones have attained...
I have received Guang’s inquiry. It would be improper to remain silent; thus, I shall engage in some trivial discourse according to my capacity, providing a provisional expedient for these times.

You must all open your eyes and observe closely for yourselves. If you further intend to deliberate or seek through conceptual thought, it will not merely be a matter of ten thousand miles of white clouds.
The Abbot of Zu’an on Mount Nanyue in Hengzhou was a successor of Qingyuan. He built a hut among the peaks of Mount Heng and lived there for over thirty years without anyone knowing of him.
One day, in a moment of inspiration, he composed a verse: "A small pot boils vegetables while rice steams above; The vegetables are cooked and the rice fragrant, yet people are still hungry.
Once this hunger-wound is healed, there is nothing more to do; Tomorrow morning, I shall paint a cat exactly as it was. Thus it is said.
This patch-robed monk braved the brambles to seek him out. Lord Zhang Wujin exerted great effort to persuade him to open a Dharma center, but he did not comply;
he ultimately passed away on this very mountain.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Jia Shan Chun.
Chan Master Qianming Puchu of Qingshan in Lizhou ascended the hall to proclaim the essential tenets of our school and offer prayers for the imperial foundation.
He prayed: "May auspicious clouds and the celestial star appear together; may the spring of nectar and the sweet dew manifest as one.

May the sovereign be a ruler like Yao and Shun, and the common people enjoy an era like that of Cheng and Kang, so that even this rustic hermit in the mountain woods may unconsciously compose a song of great peace. Furthermore—

"What is this 'Song of Great Peace'? He acts without acting; he transforms through the divine. He pours down the rain of virtue in profusion and stirs the breeze of benevolence to bring about harmony and prosperity.
The people are like wild deer; the ruler is like the branches of a tree. Do you eighteen disciples know it or not? *Liri liri*.
(He claps his hands once and descends from the seat.)

Chan Master Xiuyu Xianjing of Shengyin Monastery in Chu Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Letan Qian. He was the son of the Gao family of that same prefecture. Once, he ascended the hall and said:

"Though you have traveled all over the world, you should know that not a single step has ever been moved. Though you have passed through every gate and courtyard, there is no household where the hearth lacks smoke."
Therefore, with staff over shoulder and sandals on feet, he walks according to his inspiration; casting his line into the deep waters, he dwells according to his nature.
It is not because the lands of his hometown are good; wherever the conditions ripen, there he makes his home. Today, he takes whatever comes to hand; how often has he calculated this before?
He does not depart from the old patterns, yet every time it is raised, it is new. To those with clear eyes—
At the mere glance, he turned back. For those who have not yet awakened, recognize this very face. Now tell me: what is your original face? After a long silence, he said:
"The flowers bloom on the front stage, yet they are seen from behind; the bell tolls in the upper realm, yet it is heard below.

He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he raised the topic: "When the World-Honored One was in the kingdom of Magadha, he preached the Dharma for the assembly."

At that time, as the summer retreat was about to begin, he said to Ānanda: "The great disciples and the fourfold assembly of devas and humans have never shown reverence or respect as I constantly preached the Dharma.
Now I shall enter the *iṃśa*-mortar chamber and sit for the ninety-day summer retreat.
If anyone should come to ask about the Dharma at that time, you must speak on my behalf: 'All dharmas are unarisen; all dharmas...'"

"It shall not perish. Having finished speaking, he closed his room and sat down. The Master summoned the assembly and said, "When Śākyamuni first attained the Way of Buddhahood, for the most part he had no choice in the matter.
Hardly had he established this community when he already gave rise to thoughts of weariness and retreat."

If Shengyin had seen [the situation] at that time, he would have driven a nail through the door of the room to ensure that for the rest of his life there would be no way out, so as to spare future generations from following one another’s example. As it is said:

"If one does not transmit the Dharma to deliver sentient beings, one cannot be called a repayer of gratitude. [The Master] strikes the whisk and descends from the seat. Later, he dwelt in seclusion at Lianyi.
Tianning manifested a slight illness and wrote a verse, saying: "The shadow-play has been performed; seventy-one years have passed.
If you ask further how it is, I shall return to play another round. He set down his brush and passed away.
Chan Master Longya Zongmi of Tanzhou was a native of Yuzhang. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Do not speak in your sleep.
The monk asked, "What are all dharmas? The Master said, "Already fallen into the secondary. He ascended the hall.

When the assembly had gathered and settled, the Master said, "It is already a perfect whole; there is no need for carving or polishing. Return to your quarters and drink tea. He ascended the hall again.
Do not compare the flowers in the courtyard to this body; though the courtyard flowers fall, they meet spring again. But once this body has passed away, who knows where it will go?
The vast expanse of the triple world is enough to make one’s heart sink with sorrow.
Chan Master Zu Jian Congmi of Dongchan Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of Tingzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "Opening one's mouth is not Chan;
closing one's mouth is not the Way. If you step forward with the intent to advance, your whole body will fall into the wild weeds."

Chan Master Putong Jiao of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture was the son of the Bi family from Wanling in the same prefecture. From childhood, he was exceptionally intelligent and attained ordination before his twentieth year.
He went to Nanping to study the teachings of the Tiantai school and subsequently performed repentance rituals (*sānmó*) for lay patrons. Someone once asked him:
"Regarding the repentance you perform, is the sin you repent for your own, or is it for another? If it is for your own sin, from where does the nature of that sin arise?"

When he attempted to repent for another’s offenses, [Zhaozhou] said, "That person's offense is not yours; how can you repent for it? The Master was unable to respond and subsequently changed his robes to travel as a wandering monk.
He went to Lestam (Lengyan). As soon as his foot touched the threshold, Lestan scolded him. When the Master was about to ask a question, Lestan immediately drove him out with his staff.
One day, Lestan suddenly called the Master to his quarters and said, "I have a public case (gong'an) from an ancient master that I wish to discuss with you."
As the Master was about to offer a word in response, Xuedou Tan suddenly shouted. The Master attained sudden enlightenment and broke into a great laugh.
Tan descended from his rope seat, took the Master’s hand, and asked, “Do you understand the Buddha-dharma? The Master then shouted and pushed him away. Tan laughed heartily.

Thereupon, his fame spread in all directions, and students revered and looked up to him as their master. Later, he returned to his hometown and stayed at Tiantong, where he remained in seclusion behind closed doors, withdrawing from all worldly affairs.

In the eighth year, as the seat at the monastery happened to be vacant, the local officials ordered the Master to expound the Dharma. Fearing he might flee, they dispatched an officer to wait for him on the road;

thus, he could not decline the invitation by force. On the day he accepted the request, he ascended the hall and said: "Alas! Old Man of the Yellow Face, you have entrusted the Buddha-Dharma to kings and ministers.
This dispassionate guest beneath the forest trees is being driven to his death by official summons. Is there no one with a mind that knows the bottom [of things] who can save me from this?"
"Ma! If there were none, one could not avoid taking a wrong for right. [The Master] then descended from his seat. Whenever a monk approached, the Master would invariably shout:
"When you had not yet taken up the staff, I already explained it for you. But tell me, what did I explain? Waving a hand, washing a bowl; picking up a fan, drawing a bow;
Zhaozhou’s 'cypress tree,' and Lingyun’s seeing the peach blossoms—put all of these aside for now!"
This mountain monk has no such idle lips with which to entangle you in sophistry. Why not simply rest? [He] took up his staff and drove them away.

On the twentieth day of the third month in the Jiachen year of the Xuanhe era of Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty, he bathed, ascended the hall, and spoke this verse before passing away in tranquility.
The verse says: The jeweled staff strikes the void; everywhere there is spring. The message within this is particularly...
Encompassing all. Last night the wind stirred; the cold crags were chill. A clay ox was startled awake to plow the white clouds.
He was seventy-seven years of age and fifty-eight years since his ordination.
Chan Master Daomin of Yuantong in Jiangzhou was popularly known as an ancient Buddha. He was the son of the Cai family of Xinghua; his mother...
He dreamed that he had swallowed a *maṇi* jewel. Consequently, he became pregnant; when he was born at five years of age, his feet would not touch the ground and his mouth would not speak.

His mother carried him while visiting Ximing Temple; upon seeing a Buddha image, he suddenly stepped onto the floor, pressed his palms together, and recited "Namo Buddha," then performed a prostration.

People marveled greatly at this. Later, when he went to study in Daliang, he took refuge under Dexiang of Jingde Temple and left the household life. He passed the scriptural examination and received ordination. He traveled everywhere...
He went to visit various masters, all of whom he touched upon; he stayed with Master Zhè of Mount Huì for the longest time. Later, he admired Lètán and went to pay him a visit.

Upon seeing him, Lètán silently recognized his potential as a vessel. The Master recounted the insights he had gained from his successive visits to other teachers, but he did not receive certification.

Lètán then raised the question concerning the World-Honored One holding up a flower and Kāśyapa’s smile. Again, the Master failed to reach accord. Afterwards, while attending Lètán during a walk, Lètán rested his staff upon his shoulder.

He sighed deeply and said, "Do you understand? As the Master was about to respond, Tanzhou struck him. After a short while, Tanzhou again held up a blade of grass and showed it to him, asking, "What is this?
The Master was again about to respond when Tanzhou let out a shout. Thereupon, the Master suddenly and fully realized the Great Dharma.
He made the gesture of holding a flower and said, "This time, I cannot deceive Upāsaka Min. Tanzhou pulled him by the sleeve and said, "Speak more! Speak more! The Master replied, "The South..."

Clouds rose from the mountains; it rained on the northern peaks. [Daowu] immediately prostrated himself, and Tanyou nodded in approval. Later, he opened the Dharma at Guanjing (Guanxi) and subsequently resided at Yuan Tong, in accordance with the prediction of Daoyi.
Students flocked to him in great numbers. The imperial court bestowed upon him the ceremonial robes and the title "Yuanji" (Perfect Mechanism).
He ascended the hall and said: "When the Buddhas appear in the world, they have no dharma to give to others; they do nothing but pull out nails and extract wedges."
To sever doubt and eliminate delusions, those who study the Way must not deceive themselves.
If there is even a single doubt the size of a mustard seed, [the Master] gives a shout and says: "What is this? Do not prick your head and enter the glue pot!"
The Abbot Zhihe of Níngyuánfǔ’s Èlíng Hermitage was the son of the Zhang family of Yùfēng on Sūtái. As a child, he once practiced seated meditation while suspended from the eaves of a hall;
when the hall collapsed, his parents thought he must have perished, yet the Master remained with eyes closed, as if nothing had happened. Consequently, they allowed him to leave the household life.
Having reached the age for full ordination, he went to visit Letan. Upon seeing him, Letan asked, "What are you doing?

As the Master was about to answer, Letan struck him and shouted, "What do you call this 'Chan'? The Master suddenly grasped the essential meaning and immediately said, "Chan has no before and no after;
the waves settle in the great ocean, and the moon is reflected in the blue sky. Letan further asked, "What is the Way? The Master replied, "The Way is within the dust of the mundane world."
Vast and expansive! It requires no contrivance; fundamentally, there is nothing lacking. It is profoundly still. Next, he visited Bian of Mount Heng, who held him in particularly high esteem.
During the Yuánfú era, he settled at Zhōngfēng and Qīyún, two hermitages at Xuědòu, remaining for over twenty years.
He once composed a verse that says: "Two or three sheng of wild water from the bamboo pipes, Five or seven fragments of idle clouds at the pine-window. The wayfarer lives..."
The account is roughly as follows. It was left for people of the world to see and hear. Many who were intent on the Way went to visit him.
When a monk came for an audience, the Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "Tiantong. The Master said, "How high is Mount Taibai?"
The monk struck his forehead with his hand and made a gesture of looking upward. The Master said, "There is still this remaining. The monk said, "Then please let the Hermitage Master speak.

The Master then made the same gesture of striking his forehead. The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him. At first, when the Master was together with Tiantong, they exchanged questions and established a spiritual covenant, saying:
"In days to come, the two of us should occupy the solitary peaks and highest summits, gazing at the Milky Way, for..."
A man beyond the world, he would not, for the sake of a reputation with the government in these times, stoop to humble himself before others.
Later, when his covenant was violated, the Master ultimately refused to receive Chen Zhengyan. Chen Zhengyan had used stratagems to entice the Master out of the mountains to reside at Er-ling;
for thirty years, he lived there without any possessions beyond his basic needs, save for two tigers that attended him on his right. One day, Wei...

To those people, he dismissed them with verses. On the twelfth day of the fourth month in the Yisi year of the Xuanhe era of Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty, he passed away while sitting in the lotus posture.
Zhengyan compiled a formal account of the Master’s life and deeds, detailing his final illness and extraordinary manifestations with great precision; furthermore, a statue of him was fashioned.
Two tigers attend him; they remain there to this day.
Chan Master Xinghua Ke of Tianwang Monastery in Xi [County], Luzhou, ascended the hall and said: "The true source is profound and still, utterly devoid of arising and ceasing.
Even if a thousand sages were to emerge, it would be difficult for them to find a seam or a crack. He raises clouds and spews mist, pervading the rivers and mountains."
The sands [of the Ganges] have their horizontal and vertical alignments; their wondrous response is beyond doubt. Holding fast or letting go, they are freely deployed as one pleases.
They give rise to the eyes and eyebrows of humanity and heaven, expanding the mind-source of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. All dharmas are manifest before one; there is nothing lacking or deficient.

As it is said: "Every person is fully endowed; each individual is perfectly accomplished. Without using even a hair’s breadth of mental effort, one naturally stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. (He lets out a shout.)
Chan Master Changsha Daowu Chufang ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The former Daowu said, 'I will not speak of life;
I will not speak of death. Why do you, Master, speak of it today? The Master said, "Words cannot admit a needle, yet private paths allow for carriages and horses.
The monk said, "Truly, the waters at Lestam are no different; the pure breeze is distinct from the ordinary. The Master said, "Indeed."
A nimble monk, having realized one point and understood two, said: "Everyone, throughout the twelve periods of the day, do not err in your application of mind!
Above your head is heaven; beneath your feet is earth. Dawn brings clarity and dusk brings darkness; the waters are green and the mountains are blue.

All phenomena are distinct and manifest, from antiquity to the present. To simply accept things as they are in this way is already to create trouble where there is none; how much more so to speak further words?"
Seeking the source within the midst and searching for the subtle within the phrases is precisely to bury oneself. "O Great Assembly, it would be better to return to the hall and go drink tea.
Chan Master Xu of Xuefeng in Fuzhou was the son of Chen of Putian. After he attained the Dharma, he lived in seclusion at the southern side of Heyan.
Hu was diligent in tilling his fields to provide for himself. The district magistrate, Chen Juemin, invited him to Mount Gu; he subsequently resided at Xuefeng.
Later, withdrawing from the community, he built a hermitage at Shimen and composed songs to express his resolve. His lyrics were elegant and refined, containing such lines as:

"Clad in clouds and entering the weeds, I do not shrink from toil; meeting people, I shatter their sanctuaries of cultivation. These verses were widely circulated. Initially, the scholar-official Chen Yizai...
In the capital, he called upon Qianshi and asked about the venerable elders of his native region, inquiring who was worthy of his devotion.
Qian said, "If you return home and see Xu, that will suffice. Thereupon, he returned home and went into seclusion with the Master at Shimen.
Chan Master Cishi Ruixian of Shaoxing Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Kaixian Ying.
A native of his own prefecture, he left home at the age of twenty and received the tonsure upon passing the scriptural examinations.
He studied the *vinaya*, yet upon realizing that the nature of the precepts is like empty space and that those who cling to them are deluded, the Master [Ruixian] declared: "As for the precepts..."

This is the method for binding the body. Why bind oneself? Thereupon, he delved into the teachings of the Platform [Sutra] and read: "All dharmas are not born of themselves, nor are they born from another;
they are not born from both together, nor without cause. Therefore, it is said they are unarisen. He then had a doubt, asking:

"If they are neither from self nor from another, neither from both together nor without cause, then ultimately from where do they arise? He immediately realized: "They are produced by causes and conditions."
The three contemplations of emptiness, conventionality, and the middle suppress and elevate the ocean of nature. Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings differ in name but are identical in essence.
Through the ten objects and ten vehicles, consciousness is transformed into wisdom. The inconceivable realm is clarified only through the illumination of wisdom;

it is beyond the reach of verbal explanation. He traveled to various regions and later arrived at Touzi Shengjian. When asked where he was from, the Master replied, "From Dongyue in the two provinces of Zhejiang. Shengjian said, "Dong..."
"What about the matter of transcending? The Master said, "The Qinwang Peak is high; the Jiandao Lake is wide.
Guizhan asked, "Is the Qinwang Peak the same as yourself, or is it different? The Master said, "Sanskrit in the Western Heaven; Chinese in this land. Guizhan said, [and the Master remained silent].
"This is still a matter of confronting the thicket [of karmic obstacles]. Ultimately, are they the same or different? The Master then shouted; Jiàn struck him.
The Master said, "The kindness is so great it is difficult to repay," and then he bowed. Later, upon returning to his native village, he established the Dharma at Císhì.
In his room, he once asked a monk: "Three bags gallop on two feet; traveling ten thousand li a day, one cannot catch up. Now they are gathered within the jade..."
Quanshan did not permit people of his time to make arbitrary judgments. Where, then, would you all go to meet the Venerable Xian?
Chan Master Haiming of Daomiao in Tanzhou was a youth who studied under the same teacher as Xiaonan; they were about to travel abroad together.
While serving as the abbot, he dreamed of two large black snakes, each with a single horn and several *zhang* in length, which coiled three times around the monastery before leaping away.

At dawn, as the Master was about to depart, the dreamer said, "These two must be the 'dragons and elephants' of the Dharma gate. Later, after [the Master] had taken up residence, he ascended the hall and said:
"Dancing atop the lanterns, hiding within the pillar; the spirit Shen Efa is provoked, and the slave Kunlun is born."
[The Master] grew angry and gave a shout, saying: "A single phrase that fits the head [of the matter] leads to ten thousand kalpas of falling into the ford of delusion.
Zen Master Riyi Liaowei of Jingguang Monastery in Wenzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Yuantong Xian, was asked by a monk: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said, "One night’s journey, two nights’ journey; a thousand mountains, ten thousand mountains, all under the moon. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "In the morning look to the southeast; in the evening look to the northwest. The monk asked, "Is there anything further beyond this?

The Master said, "A person's heart is difficult to satisfy; a mountain stream and ravine are easy to fill. [The monk] asked, "I do not ask about the circumstances of the time and season; what is the story of Huichao? The Master said, "It is like..."
"What? the Master asked. "The Persian draws his bow and his face turns black," [the student] said. "What is the meaning of this? the Master asked.
"It pierces through the skull; the laughter does not cease. "I am asking with sincere intent," [the student] said. "In the Yellow Springs there are no inns;
tonight, in whose house shall one lodge? the Master replied.
Master Mingzhao Wenhui of Jinhua Wuyi ascended the hall and, as he was about to dismiss the assembly, said: "To disperse like this would already be to fall into the seventh or eighth rank.
Out of consideration for those of beginner's mind, I cannot help but speak of this repeatedly. Today is the fifth day of the fifth month;
for all of you, I shall cite the phrase that exists before one’s parents were born. Its radiance is brilliant and majestic, illuminating heaven and earth—and yet, it is still nothing."
Now there is no past either; the Buddhas of the three periods have merely applied provisional measures, and the patriarchs of the six generations have done nothing but point and direct.
Kāśyapa on the dais vainly raises his fist, and the Vajra-wielder outside the gate stands with shoulders thrust out. Then, clapping his hands, he laughs loudly and says: [The text ends here.]
"What laughter! What laughter? A lantern enters a pillar.

Chan Master Xuedou Chi of Qingyuan Prefecture, a descendant of Chan Master Xiangtian Qing, was born into the Lu clan of the local region. A monk asked: "On the Mid-Autumn Festival, the moon is not seen."
"How is it now? The Master said, "Wait until the night is deep to see. [The monk] asked, "What if black clouds have not yet dispersed?
How then? The Master said, "How can you blame the old monk? He ascended the hall and said: "To realize the mind is easy; to rest the mind is difficult.
When the source of the mind is rested, one is at ease wherever one goes. The constellations shift and the heavens break toward dawn; the white clouds still cover the green mountains."
Master Yì of Shífó in Shàoxīng Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to all under heaven; when a single speck of dust rises, the great earth is gathered up;
when one dharma is penetrated, the myriad dharmas are encompassed. But tell me, which dharma is it that is penetrated?
He then gave a shout and said, "Be careful not to mistake the donkey’s saddle bridge for your father’s jaw! Thereupon he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Daowan of Shouning Temple in Yingcheng, Anzhou, successor to Chan Master Baqin Rui. A monk asked, "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger.
I wonder, from what does the Master emerge? The Master said, "Drawing a single stroke in the void. The monk said, "How extraordinary! The Master [replied], "..."
[The monk] said, "The Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot lift it up; I ask, within the lands of the ten directions, there is only the Single Vehicle Dharma (Ekayāna).
What is this Single Vehicle Dharma? The Master said, "It cannot be exhausted even when measured by bushels.

[The monk] said, "If that is so, then moving one's countenance reveals the ancient road, and one does not fall into the silent mechanism. The Master said, "What is the silent mechanism? The monk raised his head and looked. The Master—
[The Master] raised his whisk. A monk let out a shout. The Master said, "How very quiet and still! Ascending the hall for a discourse, [the Master said]:
"The ancients saw this moon; people today see this moon. This moon remains forever constant; yet, are the ancients and those of today not different?
If a person’s mind were like the moon, its light would be bright and pure within the azure depths. This must certainly be the source of the mind. This teaching cannot be further explained. Tsk!"
The Hall Master said: "O virtuous practitioners of Zen, the three months of winter are coming to an end, and the thirtieth night of the twelfth lunar month is approaching.
How will you withstand it? After a long silence, he said: "Clothes worn through reveal the bare bones; the roof broken, one sleeps gazing at the stars."

Compiled by the Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple in the Capital, the Monk (Chao Yong).
Verified and presented for the Rinzai School by the Abbot (Subject-Monk) Chōkei of Kokaigan-ji Temple, Kyoto.

Chan Master Shuchan Liaochang of Fuzhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Doushuai Yue of the fourteenth generation under Nanyue, was asked by a monk: "What is the phrase by which Shuchan acts for others? The Master said:
He said: "The jade ruler in my breast has not yet been lightly cast; the golden hammer in my sleeve comes crashing down upon the face.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Casually let it go, and even the Buddha’s hand cannot cover it. Deliberately drawing it back, the great earth is utterly free of even a speck of dust.

I tell you: do not doubt or speculate. Everywhere, at every turn, one sees Sudhana. When the hammer falls with clarity, it is as if the essential meaning has been attained—how many weary lives are spared!"
His eyes opened naturally.
Chan Master Huizhao of Doushuai in Longxing Prefecture was the son of the Guo family of Nan’an. He ascended the hall and said: "Below Mount Long’an, the roads crisscross;
within the palace of Doushuai, the pavilions are layered upon one another. Though it is not the world, it is no other than the human realm."

Upon arrival, the mind is at peace; all discursive thoughts are utterly forgotten. As for "skillful walking," one does not shift the two feet; as for "skillfully entering," one does not move the double doors.
One can naturally laugh and smile; who cares about the misty vines? Sitting here, one lets the years and months pass away. Since it is thus, tell me: how would you say it?
"Is there anything further above? After a long silence, he said: "Do not let it be pushed down by the rocks at the edge of the cliff;

break through the clouds below that screen the sun. Ascending the hall, he held up his whisk and said: "On the Dragon Boat Festival, Longan also paddles the boat. Amidst the clouds of the green mountains, one finds carefree ease.
Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty is infinite joy; who would love to compete for the first place and seize the silken banner? He then set it aside.
Rowing a boat upon heaven and earth; waves rise from the peak of the high mountains. Striking the jade drum clearly, unfurling the iron banner in secret.
A cup of calamus tea, a few sugar-filled zong dumplings. Let us move north to Uttarakuru to compete for the forehead-mark with Jambudvīpa in the south.
(He strikes the meditation seat and descends. Entering the hall: Tuṣita has no skill at all.
Following the examples of various quarters, he ascends the hall once every five days to stir up these many dragons and elephants.

Yet, as for the Way of Chan and the Buddha-dharma, they have not yet arrived here; with what, then, shall we make offering? You must know that when Bodhidharma came from the West, he entrusted us with a single staff.
He then held it up and said: "Therefore it is said: 'If you have a staff, I give you a staff. If you do not..."
There is no staff. I have taken away your staff. Now tell me: which is the guest phrase? Which is the host phrase?
If you can decide this, then it will be of use on the journey; if you cannot decide it, then let it remain as a mere worldly convention.
He then cast down his staff.
The Prime Minister, Layman Zhang Shangying, styled Tianjue and nicknamed Wujin, was nineteen years old when he entered the capital to take the imperial examination.
The Way Master traveled to the home of the Xiang family. Xiang had previously dreamed of a divine being who informed him, "Tomorrow you shall receive a gentleman. At dawn, the Master arrived;
Xiang was struck by this and received him with great courtesy and hospitality. He then said, "Since you, a scholar, are not yet married, I offer my daughter to serve as your attendant."
The Duke declined his offer with repeated humility. Xiang said, "If this mission does not reach its conclusion, I shall not fail to fulfill my prior agreement.
Later, when he indeed passed the imperial examination, he married her. Upon his first appointment as a District Magistrate (Zhubù), he entered a Buddhist monastery and saw the Tripitaka;
