"How is it? Do you understand? [The Master] said, "I cannot help but go this way," and then pressed both hands against the air and descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'? The Master said, "Vividly aware and profoundly still.
The monk asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not the person'? The Master said, "Profoundly still and vividly aware. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away both person and environment'?"
The Master said, "Alert! Alert! Alert! Alert! [The student] asked, "What is meant by 'neither person nor environment being wrested away'? The Master said, "Still!
Still! Still! Still! [The student] said, "Today this student has bought iron and obtained gold. The Master said, "Where did you get this topic from?"
The Abbot Juehai Fayin of Pingjiangfu was the son of the Zhu family from Yushan in the commandery.

At the age of twenty-four, he donned the black robes of a monk, received full ordination, and traveled to study. Upon arriving at Donglin, he visited Huirui. Huirui brought up the pivotal words regarding Lingyun’s realization of the Way and questioned him.
As the Master was about to respond, Huirui said, "Not so, not so. Suddenly, the Master attained a profound realization and composed this verse: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
Peach blossoms bloom upon the cliff. From where do the flowers come? As soon as Lingyun saw them, he turned his head and performed the Three Platforms Dance.
Dayue said, "What you have seen has indeed penetrated the subtle; yet you must further spur yourself on to clarify the Great Dharma. Thus the Master received the teaching.
He resided on Mount Lu for thirty years, never interacting with the secular world; the monastic communities held him in high esteem.

During the Jianyan era of the Song dynasty’s Gaozong, bandits rose up in Jiangzuo, and he followed the river eastward to return home. The local people constructed a hermitage for him to dwell in, and monks and laypeople followed one after another to seek his instruction.
He once said to the assembly, "If you all maintain the power of meditative concentration with full vigor, you need have no anxiety regarding morning meals, nor need you engage in the pursuit of gain.
In his later years, he lived in carefree wandering as he pleased, calling himself a "person of the five loose ties."
Chan Master Longya said, "The Dharma heir of Chan Master Zheyuan of Dongshan in Ruizhou was Chan Master Zeyan. A monk asked, 'What is the Tamer of the Ten Bodies?
Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there. I do not know what the underlying meaning was. The Master [Longya] said, "Under his heels, there are seven holes and eight apertures."
On the day Chan Master Deqiong of Deshan in Changde Prefecture was invited to ascend the hall, he said: "The masterly man does not consent to be caught in the net."
He called out, but [the monk] did not turn his head. "Why go from east to west? [The Master] answered on his behalf: "Look in five days.

Zen Master Zhongxuan of the Fourth Patriarch’s Monastery in Qizhou, successor to Zen Master Zhihaiqing, ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas appear in the world for the sake of one great cause and condition."
The Patriarch came from the West to point directly to the human mind. Buddhas and ordinary beings, as well as sages, are fundamentally non-dual;

delusion and enlightenment do not constitute divergent paths. There is nothing in nirvana to rejoice over, and nothing in birth and death to loathe. It is sufficient simply to attain awakening through a single word.
Without rising from one's seat, one immediately realizes the non-arising [of phenomena]. With a single thought, the light returns; without lifting a foot, one pervades the entire dharma-realm.
Such is the essential path that leads to the Source School (Zongmen). Now that I, this mountain monk, have arrived here, I must not do so in vain.
Thus, he raises his whisk and says: "Look! Look! The mountains, rivers, and the great earth; the sun, moon, and stars; whether ordinary or sagely, human or divine—"
All things are entirely within a single hair-tip atop the whisk; they enter and exit, playing at will. Do you all see this?
Even if you were to perceive it here with such clarity and distinctness, you must further know that there is a path leading beyond.
I ask you all: what is the path that leads upward? After a long silence, he said: "In the sixth month, heavy snow falls from the vast sky;
in the depths of winter, fiery clouds soar over the mountain peaks."

Chan Master Yuanhui of Qianfeng in Quanzhou ascended the hall and said: "The orthodox lineage of Bodhidharma, the very nostrils of the patch-robed monks—how lamentable that those who are deluded have become as numerous as swarms!
With eyes wide open, they nod off; above their heads is heaven, beneath their feet is earth, and with their ears they hear sounds."
Breathing out through the nostrils, I dare ask the disciples in the Yun-tang: where do you place this during the course of daily life? Do you see it?
Piteous indeed is the Great Master of Shuanglin, who instead says that this very sound of speech is it. *Du!* (A rebuke)

Chan Master Huimuyu Neng of Zhongyan in Meizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Daomian Yan of Dayue. He was the son of the Lü family of that prefecture. At the age of twenty-two, he served as a school librarian.

While wandering through a mountain temple, he happened to see a collection of Chan records; upon reading them, he felt as though he had attained some realization. Thereupon, he tore off his official cap and received full ordination. One—
He traveled through various regions with his alms bowl. He first visited Baosheng Fu, whose approach was quite different from his own.

Upon reaching Jinghu, he called upon Yong’an Xi, Zhenru Zhe, and Deshan Hui; his realization grew even more profound. When he eventually arrived at Daopei, Daopei asked, "Where is your home district, Senior Seat? The Master replied, "Western Sichuan.
Daopei said, "I have heard that there is an incarnation of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva appearing in Western Sichuan; is this true? The Master—

[The Master] said, "Today I have been able to behold your compassionate countenance. [The Master] asked, "Where is the white elephant? The Teacher said, "Its claws and tusks are already complete. [The Master] asked, "Can it still turn its body?
The Teacher lifted his sitting cloth, circled the meditation seat once, and stepped out. Muzhou said, "This is not the principle. The Teacher hurried out.
One day, while Muzhou was conducting a private interview with the assembly, he asked a monk, "After Huang Chao passed by, was there anyone who..."
"Have you recovered the sword? A monk raised his fist. Guishan said, "That is just a vegetable knife.
The monk said, "But it is still of inexhaustible use. Guishan shouted and sent him out. Next, he asked the Master, "After Huang Chao passed by, was there anyone who recovered the sword?
The Master also raised his fist. Guishan said, "That too is merely a vegetable knife. The Master said, "If one can kill people, that is enough," and then drew near.
The former [master] lunged forward and struck him with his chest. Guishan said, "For thirty years I have been riding a horse, yet today I have been thrown by a donkey.

Later, he returned to Shu and established a hermitage at the old site. At the request of the fourfold assembly, he went to reside at Baen Temple. Entering the hall for the formal address, Longji said:
"The myriad dharmas are the light of the mind; all conditions are but the clarity of the nature. Originally there is no one who is deluded or awakened; it simply requires this very day."
[The monk] said, "It is understood. The Master said, "Since there is neither delusion nor awakening, what have you understood? He gave a shout. He ascended the hall and, citing an occasion, said:
One day Xuefeng was performing communal labor carrying firewood. On the way, he saw a monk and dropped down a piece of wood, saying, "The entire Great Canon of the Buddha's Teachings..."
"I speak only of this. Later, Zhenru Zhe said, "The entire Great Canon of Teachings does not speak of this.
Based on the words of these two venerable masters, are they the same or different? I, this mountain monk, do not think so. [He] raises his whisk and says:
"If you lift it up, it is 'Thus have I heard. If you let it down, it is 'Believing and accepting, we shall practice. [He] asks Chongzhen inside the room: "What is the felt rug?"
[The Master] said, "Head! How is it that you are the parents prior to the empty kalpa? Zhenlingwu replied, "Venerable Monk, please lower your voice.
He then offered this verse of spiritual resonance: "I have suffered from hunger within the Myriad-Year Granary; I have dwelt in the great ocean with insatiable thirst."
When first seeking it, one could not find it; now, when trying to avoid it, one cannot escape it. The Master granted him formal approval (*inka*).

While playing chess with Huang, the Judicial Intendant, Huang asked: "Among all these games, not a single one is the same. A thousand moves and ten thousand moves are as they are, but what is that one move?
The Master picked up a chess piece and showed it to him. Huang stood there lost in thought. The Master—
He said: "I have not seen the Way; how many people have been driven to death by delusion along those nineteen paths? The Master held the position of abbot for over thirty years.
Whenever he preached the Dharma, he did not permit it to be recorded. At the time of his passing, he wrote a verse and passed away while sitting in the lotus posture. When his body was cremated,
A violent wind suddenly arose, and wherever the smoke reached, it rained down śarīras; both monastics and laypeople who tilled that land obtained them.
His heart and tongue remained uncorrupted. His stupa was enshrined in a cliff within the central peak of Mount Ben. This was the site of the Venerable Nāgārjuna’s practice hall.
Chan Master Zongyin of Yunjing Baojue in Huai’an Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'If you recognize the bench...'"
"Surrounding it for more than a full circuit," he said. "Furthermore, the Way says: 'To recognize a bench is as different from heaven and earth as the poles.
I, this mountain monk, do not think so. To recognize a bench is simply to recognize such idle furniture. After the Master had finished his general discourse, he spoke again:
"Sons, do not disperse yet; listen further to a verse. He then said: "For forty-nine years, A scene of heated clamor. Eighty-seven..."
"Spring. An old man playing alone. Who is young? Who is old? All alike are dreaming. Return! Return! The snow is heavy upon the plum branches.
Having finished speaking, he descended from his seat, leaned on his staff, and passed away. His stupa is at Mount Ben.

Chan Master Zhengjue Zongxian of Xingxiang Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Zhaojue Bai. He was a native of the Wang family of Tongchuan. In his youth, he passed the civil service examinations and enjoyed a reputation for learning.
Once, while playing by scooping up mountain stream water during the day, he thought of it at night; consequently, he saw the cold water filling the room.
He wished to draw [the water] up but could not; yet the dusty world of phenomena was spontaneously empty. He exclaimed, "The net of worldly existence has been torn asunder!

He went to rely upon Zhaojue for deliverance and followed the assembly to inquire and consult. One day, Zhaojue asked the Master, "Standing atop the high, high peak; walking on the bottom of the deep, deep sea—how do you understand this?
At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and said, "My heels have been nailed down. Zhaojue then... [raised his whisk].
Qishi said, "As for this *bushu* (fly-whisk), how about it? The Master smiled and went out. He served [his teacher] diligently for seven years.
Later, he traveled south to the capital and journeyed through Huai and Zhejiang. In his later years, he met Wuzu Yan at Haihui.
He stepped forward and asked: "I do not yet know the pivot; it is difficult to cross Zhaozhou’s bridge. "I shall not ask about Zhaozhou’s bridge," [Wuzu] replied. "What is this pivot? Wuzu—
He said, "You stay outside the gate for now. The Master stepped forward, gave a kick, and withdrew.

The Patriarch said, "After all this time of tea and rice, it turns out there is someone who knows its flavor. The next day, when [the Master] entered the room, the Patriarch asked, "Are you the monk who questioned me yesterday?
I certainly know your point of view; it is simply that you have not yet passed the Baiyun Pass."
The Master said, “Take care,” and then departed. At that time, Yuanwu was serving as his attendant. The Master tested him with the meaning of the White Cloud Barrier (Baiyun guan).
Yuanwu said, “You simply must realize it directly. The Master smiled and said, “It is not that I do not understand; it is simply that I am not yet familiar with it.
I shall wait until I see this old fellow to settle the matter with him. The next day, when Linji went to Shucheng, the Master and Yuanwu followed after him.
He went and happened to meet at Xinghua. The Patriarch asked the Master, "Do you remember seeing me in the prefectural seat? The Master replied, "I have been attending to you fully.
The Patriarch looked at Wuzhuo and said, "This fellow is loquacious. From that time on, their karmic conditions were in accord.
Upon returning from his travels to Mount Lu, the Master reported to Wuzu the verse he had attained: "Standing atop the highest peak; walking upon the deepest ocean floor."
The Patriarch said, "I once questioned my former teacher about this matter. My former teacher said, 'I once asked Master Yuan.

Yuan replied, "A cat has the merit of drinking blood; a tiger has the virtue of reviving the dead. Without having fundamentally mastered the source, one cannot reach such a state. You have served me for a long time, and I have held you in great affection.

Now that you are departing to return to Western Sichuan, I shall give you a small discourse."* *Note: This passage describes the transmission of the Dharma from Mazu Daoyi to Baizhang Huaihai. The "small discourse" (xiaocan) was a formal teaching given by a master to his assembly upon a disciple's departure.*
He further sent a verse with him, saying: "Having been away from my hometown for over forty years, I have momentarily forgotten the dialect of Shu.
When you, Zen practitioner, return to Chengdu, You must take care to remember the language of Lu. At that time, Jue was still in good health, and the Master again attended upon him.
His reputation became widespread, and he subsequently left to reside at Changsong. He later moved to Baofu, where Xiang asked a monk: "The Buddhas of the three periods..."
The founding Patriarch could not, in his lifetime, get out of this circle. What is this circle? The Master said: "The rim of a well.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Yangshan asking Zhongyi, "What is the meaning of Buddha-nature?
Zhongyi said, "I will give you a simile; then you will understand. Suppose there is a room with six windows, and inside there is a monkey."

"Monkey! Outside there is a macaque. He called "Singing-Singing" from the eastern window, and the macaque immediately responded. In this manner, he called from all six windows and received responses from each;
only then did Yang bow in prostration. "I have just received your instruction, Master, yet I have a point of doubt," Yang said. Xiangyi replied:
"What doubts do you have? Yang said. "Suppose the inner monkey is asleep while the outer monkey wishes to meet him;
what then? Xingzhou [Zhongyi] took Yangshan’s hand at his meditation seat and said, "The *shengsheng* has already met you.
The Master said, "Do you all wish to see these two elders? I shall also give you a parable. Zhongyi—
He was very much like a goldsmith. Yangshan brought a piece of gold and had the goldsmith appraise it;
the goldsmith also offered his full price in return. As they were about to complete the transaction, the seller added extra weight to the scales.
Although the goldsmith was inwardly pleased, he could not help but harbor secret doubts. Why? "Unless this is a spy, this must surely be stolen property. Thereupon, he descended from his seat.

Chan Master Weizi of Dongchan Monastery in Huangzhou, successor to Chan Master Qizhen of Songshan, ascended the hall and said: "Whatever is grasped by the hand is none other than the work of the Buddha;
every point reveals the principle, and every thing embodies the source. In every thought-moment, Śākyamuni appears in the world; at every step, Maitreya descends to be born. If you can believe..."
If you can attain this and maintain it, then you may please sit and cut off the heads of both the Reward-Buddha and the Transformation-Buddha, and stride with high steps upon the crown of Vairocana.
Holding up his staff, he said: "Tell me, what excellence does this staff possess? After a long silence, he drew a line and said:
"It can kill and it can give life; it can yield and it can seize. Furthermore, there is another quality worthy of admiration: where there is no elegance, it is nonetheless elegant."
Zhuo struck his staff once.

Chan Master Dongyuan of Hueli in Linjiang, successor to Chan Master Huili Chang, ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas and Patriarchs establish nothing; when it rains, the street is naturally soaked."

What do ordinary beings and sages rely upon? When it is clear and dry, there naturally is no mud. Only then does one know that every single thing is the Way, and that every phenomenon is fundamentally perfected.
Cease speaking of Zhaozhou’s seven-pound robe or Caoxi’s single drop of water. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, waves surge to the heavens;
from the bottom of the great ocean, red dust rises. [The Master] lets out a shout and says: "What kind of principle is this? Investigate!"
Master Huichang of Jingde on Yunfeng at Mount Heng in Hengzhou, successor to Chan Master Nanchan Luan, ascended the hall and said: "Not not; not is."
When Bodhidharma came from the West, he deluded the masses and displayed eccentricities. King Wu of Liang exposed his deception; he crossed the river and entered Wei.

For nine years he faced the wall at Mount Song, yet upon receiving Huikong (Shenguang), he instead suffered a loss. If you, great assembly, wish not to suffer such a loss: the lingering plum rains shroud a thousand homes;
the elegant warm breeze blows through the myriad species. If you attempt to deliberate upon this as "Buddha-dharma," you fall into the weeds.
A Pack of Foxes. Entering the Hall: "The Supreme Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes discrimination. Only do not harbor love or hate, and all will be luminously clear.
Xuefeng rolls the ball; Zhaozhou’s courtyard cypress—neither falling into sight or hearing, nor being sound or form.
If you attempt to ask how this is, he gives you a slap across the jaw.
Chan Master Desuan of Fushan in Tongcheng, Anqing, ascended the hall for the formal discourse. A monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Heaven is long-lasting;
earth is enduring. The monk said, “I do not yet understand. The Master said, “Old age brings on illness. The monk said, “Born together, we die together.”
"Furthermore, how is it? The Master said, "Can you call the *śrāmaṇera* a Buddha? He then said: "The Double Well Peak, the Brocade Valley— North, south, east, and west, difficult to record.
Even with the skillful brush of Gu Kaizhi, How could it compare to reaching fulfillment within the mind upon a single visit?
He raised his whisk and asked, "Do you see? After a long silence, he struck the meditation seat and descended.
The Seat.

On the day of the opening of the hall by Chan Master Puming of Dengjue in Fuzhou, the successor of Chan Master Ying of Jianfu, after the mallet had been struck, he looked at the great assembly and said: "How marvelous!"
How wonderful! Can you all still perceive it? If you can truly perceive it here, throughout the worlds of the ten directions, it is utterly naked and starkly bare;
there is not even a hair’s breadth of a dharma that can serve as an object of seeing or hearing, nor is there even a speck of a dharma that can serve as a counterpart or a correlate.
If you cannot perceive it, it is certain that the fetters of the sense organs and their objects have not yet been severed.

[The Master] said, "Understood? As long as you have not shed the emotional and intellectual measures of ordinary people and sages, you will spend your whole days falling into error within the realm of right and wrong, gain and loss.
What use is there in that? Is there among you any monk who is transcendent, uniquely liberated, and free? Come forth, and I shall provide testimony for you.
A monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said, "The wind is clear and the moon is bright. The monk said, [and the Master continued: "..."
“How is it that the object is taken away but not the person? The Master said, “Ash on the head and dust on the face. “How is it that both the person and the object are not taken away?
The Master said, “The seas are calm and the rivers are clear. “How is it that both the person and the object are taken away?

The Master said, “Not a drop of water can leak through. Question: “What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, “Wandering alone, even more bitter and arduous. Question: “What is...? [The text ends here.]
"This is the guest within the host. The Master said, "Your question is very clear. [The monk] asked, "What is the host within the guest?

The Master said, "Reaching out a hand into the red dust of the world. [The monk] asked, "What is the host within the host? The Master said, "Drawing a precious sword from its scabbard across the chest.

[The monk] asked, "I have already received the Master’s instruction on guest and host; as for the matter of the ultimate vehicle (*zōngchéng*), what is it like? The Master said, "Wait for another time."
He came and said, "Rest! Rest! Even if your questions arise like clouds and your answers pour forth like water from a jar, you will only move further away from the Way.
Why? It is because this matter cannot be expressed by the entire Great Canon; it is that which the Buddhas of the three periods have realized for themselves alone.

Shining upon the present and illuminating the past, it transcends seeing and cuts off knowing. Pervading the ten directions of space, how could it have a fixed location? It is only because of emotional attachment..."
The arising of wisdom creates a separation; as characteristics shift and essences diverge, one cannot achieve self-awakening amidst the affairs of daily life.

For this reason, former masters were moved to turn their backs upon worldly toil, opening the gate of expedient means (*upāya*) to reveal the mark of reality (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*). Holding up his whisk, he said: "The gate of expedient means has opened!
Is there anyone who can enter? If you can enter here, you will be able to uphold the seal of the true mark and establish the Great [Vehicle].
The Dharma-banner emerges and disappears, moving vertically and horizontally; it rolls up and unfurls with sovereign ease.
Nevertheless, this still falls within the gateway of manifesting transformations and is not yet the direct, essential path of the patch-robed monks. But what, then, is that direct, essential path?
After a long silence, he said: "If you value it, you cannot possess it fully; only by casting it off is it sublime. He then threw down his whisk.
Chan Master Dayuan Zhi of Daming Mountain, of Tanzhou, was a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Daolin Yizhen. One day, he ascended the hall and cited Nanquan’s saying:
"The Buddhas of the three periods do not know it; the tabby cat and the white ox, however, do know it. The Master said: "Since the Buddhas of the three periods..."
To "know there is"—even the wildcat and the white ox have never dreamed of it. One must clearly know that there is something beyond;

only one who knows there is can truly attain it. But what kind of person is one who knows there is? They drink the official wine, lie on the official street, die where they stand, and are buried where they fall.
On the battlefields, there are countless heroic men; their corpses are piled as high as mountains and heaped like peaks.
The fifteenth generation descendant of Nanyue was Chan Master Shou of Shangfeng;
his dharma heir was Wen Ding Gong Hu Anguo, courtesy name Kanghou, with the monastic style Ca'an. Having long relied upon Shangfeng, the Gong attained [his teachings].
Regarding the intent of the Outsiders: During the Chongning era, [Fenyang] passed by Yaoshan. A Zen practitioner there raised the story of Nanquan killing the cat and questioned the Master about it.
The Master replied with a verse: "In hand, he holds the pivot of life and death, encompassing heaven and earth; His arrangements, whether expansive or restrictive, depend on the moment.
The jade hall’s rabbit and horse are not dragons or elephants; In his majestic great function, they know nothing at all. He sent a verse up to Shangfeng, which begins: "I offer my prayers..."
The melting peaks resemble the heavens of Duchaeng; ten thousand ages of rivers and mountains are present before one's eyes. One must believe that the "Dead Heart" (Sixin) never truly dies;
last night, the autumn moon was once again full together with it.
Chan Master Fuzhou Puxian Yuansu, a native of Jianning, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Shangfeng Cai. He ascended the hall and said: "The army follows the seal’s turn;

beyond three thousand li, all smoke and dust have ceased. The general pursues the talisman’s path; throughout the six periods of the day, one is utterly naked and bare. There is no need for iron banners or iron..."

When the drum is beaten, the grass naturally bends and the wind naturally blows. What need is there for seven releases and seven captures? It is simply that there is none who does not submit without thought.
As it is said: "The Great Man wields the sword of wisdom; the edge of Prajñā is like the flame of a diamond vajra.
It can destroy the hearts of external paths, but it has long since already struck down the courage of the celestial Māras. At such a time, tell me: who is the commanding general?
[The Master] gave a shout and ascended the hall. Nanquan said, "At eighteen, I already knew how to make a living.
My bag had no thread to tie even an ant; my kitchen lacked grain enough to bind even a rope. Zhaozhou said, "At eighteen, I already knew how to ruin a family and scatter a household.
I bought cheap at the south end and sold dear at the north end. Examining these two statements, they both deserve thirty blows of the staff.
Let this one move pass for now. Why? "Having once been a profligate, he feels special pity for travelers; naturally loving wine, he spares those who are drunk. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"Before a word is spoken, the instruction is already given; when you attempt to deliberate, ten thousand mountains stand in between.
Do not say that the Buddha-dharma is nothing much—it is also very difficult to penetrate the fundamental barrier. As for this fundamental barrier, how do you penetrate it?"
[The Master] gave a shout.
Zen Master Sengtang Sengxun of Gushan in Fuzhou, a native of the Ruan clan of that same prefecture, ascended the hall and said:
"Huangbo’s sixty blows from his staff—had he not understood the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, he would have been short by a little. [But] on Daoyu’s ribs..."
He clenched his fists three times and said, "Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma consists of nothing more than this. It is enough to leave people bewildered and frustrated;

you must know there is one person who strikes him over the head with a great club, yet he does not turn his head back. An old fist hammers him across the face, yet he pays it no mind. But tell me, who is this? Ascending the hall, he said:
"The north wind sweeps the ground, rolling up the yellow leaves; outside the gate, a thousand peaks show their chilling colors."
At midnight, a tortoise flies with snow; the stone woman frowns her two brows by the stream. [Deshan] plants his staff and says, "Everyone is here.
Now tell me: is it the sky that is cold, or the people? He gives a shout and says, "Return to the hall!"
Chan Master Biefeng Zuzhen of Gushan in Fuzhou was the son of Lin of Xinghua. His mother, née Chen, dreamed that a monk presented her with a bright pearl;
when she asked where it had come from, the monk replied, "I am Huang Niepan. Upon waking, she became pregnant. When he was born, he possessed extraordinary features:
his body hair was two inches long throughout. He once visited Jianchun of Gushan and subsequently studied under Foxin.

At Mount Dongshan, when [Zhaozhou] Xing moved to Mount Gu, the Master presided over the First Seat. When Xing departed, the Master succeeded him on the seat. He later moved to Fashi in Quanzhou. A monk asked:
"When Zhaozhou circumambulated the meditation seat once and said, 'The turning of the Tripitaka is finished,' what is the principle behind this?

The Master said: "When painting a dragon, look at the head; when painting a snake, look at the tail. The monk said: "The old woman said, 'I have been requesting you to turn the Tripitaka for some time now. The Master said: "She was right."
"The entire Tripitaka—why is it that you have only turned half of it? What is the meaning of this?

The Master said, "If a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate anxieties. [The student] asked, "I do not yet understand where the 'turning of half the Tripitaka' takes place.

The Master said, "If one is not a true knower, all talk of enduring the cold winters is but a weary labor. Ascending the hall, he said: "In seeking an ox, one must follow its tracks; in studying the Way, one prizes..."
No-mind. When the tracks remain, the ox is still there; with no-mind, the Way is easy to find. Holding up his whisk, he said:
"This is the track. But where is the ox? Even if you can see its head and horns clearly, its nostrils are still in the hands of Fashih.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The one path that goes upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages. He struck the ground with his staff and said: "If you understand it this way..."
"Attained. One hundred and eight thousand. But ultimately, how is it? Peach red, plum white, rose purple—when asked about the spring breeze, it knows nothing at all.
Addressing the assembly: "The Great Way is right before your eyes, yet for the moment it is difficult to behold.

If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, voice, or language. He struck the meditation staff and said: "This is sound. He then held the staff upright.
Holding up his staff, he said: "This is form. What do you call the true essence of the Great Way?

Even if you were to see it here, it would still be like a person from Zhengzhou leaving the Cao Gate. Addressing the assembly, he said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a person eating rice."
When one is full, one simply rests. If one is not yet full, there will surely be a mind that longs for food; if one eats too much, there is the affliction of injury to the heart.
Reaching this point, how does one attain the state of being just right? After a long silence, he said:
"For now, return to sleep beneath the crags, and together watch when the moon is bright. The Master once constructed stupas for the Seven Buddhas at Fashi; when the work was finished, he then...

"Everyone! Is this life? Is this death? After a long silence, he said, "Gentlemen may enter.

Chan Master Zonghui of Xiyuan in Nanjian Prefecture was a native of Wuzhou. Having relied upon Master Wushi for a long time, he attained a profound realization of the Dharma-patience (*dharmakṣānti*).
Because the temple monks reported the violation of the tea prohibition to the authorities, the officials arrested the administrative head (jishi).
The Master said to the assembly, "If I do not vindicate this matter, the guilt shall fall upon me; yet if I do vindicate it myself, they will incur punishment. I cannot bear to do either.

He then ordered the drum to be beaten and ascended the seat, reciting this verse: "The county official’s summons does not cease for a moment; How can it compare to the long-past events, which are clearly manifest?"
"Formerly there was a song of non-arising; now, fortunately, the melody has been completed. Having spoken thus, he passed away.

National Preceptor T'anran of Goryeo had succeeded to the royal throne at a young age. He held the *zongcheng* (the vehicle of the lineage) in deep admiration and, via the maritime merchant Fang Jingren, arrived at Siming.
There he recorded the words of Wushi and returned home. Upon reading them, the Master attained awakening and immediately abdicated his position to shave his head and become a monk. He then composed:
He wrote this to convey the essential points, including the verse on the four modes of deportment, and had Jingren present it to Wushi. Wushi replied:

"When the Buddhas and Patriarchs appeared in the world, they did not bestow a single dharma upon others; rather, they truly caused them to have self-confidence and self-awakening, to realize and attain for themselves."

Possessing great wisdom and insight, he spoke according to what he saw and acted according to what he spoke. Mountains, rivers, the great earth, grasses, trees, and forests have long been his witnesses.
Later, he further succeeded to the Dharma; his writings state briefly: "In the sea of birth and death, it is difficult to cross over for vast eons.
Having encountered a master of one's own fundamental nature, one is verified and determined by means of the seal of the three essentials."
This principle is truly like that of the blind turtle encountering the hole in a floating log.
Chan Master Wuzhu of Longhua in Lin’an Prefecture, a native of Guangde, ascended the hall and cited Yunmen’s raising of a *hubing* (sesame cake), saying:
"I only provide offerings for those of the Two Zhe regions; I do not provide offerings for those from the north. The assembly was speechless. Yunmen—
Zi Dai said: "The weather is cold and the days are short; two people share one bowl. The Master said: "That old fellow from Shaoyang has a hidden barb within his words;
it is like driving a gimlet into a painful spot. If you examine it closely, it turns into a poisonous drug. Do you all wish to understand?
Half is south of the Yellow River, half is north of the Yellow River—a single expanse of void, as black as ink. To contemplate this in stillness brings nothing but sorrow unto death."
"I cannot endure this old thief Yunmen! Thief, thief! Having finished speaking, he descended from his seat and did not even go on a tour of the hall.
Dongshan Ji Chan Master of Dongshan in Linjiang Commandery was a Dharma successor of Ming Chan Master of Daochang. Once, while he was with Li Chaoling and his nephew, Layman Xianglin Xiangzi...
Li Yin went to pay his respects and asked, "When the household thief troubles people, what is it like? The Master said, "Who is the household thief? Li raised his fist.
The Master said, "The thief's identity has already been revealed. Li said, "Do not try to smear the truth over me. The Master said, "The evidence of the crime is right here before you."

Li remained speechless. The Master showed him a verse, saying: "What can one do when the household thief causes such distress? Even the Thousand Sages turn their faculties back for his sake. Pervading the world and pervading space, he leaves no trace;
Without support and without dwelling, he is beyond all nets and snares. Thief upon thief! Neither fierce generals nor valiant soldiers can capture him.
He would kill the old Chan masters of the world with a single doubt, And make the ancient Maitreya in the bustling marketplace burst into laughter. Rest!"
Rest! There is no need to seek the mind outwardly. Turn your head and glance back; in an instant, the thief’s own body is revealed. Caught with the stolen goods, he has no peer in the world.
Having no peer in the world is truly worthy of veneration. From this point on, one no longer boasts of clever skills.
When one settles peacefully at home and enjoys their work, the myriad phenomena and all living beings clap their hands in unison.
Chan Master Lanna Daoshu of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Daochang Hui. He was the son of the Xu family from Sian in Wuxing. Initially, he resided at Heshan;
subsequently, he moved to Huazang. At the beginning of the Longxing era, by imperial decree, he took up residence at Lingyin. Emperor Xiaozong of the Song dynasty summoned him to the inner palace.
He asked about the essentials of the Way of Chan. The Master replied: "This matter lies within Your Majesty’s own majestic daily life where you respond to circumstances.
Fundamentally, there is no distinction between knowledge and views or arising and ceasing; nor is there any differentiation between sage and ordinary person, or delusion and awakening.

Simply protect right mindfulness, and you will be in accord with the Way. When the emotions are repelled by external objects, karma cannot bind you. Once the maladies of dullness and agitation are entirely eliminated, you will naturally forget to ask."
The meaning of the answer is this: Since the Buddha of the Stage of Succession (Upapadya) currently resides within the light of Prajñā, what thing could not be manifested therein?
[The Master] nodded his head at the top [of the hall] and addressed the assembly: "The immortal Zhang Guolao rode a donkey with pierced ears through the gate;
one heard only the clatter of its hooves—who knew it was made of paper? Later, he retired to the Yong'an Hermitage at Mingjiao. He lived in leisure...

He lived in seclusion for a long time. He inscribed a verse on a wall that read: "The plum blossoms amidst the snow are the harbinger of spring; The moonlight upon the pond possesses the spirit of night.
It is not that there have been no fine pleasures in recent years; Do not take this family tradition and show it to others.
In the eighth month of the *Pingshen* year of the Chunxi era, he manifested a slight illness. Having written a final verse, he passed away. He was interred in a stupa at Yong’an.

On the day the head seat Wuchu of Guangxiao Monastery in Guangde Commandery—successor to Chan Master Guangxiao Min—was assigned to share the teaching seat, he addressed the assembly by citing the "Wind and Banner" koan.

Upon reaching the words, "Where the mind of the person moves," he said: "The Patriarch spoke thus, but he has deceived an entire shipload of people. As for the patch-robed monks of the present day..."
Nor should you understand it in such a way. Since you do not understand it in such a way, after all, how is it? After a long silence, he said:
"In the sixth month, it is good for making sauce; one must simply take care not to put too much salt in."

The Dharma successor of Chan Master Wannian Ben of the seventeenth generation under Nanyue, Chan Master Xian of Lóngmíng Zàiyán in Wenzhou, ascended the hall and said: He cited Fayan’s words: "Recognize the bench. It is all-pervasive.
[The Master] said, "A little more than a full circle. Yunmen said, "If you recognize the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different.
The Master said, "Old man Fayan sits people to death; Grand Master Yunmen runs people to death. Longming is not like this:
if you recognize the bench, its four legs rest firmly on the ground; when you wish to sit, you sit; when you wish to rise, you rise. [He] ascended the hall and cited Zhao...
The Verse on the Story of Old Woman Kan of the Prefecture: A lady of snow and ice, her countenance most extraordinary; She constantly takes up her jade flute to blow for others.
Within the melodies lie boundless matters of sorrow; To the Lord of Spring alone, she grants the first branch.
Chan Master Dajian Yigan of Dayi Hermitage in Tanzhou was a native of Kuaiji. He ascended the hall and said: "The trees have shed their leaves and the sky is empty;
the heavens are cold and the waters are frozen. The Old Śākyamuni has nowhere to hide.

Demolishing the eastern fence to patch up the western wall, he runs straight into Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, who requests instruction on the Samādhi of Buddha-Recitation. How truly strange! Yet he replies, 'A cloud of golden radiance.'"
After the assembly retreat, "Go drink tea. Entering the hall: The Old Barbarian opened up a single path; how direct it is! He simply said, "Resting is Bodhi;
the nature is pure and the mind is luminous; it is not obtained from others. Yet later people could not find its gate;
they have been running hither and thither, north and south, east and west, exhausting years and seasons without a single place to rest. Everyone, will you now rest?
"Is it so? Enough, enough. Ascending the hall, he raised an old case: One day Huìtáng asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Nánxióng Prefecture.
Huìtáng said, "What did you come here for? The monk said, "To visit venerable elders. Huìtáng said, "It would be better for you to return home."
[The Master] said, "I have not yet understood the meaning of the Master’s command for me to return to my hometown.

Huitang said, "In my hometown, one could buy a piece of fish sauce for three coins, as large as a palm. The Master said, "I would rather have my body shattered into fine dust than ever again blind the eyes of a monk.
Huitang was worth a little more than that. There are some fellows who say, "It is hard to forget what one is accustomed to," but what does that matter?
At the Common Discourse Hall, he ascended the seat and raised the *gong'an* of the King of Kaśmīra questioning Venerable Siṃha regarding the emptiness of the aggregates (*skandha-śūnyatā*).
The Master offered this verse: When did the Venerable One ever attain the emptiness of the aggregates? The King of Kaśmīra needlessly cut down the spring breeze himself.
After the rain, the peach blossoms have already fallen; They have dyed the flowing waters of the stream crimson.
Chan Master Xue’an Congjin of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Zheng family of Nanxi in Yongjia.

He received the tonsure under Zihu Puan and visited Xinwen at Ruiyan. One day, while entering the master’s room for instruction, Xinwen raised the koan of “a flake of snow on a red-hot furnace” and questioned him.
As the Master was about to offer a reply, he suddenly attained realization. He remained in attendance for three years, then traveled to Min to see Fozhi at Xichan.
Zhì asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Sīmíng. Zhì said, "Have you ever seen Hǎn Bùdài? The Master gave a shout; Zhì struck him.
The Master caught his fist and said, "Abbot, do not be so hasty. Zhì said, "Blind fellow! Stand over here. At that time, Xīnwén was the head of Jiāngxīn;
the Master returned to visit him and was appointed as the *weínà*. One day, he questioned the Master about "the one."
"A single shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function act simultaneously. [The student] asked, "What is this 'one shout that distinguishes guest and host'?
The Master then gave a shout. Wumen asked, "Regarding this one shout, is it the guest or the host? The Master said, "As for the guest, it is always the guest; as for the host, it is always the host.
Wumen laughed and said, "You have lost your eyesight again. The Master then presented a verse: "One shout distinguishes guest and host; [It is] based on..."
However, his eyes were clouded; he performed a somersault backward and stepped on a frog, killing it. He first resided at Lingyan in Yizhen and later moved to Tiantong.
A monk asked, "What is the realm of Lingyan? The Master replied, "The cold waters of Deer-Run Spring soak the bright moon."
In Longdougang, white clouds are deeply hidden. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "At midnight, Mount Sumeru is placed in the nostrils. The monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Looking up, one does not see the sky.
The monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The whole body enters the wild weeds. Ascending the hall, he said: "When the golden mallet is moved, the Buddhas of the three periods..."
The Buddha dares not face him head-on; when his laws and decrees are put into practice, the heterodox and the celestial Māras all fold their hands in submission.

Lofty and towering, he is fundamentally beyond reaching or gazing up at; pure and naked, there is no need for contrivance. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, there is no need for suspicion.
Good and evil, right and wrong—let them all be cast down at once. Only then may one mix mud and water, pull the plow and handle the handle, proceeding with effortless spontaneity.
Transverse! In total, there is no obstruction. At this very moment, tell me: how does one sing the "Song of Great Peace"?
After a long silence, he said: "An iron boat lies across the ancient ford; the old family style is restored. Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"To turn the body within the diamond circle is to strike the nostrils of Śakra. To let go of the hand atop the precipice is to bring forth the eyes of Bodhidharma. He went on:

Again, three times. His inspiration was still not exhausted; once the pivot of the wheel turns, its momentum cannot be halted. Grasping the tail of a scorpion upside down, he makes the Śrāvakas his servants;
stroking the whiskers of a tiger in the natural direction, he calls the Bodhisattvas his slaves. Śākyamuni has already passed away and Maitreya has not yet been born;
the ancestral commands of the Buddha-dharma are now entirely in the hands of this new Celestial Child. For now, he holds fast and then lets go—how will he provide for them? Truly.
Jiurou said: "A holeless iron hammer is hurled right at one's face; a pure breeze rises across the heavens and throughout the earth.

On the twenty-third day of the seventh month in the Gengshen year of the Qingyuan era of Emperor Ningzong of the Song dynasty, he requested a bath, changed his robes, wrote this verse, threw down his brush, and passed away.
He was eighty-four years of age and seventy *lǎ* (years since ordination). His entire body was interred to the right of the Xinwen Pagoda.
Chan Master Jingmeng of Gu’an at Zhimen in Wenzhou Prefecture was the son of the Shao family of Pingyang in Wenzhou.

From his youth, he delighted in hearing the sounds of bells and sutras. At thirteen, he donned the black robes and studied the Tiantai teachings; however, finding that the study of names and characteristics was insufficient for resolving the Great Matter, he abandoned it.
He went to visit Fozhi at Yuyang Monastery, where the Master asked him about his native place. The Master replied, "Yongjia. The Master [Fozhi] said, "Do you still recognize Yongjia?"

"Do you recognize the Great Master Yongjia? The Master was about to answer when the King shouted, "Get out! Thereupon, the Master became as if dazed and remained so for months, unaware of whether he slept or ate.
One day, hearing the sound of a bell, he suddenly attained awakening. He went up to the abbot’s quarters, where the King asked, "Do you still recognize the Great Master Yongjia?
The Master replied, "Today, I respectfully wish the Abbot ten thousand blessings in your daily life. The King said, "As for the matter beyond [this world]..."
"How is it? The Master was about to respond when the King struck him with his staff and drove him out. The next day, he went again to the abbot’s quarters;

as the King was about to pose a question, the Master raised his voice and said, "This old man has failed today! He gave a shout and departed. Consequently, he returned to his hometown to visit his parents and saw Longxiang.
Longxiang asked: "Words do not unfold the matter; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases..."
[The Master said: "This is delusion. Try to pass through this message at the place where words and explanations fail.
The Master drew a circle (○) with his left hand; Xiang struck it with his whisk from the left. The Master drew a circle (○) with his right hand; Xiang struck it with his whisk from the right.

The Master drew another circle (○), and between them, he presented both hands [in a gesture of offering]. Xiang made two strokes with his whisk. The Master rose from his bow and stood up. Xiang smiled and said, "Three."

For ten years he had been selecting cats; today he has obtained this "black-berried" one (a term for a rare, high-quality cat). He returned to Deer Park and named his hermitage Xiangyuzi after the valley’s name.
He once visited Xianing Zhi and initially went forth to reside at Zhimen, later moving to Ruiyan. The Master was solitary and transcended the mundane;
though physically frail and unable to bear even the weight of his robes, he was stern, cold, and severe, such that one could not easily approach or fathom him.

Chan Master Yangqi Fanghui of Yanzhou, the eleventh-generation successor in the lineage descending from Nanyue and the dharma heir of Chan Master Shishuang Yuan, was born into the Leng family of Yichun in that prefecture. From his youth, he was alert and quick-witted; by the time he reached adulthood—
He did not concern himself with brush or inkstone. He registered his name at a commercial tax office and excelled in collecting duties, but was punished for dereliction of duty.

Thereupon, he fled by night to Jiufeng in Ruizhou; the place felt as if it were a familiar haunt, and out of deep affection, he could not bear to leave. He subsequently shaved his head. Whenever he read the sutras, his mind was harmonized and his spirit attained realization.
He was able to humble himself to seek instruction from veteran masters. From Nanyuan, Ciming moved to Daowu and then to Shichuang.
The Master assisted him in all matters pertaining to the general affairs of the monastery. Although he remained there for a long time, no realization had yet dawned upon him.

Whenever he sought instruction, Yuanmiao would say, "The administrative affairs of the storehouse are busy; go now. On another day when he asked again, Yuanmiao said, "Head monk, in the future your descendants will spread throughout the world;
why be so anxious? One day, just as Yuanmiao was about to go out, it suddenly began to rain. The Master scouted for him along a small path.
Having seen him, [Dongshan] grabbed him and said, "Old man, you must explain this to me today; if you do not, I shall beat you away.
Ming said, "Monk-in-charge, since you know such matters, let it be. Before he had finished speaking, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He immediately prostrated himself on the muddy ground and asked, "How is it when we meet on a narrow path? Ming said, "You should step aside; I have somewhere else to go."

[The Master] went inside. The Teacher returned. On the following day, he prepared his full ceremonial attire and went to the abbot’s quarters to pay his respects. Yuanmiao scolded him, saying, "It is not yet finished.

From then on, whenever Yuanmiao went out for walks in the mountains, the Teacher would invariably wait for him to emerge; even if it was late, he would inevitably strike the drum to assemble the assembly, and Yuanmiao would immediately return.
The Master (Mingzhao) said in anger, "In the morning there was a gathering in the forest; in the evening you ascend the seat. From where did you obtain such rules and regulations?
The teacher (Fenyang) said, "This is Fenyang’s late-afternoon informal discourse (*wanchan*). Why do you say it is not a rule and regulation?

One day, when Ming was presiding over the assembly, the teacher came forward and asked, "When the dark birds warble their songs and leave the clouds to enter the chaotic peaks—what then? Ming said, "I walk amidst the wild weeds; you, moreover, enter the deep thicket."
Cun. The Master said, "The official does not permit even a needle to pass. Ming then asked another question. Ming gave a shout. The Master said, "A fine shout!
Ming shouted again. The Master also shouted. Ming shouted twice in succession. The Master prostrated himself. Ming said, "This matter can only be carried by one who is a true person.
The Master shook his sleeves and departed. Ming moved to Xinghua. The Master took his leave and returned to Jiufeng. Later, both monastics and laypeople...
He went to reside at Yangqi, and subsequently moved to Yungai. On the day he accepted the invitation, he held up his Dharma robe and showed it to the assembly, saying, "Do you understand?
Today, this mountain monk has, for no reason, walked into the ranks of the water buffalo. Do you know? Nine Peaks of Yunyang, floating gourd of Ping, Yangqi.
He then ascended the seat. At that time, a monk stepped forward; the Master said, "The old fisherman has not yet cast his line, yet the leaping scales—"
A monk came charging forward. The Master then shouted. The monk said, "I do not believe you. He clapped his hands and returned to the assembly.
The Master said, "How much wind from the Dragon King can you endure? A monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose lineage of the school's spirit does he succeed?

The Master said, "When there is a horse, I ride the horse; when there is no horse, I walk on foot. The monk said, "An elder with such youthful vigor must possess many clever stratagems. The Master said, "I take pity on your age."
"Old man! I grant you thirty blows. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A three-legged donkey prances about on its hooves.
The monk said, "Is it not just this? The Master said, "Elder of Hunan. Then he said, "If there are any others who wish to ask questions, come forth and meet me.
Yangqi’s life today rests in your hands; feel free to drag him along as you please."
[The Master] was dragged backward. "Why is it so? [he asked]. "A great man must make a decisive judgment before the assembly;
if you cannot do so, Yangqi has lost face today. The Master then descended from his seat. Jiufeng Qin held him back, saying, "Today I am happy to have found a fellow practitioner.
The Master said, "What is this matter of being a fellow practitioner? Qin said, "Jiufeng plows the furrow; Yangqi drags the plow."
[The Master] was weeding. The Master said, "At this very moment, Yangqi is in front; Jiufeng is in front.
As Fulin hesitated, the Master pushed him away and said, "I thought you were a fellow practitioner, but it turns out you are not.

He ascended the hall and said, "Baizhang held a torch while clearing the fields and spoke of 'Great Meaning'—what kind of talk is that? Yangqi spent two days planting rice, yet he too had a most extraordinary saying."
He then said: "Master Bodhidharma had no front teeth. Ascending the hall, he said: "Yangqi’s single word is circular according to the square.

If you hesitate to deliberate upon it, there are eighty thousand miles [between you and the truth]. Ascending the hall, he said: "Autumn rain washes the autumn forest; the autumn forest is entirely verdant.
Alas for Master Fu! Where can one seek Maitreya? Ascending the hall, he said: "Ordinary beings and sages do not fall [into categories]; Buddhas..."
"Where does the Patriarch stand? O Great Assembly! In a world of pure peace, one does not permit others to snatch away their place in the marketplace.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Yangqi has newly settled here; the walls of the house are sparse. The entire bed is covered with snow and true pearls.

Shrink my neck and sigh in secret. After a long silence, he said: 'I am reminded instead of the ancients dwelling beneath the trees. Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring rain moistens everywhere; every single drop..."
[He] set it aside elsewhere. Holding up his staff, he struck it once and said, "Do you understand? For nine years he sat facing the wall in vain;
now that he is old, his heart grows lonely. Ascending the hall, he said: "When body and mind are pure, all objects are pure;
when all objects are pure, body and mind are pure. Do you know where the old man of Yungai lands? He then said, "Losing a coin in the river, one must fish for it in the river."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The end of the three months of spring approaches, and the four seas are clear and vast; the wind is calm and the waves are still—this is something everyone knows.
But tell me, how do you express the phrase 'using the long to complete the short'? After a long silence, he said: "How many times have black winds tossed the great ocean?
Yet I have never heard it said that a fishing boat has capsized. *Chan.* Ascending the hall, he held up his staff, struck once, and said: "Great!"
[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "The assembly, even if Dharma had a true message, it would still fall into the secondary faculty of everyone present.
Consider this: 'A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti let go and return home. Yungai speaks thus."
This too is looking at a rusted bolt. There is further discourse; do not misquote it. Ascending the hall, he said: "Aha-ha! What is this?
Go drink tea in the Sangha Hall. He descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he threw down his staff and said:
"Old Śākyamuni tripped and fell, yet he stole a laugh. Yungai spoke in confusion. Nevertheless, though the world is level and smooth, it is still a matter of diligent effort."

Jiegou Pass is increasingly difficult to traverse. [Later,] he ascended the hall for formal instruction. "If there is a single dharma that possesses form, it obscures your eyes.

When the eyes are not clear, the world appears treacherous and towering. He held up his staff and asked, "Do you see it? If you see it, then you have blocked the light of your own eyes. If you do not see it, then..."
Having lost his staff, how can one speak a phrase that is not deceived by others? After a long silence, he said: "The level ground is not yet considered perilous;
how could the distant mountains be deemed high? He struck the meditation seat with his staff and ascended the hall. Tapping the meditation seat, he said:
"It is not mind, nor is it Buddha. I ask you: what, after all, is it? Last night, Vajrapāṇi bared his fangs in a fit of rage. One.
With a fist he breaks through the grotto of spirits. *Hè!* He ascends the hall. A swift horse requires but one lash;
a swift man requires but one word. Even if it were so, you would still be but a dullard. Then he calls to the assembly, saying, "Go drink tea. He ascends the hall.
On the day of the Start of Spring, they strike the clay oxen. One blow, two blows—thousand heads, a hundred heads. Deeply covered by falling snow, they cannot be distinguished. Their horns...
The gatekeeper, a blind disciple, idly claps his hands and says, "Lara-lari! The spring breeze continues to disturb all, never ceasing.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The golden-maned lion lets out a single roar; it startles the Dharma-body hidden within the Northern Dipper. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have nowhere to run.
Even the blue-eyed one vainly boasts of his skillful hand. He gave a shout. Ascending the hall again, he held his staff crosswise and said:
Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. Licorice is sweet; yellow bitter gourd is bitter. The vast waves surge boundlessly, their crests reaching to heaven.
Atop the summit of Mount Sumeru, the sun stands at its zenith. [The Master] struck his staff and ascended the hall, saying: "The Supreme Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes discrimination."
Holding up his staff, he said, "Baoning’s staff has, in a single stroke, pierced through the nostrils of all the patch-robed monks in the world.
He struck it once. Ascending the hall, he said: "Spring rain is like fat; spring wind is like a blade. It fills the ditches and blocks the ravines; it uproots trees and makes the branches whistle.
Do you understand? When the fish swims, the water becomes turbid; when the bird flies, feathers fall. Ascending the hall, he said: "In the gate of the Patriarchs, there is no..."
A person walks; the depth and peril exceed that of a ten-thousand-fathom pit. To dangle one’s hands [into it] is but a waste of effort.
Let the green moss grow upon the hall floor. Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Palace, Gong, Shang, Jiao, Zhi, Yu; Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth."
He struck the desk once and said: "The divination chart distinguishes between good and ill; look for it after three days. Ascending the hall, Baoning said:
"In my ordinary dealings with people, I am directly faceless. If one were to beat the bones to extract the marrow, it would cause the gods to wail and the ghosts to weep.
He clapped his hands and laughed, saying: "Benevolence and righteousness are all severed at the point of poverty; worldly sentiment leans toward those who have wealth."
Ascending the hall, he held his staff horizontally and said, "You great men of integrity must cut through things with a single stroke, leaving nothing behind;

you must be able to move freely in all directions, vertically and horizontally. He then threw down the staff and said, "Wait for the people of the world to pass judgment. A monk asked, "The cold wind withers the fallen leaves;
we still rejoice that an old friend has returned. We do not yet know, who is this 'old friend'? The Master replied, "Yangqi passed away long ago."
[The monk] said, "Who else is there who knows this? The Master said, "The blind village elder nods his head in the dark.
[The monk] said, "A dead log has neither smoke nor fire; surely no one can know it alone. The Master said, "Today the furnace has not yet been opened.
[The monk] said, "What if one suddenly encounters a time of 'seven releases and eight crossings'? The Master said, "It would be better to withdraw your hand. [The monk] said, "Who knows the smoke?"
"Amidst the mist, there is still a fisherman. The Master said, "Do not speak so recklessly.

While the Master was reciting the verses on the Three Statements with Li Taibo, Taibo remarked, "This is merely an unresolved case. The Master said, "I ask you, Great Scholar, to try and judge it for me."
Fobo said, “Seven blows for thirteen. The Master asked, “What fault did Baoning commit? Fobo was speechless.
The Master said, “This is precisely an unresolved public case. He ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered, he remained silent for a long while and said, “What can this possibly be used for?
Then he descended from his seat. He ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered, he remained silent for a long while and said, “It is still somewhat lacking. Then he descended from his seat.
Seated on the platform, he ascended the hall. "The myriad phenomena of the universe all appear within the mirror. Pointing with his staff, he said, "To the north is the kitchen and storehouse;
to the south is the monks' hall; in the middle is the Buddha Hall. Pointing directly downward, he asked, "What is this?

He then said, "Even the person treading upon the platform does not recognize it. Ascending the hall again, he said, "The hundred rivers flow in different directions, yet they all return to the same source."
"The ocean: ten thousand divergent paths all enter this school. Holding up his staff, he said: "To heal a sore under the eye, one gouges out the flesh from the heart.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I raise it at every moment; I speak of it everywhere. There is no taboo, no interruption. Laying his staff across [his lap], he asked:

"Do you understand? A night of falling flower-rain; the entire city is filled with the fragrance of flowing water. He struck once. Ascending the hall again, he said: [The same as above]. He struck once.
All things flourish through a single rain; sprouts grow without departing from the soil. A sweet melon is sweet to its very stem; a bitter gourd is bitter to its roots. [The Master] ascends the hall.
From morning until evening, he speaks horizontally and vertically, yet he has never moved so much as a single hair’s breadth of it.
He picks up his staff and says: "Do you understand? The third and the first, the middle ninth and the lower seventh. Do not ask about the *Tiāngāng* or the *Héshí*."
[The Master] said, "What is there to say about 'Great Auspiciousness' or 'Small Auspiciousness'? He made a single stroke with his hand, ascended the hall, and called to the assembly.
Pointing upward with his finger, he said, "This is Śākyamuni. Raising his fist, he said, "This is Kāśyapa. Joining his palms, he said, "This is Ānanda.
Spreading out both hands, he asked, "What is this? [He added,] "It puts people to shame! This was on an occasion when he ascended the hall. Day.
The moon may be cold; the moon may be hot. No demons can destroy the true teaching. Baoning, however, was not so: the moon may be cold; the sun may be hot;
yet even demons can destroy the true teaching. What, then, is the true teaching? "Planting rice in the tidal fields, one reaps a heavy harvest of grain;
meeting people on the village road, half are monks. Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Generally speaking, when performing such a task, one must open..."
With such a mouth, speaking such words, one must be such a person to begin with. But as for such a person—do they still agree with being spoken of in this way?
[The Master] shook his hand and said, "Lower your voices! Lower your voices! He ascended the hall and said: "Whether it be right or wrong, people do not know;
whether it be acting contrary or acting in accord, even Heaven cannot fathom it. Great Assembly, what is this? After a long silence, he said, "It exists."
When gold and jade are together, there is shared joy; when there is neither rice nor firewood, everyone frowns. Entering the hall: What is this that is so difficult to understand?
What is this that is so easy to comprehend? Do you understand thoroughly? It is not unless one is an enemy that they do not meet head-to-head.
Entering the hall: Upon this mass of red flesh is the True Person of No Rank. Eight *liang* in the left eye, eight *liang* in the right.
The eye is half a catty; buying high and selling low. Gold and silver. [Ascending the hall: I have a mouth, within which lies a tongue three inches long.
My teeth are all complete; there is no right or wrong that I do not speak. Zhaozhou’s wooden Buddha emits radiance; Shaoshi’s iron ox has its two horns broken.
[He strikes the meditation seat. Ascending the hall: The karma-mirror stands upon the dais; it is the thief’s own body.
"It is already exposed. Since the stolen goods are right here before you, why do you refuse to confess? Do you understand? Three thousand blows at dawn, eight hundred blows at dusk.
[The Master] descended from the hall and returned to his quarters. The frosty wind howls and the leaves fall in profusion; at dawn he enters the gate of an old villager’s deep-seated home.
Upon meeting, they simply sit together in silence, with not a single thing left to discuss. After a long while, he said:
It is easy to enter the mountains and capture a tiger; it is difficult to open one’s mouth toward others.
A monk asked Master Shishuang Chouzun of Tanzhou: “You do not speak of life, nor do you speak of death. Why do you not speak? The Master said:
“Once a word has been uttered, it passes from east to west. The monk asked: “What about then? The Master said: [Silence].

"Four horses are hard to overtake. [The Master] said, "Students do not all act in this way. The Master said, "It is easy to begin with words, but difficult to maintain the heart through the cold of winter.
The Layman Yù of Dìnglín Monastery in Chángshā Ténglíng was a native of his own province; he shaved his head at a young age and devoted himself solely to providing offerings for the Sangha.
This was his primary concern. His monastery was situated at a major thoroughfare where monks from various temples passed to and fro. One day, the master Făng-ch’i arrived as a visiting teacher.
The Master questioned him regarding the Chan school, and the teacher cited a monk’s question to Fa-teng: "How does one advance further atop a hundred-foot pole? Fa-teng replied, "Agh! (O!).

The Master investigated this from that point onward, never for a moment letting go of the thought. Once, while responding to an invitation elsewhere, he was riding a lame donkey across a bridge over a stream when the donkey—
His foot became stuck; as the master fell from his donkey, he involuntarily uttered the sound "Agh! and suddenly attained awakening. He composed a verse, saying:
"I possess a divine pearl, Long held captive by the dust of worldly toil. Today the dust is cleared and its light shines forth, Illuminating the myriad peaks of the mountains and rivers.
He went to visit Yangqi to seek formal confirmation (*kanna*).
The lay practitioner Sun of the Bibu Department came to visit Yangqi Hui. It happened that the Master was presiding over a legal case.

The official said, "I am bound by royal duties; by what means may I be released from them? Yangqi pointed at him and said, "Have you understood thoroughly? The official said, "I hope the Master will point it out for me."
Qiji said, "This is because the minister’s vast vows are profound and far-reaching, seeking to benefit all living beings. The official asked, "I do not yet understand how this is so.
Qiji showed him by means of a verse, saying: "Manifesting in the body of a civil official, He widely propagates his compassionate vows, which are deep. For the sake of people, he points out the way."
"Under the staff, blood flows profusely. At these words, the Master attained realization.
He was a successor in the thirteenth generation under Nanyue, a dharma heir of Chan Master Baiyun Yuan.
Chan Master Wuzu Fayan of Qizhou was the son of the Deng family from Mianzhou. At thirty-five, he first left the household life, shaved his head, and received full ordination.
He went to Chengdu to study the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra* and the *Śata-dharmaka-śāstra*. There, he heard that when a Bodhisattva enters the Path of Vision (*darśana-mārga*), [he realizes...]

When wisdom merges with principle and the objective realm unites with the spirit, there is no distinction between the subject that realizes and the object realized. Once, a non-Buddhist practitioner from the Western Regions challenged a Bhikṣu, saying:
"If you do not distinguish between the subject that realizes and the object realized, then by what means do you realize? No one could respond.

The non-Buddhist disparaged him, ordering that he be forbidden from sounding the bells and drums and forced to wear the *kāṣāya* robe in reverse. When Dharma Master Xuanzang arrived there, he rescued him.
The Master said, "It is like a person drinking water; whether it is cold or warm, they know it for themselves. This resolved the difficulty.

The Master continued, "One may know whether it is cold or warm, but what is this matter of 'knowing for oneself'? He then questioned the Head Lecturer, saying, "I do not understand the principle of 'knowing for oneself.
How is it so? The Lecturer did not doubt his question, but merely guided him, saying, "If you wish to clarify this, you should go to the South and seek out [a teacher]."

As one who transmits the Buddha’s mind-seal, the Master immediately took his books upon his back and crossed the mountain passes. Whichever venerable elders he encountered, he consulted them all on this matter, yet his doubts remained unresolved.
Eventually, upon visiting Yuanzhao Ben, all the karmic conditions of past and present were exhausted; however, there was only one point he did not understand:
a monk once asked Xinghua, "When they come from the four directions and the eight quarters, what then? Xinghua said, "Strike the one in the center. The monk... [acted].

The Master thought to himself, 'If that is the case, it is still far from sufficient. One day later, Yuan said to the Master:"
"I am old; I fear that I may have wasted your precious time. You should go and rely upon Baiyun. Although this old man is of later birth, I have not yet met him in person;

The Master wept as he paid his respects and took his leave. Upon arriving at Baiyun, he then raised the question: "A monk asked Nanquan, 'What is the mani-jewel?'"

The Master asked a question, and Yunfu scolded him. The Master attained realization and offered this verse of spontaneous inspiration: "A plot of vacant land before the mountain; With hands joined, I earnestly questioned the patriarchs:

Yunfu specifically granted him approval and ordered him to oversee the milling operations. Not long after, Yunfu came to him and said, "There are several Zen..."

When I cite causes and conditions to question them, they understand clearly; when I ask them to offer a phrase, they can offer one. Yet, it is simply not yet there.
The Master was greatly perplexed and thought to himself: "If they have already awakened, and can both speak and understand so clearly, why is this?"
"It is not yet so. He then spent several days in intensive investigation. Suddenly, he attained awakening; everything he had previously cherished was cast aside all at once.
He went to see Baiyun, who began to dance with hands and feet. The Master merely smiled.
Later, the Master said, "Because of this, I broke into a cold sweat and came to understand the 'breeze of a thousand carts. One day, Baiyun addressed the assembly, saying:
An ancient said: "It is like casting an image in a mirror; once the image is formed, where does the light reside? The assembly offered various responses, none of which were in accord with the truth.
Yunjian raised the case to ask his teacher, who stepped forward to pay his respects and said, "It is not even a matter of comparison.

Yunjian smiled and said, "One must be a true practitioner to achieve this," and thereupon ordered him to share the seat and instruct those yet to come. He first resided at Sifeng, then moved to Baiyun, and finally lived at [Mount] Nan.
Dongshan ascends the hall: "The Buddhas of the three periods look on from afar and pay homage; the Patriarchs of the six generations cannot open their mouths.
Today, I shall provisionally act as your guide. But tell me, what is it? One, two, three, four, five.
To boast of a cloth drum at the Gate of Thunder is to mock General Li; it is like shooting at a stone tiger in Lan-tian. Ascends the hall: "The Real..."
"Ordinary people and sages alike are all but dream-like words; Buddhas and sentient beings are merely designations.

Someone might come forward and say, "Old Man Panshan! To which you should simply reply: "Were it not for the early blossoming of flowers along the purple paths, how could the yellow oriole alight upon the willow branches?
If they ask further, say: "Old Man Simian [Sichuan] himself said, 'Be alert and awake! [He ascended the hall. Zhong.

[He] then descended from the seat. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Last night was the end of the year; this morning is the New Year’s Day. For the most part, these are but ordinary days."
People of the world harbor divergent views; they do not understand how to pursue the root source, but merely follow the branches and tendrils.

New and old are just as they are right now—look closely and clearly. If you attempt to deliberate further, it is like the "axle-rattling" of the Qin dynasty. The elders of various monasteries entered the mountain.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "When Linji enters the gate, he immediately shouts. What kind of sound is this? When Deshan enters the gate, he immediately..."
A blow of the staff! To bend what is crooked and make it straight. Yunmen’s three phrases, Caodong’s five ranks—this is to open one's eyes wide and yet dream on.
Why is this so? "At Guoqing, the talented are esteemed; in a wealthy house, the children are pampered. Upon arriving at Longmen, he ascended the hall:

"There is the ancient He Li; though he has no mouth, he is not mute. Seven out, eight in; refined and elegant. He then descended from his seat. Upon arriving [at the next temple], he ascended the hall.

When there are no seams or gaps, who knows its price? Is there anyone here who knows its price? He then said: "One, two, three, four, five. Upon arriving at Xinghua, he ascended the hall and said:
"Worldly affairs are as tangled as hemp; the path to the Empty Gate grows ever more remote. Among those guests beneath the green pine forest, how many [truly know it]?"
Having returned home, they sing the *Hujia* melody together; they part the five-petaled flowers. Fortunately meeting fellow practitioners, they ascend together upon the White Ox Cart.
"Great assembly, the cart is here; where is the ox? At the head of the fragrant grass ford, it cannot be found;
through the night, it remains as before, lodging among the reeds. Elder Ganluzi held the Master and said, "Shuzhou Guan."

[The Master] said: "Short! The horse is lean and its hair is long. Thus it is said: 'The Patriarch could not describe it; the Buddha-eye cannot see it.

With a grandmotherly heart on all four sides, I shall open a single thread for you. Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring air is now cold, now warm; the spring clouds sometimes roll up, sometimes unfurl.
This has drawn forth the Old Man of Shaoyang to release a fish from within the eye of a needle. He then said: "Wrong! [He then] thanked those who were present.
