The monk asked, "What is the King asking for the *santapa*? The Master said, "The imperial carriage has not yet been arrayed, yet the commands have already been issued.
The monk asked, "What is the *santapa*? The Master said, "The eyes glisten and the ears grow warm. The monk bowed. The Master said, "A dot. He then said, "Mañjuśrī..."
Raising the sails, Samantabhadra takes the helm; Mahāsthāmaprāpta and Avalokiteśvara join in the chanting. Thus they win the right to sit in meditation amidst the clamor of the two springs.
Sitting in meditation is indeed not a matter of doubt, but tell me: how does one sing the "Song of the Boat Descending the River"?
*Luo-luo-li, luo-luo-li*—worldly airs have not been removed. Ascending the hall: Tonight is the fifteenth day of the first month; heaven and earth are all one.
A Fragment. The Gate of Samantabhadra stands wide open. Meeting yet not seeing one another, he said: "In whom does the fault lie? Ascending the hall, he said: "Silence! Silence!
Unsurpassed Bodhi is attained from this very point. What a pity—people are deceived! He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Above is heaven; below is earth. North, south, east, and west remain as they were. Śākyamuni the Old Man merely plays with his own spirit. Da...
In the West, there are many taboos and prohibitions. Suddenly, if someone comes forward and says, "Monk, speak in a low voice," simply tell him:
"I only wish to throw a brick to draw out a jade. Ascending the hall, the mountain monk declares: Today, I shall turn the mountains, rivers, and the great earth entirely into gold.
Sentient and insentient beings alike shall all be made to attain Buddhahood. Only then will I enter this state of Great Peace. Not otherwise.
Preserving the Community. Why? Because there is not enough to be gained by contending, yet there is more than enough in yielding.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Tàipíng does not understand Chan; he has been wandering outside all along. On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, he will end up with nothing but a mouth.
But tell me, which one is Tàipíng’s mouth? He said himself: "I do not even recognize these two pieces of skin. Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Bǎoshòu acting as a street monk.
At that time, he saw two men quarreling. One struck the other with a single punch of his hand and said, "How can you be so shameless?
Bao-shou thereby attained entry. If one knows the point of this, it may be called both public and private discernment.
"Everyone, listen to this verse. It is most wonderful, most wonderful! Herein one knows life and destiny.
A snout-splitting blow and a single punch—right then, he struck it dead. He ascended the hall and said: "A fellow from the turbid waters of Taiping; every single matter has been thoroughly traversed.
Thus for three thousand years, there have been those who offered praise. But tell me, what did they praise? A fine fellow from the turbid waters!"

Han ascended the hall and said: "The teachings state: 'Even if the entire world were filled with those like Śāriputra, and they were to exhaust their thoughts together to measure it, they could not fathom the Buddha’s wisdom.
Now, when we examine the family of patch-robed monks, they give a high bow to Śākyamuni and do not prostrate before Maitreya."

This is to accord with the Buddha’s wisdom; it is not to accord with the Buddha’s wisdom. That which exists within the assembly exists, yet it is merely like hiding one’s tusks and concealing one’s claws.
In this Great Peace, there is a place of seeing; without sparing my eyebrows, I present it to all of you. I wait for someone to ask, and then I shall answer as the moment dictates.
Ascending the hall, he said: "With salt, it is called salty; without salt, it is called bland. When Taiping hears talk of the mouth, it is like a flat carrying-pole."

He descended from his seat and ascended the hall. His spiritual powers and wondrous functions lack not the slightest bit; for those who have attained thorough understanding, there is no need for further deliberation.
When the mud is deep, the Buddha is great; when the water rises, the boat grows high. Ascending the hall: "The single moon universally appears in all waters."
"All waters and moons are encompassed within a single moon. How true these words are! It may be said that it cannot be sculpted nor can it be painted.
Last night at the third watch, the moon was as bright as day. At the Dharma Hall, Master Xie addressed the assembly: "Though it is easy to transform the raw into the cooked,"
It is increasingly difficult for many voices to reach harmony. If one truly knows the flavor of saltiness and blandness, hunger and satiety will naturally not interfere with one another.
[The Master] ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said: "Last night at the third watch, I dreamed of this staff.
It instructed me to give a single piece of Chan. It told me: 'Master, tomorrow morning when you rise to ascend the hall, present this to the great assembly. Yesterday..."
Adding flowers upon brocade. Today, tread the solid ground. Just look at today; what will you say tomorrow regarding the intent of the Patriarchs?
Reflecting back on the Old Man of Yellow Face, his so-called "bestowal of prophecy at Vulture Peak" was but a deception—even the mountains and rivers of the great earth [are no more than this].
“Borrowing my nostrils to breathe out” is not as good as letting go of body and mind; then benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom will naturally manifest.
Ascending the hall, he said: “Today is the fifteenth day of the first month. I meet with you all: the tender wheat grows new shoots, every grain shall become flour.
Whether it is offered or not, it entirely depends on the fanning of the spring breeze. Ascending the hall, he raised his fist and said: “If you call this a fist...”
A fist. It is just like one who has never traveled on pilgrimage. If you do not call it a fist, you are deceiving me face-to-face.
Apart from this, you cannot be without a fist. Returning from the expedition, he ascends the hall and says: "I was away on the expedition for half a month; my eyes could not see my own nostrils.
I forgot the Zen of the Patriarchs and picked up a piece of junk. Tell me, where does it belong?"
[The offering is] presented. One portion is offered to Śākyamuni Buddha; one portion is offered to the Stūpa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha.
At the Hall, after thanking the Head Seat: Maitreya cannot see it; Śākyamuni cannot speak of it. Thus noble and precious, its daily application is without error.
Whether attained or not, whether recognized or not—its three virtues and six flavors are ever more abundant. For ten thousand ages, it remains so.
Regulations for the Ascending the Hall. A monk asked, "What is it like before the lamp is lit? The Master said, "It leaves people in doubt. "What is it like while the lamp is being lit?
The Master said, "Mistakenly identifying the zero point on the scale. "What is it like after the lamp has been lit? The Master said:

A moment of embarrassment ensued. He then said: "Every month there is a fifteenth; from beginningless kalpas until the time Maitreya descends to be born, there will inevitably be both sweetness and bitterness.
But tell me, what is it ultimately like? The white-fanged tiger of the South Mountain was originally the fierce tiger of the West Mountain.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The sun may grow cold, and the moon may grow hot; the various māras cannot..."
He was able to refute the true teaching. "Great Assembly, what is the true teaching? He spoke with such wild and reckless abandon that if you do not believe him, Baiyun will tell you for you:
"First, it must be understood by all people; second, it must be known by the dragons and spirits. Then, picking up his dharma robe, he said: "This is truly red;
one would be stubborn indeed to say it is crimson. Ascending the hall, [he said]: "The wind is gentle and the sun is warm. The ancient Buddhas..."
The family style: willows green, peach blossoms red. The true nose of the Patriarch: it must be recognized with one’s own hands and eyes; mere alertness of mind is not enough.
To be eloquent with mouth and tongue only distances one further from the Way. Those who enter through the gate do not possess the family treasure. But tell me, what is it ultimately like?
We have met again, yet there is nothing more to say; though you do not come, I still think of you. [The Master] ascends the hall, strikes his staff once, and then raises it, saying:
"Staff! I dare ask you: can you speak of the Buddha-dharma (Tathāgata-dhyāna)? He then says himself: "It cannot be spoken."
"Can you still speak of the Patriarch’s Zen? He replied, "I cannot speak of it. Since you cannot speak of it, Baiyun shall today express his own intention.

The monk asked, "How is it when the flower has not yet emerged from the water? The Master said, "Good. The monk asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the water?
The Master said, "Good. The monk asked, "What is the lotus flower? The Master said, "Good. The monk bowed. The Master said, "I have given him three 'Goods. All matters are resolved at once.
Lin asked, "I do not ask about 'hiding the world within the world. But as for this—[raising his fist]—what about this?"
“This—how would you hide it? The Master said, “What difficulty is there? He asked, “And how, for now, would you hide it? The Master said, “In the sleeve of my robe.
He asked, “I wonder, what kind of person is one who upholds the Buddha-dharma of Ji-gang? The Master said, “It cannot be a ghost.
He asked, “If one were suddenly to encounter someone who kills Buddhas and kills patriarchs, how would you deal with them? The Master said, “The old monk [would deal with him].”
[The Master] said, "There are those with eyes who have never seen. A student asked, "I am newly entering the monastery; I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "Eat your porridge and eat your rice; do not leave them behind your head. The student said, "Throughout the day I eat, yet I have never truly eaten.
The Master said, "You heartless monk; you do not recognize good from bad. [Another] asked, "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder about this—"
The monk said, "There is no such thing as 'bad' either. The Master said, "Who told you to ask such a question? The monk stepped forward, bowed, and said, "I hope you are well.
The Master said, "Is this 'bad' or not 'bad'? The monk was speechless. A monk asked, "What is Chan in the mountains? The Master said:
In the courtyard, tender bamboo sprouts forth its first shoots; beneath the mountain stream, the withered pines grow long branches. [The questioner] asked, "What is Chan in the marketplace?

The Master said, "The bells and drums of the six streets beat with a deep *dong-dong* resonance; it is right here within this world spread with gold. [The questioner] asked, "What is Chan in the village?
The Master said, "Thieves and bandits have vanished, silkworms and wheat are ripe; people sing and dance, rejoicing in peace and prosperity."
Question: "What is the place from which all Buddhas emerge? The Master said, "Your question is most appropriate. Question: "If one proceeds in this very manner, what then?
The Master said, "The answer is even more extraordinary. Question: "Because of the mountain one sees the water; seeing the water, one forgets the mountain."
"Mountains and waters are both forgotten; where does the principle return? The Master said, "The mountain monk has sat his tongue shut.
In the darkening of heaven and earth, there was an old master who offered this statement: "A thatched toilet is erected at the crossroads, yet people are not permitted to defecate therein.
A monk brought this up to question the Master. The Master said, "You have already defecated yourself; what more do you want anyone else to do?"
[The Master] defecated. Suwen [heard of this] and burned incense while gazing afar at Daisui, bowing twice in gratitude.

In the seventh month of the autumn of the Yimao year of the Xiaozong Shaoxing era, there was a great rain and snow, and strange omens appeared within the mountains. The Master said, "My time has come. On the seventeenth day, he passed away.
He took leave of the Prefect of Biejun. Three days later, he indicated a slight ailment while at Tianpeng.

On the night of the twenty-fourth, he said to his attendant monk, "When the sky dawns without moonlight, what then? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "It would have been better if you had taught me how to perform the cremation for you.
The following day, he returned to the Xiyuan Monastery in Pengkou and left behind his final instructions. He then passed away peacefully and serenely. His disciples...
He was enshrined with his entire body. Smoke and mist gathered from all four directions, and monkeys and birds wailed in grief.
When he was cremated, a wondrous fragrance pervaded the wilds; his tongue remained as it had been before. Relics of five colors were beyond counting.

He was interred to the west of the Dingguang Stupa. Tiantong Wenli composed a eulogy for the Master’s portrait, saying: "Among the assembly at Mount Dongshan, only he was not petty; elsewhere, he found leisure."
The Abbot’s quarters are difficult to investigate within the forest; from the pond at Fangshui, a snake emerges. Startling people with a dull iron cauldron, the rooster crows in broad daylight.
Amidst the performance of a farce, the full fire is kept on standby until late evening. Indolent and lax, he instead harmonizes with the mundane. The diligent Ba-zi sent someone to verify this;
casting down the incense and applying the seal reveals the true family style. Even if Dingguang had no Buddha, it would have been a waste of a cage.
As he was about to depart, he shook his bell toward the void; who would have known that the White Cloud school had been utterly extinguished?
Chan Master Wúwéi Zōngtài of Hànzhōu was a native of Fúchén. After leaving the Pass, he traveled extensively among the monastic communities.

Upon arriving at Wǔzǔ, on the day he presented incense, the Patriarch brought up the story of Zhàozhōu washing the alms bowl and assigned it for his investigation. When [Zōngtài] entered the room, the Patriarch again raised this same story.
He asked the Master, "Tell me, what did Zhaozhou say to him that the monk immediately attained awakening? The Master said, "He told him to go wash the bowl.
The Patriarch said, "You know only the matters of the road; you do not know the flavor of the road.
The Master said, "Since he knows the matters of the road, what flavor could there be on the road? The Patriarch said, "Do you not know? He asked again, "Have you understood?"
"Have you traveled through Zhejiang? The Master replied, "Not yet. The Patriarch said, "You have not yet attained awakening. From that time on, for five years, the Master was unable to respond.
One day, the Patriarch ascended the hall, looked at the assembly, and said, "An eighty-year-old old man rolls a brocade ball," and then descended from his seat.
The Master joyfully stepped forth from the assembly and said, "Preceptor, try rolling one round and see.

The Patriarch made a gesture with his hands as if beating a war drum and, singing in the Sichuan dialect, performed a folk song from Mianzhou, saying: "On Mount Douzi, they beat the earthen drums; On Mount Yangping, they scatter white rain.
As the white rain falls, they fetch the Dragon Maidens; They weave two zhang and five chi of silk, Half belongs to Luo Jiang, and half..."
Half [of the territory] belonged to Xuanwu. When the Master heard this, he attained great enlightenment. Covering the Patriarch’s mouth, he said, “It need only be chanted up to this point.

The Patriarch laughed heartily and returned home. Later, when the Master returned to Shu, the fourfold assembly requested that he open the Dharma at Wúwéi. He was subsequently appointed to the position of Zhèngfǎ and ascended the hall to give a formal address.

This great matter of cause and condition has, since the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kāśyapa smiled, been entrusted by the World-Honored One as the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye to Mahākāśyapa.
Thereafter, it has been passed down from lamp to lamp and transmitted from patriarch to patriarch until the present day, continuing unceasingly without falling into decline.
It has truly reached the point where flowers bloom everywhere on the ground; therefore, it is called Nirvana.

"Wondrous Mind. It is also called "Original Mind," "Original Nature," "The Original Face," "The Ultimate Truth (Paramārtha-satya)," "The Akṣobhya-Eye," and "Mahā-prajñāpāramitā. In a man it is called "man"; in a woman it is called "woman.
You all, simply awaken to it yourselves! All such things are merely idle words. [He then held up his whisk.]
Qifu said: "To understand it upon its arising is called Chan; yet for those who have not yet awakened, it is truly difficult, difficult, difficult—before one's eyes stands a Mount Sumeru.
Once awakened, it is easy, easy, easy; whatever comes from the mouth is nothing but the truth.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Who told you to ask such a question? As the monk hesitated, the Master said, "Understood!"
Chan Master Baizhi of Wuzhuo was a native of Huai’an. He initially relied upon the Fifth Patriarch for the longest period of time, yet he had not yet attained realization.
At that time, Yuanwu served as the Seat-Holder (Zuoyuan). The Master went to seek his instruction, and Yuanwu said, "If you have a point of doubt, try telling me about it.
The Master then cited the passage from Deshan’s informal sermon: "I do not answer questions; those who ask questions receive thirty blows of the staff. Yuanwu said, "Prostrate yourself!"
"I have become your teacher, yet you still do not understand this story. After the master had finished bowing, Wuzu asked him to repeat the previous story.
The master said, "Deshan’s informal sermon says he does not answer questions. Wuzu covered his mouth and said, "Just look at it like this.
The master went out and cried out loudly, "A grievance! A grievance! How can there be such a public case? It merely teaches people to look into the principle of a single phrase. There was a monk...

He said to the Master, "Brother, you must not speak in such a manner. The Head Seat must employ skillful means. Because he sat in quiet meditation and investigated this for ten days, his doubts were suddenly resolved.
He went to see Wuzhuo to pay his respects and express his gratitude. Wuzhuo said, "Brother, you have finally realized that I did not deceive you.

He then went to the Abbot’s quarters; the Patriarch (Zongmi) welcomed him with a smile. From then on, his understanding of the profound and mysterious depths grew daily. When the Patriarch was about to pass away, he left a message to the Prefectural Governor.
Shouming succeeded him on the seat, and monks arrived from all directions in such numbers that they could not be stopped. The Master posted a notice at the door of the attendants' quarters, saying:
"Dongshan has three statements; if anyone can explain them, they shall be granted formal enrollment. The monks were all disheartened.
One day, a monk carrying his sitting mat went straight to the master’s chamber and said to him, "I cannot explain them, but I simply wish to be enrolled. The Master— [was greatly pleased].
Xì called for the *vinaya-dhara* to prepare the high seat beneath the bright window for the formal discourse (*shàngtáng*). When the World-Honored One held up a flower, Kāśyapa smiled.
People of that time knew only of the holding up of the flower and the smile, yet they failed to recognize the World-Honored One.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Dancing the *zhèzhī* within a thicket of brambles. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha?"
The Master said: "A newborn child throws away a golden basin.
Chan Master Daochu of Longhua in Qizhou was the son of the Ma family of Zizhou; he served as the attendant to the Fifth Patriarch for many years.
He went out to reside at Longhua. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "When a rooster sees another, it fights; when a dog sees another, it bites.

The *chīwén* (ceramic ridge-end ornaments) atop the hall face one another all day long—why do they never grow angry? The Master’s wit and eloquence were sharp and swift, yet his disciples were unable to fathom the depth of his realization.
One day he said to the assembly, "Yesterday I left the city; white clouds drifted to and fro in the void. The pine wind cleansed my ears and eyes;
it was truly superior to the human world. He then summoned the assembly and said, "This is the final word of my late master. After a short while, he passed away with serene composure.

Chan Master Qing-su of Jiuzheng was the son of the Guo family in that prefecture. He received the tonsure and ordination at Qianming Temple and traveled extensively, knocking at the gates of various Chan masters.
Later, he visited Wuzu Fayan; upon hearing Wuzu cite the words of Shoushan regarding the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, he attained sudden enlightenment.
He recited a verse: "Inversion upon inversion, topsy-turvy; The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. To act thus is utterly groundless;
Turning one's head, one does not notice the robe has been torn. When the Patriarch saw this, he asked, "As for Baizhang’s story of the wild fox, what do you say?
The Master said, "Those who come to speak of right and wrong are themselves the people of right and wrong. The Patriarch was greatly pleased. After some time, the Master took his leave.
He returned and resided at Qingxi. Later, he moved to Jiuding.
When Governor Lü came to visit the Great Image, he asked, "Since this is the Great Image, why does it carry two pillars on its shoulders? The Master replied, "There are no idle hands on a boat.

Upon reaching the pavilion and beholding the Avalokiteśvara image, he asked again, "This is the realm of Maitreya; from where has Avalokiteśvara come? The Master replied, "In a wealthy household, the young children are spoiled."
Shou performed a prostration. When Qin Lao arrived, the Master asked, "When the sword is at the throat of the dance, what then? Qin replied, "I humbly pray that you will accept this offering.
The Master scolded him, saying, "Old thief! Go die! You ask me! Qin then repeated his previous words and questioned him again. The Master folded his hands, bowed, and said, "Drag it apart!
On the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month in the year of Yimao during the Xiaoshing era of Emperor Gaozong of the Song dynasty.
He fell slightly ill and wrote a verse to his followers, saying: "The wooden man prepares the boat; the iron man prepares the horse.
The child of the Bing and Ding stems mounts steadily; with a shout, he scatters the white clouds and returns home. Thereupon, he passed away into stillness.
The Head Seat Yuanli was a native of Min. He had studied under Jiaoshan and initially attended lectures with Baiyun.
Whenever he entered the room for instruction, Baiyun would invariably say, "Monks, you must clearly distinguish between the black and the white. The Master harbored persistent doubts about this.
One day, as Baiyun ascended the hall, he cited the saying, "The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it," and asked, "Do you all understand? Do not..."
He asked the bride and her mother-in-law, "To avoid troubling you on the road, when I meet with rice, I eat rice; when I meet with tea, I drink tea.
We enter and exit through the same gate—old enemies from past lives. At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened and said, "Today, the distinction between the monastic and the lay is clear.

In the Jiumao year of the Yuanfu era of the Song dynasty (1099), Chang'an Yan invited him to occupy the seat at his ancestral mountain, but he declined the offer to share the dais. When Yan passed away, [he immediately...]
He departed. During the Chongning era, he returned once more to Wuzu. A monk asked, "Where has Wuzu gone after his parinirvāṇa?
The Master said, "Having eyes but no ears, sitting by the fire in the sixth month. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "When one's house is poor, it is still tolerable;
when one's path is poor, it brings one to despair. Or, someone asked: "The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* says, 'All wholesome dharmas...'"
"What is the Dharma? The Master said, "Above is heaven; below is earth. Those sitting in the middle sit; those standing stand. What do you call 'wholesome Dharma'?
The monk had no reply, so the Master struck him. Later, he passed away at Ruiyan in Siming.
Puyong Zhizang was a native of Fuzhou. He was the next to enter the room of the Fifth Patriarch. The Patriarch brought up the story of the "Two Women and the Separated Souls" to question him;
Zhizang attained a realization and presented this verse: "The two women merge into one daughter-in-law; The wheel of mechanism is severed, impossible to intermingle."
From the beginning, his coming and going have left no trace. Travelers, do not ask for the path he took when he arrived.

Whenever a monk from the local area came to visit, he would speak in the Min dialect and recite these vernacular lines: "At the beginning of the letter, I instruct my mother to be diligent in her rest;
at the end of the letter, I instruct my mother not to nod off. Now tell me, what did he say in between? As soon as a monk attempted to answer, the Master would immediately push him out.

The Elder Fashu had long relied upon the Fifth Patriarch without yet attaining realization. One day he went to the patriarch’s quarters, and the patriarch asked, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion?
Fashu replied, "Fashu is not like that. The patriarch pointed his finger and said:
"Stop, stop! The Dharma-multitude is not so. How is it? At this, the Master was awakened. Later, he went to Donglin and sat beneath the seat of Master Xuanmi.
There he saw that [Xuanmi] had attained the principle of "evenness and reality.

One day, [Xuanmi] held up a flower, walked once around the meditation platform, turned his back, and inserted the flower into the incense burner, saying, "Master, tell me: what is the meaning of this? Xuandu repeatedly descended from his seat.
[The monk] spoke, but none of it accorded with [the Master's intent]. After two months had passed, he finally asked the Master to try explaining it for him.
The Master said, "I simply took some flowers and stuck them in the incense burner; you yourself were suspicious—what business was there in that?"
A monk asked Zen Master Zixian of Chengtian Monastery on Mount Heng in Tanzhou, successor to Zen Master Yungai Ben: "The assembly has already gathered and awaits your thunderous voice;
now that you have ascended the lion throne, we pray that you will reveal the truth. The Master said, "Performing somersaults atop the top of the flagpole. The monk said, "In that case..."
"Then auspicious mists will rise before Mount Yue-lu, and auspicious clouds will form beneath Mount Zhurong. The Master said, "Within the purple silk curtain, glistening pearls.
He ascended the hall, took up his staff, and said, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing.
He struck the meditation seat once and said, "For you, I shall shatter the cave of spiritual numinosity; though soil be tossed and dust raised, there is nowhere to go."
Investigating: A thousand mountains, ten thousand mountains, all starkly protruding. Striking once more, he said: "Return to the hall. [End of] Session. Ascending the hall:
One body in high seclusion, only at Mount Nanyue; I laugh at myself, for even this solitary cloud is not yet at ease.

He who sits upright by the pines and waters must also, according to custom, speak of dwelling in the mountains. *Du!* [Strike! Ascending the hall: The waning moon falls at the fifth watch; dawn breaks white.
Clouds fly. This is clearly a matter before one’s eyes, yet it is not the mechanism of the present moment. Since it is a matter before one’s eyes, why is it not the mechanism of the present moment?
After a long silence, he said: "Wishing to speak, words fail; beneath the forest trees, they deliberate."

Chan Master Hui-lian of Chengtian Temple on Mount Nanyue in Changsha ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Chengtian? The Master picked up his whisk and held it up. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm?
The Master struck the meditation seat once with the whisk and said, "The person and the realm have already been pointed out by the Master.
The monk asked, "As for the ultimate vehicle of the ancestral school, what is it like? The Master hung the whisk back on its stand.
At the old site, he said: "In recent days, things have changed somewhat in Hunan. The light snow has fallen on time and according to the season;

it merely piles up like mountains and mounds, regardless of whether it is the cold of spring or the heat of autumn. A-he-he! Truly delightful. The fragrance of the yellow tangerines beneath the courtyard does not reach [the senses].
Ascending the hall, he said: "Recognize the ancient Buddha in the midst of the bustling marketplace. Realize the old monk upon the tips of the hundred grasses. Bustling!"
Setting aside for a moment the ancient Buddha within the marketplace, how will you, O old monk atop the hundred blades of grass, realize him? After a long silence, he said:
"It is not that one boasts of being a skilled hand to those met; it is simply that one's character naturally accords with elegance."
Chan Master Weide of Xiangshan in Luling, Jixian, ascended the hall. A monk asked, "When one ascends the lion’s seat and lets out the lion’s roar, what then?
The Master said, "Step back three paces. The monk asked, "If Mañjuśrī should suddenly appear, what would you do? The Master said:
Standing downwind, he said: "Sitting alone within a thatched hut, Śāriputra has not yet understood;
the devas and nāgas do not know at all from where the rain of flowers falls. Mahākāśyapa merely closed his room; Vimalakīrti’s mouth was left empty and shut.

Upon waking from sleep, a single cup of tea—this is a flavor entirely distinct. He gave a shout. Ascending the hall, he said: "Difficult, difficult! Even a hair's breadth still leaves ten thousand layers of separation."
Mountains! How easy, how easy! In a single kṣaṇa, one arrives at the ground of non-birth. One can truly admire Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti, the two of them discoursing so vigorously on non-duality.
This mountain monk, however, says it is difficult, difficult. To discern with clarity—look for yourself!
Chan Master Qing of Zhizheng at Guanyi Rock on Mount Heng in Hengzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Zhizheng?
The Master said, "In the stone chamber the night is deep and the frosty moon is white; the grass robes have grown old and the rush mats are cold. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "Carrying a staff to welcome the distant waters; washing the bowl to catch the morning meal. The monk asked, "Beyond this..."
"Is there anything else? The Master said, "A wooden horse neighs in the wind; a clay ox crosses the sea. He then said, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing.
Let loose the falcon of the vast sky—do you see it? Under the clear breeze and the moon, the man who waits by the stump;
the cool rabbit grows distant as the spring grass turns green. With a shout, he ascended the hall. "All day long in a blur, what is that matter?"
"No hindrance. But tell me: what is that matter? After a long silence, he said: "The fallen leaves know the flowing water; the returning clouds recognize the old peak.
[He was] a Dharma successor of Chan Master Xianglin Chengxian.

Yudao Po was a native of Jinling. She made her living selling oil-cakes and regularly followed the assembly to visit Langya for instruction. Langya showed her the koan of Linji’s "Unlocated True Person.

One day, she heard a beggar singing the "Lotus Music" (Lianhua Yue), which said: [...text omitted... (Note: As the source text provided here is incomplete, the translation reflects the portion available.)
"If it were not for Liu Yi’s transmission of a letter, by what means could I have reached Lake Dongting? Suddenly she attained great enlightenment;
she threw her rice-cake tray to the ground. Her husband looked askance and said, "Are you mad? His wife slapped him and said, "This is not your realm. He went to see Langya.
Fayan Xie gazed at him and, recognizing his level of realization, asked, "Who is that person of no rank? Ba responded instantly, saying: "There is a person of no rank;
six arms and three heads, he exerts himself in wrath. With one snap of the fingers, Mount Hua is split in two;
the ten-thousand-year flowing waters know nothing of spring. From this, his reputation spread far and wide. When Yuanwu was inaugurating the hall at Jiangshan, Ba arrived at the Dharma assembly.
Before the seat, the old woman leaped out from among the assembly; she pressed her body against him once and then returned to the group.
Huizhu said, "To see the strange is not strange; the strangeness destroys itself. The next day, Huizhu went to her home, but the old woman did not come out.
He spoke in a stern voice, saying, "A child with such yellow lips claims he has come out to open the hall and preach the Dharma. Huizhu said, "Old woman, stop showing off your wares; I know you."
"You have understood me," the old woman said, and she laughed loudly. She went out to meet [the visitor]. Whenever a monk arrived, she would say, "Child, child!
If the monk hesitated, she would immediately close the door. Fodeng Xun went to test her; when the old woman saw him, she questioned him as she had before. Xun said:
"Where is my father? The old woman turned around and bowed to a pillar. Xun immediately kicked it over and said, "I thought there was something truly extraordinary here.
He then went out. The old woman scrambled up and said, "Come back, my son! Come back, my son! I recognize you! But Xun paid her no heed.
When An Shouzuo arrived, the old woman asked, "Where have you come from? An replied, "From Deshan. The woman said, "Deshan Tai was indeed a son of an old woman.
An asked, "Whose son are you, old woman? The woman said, "Having been questioned by you, Senior, I am driven to stand right here and urinate.
The old woman once composed a verse on the occasion of Mazu’s illness, which says: "Sun-face, Moon-face, empty..."
A flash of lightning in the void. Although it cuts off the tongues of all the monks under heaven, it clearly says only half the truth.

reviewed by the Abbot of Kokegwan-ji Temple in Kyoto, the Monk (臣) Chōkei; presented for imperial inspection.
Dharma heir of Chan Master Zhaojue Qin of the Fifteenth Generation under Nanyue in the Linji School.
Chan Master Shaolong of Huqiu in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of Hanshan in Huazhou. At the age of nine, he took leave of his family and entered Fohui Monastery.

After more than six years, he received the tonsure and full ordination. Another five years passed before he traveled to Longbao to pay respects to Changlu Zongxin, from whom he grasped the general outlines of the teachings.
When a transmission of Yuanwu’s words reached him, the Master read them and sighed, saying, "It is like imagining the sourness of a liquid that has not yet been produced; although it is not yet..."
It washes the intestines and drenches the stomach, truly bringing one a sense of joy and liberation; my only regret is that I have not yet heard his voice.

He then proceeded from Baofeng to rely on Zhantang, stayed as a guest at Huanglong to consult Sishin, and subsequently visited Yuanwu. One day, upon entering the inner chamber for instruction, Yuanwu asked:

"When seeing the seeing, the seeing is not the seeing. Seeing is already apart from seeing; seeing cannot reach it. He raised his fist and asked, "Do you see it? The Master said, "I see. Baizhang said, "This is placing a head on top of a head.

Upon hearing this, the Master attained a sudden realization. Baizhang rebuked him, saying: *Note: This passage describes a pivotal encounter between Mazu Daoyi (the Master) and Baizhang Huaihai. The dialogue concerns the nature of perception and the transcendence of dualistic views.*
"What have you seen? The Master replied, "The flowing water passes through even where the bamboo is dense. Yuanwu approved of this. Subsequently, he was appointed to oversee the library.
Someone asked Yuanwu, "Master Long, if a storekeeper is as gentle and yielding as this, how can he accomplish anything? Yuanwu said, "He is a sleeping tiger.
Later, he returned to his home district and resided at Kaisheng Temple west of the city. During the disturbances of the Song dynasty’s Jianyan era, he built a thatched hut on Copper Peak.
Below this, the Prefectural Governor Li Guang invited him to reside at Zhangjiao; subsequently, he moved to Huqiu. His Way became widely manifest.

Thereupon, reflecting upon the precedent established by Baizhen Yuan at the Ancestral Hall, he said: "As one who follows after [a master], how can it be right in principle not to personally practice their bequeathed instructions?
He then had his portrait painted and enshrined it there. Upon ascending the hall for a discourse, a monk asked: "By means of the One..."
"How is it when one layer departs another layer? The Master said, "A dull bird leaves its nest. [The monk] asked, "How is it when one does not depart one layer with another layer?
The Master said, "As swift as a split arrow. [The monk] said, "It is just like Muzhou saying: 'Yesterday I planted eggplants.'"
"Today I planted a winter melon. Furthermore, how is it? The Master said, "The eyes look toward the southeast, but the mind is set on the northwest.
[The monk] said, "Thank you for answering my question, Master. The Master said, "I have lost today. He then said, "This monk asked in such a way, and I answered in such a way.
Now tell me, did he see Muzhou’s meaning, or did he not see Muzhou’s meaning? If you say he saw Muzhou..."
"Intention! Now tell me: what was Muzhou’s intention? If you say you do not see Muzhou’s intention, then the question and answer we just had cannot have been in vain.
Today I shall open another path for you all to travel east or west.
[The Master] suddenly picked up his staff, struck it once, and let out a shout. [He] ascended the hall. A monk asked, "An ancient said..."
The entire expanse of heaven and earth is gathered up as small as a grain of millet and scattered before everyone’s eyes.

Yet the "lacquer buckets" do not understand; beat the drum and invite all to look! I wonder what the meaning of this is? The Master said: "In a single mu of land, there are three snakes and nine rats.
The monk said: "I do not yet understand the Master's meaning; I beg the Master for further instruction. The Master said: "It is difficult to express with a mouth as vast as the sea."
[The monk] said, "The entire earth is already as small as a grain of millet. As for the myriad phenomena, humans, animals, grasses, and shrubs—where do they reside?
The Master said, "This question is not bad. [The monk] said, "Is there no expedient means? The Master said, "One cannot die even if struck with a staff.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "Half is saved. He then said, "An imperial decree within the realm; beyond the frontier..."

The General’s Command: With a single phrase, heaven and earth are settled; with a single sword, the world is pacified. Thus one sees the times prosperous and the Way flourishing, and the four seas at peace.
Yet, under the gate of this monk, it is not so. The staff has swallowed up heaven and earth; there is not even a hair’s breadth of leakage.
Where else could there be a single thing to serve as a condition for people? For their sake...

"Yes. "Do you understand? After a long silence, he said, "Each of you, please return to the hall to drink tea. Ascending the hall, he said: "The ox-head is lost, the horse-head returns. He has no land;
the True Person of No Rank suddenly emerges, difficult to discern. Where do you encounter him?
Like sparks struck from stone, like a flash of lightning—whether you attain it or not, you cannot avoid losing your body and life. But tell me, when the wind is calm and the waves are still..."
A single phrase. How do you say it? "Since Shancai departed, who has recognized him? The pavilion doors remain open all day long. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
"What is the true source of the Great Way? The Master said: "Muddling through the mud and blending with the water.
The monk asked: "If one goes forth in this manner, what then? The Master said: "Cut off the heel of your straw sandals. He then said: "The Great Way is right before your eyes."

[The Master] stepped forward. "For now, it is difficult to perceive before one's eyes. If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, speech, and language.
Where the wind cannot enter, it blends with water; where it blends with mud and water, the wind cannot enter.
Even now, you cannot avoid it, yet you further place a head upon your own head. He then raised his whisk and said, "Do you see this? This is form."
Again, he laughed loudly and said: "This is sound. Where is the true essence of the Great Way? A pair of mandarin ducks is embroidered, yet there is no back;
who knows how to find the golden needle? Ascending the hall, he said: "The eye does not admit a grain of sand."
"Water does not enter the ear. How laughable is old Kūṭi! Pointing upward at no cause or reason. "O Zen practitioners, tell me:
who is it that understands this laughter? Do you understand? From the midst of a bustling marketplace, he presses out the Kauśika;

his tongue is three thousand miles long! Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Great wisdom is perfectly luminous; its essence has no front or back. It is still, profound, and tranquil, pervading the great [expanse]."
Empty. It covers heaven and earth; its constant light is uniquely revealed. Traces are erased and footprints extinguished; it is free from form and beyond name.
At this very moment, when the ground is unmoving—how do you speak this one phrase? "All waters and moons are subsumed within the single moon.
[The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks, "I request the Master to answer my question. The Master says, "A mass of fire clouds burns the sky. The monk says, "But tell me, does empty space still..."
"Is there transformation, or not? The Master said, "Satiated with gruel, satiated with rice. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then there is transformation.
The Master said, "What transformation is there for a hired laborer? He then said: "The scorching heat steams the people;
sweat is like boiling broth. That which Yanquan employs—is it ever ordinary? Do not ask about the light shaking; the rhinoceros is there. He brings it forth, and the pure wind cools the universe."
"Virtuous practitioners of the various dhyānas, where have you been looking for Old Man Yan-guan? If you can see him, his kindness will be difficult to repay;
if not, your sweat will soak through your back. Once, when he had applied himself with effort once, he immediately betrayed his heart on the Mid-Autumn Festival.
Ascending the hall, he cited the case of the two senior monks, Shen and Ming, who were traveling together. They saw a fish leap out of the net. Ming said, "How magnificent!"
He was just like a monk. Xuedou said, "How is it? It would have been better not to enter the net at that time.
Baofeng Ming said, "Brother Shen, you still owe me an awakening. After traveling several li, Shen finally attained realization. The Master said, "Upādhyāya Ming had bait on his hook;
the old Chan master Shen took the single cast and was hauled in. Had Tiger Hill seen him at that moment, when he said, 'Brother Shen, you...'"
There is still a lack of awakening. I simply reply: "Today I have caught one in the net;
this not only silences Master Ming, but also ensures that for a thousand ages to come, no one will mock me. I, this mountain monk, possess a single all-encompassing net.
He then raised his whisk and said, "Do you see it? I, this mountain monk, have already called it a 'whisk.
But what do you all call it? If you call it a 'whisk,' you have not yet escaped my net.
If you do not call it a 'whisk,' where is the eye of a traveling monk? You people—do you still see where I, Tiger Hill, am acting for others?"
"Ma! The third wave surges high with a thunderous crash; in one sound, it penetrates the Dragon Gate of Yu. Ascending the hall, he said:

"Light does not illuminate objects, and objects do not exist. When both light and objects are forgotten, what is this? Let us set aside for a moment the laying down of arms at the tips of the hundred grasses.
Suddenly, if the Great Elephant of Jiazhou were to ride backward, and the Iron Ox of Shanyu were to grasp Mount Sumeru—"
"A mountain! A single blow and it is smashed to pieces. Riding a horse through the land of Silla; preaching Chan in Jambudvīpa. But how about this? On Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice;
before the steps of the Buddha Hall, there is dog-urine sky. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Day after day the sun rises in the east;
day after day the sun sets in the west. Human life lies in a single breath; a hundred years pass in a mere flash. Suddenly—
The ground meets the stream; the cave of birth and death is overturned, releasing the falcon from the vast heavens.

A single breakthrough through ten thousand layers of clouds; the entire earth is gathered up as a grain of millet. Within a single hair-tip, heaven and earth appear. Dwelling at home is not separate from the journey;
one is always on the road without ever leaving the gate. (He lets out a shout. A monk asked: "Xuefeng addressed the assembly..."
The Way: The entire earth is this gate of liberation. One may hold out a hand to lead someone in, yet they will not enter. I wonder, who is it that remains outside the gate?
The Master said, "Hū Zhangsan and Hē Lisi. [The monk] asked, "Why do they refuse to enter?
The Master said, "They possess the eyes of a traveling mendicant. [The monk] said, "In that case, they have passed right through the nostrils of all the ancestral masters of the past."
The Master said, “Can you leap out of this, *ācārya*? He replied, “If that were so, though one might live for three steps, one must die at the fifth.

The Master said, “You still owe me one question. He replied, “Does the Master not provide a moxibustion treatment for the sake of his students? The Master said, “You have mistaken the zero-point on the scale.
He ascended the hall and said, “In the kingdom of Magadha, this edict was personally enacted. He then suddenly picked up his staff.
[He] struck the meditation desk once and said: "A large month has thirty days; a small month has twenty-nine. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The true body is revealed in its full majesty before one's eyes. Do not say that it was bestowed upon Yinguang in those days.
Since he was a man of great capacity, so am I; do not further scar good flesh with a wound. Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Minister Chen Cao visiting Zifu. When Zifu saw him...
As he approached, [Fuzhao] drew a circle. Zhao said, "When my disciple came this way, I was already not quite right;
yet you have drawn another circle. Fuzhao then shut the door. The Master said, "Zifu bought iron and got gold—a great display of wealth and honor.
While this is so, the public case remains unresolved. Today, all you Great Beings have come into the mountains to meet me; I, the mountain monk, will not..."
He drew a circle and did not even close the gate of his quarters. Tell me, is this one with the Elder Zifu, or two? Do you know where it lands?
"Meeting at the bamboo courtyard, there is nothing to do; everyone drinks Zhaozhou’s tea together. Entering the hall:
The hundred birds do not come, yet spring is warm again; leaning on the railing, the water before my eyes is like the sky. Mindless, he returns.
"Like tonight’s moon, it illuminates the three thousand and the great chiliocosm. Ascending the hall for the informal session: "Sickness has arisen;

clouds, mountains, grasses, and trees are in autumn. The fleeting affairs of the world drift aimlessly. From the beginning, the myriad dharmas have been no companions. How can they compare to Shao Yang’s ‘Six Non-acceptances’?
[He lets out a shout. Ascending the hall: "Leaves fall and return to the root. Originally there was no mouth; nothing remains."
The traces of my footsteps: I have leaped up into the fires of the Big Dipper; a cricket has swallowed the Great Elephant of Jia Prefecture.
The horse’s belly in Yi Prefecture swelled without its knowing it; the lanterns and the pillars laughed aloud; Shi-de and Han-shan clapped their hands. Do you understand?
Do not wait for right and wrong to enter your ears; those who were once close friends will turn into enemies. Ascending the hall, he said: "I have already understood how to cast off the body."

*The Dream of the Southern Branch*. One first realizes that all affairs in the human world are empty. Blowing forth the unperforated flute for returning home, the setting sun slants upon the crimson of the azure clouds.

In the summer of the Bingchen year of the Shaoxing era during the Song dynasty, Emperor Gaozong, having been afflicted by a slight illness, addressed the assembly on the eighth day of the fifth month, saying:
"Zongda, the First Seat, shall succeed me in the affairs of the monastery. The assembly requested permission from the local administration, which granted it accordingly.
When the matter was concluded, he took up his brush and wrote a verse in large characters, saying: "There is no dharma that can be taught; this is called teaching the Dharma.
Thus, in the Buddha-dharma, there are no superfluous words. "Take care," he said, and casting aside his brush, he passed away. A stupa was erected on the southern slope of his home mountain.
He was sixty years of age and forty-five years of *saṃgha*-seniority.
Chan Master Dahui Pu-jiao Zonggao of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture was the son of the Xi family of Xuancheng. At the age of thirteen, he entered the local school.
One day, he sighed and said, "For a man of great purpose, why study worldly books rather than investigate the supramundane Dharma?
He immediately went to Huiyun Monastery on East Mountain and served under Master Huiqi. At seventeen, he shaved his head and received full ordination in the Vinaya. Once, by chance—

I read the *Record of Yunmen* and felt as if it were something familiar from my past training. Formerly, I relied upon Guangjiao Cheng and once requested instruction on Xuedou’s verses on ancient cases (*songgu*) and the causal conditions (*nidāna*) of ancient masters;
however, I did not find resonance there. Subsequently, I met with the venerable elders Taiyang Yuan and Dongshan Wei.
Having attained their explanations, I went to Mount Baofeng to pay my respects to Zantang Zhun. Master Zhun regarded me with favor and had me attend to him by carrying his robes and towel. One day—
Daitō asked, "Why is it that your nostrils are missing one half? The Master said, "Under the gate of Bōhō. Daitō said, "A fabricated Zen monk!
Later, while the images of the Ten Kings were being sculpted, Daitō pointed to one and asked, "What is this official's surname? The Master said, "His surname is Ryō.
Daitō patted his head and said, "But for one with the surname Ryō, there is lacking a *bokuto* (head-covering). The Master said, "Though the *bokuto* is lacking," [the name remains].
One day, Dahui Zonggao’s teacher, Dahui Zongmen, said to him, “Upādhyāya Gaofeng, as for this little bit of Chan I possess, can you comprehend it point by point?
Gaofeng replied, “I can comprehend it. Dahui said, “If I were to teach you to speak it, you could speak it; if I were to teach you to practice it, you could practice it.
You would be capable of all things—citing ancient cases, composing verses on them, giving small sermons, or giving general lectures. However, there is only one thing that is not right.”
"Do you still understand? The Master asked, "I do not yet know what matter this is. The Hall Monitor said, "You simply lack that one sound of 'effort' (*li*).
That is why it is said: when spoken, it exists; when unspoken, it is absent. When entering the abbot’s quarters, it exists;
when leaving the abbot’s quarters, it is absent. When alert and awake, it exists; when fast asleep, it is absent. How can you withstand birth and death? The Master said, "Precisely..."

This was where Zonggao harbored his doubts. When Master Tang was on the verge of death, he instructed the Master, saying, "After I am gone, you should see Chuanqin; he will surely be able to fully exhaust your potential.
After Master Tang passed away, the Master hurried to pay his respects to the Layman Wujin to request an inscription for Master Tang’s stupa.

The Layman Wujin maintained a high standard in his gate and rarely granted approval to anyone; however, upon finding that he shared a mutual accord with the Master in a single word, he provided him with lodgings and invited him in, naming the Master’s hermitage "Miao" (The Sublime).
Xī visited him again later and was further instructed to go see Yuánwù. When the Master arrived at Tiānníng, one day he heard Yuánwù ascend the hall and cite a monk’s question to Yúnmén:
“What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? Yúnmén replied, “Water flows uphill on the eastern mountain.
“If it were Tiānníng,” [Yuánwù] said, “it would not be so. Suppose someone were to ask me: ‘What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?’”
He simply said to him: "The fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. At these words, the Master suddenly had the barriers of past and future severed.
Although the appearance of movement did not arise, he remained sitting in a state of pure nakedness. Wuzhuo said to him:
Nor is it easy for you to attain this field. It is a pity that once dead, one cannot return to life.
Not doubting the words and phrases is itself a great illness. Have you not heard it said: "Letting go at the edge of a precipice, one spontaneously takes it up; after death, one revives again"?
"You may not deceive the Master. You must believe that this principle exists. He then had him reside in the Zhemu Hall as a *shizhe* (attendant) who did not manage administrative affairs.

Every day, he entered the room together with the *shidafu* (scholar-official). Yuanwu would frequently raise the question, "There is a phrase, there is no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree," and ask him about it.
As soon as the Master opened his mouth, Yuanwu would say, "Not so, not so. After half a year had passed, the Master finally questioned Yuanwu.
He said, "I heard that when you were with the Fifth Patriarch at that time, you once asked this same question.
I do not know what the Fifth Patriarch said. Wuzu smiled but did not answer. The Master said, "At that time, you must have asked it before the assembly; there would be no harm in saying it now.
Wuzu, having no choice, said, "The meaning of my question—'Is there a phrase or is there no phrase? Like a vine leaning against a tree?'—was as follows:"
"What? the Patriarch asked. "It cannot be traced; it cannot be painted. He was further asked, "What is it like when the tree falls and the vines wither?
The Patriarch replied, "It has followed along. The Master immediately attained release and said, "I understand!

Wuzhuo then cited several karmic causes and conditions to cross-examine him, but the Master responded without hesitation. Wuzhuo said, "Now I know that I did not deceive you," and he subsequently composed [the verse].
He was entrusted with the *Linji Zhengzong Ji* (Record of the True Lineage of Linji) and appointed to oversee the secretariat. Before long, he was ordered to share the seat [with the master].
In the meditation hall, he wielded a bamboo staff to test his students; thus, the monastic community came to revere him profoundly, and his fame resounded throughout the capital.

The Right Chancellor, Lü Shuntu, submitted a memorial requesting that he be granted the purple robe and the title "Buddha Sun" (*Furi*). Shortly thereafter, the Jurchen rebellion broke out, and its leader intended to seize the Chan masters.

There were about ten monks in the assembly, and the Master was among those selected; thus, he was spared from having to go to Wu. He spent the summer retreat at Mount Huqiu, where he studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

Upon reaching the section on the Bodhisattva’s ascent to the seventh stage and his realization of the *anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti* (the patience of the non-arising of phenomena), he gained profound insight into the causal circumstances of Yaśodhara (Yangjuemuo) carrying his alms bowl to the house of a woman in childbirth—matters he had previously inquired about with Zantang.
At that time, he attained awakening. By imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Yunju, whereupon the Master went there to visit him.
Upon arriving at the mountain on the following day, [Wuzhun] was immediately invited to serve as the First Seat (*dìyīzuò*).

At that time, there were many "dragons and elephants" (eminent masters) in the assembly who, having long been accustomed to occupying the seat of the Head Seat (*zhuázhuàn*), felt quite resentful toward Wuzhun’s arrival.

When it came to the winter solstice and he was to hold the *fú* (the formal discourse), Zhaojue Yuan stepped forward and asked, "When the sword is suspended between the eyebrows, what then? Wuzhun replied, "Blood splatters against the Brahma Heaven. Thereupon, Yuan bowed at the base of his seat.

He gestured with his hand and said, "Stop! Stop! Your question was excellent; your answer was even more marvelous. Yuan then returned to the assembly, and from that time on, the monastic community underwent a transformation.
Wugu returned to Shu, where he established a hermitage at the ancient site of Yunmen behind Mount Yunju to reside.
Students gathered there like clouds. After some time, he entered Min Province and built a thatched hut at Yangyu in Changle. Those who followed him [attained realization].
As for the Dharma, there were thirteen people. He subsequently moved to Yunmen Hermitage at Xiaoxi. Later, he accepted the summons from Chancellor Zhang, Duke Wei Jun, to Mount Jing.
The flourishing of his Way and Dharma was preeminent in his time; his assembly numbered over two thousand, all of whom were eminent talents from various quarters.
Zhang Gong Jiucheng, the Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, also followed him in his travels and attained a clear realization. One day, while discussing...

Regarding the administration of the court, he incurred misfortune along with his teacher. In the fifth month of the *Xinyou* year of the Shaoxing era during the reign of Emperor Gaozong of the Song dynasty, his monastic certificate was revoked, and he lived in seclusion in Hengyang.

Thereupon, he compiled the pivotal sayings of the former masters, interspersing them with his own critical comments (*nianti*), dividing them into three fascicles and titling them the *Zhengfayan zang* (The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye).
After ten years, he moved his residence to Mei Yang; five years later, by special imperial favor, he was released to return home. In the spring of the following year—
He returned his *saṃghāṭī* robe and declined all invitations to occupy vacant seats at the four directions. Later, he received an imperial decree to reside at Yuyang Monastery;
after more than a year, he was ordered by imperial edict to move to Mount Jing. Both monastics and laypeople admired him as they had before.

When Emperor Xiaozong was still the Prince of Puan, he dispatched an Inner Palace Supervisor to the mountain to pay his respects to the Master. The Master composed a verse to present to him. Furthermore, while the Emperor resided in the Prince’s residence, he again sent [an envoy].
The Inner Official-in-Chief arrived at the mountain to provide offerings for five hundred arhats and requested the Master to preach the Dharma, praying for the prolongation of the Emperor’s life.

The Emperor personally inscribed the three characters "Miaoxi An" (Amitābha Hermitage) and composed a eulogy, graciously entrusting them to him. Upon ascending the hall, he took up his staff, struck it once, and said:
He gave a shout and said, "Fortunately, you are pitiable beings. Why do you needlessly strike out and shout in such disorder?
[He] threw down [his staff] and said, 'Place a fire where it is cold. [He] ascended the hall and said, "Today is the fifteenth of the eighth month. Who does not behold the hare in the heavens?
Had it not been for the Little Śākyamuni of this land, Changsha would have let this tiger go free. [He] ascended the hall.
The Master cited a monk’s question to Changsha: “How can one turn the mountains, rivers, and the great earth back into oneself?
Changsha replied, “How can one turn oneself back into the mountains, rivers, and the great earth? The Master said, “It is easy to turn the mountains, rivers, and the great earth back into oneself;
it is difficult to turn oneself back into the mountains, rivers, and the great earth. If there were someone who could say it is neither difficult nor easy—”
A verse on the *Yì*: "Yet you come into the hands of Jingshan; I invite you to eat a blow of the staff. Ascending the hall for the mid-spring month of the second lunar month:
"The rain has lasted long without clearing. Yunmen’s one *zhā*—his virtue has no neighbor. He then looked at the assembly and said, "The *zhā*! He spoke again, saying, "It puts people to shame.
When Layman Budong arrived and ascended the hall, a monk asked: "Jingshan has deployed the array of dragons and snakes. Where does he dwell?"
"With only a few paces of earth, a horse, and a single spear—when it comes to such a time, how do you see one another? The Master said, "I, this old monk, beat the retreat drum.
The student said, "A great beast encounters a tiger with heavy fangs. The Master said, "Do you still hear the sound of thunder?
The student said, "It is simply because I have become accustomed to hearing it. The Master said, "Do not pretend to be clever. The student said, "Then I beg the Master to speak for me."
The Master said, "Had I said anything, you would have been shattered into a hundred pieces. The monk replied, "I have spent my life in joy and liberation!
The Master sighed and said, "With eyes empty of the universe, there is nothing at all; sitting grandly before the hall, who would dare to peer?

Having already finished both the selection of Buddhas and the selection of officials, those who share the same path hold hands, yet they do not return together. He then asked the assembly, "Since you share the same path and hold hands, why do you not return together?"
Why do they not all return the same? Do not mistake the cry of a crane for the song of a warbler. Ascending the hall, he said: "Mount Jing has not a single inch of land or field.
This summer, we have gathered the necessary conditions as best we can. Too weary to discourse on the Way, too indolent to talk of Chan; I carry my staff here, and everything is complete.
There is no need to stifle the mind or eliminate delusive thoughts; everyone simply eats their fill and then goes to sleep. Go to sleep."
"It is not non-existent. [The Master continued: "Suppose there were someone in a dream demanding payment for rice—how would you deal with that?
'Faintly like a melody, barely fit to hear, it is blown by the wind into another tune. [He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of radiance.
I do not ask about the radiance; I wonder, does the Dharma-body still possess the four great elements? The Master said:
[The student] asked, “What is the Dharma-body? The Master said, “Earth, water, fire, and wind.
[The student] asked, “What are the four great elements? The Master said, “A lacquer bucket is not clever. [The student] asked, “Beyond the Dharma-body, is there anything further or not?
The Master said, “Simply understand it by looking downward. He then cited a monk who asked Zhaozhou, “What is the person who comes forth? Zhaozhou said, “All Buddhas.”
The Master said, "Bodhisattva, how small-souled is Zhaozhou! Originally, his gallbladder was tiny.
Or when someone asks Jingshan, "What is it that comes forth? he says to him, "A mud-pig, a scabby dog.
If the other were to say, "Jingshan’s tongue is so free and easy," I would know you are a lacquer bucket. Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "When the myriad functions cease..."

[The Master] stopped. "Sitting alone upon the great square [of the earth] is still a matter of the lower path. What is the matter of the upper path? The Master said, "One must not speak of dreams before a fool.
[The monk] said, "The old monk’s three-inch [tongue] is very tight. The Master said, "It is difficult to deceive the eyes of the multitude."
[The Master] said: "It is just like when a monk asked Dongshan, 'What is the Buddha? He replied, 'Three pounds of flax. What about that? The Master said:
'The great garuḍa spreads its wings, covering the ten continents; the creatures by the hedge merely chirp in vain. Then he said: 'Yesterday was sunny, today it rains;
the times do not correspond. Look after three days! [He] struck the meditation seat and descended from the platform."
The Hall. "The moon arises as one": the Iron Wheel-turning King issues his decree throughout the realm. "The moon arises as two": Fenggan rides a tiger into the bustling marketplace.
"The moon arises as three": a giant turtle turns over within the eye of a gnat. [Jian] suddenly brandishes his staff and says, "Is there anyone who shares in life and death?
