Mist-laden smoke already signals autumn; each fruit is crimson, its fragrance pervasive.
With eyes protruding and a mouth open in laughter, this time it no longer clings to its old branch. This was when he shaved his head and received the precepts.

Master Shanzhu raised the story of Lingyun’s awakening upon seeing peach blossoms, and the Master offered this verse: Lingyun saw them once, and his brows were knit tight; He drew forth the fisherman’s clever ruse.
When the white waves arise, cast out a single hook; let the fish and turtles compete for it at their own head. Later, upon ascending the hall, he said:
"Those who study the Buddha merely say that 'the true' does not stand; those who practice Chan mostly act in contradiction to the Way. Forget the mind and forget the objects; quickly turn back."
Without ground and without a needle, he turns his steps and returns. The Buddha is neither mind nor anything else; accepting him directly in his true essence, one is free from all dependence.

Like the moon in the empty expanse over the ten-thousand-year-old azure pool, only after repeated scooping and searching will you finally know. Ascending the hall, [the Master] remained silent for a long while, then called out to the assembly:
"Do you understand? He spoke again: "The deficiencies are not few. Ascending the hall, [he cited]: Changsha said, "A hundred-foot pole..."
One who sits at the very top of the head—though they have gained entry, it is not yet the truth.
Take another step forward from the hundred-foot pole, and the entire world of the ten directions will manifest as your whole body. Great Master Dahui said: "Do you wish to see Changsha?
Take one more step forward. Baoning, however, was not like this: "Do you wish to see Changsha? Take one more step back. Ultimately, how is it? It is changing the bones and washing the marrow.
Reorganize your inner being. Your whole body is eyes, yet you must still investigate further. The Master arrived at Lingyin and was invited to ascend the hall for formal instruction.

"The orthodox lineage of Vulture Peak—those who have attained it are still bewildered by it. When light comes and when darkness comes, who can discern the truth? When both are gathered in and both are released, who can grasp the beginning?
Even if a thousand sages were to appear, they would only have their tongues tied. Why? Because people return to the Great [Way]."
A country is valued for its integrity; when the waters reach the Xiao and Xiang rivers, they finally become clear. He spoke again:
"Just now, Master Songyuan raised the story of the bamboo whisk, causing Tiantong to suffer defeat. Do you all wish to know? Listen to this verse:
'Grasping the black-lacquered bamboo whisk, It is like a sudden thunderclap—no time to cover one's ears. Deshan and Linji stare blankly; How can those who are bewildered cope? "
The Master’s own eulogy for himself reads: "A rustic fellow whom no spoon can pick up; Not a single speck of literary refinement in his breast. He once pried the very bones from empty space;
His ill repute has won him fame throughout the rivers and lakes. In the *dingmao* year of the Kaixi era of Emperor Ningzong of the Song dynasty, he passed away.
He was seventy-one years old by secular age and forty-five years since his ordination. His stupa was enshrined at this mountain.
Chan Master Daomiao Fabao of Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "If you call it a bamboo stick, you offend it;
if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you turn your back on it. You must be like a lion that bites; do not act like a hunting dog chasing a clod of earth.
A-he-he! Do you understand? Under the feet of Vajrapāṇi is an iron Kunlun; he has caught the doltish Bagua of Mingzhou. He ascended the hall again and said: "A thousand..."

Speaking in general terms, there are ten thousand kinds of metaphors; they simply aim to teach you to return home early. Last night a single mass of black clouds arose—do not let it cause you to lose the path ahead in the mountains.
*Duḥ!* (A shout of exhortation.)
Chan Master Tanyi of Yùquán in Fúzhōu had long relied upon Yuánwù, claiming he harbored no doubts.

At the beginning of the Shàoxīng era of the Sòng dynasty, he went forth to reside at Xiāngyún in Xìnghuà, where his Dharma assembly was quite flourishing. When Dàhuì entered Mǐn, he realized that Tanyi’s realization was not yet definitive.
A letter was sent for the Master to come. The Master delayed; however, Dahui held a small assembly (xiaocan) and severely rebuked him, subsequently posting a public notice to the fourfold assembly.

The Master, having no choice, broke the summer retreat to visit him. Dahui interrogated him regarding his realization. Afterward, he said, "With such a view as yours, how dare you claim to be the successor of Elder Yuanwu?
The Master withdrew from the monastery to attend upon him. One day, during a private interview (nishu), Dahui asked, "I want someone who..."
"One who cannot practice Chan cannot serve as a National Teacher. The Master said, "I shall go and become a National Teacher. Hui shouted at him and sent him out.
Not long after, he said to him, "Xiangyan’s place of awakening was not on the side of the striking bamboo; Jushi’s attainment was not on the tip of the finger.
Thereupon, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. Later, while residing at Yuquan, he offered incense for Hui, continuing his lineage from Hui.
At Xiaoxi, Hui took his seat on the dais. He raised the case of Yunmen, who one day held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying:

"Ordinary people truly say it exists; those of the Two Vehicles analyze it and say it does not exist; Pratyekabuddhas call it illusory existence; Bodhisattvas realize that its very substance is emptiness."
When a patch-robed monk sees a staff, he simply calls it a staff; when walking, he simply walks; when sitting, he simply sits;
in all cases, he must not touch upon it. Huì said, "I am not like the old man Yúnmén, who digs a hollow in empty space.

He then suddenly picked up the staff and said, "This staff does not belong to existence, nor does it belong to non-existence; it does not belong to illusion, nor does it belong to emptiness. He struck the ground once with it.

The text below says: "Ordinary beings, those of the two vehicles, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—all turn toward this very place. Each, according to their own capacity, attains full enjoyment [of it].
Yet, within the domain of the patch-robed monk (śramaṇa), it acts as a harm and a grievance: when one wishes to walk, one cannot walk; when one wishes to sit, one cannot sit.
To take a single step forward, one is bewildered by the staff; to retreat a single step, one is [bewildered] by..."
"The staff has already pierced through the nostrils. Is there anyone here now who is not satisfied? Come forth and meet this staff!
If there is none, next year there will be new branches; the spring wind, causing such disturbance, will never cease.
At this very moment, what should be done? [The Master] descends from his seat. "I trouble Yquan to bring this out for the sake of the assembly. The Master ascends the seat and delivers his discourse.
Having finished his thanks, he then brought up the previous conversation, saying: "The Abbot’s critique just now was much like a weary fish confined to a pond or a sick bird perching on a reed.
If it were Yuquan, it would not be so. He took up his staff and said:

"This staff can exist, and it can be non-existent; it can manifest illusion, and it can be empty. It reaches all ordinary beings, those of the two vehicles, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas. He struck once.
He said: "Just now, everything here was shattered into a hundred fragments. Only within the domain of the patch-robed monk is it like a dragon finding water, or a tiger relying on its mountain;
when he wishes to walk, he walks; when he wishes to sit, he sits. To take one step forward, heaven and earth tremble;
to take one step back, the grass bows and the wind blows. Now tell me: as for this phrase of neither advancing nor retreating, how would you speak? After a long silence, he said:
Leisurely holding a sutra scroll, he stood leaning against a pine tree. Smiling, he asked the guest, "From where have you come?
Chan Master Wuben of Jianfu Temple in Raozhou was a native of Jiangzhou. Having originally studied under Yunmen in Jiangxi, he later attended upon Miaoxi.
They arrived at Xiaoxi in Quannan, where men of outstanding talent gathered from all quarters and many received the seal of transmission (*kanna*).
The Master privately thought they were abandoning him and intended to depart. Miaoxi, knowing this, said to him: "You need only focus your mind on investigation;
if you have any realization, even before you open your mouth, I shall already know it. Shortly thereafter, there were reports that the Master had entered the room for private instruction.
He said to his teacher, "I have been a personal attendant for many years, yet day after day I can only say, 'I do not understand.
The teacher scolded him, saying, "You little rascal! Before you were even born, I already had your teeth pulled out three times at the Huoshan Temple.
This will surely let you know! From this, [the student] became even more resolute in his resolve; taking up the koan of "The dog has no Buddha-nature," he brought it forth.

He called out the characters to rouse himself. One night, when the third watch was approaching, while he was leaning against a pillar in the hall and drifting off into a drowsy sleep, he did not realize that words were escaping his lips.
Suddenly, he attained sudden enlightenment. Three days later, Miaoxi returned from the prefectural city.
The Master hurried to his quarters; as soon as his feet had crossed the threshold, before he had even uttered a word, Miaoxi said, "Old Shaveling, this time you have finally reached the very end."
At first he resided at Boshan in Xinzhou, where his establishment of the Dharma path was most rigorous and orderly. He subsequently moved to Jianfu Temple, where he ascended the hall and said:
"As for those who bow high to Śākyamuni but do not prostrate to Maitreya—I would give them thirty blows with my staff. Why?
Because they only know how to climb higher step by step, but do not know how to let go from the void. They plow for the eastern neighbor and drag the harrow for the western neighbor."
"I would give him thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because he only knows how to let go from emptiness; he does not know how to ascend step by step.
When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, is there any fault in it? Is there anyone among you who can examine this and find it?
If you can examine it and find it, we shall walk hand in hand on the southern side of Mount Sumeru. If you cannot examine it and find it—"
An old crow in a cloth bag; though alive, it is as if dead. Entering the hall for discourse: Śākyamuni shut his room in Magadha;
Vimalakīrti sealed his mouth in Vaiśālī; Subhūti proclaimed non-speaking to manifest the Way;
and Śakra and Brahmā ceased seeing and hearing as they rained down flowers. O Great Assembly! This lot of incompetent fellows, for no reason, took the ancestral estate and fields...
They drew up a covenant, each demarcating their boundaries according to the four limits—square, round, long, or short—and in an instant, they had finished carving out their portions with flowers.
This caused their descendants in later generations, even after a thousand years, to have not a single tile to cover their heads above, nor a spot of ground to set a needle upon below.
Had Boshan seen this at that time, he would have dug a bottomless deep pit at the crossroads and called them all over.
At that time, [the matter] was buried; thus we may avoid being mutually obstructed by dullness. Why is this so? Have you not heard it said: "When the family prospers, filial sons are born;

when the state is hegemonic, there are strategic ministers"? [The Master] ascends the hall: "Once the Gandharva King performed music, and the mountains, rivers, and great earth all offered their tribute.
How can this compare to the lame old Yunmen, who could say, 'The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month'? Bo Shan now...
If there are branches, grasp the branches; if there are no branches, grasp the precedent. One must, after all, respond to the occasion.

[The Master] suddenly picked up his staff, rested it horizontally across his knees, and made the gesture of playing the zither, saying: "Is there anyone here who can appreciate the sound upon hearing the strings? After a long silence, he said:
"Even if one were to produce the cry of a phoenix, in the end, who would truly know the technique of the fingers? With a sharp strike of the staff, he descended from the seat.
Chan Master Dàyuán Zūnpó, the Great Teacher of Yùwáng in Qìngyuan Prefecture, was a native of Fúzhōu. In his youth, he studied the Way alongside Yùquán Yì under Yuánwù for several years;
thereafter, he returned to his hometown to assist Yì at Xiángyún in Púzhōu. This was during the Jiǎyín year of the Shàoxīng era of the Song dynasty.

Dahui resided at Yangyu. When the Master went to visit him, as they were entering the room, Dahui asked, "Regarding the saying that 'Three Sages and Xinghua go out, while others do not'—is this a matter of acting for oneself or acting for others? You tell me: do these two old fellows have a way to manifest themselves, or not?
The Master gave Dahui a punch on his knee. Dahui said, "Just this one punch of yours acts for Three Sages."
"Qi! This is for the sake of manifesting the Dharma; speak quickly, speak quickly! As the Master hesitated, Huì struck him and said, "You must not forget this one blow under any circumstances.
Later, while in his quarters, Huì asked a monk, "Deshan would strike a monk as soon as he entered the gate;
Linji would shout at a monk as soon as he entered the gate; Xuefeng, upon seeing a monk enter the gate, would..."
"What is the Way? When Muzhou saw a monk, he would immediately say, "This is a settled case; I grant you thirty blows.
You say, "Do these four old fellows have any way of benefiting others or not? The monk said, "They do. Huai said, "Zha! (A sharp, piercing sound).
As the monk hesitated, Huai gave a shout. Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly grasped its subtle meaning, and Huai joyfully granted him approval.
Chan Master Nanyuan Zuyuan of Nengren Monastery at Yanshan in Wenzhou was a native of the Lin clan from Min.
Initially, he visited Xuefeng Yu, and subsequently relied upon Foxin Cai; with both, his spiritual capacity was in accord with their teachings.

Later, while relying on Dahui at Yunmen Hermitage, as he sat in meditation one night, he saw a monk trim a lamp and attained full realization. He composed a verse which said: "To trim the lamp is fire; throughout kalpas..."
Ignorance was shattered by the light; returning to the hall, he encountered the Holy Monk (Śāstrī) and nearly let him pass right before his eyes. What is it that was not missed?
"Extraordinary fifteen years ago, it remains exactly this very same thing as before. Hui offered him a verse, saying:
Releasing the body atop a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, one rises and remains as alert as ever. Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, there is nothing at all to do;

what need is there to discuss whether one is the person of old or not? When he first resided at Fuyan Hermitage in Lianjiang, the number of mouths to feed was very large and daily affairs left him no leisure.
He posted a verse at the shrine of the monastery guardian deity, which said: "A small hermitage, a small cottage, a small grove—what can the local deity do?"
"Eight or nine people are required. If you understand how to take turns coming forward to strike, you will avoid having [the staff] smashed into a heap of dust.

That evening, he had a dream of a lay donor from before the mountain who requested that his instructions be followed as given. In the spring of the Jisi year of the Shaoxing era of the Song dynasty, he went forth to reside at Nengren Temple and ascended the hall, saying:
"Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; treading upon a scale-weight, it is harder than iron. Where there is no Buddha, hurry—"
He has passed by. The grass beneath his feet is three feet deep. Three thousand miles away, do not fail to speak when you meet someone.
The Northern Dipper hangs from Mount Sumeru. If that is so, then he does not go. With a staff, he lifts the sun and moon. Plucking the willow flowers—plucking the willow flowers.
The pupil in the eye wears embroidered shoes. (He struck his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The withered tree of Yanshan is true head-seal Zen;
it does not lie in clever or novel phrases. Suddenly, reaching back with one's hand and grasping it, the long whale swallows the moon and the waves overflow the heavens."
Chan Master Liaoxing of Dong’an at Lingya in Zhenzhou ascended the hall and said:
"To have already seen through [the matter] and yet let one move pass—that is the tattered straw sandals of a monk. To manifest the form of an asura while a woman bows—that is a wild fox spirit.
To draw a circle and drop a dot within empty space—that is the trickery of a child. To strike the cheek with a palm and then sweep the sleeves away—"
"Acting. This is precisely the karmic consciousness wandering aimlessly, with no foundation to rely upon.
Even if you were to suddenly cut it off all at once before the black bean has even sprouted, you would still not have the right to receive Lingyan’s staff. I dare ask the assembly:
tell me, where does the crux of helping others lie? Do you understand? Since the spring colors came to Songshao, thirty...
The six peaks remain green to this day. Entering the hall: A single reed by the riverbank, willows in spring; in the heart of the waves, the man of old is not to be seen.
To recognize the man of peace of mind in the snowy courtyard, his nostrils still rest upon his upper lip.
Raising his whisk, he said: "The Patriarch has arrived! Do you see him? If you can see him, realize it right now. If not yet, then listen."
The road to the Western Heaven from here extends more than one hundred thousand li. A monk asked, "When humans and devas meet, how do you instruct them?

The Master said, "The eight-sided iron staff in the hand of Vajrapāṇi. The monk asked, "If a student were suddenly to pierce through both the mundane and the sacred, striking right through the primordial barrier, what then?
The Master said, "An iron pillar stands across the gateway to the sea. [The monk] asked, "What is it?"
The Master said, "A cat sleeping beneath a peony flower.
Chan Master Yiguan Shan-zhi of Jiangshan in Jiankang Prefecture was a native of Yunze in De’an. Initially, he visited Miaoxi at Huíyàn Peak.
One day, Miaoxi asked, "Where are you from, Upādhyāya? The Master replied, "I am a man from Anzhou. Miaoxi—
[Daowu] said, "I have heard that you people of Anzhou are skilled at wrestling. Is this true? The Master then assumed a wrestling stance.
Daowu said, "People of Hunan eat fish; why is it that people of Hubei get fish-bones stuck in their throats? The Master performed a somersault and left. Daowu said:

Who would have known that within cold ashes there was a single bean that burst forth? He went to live at Baoning. Entering the hall for instruction, he said: "The Buddhas never appeared in this world;
everyone’s nostrils reach the heavens. The Patriarchs never came from the West; every person stands solitary like a cliff a thousand fathoms high."
To bow high to Śākyamuni and not prostrate to Maitreya is but what is logically fitting. To cut off the path of the thousand sages and walk alone through the great chiliocosm is no extra effort.
If you can understand this at the place where the Buddhas appear in the world and take it up at the point where the Patriarchs came from the West, you will not even be able to save yourself;
you will suffer indignity for a lifetime. Is there any true man who can take this up?
"What kind of man is this? Come forth and contend with Baoning! Had it not been so, it would have been better to simply tear it to shreds.
[He] then descended from his seat. One day, Chancellor Chen Junqing, the Guardian of the Capital, hosted a tea gathering at the mountains to discuss the public case:

"The phrase exists, the phrase does not exist; like a vine leaning against a tree. He commanded the various mountain masters to offer their critical judgments, and they all sought to impress him with wondrous words.
He paid his respects. The Master said at the end: "Zhang beats oil; Li beats oil; they do not beat the whole body, but only the head. Chen was greatly pleased.
Zen Master Zihū of Wanshòu in Jiànzhōu ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'If a person recognizes their own mind, the great earth...'"
There is not an inch of soil. Wanshou, however, was not like this. If a person recognizes their own mind, that is not yet the ultimate point.
But where, then, is the ultimate point? He held up his staff, struck it once, and said: "The sweet melon is sweet all the way through to its stem; the bitter gourd is bitter even to its roots."
Chan Master Dalian Jinge Yun of Mount Maitreya in Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "The single melody of Yunmen:
on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, auspicious snow falls from the void, piling up across the mountain valleys. On the steep ridges, the cold plum blossoms are just beginning to bloom.
Grasping the *Sumeru* mallet, he laughs as he beats the drum of emptiness. This startles Kātyāyanīputra, who breaks into a cold sweat that pours down like rain. He was enraged.
The wrathful Asura King clenched his fist against his chest and asked, "Ultimately, what is the essential principle? [The Master] said, "Tsk!
Even before the peak of Shaoshi, you have already made a mistake."
Chan Master Shui'an Liaoyan of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Right before one's eyes, it is smashed to pieces; heaven and earth are vastly different.

Having broken through the secure barrier, white clouds stretch for ten thousand miles. Even if you were to cut off both ends and find another way to turn, even after sixty kalpas over three lifetimes, you would not have seen it in a dream.
He let out a shout and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Ciyuan of Guangxiao Temple in Taizhou ascended the hall and, citing the story of the woman emerging from samādhi, said:
"From of old, beating the drum and playing the lute requires meeting with one who understands; when the jade pendants and phoenix bells have finished their song and dance."
The setting sun slants as it did before the gate.
Chan Master Chongsheng Puci Yunwen of Xuefeng in Fuzhou, a native of the Shen family of Hongzhou, addressed the assembly:
"A sandalwood grove is surrounded by sandalwood; a lion’s grove is surrounded by lions; a tiger and wolf’s grove is surrounded by tigers and wolves."
Wolves surround it; thornbushes and forests surround it. Great assembly, among these four kinds of forests, which one would be best for you to dwell in during the summer retreat?
If you can understand this, within ninety days you will surely each become a Buddha or a Patriarch.
If you do not yet realize this, the forest of Prajñā will wither year after year, and the wild weeds of ignorance will grow more thickly every spring.
Chang: Chan Master Daoneng of Lianyun Dao in Chuzhou was a native of the He family of Hanzhou. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of Jingqing’s 'Six Scrapings'?
The Master said, "It pierces through your nostrils. The monk said, "If I have nostrils, you may pierce them; but if I have no nostrils..."
“Kong, what else has he pierced? The Master said, “To carry one’s own stolen goods while crying out for injustice. The Master asked, “What is ‘scraping the dust off the fur’?
The Master said, “Yun, Yuan, Qian, Ji—holding a brush atop one’s head. The Master asked, “What is ‘scraping the fur off the skin’?
The Master said, “Shi City, Qian Hua—speaking and cursing one another. The Master asked, “What is ‘scraping the skin off the flesh’? The Master said, “Jia, Mei.”
Guo Lang held up his robe and said, "What is 'scraping the flesh from the bone'? The Master said, "In Zhangquan and Fujian, people have heads as flat as fans.
He asked, "What is 'scraping the bone from the marrow'? The Master said, "At Yanglan and Zuoli, waves rise even without wind.
He asked, "And how does one scrape the marrow? The Master said, "On the eighteenth and nineteenth, fools run about at night. He asked, "Six..."

Having been polished [by his training], he received the Master’s instruction: "How is it that a single word cuts straight through the meaning? The Master said, "There is a portion where the tongue is tied.
Chan Master Zu’an Daoyin of Lingyin Temple in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Hanzhou.

He ascended the hall and said: "The tiger beneath Mount Daxiong; the turtle-nosed snake of the South Mountain. If you happen to run into them, you will return home with your prize. If you do not spare your skillful hand..."
He then pulled out the heavy tooth for him. "Is there? Is there? Ascending the hall, he said: "Five times five is twenty-five.

Shattering the drum of empty space, the great earth cannot admit even a needle. Throughout the ten directions there is not a single inch of soil. When spring brings forth life and summer nurtures growth, what more is there to say?"

What is sweet is sweet; what is bitter is bitter. On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, the Master ascended the hall and cited the public case of Master Mazu, Xitang, Baizhang, and Nanquan as they gazed at the moon.
The Master said: "Master Mazu let out his line a thousand fathoms deep; his intent lay in the profound pool."
Xitang shook his mane; Baizhang wagged his tail. Though they surged through the waves and raged against the billows, they could not avoid falling upon another’s hook and line.
Nanquan claimed for himself that he had leaped past the Yu Gate; who would have known that, as before, he remained caught in the great net?
Is there anyone here now who can break free from the cage and emerge from the nest? It would be well to come forth and reveal a bit of news, so that the Flower Treasury may be known.
To the Gate: May you not remain in solitude. Should this not yet be so, then on this night, as the single orb reaches its fullness, where would its pure light not be present?
Chan Master Zongyuan of Zhuyuan, in Jianning Prefecture—a native of the Lin clan of that same prefecture—had long relied upon Dahui and shared his seat at Xichan Monastery.

When Zhang Jun, the Chancellor, was the military governor of San Shan, he invited him to several monasteries, but he did not accept; instead, he returned to his old hometown to establish [his hermitage].
At Maohao Zhongmiao Garden, where veteran monks and lay practitioners had gathered and requested him to open the Dharma for them, he addressed the assembly:
"If you investigate this matter, it is like having lost the key to a lock.

You must simply continue searching, searching here and there, until suddenly you strike upon it—'Aha!'—and right here, having opened the lock, you shall see your own storehouse, wherein all provisions and enjoyments are fully present."

Sufficient. There is nothing else to be sought from others; what other matter is there? Addressing the assembly: In all quarters, people pull out nails and extract wedges, untie adhesions and remove bonds.
Here, I provide people with additional nails and wedges, adding more ropes and further bonds, then send them off into a deep pool to see for themselves how they will manage it.
Addressing the assembly: A person who presides over the Dharma must have a spirit that swallows the universe.

Zhou was a great Dharma King. Even if Śākyamuni the Old Man and Master Bodhidharma were to appear, he would have them join their palms and stand behind him, until their hair stood on end with cold; yet even this would not have been considered extraordinary.
One day, when the Master raised the saying, "When the World-Honored One was first born, [he declared] 'In heaven and on earth, I alone am honored,'" Zhou said, "I find this strange."
"There is nothing strange. That which is strange will destroy itself. He spoke these words:
"This very thing is just like encountering a murderer. If you do not kill him, he will kill you."
The attendant San Shan, who had long served Da Hui, once investigated the "Bamboo Cudgel" koan in silence without gaining any entry into its meaning.
One day, after leaving his private quarters, he requested further instruction. Da Hui said, "You are a man from Fuzhou. Let me give you a metaphor:
it is like taking a fine grade of lychee and, all at once, stripping away the skin and shell, then placing it directly into your mouth with your hand."
[The Master] said, "It is simply that you do not know how to swallow it. The Master could not help but laugh and said, "If the Abbot swallows it, it will be a disaster.
Later, Huì asked the Master, "Regarding the lychees swallowed the other day, it was simply that you did not know their flavor.
The Master said, "If one knows the flavor, one encounters even greater disaster."
Chan Master Liaoming of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was the son of the Lu family of Xiuzhou. He stood eight feet tall and his belly measured several spans in circumference;
wherever he went, people would inevitably gather to gaze upon him. When Miaoxi was first exiled to Mei Yang, the local prefectures and counties maintained extremely strict guard over his transport.
The Master traveled while bearing the cangue, enduring hardships and obstacles without ever slackening for even a moment.

Upon arriving at his place of exile, hundreds of disciples followed him, seeking instruction. Fearing that food supplies would not suffice and apprehensive of further calamity, Wuxiao urged them to depart.

The Master would invariably refuse, taking personal responsibility for the vegetarian meals and gruel. He would frequently carry a *kaolao* (a large wicker basket) on his shoulders to beg for alms, returning at evening with the food and provisions arranged in rows.
For seventeen years, he remained as constant as a single day. When he received the imperial decree to resume his monastic robes and reside at Yuyang Monastery, he never departed from this practice.
Within Miaoxi’s quarters, he did not permit his disciples to shout the *he*; when the Master entered, [he likewise observed this].
Upon entering the room, he would invariably let out a loud shout and withdraw. Miaoxi had posted a notice stating: "Those who shout 'ha' shall be fined one *guan*.
The Master then secretly prepared a thousand coins in his sleeve; upon reaching the room, he first placed them on the floor, let out a loud shout, and then departed.
This happened several times, yet Miaoxi could do nothing about it. He posted a notice again, stating: "Those who shout 'He' shall be punished with one portion of the day's hall-provisions.
The Master then went to the storehouse and said, "The Abbot requires ten taels of gold.

The official in charge did not doubt him and gave it to him immediately. The Master slipped it into his sleeve and entered the Abbot’s quarters; he then placed it on the floor and let out a loud shout. Miaoxi was greatly startled.

When he had finished entering the room, [Fengxue] asked him leisurely; knowing this was so, he smiled with delight and said, "For you, a fat fellow like this, to understand Chan in such a way—even in a donkey's year, you have not even dreamed of it.

The poem says: Before the green bamboo hat, heaven and earth are vast; Beneath the blue grass-cloth robe, water and clouds are wide.
Without speaking or saying a word, one knows what it is— Simply not deceiving one's own human heart.
The Gentleman-in-Attendance (Neihan) Master Zeng Kai, whose courtesy name was Tianyou, had long studied under Yuanwu and had been coming and going at Dahui’s gate for some time.
In the *Xinwei* year of the Shaoxing era, Fohai was appointed to Guangxiao Temple in Quzhou;
Master Kai and Zhao Chaoran went to visit him and asked, "What is a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*)? Fohai replied, "Lanterns, pillars, cats, and dogs. Master Kai—
The official asked, "Why is it that praise brings joy while disparagement brings affliction? Haichang said, "Attendant, have you ever met a true teacher (Sanskrit: *kalyāṇamitra*)?
The official replied, "I have been seeking instruction for thirty years; how can you say I have not seen one? Haichang said, "Look at him where he feels joy; look at him where he feels affliction.
As the official hesitated, Haichang let out a thunderous shout and gave a blow with his staff. As the official was about to respond, Haichang said, "Open your mouth!"
"It is not so. Gong was bewildered. Hai called out to him, "Where have you been, Minister? Gong suddenly attained realization and nodded his head. He then spoke a verse: "Alas!
This blind donkey, a pestilence to the monastic community! With one roar that shakes the earth, the celestial mechanism has been leaked.
If anyone asks further what the meaning is, I will lift my whisk and strike them across the mouth! Hai said, "It is still only..."
He attained the "single peg.
The layman Ge Yan, Prefectural Governor, whose courtesy name was Qianwen and style name Xinzhai, had passed the highest imperial examination in his youth.

He devoted himself to the joy of Chan and first visited Wuan, who instructed him to investigate the phrase "This very mind is Buddha. After a long time without attaining realization, he requested, "What method does the Master have?"
“Please allow me to enter,” he requested. Wuan said, “Layman, you are truly insatiable.

Later, when Fohai came to reside at Jianchi, the Master followed him there and brought up the words previously shown by Wuan, requesting that he preach them for the assembly. Fohai expounded upon them, saying:
“‘This very mind is Buddha’—his eyebrows trail the ground; ‘Neither this mind nor Buddha’—his two eyes stare wide. A butterfly’s dream.”

The journey to the Middle Kingdom was ten thousand *li*. Under the branch of the *subing* (cuckoo) tree, the moon was in its third watch. After staying for ten days, he returned. One day, he raised the question:
"Is it not mind? Is it not Buddha? Is it not something? At these words, he attained sudden enlightenment.

He composed a verse: "Neither mind, nor Buddha, nor even an object; Before the Five Phoenix Pavilion, the mountain rises abruptly. In the midst of the radiant sun’s shadow, he turns his body upside down; A wild fox leaps into [the lion's den]."

Jinmaoku (Golden-Haired Cave) did not approve of Wuan’s [verse]. He immediately sent a letter and a verse to present to Fohai. Fohai replied: "This matter cannot be fully expressed by paper and brush.
If you, Layman, can come to see me, you shall surely hear what is to be heard. Thereupon, he returned to Huqiu. Fohai went out to meet him and said:
"Your realization, Layman, is sufficient only to enter the realm of the Buddhas; as for entering the realm of the Māras, you have not yet attained it."
When Master Gong continued to pay him extraordinary honors without ceasing, Hai Zhengrong said, "Why do you not say, 'The golden-haired lion leaps into the wild fox's den'?
At this, Master Gong was suddenly liberated. He once asked various Chan masters: "Suppose a husband and wife are having intercourse and their son acts as witness.
Tell me, does he bear witness for the father, or does he bear witness for the mother? Houan Ti added a commentary, saying: "A small exit, a great matter."
During the Jihai year of the Chunxi era of Emperor Xiaozong of the Song dynasty, while serving as Governor of Linchuan, he fell ill in the Xinchu year.
One night, he suddenly requested a brush and wrote a verse: "Beating a drum within the vast ocean, Hearing a bell atop Mount Sumeru.
The mirror of karma suddenly shatters; Turning over, one emerges into the void. He summoned his subordinates and showed it to them, saying: "Life and death are like day and night."

"It is night; there is nothing strange about this. If one speaks in terms of the Way, how could there be birth and death? If one interprets it as birth and death, then one is far removed from the Way.
Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away.

Chan Master Biefeng Baoyin of Jing Mountain in Lin’an was a successor of Chan Master Huazang Min. He was a native of the Li clan from Jiazhou. His family had resided for generations at the foot of Mount Emei.
In his youth, he mastered the Six Classics but grew weary of worldly affairs; he subsequently followed De Shan Qing Su to receive ordination and full precepts.
Later, he studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* and the *Awakening of Faith*. Having exhausted their expositions, he abandoned his reliance on [the teachings of] Mimi (Miyin) at Mount Zhongfeng.

One day, Miyin raised a case concerning a monk who asked Yantou, "What is it like when arising and ceasing do not stop? Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases? At this, the Master attained awakening and immediately nodded in agreement.
When Yuanwu returned to Zhaojue, Miyin sent the Master to visit him; consequently, he entered the assembly along with the others.
In the room, Wuzhuo asked, "How do the sages of the past receive people? The Master held up his fist. Wuzhuo said, "This is what this old monk uses;
how is it that the sages of the past use? The Master waved his fist at him. Wuzhuo also raised his fist, and as their fists crossed, they laughed heartily and ceased.
Later, he went to Mount Jing and visited Dahui. Dahui asked, "Where have you come from?"

The Master said, "Western Sichuan. Huì said, "Before you have even passed through the Jianmen Pass, I shall give you thirty blows! The Master said, "It was not right for you to stir from your seat, Reverend.
Huì was delighted; he swept his quarters and invited him in. When Huì moved southward, the Master returned west and presided over several monasteries.
Later, he again crossed the gorges and resided at Baoning, Jinshan, Xuedou, and Jing Mountain, where he ascended the hall to open the dharma assembly.

Ascending the seat, he said: "When the World-Honored One first attained perfect enlightenment, he turned the Wheel of the Four Noble Truths within the Deer Park, and the bhikṣu Kauṇḍinya was the first to realize the Way.
Later, Zhenjing said: 'Today, inside the cave of Xinfeng, I am merely turning a staff.
He then took up his staff, placed it on his left side, and said: 'Is there anyone here who has realized the Way from the very beginning?'"
"Ma! If there were none, a man would naturally have the ambition to pierce the heavens; do not walk where the Tathāgata has walked.
He then let out a shout and descended from his seat. If it were Master Yin, he would not have acted thus.
Today, within this Phoenix Mountain, I have no leisure to turn the Dharma wheel of the Four Noble Truths, nor do I have the strength to turn the staff. I simply instruct all of you to practice.
Walk slowly; speak with a low voice. Why? Because you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell. Do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time expound hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of phrases from a single phrase, yet they condense those hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of phrases back into that single phrase alone.
Under the gate of the Patriarchs, there is not even half a phrase. What, then, is it?"
"How many painful blows of the staff do you deserve? You all, tell me: are the Buddhas right, or are the Patriarchs right?

If you say the Buddhas are right and the Patriarchs are not, or that the Patriarchs are right and the Buddhas are not, you have failed to let go of acceptance and rejection. If it is truly so, then Buddhas and Patriarchs are both right at once."
The Buddhas and Patriarchs were, for a moment, not so; their bluntness was no small matter. Now, let us cut off this tangle of vines: how would you say it?
"A tiger wearing a paper hat—amusing, yet startling. Again, he cited the monk who asked Yantou, "In the midst of the vast dust of the world, how does one discern the host?
Yantou replied, "A copper saucepan filled to the brim with oil. The Master said, "What a great master Yantou was!"
He lost his nostrils. Suddenly, someone asked Baoning, "In the midst of such vast dust and clamor, how does one discern the master?
He replied to him, "The weather is cold; I have not had time to take off my hat. Ascending the hall, he said: "The first day of the sixth month: the sun burns the sky red.
At the crossroads of the street, the snow is a foot deep. There is no leisure for sweeping; there is no time to avoid it. It freezes the Liáo of East Village."
Master Huzi. At midnight, he stood upon the water wearing his boots. He ascended the hall and said: "If you try to use the mind to eliminate delusion, delusion is difficult to remove;
if you seek to clarify the mind through delusion, the Way becomes circuitous. When the bottom of the bucket is kicked away, there is no more inhibition; in an ordinary step, there is a lotus flower.

When the Master arrived at Jingshan, Emperor Xiaozong of the Song dynasty summoned him to the Xuande Hall for an audience. His response pleased the Emperor. On the day he entered for the audience, the Emperor bestowed upon him a shoulder-cot.

His carriage was escorted within the East Flower Gate. In the second month of the Gui-mao year of the Chunxi era (1183), the Emperor annotated the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* (Yuánjué jīng) and dispatched an envoy to present it to him, commanding him to compose a preface.

As the Master had reached an advanced age, he grew increasingly weary of his duties as abbot. In the winter of the Wu-shen year (1188), he submitted a petition requesting to live in seclusion at a hermitage, and his request was granted.

In the eleventh month of the Gengxu year of the Xiangxing era, he went to see his successor, Ce, to bid him farewell. When Ce asked for the date of his departure, the Master replied, "When the water arrives, the channel will be complete.
Upon returning home, he sought paper and wrote the nine characters: "The seventh night of the twelfth month, at the hour of the rooster. He passed away exactly according to that schedule.
His remains were brought back to the Dharma Hall of the monastery and remained there for seven days; his complexion was bright and lustrous, and his hair had grown long.
His head grew warm. After seven days had passed, he was buried on the western ridge of the hermitage. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Cidian, and his stupa was named Zhiguang.
He was eighty-two years old in secular age and sixty-four in monastic seniority.
Chan Master Fengqi Huiguan, a successor of Chan Master Zhaojue Yuan, ascended the hall and said:
"The fallen leaves are exhausted in the village ahead; the osmanthus flowers have withered in the deep courtyard.
Tonight is the beginning of early winter; from now on, it will grow especially cold. Therefore it is said: 'If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the seasons.'"
When the causes and conditions and the proper time arrive, the principle will manifest of itself. [The Master] let out a shout and said:
"To speak in such a manner—those who benefit others are few; those who ruin others are many."
Chan Master Huifang of Chuan, in Tanzhou, was a successor of Chan Master Wenshu. He was the son of the Xu family of that same prefecture. He visited Wenshu at Dabie;
not long after, the temple was converted into a Shenxiao Palace. While traveling south along the Xiang River by merchant boat, he heard a person on the bank speaking his native dialect.
At the sound [of the call], he cried out in a harsh voice, "Jiuna! Through this, he attained realization. He immediately spoke a verse: "A single cry at the heart of the river on Mt.

Mian— Only now do I realize my lifelong purpose. After many years of parting, we meet again; The thousand sages return together, walking the same path. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he said:
"In my old age, I have finally assumed the title of Abbot, yet I possess not a shred of original vital energy (genjō). He opened [the teaching].
The mouth is nine times out of ten at odds; when asked about the east, one answers about the west. If one proceeds in this manner toward the world, how can one investigate the ultimate mystery?
At times he sets aside three and lets go of two; at times he acts according to the immediate circumstances. Although it is thus, only those on the same path truly know.
But tell me: what is the matter that is known? You must turn over the nostrils before you will succeed. [Ascending the hall: "Bodhidharma."
The Patriarch is underfoot; you cannot tread upon him, nor can you lift him up. Examine him closely right before your eyes: where did the illness reside at that moment?
Zhang Gong is skilled at diagnosing the pulse; Li Gong is skilled at administering medicine.
The two vie with one another to treat him at once, yet neither medicine is employed nor do they harmonize. A mistake, a mistake! "Go drink tea."

Chan Master Wenshu Siye of Changde Prefecture was a butcher by trade in his worldly life. One day, while slaughtering a pig, he suddenly attained a profound and penetrating realization of the source of the mind.
He immediately abandoned his occupation to become a bhikṣu and composed a verse, saying: "Yesterday was the heart of a yakṣa; today is the face of a bodhisattva.
Between the bodhisattva and the yakṣa, there is not even a single thread’s distance. He went to visit Wenshu, who said, "You are..."
"When slaughtering a pig, what did you see that caused you to shave your head and set out on pilgrimage? The Master then made the gesture of wielding a butcher's knife and shouted, "This butcher!
Go to the hall! The Master then went down to the hall. Later, while presiding over the seat at Wenshu, he ascended the hall and, citing the story of Zhaozhou’s interrogation of the old woman, said:
"The old man Zhaozhou has seen through the old woman; his face is green and his eyes are black."
Han: "You cannot deceive me.
Chan Master Haoshan Xun, a successor of Chan Master Liaoyun of Chouyan in Yiwu, Wuzhou, ascended the hall and raised the case of Zhaozhou’s “The dog has no Buddha-nature.”
The *huatou* says: Zhaozhou’s dog has no Buddha-nature. Ten thousand layers of green mountains conceal an ancient mirror;
a barefoot Persian enters the Great Tang; the eight-armed Nārāyaṇa executes the true decree. *Du!* (Hush!)
The lay practitioner Pan Lianggui, whose courtesy name was Yirong, was forty years of age when he turned his mind toward the ancestral gate.

Wherever he went, he followed the assembly to inquire and test his understanding. Later, he relied upon Fodeng; after a long time, however, he did not reach accord. He therefore complained, saying, "I only wish to know:
what is it like at the moment of death? Fodeng replied, "A fine envelope! Keep it for use; if you do not resolve this now, it will not be right later."
As he was leaving, the other suddenly swapped the envelope with him, leaving him utterly at a loss for how to rectify it.
The Official said, "I have been contemplating Nanquan’s story about the cat for a very long time, yet I still cannot penetrate it thoroughly; what can be done?
Dēng replied, "You are merely occupied with trying to understand another's cat, unaware that you have lost your own dog. At these words, the Official was as if awakened from a drunken stupor.
He then presented a verse, saying: "My own cat has long been lost; the neighbor's cat, when asked about it, is regrettable.
Falling flowers and flowing water—let them intrude as they will. Deng said, "It is not easy for you, sir, to have taken this step forward.
You must further know that there is a matter 'above' before you have attained it. Nowadays, scholars and officials who speak of Chan and speak of the Way merely rely upon intellectual principles."
One simply feels joyful. For the most part, it is like buying oil-cakes with money: once eaten, one is no longer hungry;
as for everything else, people say it deceives them, which is also quite laughable. Gong responded, "Yes, yes."
Chan Master Shouyuan of Suian, Wuweisi of Hanzhou, was a dharma heir of Chan Master Litan Ming.
He was the son of the Shi family of that same prefecture. At the age of thirteen, he suffered from blindness in his eyes;

he subsequently went to rely upon Chan Master Neng of Qichan, where he received full ordination. Later, he traveled out of the gorges to Baofeng, arriving just as the Master was ascending the hall. Baofeng quoted Yongjia, saying:
"The single moon universally manifests in all waters; all the moons in the water are subsumed within the single moon. Upon hearing this, the Master was relieved and attained realization.
Later, when he ascended the hall to teach, he unified the myriad with the one: "The single moon universally manifests in all waters," thereby bringing the myriad back to the one.
All waters and moons are encompassed within a single moon. When expanded, it pervades the entire Dharma-realm; when withdrawn, not even a hair’s breadth remains.
Nevertheless, although the paths of expansion and withdrawal differ, this matter fundamentally possesses no diverse essence.

Only by being able to fix a single eye upon the root source can one see that all Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of successive generations have all manifested from within this very midst. III.

The twelve divisions of the canon and all the sūtras flow forth entirely from within this. Heaven and earth, the sun and moon, and the myriad phenomena of the universe are all established from within this.
The three realms and nine stages, the seven destinies and four modes of birth, all emerge and submerge from within this.
From the hundreds of thousands of dharma-bodies and immeasurable subtle meanings, down to the worldly arts and crafts of various skills—all arise therefrom.
All have fully manifested this reality. Thus, when the World-Honored One held up a flower, Kāśyapa immediately smiled;
when Bodhidharma faced the wall, the Second Patriarch thereby attained peace of mind. When peach blossoms bloomed profusely, Lingyun’s doubts were completely purified;
when striking bamboo produced a sound, Xiangyan suddenly forgot all that he knew. This extended to Panshan awakening to the Way at a meat counter, and Maitreya toward...
In the fish market, he received people with sincerity; it was said that even in moments of haste or distress, he was always thus.
Walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, he was always within this state.
Since he possessed such wonders, such radiance, such vastness, and such omnipresence, why is it that you all still have delusion and enlightenment? Do you wish to know?
Fortunately, there is no place where he does not shine; yet, there is still a time when he is not fully manifest.
Chan Master Wanan Desheng of Yunju in Nankang Commandery, a dharma successor of Chan Master Longxiang Gui, was born into the He family of Hanzhou. At the age of twenty, he received full ordination.
He practiced and lectured for a long time, after which he abandoned his studies to seek the Way from Mañjuśrī, asking about the essential points of the Buddha-dharma.
Mañjuśrī showed him this verse: "The Khitans have broken the Persian camp; They have seized the precious jewel and are selling it in the village.

The destitute beggar at the crossroads Has a bag of elegance hanging from his waist. As the Master was about to respond, Mañjuśrī said, "Do not err. The Master withdrew to reflect for three years before finally attaining realization.
Regarding his intent: he went to see [the master] in order to perceive the Buddha-nature, but his faculties did not accord with the teaching.

He entered Min Province and visited Zhuan-an at Gushan, where he immediately asked, "The National Teacher said, 'I do not step over the stone gate. What is the meaning of this? An responded with a shout, saying, "Idle words!
At that moment, the Master attained realization. Later, while residing there, a monk asked: "I do not ask about the Sage who transcends the three realms without reliance; how is it otherwise?"
“This is the true person of no station. The Master said, “When heard, it is rich and noble; when seen, one is poor. [The monk] said, “Lift your head and you must cover your ears;
tilt your palm and you immediately turn over. The Master said, “Where is this true person of no station?
[The monk] said, “Old man, you do not even recognize the pivot of your own discourse. The Master said, “I grant you thirty blows.”
Chan Master Huiwen of Lu’an at Langshan in Tongzhou was the son of the Zheng family of Fuzhou. He traveled extensively to study under various masters.

Later, he relied upon Zhuan’an at Donglin; not long after, when Zhuan’an retired from his duties, the Master went to visit Gao’an Wu, Nanhua Bing, and Caotang Qing, all of whom recognized his potential.
When Zhuan’an moved to Qianyuan in Min, the Master returned to visit him. Zhuan’an asked:
Sentiment creates a barrier to wisdom; conceptualization alters the essence. Do not remain imprisoned; bring forth a single phrase that will lead you toward the path of long-standing wisdom.
The Master was then relieved and composed a verse, saying: "Squeezed out until my whole body is a mouth, What prevents me from scolding the rain and rebuking the wind?

Last night, a fierce tiger in the village ahead Bite to death the great beast of the southern mountain. The head of the hermitage nodded in approval. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he said: "Śākyamuni..."
Laozi spent forty-nine years plotting within his command tent; Maitreya Bodhisattva has spent ninety-one kalpas wading through water and dragging through mud.
Ordinary sentiments and the measures of sages cannot be eradicated; even when the principle is illuminated and awareness attained, there still remains a mere proclamation.

To take the Buddha’s intent and the Patriarchs’ intent as such is like using fish eyes for bright pearls; to distinguish between the Mahayana and Hinayana is like mistaking orange peel for a fierce fire.
"O people, you must open wide the treasure-store of your own breast and bring forth the precious jewels of your own house to bestow them universally upon the poor at the crossroads.
Suddenly, if there should be a clever fellow among the assembly who comes forward and says, 'Fine food is not for the well-fed to eat,' I would simply say to him:
'Yongzhou is still tolerable; the most bitter suffering is Silla.'"

Chan Master Shuanglin De-yong of Wuzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Yunju Wu, was the son of the Dai family of that same prefecture. He ascended the hall and, raising his mallet and竖 (upright)ing his whisk, said:

"Under the gate of the Patriarchs, one uses yellow leaves to stop a child's crying; to speak of the wondrous and discuss the ultimate before the eyes of a patch-robed monk is like looking for plums at a plum grove."
And so it quenches thirst. Today, at this mountain boundary, I shall cast it all away—this "it," "that," and "so-and-so. No longer shall I point east or paint west;
rather, from within the life-vein of the Buddhas of the three periods and the very marrow of the patriarchs of the six generations, I shall pour out my heart and explain it thoroughly for you all.
After a long silence, he said: "To weep until the blood flows is of no use; it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring."

Chan Master Daoxian Wuzhuo of Wannian, Tiantai, was the son of the Hong family of that prefecture. He ascended the hall and said: "To oppose the superior with one’s full capacity is still to be halfway there.

When the pecking and the breaking of the shell occur simultaneously, white clouds stretch for ten thousand miles. As soon as a trace of manifestation arises, one has already fallen into the second or third rank.

If you do not reveal even a glint of your edge, what principle could possibly be established? Tell me, how should the matter of the ancestors from of old be handled? He then struck the floor with his staff and descended.
"The fault of man: to impose punishment upon him for his crime. Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Qianfeng, who addressed the assembly, saying:
"If you raise one, you must not raise two; if you let one point pass, you fall into the second. Yunmen stepped out from the assembly and said:
"Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan. Qianfeng said: "The head cook shall not be required to join the communal labor tomorrow. The Master said: [This concludes the case.]
When we meet, there is no need for anger; you are destitute and I am poor as well. You say I am encroaching on my early rising, yet there are still those traveling at night.
Chan Master Zhongji Shanneng of Fuzhou was a native of Yanling. He had been coming and going between Longmen and Yunju for many years without attaining any realization.
One day, while they were working together on a communal task of sorting vegetables, Gao'an suddenly threw a cat into the Master’s lap.
The Master was about to deliberate when Chan’an grabbed him by the chest and tripped him over. Thereupon, the Great Matter was clearly understood. He ascended the hall and said:
"Ten thousand ages of the eternal void; a single day’s wind and moon. One must not let the wind and moon of a single day obscure the eternal void of ten thousand ages.
Nor must one fail to understand the wind and moon of a single day because of the eternal void of ten thousand ages. But what, then, is the wind and moon of a single day? [A monk] stepped forward.
All fear the scorching heat; I cherish the length of summer days. A fragrant breeze comes from the south, bringing a subtle coolness to the halls and pavilions.
Whether you understand this or not, take care not to take it upon yourself as something to be grasped.
Chan Master Yunju Puyun Ziyuan of Nankang Commandery was the son of the Yong family from Mianzhou. At the age of nineteen, he passed the scriptural examination and received full ordination.
He remained in the garden of the teachings for five years before crossing the pass and traveling south. There, he visited various eminent masters in succession; he first went to Longmen.
One day, while in the corridors, he beheld a portrait of a Westerner (an Indian) and attained realization. That night, he informed Gao’an, who then raised [a koan] for him.
The Gatha of Fayen says: "Head adorned with a sable-fur hat, A horned awl suspended at the waist; His words do not allow others to understand— One must have someone to interpret them for him.
He then struck a match and showed it to him, saying, "I have finished translating it for you. At this, [Dongshan] attained great enlightenment.
He presented a verse, saying: "The sounds and languages of foreign lands are inexhaustible; beneath Qiyun Peak, they are all understood at once.
The gateway of the mouth is vast and boundless; it swallows whole the thorny chestnuts of Yangqi. Yan'an sent the Master to rely on Foyan. Foyan said to him:
"My Way is heading East. [The Master] ascends the hall. He cites a monk’s question to Yunmen: "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body?
Yunmen said, "Hiding one's body within the North Star. The Master says: North, South, East, West—ten thousand, ten thousand, a thousand;
Heaven and Earth, above and below—both are boundless. Meeting and seeing one another, they laugh "he-he"; Fingers counting, head raised—the moon is halfway up the sky.
Chan Master Tui’an Xiū of Jiànfú in Ráozhōu, a successor of Chan Master Wùjù Xíng, ascended the hall and said: "At the time of entering the summer retreat, the left eye weighs half a catty;

at the time of concluding the summer retreat, the right eye weighs eight taels. In vain do we speak of the ninety-day *an-gu* (summer retreat); all we gain is a belly full of deluded thoughts. Straight!
Though they may be full of holes and cracks, they cannot escape the staff of this mountain monk.
Even so, a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt does not fire its trigger for the sake of a mere field mouse. [Ascending the hall:

The late Master habitually used a single blow from behind the head to strip away the many crookednesses within the students' chests. In his day, Vinaya Master Kebin once fell victim to this poison of Xinghua.

Often throughout the monasteries of the world, this is called "surpassing the lineage and having extraordinary eyes. This not only fails the legacy of Xinghua, but it also means Kebin has suffered humiliation.
If one were a true descendant of Linji, they would never merely cling to the grass or attach themselves to the wood.
Zifu was delighted to see a fellow practitioner today who emptied his heart and laid bare his belly; he then planted his staff and gave a shout, saying: "Do you still recognize the former master?"
“Where do they land? These dead Zen practitioners are like hemp and millet. Ascending the hall, he said: “Speech issues forth but is not sound—what is this?
Form precedes things but is not an object. Do not confuse the needle and the chisel; pass through! The wind and waves at the Dragon Gate are even more perilous. *Du!*”
Chan Master Huiguang of Guifeng in Xinzhou, a native of Jianning, ascended the hall and said: "For several days now, the heat has been like being scorched by fire;
with this entire body having nowhere to rest, even such reflection is a source of affliction for people. This, however, is not yet the true affliction.
To have matters concerning one's own fundamental nature that remain unclarified—this is truly affliction. Therefore, Bodhidharma..."
The Master was vexed. He wished to swallow all people, but his throat was too narrow; he wished to spit them out, but his teeth obstructed him.
Unable to take them in and unable to let them go, he was vexed for nine years. Had he not been willing to sacrifice his life for the Second Patriarch, he would often have found no way to turn back.
His vexation was such that he wished for death; this is what is meant by "the patriarchal ancestors left their affairs unfinished."
The calamity extends to their descendants. Later, the Hermitage Master of Lotus Peak arrived here and, being vexed, refused to stay.
Nanyue Huairang the Great arrived here and, being vexed, refused to descend the mountain. Furthermore, Linji and Deshan exhausted their own efforts, yet their underlying anxieties remained;
today Guifeng provides for them a handleless bowl, so that they may forever be free from idle concerns.
I shall clarify this for you all, breaking it down from the very beginning. (He strikes the meditation staff once. One person has his cheek exposed at the back of his head;
another has no teeth in front of his face; and there are several more whose nostrils are missing half.
Without the need for further examination, you all should cease standing here drowsing; you simply do not realize that the rice basket and the cooking pot are right within your own home.
At that moment, it was all lost. If you do not believe this, simply go home and check for yourself.
