Sinking black beans, one’s whole life is obscured; One must speak of the bountiful harvest beyond the kalpas. The white snow is spun, and the mulberry trees grow thick..."
Green. The yellow clouds of grain have been harvested, and the rice is now turning green.

Chan Master Guyuan Dao of Jingci Temple in Hangzhou cited the public case of Danxia Tianran’s initial meeting with Shitou, regarding the incident of weeding the grass before the Buddha hall, and offered this verse:

Master Wuxin of Beihai at Daochang Monastery in Huzhou addressed the assembly, citing the following:

When Huangbo was in the hall of Yanguan Monastery paying homage to the Buddha, Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang dynasty was then a śrāmaṇera and asked: "Do not seek by clinging to the Buddha; do not seek by clinging to the Dharma."
"Seek not in the Sangha; when you prostrate to an elder, what is it that you seek? Baizhang replied, "Seek not in the Buddha, seek not in the Dharma, and seek not in the Sangha.

The Kelp Seed Causality. The verse says: Mixing water with mud, busy with such trivial matters; He has been exposed by him, a great perversion.
Though he may indeed have grasped the Emperor’s intent, How can he avoid plunging his entire body into the cauldron?
Chan Master Daxie Zhongqian of Xuedou in Mingzhou was the son of the Ying family from Yiwu.

In his youth, upon seeing the *Mind-King Inscription* by Master Fu Dashi, he resolved to leave the household life. He first visited Xian’an, who, recognizing his potential yet wishing to test him, suppressed him, saying:
"If you have not eliminated the habitual tendencies of a Confucian scholar, how can you study the Way? To reach the state of great rest and great cessation, you must be like a wooden puppet."
He departed. Inspired by this stimulus, the Master redoubled his efforts, striving diligently morning and night without slackening.

One day, he suddenly attained realization and thereafter named himself Dayixie (Great Rest). Later, he relied upon Songyuan Yue. One day, while in the meditation hall, Songyuan raised the koan of Bimozhe holding a fork;
the Master was suddenly and completely enlightened. He ascended the hall and said, citing the story of how Master Ying’an asked Master Miam: "How..."
"This is the Eye of the True Dharma. Mi said, "A broken sand pot. He spoke in verse: "A white jade ball carved from mud, A golden *kūṇa* (Kunlun) cast from iron.
A thousand-year-old滞貨 (stale goods) no one buys; It cannot avoid burdening descendants today.
[He] sent a verse to the *vina* (chant leader): "Xinghua struck Kebin in those days; The story remains a topic of talk in the monasteries for a thousand years. The clouds..."
Huang Youbang set it high on a shelf; he simply brewed tea and sent it out the door.
Chan Master Nuo’an Ruozhao cited Songyuan’s instruction to the assembly: “Why do clear-eyed monks lose their nostrils?
There is a thief, yet no stolen goods. Verse: Killing ten thousand people and injuring three thousand— Solely wielding the single-pointed staff.
The mechanism is incomplete. Ten thousand acres of blue waves on a bright moonlit night; a single short blast from a flute on a fishing boat. Inscription for the Second Patriarch:
Seeking the mind, there is nowhere to find it—self-deception in vain. He willingly endured the cold of snow waist-deep. Rising after three prostrations, he stood in his place;
Who would have known that the entire world is a surging wave? Verses on Recalling the Past at Huating: My livelihood...
The entire boat is cast in a single haul; once the scaled fish are in hand, its head is pulled out. Having come here, I did not behold the Master’s personal instruction;
by the willow bank, the trees lean as they dip into the azure current.
Chan Master Yun’an Puyan of Daofang in Huzhou inscribed this eulogy for the portrait of Zhaozhou:

“Without reason, he held up the seven-pound robe; How many practitioners have applied their minds to study it? They all take refuge in Qingzhou, Failing to realize that spring’s colors lie in Jiangnan.
Addressing the assembly, he cited the koan of Dongshan eating fruit on a winter night and offered this verse: Dongshan...

The disciple brings disgrace upon his family tradition; the Head Seat buries his own potential. Both have embroidered the *yuanyang* (mandarin ducks), yet for a thousand ages they remain unable to lift them up.
When Chan Master Jili Tan first resided at Yanqing in Siming, he later moved to Qionglong in Suzhou.
[He taught at] Zhenze Puzhi, Zhenjiang Ganlu, and Zhenzhou Changlu, later residing at Huqiu. Entering the hall, he raised the following case:
A monk asked Xianglin, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? Lin said, "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains.
The Master said, "How could a rabbit ever leave its burrow? If someone were to ask Yanqing, 'What is the matter beneath the patched robe? I would simply say—"

He said to him: "Fish purchased from the boat are exceptionally delicious; wine bought after treading through the snow is doubly fragrant. Entering the hall for instruction, he said: "In every thought, Śākyamuni appears in the world;
at every moment, Maitreya descends to be born. Thus, one suddenly transcends the time before heaven and earth were yet divided."
Without traversing the rungs of the ladder, he overturns the treasure-store and departs just so. Thus, one can open immeasurable Dharma-gates;
thus, one can expound hundreds of thousands of wondrous meanings. Suddenly grasping his staff, he strikes it once and says:
"The immeasurable Dharma-gates and the hundreds of thousands of wondrous meanings are all completely shattered right here. Do you know where Tiger Hill has landed? Rely on the staff!"
Zhaozhou said: "When the ancestors do not understand, the calamity reaches their descendants. Regarding the verse on the story of Lingyun seeing peach blossoms:
"Peach blossoms bloom everywhere in the third month; Lingyun’s two eyes were filled with dust and grime. Master Xie has once again refined the hands that once caught the giant fish."
"One cannot help but bury oneself in a single place.
Chan Master Shaoshi Guangmu of Ruiyan in Taizhou ascended the hall and said: "He raised the case of Caoshan Xuanhua.
Once, while a monk was standing in attendance, Caoshan said, 'The Way-farer, it is quite hot. The monk replied, 'Yes. Caoshan asked, 'As for this heat, where does it turn back?'"
[A monk] said, "I avoid it by evading within the cauldrons and furnace coals. Shan said, "But as for being within the cauldrons and furnace coals, how do you evade?
The monk said, "The various sufferings cannot reach me. The Master composed a verse:
"Blinding the three eyes at the crown of the head, One wanders freely amidst the cauldrons and furnace coals. If one says the various sufferings cannot reach him, When has this ever truly been so?"
Dītóu’s Inscription and Eulogy on the Portrait of the Fourth Patriarch: Purple clouds fly from the summit of Pòtóu Peak;
Three times he declined the imperial summons in the verdant heights. Though this "stale merchandise" has no further use, It should not be handed over to a mere child.
Chan Master Shankaikai of Jinshan in Zhenjiang Prefecture ascended the hall and, citing the story of Mian’s “Broken Sand Pot,” offered this verse:
Fayan brought it up and was already deceiving himself; Needlessly, he wrongly matched it to the broken sand pot. Now it is impossible to cover it over throughout the world;
It brings calamity upon the monasteries and their descendants.
Chan Master Wuxiang Fan of Xuedou in Mingzhou ascended the hall and said: "He cited Zhaozhou’s words:
'As soon as there is right and wrong, confusion arises and the mind is lost. Is there still any possibility of answering? A monk related this to Luopu, who tapped his teeth.
He then related it to Yunju, who said, 'Why bother? When the monk returned and related this to Zhaozhou, Zhaozhou said, 'There are many such people in the South.'"
He lost his life and forfeited his existence. [The monk] said, "I beg the Master to bring it up.

Just as Zhaozhou was about to repeat the previous dialogue, the monk pointed to a monk nearby and said, "This monk, having finished eating his rice, speaks such words. The Master composed a verse, saying: "The seated one sees the standing one."
"Standing here, I see one sitting there. Alas, old Zhaozhou! Seeing ghosts with one's own eyes in broad daylight!
The lay practitioner Lu You, styled Wuguang and nicknamed Fangong, was a native of Shanyin.

He once visited Songyuan at Lingyin Monastery and asked, "May I hear about the study of mind-to-mind transmission? Songyuan replied, "Since it is a mind-to-mind transmission, how could it be obtained through hearing?"

He attained it. Shidian nodded in silent understanding and presented this verse: "How many times have I driven my carriage into the imperial capital? Whenever I met a monk, my eyes were equally clear and green.
Only today do I see the distinction of the Zen school: To speak of existence or non-existence requires you to listen with your eyes."

Master Qingxi Yuan of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Tian Tong Jing, ascended the hall and said: "When Bodhidharma came from the West, he occupied the entire area of a single sitting mat.
Once Shen Guang paid him three prostrations, it was all taken up at once, leaving no room for the descendants of later generations to carve out their own strength."

"A separate realm. For those in the lineage of patch-robed monks, they brush aside the weeds and gaze at the wind, traveling from Wu to Yue morning and evening; to Mount Tiantai in the south and Mount Wutai in the north.
Have you ever trodden upon the tip of the staff or the sole of the straw sandals? After a long silence, he said: 'Above all, do not tread upon them.'"
Chan Master Xixi Xi of Gongan in Jingzhou ascended the hall and said: "The place where mind-mind is shallow is in truth most profound;
The path of the Way is remote and mysterious, with no one reaching it. If you walk too fast, you will not tread upon it; If you walk too slow, you will miss it.
For many years at Shaolin, I sat through the blossoming of spring flowers; Yet I recall the Western-come Hu Daomo."
Chan Master Yuantian of Xichan Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall to open the furnace for the winter retreat. "Everyone guards the sky within the jar;
though earth may overturn and heaven may fall, I am not like this. With a single stroke of the hammer, sparks fly forth;

the Luojiang River has burned the boat of Master Xie. In praise of the portrait of Monk Zhoutou, he said: "Bloody and raw—this is the heart of the ancient Buddha. How many times has it been raised up? Who..."
This is the record of Master Jichuang Youzhao of Yuwang Monastery in Mingzhou, whose secular surname was Deng and who hailed from Fuzhou, Min County.
He received the full precepts under Huiduo of Jiufeng Rong’an. At that time, Kuchan Jing was propagating the Way at Yishan; the Master went there to visit him. One day, Jing—
Question: "Ever since the first sight of the peach blossoms, until now I have had no further doubts. Wherein lies his state of being without doubt?
The Master laughed loudly and walked out. Jingshen approved of this. Later, when Jingshen moved to Lingyin, the Master served as the Head of Records (*neiji*).
Subsequently, he also visited Damei Shiyuan, Huqiu Jili, Mufeng Wuzhun, and Dajue at Jingshan. All...
The elders all held him in deep esteem and respect. When he returned home to visit his aged mother, Xuefeng Chijue retained him to serve as the head of the secretariat.
The Governor of Min, Zhao Ruyu, who was well-acquainted with the Master’s reputation, invited him to propagate the Dharma at Daxiangshan and later moved him to Huangbo in Fuzhou.
At that time, Lin Xiyi, the Left Historian of Zhuxi, followed the Master to discuss the mind-dharma, serving him with devoted sincerity. He composed the *Lao Lai De*... [text fragment].

Regarding the verse, "Friends are like teachers and juniors; when parting, who will be my companion in leisure? he was appointed by imperial decree to the Jiangxin Temple, later transferring to Yujia.
When a disaster struck, he exerted all his strength to restore it, for which the court bestowed gold and silk. He then constructed a precious *śarīra* stupa.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The Eight Auspicious Ones. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "The Six [Perfections]."
"Extraordinary! [A monk] asked, "What is the Sangha? The Master said, "Its face and eyes are present right now. He ascended the hall and said: "The six sense-objects are not evil;
they are identical to perfect enlightenment. The crow caws, 'ka ka'; the magpie chirps, 'jiao jiao. North of the river and south of the river, the tide rises and the tide falls."
The spring breeze in the third month brings fragrance to the flowers and grasses. Where does Sudhana seek the pavilions? *He!* [A shout. Entering the hall, he asked:
"What is the Way? "A wooden post. "What is Chan? "A brick. When the ancient worthies gave such instructions, ten people were left with five pairs of hands.

He remained unconcerned and did nothing about it, little realizing that he was precisely scratching the itch of Mount Mao. Why? Because the construction of the temple hall was exactly what was required.
Chan Master Yuzhu Yuanzhi of Fashi Temple in Quanzhou, a native of the Xue clan of Changxi, attained enlightenment while studying under Tiantong.
He presented a verse on dwelling in the mountains, saying: "A saffron-colored *kāṣāya* with a thousand or ten hundred folds, Leaning against a pine tree, I stroke my belly and watch the clouds fly.
If someone asks me about the joy of dwelling in the mountains, I tell them: 'In the depths of spring, the bamboo shoots and bracken are lush.

In the first month of the Bingyin year of the Xianchun era of Emperor Duzong of the Song dynasty, he sat in the lotus posture, wrote this verse, and passed away. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the Southern Monastery of Gushan.
Chan Master Baoen Taigu ascended the hall and said: "If one discusses this matter, it does not involve the workings of thought or intention;
it has nothing to do with silent illumination or the forgetting of the self. To attain a state of transparent clarity, you must undergo a 'pouring of sweat' [a moment of great realization].
But tell me, what is it like after the sweat has poured? Suddenly he called to his attendant: 'Bring me the fan! He ascended the hall again and said: "The night is cold and the frost is heavy."
The wind blows and the cold increases all the more. As the seasons pass by in negligence, how is one’s own matter? Striking the meditation seat, he said:
"How can one present this to those who are not true知音 (zhīyīn—those with knowing ears)? Ascending the hall for the discourse, he said:

"For members of the monastic community who travel abroad on pilgrimage, brushing aside the weeds and gazing at the wind, the first requirement is that you recognize the path. Only then will the path not lead you astray regarding east, west, south, or north, so that you may arrive."
The dwelling is the home. Should one slightly stray into defilement or deviation, there is a single signpost at five li and double milestones at ten li. "Where is it?
Where else could it be? Throwing down his staff, he said, "Look beneath your feet."
Chan Master Choun of Xiujing in Shaoxing composed a verse for the Buddha’s Birthday: The poisonous seeds of Vairambha wind have blossomed into toxic flowers;
They add but more to Yunmen’s cup after his drunkenness. Today at Keqiao the weather turns foul; Thin mist and sparse rain wash away the yellow plum blossoms. (Note:
This verse is recorded in *Zadudhai* as being by Xiyuan, which is an error.)
Chan Master Gaofeng Chong’s Verse on the First Patriarch’s Encounter with Emperor Wu of Liang: Unfurling his banner and deploying his array, he entered the realm of Liang;

Before even beholding the Emperor’s countenance, he had already surrendered. Though he possessed supernormal powers, they could not be displayed; With a single reed-raft, he crossed the vast Yangtze River.
Chan Master Chijue Daochong of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Jianfu Sheng. He was the son of the Xun family from Wuxin.

Possessing a character that far surpassed his peers, he initially attempted the imperial examinations as a *jinshi* candidate but did not succeed. He subsequently studied under the master at Miaoyin Monastery in Zizhou and later traveled to Chengdu.
He had been studying the sutras and śāstras at a lecture hall when, in the *Renzi* year of the Shaoxi era of the Song dynasty (1192), he left the Gorges.

At that time, Caoyuan Sheng was appearing in the world at Miaoguo; the Master went to pay him a visit. Upon hearing his formal instructions (*dichang*), he attained a realization. He entered the meditation hall and was appointed to attend to the incense.

Day and night, he was subjected to severe blows and heavy staff-strokes without any leniency. Consequently, much of the Master’s lifelong intellectual views and attachments vanished without a trace. When Sheng moved to Guipeng, the Master...
He served [his master] for another three years before departing to travel through Zhejiang with a verse that included the lines: "There remains but one pair of hands in this state of poverty;
I shall go toward all quarters to scratch my itches. Later, he visited Songyuan at Lingyin Monastery. Songyuan’s gate was steep and forbidding;

although he stayed there for eight months, he did not gain entry into the inner chamber. When someone reported that the Master had lost a worthy disciple, Songyuan said, "I have already opened wide the eight characters."

"Registering as a guest. "He is indeed he; you have missed him right before your face. Upon hearing this, the Master lost both his verbal and auditory faculties, and he gained a thorough vision of the Cao Yuan at Miaoguo.
At Guifeng, [Zhaozhou’s] laughter, jests, scoldings, and rebukes were all skillful means for the benefit of others.

From then on, he no longer harbored doubts regarding the tongues of the old monks throughout the land. He first took up residence at Tianning Monastery in Jiaxing, where his reputation reached the imperial court.

Zhongxian Prince Wei was appointed to Jiangshan by imperial decree; he resided there for thirteen years. In the Jiaxi year, the Ji-hai cycle (1259), Gushan sent an invitation, but before he could depart, a summons from Xuefeng arrived.
He had been at Xuefeng for only half a year when an imperial edict transferred him to Tiantong.
When the seat at Yuwang was vacant, he concurrently assumed the position of abbot. Entering the hall, he said: "That which Tiantong used, Yuwang has no need to use. Yuwang..."
The King uses it as his foundation; the Celestial Youth has no further use for it. Even so, where there is no use, there is abundance of use.

One arrow, two vultures—both fall at the hand. On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, he ascended the hall and spoke on the occasion of the World-Honored One’s realization of the Way upon beholding the morning star, saying:
"Before Mount Zhengjue, the eyes were lost; whether ordinary or sage, all are born blind. To this very night..."
At night, the morning star appeared. "Who would be willing to walk where he walks? After a short while, he received an imperial decree to move to Mount Jing.
One day, he suddenly wrote a record for his funerary stupa as a final letter, saying: "The anniversary of Wuzu’s passing is on the eighteenth day of the third month;

I shall depart on the fifteenth, so I cannot offer incense or perform the ritual offerings. Order the drum to be beaten, ascend the seat, and take leave of the assembly. He then ascended the hall and gave a discourse, citing the world...
As the World-Honored One was about to enter nirvana, he addressed the assembly, saying: "You should all carefully contemplate my body, which is the color of purple-polished gold.

Behold it with full satisfaction; do not allow yourselves to have cause for regret later. Today it exists, but tomorrow it shall be no more. The Master said: "Throughout his life, the World-Honored One exhausted every skillful means.
Yet at the moment of his departure, he could not attain birth when seeking birth, nor could he attain death when seeking death. It was like being on a mountain..."
The monk was not like this. When he wished to act, he acted; when he wished to depart, he departed. Even the eight-armed Nala could not have stopped him.
Rising from his seat during the middle watch of the night, the attendant requested a verse. The Master said, "The final word cannot be deliberated upon;
it requires only that a person directly take it up. A short while later, he passed away. At his cremation, there were countless five-colored *śarīra* relics, which were enshrined as a legacy.
He was instructed to return for burial at Yushan Hermitage in Jinling. His disciples divided his remains, with half being enshrined in a stupa at Changpu Field.
He was eighty-two years old and had been a monk for sixty-one years.

Chan Master Shuangshan Yuan of Pingjiang Huqiu, a successor of Chan Master Yinjing Rou, addressed the assembly. He cited the story of Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty dreaming of a divine being who exhorted him to resolve upon Bodhicitta, and offered this verse:
"Ten thousand miles of songs celebrate the Sage’s transformation; Gentle breezes and timely rains bring joy to woodcutters and farmers."
Not because of the three calls at Mount Song, who would recognize true peace in the absence of form? [He] raised the story of Miam’s “Breaking the Sand Pot” and offered this verse:
“When the young son of a nobleman from the Five Tombs was in his prime, He galloped on horseback through the spring breeze with joyful intent.
Spending no regret over his golden pellets, he struck the yellow orioles beneath the sea-blossom trees. [He] inscribed these [verses] upon the wall paintings of the two corridors at Cold Spring.
It is said: Within each and every atom is the firm and dense body; changing heads and faces, it shifts its spirit.
Who would know that striking the east wall is the west wall? All are people from the assembly on Vulture Peak.

Compiled by the Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple in the Capital, the Monk (Chao Yong).

Chan Master Xueyan Zuqin of Yangshan in Yuanzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Jingshan Fan of the twentieth generation under Nanyue.
He was a native of Wuzhou in Zhejiang. He entered the monastic order at the age of five. At ten...

At sixteen, he underwent tonsure; at eighteen, he began his travels as a wandering monk (*paryaṭaka*). He first visited such venerable elders as Shuanglin Yuan and Miaofeng Shan, yet he attained no realization.

Hearing that Master Mie was residing at Jingci Monastery, he carried incense in his breast to seek instruction. Master Lie showed him the story of the three blows of the staff from the Linji tradition.
There was likewise no place for him to enter. He subsequently went up Mount Jing to pay his respects to Wuzhun Shanfeng.

He relied upon Shanfeng for the longest period, pursuing his inquiries with such keen resolve that he remained shrouded in his robes, his side never touching the mat for several years. One day, as he sat upon his meditation cushion, the space before him suddenly opened wide.
It was as if the earth had collapsed, leaving the ground completely bare for over half a month; no signs of movement occurred, and from that point on, he remained seated in meditative absorption.
This obstruction in his chest persisted for ten years. Later, together with Zhong Shiliang, he traveled to Tianmu Mountain in western Zhejiang. One day, while walking in front of the Buddha Hall...
Raising my eyes, I beheld the ancient cypress tree. This triggered the realization of the state I had previously attained; everything, including its very foundation, was cast away at once.
That which had been obstructing my chest dispersed with a sudden burst, like emerging from a dark room into the light of day.
From this point on, I no longer doubted birth, no longer doubted death, no longer doubted the Buddhas, and no longer doubted the Patriarchs. Only then did I truly see where the old man Wuzu stood.
On account of the casting of a bell at Mount Jing, he was commissioned to compose a preface. The Master took up his brush and composed a verse, saying: "The entire body is but a single mouth;
Rolled forth from within the furnace of a hundred refinements. After escorting the setting sun back to its rest, It now urges the bright moon up the towers.
From this point on, his reputation resounded throughout the monastic community. He first took charge of Longxing Temple in Tan, and subsequently moved to Xiang.

Xi Daolin resided at Nanming in Chuzhou, Husheng in Xianju, and Guangxiao in Huzhou. During the Jiyi year of the Xianchun era of Emperor Duzong of the Song dynasty, he took up residence at Yangshan in Yuanzhou.

Lamenting that the fundamental tenets of the school had lost their foundation, the Master consequently brought forth and expounded upon the *citations* (tí) and *verses* (nìng), vigorously promoting the dynamic interplay of "striking" and "singing.

His realization of the ultimate truth was transcendent and peerless; for a time, the wind of the school was revitalized by him. Later, the Great Khan Se-chen of the Yuan dynasty bestowed [an honorary title] upon him.
The honors bestowed upon him were also most magnificent. Entering the hall: Last night the sun set in the west and the old year has passed;
this morning the sun rises from the east and the new year has arrived. Now that the new year has come, what is so extraordinary about it?

An iron tree blooms before the wind—a springtime of a different sort. [After the assembly has left, the Master] enters the hall to thank the Head Seat and the Rector. The Eye of Humanity and Heaven...
The Eye. The guiding principles of the Buddhas and Patriarchs differ in a thousand ways and ten thousand variations, yet they are all unified by a single thread.
How can this be seen? When Kēbī was defeated in a battle of Dharma, Nánquán slew the cat. Ascending the hall, he said: "On a spring day at dawn, the scorched earth turns green;
the cuckoo calls everywhere, urging the plowing. Although this matter is most clear, one must not look upon it with the eyes."

Listen with your ears. Why? As soon as there is a single thread, there is already a single thread. On the day of the Buddha’s Enlightenment at the Eighth Day of the Twelfth Month, he ascended the hall and said:
"The Old Man with the Yellow Face toiled for six years until he found his own nostrils, yet he lost his eyesight.
Tell me, where did it land? Under the midnight sky on the Snowy Mountains, a single star. He ascended the hall again: "Good beans make sauce; good salt makes soup."

Rice can cure hunger; tea can quench thirst. Following this direct line of transmission from above down to the point where principle is ultimate and emotion is forgotten, there is nothing that surpasses this.
For what reason, then, did the old fellow Yangqi say, "A kicking donkey has three legs;
it is right when the eyes are open, and it is right when the eyes are closed"? Ascending the hall, he said: "The rocky gate is steep and perilous; the Jade Gorge flows with murmuring streams."
If you have not yet reached this point, it is natural to harbor doubts. But once you have reached it—how do you express that single phrase of level, open expansiveness?
An ancient path where an iron snake lies across. Ascending the hall, he said: "Heaven cannot cover it; earth cannot support it. Its very substance is fundamentally non-existent."
If you discard it, it remains; if there is no root, it is not non-existent. If it is present, it is not present.

A vajra and a clay deity—rubbing their backs together, they shatter into dust with a single stroke. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Gate of Expedient Means, the Gate of Liberation, the Gate of Vairocana’s Jewel Pavilion.
Striking once with his staff, he said: "All eight characters are opened wide. Nevertheless, although this is so, I permit you only to lodge here for a brief while."
A single breath and a single meal is all there is. If you wish to be directly pointed toward the ground of great rest, great repose, and great bliss, there is a vast living path ahead of you.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The cuckoo cries until its blood drenches the flower branches;

In haste, it bitterly urges one to return home. Yet upon returning to one's native land, one is still like a traveler; In every village, the greens are deep and the reds are sparse. The seal covers all things.

The phrase of *Kun* (Earth). The phrase of following the waves and riding the currents. The phrase that cuts off all streams. If you can realize it here, they will all be strung together on a single thread.
Yangqi’s donkey has three legs. Ascending the hall: All day long the window stands open as I sit in stillness and solitude.

Before the crags, the young bamboo shoots are nearly waist-high. A secluded bird suddenly takes flight and the wisteria flowers fall; the sound of the mountain torrent blows across the stone bridge. At this—
This was seen by Nanming thirty years ago; he took it only as an object of perception. If one were blind and deaf, there would still be one step missing at the top of the hundred-foot pole.
During the first forty-five days of the summer retreat in China, one knows how to advance but not how to retreat;
during the latter forty-five days, one knows how to retreat but not how to advance. On this very day, both advancing and retreating are forgotten. It is the end of the season.
The summer heat reaches its peak; the scented breeze brings coolness from afar. Pointing his staff upright, he said: "At times, one hears the fragrance of a cluster of lotus flowers.

For the Memorial Service, he ascended the hall: The thunderous sound cuts through the plum-shaded mist until it clears away; the formless aspect of the former Buddhas suddenly emerges, beyond the reach of birth, abiding, change, and extinction.
The mountains of Lake Dongting rise steep and azure. He ascended the hall: To say "it is" is to erase it; to say "it is not" is likewise to erase it.

"Scraping away! Let there be no partiality below. There are eyes at the tip of the staff. Thinking thus, I recall the Great Master Huangbo saying, "All of you who travel as monks in this manner—where could you have such a day as today?
This too was Muzhou carrying a single board. Opening the furnace, he ascended the hall.
Upon a dead log there is neither smoke nor fire; within a crystal palace, a blazing conflagration burns the void.
The Śūnyatā-deva’s eyebrows and beard fall off of their own accord. [The Master] picks up his staff and says: "When the staff hears you speak like this, does it believe? Or does it not believe?
He strikes the ground with the staff and says: "Both are shattered. [At the Buddha's Nirvāṇa Temple, he ascends the hall. The willows by the bank sway in gold; the peach blossoms by the stream—
Spitting out jade. Pāpīyān dances without cause; Ānanda weeps on level ground. Why is it so? To personally behold the countenance of the Tathāgata.
Ascending the hall: The spring days linger; the greens are deep and the reds are thin.

One cannot bear the mountain thrush of the deep woods, who also mimics the cuckoo of Jiangnan, crying out every moment, "It is not as good to return home. When Yangshan speaks thus, what does he mean?
This is ultimately the language of the guest; it is the language of the host. When meeting people, do not misquote it. Ascending the hall:
A thousand explanations and ten thousand expositions are not as good as seeing one face in person. A thousand searches and ten thousand inquiries are not as good as having it right at hand.
The cold wind whistles, yellow leaves drift. Cranes sleep atop the pines; clouds lie around the mountain waist. How many times today has dawned once more?
Morning Assembly. The Way is present in daily life, yet in daily life it is not recognized. When hungry, one simply eats; when cold, one simply adds clothing.
On a clear day, one enjoys the sun while leaning on a withered staff, inspecting the plum trees by the stream as they stealthily put forth southern branches toward the warmth.
To advance is to strike one’s head and forehead; to retreat is to fall into pits and ravines; to move is to offend the hand and wound the blade.
"When has the Buddha-dharma ever been seen face-to-face? *Tu!* Do not say that on this day Yangshan lacks the skillful means of a man of no-birth.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Before one's parents were born, what was it ultimately? In its very essence, there is no trace; to seek it is to miss it.
If you do not miss it, are north, south, east, and west not yourself? Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace, he said: "Neither cold nor hot."
The furnace and bellows cast half-true, half-false gold and brass into vases, basins, hairpins, and bracelets; yet they result only in firewood shaped like the character "成" (chéng).
Tell me, how far removed is this from Zhaozhou’s “no guest or host” dialogue? If you have doubts, seek another teacher.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Good rain knows the proper season; in spring, all things sprout forth. An uprooted tree planted upon a rock—its branches and leaves reach everywhere."
The body sprouts in a single night. A monk holding a whisk said: "If the dust of the passions has not been shed, one has eyes but is as if blind.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind is the root; phenomena are the dust. These two are like stains upon a mirror. Once the mirror is broken, the phenomena no longer exist.

Sparse shadows slant across the shallow, clear water; a faint fragrance drifts as the moon sinks into twilight. Ascending the hall, [he noted]: "The Southern Winds enter the performance at the palace..."
A cool breeze arises in the pavilion. The ancestral intent from the West must never be subjected to deliberation. Why? Because what follows is a long discourse.

On the anniversary of National Teacher Wuzu’s passing, he offered incense, saying: "The three turns of speech by Baling; a single cup of tea from Dayang. Where there is kindness, resentment is formed."
To have no affairs is to be an enemy’s house. The cuckoo cries until its blood dyes the mountain flowers. [Ascending the hall: It is the full moon of an intercalary month.
The moon is as it always is; when clouds bury it, it is dark; when the clouds disperse, it shines. Holding up his whisk, he said: "Tell me, is this the cloud?"
Is this the moon? Forbidding the blurring of one's eyes. Little Śākyamuni avoided offering incense; he stood with his spade thrust into the ground, appearing as if ten parts dead.
Then, pulling out the spade, he departed—playing with the restless spirit of a ghost. The mountain birds and mountain flowers laugh themselves to death.

In shame and confusion, I light this single burner of incense. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Single Barrier of Jiyun seems like a matter of indifference; it appears easy when looked at, yet difficult to penetrate."
At that time, it was truly difficult. The myriad phenomena of the universe were made to look askance at the Teaching; the Buddhas of the three periods were utterly beyond reach.
A single path where ancient pines are covered in mottled moss and lichens. Entering the hall, he called six "five" and split two into three;
his eyes looked toward the northeast, yet his intent lay in the southwest. Under the gate of Yangshan, however, such fare was not required. Why? Because the Buddha-dharma...
"Unafraid of Ruin. Entering the hall for the discourse: "The Dharma I teach is subtle and inconceivable; it is likewise beyond words and speech.

When Baizhang visited Mazu for a second time, Mazu’s single shout left his ears deaf for three days, until Huangbo had to stick out his tongue in shock. [Baizhang] held up his whisk and said: "What connection is there?
On the Mid-Autumn Festival, entering the hall for the discourse: "Excellent offerings! Excellent cultivation! With this, he shook his sleeves and departed—no more than that.

[The Master] disputed [the point]. Why? "This night, the single orb is full; where is its pure light not present? Ascending the hall: The ultimate transformation has no fixed direction; the ultimate virtue possesses radiance.
The long days make the rivers and mountains beautiful; the spring breeze makes the flowers and grasses fragrant. Within the reflection of the jade pitcher, the springtime lasts for kalpas.
Standing alone in heaven and earth, it is revealed in its majestic presence. Ascending the hall: The spring mountains are layered upon one another; the night rain falls in a misty haze. Long...
Even upon the bed, with eyes closed and brows shut, one sleeps until the dawn bell; the mind is empty, the Dharma is empty—do not give rise to a second thought.
Thus one sits and cuts off the master; how peaceful and blissful it is, brothers! Entering the hall: there is nothing before to advance toward and nothing behind to retreat from;
even a hair’s breadth of discrepancy becomes a trap. On the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month, Dongshan departed from Chadu.
Yunmen said, "I would give you thirty blows. But how about this? "Endlessly, endlessly! Suffering upon suffering!

In the Dinghai year of the Zhiyuan era, [Wuzhun Shifan] sent a bamboo whisk and a fly-whisk, along with the "Record of Receiving the Seal" (Tongshouji) concerning Green Water and Blue Mountains, together with a written true eulogy, to Gao Feng Yuanmiao, saying:
"The Great Master [Fayan Wenyi] has now passed away; Xueyan [Zongguo] knows the proper etiquette."
...Indeed, his empty fame filled the heavens and earth. He entrusted [the Dharma] to the attendant Yuanyao. At over seventy years of age, he passed away.
Chan Master Duangqiao Miaolun of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou was the son of the Xu family of Huangyan, Taizhou. His mother was Liu. She conceived him after dreaming of the moon.
At the age of eighteen, he shaved his head at Guangci Monastery in Yongjia. Initially, he went to see Guyuan Dao.
Suīyán heard the story regarding the "three pounds of hemp" and harbored doubts about it. He traveled everywhere, seeking instruction from masters in various quarters.

One day, while at Yúnjū, he was reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* in the Shāntáng Hall when he reached the passage: "Even mosquitoes, insects, and ants have no speech, yet they are able to accomplish their tasks.
At this, he attained a sudden realization and said, "Zhàozhōu’s ‘Cypress Tree’ koan is truly direct and to the point. Thereupon, he went to visit Wúzhǔn Fǎn at Xuěfēng.
Doubt. Fan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Tiantai. He asked, "Did you manage to cross the Stone Beam Bridge?
The Master said, "I stepped across it with one foot and broke it in two. From that time on, people called him Duanqiao (Bridge-Breaker).

One day, Fan asked the Master why a dog has karmic consciousness, instructing him to provide a response. After thirty turns, no answer was in accord with the truth. The Master said, "Is there not a method?"
"It is so. Zhi-fan showed him the verses he had composed regarding True Purity (*zhenjing*). The Master stood in awe. After a long while, he suddenly heard the sound of the wooden board;
his entire body broke into a sweat. Thereupon, he was liberated and free from doubt. When Zhi-fan moved to Yuwang and Shuangjing, the Master shared the seat with him.

He subsequently took charge at Zhiyuan, then transferred to Ruiyan and Guoqing, and later presided over Jingci. Entering the hall, he said: "In the mountains of Jing there is jade; once it is obtained..."
Those who obtain it do not find it on Mount Jing; the pearl is in the Red Water, yet those who pick it up do not find it there.
Zen monks possess the True Person of No-Rank, yet those who realize it do not find its entry or exit at the face-gate. He suddenly picked up his staff, held it crosswise, and said:
Do you understand? A stone man crouches at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou. [He] ascends the hall. He cites the case of Ciming, who kept a basin of water in his room.
Across the basin he laid a sword, and upon the sword he placed a pair of straw sandals. Whenever a monk arrived, he would simply point to them.
"As soon as he attempted to deliberate, [the Master] struck him. The Master then offered this verse: "Amidst a thicket of flowers, the whip flashes by;
How much elegance and refined grace there is! The unexamined scholar peeks with stolen glances; What can be done about the old sorrows filling his breast?
Ascending the hall, he said: "Deshan lowered his head; Jiaxian nodded his head; Jueyi held up a finger; Xuansha broke his own toe."
Holding up his staff, he said, "All of it is not outside the tip of this mountain monk’s staff. How do you see this?
He struck the ground with the staff and said, "When one leaf falls, autumn comes to all under heaven. He ascended the hall and, citing Daguan Ying, said, "The Seven Buddhas are subjects of nature."
"The myriad dharmas are slaves to the mind. Now tell me, where is the master? [The Master] struck himself with his hand and said, "All Buddhas from the Seven Buddhas down have appeared.
Then he nodded to himself and said, "Each attends to their own duties. The Master remarked:

"To call the Seven Buddhas 'slaves to nature' and point to the myriad dharmas as 'slaves to the mind,' Dahui claims for himself a way to manifest his own person. Yet when he strikes himself and nods to himself..."
"This is merely the business of a slave; when has the master ever dreamed of it? Does the great assembly wish to see it?
With these words, he gave a single stroke with his whisk and said: "A spring breeze stirs at dawn, opening a hundred varieties of flowers throughout the gardens.

As he was about to pass away, he entered the room with the assembly and composed a handwritten letter bidding farewell to the various mountains and the Duke of Wei. The Duke had sent him medicine, which he did not accept.
The messenger was sent again to inquire: "Your Eminence was born at Tiantai; for what reason did you die at Jingci? The Master replied:
"The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. He then wrote a verse and passed away. His secular age was sixty-two, and his monastic seniority was forty-four.
Chan Master Yunsou of Lingqu Temple in Taizhou ascended the hall and said: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "True Suchness and ordinary or holy beings are all but dream-talk;
what then is true speech? Zhaozhou replied, "Oṃ bhrūṃ phaṭ. The Master said:
"Zhaozhou’s Chan resides merely on the surface of his lips. Look at him acting this way—it is like calling a bell a jar. Suppose someone were to ask me, Yunsou:"
He then said to them: "When hungry, simply eat your rice. Now tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different?

The Western Heavens use Sanskrit; here in this land we use the Tang language. Ascending the hall: Heat is heat; coolness is coolness. The Dharma is not a dualistic dharma; there is no need for deliberation.
It is just that everyone’s nostrils are right on their faces—this is certainly knowing it exists. Yet I ask further:
You. The fragrance of lotuses in a secluded marsh—how does it compare to the scent of rice in a deep village? The Verse on Guarding the Mind as a Fortress says:
"The six gates are locked with long chains; the old borders are firmly sealed. Already, clinging thoughts have ceased and ten thousand anxieties are forgotten.

Last night, a poor house was suddenly plundered; it turns out the disaster arose from within the inner walls. The Verse on Guarding the Mouth as a Pitcher says: "Clearly, it is right beneath the nostrils. When [the mind] moves..."
Attachment is nothing other than a gateway to calamity; direct and relaxed instruction is like a wooden wedge. Under the clear blue sky and bright sun, a thunderclap rages forth.
Chan Master Bieshan Zuozhi of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Yang family from Shunqing in Sichuan. At the age of fourteen, he received full ordination.

Initially, while listening to a monk reciting the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he heard it said that once one has entered the towers and pavilions of Maitreya, they close behind him; he felt as if he were in a dream.
Jue then composed verses on Lingyun’s verse regarding the seeing of peach blossoms, including the lines: "A single red dot amidst ten thousand greens;
how many rejoice, and how many grieve? He then traveled extensively to seek out masters such as Xiweng Yan, Wujipai, Gaoyuan Quan, and Chun'an Jing.

Miaofeng was skilled at studying under various veteran masters. Finally, he met Wuzhun Shanfeng at Xuedou. Shanfeng recognized him as a vessel for the Dharma and treated him with ever-increasing severity;
at times, staff blows and shouts were delivered together, not sparing him a single word. Whenever the Master attempted to respond, his mouth would suddenly clench and he could not utter a sound.
Through this, all his intellectual understanding was utterly destroyed. After a long time, he spoke up and said, "All the skills I have cultivated throughout my life..."
"All are subject to the law of death. Now, seeing this elder, I have begun to tread the path of life. Subsequently, when Fǎn moved to Jìngshān, he commanded the Master to share his seat.

In the *jiāxī* *wùxū* year of the Song Lǐzōng reign, the throne at Tāiwáng on Dòngtíng was vacant; they invited the Master to preside over it. In the *bǐchén* year of the Bǎoyù reign, Tiāntóng Monastery was destroyed.
The regional commander, Duke Wú Qián, memorialized the Emperor regarding the Master’s spiritual conduct. The Master received an imperial decree and, carrying only one...
Carrying a single bowl, he arrived and dwelt there, thatching with reeds. For a long time the region of Ning had not seen rain; when the Master prayed for it, it responded immediately.
Consequently, people flocked to him, and within three years all neglected affairs were restored. Tiantong thus returned to its former glory.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] cited the occasion when the World-Honored One was about to enter nirvana and Mañjuśrī requested him to turn the wheel of the Dharma once more. The World-Honored One rebuked him, saying: "Mañjuśrī!"
"For forty-nine years, I have never spoken a single word. You ask me to turn the Wheel of Dharma once more;
have I ever turned the Wheel of Dharma? He spoke in verse: "This old man has lived his life in great deception; He takes what does not exist and uses it to deceive the blind and the deaf."

"A single phrase at the moment of departure is truly real. This was also the "Bell after Meals" for the *ācārya*. On the first day of the ninth month in the Gengshen year of the Jingding era, he suddenly addressed the assembly, saying:
"The clouds are thin and the moonlight is fresh; the trees have shed their leaves and the mountains reveal their bones.

Since heaven and earth first came into being, how many have had eyes that see clearly? To those who asked for instruction upon realization, the Master said: "It is too late to meet [me now]; each of you must exert yourselves."
Ten days later, during the middle watch of the night, he called his attendant and entrusted him with his final affairs. With palms joined, he passed away peacefully.
He was sixty-eight years of age and had spent fifty-four summer retreats in meditation. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the right of the Mian Stupa at Mount Zhongfeng.
Chan Master Huanxi of Xuefeng in Fuzhou cited the passage: "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas;
yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him, and he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood. He then offered this verse: "The seal of Vairocana was cast at the beginning of the kalpa;
The ancient inscriptions, though worn like insects, remain distinct. How laughable and how tragic that people do not recognize it— They instead resent that the characters are not perfectly complete."

Inscription for the Praise of the Bag-Holder Monk (Pú-dài-hé-shàng): Whenever he meets a person, he begs for a single coin; yet within his bag, he possesses the wealth of a rival state. It is not that his descent into this world was late;
rather, he detested being a Buddha and refused to become one. Regarding the phrase "This very mind is Buddha" (*jì-xīn-jì-fó*), the verse says: "This very mind is Buddha."
Arsenic and wolf-poison can raise the dead back to life; it takes not even a single dose.
Zen Master Ming of Yuepo at Tiantong in Mingzhou cited a monk’s question to Yunmen: “When it has rained continuously and does not clear up, what then?
Yunmen said, “Zha! The Master offered this verse: Yunmen’s single *zha*— A hair-splitting blade, its luster shining through the scabbard. If it were not...
Zhang Hua: In vain he blinks his eyes. [The Master] cites the kōan of Liangsui’s visit to Magu, and offers this verse:

Carrying his hoe, he did not look back; he should have returned right then. Who would dare say, "You are a lecturer"? [The Master] cites the saying, "Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations," and offers this verse:
Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations—passing the blame back and forth, who has ever known? This monk...
Carrying a load of bewilderment, one exchanges it for two heads of muddied water. This refers to the koan: "The fragrant breeze comes from the south;
the halls and pavilions grow cool. The verse says: "The old woman selling fans shields her eyes with her hand; A single style of wind flows from the head of the house.
Tell this to the traveler who has not yet returned home: Why need you go outside to eat the *pōzhā*?"
Chan Master Zhizhi of Donglin Temple on Mount Lu sent this verse for a monk returning to Chengdu: "Where wisdom does not reach, utter a single word;
A single word that hits the mark is arriving home. Before the Heron Pavilion, the wind stirs the willows;
Beside the city of Gansu, the rain hastens the blossoms."
Chan Master Xuesou Hishou Shaotan of Mingzhou was a native of Western Sichuan. Having appeared in the world at Fulong, he ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "As for the matter of the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school, what is it like? The Master said, "Drip, drip from the eaves; distinct and clear. He then continued:
Drifting on the vast waters by the West Lake, one gazes upon the cold green willows hanging along the embankment. Who would have known that karmic debts are so difficult to evade?
With eyes wide open, one enters the cauldron of boiling oil with such dignity. Being here, how can one find a way out? One might wish to rot and stew in the yellow mire.
Alone, he disregards the purple clay seal; yet he cannot avoid treading upon the footprints of the ancients.

He intends to lock up the void and bar dreams, to block the roads and break the bridges, yet he fears sitting trapped within a thicket of entanglements. It is better, therefore, to accept things as they are and act in accordance with the times.
He picks up his staff and says: "Vertically it exhausts the three periods of time; horizontally it spans the ten directions. He leans on the staff and says: "The blue-eyed [foreigner]..."

The Yellow-Headed Assembly cannot grasp it. Wild plum blossoms, when the wind stills, drift with their fragrance in the dark. Entering the hall: The spring of the third month is said to be drawing to a close;

its splendor is as rich as wine. Orioles sing in the rain upon the willows; butterflies frolic in the breeze among the sea-blossom trees. If you understand this as an external scene, you are like one who crosses mountains searching for the tracks of ants.
If you do not understand it as an external scene, you are like one who wades through water seeking the traces of fish. Ultimately, how is it? Return to your native land.
The road is long; the day is fading as he weeps at the end of his journey. Residing at Xuedou, he ascends the hall and says: "One Night’s Awakening" and "Three Loads of Earth":
before his feet have even crossed the threshold, his essential character is already revealed. In taking a casual step, the perilous path is covered in frosty blossoms;

in displaying a single function with a stroke of color, the precipice sends a waterfall cascading down. Nevertheless, while it is easy to cross the gate of Rufen Peak, to truly enter Rufen Peak— [The text ends here.]
This is difficult. Why? "The wild goose flies into the vast darkness; what does the hunter long for? Entering the hall:

When one can give rise to a single vital turn of phrase and utter a single word that hits the mark, there are not even a few clouds ten thousand miles away, yet the blue sky deserves a blow of the staff.

Without waiting for the spring breeze to intentionally cause it to bloom, the hidden fragrance is already upon the plum blossoms. Case: A monk asked Nanquan, "The Master resides in the abbot’s quarters."
"What shall I take as my guide? Quan replied, "Last night at the third watch, I lost the ox; when dawn broke and I arose, I lost the fire. He then offered this verse:
"With servile countenance and cringing knees, one runs through the world; I am ashamed to see you in sheepskin robes on the Qili River shoals.
Though Wen-shu is noble as the Son of Heaven, Zi-ling regards him merely as an old friend. He sent this gatha to Tiantong: "The old man is eighty years old..."
Reborn sprouts. Chewing the void thoroughly, he spits out the seeds and scatters them toward the trees by the Linglong Rock;
branch after branch, leaf after leaf, they are all *dharma*-flowers.
Chan Master Ning, who retired from farming at Lingyin in Hangzhou, first resided at Chongsheng in Jiaxing and subsequently moved to Baoguo in Suzhou.
May His Imperial Majesty’s grace and wisdom endure for ten thousand years under heaven. Later, he moved to Lingyin Temple. Entering the hall, he said:

"There is no dharma before one's eyes; the meaning lies right before one's eyes. After the rain, the mountain colors are verdant; in the warm breeze, the birds' songs are clamorous. He struck the meditation seat and said:

"It is laughable that the Old Barbarian had no transformative wisdom, yet sat before the Peak of Shaoshi for nine years. Entering the hall again, he cited the case of Xianglin, where a monk asked him: "The year is at its end..."
"How is it at the end of the year? Lin said, "The old king of the eastern village burns paper money at night. The Master said, "The old king burns money;
his words are consistent with his speech. A cotton-wrapped special stone; an iron-encased lump of mud. Ascending the hall, he said:

"A thousand peaks stretch before the eyes, locked in emerald green; willow catkins and cotton float through the air. Alas, the True Man of No Rank has been sleeping in the grass and under the dew all along. Hah!"
The three springs have passed by my gazing; when will this be the year of my return? Rantou raised the question to Qingshan:
"What is the true word? Qingshan replied: "Namo Buddhāya. The verse says: Responding to the occasion, answering as the question arises— It is neither Chan, nor is it the Original Source.
Later generations, without cause, translated it out; They took the Sanskrit words and rendered them into Chinese.
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is your surname, Master? Zhaozhou said, "It is found in Changzhou. The monk asked, "How old are you? Zhaozhou said, "It is found in Suzhou.
The verse says: Suzhou has it; Changzhou has it. In the third month, the partridges cry in Jiangnan.
How laughable are those men who possess years but no virtue; when pressed by others, they must laboriously offer evasive explanations.
Chan Master Ke Xiang of Xuefeng on the precipitous cliffs of Fuzhou was a native of the Ge clan of Ninghai in Taizhou.

He cited the case where a monk asked Caoshan, "The snow covers the thousand mountains; why is the solitary peak not white? Caoshan replied, "You must know that there is the extraordinary within the extraordinary."
[The monk] asked, "What is the 'extraordinary within the extraordinary'? The Mountain Master said, "It does not fall into the forms of any mountain.

He then offered this verse: Within words, both self and other carry the profound source; All seek to discern the correct and the pervasive within words. How regrettable that the single imperial highway is neglected; Vast and boundless, it lies even before the moonlight.
[The Master] cited a monk asking Guizong, "What is the original intent? Guizong said, "No one can [express it]."

Yunmen said, "What was it like before? Donggu returned, "If there is 'before,' one has already deviated. Yunmen asked, "What about when there is no 'before'? Donggu replied, "Who seeks the original intent?
Yunmen spoke again, "When you depart, there is no place for you to apply your mind. Donggu asked, "Is there not some skillful means (upāya) that allows students to enter?
Yunmen replied, "The wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom can save the world from suffering. Donggu asked, "What is this 'Avalokiteśvara'?"

Guishan, possessing the power of wisdom regarding the subtlety of sounds, struck the lid of the cauldron three times and asked, "Did you hear that? The monk replied, "I heard it. Guishan said, "Why did I not hear it?
The monk was speechless, so Guishan drove him away with his staff. He composed a verse on this: "The three strikes upon the cauldron lid open the Universal Gate."
The weary lives in the sea of suffering cannot be called back. Half of the spring’s ninety days has now passed; empty flying petals dot the moss.
The Verse for Reception at Yupu says: Beyond the mountains of Wu, before the mountains of Yue, There is food to satisfy hunger and a mat to sleep upon.
If one can find rest and repose here, The imperial capital remains a boat’s length away across the tide.
Chan Master Xiyuan Liaohui of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Luo family from Pengzhou.

While still a young child with hair hanging down, he would play with other children, invariably molding sand and mud into Buddhist stupas and images. One day, Zudeng arrived at his home from Yuzhangshan;

the Master joined his palms toward him, and because his parents perceived a karmic affinity between master and disciple from past lives, they allowed him to leave the household life. Zudeng then transmitted the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi* (Banzhou) to him.

His mind was not set on *samādhi*. He took his leave to go to Chengdu to pay his respects to Gu’an Zhao at Zhaojue Temple. Zhao recognized his potential and commissioned him to travel south to seek instruction.
He subsequently visited Zhejiang Master Yan at Mount Jing. Hearing that Gao Yuanquan was a man of straightforward character, he admired him deeply and went to call upon him.
It happened that Yuanquan was traveling to Ruiyan in Taizhou, so the Master accompanied him. One day, Yuanquan asked: "The mountains and rivers are vast..."
"Is it existent? Is it non-existent? As the Master was about to open his mouth, Baizhang (Quan) shouted at him. The Master then presented a verse. Baizhang said, "There is no connection.

One day, the Master happened to write down the words he had spoken to the assembly regarding the white poplar tree. When Baizhang read it, he laughed and said, "You may be quite capable of writing characters and composing phrases, but what can you do about there being no connection?
The Master was filled with indignation. Baizhang said, "Your karmic affinity does not lie here."
"You may go and see Master Xuedou Fan. Following these instructions, the Master went to pay his respects and presented his background.
Fan scolded him, saying, "Go back to sleep! Subsequently, he appointed him as a non-administrative attendant (*wushi*). One day, Fan said to the Master:

Tell me, is this sentient or insentient? Beneath Mount Nanping, three barriers stand like a sheer cliff. For those who cannot pass through, one error leads to a hundred errors;

for those who can pass through, a thousand difficulties lead to ten thousand difficulties. Suddenly, there may be someone who comes forward, dissatisfied, and asks: 'If one has already passed through, why...'"
"It is difficult to let go. Come tomorrow; I will examine you closely with you. The Master asked a monk, "What is your own self?
The monk prepared to respond, but the Master pushed him out. [The Master] cited the karmic connection between Huanglong and Ciming, and offered this verse:
"Wrong! Wrong! The dragon of the playful sea, the soaring phoenix of the sky. Old Ciming, peerless and unattached, reveals layer upon layer within his smile."
The moment the Buddha’s hand unfurls its seal, sun and moon grow dim; from this point on, the great river’s winds and waves turn treacherous.
Chan Master Binggu Yan of Tianning Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "How cold and whistling blows the north wind, ruffling the robes beneath the crags.
My ancestral estate has long been overgrown with weeds; why wander through the heavens without returning? A hundred years of human life—how can it be preserved forever? Yesterday...
The youth of yesterday is now old; I recall Han Shan once more. For ten years I have been unable to return, and I have forgotten the path by which I came.
[Ascending the hall: "The kalpa-stone may wear away, but the bonds of affection are difficult to sever. He strikes his knee once and says:
"Beneath the green pines, year after year, paper money is hung. [Ascending the hall: "Cold winds and sparse rains mark the beginning of the new year. In solitude and chill..."
By the ancient stream, ice thickens; in the warm chamber, a brazier roasts firewood. To bid farewell to Poverty, there is no need to burn paper money.

Ascending the Dharma Hall on the Imperial Birthday: The King of Mind unifies the Six States; Heaven and Earth are vast, the chariots and books are one. The wind follows the tiger, the clouds follow the dragon. Deep is the sea, high is Mount Song.
Of the myriad spirits, none can participate in the work of transformation; they know only that the One Qi returns to the Grand Beginning.
Mong. Zen Master Yungeng Jing of Tiger Hill in Suzhou ascended the hall and said: "If I do not break it open for you, I fear you will not turn back;
yet if I do break it open for you, I fear that later on everyone will curse me away. Ascending the hall, the mountain monk said: "If I..."
To truly bring this forth: at the Pavilion by the River, there is no place for you to set foot. For now, restrain your majestic brilliance and act according to your own capacity;
I shall not speak of transcending the school or possessing a unique perspective.

If you can recognize that the Tiger Hill Pagoda—one hundred and thirty feet high—was established during the Sui Dynasty, I will grant you an entrance. Even if you are content with being inferior, what does it matter?
"It is no wonder that the old monk ascends the hall. At the Dragon Gate, there are no guests who stay overnight; each and every one possesses the principle of having no step backward.
Short Sushan sold his bedding three thousand *li* away; lame Yunmen had his leg broken under pressure. You lot simply go on passing your days in idle indolence.
Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bath ceremony: "I contemplate the Tathāgata: he does not come from the past limit, nor does he [go to] the future limit..."
It does not go; now it does not abide either. But tell me: what is it that is bathed with fragrant water in the Great Hall?

If you understand this, you will be free to pick up or set down the ladle in your hand. If you have not yet attained this, then on this very day next year, you will still be splashing about recklessly as before.
[Ascending the hall: Cold as ice and frost, fine as rice powder; water cannot wash it away, nor can fire [burn it].

It cannot be heated. The Queen Mother descends by day with her cloud-banner unfurled; the night-bird cries out at night and the mountain bamboo splits. Entering the hall, [the Master] said: "The ancients said:
'To interpret the meaning according to the scriptures is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three ages; to deviate from the scriptures by even a single word is to speak like a demon.
Since both 'relying' and 'deviating' are unattainable, what ultimately is the case? He struck the meditation staff and said: "The fisherman watches only the fishing line."
[The Master] ascended the hall. Without seeing the reeds blooming white against the red smartweed, he took up his staff and said:

"When Yunyan views the mountains and plays with the waters, this staff also views the mountains and plays with the waters. When Yunyan is afflicted throughout his entire body by illness and suffering, this staff also is afflicted throughout its entire body by illness and suffering.
When Yunyan is liberated in his whole being and finds ease, this staff also is liberated in its whole being and finds ease."
Zhuo leaned on his staff and said: "It is easy to cleave apart Mount Hua; it is difficult to eliminate love and hatred.
Huazang Tong Chan Master was the Dharma heir of Xuzhou Jingshan Xuzhou Puduo Chan Master.
He was the son of the Shi family of Jiangdu in Weiyang. As he grew older, he... [text fragment ends]
While he was living as a layman, his mother recognized his aspirations and sent him to Tianning Monastery in the prefecture to renounce the world.
There he encountered General Bi on a boat and conversed with him. Bi was greatly amazed by him, saying, "This boy is short and sturdy, yet his voice resonates like a bell;
he will be a 'claw and fang' for the Dharma-gate in the future. He took him back to Wulin, where the Master studied under Zu Xin of Dongtang Monastery. The Master exerted himself...

His aspirations were set upon traveling to various regions. Initially, he met Tien-niu Yin at Ling-yin; subsequently, he traveled extensively throughout the east and west of the Yangtze River and the north and south of Lake Tung-t'ing.
At that time, Wu-ai T'ung was propagating the Way at Chuan-fu Temple. The Master went specifically to visit him. Upon entering the room for instruction, T'ung asked:
"Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as companions? The Master said, "An iron Kunlun under a golden incense burner.
Tong said, "I thought this short man had some long reach. The Master bowed deeply and said, "Thank you, Preceptor, for your witness.
Tiantong Huiryan Guang, Daci Shiyuan Lian, and Huqiu Shishi Di saw him once and all recognized his potential.

Biography: At the beginning of the Chunyu era of Emperor Lizong of the Song dynasty, Zhao Xinan, the Governor of the Military Headquarters, requested the Master to take charge of the community at Bānshān in Jīnlíng.
Subsequently, he moved to Jīnsān in Rùn, Lùyuàn in Tán, Shūsān in Fǔ, and Chéngtiān in Sū.

During the Jingding era, he was appointed to Central India. By imperial decree, he was promoted to Lingyin Monastery. In the Dingchou year of the Yuan Shizu Zhiyuan period, he was summoned by edict to reside at Mount Jingshan.
He ascended the hall and said: "When a person of heterodoxy speaks the True Dharma, the True Dharma becomes entirely heterodox. When a person of orthodoxy speaks heterodox dharma,"
"All deviant dharmas are entirely correct. [He] struck the meditation staff once and said, "Deviant? Correct? He struck it again and said, "Explainable? Inexplicable?
"If you can discern and distinguish within this, then having a house made of gold is not what is noble; what need is there for jade food and brocade robes to bring honor?
[He] ascended the hall and said: "The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are only the awakening of the nature. Fundamentally..."
There is no person who is deluded or awakened; it simply requires realization today. Since there is neither delusion nor awakening, what is there to realize?
He struck his staff once and said: "A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them; they follow the warbling oriole over the low wall. [He then ascended the hall.]
Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying, "All of you who are here passing the summer retreat: I, this mountain monk, truly do not wish to speak to you. Just take care of your eyebrows!
The Master said, "Yunmen was like a numinous tortoise dragging its tail; as he wiped away the tracks, more tracks were produced.
Lingyin is not so. All of you who are here passing the summer retreat: I, this mountain monk, shall speak to you directly. [He opened his mouth.]
"This is a gateway to calamity. [He] ascended the hall. He cited Linji’s words: "There is one person who, for kalpas, remains on the road yet never leaves home;
there is another person who leaves home yet is not on the road. Which of these two is worthy of receiving the offerings of devas and humans?"
The Master composed a verse: "Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have none. An inch of hair, a centimeter of silk—vast and empty are heaven and earth.
Pan Lang rides backward on his donkey; He falls and kills Huang Fancho. While the Master was residing at Mount Jing, he encountered the aftermath of a fire and resolved to restore it.
Just as his efforts were gaining momentum, he suddenly manifested a slight illness. He requested a brush and wrote in large characters: "Eighty-two years, riding a bottomless [boat]."

He boarded a boat, capsized it, and returned home. Under a single sky of bright moonlight, he cast aside his brush and passed away on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month of the year Wuyi (1295) of the Yuanzhen era.
His entire body was enshrined in a pagoda at the foot of Fusiwu, ten *li* east of the temple.

Chan Master Jue’an Mengzhen of Chengtian Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Xuedou Qian. He was a native of Xuanchuan; he became a monk at the age of eight and received full ordination at nineteen.
At twenty, he began his travels to visit various masters, yet none could provide him with definitive resolution. He subsequently came to admire the spiritual style of Wuzhun Fayan.
He then ascended Mount Jing and sought an audience with [Zhaozhou]. Every time he entered the meditation hall, he was so overcome by fear and trembling that he forgot his *huatou*.

From then on, he no longer entered the room; day and night he did nothing but practice seated meditation. One day, while walking in the corridor, he heard the sounding of the wooden board for the meal and attained realization.
He rejoiced to himself, knowing where his "original life-source" (*benming yuanchen*) lay. Thereupon, he entered the room. Fan asked, "You are one who eats..."
"Monks who eat gruel and rice; monks who practice *chan* and study the Way. The Master raised his voice and said, "Monks who eat gruel and rice.
Fanzhao said, "One must eat until full before it is truly so. The Master replied, "Thank you for the Master’s offering.
From this point on, he focused solely on the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature, yet found no way of entry. He then went to Xuedou to see Dayue. Qian asked, "What is it?"
Regarding the matter of birth and death, the Master said, "The eyebrows are placed above the eyes. Xian asked, "Why are the eyebrows placed above the eyes?
The Master said, "To speak of it makes one feel all the more unbearable. Xian asked again, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Mount Jing.
Xian said, "What is the state of affairs after the fire? The Master said, "The five peaks still pierce the heavens as high as before. Xian said, [and continued].
"Has that matter ever been destroyed? The Master joined his palms and stepped forward, saying, "Fortunately, it has never been disturbed. He then hung up his belongings and returned to the hall.

Knowing in his heart that he was not yet settled, his mind remained constantly restless and agitated. One night, deep into the night, he looked up and saw a crystal lamp; at that moment, he attained great enlightenment.
Everything he had previously acquired vanished all at once, like ice melting or a fortress crumbling. Next—
One day, when entering the room, Xueqian asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "A three-legged donkey prances on its hooves.
Before the sound had even faded, the Master said, "Go ahead and leap about as you please! Xueqian asked, "Where did you meet Yangqi? The Master said, "You missed it right before your face."
He served [the Master] for a long time again. He taught at Yongqing, then moved to Lianyun, and ascended Mount He. When presiding at Chengtian, he ascended the hall and said:
"If you intend to use the mind to study the Buddha, you will be drawn into the palace of Māra. If you intend to use the mind to practice Chan, you will fall into the realm of the skandhas.
Even if you despise the Buddha and refuse to become one, you will still be pierced through the skull by this staff. Viewed in this light, it is truly without [reliance]."
At the place where he applies his mind, he plants his staff upright and says: "Carry your poems and books back to your old retreat; wildflowers and singing birds are one and the same spring.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The green bamboos before the courtyard are lush; the yellow chrysanthemums beneath the steps are dense.
To call them the essence of True Suchness (Tathatā) is yet the function of Prajñā; to call them the function of Prajñā is yet the essence of True Suchness. Suddenly, there is one who emerges..."
[The Master] said: "Come, let me speak of the Way. I have observed that from the Buddhas and Patriarchs above, they have explained ten thousand instances of essence and function;

they were not at all like this eccentricity of yours, Chengtian. Is it that your wisdom surpasses the Buddhas and Patriarchs? Or is it merely a fabrication of your own arbitrary conjectures? He struck his staff and said:
"It is best to gaze toward the evening sky and the sands, where the west wind startles the geese into a slanting flight. He ascended the hall and, citing National Teacher Shaor, said:
"At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of this human world. Outside the mind there is no dharma; before one’s eyes are green mountains.
The Master called to the assembly, saying, "National Teacher Shaoruo has indeed composed a fine verse, yet it strikes two separate blows. Chengtian also has a verse of its own."
Atop the twin peaks of Emei, above is the blue sky; at midnight, one seizes a black chicken, yet reaching out, one cannot see one’s own palm.

(He lets out a shout. Entering the hall for formal discourse: "The heat of the three summer months is not like the heat of the human heart; the dangers of the road are not like the dangers of the human heart."
Ten thousand pecks of pure breeze within a jade-green basin. I know not who is leaning against the balustrade with me. Suddenly, someone comes forth and asks:
"Venerable sir, at this very moment, what is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? To him, one says: "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive. [Case]:
When the World-Honored One was first born, he pointed with one hand toward heaven and with the other toward earth, and walked seven steps.
Bodhidharma looked around in all four directions and said, "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
Yunmen said, "Had I seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow of my staff and fed him to a dog, just to ensure peace in the world. He then offered this verse:
"Since birth, I have regretted being of the same lineage; Even an iron heart and liver would deserve to be consumed. I return to you your 'sole honor' within the three realms."

How could this be? Today and again tomorrow... During the Zhiyuan era of Emperor Shizu of the Yuan dynasty, there was a master of the Xianshou school who petitioned that the famous monasteries of Jiangnan and Liangzhe be converted into Huayan teaching temples. By imperial decree, he traveled south and arrived at Chengtian.

On the following day, the Master ascended the seat and extensively cited the essential tenets of the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*, expounding with great breadth and confidence, while interrogating and analyzing various masters.
The treatise’s analysis of subtle details was as clear as pointing at one's own palm. The lecturer heard what he had never heard before and received great benefit from the Dharma.

He remarked, "If even an Elder such as Chengtian is thus, how much more so a Great Master of a major monastery in Hangzhou? He subsequently submitted a memorial, and the previous imperial decree was consequently rescinded.
Chan Master Huo Shan Zha of Xuedou, Ningbo, ascended the hall and said: "‘This very mind is Buddha’—the people of Jia, Mei, Guo, and Lang have documents tucked in their sleeves.
‘Neither this mind nor that Buddha’—the people of Jun, Yuan, Qian, and Ji stick brushes in their hair.
‘Neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing’—the people of Zhang, Quan, and Fujian have heads as flat as fans; they may be heard of by name, but one cannot see their faces."
Chan Master Haeyan Sangtam Yeong ascends the hall and cites the following:

When National Teacher Wuzhuo arrived at Mount Wutai and was drinking tea with an old man, the old man picked up a crystal cup and asked, "Is there such a thing as this in the South? Wuzhuo replied, "No.
The old man said, "What do you usually use to drink your tea? Wuzhuo had no reply. Regarding this causal occasion, he recited this verse: Mount Wutai is frozen still...
Longing and waiting with lingering thoughts; under the bright sun and clear sky, one is bewitched by ghosts. There is one most painful aspect that is difficult to comprehend:
when drinking tea from a crystal cup.
One day, Chan Master Huguanpu cited Mazu’s instruction for a monk to ask Damei: "When you first saw the Great Master Mazu, what did you understand?"
"What did you attain that you dwell on this mountain? Mei replied, "The Great Master said, 'This very mind is Buddha.
I have dwelt here because of that causal condition. He then offered this verse: Using only Mazu’s lead blade, I tore asunder the iron mesh covering the heavens.
In the emerald pool at night, rain beats upon lotus leaves; To this day, I am poor and resent having but one body.
The General Discourse of Chan Master Zize of Guoqing Temple in Taizhou states in brief:

"When a superior practitioner of the Yuan school or a high-ranking traveler of the Way brushes aside the weeds and observes the wind to arrive at a certain place, they immediately present themselves. Upon entering the gate, they offer their credentials, saying:
'The matter of birth and death is great; impermanence is swift. Brothers, if birth and death truly existed, from antiquity until now—"
There is not a single person who can escape birth and death. If it were non-existent, what could one do about the birth and death right before one's eyes?
Birth and death both exist and do not exist; they are neither existent nor non-existent. At such a time, is there anyone who has slipped through the net?
Since there is nowhere to flee, when the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month arrives and [death] crashes before you, how will you ultimately manage to cope? Wait and see.
