He initially registered as a guest at Zhantanlin, where his rustic demeanor drew derision from those who saw him.
Resolving to exert himself, the Master immediately traveled to Tianmu to study under Zhongfeng and request instruction; thereupon, he devoted himself to meditation, neglecting both sleep and food.
All [his efforts] were abandoned. After a long time, he found no place of entry. At that time, Dongzhou resided at Huqiu, Gulin at Kaiyuan, and Dongsu at Hanshan.
The Master entered the gates of these three elders for many years. Later, he resided at Longhua, where he succeeded Gulin as his dharma heir.
At the age of ninety-three, he went to Yuyang to guard the ancestral stupa of Hengchuan. He happened to injure his left foot, making it difficult for him to walk. Day by day...
While sitting on his bed, whenever the clear night arrived, he would chant aloud the verses of the ancients.
His disciple Wen-huan said, "Master, having spent your entire life studying the Way, you have reached this point without being able to put it into practice; you rely on chanting to pass the time.

The Master laughed and said, "Have you not seen how the Patriarch Dahui was groaning from illness? His attendants asked him, 'Throughout your life you reviled the Buddhas and scolded the Patriarchs; why are you now like this? Dahui replied:"
"Dao. The foolish son groans; is this not so? Upon hearing this, Huan prostrated himself. After [Zhaozhou] passed away and was cremated, a wondrous fragrance permeated the air.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Hai of Lingyin.
Chan Master Dàqiān Huìzhào, the Great Teacher (Yùwáng) of Míngzhōu, was the son of the Mǎ family of Yǒngjiā.

At the age of fifteen, he left home at Ruìguāng Monastery in his native district; there he paid respects to Lǎodìng for the tonsure ceremony. After receiving full ordination, he first visited Huìméi at Jìngcí Monastery.
One day, while reading the words of Zhenjing, he thought: "The Head-dhūta Rock is enveloped by moss; the Throwing-Pen Brush Peak is entangled by *pi-li* vines.
Understanding this intuitively and with immediate penetration, he went to visit Haichao at Jianyan. Haichao asked, "Rushing east and west, what do you intend to do?
The Master replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects. Haichao said, "The sky has no four walls; the earth reaches beyond the eight frontiers. Toward which—"
"Where can one set foot? The Master struck the table and withdrew. Hai summoned him back again, and after they had examined and debated the matter repeatedly, he was retained as an attendant.
In the Wuchen year of the Yuan Tianli era, he appeared in the world at Mingqing Monastery in Leqing. Addressing the assembly, he said:

"If you wish for the Buddha-dharma to manifest before you, do not harbor intellectual understanding. Studying Chan or examining the scriptures are both obstacles. How can it be otherwise than by not [clinging to] a single dharma?"
He stood up. "Are you free in your daily activities? Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout were also matters of great necessity.
In the year Yiwu of the Zhizheng era, he moved to Baode. Not long after, the Xuanzheng Yuan appointed him as the abbot of Yuyang.
In his quarters, he set forth three "gateless barriers" to test those who came to study. The first said: "The fierce tiger in the mountains takes meat as its life; for what reason..."
First, he said: "They do not eat their own offspring. Second, he said: "Space has no back or front; by what cause are there east, west, south, and north? Third, he said:
"One may drink as much milk as the four great oceans and pile up bones like Mount Vipula; who were your very first parents?

At that time, there was rarely anyone whose capacity for understanding accorded with his teaching. After nine years had passed, he retired to the banks of the Miaoxi Spring (Spring of Wondrous Joy) and constructed [a dwelling].
His studio was named Meng’an (Dream Hermitage). He lived in seclusion behind closed doors, where layers of dust accumulated upon his desk, yet he remained as tranquil as ever.

In the year *guichou* of the Hongwu era of the Ming Emperor Gaozu, he bathed, changed his robes, and requested paper to write a verse. Then, sitting peacefully, he passed away at the age of eighty-five.
His monastic seniority reached seventy years. Upon his cremation, his teeth, eyes, and pupils remained uncorrupted, and his *śarīra* relics appeared in five colors.
A stupa was erected behind Meng’an.
Chan Master Yantang Yan of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou left the household life at Baolin in Wuzhou and received the Dharma from Dongyu.
He first resided at Dongchan Monastery in Kunshan, then moved to Wanshou, was promoted to Jingci, and later presided over Tiantong Jingshan.

He ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One spoke what is not spoken; Kāśyapa heard what is not heard. Today, before this assembly of devas and humans, I, this mountain monk, raise up this matter.
Do you hear it? If you hear it, I have ultimately never spoken. If I have spoken, you [have not heard]."
This has never been heard before; each person should investigate it for themselves without taxing their ears and eyes. By imperial decree, he was bestowed with a golden-embroidered Dharma robe.
Chan Master Xuechuang Wuguang of Yuyang in Mingzhou was the son of the Yang family from Xindu in Shu. He first entered the world at Bai...
Ma. Jiqian succeeded Kaiyuan and Yuyang, and later presided over Tiantong.

When the Duke Yu Wenjing Ji once went into the mountains to inquire about the Way, the Master said, "In this place of mine, there is no Way to discuss. If you wish to seek the Way, you must go elsewhere to study it.
The Duke withdrew and sighed, saying, "Of the lineage of Foguo, you must be its phoenix-feather and unicorn-horn. (There were four [sections]).
The *Huìyùlù* (Recorded Sayings of Huì). Prefaced by Wenxian Gong Lian of the Song dynasty.
Zen Master Jing of Yuèlín at Mount Jìngshān in Hangzhou was a native of this very province. He received his formal ordination under Wúchuán and long relied upon Dōngyǐ.
Thereupon, through investigating Běnláirén (the Original Person), he attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "The Original Person, the Original Person—no head, no..."
"What are you searching for? he asked. Suddenly, [the monk] grabbed his own nostril. "Try looking; it turns out to be a commoner," the Master remarked.

At that time, an elder looked askance at him and said, "Is that so? The Master gave him a slap. From this, his reputation resounded throughout the monastic community. Later, he presided over Mount Jing.
He passed away in the Jīmūta year (1359) of the Zhizheng era of the Yuan Emperor Shundi, at the age of eighty-six. His stupa was erected on the eastern cliff of Mount Lingxiao.
Chan Master Daguizhengzhang of Doufeng in Jianning Prefecture was a native of Fucheng, Fuzhou. He received the tonsure under Jueting of Hunan. Later, he studied under Dongyu Hai.
Upon hearing Hai’s verse on the story of Zhizhi holding up a finger, he attained sudden enlightenment.

He then went to the abbot’s quarters to present his realization. Dongyu asked, “What is it? The Master replied, “A matter already perfected throughout past and present; why must one involve discursive thought?”
Baizhang said, "Since you do not engage in thought, what are you doing here? The Master replied, "I ask the Master to bear witness.
Baizhang asked, "Witness to what? The Master gave a shout. Baizhang then had him compose a verse on the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature.
The Master suddenly said, "The dog has no Buddha-nature; look at it and its eyes will wither. In a flash, it turns over—Oṃ Śrī Sūru.

He patted [the disciple] and sealed him with the mudrā. Later, he built a thatched hut on Mount Doufeng, which gradually developed into a monastic community. He ascended the hall and addressed the assembly:
Looking around at those present, after a long silence, he said, "Though gold is precious, once it enters the eye, it becomes but dust. He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"The jade palace is clear with frost; the emerald grove’s leaves have fallen. When the single phrase is fully raised, the myriad functions are stilled.

Those who act as true masters should seek the medicine for when they are ill. Ascending the hall, he brought up the story of the "Qingzhou Cloth Shirt" and offered this verse: Last night, in the third watch, ...
Rain falls; it wets the void. Does the wildcat know or not? It climbs up and stands upon the treetop. On the occasion of the New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall and said:
"The beginning of the new year brings forth prosperity; all things flourish. To call this the Buddha-dharma of the New Year is to blind your eyes.
Not to call this the Buddha-dharma of the New Year is to tie my tongue. Ultimately, what is it? Thereupon, he descended from his seat.
The verse for his passing says: "Birth is fundamentally without birth; cessation likewise has no cessation. As illusions come and go, what use is there in discrimination?
The great assembly, take heed! It does not reside in words. With palms joined, he passed away.
Chan Master Mingyin Tianyuan Zhan of Zutang received the Dharma from Dongyu. He once relied upon Fengshan Yiyuan and sat on the teaching seat to expound the Dharma.
One day, he presented his words regarding the whisk, saying: "Before Mount Xiangfeng, walking while gazing at white clouds that suddenly unfurl and suddenly curl;
by the side of Youquan Pavilion, sitting while listening to flowing water that sometimes subsides and sometimes rises—where the eye acts as the ear."
"The Buddha-work: performing the Buddha-work of the eye-faculty through the ear-faculty, one immediately sees that it is not only Avalokiteśvara who does so;
I too have realized it therein. Fengshan pointed to the two characters "immediately sees" (*biàn jiàn*) and said, "With these two words, this becomes the talk of another person.
The Master could not help but smile, nodded his head in thanks, and withdrew. Upon leaving, he said to others: "A single grain of elixir can transform iron into gold."
"He has become gold"—this is what is meant by the phrase "the old man of the Hall.
Regarding the Dharma heir of Chan Master Tianning Tan, the Man of Three Emptinesses (Sankong Daoren):
from childhood he possessed the ambition of a great man; he could not be swayed by wealth or status. Upon meeting Zhuyun Tan, he...
He was shown Zhaozhou’s “Mu” (No) kōan. After several years had passed, one day he saw Tan again and asked, "When birth and death arrive, what is it like?
Tan replied, "Who is born? Who is dead? Kong then bowed his head in greeting.
Tan perceived that this was different from his usual behavior and questioned him again with the previous dialogue. Kong again bowed his head in greeting. Tan rebuked him.
He said, "By all means, do not let yourself die here. He held up his *nuzi* beads and remarked, "These are one hundred and eight.
A few days later, he manifested a slight illness, spoke a verse, and passed away. After the cremation, countless *śarīra* relics were obtained.
Chan Master Huizhong Huixin of Tianjie Temple in Jinling was a dharma successor of Chan Master Tantan of Tiantong. He was the son of the Jia family of Fenghua.

At the age of fifteen, he left home to become a monk and studied under Zhuxi Tan. Following his tenure at Huazang, he was transferred to Tiantong. One day, in the meditation hall, [Tantan] raised the case of Xinghua striking Kewen.
Regarding the circumstances of his reception as a guest, the Master said, "How magnificent, you lion cub! He stroked [Tanyan’s] chin and appointed him to the position of Rector (Vina).
Later, he appeared in the world at Guanyin Temple in Mingzhou and was subsequently transferred to Putuo. By imperial decree, he was granted the title Chan Master Guanghui Miaowu Zhibao Hongjiao.

During the Zhizheng era of the Yuan dynasty, he ascended to the Central Peak (Zhongzhu) and later resided at Tiantong. The Censorate submitted a memorial, ordering him to preside over the Great [Monastery].
At Longxiang Jiqing Temple, when the Ming troops descended upon Jinling, the monks fled and dispersed. The Master remained seated in meditation in a single room.
Emperor Taizu of the Ming personally visited him and praised his conduct; by imperial decree, Longxiang was renamed Dajianjie Temple.
One day at dawn, he arose, bathed, changed his robes, and sat cross-legged. He said to those around him, "I am returning home," and then closed his eyes. An attendant monk shook him.
"Please recite a verse. The Master glared at him and rebuked him. He then took up his brush and wrote: "A lifetime spent for others, managing and guiding;

Seventy-eight years of leaking and revealing. This morning, I cast off my hands and depart; Ten thousand miles of clear sky, a single flake of snow. Having finished writing, he closed his eyes once more.
This was the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month in the year of Dingyou. At that time, the Emperor was leading troops at Jiangyin and dreamed of meeting the Master.

The Emperor asked, "Master, what brings you here? He replied, "I am about to return to the West to bid you farewell. Later, when the Emperor heard that the Master had passed away, he found it to accord with his dream;

he marveled at this. By imperial decree, silk and currency from the inner treasury were issued to assist with the funeral rites, and an order was given to select a site for the burial niche at Mount Funiu.
On the day the coffin was moved, the Emperor personally presented offerings and escorted it out through the capital gates. After the cremation, the *śarīra* relics were as large as beans.
His remains were enshrined in a precious vase from which light radiated outward. His secular age was seventy-eight, and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇera-vassa) was sixty-nine.
Wen Xian Gong Luo of the Song dynasty composed an inscription for him.
Chan Master Tianning Shuntian Mingmu was a native of Huangyan in Taizhou. He left the household life at Sanxue Temple in Xianju.

Having heard of the great reputation of Tiantong Tan, he went to visit him. Tan asked, "Dharma does not come to the Eastern Land, and the Second Patriarch does not go to the Western Heaven—what is the meaning of this?
The Master replied, "Gold is not traded for gold; water is not washed with water. Tan marveled at his response.

He said to those around him, "This Dharma-gate is my very talon and fang. He further traveled extensively to consult renowned masters, including Gulim Mao, Zhu Yuandao, Dongzhou Yong, Yuansou Duan, and Dongyu Hai, all of whom held him in high esteem.
At that time, Rixi Yong was residing at Tianning Monastery, and the Master engaged with him in mutual exhortation and debate.
In the early years of the Yuan Taiding era, he appeared in the world at Jinghui Monastery in Tiantai, and subsequently moved to Xianju.
He traveled extensively through the mountain ranges of Chuzhou before eventually retiring to live in seclusion at Mount Yan.

The Chancellor Lhe-khye-li Pu-hua forcibly invited him to preside over Tianning Monastery, where he was bestowed the title Chan Master Fozhi Puhui and granted a golden-embroidered dharma robe. The Master’s demeanor was as solemn as autumn;
he once established a chamber on Middle Peak (Zhongfeng) to dwell in, kept a crane, and styled himself the "Master of the Crane-Pine. One...
Nichō suddenly died, and the Master composed a poem in mourning for him. More than a year later, the Master also passed away.

Zen Master Tōhō Chū of Jinling’s Jiangshan Temple, a successor of Zen Master Ganshin Shuzen, was a native of Nankang. Because the temple had suffered a disaster, the following day the Prince of Liang ascended [the mountain].
Mount [Shan] said to the Master, "How will you restore it? The Master replied, "We rely on the presence of a great donor.

The King asked, "Since the temple has been destroyed, upon what shall the Buddha reside? The Master replied, "The Buddhas of antiquity have passed away; now the Buddha returns once more. The King was greatly pleased.
He laughed and said, "What is this 'coarse porridge of Jiangbo' that the patch-robed monks speak of? The Master replied, "I take it Your Highness means..."
He was posthumously granted the title Great Master Guanghui Yuanwu.

Chan Master Yuejiang Zhengyin of Mount Yuyang in Mingzhou, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Fu of Jingshan, was born into the Liu clan of Cishui in the commandery. At the age of thirteen, he...
He received formal training under Yuexi. Later, he attended Huayan Fu, with whom his spiritual affinity was such that he received his seal of approval.
He was first appointed as the abbot of Daochang in the Teao region, and subsequently moved to Yuyang. A monk asked, "What is the body of the thousand-fathom Śākyamuni? The Master said:

"Fat, yet no flesh is revealed; thin, yet no bone is revealed. [The monk] asked, "What is this body of sixteen feet, purple-gold in color? The Master said, "Above all, do not mistake the servant for the master. [The monk] said, "But do not, O Monk, force the honorable to become lowly. The Master said, "I have always been a Liu Xia Hui. [The monk] asked, "Regarding the phrase 'having a phrase or being without a phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree,' what is the meaning of this? The Master said, "It is because you have not yet seen the tree that you seek the vine. The monk said, "If one has already seen the tree, why look for the vine? The Master said, "If you have already seen the tree, you will naturally know the vine. The monk said, "If one has not yet seen the tree, how can one know the vine? The Master said, "If you have not yet seen the tree, you will naturally not know the vine. The monk said, "If one has neither seen the tree nor knows the vine, what is the meaning of 'having a phrase or being without a phrase'? The Master said, "This is precisely why I say: 'Having a phrase or being without a phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree. The monk said, "If so, then there is nothing at all. The Master said, "If you say there is nothing at all, you are still clinging to something. The monk said, "If one clings to something, is that not the same as having a phrase? The Master said, "If you say it is the same as having a phrase, you are still clinging to something. The monk said, "If one does not cling to anything, is that not the same as being without a phrase? The Master said, "If you say it is the same as being without a phrase, you are still clinging to something. The monk said, "If one neither clings nor does not cling, is that not the same as 'neither having a phrase nor being without a phrase'? The Master said, "If you say it is the same as 'neither having a phrase nor being without a phrase,' you are still clinging to something. The monk said, "If one neither clings nor does not cling, and neither affirms nor denies, is that not the ultimate meaning? The Master said, "If you say it is the ultimate meaning, you are still clinging to something. The monk said, "If one neither clings nor does not cling, and neither affirms nor denies, and even the ultimate meaning is cast aside, is that not the true meaning? The Master said, "If you say it is the true meaning, you are still clinging to something. The monk said, "If one neither clings nor does not cling, and neither affirms nor denies, and even the ultimate meaning is cast aside, and even 'clinging' is cast aside—what then? The Master said, "At this point, even if you were to bring forth a thousand sages and ten thousand patriarchs, they would have no place to set foot. The monk said, "If so, then there is no way to express it. The Master said, "If you say there is no way to express it, you are still clinging to something. The monk said, "If one says there is no way to express it, is that not itself an expression? The Master said, "If you say it is an expression, you are still clinging to something. The monk said, "If one says there is no way to express it, and yet does not cling to that non-expression, is that not the true meaning? The Master said, "If you say it is the true meaning, you are still clinging to something. The monk said, "If one neither expresses nor does not express, and neither clings nor does not cling, is that not the ultimate reality? The Master said, "A toothless tiger sits blocking the road. Shushan asked, "If suddenly the tree falls and the vines wither, where do the words return?
Muzhou laughed loudly. Shushan asked again, "And what then? The Master said, "Caoye reading the night inscription."
[The monk] said, "Later, Mingzhao broke through it for him. Was he truly so, or not? The Master said, "Looking down from a cliff edge at the water below;
a groundless cause for sorrow. [The monk] said, "Today a student asks the Master: 'When the tree falls and the vines wither, where does the phrase return?
I do not know how you will instruct me. The Master gave a shout. The monk bowed. [Another monk] asked, "Leaving the East this morning..."
"Tuo. At dusk he went to the Western Heavens. Who is this person? The Master said, "The Stone Daren at the crossroads.
[The monk] asked, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai; why did he go toward Nanyue? The Master said, "A catfish climbing a bamboo pole."
[A monk] asked, "There is one person who is always on the road and never leaves home; there is another person who has left home and is not on the road.
Tell me, which is superior and which is inferior? The Master said, "Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have no horns.

[The monk] said, "If that is so, then when a single leaf falls before the courtyard, the whole world knows it is autumn. The Master said, "One who knows the time and distinguishes what is appropriate is fit to be a teacher."
The Acharya asked, "What was the meaning of Bodhidharma’s wall-gazing? The Master said, "Rancid rice and a clay tea stove.
The Acharya asked, "And what about the Sixth Patriarch treading the pestle? The Master said, "A rabbit eating cow's milk. The Acharya asked, "'One person says he does not recognize it;
another says he does not understand. Wherein lies the meaning? The Master said, "Fenglin scolded him. [The Acharya] asked the Master.
"Whose tune are you singing? Whom do you follow in the ancestral wind? The Master said, "The wind blows through the stone mortar, chanting *Mahā*.

[The monk] said, "If that is so, then one has already received the good news of the True Man; there is no further doubt between heaven and earth. The Master said, "Catching a qilin at the bottom of the water.
[The monk] asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said, "The people of the West do not understand the Tang language."
[The student] asked, "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? The Master said, "When there is a horse, one rides the horse; when there is no horse, one walks.
[The student] asked, "What is 'seizing both the person and the environment'? The Master said, "Beating a drum in Silla while holding a vegetarian feast in the Great Tang.

[The student] asked, "What is 'neither seizing the person nor seizing the environment'? The Master said, "Throwing a brick in the middle of a bustling marketplace. [The student] said, "I have already received instruction regarding the person and the environment..."
The student asked, "Regarding the matter of the supreme vehicle (*zōngchéng*) pointed out by the Master, what is it like? The Master said, "Where there is water, the moon is contained;

where there is no mountain, it does not bear clouds. The student said, "As for the words of the Patriarch Yangqi: 'Treading upon the iron pestle, hard as steel; the mute man has a dream—whom can he tell it to?
At the summit of Mount Sumeru the waves overflow the heavens; at the bottom of the great ocean the sea suffers the heat of fire. How clear this is!"

"What about such matters? The Master said, "It is like a donkey looking into a well; it is like a well looking at a donkey. [The monk] asked, "What is the golden Buddha that does not pass through the furnace?
The Master said, "Sulu sulu. [The monk] asked, "What is the wooden Buddha that does not pass through fire? The Master said, [Sulu sulu].
"Sili sili. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of 'The mud Buddha does not cross the water'? The Master said, "West of East Hall in Zhaozhou."
[The student] asked, "What is it like for the true Buddha to sit within? The Master said, "Puo-zao-duo of Mount Song.

[The student] asked, "What is the meaning of 'one gives rise to two'? The Master said, "The sovereign is enlightened; the ministers are virtuous. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of 'two give rise to three'? The Master said:
"The Yellow River clears once every three thousand years. [A monk] asked, "What is meant by 'the three lives give birth to the myriad things'?

The Master said, "Mountains and rivers have no obstruction; light and radiance penetrate everywhere. [The monk] asked, "As for the Buddha-dharma at the beginning of a new year, is there still this very message?
The Master said, "Fan Kuai trampled at the Hongmen Gate. On the occasion of the Chief Administrator’s preparation of a vegetarian feast, Yunmen ascended the hall and addressed the assembly:
Eating steamed buns, one bites into the nostrils of Śakra; eating *bādōu* noodles, one bites into the tongue of Kauṇḍinya.
When all of you pass through the hall twice a day to eat porridge or rice, how should you act?

the Minister comes by the river'—there is no place for you to evade it. You practitioners of the patched robe, going out in the morning and returning in the evening, with every step before and behind, must be careful.
Suddenly, if you strike against it or bump into it, the staff of Jingci will have a different way of handing it over to you."
Ascending the hall: One sheng and three he. At the tip of the staff, ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains. Beneath the sole of the straw sandals, one receives it before a word is spoken.
In whose hearth is there no smoke? Raising the robe and walking away—everywhere there is water in the well.
Do not say you come empty-handed and go empty-handed; these many paths do not leave you alone. Ascending the hall: A single phrase cuts off all subtlety and trace.
A seamless whole, without a single crack. For seven days, Sudhana could not find it; for five years, Zhaozhou could not unravel it.
Today at Ling Shan, such a rare opportunity is difficult to encounter. To open up a single thread: selling pine-wind in the sixth month—fear there is no price for it in the human world.
Ascending the hall, he circumambulated the meditation seat once, struck the incense table once, and declared: "The turning of the Tripitaka is finished."
The lecture on the sutra is finished. Only those who possess the eye for discerning the scriptures will know where the meaning truly lies.

If this is not yet the case, to interpret the meaning based solely on the literal text is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three periods; to deviate from a single word of the scripture is to speak like a demon. Ascending the hall, he said: "Zhaozhou says, 'Go drink tea.
Nanguan says, 'Come eat rice. At Longmen, there are many distinguished guests. If anyone can provide the final phrase, I shall grant it."
You entered the Dharma-gate of the letter A. On the fourteenth day of the sixth month in the Guihai year of the Jingding era of the Song Dynasty’s Emperor Lizong, you passed into nirvana.
Your worldly age was seventy-five; your years as a monk were fifty-eight.
Chan Master Daguang Putong Cuiji of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou was a native of Fenghua in Mingzhou.
Once, he ascended the hall and, citing a monk’s question to Master Muzhou—“What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?”—Muzhou replied, “A group of monks comes;
a group of monks goes. The Master composed this verse: A group of monks comes; A group of monks goes. The barrier of Muzhou is shattered.

The great earth has not a single inch of soil. He inscribed this upon the portrait of the World-Honored One Emerging from the Mountains: "Dragon-like insignia and phoenix-like essence, he departed from the royal palace;
With sleeves bared and robes tattered, he descended the Snowy Peaks. His wisdom and vows shall surely empty all realms of existence;
I know not when these realms of existence will be emptied. He composed this verse to see off a monk: "Clouds shroud Jian阁 for three thousand li; Waters divide Gutang’s twelve peaks."
I have emptied my guts and entrails to tell you this: do not mistake a jar for a bell. The Spider’s Verse says:
A single thread hangs suspended in the void; from a hundred billion thread-tips, a murderous air arises. Above, below, and on all four sides, it has woven its web.

Only when the talk of the "Net of No-outflows" (anāsrava-jāla) is finished will it proceed. The Master compiled the *Wudeng Huiyuan* (The Compendium of the Five Lamps), which has circulated throughout the world.
Chan Master Yuanzhao of Huaihai at Mount Jing in Hangzhou was the son of the Pan family of Jinghai in Tongzhou; his mother was Chen.
In his youth, he left home to become a monk under Miaoguan of Lihe in his native district. At the age of nineteen, he shaved his head, received full ordination, and went to study under Zhe’ung.
At Jingshan, Master Weng asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "From Huaidong. Weng said, "Why did the Great Sage of Sizhou appear in Yangzhou?
The Master said, "Today he has run right into him here in Hangzhou. Weng said, "I am glad there is no connection [between us].
The Master spoke slowly, "I have come from afar to seek your instruction. Seeing that the Master was alert and quick-witted, Weng wished to rouse him further, but—
He was permitted to enter the hall. As soon as he saw [the Master], the latter said, "Offer me a turning word. Just as the Master was about to open his mouth, [the Master] shouted him out.
The Master then submitted a letter and presented a verse, the final line of which read: "Empty space teaches one to turn one's head and gaze toward Chang'an.
The Master said, "What kind of place is this? The Master replied, "I thank the Abbot for granting me lodging. Thereupon, he was secretly admitted into the ranks of those who enter the inner chamber.
He was appointed to oversee the Secretariat. After the Elder passed away, the Master entered the world at Guangxiao Temple in his native village.
He subsequently moved to Shuangta in Wucheng, Qingliang in Jinling, Wannian in Tiantai, Wanshou in Suzhou, and Jiangxin in Yongjia.

When the seat at Yuyang in Siming became vacant, the imperial court petitioned for the Master to fill it. He further moved to Jingci, Lingyin, and Jingshan in Hangzhou. His tenure at these monasteries...

At Jingshan, during a period following a famine, outstanding debts were piled high like mountains and the monks were few while the buildings were dilapidated. Yet, before long, multi-storied pavilions rose toward the heavens and monastics in cloud-like robes arrived in succession;
the atmosphere was no less magnificent than during the peak of Master Zhe’s era. Suddenly, he fell ill and instructed his disciples, saying, "Dig for me a burial plot at Dongjian.
This shall manifest my intent to serve my master even beyond life and death. On the tenth day of the sixth month, he passed away.
Having finished his bath, he wrote a verse and passed away. He once praised a portrait of Bodhidharma, saying: "He trampled the axis of earth and the gate of heaven;
The people of the entire nation followed, yet he did not return. Gone, gone—his single body as light as a leaf; The eternal waves of the Long River rise like mountains."
Chan Master Bingshuo Peng of Shuanglin in Wuzhou ascended the hall. He cited the case of Mingzhao Qian, who one day, when the weather was cold, ascended the hall.
Just as the assembly had gathered, Mingzhao said, "The wind is quite stiff; let us return to a warm place to deliberate," and he immediately retired to his quarters.
The assembly followed him to a place where he stood in meditation. He beckoned to them, saying, "As soon as you reach this warm room, you immediately fall asleep.

With his staff, he drove them all out at once. The Master composed a verse, saying: "The head was already stiff and perverse; He further buried himself in warmth. It caused a thousand ages of traces to remain;
In vain did he eat the white rice of Luoshan. This was because he saw the portrait of Master Yushan.

Yet not a single word of that "True Cause" has he heard. The corners of his *kāṣāya* robe, tattered and frayed, Have caught several fragments of clouds drifting atop the Lingxiao Peak.

[The Master] asked, "Where are you going? Caoshan replied, "I am going to the place where there is no change.

The place attained: the peach blossoms grow ever more exquisite. Once Lingyun saw them, he departed without doubt; Xie Lang’s rowing of the oars further displayed his skill.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Guizong slew the snake; Bimao held up the forked staff; Heshan beat the drum; Zhaozhou offered tea."
Opening a shop at the crossroads, he buys and sells for cash with no credit. Ascending the hall, the Master said: "For thirty years I have sought a swordsman;
several times the leaves have fallen and branches have sprouted anew. Since the moment I first beheld the peach blossoms, until this very day, I have had no further doubts.
The Master added: "Ordinary spring dreams possess nothing extraordinary; only Lingyun spoke of them."
People! It is just like Xuan Sha saying: "How perfectly true, how profoundly true! I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate.
What does this mean? "If one does not sleep on the same bed, how can one know there is a hole in the lining of the quilt? Ascending the hall, he said: "Ten thousand miles, not a blade of grass."
Vast and boundless above my head; once I step out the door, it is all but weeds. Vast and boundless beneath my feet;
traveling by night, I heedlessly covet the bright moon, unaware that I am crossing through water in my clothes, chilled by the cold.

Chasing the waves and following the currents, you are no true man. When you hold it up with both hands toward people, Yet..."
"Exchanging fish eyes for bright pearls.
Chan Master Wujiguan inscribed this on a portrait of the World-Honored One Emerging from the Mountains: "He did not remain in the royal palace—a simpleton indeed.

Climbing over the city walls at midnight was truly strange. Who would have cared for his six years of asceticism? When his resources were exhausted, he had no choice but to emerge from the mountains."
Chan Master Wuliang Chongshou of Ruiyan in Mingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Ruyi Yuwang, ascended the hall and said:
He cited the case where Bai Shilang asked Niaoke, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Niaoke replied, "Commit no evil; practice all that is good. Shilang said:
"A three-year-old child can also speak in this way. Guo said, "Though a three-year-old child can speak thus, an eighty-year-old man cannot act accordingly.
He then offered this verse: "Evil has no appearance; goodness has no form. Both grow from the field of the mind.
Without revealing their sharp edges, they are lightly pierced through; Bodhi and afflictions are equal, as vast as space. He addressed the assembly, citing the world at large...

Han words and Hu tongues, tens of thousands upon ten thousands. You beggar who became rich overnight, stop talking in your sleep; In whose kitchen is there no smoke from the fire?

Chan Master Wujing Che of Tiantong Monastery in Mingzhou, successor to the Tian Tong lineage, ascended the hall and said: He cited the story where a monk asked Yantou, "In the midst of vast confusion, how does one discern the host?
Yantou replied, "A copper cauldron filled with oil. He then offered this verse: "A million brave soldiers..."

Entering the Han Pass, his majesty was like a fierce tiger and his formation like a mountain; with a single blade he straightway took Yan Liang’s head—had it not been Lord Guan, it would have been most difficult indeed.
Chan Master Ding of Aofeng in Fuzhou praised the portrait of Xuansha, saying: "He refused to exchange his green straw raincoat for a golden seal. For a thousand...
"An ancient air belongs to Master Xie; having caught a scaled fish of fine hue, no one offers it up. On a cold night, one listens to the clashing of the oars upon the sand.
Chan Master Wumen Can of Jianfu Temple in Raoyou was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Kanhui of Yewang. He was a native of Taihe County in Jixian. He received the Dharma from Yewang. At [Jianfu],...
In the sixth month of the Dinghai year of the Baoping era of Emperor Lizong of the Song dynasty, he resided at Jianfu Temple. Subsequently, he moved to Kaixian.

In the Jichou year of the Shaoding era, he returned once more to Jianfu and took up residence in his quarters. Today, this mountain monk opens the gates of hell for a universal invitation to all people throughout the great earth.
One creates the karma of hell and realizes the fruit of hell. If there were even one person who attained Buddhahood or became a Patriarch, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment myself.
[The Master] ascends the hall. Having finished offering incense, he says: "Heaven is high and earth is deep; the moon waxes and wanes.

To fully uphold [the Dharma] or to uphold it only half—these are worlds apart. Chan Master Can, throughout your life, you have only known how to put on clothes and eat food. When you hear people speak...
The two words "Buddha-Dharma" are like the wind passing over the treetops, or water poured upon a stubborn stone.

Today, having torn open my own face, I am called an "Elder," and I wish to discuss the matter with you all for a while. Yet, without cause, I have braved the great heat of the fifth and sixth months and traveled two thousand li;
this long journey has been utterly lost in an instant. Nevertheless, I am fortunate to have this staff.
Standing there, he held up his staff and said, "Staff, try to say something! He struck it once and said, "In this world of clarity and peace, one must strictly avoid false speech.
That evening, for the informal discourse (xiaochan), he said: "Plying oars and hoisting sails, I steer a bottomless boat, sailing freely across the sea."

With god-like heads and ghostly faces, they employ seal-marks of no pattern to examine all quarters. Having come from as far as two thousand *li* to dwell upon this mountain, they single-mindedly uphold this matter.
Raising his whisk, he said: "Look! Look! The seal-pattern has already been revealed. He drew a line and said: [The seal-pattern has already been revealed.]
The seams of the brocade have already opened. Whether Buddha or Patriarch, whether sage or ordinary person, all are sealed within this very place by a single seal.
It reaches such a point that the entire expanse of heaven and earth is filled with a whistling wind.

“Samādhi. Again, how is it? [He] struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, [the Master said: “Yunmen bestowed three blows of the staff upon Dongshan;

[The Master] ascends the hall. "The Dharma-gates of all Buddhas, the essential mystery of the Patriarchs: last night, with rain falling from the four eaves, it was preached so thoroughly that not a drop could leak out.

they step directly upon it the moment they lift their feet. If one cannot distinguish east from west or north from south, one cannot avoid having one’s borders encroached upon by others.
Under the gate of Jianfu Monastery, all are people whose fields and grounds are secure and firm. Whether lifting the incense spoon or setting down the fire tongs, each and every action—
"Natural and true. Why is it so? The public evidence is clear. Entering the hall: "Half a ladle at Linji’s place, half a ladle at Moshan’s place.

On the Dragon Boat Festival, entering the hall: "No talismans are written, no herbs are gathered; the incantation to raise the dead is forbidden."
Xiang took up his staff and said, "Fortunately, this one is here. He struck it once and said, "A fragrant breeze fills the courtyard;

summer days are long. People dwell in a world of lotus fragrance. At Kaixian, for the summer retreat *xiao-chan* (small private instruction): The great Flower Treasury Ocean (*Mahā-garbha-kośa-samudra*) is vast and boundless.
Rivers, streams, brooks, and creeks flow into it, all losing their original names. Fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs swim therein.
Swimming within it, all lose their original nature. Within this, the Buddhas of the three periods attain equal and perfect enlightenment;
within this, all sentient beings drift through birth and death; within this, the great assembly before me achieves effortless learning.
[The Master] picks up his staff, strikes once, and says: "Kaixian’s staff has sucked it all dry in a single gulp. The Buddhas of the three periods...

"When the waves at Caoxi are like those elsewhere, countless ordinary people sink beneath the earth. Winter Solstice Small Lecture: When droplets of water turn to ice, you must not yet cease your efforts;

The length of the thread: for now, you have not yet mastered even one inch of length. Even if you were to master that one inch of length, you still have not yet mastered the one inch being long.

in a state of restless bustle, from the morning cock to the evening bell, calling winter summer and summer winter—who cares about the length of a single inch?

Head. There is not a single thread of the appearance of coming or going; there is not a single thread of the appearance of new or old.

He did not take it to heart and consequently had no intention of entering the world. Now, none of his initial aspirations have been fulfilled.

Having resided at the monastery for ten years, he is known as an Elder; yet he remains simply the former Chan-zhao, with his eating, drinking, and daily conduct no different from those of the monks in the hall.
The disciples who follow him number no fewer than one hundred or so each year. On the fifth day, when the drum is beaten and he ascends the hall, he conducts himself as usual.
Among the elders, I have obtained subtle and great Dharma gates; according to my capacity, I have spoken here and there.
I dare not, for my part, use empty words to ensnare students, nor do I dare use over-the-top words to deceive them.
When I reach a point where there is no handle and no flavor, I laugh joyfully to myself—though those who listen may not understand why they should laugh. Thus it is with the scholar-officials.

Generally, people know one another well; however, those known are no more than those who are said to have read books, to be able to compose literature, to be capable of reviving neglected matters, or to possess a stiff backbone.
Indeed, if one has but a few hairs on their gallbladder, those who know them are few indeed.
Chan Master Xing of Beishan at Xuefeng in Fuzhou, a successor of Chan Master He Shanqing, addressed the assembly.
He cited the karmic occasion of the World-Honored One’s realization of the Way upon beholding the morning star, and offered this verse:
Six years of freezing left his eyes devoid of light; A single glimpse of the morning star was like frost after the snow. Carrying water out...
The mountain repeatedly calls out to sell [her wares], yet one knows not that the rivers and seas are vast and white.

Zen Master Shantong Guan, a successor of the lineage of Zen Master Sūzō Ryūtaku Zennichi of Suzhou, inscribed a eulogy for the Image of Avalokiteśvara Carrying a Fish Basket, which begins: "Cloud-like tresses..."
Heavily made-up and forced to wear a smile, he enters the dusty world for the sake of trivial matters. Though he brings with him that which is truly alive, no one buys it;
they view it merely as ordinary dead merchandise.
Chan Master Wenwei of Tianyi Xiaoyan in Yuezhou ascended the hall. He cited Yunmen’s instruction to the assembly: “Everyone possesses a luminosity;
yet when looked for, it is not seen, remaining dark and murky. What is this luminosity of yours?
[Yunmen] spoke on his own behalf, saying, “The kitchen, the storehouse, the mountain gate. He further said, “A good thing is no better than nothing. He then offered a verse: “Everyone possesses...”
There was light present; when one looked, no dark gloom was seen. He kicked over the mountain gate and the kitchen storehouse;
at that moment, light and darkness were naturally distinguished.
Chan Master Ning of Baiyan composed this verse on his tattered robe: "Falling apart and falling to pieces for many years; picked up at random as it comes to hand."
Draping one shoulder, at midnight he surely returns to fold his robes; who can transmit the message within this?
Master Chan Shanjing of Huazang Chun’an ascends the hall and cites the Sixth Patriarch’s dialogue on the wind and the banner, offering this verse:
"It is neither wind, nor is it the banner; where the white clouds end, the green mountains appear. How pitiable are the countless men of spirit and brilliance! Opening...
The Eyes enter the Death Barrier with dignity.
Zen Master Jing-sou Ru-jue of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was a successor of Zen Master Tian-tong Ying; he was a native of Wuzhou. Initially, he visited Chi-dun. One day, in the master’s room...
Zhongchi asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master suddenly replied, "A rotten melon. He then presented a verse, saying: "What is the Buddha? A rotten melon.
Biting into it, the frost penetrates the teeth. Though its roots and stem have no storehouse, Once a year, it blooms once.
He also once composed a gāthā to present to Chidun, saying: "At Mount Zhong, amidst white blades, bare-bodied."
Ai! Several times I have nearly been buried alive. Since my family was destroyed and I lost my kin, I have realized there is no fixed position to be arranged.
After his retirement, on the New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall: A new year strikes a new drum, Universally bestowing the fresh rain of Dharma.
All things are renewed; Each and every one conforms to the rules. The Great Being Samantabhadra rejoices, Seizing this moment to throw open the gates.
At the gate, he released the White Elephant King; there was no place on earth to be found. Holding up his staff, he said:
"Only this one does not belong to the old or the new. If you open your mouth casually, you swallow the Dharmakāya. He threw down the staff and said: "What is it?
Within a peach pit from a thousand years ago, there is still the original kernel. Small Retreat Assembly *Xichan*: This school of ours maintains the true command.
The total presentation is like a violent wind and sudden rain, surging forward with no resistance; like a spark struck from stone or a flash of lightning, one cannot catch up to its flight.
To raise a thought is to lose the source; to lift the eyes is already to have missed it. This is not a dharma of the present moment; do not give rise to various kinds of thoughts.

Even if you practice the three modes in alternation and strive to attain realization within a fixed period, these are merely the second head and the third summit—propping and bracing them up in myriad ways. Turn [back].

Seeing the breath in haste, one fails to realize that before the skeletal frame is complete, the eye of one's own nature is already clear. With a single cry of "kwaa," everything is finished and settled once and for all.
Even so, those who have realized this through personal experience are not even one or two in ten thousand; those who misunderstand it are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
A verse on the Buddha’s Enlightenment says: "Only after six years on the Snowy Peaks did he attain the Way, Striking out the ghostly eyes he had possessed since of old."
His face was filled with shame and confusion, with no place to hide; to this day he fears seeing the morning star.
Chan Master Demeng of Xuefeng in Fuzhou composed a eulogy for the Baguāng Monk (Pùtáihéshàng), saying:

*Carrying a cloth bag upon his staff, he wanders through the red dust of the world. How could he have ever seen the fundamental reality? His karmic consciousness is vast and boundless, lacking any basis; he does not know...*
"Who is it that laughs with open mouth?
Master Gao Yuan Zuquan of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Qiji of Jinshan, recounted how Jingqing was once at Xuefeng. One day, during a communal work assignment (pǔqǐng)...
Next, Xuefeng said, "Guishan said, 'When you see form, you see the mind. Is there any fault in this? Qing said, "For what reason did the ancients say that?
Xuefeng said, "Even so, I wish to deliberate with you. Qing said, "If it is like that, it is better that I go out and use my hoe.
The Master commented, "Xuefeng held the probe in his hand; Qing followed along with the shadow-grass."
Body. Had it not been for Jingqing, the communal labor would have nearly resulted in chaos.
[The Master] cites the dialogue between the Ninth Patriarch, Buddhabhadra, and the Eighth Patriarch, Buddhanandi: "My parents are not my kin; who is the most intimate kin?
The Buddhas are not my Way; who is the ultimate Way? A verse says: "It is clear that my parents are not my kin; the Patriarchs’ liver..."
I pour out my heart toward you. If you can directly realize this for yourself, the *udumbara* flower blooms as spring within the fire.
A verse presented to Huang Hanling Kai as he opened a reception hall: The road winds around the crest of a ten-thousand-fathom precipice;
When travelers reach this place, they are filled with sorrow. Suddenly finding a place of rest, They wander at ease through layered passes and mountains.

Chan Master Wumen Huikai of Huanglong in Longxing Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wanshou. He was the son of the Liang family of Liangzhu in Hangzhou; his mother was of the Song clan.
He received the precepts under Tianlong Heng and studied under Yue-lin at Wanshou Monastery. Yue-lin instructed him to contemplate the "Mu" (No) koan. After [a period of time]...
For six years, he made no progress whatsoever. He then resolved with fierce determination, vowing: "If sleep does not depart from me, let my body rot away.

Whenever he reached a state of exhaustion, he would pace back and forth along the corridors; when drowsy, he would strike his head against a pillar. One day, upon hearing the sound of the vegetarian feast drum, he attained enlightenment and composed this verse:
"A bolt of thunder in the blue sky and bright daylight— The eyes of all living beings on the great earth are opened wide. Ten thousand...

The elephant-like forest of beings bowed their heads in unison; Mount Sumeru leaped and danced through the three stages. On the following day, he entered the room intending to communicate what he had attained.
Lin suddenly said, "Where have you seen gods or ghosts? The Master gave a shout; Lin also shouted. The Master shouted again.
From then on, their spiritual functions were perfectly harmonized. In the Wuyin year of the Jiading era of Emperor Ningzong of the Song dynasty, he appeared in the world at Baoguo Temple in Anji.
He subsequently moved to Longxing Tianning, Huanglong Cuiyan, Kaiyuan and Lingyan in Suzhou, Jiaoshan in Zhenjiang, and Baoning in Jinling.
In the *bingwu* year of the Chunyou era of Emperor Lizong, by imperial decree, he ascended the hall at Huguo Renhuang Temple to give a discourse:
"If a person recognizes their own mind, there is not an inch of land in the great earth. When the ancients spoke thus, Huanglong [said]:
Not so. If a person recognizes their own mind, the entire great earth is but soil. Ascending the hall, he said: "Right and wrong, long and short—these are but winds at the ear.
Do not seek difference or sameness therein. If you wish to remain unmoved by the eight winds, let the ground of your mind be as vast as empty space.
The Elder Cishou only knew how to set sail with the current; he could not steer against the wind. Huang...
The Dragon, moreover, is not so. Both right and wrong have been cast off entirely; seek realization within right and wrong. Why is this?
"How many times the black winds have tossed the great waves, yet never have we heard that the fishing boat has capsized. Ascending the hall, he said: "Three parts of time have already passed as two.
The ox of Huai Prefecture eats the grain; the single point of the numinous terrace is never wiped clean. The horse of Yi Prefecture suffers from bloating; greed..."
"Born into this world, one busies oneself day after day; one searches the whole world for a physician. Even if called, they do not turn their heads—what can be done?

By cauterizing the left shoulder of a pig, one may attain realization here and bring an end to the quest for study. If this is not yet so, he took up his staff and said: 'I invite the Elder Wood to explain it clearly for all of you.
He struck the ground with the staff and descended from the seat. [He ascended the hall and said: "Zhaozhou said: 'The South...'"

Those coming from the south, he unloads for them; those coming from the north, he loads up for them. This is very much like worldly sentiment gauging warmth and cold, and people’s faces following the rise and fall [of status].
Cishou said: "To those coming from the south, he gives one side of a smile; to those coming from the north, he gives the other side of a smile.
This is very much like 'joyful slaughter'—there is a blade within the smile. If it were Jiaoshan, moreover—
It is not so. Those who come from the south, treat them with equanimity; those who come from the north, treat them with equanimity.
Do not be angry, do not laugh, do not be lowly, and do not be haughty. Why? Because in a world of purity and peace, there is no need for weapons.
As the morning sun verse says: "When it is cold, one urgently needs what is at hand; take advantage of the warmth to do some needlework. Suddenly, winter...
The moon has arrived; there is no need for feet to scramble and hands to fluster. He spoke a verse regarding the moon: "I have just seen a little light and shadow;
I wish to resolve this final segment. If it were my 'fist of no door,' I would not strike such a dull-witted fellow.
In his later years, the Master grew weary of the mallet and whisk. He lived in a hermitage on the shores of West Lake, yet his students remained numerous. Emperor Lizong summoned him to court.

While preaching at Xuande Hall, he moved Heaven through his prayers for rain; consequently, an imperial edict bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered dharma robe and the title "Foyan" (Buddha-Eye). Chan Master Deshou of Gusong on Nanshan in Xinghua Prefecture was a native of the Chen family of Lianjiang, Fuzhou. He received the tonsure at Hanshan in Suzhou. Once, while ascending the hall, he cited a case: A monk asked Xuefeng, "What is the first phrase?

Feng replied, "A good lad. He then said: [The Master] raised this case... Feng said, "A good lad. He further stated: "If you can understand this one phrase, you will see that all the Buddhas of the three periods of time, all the patriarchs, and all the ancestors of the ten directions have been born from within it. It is not something to be sought externally; it is right here before your very eyes. If you can grasp it, you will attain liberation; if you cannot, you will remain bound by the net of views. He continued:

"This 'first phrase' is like the great void—it has no front or back, no inside or outside. It is the source of all dharmas. If you can enter this gate, you will find that the myriad phenomena are all its manifestations. Do not seek it elsewhere; it is simply your own original face. He concluded: "If you can recognize it, you are a true heir of the Buddhas and patriarchs; if you cannot, you are merely a person wandering in birth and death. Thus he spoke.
Jiuzhou presented this to Changsheng. Changsheng said, "This is the second phrase. Xuefeng then instructed a monk to ask Changsheng, "What is the first phrase?
Changsheng said, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master said: "When these two great elders acted thus, tears flowed from their hearts in deep pain.
As for the first phrase, they had not yet even dreamed of it. Suppose someone were to suddenly ask Yishan:"
"What is the first phrase? [The Master] simply said to him: "The sword has long since departed. Ascending the hall, he raised the example of Zhenjing’s words:
"The head-dhūta rock is enveloped by moss; the Peak of Thrown-Pen is entangled by *bìlì* vines.
At Luohan Monastery, three practitioners are ordained each year; at Guizong Monastery, they drink tea after the formal meditation session. Does the assembly wish to understand this? Listen."
One verse: When the sky clears and the sun rises, rain falls and the earth becomes damp. I have spoken my heart’s content; I only fear you will not believe it.
Chan Master Zhuyan Miaoyin of Shishuang in Tanzhou was the son of the Wan family of Jinxian. He received his monastic precepts at Longtang.
Fashao traveled extensively, visiting various regions before arriving at Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou to pay his respects to Yuelin.

One day, during a period of private instruction, Yuelin asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "A rat gnaws through a lamp bowl. Yuelin nodded in approval.
He subsequently presided over several monasteries before moving to Shishuang. While reading the sutras by moonlight, he composed this verse: "Before the tongue moves..."

The patterns and colors are revealed; in five thousand scrolls, all is complete at once. If one says that one must wait for the moon to open the volume again, I dare guarantee that by the time of the donkey’s year, one will not yet have reached the end.
In his later years, the Master built a hermitage called Zixia (Purple Mist). Prime Minister Zhao Gong Kui, while residing in his private residence, once invited the Master to inquire about the Way.
On the twenty-third day of the eighth month of the year Baimao of the Baoyu era of Emperor Lizong of the Song dynasty.
He manifested illness and wrote a verse, saying: "Sixty-nine years—a single great dream. Return, let us go; take care, take care.
Having finished writing, he passed away peacefully. He was interred in a stupa at Zixia.

Chan Master Gutang Zu Jian of Gushan, a descendant of Chan Master Qiyuan Ying, was the son of the Xu family. He received the tonsure at Mount Zhong under Master Zhen and received full ordination there.

He subsequently went to rely upon Master Xiatang Yuan, serving him diligently for five years. Upon returning to Min, he visited Chan Master Qiyuan Ying, where he finally attained realization of the Great Matter and emerged [from his training].
He was originally from Langye in Chuzhou. Not long after, he moved to Beishan in Zhenzhou. He subsequently presided over Zifu Temple.

Provincial Governor Cheng invited him to Chengtian Temple, and he later moved to Guangxiao Temple. Provincial Commander Ye requested that he take up residence at Gushan, where he remained for seven years.

In the second year of the Kaiming era (1205), he retired from his duties; five months later, as the Master was about to pass away, he spoke this verse: "Throughout my life, I have suffered from words..."
Much more could be said, but what else can be spoken at the moment of death? I have exhausted my strength to present this to you: a single flake of snow upon a red-hot furnace.
Chan Master Zhengyin of Huangshan in Huizhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Yuyang Kuo.
He was the son of the Yu family of Renhe. Having gone to attend upon Yuyang, one night he heard a clap of thunder.
A thunderous sound erupted, and sweat poured from his entire body. Clapping his hands, he laughed loudly and said, "So it is, so it is.

When Emperor Shizu of the Yuan dynasty invited him to preach the Dharma, he pleased the Emperor's mind, who conferred upon him the title "Yuánmíng Tōngyìng" (Perfectly Enlightened and Universally Responsive). One day he told his disciples, "I shall depart in twenty-seven days.
When that time arrived, he passed away.
Chan Master Xuanzou Xingduan of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Zhen of Jing Mountain, the nineteenth generation descendant of Nanyue.
He was born into the He family of Linhai in Taizhou; his mother was Chen. His family had been of the world for generations.

He was a Confucian scholar by profession. From birth, he was exceptionally gifted; he could recite from memory anything he saw once. At the age of twelve, he followed his paternal cousin Mao to the Huacheng Monastery in Yuhang to receive the tonsure.
At eighteen, he received full ordination. Having heard that Zang-sou Zhen was propagating the Way at Mount Jing, he went there to rely upon him as a disciple.
Zheng asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Taizhou. Zheng gave a shout. The Master spread his sitting cloth. Zheng shouted again. The Master folded up his sitting cloth.
Zheng said, "I grant you thirty blows; go attend to the hall. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
One day, while attending him, Zheng said, "There are no monks in my land of Quannan. The Master said, "What about the Master? Zheng struck him. The Master caught the staff.
Zhuzhu said, "Do not say that it is better to have no monks. Zhen nodded in agreement and ordered him to enter the office of attendants.

When Zhen passed away, the Master went to Jingci Temple and relied upon Shilin Gong. Gong appointed him to oversee the secretariat. He later studied under Xueyan Qin at Yangshan. Xueyan asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "From the Two Zhe regions. Xueyan asked, "Why is your speech different? The Master replied, "Shut your mouth!"
"Stinking mouth! said Yanguan Qian. "The bridge at Taji is high and the peak of Jiyun is steep; I do not yet know where the Secretary resides.
The Master clapped his hands and said, "The duck swallows the snail; its eyes protrude. Qian laughed and, looking back at his attendant, said, "Serve some fine tea."
The Master said, "It is not necessary. After three years, Yinzhi passed away, whereupon he returned to Zhejiang. He served as the First Seat at Mount Jing.

In the *gengzi* year of the Dade era of Emperor Chengzong of the Yuan dynasty, he entered the world at Zifusi in Huzhou; by special imperial decree, he was granted the title Chan Master Huiben Zhengbian.
Subsequently, he moved to Tianzhu. In the *renzi* year of the Huangqing era of Emperor Renzong, he was transferred to Lingyin, where an imperial edict was issued.

He established a water and land assembly at Mount Jinshan and was commissioned by the Emperor to preach the Dharma. Upon the conclusion of the ceremony, he entered the audience chamber of the private palace, where he was granted the honorary title "Buddha-Sun Shining Universally.
Taking his leave, he returned south to reside at West Hill in Liangzhu. In the *Renxu* year of the *Zhizhi* era of Emperor Yingzong (1322), he was once again appointed to Mount Jing.
He received the gift of the golden brocade robe on three occasions, and his reputation and spiritual radiance became widely renowned. [He] ascended the hall and addressed the assembly: "Attaining..."
Vimalakīrti is an old, coarse-bearded fellow; Śākyamuni is a dried-up dung-stick; Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are dung-carriers;
the two levels of enlightenment, Equality and Wondrous, are precept-breaking commoners; Bodhi and Nirvāṇa are hitching posts for donkeys; and the twelve divisions of the teachings—

This is the register of ghosts and spirits. From those at the initial stage of the four fruits and three stages of worthiness up to the ten stages (*bhūmi*), these are all ghosts guarding ancient tombs.
Even if you perceive it in such a way, you are still mistaking the zero-point on the scale. [Ascending the hall: "Having shaved your head and donned the *kāṣāya*, you ought to practice the Holy Path.
All other miscellaneous matters are causes for birth and death. Eating and wearing clothes—these are merely miscellaneous affairs."
Matters such as viewing mountains and playing with waters are trivial affairs; even Bodhi, Nirvana, True Suchness, and Liberation are trivial affairs.
Ultimately, what can be called the Holy Path? Striking the whisk, he said: "The young maiden has already returned to the celestial expanse."
The simpleton still crouches by the fire. *Ordinary Assembly on the Lantern Festival*, and expressing gratitude to the *jianshou*, the bath master, and the *weina*.
A thousand grains, ten thousand grains—all arise from a single grain. From where does this single grain arise? A thousand lamps, ten thousand lamps...
It arises from a single lamp. From where does this single lamp arise? Once you recognize one lamp, then a thousand lamps, ten thousand lamps—lamp after lamp, without doubt.
Once you recognize one grain, then a thousand grains, ten thousand grains—grain after grain, without uncertainty.
A three-legged donkey prances on its hooves, trampling through the boundless seas of fragrant water. Holding up his staff and striking it once, he said: "Even at the crown of the head!"
"One blow is not permitted for those who are young. Entering the hall: "Today is the first day of the third month. The affairs of spring are nearly at an end.
The vegetables and wheat, green and yellow, fill the rivers and fields. A gentle breeze blows;
from kalpa after kalpa until this very moment, not a single hair’s breadth has ever been lost. Alas, these deluded and ignorant folk, who needlessly chatter and clamor. Entering the hall.
The mind is not the Buddha; rabbits and horses have horns. Wisdom is not the Way; oxen and sheep have no horns. [He] suddenly brandishes his staff, draws a line, and says:

"A night of falling flower rain; the whole city is fragrant with flowing water. Ascending the hall for the Buddha-Bathing ceremony, he points to heaven and points to earth, declaring himself number one:
"Having once emerged from the womb, today I appear once more. Yunmen would beat him to death and feed him to the dogs."
The monk of Xiangfeng Mountain pours foul water; ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat:

Two thousand two hundred and fifty years ago, within the Treasury of Radiance, the Golden Mouth personally bestowed this entrustment. Two thousand two hundred and fifty years later, the bhikṣu Xingduan shall now reveal it:
To protect life, one must kill; only when all are killed does one enter the summer retreat. If you can understand this point—
[The Master] ascended the hall to give a discourse. He thanked those who had served as *bǐngfú* (dharma-mace bearers) during the summer retreat. Xuefeng said:

"To expound a single phrase, then a thousand phrases and ten thousand phrases will circulate; set this aside. To drink a single flavor, then a thousand flavors and a hundred flavors are fully present;
set this aside. Xuefeng lowered his head and returned to his hut. When Yantou heard of this, he said: "Xuefeng and I are of one mind."
Born of the same lineage, yet not dying with me of the same lineage. But how is it so? At the edge of the cutting board. Planting crabapples at the bottom of a well.
This year’s peach and plum—each fruit is worth a thousand pieces of gold. Ascending the hall, he thanked the Head Seat and the Rector:

Before the golden mallet has even been struck, the great earth, mountains, and rivers are shattered into a hundred fragments. Before the jade whisk has even been waved, the myriad phenomena of the universe are revealed.

All interactions are interpenetrating. The people of the Yin dynasty used cypress; the people of the Zhou dynasty used chestnut. My home is east of Haimen; at dusk, I await the sun on the mountain. Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat:
On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, the retreat is established. He raises his staff and strikes it once to the left, saying:
"Within the various directions, one observes the *varṣā* retreat; on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, it is concluded. [The Master] picks up his staff, plants it firmly to the right, and says:
"Within the various directions, the summer retreat ends and the *pravāraṇā* ceremony is held. Before the empty kalpa, there was no name for Buddha and no name for sentient beings.
What is there to bind when binding? And what is there to unbind when unbinding? [He] leans on the staff and descends from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The moon is limpid and the clouds are clear; the ocean of enlightenment is autumnal. Fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs float and sink as they please.

Those who hang a thousand-fathom iron net high above should surely laugh at Yushan’s mere straight hook. Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace, as soon as the assembly had gathered, he looked to his left and right and said:
"Fortunately, we enjoy a peace that leaves no trace of its form. Why then dig a sore into good flesh? He then descended from his seat.
At the invitation of Zhong Tianzhi Temple in the Hangzhou Prefecture, he ascended the hall separately from the assembly and said:
"In the past, when I was at Yuquan, for four years and eight months, I beat the drum and played with the monkeys, never knowing rest by day or night.

Now that the public way has opened under the imperial court, we have encountered wise and enlightened men who divide the administrative branches, rectify abuses, eliminate greed, and search for the worthy and select the heroic. Why then, at the peak of Tianzhu, do I..."

Entrusted to the ignorant and clumsy, the government officials’ coercion drives one toward death; there is no room for further explanation. Packing my bundle, I set out on the road ahead, parting briefly from the multitude.
A thousand-year-old Chan rock leaps up into the sky; amidst the fire-clouds of the sixth month, auspicious snow flies. [Ascending the hall.]
The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; the wooden Buddha does not pass through fire; the clay Buddha does not pass through water. The true Buddha sits within.
Everyone recognizes the golden, wooden, and clay Buddhas, but how is it that one recognizes the true Buddha?

There are some clumsy fellows who say, "When it is long, it is the long Dharmakāya; when it is short, it is the short Dharmakāya. They do not realize, however, that within the treasury of our King, there is none.
Thus, on the occasion of the Double Fifth Festival, he ascended the hall: "Zhongfeng, this morning is the fifth day of the fifth month. There are no peach talismans nor mugwort tigers;
facing the sun directly, one immediately knows the pivot of the mechanism. Wondrous function, free and easy, transcends all location. You practitioners of the patched robe, do not be reckless!

When the sweet melon is sweet to the very stem, the bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. On the occasion of the Summer Retreat’s conclusion, he ascended the hall: "The autumn mountains are as if carved..."
Jade polished with autumn water; copper refined. East, west, south, and north, the living path is open. A pair of straw sandals as sturdy as tigers; a single tin staff as fierce as dragons.
Suddenly he bumps into Zen Master Ding, who asks: "The True Person of No-Station and that which is not the True Person of No-Station—how far apart are they?
Be careful not to remain silent, or your face will turn red. Ascending the hall: From the very beginning...
Without mind, there is nothing to transmit. Why need one dig into the earth to seek the blue sky? A mindless state is just like the moon on the Mid-Autumn Festival;
it illuminates the three thousandfold world and the great chiliocosm. [Ascending the hall, he thanked the Head Seat, the Librarian, and the Attendant. To speak with the mouth open is to hit the mark.
A hawk flies over a new fence; it takes a step and treads upon it. A monkey enters a cloth bag. Under Zhaozhou’s assembly, two monks pushed each other, refusing to accept the position of First Seat.
A good harvest arises from righteousness. Nanquan said, "The one with whom Master Wang comes and goes is the treasury.
Frugality gives rise to unfiliality. National Teacher Huizhong said, "I thought I had failed you; it was originally..."
Come! You have betrayed me. There is a thorn in the soft mud. In Central India, a swift opportunity is hard to encounter;
now it has been overturned all at once. If you understand, the heavens are high to the southeast; if you do not understand, the earth tilts to the northwest.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The Great Radiant Treasury is free from obstruction; its eight facets are brilliant and clear, yet they strike one with cold dread. Throughout the twelve hours of the day, one does not know where it is."
The entire body is mostly a vast expanse of blackness. [Ascending the hall: The Master raised the case where a monk asked Zhaozhou, “The myriad dharmas return to One;
where does the One return? Zhaozhou said, “I am in Qingzhou, making a robe of plain cloth that weighs seven catties.

The Master said, “Zhaozhou’s words are excellent, yet they do not meet the challenge of the present occasion. At Mount Zhongfeng, it is otherwise: ‘The myriad dharmas return to One; where does the One return?’”
"Where? In the fourth year of the Dàshí era, the floodwaters of the Western Mountains surged and overflowed. One night, they swept away three stone bridges.
The stone lions at the mountain gate let out a great roar, and the mountains, rivers, and the great earth all shook.

This was on the seventeenth day of the intercalary eighth month of the Jiwu year of the Yuan Renzong Yanyou era. He was eighty-two years of age at the time of his death.

Chan Master Yunfeng Miaogao of Mount Jing, Hangzhou, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wen of Jingci.

In a dream, he saw an infant with palms joined, sitting upon the heart of a lotus flower on the surface of a pond; he reached out his hand and received it. Upon waking, he was born.

Because of this, the Master named him Mengchi (Dream-Pond). His spiritual brilliance was exceptionally clear and penetrating; he was fond of books and studied with great diligence, having a particular devotion to the Buddhist scriptures.

On the seventeenth day of the month, at the age of seventy-five and with fifty-nine years of monastic seniority (*saṃgha-rakṣā*), he was interred at the western foot of the mountain within the monastery.
Master Tiejing Zhiming of Heshan in Huzhou was the son of the Wang family of Changxi in Fudang.

In the *Gengzi* year of the *Dade* era of Emperor Chengzong, he returned once more to Heshan.

Chan Master Zhihong Jian of Tiantong in Mingzhou first resided at Zhenru in Xinzhou and later moved to Tiantong. He ascended the hall and addressed the assembly:
The Buddhas are not ultimately real; they preach the Dharma to deliver all living beings. Bodhisattvas possess wisdom, yet their vision of the nature is not yet clear.

He attained sudden enlightenment. He went to visit Yunfeng Xin, who asked, "Where do you dwell, Senior Monk?

if you cannot answer, your teeth will be broken. To boast of spiritual powers instead is to have a share in crossing the river in secret.

Laywoman Shen Dao of Anji Prefecture asked: "How many phrases are there regarding the barrier of right and wrong?"
