Chan Master Zhengning Wanshan of Gushan in Fuzhou was a successor of Chan Master Gushan Liaoxiu. He was a native of the Li clan from Dahu in Shuzhou. At the age of seventeen—
Having lost both his parents, he went to Huangzhou to join Shuangquan Daoying, where he shaved his head. He received full ordination at Kaiyuan Temple.
He first attended upon the Third Patriarch Huan’an Lian; next, he attended upon Chijue Chong of Zhongshan, as well as Zhe of Changlu and Nanshan.
With none of them did he find resonance. Later, he attended upon Wuming Xing of Shuangta. Wuming asked him, "What was it like when Bodhidharma sat facing the wall for nine years?"
The Master said, "There is a principle that is difficult to extend. He struck the Master across the chest with a fist.

Suddenly, the Master attained realization and sighed, saying, "That which I have employed throughout my life has been shattered by this old man's single blow; it has dissolved like ice melting into water. He then returned to Min and paid his respects to Gufeng Xiu.
Gufeng presented him with the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature, but the Master was unable to answer. After more than half a year, he finally reached the inner gate of its meaning.
A-ou then recited a verse: "Zhaozhou says 'no'; the arrow does not miss its mark. Striking it, bumping into it—completely saving, completely killing.

Feng said, "You have attained it, but you have not yet reached the ultimate. One day, Feng raised the story of Deshan seeing Longtan and asked, "Where is the place where Deshan reached his own true ground?
The Master covered Feng’s mouth with his hand and immediately spoke this verse: "The pond..."
The dragon seen no longer appears; his entire body has already entered the Hall of the Empty King. Returning from a dream, he suddenly hears the dawn oriole singing;
the spring breeze has blown away all the peach blossom petals. Feng said, "Only today do you know that the Great Sage of Sizhou does not appear in Yangzhou.

He then instructed him to protect and uphold [the Dharma] himself and appointed him as the attendant for the incense. When Feng later moved to Xichan and Nanshan, the Master followed him in both instances.

[He served as] an attendant. After Feng returned to stillness [passed away], he went to rely upon Xuefeng Shuanglin Guo, who requested him to serve as the head of the administrative board (*ban-shou*).

In the *Dingyi* year of the Baoyu era of the Song Dynasty’s Lizong Emperor, he appeared in the world at Diaotai in Fuzhou; subsequently, he moved to Wansui. After some time, Grand Preceptor (Da-fu) Jia Pingchang requested him to reside at Gushan.
Under his mallet and whisk, the assembly numbered over four thousand disciples. Scholars and officials bared their robes to inquire after the Way, regretting that they had not known him sooner.
The Master ascends the hall late in the evening. It has been only three days since his entry into the monastery; he is busy attending to the affairs of others.
The lantern and the pillar are consulting one another in close detail. But tell me, what are they discussing? [He strikes the meditation seat.

"Last night, the blue heavens were calm and the winds and waves stilled; a single bright moon reflects upon the Lu Jiang River. [Ascending the hall: On the first day of the sixth month, summer is already at its midpoint.

Lotus flowers bloom upon the water; lychee fruits reflect the crimson of the mountains. The Unstationed True Person meets one everywhere. Should you hesitate, the clouds and mountains will be ten thousand layers deep.
At Mount Gu’s entry into the monastery, he ascended the hall and held up his staff, saying: "Lay down the pickaxe for tending the mountain;
take up the Patriarch’s sacred arrow. He struck the ground with the staff and said: "A single shaft pierces the three barriers; the sharpness of the pivot is like this."

A flash of lightning! Meeting the source from both left and right, the full mechanism of killing and giving life is such that even Dading Peak and Xiaoding Peak look toward the sky and rub their foreheads in admiration;
Baiyun Pavilion and Yongquan Pavilion nod their heads within a smile. At this very moment, tell me, where does the merit reside? Leaning on his staff, he says:
"The carved bow is already hung; the smoke of war has ceased. Ten thousand nations come to court and celebrate peace."
Addressing the assembly: Where ten thousand functions reach no further, where a thousand sages knit their brows—when the true command is being exercised, who dares to conceive of it?
To understand it in such a way already falls into the secondary truth (dvitīyārtha). It is much like hoping for plums to quench one’s thirst; what joy is there in that?
Members of the monastic community take black beans to exchange for people's eyes, and seize the binding rope to pierce through people's nostrils.
This is not beyond one's capacity. But tell me, what principle do these patch-robed monks perceive? He strikes his staff once and says:
"If there were no such eye for selecting the Buddha, how could the ancestral wind have reached the present day? He cites Xuefeng’s instruction to the assembly:
"This matter cannot be obtained from the lips; it cannot be obtained from the yellow scrolls; it cannot be obtained from the venerable elders of all quarters."
"It is obtained. "From what source must it be obtained? You must be careful. He spoke in verse: "A single drop of true pearl, red as spiced wine;
With earnest entreaty, two or three times urged. When at last the Master’s intent is exhausted, He swallows the cup just before departing on horseback.
As his end approached, he gathered the members of the two orders and showed them his final sincerity. He requested a brush and wrote this verse: "Eighty-four years..."
It is like a dream; when the dream breaks, it returns to emptiness, and there is not a single thing remaining. He passed away while sitting upright.
Chan Master Jie of Shuanglin in Wuzhou composed a verse on the occasion of the Great Master Fu putting on his patched robe, wearing the Daoist cap, and the Confucian shoes:
Neither Confucian, nor Daoist, nor yet Chan, His contrived cultivation is truly pitiable. He has brought his own life to naught.
The third [case] remains unresolved. More than eight hundred years have passed since then.

Chan Master Zhonghe Zhang of Qingshou Monastery in Yanjing, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Rongyang Hai, demonstrated his teaching to his disciples in the meditation hall by sometimes brandishing a wooden sword or holding [a staff].
Jin She dreamed one night of a strange monk who, leaning on a staff, hurried to the abbot’s quarters and sat upon the lion throne.
At dawn, he told the guest prefect, "Today, whenever a monk passes by, you must have him come see me. That evening, Haiyun arrived. The Master smiled and said:
"This is precisely what I dreamed last night. Yun said, "I have come without coming; how shall we meet?

The Master said, "In study, you must study truly; in awakening, you must awaken truly. Do not dig up old stumps. Yun said, "Because I struck the fire and the sparks flew, I came to know that my eyebrows are horizontal and my nose is straight.
The Master said, "It is different here where I am. Yun asked, "How do you express this conviction?"
The Master said, "The teeth are a set of bones; the ears are two pieces of skin. Yun said, "I thought there was something else. The Master said, "Wrong.

Yun gave a shout and said, "The grass bandit is utterly defeated! The Master then desisted. The next day, the Master brought up the case where Linji’s two head monks in the two halls both shouted at once.
A monk asked, "Is there still a distinction between guest and host? Linji said, "Guest and host are clearly distinct. You [should]..."
"How do you understand this? Yun said, "Shatter the mirror of the Qin dynasty; sharpen the ancient awl.

When the dragon soars beyond the clouds, what need is there to strike it further with a mallet? The Master said, "You have grasped its mechanism, but not its function. Yun then overturned the meditation seat.
The Master said, "The pleasures of the road do not mean one has finally reached home. Yun gave him a slap and said, "A thousand spirits!"
"Carrying a wild fox spirit, you have now seen through it; it is not worth a penny. The Master struck him with his whisk and said, "You have only attained its function, but not its essence.
Yun stepped forward and said, "The green mountains tower with a cold hue; the moon shines upon the clouds over a stream."
The Master said, “You have attained its essence, but you have not attained its wisdom. Yun said, “Flowing water moves from west to east; falling flowers have no front or back.

The Master said, “Though you are skilled in the samādhi of eloquent speech, it still has nothing to do with the matter. Yun raised his fist and then gave a single clap; at that moment, the meditation hall shook.
The Master said, “So it is, so it is! Yun— *Note: The text provided ends abruptly with "Yun," indicating the narrative likely continues beyond this point.*
He shook out his sleeves and departed. One day, [the Master] bestowed upon him a verse, saying: "Heaven and earth share the same root; there is no difference between them.
Wherever one turns toward the home-mountain, one encounters Him. I now entrust to you the Seal of the Empty King; The radiance of the myriad dharmas is all of one suchness."
Chan Master Gelu Tan cited a monk’s question to Shixi: "What is the Buddha? Shixi replied, "A short man watching a play.
He offered this verse: Majestic is the sixteen-foot body of purple-golden countenance; Within the arena of a hundred performances, there is transformative skill.
The short man watches with eyebrows raised high; An unperforated iron hammer dances in the spring breeze.
Chan Master Kumu Rong, a successor of Chan Master Wufang An, offered this verse in praise of the Third Patriarch: "Chronic illness entangles the body and life; the world offers no cure.
A poor family meets with robbery—how even more tragic! Who would have known that seeking the culprit leaves no trace? This is precisely the moment the thief returns to an empty house."
The Eulogy on the Portrait of Master Xinghua by Chan Master Yixi of Lushan Yuan Tong, Successor of Chan Master Bian Shan Qian, says: "A precious treasure from the Central Plains has its origins;
It pressed the King until he drew back his official head-covering. If one did not possess the 'blue and white eyes' upon reaching this point, Who would dare to deceive when the opportunity arises?"
A Brief Response.

Chan Master Guankui Chang of Yuezhou, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Wujing Che, spoke these verses on mountain dwelling: "When at leisure, I gaze upon the tall pines upon the rocks; my hundred-seamed robe..."
The Zen robe is torn and mended again; today one does not worry about tomorrow’s affairs. One’s entire life is contained within the bowl.
Master Wuji of Baolin Temple in Wuzhou, successor to Master Lingyinquan, ascended the hall and spoke.
He cited the verse by Miaoxi on the *Complete Enlightenment Sutra* (Yuánjué jīng): "Abiding at all times..."
Do not give rise to deluded thoughts. Do not attempt to extinguish the various deluded minds. Abide within the realm of delusive appearances without adding further cognitive discernment;
do not seek to distinguish reality within that lack of discernment. It is said: "The lotus leaf is round and round, as round as a mirror;

the water chestnut angles are sharp and sharp, as sharp as an awl. The wind blows the willow catkins like a ball of fur; the rain beats the pear blossoms, and the butterflies fly. The Master said: "Excellent!"
Xikě may be likened to peach blossoms and plum blossoms; together they form a single family. Shuanglin, however, is not so.

"Ten autumns have passed since I stayed at an inn in Bingzhou; My longing for home day and night recalls Xianyang. Without cause, I crossed the Sanggan River once more; Looking back toward Bingzhou, it is now my true hometown.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Reeds flower against the red of the smartweed; the trees have fallen, and the mountains reveal their bare bones. It is like the scene at Yang..."
The province is vaguely like the state of Yue. He picks up his staff and strikes once, saying: "For your sake, I strike through the cave of the spirit;
the True Man of No Rank is stark naked."
Chan Master Xingyuan Huirang of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou, whose alternative name was Huanyin,
was the twenty-second generation descendant of Mount Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Jiading Shanfu. He was born into the Xiang family of Huangyan, Taizhou.
His father was Zi and his mother Chen. He left home to become a monk at Baoguan Temple on Mount Lu, following the local custom.
He first studied under Zhuyuan Dao at Zituo, and subsequently went to Jingshan to visit Yuansou Dan. Dan asked, "Do you come from the eastern ridge or the western ridge?
The Master pointed to the straw sandals on his feet and said, "These were bought for three copper coins. Dan said, "Not yet; speak further. The Master replied, "I..."
Jiashan said, "It is just so. [The monk] asked, "I do not know, Master, how you would act? Duan said, "Because you have come from afar, I grant you thirty blows.
The Master then realized the essential meaning. After some time, he exhausted the depths of his realization and said, "As soon as one involves discursive thought, it all becomes superfluous dharma.
He went out into the world at Wufeng in Yingzhou and later moved to Jinge. In the *Renzi* year of the Hongwu era of Emperor Taizu of Ming, he was summoned by the Emperor from throughout the land.
The eminent monk established an assembly on Mount Zhongshan; the Master and Jitan Le were both present.

Le was appointed by imperial decree to reside at Tianjie Temple, where the Master served as the First Seat (Diyizuo), providing the essential framework and leading the monastic community with such propriety that he was praised for his fitness for the role at the time. The following year, the Master was appointed to preside over Jinshan.
In the year Wu-wu, he ascended to Lingyin Temple. On the day of the Buddha-Bathing Festival, he entered the hall and cited the story of Yaoshan Yuan. Because...
Zun Bu-na served as the temple director. During the occasion of the Buddha-bath ceremony, Mount Yunmen asked him, "You have bathed this one;
can you also bathe that one? Zun replied, "Bring me that one and I shall. Thereupon, Yunmen desisted. The Master said:
"This one and that one—each and every one has been bathed from the very beginning. Yunmen and Bu-na merely debated them; look closely and you will see."
He completes the talk and falls into error; completing the talk and falling into error leads to further confusion. He strikes the meditation seat and says: "The spring in Wulin has already passed;
the terraces and pavilions are now thick with green shade. On the occasion of the Buddha’s birthday, he ascends the hall:

As soon as the World-Honored One was born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, took seven steps, and looked around in the four directions, saying: "In the heavens above and on the earth below, I alone am honored. Truly accomplished!

"This is the mark of a Great Man; it is no child’s play. Yunmen said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to a dog, so as to bring peace to the world.
If you wish to belong to the lineage of Gautama, you must act exactly like this.
Fachang said, "That one blow was far too late. Before he left the Tuṣita Heaven, a blow should have been delivered right beneath his heels."
"A single awl—how could it have reached this day? Even so, it is much like drawing one's bow after the thief has already fled.
One might think that because the barbarian’s beard is red, there must be another with a red beard; yet the Yellow-Faced Old Man is surely merely showing off his cleverness at the end.
He seems as if he were unconcerned by anyone else. Although Yunmen and Fachang acted with courage when they saw what was right, alas, the sword had long since been lost."
Just as he was about to carve [the characters] into the boat, he drew a line with his staff and called to the assembly, saying: "Do you understand? A tangle of willow threads cannot be gathered;
it is draped with mist upon the jade balustrade. Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the first day of the intercalary fifth month. As always, the sun rises from the eastern side.
Every single patch-robed monk knows how to appreciate the sound; their short verses and long chants all accord with the musical laws."
The plum rains have cleared and the tree shadows are dense; wandering leisurely beneath the forest, what gain or loss can there be?
The "True Person of No Rank" is but a lump of red flesh; casually leaning him over, one topples Vimalakīrti. On the day of the Buddha’s *nirvāṇa*, he ascended the hall and said:
"Nirvāṇa and birth-and-death are equally flowers in the sky; 'Buddha' and 'sentient beings' are both superfluous words. When you people arrive here, how will you understand? Liang.
[The Master] struck the meditation seat and said: "I see only falling blossoms carried away by the water; I know not where they flow out the spring within the cave.
On the occasion of the Buddha-Bathing ceremony, he ascended the hall. Xiangyan said: "Last year’s poverty was not yet true poverty;

this year’s poverty is the first true poverty. Last year’s poverty allowed for the space of a single awl; this year’s poverty, there is not even an awl. If there were someone among the assembly who could come forth...
"Come here! Elder, you have erred. Today is the eighth day of the fourth month; it is the Buddha’s birthday. How can you raise this public case?
This mountain monk simply replied to him, 'The duties of the abbot are many. [He] descended from his seat.
For the cremation of Master Bifeng, he offered tea, saying: "Picked up from Mount Wutai—truly no ordinary seed. The man from Guansi has no head."
The brain is, indeed, the root of spiritual intelligence. Only this single cup of clear tea can wash away the feverish afflictions of sentient beings.
Consider, for instance, when Zechuan cast down his tea basket and Yangshan shook the tea tree—what matter did they ultimately clarify?
Du said, "Treading over the sea of birth and death, knocking down the city of nirvana. The Master [Zhaozhou] used this because students were mired in intellectual understanding.
Once, while speaking in private within the hall, he said: "Last night, Lotus Peak was eaten away by mayflies on one side.

Why do you not know? He further said: "Setting aside for a moment the question of Cold Spring Pavilion swallowing Ravine Thunder Pavilion, at what level of spiritual mechanism does South High Peak and North High Peak contending for the forehead rank?
None among the assembly had a realization. Before long, he was subjected to false accusations.
When the disaster of his arrest arrived, some advised the Master to plan for himself early on; he paid them no heed. With a serene countenance, he went to the authorities.

Before the interrogation had even begun, he recited a verse beneath the corridor and passed away while sitting upright. This was the twenty-third day of the sixth month in the year of Bingyin during the Hongwu era.
He was sixty-nine years old and had spent fifty-eight summer retreats.
Chan Master Fanchi Chu-shih of T'ien-ning Monastery in Chia-hsing Fu was the son of the Chu family of Hsiang-shan in Ming-chou.

On the day of Ding-si in the sixth month of the year of Ping-shen during the Yüan-cheng era of Emperor Cheng-tsung of the Yuan dynasty, his mother dreamed that the sun fell into her bosom when he was born.

While he was still in his swaddling clothes, a divine monk rubbed the master’s crown and said, "This child is the Sun of the Buddha; in days to come, he shall surely cause the Buddha-dharma to flourish and illuminate [the world]."
He illuminated the dark alleys [of ignorance], and for this reason he was given the name Tanyao. Having lost both his father and mother at an early age, he was raised by his grandmother.
At seven years old, he was able to compose verses; far and near, he was hailed as a prodigy. At nine, he entered Yongzuo Temple to receive instruction from Master Ne.
Subsequently, he followed his paternal great-uncle, Master Jin, at Chong'en Temple in Huzhou. When Duke Zhao Wei saw him, he recognized his potential and took him under his care.

He purchased a monastic certificate (*sengdie*) to receive ordination. At the age of sixteen, he received full precepts (*upasampadā*). When the monk Weng Qian moved to Daochang Monastery, the Master served as his attendant and subsequently took charge of the library keys.
One day, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he reached the passage: "When seeing arises from conditions and clarity is the cause, darkness constitutes non-seeing;

yet when clarity does not arise of itself, then all appearances of darkness can never darken it. At this point, he attained a realization. He then perused various scriptures, feeling as if they were suddenly revealed to him.
There was a karmic affinity from former lives. At that time, Yuansou Duan was propagating the Way at Shuangjing.

The Master went there to seek instruction and asked, "What is it that when speech issues forth it is not sound, and when form appears it is not an object? Yuanse suddenly said, "Speech issues forth but is not sound; form appears but is not an object. Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
As the Master was about to offer a reply, Yuanse let out a thunderous shout. Startled and flustered, the Master withdrew. It happened that Emperor Yingzong summoned eminent monks...

The Monk [Dahui Zonggao] was commissioned by imperial decree to transcribe the Great Canon (Tripitaka) in gold. When the Master entered the capital in response to this summons, he rose from sleep one night and heard the sound of drums;
he attained sudden, great enlightenment. Sweating like rain, he struck the table and laughed, saying, "Today, the nostrils of Mount Jing have fallen into my hands.

"Is there anyone who does not involve either of these two? [The Master] struck the meditation seat and said, "I almost let the prisoner go free and allowed his cleverness to grow.

Ascending the hall, he said: "One word, one silence; one action, one cessation—how do these compare to mercury falling to the ground? A monk asked Zhaozhou: [The Master said: "It is like mercury falling to the ground."

The monk requested instruction from the Master. The Master said, "Have you eaten your congee yet? The monk replied, "I have finished eating my congee. The Master said, "Go wash your bowl. Ascending the hall, he said:
"All day long I wear clothes, yet never a single thread has ever hung upon me. All day long I eat rice, yet never a single grain has ever been bitten by me.
It is like the earth supporting a mountain, unaware of the mountain’s towering height; it is like a stone containing jade, [unaware of the jewel within]."
Knowing that the jade is without flaw, he made no request of the Buddha, no request of the Dharma, and no request of the Sangha. Holding up his staff, he said:
"At times, riding upon the bright moon, I travel unexpectedly across the vast ocean. One day, as his illness grew critical, his attendant requested a verse.

The Master rebuked him, saying, "My worldly lifespan still has three years remaining. Subsequently, this proved to be exactly so. On the day of his passing, he suddenly clapped his hands and said, "A-he-he!
Great assembly, look at this! Thereupon, he passed away in silence. He was eighty-four years old and had been a monk for sixty-four years.
His disciples enshrined his entire body and buried it on the ridge to the right of Jizhao Temple.
Chan Master Liaohan Falin of Lingyin Bamboo Spring in Hangzhou was the son of the Huang family of Ninghai in Taizhou.

He left the household life together with Fayuan Taixu according to the Dharma. While contemplating the words of Muzhou, he attained a realization and said to Taixu, "From birth until death, it is only this;
it does not depend on anyone else. Taixu silently recognized his potential as a vessel and sent him to study under Yuansou Xuedou at Mount Zhong.
Zhudu asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Tiantai. Zhudu said, "Have you seen Hanshan and Shide?
The Master joined his palms and stepped forward, saying, "Today I have personally seen the Abbot. Zhudu said, "You liar and deceiver! Go attend to the hall!
He subsequently had him serve as the incense attendant and later manage the storehouse keys. One day, while the Master was reading the sutras, Zhudu said, "Reading the sutras, are you? The Master—
Fayan said, "It is so. Xuedou asked, "What will you use to look? The Master said, "I will use my eyes to look. Xuedou raised his fist and said, "Why do you not say, 'Use this to look'?
The Master said, "Put down your fist; with what will you look? Xuedou smiled. Later, when Dongyu resided at Jingci, he invited the Master to share the seat.
At that time, Zhuyu was living at Fushan; upon hearing the Master’s words of exhortation, he praised him highly.
He did not remain there. Soon after, he composed a verse. Among a congregation of five hundred, he was the foremost; his profound understanding made him fit to be a teacher for humans and devas.
He succeeded to the position at the Meng Hall of Jingci Monastery, where he remained behind closed doors for nine years.

The Left Chancellor of the Provincial Administration, Duke Tuohan, invited him to preside over Wanshou Monastery, and he subsequently moved to Zhongzhu. Upon reaching the Buddha Hall, he said: "Dust is brushed aside to reveal the Buddha; who would have known?"
"The Buddha is also but a speck of dust. Rarely do we encounter those who have pierced their ears; we see many more who mark the boat after the thief has gone. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The Dharma is the eternal Dharma; the Way is the eternal Way. To break through the gateway of the face—when the point is reached, it is not yet arrived.

For seventeen hundred years, the spiritual benefactors at Xuefeng spent morning and evening merely rolling three wooden balls. As for the old Chan practitioner Zhaozhou, who has lived for seven hundred autumns—"
When people see him, they simply say, "Go and drink tea. Zhongfeng often saw his brothers visiting him; they would merely exchange greetings of courtesy, burn incense, and join their palms.
If one is a true offspring of the Golden-Maned Lion, there will certainly be a sense of paradox even three thousand miles away.
In the Wuyin year of the Yuan Zhiyuan era, he moved to Lingyin. Ascending the hall, he raised the case of a monk asking Zhaozhou, "The myriad dharmas return to One."
"Where do they all return? Zhaozhou said, "I am in Qingzhou making a cotton shirt that weighs seven *jin*.
The Master remarked, "Although Zhaozhou skillfully wields the Great Sword to cut off this monk’s tongue, he cannot avoid exposing his own family's disgrace."
At Lingyin, it is not so. Suddenly, a monk asked: "The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return? He simply said to him:
"Today is as hot as yesterday. Ascending the hall, he said: "Within the jurisdiction of Old Hangzhou lies the famous mountain of Lingyin.
It was first established during the Xianhe era of the Eastern Jin dynasty. Dharma Master Huirui was its first patriarch. Today is the Lantern Festival."
[The Master] paused. "Lamps are being lit in various places. The administrators and the year-steward must each take care of the wind and the candle.
Then he descended from his seat. "For the sake of Chan Master Sen, [I say]: 'The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand images are all sealed by the One Dharma.
Right now, for you, I have already removed both the diamond circle and the thorny jujube. What do you call 'the One Dharma'? Two arises because of one; even one..."
"Do not guard the fire-tortoise; let out a lion’s roar! The Great Dragon soared through the void.
Star-Kichi Daisō dispatched gifts to invite the Master, but he declined and did not go. After the messenger had traveled back and forth three times, the Master took refuge in the mountains of Kuaiji.
The Imperial Court, realizing he could not be compelled, submitted a formal petition requesting him to return and lead Lingyin once more. Three years later, he retired to Liaohan.

Ānanda. In the spring of the year Yiwèi (1355) of the Zhìzhèng era, he was afflicted by a slight illness. On the second day of the second month, he gathered the assembly and recounted the beginning and end of his life’s conduct, exhorting them, saying:
"The decline of the Buddha-dharma has never been more severe than it is today. You should each exert yourselves. My worldly karmic conditions have come to an end here.
He then requested a brush and wrote this verse: "Seventy-two years; a wedge driven into empty space. At the very end..."
He uttered a single phrase: "Not said, not said. Thereupon, he passed away peacefully. His shrine remained for ten days, his countenance unchanged.
His entire body was interred to the west of the Songyuan Pagoda. The scholar Huang Puqing composed an inscription for his pagoda.
Chan Master Guding Zuming of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was the son of the Ying family of Fenghua in Siming. He received his formal training at Jinei and was ordained there.

During the Yuan dynasty, when Zhu Xi Tan was the abbot of Tiantong, the Master went to rely upon him and served as the Director of Internal Records. Later, he traveled to Min and then returned to Zhejiang.

It happened that Yuansou was residing at Lingyin; the Master went there to pay his respects. One day, while entering the inner quarters for instruction, he questioned [the Master] regarding Huanglong’s encounter with Ciming.
[The Master] explained the causes and conditions. The Old Man (Ciming) questioned him, saying, "As for Zhaozhou’s words regarding 'The Hermitage Lady was exposed by me,' Ciming, you laughed.
Is that an insult? Tell me, do the applications of these two old fellows coincide or differ? The Master said, "A pair of unperforated iron hammers.
The Old Man said, "If one awakens directly beneath Huanglong, what then? The Master said, "That too is [an unperforated iron hammer]."

"It is like seeing flowers in the sky with diseased eyes. The old man said, "It is not so, it is not so. As the Master was about to offer a word in response, the old man gave a shout. At that moment, the Master attained a state of vast clarity.
He was appointed to the position of Secretary (Jishi). At the age of fifty-four, he first entered the monastic world as abbot of Longjiao Temple, followed by Baota and Zhongtianzhi.
In the Dinghai year of the Zhi Zheng era of Emperor Shun of the Yuan dynasty, he was summoned by imperial decree to move to Jing Mountain, where he was bestowed the honorary title Huixing.
Chan Master Wenmin Hongjue Pujie. A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said, "A broken winnowing basket gives birth to a broom. The monk bowed and said, "I thank the Master for his instruction.
The Master said, "Last night at the third watch I lost the ox; when I rose at dawn, I had lost the fire as well. [The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A scale."
[The Master] dipped a hammer in vinegar and asked, "What is the matter that lies beyond? The Master said, "Looking up, one does not see the sky.
[The student] asked, "I recall a monk asking Yunmen, 'What is the Buddha? and Yunmen replied, 'A dry piece of dung. What about that? The Master said, "Yunmen was not being kind-hearted.
[The student] asked, "How far apart are 'a dry piece of dung' and 'a hammer dipped in vinegar'? The Master said, "[Not far at all]."
"In the boiling cauldrons there is no place for cold. The monk prepared to offer a word in response; the Master then gave a shout. Ascending the hall, he said:
"I shall place the worlds of the ten directions upon the eyelashes of everyone present, without the slightest movement.

I shall pour the waters of the four great oceans beneath the heels of everyone present, without a single drop flowing away. Those who understand medicine have few ailments; those who know their lot have little sorrow. Ascending the hall, he said: [The same as above.]
Daguizhi held up a stalk of pickled vegetables and showed it to the assembly, saying: "Everyone has gathered here to eat this single stalk of vegetables.

If you call it 'a single stalk of vegetables,' you will enter hell as fast as a shooting arrow. The Master said: "When a patriarch acts for the sake of others, he is like a household with lethal poison;

he places poison within their food and drink and gives it to people, never failing to desire to sever their life-root. Nevertheless, those who are his karmic adversaries can [still attain liberation]."
There were several individuals among them; the Chancellor, Duke Kangli, would frequently visit the Master to inquire about the fundamental principles of the Chan school.

One day, while the Master was reading a scripture, the Duke asked him, "Why are you not reading the scripture? The Master replied, "Is merely tracing the lines and counting the characters what constitutes reading a scripture?

The Duke was speechless. The Master turned the pages of the scripture and said, "The old monk is going to read the scripture. The Duke covered the scripture with his hand and said, "I beg the Master to [read it] for me."

[The Master] said, "Explain it clearly. The Master asked, "Who were Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou? In the Wuxu year of the Zhizheng era, as he was about to pass into *nirvāṇa*, he wrote a letter entrusting the Chancellor with his protection.
He further composed a verse, saying: "Life and death are pure and true; the great void is perfectly full.
For seventy-nine years, the cradle rope has snapped. I cast down my brush and depart. Upon cremation, neither his tongue nor his prayer beads were consumed by the fire.
His relics were beyond counting; they were distributed and enshrined in pagodas at Jingshan, Longjiao, and Putuo. His secular age was seventy-nine, and his monastic seniority was fifty-five.
His *Recorded Sayings* from four assemblies, along with his *Collected Works*, have been circulated in the world.
Chan Master Gu'an Zhongyou Zuchan of Tiantong Monastery in Mingzhou was a native of the Chen family of Ning County.

He received the tonsure under Fozhi Changqing Kuangzhen and attained the essential meaning of the Dharma while studying with Jizhao at Mount Jing. He subsequently took charge of monasteries at Mount Lu and Xiangshan, before ascending to the abbacy of Tiantong Monastery in the prefecture.
Upon ascending the hall, he said: "If one were to discuss the 'First Phrase,' the Buddhas of the three periods have not spoken it, nor have the Patriarchs of the six generations."
The Way of the Teacher cannot be attained. The old monks of the world cannot speak it; this mountain monk cannot speak it; the great assembly cannot speak it.
Holding up his staff, he said: "Can this staff speak? To speak it would be the second phrase. Entering the hall, he said:
"This mind is Buddha; not this mind, not Buddha. Not mind, not Buddha. On Mount Wutai..."
Clouds steaming rice. Before the steps of the Buddha Hall, a dog-urine sky. At the top of the bannerpole, a frying pan. Three monkeys tossing coins at night.
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: Before the fifteenth day, head and tail are golden lotuses.
After the fifteenth day, white oxen and tabby cats run in packs. On the very fifteenth day, the pavilions...
The fire above and the fire below illuminate one another; the carriages and horses pass back and forth as people watch people. How excellent! O Great Assembly, tell me: in what way is it excellent?
It is difficult to deceive the eyes of the multitude. [With these words, he descended from his seat.]
Chan Master Yuzhong Shanru of Kaiyuan Monastery in Suzhou was a native of Wujiang. He ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddha-body pervades the entire Dharma-realm, universally manifesting before all sentient beings.

Why was it that when the residents of Hudu and followers of Huang-Lao (Daoism) went to welcome him, a violent storm arose and the image immediately sank? [This happened] when Zhu Ying of Wu County and the nun Dongling Bo invited him.
The two spiritual forms were towering and floated side by side; when he attempted to lift and carry them, they suddenly ascended the boat.

The stone images of Vimalakīrti and Kāśyapa currently enshrined in the mountain are these very ones. Is this not a manifestation that reaches everywhere in accordance with conditions, yet remains eternally upon this seat of Bodhi?
Nevertheless, even though it is so, if you understand it in such a way, you are like a tiger watching a water mill.
Do not understand it in such a way. From Zhenzhou to Changlu—whether it be "such" or "not such"—if you set both aside, then what?
In a world of peace and clarity, there is no need for deceptive words. He presented this verse to a monk from the Grass Hut:
"The National Teacher is a virtuous teacher for ten thousand generations; The Grass Hut at Yandang is renowned throughout the world. For those who dwell within it, Birth is difficult to encounter."

Having encountered [the Buddha], one repays his profound kindness. The ordination certificate descends directly from the heavens; having obtained it, how could its value be worth less than ten thousand pieces of gold?
If one does not cultivate the monastic practice during this time, one betrays the singular heart of the Emperor and the King.

In his later years, the Master, because of the Dharma-son Huángyíngzhōng, resided at Wànshòu Monastery. He cleared out a room in the courtyard to dwell there for his old age. Subsequently, Xiāng Běnkōng succeeded him.
He treated him with exceptional hospitality, enabling him to dwell at ease and find joy in the Way.

He once resided at Zhizhi An (Direct Pointing Hermitage) in Fengmen, and people consequently called him Master Zhizhi. When he was about to pass away, he summoned his sons to bid them farewell and departed in serene stillness.
Chan Master Chunchi of Wanshou Temple in Suzhou sent this verse to Attendant Zhong:
"When Niaoke blew up his cloth hair, the attendant was enlightened on the spot. This pair of unperforated iron hammers is nothing but the ghostly livelihood being flaunted."
If one is a sharp and discerning master, possessing a natural and innate air of dignity, they will expand the radiant light of the original ground and manifest the very core of the patch-robed monk.
They will encompass the great trichiliocosm within the tip of a single hair and contain Mount Sumeru within a mustard seed;
they walk directly upon the crown of Vairocana’s head, such that even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot block their path.

Chan Master Wuan Benwu of Shangzhu, Hangzhou, was a native of Huangyan. He received the tonsure at Fangshan in Jingci Monastery and relied upon Jizhao at Zhongzhu, where he served as the administrator of the monastery’s affairs.
His maternal uncle, a venerable elder of the Confucian school, entreated him to change his religious affiliation.
Thereupon, he saw that Zantang Cheng was at Yanfu Monastery, where he had been refining his mastery of the scriptural divisions (*śāstra*). Jizhao lamented his departure and sent him a verse, saying:
"Entering Chan from the Teachings has occurred in both ancient and modern times; Entering the Teachings from Chan has never existed before or since.

Though the gates of 'One Mind' and 'Three Contemplations' differ, The moon remains solitary as it fills the thousand rivers. Later, when he appeared in the world to propagate the teachings, he served as the successor to Zantang.
The successor then burned another incense stick to offer thanks to Jizhao, not allowing their minds to become divided by the difference in their outward traces.

When Jizhao passed away, the Master was residing at Yanqing in Siming. Jizhao specifically sent a letter entrusting him to vigorously propagate the essential teachings of the two houses—Dasu and Shaolin—without mentioning anything else.
At the memorial service, the Master held up the incense and said: "The fifth transmission from Miaoxi..."
Most radiant brilliance! The tranquil illumination of the nectar-gate of this entire lifetime—casually touching it, one’s liver and brain would shatter;
sudden frost turns into the warmth of spring. I think back to the day I lost my nostrils; what kind of breath remains even now?

The celestial wind blows from the north as the year draws to a close; why seek traces in the void with a flash of lightning? Later, at the time of his passing, he was without illness, sitting upright until his death.

Baiyun Tai. Chan Master Husheng Diyuanqi of Taizhou Prefecture was a native of Linhai. While he was still a scholar, he paid his respects to his paternal uncle, the Venerable Jian, at Baozang Temple in the village.
He happened to read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, reaching the passage concerning the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
"All these are objects manifested within the wondrously luminous mind. Having set aside his scrolls and reflected for a long time, he suddenly attained realization.
He informed his parents of his desire to leave the household life and took Jizhao as his teacher. He donned the robes of a dhūta practitioner, becoming increasingly diligent over time.

Later, he emerged into the world to protect the sacred teachings. Afterward, he retired to the eastern hall for seven years and composed works titled *Dapuhuanhai* (The Great Universal Illusory Sea) and *Fafa* (The Dharma).

His works include the *Yuntong lüe* (Brief Account of the Transmission of the Dharma), the *Zhuitan* (Discourse on the Superfluous), the *Woushuo* (Discourse on the Tumor-like Growth), and the *Rushishenghua* (The Essence of Confucianism and Buddhism), totaling several volumes.
He also composed the "Fu on the Genealogy of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. At the time of his death, he was forty-three years old.

Chan Master Wufang Zhipu of Ba’en, a dharma successor of Chan Master Wan of Jiangxin, was the son of the Long family of Guiyang. After taking up residence there, he ascended the hall and said: "In the sixth month, the traveler’s mouth spews smoke;
they toil and struggle only because they are dragged by profit and fame. How can they compare to the disinterested guest beneath the forest trees, who takes a single great sleep?"
He slept until dawn in his robes. Striking the meditation seat, he said: "Ganming does not begrudge his verbal karma; I have explained it all for you.
On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, Old Yan will question you; he will demand the payment for the food. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The spring colors are deep, the spring days are bright; the gardens are warm and the wild peach blossoms are red. In the past, as soon as Lingyun saw them, he transcended both form and emptiness."
Now all these people see it collectively; for what reason do they not awaken? If they do not awaken, their eyes will be caged by forms. Striking the whisk, he said:
"To teach people wrongly is to resent the wind at the fifth watch."
Master Dà Chánshī Xiǎoyǐn of Yúnjū in Nánkāng Prefecture sat upright in his quarters all day long, appearing as serene as still water.
When he shaved off his remaining beard and hair, his attendants plucked out the live roots and vied with one another to preserve them; after two nights, they produced *śarīra* relics.
He once composed a verse for the practitioner Xìn, which says: "Faith is the source of the Way and the mother of merit; if a medicine is effective, it does not require much."
If a superior person can directly accept this, what can even the Buddhas and Patriarchs do against them?
Chan Master Xiaoyin Dayin of Jinling Daxiang Jiqing Temple was a dharma heir of Chan Master Xiyuan of Mount Jing; he was born into the Chen family of the Yimen clan in Jiuyang.
The Master was tonsured at Zhui-shuiyuan Monastery in Jun County. From childhood, his intelligence and clarity were peerless. Initially, he visited Yishan Wan;

subsequently, he was sent to Bai Zhang to study under Huiji Xi. Upon their first meeting, Xi recognized his potential and held him in high esteem, appointing him to oversee the secretariat. One day, Xi asked:
"After Huanglong received the essential teaching from Letan, he led his disciples on a journey to travel among various masters. Yet, upon meeting Ciming, his spirit was drained."
[The Master] said, "Sweat and purge! Where does the fault lie? The Master raised his voice and said, "In a peach pit a thousand years old, what old kernel are you looking for?
Furthermore, while standing in attendance in the meditation hall, Yuanxi brought up the story of Baizhang’s wild fox to interrogate him, saying, "Not falling into cause and effect..."
He immediately fell into the body of a wild fox. Not being ignorant of cause and effect, he then shed the body of the wild fox.

But tell me, where does the point of benefit and harm lie? As the Master was about to answer, Xizhen let out a thunderous shout. At that moment, the Master’s doubts were completely dispelled like ice melting away.

Because his fellow practitioners pressed him with difficult questions, the Master replied with this verse: "Bai Zhang’s wild fox, the wild fox of Bai Zhang— Buried together in a single pit. May you rest in peace."
May he enjoy long life. Later, he moved from Wuhui on Lake Hushan to Baoguo Zhongzhu in Hangzhou.
In the year Jisi of the Yuan Tianli era, Emperor Wen established the Great Longxiang Jiqing Monastery at his former princely residence and selected a man of renowned virtue to be its founding abbot.

The Master was the first chosen for this post; he was granted the title "Great Chan Master Guangzhi Quanwu" and was subsequently summoned by imperial decree to the capital, where he had an audience with the Emperor.
At the Quanzhang Pavilion, he was granted a seat and consulted regarding the essentials of the Dharma. When Emperor Shun ascended the throne, his treatment became even more honored.

Later, seeking retirement due to old age and illness, he received a gracious imperial decree refusing his request; the Emperor commanded the provincial authorities to provide him with protection and supervision, so that he might dwell in peace until the end of his life.

Ascending the hall, he said: "In the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (Sukhāvatī), the waterfowl and the groves of trees all recite the Buddha’s name. In the Heaven of Contentment (Tuṣita), the trees stand supporting one another."
While touching upon the teaching of suffering and emptiness, he held up his whisk and said: "This mountain monk’s whisk has pierced through the nostrils of you all.
Where, then, can you all breathe out? Heh! Entering the new temple, he ascended the hall and said: 'The primary truth is as clear as the bright sun and as vast as the great void.
The myriad phenomena are dense and manifold, yet not even a hair's breadth is established within it. To cite the present based on the past is nothing other than [this truth].'"

To branch out from the main point is like driving a stake into empty space; yet, when the Imperial Decree establishes a temple and various officials attend the assembly, one cannot simply let it end there.
Is there anyone who can stir up the spirit and challenge this? (The questions and answers are not recorded. Then he said:
"Śākyamuni Buddha renounced the Golden Wheel to ascend the rank of Buddhahood; the present Emperor likewise [renounces the throne]..."
Occupying the rank of a Buddha, he governs the golden wheel; he gathers the ocean of three thousand worlds within a single seal and fully embodies eighty thousand dharma-gates upon a single hair-tip.

Like the Bodhisattvas in the assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, who have attained the liberation door of the inexhaustible treasury of merit, he produces various delicious foods and drinks from a single vessel. Furthermore, as the assembly gazes upward, they behold...
From the midst of the air, various kinds of precious jewels rained down, completely satisfying the hearts of all sentient beings according to their inclinations.
Thereafter, those who obtained these jewels fully realized the Dharma-gates; those who tasted their flavor all attained the wondrous Way.

There was not a single speck of dust that did not embody the Buddha-work, nor a single dharma that did not perfect the True Teaching. Thus, the precious monastery is now being established to propagate [the Dharma].
The Dharma is bestowed as a gift. The celestial music of the devas resounds spontaneously without being struck; the Brahma-songs and hymns are naturally performed and presented.
Bodhisattvas from the ten directions all assemble at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), and the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, together offer praise and celebration.

Are there any who, bypassing the illusory city, ascend directly to the precious abode? Striking the whisk, he said: "The four seas have already come under the imperial transformation; now that the times are peaceful, rest."
Singing the Song of Great Peace, he ascended the hall. "Atop the solitary peak, gazing at the clouds and sky—is this not burying one's own spiritual brilliance?
In the crossroads of the street, mixing mud and water—here, we value the circulation of the true eye. He held up his staff and said: "Śākyamuni has already passed away;
Maitreya has not yet been born. Right now, at this very day, it is the life-vein of the thousand sages and the tongs and hammer of the patriarchs."

In the hands of the new National Master, when he picks it up, there are openings in every direction; every aspect manifests the boundless wondrous body. When he sets it down, it mirrors the earth and illuminates the heavens;
everywhere the ocean of jewel-kings' lands is revealed. What need is there to say that "streams and mountains differ, yet clouds and moon are the same"?
The ultimate transformation is non-active, its function unmastered; vast and open is this single expanse of the ancient sovereign’s wind. Once again—
Master Ji sent someone to deliver a message to Sida, saying: "Why do you not go down the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings?
What are you doing, gazing fixedly at the clouds and the Milky Way? Sida replied: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have all been swallowed by me in a single gulp;
where else are there any sentient beings left to be saved? The Master said: "Sida was so thoroughly pressed by Master Zhi that he was brought directly to [the realization of]..."
"Retreat three thousand paces. On two occasions, he ascended the hall for formal discourse. With a mind empty, one attains the highest degree; why need one select an official?

To shoulder the burden of the monastic community for the sake of the assembly is just as if it were for oneself. To serve the nation and the Dharma by selecting the right person and assigning office according to their capacity is like the performance of the Ninefold Music:
every movement to the left or right, every advance or retreat, is perfectly in accordance with the measure. It is just like a single shout that distinguishes guest from host.
"Master, when illumination and function operate simultaneously, how do people distinguish between them? [The Master] gave a shout and said:
"When the nine-myriad-li Peng bird first exerts its power, the three-thousand-year-old crane immediately soars. Ascending the hall, he said: "Words are uttered but are not sounds;
forms appear but are not objects. What is the reason for this? To sleep amidst sound and form, to sit and lie down amidst sound and form—this is already somewhat better."
Therefore it is said: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing; there is no further sound or form to present to you. If one understands this, there is nothing at all;
why then need one distinguish between essence and function? Suddenly picking up his staff, he said: "Where do the flowing waters and yellow leaves come from?
An ox, trailing crows in the cold, passes through a distant village. He struck the ground with the staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Huangbo:
In his room at Longnan, he gave this "hanging word": "What is my hand like? It is like a Buddha’s hand. What is my foot like?
It is like a donkey’s foot. Every person has their own karmic affinity for life; what is the senior monk’s karmic affinity? This is known as the Three Barriers of Huanglong.

They are like the laws established by Shangjun: although the laws were established, they discarded the Way of the former kings. Thus, those who emerged from his school at that time were very numerous.

There were many who received his transmission, yet those who truly mastered it became even fewer. Had he strictly adhered to the family precepts of Ciming, his descendants would not have been on the verge of extinction.
While a monk was standing in attendance, the Master spread out both hands and said, "I have opened it wide with these eight characters;
why do you refuse to accept it? The monk replied, "Do not try to deceive me. The Master said, "For so long, you have lacked even a single breath of life."
[The Master] struck him. The Master asked the assembly, "The 'Seven-Pound Linen Shirt of Qingzhou'—the ancients have already spoken of it.
Ultimately, the myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return? A monk stepped forward and said, "At the head of the eastern corridor, under the western corridor.
The Master said, "Where did you see Zhaozhou? The monk hesitated, and the Master said, "Under the staff, one does not become a dragon."

A monk came for an audience. The Master said, "Raising the whisk and brandishing the mallet are the models of the ancients; holding up the pitchfork and dancing with the sword are the regulations of the patriarchs. Under the gate of a patch-robed monk, how should one act?
The monk paid his respects and departed. The Master said, "Not even a single tally was required.

The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from traveling the mountains. The Master said, "Under your straw hat, you have crushed it all—Luopo!"* *Note: "Luopo" (洛浦) refers to Luopu Yuan'an (洛浦元安), a famous Chan master of the Tang dynasty known for his rigorous teaching style.*
"What is it that you have penetrated? The monk replied, "Even before entering the gate, I have already presented it to the Master. The Master said, "Why then do you not bring it forth now?
As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. In the fifth month of the Jiashen year of the Zhizheng era under Emperor Shundi, he manifested a slight illness.
He wrote a letter by hand to bid farewell to his friends and instructed his disciples to use the gold bestowed upon him by the two dynasties [the Yuan and Ming].

He offered ceremonial gifts and constructed the Wanfo Pavilion (Ten Thousand Buddhas Hall) as a means to repay the grace of the state. On the twenty-second day, he wrote a verse and passed away while sitting in the lotus posture.
On the sixteenth day of the eighth month of the autumn of that year, he was buried on the rear ridge of the stupa courtyard at Shitou City.
He was sixty-one years old by secular age and forty-six years of *dharma-śāsana* age. Huang Wenxian Gong Qin composed his epitaph, and Yu Wenyong Gong Ji recorded [his life].
Record of the Journey to Practice the Way. In the *jiayin* year of the Hongwu era, he was reinterred at Boyun Mountain, adjacent to the ancient stupa of Kang Senghui.
His works, including the *Chanyuan Qinggui*, the *Siyi Yulu*, and the *Pushu Ji*, have been circulated in the world.
Chan Master Nianchang of Meiwu in Xiangfu, Jiaxing Prefecture, was the son of the Huang family of Huating. His father was Wenyou and his mother was Yang.
She became pregnant after dreaming of an elderly monk seeking lodging. He was born on the twelfth day of the third month in the Renwu year of the Zhizhi era of Emperor Shizu of the Yuan dynasty.
That night, divine light illuminated the chamber and a wondrous fragrance permeated the air. From childhood, the Master delighted in sitting alone. At the age of ten...
Second, he left home under Tizhi at Yuanming Monastery in Pingjiang. At fourteen, he shaved his head and received full ordination.
In the Wushen year of the Zhida era, Fozhi Huiji moved from Baiyang in Jiangxi to Jingci in Hangzhou; the Master went there to attend upon him.

He happened to encounter Fozhi ascending the hall to give a discourse, citing the karmic conditions of Elder Fu of Taiyuan, who attained enlightenment upon hearing the sound of a horn. The verse [Fozhi] spoke was: "The lute..."

He was born and entered the vast ocean. The Grand Historian traveled to famous mountains; from then on, along the road outside the city of Yangzhou, strict orders were issued forbidding the gates from being opened early.

When Fozhi moved to Mount Jing, the Master took up the position of the Rear Board (*houban*) and led the entire assembly. In the year of Bingchen...

Selected by the Imperial Court, he emerged from seclusion at Xiangfu Temple. In the year of Zhizhi Guihai, he traveled to the capital, where he entered and exited the Golden Gate to discuss the ancient classics;
from the Imperial Preceptor downward, all held him in high esteem and affection. Upon returning south, he presided over Wanshou Temple in Gusu.
Among his writings, the *Fozu Tongzai* (Comprehensive Record of the Buddhas and Patriarchs) in twenty-two fascicles remains in circulation.
Chan Master Shishu Zuying of Xuedou in Mingzhou was the son of the Chen family of Wujiang. He entered the monastic life at the Puxiang Temple during his childhood.
At the age of fifteen, he shaved his head and received full ordination, whereupon he took up his staff to travel and seek instruction. Initially, he followed Xugu Ling at Yangshan;
however, hearing of the spiritual reputation of Huiji at Mount Jing, he went to join him immediately. Upon their first meeting, they attained mutual resonance, and thus...

He remained as the *zhǔjì* (administrative director). Later, he emerged into the world and resided at Longjiao in Mingzhou, then moved to Wanshou in Hangzhou, and finally to Xuedou and Yuwang in Mingzhou.
When asked about his illness by Tiantong Pingshi Di, he offered this verse: "This body is without self, yet the roots of illness run deep;
I am ashamed that Mañjuśrī has come from afar to visit me. There are naturally mountain flowers to discuss non-duality; Facing each other before the green lamp, we laugh and chant."
The Dharmakāya pervades all places; eating rice or eating emptiness, one attains freedom. At Taibai on Mount Mao, amidst the mist and rain, the bamboo shoots coming and going are also elegant.
In his later years, he suffered from a wasting disease of the limbs. He constructed a small shrine called "Wooden Casket" and sat within it daily, no longer engaging in worldly affairs.
In the third month of the Guiwei year of the Zhizheng era of Emperor Yuan Shun, he saw one...
A woman wearing a straw raincoat prostrated herself and requested that the Master take rebirth as a king. The Master said, "I do not wish to be born into the family of a celestial king.
Seventeen days later, he passed away while sitting in the lotus posture. His verse at the time of death read: "For fifty-three years, I have played with cleverness only to end up clumsy.
Treading through the void, I walk barefoot; The myriad phenomena and all living beings laugh without ceasing. His body was cremated according to the prescribed rites.

As instructed, his remains were cremated; when the charcoal was consumed, fragrant wood was added. Though subjected to a hundred refinements, they did not melt away, but instead took on the color of gold and bronze.
When struck, they produced a resonant sound. They were interred to the right of the stupa of the Tripitaka Master Daofa.
Chan Master Zhiguan Zhengkui of Zhongzhu in Hangzhou was the son of the Fang family from Fanyang. He went to study under Huiji Xi at Jingci Monastery.
Xi asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Fanyang. Xi asked, "How deep is the water in the Fanyang Lake?"
The Master said, "Staring with wide-open eyes, one cannot see the bottom. Xī said, "If that is so, then the nostrils of the patch-robed monk will be soaked and rotted away.
The Master said, "I certainly will not breathe out through the nostrils of the Venerable One. Xī said, "In the end, through whose nostrils do you breathe out?"
The Master said, "I respectfully wish the Abbot ten thousand blessings. Xi accepted this and appointed him as attendant (*śaikṣa*).

After more than two years had passed, he went to Tianmu to study under Zhongfeng and again visited Yuansou of Mount Jing, where he was appointed to serve as recorder (*karmadāna*). When Xiaoyin presided over Zhongzhu Monastery, he had the Master share the teaching seat with him.

He subsequently took up residence at Chongyin Monastery in Jinling, where the Imperial Preceptor conferred upon him the title "Buddha-Sun Universal Illumination" (*Furi Puzhao*). He was later transferred to Feng... [text fragment ends].
Shan Zifu ascended to serve the state; he was later transferred to Zhongzhu. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way.
A single thought involving deliberation causes the whole body to enter the weeds. Therefore it is said: 'Before one's eyes there is no dharma;
the meaning lies before one's eyes. It is not a dharma of the present moment; it is beyond the reach of ears and eyes. Throughout the heavens and earth of past and present..."
The sun and moon; the mountains and rivers of past and present; the human relations of past and present—each and every thing is manifest, each and every object is fully revealed.
It is not borrowed from the thousand sages, nor sought through the myriad functions. Internally and externally, there is nothing to take up; throughout past and present, there is no location.
To understand it in such a way is still to mistake the bridge of a donkey’s saddle for one’s father’s chin. Nevertheless, since this is Sizhou...
"Great Sage, for what reason did you appear in Yangzhou? After a long silence, he said, "Investigate! Later, he passed away;
his worldly age was fifty-seven, and his years as a monk were forty-four.

Chan Master Zhongfang Tientun of Foyan in Mingzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Xiangshan. From childhood, he was precocious and extraordinary. He entered the monastic order under Zhuyuan at Tianning Monastery in Guangde.
Zhuyuan said, "Your aspirations are vast and far-reaching; you are capable of upholding the Great Dharma. Do not let me detain you. Thereupon, he went to see Yong of Dongzhou at Huqiu.
While passing through the Sandalwood Forest, he happened to view the *Biographies of Eminent Monks* with a fellow monk.
In the *Lamp Records*, a monk said to the Master, "The seventeen hundred cases are like a mass of raw iron locks;
one simply needs the key to enter one's hands. At these words, the Master nodded his head in silent understanding. He then went to study under Huiji Xi at Jingci Monastery.
As soon as he entered the gate, Xi said, "The lakes and mountains are misty, the lake waters ripple, soaking your nostrils and stuffing them up."
"I am going to destroy your eyes! Why do you not understand? The Master said, "Throughout my entire being there is no shadow or image; at every step, all traces of form are cut off.
Xī said, "That is not it yet; speak further! The Master shook his sleeves and departed. Xī then appointed him to the position of Attendant and later entrusted him with the keys of the storehouse.
The Master found their proliferation tedious and sighed, saying: "The age has declined and the Way has waned; the faculties of men have become frivolous and shallow.

Even masters of long standing and great virtue, possessing vast knowledge and insight, are not yet fully trusted or accepted by students. There is no other reason for this than that their inner and outer selves are not pure.
From then on, he resolved to eliminate all traces of his past. Hearing that the Peach Blossom Gorge in Wuxing was secluded and remote, he went there to bind straw mats and dwell. One day...
While watering the garden, the clouds suddenly darkened over the four mountains; a torrential rain and fierce winds broke the trees and shrubs.
With a single clap of thunder, the doubts and obstructions within his breast were instantly released. He then exclaimed, "How marvelous! How marvelous! Truly marvelous!
One picks up empty space and rides it upside down; a gnat swallows the five Mount Sumerus! He added, "In the past, within my quarters at Nanping, I repeatedly questioned the Old Monk [Zhaozhou]."
He ultimately refused to speak for me. Had he explained it thoroughly at that time, how could there be a "today"?

In the Dingmao year of the Yuan Taiding era, he went forth to preside over Dongquan in Guangde, then moved to Foyan in Mingzhou. While Xiaoyin resided at Longxiang, he invited the Master to share the seat and preach the Dharma.
Tuluhu, the Secretariat Director of the South Terrace, came several times to inquire about the Way; his general discussions with the Master reached a state of perfect accord. He then raised [a koan]:

The Master was at Baoning; a monk came for an audience. The Master said, "What a fine monk you are, traveling on pilgrimage like this. The monk said, "I pluck through the weeds and gaze upon the wind;

how could I be seeking anything else? The Master said, "Have you yet received a blow of the staff? The monk hesitated, and the Master gave a shout. [Another monk] asked, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master's house?
The Master said, "Who cannot see it? [Another monk] asked, "What is it? The Master said, "Who can see it?"
"This is the Samādhi of One Mark. The Master said: "Blue, yellow, red, white. [The monk] asked: "What is the scenery of Fengtai? The Master said: "What scenery is there at Fengtai?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The first and the eleventh; the middle ninth and the lower seventh.
Seven times nine is sixty-three; nine times nine is eighty-one. In the morning one goes to India; in the evening one returns to Tang. From one horse, three are born."

Ascending the Hall: Words do not unfold the matter; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded. Thus it is.

In his later years, the Master built a dwelling to the west of Fengtai, calling it Xianan (New Hermitage). As he was about to pass away, he said to Jingjue Tan, "I wish to trouble you with my final affairs.
What day is it today? Jingjue replied, "The twenty-ninth. The Master said, "The month has ended, but the day has not yet passed."
"It is fitting that I depart. Tomorrow, on the first day of the fifth month, I shall go. When the appointed time arrived, he summoned his disciples to give them final instructions;
raising his hand in farewell, he sat upright and passed away. He was sixty-six years old in age and fifty-one years since his ordination.
Chan Master Hai Zi Qing of Tianyi Monastery in Yuezhou ascended the hall and said: "A three-year-old child embraces a flower-drum;
an eighty-year-old elder rolls a brocade ball. Their coquettish shyness and aged ugliness are fully revealed, causing everyone to laugh without ceasing."
This mountain monk, in the past, while beneath Mount Nanping, picked up a tattered robe from a heap of refuse.
Shaking it out, I presented it to Tianmu, but he did not deign to look upon it. Later, I passed through Chongde and encountered a fierce fellow who tore it apart until it was riddled with holes.
I gathered the fragments back and hid them deeply at Nanping for over forty years, never bringing them forth.
He casually handed it to an outsider. Without cause, today it has come to Tianyi. Upon inspection, its worn appearance and color are just like before;

yet when put on, one dislikes the large sleeves, and when rising to dance, one feels the sky is too vast. It reaches the point where the ten peaks all rise in dance together and the two mountain streams join in roaring rapids.
Everyone watches the stage master Bāolǎo, unaware that they themselves have been made to laugh until they fall over. Thereupon he laughed heartily and took up his staff.
He drew a line with his staff and said, "Take up another holeless flute; casually blowing it forth, one produces ten thousand years of joy.

He then cited the saying of Sansheng, "Whenever he meets someone, he comes out," and the Master said, "These two great elders stole a mere trifle of Linji’s private property and each went about showing it off.
If one were to examine them closely, they should be buried together in a single pit. [The phrase] "Fellow practitioners, when you reach the highest" [is the conclusion].
The Hall. A cool and rustling landscape; companions visit this desolate place. Brewing tea by the mountain stream, burning firewood from the mountain depths.
The Compassionate Patriarch used the property of the Sangha as his own personal gift; Tianyi was not like that—offering to the Buddha, he did not pick up the flower;
extending hospitality, he did not brew tea. Do not resent the lack of formal etiquette; such frugality is the way of monks. The Master enters the world.
Tianyi. At that time, he was already eighty-six years old.
Yuan’an Huì, the head librarian (zàngzhǔ) of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou, was a native of Lín’ān. He studied under Huījī at Jingci and resided in the Móngtáng Hall.
While overseeing the renovation of the Nirvāṇa Hall, he composed a verse which said: “The single path of nirvāṇa has been completely overturned; at every point, one’s practice...”

Chan Master Baozhou Jue'an of Songjiang, a descendant of the Wu clan of Wuxing, entered the monastic order under Dugu Ming.
Fashouju (髮受具) and Meiwu (梅屋) were both disciples who emerged from the gate of the Buddha’s wisdom.

One day, while he was spontaneously expounding the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* for the assembly, when they reached the section on the "Sevenfold Investigation of the Mind," water suddenly surged up from his pure pitcher and poured into the Master’s lap.
The listeners were struck with amazement, but the Master smiled and said, "This was merely a coincidence."
Chan Master Yixi Zhiru of Zhongzhu Monastery in Hangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Jingshan Gao. A native of Min, he encountered Yuan troops descending upon the Jiangnan region in his youth;
he was seized by wandering soldiers and brought to Lin’an, where they abandoned him and departed. He was taken in and raised by the wealthy Hu family, who had him attend to their son’s studies.
The Record states: Master Yu stood by his side, silently observing him without missing anything. When Hu’s son had grown up, he sent him to become a monk at Wuxiang Temple in the village.
There, he studied under Yunfeng at Mount Jing and attained the essential teaching. He first took up residence at Wanshou Temple.

At the beginning of the Tianli era of the Yuan dynasty, Xiaoyin Yin of Zhongzhu was summoned by imperial decree to establish the monastery at Longxiang. Consequently, [Hu’s son] was recommended as one of the three men to succeed him.

The Emperor personally inscribed the Master’s name. The Xuanzheng Yuan submitted a memorial requesting that the Master reside there. There was a woman of the Huang family who deeply revered the Master’s conduct;
she once provided him with *īpūṣa* (vegetarian) offerings. One day, she invited him to her home, where she continued to present offerings with even greater diligence.
He then opened his private treasury and displayed the gold and jade he stored there to the Master. The Master returned in indignation and said to his disciples:
"That Huang family showed me the treasures from their treasury because they wish to entice me to leave home and become their son. For one who has left the household life," [he continued].
One should regard gold and jade as mere rubble and pebbles. Since antiquity, many have fallen into this trap;

it has occurred not only for the sake of their children, but even for the sake of their oxen and horses. Consequently, he severed all ties with the Huang family. Later, when he passed away, his body was cremated, and there were many miraculous manifestations.
Chan Master Gu Zhizhe of Donglin in Jiangzhou was the son of the Chao family of Duchang. Initially residing at Xingsheng Monastery in Xingguo, he later moved to Donglin.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the past have already spoken; the Buddhas of the future shall speak; the Buddhas of the present are speaking now.
But tell me, ultimately what is it they speak? He struck his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall again, he said: "To clarify..."
Coming, he thanks in secret; wisdom arises and delusion perishes. A black ox lies dead in the water; a mangy horse is tethered to a withered post.

How does this compare to the old Black Wang of East Village, who at dusk stretches out his legs to sleep and wakes only when the light of dawn appears? When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, you must take care not to misunderstand. [Ascending the hall:
"When the entire command is taken up as the guiding principle, neither sages nor ordinary beings can fathom it. When the thread of the path is cast wide open, it is universal."
I ask my fellow practitioners: "A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. Ascending the hall, he said: "The Patriarch said:
'Perfectly identical to the great void, neither lacking nor superfluous. Beneath the three rafters, before the seven-foot mat—do not rely on others for interpretation.
Is there anyone who has emerged from beyond the heavens? He then said: "Circumambulate the hall and drink tea. He paid homage to Master Xian.
The verse for the stupa says: "The skull has possessed its own numinous light from the beginning; How could Xuedou ever have shaken out his guts? He cut off the three-inch tongue of the old woman;
To this day, the two swords lean against the heavens. The verse for sending Chan-man Wan to visit Xugong of Mount Jing says:
"Ten thousand tracks and a thousand paths are on one carriage; The eye of one who travels for instruction is correct and never errs. One thousand..."
The Lord of Seven Hundred Disciples was originally the Little Śākyamuni of Mount Yangshan.
Master Guaisi Qichan of Tiantong, Mingzhou, addressed the assembly: "Studying Chan is fundamentally neither difficult nor easy;
it simply requires possessing great roots of faith and a resolute will. Cease all worldly activities, let not even a thousand sages lead you astray, and sit firmly cutting off all conditions."
Maintain a single dharma. Like the great void, it is utterly devoid of trace or mark; like Mount Sumeru, it stands firm and immovable.
Only then can one hope for the unsurpassed True Vehicle. Addressing the assembly: This matter is like a person suffering from hunger or thirst.
Merely speaking of drink or food cannot provide a cure; one must directly drink water oneself and eat rice oneself before there can be any real efficacy.
Addressing the assembly, [the Master] cited the essential words of the ancient worthies of old, spoken out of their deep compassion for others.

He showed that if one can, within this very context, empty the mind and neither cling to the characteristics of phenomena nor depart from them, then upon hearing [the teaching], one attains sudden enlightenment.
This is precisely the moment at the Nirvana Assembly when the broad-faced butcher cast down his blade and became a Buddha on the spot. It is indeed so.
