Shushan said, "Why must you break it? The Master said, "What then of the reflections in the mirror? Shushan said, "Where are the reflections in the mirror? At these words, the Master attained realization.
One day, Shushan asked the Master, "Has your former doubt been resolved? The Master held up his palm.
Shushan said, "Are you not using the formless to inquire about a shadow? The Master said, "Beyond this, there is nothing else that exists. Shushan said, "Try to open your robe."
He examined this. For two years he practiced with increasing diligence and progress.

[The Master] quoted Dongshan’s saying, "I am not that person now," and questioned him, saying, "If you are not that person, then ultimately who are you? The Master attained realization and replied with a verse:
"If you wish to know this person, there is a true message: Formless, it fills all of empty space; With form, it leaves no trace. In the past..."
The Master Fozu once composed the *Qiankunze* (Model of Heaven and Earth): "From a whisk of tortoise hair, a pure breeze arises; from the tip of a staff of hare horns, the bright moon emerges.
He wrote: "My son, do not merely repeat the words of others; you must further enter the gate of awakening. The Master said: "I do not even borrow from conditions."
"By what gate do you enter? the Official asked. The Master said, "Since I do not rely on conditions, why have I come here?
The Official said, "Regarding the phrase 'not relying on conditions,' what is its meaning? The Master said, "A colorful phoenix soars with body at ease;
an iron ox gallops and bellows with mind ever at leisure. The Official said, "Excellent! The next day, the Master took his leave.
He wrote a verse of entrustment, saying: "You shall certainly become a Lord of Men and Gods; you must contemplate the autumn at Shaoshi. The Master asked, "Who is Changrun?
How would I dare to presume upon such a position? [Zhaozhou] wrote a note of instruction, saying: "The Way has long been in decline; how can you fold your hands and do nothing?"
The Master replied, "Yes, yes. When the letter announcing his passing arrived, everyone deliberated that none but the Master could occupy the seat of the patriarch.

Although the Master declined out of humility, refusing the request twice, the assembly then presented him with the letter containing the verse of entrustment. The Master suddenly shed tears and said no more.

In the autumn of the *jiashu* year of the Wanli era of Emperor Ming Shenzong, he took charge of Shaoshi. The Master’s physical presence was robust and imposing, and his voice resonated like a great bell.

He shared in the simple frugality of his fellow students, yet his character was profound and expansive. He single-mindedly bore the burden of the Great Dharma, remaining diligent morning and night without the slightest hint of weariness.
Those who entered his room to receive the incense were two hundred and seventy people.
On the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month in the year of Yiyou, he wrote a verse and announced his passing.
Chan Master Changzhong Yunkong of Lingshan in Jianchang Prefecture once asked Shouchang about the essentials of the Dharma.
The Master said, "If you can be diligent and refuse to deceive yourself, that is the practice from beginning to end.

One day, hearing his brothers discussing the meaning of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* with great eloquence, the Master laughed and said, "If the eye of the school is not clear, it cannot be considered ultimate. Shouchang heard this.
He was utterly bewildered and lost, so he asked, "What is the Eye of the School? The Master shook out his robe and rose.
Later, Chang requested further instruction, to which the Master replied, "I truly do not know; you must look for it yourself. Later, while at Dayao Shan, Chang attained awakening.

He entered the abbot’s quarters to communicate what he had realized, whereupon the Master said, "Your awakening is indeed not without merit, but you must ensure that you have a practical mastery of its application."
Not so; I fear this is merely the "eternal silver" Chan.
*Wudeng Quanshu*, fascicle 611; *Wudeng Quanshu*, fascicle 612.
Compiled by the Abbot of Seigan Zen-ji Temple in Kyoto, the Monk (臣) Chōei;
reviewed by the Abbot of Kokaigan-ji Temple in Kyoto, the Monk (臣) Chōkei; presented for imperial inspection.
Dharma Heir of Chan Master Shaoshi Run of the 34th Generation under Qingyuan in the Cao Dong School.
Chan Master Cizhou Fangnian of Beijing Dajue Temple was the son of the Yang family from Tang County.

At the age of ten, he entered the monastic order under Master Yiji of Guangde Daci Temple in Jintai, where he shaved his head and received full ordination. Hearing Master Gudao lecture on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, when he reached the section on the "Investigation of the Mind in Seven Locations," he began to perceive that conditioned arising is not substantial.
He subsequently traveled through various lecture halls, thoroughly investigating the principles of both Nature (Xing) and Characteristics (Xiang), yet realizing they were not the ultimate truth.
Yao then went to Shaoshi Mountain to attend upon Huanchou Run. Upon seeing him, Run immediately asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from the north.
Run asked, "How does the Dharma in the north compare to that here? The Master said, "The waters branch into a thousand streams, yet they flow from a single source.
Seeing that his speech was elegant and profound, Run appointed him as the *weina* (administrator). One day, while the Master was visiting the First Patriarch’s wall-gazing cave, Run said:
While at the monastery, he suddenly attained realization and said, "Before the Five Milk Peaks, what a marvelous message! Large and small stones, each one firmly planted on the ground.

He went to the room to present this to Master Run, who instructed him, saying, "From the Buddhas and Patriarchs of antiquity down to the present, they have transmitted their own realizations to one another, desiring that all sentient beings know they exist. I have received this from Xiaoshan."

The Master said: "I have waited for more than ten years as if for an old friend. Now I transmit it to you. You should take the mind of the Buddhas and Patriarchs as your own mind to continue the life of wisdom.
Nevertheless, though this is so, you should remain hidden in forests and springs, emerging only when the time is right.

He then bestowed upon him a verse, saying: "The unsurpassed mind of Nirvāṇa, Transmitted and entrusted by the Buddhas and Patriarchs, Is now the moment of my transmission; Clouds clear atop the peak."
With his head bared, at the age of twenty-eight, he entered seclusion behind closed doors on Mount Wutai. During the day he ate but one meal; at night he sat alone.
Later, while traveling to the East Terrace to pay his respects, his two eyes suddenly went blind. The Master said, "This illusory body does not truly exist; from where could illness come?
After practicing meditative concentration for seven days, both eyes were restored to sight. He traveled south to visit Putuo Shan and returned; subsequently, he went to Dashan in Yue.
At a temple, the assembly requested him to preach the Dharma. Zhanran Cheng went to pay his respects, and the Master asked:

"When the wind stops and the path leads toward the green mountains, and the city of the King of Yue lies by the distant blue sea—what then? Cheng replied: "The moon pierces through the blue sea; the Persian does not raise an eyebrow."
The Master asked Chengdong about the essential meaning of the school’s fundamental principle. Chengdong spoke a verse, saying: "The five ranks of ruler and subject must be known intimately;
within them, why wait for deliberation? The stone woman is skilled at playing without needle or thread; the wooden puppet can raise the mechanism beyond transformation.
Red dust billows and swirls from the bottom of the well; white waves surge and fly over the mountain peak. Birth itself is originally effortless."

"Unawares, you have naturally attained the imperial capital. The Master said, "Your words and phrases are dense and subtle; they do not fall into the extremes of beginning or end. You are truly a scion of this house.
He then summoned him into the room and certified him with the seal of the brown rush meditation cushion.

He further said, "In the future, when you open your two lips, you shall have the capacity to cut off the tongues of all people under heaven. He then bestowed upon him a verse, which began: "The single source of Cao..."
A drop of water. The Buddhas and Patriarchs transmitted it to one another; even now, at the time of its transmission, the great earth becomes nectar.

*Tu!* At the peak of Wuyufeng, a single arrow struck down half a child from the South. In the *Renchen* year of the Wanli era of the Ming Shenzong Emperor, the monastics and laypeople of Jiaxing invited him to preside over Dongta.
Subsequently, he accepted invitations to Yunju and Mount Lu. In the autumn of the *Jiamu* year, [he went to] Wutai.
Qingliang again requested that his teacher expound the Dharma. Both the monastic and lay communities earnestly entreated him to remain. Later, he manifested parinirvāṇa.
His disciple Cheng escorted the remains and enshrined them in a stupa on the southern mountain of Xiansheng.
Chan Master Wuyan Zhengdao of Shaoshi on Mount Song was the son of the Hu family of Yuzhang. He went to Shanglan Temple to undergo tonsure and ordination.
At the age of fifteen, he met the elder Zhihou, who pointed out the essentials of Chan to him; he subsequently followed Zhihou to travel about.

While resting at Jingping Cliff on Mount Nanyue, he questioned and consulted [his teacher] morning and evening. Zhihou said, "If you wish to investigate and clarify this matter, you must thread through the entanglements of the teachings and the scriptures."
It was only after some time that [Zhaozhou] began to recognize him. He pointed to Cansun’an and Angan and said to Xiu, “Wuyan is truly worthy of being called a vessel of the Dharma.
You must not allow him to harbor even a fragmentary understanding within his breast; instead, have him travel north to seek realization for himself through his own inquiry.

Xiu then brought up the verse by Zhang Zhuo to test his level of practice. The Master said, “Since even *tathatā* (Suchness) cannot be established, how could there be a verse? Xiu [was thus satisfied].

Seeing his keen intelligence, [Zhaozhou] pointed him toward Shaoshi Mountain to study under Huanchu and Zhiren. One day, as Zhiren was ascending the hall, the Master asked, "What is the家风 (family style) of the Dongshan school?
Zhiren replied, "Three flowering trees beneath the moon; twin cassia branches before the peak. The Master said:
"Does the Master have anything else? Yunruen said, "There is only this one reality; there is neither two nor three.

At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and immediately presented a verse: Clouds gather at the summit; the moon locks the secluded cliffs. The stone man claps his hands; the wooden woman smiles.
Yunruen sealed this with a verse: "The wordless meaning is not separate from words; The original song and the original transmission are wondrous."
The transmission was severed. Today, it is transmitted as a single lineage through direct seal and entrustment. In years to come, the "Double Osmanthus" shall benefit humans and devas.
In the *Gengyin* year of the Wanli era of Emperor Shenzong of the Ming dynasty, he presided over Shaoshi. At that time, Prince Zhou invited the Master to expound the Dharma of "Preserving Longevity.

The Prince attained great awakening. When Prince Chong heard of this, he also invited the Master to preach the Dharma. At that time, the Prince’s heir-apparent suffered from a foot ailment and had to lean on a staff.
As he stood there, the Master led him around in seven circumambulations. Sweat flowed like a torrent, and his feet were immediately healed.

A monk asked, "The World-Honored One remained silent for a long time when neither 'having words' nor 'being wordless' was questioned. What was the meaning of this? The Master said, "To move one's countenance is to reveal the ancient path;
do not fall into the trap of the silent mechanism. He asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma of the new year? The Master—
Brandishing his whisk, he asked, "Do you understand? [The monk] said, "I do not. The Master said, "Next year there will be new branches;
there is no need for further detailed explanation. An old practitioner asked, "What is 'wordlessness'? The Master said, "The four seasons proceed according to their course."
Another monk asked, "What is 'wordlessness'? The Master replied, "All things arise therein. The Master’s intellectual acuity was swift and sharp, and his character was humble and sincere.
Later, he passed away and was interred in a stupa at Zu-long.

Chan Master Shouchang Wuming Huijing of Jianchang Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Linshan Zhong. He was born into the Pei family of Chongren in Fuzhou. From birth, he was exceptionally gifted;
he lived with a serene detachment, having no worldly attachments or preferences. At the age of nine, when he entered a local school, he immediately asked: "What is this 'vast and unyielding qi'?"

"What is this? the tutor wondered, for he marveled at him. When [Dongshan] grew up, he recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* as if recovering a long-lost possession. He subsequently went to rely upon Linji Yixuan (Lingshan Zhong).
He once harbored doubts regarding the "four-line verse. One day, while reading the verses of Master Fu Dashi, he read: "If one speaks of the four-line verse, it should not be separate from the body.
Suddenly, his mind was liberated. At that time, he was twenty-four years old. Later, he happened to be reading the *Tripitaka*.
Upon consulting the *Zongyan pin* (Chapter on the Eye of the School), he finally came to understand the principle of the "special transmission outside the teachings.
He then took his leave of Ling Shan and built a thatched hut at the summit of Mount E. He made a vow to himself: "I shall not descend from this mountain until I have realized the Great Matter.

Suddenly, while examining the *Chuan deng lu*, he saw a monk ask Xingshan, "What is the Way? to which Xingshan replied, "A most magnificent mountain. At this, his state of doubt was suddenly resolved.
He set out with such intensity that he forgot both sleep and food. While moving a stone, it was so firmly rooted that it could not be lifted;

as he pushed with all his might, he attained a sudden and great enlightenment. He immediately composed a verse, saying: "If one wishes to study the path of unsurpassed Bodhi, One must quickly clear away this great mountain.

Only upon knowing the Way does one realize the mountain is no longer there; Turning the body around, one leaps out of the Patriarch’s Barrier. He presented this to Zhong, who certified him as a vessel of the Dharma.
It was only at this time that he first shaved his head and received full ordination. He had remained within the mountains for another twenty-four years.

In the *jiawu* year of the Wanli era of Emperor Ming Shenzong, he moved to reside at Baofang in the local district. A Zen practitioner asked him, "Whom have you studied under before coming to dwell on this mountain?
The Master replied, "I have never yet traveled abroad. The practitioner said, "How can one limit oneself to a single corner and thus diminish the vastness of the world?"

The Master approved of his words and subsequently traveled to Hangzhou to visit Yunqi. He then journeyed north again to pay respects to the elder masters Wuyan and Daguan, and ascended Mount Wutai to study under Rui Feng.
Rui Feng’s teaching style was austere and formidable; upon meeting him once, the Master attained a profound resonance with his realization.

He then requested instruction on the karmic encounters (*jigen*) of ancient worthies and presented several verses of his own. Rui Feng deeply affirmed his understanding. The Master then returned to Suichang and took up residence there.
He attained the status of a Chief Seat (Śrāmaṇera) without peer; the relationship between teacher and disciple was harmonious and refined. He extensively propagated the school of Dongshan.

The Prince of Yifan, admiring the Master’s virtue and character, once sighed, saying: "The time since the Sage has passed away is remote; fortunately, this old man remains. Ascending the hall, he said:
"An old man with blind eyes and a deaf wife—both sight and sound are lost, yet it is perfectly so. Furthermore, there is a handless man who performs a fist-punch, and a tongueless man who speaks."
The Way. Four people discuss long and short; one person laughs heartily right there in the midst of it. But tell me, what is he laughing at? How extraordinary!
Puhua performs a somersault, truly not failing the legacy of the Golden-Colored Dhūta. [He] ascended the hall for the formal discourse.
Seize upon one move, and Buddhas and Patriarchs are caught all at once. Let go of one move, and sages and worthies are all bound.
The revolving wheel flies up to the celestial court; the clay ox sleeps across the earth’s corners. Not only do the nine realms receive grace, but the four modes of birth also enjoy bliss.
Only the Eight Great Vajrapāṇis glare with eyes wide and brows knit, holding their staffs askew and upside down. Why? Because it is not permitted.
Sentient beings scribble and sketch in confusion. Entering the hall: The green mountains are green; there is no mountain that does not harbor clouds. The green waters are green;

there is no water that does not give rise to trees. Only the mind of the patch-robed monk is straight as a line, without any crookedness. (He strikes the sounding block once. Descending from the seat, he enters the hall:
A true son of the dragons and elephants sometimes cannot lift up what he has let go, and sometimes cannot let go of what he has lifted up.
"Lower it and lift it up; do not play with the snake's head, but seek to grasp the living tiger's tail.
Sometimes one leaps upon the back of the golden-haired lion, and naturally a cool breeze rises beneath one’s feet. Is this so? Heh! When the waters do not dry up, the fish are at ease;
when the mountains are green, the birds are tranquil. Be careful! Thus he ascended the hall. "The winter solstice has arrived; how extraordinary the occasion! The sea wind blows..."
The coral branches were overturned; the Dragon King was startled awake and returned to the realm of space. The River God and the deities lost their majesty.
"Such matters as these you should know for yourself," [the monk] said. The Master asked, "What is the use of knowing? The monk said, "It is better not to know. The Master asked, "Why?
The monk replied, "A monk does not act for the sake of leisure; instead, he becomes even more like one who suffers. The Master said, "So it is."
He struck [the assembly] and ascended the hall. It has long been said that "ignorance is truly not ignorance. Relying on this staff, he tests who is distant and who is intimate.
When Buddhas and Patriarchs come crashing in, he simply strikes them. Look at which one among them can turn over.
You must ensure that where you hide your body there are no traces, and where there are no traces, do not hide your body—only then will it be so. What is "hiding the body where there are no traces"?
"Do you understand? Shide clapped his hands and laughed heartily. "Hanshan has forgotten the path he came by. "Take care! [End of] the formal discourse.
"Tonight is the third; tomorrow is the eleventh. If you ask about the Buddha-dharma (Tathāgata-citta), everything is already concluded.
How do you understand the Patriarchal-dharma (Ācārya-citta)? "Nine in the middle, seven at the end. [End of] the formal discourse. The Master snapped his fingers once and said: "Great!"

"How do you all understand this? The assembly was silent. The Master said: "One who does not understand the Teacher Who Transcends the World has merely exerted himself in vain with a single snap of the fingers.
This most unambiguous phrase is truly difficult to grasp. A long sword leaning against the sky strikes terror into men;
were it not for the right person, one would only stand by and listen. Only then will you know that the single mani pearl can only be used by a Hanshanzi. (End)
The Hall. The myriad peaks compete in their upward thrust, needlessly vexing Mount Sumeru; the ten thousand streams vie to flow toward it, fruitlessly doubting the vastness of the ocean.

Thus, its Great Sameness is beyond compare, and its true nature transcends all directions. It is like a scaled dragon leaping alone through the Dragon Gate, spared the trouble of having its forehead branded;

or like a fine steed bursting through its reins and bit, rendering the whip’s flickering useless. With a thousand feet of line trailing behind, it does not look back; the finest bait fills the platter.
Without attachment, one is as deep and vast as the ocean, sovereign and free; on islands in the sea, one wanders at ease.
You must know that whether it be "thus" or "not thus," neither can be expressed in a single word. This requires a person of true caliber. Do you understand? Tao Qian refused to let his cup go;
today, those of the Lotus School merely hang their names in vain. Ascending the hall, he said: "‘This very mind is Buddha’—how many can accept this? ‘Neither mind nor Buddha’—murmuring."
[Those who say] "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing" are many. Even clear-eyed monks are often dazed by this.
Although Daiman said, "I take 'mind is Buddha' as it is," that too is like a viper clinging to its den. How can one begin to avoid dragging through the mud?
*Pfft!* He added, "Just so," and then descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "If this matter is raised..."
Dust rises without wind; it is like letting go. It is still like clouds obscuring the sun. Even if one neither raises nor lets go, one remains in a state of dull indifference (*páng-hàn*).
To eliminate everything is not yet the realm of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Ultimately, what is the realm of the Buddhas and Patriarchs?
"When the mountain wind arises, heaven and earth shake; when the kalpa-fire burns, the world is empty. [Ascending the hall, he] "pulled out the sinews" [of the assembly].
The skin does not move; changing the bones, no blood is seen. Tendons and bones are all at once empty; one wanders about without falling.
Master Bodhidharma understood extinction but did not understand birth; Old Śākyamuni understood birth but did not understand extinction.
To know that birth and extinction do not interfere with one another—apart from this year’s dried dung-stick, there is nothing else. Small Assembly Sermon: Buddha-dharma is not dharma; it is precious.

Regarding awakening and reaching: the Way of the Patriarchs is not a "way" [in the conventional sense]; one must personally arrive there. To awaken is to resolve the right and wrong of the holy and the mundane;

to arrive is to sever the karmic retribution of humans and devas. Whether one awakens or not, the realization that "all phenomena are unborn" will surely manifest of itself in a single thought-moment.

Once it has manifested, a thousand lamps share a single light; there is no need to further deliberate upon arising and ceasing. Whether one arrives or not, a single thought-moment of pure truth is what constitutes true reality.

It is created. When the conditions for its creation have reached maturity, it will certainly fall down from the void. What need is there to discuss Buddhas and Patriarchs? What need is there to talk of the Way of the Dharma?
Throughout the ten directions of the dharma-realm, all traces of movement are cut off; where can one seek mirages or flowers in the sky? (Small Lecture)
Last night, thunder crashed and lightning flashed; the void was shattered and my skull split open. Unable to bear it, I pleaded with Vairocana, yet he could not render a fair judgment.
"Great assembly, is there anyone who knows? Speak up for him to clear his name! A monk said, "It all depends on the Master. The Master said, "I shall give him a slap.
The evening retreat for the New Year: It is now the thirtieth night; you should know the point where all things converge.
Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. Nine times nine is eighty-one; five times five is twenty-five. The four-seven schools of the Western Heaven;
the two-three patriarchs of this Eastern Land. A sweet melon is sweet from stem to end; a bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. Zhaozhou and Huangbo.
"Not falling into any number. On the eve of the New Year in the year of Ding-si, the Master ascended the hall and said:

"This year, there is only this moment remaining. Let me ask you all: do you know it or not? He spoke again: "This is the final instruction of this old monk. Great assembly, you must cherish it with utmost care.
On the thirteenth day of the new year, he manifested a slight illness and subsequently ceased eating, saying: "The old man..."

"Monks, I am not ill; I must certainly depart. On the sixteenth day, he composed a verse on the kindling of the funeral pyre. The following morning, he gathered the assembly, took up his brush, and wrote in large characters:
"Today, I clearly point the way. He then cast down his brush, sat upright, and passed away. Upon cremation, the flames were of five colors.
His cranial bone and teeth remained uncorrupted. A stupa was erected in the abbot’s quarters of his original temple. His secular age was seventy-one;
his monastic seniority was forty-four.
He belonged to the thirty-fifth generation under Qingyuan.

Chan Master Zhànrán Yuánchéng of Yúnmén Xiǎnshèng Monastery in Shàoxīng Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Dàjué Niàn. He was the son of the Xià family of Huìkě. His mother conceived him after dreaming of a monk.
When he grew up, he had large eyes and a prominent nose; his lips were thick and his teeth bared. He was straightforward in character and candid in speech. After his parents passed away...
He was extremely impoverished and served as a postal guard. Once, having mistakenly delivered official documents, he was arrested; fearing disgrace, he fled to hide at Mount Yinfeng.

There, Yinfeng instructed him to contemplate "Who is it that recites the Buddha’s name? After three days and nights, he attained realization. At that time, he was twenty years old. He immediately went to Miaofeng on Mount Tianhuang to shave his head.
Coincidentally, upon hearing monks discussing the *Dharma-body Gāthā* of the Great Master Fu (Bodhisattva Fotuo), he was able to memorize and retain the scriptures.
Having mastered all principles and meanings, he went to Yunqi to receive full ordination. Upon his return, he immediately closed himself in retreat at Baolin.
Recalling the dialogue between Qianfeng regarding "raising one, one cannot raise two," he attained a great awakening. His verse reads: "Raising one, raising two—these are but external signs;
Within this very place, there is fundamentally neither right nor wrong. The tune of the Snow Song is high and sublime, yet few understand it; I grant my approval only to Shaoyang’s harmony."
They attained equality. How could those two elders have ever moved their tongues? Everywhere else, people vainly knit their brows. To deliberate upon this is like a hawk flying beyond Silla;
it is like marking the boat to seek a lost sword—one is fundamentally deluded. [The Master] went to Yunqi Hong. Hong brought up the story of High Peak’s “mud ox at the bottom of the sea.
The Master pushed out a monk standing nearby and said, “The assembly shall bear witness. Hong nodded his head in approval. Later, when a monk returned from a cremation, Hong asked about the deceased.
After the Master [Seng] had passed away, [Hongxiu] asked, "Where has he gone? The Master came forth and said, "Thank you, Venerable, for your concern.
Hongxiu departed. Cizhou Nian came from Beijing and preached the Dharma at Dasha. He sought to have his realization verified by the Master, presenting a verse for mutual confirmation.
The Master granted him a single mat made of *zong* and *pu* grass, whereupon they established the formal relationship of teacher and disciple. (Taishi Tao...)
The Master of the Stone Coffer at the Imperial Academy, Zhang Jun Xunyuan, requested the restoration of Xiansheng Monastery.

Having served as its abbot for thirty years, he took it upon himself to propagate the Way. In the *jiayin* year of the Wanli era of Emperor Ming Shenzong, he presided over Guangxiao; in *yimao*, he presided over Jingshan; and in *bingchen*, he presided over Dongta.
Ascending the hall, he gathered the assembly. After a long silence, he said: "From the beginning, it has never been thus; only now does it begin."
"So it is. The World-Honored One has already exposed this for you; do not attempt to further soil the fields of the heart of you brothers with urine and excrement.
For this reason, there is no need for the Rector to strike the gavel. "The weather is hot; take care. Descending from the seat, he ascends the hall and says:
"The old case of Yunmen—this mountain monk shall judge it anew. If you wish to know the 'one thousand coins,' there are two [of them]."
Five hundred strings of cash. Nevertheless, although the public case is already manifest, you must not leave it cast aside in the armor of "nothingness.

You must know that within a single phrase the three origins are contained; within a single origin the three essentials are contained. There are origins and there are essentials; there is the provisional and there is the real.
Only when there is both illumination and function can one begin to avoid failing one’s own school. If it were not so, everyone would be nothing but a corpse fallen into the abyss.
Do you understand? If you still do not understand, I, this mountain monk, have a phrase regarding the Three Principles and Three Essentials;
I shall bestow it upon the assembly. After a long silence, he said: "Xuefeng Xie Sanlang was originally a fisherman. [He] ascended the hall. As soon as the Master...
As he sat, he suddenly heard the crowing of a cock and said, "Aha! Venerable Golden Cock, you have already turned the Wheel of the Fundamental Dharma of the First Noble Truth for you all.
What further news do you seek? If you still do not understand, I shall raise it again.
He struck his whisk once and said, "This is sound; all who have ears can hear it—surely you are not deaf men!"
Holding up his whisk, he said: "This is form; those with eyes can all see it—it is certainly not for the blind. There is not even a hair’s breadth of deception here. Has it not been said:
'Calling for Little Yu repeatedly was originally no business at all; it was simply that the husband wished to recognize the voice'? Ascending the hall, he said:
"This old fellow does not even know how to read the basic characters, yet he forces himself to step forward and preach the Dharma. He has misread Zeng Shen as *shang*."
"Ruthenian Ginseng. The entire assembly in the hall burst into laughter. There is a marvel within this laugh.
If you can awaken to its underlying meaning and pierce through that very first orifice, [you will understand]. "Assembly, what is this one orifice? After a long silence, he said:
His movements express the ancient path; he does not fall into the trap of silent stillness. Entering the hall, the old monk has no ability;
yet his actions are naturally free. His teeth are missing, so he cannot whistle; his mind is straightforward and his speech is swift. Last night, he knocked over Mount Sumeru.
It has reached the point where half a block of the precious throne of the Honored One Śakra-devendra has been removed. Tell me, O assembly:
when I, this mountain monk, proclaim it in such a manner, what principle does this represent? After a long silence, he said: "It is much like a person from the Three Rivers singing a song.
Ascending the hall to preach the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*: When I hold fast, even gold loses its luster; when I let go, even rubble gives off light. Śākya-muni.
Kālacitta, you have been exposed by all of you for no reason. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys a sesame cake with money;
when he lets go of his hand, it turns out to be a steamed bun. You brothers, if you do not understand this, I shall bow three times to you.
If you do understand, I have thirty blows for you; take them outside and strike yourself. Why is this so?
This is precisely to ensure that rewards and punishments are clearly meted out, to decide victory and defeat within the field of dragons and snakes.

Entering the Hall: "The spring breeze has arrived; cast off your cold-clad robes. The mountain birds warble melodiously in the upper groves. What a fine messenger of universal penetration! Yet alas, people of this age do not know how to listen.
Entering the Hall: "Killing and giving life, letting go and seizing; holding fast and releasing—this is the majestic wind of the high bank."
The banks [of the river] have an order that must be carried out; his presence is majestic and grand, possessing a formidable authority that none may transgress.

At times he reviles the Buddhas and scolds the Patriarchs, fearing not even the thunderbolts of heaven; at other times he calculates causes and deliberates upon effects, yet he stands in awe of the Great King Yama.
Now tell me: which is the one of great courage, and which is the one of cautious mind? Is there anyone who can definitively judge this? If there is not, I, this old monk, shall decide.
It is time to depart. Wearing horns and shrouded in fur, he upholds the True Command. His entire body is covered in mud and water—who knows him?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The western wind is fiercely violent; all phenomena are withered and desolate. Branches and leaves have fallen away completely, revealing that one crucial point."
The assembly, tell me: which one is that single point? After a long silence, he said: "Where did the fire come from last night? It burned out the ancient tomb. Ascending the hall, he said:
"There is that which is attained within non-existence; there is that which is sought within existence. If you wish to understand the meaning therein, it is 'Six Non-inclusions' of Shaoyang.
Ascending the hall, [he noted]: "The heavy rain has fallen continuously these past days; among those on the road, there are none who do not huddle together."

Meyi: This old monk has no other words to add. Being cold, he wishes to put on more clothes. Great assembly, if you wish to understand the fundamental point, you must clarify the highest-grade capacity (*uttama-yāna*).
A monk asked, "What is 'acting among those of different species'? The Master said, "Strike me lightly! Strike me lightly!
The monk said, "I understand! I understand! The Master said, "How do you understand it? The monk acted like a donkey.
[The Master] said, "Ming! Go rest. A monk asked, "Regarding Nanquan’s 'beheading of the cat,' what was his underlying meaning? The Master said, "Do not slander Zhaozhou.
The monk asked, "What constitutes slandering him? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! A monk asked, "Are the Zen of the Patriarchs and the Zen of the Tathāgata the same or different?
The Master said, "Guangzhou is Hangzhou. The monk said, "If that is so, then they are the same. The Master said, "The Long River..."
Distinguishing between self and other, one asks about the joy of the path; yet in the end, this is not arriving home. "What is the joy of the path? The Master said:
"Opening the mouth forms a pair of pegs; raising the eyebrows falls into two or three. "What is the matter of arriving home? The Master said:
"If you want the head, cut it off and take it. There was a blind man who requested instruction. The Master pulled at his finger and said: "This..."
"This is a chair. This is a table. The blind man immediately prostrated to the Master and said, "The members of this entire hall are not equal to this blind man.
The Master asked, "Before your parents were born, please let the Master say one word for you. The Master said, "It cannot be relied upon entirely;
old monk, ask me what the 'Bright Pearl that Anchors the Sea' is. The Master said, "Yesterday it was taken away by someone. [The blind man] said, "..."
"How is it that the dark moon appears immediately and the white moon disappears immediately? The Master said, "You have recognized only half.
Later, the Master stayed at Jiaxi Temple in Beijing. One day, he was together with Master Da, Dharma Master Yuechuan, and Tao Shikuī.
The two Grand Historians, Huang Shunxuan and [his brother], were enjoying the moon when Shunxuan lay down. [The Master] asked about the karmic conditions regarding Mazu’s “Enjoying the Moon” story.
The Master said, "You lie down while I stand; I cannot preach the Dharma for you. Shunxuan immediately rose and apologized.
Yuechuan said, "The Grand Historian has missed his chance. Da dashi said, "My way of phrasing it does not equal that of this old man. The Master [concurred].
Upon passing through Hangzhou, he heard that several of his spiritual friends, such as Gu Huiwen and others, along with various Dharma protectors, had each sent a letter of invitation to welcome him.
Huiwen’s letter stated: "Today the great assembly wishes to meet the Master as a peer of equal standing. If the Master will come..."

"Having already fallen into the realm of emotional consciousness, the Preceptor did not come; he still lacks compassion. After the Master finished reading it, he tore up the letter and said, "You hired hand!
You have come before this old monk to meet your defeat. As soon as the Master arrived, he ascended the hall and stood facing south.
Huìwén said, "Preceptor, do not try to wield an axe at a gate you do not know. The Master then gave him a slap and said, "Quickly!"
"Quick! Quick! [The Master] called out. Wen’s face turned red and he remained speechless. The Master said, "Dead man!

Later, while the Master was sitting around a brazier with Wunian, You-si Cheng, and Tao Shi-kui, Tao said, "Master Wunian is here; I beg you to cite for us the phrase by which you attained realization.
The Master said, "Facing the fire, my back is still cold. Su Yunpu, the Provincial Commissioner, asked, "When a pair of mandarin ducks is embroidered out..."
"Looking at it from your perspective, you do not take the golden needle and pass it on to others. "What is this golden needle?

The Master said, "This mountain monk traveled once through the capital, yet I did not encounter a single person [who understood it]. Su was about to offer a word when the Master said, "The ancient Buddhas have long since passed away.
Later, the Master visited Wunian Youwen. Youwen asked, "An ancient said: 'It is like a flake of snow flying onto a red-hot furnace.'"
"Similar. Now tell me, did the ancients possess the eye that penetrates the barrier or not? One replied, "I do not see what 'ancient' there is.
The Master suddenly pointed behind him and said, "What about the one behind you? Upon this, the man simply ceased. Throughout his life, the Master was free from artifice;

whether meeting the noble or the lowly, he maintained a single, authentic style. During his five periods of presiding over monastic seats, he provided benefit and salvation for all sentient beings without exception.
He did not engage in worldly affairs. In the twelfth month of the Bingyin year of the Tianqi era of Emperor Ming Xizong, Yu Xian sheng delivered his words of entrustment.
On the fourth day, he ascended the hall at Tianhua; his disciple Bai went to Jiuhua. The Master said, "You go; I, this old monk, shall set out this very moment.
He then spoke earnestly and repeatedly to the assembly until midnight, when he passed away lying on his right side. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at...
Xian Sheng of Nanshan lived to the age of sixty-six and had been a monk for forty-six years.

He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Xiaoxi Huixi of Shaoshi on Mount Song, who was himself a successor of Chan Master Dao of Shaoshi. He was the son of the Liu family from Mancheng in Baoding; he entered the monastic order at...
Pujie requested further instruction from Panshan sixteen times, investigating the methods of cultivation with such resolve that he never grew weary, even to the point of forgetting sleep and food.
One day, while reading the *Transmission of the Lamp*, he reached the passage where a monk asked Xuansha, "What is the seamless stupa? Xuansha replied, "This very seam—how large or small is it?

At this, Puji attained sudden enlightenment. He went to see Wuyan, and after a long time, he achieved thorough realization. Wuyan entrusted him with a verse, saying: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
The Esoteric Dharma cannot be transmitted. If it is to be transmitted, how can it be transmitted? There is no place for transmission or entrustment;
clarity and darkness are wondrously identical in practice. Later, without a word, he passed away. The Master succeeded him as the abbot. A monk asked, "What is the Lord?
The Master said, "A son of a thousand pieces of gold does not sit precariously on the eaves. The monk asked, "What is the Minister? The Master said, "When a man leaves his country, he travels far."
Sishi asked, "What is the convergence of the Way between sovereign and subject? The Master replied, "The Son of Heaven’s edict descends within the realm;
the General outside the passes returns with reports of victory. In the winter of the Jimao year of the Chongzhen era, he manifested a slight illness.

As the assembly gathered around to inquire after his health, the Master counted on his fingers and said, "I shall recover on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. When that date arrived, he took a bath, sat upright, and passed away at the age of seventy.
Sixth: His disciples erected a stupa for him to the west of the temple.
Chan Master Wuyi Yuanlai of Boshan in Guangxin Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Jing of Shouchang. He was a son of the Sha family of Shucheng; at birth, he was clothed in white.
He wrapped his robes with great care and strictly abstained from meat and wine. At the age of sixteen, he traveled to Jinling to listen to lectures; thereupon, he ceased his study of literary texts.
He went to Mount Wutai to follow Master Jing’an Tong, shaving his hair and renouncing worldly taints. He practiced the contemplation of emptiness for five years until he realized his errors.

He then went to Mount E to consult Master Shouchang Jing, but they did not reach accord. He entered Min Province to visit Baiyun Peak, where he contemplated the koan of "the body hidden so that no trace remains. One day, while reading...
Zhaozhou had a lingering doubt regarding the karmic cause and condition concerning "not abiding where there is a Buddha. He went again to visit Juejing at Baofang. Jing asked:
"Ants know how to seek out the place of carrion; flies tend to fly toward the side of stench.

Is this a matter for the ruler, or a matter for the minister? The Master said: "A matter for the minister. Jing rebuked him, saying: "There are many who would laugh at you! The Master said: "As for what I said before..."
"The treatises are all correct. Why, then, is it not so here? The Sūtra says: "This one is not; all those others are not. The Master then became indignant.
Upon seeing the statue of the monastery guardian fallen to the ground, he attained realization. He lived separately in the Zongcheng Hall for two years.
One day, while using the toilet, he saw a man climbing a tree and was suddenly and completely enlightened. He hurried to see the Sūtra. The Sūtra says: "Po..."
"What kind of eyes do you possess? he asked, and then he burned down the hut. The Master said, "The gold is made even more brilliant. He then raised the kōan of Xuánzé:
"The dragon roars and mist rises; the tiger sighs and wind arises. The Master stood and presented this verse: "Killing and giving life, each vies for mastery—each has its own marvel.
How could the dim-sighted, common eye perceive it? Though it emits light, it does not follow the whims of the age. As before, it is spring."

Fengzhu followed the horse's hooves and approved of this at the outset. In the *Ren-yin* year of the Wanli era of Emperor Ming Shenzong, when the Master was twenty-eight years old, he went forth to reside at Boshan.
Subsequently, he presided over Dongyan, Dayang, and Gushan in Min. This was during the *Ji-si* year of the Chongzhen era of Emperor Yizong.
Ascending the hall at Tianjie Monastery in Jinling, he said: "When the torrents pour down and the mountains topple, the entire great earth is encompassed;
when soil is tossed and dust is raised, not even a speck of motes remains. To encompass it all is to be vast and inclusive—yet you must know that even as the sun is high, the cock may crow.

Not to establish anything is to be tranquil, empty, and luminous—who understands that in the midst of red dust, the dog may bark? Whether it be a Buddha, strike him; whether it be a demon, strike him too. It is up to me."
Whether by boat or by land, whether hungry for one meal or full for one meal, I am glad that the firewood is dry and the water is convenient.
Without a trace to hide the body, I meet people with a pair of bare hands and beg for a single coin. Where the body is hidden there is no trace;
with two brows knit together, even meeting a Buddha, one can offer three prostrations. I have been at Yaoshan for over twenty years...
To clarify this matter: these words come from my own mouth; do not let outsiders hear them. Where all people hide their bodies, Bozan knows it all;
where Bozan hides his body, no one knows. Brothers, today you are here at this Dharma assembly.
It cannot be avoided that we present it face-to-face. If you travel to various places, do not fail to speak correctly when meeting people.

Take care! On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, the Master ascended the hall. After the Rector had finished striking the gavel, the Master said: "How does one contemplate the primary principle?
To look at it is to go blind; to smell it is to split one's brain. When taking a step, there is no trace left behind; when a thought moves, it is neither arising nor ceasing. Eye and form—"
The sounds of the ears; the mind forgets its tracks and thought ceases. The sages and worthies of past and present have taken the same path yet followed different tracks:
the lute beneath the waters at Mount Zhongfeng, the moon in the sky of Master Ma, the oil in the hands of Touzi, and the cypress before the courtyard of Zhaozhou.

Bo Shan had nothing to show, yet it leaked forth from the branches of the plum blossoms—emitting emerald green and holding fragrance, withstanding the freezing cold and defying frost and snow. Its pure scent...
Filling the ten directions, it strikes the entire body so that blood flows; one beats one’s hands and wails to the blue heavens. Old Fubei is tongue-tied.
Brothers, at that time on the eighth day of the twelfth month, Śākyamuni Buddha shattered the void, tearing it into seven pieces and eight fragments.
Throughout the entire earth, not a single person understands this. Thus, Bao-fang said: "Were it not for Ling Xingpo, who could untie the heart-knot?
On the first day of the New Year, he ascended the hall and said: "The spring breeze has just stirred, and the spring flowers bloom; the spring rain urges them on, and the spring waters come.
Only the rock atop Tongxuan Peak remains as before, covered with white lichens and green moss. Great assembly, what do you say to this?"
"This is the Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year. He spoke again: "The birds beneath the trees of the East and West Groves have added to their beautiful songs.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Water flows to the damp; fire seeks the dry. Where there is water, there are fish; where there are forests, there are birds.
When eating rice, one bites one's own tongue. One can say: 'The blue sky requires no sweeping. Brothers, you must settle this for yourselves. Under the same night..."
Xiao. Try spreading these words throughout all quarters. Do not say that the wasteland does not discriminate among the weeds;
look further at Yunmen’s staff, which has transformed into a dragon and swallowed up the mountains, rivers, and the great earth. Brothers, tell me: where is Boshan right now?
After a long silence, he said: "Profound, firm, secluded, and remote; no one can reach it. [Ascending the hall: "Clear."
Darkness and light intersect; the orthodox and the deviant alternate in splendor. Within words there is resonance; beneath phrases there is no partiality.

When the clouds and mist are lifted, the blue sky is revealed. After all, who is it that has been branded on the forehead? At the ten-thousand-fathom Dragon Gate, I laugh as I watch the winds and clouds beneath my feet.
With a single golden pellet, I play with the iron tools in my hands. An ancient said: "I go even to where a single person resides. [He] held up his staff.
The Master did not understand; yet all of you have understood it. You have reached even the place where half a person resides.
The staff understands it, while you do not. Therefore it is said: "If the stone man’s wit were like yours, he too would know how to sing the *bā* song.
If you were like the stone man, you would surely respond to the *xuě* melody. To deliberate in such a manner—only the Monk on the Wooden Seat is somewhat better. Take care!

Ascending the hall, he was asked: "What is the principle of the Dharma-body? The Master said: "Stretching out one's hand, one does not see one's own palm. The monk asked: "Where is the Dharma-body established?
The Master said: "Only then does it startle people in the darkness. The monk asked: "I do not know what realm the Dharma-body is.
The Master said: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The monk asked: "Apart from the Dharma-body, how is it then? The Master said: "A flash!"
He shattered the four continents. The assembly prostrated, and he said: "This dharma is non-dharma; this mind is non-mind.
Non-dharma is precisely dharma; non-mind is precisely mind. He overturned the lacquer bucket; the great earth sank level. Master Yunmen was truly extraordinary:
"The cup falls to the ground; the plate shatters into seven pieces. He further said: "The fan leaps up thirty [feet]."
"Three days. It hits the nostrils of Śakra. A carp from the Eastern Sea receives a blow of the staff, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin.
Brothers, today Bozan is also like the Great Master Yunmen; his spirit and bearing are like those of a king. If he were to come here to meet me, what would you do?
The assembly was silent. The Master said, 'The staff is not here; I shall use the handle of a broom for now.'"
30. At Shouchang, observing the seven-day retreat. The assembly requested that he ascend the hall. One, two, three, four, five, six.
Heaven and earth take their places; the myriad things flourish. Within this, there is a hornless mud ox that touches the east and touches the west, yet to this day has nowhere to hide its tracks.
It can do nothing but blend with the dust and mingle with the mundane. Furthermore, you must know that the level place is perilous and the straight path is crooked. Strike through the heavy layers.
Do not treat this with frivolity or negligence; in the universe of Great Peace, the deluded and the stubborn are severed. This is the direct entrustment of the Zen school. A direct entrustment!
It is like a fly emerging from the back of a broken donkey. Bodhidharma did not know how to practice Zen; Sun Bin did not understand how to divine by means of the *gua*.
Only the Old Man Shouchang spent his entire life wielding the hoe, leaping freely in every direction;
even today, he continues to fill the pits and block the hollows. Brothers, is there anyone here who will speak out on behalf of the Abbot?
Fortunately, today we have this unworthy descendant of Boshan to clear his master’s grievance. Entering the hall: "One is all; all is one."
It is simply one. Clarity is like the dark moon; darkness is like the bright sun.

If you can realize this within these four propositions, you will see Master Can leaping freely in all directions—seven strides forward and eight sideways—and see Śākyamuni Buddha in his nine purples and ten reds. If this is not yet so, there is an even more accessible Chan for you;
I shall analyze it thoroughly for you. Have you not seen a lantern hanging on the surface of the water, striking the western wall from the eastern side?
The Wall. Cast from raw iron, it produces *jili* thorns; it squeezes out the essence of gold. A-ha-ha! How extraordinary!
An enlightened monk must discern this. Study! Entering the Hall: Ten thousand miles, not a single cloud hangs; from within the void, the eyes protrude.
"Letting go in pieces by the sevens and eights; gathering them back in bits by the tens and twos—even if one were to have eyes all over one's body, it would still only amount to eighty percent.
Great assembly, is there any monk here who possesses the full hundred percent? Heh! Do not even mention it. Having said this, he descended from his seat.
On an occasion when Master Gushan ascended the hall, he said: "In the past, at the assembly on Vulture Peak, the World-Honored One held up a flower and showed it to the multitude."
There remains one branch still in the hands of Boshan. Today, upon the platform of Yongquan Hall, it shall be offered to the great assembly.
An ancient worthy said: "Yesterday he was an infant; today his years are old. Yet he has not yet understood three, eight, and nine."
Difficult to tread upon is the ancient imperial path. To speak thus is to bare one's heart and pour out one's gall, to reveal the ultimate compassionate mind.
But tell me, how do you explain the principle of "three, eight, and nine"? He struck his staff and said: "The Yellow River overflows, the Yellow River;
the misty mountains connect, the misty mountains. Be careful! [Ascending the hall: A black dog with silver-clawed paws, in broad daylight...
Barking all night long. A barren woman holds a needle upside down. Wooden men converse face-to-face.
Brothers, if you can pass through these four lines, then even when they come from the four quarters and eight directions, or when empty space strikes you with a staff, you will be ready.
Therefore it is said: "A pair of solitary wild geese fly high, close to the ground; two mandarin ducks stand alone by the pond. This may be called holding a bright pearl in one's palm. Treasure.

A mirror set upon its stand: when both the bearded barbarian and the Han person approach, there is no way to hide or conceal anything. Brothers, you may gather the great chiliocosm within the palm of your hand and cast the lands of transformation to other directions;
you may delve into the fragrant waters beneath the golden wheel—if you can truly do such things, it is indeed most extraordinary.
"But you must not touch it at all. If you touch it, I shall break your donkey-waists! A monk asked, "What is falling into sound and form without interruption?
The Master said, "The broken bridge divides the wild waters. The monk asked, "What is falling into categories?
The Master said, "A solitary boat is raised upon the vast plain. The monk asked, "What is the fall of the noble and honored? The Master said, "Tearing asunder several layers of purity."
"In the world, one rides a jade elephant backward to pursue a qilin. In the autumn of the Gengwu year, the Master entered nirvana.
The Head Seat asked, "How is the Master’s health? The Master replied, "I still have some measure of enjoyment.

The Seat asked, "Is there anyone who is not ill? The Master said, "Are you suffering from a fever? The Seat said, "Coming and going with freedom—please speak a word for me. The Master [responded] for him.

He wrote out the four characters "Li-li-fen-ming" (Clear and Distinct) with his brush, then cast down the pen and sat in meditation until death. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain.
He was fifty-six years of age and forty years since his ordination.
Chan Master Huitai Yuanjing of Dongyuan in Jianning was the son of the Feng family of Jianyang; his father was Tianzai and his mother was Wu.
He was born in the sixth month of the Dingchou year of the Wanli era of Emperor Ming Shenzong. From childhood, he was exceptionally gifted and deeply devoted to filial piety and fraternal kindness.
In the Jiachen year, he went to Lixingkong at Huxiao Rock to receive instruction. While reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he attained realization at the point where "seeing is not seeing."
He then tucked up his robes and went to attend upon Shouchang Jing, presenting his insights to him. Jing rebuked him sternly, saying, "You are a man who has fallen into a great and perilous pit!
The Master was startled and shaken, losing his composure. Thereupon, he redoubled his resolve to investigate the truth, remaining for a long time without finding its flavor.
One day, while casually reading the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, he reached the passage where Vimalakīrti says, "Why is this room empty and without an attendant? and Vimalakīrti replies, "The Buddhas..."

The lands, too, were entirely empty. Suddenly and expansively, he attained realization and entered [the Way]. He composed a verse, saying: "Consciousness, once pierced through, is not worth half a coin;
Pity how many years have been spent in vain groping. The entire lineage of the school consists of nothing but deceivers of the heart;

What need is there to speak of a separate transmission from the West? He entered the master’s quarters to present his realization. The master said: "Zhaozhou exposed the old woman. You tell me, where was she exposed?"
At the point of realization, the Master said in a stern voice, "Old monk, stop acting so strange. Jingwei assisted in the celebration. Boshan came to open the Dharma at Dayang;
the Master went specifically to visit him. Boshan asked, "I hear that you, elder brother, personally saw Shouchang.
Tell me, where did Shouchang’s life-root (minggen) break off in those days? The Master gave him a slap across the face and said, "Where?"
Deshan was at his quarters when Linji arrived, but Deshan did not acknowledge him. Linji shook his head and departed. Later, Linji said, "What a pity! The attendant was not here;
I have left thirty blows for him. That very day, Linji went up to the hall. As Deshan was about to enter the assembly, Linji called out, "Heitai! Who told you it was Heitai?
Deshan stepped forward and let out a thunderous shout. The assembly was stunned. Linji said, "Bring me the staff! Deshan replied, "..."
"This is leftover food; there is no need to pick it out. He then asked, "Tell me, when Mazu let out a shout and Baizhang was deaf for three days—what were those three days?
Layman Lai replied, "The autumn wind carries much killing; the autumn dew grows ever colder.
The Master shook his sleeves and returned to the assembly. Lai said, "You have only learned how to run. The Master paid him no mind. In the year Wumu, he went forth to reside at Shu.

At Dongwon Hermitage in the forest, during the first year of Emperor Gwangjong’s reign, Gaitang (the *gengshen* year), he ascended the hall at Ilji-am to preach the Dharma. He said: "The Way and its Teachings are fundamentally not many;
the Southern Dipper pierces through the Northern River. All that is required comes down to these twenty-one characters.

Having exhausted all demons and ghosts with this, he returned to seclusion on Mount Wuyi. There, he built a hut at Seopyeong Rock and lived with two or three practitioners who followed him to gather firewood and draw water.
Once, there was a monk who sought instruction by parting the grass. The Master shouted, "You bald-headed fellow! You have lost your soul; what are you doing here?
He then sat motionless on a precipitous cliff. A monk asked, "What are you doing here, Master?
The Master called out, "Come up here! I will speak with you. The monk looked over the edge of the cliff and withdrew. —Yizong (Ji)
In the Gengwu year of the Chongzhen era, the Master suddenly fell ill. Pointing to the base of a cliff, he said to an attendant, "This place will do for my burial.
The attendant asked, "Suppose you were to die and be buried here, what would happen then? The Master let out a great laugh and said, "That would be just right.
When the attendant asked again, the Master had already passed away. He was fifty-four years of age and twenty-six years of monastic seniority. He was interred there.
At the stone cliff thus indicated, Huang Duanyu of the Sacrificial Bureau (Cibu) composed an inscription engraved upon the rock.
Chan Master Qiuran Yuanmi of Shouchang in Jianchang Prefecture was the son of the Hu family of Nancheng in the commandery;
from childhood he was upright and tranquil, taking no pleasure in the study of literary commentaries. At twenty-one, he accompanied his father to visit Wuming at Baofang, where it was as if...
An old acquaintance arrived again after a month had passed. When he requested ordination, it was not granted, so he went to Linchuan to pay respects at Jinnshan Monastery and shaved his head.

The following year, he visited Ming once more and was appointed as the kitchen supervisor (huotou). His parents were filled with lingering attachment and would not let him go, but the Master cut through their bonds with painful resolve, saying:
Affection and love do not cease; birth and death do not cease. How can the kindness of one's parents be repaid? Thus, his parents permitted him [to become a monk].
One day, Ming was discussing with a monk the long-term causes and conditions of the World-Honored One. The Master stepped forward and asked, "What principle is this?
The monk said, "There is no share for you in this. The Master said, "Everyone has their share; why is it that I alone have none?"

Ming said, "Since you already have the karmic lot, why do you seek others? The Master had no reply. Thereupon, he practiced with great diligence and investigated with bitter earnestness for a long time, without ceasing day or night.
