"One hundred thousand *li*—yet you still hesitate here. The Master then struck his staff on the ground and said, "Even so, were it not for the guidance of the fisherman, how could one have seen the surging waves?
A monk asked, "How is it that by attaining realization within the 'First Phrase,' one is fit to be a teacher to the Buddhas and Patriarchs?
The Master replied, "Face-to-face, the spring breeze is full of harmony; the eyebrows are parted in eight characters."
[The Master] said: "Transverse. [A monk asked: "How is it that one who realizes the meaning within the second phrase is fit to be a teacher for gods and humans?

The Master said: "Reveal the moon amidst the clouds; do not travel in the darkness. [The monk asked: "How is it that one who realizes the meaning within the third phrase cannot even save themselves? The Master said:
"If you know where to return when there is resonance within words, you cannot avoid borrowing the path of others. [The monk] asked: "What is it? The Master said: "Transverse."
[Question: "Regarding the matter of the Dharma-body (dharmakāya), Master, [what is it? [Master: "A black lacquer bucket. [Question: "What is the Dharma-body?
[Master: "A rotten pumpkin. [Question: "What is the matter that lies beyond the Dharma-body? [Master: "The wine sign at a village of three households. [Question:
"What is 'the phrase reaching but the meaning not reaching'? [Master: "Every word reveals the Truth; every step obscures the tracks. [Question: "What is the meaning?"...

"Reaching the phrase but not reaching the meaning. The Master said, "It is right on the tip of the tongue; one cannot spit it out no matter how hard one tries. "What is 'both meaning and phrase reached'?
The Master said, "Sometimes leaning alone against the courtyard railing, idly watching three or five branches of plum blossoms open.
"What is 'neither meaning nor phrase reached'? The Master said, "The falling flowers flow away with the stream, leaving the wandering traveler to bear his emptiness in vain."

Question: "The mountains crumble and collapse; why do the mists and clouds not disperse? The Master said: "You abandon the great and cling to the small. Question: "One stands alone before the jade mirror;
why are the features of the face not seen? The Master said: "Break the mirror and then we shall meet. Question:
"In the daytime it exists, but in sleep it is absent. How can one attain suchness where waking and sleeping are one? The Master said: "Who told you that?"
[The monk] asked about existence and non-existence. The Master said, "I do not understand. The Master continued, "Not understanding is most intimate.
[The monk] asked, "I do not ask about the very first step; I wonder, what did he tread upon? The Master said, "Stealing melons in the middle of the night.

[The monk] asked, "What was it like after stealing them? The Master said, "You have not yet arrived. [The monk] asked, "When the World-Honored One beheld the morning star, what was his intention? The Master said:
"Black within, white. [The student] said, "The Three Vehicles equally contemplate the emptiness of nature (*dharmatā-śūnyatā*) and thereby attain the Way. What is this 'emptiness of nature'?
The Master picked up his whisk and showed it to him, saying, "This was bought for thirty-seven coins.

A student asked, "Before I have even reached Qing Shan, I have already received a beating. The Master said, "You bald-headed meditators! The student said, "I beg you once more to grant me a beating. The Master said, "The old monk has none."
This man possessed extraordinary vigor and a majestic, imposing demeanor. By nature, he was serene and inclined toward reclusion.
Having personally attended the Dragon Pond (Longchi) for eighteen years, he was repeatedly summoned by imperial decree to share the seat and preach the Dharma, yet he declined each time.

Upon first entering Qingshan, he encountered heavy snow that lasted for over fifty days, during which the smoke from the cooking fires nearly ceased. Amidst hungry birds and wild beasts, the Master remained settled and composed as if at ease, reflecting only upon...
The Dharma-gate was in decline and the Way of the Teacher was being eclipsed. He strove to restore the supreme ancestral lineage and extensively expounded the purport of the separate transmission.

He bitterly rebuked those who engaged in forced interpretations and strictly distinguished between the correct and the heterodox. Scholars from all quarters who turned toward the Way followed his influence one after another, their voices clamoring throughout the realm.
On the twenty-third day of the ninth month of the Yihai year of the Chongzhen era, he manifested parinirvāṇa at the age of sixty-one.
His monastic seniority was thirty-seven years. His entire remains were enshrined in a stupa at Ba’en Temple.
In the Jihai year of the Shunzhi era (1659), his disciples followed his final instructions and relocated the stupa to the left of Haihui Temple in Jingxi.
Chan Master Xueqiao Yuanxin of Yunmen in Shaoxing Prefecture was the son of the Zhu family from Ning County. At the age of nine, he heard the *Amitābha Sūtra* being recited:
"The water birds and the trees all constantly chant the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Thereupon, he came to know and place his faith in the Buddha Vehicle.
At twenty-nine, he left the household life and later visited the mountain master Miaozhen at Mount Qinwang. Zhen raised [a koan]:
A monk with the supernormal power of reading others' minds asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From India. The reader said, "I have heard that there are three Indias.
From which one have you come? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk was at a loss and had no reply. When the Master heard this account being related, his doubt was suddenly aroused.
The next day, he took up his staff, climbed onto a large rock, and called out loudly, "From which India have you come? Speak quickly!"
"The Way is swift! The Way is swift! Suddenly, the past and future limits were severed, like the sun’s disk bursting forth from the sky.
He then spoke a verse: "The stone is pressed against the spine; The body turns over, the ribs on the side. Look closely at this: Though it moves, it cannot move. He then shouted:
"Zhang San has committed murder; Li Si must repay the debt of life! Desiring to go to Tiantai to seek out one who knows.

As he was verifying this through his consciousness, he suddenly raised his head and saw the three characters "Ancient Yunmen. He attained sudden and great enlightenment. He further spoke a verse, saying:
"Once ascending Mount Tiantai, the clouds grow deeper; My heels have snapped the laces of my straw sandals. The five hundred bhikṣus left no trace; If I see them again, I shall break their tendons.
He then returned and bound himself with thatch on Double-Tuft Peak (Shuangji Feng). Later, he visited Yunqi Lianchi.
Master Chizhen presented this verse: I do not understand the West, nor do I study Chan; Having come by chance to this dusty world, I simply follow conditions.
In a thatched cottage of three bays beside a stream, With two bamboo windows, I sleep as the moon enters them. My patched robe is worn through, yet I have no intention to mend it;
I let my hair grow long, as if I were going mad. Since I realized the meaning of the Westward Journey, The white snow has drifted on for six...
The Moon Deity. Next, he visited Longchi (Dragon Pond). There, through a karmic resonance within the chamber, he immediately attained the Mind-Seal (*cittamudrā*).
In the forty-third year of the Wanli era, he moved to Qianzhi An on Mount Jing. Later, he resided at Kaixian on Mount Lu. In the Guiwei year, he moved to Dongta on Jiahe.
In his later years, he stayed at Yunmen in Yue. At the Hall of the Great Way on Mount Jing, he said: "How truly marvelous! How truly marvelous! The insentient preach the Dharma."
Inconceivable! In the space of a finger-snap, the Stone Tiger bites and kills the Green-Field Chicken.

The lanterns and pillars cannot restrain their amusement and leap up; the Peng bird soars to the mountain peak and lets out a great roar. But tell me, what does it roar? A moon is added to the pool of merit;
its radiance fills the forest, a splendor worth pursuing. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The ancestral school of Yunmen is cut off."
Deliberation: Encompassing heaven and earth, there is nothing hidden. To touch the crown of the head is to stumble and fall. With the staff, he points out the true son.
A monk asked, "What is it like when one swallows the waters of the West River in a single gulp?

The Master said, "The wild fox spirit is exposed. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. Ascending the hall at Kaixian Temple on Mount Lu, [the Master] said: "From antiquity, it has been opened..."
First, the scenery was different; what is this mountain like? It is like a purple *kāṣāya*. The silent boy speaks clearly: "Which man will be the first to reach home?
He shouted, saying: "Easy, indeed easy! Difficult, indeed difficult! Who can extend the great arm to sever the barrier of the Patriarchs?
Returning from his excursion to Mount Jinyun, he ascended the hall and said: "Having finished my tour of Mount Jinyun, I have returned to Zhaoyin."
[The Master] sat. "Yesterday the old man went there to pay respects at the stupa; today he has just returned. You virtuous ones, did you see the old man go and come? After a long silence, he said:
"When the yellow leaves have fallen from the treetops, one shall surely see the distant mountains turn green. On the occasion of the opening of the retreat, he ascended the hall and said:
"For forty years I have practiced in this manner; I have slashed open the azure sky until it reeks with blood. Within it, there is indeed something rare."
A wondrous matter! The lion roams about without asking for directions.

He bows his head to the Tathāgata Lamp-King and universally prays that the sentient beings of lands as numerous as motes of dust may all together enter the gate of Prajñāpāramitā. But tell me, how does one enter the gate of Prajñāpāramitā?
Raising his whisk, he said: "To discern. [He ascended the hall. He cited a monk who asked Yunmen: "In a single thought-moment..."
[The Master] rose. "Is there still a fault here or not? Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru. At that time, if that monk had attained awakening, he would have snapped Mount Sumeru into two pieces.
Is there anyone present today who understands this? Come forward! If you do not understand, I, the old monk, shall break it open for you:
"When not a single thought arises, Mount Sumeru is the Blue Sky and the Bright Sun—the Gate of Ghosts. Yellow... [text ends].
Before the Crane Tower, by the Parrot Bank, white artemisia and red smartweed are stained with blood. Entering the hall, [the Master] raised the case:
Master Dayuan of Tianmu said, "The great earth, mountains, and rivers are a single expanse of snow; once the sun shines upon them, their traces vanish.
From this point on, one no longer doubts the Buddhas and Patriarchs—what north, south, east, or west could there be? He gave a shout. "It is well, indeed it is well."

This is indeed beautiful. What prevents this from being the time for our departure? It is only because the road ends and the mountains grow ever more remote that we must be pitied as we fall into the state of servants.
Upon ascending the hall after the lifting of the retreat: How does the lifting of the retreat compare to its commencement?

With the spring breeze blowing north and south, each finds rest in their own place. Seeking alms in the village, there is not a single grain; with a single empty belly, one composes a poem. Sixty-five days.
Where did you come from before? Where will you go after sixty-five days? This is a great divine mantra; this is a great illuminating mantra.
Ascending the hall on the Emperor’s birthday, he observes the events of the previous Xinwei year: "Throughout the night I pondered them, my tears never drying.
An old man remembers when as a child he rode a bamboo horse, playing the clay drums in groups of threes and twos. A-he-he!"
*Chang li luo. Tiao ti tiao. Wu ti wu. One laugh, one sorrow. How pitiable! Year by year I grow old; now I am seventy.
Yet I recall back to when I was thirty, forty, and fifty.* *Du!* [He ascends the hall. He cites Master Fu Dashi, who said: "There is a thing prior to heaven and earth;
formless, it is fundamentally still and vast. It is able to be the lord of the myriad phenomena, yet it does not follow the four seasons."*
"Time withers. Is this not your own true master? After a long silence, he said, "Do not misunderstand.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the Unsurpassed Vehicle? The Master said, "The pinnacle of the pagoda.
The monk asked, "What is the matter of descending? The Master said, "The banner pole is moving. The monk asked, "What is the underlying meaning? The Master said, "Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva."
Ascending the hall on New Year’s Day: With the single blast of a firecracker, heaven and earth grow old; before the pagoda, there is nowhere that does not shine with brilliance.
This very thing is the Dharma; this very thing is the Way; this very thing is practice. Great assembly, you have stood for a long time; take care and be well.

Ascending the hall upon the conclusion of the retreat: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Standing alone on the crest of a ten-thousand-fathom peak with but one foot. After a long silence, he said: "One."
The period has passed; not a single person, not even half one, is to be seen in the hall. How fortunate that all is peaceful!
Yet, on the crossroads, you might run into Master Ma, who will demand payment for your meal. How will you respond? He gave a shout and said: "The spring breeze reaches every garden day by day;
night after night, face south and gaze at the Northern Dipper. — From the Cloud Gate Monastery in Yuezhou.
The Hall. The entirety of the worlds of the ten directions is the gate of light of Dīpaṃkara Buddha.

The entirety of the worlds of the ten directions is the gate of dhāraṇī of Śākyamuni Buddha. The entirety of the worlds of the ten directions is the gate of liberation of the Venerable Maitreya in Tuṣita Heaven.
The entirety of the worlds of the ten directions is the gate of prajñāpāramitā of Mañjuśrī, the Prince of the Dharma.
The gate of the *Ratnamegha* (Cloud of Jewels). The entire world-system of the ten directions is the gate of the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
The entire world-system of the ten directions is the gate of the ocean of diverse meanings of all *sūtras*.

The entire world-system of the ten directions is the gate of the arising and ceasing of insects, fleas, and lice—the most minute and subtle of all—among ordinary beings within the four modes of birth and the six realms of existence. [He] brushes it away with a whisk.
The Master drew a circle and said, "Do you understand? He gave a shout and descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The Yellow-Faced Old Man said, 'I have no dharma by which I attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. What kind of words are these?
Yet, Dīpaṃkara Buddha bestowed upon me a prediction, naming me Śākyamuni. He laughed heartily and said, "The title is clear!"
Ascending the hall: Green mountains and bright days; springs, rocks, pines, and clouds—meeting you face-to-face, I do not know whose child you are.
If you can understand it here, you may sit securely upon your own mountain home. If this is not yet so, by all means do not utter empty or false words.
Ascending the hall: Those in the world who act as merchants or travelers, regardless of whether they travel a thousand or a hundred li, all...
One must reach home; only the old man has no home to which he can return. Why is this? Because here there is no place for you to lodge.
Suppose you arrive late on the evening of the thirtieth—what then? A thousand sages share the same path, yet not the same tracks.
Is there anyone who follows along? [He] raised his staff. Entering the hall, he said: "The clear and harmonious days refresh the spirit daily; the wind carries the willows..."
The flowers fill the four directions; entrust them to the nightingale, though it may bleed in vain. Next year there will be even more spring. Raising his whisk, he asked, "Do you understand?
He drew a circle and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "Last night, the neighbor to the east returned while treading upon the moon."
"The smartweed and willows come toward me; clearly, this is a piece of good news. Yet alas, the eyes of people of this age do not open.
While the Master was scratching a louse, Gu-shi came up behind him and gave his shoulder a tap, saying, "Master, please be more compassionate.
The Master replied, "Everyone sees blood. Question: Among the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion (Mahākāruṇika), which one is the true one?
"Eye. The Master said, "An exposed stone mortar in the open air. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Blind.
[The monk] asked, "What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth? The Master said, "It cannot be opened up. [The monk] asked, "How does one pass through the Dusk Pine Pass?
The Master said, "Do not mistake it for a false cock crowing. [The monk] asked, "What is the 'blow-off-hair sword'? The Master said, "Two or three dull birds."
Xing asked, "What is the Vajra King’s precious sword? The Master said, "It does not slay wild fox spirits.
He asked, "What is the lion crouching on its haunches? The Master said, "The eye. He asked, "What is the probing pole and the shadow-grass?
The Master said, "I knew early on that you were still on the road. He asked, "What is the single shout that does not function as a single shout? The Master said, "I want you."
[The Master] died naturally. Question: "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said: "Day after day, the sun is in the sky. Question:

"What is the house style of the Double-Tufted One (Shuangji)? The Master said: "A single mound of earth for a stove; ten thousand peaks at the summit. Question: "Whom did the Great Master succeed? The Master said:
"Gazing all day at the distant mountains; an iron ox neighs within the clouds. Question: "How is it? The Master said: [Silence].
"This is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. The Master said, "He broke two into three. Question: "What is the method for ceasing the consumption of grain?
The Master said, "Two bowls of congee and one meal of rice. Question: "What is the principle behind this?

The Master said, "I have never chewed a single grain of rice. Question: "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Having once been a profligate, one especially pities the traveler; beneath the moon, amidst the wind..."
[The monk] asked several times before, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said, "A staff slung over the shoulder, heedless of others;
straight into a thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks. [The monk] asked, "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, "A single mass of spring clouds flies out over the ridge;
to this day it drifts away and does not return to the mountain. [The monk] asked, "What is the host within the host? The Master said, "The eye..."
The pupils within are two infants; from birth, whether they be handsome or ugly, let the master look as he will.
A question was asked: "It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha, and it is not a thing. What is it? The Master said: "This is precisely when you must apply yourself with effort.

Qi Jichao pointed to a tree in the courtyard and asked: "When did this tree attain Buddhahood? The Master said: "It attained Buddhahood long ago. Jichao asked: "If so, why has it only just now grown?"
[The Master] grew [in stature]. The Master said, "A being with heterodox views. While the Master was basking his back on the steps below, he saw Cheya approaching.
Suddenly assuming a kneeling posture, Cheya asked, "What is the essential meaning? The Master replied, "There is no small amount of trickery here.

The Master hurried back to the abbot’s quarters and asked, "How was it before Ox-head had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "When the water rises, the boat floats higher. [Cheya asked,] "After he saw him..."
"How is it? The Master replied, "When the mud is deep, the Buddha is great. One day, the Master manifested a slight illness and wrote a verse of parting for the assembly, saying:
"You little children! On the road of birth and death, one may roam with ease. Under the bright moon and frosty dawn, having drunk a cup of tea, I sit and depart.
He then instructed his attendant to bring him tea; having finished drinking, he passed away. This was on the twentieth day of the eighth month in the Dinghai year of the Shunzhi era.
He passed away on the sixth day. His worldly age was seventy-seven, and his years of monastic seniority were forty-eight. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the right foot of Mount Yunmen.
The one who oversaw the funeral arrangements was his nephew, Chan Master Hongjue Man.
The Emperor Shizu Zhang was well-acquainted with the Master’s reputation;

regretting that he had not yet been granted an audience, he specially bestowed five hundred taels of silver to order the reconstruction of the Master’s stupa, and issued an imperial decree to the Chan Master Hongjue stating: "The mendicant’s staff has returned to the mountains."

At this time, as I dwell upon distant thoughts, I have now received your letter, which brings great comfort to my mind. As your messenger returns, I am composing this reply to send along with him. There are matters I wish to speak of:

whenever I contemplate the Dharma-gate, I am reminded of the examples set by the ancients. The memorial stupa of the Great Master Xueqiao stands majestically at Yunmen; all students from every quarter should together gaze upon it with reverence.

Recently, I have heard that although the mountain boundaries have been divided, the foundation remains— [Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly. The translation reflects the available portion.]

The foundations have gradually crumbled. Fearing that with the passage of years and the distance of time, its destruction may become a source of concern, I now contribute five hundred pieces of gold to restore it.
Although this may not suffice to cover the full cost of a stūpa, once it has been renovated by my hand, people will surely change their perception and give rise to reverence;
they will henceforth never again dare to commit acts of encroachment or insult. May the Meditation Master, mindful of this model, long cherish this honor.
I exhort you to diligently manage this matter, so as to fulfill my long-held intention of paying respectful homage to the venerable elders.
Therefore, I specifically entrust this to you; may the Chan Master take full cognizance of it.
Chan Master Jingming Baopu Lian was the son of the Luo family of Lin’an. At the age of fifteen, he went to Miaoyan to receive the tonsure;
at twenty-two, he traveled to Yunqi to receive full ordination. Initially, he frequented lecture halls, but one day he thought to himself: "For several years past..."
Although there were points where his understanding accorded with the essential purport of the doctrinal teachings, these proved entirely useless at the very brink of birth and death.
He subsequently changed his robes and entered Mount Jing. During a seven-day period of intensive Chan practice, he attained a vast and penetrating realization.

He composed a verse, saying: "Since childhood I lost my mother; I searched for her everywhere in foreign lands. Suddenly, we met face to face—no further deliberation is needed. Immediately upon the conclusion of the retreat, he departed.
He went to Jingxi to visit Master Zhuanzuo at Longchi. He asked, "I have come from afar to pay my respects; I beg the Master for instruction.
Zhuanzuo said, "This old monk’s teeth are sparse and missing. The Master said, "As for the most intimate point, I beg for one more word.
Zhuanzuo remained seated. The Master called to his attendant, "Bring some tea! Zhuanzuo said, "Not bad—clever, clever! The Master said, "My ears are deaf. Zhuanzuo [remained silent].
"Rest! one day [Zhaozhou] took his leave. Baizhang said, "The old monk still has words that have not yet been exhausted.
The Master said, "Although the Master’s words are not yet exhausted, I already know their meaning. Baizhang said, "Tell me then, what is the meaning of the old monk?
The Master gave a shout. Baizhang said, "Give another shout and see. The Master turned around and went out. Baizhang then presented him with the lineage seal.
He bestowed the whisk upon him. After [Xuefeng] had taken up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'Buddha'? The Master said, "The meaning of awakening.

The monk asked, "Is a Buddha still deluded? The Master said, "Yes, he is deluded. The monk asked, "Since he is already awakened, why does he become deluded again? The Master said, "If he were not deluded again, what would you have asked?"

[The monk] said, "I must ask about this transgression. The Master raised his staff and struck him out. [The monk] asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said, "A swallowtail butterfly pierces through flower shadows.
[The monk] asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'? The Master said, "Lifting the eyebrows, one sweeps away the white clouds.

[The monk] asked, "What is 'taking away both person and environment'? The Master said, "Neither has any news. [The monk] asked, "What is 'leaving both person and environment intact'? The Master said, "The spring wind blows over the ten thousand things."
"What is it like when both person and environment are not taken away? The Master said, "Pushing open the window, one gazes at the bright moon.
The layman Xiong Yushan asked, "All phenomena return to the One; where does the One return? The Master raised his tea cup and invited him for tea.
Xiong said, "I was in Qingzhou making a robe of plain cotton cloth weighing seven *jin*. What about that? The Master said, "A shelled turtle takes flight."
The Emperor asked, "What is the meaning of 'three catties of hemp'? The Master replied, "The weight is clearly defined.

The Master passed away in the eighth month of the Jisi year of the Chongzhen era. His stupa was enshrined at Jingming. He authored a single volume titled *Chancong Qimeng* (An Introduction to the Chan School), which has circulated in the world.
During the Shunzhi era...

The Emperor Shizu (Emperor Wen of Sui) inquired about the Way at Mount Kongtong. Imperial carriages were dispatched in all directions to seek out masters of the Way and their conduct. He sought out the surviving images [of these masters] and presented them to the Inner Palace.
This concludes the section on the dharma heirs of Chan Master Guang of Nanming.
Chan Master Yunhu Yong of Puming Temple in Jianning, Fujian, was the son of the Zheng family of Haining.

He received his training under Guang of Nanming and once visited Wuhuan Chong, from whom he received instruction on the essentials of the Dharma. While spending the summer retreat at Jingshan, he happened to read the *Siyi jing* (Sūtra of Additional Benefit) and attained a realization.

He composed a verse to present to Guang, who rebuked him. For several years, Guang held him closely. One day, while examining the *Chuan deng lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp), he reached [the entry on]...
Below the section on the Patriarch Yan, the *Caiqingfeng Gong'an* (The Case of Master Qingfeng) is recorded. His doubts were resolved, and he received broad certification.

He emerged from seclusion to take up residence at Puming Monastery. Upon ascending the hall for formal instruction, a monk asked: "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master struck him. The monk asked again: "What is the mind of a student? The Master said: [He struck him again].
The Master said, "One who wishes to seize a soaring dragon will end up as nothing more than a wall-crawling lizard. [A monk] asked, "What is it, after all?

The Master struck him with his staff three times and drove him out, then descended from his seat. Later, while the Master was enjoying the moon with Great Master Xueqiao, Xueqiao pointed at the moon and said, "Where has that half gone?
The Master remained silent for a long time and then asked, "Do you understand? Xueqiao replied, "I can only get half of it too. The Master said, "This..."
"Half of it is gone. Jiao also remained silent for a long time. The Master said, "One can only get half of it. They laughed together.
On the first day of the New Year, he ascended the hall and said: "The ancient Way is naturally restored in the phoenix calendar; The songs of Yao and the hymns of Shun bring boundless joy.
Clouds enshroud the vermilion cassia, its golden stalks exquisite; Rain bathes the jade forest, its emerald leaves growing long. Chongzhen Renwu (1642).
On the eleventh day of the tenth month, at the hour of the Dragon (7–9 a.m.), he took up his brush and wrote a verse: "To be born was an error; to die is also an error.
The iron lion has snapped the golden cord. He cast down his brush and said, "Hah! Thereupon he passed away. His secular age was fifty-six, and his monastic seniority was thirty-nine.
He was interred in a stupa on the mountain where he resided.

Compiled by the Monastic Subject (Chao Yong), Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple in the Capital.

the Monk Chōkai.
Chan Master Wuping Ruxue of Mount Wuyun in Weishan, Changsha Prefecture, was a successor of Chan Master Tiantong Wu, the thirty-fourth generation descendant of Nanyue.
He was the son of the Ren family of Lintong; he lost his father when he was still a young boy.

He received the tonsure at Wutai Tianqi and completed his full ordination under Vinaya Master Cheng. He subsequently traveled extensively through various regions and went to visit Tiantong Wu at Jinsu.
One night during their conversation, Wu suddenly extended his leg and asked, "How do you deal with this?
The Master kicked it with his foot. Wu laughed and said, "Not yet. The Master said, "Let the Master speak. Wu lay down flat on his back. The Master said, "So there."
He was merely exhausted. Wuzu said, "And you go off like this again? The Master then prostrated himself. Wuzu appointed him as the West Hall attendant.
One day, as the Master was taking his leave, Wuzu held up his whisk and said: "To call it a whisk is to encounter it; not to call it a whisk is to turn one's back on it.
You must not pick it up, nor must you put it down. You must not remain silent, nor must you speak. You must not err."

[The Master] raised [the whisk]. When the Master did not err in his presentation, he handed it over to him. The Master leaped up and said, "No, no! Wuzu said, "This is still just shouting and leaping about.
Try raising it again. The Master turned around and said, "I am going. Wuzu then bestowed upon him the lineage seal and the whisk.
Later, while in retreat at Hongji Temple, a monk asked, "What is the meaning within the gate?"

The monk shouted again. The Master said, "A confused shout. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. The monk was speechless.

Touzi. The Master splashed tea across his face. The monk prostrated and said, "I thank the Master for his compassion.

[With these words,] he bowed solemnly and withdrew. Question: Before the words had even ceased—"Mañjuśrī gave rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma"—

The Master struck him directly and looked back at a monk standing nearby. He drew a circle (○) on the ground with his staff. The monk then sat down within the circle.
The Master again drew a large circle around him with his staff. The monk rose and stood to one side. The Master smiled and asked:
"What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth? The Master replied: "The entire world is pitch-black. "How about this? [the monk asked].

The Master said, “From where have you come, *ācārya*? He replied, “From Mount Bian. The Master struck him and said, “Speak clearly!
Later, when the Master was at Daopei Tongqing Temple sitting by the ancestral pagoda, Vinaya Master Ming came to pay respects at the pagoda. The Master said, “Pay respects.”

The Master said, "Where is it not secluded? Ming struck the Master with his palm. The Master said, "Why? Ming replied, "Where is it not secluded? The Master laughed heartily.

On the thirtieth day of the sixth month of the You year, he recounted his own life’s journey. Thereafter, he neither drank nor ate, sitting upright all day long without his side ever touching the mat.

In the autumn of the Jiǎzǐ year of the Heavenly Opening (1624), while Tiantong Wù was flourishing his transformation at Jīnsù, the Master went to pay him a visit. He encountered Wù ascending the hall, where Wù cited the story of Huangbo’s study under Baizhang:

"Not a hair's breadth [of it] can be grasped. He gave a shout and said, "Did the assembly hear that all at once? Then he descended from his seat.

The Dharma: Preventing the Small to Stop the Great. Ascending the hall, he said: "In this pointed-thatched grass hut, the scent of roots is fragrant; one's livelihood depends entirely upon a broken-legged cauldron.
Having eaten the wild vegetables together with their very roots, one washes and scrubs the alms bowl once more to deliberate further. Tell me, Great Assembly, what do you say?"
What are you discussing? Tea prices have been high lately; when guests arrive, serve them mugwort soup. The Arhat from the West was invited to ascend the hall.
Having come ten thousand *li*, he did not speak a single word. He resembles Bodhidharma in his bearing; he is like the True Dharma itself.

You must further take care where you step. To hesitate and fail to advance is truly to miss the mark; it cannot be remedied before your eyes and only adds shame to your face.

It does not hinder one from giving rise to views according to others, nor from acting as a condition in every place. After a long silence, he said: "Do you understand?"

A flood surged forth from the niche. Thereupon, he was cremated according to the Dharma, and over a thousand śarīras were obtained, as lustrous and clear as soybeans.
His disciples divided them and returned home, constructing stupas at various locations including Xihu, Xizi, and Helin.
Chan Master Tongxian Baoen Fushui of Duncun, Suzhou Prefecture, was a native of Pinghu. His secular surname was Li. From childhood, he abstained from meat and strong flavors.
At the age of nineteen, he left the household life. He traveled to visit Zhenji and Yunmen, yet remained bewildered and found no way in.

Consequently, he went with like-minded companions to the summit of Yingke Mountain, where they sealed themselves in a "death-gate" retreat. Hearing the saying, "The corpse is here; where is the person? he suddenly—
He had a realization. Later, he attended upon Tiantong Wu and attained his essential teaching. He subsequently resided at Ba’en Temple in Wujiang. Upon ascending the hall, he said:

"Even if one were to carry [the Buddha] on one's head for hundreds of thousands of kalpas, and offer one’s own body as a seat throughout the three thousandfold world-system, if one does not transmit the Dharma to deliver sentient beings, there would ultimately be no way to repay that kindness.
He raised his whisk and said: "Today, Ba’en transmits the Dharma. Great assembly!"
Carry this burden together. (He throws down his whisk and descends from the seat. Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat:
Before the fifteenth day, there is spring chill and the sorrow of rain; after the fifteenth day, there is summer heat and the stinging breeze.
On the fifteenth day itself, the Chan practitioners within Baoen Monastery are neither cold nor hot; they are carefree and at ease. When hungry, there is food.
If you are thirsty, there is tea. Play in the monastery of Perfect Enlightenment; dwell in the samādhi of the wisdom of equality. I dare ask:
for what reason have you all reached such a state? Do you understand? Had it not been for the three times he offered his severed feet, how could the price of the city have become so much higher?
Ascending the hall: After the snow, rain falls for days on end; the cold wind sweeps across the earth. Within this—
There is nothing to grasp; he stands alone, embracing the cold and ice. The assembly, tell me:

what kind of person’s realm is this? Do you know? For nine years he faced the wall, yet no one recognized him; when the five-petaled flower blooms, its fragrance pervades the entire world. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
"Regarding the command that is not transgressed by clarity, is it permitted for others to attain awakening? The Master said: "That still falls into the secondary. The monk said: "If so, then..."
"Easy to open are the mouths from beginning to end; difficult to preserve is the heart through the cold of winter. The Master said, "Go out after receiving this instruction," and then added:

"In the first month of winter, a single herb and tree cause the entire forest to lose its luster. It is only because the frosty wind is as swift as a blade that, upon entering the green grove, they become withered leaves.
All people of the time are robbed by external conditions; even when their black crow is changed, they do not recognize it. If you wish to recognize it, how [can you?]"
"Wait until you come to question Maitreya. Aha ha! Do you see it? Do you see it? A yellow oriole perches upon a branch with a single flower;
a white egret descends into the field—a thousand dots of snow. Ascending the hall, he drew a circle in the air with his whisk and said, "Does the assembly see?"
On Vulture Peak, [the Buddha] spoke of Caoxi; at Cold Mountain, he made comparisons. Only Panshan said: "The moon of the mind is solitary and perfect; its light swallows the myriad phenomena.
The light does not illuminate objects, nor do objects exist. When both light and objects are forgotten, what is it? Holding up his whisk, he said, "A mirror.
When light and objects are not yet forgotten, what is it? Lowering the whisk, he said, "Blind! Do you still know Bao’en’s descent?
"Understand? If you truly understand, it will not hinder you from breaking your staff and hanging up your alms bowl; you may then follow circumstances with ease and wander at will as you please.
But if this is not yet the case, Baoen shall open another path for you. With his whisk, he makes the gesture of drawing a bowstring and says:
"Fullness and deficiency both lie within the two strings; concealment and manifestation return to the single reflection. [End]

The Hall Master raised the case: When the World-Honored One was first born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, walked seven steps, and looking around in the four directions, said, "In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am honored. Yunmen said, "If I had seen him at that time..."
"Strike him dead with one blow and feed him to the dogs; this is for the sake of peace throughout the world. The Master said:
"The World-Honored One founded the enterprise and established the legacy, transforming the myriad regions through the Way. How could he have anticipated that later generations would overturn it?

Yunmen has newly issued his phoenix calendar to sweep the universe clear, yet he has recklessly overturned the bequeathed regulations of his ancestors. Although he may thus glorify his predecessors and enrich his descendants—having both ancestor and descendant—"
If one examines the future, there will inevitably be self-inflicted suffering. Ultimately, how can one attain the state of being exactly right?

He then offered this verse: "Innate habitual tendencies are most difficult to forget; As soon as they emerge, their flames flare up fiercely. I thought no one could resist them," he said, "but now I see it is not so."
Who would have known that in later generations there would be Shao Yang? On the eighth day of the twelfth month, he ascended the hall; at the Snowy Mountains, he dismissed the assembly;
at Bao’en, he established the retreat. Two colors, one match; from beginning to end, they are not two. But tell me, what is the meaning of this "one match"?
Zhang’s sleeves are wide; Li’s hat brim is high. On his birthday, he ascended the hall: "The spring colors are harmonious, and one knows the scenery is new. Tender...
The scarlet blossoms and green birds add their voices; the old monk has no need for the effort of contrivance. For sixty years he has let things change as they will. Entering the hall:
The three springs have passed, and the early summer is at hand. Gathering our fellow disciples amidst the groves, we spread the true wind beyond the world.
We take up the seal of the uncarved mind and bring forth the vehicle of the extraordinary school. But tell me, what is this extraordinary school?
"Mounting—how do you lift it up? Is there anyone who can say it? After a long silence, he said: "The ears of wheat hang down; spring heat is pleasant.
The mouth of the bean flower spits out its pods before the heart. He ascended the hall and said: "A wild goose flies across the vast sky; its shadow sinks into the cold water.
A monk enters the treasure-place, traveling to transform beings according to the various directions. We do not prize empty rhetoric; we seek only the true and real. He then shook his whisk.
Dongye said: "Stop, stop! There is no need to speak. My Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive. Those with overweening pride will surely fail to respect and believe it upon hearing it.
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall: Within Guanghui Temple, the furnace is opened once more. Is there any true gold produced from the ore?
If you can directly and immediately give rise to no inverted views, I shall ensure that both the sentiments of the ordinary and the sage are withered away. Therefore, the ancients said:
When the sentiments of both ordinary and sage are exhausted, the true permanence is revealed; when phenomena and principle are non-dual, one is the Buddha of Suchness.
But tell me, where is the Buddha? A thousand tents in the north of the pass; ten-thousand-hu ships in the south of the river. Ascending the hall, he said:

"The winter retreat was entered late, and this spring the retreat is concluded early. One simply desires clarity regarding one's own matter; it matters not whether the period is extended or shortened. [He drew a Bodhisattva with his brush.]
Walking through fire; molding a Vajra from mud to sleep beneath the water. Without engaging in extraordinary deliberation, one has already attained the vision that transcends Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Hehehe! Do you understand? Unfasten the mouth of the cloth bag and let out the goose from the jar.

On the occasion of the New Year, he ascended the hall: "The New Year brings a myriad of auspicious things. Monks need not add further study; take it for granted that the eye pervades the entire body."
Chè. Why? Because he does not envy the iron ox plowing the dry land; he is accustomed to planting crabapples at the bottom of a well.
While residing at Qizhen Temple in Xiushui, he ascended the hall and said: "The lotus leaves are round, holding up emerald canopies; the lotus flowers are brilliant, vying with red makeup."
Its fragrant scent is extraordinary, yet no one offers it as tribute; it further draws the perfumed breeze across the wild pond.

Nevertheless, it is just like the Great Master Fu said: "Mount Sumeru is the father of the mustard seed; the mustard seed is the grandfather of Mount Sumeru. The mountains and waters are level and plain;
strike the ice to brew tea. Tell me, what matter does this clarify? Holding up his whisk, he said: "Do you understand? Old bones from years past. Dongwu.

A person asked this. [The Master] held it up; it strikes fear into those before one. He struck his whisk. While residing at Jianxi Shanguan Temple, he ascended the hall for the opening of the retreat.
"At Shanguan, we hold the winter retreat in the twelfth month; we do not follow the old precedents of other quarters, nor do we seek to put forth a singular innovation.
We simply wish for everyone to understand together. But tell me, how do you understand? In years past, Kāśyapa served Ānanda."
"Overturn the banner-pole in front of the gate; today, everyone together shall support it upright. To become a true descendant is not in vain. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The crow flies and the hare runs as swiftly as a shuttle. Brightness and darkness have never been able to obscure Him. Herein, from the beginning, there is nothing to be said;
yet to say 'there is nothing to be said' already constitutes much. He raised his whisk and said: "Tell me, assembly, is this..."
Some say there is something to be said; others say there is nothing to be said. [The Master] threw down his whisk and descended from the seat.

A monk asked, "How was it before Niu-t'ou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "A banquet is spread in the flower garden. The monk asked, "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "Thatched huts with sparse fences.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "The wind passes by, and the tree tops sway. A monk asked, "What is the One? The Master said—
[The monk] said, “A thief. [The monk] asked, “What makes a student of the Way a thief? The Master said, “To cry out for injustice while clutching stolen goods.
[The monk] asked, “Walking, standing, sitting, and lying down—none of these depart from this very thing. What, then, is ‘that’? The Master said, “I grant you thirty blows.
[The monk] asked, “Where does the fault lie? The Master said, “An empty target draws the arrow. [The monk] asked, “When one’s own kinsmen act as demons, what is that like? The Master said:
"I have only this talisman for protecting the body. [The monk] asked, "What is this talisman for protecting the body? The Master said, "Just raise it up like this.
The Master habitually used Mazu’s single shout that left Baizhang deaf for three days to test those who came to study under him;
few were able to grasp his essential point. In the seventh month of the Dingwei year of the Kangxi era, he manifested a slight illness. He sat upright until the end.
On the twenty-fifth day, at the hour of the *chen* (5–7 a.m.), he requested a bath and sat in meditation until his passing.

He had lived seventy-five years in the world and maintained fifty-six years of monastic seniority (*śrāmaṇera*). His disciple Gu Zhuojun escorted the reliquary casket to inter the entire body beneath Mount Pengtuan on Mount Jing.
Chan Master Tongqi of Tōngxuánlín in Tàizhōu Prefecture was the son of the Cǎi family of Hézhou in Shū.
From birth, he was serene and tranquil, and he took no pleasure in eating meat. His parents fulfilled his wish, commissioning him to become a novice under his uncle Dàorán at Jīnzhōng Temple.

At the age of seventeen, he shaved his head and received the precepts. By nature, he delighted in meditative stillness and grew weary of reciting scriptures. At nineteen, he was filled with profound resolve.

This stirred within him a longing for the mountains beyond. Consequently, he left the gorges to travel south. Having fully satiated himself with the lecture halls, he rested his shoulders by Lake Danghu.

He had just begun to expect to retreat into a room to peruse the temporal teachings when, suddenly, he suffered from dysentery and was on the verge of death. Only then did he realize that the study of sutras and śāstras was not the ultimate Dharma.
Just then, he received a copy of the verses on Zen meditation (chan) by Tian Tong, and a sense of doubt (yiqing) arose all at once. One day, he lost his footing.
He fell from the tower. Suddenly awakening, he composed a verse, saying: "Before the arising of a single thought, the six gates are cut off from all news.
In a flash, my two brows are raised; it seems as though my eyes lack strength. Thereupon, he broke through his barriers and went to study under Tiantong Wu at Wumen.
When Huineng went to Mount Mao, the Master also went there. It happened that a donor entered the mountain to offer tea.

Huineng raised the kōan regarding Dongshan’s giving fruit to the head seat Taishou and commanded the assembly to provide a response; he stipulated that only a precise and correct one would be accepted for recording.

At that time, the Master was among the assembly and immediately said, "The food has reached the edge of his mouth, yet it is snatched away by him. Huineng nodded his head in approval. Later, on the occasion of the Buddha’s birthday, Huineng...
Addressing the assembly, the Master said: "As soon as the World-Honored One emerged from his mother’s womb, he already knew how to point to heaven and point to earth.

You people here are still trying to pry something out of this mountain monk—what a shallow bowl you seek! [With these words,] he seized his staff, descended from the seat, and struck everyone down at once, dispersing them.
From that time on, the Master was completely liberated. One day, while taking oil from the storehouse with a broken bowl, Wuzhuo asked him: 'Why did you break the monastery's property?'"
The bowl. The Master said, "This is not the one I broke. Wuzhuo said, "Why is it in your hands?

The Master said, "When the city gate catches fire, the disaster reaches the fish in the pond. Wuzhuo said, "I have lost the bowl and must pay for it. The Master then opened both hands. Wuzhuo withdrew.
In the *guīwèi* year of the Chongzhen era, he resided at Tongxuan on Mount Tiantai; subsequently, he lived at Qizhen at Dongta in Jiahe; later, he moved...
At Tiantong, ascending the hall on the Buddha’s Birthday:
"In the past, when our Buddha was born, he took his bath in a golden basin and immediately pointed at heaven and earth, appearing quite shameless. He further declared, 'Only I am honored.
This mountain monk does not yet dare grant him permission. But tell me, what longings does this mountain monk have that he can open such a wide mouth? [He] then struck with his staff."
One scholar said: "Do not plant thorns by the gate; later generations' descendants will have their clothes snagged.
When Master Fei of Jinxu was invited to ascend the hall, [the Master said]: "Before arriving at this realm, one shifts the boat to familiarize oneself with the currents;
once arrived at this realm, one forgets the other waves. When kinsmen of the same school meet unexpectedly, there is no need to lift the eyes to arrange guests."
"Master, let us joyfully practice together and sit together. The tune of the stringless lute must be harmonized in unison.

But tell me, how is the tune of the stringless lute harmonized? Suddenly, he took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "Everyone who strikes their eyes is a Ziqi; why should there not be another melody?
He struck it once more, descended from the seat, and departed. Upon returning from a journey, he ascended the hall and said: "In the past, the Fifth Patriarch..."
The Way. Having been out the door for half a month, my eyes could not see my own nostrils; I forgot the Zen of the Patriarchs and picked up a piece of junk.
Now tell me, where shall it be placed? "One part I offer to Śākyamuni Buddha; one part I offer to the Stūpa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha.
When the Fifth Patriarch spoke thus, he was truly clutching an empty fist to deceive small children. As for me, the mountain monk, I do not...
Nevertheless, more than two months after leaving the gate, my two eyes were able to see again. I do not prize the Chan of the Patriarchs; taking a step is quite light and easy.
In truth, I went empty-handed and returned empty-handed. But tell me, how far apart was I from the Fifth Patriarch?
Is there anyone who can judge this? If you can judge it, you may pass your days in peace. If you cannot judge it, [then consider] the flask and bowl.
Hanging high on the corner of the meditation seat: swallow the *liji* thorn with fierce force. On the anniversary of the Patriarch’s passing, he ascended the hall:
To say there is birth is already a deception; to further say there is no birth is even more remote. If both these secure barriers can be kicked away—
Just as one is about to offer tea to the former Master, brothers, tell me: has the former Master come or not?
If you say he has come, by what means would you verify it? If you say he has not come, then the offering becomes a mere empty formality. At this point, how do you resolve it?
After a long silence, he said: "One does not know the depth of winter's cold until after the twelfth lunar month. The senior monks of this mountain requested that I ascend the hall.
Yesterday, when I arrived here, I already ascended the seat; now I have ascended once more. Yet, I have never yet uttered a word regarding the mutual encounter between host and guest.
"It would not do to leave this unexplained; let me break it down for you once more. [The Master] suddenly picked up his staff and said, "Tell me, is this the guest or the host?

If you perceive this as a meeting between guest and host, you are merely pressing on your eyes until flowers appear. If you do not perceive it as a meeting between guest and host, you are still putting grit in your eye.
Even if you were neither of these, it would still be the view of a wild fox. So tell me, what is it ultimately?"
He then threw down his staff and called out loudly to his attendant, saying, "Bring it back for this old monk. Ascending the hall, he raised the following case:
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? Yunmen replied, "A sesame cake.
Now tell me, does Yunmen’s answer in this way contain the principle of transcending Buddhas and patriarchs, or not? If you say there is, it is precisely...
To slander the former sages by claiming they did not exist is, moreover, to bury one’s own spirit. How would you judge this public case?
"Where the land of Wu ends at the river, beyond the bank are many mountains of Yue. Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "In the past, I studied Confucianism;
recently, I have donned the black robes to study Buddhism. Although Confucianism and Buddhism are different, he suddenly took up his staff and said: 'It does not go beyond this.'"

Newsflash. Is there anyone among the assembly present here who does not involve themselves with either Confucianism or Buddhism? Again, he strikes the sounding block once and says: "Lifting one's head to look beyond the heavens—who is a person like me?
Ascending the hall for the summer retreat, [the Master] said: "The ancients said:
'The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs resembles the mechanism of an iron ox. If you go toward it, it seals you; if you stay still, it breaks you. Such is the manner of upholding it."
"It is like scratching an itch through a boot; what pleasure is there in it? I, this mountain monk, dare say:
the Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox—it does not seal you when you depart, nor does it break when you stay. Departure and staying depend on you to avoid error.
Do you all accept this? If you do not yet accept it, then beneath the three rafters and upon the seven-foot mat..."

Previously, when I took my seat upon the high platform at the conclusion of the summer retreat (*varṣā*), I told you all to strive for realization; this was much like a clever child falling into a trap.

Even if you were to banish the intellect and forget the emotions, how could that compare to the peace of simply letting go? Today, the mouth of the sack is opened; let it be as it may whether you head south or north.
Nevertheless, you must first grant it your own consent. Why? Because "after a character has been written three times, it becomes a crow. (烏)
"How is a horse completed? [He] ascended the hall and said: "I have a single phrase that pervades heaven and covers the earth. I present it to you all; do not attempt to deliberate upon it.
Tell me, O assembly, what phrase is this? He then descended from his seat. While residing at Tiantong, he ascended the hall and said:
"In recent years, my disciples have galloped in all four directions, exhausting yourselves with toil, yet in the end it has been of no benefit. You do not realize that every person..."
There is a single sitting mat upon which not even a hair’s breadth has ever been lacking.
It is only because the title deed is not clear that one cannot enjoy its use. I, this mountain monk, have long examined the title deed. Again, he raises his whisk and says:
"Today, before this assembly, I reveal it to you. You must urgently realize it! If you can realize it here, you will understand all interpenetration."

Functioning thus, the small and the great are mutually integrated; entering and exiting without difficulty, one sports with sovereign ease. If you miss this opportunity now, regret will be difficult to undo.
Moreover, we encounter a time of peace and prosperity, where the noble and influential provide protection, the common people rejoice, and humans and devas share in celebration.
For the benefit of self and others, there is nothing that is not appropriate. Yet tell me: how do you express the phrase "knowing gratitude and repaying kindness"? Mount [Name].
In my chamber, I rest in peace with no other concerns; throughout the long day, I burn incense to celebrate the Great Peace. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:

"If you wish to recognize the face before birth, do not engage in prior reflections or subsequent calculations. Simply be able to still your thoughts and forget external conditions; then, at every turn, everything will be revealed."
Self and others are not separated by so much as a hair’s breadth; from beginning to end, they do not depart from the present moment.

Great assembly, do not seek Chang’an within the Hanyuan Palace, nor hope for rebirth in the Inner Court within the palace of Maitreya. [The Master] then struck the meditation seat and descended. Ascending the hall:
The spring light is brilliant and the harmonious atmosphere is pervasive. In every dharma and at every point, nothing is an external object. This matter...
Coming without interval—why must one rank host and guest? The ten characters unfold as eight, their brilliance overflowing the eyes throughout the entire world.
To "point" is to fail to reach; to "approach intimately" is to be unable to attain it. To "reach" is to fail to point; to be "distant" is to have more than enough.

If you hesitate with bowed head, you cannot avoid being obscured right before your own face. Now tell me: what is the single phrase of non-dual integration where host and guest are not established? It is like...
How is it displayed? "The moon over every household in the Chang'an market; frogs in the spring grass by every pond. Entering the hall, [the Master said]:

"In the past, beneath the assembly of our former teacher, ten thousand fingers surrounded him; those who soaked themselves in the flavor of the Dharma were many. Who among you most urgently pursues the milk of the Dharma?
This mountain monk raises up Prajñā to repay the incomparable kindness of my former teacher. It may be said that where there is resentment..."
The principal debt has a creditor. This one phrase from the past that gained power transcends both present and antiquity.
But tell me, what kind of phrase is it? [He suddenly grasps his staff, strikes it once on the ground, and says: "Do you all understand? No one recognized the merit of his past labor;
he simply wished to re-examine his epoch-making achievement. On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and held up his staff, saying: "Last year’s year..."

In the morning, he took up his brush and with a single stroke wrote out the entirety of the Tripitaka. Although the literary brilliance was fully manifested, the tip of the brush had not yet been released.
This year at the New Year, taking up his brush, he drew a single line and said: "With a single stroke, I have written out the entire Confucian canon.

Although the tip of the brush has now been released, ultimately the literary brilliance has not yet appeared. Now tell me: regarding the principles within these two, is there a distinction of superiority or inferiority?
[He said: "There is none. He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, the Mountain Monk said, "My four elements are not robust; I am unable to preach the Dharma for the assembly.
He then took up his staff and said, "Only this wooden senior monk (the staff), though it has no apertures at all, is able to skillfully expound the essentials of the Dharma.
Striking the incense table, he said, "Do not follow its delusions and inversions. He addressed the assembly: "The Dharmakāya, the Sambhogakāya, and the Nirmāṇakāya..."
"The body—this mountain monk has threaded it all onto a single string. Although this is so, it is extremely concise; it spares everyone from groping about in the dark. "The assembly, how joyful!
Suddenly, he took up his staff, struck it once on the ground, and said: "A praiseworthy qilin has but a single horn.
When the Master reached the outer gate of the monastery, he saw several monks standing there. He asked them, "Do not stand either inside the gate or outside the gate. The monks all...
[The monk] remained silent. The Master said, "Lately the mountain has been overgrown with weeds.

As soon as the monk entered the gate, the Master seized him by the collar and said, "Try to utter a single phrase from a place where the mind's machinations and conscious awareness do not fall. The monk was about to reach out his hand when the Master gave him a shove and said, "Do not engage in idle conceptualization.
The Master asked Yin Yue-lin: "When you see the moon, cease looking at the finger; once you have returned home, stop [seeking]."
Cheng asked, "What is the one phrase for returning home? Yunlin then shouted. Cheng said, "A good slap would have been appropriate.
Yunlin said, "Please rise, Master. Cheng raised his staff; Yunlin then departed. Another asked, "I do not ask about movement and stillness;
what is 'not a single thought arising'? The Master said, "Shattered into a hundred pieces. The monk asked, "How can one cut off the life-root? The Master said, "Stop."
Zhao Li asked, "I do not ask about the summit of Jinxu Mountain; how is it at the peak of Tongxuan? The Master said, "It would freeze one to death.
The monk said, "Today I have finally met the Master. The Master said, "What is it like? The monk snapped his fingers.
The Master said, "You have mistaken the zero point on the scale. Later, while the Master was meeting with the layman Wang Haixian, the official... [text ends]
[The official] said, "Is it the Southern manner of greeting or the Northern manner? The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, cannot provide an explanation.
The official was at a loss. The Master said, "Please bow. [The official] asked, "Is it the superior seat or the inferior seat? The Master said, "Neither end is appropriate;
even the middle way is not settled. The official said, "Please come outside. The Master said, "What kind of place is this? To speak of 'inside' and 'outside'—it is too little."
Recently, the Duke asked, "When Nanquan smashed the rice-pot, what was his meaning? The Master said, "It is enough to cause doubt.

The Duke asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master snapped his fingers. The Duke asked, "Is there anything more? The Master then gave him a slap. The Master traveled to Lou-dong. An old woman came to consult him.
A gentleman standing by the side said, "This old woman has recently applied her mind to this Way. She has..."
As she was entering, the nun said, "The Master naturally possesses the eye; why do you need such a talkative layman?
The Master said, "It is difficult to deceive one who knows the local terrain. The nun said, "The Master is also included within that. The Master said, "I, the old monk, am not of your kind.
The nun said, "Today I have caught the Master out," and she swept her sleeves and departed. The Master said, "The old monk has suffered a loss."

On the nineteenth day of the third month in the Renchen year of the Shunzhi era, as the Master was about to pass away, the Head Seat asked, "When the ancients faced their final moments, they would leave behind a word or a phrase to serve as an eye for the future. What instruction do you have to leave behind now?
The Master said, "To move is to invite calamity. The Head Seat said, "The official allows not even a needle; yet in private, carriages and horses pass through. The Master said, "Too many words."
"What do you say? he asked. [The monk] replied, "It is not an extra burden. The Master struck him in the face with a fist. The monk then prostrated himself.

When the assembly requested a verse for his departure from this world, the Master glared at them and said, "If you want to go, then go! What a burning fever! At that time, there was an elder named Chuyue who sought a new name.
The Master took up his brush and wrote the two characters "Xingguo" (Fruit of Practice). He then said, "The fruit of practice is perfected," and finally cast down the brush. He passed away upright.
He passed away while seated. His secular age was fifty-eight, and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇeraka-vaṣa) was forty-one.
His entire body was interred in a stupa beneath the Linglong Rock at the left side of the New Hermitage in his home temple. Shanweng Min composed the inscription for the stupa.
Zen Master Linao Benyu of Zhulin in the Prefecture of Zhenjiang was a dharma successor of Zen Master Xiu of Qingshan. He was the son of the Chen family of Kunshan.

At the age of seven, he paid respects to the elder master Zhanchuan of Yao Peak and left the household life. After receiving full ordination, he traveled extensively throughout various regions to study under masters, eventually visiting Boshan Yuanlai. Yuanlai said to him:
[Zhao] Lái said, "Not yet placed in a golden cage, whose wild sparrow is this? The Master said, "A crane soars through the blue sky from the nine ravines;
a horse that lacks the thousand-li stride merely chases the wind in vain. Lái said, "If one applies the adze without being at the Yǐng Gate, one cannot avoid leaving scars.

The assembly was filled with grief and longing. The administrator said, "The mountain master has gone elsewhere and has not yet returned; we pray that the Venerable Master will delay for one more day.

Chan Master Wenda of Ri’an on Nanjian Mountain in Hangzhou Prefecture,
the thirty-fourth generation descendant of Nanyue and dharma heir of Chan Master Xiu of Qingshan, was born in Wujiang. His family had resided for generations in Jingxi.

His father, Xu Changyu, was a retired scholar who, in his later years, lamented having no son. He established a hundred-day *wu-cha* (unrestricted) assembly as a prayer for offspring, and [the Master] was born in response to that petition.
In his youth, he roamed the groves of arts and exhaustively investigated the principles of the mind and nature. Once, while visiting a mountain temple, he read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.

Upon reaching the passage stating that this body and mind, as well as all things external down to empty space, mountains, rivers, and the great earth, are all objects within the wondrously luminous true nature, he had a realization.
This triggered his realization. He went to visit Qingshan Xuyun, who assigned him the koan regarding the state before one's parents were born.

Later, due to the intense pressure of an arranged marriage, he fled under the cover of night. Upon reaching Wulin, he shaved his head under Master Fayu, but soon returned to Qingshan. There he practiced with morning inquiries and evening knocks.
One night, hearing a great wind crashing against the cliffs, he attained enlightenment. He composed a verse which says: "A thousand origins and ten thousand wonders are veiled by layers upon layers."
Within this state, no self-interest is tolerated; it is a melody upon a single-stringed zither, blown by the cold winds of the fifth watch over a frozen cliff.
Xiu said, "I do not ask about the primordial mystery; how is it that there is a phrase that is not separated [from reality]? As the Master prepared to respond, Xiu struck him.

He served with diligence for several more years until he thoroughly penetrated the Great Dharma. Xiu then certified his realization with a verse, which included the line: "In another life, he shall arise from my presence."
Regarding the phrase from the Ji lineage, "Killing and enlivening, moving freely to open the Tianmu eyes":
later, having received his formal training at Shunshi, he was invited by the gentry and officials of Wulin to return to Nanjian, where he served as the first patriarch to transmit the Dharma.

The Master said, “Please have some tea first. [Xueqiao] said, “A true adept. The Master said, “When meeting people, take care not to misrepresent [the teaching].

The Master said, "How many people have misunderstood the Great Master’s meaning? Xinxing said, "Even if they did not misunderstand, they would still be far from it.

Zhizhi pointed with his staff and said, "Clouds arise over there. Suddenly he threw it down and said, "A single rain nourishes all.
On the anniversary of Master Shouye’s death, I offer incense. Having stumbled while crossing a bridge, one picks up a bright pearl from a heap of refuse;

rubbing it, light is produced. In the bathhouse, one pushes aside a lacquer bucket. Although father and son are simultaneous, when examined closely, they instead become outsiders. How can this compare to—?

Ultimately, how is it? He performs a woman’s bow and says: "The tea pours from the summit of the cave; the incense burns the *jīsū*."
Ascending the hall, [a monk] asked: "In years past on this very day he departed; now the first anniversary has already passed.

"Since he is one who is brilliant and penetrating on all eight sides, why must he borrow your nostrils to breathe? The Master said: "You have not yet become his descendant. [The monk] said: "Today we are busy..."
[The Master] was observing the fast. [The monk asked,] "Will you come back to receive the offerings? The Master said, "I will come as soon as you can say something.

The monk then said, "I am born of the same root as the bamboo grove, but I do not die of the same root as the bamboo grove. It is easy to be born of the same root; it is difficult to die of the same root."

It is easy to die with those who are not of the same lineage; it is difficult to die with those who are of the same lineage. When dying with those of the same lineage, thousands or ten thousand people are revived all at once.
