Now, on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, each of you must utter a phrase for turning about. If you can speak such a phrase, then upon this seat there will be no mountain monk.
In the past, there were no *ācāryas*. If you say [the Dharma] cannot be attained, then this mountain monk is simply this mountain monk, and the *ācārya* is simply the *ācārya*.
Time passes away like flowing water; how can we fail to live up to the single-minded resolve of these three winter months? [This was the] evening instruction. Everywhere else they sell honey.
Jin-su sells gallnuts. Although buying and selling are one and the same, there is sweetness and bitterness therein.
That which is sweet is easy to consume; that which is bitter is difficult to bring to the mouth. Once it enters the mouth, the bitterness ends and the sweetness comes forth, its flavor lasting long.

Ascending the hall to preach the precepts: In the age of antiquity, transformation occurred without words, governance was achieved without administration, retribution was meted out without punishment, and rewards were bestowed without merit.
I exhort you: when the people commit transgressions, I used to mark them with circles of ash to restrain them. Today, I, this mountain monk, shall also make several circles.
When you are asleep, I give you one circle; when you are awake, I give you one circle;
when you put on your clothes, I give you one circle; when you eat your meal, I give you one circle; and when you defecate or urinate, I give you one circle.
When you lift your feet and take a step, I give you a circle (○). Holding up his staff, he said, "Elder, why do you use so many circles?
He forbids you from leaping about. What is it like when you do not leap about at all? The subsequent text is long; it is entrusted for another day. Question:
Great spiritual friend, your compassion is inexhaustible. For those on the stage of learning, awakening is the goal.
"I do not yet understand: do you still permit students to attain awakening? The Master said, "How long has it been since you were lost in delusion? (This refers to Shanseng Min’s successor.
Chan Master Dian’an Xu of the Precepts Platform in the Capital ascended the hall and said: "A black lacquer leather lantern lacks a single dot in its center.
If there is anyone who can provide the spark, I will give them a coin of great light. He struck his staff on the ground and said, "Is there anyone here to provide the spark?"

"Ma! After a long silence, he whirled his staff like a whirlwind and drove them all away. In the Jiachen year of the Kangxi era, the Master was serving as the head seat under [Master] Min at Jinsu Monastery.
One day, he suddenly took leave of the assembly and sat down peacefully to pass away (Master Min, known as Shanweng, was his successor).
Chan Master Qianchao Ming of Taicang ascends the hall: The gourd is curved and winding; the winter melon is straight and blunt.

It is laughable that people of this age have no reason [to understand], debating straightness and curvature without ever reaching a conclusion. This is enough to provoke the Heavenly King to clench his fists in rage.
Maitreya laughed incessantly. [Zhaozhou] struck his staff and said, "In the end, what is it? "The gourd is curved;
the winter melon is straight. (Shanweng Min was his successor.)
Chan Master Yuan’an Fu of Ruiyan in Ningbo was the son of the Lu family of Kunshan. He received the tonsure at Tiantong and attained the Dharma under Guangrun.
He first resided at Shending in Changsha and later succeeded to the seat at Tiantong. Ascending the hall, he said:
"For a long time it has been dry and parched, with not a trace of flavor; these past days have been soaked with water, so there is quite a bit to taste."
If you seek flavor in places where there is something to be tasted, though the delicacies may be exquisite, they will merely satisfy the appetite but not nourish the person.
If, however, you bite down once upon a place where there is no flavor, hunger and emptiness will be instantly stilled, and the natural state of perpetual seeking will be forever severed.
"Arriving here, it is neither mind nor Buddha. Upon the plum branches, the moon of the third watch; for every statement made, another is overturned.
The red dust beneath the sea cannot fly away. I announce to all you people: you must fiercely and resolutely open the eye of time.
If you wish to penetrate the pure barrier on the other side, you must truly possess a single iron bar ten thousand miles long. [He ascended the hall. Xiangyan said:
Poverty last year was not yet true poverty; poverty this year is only then true poverty. Last year’s poverty, one still had enough ground to set a single awl into;
this year’s poverty, there is not even enough ground for an awl to be set. True Purity (Zhenjing) said: Wealth last year was not yet true wealth;
wealth this year is only then true wealth. Last year’s wealth, one possessed only a single black woolen robe; this year’s wealth, one has added to it—[a second].
A single thread of water-dyed *kāṣāya* robe; at the turn of the year, he donned it upon the precious king’s throne.
One must believe that this *fengluo* (spontaneous expression) flows from within the house. Chushi said: "Xiangyan’s poverty is not yet true poverty, for he still possesses a whole body.
Zhenjing’s wealth is not yet true wealth, for he has revealed his entire household property. Fengshan says neither of wealth nor of poverty; he follows the abundance of his own house.

When Jie was about to pass away, he distanced himself from his relatives. Holding up his fly-whisk, he said: "When gathered in, the rabbit's horn is three feet long; when let go, the tortoise's hair weighs nine catties.
The Master [Zhaozhou] said: "Xiangyan speaks of poverty; here there is not even two taels of silver.

Zhenjing speaks of wealth; the common man buys three sheng of wine. Fengshan neither speaks of wealth nor speaks of poverty—this too is merely covering one's ears while stealing a bell. How can it compare to...?
A flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech; clever words are not as good as the direct path. But tell me: how is it here at Tiantong? Listen to this verse:
"In extreme poverty, one still laments that a thousand mouths are too few; In times of wealth, one simply rejoices that there is not a single coin."
"It is not a matter of being essential or different from other regions; whether poor or rich has never resided in the mind.
A monk asked, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? The Master said, "What are you saying? When the monk repeated his question, the Master said, "Old fellow Meng!
The Master then picked up a bamboo stick and said, "Now tell me, does this bamboo stick have Buddha-nature? The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master then struck him.
[The Master] struck him. A monk standing nearby said, "That was quite a slip. The Master struck again and said, "A talkative old fellow! A monk asked, "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas;
why was he unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi? The Master said, "Gold cannot purchase gold.

The monk asked, "Wangming is a Bodhisattva of the first stage (Prathamabhūmi); why was he able to emerge? The Master said, "Look for the hole to drive the wedge through. The monk asked, "As for the woman’s own state..."
"Furthermore, how is it? The Master said, "Even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.
A monk asked, "Regarding what Yantou said, 'The great Deshan has not yet realized the final word. What is the final word? The Master said, "I will tell you thirty years from now.
[The monk] said, "Yantou secretly revealed its meaning. What is this secret revelation of its meaning? The Master said, "Just so."
A wooden peg was inserted into a round hole. [The Master] said, "Tomorrow, Deshan will ascend the seat; it will indeed be different from usual. Where can you see this?
The monk replied, "It would change your very eyes. As the monk hesitated, the Master gave a shout. The monk bowed, and the Master said:
"I was born of the same lineage as Yantou; I shall not die of the same lineage as Yantou. How do you understand this?
He replied, "I am currently in doubt about the Master. The Master said, "Set aside for a moment my being doubted. But when all the people in the world doubt you, what then?"
As a monk was about to offer words [of inquiry], the Master said: "A hawk flies over Silla. The Master resided at Tiantong for several years, where disciples gathered like clouds.
Later, he retired to Ruiyan and passed away. The deep mountains and remote valleys were once again transformed into a new realm.
He entered nirvana in the fourth month of the Renxu year of the Kangxi era; his secular age was sixty-one, and his monastic seniority was forty. His disciples enshrined him in a stupa.

At the foot of Mount Sanshuxiong to the left of the temple (where Shanweng Min succeeded), Master Wuan Benyuan of Wanshou Monastery at Daochang in Huzhou addressed the assembly: "Yesterday was the heart of a yakṣa;
today is the face of a bodhisattva. With the heart of a yakṣa and the face of a bodhisattva, they emerge in their very essence, not separated by so much as a thread. At this moment, if..."
Failing to investigate the root source, one辜负 (fails) the single-minded heart of the Patriarchs. "Great assembly, tell me: what is the heart of the Patriarchs?
Raising his whisk, he said: "Quickly, you must turn your eyes to look at the immortal; do not look at the fan in the immortal’s hand. To the assembly:
"The earthen ox bellows and the mountains and rivers run; the wooden horse neighs and heaven and earth darken. At midnight, the Persian chews raw meat."
"Iron! [The Master] plucks away his nostrils and puts down his chopsticks. Striking the whisk, he says: "The celestial Qilin has but one horn.
Evening Assembly: "The cup falls to the ground; the dish shatters into seven pieces. It is the sword that kills and the sword that gives life.
If you hesitate for even a moment, it will strike you through and through. He plants his staff on the ground and says: "This is the sword that kills. What is the sword that gives life?"
"Quick! Quick! No one spoke. The Master struck them all at once with his staff and dispersed them. Small Assembly Sermon: Bodhidharma did not understand Zen;
Confucius did not know how to read. The mountain gate seizes the tiger’s head; the lantern gathers the tiger’s tail. Hanshan and Shide fall over laughing.
Ultimately, what is the essential principle? He let out a shout and said: "A sudden clap of thunder—there is no time to cover one's ears."
Addressing the assembly, he asked: "The golden needle and jade thread pierce through the five-colored auspicious qilin; the silver hook and iron strokes embroider the jeweled palace and flower crown.
At this very moment when the way of sovereign and subject is in harmony, I ask the Master to bring it forth.

The Master said: "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. [The student] said: "Setting aside the banners and spears, what is 'the partial within the central'? The Master said: "The dawn at Chang'an."
"Who can harmonize with form? [The Master replied: "The bright moon and the reeds nod in the dark. [The student] asked, "What is 'correctness within partiality'?
The Master said, "Concealing strategy and artifice, one returns to the True Transformation; a single arrow hits the red heart, never missing. [The student] asked, "What is 'coming from the center'?
The Master said, "A single orb in the azure sky, white with the clouds; its pure radiance above and below penetrates the Great Void. [The student] asked, "What is..."

"This is 'reaching within the simultaneous' (jiānzhōng zhì). The Master said, "Inverting the application and deploying horizontally, the full imperial decree is issued; the dragon roars and the tiger howls as they pass through the Pass of Qin. [The student] asked, "What is 'arriving within the simultaneous' (jiānzhōng dào)?
The Master said, "Hiding his flower crown, he sits amidst the charcoal; from time immemorial we have lived together, yet you do not know his name.
[The student] said, "If that is so, then the spring colors of the imperial palace come forth across heaven and earth; the roses fill the trellises throughout the entire courtyard."
The incense has departed. The Master said, "A jet-black Qunlun spirit lifts up a pillar. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. Then, planting his staff, he said:
"Startling that jet-black Qunlun, he strips off his mother-born cloth trousers; he pulls apart golden needles and jade threads, failing to dwell in the immortal palace of Penglai.
He suddenly crosses over from this eastern land to the western heavens, riding backward upon a horned, fierce tiger, charging forth."
He broke through the iron wall and silver mountain; the bright sun stood high at noon.
He then looked at the assembly and said, "Right now, when both function and status are hidden, where can you meet this mountain monk’s staff? After a long pause, he gave a shout and said:
"It is easier to turn stones into gold and jade than it is to advise people to eliminate their right and wrong. Early morning assembly. The assembly gathered. He held up his staff.

Holding his staff, he looked silently east and west and said, "Watch your step. The assembly hesitated; he struck the ground once more with the staff and said, "After three transcriptions, the characters 'wu' and 'an' become 'ma'.
He then returned to the abbot’s quarters. In a small-scale discourse (*xiaocan*), he asked the assembly: "The sword leaves its precious scabbard because of injustice;
the medicine comes from the golden jar to save the sick. But tell me: when the four elements are fundamentally empty and the five aggregates do not exist, where is the sickness?"
"From where does it come? The assembly offered various responses, none of which were correct. The Master then provided his own substitute answers, saying: "The sweet melon is sweet from stem to tip;
the bitter gourd is bitter from root to fruit. He further said: "All are moistened by the same rain and grow in the same soil; why then is that which is sweet naturally sweet?"
"Suffering is self-inflicted. A monk said, "In the spring colors there is no high or low; the flower branches are simply short or long.
The Master said, "If that is so, since the spring colors have no high or low and the flower branches are simply short or long, for what reason is there 'acceptance' and 'non-acceptance'?
The monk bowed. The Master struck him, saying, "Why do you not say: 'The handle of the ladle is in the hands of the Abbot'? *Small Assembly Sermon.* The assembly gathered.

The prostrations were performed unevenly. The Master rebuked them, saying: "Seven rises and eight inversions! Rain beating the banana leaves—the east wind shakes them eastward, the west wind shakes them westward.
You lot, you lacquer buckets! I shall not break your waists. He took up his staff, drove them all away at once, and returned to the abbot’s quarters (Master Mǎnshāng was the successor).
Chan Master Xinghua Longzhu Senjianche was the son of the Xu family from Chaozhou in Guangdong.

After receiving the tonsure, he went to Zhuan’u Heng to receive full ordination and was instructed to visit Tiantong. Upon first meeting him, [Tiantong] asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Guangdong."
Wu said, "Once you pass the Mei Ling Pass, it is Guangdong. The Master asked, "Have you ever been there, Monk?
Wu replied, "I left home at thirty years of age; how could I have had the leisure to travel idly? Upon hearing this, the Master was struck with awe and attained realization.
He went to visit Bao Hua Ren and asked, "The fragrant breeze comes from the south, and the halls and pavilions grow cool. How do you understand this? The Master replied:
"How refreshing! Linji said. Baizhang Huai-ren asked, "What about the cypress tree in the courtyard? The Master replied, "I have never had eyes that see flowers.
Huai-ren took up his staff, struck once, and asked, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. Huai-ren struck him, saying, "How refreshing!
Later, the Master followed Xuedou Cong-meng at Guangrun Temple. One day, Meng asked, "A person whose entire body is a mouth—why can they not speak?"

[The Master asked about] the teacher’s surname. The teacher said, “Traditionally, a filial son avoids pronouncing his father’s name. One day, while picking tea, Mian said, “The direct source of the root is what the Buddhas have certified;
why do you pick leaves and seek branches? The teacher immediately called out in a loud voice, “Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is coming!
Mian nodded in approval. [He then ascended the hall for the "Period of the Withered Tree. He sat peacefully for six years on the Snow Mountains.
Zen. At Shaolin, [Bodhidharma] sat facing the wall for nine years; Longzhu set a period of a thousand days. It was simply that they sought to harmonize with the models of antiquity and the present.
Thus it is said: "If one does not cry out for three years, when one cries out, it startles the world. If one does not fly for three years, when one flies, one pierces the heavens.

To pierce the heavens, one must have the will to pierce the heavens; to startle the world, one must have the phrase that startles the world. If you possess the phrase that startles the world, the void is pulverized.
"Crushed! Possessing the will to soar to the heavens, the great earth sinks level. When the great earth sinks level, the paths of the mundane and the sagely are cut off.
When empty space is pulverized, both the primordial and the wondrous are forgotten. Reaching this point, there is a mountain of Iron Encircling Mountains;

you must all exert your own strength. To break through it is to be a true adept. He surveyed the great assembly for a long while and said: "At the place where one enters directly with a single blade, do not..."

To record the meritorious achievements, he ascends the hall. He takes up the trident and armor of the Three Mysteries, arrays the banners and spears of the Five Ranks, deploys the great formation of the ten thousand dharmas that leave nothing confused, and opens the great path of achieving success through non-action.

To directly seize the wondrous station of the Peerless, one must recognize the commander-in-chief of the central army: what is his surname? What is his name? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! A monk enters for an audience. The Master says:
Question: "Where have you come from? He replied: "From Baoen. The Master said: "How many hairs are there on Baoen’s eyebrows? He replied: "The same as the Master's. The Master said:
"Then tell me, how many hairs are there on this mountain monk’s eyebrows? The monk was speechless. (This case is from Shanweng Myn, who succeeded [to the lineage]).
Chan Master Yunso of Longya in Tanzhou was a native of Anlu in Chu. He did not disclose his clan or lineage.
Having received full ordination at Daguang Miao, he entered the gate of Helin [Xuedou] and attained a deep realization. Later, while following Master Yiweng Min at Qingzhou, he received the Dharma.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "In this way, in this way—where there is nothing of a hair’s breadth or a speck of dust—it is like mountains and peaks. Not in this way, not in this way..."

"Ma! In a place as vast as mountains and peaks, there is not even a hair’s breadth or a speck of dust. Within suchness, there is no suchness; let loose a hair’s breadth and there is no path left for obstruction.
Yet within non-suchness, there is suchness; remove the mountains and peaks, and there is more than enough spaciousness.
Holding up his staff, he said: "Mountains and peaks, hairs and specks—all are upon the tip of this staff. Do you see? If you see, take it up!"
"Go! If you do not see [it], I shall discipline you, press you down, and obstruct you until you are killed! Evening Sermon: The Founder-Dharma-Hero of this mountain, Tunchu, said:
"I traveled to famous mountains throughout the world because of my feet; after many years of hardship, they were worn through like socks.
Now that I am old and can no longer walk, I hold in my hand a broken wooden ladle. The Master said: "This mountain monk lives in his temple and uses his ladle."

Although we generally support our families in the same way, our paths are nonetheless distinct. Reaching every famous mountain without moving a foot, one steps upon the high and low, the near and far, at every turn.
Now, residing in this monastery, I am ashamed to lack such merit; with feet in straw sandals and hands holding a ladle, I address the assembly because of the snow.
Last night the heavy snow fell in profusion; by dawn it still does not cease. Three feet of it covers the level ground.
One foot, two feet. Piled high like mountains, pressing down upon the trees; each one encircling the earth and filling the heavens.

Not a single fragment falls elsewhere. To Manjusri’s eyes, it adds a speck of grit; to Samantabhadra’s pores, it gathers dust. The more one exerts oneself to shovel and sweep, the more it increases. Hanshan and Shide are greatly incensed.
It adds countless pearls to Yangqi’s bedside, scattering them wildly until a Great One emerges.
Gazing up at the lion in the courtyard before him, its cold majesty was fearsome. Longya pursued the pack with a roar; as the song was sung, snowflakes flew.
Then, striking his whisk, he chanted: "The wind is piercingly cold; the fisherman rows his boat, standing upon the waves. At times he grips the line and hauls in the hook;
mostly it is the cold river and the snow. This was the evening *can*. "It is not mind. It has been scorched by the sun and blown by the wind since antiquity."

"Up to the present, it is not the Buddha; Śākyamuni and Maitreya are merely muddying the waters together. It is not a thing; ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences emerge from this. [The Master] throws down his staff and asks:
"As for the meaning of 'The monk’s robe from Qingzhou weighs seven pounds,' what is its intent?

The Master says: "It is cold as ice in the lands north of the Great Wall. The student says: "I do not understand. The Master says: "The northern wind cannot blow through it. [The Master] addresses the assembly:
Upon entering the gate, he strikes with the staff; a thousand ends are settled at once. He shouts directly into one’s face; the clouds part and the sun shines forth. He raises a single finger;
it penetrates from top to bottom. He rolls out three balls; principle is perfected and affairs are complete.
As for the rest—those who strike the ground, those who hold up the pitchfork, those who brandish the ritual tablet, and those who draw the bow—all these old fellows are nothing but...
Supported by power, one carries the whole body upon the shoulders; yet, this too only reaches this point. Although it is thus, it is like a casual address to the assembly:
"Red fills the branches, green fills the branches; in every village, the green is deep and the red is sparse.

The oriole speaks, the cuckoo cries—what matter is this? Each sound is a bitter exhortation to return. Spring is already late; the trees bear no blossoms. A mess upon the branches, a lingering resentment."
[The Master] spoke more slowly. Throwing down his staff, he said: "Who will obtain this single fragment? It flows through a hundred thousand households.

On the tenth day of the eighth month in the Bingchen year of the Kangxi era, when he was about to pass away, the Master posed three questions. The first was: "The four great elements are fundamentally empty."
The five aggregates do not exist. Tell me, from where does the illness arise? Second:
after the four elements and five aggregates have dispersed and ceased, tell me, is the one who suffers the illness still ill or not? Third: tell me, as for this one who suffers the illness—

This refers to the sickness of the four great elements and five aggregates; it is not the sickness of the four great elements and five aggregates. The assembly was without opposition, and he subsequently transformed [them] (the mountain elder Mian being his successor).
Chan Master Shangsheng Benzong of Mo’an at Jingshan in Hangzhou was a native of Huangzhou in Hubei.

He had long studied under Tiantong Wuzu and attained awakening through a blow from the staff. He was renowned as a venerable elder throughout the various monastic centers of the four directions. Later, he received the Dharma from [Tiantong] Wuzu.
Master Weng Min held the whisk at Long’an in Shengjing. Upon receiving an invitation, he resided at Jingshan. He ascended the hall and said:
"At Jingshan, there is no Chan; there is no subtlety. We do not know how to arrange flowers or cluster brocade; how could there be short verses or long songs? He raised his staff and said:
"Relying solely upon this withered jointed old black rafter, we transmit the true pulse without confusion. He gave a shout and said: "A golden lion emerging from its den!"
"O Lion Cubs! With full majesty you roar and scatter the foxes. He then let out another shout and descended from his seat. (This was the lineage of Shanweng Min.
Chan Master Luyan Benyue of Shanguo Temple in Yanjing was the son of Sun of Shuixi.

In his youth, he received the tonsure at Riyuelun; he received full ordination at Fojiang. He traveled everywhere, visiting various masters, and finally studied under Bao'en Xiu. Xiu asked him: "If one calls it..."
"If you call it a staff, you contradict it; if you do not call it a staff, you turn your back on it. Ultimately, what would you call it? The Master said, "Please, Reverend, put it down.
Xiu said, "Once it is put down, what then? The Master said, "Your words have fallen into error. Xiu then struck him, and the Master went out.
He subsequently appointed Xiu as the head of the Secretariat (Jishì). One day, Xiu asked: "Without adding a single stroke to a single character, what is it?"
"What character is this? The Master said, "The patterns have already been revealed. Xiu nodded in understanding. Two years later, he visited Nengren Min.
Min asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Daxiong. Min said, "Towering alone atop Daxiong Peak—what kind of person’s realm is that?
The Master replied, "Today I have personally seen the Master. Min said, "Go to the hall for practice. The Master was constantly puzzled by the bamboo.
Regarding the koan of Bi-zhi and Ju-ti’s "Single Finger": After some time, he followed Ming to Faqing Temple in Qingzhou.

One day, while attending the hall for the midday meal, he suddenly seized a bamboo skewer and attained great enlightenment. He presented a verse on "The Single Finger," whereupon Ming immediately appointed him to hold the whisk and share the seat.
Not long after, he followed Ming to the imperial summons and took up residence at the Wanshan Hall within the Great Palace, where he was honored.
The Emperor issued an edict for Shanguo to open the hall. Later, he successively resided at various monasteries, including Fengsheng and Longchi.
Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The Dharma has no fixed form; its propagation depends on the person. It is like thunder rolling and rain falling, or like a dragon leaping and a tiger bounding.

Without shifting one's body or changing one's step, it directly enables the protection of the state and the peace of the realm. He then gave a shout and said: "All you venerable practitioners, have you grasped this?"
If you can grasp this, it will naturally be like water reaching the channel or wind passing through the grass;

from the imperial capital to the frontiers beyond, it will instantly cause a misty spring to arise, and even in empty valleys and remote corners, it will ensure that all things flourish in harmony and excellence. This is the most supreme among the supreme.

When the grain bears nine ears on each stalk, everyone speaks of a time of abundance; among the most extraordinary things, this is the most extraordinary. As a cold wind sweeps across the nine realms, all sing of the perfection of governance.
Only then do we know that the Way of the Emperor is level and even, and his grace and light are vast and boundless.

Although he has manifested great potential and displayed great function, it still belongs to the man beyond the ordinary who wields extraordinary wisdom, penetrating sound and form to reveal the fundamental principle. One must be a person of immeasurable capacity.
The unfolding of immeasurable deeds has coincided with the flourishing reign of the Sagely Sovereign; thus, we have witnessed the radiant ascent of the Dharma-transformation.

Just as with these newly ripened fruits of goodness, today you have received the Imperial Decree to open the hall. How, then, can one communicate the single phrase that assists and upholds the Imperial Way?
The myriad nations have drunk their hearts’ fill from tasting the great cauldron. Meeting, we join hands and ascend the high terrace. Ascending the Hall on Mid-Autumn Day:
Year after year we gaze together upon tonight’s moon; Age after age we share the fragrance of the aged cassia tree. If only there were not a single thing apart from the mind.
What luminous object could there be to forget together? Yangshan had no use for it; Caoqi’s pointing finger had not yet appeared.
He brandished his whisk and said: "The drifting clouds from the azure void have vanished; it is a single, vast expanse of cool clarity. At night, the bamboo is deep within the thatched cottage;

in the autumn courtyard, the stone bed is cold. Opening the furnace, he ascended the hall: "Tang’an has received an imperial decree to specially open the furnace. Monastics and laypeople alike rejoice, their voices shaking the earth."
Yuanmo: "If you wish to recognize the 'host and guest' phrase from years past, Zhaozhou hangs a gourd on the eastern wall.
[He strikes the meditation seat once. Ascending the hall, the Master said: "In the first nine days, and the second nine days, when we meet, we do not take each other's hands.

Suddenly extending both hands, he said: "I, this mountain monk, have already taken your hand. But how will the assembly express the phrase for 'meeting'? After a long silence, he said: "The cold snap."
The wind sweeps the ground, rolling up yellow leaves; outside the gate, the western breeze is cold with nightfall.
[The Master] struck the meditation seat once and ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, the Master said, "Today the wind is somewhat harsh;

everyone must look after their own heels. "Do you all understand? The assembly remained silent. The Master then strode down from the seat, dispersing them like a whirlwind, and returned to his quarters.
Ascending the hall: Suddenly it is the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. A single melody from Yunmen illuminates the universe. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth emit a wondrous sound;
the Buddha Hall and the Cloud Hall all rise in dance. The tortoise-nosed snake rushes forth; the white-browed tiger roars with a thunderous cry.
Those who look on are deaf; those who hear are blind. He whose great belly makes those before the gate laugh until they fall—this one has mounted the hall.
Lofty, there is nothing above him; one looks up but cannot reach him. Abyssal, there is nothing below him; his depth cannot be measured.

Where he is unattainable by looking up, the celestial chariot suddenly descends from the nine heavens. Where his depth is unfathomable, the golden wheel suddenly turns upon the great earth. Throughout the bustling marketplace...

Beholding the Most Holy One, we together upon the meditation platform gaze upon his Great Majesty. Only now do we see that imperial benevolence is vast and universal, and the sagely grace is long and nourishing.

Auspicious mists gather over the forests and springs; radiance ascends through the monastic community. Having already enjoyed the prosperity of this golden age, and further encountering such profound favor, how can we ultimately express our gratitude for this generous protection?
Raising his *ruyi* (wish-fulfilling) scepter, he said: "Acting without acting; transforming through the divine."
Evening Sermon. The Way is in daily life; yet in daily life, one does not know it. The spring breeze blows through distant trees; the night moon shines upon the empty courtyard.
Cease seeking and pondering beyond sound and form; let go casually—do not let it be too late. Suddenly tossing down his staff, he said: “He is no longer me; who, then, am I now?
Address to the Assembly on the Full Moon of the Fourth Month. Kai-zhou Po-yen did not [distribute] congee.
Grasping it and deliberating upon it—West Yuan was far too obscure. When meeting, there is no need to air one’s family’s disgrace;
let the fragrant breeze do as it pleases, intoxicating the *bìluó* vines. A monk asked, “If one clearly knows the principle that birth is non-birth, why is one still transmigrated by birth and death?
The Master said, “It has nothing to do with this mountain monk. The monk then departed. The Master called out, “Canyong, you upādhyāya!”
The monks paid him no heed. The Master said, "If one does not turn their head when called, what can be done? The Master retired to Jiufeng in Songjiang, where he remained for ten years.
On the fourteenth day of the first month of winter in the Bingchen year of the Kangxi era, hearing the sound of a bell, he informed the assembly and passed away.
His stupa was erected to the left of the Studying Platform on that same mountain (he was the successor of Shanweng Min).
A monk asked Zen Master Wugou Dalingbenpei of Henan: "When Sansheng asked Xuefeng, 'The golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net—what does it eat?
Xuefeng replied, 'Wait until it comes out of the net, and I will tell you. I do not know what kind of mental activity Xuefeng was engaged in.
The Master said: "If you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire. [The monk] said: "Sansheng said, 'One thousand...'"

Wuzhun Shifan asked, "The five hundred people do not even recognize the *huatou* (critical phrase) of their spiritual friend; what then? Feng said, "I am a retired monk; my duties as abbot are many and busy.
The Master said, "A cart is not pushed sideways; there is no justice in a crooked judgment. (This refers to Shanweng Meng, who succeeded [Fengxue]).
Chan Master Xiaoxi of Tiantong Mountain in Mingzhou was the son of the Qiu family from Chongqing in Sichuan. At the age of nineteen, he set out on pilgrimage with his satchel over his shoulder.
He first visited Bao’en Xiu to investigate the koan regarding the ox passing through the window lattice, but he found no way to penetrate it. He then went specifically to visit Wulei Min.
One day, following the master’s inquiry, he asked: "I do not ask you about the true moon; what is the second moon? The assembly [could not answer].

Their words did not accord. Mǎn himself provided a substitute reply, saying, "This will deceive people to death. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. He soon received formal certification.
Later, he accompanied Mǎn to the imperial summons to preach the Dharma at Wànshàn Hall. On the day of his leave-taking, Mǎn invited the Master to preside over the *jiézhì* (retreat) at Lóng'ān.
He gave a formal address on the fifteenth day, saying: "Before the fifteenth day, the芒種 (Mángzhòng) festival has passed; after the fifteenth day, it is the summer solstice."
The days grow longer; it is precisely the fifteenth day. A fragrant breeze comes from the south, bringing a subtle coolness to the halls and pavilions.

The Buddhas have no place to hide their bodies; the patch-robed monks stand out with self-reliance. Their horns and crests are towering and magnificent—just like those at the foot of the Southern Mountain.
What is it that is just like the foot of the Southern Mountain? Fresh bamboo shoots break through the earth to pierce the clouds and stars, their tender green rapidly spreading.

He hurriedly passed over the low wall; this was for the evening assembly. Generally speaking, when expounding the School of the Patriarchs, every single phrase must possess the three gates of a single principle, and that single principle must possess the three pathways. There is the provisional and the real;
there is illumination and function. How do you all understand this? If you can understand it, the old man Linji will be beneath the soles of your feet. Its...
Perhaps not yet so. This mountain monk shall provide a commentary. Taking up his staff, he descended from the seat, struck out like a whirlwind, and scattered [the assembly].
Throwing down the staff, he said, "Tell me, is this provisional or real? Is it illumination or function? He then gave a shout and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Evening Sermon: The mountain rain falls steadily and ceaselessly; the valley clouds drift as if floating or sinking. The new grain has not yet...
Leaving it out to dry in the sun. The administrative officer was half-pleased and half-angry. It is difficult for a patch-robed monk to dispel drowsiness;
leaning on the bed and propping against the mat, he props up his Zen and the Way. To set forth the whole matter at once, yet he still seeks further for a Buddha and a mind.
Suddenly, he lets out a shout and hurls down his staff, saying: "A day of thunder and rain comes again, soaking the eyes of Bodhidharma. Evening assembly: Do not let it go within.
It goes out; it does not enter from without. It fills and obstructs empty space, cutting off all return and all interaction. At such a time as this, how is it?
Walking while singing a song upon the tip of a sword’s edge—where the fine rain falls in mist, yet the road remains unwet. Evening Chán Session:

Before Bodhidharma came to the Eastern Land, everyone’s eyebrows were horizontal and their noses upright. The world was originally at peace; it was the act of severing one's arm that first set a terrifying precedent.

Without cause, he left behind a single sandal; his descendants fled in all directions with nowhere to go. Some men of spirit and blood have been driven until their skin is worn through and their bones are exposed.
As for those who do not suffer such weariness, where else could they hide? After a long silence, he said: "A shrimp cannot leap out of its measuring basket.
On the occasion of the *qǐqī* (seven-day retreat), he addressed the assembly: "Before one's parents were born, what was it, after all? He then departed.
Seek where he disappeared last winter; hide where he vanished this year. Arriving on the night of the third day of the month, I ran into this group.
Striking them with my staff like a whirlwind, I said: "Do not let me miss you! Ascending the hall, a monk asked:

"The former Old Monk has finished preaching the Dharma upon this precious seat. Now that the drum is beaten and you have ascended the hall, what further matter do you manifest? The Master said: "Try and say it."
"Look at the fundamental principle. As the monk hesitated, the Master shouted him away and said, "Today, the Elder Hongjue passed away;
it is the hundredth-day anniversary. [Holding up his staff,] he struck it once and said: 'He deserves thirty blows of the staff. Leaves fall and return to the root;
tracing back to the origin and exhausting the source. When the Great Moon was in the Dipper and he descended to take birth in the Lin family in Lingnan, he deserved thirty blows of the staff."
To treat a Confucian scholar of Lu as one who tears apart the robes and collars—thirty blows well deserved! To prefer the teachings of the Śākya clan and yet feel superior—thirty blows well deserved!
From the north of the Chang River to the east of the Great River, spreading poison afar and creating vast calamities—thirty blows well deserved!
To ascend to Tuṣita Heaven for no reason within a dream, causing the Mount Huayan to be erroneously transmitted for a thousand years—thirty blows well deserved! Great Assembly!
Now tell me: were these thirty blows actually struck him, or were they not? If they were not struck him, he is no one of the lineage who can carry on the family business;
if they were struck him, he becomes a son who commits filial impiety. Ultimately, how shall we judge this?
If you cannot judge it, he suddenly held up his staff and said: "The Old Man Hongjue has personally arrived at this Dharma assembly to judge for all of you.
That a filial heir acts contrary to his father is but a trivial matter; to raise up the bannerpole is true gratitude."
Holding up his staff, he gave the evening *can* (evening discourse). He cited Master Mi’s ascent of the hall, where he said: "In this place of Tiantong, we do not dare to shortchange anyone.
If you have half a catty, we weigh you at eight taels; if you have ten feet, we measure you at one zhang.
If there were someone among you who, hearing such words, were to come forward in a fit of indignation and say, 'All that is merely a scale and a measuring rod without any stars!'"
Furthermore, what is being weighed? The old monk simply says: "Caught on the first cast. If you can understand this, those with merit shall be rewarded;
if you cannot, then grasp the meaning of this verse on the hook, and do not fixate upon the zero point of the scale. The Master said:
"Although the Patriarch’s scales and measure were fair and impartial, he could not avoid betraying his compassionate heart. Suppose there were a man of impetuous temperament—"
When you wait for the Way, it weighs you at half a catty; when it scales you, it measures you at eight taels. When you have ten feet, it measures you as one zhang.
At that moment, he stepped out from the assembly and let out a thunderous shout, completely shattering the scale and the measuring rod that lack even a single star.

You may be certain that the Master will look upon you with eyes wide open. Is there anyone among this assembly right now who is like this? If there is, this mountain monk will grant you the summer retreat.
The matter is concluded. Should it not yet be so, before this single mat of seven feet, let everyone exert themselves to avoid being weighed and measured by others.
This is for the evening discourse. [He] takes up the staff, strikes once, and says: "Deshan’s staff is set aside to one side. He lets out a shout and says:
"Linji’s shout has no place to be used here. Nevertheless, how does one unfold the teaching in accordance with the exigencies of the times? Thereupon he said:
"Up there is the Great Man, Qiu Yi Ji. He transformed three thousand seventy scholars. You, little students, eight or nine of you, carry the staff and leap forth upon the Way.
This is the talk of the Confucian school; it has no place in the Gate of the Patriarchs (the Chan school). The Master laughed heartily and said, "One can see that he knows the rites!
The Master composed the *Zongmen Baoji Lu* (Record of the Jewel Accumulation of the Gate of the Patriarchs), which circulated in the world. (Shanweng Myn was his successor.)
Small Assembly at Zen Master Jingyun Yijiu Benzhe of Jiaxing Pinghu The summer solstice brings coolness; the heat is like autumn. The thoughts of those with "wax hearts" clamor and chatter.
If you seek to grasp tenfold accomplishment, what can you take? If you know this is such a matter, then simply rest.
A monk asked, "When one does not admire the various sages and does not value one's own spiritual essence, what then? The Master said, "The Long River."
He used inkstones and ink to repeatedly transcribe letters on severing ties (the "Shanweng Min" succession).
Master Xizhao Benchue of Xilin on Mount Lu was a scholar of the Classics from Jiangyou who, following the dynastic upheaval, shaved his head and donned the monastic robes.

Having traveled to various quarters and attained the Dharma, he secluded himself behind closed doors north of the Huai River. Later, while traveling through Shangyang, he thatched a hut at Du’o Hermitage to dwell in profound accumulation and mature cultivation.
Subsequently, he appeared in the world; he first presided over Xilin and later resided at Nengren in Jiangzhou. Ascending the hall, he said: "The crane is white and the crow is black."
The mountains are blue and the waters are green; the crane is long and need not be severed, the wild duck is short and cannot be extended. To speak of "Direct Pointing" is already a detour.
How much less can one take tiles and rubble for gold, or embrace a mere piece of jade-stone as true jade?

It is necessary to take the great earth as a furnace and bellows, and bind the myriad phenomena into firewood. Let those with copper heads and iron brows all turn themselves around within the flames. Directly...
"The skin must be pierced through to the bone and fall away. Nevertheless, after the skin has been pierced and the bones have fallen away, what can be done?
Mount Lu boasts many peaks, yet six times six remains thirty-six. Again, it is said that when Chan Master Danxia passed by a monastery...
Encountering a great cold, he took a wooden Buddha and burned it for fire. The head of the monastery scolded him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden Buddha?
Huixia used his staff to poke at the ashes and said, "I am burning it to retrieve the *śarīra*. The head of the monastery asked, "How could a wooden Buddha have *śarīra*?"
Danxia said, "Since there are no relics, let us take two more statues and burn them. Afterward, the temple administrator’s beard and eyebrows fell out.
The Master said, "Danxia was like an insect boring through wood; the administrator happened to form characters [by accident].

Listen to this verse from me, this mountain monk: 'Even if it were a Buddha, it would be hard to keep; Why not burn the withered wood and leave it at rest? It is not that a great furnace can melt snow.'"
"How can one cause the cataracts to clear so that both eyes are opened? [The Master] ascends the hall and says: "The plum blossoms in the forest are frozen through, awaiting the return of warmth;
before the peaks, the Stone Maiden is pregnant. At an ordinary midnight she has given birth; throughout the great earth, there is nothing that is not an opening treasure-trove. Great assembly!"

The treasure store has been opened; it may be admired but not grasped. For those of many generations who have worn the ceremonial hairpins and sashes, even rare jewels would not be considered an auspicious omen.
For the destitute son who suddenly becomes wealthy, even an ocean of silver cannot prevent the appearance of flowers [of doubt]. Nevertheless, I fear it may not be jade;
if it is indeed jade, how marvelous! Ascending the hall, he asked: "What is the precept? The Master said: "Slaughtering pigs and butchering dogs. He asked: "What about..."
“This is samādhi,” the Master said. “Chasing the waves and following the currents. [The student] asked, “What is wisdom? The Master said, “Ignorance and afflictions.
[The student] asked, “As for the phrase that points beyond this, what about it? The Master said, “For now, just pay your respects. Then he said:
“If water does not enter the ear, and grit does not enter the eye, how could one know the east has turned white while clutching a night-light talisman? Alas, old frozen fellow!”
Pus. Only upon seeing the stars does one finally catch a glimpse. Wisdom and the marks of virtue are like placing space within the ear-cavity.
If you are a man of true character, would you ever be willing to follow the old tracks? When the morning star and the sun are in the sky, those who see them are not deluded.
This mind does not betray anyone; facing it, there is no cause for shame. But then, what is this talk that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? Put down the whisk.
The Master said: "If you do not enter the water, how can you see the tall man? New Year’s Eve Small Sermon: This ruined monastery has always required propping and supporting.
This year’s poverty surpasses last year’s poverty; Before Fenghua had to drag his sack across [the river], It forced Nanquan to want to sell himself.
Yet, it is a joy that on this night when the year draws to a close, There is not a single person among the ten thousand miles who has not returned home. Great Assembly, since...
There is no one who has not returned; thus, everyone sits securely at home. But how shall we spend the year-end festival?
Having cast away all the old almanacs, the pepper-dish is set forth—this is something truly new. [The Master] enters the hall. Without cause, he intends to hold a seven-day retreat.
The seven days have already passed; one slumps in drowsiness, unable to wake from it. The knot of doubt cannot be burst open. The lamp-light pierces through the eyes;
the sound of rain drips through the ears. Clearly manifest in its entirety before one’s very body—why labor to pull the ox or turn the millstone?
It is not a thing, not the mind, and not a Buddha. Yet even so, one can still say: "A nun is originally just a woman. — Yunmen.
The Hu-bing (barley cake) has turned into a steamed bun (*mántou*). When questioned, it remains as nothing but a *mālā* (a heap of confusion).

My word to you: let the exhausted bird not rely on the reeds. The swift falcon is unshackled; the heavens themselves are vast. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Bimā holds up his staff; Heoshan beats the drum.
Linji is a thief who steals in broad daylight; a probing pole among the weeds. Yunmen, the old man with the lame foot, flashes a red banner. Yantou rows his boat. Hua..."
The pavilion shook as the oars were rowed; there was not one who did not vie for the first stroke, risking their lives in the peril.
To this day, victory and defeat remain undecided, inevitably provoking the laughter of bystanders. Thereupon, he let out a thunderous shout and said:

"If I, this mountain monk, had not shouted to stop you, you would have remained nothing but a crew of dragon-boat rowers, drifting with the waves and following the current, with no end in sight. Nevertheless, now that you have been utterly cut off—"
"But how is it? "Shide has the Dragon Sword of Yanping; there is no harm in hiding one's body among yellow leaves. Ascending the hall [he said]:
"There is no Buddha to be boiled, and no Patriarch to be forged. The non-Buddhist practitioners of the Western Heaven are called the foremost for this.
If there were a Buddha to be boiled and a Patriarch to be forged, even one with wisdom like Mañjuśrī would have to descend into the Iron Ring Mountains. Thus, at Xilin now..."

On the day the furnace was opened, [the Master] asked, "What should be done? He then looked around left and right and said, "To revive after death—this cannot be deceived. [The Master] was offering orchid flowers to the Buddha. He asked a monk, "Have you smelled the fragrance of the flowers yet?
The monk replied, "I have not. The Master said, "Where are your nostrils? The monk replied, "They are in the Master’s eyes. The Master said, "If that is so, why do you not smell them?
The monk was speechless. The Master then struck him. [Another] asked: "The ancients wore a single pair of shoes for thirty years. What does this mean?"
"What do you think? The Master said, "Stale goods are difficult to sell. Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master sneezed. Question: "Why does Zhaozhou’s dog have no Buddha-nature? The Master said, "Do not inflict sores on healthy flesh. Question:
"The Buddha-mind is great in compassion and manifests transformation bodies according to the species. Within a herd of donkeys and horses, is there still [a Buddha]? The Master said, "..."
"Even the Buddha-Dharma does not exist," the Master said. "They wear iron bits and carry saddles; they are dragged by plows and pulled by harrows.

A scholar asked, "As for Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, people in the world fashion only female images. I fear it may not be him. The Master said, "It is not certain that even a male image would be him either.
The scholar asked, "Ultimately, what kind of image is it? The Master said, "You must see him directly for yourself before you will understand. (Shanweng Min was his successor.)
Chan Master Mingyin Xiaoyin Bentong of Ningguo ascended the hall and said: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes discrimination.

If you act in this way, then even the skins of tigers and leopards [are no different from common beasts]. Just do not harbor hatred or attachment, and all will be transparently clear. He struck his staff and said:
"It does not lie in mere intellectual clarity. He struck the desk once more and said, "Is there anyone here who still feels dissatisfaction?
After a long silence, he whirled his staff like a whirlwind and dispersed them. (This refers to Shanweng Min, who was a successor.)
A monk asked Chan Master Guifeng Songbi of Yuezhou, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer? The Master said, "The Qinwang Peak is high;
the Mirror Lake waters are vast. The monk asked, "How do you function [as such]? The Master said, "Even when the water is clear, it still carries its burden."
The peak’s emerald hue reflects upon people with a chill (by Shanweng Min).

Recorded by the Third-Fifty Generation of the Linji School under Mount Nanyue, Chan Master Benwei of Caoyuan on Mount Huizhou in Guangdong, a descendant of the Fu clan of Chaozhou. He ascended the hall and said: "All..."
As he spoke of Chan with great breadth, it was like a spring swallow perched on a painted beam or an autumn cicada on an ancient tree. But tell me, how does one speak of Chan?
A monk stepped forward and asked, "Regarding the masters of old who ascended the seat and entered the room for private instruction—what was it they were doing?"
The Master threw down his staff and said, "Look! Look! Then he returned directly to the abbot’s quarters.

One day, upon returning from a meal, a monk asked him midway along the path, "When a donor provides a meal for the monks, is there still merit to be gained? The Master replied, "One must not seek it through the mind."

[The questioner] said: "It is like Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, who established a shrine every five li and a monastery every ten li; why did the First Patriarch say that there is truly no merit in this?
The Master said: "One must not seek with a deliberate mind. [The questioner] said: "Setting aside these two paths, please speak one sentence. The Master said:
"The Great Way penetrates Chang'an" (Shanweng Myn was his successor).

Chan Master Benyuan of Shiyuan Qu’an in Ezhou ascended the hall for the formal discourse. When masters from all quarters beat the drums and ascend the hall, Shiyuan’s taking his seat is the most bitter:
the fields and crops have met with drought, and the monastic quarters have been entirely plundered by bandits.

Morning bells and evening drums urge one on, yet they cannot satisfy the fire of hunger. He drew a circle (○) and said, "Do you understand, great assembly? In a moment, it will be at the bottom of the bowl."
Toujianqu (successor of Shanweng Min).
Chan Master Daxian Benxian of Dongshan in Jinling was the son of the Ren family of Guang’an in Chuannbei.

In his youth, he read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, which inspired him with a resolve to seek ordination. At the age of twenty-five, he paid respects to Yangshan Zongchi and completed his tonsure and full ordination.
[The Master] was fully equipped [with the necessary conditions]. At that time, he encountered Poshan Ming. While avoiding the war at Shizhusi, the Master went there to seek instruction.
Ming asked, "What is your secular surname? The Master replied, "It is Ren. Ming asked, "Before your parents were born, what surname did you have?

The Master was unable to answer. He prostrated and requested an explanation. Ming struck him and said, "Investigate! From then on, the Master harbored a doubt and investigated with fierce diligence. He requested [instruction] once more.
