Chan Master Hanyi Tao of Jingshan Xingjiao in Danyang, Runzhou, was the son of the Shen family from Anfeng, Taizhou.
The West Hall of Tiantong held the whisk; his style was of an extraordinary caliber, a model for ten thousand ages.

Stillness and illumination were凝然 (concentrated and unmoving), the essential pivot before one’s eyes. Clouds shrouded the green peaks, fully manifesting the family tradition beyond kalpas; rain dripped from the eaves, providing guidance. The uppermost aperture is a shimmering rock;
the Heart Seal reflects light, the wind of Taibai. His gate and courtyard are steep and precipitous—just like Puhua...
When the time comes, he roars; the sound of the Dharma drum resounds, causing dragons and elephants to leap and surge, each vying for the lead in their stride.

Arriving here, every one has his heels planted firmly on the ground, and everyone’s nostrils reach toward the heavens. Yet, how can one unfold and display that which does not fall within the realm of seeing and hearing?
After a long silence, he said: "A three-inch tongue has no place to use it; a pair of empty hands cannot form a fist. (Muyun Mon, successor to the lineage).
Chanshi Hongwen of Longshan in Suzhou was the son of the Xu family of Haining. Upon ascending the hall, after concluding the story of Baizhang and the Wild Fox, the Master said:
"Not falling, not being obscured—this is to spin into a snare. Not obscured, not falling—this is to bind oneself without a rope.
You pack of wild foxes! Why do you pierce haphazardly and dig aimlessly? Cease your conjectures! A solitary falcon soars across ten thousand miles of blue sky. (Muyun)
[The Dharma] heir. Chan Master Qingliang Yemo of Shiwu, Fujian; son of the Zhou family of Wuchang, Hubei. Small Assembly (Xiao-can).
At Qingliang Temple, harvesting grain: this sickle is sharp and keen; there is no need for the Elder to ascend the hall—those who hear this [should understand].
His entire body was dripping with sweat. Since he was already in a cool place, why did he still have sweat dripping? Do you know where he turned himself around?
After a long silence, he said: "The heat of the day has been great; may the assembly take pity on one another and each please return to the hall to rest. One day, he passed away.
When his disciples had finished painting a portrait of the Master, he suddenly opened his eyes and gazed at it. The assembly was all struck with amazement;
thereafter, he sat upright and passed away. He was enshrined in a stupa on Baiyun Peak in Fuzhou (he was a successor in the lineage of Muchun).
Chan Master Yibei of Baoke Monastery in Jintan was the son of the Zou family from Shunjiang in Yue. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Baoke?
The Master said, "A crow pecks at the white clouds as they open and close. As the monk hesitated, the Master held up his staff and said:
"Do you understand? He replied, "I do not. The Master said, "Even this old monk’s staff does not understand," and he struck him.
New Year’s Eve Small Lecture: In one year, there remains but a single night; in a single night, one looks back upon a year that has passed. This public case is raised every year without weariness.
Old Wang of the Eastern Village burns paper money at night. (Muyun Mon)
Chan Master Wanyou Yuanzhan of Yuyao was the son of the Wu family of his native district. Initially, he studied under Feiyin Tongrong of Tiantong, who instructed him to contemplate the saying:

"Though gold dust is precious, it becomes a cataract when it falls in the eye. While he was investigating this with intense vigor, he suddenly looked up and saw the moon, at which point he attained realization.
He presented a verse, saying: "The moon descends upon my head in the night; The livelihood of the ghostly household is finished. Ten thousand strings of cash are wrapped around my waist."
"Riding a crane up to Yangzhou. After reading this, Rong said, "The karmic conditions for this son will be fulfilled later in Yangzhou.

Subsequently, after he had attained the Dharma, he traveled to Yangzhou and greatly propagated the teachings. On the twenty-seventh day of the first month of the Renxu year of the Kangxi era, [he passed away].
Suddenly, he addressed the assembly, saying, "I shall depart on the first day of the month. When that day arrived, he spoke a verse to bid farewell to the world, saying:
"For seventy years I have said nothing else; To show people, I have only taught the emptying of all existence. Today the time has come; it is good to return home.
I walk, carrying the bright moon upon the tip of my staff. Having finished speaking, he passed away suddenly. (Muyun Men was his successor.)
Chan Master Lin-yeh Wu-p’u of Mount Chi-hsing in Su-chou was a native of Ju-k’ung.
He left the household life at Ch’ing-liang Hermitage in Chin-ling and traveled extensively to study under various masters. After long relying on Hsueh-tou, he attained realization;

later, while traveling through the Wu region during the time of Ku-nan, he took up residence at Mount Chi-hsing and founded the Lai-ho (Welcoming the Crane) Monastery. One day, when a separate room was completed, the Master was invited to reside within it.
Addressing the assembly: Since the drum was beaten and I retired from this mountain, the fires have grown cold and the clouds have turned frigid, leaving no trace behind.

I do not speak of the Buddha-dharma, nor its fundamental characters; my lips and mouth are like two pieces of sealing wax. It is laughable that Lu Zu faced the wall; his boundaries were not strictly maintained.
Nanquan smashed the rice pot; it only created more complications. How could it compare to what happens here at Laihe?
Throughout antiquity and today, wind and moon pass by as they drift along. Though the mountain gate possesses not an inch of land or field, we gather several monks as circumstances allow.
We sever the tangled vines upon the sproutless branch; we stew rice-less gruel beside the broken-legged cauldron. Thus, there is no hindrance to being amidst the dust and earth.
His head is covered in ash; everyone’s eyebrows are knotted together. Fame and profit are both severed; right and wrong are utterly forgotten.
For no reason today, being pressed and driven by lay practitioners from near and far, he has no choice but to come forth and reveal a bit of his message. After a long silence, he said:
"The tongue was originally in the mouth" (from Master Mumen of Mugun, successor to Yunmen).
Zen Master Jikai of Xizi went to visit Master Mumen to seek instruction. He was directed to enter the hall and investigate the koan:
"From where does one come when born? To where does one go when dying? He applied himself with fierce intensity, neglecting both sleep and food. On the seventh night, he emerged [from his meditation].

Upon withdrawing and reflecting, he beheld the moon as bright as day; his body and mind were suddenly liberated. He went to the Master’s chamber, where the Gatekeeper (Dongshan Liangjie) saw him and said with a smile, "If you already know such a matter, then simply rest;
why have you come here? The Master replied, "I also wish to report the truth of my realization," and then prostrated himself.

The Master had attended him for many years, and their spiritual affinity was perfectly harmonious. As he was about to depart, the Gatekeeper instructed him, saying, "In the future, when you take up the thatched roof [of a hermitage], do not aspire to seek fame."

He established himself as a master of his own station and a guiding model for later students. The Master [Wumen] then received his instructions and resided at Xizi until the end of his life (he was a successor of Muchun Men).
Chan Master Linpuxingru of Hezhong in Zhenjiang was a native of Jiangdu. He was the son of the Wang family. Entering the hall, he said:
"Today is the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. Do not give rise to doubt regarding its application. If someone comes and asks, 'What school is this?
pick up your fist and strike them. If they ask further, 'How is it? What about it? give them a good shout right in the face. Thus you press out the True Person of No Rank."
Severing east, west, south, and north at once, he overturns his hand and smashes Mount Sumeru. What need is there to seek heaven or hell? He spreads out the precious cage of eight facets;
transverse and vertical, free from all constraints. Now tell me: what is the "true person of no station"?

After a long silence, he said: "In the twelfth month the plum blossoms open; the spring thunder rolls amidst the lingering snow. Ascending the hall, he said: "The willows by the bank hang golden threads; the cold plum..."
The jade embryo is produced; it is the original true face. There is no need for confused doubt or conjecture. Even if you can recognize it here, you are still halfway there.
If this is not yet so, ten thousand miles of white clouds lie ahead. (Muyun Men’s successor)
Master Wencan Molang of Yushan in Songjiang retired to Jingshan to spend his final years. Addressing the assembly, he said: Carrying my short staff, I enter the village of Wanxiang;
My traces are hidden among the craggy peaks where clouds form the gate. Through my simplicity, I find leisure to sleep through the day;
In my wildness, I seek lines of verse as dusk falls. The sweeping bamboo colors clear my brows and eyes; The moon-piercing sound of the spring chills my dreams and soul. Aside from this—
Its flavor is like ice and snow; what else is there to comment upon? (Moyunmen Sisi).
Chan Master Ruoneng of Helin in Runzhou, a native of the Zhang family of Dantu in that same prefecture, gave this small instruction:
"Last night in my dream, I met a fellow practitioner with whom I exchanged some words of daily life. That fellow practitioner then instructed me to contemplate..."

[The student] was looking at the *yulu* (recorded sayings) and was thoroughly occupied with the texts. The mountain monk said, "This is your elder brother's business; I, your younger brother, am illiterate.
He then said, "If you understand this one thing, all matters are finished. Why do you make a living out of paper?
The student said, "This 'one thing' of yours is not fit for anything. The mountain monk said, "Even Śākyamuni, the Old Man, got only this one thing. East... [text ends].
"The Sixth Patriarch of the Earth obtained but one peg; our late Master of Tiantong and my own Preceptor also obtained but one peg each.
I wonder, elder brother, how many pegs have you obtained? He replied, "I urge you to practice, to practice! You have so much entanglement.
The mountain monk said, "I urge you to rest, to rest! You have so many delusive thoughts. The two men [parted].
At the very moment they were contending, a beardless man suddenly stepped out and said, "Stop, stop! I have a principle to analyze for you two.
He then recited a mantra: "This is a great divine mantra; this is a great illuminating mantra. Suddenly, I, this mountain monk, was startled awake.
Today I bring this up for the assembly: do you all understand it thoroughly? It is broad daylight and a clear sky—how earnestly!
Do not speak of dreams. Take care (the successor of Muye Mon).
Zen Master Zhuyu Bin of Zhantanlin in Hangzhou visited Helin and, before paying homage to the stupa containing the relics of the Elder Mu, said:
"How strange! This object has remained undecayed through kalpas past; the entire body of my late teacher is suddenly still here. After all,"
"How so? [The Master] performed three full prostrations (the lineage of Muye Men).
Chan Master Shijianzhao of Yihualin in Jiaxing was a native of Nanchang, Jiangxi. Initially, he studied under Cuiyan, Xuedou, and Fuyan;
later, he visited Gunan Men at a time when the master was precisely berating his contemporaries. Thereupon, he said to the assembly: "Everyone..."

Nan said, "I am extremely cruel. The Master said, "The tiger possesses the virtue of reviving the dead. A monk standing nearby made a sound of terror; the Master said, "You deserve a blow with the staff right now.
Nan said, "What proof do you have that you have attained Zen? The Master said, "Master, do not degrade the noble by treating them as lowly.
Nan nodded his head in agreement and ordered him to serve as attendant. He served diligently for many years, and after receiving the formal entrustment (shuritsu), [he went] to Gunan.
The incense offering at the Patriarch’s Hall says: "O, our Elder! You were born of excellence on Mount Po-shan and transmitted your fragrance from Mount Tai-bai.

Your patriarchal wind pervades heaven and earth; your Dharma torch illuminates the realms of humans and devas. The sun might grow cold, the moon might grow hot; yet the more one looks up, the higher you are.
Mountains may run dry, oceans may be measured; yet no eulogy can ever reach you. Your spiritual pivot strikes like a flash of lightning; the blow from your staff is swift as thunder."

Rushing forward in pursuit of his venerable compassion, there is no way to repay it; incense is burned and offerings set forth to honor the True Teacher. Thus, prostrations are performed (by the successor of Muye).
Chan Master Shizongqi of Xiuzhou, a native of the Lu family of Leqing in Dongjia, gave a small assembly talk: "The old plum tree spits forth jade."
Unfolding the profound mechanism of the upward path, the tender willows unfurl their golden threads. To manifest the wondrous function of the Dharmakāya, the matter must be such a matter;
the person must be such a person. If one is not such a person, it is difficult to clarify such a matter.
O people! Each of you is a true man; do not belittle yourselves or yield in spirit. If you can realize this, only then may you open your mouths wide.
To speak such great words—calling an ox a horse and pointing east while speaking of the west—is something that even the old monks of the world can do nothing about.
If you truly reach such a state, both Buddha and Patriarch are utterly unattainable; how could there be any signs of birth, death, coming, or going?
If this is not yet the case, you must stake this very life and form, exerting yourself with fierce vigor, until you have struck through to the bottom.
Become a man of ease and detachment; only then will you realize that you have not been deceiving yourself.

If you remain drifting and wavering, half-doubting and half-believing, mired in the armor of "doing nothing," then when the day comes that your eyes fall to the ground, you will be a man with an iron face.
I shall provide you with the cost of your meal. Do not say that this mountain monk has nothing to say.
Take care. (Muyun Men’s lineage).

He was a native of the Liu family from Changle, Fuzhou. In his youth, he left home for ordination at Longshan.

Later, he went to study under Gushan, whereupon he attained realization upon hearing the crowing of a rooster. Subsequently, he paid his respects to Xian of Baoen Temple. Xian asked him about [the meaning of] "the person in front of the courtyard."
Regarding the meaning of the "Cypress Tree," the Master said: "In a household where there is a *gǔ* poison, do not taste the water. He was asked again: "If it is thus, what then? The Master replied:
"How can it compare to the third month in Jiangnan, where the hundred flowers are fragrant where the partridges cry?
Xian then struck the drum and ascended the seat; he entrusted the Master with the words: "An old robe remains to protect your body; give this to my son and return to Min."
As the honored leader among the assembly, he arrived at the vacant seat of Tongxuan on Mount Tiantai. Xuedou Yun personally escorted him into the mountains. Entering the hall, he said:
"At the head of Luohan Ridge, the clouds reach ten thousand fathoms deep; by the shores of Tiechuan Lake, the waters flow a thousand fathoms wide.

Within the seas, this is hailed as the lair of dragons and elephants; on the peaks of Tiantai, it is renowned as a forest for monks. Here, the pines and cypresses stand in irregular array—the legacy of National Teacher Shao."
The wind is present now; the pavilions and towers stand out prominently.

Realizing that the old man’s countenance is still there, if you can recognize this at once, then feel free to thump your chest and ribs before the Pure Hall, ride from the Buddha Hall out through the mountain gate, and knock over Mount Xianglu.
"Trample upon Geumji Ridge. If this is not yet so, do not move it; if you move it, I shall break your waist. Entering the hall:
"If you wish to ascend the peak of Mount Tai, take the first step as the beginning. If you wish to traverse ten thousand acres of vast waves, first set out from this shore.
Do not shrink from diligent toil; do not weary of exhaustion. As days turn to months and time deepens, until at last the mountain ends and the water runs dry."
At that moment, he performed a back-flip somersault and stood upright like Maheśvara. [The Master said: "The great chiliocosm and all its realms are but bubbles in the sea;
all sages and worthies are like a flash of lightning. A monk came for an audience. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Jiading.
The Master said, "In the city, the troops and horses are in great confusion. How did you manage to pass through? He replied, "I did not see them. The Master said, "Is it not so?"
Someone came from within the city and said, "It is this. The Master said, "He does not even know how to lose his body or forfeit his life" (referring to Fu Shi Xiansi).
Zen Master Baozang Wenzhe of Jiangxi was a native of Wuyun in Jixian. His clan name was Chen. He was fourteen years old [when he entered the monastic order].
At twenty-one, he went to Mount Dongtang in the eastern suburbs of Yiyang to shave his head.

There he attended upon the elder master Xiyan, who gave him instruction by stripping away the four great elements to ask, "What is the body? and tracing back the six sense organs to ask, "What is the mind? He was told to investigate and seek this day and night.
One day, while eating rice, he saw a black-husked insect in the bowl and suddenly attained realization. He spoke a verse, saying: "The insect in the rice, originally..."
The face and eyes as they appear now are the same as mine. A laugh—ha ha—and all of life is joy. Buddhas and sentient beings are both within a dream. [This was] presented by Yang.
Yang said, "I am going to travel to various quarters. He then went up to Tiantong. He asked:

"As for 'When the hundred limbs have all decayed and scattered, one thing remains eternally spiritual,' I do not ask about that. When the hundred limbs have decayed and all returned to the earth, where is that eternally spiritual one situated? This.
"What do you think? Daowu said. "You are so deluded. The Master had no reply.
The next day, he entered the room again and asked, "The words I spoke yesterday were not incorrect either. Why did you say I was deluded? I do not know where my delusion lies.
Daowu struck him with a succession of blows until the pain became unbearable; his doubts remained unresolved. Later, he went to consult Baen Xian.
Question: "One does not doubt the tongues of those from all quarters; since one's own task is finished, why is it that doubting words and phrases is considered a great illness?
Xian said: "I do not worry about swords and halberds falling from the sky; I only fear being bound and killed by lotus fibers. Under these words, the Master attained realization.
Suddenly he attained a thorough understanding of the teaching. One day, Xian asked him, "Your name is Wanwei (Encompassing the Universe).
Right now, where do you reside? The Master replied, "I am never hidden throughout the entire world. Xian said, "Are you the encompassing universe, or is the encompassing universe you?

The Master replied, "Only I am supreme. Xian said, "Lower your voice! Lower your voice! Thereupon, he transmitted his instructions to him. When Xian became the abbot of Tiantong, he commanded the Master to succeed him on the seat.
Ascending the hall for the commencement of the retreat: Upon this bare lump of flesh, it stands like a precipice of a thousand fathoms. Only this sharp, spiritual blade—who dares to confront it?
If you can realize it here, where would you place the binding and unbinding, or delusion and awakening?
Now, having no choice in the matter, I shall set up patterns and draw models; I establish patterns where there are none, and I set up ropes where there are no cords. I wish—

He causes all people, within ninety days, to suddenly leap out of their cages and break their ropes, until the myriad phenomena and the ten thousand things dance, and the hundred rivers and the great ocean surge with waves.
At such a time, it is precisely right to take a blow from the staff of the Treasure Store. Why?
Because "In a world of peace, the foolish and stubborn are executed. [The Master] addressed the assembly: "In a place beyond thought and deliberation, consciousness..."
The nature of things is difficult to fathom. The waves of the Nine Peaks flow surging on; the ripples of the Three Lakes rise in layered succession.

The fisherman casts his net amidst the pines and wind; the woodcutter fills his pack with fish and turtles. Those watching by the Huangpu River cannot help but laugh until they are spent. After a long silence, he said: "Pointlessly, one drives a stake into empty space.
A monk came for an audience. The Master asked: "Prajñā is like a great mass of fire. How can one draw near to it?"
The monk remained silent. The Master said, "Yet you have spoken with great intimacy" (Fushí Xiànsì).
Chányī Tiāngǔzhèn Chánshī of Yún'yán in Sūzhōu was the son of the Tán family of the commandery. He first restored the Chan seat at Yún'yán.
Having undergone many hardships, he traveled to various monasteries such as Mount Kuānglú and Cùiyán, where he was invited to take up the seat of abbot;

however, he did not accept. Later, he presided over Guǎngfú Monastery. Entering the hall, he said: "Beyond the limit of Avidyā (Weiyīn), the myriad phenomena are vividly present. Facing each other directly, not a single mechanism is established."
The primordial path is opened wide; tigers gallop and dragons soar. The notes of *gong* and *shang* shift anew, yet the melody is so sublime that those who can harmonize with it are few.
If you can once break into a profuse sweat of realization, you will tear away the nostrils of the Patriarchs. Entering a desolate field without discrimination, you take whatever comes to hand.
Illumination and function proceed together; guest and host exchange places. Even if a thousand sages were to arrive, they could not capture this in a sketch. Today, the Mountain...
The monk did not abandon his compassion and conveyed a message to him. He struck the meditation staff and said, "Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas" (Fushí Xián sì).
Chan Master Hóngyǎn Hào of Yángguān, Zhèjiāng, ascended the hall and said: "In my school there are no words or phrases; in truth, there is not a single dharma."
With others: Yunmen’s red banner flashes; Linji’s hot shout thunders. After a long silence, he said: "Though a sharp blade is swift, it does not slay the innocent.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Last month, I bound the source, yet there was no binding; I suddenly drove a stake into empty space. Today, I unbind the source, yet there is no unbinding;
my straw sandals are tightly fastened—truly carefree. Since there was never anything to bind, how could there be anything to unbind?"
It has never been tied. The scale-weight was originally raw iron. At the critical moment, it delivers a painful hammer-blow to the crown of the head.
I ask you all: do you perceive it or not? If you perceive it, go about the world as you please. If you have not perceived it, I shall further examine and distinguish it for you in detail:
the toad at the bottom of the well swallows the moon. [Ascending the hall: The white snow has vanished with the last days of winter; the plum blossoms...
Releasing the early spring: the meaning of that which comes from the West is utterly inscrutable and cannot be discussed.
Since it is inscrutable, why can it not be discussed? "Sparse shadows slant across the shallow, clear water; a hidden fragrance drifts as the moon sinks in twilight. Ascending the hall, he said:

"Throughout ancient and modern times, the striking of the mallet and the raising of the whisk, the snapping of fingers and the clearing of the throat—these are like a single mote of dust flying through the Flower Treasury World. Furthermore...
When have I ever raised even a ten-thousandth part of what is found within the School of the Lineage? Do you wish to understand? The Flower Treasury World is contained within a single mote of dust.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Clenching an empty fist to compete in wealth with the dragon deities—I am not yet willing to concede the tally on the field."

All day long leaning against the rice basket and crying out from hunger, one certainly does not know that the rice was made by oneself. Casting the ocean of worlds (*kṣetrasāgara*) to another direction—it is fundamentally unmoving.
Spending a *dou* of gold daily is no more than one’s natural allotment; yet placing a mere hair-tip upon the ground, one hesitates and wavers.
Not even a single thread of silk or grain of rice can be easily digested. Even when hundreds of thousands of extraordinary phenomena arise, they cannot be shifted or exchanged. A thousand people...
Ten thousand people cannot contain it. Reaching this point, I dare to smash it all to pieces with a single blow of the mallet.
Do you all understand this thoroughly? Do not blame me for my former abundance of spirit; he [the Master] once trod upon that highest pass.
[Ascending the hall: Xuefeng rolled three wooden balls; Juzu raised a single finger; Shigong drew his bow and set his arrow.
An arrow. A short oar and a lone boat at Huating. This mountain monk has no many wiles; he simply sits and watches Yangzhou.
The wind drifts on, the waves drift on; the reeds on both banks smile and nod their heads. Before the green bamboo hat, there are boundless matters;
beneath the green straw raincoat, all at once they cease. Question: When the deluded mind has nowhere to abide, that is Bodhi. Precisely when it is deluded—
[The monk] asked, "At that time, was there still Bodhi or not? The Master said, "Striking ice, one does not see water. [The monk] asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body?
The Master said, "A urine bucket. [The monk] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Hire someone to carry it away. [The monk] asked, "What is the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "Bricks and clods of earth. [The monk] said, "I understand. The Master said, "Block the ditches and fill the ravines."
A questioner asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The sun rises in the east at the hour of Mao.
The Master asked a layman, "What practice do you usually engage in? He replied, "I am entirely without mind. The Master said, "Do you hear the grasshoppers chirping outside the window?
He replied, "I hear them. The Master said, "Is it with a mind that you hear them, or without a mind? As the layman was about to answer, the Master struck him with a look of majestic awe.
One shout. Then he struck him (Fushi Xiansi).
Chan Master Yanguan Faxi Qianyun Zhan was the son of the Huang family of Wujiang. Ba’en Xian asked him, "Cease your prostrations for a moment;
what is your daily activity? The Master said, "I put on my clothes and eat my food. Xian said, "Setting aside putting on clothes..."
"Are you wearing clothes and eating rice? the Master asked. Xian said, "I ask the Old Man to speak. Xian replied, "What does what the Old Man says have to do with you?
The Master said, "The calamity reaches the descendants" (referring to Fu Shi Xian as his successor).
Chan Master Chongsheng Baizhao [Yong-Hao] ascended the hall and said: "Yesterday the bell was struck; today the drum is beaten.
What a fine Gate of Perfect Penetration! How many have ever awakened to it? If you have not yet passed through the Patriarch’s Barrier, do not follow the path of intellectual understanding.
Xuefeng played with a turtle-nosed snake; Xuansha is your tiger. Nanyue ground bricks and stones upon a whetstone; Niutou ate his meals in the refectory."

The preceding dance is a wondrous application of supernatural power, not something ordinary. In every step now, it transcends both past and present. Those who study the Way must be as discerning as the hours of noon and midnight;
do not harbor miscellaneous poisons within your heart and belly. Licorice is not inherently sweet, and yellow bitter-wormwood is not inherently bitter.
The west wind falls the leaves as ten thousand mountains turn autumnal; across the vast expanse of clear blue sky, the jade hare soars. *Small Assembly.* The lion cub leaps beyond.
A single roar from this assembly shakes the three thousandfold world; wild jackals, foxes, and wolves all retreat. Walking alone in the Great Dharma, he moves freely in every direction;
crouching on the ground and turning his body, he is without fear. If one is a fellow being born and dying together, then at every moment of engagement, one must transcend conceptual thought.
But tell me, what is the phrase that transcends conceptual thought? He strikes the meditation staff and says: "Empty space merges."
"Emptiness is like water merging with water. Small Session (Small Precept). Opening the eyes, one sees; closing the eyes, one sees. But tell me, what is it that you see?
If you say there is nothing seen, from where do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth come? From where do light, darkness, form, and emptiness arise?
Furthermore, where can one find rest? If you say there is something seen, this is still a false recognition of the shadows of mental discrimination regarding external objects.
But how can one transcend emotion and leave behind views? A wooden man rides a bamboo horse and knocks over Mount Sumeru.
*Small Assembly*: Today is the fifteenth day of the fifth month; green willows hang their threads in wild dance, and the yellow bird sings once.
"Two sounds! Every person becomes a Buddha or a Patriarch. He held up his staff and said, "Tell me, is this staff holy or ordinary?
He struck it once and said, "The sweet melon is sweet from stem to tip; the bitter gourd is bitter from root to end. (Fushí Xián’s Successor)
Master Chan Hanchan of Yanguan Zhenxiang initially studied under Xuedou, where he contemplated the "Mu" (No) koan.
Later, while studying under Baoen, one day water splashed onto his face, triggering a sudden realization. He went to the abbot’s quarters, and Xian asked, "What is the meaning of the 'Pine Tree'?
The Master held up his fist. Xian said, "That is far too remote. The Master said, "I thought there was something else. Xian said, "Not yet."

While they were on the way back, the Master said, "Preceptor, you should not deceive people. Xian nodded his head in agreement. While Xian was residing at Qizhen, the Master entered the room with the assembly.
Xian asked the assembly, "Why does Qizhen not reside in truth? The Master replied on his behalf, "Dead water does not harbor dragons.
Xian asked, "What is the dragon of living water? The Master said, "It stirs up waves but does not create billows. Xian said, "Excellent!"
[The Master] gave him thirty blows. The Master said, "Rise, Reverend Sir" (this was Xiansi of Fushí).
Chan Master Donghui Hao of Qingliang in Huzhou was surnamed Mei Liang; he was the son of the Thousand-Household Commander Wei of Panstone in Dong’ou.

After the dynastic change, he entered the monastic order at Ba’en Temple. He took up the "Wu-Wo" (The Dog) koan and attained realization through it, subsequently seeking further instruction from Xitang.
Fangwei Ze said, "How could a turtle ever escape from inside a jar? The Master replied, "It is right here and now. Ze then struck him with his palm, and the Master attained great enlightenment.

In the eleventh month of the Bingshen year of the Shunzhi era, the Master suddenly addressed the assembly, entrusted the dharma heir Songchao with his robe and whisk, sat in the lotus position, and passed away (his successor was Fushí Xián).
Chan Master Guǎnghuì Jūnshí of Hǎimén was the son of the Lěn family of Chángzhōu. He succeeded to the abbacy at Bào’ēn Temple.
On New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall and cited an ancient worthy who said: “Year after year, one’s countenance gradually fades;

what began as childhood play is now seen as streaked white hair. Although these words of the ancients are renowned sayings for warning the world, they cannot entirely avoid following [the flow of time].
While worldly affairs undergo change and flow, I, this mountain monk, am not so. Last year’s year is this year’s year; year after year, the original countenance remains unchanged.
Within the world, the sun and moon have neither newness nor antiquity; from childhood to a hundred and twenty years of age, there is no difference between the two.

In the *Xin-chou* year of the Kangxi era, I retired to Feng-yeong-ryeong. On the eighth month of the *Jia-chun* year, I chose an auspicious day to inform the assembly and passed away. (By Xian-si of Fu-seok.)
Chan Master Yutian Run of Guangxiao Temple in Taizhou was the son of the Tang family of Hezhou in Western Sichuan. He first visited Tiantong, but did not reach accord.

He went again to Baoen, where he participated in a seven-day intensive meditation retreat (*qijiu*). One day, during the formal assembly in the hall, the Master stepped forward and asked: "The jade candle shines brilliantly."
"The golden incense is richly fragrant. What is the matter of completing the seven-day period this morning? Xian said, "You tell me yourself.
As the Master hesitated, Xian struck him and said, "Why do you not say, 'The jade candle shines brilliantly and the golden incense is richly fragrant'?
At these words, the Master attained realization (he was the successor of Fushixian).
Chan Master Yunhan Man of Fucheng on Mount Yu was the son of the Zhang family of the local district. In his youth, he served as a provincial scholar (*zhusheng*).
In the *jiashen* year of the Chongzhen era (1644), he received the tonsure and ordination at Sanfeng. He served as the *jianyuan* (superintendent) there for three years.

In the *wuzi* year of the Shunzhi era (1658), when Xian of Ba’en went to Guanghui, Man crossed the sea to follow him and was appointed as the *jishi* (secretary). Subsequently, he received the transmission of the Dharma and resided at Ba’en, later residing there once again.

At Maitreya Monastery in Tongzhou, he later moved to Mount Yu, where he authored works such as the *Fuzong lun* (Treatise on Supporting the School) and the *Dianhua lu* (Record of Touching the Flowers).

His contributions to the vehicle of the Dharma (*zhongsheng*) are such that they shall endure imperishably. The *Hejing lun* (Treatise on Harmony and Stillness) states briefly: "Beyond the limit of Aviddhakarṇa, do not speak of 'how';

as soon as one enters the realm of form and sound, one immediately distinguishes between facing toward and turning away. To divide [reality] according to the four propositions is called being an outsider; cast it all into a single lump."
To emerge is what is called "total presentation. Thus, phenomena fall into two extremes and things are divided into self and other.

Where there is establishment, there is removal; where there is removal, there is establishment. In the past, when the World-Honored One preached the Dharma for forty-nine years, that was establishment.
To say, "I have never turned the wheel of the Dharma," is removal. "This very mind is Buddha" is Mazu’s establishment.
It stands thus: "Neither mind, nor Buddha. This is Mazu’s sweeping away. All manner of ritual forms are without exception like this;
why then doubt only Tian Tong and San Feng? Do not say that the Old Master’s single blow was ignorant of the fundamental principle (*zongzhi*).
Rather, he gathered the fundamental principle within that single blow, and through that single blow, he fully manifested the fundamental principle. He did not begrudge it.
Regarding the karma of speech: let me try to express this with a single word—*xianti* (顯提). A single blow contains the "phrase" (*ju*); not conceiving it as a blow is the "no-phrase.
Wherever it encounters anything, there is nothing it does not shatter; this is the "correct phrase. Thus, a single blow fully possesses these three phrases;

it encompasses heaven and earth like a box and its lid. With a single blow, one occupies and cuts off the vital ford, severing all currents. With a single blow, one applies the teaching according to the immediate occasion.
It is to go with the waves and follow the currents. To apply a single blow while the person does not perceive it is "to take away the person, but not the environment.

To turn one's body from beneath the blow is "to take away the environment, but not the person. When the blow is delivered and there is nothing that can be done, both person and environment are taken away.
When a single blow contains both killing and giving life, neither person nor environment is taken away. At the moment of the blow—
When sentiment is severed and meaning forgotten, this is the True Buddha. To penetrate through the stagnant waters of death with a single blow—this is the True Dharma.
To be free and sovereign in every direction with a single blow—this is the True Path. A blow that distinguishes guest and host is the First Phrase.
A blow that possesses the power to cut off the stream is the Second Phrase. A blow that contains the person within is the Third Phrase. A single blow encompasses all these.
Marvelous! Opening and closing; closing and opening—this is the essential point of the Three Mysteries. Not knowing where the single blow falls is the guest within the guest.
Using only the blow without recognizing its mastery is the host within the guest. Probing the situation with a single blow is the guest within the host.
With a single blow, completely gathering it all at the end is the host within the host. Thus one administers the blow.

To strike in accordance with [the student's state] is to employ function (*yòng*) after having first applied illumination (*zhào*). To strike when the inquiry has reached its ultimate limit is to apply illumination after having first employed function.

To strike immediately upon the sound of the question is for illumination and function to occur simultaneously. To strike while granting or withholding according to what is appropriate is for illumination and function to occur at different times.
A single blow that fully brings forth the Great Function is the Vajra King; beneath that blow, the myriad spirits tremble.
"Terrifying! A lion crouching on the ground. With one blow, he tests the capacity of the seeker; it is like a probe-staff or a shadow-grass.
With one blow, there is an eye at the tip of the staff; this one blow is not used as a single shout. This is what Sanfeng calls the single school of Linji.
The other four schools can be inferred by analogy. My venerable teacher was not unaware of this; since he knew it," so it was said.
And why sweep it away? Since ancient times, it has been valued only for causing people to doubt, not for causing them to awaken.
When one is made to doubt and then awakens on one’s own, one attains realization with joy and maintains it with firmness. To have a dharma handed down to others is but dead words;
how can dead words bring one joy? An ancient worthy said: "I do not value the moral virtue of my former teacher; I only value his..."
The Master did not explain it through for me. Xiangyan said, "If he had explained it for me at that time, I would certainly have cursed him today.
Those who have not yet attained awakening but presume upon it as a source of pleasure are known by all; their calamity is still shallow.
But those who understand the essential tenet while actually remaining unawakened—though their speech may be coherent—their calamity is inexhaustible. Therefore, [it is] painful.
He swept it away. When sweeping was insufficient, he cleared it out. When clearing was insufficient, he rescued it; then he both rescued and cleared it.
This was the master’s earnest effort to uphold the True Dharma Eye. Sanfeng was not unaware of this.
That one establishes [the teaching] without ceasing is likewise to remedy the maladies of superficiality, negligence, and lack of systematic order;
yet, the fundamental principles (gangjong) must not be made into a fixed attachment (bu-seok hyeon-si).
Chan Master Dunfu Hui of Hongjie Monastery in Yingzhou was over seventy years old, yet his diligent investigation of the Way never faltered.
Later, he visited Xian of Ba’en at Guanghui, where he received the Dharma. He subsequently went forth to preside over Hongjie. Entering the hall, he said: "I will not speak of life;
I will not speak of death. The crab walks sideways; the frog leaps straight up. A monk of the fundamental school must not be careless. He struck the meditation staff down.
One day, while a temple monk was involved in a legal dispute, the Master was also arrested. At the time of his detention, the Master remained serene;

he ascended the seat, spoke a verse, took leave of the assembly, and passed away. When the military commissioner of Huai and Xu heard of this, he led his fellow officials to prostrate themselves before him.
The officials and commoners gathered funds to build a stupa behind the temple (by Fu Shi Xiansi).
Chan Master Chuyun Han of Jingde Temple at Yuyuan in Jingzhou, a son of the Feng family of Wujiang, ascended the hall and said:
"When the myriad plants have withered to their ultimate limit, the manifold capacities of beings just begin to manifest a new form. Clearly, last night the Lord of Spring spoke, wishing to—"
Relying on the "mindless staff" for passage, he then took up the staff and looked at the assembly, saying: "This is the mindless staff. Tell me, what does it pass through?
He struck the ground once and said: "When every last twig and leaf has fallen away, a brand-new decree brings the spring wind.
*Small Assembly Sermon:* "Dense frost covers the earth like layered brocade; a single bright moon is like ice."
Round. The wild geese’ cries, sharp and piercing, urge on again and again. How many destitute children suffer through the bone-chilling cold!
At such a time as this, regarding the phrase "a drop of water, a drop of ice"—how do you speak? "Shutting the door, one pays no heed to the snow before the steps;
with the patched robe covering the head, it is best to rest. (Fushiku Enshi)
Chan Master Gu Yuanyan of Changlu in Zhenzhou [Qiujian], at the request of the Imperial Historian Yao Sicao, presided over Shanqing Monastery.
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: A monk asked Touzi, "What is the great matter of cause and condition?
Touzi replied, "The Minister Yin is opening the hall for me to uphold this matter; it must rely on the essential, raw hammering of the Buddha-dharma and worldly dharmas."
It is forged into a single whole. Today, if someone asks this mountain monk, "What is the great causal condition? I simply tell them:
"The Imperial Historian Yao has invited me to open the hall. Some may say, "How can you, Elder, merely copy the mold and clear the pit?"
He replied to him: "The matter exists as the meeting of a box and its lid; the principle should be like the point of an arrow meeting its target" (attributed to Fushí Xiànsì).
Zhāoyǐn Lùquán Shānyī Tóng Chánshī, whose late title was Dúchī, was the son of the Wáng family of Tóngxīng.
At the age of twelve, he entered the monastic order at Zhulin Temple. He took up the koan regarding one's "original face" and practiced it for a long time.
One day, he heard a monk ask Yunmen, "When a single thought has not yet arisen, is there still transgression? Yunmen replied, "Mount Sumeru."
Upon hearing these words, the Master suddenly attained realization. He then traveled extensively to visit various monastic centers, including Baohua, Tiantong, and Xuedou.

Finally, he visited Bao’en Xian, with whom his spiritual faculties were in accord; he was immediately granted the transmission of the Dharma. He subsequently went out to reside at Changlu and later presided over Lùquán.
When Xian passed away, he bequeathed the command for him to reside at Bao’en. Ascending the hall, he said: "All obstacles are, in themselves, the ultimate."
Jue: Just now, two monks were quarreling without ceasing, which provoked the staff of Baen to break into a rage.
Immediately, their heads split open and their brains spilled out, dripping with blood. Is there anyone here who can observe from the sidelines and reflect within?

Even if a duck hears the sound of thunder, how can one blame the blue sky for being far too hot? Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "I have been burying my head in the mountain valleys all along. When he saw...
"Meeting the person is not as good as hearing their name; today, his entire being has been laid bare. Hearing the name is not as good as meeting the person;
therefore, the Buddhas and Patriarchs appeared in the world for the sake of this one great matter. I, too, am here for the sake of this one great matter."
Appearing in the world, he raised his whisk and said: "This great matter—who among you lacks it? Ascending the hall, he said:
"As for this matter that has been passed down from of old, do not act with haste. To speak of it is not as good as seeing it; to see it is not as good as practicing it to the end.
Thus, Sīxin said: "One must reach the place where a single person is; one must reach the place where no person is."
"One must reach the ultimate even while still present. I venture to ask you all: which one among you has spoken to the bottom, seen to the bottom, and acted to the bottom?

If you can be scrutinized and found worthy, I shall bestow upon you with both hands this staff of Zhao Yin. After a long silence, he said: "Do not say that you do not wish to avoid being deceived. A monk asked:
"What is it like when one sees that all marks are non-marks; then one sees the Tathāgata? The Master [replied]: [Silence].
He said, "Wild geese fly up slantwise from their roosts at Hengtang; several silver jars hang from the middle of the trees. A monk asked again, "What is the master’s house style?
The Master said, "Within, there is not a single thing; without, there is nothing sought. The Master had opened his Dharma hall for many years; his teaching style was lofty and rigorous.
Monks flocked to him from all quarters upon hearing of his reputation, and it was called the height of prosperity for that time. There were various assemblies.
Recorded Sayings. Circulated in the world (by Busok Hyeonsi).
Master Pocheon Wok, a Chan master of the Seven Pagodas of Putuo on Ningbo, was the son of the Ge clan from Tongzhou. A monk asked him:
"How is it that you have a staff? I give you a staff. The Master said, "When light and shadow are both forgotten, look closely.
"How is it that you have no staff? I snatch away your staff. The Master said, "There is another spiritual light;
it makes one’s gallbladder cold with fear. "If that is so, then the wealthy regret that a thousand mouths are too few, while the poor lament that a single body is too many."
The Master said, "Do you understand this through intellectual reasoning? (Fushí Xiànsì).
Chan Master Tīngfēng Qīng of Shítóu Mountain in Jīnlíng was the son of the Zhèng family of Suīníng in Sīchuān. He sought to leave the household life, but his parents would not permit it.
They forcibly provided him with a wife, but the Master secretly purified himself; he died and then returned to life, thereby fulfilling his original aspiration.
Having shaved his head and received full ordination, he built a thatched hut and closed himself in retreat to contemplate the "Mu" (No) kōan.
After four years had passed without realization, he broke through his seclusion to travel south in search of instruction. He visited various monastic centers until he met Master Xian at Baoen Temple.

Xian asked, "When Mazu’s single shout caused Baizhang to be deaf for three days, why was that? The Master immediately shouted in response. Xian said, "He shouted; you also shouted. What have you accomplished by this?"
"What is it? the Master asked. Xian said, "A good text has many similarities. Xian said, "Try turning the words for me. The Master said, "The family property is completely spent;

sight and hearing are utterly severed. Xian said, "I agree. The Master presented a verse: "Lightning flashes and thunder roars, the scorched tail; The staff at Gepei has already transformed into a dragon-snake.
The rhinoceros, because of gazing at the moon, develops patterns on its horn; The elephant, startled by thunder, receives flowers within its tusks."
He resided successively at Jisheng, Huazang, Daci, and Qingta in Jiangning, and later passed away at Qingliang Temple on Qianjiang (his successor was Fushi Xiansi).
Master Hóngyá Gùtiānchún was the son of the Wú family of Huīzhōu. Having lost his mother in childhood, he followed his father into the monastic life.

He first visited Jiāshān Yù, who asked him, "Can you shoulder the burden of the construction work in the mountains? The Master made a gesture of shouldering a load. Yù said, "You are making things up.
The Master said, "I knew there would be this one opportunity. Yù struck him, saying, "What a fine 'having this'!"
Yiji. Next, he studied under Bao’en Xian. Xian brought up the story of Mazu’s single shout that left Baizhang deaf for three days.
The Master said, "A thief strikes when the house is unguarded. Xian asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "The land is vast and the people are few;
those who meet one another are rare. When Xian moved to Tiantong, the Master stood in attendance one day. Xian posed a question: "Great snow fills the long sky—what is its meaning?"
"What is the meaning of this? the Master said, "The King’s command has already been issued throughout the world; the General beyond the frontier has put an end to all smoke and dust.
Xian said, "Since it is Taibai Peak, why is its color green? The Master said, "Crookedness does not conceal the straight. Xian said, [and continued].
"Linglong Cliff" is known by people throughout the world; why then do those within the mountains not know of this leakage? The Master said, "It is precisely because they are within the mountains.
Xianxiu approved of this. The Master held seven assemblies for the opening of the hall, preaching the Dharma according to the capacities of his listeners.
In the twelfth month of the Jia-yin year of the Kangxi era, he manifested illness. On the twenty-third day, he wrote a verse to inform the assembly, saying:
"In years, fifty-seven; like lightning rolling through empty flowers, it is all finished. Casting off my hands, I return home; even a fine horse cannot catch me.
Having cast aside his brush, he passed away. His stupa was erected behind Fantian Temple in Hangzhou (by Fu Shi Xiansi).
Chan Master Fandian of Shengguo Monastery in Hangzhou was the son of the Zhu family from Yiwu. When he first arrived in Hangzhou, he stayed at the Bingluo Wooden Barracks.

One day, seeing the corpses of defeated soldiers, he became acutely aware that the matter of birth and death is of great importance. He took leave to join Chongsheng Monastery, where he received the tonsure and the full precepts.
Later, he went to Shangtian Tong Monastery to see Master Xian; after a long time, he attained thorough realization. Consequently, Master Xian appointed him to hold the whisk. He then split...
Striking through the spine and jaw, Taibai Peak knows how to follow the head with the tail. Presenting the fist and pointing upward, he awakens them;
Linglong Rock listens intently for the sound. How so? What is it like? Have you not heard?
"The mountains, rivers, and the great earth—all reveal the body of the Dharma King. Today, this new teacher opens wide here, speaking with earnest persistence. Directly...
Hū! The mud-ox sticks out its tongue; Huangbo vainly boasts of his skill. The stone man raises his hand—Great Fool, you must avoid harboring alarm.
The elephant king tramples and stands majestically in the Dharma hall; he smelts and refines the sly foxes until they turn into lions yawning.
Setting aside for a moment the lion’s yawn, O assembly: do you see the lion’s claws and fangs? *Zhen*.
Wei gave a single shout, saying: "The bright construction of the plank road is for you to recommend; the secret crossing of Chen’ang—no one knows it of me.
He struck his staff once and descended from the seat. (Fushí Xián was his successor.)
Chan Master Yu'an Guo was a native of Andong in Huai, with the family name Chen. While at Tiantong, he ascended the hall to hold the whisk and gave this address:
"If you can understand it in this way, you will be unhindered within the three realms; acting as a model for all things, you have fulfilled your duties both in the mundane and the supramundane.
If this is not yet so, listen further to these entangling vines. Therefore it is said: 'A hair's breadth...'"

Fix your mindfulness upon the karmic causes for the three miserable realms. A fleeting thought arises, and one is shackled for ten thousand kalpas. The names of "saint" and "ordinary person" are all but empty sounds;
their extraordinary features and inferior forms are entirely illusory colors. To pursue them is to accumulate heavy burdens; to reject them is to invite calamity.
Investigating their beginning and end, they are all instances of self-deception. Such a report is most remarkably manifest. Now tell me: how do you respond to the timing and the occasion?
"What about the phrase? He held up his whisk and said: "The willows unfurl their golden blossoms to open the true eye;
the plum blossoms fly through the snow, revealing the true heart. (Fushiku Enshi)
Chan Master Yueshan Yuan of Baoguang Temple in Jinling was a native of Siming. He ascended the hall and said: "This ancient site of practice has endured for over eight hundred years;

it was first opened during the Liang dynasty when a divine light appeared. Sages and ordinary beings have gathered here in assemblies of a thousand monks, causing the teachings to resound throughout the world and be proclaimed together.
The 'Separate Transmission Outside the Teachings' is the True Dharma Eye; holding up the ultimate truth alone, we establish the fundamental principles. Today, this mountain monk..."
Ascending the seat, [the Master] asked: "What is the phrase that conveys the transmission of the Patriarchs' intent? Consider this:

when the Snow Mountain [ascetic] practiced the Way for six years and, at night, beheld the morning star and attained awakening—did you not see how the Yellow-Faced Gautama flaunted his brilliance, acting as if no one else were present?"
If Baoguang had been present at that time, he would have given him a shout. Why? In whose hearth is there no smoke or fire?
Which man among them is not a true hero? (Fushí Xiànsì)

Master Baikeyi of Qizhen Monastery in Jiaxing ascends the hall at the conclusion of the retreat period (*jie zhi*). For one entire winter, you have been buried and submerged; the cord was held fast, not permitted to slacken.
This morning, the sack has been untied in accordance with the season; north, south, east, and west, the paths are naturally the same.
Grass sandals are as fierce as tigers; the staff is as alive as a dragon. For the most part, once you step out the door, it is all grass—do not look back!
The long road of Chang’an reaches its end; let go and proceed with ease. One remains sitting upright in stillness and solitude.

He gave a shout and said: "A crane has nine peaks before it spreads its wings; a horse lacks the thousand li before it can chase the wind. In the winter of the Dingwei year of the Kangxi era, the Master was guarding the stupa at Mount Jing.
One day, encountering a great snowfall, he informed the assembly that he was departing. They urged him to stay firmly, but he would not.

"Granted. The following morning, a woodcutter reported to the monastery’s permanent residents, "The Master has already passed away while standing in the snow" (referring to Fusuk, who was the dharma heir of Hyon-si).
When Seamsong Song, a Chan master from Shimen Huxiao, visited Hyon-u of Baeon Temple while he was living in retirement at Yeondam Village, he received a severe beating in the guest quarters.
His entire body was covered in blood, and through this, he attained realization. One day, Hyon asked him, "What is the meaning of Nanquan’s beheading of the cat?"
The Master said, "A sword leaves its precious sheath because of injustice; medicine comes from a golden jar to save the sick.

Xian asked, "What about Zhaozhou putting on his straw sandals and walking out? How was that? The Master said, "If it were not for the daughter-in-law exposing the family's disgrace, who would have known whether the mother-in-law’s feet were long or short?
He asked again, "Regarding Mazu’s single shout that left Baizhang deaf for three days—what was the underlying meaning?"
"How is it? the Master said. "The spring colors fill the garden and cannot be kept in; a branch of red apricot blooms over the wall.
Xian asked, "As for Huangbo hearing this and involuntarily sticking out his tongue—how would you explain that? The Master said, "The water flows cold from the side of the rock;
the wind comes fragrant through the midst of the flowers. Xian nodded in agreement and subsequently received his formal entrustment, departing to reside at Huxiao.
Every day he rowed a ferryboat to welcome and guide monks coming and going. Fuyan Rong sent him a verse of praise, saying:
"On that day at Zhujing there was a boatman; Who knew that today he would be here? Does the one who comes to study not resemble Jia Shan?
He need not fear being struck by a single oar and falling into the water. (Fu Shi Xian’s Successor)

Chan Master Jianlong Fayin [Jie] of Yangzhou was the son of the Peng family of Changzhou. He was born and raised in Xinghua; at the time of his birth, there was an auspicious sign of lotuses blooming on dry land.
While still in his mother’s arms, he would rejoice upon seeing the appearance of a monk. As soon as he began to learn to speak, he sought to become a monk.
His mother, Lady Yang, wished to grant his request, but his father, Tingbi, said, "My son is a member of a Confucian family; this is not permissible."
The mother prayed silently for her son every day. One day, she was moved by a golden-armored celestial deity who appeared in a dream and said to her, "Your son has sought to leave the household life;

why do you refuse him? The father was greatly astonished and amazed, and immediately sent him to Lubu Temple in the district to undergo the tonsure, placing himself under the guidance of Master Rongzhi as his preceptor.
On that same day, both parents shaved their heads simultaneously, and the entire family entered the Way, an event that spread throughout the nation.

He found this extraordinary. At the age of ten, the Master was already able to recite the *Lotus Sūtra* from memory. He encountered Xuedou Yun, who was in retreat at Nan’an, where Yun constantly showed people the koan:
"When your single breath does not return, where will you find a place to settle your body and establish your life? The Master felt a private sense of wonder and doubt.
When he reached thirteen, he suddenly brought up the previous conversation and went to ask Yun about it. Yun said, "Wait until your single breath does not return, and then I shall tell you."
The Master said, "What kind of mental activity is this, Preceptor? Yun said, "I give you thirty blows.
The Master said, "The Preceptor shall take half of them as well. Yun asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Master gave a shout and departed. At seventeen, he received full ordination.
Several fellow practitioners formed a seven-period retreat of diligent practice to investigate the "original face" koan. On the sixth day, one of them attained a point of entry, saying:
"Six times six is originally thirty-six. He subsequently traveled to visit Lian’an, Longchi, Weigu, and Nanmen, with whom he found mutual resonance in their karmic conditions.
He then visited Bao’en Xiu again; Xiu asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Yangzhou."
Zhaozhou asked, "Have you seen the Great Sage come? The Master said, "I have. Zhaozhou asked, "What kind of face does he have?
The Master cupped his mouth with his hands and said, "A cat! Zhaozhou then shut his room. The next day, Zhaozhou specifically ascended the hall and asked, "When will the cypress tree become a Buddha?
The Master said, "It became a Buddha long ago. Zhaozhou asked, "Who can testify to this? The Master snapped his fingers.
[The Master] gave one blow. Xiu laughed loudly and departed. Later, when they were coming out of the work period, Xiu asked, "Is your name Fayin (Dharma-Sound)?
The Master bowed. Xiu said, "Why does your head smell of excrement and urine? The Master said, "This is precisely my great function manifesting.
Xiu asked, "In what way is it your great function manifesting? The Master let out a shout. Xiu struck him severely. This continued until the third day.
Xiu repeated his previous words. The Master answered as before. Xiu asked this three times, and the Master likewise answered three times.
Each time, he was severely beaten. The Master then took his leave and went to visit Xian of Baoren and Tiantong. Xian asked, "Where have you come from?"
The Master said, "Repaying kindness. Xian asked, "What words or phrases are there regarding 'repaying kindness'? The Master recounted the previous story. Xian said, "Give him a severe beating!
The Master remarked, "Fine food is not for the stomachs of those already full. Xian suddenly asked, "Why was Baizhang deaf for three days because of Mazu’s shout?
The Master answered several times, but none of his responses were in accord with the truth. He returned to the hall and applied himself with intense effort to investigate the matter. One day—
While drinking tea, he suddenly heard the sound of thunder. A tea bowl fell to the ground, and he attained great enlightenment. He went to the abbot’s quarters and presented a verse, saying:
"Under the blue sky and bright sun, a single clap of thunder resounds; the true eye is opened wide, and the great earth is serene and peaceful.
Xian asked, "What is the message regarding the three days of deafness? The Master said, "Recognize the three before and the three after. Xian asked, "Furthermore..."
"Watch the Way," the Master said. He gave a shout, covered his ears with his hands, and departed. Xian laughed and said, "You have understood. He then bestowed upon him the robe and whisk.
[The Master] subsequently resided in succession at Dongling Yuanfeng, Yanling Longshu, and Daquan in Jinling. While ascending the hall for a discourse, he said:
A monk asked Ba Ling, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
Ba Ling said, "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; when the duck is cold, it goes down into the water. Wuzu Yan said, "Big as he was, Ba Ling only managed to say half of it.

Baiyun said, "I am not like this: gathering water, the moon is in my hand; playing with flowers, the fragrance fills my robes. The Master said, "The first arrow was still light; the second arrow is deep."
The five patriarchs, both great and small, could only speak half the truth. Nāgārjuna was not like this: "Where there is practice, ghosts do not recognize it;
where there is no mind, people do not know it. Why is this so? Because one who acts for others must act to the very end.
Ascending the hall, he raised a case: A monk asked Master Wugu: "Yesterday you gave me three blows with your staff; today you have set the staff aside. Master Wugu said: "Today..."
"I will not strike you," the Master said. "The crimson leaves depart without inscribing the flowing stream; how many fine households there are on the spring mountains!
To understand this monk is easy; to recognize the Master is difficult. Why is that? "When one reaches the river, the land of Wu ends;
beyond the bank, the mountains of Yue abound. If it were Chan Master Heng, it would not be so. This monk said, "Today, having cast aside my staff..."

[The Master] took up his staff; as soon as [the monk] made a sound, he struck him with the staff and drove him out of the Dharma Hall. "I guarantee that this monk will be right from head to toe. [The Master asked:
"Is there anyone among the assembly who would come to the defense of this monk? He threw down his staff and said: "When people are level, they do not speak;
when water is level, it does not flow. A monk asked: "What is it like to practice apart from mind, intellect, and consciousness? The Master grabbed him by the chest and said: "Apart from the mind!"
Before the monk could offer a word, the Master pushed him aside and said, "The deluded mind has been cleared away. The monk asked, "What is the First Origin?
The Master said, "In the sixth month there is no frost, yet it chills to the very bone. "What is the Second Origin?
The Master said, "To obtain his skin and marrow is to be deceived by him. "What is the Third Origin? The Master said, "If you wish to seek peace of mind, you will become even more unsettled."
"What is the first essential? The Master said, "Which of the thousand sages would dare speak head-on? "What is the second essential?
The Master said, "I alone permit the Lord of Spring to break into a smile. "What is the third essential? The Master said, "A beauty amidst snow and ice rides in a flower-littered palanquin.
The student said, "The three origins and three essentials have been pointed out by the Master; I pray you, Master, proclaim the final phrase."
The Master said, "I do not proclaim it. The monk asked, "Why do you not proclaim it? The Master said, "Śākyamuni has already passed away; Maitreya has not yet come.
The monk asked, "As for this single phrase right before us, how would you speak of it?
The Master joined his palms and said, "I do not dare to treat you with contempt; you shall all become Buddhas. (Fushiku Enshitsu)
Chan Master Daoyuan Zhi of Shigan Shian was the son of the Peng family of the district. He studied under Master Xian at Ba’en Temple and at Fucheng on Mount Yu.

On the day he received the Dharma transmission, he ascended the hall to wield the whisk and address the assembly: "The tradition of this new pagoda is distinct: to kill a man, one must see the blood."
An earthen jar suddenly roars like thunder, startling the void until it splits asunder. As the void bursts open, the great earth sinks entirely away.
Thus, above, there is nothing to grasp or look up to; below, one’s own self is utterly severed. Purely naked and starkly bare, one is completely liberated from all dependence.
Furthermore, tell me: how do you express this single phrase of being entirely without dependence? "The myriad worlds of the great chiliocosm are but bubbles in the sea;
all sages and worthies are like a flash of lightning. In the spring of the Dingwei year of the Kangxi era, the Master fell ill. He sent his fly-whisk back to Baoyun Temple.
He subsequently passed away (his successor being Pusok Hyeon).
During the Taeping era, Cheongshin asked Master Ancheom: "The physical body perishes; what is the indestructible Dharma-body?
The Master said, "Tonight the wind is blowing fiercely. The monk shouted. The Master said, "A true adept. As the monk was about to bow, the Master—
He struck him once across the spine and said, "Quickly, fix your eyes and look! The monk burst out laughing. The Master said, "Were you planning to engage me in some verbal entanglement?
The monk bowed again. The Master struck him once more and said, "First of all, do not forget. The Verse on the Dharmakāya by an Ancient Sage says:
"A family has a daughter, and a hundred families seek her hand; A family grants her in marriage, and a hundred families' pursuits cease. How laughable is the matchmaker!"
Competing for wealth and honor, he simply used a golden hairpin to secretly cast his lot (Fu Shi Xiansi).
Chan Master Lingdin L빙汶 of Suzhou was a native of Baoping. He registered as a resident monk at Fuyan Monastery and lit lamps in the quarters.
Yong was passing by from outside and said, "Had I known earlier that the lamp was fire, the rice would have been cooked long ago.
The Master struck out the lamp and said, "Everyone blows it out and walks in the dark. Yong said, "So there is someone inside the room after all. The Master said, "Thief! Thief!

Later, he went to see Xianyu at Baoen Temple in Fucheng and received his formal entrustment (*shishou*). He subsequently accepted an invitation to Lingdian. Addressing the assembly at Lingdian, he said: [The text continues with the discourse at Lingdian.]
When questioned about the Buddha-dharma by others, he left them with their mouths hanging on the wall. "Is there anyone among you who can say something?
After a long silence, he said, "I am not your equal" (Fushiku Enshi).
The Evening Assembly of Chan Master Yuzun Peng of Yunju on Wushan, Hangzhou. "The heavens are cold, the earth is cold; water drops freeze, ice forms.
Spreading the net and casting the line, they ensnare dragons and strike down phoenixes. This is the "five-flavors Chan" of all quarters;
when this mountain monk raises it, people’s heads ache. Brothers, as I announce this to you now, do not come crashing in recklessly after thirty years have passed.
A wild collision. He collides right into another’s mortar of minced vegetables. Evening Sermon: Yesterday was sunny; today it rains. The great earth is vast and dark.
The rivers and peaks all dance together. If you gentlemen wish to pass through the barrier of birth and death, you must discern the Master amidst the heap of sounds and forms.
[The Master] picks up his staff and holds it upright, saying: "Good people, this is form. [He] strikes the ground once with the staff and says: "This is..."
"Sound! What is the master? [He] let out a shout and said, "Look here! Addressing the assembly, he asked: "Do you understand?
If you say it is a matter of being simple and sleeping soundly at one's ease, people today are like those peering through a tube to see the sky.

They are accustomed to settling in cool, secluded places, indolently refusing to study the 'noisy' Chan of various quarters. With hearts exhausted and tears falling, I do this out of compassion for this assembly as they seek the Ultimate."
[This refers to] one who was unwilling to compete for precedence and vigorously applied the whip [to his own efforts] (Fu Shi Xiansi).
Chan Master Zhun of Qianfo Temple in Dengzhou was a native of Shu. Having long resided at Ba’en Temple as the head seat, he went out to reside at Qianfo Temple in Dengzhou.
On New Year’s Eve, he addressed the assembly: "Tonight, from Penglai, we gaze upon the sea water—vast, expansive, and boundless."
A free monk who has cast off constraints: he dwells in seclusion without using the three-pronged comb; he stands supported only by his seven-foot rattan staff.
Sitting in a circle around the brazier, he frequently adds charcoal; wrapped in his quilt upon a grass mat, he idly picks up the lamp. Following established custom, he must cook and slaughter;
I ask you, have you ever offered the head and hooves? (By Xiansi of Fushí)
Chan Master Mihe Li of Xilin Monastery in Kyoto ascended the hall and, rising from his seat, said:
"Virtuous ones, do you see the Prajñā-Dharmakāya? If you do not see it, then who is it that rises at dawn and sleeps at night, who bows and turns as you move about?
If you say you see it, then this very act of sleeping at night and rising at dawn, of bowing and turning as you move about, is fundamentally complete."
What need is there to seek further outward? Having arrived here, how can one speak of the principle of seeing or not seeing?
You all have each traveled extensively throughout the various regions and have long studied under eminent masters; have you ever seen such a person or heard such words spoken?
Even if you had seen or heard them, you would still be unable to avoid having these subtle words stagnate within your minds. Instead—
It becomes the field of objective perception; the ultimate reality (bhūtakoṭi) that dwells before one’s eyes is turned into a realm of names and forms. Thus it is said:

"Practicing through three lifetimes and sixty kalpas, or four lifetimes and one hundred kalpas, even until the fruit is perfected after three great aeons (trikalpa-asaṃkhyeya)—this is not as good as the realization in a single thought-moment that conditioned arising is unborn, thereby suddenly transcending the provisional teachings of the Three Vehicles. Then, looking to his left and right, he said: "Tell me, how is it like this?"
"What is the dependent origination of a single thought? He then struck his staff and said: "A snap of the fingers perfectly accomplishes the eighty thousand gates;
in an instant, the three great kalpas are emptied. Ascending the hall, he was asked: "The Master has not yet revealed his family style, and the student has already presented his conduct."
"Please grant me your high discernment. The Master struck him and said, "You field-slave! [The monk] asked, "What is the sword that kills the living?
The Master said, "It breaks down the city of Caizhou. [The monk] asked, "What is the blade that slays men? The Master said, "It hacks down Wu Yuanji. Then he said:
One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Striking teeth within the mouth of a venomous beast;
probing the bones upon the back of a black dragon. Seven, six, five, four, three, two, one. Rolling back the great void like a lion cub, tossing and turning with wild vigor.
One-seven, two-seven, the two intermingled; the entire dharma-realm is completely filled and obstructed. Pick up the "one" and cast away the "seven"—a flash of lightning.
Within the light, a thunderclap whirls; both "one-seven" and "two-seven" are forgotten. The deluded person still stands on this side. Letting go, one comes from the other side;
the hawk has already passed over the kingdom of Silla. Striking the desk with his hand, he said:

"Suddenly, having penetrated through the two layers of barriers, I grant you that the business of a lifetime of study is finished. When the two kings arrived, he ascended the hall and was asked: [The question follows.]

[The Master] manifested the body of a king and preached the Dharma for the assembly. [A monk] asked, "What is this Dharma that is being preached? The Master said, "In the lecture hall, swinging my arms.
The monk said, "If so, then the prediction at Vulture Peak has its place here. The Master said, "The entire assembly is present, as solemn as ever.
The monk said, "As for Zhaozhou of old, who spoke of 'ten thousand blessings' before even meeting you—was he perhaps deceiving you because you were his attendant? The Master said, "..."
The Master pointed directly at him and said, "Why did you later speak in such a manner? The monk replied, "I knew you would not understand.

As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him, saying, "After the rain has passed, the autumn waters in the night pond are deep. He then cited the case of Zhaozhou, when the Great King of Zhenzhou came to visit.
The attendant announced, "Master, the Great King is here. Zhaozhou said, "May the Great King be well. The attendant said—
"Not yet; I have only just arrived at the mountain gate. Zhaozhou said, "And you say you have come? The Master said, "Some say, 'The attendant only knows how to announce guests;
he does not realize his own body is in the imperial capital. It is intolerable that people should thus engage in false theft, failing to be monks of their own proper station.
Others say, 'Zhaozhou, for the sake of the shrimp's offspring, unconsciously struck out its eyes—this is valued only for its function.'"
Mute and deaf, they do not value the practice of citing evidence to settle a case; they insist on seeing Zhaozhou’s attendant, yet his simple and practical application of the Way is still not there.
This mountain monk has reviewed it once: it is simply that Your Majesty was improper to loiter outside the gate, causing such unnecessary circumlocution.
How does this compare to the two Princes, who have graced us with their presence today by proceeding directly to my chamber? Thus, there is no need to rely on the delivery of a message.
The tradition says that when the encounter and the strategic maneuvers are brilliantly displayed and vigorously raised, even this mountain monk would not be merely addressing the void.
Do you all see the master king? On Vulture Peak, the record of those years has not been forgotten;
the tip of the needle in the bag is exposed as the first phrase. A monk stepped forward and asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master held his staff crosswise.
The monk prepared to speak, but the Master struck him, saying, "This is the second phrase. He then descended from his seat. He ascended the hall again.
A monk asked, "When Śākyamuni said, 'At the moment of such reflection, the Buddhas of the ten directions all appear,' what is this appearing Buddha?"
The Master remained silent. [A monk] asked, "Master, you remain silent; are you not engaging in thought? The Master still did not look at him.

After a long while, he said, "O worthy ones, at such a time as this, some might say that one should deploy the noble and transcendent spirit of Shao-wu to critique the ancients, or exert the mechanism of Baiyun’s crossing the threshold to face the enemy from all eight directions. Who does not know that within the purple silk curtain?"
"I have always been too lazy to scatter real pearls," the mountain monk said. Looking to his left and right, he asked, "Do you understand?
There must be those of penetrating insight who can appreciate this sound together. A question was asked: "When Mañjuśrī’s sword did not spare him at that time, what was it like?
