To attain awakening at a mutton stall in a bustling marketplace still involves a long journey; to step upon it before a crossroads is merely to encounter a shadow or an echo.
Therefore it is said: "The source is not far; the ocean of nature is not remote. Simply seek within yourself; do not search for it elsewhere.
If you seek it, you will not find it; even if you find it, it is not real. Within this state, you must be utterly naked, with not a single thread of attachment remaining. Be bare and unadorned.
Hàn heard this being said and took it upon his own shoulders, never looking back; he had a measure of resonance with it. To deliberate or reflect upon it is to lose all connection.
Why? He brandished his whisk and said: "A single mirror on the dais is as bright as the sun; ten thousand ages of clear sky are free from right and wrong. He ascended the hall and said:
"When the ox comes into the mountains, there is plenty of water and plenty of grass. When the ox leaves the mountains..."
Touching east, touching west—suddenly piercing through the vast void. It is not the mind, nor is it the Buddha. If someone on the road ahead asks, "What school is this?
it is precisely the right time to strike them across the mouth with a heavy fist. Do you not see? A hawk from the heavens of Liao: amidst ten thousand layers of clouds, it makes but a single dash.
The golden lock of the primal gate opens at the opportune moment; in this life, one shall not leave it buried in vain. This is it.
"It is so. Many people laugh at this mountain monk for corrupting the sons and daughters of others. After a long silence, he said: "My heart bears no grudge against men;
my face shows no color of shame" (Lin-yeh Qi-si).

Chan Master Yunfu Bian of Dongshan in Andong was the son of Jiang [family] of Jiangxi; his mother was Chen. He addressed the assembly, citing the case where a monk asked Guizong, "What is the Buddha? Guizong said, "I tell you, fearing that you might not believe me. The monk said, "Since the Master speaks with such weighty words, how would I dare not believe? Guizong said, "It is simply you. The monk asked, "How does one maintain this? Guizong said: [He continued: "When you walk, do not think of walking; when you stand, do not think of standing; when you sit, do not think of sitting; when you lie down, do not think of lying down. This is called 'maintaining. Furthermore, when you see forms, do not grasp at their appearance; when you hear sounds, do not cling to their resonance. This is called 'maintaining. Moreover, when thoughts arise, do not follow after them; when thoughts cease, do not seek them out. This is called 'maintaining. The monk said, "If one maintains it thus, what fault will there be? Guizong said, "There will be no fault, but you must not let it become a habit. The monk said, "How can I avoid letting it become a habit? Guizong said, "Do not be mindful of non-mindfulness. The monk said, "Who is it that is mindful of non-mindfulness? Guizong said, "The one who asks is precisely that which is mindful of non-mindfulness. The monk said, "If so, what is the ultimate meaning of this matter? Guizong said, "The ultimate meaning of this matter is simply this: do not be mindful of non-mindfulness. The monk said, "If one is mindful of non-mindfulness, is that not still being mindful? Guizong said, "If you are mindful of non-mindfulness, you are not yet free from mindfulness. The monk said, "Then how should one act? Guizong said, "Just act as you do now, but do not be mindful of non-mindfulness. The monk said, "If I am mindful of non-mindfulness, I am still not free from mindfulness. If I am not mindful of non-mindfulness, I am not yet free from non-mindfulness. What should I do? Guizong said, "If you wish to understand this matter, you must first sever the root of the mind. Once the root of the mind is severed, all phenomena will naturally vanish. When all phenomena have vanished, the mind has no place to dwell. When the mind has no place to dwell, the Way is spontaneously realized. The monk said, "If the mind has no place to dwell, how can one attain liberation? Guizong said, "Liberation is simply the absence of dwelling. There is nothing else to be attained. The monk said, "If there is nothing to be attained, why do people still practice the Way? Guizong said, "People practice the Way because they fear birth and death. If you realize that there is originally no birth and death, what need is there for practice? If you realize that the nature of the Way is originally complete and perfect, there is no longer anything to be sought. The monk said, "If there is nothing to be sought, what is the purpose of the Buddhas and Patriarchs appearing in the world? Guizong said, "The Buddhas and Patriarchs appear in the world solely to point directly to the mind, so that sentient beings may awaken to their own nature. They do not seek anything outside of the mind. The monk said, "If one awakens to the mind, is that not itself the Way? Guizong said, "Awakening to the mind is indeed the Way, but do not mistake the awakening for the Way. The Way is not something that can be awakened to; it is simply the original state of the mind. If you can recognize your own face before your parents were born, you will know that the Way is not something created by the Buddhas and Patriarchs. The monk said, "If the Way is not created by the Buddhas and Patriarchs, who created it? Guizong said, "The Way is not created by anyone. It is simply the reality of all things. All things are the Way; the Way is all things. If you can see all things as the Way, you will not fall into the view of existence. If you can see the Way as all things, you will not fall into the view of emptiness. Free from both existence and emptiness, you will transcend all conceptualizations. The monk said, "If I transcend all conceptualizations, is that not the ultimate realization? Guizong said, "Ultimate realization is simply the absence of conceptualization. Do not seek realization outside of conceptualization; do not dwell on realization within conceptualization. If you can be free from both seeking and dwelling, you will be in accord with the Way. The monk said, "If I am in accord with the Way, what is my daily conduct? Guizong said, "Your daily conduct is simply your ordinary activities—eating, drinking, working, and resting. Just do not add any artificiality or contrivance to them. If you can act naturally and spontaneously, you are acting in accord with the Way. The monk said, "If I act naturally and spontaneously, how can I avoid falling into the trap of self-indulgence? Guizong said, "Self-indulgence arises from attachment to the self. If you realize there is no self, where can indulgence occur? If you can maintain this awareness at all times, you will not fall into the trap of self-indulgence. The monk said, "If I maintain this awareness, is that not still a form of grasping? Guizong said, "Maintaining awareness is not grasping; it is simply being present. If you grasp at presence, that is grasping. If you do not grasp at presence, there is no grasping. The monk said, "If there is no grasping, is that not liberation? Guizong said, "Liberation is not something that can be attained through effort. It is simply the cessation of all striving. When all striving ceases, the mind is at rest. When the mind is at rest, there is liberation. The monk said, "If the mind is at rest, how can one respond to circumstances? Guizong said, "Responding to circumstances is the function of the mind. If the mind is at rest, its function is spontaneous and unimpeded. Like a mirror reflecting images, there is no deliberation or calculation. This is true liberation. The monk bowed and withdrew. Guizong said, "This matter is like a great mountain: if you try to climb it, you will exhaust yourself; if you try to cross it, you will never reach the other side. You must simply let go of all efforts and rest in the natural state. Then, without going anywhere, you will arrive; without doing anything, you will accomplish everything. The monk said, "If I rest in the natural state, how can I avoid falling into the pit of indolence? Guizong said, "Indolence is the opposite of diligence. If you rest in the natural state, there is no indolence. Diligence and indolence are both mental constructs. If you can transcend these constructs, you will find the true path. The monk said, "If I transcend these constructs, what is the ultimate goal? Guizong said, "The ultimate goal is simply the realization of the original nature. Once the original nature is realized, there is no further goal to be reached. The monk said, "If there is no further goal to be reached, why do the scriptures speak of attaining Buddhahood? Guizong said, "Attaining Buddhahood is merely a metaphor for the realization of the original nature. It is not a physical transformation or a change of status. It is simply the awakening to the fact that one's own mind is fundamentally identical to the Buddha-mind. The monk said, "If my mind is fundamentally identical to the Buddha-mind, why do I still experience suffering and joy? Guizong said, "Suffering and joy are like clouds passing across the sky. They arise and pass away according to conditions, but they do not affect the nature of the sky. Likewise, suffering and joy arise and pass away according to conditions, but they do not affect the nature of the mind. If you can remain unmoved amidst suffering and joy, you have realized the nature of the mind. The monk said, "If I remain unmoved amidst suffering and joy, is that not the state of a sage? Guizong said, "A sage is simply one who has realized the nature of the mind. There is nothing more to it than that. The monk said, "If I have realized the nature of the mind, what should I do next? Guizong said, "There is nothing to do next. Just continue to live your life as before, but with a mind that is free from attachment and delusion. This is the practice of a Bodhisattva. The monk said, "If I practice as a Bodhisattva, how can I benefit sentient beings? Guizong said, "Benefiting sentient beings is the natural expression of a Bodhisattva's compassion. It does not require any special effort or artifice. If you can maintain a compassionate heart in all your actions, you will naturally bring benefit to others. The monk said, "If I maintain a compassionate heart, is that not
"A single film over the eye causes empty flowers to fall in confusion. A monk had an awakening. The Master said, "Old man Guizong was far too reckless in not sparing his eyebrows.
What kind of monk is this, swallowing the whole date at once without cause? When examined closely, he deserves a blow with the staff.
Someone asked, "How is it, Master, what is the Buddha? The Master simply said to him, "Gourd and winter melon. How so?
Guaranteeing and maintaining it: the straight is straight, the crooked is bent. Addressing the assembly, he gave a shout and said: “Do you understand?
If there were Chan to speak, a Persian would close his mouth and chew raw iron. He shouted again and said: “Do you understand?
If there is no Chan to speak, striking Mount Sumeru with a whip brings no pain at all; Mañjuśrī beats his breast and reviles Samantabhadra; Hanshan claps his hands.”
The hands laugh as they pick up what is found; the eyebrows above the eyes arch like the character "八" (eight). From the beginning, there has never been a single thing lacking.
Only these two lips and tongue harbor resentment day and night without ceasing. Why is this?

It is because you, my fellow brothers, during the twelve periods of the day and night, have far too many unexamined words and far too little effort in investigating the essence. Return to the hall and each examine yourselves.
(Lin’ya Kishi). Zen Master Taiching Fanchin went to visit Lin’ya Kishi at Tiantong. Kishi asked, “If you call it a bamboo stick, you encounter resistance;
if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you turn your back on it. Ultimately, what would you call it? The Master replied, “I am poor and have nothing.”
Pegui covered himself with his robe. Qiji asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The original person is revealed. Qiji asked, "Who is the original person?
The Master said, "A three-headed, six-armed pillar supporting the heavens; the wrathful Nezha strikes the Imperial Bell. Qiji said, "Not yet—speak further!
The Master said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice. This attendant is fortunate to be at home."
Renqi nodded his chin in approval. Renqi asked, "How many people in this hall are paying back their meal money? The Master said, "What need is there to mention 'how many'?

Every person stands head-to-heaven and feet-on-earth; each and every one has a straight nose and slanting eyes. Renqi said, "If that is so, why is it necessary to practice the seven-day retreat (*qijie*)?
The Master said, "If we did not practice the seven-day retreat, how could we manifest his excellent qualities? Renqi asked, "Where, then, is he?"
Qichu said, "Everyone stands with their heads reaching heaven; each person has a straight nose and slanting eyes.
One day Qichu asked again, "In the hall, how many are fit for carving? How many are unfit for carving? The Master said, "Ask the Holy Monk.
Qichu said, "What are you doing in the hall? The Master said, "Last night we served the evening meal. I..."
He ate two bowls with the assembly. In the eighth month of autumn in the Gui-si year of the Shunzhi era, the Master fell ill. At the time of his passing, he sat upright and departed.
A disciple who had received some of his teachings asked that he might be entrusted once more with one or two others. The Master said in a stern voice, "Quanzi has already gone;
what more is there to do now? Thereupon, he passed away. (Lin Ya Qi was his successor.)

Chan Master Yishan Xintang of Hangzhou was the son of the Xianyu family of Chongqing. Having left the household life to travel as a mendicant, he received formal transmission upon contemplating the saying:
"For three years he did not eat a meal; yet before his eyes, there was no one who was hungry. He ascended the hall and said:
"Sentient beings and Buddhas, the great earth and mountains and rivers, the past and present, the worlds beyond and this world—all are entirely within my staff."
Upon his head, he emits a great radiance. Together they speak a few words of meaningless talk.
If one examines them closely, it turns out they can indeed be spoken; every sentence is manifest and complete. But tell me: what is this manifest sentence?
"An octagonal millstone rolls in empty space; a three-legged donkey trots on its hooves. A wooden man claps a board in the clouds; a stone woman..."
Blowing a sheng flute from the bottom of a well—the lanterns and the pillar laugh heartily. What more need be said of the "dry dung pellet" or the "three pounds of hemp"?
Having seen through all these stone lands and earths, even if one can speak, one cannot practice (according to Lin Ya Qi’s succession).
Chan Master Daoan Jing of Xiangyan on Mount Huqiu in Gusu was the son of the Zheng family of Yuyao in eastern Zhejiang.
His original name was Xilong, and his courtesy name was Liuyu. He was born after being in the womb for twelve months. From childhood, he was notably grave and quiet, seldom speaking or laughing.
When he was four or five years old, upon seeing cracks in the walls of the classics and the collapse of dilapidated houses, he would immediately feel a sense of sorrow and apprehension.
He was fearful. One day, a mendicant reciting the Heart Sūtra reached the passage: "Because the mind is without hindrance, there is no fear.
Unconsciously, his heart felt expansive and his spirit at ease, as if emerging from a deep valley; his doubts and fears were removed from that moment on.

Whenever he beheld the majestic and adorned features of the Buddha, he would rejoice and sigh with admiration, regretting that he could not personally experience such a presence. At times, when entering or leaving [the temple], he encountered...
The patch-robed monk must be sincere and reverent, as if meeting an old friend. As he gradually grows, the thought of transcending the world arises;
when discussing worldly matters, he feels a sharp sense of unease. Upon seeing women, he feels revulsion and resentment, resolving never to marry.
From the age of ten until twenty, the Master has already enrolled him among the disciples, providing him with a stipend from the granary; thus, all worldly attachments are dispersed and severed.

There was not a single object that could stir his emotions. At twenty-one years of age, he studied under Guan Xiabiao, who instructed him with works such as Yuan Liaofan’s *Gongguo lu* (Record of Merits and Faults).
He rejoiced greatly and practiced according to these teachings. Later, he met Shen Qiuru of Shilang.

Having consulted [his master] to resolve his doubts regarding the mind, he finally recognized the single path of Chan meditation. He ascended the dharma hall three times and attended the assembly nine times, practicing with earnestness and without interruption.

Within one or two years, he occasionally experienced moments of insight, yet he had not yet attained full realization. One autumn, he resolved to exert himself, taking up the koan "The myriad dharmas return to one.
On a single meditation cushion, he sat rigidly as if prepared to die, not breaking his session for six days and nights. As he stepped out through the gate of the platform, he encountered...
The great waters were vast and boundless; the wind was pure and the moon bright. My body, mind, and the world were expansive and utterly solitary.
Having realized the principle that "above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored," I could not help but dance with hands and feet, spontaneously composing several long songs and short verses.
I still recall a few lines: "Originally there is no constraint; why then would one not be free?"
"Not free; it is simply because you seek elsewhere. Rest, rest! The great trichiliocosm is gathered within a single hair.
From then on, he visited and questioned Tiantong Wu, seeking instruction in many matters. One day he asked, "For one who has attained great realization, how does one pass the days?
Wu struck him with his palm. The Master said, "How does one reach the state where not a single thought arises? Wu said, "This is your dwelling place."
"Where is the head? The Master said, "Zhaozhou said, 'Except for the two times of rice gruel and meals, there is no place for the mind to be distracted.
What is the meaning of this? Wuzhuo struck him immediately. Thus, he asked several times and was struck several times; his sleep and food were no longer at peace.
One morning, kneeling upright, he asked, "Ultimately, what is Zhaozhou’s place of mental application? Wuzhuo gave him a blow right to the head and said, "Zhaozhou!"

"The Prefect gives it to you; what does it have to do with you? At these words, the Master was as if ten suns shone at once, like the sudden laying down of a burden of hundreds of thousands of catties.
He sprang to his feet, cried out, "I, your disciple, shall simply go thus!
and went out dancing. Turning to his attendant, he said, "This fellow is indeed somewhat stubborn. From that time on...

Though situated amidst the field of fame and profit, he remained at ease wherever he was, unchanged by circumstances. Originally intending to don the black robes [of the monastic life] at age thirty, he did so because the debts of gratitude owed to his sovereign and parents had not yet been repaid.
He entered the Zhejiang provincial examinations twice, meeting with failure each time. Subsequently, invited by his elder brother, he traveled to the Northern Capital;

there, he unfortunately encountered national turmoil and suffered such terror that he nearly lost his life. He braved dangers to return south, enduring various extraordinary hardships, yet his mind remained undisturbed.
He was moved, yet it remained only as a faint, lingering sensation; he did not know why there was a certain point that could not be let go of or dissolved.

Not daring to deceive himself, he went at once to Shilang, where he stayed for some time to investigate the matter to its ultimate conclusion. Shilang then recounted the karmic circumstances regarding Gaofeng.
The Master asked for further instruction, saying, "If someone had asked you, Teacher, at that time, how would you have answered? Lan Zhi replied, "I would have given him three blows with my fist.
From then on, all his stagnation was completely resolved; he became liberated and unimpeded.
While wandering by chance at Puzhu Ridge in Ninghai, he found the mountains and rivers extraordinary, as if there were another world. He settled there and founded the Zhengjue Chan Monastery.
He entered Mount Taiyang and paid respects to the venerable elder Miaoxing, requesting ordination. The Master [Miaoxing] then transmitted the Dharma-sea seat to him as his successor.

Following Miaoxing’s passing, the Master completed the arrangements for the stupa and funeral rites. He subsequently traveled extensively through various monasteries to seek out and consult with learned masters.
Later, he visited Tiantong Qi, who asked: "As soon as there is right and wrong, confusion arises and the mind is lost; how is it that you do not interfere with this?"
"This is not the case," said Master Qi. "The night is still and deep, and people are sleeping soundly. He gave a shove.
The Master said, "Why trouble the bright moon to come and peep again? Qi then severely rebuked him. Later, when he came to consult again, Qi said, "Your response was not intimate enough."
"How can the Great Function be made manifest? The Master bowed with trepidation and asked, "As for you, Reverend, how would you do it?
Qi suddenly raised a single fist. At that moment, the Master felt like a dragon finding water or a tiger relying on its mountain;
he then understood why Mazu’s single shout had left Baizhang deaf for three days—it was truly for this reason. Qi nodded in approval and immediately conferred upon him the lineage.
Liuyi Fu resided at Daolin in Shanyin, Fayun at Yanguan, Jingxiu in Tainan, Fahai in Siming,
Xingguo and Ganlu in Gusu, Jingshou, Cixiang, and Shenggan at Caoqi in the capital,
Daping in Linqing, and Shihe in Henan; in his later years, he returned south.
He retired to Xiangyan on Mount Huqiu, where his life was recently recorded in the *Zhizhuyulu*.
His compassionate heart in guiding others and his high reputation throughout the world were indeed not in vain. Ascending the hall, he said: "The single move facing forward cuts off all diversities.
The Buddha-dharma and the Way of Chan are like a worn-out straw sandal; Xuanzha’s intellectual understanding is nothing but a dried piece of excrement. Deshan’s staff, Linji’s shout—"
"Jihe! "Ciming thrusts his sword. "Zihu looks at the dog. The applications of these ancients were different, yet they still did not accord with the fundamental source.
If one could indeed accord with the fundamental source, then Hu Zhangsan and Hei Lisi—when old friends meet, what words are there?
"Yesterday was sunny, today it rains"—the livelihood of a patch-robed monk is just like this. Pointing with his staff, he said: "Just now..."
The Venerable Elder said just now: "When meeting people, do not err in your conduct. [He] ascended the hall and said:
"I, this mountain monk, have been a guest for a long time; my staff has grown eight inches shorter. If any among you can cause it to grow back, I shall appoint you as a head official.
Otherwise, remain in quietude and wait for it to grow on its own. The assembly remained silent. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "At night, beholding the morning star, the World-Honored One attained enlightenment. This is like an old gourd; it remains just as it was.
Whether it is good or not good, those looking on from the sidelines will laugh. But tell me, who is the one looking on? Speak! Speak!
After a long silence, he gave a shout and ascended the hall. "Today is a spring day. I remember when I was at Fuyuan, a monk asked about the Patriarch from the West."
Regarding the meaning of these [sayings], he replied: "A sunny spring day, a yellow oriole singing. That monk was suddenly enlightened.

When he was abiding at Fayun Temple, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He replied, "A sunny spring day, green spring grasses. That monk was suddenly enlightened.
Last year, while he was at Jingshou Temple, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He replied, "A sunny spring day, the spring breeze is still."
That monk danced as he went out. Had he been able to realize it within the phrase "Fuyuan," he would have been fit for Zen understanding;

had he been able to realize it within the phrase "Fayun," he could have been called a member of the Zen assembly; had he been able to realize it within the phrase "Jingshou," he would have been what the ancients called a "Zen Champion.
If you have not yet attained clarity in all these, you will meet [the master] and fail to grasp it, returning empty-handed from the mouth of the cave.
"Peach blossoms also laugh at people. [He] ascends the hall. "The Buddha-dharma exists in the New Year; face south and look at the Big Dipper.
The Buddha-dharma does not exist in the New Year; press a gourd upon the water. Neither existent nor non-existent: a tiger watches a water mill. No calculations or deliberations can reach it.
It is better to dwell happily in whatever circumstances one finds. [He] ascends the hall. "Never departing from this very place, it is eternally..."
"Profoundly still. If you seek it, you know it cannot be seen. When this mountain monk first began his studies, I obtained these two phrases;
they were like a tiger relying on its mountain, or a fish finding its water. To this very day, I have not exhausted their utility.
Today, I have specially prepared a great vegetarian feast to offer to all of you. I pray that you will eat your fill and drink deeply, and that none of it shall fail to be digested.
Ascending the hall: In the past you analyzed this in detail; today you have requested it once more. Truly, there is no reason for this;
it is also a sign of insatiable greed. The Master is ever-awake; you must know how to look down the well, and never let the donkey look down the well.
There is no need to seek elsewhere: the Jewel Cavern lies atop the level slope. Ascending the hall: The wind here is somewhat stiff; for now...
He returned to the warm room to deliberate. After a long while, he said: "I have annotated it far too extensively. Ascending the hall, he said: "The fan is the fan; it is the fan.
Throughout kalpas, it has been clearly and inconceivably so. People of this age do not recognize the Buddha of True Nature;
they take Vairocana to be an ant. Twenty years ago, I spoke thus; yet looking back now, it turns out otherwise."
"Indeed. Harmony-fanning, harmony-fanning, it is so. Throughout kalpas, it is luminously inconceivable.
If people of this age recognize the True Buddha, then ultimately Vairocana is but an ant. Question: "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said:

"South of the Heavenly Terrace, north of the Five Terraces. Question: "What is the host within the guest? The Master said: "The nest knows the wind; the burrow knows the rain. Question: "How... [The text ends here.]
"This is the guest within the host. The Master said, "Raise your hands high; bow low. "How is it the host within the host?

The Master said, "He employs men of heaven and drives away Buddhas and patriarchs. [The student] asked, "I ask for the Master’s single pointer regarding the essential point of the School Gate. The Master raised his fist and said:
"This is not a fist. [The student] asked: "What is the Master’s point of intimacy within illness? The Master said: "A thousand kinds of suffering. [The student] asked:
"What is the Master’s place of efficacy? The Master said: "It cannot be rotted by boiling or steaming. [The student] asked: "What is the Dharma-eye? The Master said:
"Bright by day and dark by night. [The student] asked: "What is that which is above the Dharma-body? The Master said: "Daylight and nighttime."
[The student] asked: "Master, you sleep at night and rise early in the morning. [The Master] said: "When it was thus, I was truly unmoved. [The student] asked:
"Are the Essence (Zong) and the Teaching (Jiao) the same or different?
[The Master] said: "A fist and an open palm. [The student] asked: "What is the matter regarding the portion of the patch-robed monk? [The Master] said: "Do not [speak]."
[The monk] asked about the ox passing through the window lattice: "The head, the horns, and all four hooves have already passed through;
why is it that the tail cannot pass? The Master said, "What ghost are you trying to beat? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him directly and sent him out from the abbot’s quarters.
The Master asked a monk, "How do you reconcile the mountains, rivers, and the great earth with your own portion of reality? The monk said, "Do not speak of them as two."

"Two stakes. The Master struck the monk once with his staff and then struck the incense table once, saying, "Why is it that when I strike you, you feel pain, yet when I strike the incense table, there is no pain?
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Those two stakes are yours; these two stakes are mine. A monk arrived for the first time.
The Master asked, "For what reason have you come? The monk replied, "I have long been directed toward the Master. The Master said, "Now tell me—"
"Where is this mountain monk? The monk was speechless. The Master struck him out directly.

In the seventh month of the autumn of the Jisi year, the Master returned from Yao River. Upon arriving at Xiangyan, he manifested slight illness. When his disciples first brought medicine, the Master said:
Regarding my illness, the physicians of this world have been unable to cure this old monk; their prohibitions are exceptionally strict.

Nevertheless, I have daily taken up and examined the public cases (gong'an) of the ancients without the slightest weariness. To anyone who came to inquire after my health, I would immediately demand a response (a "turning word").

When the Double Ninth festival arrived, I announced in advance the date of my departure. At midnight on the thirteenth day, when the time had come, the assembly gathered before the Master and helped him to his feet.
Having finished his bath, he then gave these instructions: "The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye is not like the dissemination of worldly conventions.
Do not report my death or wear mourning garments; do not concern yourselves with empty formalities," and so forth. He then requested a verse. The Master said, "Why such worldliness?

In the past, our late Patriarch Tiantong also had nothing to say. Take care of yourselves each according to your own station; this old monk shall depart into liberation wherever he may be. He passed away.
Thus he entered into quiescence. His secular age was seventy-eight, and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇerī-vassa) was forty-four.

He was interred at Gaofeng in his native prefecture, in a burial site oriented toward the hexagram Hai and supplemented by Qian, where metal receives water. His *Yulu* (Recorded Sayings) in thirty fascicles circulates in the world. (By Lin’ye Qi’s Succession)
Master Xingmi of Jizhao at Tongxiang ascended the hall. Suddenly grasping his staff, he called to the assembly, saying:
"The youth Bingding has arrived! Take care of your eyebrows! (Linye Qi succeeded him).
Chan Master Yuan of Xiangyan on Mount Dang in Nanyang was the son of the Zhao family from Dazhou in Western Sichuan.

After both his parents had passed away, he went to Ba’en Temple to pay respects to Master Youshi and received the tonsure. He subsequently left Sichuan; first he visited Master Wen of Zhulin, and next he called upon Master Qi of Tongxuan at Dongta in Jiahe.
He took up residence in the meditation hall. That night, as Master Qi entered the hall, he said: "If you take this as a staff..."

Chan Master Yuan Mifrung of Tianshou, the thirty-fifth generation descendant of Nanyue, initially stayed at Boshan.
There he investigated the "Wu" (No) kōan regarding the dog and attained a realization.
Later, he visited Lin’ao Yu at Jiaoshan; upon seeing him, [Yu] immediately said, “I have long heard of the Master. Today I have seen you in person.”
Yuan said, "Do not open your mouth in vain; speak one word of intimacy. The Master made a gesture of salutation and said, "Please, Preceptor, speak.
Yuan tapped him three times with his whisk. The Master held up one hand. Yuan asked, "Where did you learn that?
As the Master was about to open his mouth, Yuan let out a loud shout. He entered the hall for formal instruction and cited the teachings, saying: "One should not grasp at dharmas..."
He should take up what is not the Dharma. Then he held up his whisk and said: "This is the Dharma; which one is not the Dharma?
This is not the Dharma; which one is the Dharma? He asked, "Does the assembly have anyone who does not fall into existence or non-existence, nor descend into right or wrong?
After a long silence, he said: "You bhikṣus, you must understand my preaching of the Dharma. (Lin Gao Yu succeeded him.)
Chan Master Kai of Shimen in Huzhou attended the assembly at Zhulin.
The Master asked, "When Deshan carried his almsbowl past the hall, Xuefeng said, 'The bell has not yet rung and the drum has not yet sounded; where did the Master go with your bowl?
Deshan lowered his head and returned to the abbot’s quarters. What was the meaning of this? Yu said, "That truly scratches my itch. The Master said, "As for Xuefeng..."
Feng raised the case as an example for Yantou. Yantou said, "The Great Master Deshan has not yet realized the final word.
Regarding Yantou speaking thus, what principle does it accord with? Yuyu said, "A son conceals his father's faults.

The Master asked, "When Deshan heard this, he ordered his attendant to summon Yantou and say, 'Do you not approve of me, old monk? What was the meaning of this? Yuyu said, "A father conceals his son's faults."
Yinyuan said, "Yantou then secretly revealed his intention. [The Master asked: "Where is the point of the secret revelation? Yuyuan said, "Ask me and I will answer.
The Master said, "The next day, when Deshan ascends the hall, it will indeed be different from usual.
Before the Dharma Hall, Yantou clapped his hands and said, "I am glad that this old fellow has understood the 'final word. What is the final word?"
Yuzhao said, "You have not asked the right thing, and I cannot answer it. The Master said, "Yantou said, 'Even so, he will only live for three years.
Later, the mountain indeed came to pass according to those words. How do you explain this? Yuzhao said, "It cannot be traced; it cannot be painted.
The Master said, "I do not understand it in that way at all. Yuzhao said, "How then would you act?"

"How is it? The Master replied, "Only by raising children does one come to know the kindness of one's parents. Before he had finished speaking, [Lin Gao] immediately prostrated and said, "I thank the Master for answering my question.
Lin Gao said, "Jian" (Lin Gao Yu was his successor).
Chan Master Jingkou Jia Shan Qu Fu Yi was the son of the Li family from Yizhang. At the age of eighteen, he entered the monastic order under Wansong.
Initially, he studied with Hanshan Deqing at Caoxi, where he investigated the koan "The myriad dharmas return to One," but for three years he could not penetrate it.
He subsequently visited Tiantong Juexin, under whose staff he attained awakening. Later, when he arrived at Jia Shan, [the Master] asked him in advance, "From where have you come?"
The Master said, "In Zhejiang. Yuzhu held up his whisk and asked, "Have you recovered this? The Master said, "It fills the void; who does not possess it?
Yuzhu said, "Show it to me, old monk. The Master shook his sleeves and departed. One day, the Master...
While [Zhaozhou] was transcribing documents in the record office, Zhao Yü called out to him, saying, "You spend all day recording; tell me, what exactly are you recording?
The Master replied, "Today I have a cold and a headache. Zhao Yü said, "Set aside the headache for a moment;
after all, from where do you derive this record? The Master let out a loud shout. Zhao Yü said, "This shout does not function as a single shout. How will you use it?"
"How is it? the Master asked. [Feng] Yu replied, "Transforming through the light of heaven, one becomes a model for ten thousand ages.
He then received the transmission of the Dharma and was appointed to preside over Shiqiao. After three years, he left to reside at Jiufeng in Chu.

Following the passing of Feng Yu, the seat at Jia Shan was vacant; Mochun Monastery nominated the Master to succeed him. In the eighth month of the autumn of the Gengzi year of the Shunzhi era, the Master fell ill.
On the fifth day, he called for his attendant and completely burned his recorded sayings and verses.

His disciples entreated him with great sorrow to allow them to be circulated, but the Master rebuked them, saying, "Even the entire Tripitaka is but old paper; who would look at it? Having said this, he closed his eyes and passed away.
The disciples enshrined the remains and erected a stupa at the right side of Dading Temple in Liyang (Lin Gaoyu was his successor).
Chan Master Wuchen Zeng of Baosheng Temple in Yangzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Pengcheng.

At the age of nineteen, he went to Shantong to complete his training; when the Old Man summoned him to enter the hall for formal study, he made no progress whatsoever. He subsequently studied under Nanjian.

He was instructed to contemplate the "Ten Thousand Dharmas Return to One" koan, but after a long time, he remained unable to realize it. Later, while under the guidance of Yuhui at Jia Shan, he devoted himself to ascetic practices, prostrating to the Buddha day and night in his quest for awakening.
Suddenly, he attained a profound realization. One day, as they were passing through the hall for the meal, Yuhui asked him:
"What is the matter of daily life? The Master said, "I have just eaten porridge this morning;
now I feel hungry again. Yuyi said, "What a fine elder of Hunan you are! The Master said, "You must not defame me.
On another day, as the Master was walking ahead carrying a load, Yuyi grabbed hold of him and asked, "How heavy is this load? The Master said, "Neither much nor heavy. Yuyi—
With a single shout, the Master set down his pack and stood with his hands folded. Yuan said, "Even for one of such coarse conduct, there is this one stroke.
At these words, the Master attained sudden and great enlightenment. Yuan appointed him as the head of the assembly (canchou), and he served in this capacity for ten years.
One day, he took his leave and descended the mountain. Baizhang asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "I am going to live on a mountain.
Baizhang said, "You must not forget what came before or lose sight of what follows. The Master bowed. Baizhang wrote a verse to entrust him with it.

As he was departing, he again held up his straw hat and gave it to the Master, saying, "This is something I have used for twenty years without exhausting its utility; today I give it to you to cover your head."
[The Master] departs. The Master says, "Not only you, but all people under heaven are also within this. Yu says, "Setting aside all people under heaven for a moment, what exactly do you do?
The Master puts on his bamboo hat and walks away. When the Master first built a thatched hut at Zhaoyang, disciples gathered there daily.
The monastics and laypeople of Weiyang invited him to preside over Baosheng Temple. He ascended the hall and said: "In the human realm and the heavens above, there is no Maitreya."
It cannot be hidden away within Baosheng Temple; it is right here in the bustling marketplace of Huacheng City.
When meeting people, one laughs "he-he"—hard to understand! What seems difficult is actually easy. Even so, let me ask you all: tell me, where is Maitreya right now?
[He] strikes his staff and descends from the seat. The eighteenth day of the fourth month, the Wuma year of the Kangxi era.

Suddenly, he manifested illness. He summoned his disciples and took leave of them, saying, "Within seven days, this old monk shall depart. You who practice the Way, each of you must strive with diligence.
On the twenty-fifth day, he took up his pen and wrote a verse: "Reaching seventy years of age is not being old; The conditions for guiding humans and devas are now complete.
Casting off my hands, I return to the West alone; A single bright moon shines with radiant clarity."
He cast aside his writing brush and passed away. His stupa was enshrined at Jia Shan (where Lin Gao Yu succeeded him).
On the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Liaoran Xiaohan Yushang delivered this discourse: "One, two, three, four, five; five, four, three, two, one.
Turned over and then flipped back; sucking the broth from within a sesame cake. On the left, he writes Yu Lei; on the right, he writes Shentu. Once—

There are no such demons; what need is there for the White Deer (Baize) map? A bowl of chrysanthemum tea, three chestnut-yellow *zong* dumplings—half a phrase contains it all, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Day after day drifting, night after night drifting: beneath the Hall of the Bright Moon, the nine summer months pass moment by moment;
under the Gate of the Great Sun, the three autumn seasons go day by day. Until the cultivation of the mind reaches the groundless state, ten thousand kinds...
A thousand ways of chasing after the flow of water—ascending the hall. The entire earth is oneself; sitting until millions upon millions are killed.
The entire earth is not oneself; running until millions upon millions are killed. You monks of the patched robe must overturn the old molds.
Establishing a separate life-path: meeting a Buddha, kill the Buddha; meeting a Patriarch, kill the Patriarch. What need is there to speak of "South of Xiang" or "North of Tan"?

It is the business of donkeys and the business of horses. Walk when it is time to walk; sit when it is time to sit. Cultivation and realization are not non-existent, but simply do not let them defile you. [He] suddenly gave a shout and said:
Vaguely like a melody just barely fit to hear, it is again blown by the wind into another tune.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "There is a ten-foot sail that can harness an eight-foot wind; without a three-foot whip, it is difficult to control a thousand-li horse.
He gave a shout and said, "What words are these? He then cast down the staff. Ascending the hall, [he said], "This very mind is..."
The Buddha recognized a slave as his lord. It is neither mind nor Buddha; it is a madman running outside. It is not the mind, not the Buddha, and not a thing.
What is it? It is a dried-up dung-club. A great man has a backbone as hard as iron; it cannot be bent or broken.
Moving freely in seven directions and traversing in eight ways—what path is there? [The Master] draws a line with his staff and says: "Coral branches support the moon branch by branch.
On his birthday, he ascends the hall: "The Yellow-Faced Old Man was born today; empty space and the great earth were born simultaneously. What has been accomplished in seventy-four years?
Proving a tortoise to be a soft-shelled turtle, he incurs the world's resentment. Before parents were born..."
[The Master] said, "Previously, your nostrils reached the heavens! Alas, having no way to evade, you have once again suffered defeat. You old man, you do not know when to stop;
it is much like the hunchbacked woman (Mokumō) staring into a mirror—what conversation can there be? A monk asked, "All phenomena return to the One. Where does the One return?
The Master said, "When the weather is clear, it is good for drying rice. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master [said],...
[The monk] asked, "The mountain is high and the cold is heavy. The Master said, "What is your meaning? [The monk] said, "It would freeze the Stonehead Hermit to death.

A monk asked, "When the bright moon hangs in the sky, there is nowhere it does not illuminate. Why does it not shine beneath the overturned basin? The Master struck him across the back and said, "You lacquer bucket!
A monk asked, "When many hands sift through gold, who is the one that obtains it? The Master said, "Do not engage in false imaginings."
The monk Fa-k’ung prostrated and said, “The entire earth is this very *huatou*. Having reached this point, there is no way out.
The Master asked, “What do you call the *huatou*? The monk paused in thought. The Master struck him and said, “Give me back my Fa-k’ung!
(Ruo-an asked about the succession.)
Chan Master Qianren Gang of Huangmei Wuzu was a native of Ningbo. His secular surname was Wang. At the age of twenty, he joined the assembly of Yufeng Xinxin and left home at Shuangjing.
He subsequently received full ordination at Tiantong and, having attained awakening through this, was instructed to investigate the "Mu" (No) koan.

Suddenly experiencing a profound realization, he presented a verse, saying: "The dog has no Buddha-nature— Do not say that what you have said is good. A young girl learning how to act as a matchmaker."
His own life was also difficult to preserve. Later, he went to Jia Shan to visit Zhuan’an Weng.

Upon hearing the account of High Peak’s kōan regarding the pillow falling to the ground, he attained great enlightenment at that very moment. He then presented this verse: "I have long remembered Pingzhou as my native land."
Now that his body has already reached Xianyang, had he been taught to forget the path by which he came, even one who is not naturally sorrowful would break his heart with grief.
[The Emperor] asked about him with rhythmic clapping in praise and commanded him to lead the assembly. He subsequently appeared in the world at Jinsen in Runzhou and Huanglong in Ezhou.
Shu zhi fudu (The Floating Crossing) Ascending the seat: "Ordinary people do not see the Buddha; how can they understand the sculpted Buddha?
How can they know this is the Buddha? How can they know this is not the Buddha? I ask you: what Buddha is this? Shakyamuni Buddha Ascending the Seat.
The crow cries "ya ya"; the magpie cries "que que"; the *pobing* bird cries "pobing"; the *guye* bird cries "guye.
Remember each and every bird upon the branches: what sound is not your own voice? A monk asked: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth..."
"The seal of the one dharma. "What is this seal? The Master said, "It cannot be traced or depicted. [The monk] asked, "How is it when it is put into use? The Master said, "Shatter empty space!
[The monk] asked, "When the five tigers pounce upon a sheep, what then? The Master said, "If you move, you will meet their mouths.
[The monk] asked, "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas; why was he unable to emerge from the woman's samādhi? The Master said—
The Master said, "Not only could Mañjuśrī not come out; neither could this mountain monk. The monk asked, "Wangming is a Bodhisattva from the lower regions;
why was he able to come out? The Master replied, "Not only could Wangming come out; you, Venerable One, could also have come out.
The monk bowed, and the Master said, "Tell me, where are Mañjuśrī and Wangming right now? The monk was at a loss. The Master—
He struck the staff and shouted, "The Master has hit it. He had twelve volumes of the *Chunhua ji* (Spring Flowers Collection) and two volumes of recorded sayings (*yulu*) circulating in the world.
(Ruo’an asked about his succession.)
Chan Master Meiweng Gaofu of Nanjian in Wulin was the son of the Zhang family of Changzhou. He could read ten lines at a single glance.
While casually perusing the *Recorded Sayings of Miaoxi*, his resolve to leave the household life was awakened. He first visited Tiantong Wu;

encountering Wu ascending the seat, the assembly looked around expectantly, but Wu spat once and descended from the seat. The Master attained sudden enlightenment and immediately presented a verse, which began: "At that time..."
The phrase "seeking to find, one finds nothing; now wishing to avoid, one cannot avoid" was further investigated by Zhuo’an with Jia Shan. At that time, Jia Shan was observing the precept of silence.
Upon hearing that the Master had arrived, he immediately summoned him inside. He raised his whisk and brushed it to the left, then questioned him.
The Master said, "Every dot remains outside the willow. He then raised his whisk and swept it to the right, saying, "Every sound resides within the banana leaf.
He asked with a change of expression and a shout of "Tut!": "Even so, how could you have attained it? The Master replied, "I certainly do not deceive myself.
The questioner asked, "What is the principle of your not deceiving yourself? The Master let out a shout and then departed. The questioner asked again.
He immediately commanded [the assembly] to take their seats in the West Hall. As he ascended the hall, the great sun flooded his eyes;
ten thousand *li* were clear, without a single speck of cloud. Even the blue sky must receive a blow of the staff. But tell me, what fault does the blue sky have? He gave a shout and said:
"Even if empty space were to crash to the ground—do any of you here have a hand that can reach out? If there is none, this mountain monk shall display his own spiritual powers himself.
He departs. Behold this seven-foot mountain-shaped staff; it props up half the heavens of the southeast. Evening Session:
The vast net is spread out in all eight directions; where can one find a path to escape? A trap for tigers lies in ambush on level ground;
do not discuss the merit of surpassing the age. It comes straight down. Riding the bandit’s horse to pursue the bandit, seizing the bandit’s spear to slay the bandit—return!
How could one possibly attain it? Where there is no Buddha, pass by swiftly; where there is a Buddha, do not dwell. Born of the same lineage, yet dying of different lineages.
Startling up the Iron Ox of Shanzhou: when Lord Zhang drinks wine, Lord Li gets drunk. This makes the Land Steward of Yunju fall over laughing.
Even if mountains are mountains and waters are waters, and everything is clear at every touch—what can be done about the seven stars of the Southern Dipper and the Northern Dipper?
8. Following My Perversion. Entering the Hall: An octagonal millstone rolls through the void; a golden-maned lion transforms into a dog.
If you wish to hide your body within the Northern Dipper, you must join your palms behind the Southern Dipper. Look at this one true mantra:
it causes the heavens to rotate leftward and the earth to rotate rightward. Nevertheless, wherever there is a pond, there is a moon. Who—
There is no smoke from the household hearth. Let Yang Dainian say what he will;
though he may speak and realize the "zhi-hu-ye-zhe" within the great void, how can this compare to you all recognizing the original source of a single phrase? Tell me, which is that one phrase?
[He] gave a shout and ascended the hall. "The entire earth is the question. How can you raise it?
That which cannot be understood—fear only that it is not jade; if it is jade, how truly marvelous! Furthermore, suppose a person comes from Mount Tiantai and goes to Mount Nanyue:
what principle is this? After a long silence, he said: "In the Lion Grove of Xihe, there are five hundred [monks]."
The Venerable One went to the meal. Among those present was one who took his heart, liver, and five viscera and offered them before the assembly.
You must know this! Ascending the hall, he held up his whisk and said, "A variegated phoenix dances in the crimson heavens.

He lowered the whisk and said, "An iron snake lies across the ancient road. Again he took up the whisk and swept it to the left and right, saying, "He turns the pivot of heaven and revolves the axis of earth."
The Axis. Holding it up beyond the ordinary, it encompasses all before one’s eyes; it stands out prominently, yet has no handle to grasp.
"Neither can, nor cannot"—thus he instructs the assembly: "The autumn wind is cool, the autumn night is long; the traveler on a distant journey yearns for his native land.
What is this native land? Try saying something! The Master remained silent for a long while. When the assembly had no reply, he struck the meditation seat with his whisk and said: "Study! (Kangxi)

On the third day of the first month in the year Wumu, the Master went to the residence of Zhizhu at Helin and took his leave, saying, "This frail body will not last long; I shall depart from this world before long.
When that time comes, I ask you to show me great favor by drawing a perfect circle for me. Zhizhu said, "It is the beginning of the New Year; how can you speak of such final words?
The Master replied, "Truly, these are no idle words. After my bones have been cremated, I beg you to cast them into the Great River. Do not go against my wish."
Thereupon, they parted with mutual laughter. On the twenty-fourth day, at the hour of the Snake (10–12 AM), a fire broke out in the neighboring hut.
The Master adjusted his robes and sat in full lotus posture, remaining composed. An attendant monk said, "The flames are already closing in. The Master replied, "My time has come.
The attendant monk said, "If the Master acts thus, how could I dare to leave your side? Thereupon, they together realized the Samādhi of the Radiance of Fire. [End of Chapter] on the Gate.
The Master followed his final instructions and had his bones interred at Longmen on the Great River, at Jinshan Island in the sea.
His disciples established a biography for him and compiled his recorded sayings in ten volumes, which have been circulated in the world (as requested by Ruan’an).
Chan Master Yue of Meigu at Jinling Temple in Jiangning ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Before you had left the chamber at Donggao, you were already seated in the Dharma-hall at Jinling.
Setting aside for a moment the fact that the fourfold assembly has gathered like clouds, what is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said, "The bright sun has already appeared, shining upon the door; it still instructs the bells and drums to announce the new clearing of the sky. The monk said, "The myriad phenomena manifest their reflections."

[The questioner] said, "Without any mutual exclusion, what is the realm of Jinling? The Master said, "The courtyard contains two ancient *śāla* trees; the gate breathes forth a peak ten thousand fathoms high.

[The questioner] said, "In the Hall of Dharma-preaching, there are a million fingers pointing; which one is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Its atmosphere first arrived surpassing Bodhidharma;
its style and regulations have recently settled, excelling Yangqi. [The questioner] said, "I have already received instruction on the person and the realm..."
The Master pointed and instructed: "How is it that the Great Wheel of Dharma turns? The Master said: "In a wondrous dance, there is no need to boast of every clap;
the three stages rely on the weight of everyone’s urging. [The student] said: "If that is so, then all beings among devas and humans alike receive the power of the Master.
The Master said: "Truly, when a dragon gives birth to a golden phoenix, it is indeed as one would expect; joy under such a name is never in vain. Then he said:

Let this dialogue cease for a moment, O Great Assembly. The direct intent secretly transmitted at Shao-shi and the authentic sound of the single-lineage transmission at Vulture Peak are as bright as the blazing sun and as vast as the great void.

Yet, because the tendency toward acceptance and rejection has not been forgotten and the emotions of gain and loss continue to obscure the mind, many remain stuck in words and phrases, while the majority rely on side doors and lean upon gateways.
If you can transcend all upward striving and cut off all downward self-attachment, [only then will you realize it].

Acceptance and rejection are suddenly forgotten; gain and loss are completely purified. I venture to guarantee that one has thus reached the Imperial Capital and ascended directly to the Precious Abode, where all experience and enjoyment are shared simultaneously, like the synchronicity of the chick pecking and the hen tapping.
Nevertheless, this must involve weighing the faculties of others with precise discernment, such that by raising one, the three are illuminated.
Only then can one truly uphold the treatises. Why? Because they have not seen the Way; those who are true masters do not wait for the "pecking" before the "cracking.

Do you all understand this thoroughly? After a long silence, he said: "The single breath remains silent, yet it contains all forms; where could the myriad spirits go to express their gratitude for its impartiality?

On the occasion of inviting the two orders of the monastic community to ascend the hall while remaining in the snow, [he said]: "If I press my finger, the Sea-Seal emits light; the water dripping from the eaves is vividly clear."
It is all clearly manifest. As soon as you raise your mind for a moment, the dust of worldly toil arises first. "Fine snow falls flake by flake; it does not land elsewhere.

A single phrase encompasses the three gates of liberation. Within each gate there are three essentials; if even a hair’s breadth remains unexhausted, one is as if separated by the Iron Ring Mountains.
People should seek the old; things should seek the new. If a single thought of emotion arises, one is bound in shackles for ten thousand kalpas. There is the provisional, and there is also...
It is real. There is illumination; there is function. Opening the mouth is not a matter of the tongue. For those with clear eyes, there are no fixed patterns.
In the fundamental matter, there is no entanglement. A leaking oil lamp reflects the earth and shines through heaven; the wild duck emits sounds like golden bells and jade chimes.
When a guest arrives, there is no tea; instead, mugwort broth is served as the ritual offering. One pulls open the locks of the golden hall and strikes the bells of the jade tower.
Setting aside for a moment the fact that one eats without chewing a single grain of rice, why did Master Fu say:
"All day long picking incense and choosing fire, yet not knowing that the body itself is the site of enlightenment"? Do you understand? Words spoken with a shared heart—how fragrant they are!

Lan. Having stood for a long time, take care of yourselves. On the Mid-Autumn Festival, ascending the hall: the teachings of the Three Vehicles and Twelve Divisions were like the Buddha on Vulture Peak still speaking of the moon;
"It is not the wind or the banner that moves—it is the mind of the wise man that moves. Caoxi was like pointing at the moon; amidst a thousand crags and ten thousand gullies.
How many times have they left their traces by the forests and beside the waters, chanting and intoning aloud? Hanshan was merely good at imitating the moon;
as for the rest—Yunmen, Zhaozhou, Deshan, and Linji—they exhausted all their lifelong skills, yet it was all merely copying and following patterns here.
As for their ultimate way of benefiting others, when has it ever been decisively thorough? Do you all wish to see the true moon? It is at Nanping.
Before the mountains, ten li away, the lake’s radiance is like daylight; how joyful are the singing towers and pleasure boats! Inside Lian’an Temple, they beat the drum for a communal tea service.
[The Master] enters the hall and addresses the Abbot and Attendant: "That which comes and goes with you is the Treasury."
"That which does not come and go with you is also the treasury; it has been placed upon the tray and presented. Do you see the ancients?

He suddenly took up his staff and said, "Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations; do not compete for superiority, but rather avoid competing for victory. Do not confuse the needle and the awl! Then he struck once.
On the occasion of heavy rain on the eighth day of the twelfth month, he ascended the hall and said: "The snow-capped peaks two thousand years ago and the bright star..."
At the time of his radiant splendor, the Yellow-Faced Old Man attained perfect enlightenment.
Now, two thousand years later, amidst the torrential downpours of the Nine Creeks, do you all also possess the attainment of perfect enlightenment? [The Master] raised his staff and said:
Not a single drop falls elsewhere; every drop reaches your own eyes. He strikes once and says:
"Of one and the same sound, there are infinite meanings—some are worthy of hearing, some are not. He strikes again and says: "Do not walk where the Tathāgata has walked.
Ascending the hall, he said: "There is a person who deeply understands the path of the ancient Buddhas, yet does not know their own path."
"Where is the head? There was one person who deeply understood the path of his own self, yet he did not know where the path of the ancient Buddhas lay.
"O Assembly, do you recognize the ailments of these two people? If you can discern them, I shall give you a piece of gold.
On the occasion of opening the furnace, the Master ascended the hall and said: "O Assembly, as for the fire-furnaces of all quarters, there are some..."
Cast from iron, yet composed of clay; for ages, the Southern Stream has been carried about by those who fail to grasp its true intent.
Suddenly, he brandishes his staff and says: "Take this black-lacquered staff and turn it into a blazing furnace.
If you turn your back on it, it will burn you to death; if you face toward it, it will freeze you to death. If you do not believe me," he then plants the staff firmly in the ground.
Zhuo said, "The fire has broken out! Look, look! A monk asked, "What is the student’s original face?
The Master said, "It is not difficult for me to tell you. The monk said, "Why do you not tell it to me? The Master said, "Because you do not recognize it.
A layman asked, "Among the seventeen hundred public cases (gong'an), which one contains the most ambiguity? The Master said, "This very mind."

[The Master] said, "It is the Buddha. The layman said, "This is extremely easy to understand. The Master asked, "How do you understand it? As the layman was about to respond, the Master said, "Is this not confusing? A monk asked, "Why did Zhaozhou say 'no'? The Master said in a stern voice, "You do not even recognize good from bad; you ask in such disorder. The monk was at a loss. The Master said, "As expected. A monk asked, "Why is Mañjuśrī called one of the seven Buddhas? The Master said, "Because he is the first to have attained realization. The monk asked, "What about Śākyamuni? The Master said, "He is the last to have attained realization. The monk asked, "What about Maitreya? The Master said, "He has not yet attained realization. The monk asked, "What about you, Master? The Master said, "I am neither the first nor the last. The monk asked, "Who is it then? The Master said, "If you can find him, I will tell you. The monk said, "I cannot find him. Yuanzhou Yangshan Xuegu Gushih Xingzang Chanshi was a native of Jiangxi. He entered the monastic order under Wen of Li'an. One day, he requested instruction.
Wen said, "In practicing Chan, you must investigate the 'live word'; do not investigate the 'dead word. The Master stepped forward.

He also said, "To say 'I have attained the Way' is a dead word; to say 'I have not attained the Way' is also a dead word. With these words, he took up his staff and left the hall.

From that point on, the Master applied himself even more diligently to inquiry and practice. One day, because the assembly had composed verses on the snow lion in the courtyard, the Master produced this verse:
"Lofty and solitary, it sits well before the courtyard; Without relying on skin or fur, its will is naturally high. I only fear that here, it might leave a trace."

It does not abide; in the end, it returns to the great ocean to form waves and surges. The next day, when asked about the matter of his transfer of office, [the official] did not comply, showing a slight disregard for the Master’s intent.
The Master immediately snapped his staff in two, threw it down, and said, "I will not strike this dead man! At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
He resided at Miaozhan in Pingxiang and addressed the assembly: "Just as my own body is empty, so all dharmas are empty—of the thousand grades and ten thousand species."
All are exactly the same. [The Master] suddenly held up his staff and said, "Tell me, is it empty or not? Those who revile others are stinking excrement slaves. Tell me, are they the same or not?
If there is anyone who can discern this, I will give them a bolt of cloth. Addressing the assembly, he said: "A single phrase from Xuegu is handed over face-to-face.
Wash yourself in the bathhouse; take off your trousers in the hall. A monk asked: "Before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch..."
"Why do a hundred birds carry flowers for you? The Master said, "There is a treasure at my waist. [The monk] asked, "After seeing it, why do they not carry flowers for you?
The Master said, "There are no shoes on my feet. In the Wuma year of the Kangxi era, as the Master was about to pass away, he requested a brush and wrote this verse:
Seven-sevens and eight-eights; high and low, lofty and vast. Following where I go—ha ha! A great laugh.
He cast aside his brush and passed away (Zhao Ruo’an asked about succession).
When Chan Master Xiuxi Liujian of West Creek in Hangzhou was first presiding over the ordination platform at Shengfa Temple in Qinchuan, Suzhou, he once went with Xiaohan Yu to Ba’en Temple.
Seeing fish leaping in the pond, the Master asked, "This sentient being has neither hands nor feet;

[The Master] went out. Dayu said, "How can one blame others? The Master said, "You are old and decrepit, yet you do not even recognize the head of the matter.

Dayu said, "To catch the whale and the leviathan, one must sink into the vast depths; yet I pity those who display their efforts only within a few steps of mud and sand. The Master let out a thunderous shout.
A monk asked, "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas; why did the Buddha-dharma not manifest before him?"
The Master said, "One must not speak of dreams before a fool. [The monk] asked, "Why then does it manifest before one's eyes after ten kalpas?

The Master said, "Today I rely on you to raise this again. When the Master first resided at Shengfa in Qinchuan, he had a record of his sayings (*yulu*) that circulated in the world (as recorded in the *Wen Si* section of the *Ruo'an*).

"Plowing the bright moon to plant plum blossoms"—when the ancients spoke thus, was it to conform to worldly truth (*saṃvṛti-satya*), or was it to exalt the Buddha-dharma?
At this time, when the green and yellow [crops] have not yet been harvested, how shall those of high caliber who cultivate the Way understand this?
After a long silence, he said: "To gird my waist, I am too lazy to use the triple bamboo strip; From my pores, the seven-day incense wafts forth. [End of text]

The Hall. A thousand mountains shrouded in deep green; ten thousand trees with sparse red blossoms. Azure birds burst through the mist of the azure void; yellow monkeys cease their cries as the rain falls upon the green woods.

The Plum Blossom Exudes Fragrance: A Small Lecture (Xiaocan) The spring light is bright and clear; ten thousand plants vie for their splendor. The peach blossoms open eyes of laughter; the willows unfurl brows of joy.
Even more, the passionate cuckoo cries out, calling you, the traveler, to return home.

The Small Lecture says: Light warmth and light cold—the spring has already departed; sudden sun and sudden rain—summer is about to arrive. The head is lost, like the one who searched for his own reflection in the water.
Running about in madness. On what day will the flower of the mind suddenly bloom? [This is] the late assembly. There is no one who does not eat and drink;
why is it that out of ten people, five pairs do not know that rice is made from grain?
You, the great assembly—reaching this point, you cannot help but doubt. Question: "When a person who has died the Great Death returns to life, what is it like? The Master said: "Just..."
He attained "one peg" [of realization]. [The Master] said: "I do not permit traveling at night. When you must arrive by dawn, what then? The Master said: "This night, the single orb is full;

Chan Master Haihong Jiyan of Fushui Rock on Yushan in Changshu was a native of the Zhang family of Wenxi in Shanxi.

Even so, do you see where the former Master has landed? You, the assembly here before me, must take care not to have your eyes changed by the morning star.

Chan Master Daixiong Laiyunyan of Hangzhou was the son of the Pan family of Huizhou. He ascended the hall and said:

Now tell me: how is the wish-fulfilling jewel realized? If you can speak of it here with suchness and clarity, you will not have lived in vain with us.

He could only express half of it. The Master entered nirvana at Hanyin-an in Bagongdong, Runzhou.

They engaged in a back-and-forth debate with extremely sharp spiritual flashes (*jīfēng*). When Yisheng asked [a question] and remained silent, he granted his approval.

He assembled the community to bestow the robe and whisk upon the Master, but the Master firmly declined and retired to Dongyin. Yisheng summoned the Master once more, who then stayed in the abbot’s quarters. When Yisheng entered *mahāparinirvāṇa*, the Master remained there.
