Yan asked, "Master, [you] have pierced the face of the Elder. Shuang said, "I say that throughout the entire world, it has never been hidden.
The Master said, "You may be said to have spoken half of it. Later, a monk asked Xuefeng, "What is the meaning of 'throughout the entire world, it has never been hidden'?
The Master said, "An arrow shot behind the head. Xuefeng said, "Where is it not Shishuang? The Master said, "What about you, Preceptor? The monk [remained silent].
[The Master] recounted this to Shishuang. Shishuang said, "What is this old fellow in such a rush to die? The Master said, "Why did you not say so sooner?
Xuansha said, "He has already missed it. The Master said, "Missed! Missed! The Master further remarked, "This monk merely transmits words and delivers messages;
when will there ever be an end to it? Shishuang’s response to the question was quite a mess. Furthermore, he encountered Xuefeng, who chased him away."
Shi said, "Where is it that Shishuang is not [at fault]? Shishuang then covered it over, saying, "You old fellow, why such a frantic rush?
You do not realize that you are only making yourself more unbearable. Xuefeng’s speaking in this way also only saves half of it.
Why is this? Family scandals should not be broadcast abroad. Addressing the assembly: When the World-Honored One was at the assembly on Vulture Peak, he held up a single flower.
Among the hundreds of thousands of devas and humans, none could fathom it; only the Venerable Kāśyapa broke into a smile.
The World-Honored One said, "I have the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa; I entrust it to Mahākāśyapa."
[The Master] said, "Throughout his life he was all 'alu-’lu' (ineffectual/confused), yet at the end he still managed a bit.

Had I seen him then, as soon as he reached out his hand, I would have said, 'No need to bring it forth. Not only would I have cut him off then and there, but I would also have spared him from bringing trouble upon his descendants.
Addressing the assembly, he cited a case: A monk asked Linji, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Linji then gave a shout.
The monk prostrated. Linji said, "This monk is indeed fit for debate. The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "This monk initially wished to see the moon, but as soon as he saw the pointing finger, he stopped.
Although Linji was skilled at deploying troops and engaging in combat, employing divine stratagems, he was nonetheless buried by Zhaozhou’s subtle maneuvering.
Examining this from the perspective of the future, it is merely the shaking of the "poisonous drum" (chutu-du) without the "resuscitating incense. Master Zhoushang was not like this:

when a monk saw him and was about to open his mouth, he would immediately let out a single, awe-inspiring shout (*he*). Would this not cause that person to see the sun breaking through the clouds at that very moment?
(Yulin Xu was his successor.)
Master Yuanzhao Ciweng [Er]xi Sen was a native of Boluo, Huizhou. He was the son of Li Shaojue, a Vice Minister of the Ministry of Punishment during the Ming dynasty, and his mother was Lady Li.
His birth was preceded by a vision of white light entering her womb. As he grew up, he excelled in the study of various texts and could read several lines at once.

By virtue of his father’s official rank, he entered the National Academy. At the age of twenty-seven, he fell gravely ill; this experience, triggered by a harrowing dream, led him to take refuge in the Dharma.
It was said that he went to the capital for the autumn examination. Along the way, he stopped at Guizong and sought out Master Bao to receive the tonsure.

He first visited Boshan, but there was no accord; he then traveled again to Yunmen to see Xueqiao Xin. One day, while in the hall, the Master asked, "What is the phrase for not having left the abbot’s quarters?
Xin tilted his ear toward him. The Master said, "Thank you for your answer," and subsequently permitted him to enter the room, calling him the "Elder Son of Lingnan."
Later, he went to attend Daxiong Xiu. Upon seeing him for the first time, Xiu immediately commanded him to compose a verse on his "original face.
The Master then recited spontaneously: "The Teao Creek winds its way with murmuring waters; ten thousand layers of passes and mountains, a single realm of leisure.

After the clouds disperse following the shifting rain and sun, the wind and moon fill the heavens and reach the human world. Xiu nodded in approval. One day, Xiu looked at the Master and said, "The ancients said..."
"If one awakens, it is not non-existent. Yet, how is it that one falls into the second position? Since one has already awakened, for what reason does one fall into the second?

The Master replied, "Because there is still awakening remaining. Xiu then gave a shout. At this, the Master suddenly penetrated the source of the Dharma; that very day, he was appointed to the position of First Seat.
The Master served as the head of the assembly at Daxiong Ba’en Temple for seventeen summer retreats. His engagement with students was swift and incisive; people called him "The Iron Staff.
With his own hands, he cleared the path at Longxi to establish the Dharma for the community—this is the present-day Chuanzhao Temple, which received imperial edict [for its restoration].
In the summer of the Jihai year of the Shunzhi era, Xiu recommended the Master for this appointment.
Imperial Edict: He entered the capital and had an audience with the Emperor Shizu.
There were many occasions for dialogue and discourse, which are recorded separately in another volume. Small Assembly (Xiao Can): A "Granny" turns over the entire Tripitaka;
she measures intimacy by the pint and the peck. As for the three-part meaning of Nirvana, even Mañjuśrī can do nothing about it. How laughable! Yangshan... [text ends].

The Mountain Old Man dreamed of performing the *Mahā*. "Tsk! the Master said. "Compassionate Elder, Compassionate Elder, what else do you say? Bending his body, the old man replied, "It is not much less either.
Later, the Master traveled to Mount Wutai and stayed overnight at Xiantong Temple.

Before the temple, he saw an old woman with her head wrapped in red cloth, mountain flowers and eagle feathers tucked in her hair, wearing a patchwork robe. On her left foot she wore flower-patterned sandals, and on her right foot yellow shoes.
Her gaze pierced people; she carried a bamboo basket in her hand, which was filled with various items, while she herself ate pebbles from her mouth.
The Master asked, "Old woman, what are you doing here? The old woman replied, "I am begging for a single coin. The Master asked, "How old are you? The old woman replied, "Sixty-six.
The Master asked, "Do you have a master over whom you rule? The old woman replied, "The entire earth is my domain. The Master laughed loudly; the old woman stared at him.
The Master looked at her; she immediately struck him. "Bāhē! she cried. The Master struck her again. Bāhē took up her basket and danced away.
When the Master returned from his tour of the Central Terrace, the woman was still there on the road eating stones. Upon seeing the Master, she laughed and repeatedly called out, "Namo Buddha!
Namo Buddha! The Master asked, "Where is your place of origin, old lady? She replied, "Taiyuan. The Master asked, "When did you arrive here? The woman—
[The Master] said, "Today is the twenty-seventh of the sixth month. The Master said, "I recognize you. The old woman joined her palms and said, "Greatly Enlightened Buddha!
Greatly Enlightened Buddha! She then prostrated herself and departed with her basket. The Master said, "I nearly failed to question her through."

The late Emperor’s final testament summoned the Master. Upon arriving at the Shouwang Hall on Mount Jing, he held up a torch and said, “When Śākyamuni entered nirvana, humans and devas attained awakening together;
now that the former Emperor has been cremated, we have taken another step further. He looked to his left and right and asked, “Does the assembly understand?
Before the Shouwang Hall, along the main road for official horses, he then advanced the torch. In the evening discourse: “The river is calm; autumn stretches ten thousand miles. All is still.”

In the first watch of the night, as if from beyond the cold mist, the sound of wild geese alighting on the Long Island reaches us. The vastness of heaven and earth throughout the ages cannot be fully beheld;
atop the pagoda in Haichang, it all appears clearly and distinctly. Morning Assembly: Days are short and reading is little; nights are long and tossing in bed is much.
Not so, not so! How can this be? How can this be? One knows only one thing, but not others;

one knows only the "fierce tiger," but not the "crossing the river. When a deer reaches three years of age, its antlers fall out. Morning Assembly: A single act of joy is insufficient to constitute goodness;

it is through the accumulation of joy that virtue is formed. A single act of resentment is insufficient to constitute wrongdoing; it is through the accumulation of resentment that hatred is formed. Thousandfold.
Accumulating fame for a lifetime, yet facing a hundred generations of accumulated slander—where can one find Old Śākyamuni?
This morning, the first day of the eighth month: are the eyes not simply lacquer from Jinzhou? Evening Assembly: The carved clouds roll high and the evening breeze is clear;
A lone wild goose from beyond the heavens sends forth its distant cry. It reports that the mountain ridges slant across the path; Do not doubt the twisted shadows of the trees.
Branches stretch across; clearly, clearly, the fledglings divide the waves. Emerging from scorched traces, entering ancient cities. Hehe! I have changed your eyes.
Early morning assembly on the eighth day of the twelfth month: Śākyamuni Buddha. On the worldly path there is no one who understands; in heaven and earth, who loves talent?

The mountain retreat at Mount Heng remains; I am glad you have returned so early. Inside the temple at Yanguan, we burn incense and make offerings. I, an old man, respectfully offer one matter of celebration:
just now the assembly has risen, and the entire household rejoices. This morning’s congee was served with fruit. Evening Sermon on Praying for Rain:
This point, that point—difficult to grasp, difficult to grasp. Down! *Note: The term "下" (xià) at the end is a traditional marker indicating the conclusion of the sermon.*
**Commentary:** Suddenly it is a clear blue sky and bright day; suddenly it is pouring rain.
*Strike once with the whisk.* **Evening Sermon:** When you open your mouth, it becomes redundant speech; when you do not open your mouth, it becomes superfluous speech. Little fellow Sun!
Tonight’s sound at Yan-uan is not the score from those years past. Great Virtues, do not go about in this way; it is truly a pity. *Evening Sermon*
Case: A single moon over Tianxi; ten thousand households with the sound of pounding clothes. To go this way is to meet a nail on dry land;
not to go this way is to have eyes like the blind. Ultimately, what is it? A three-legged donkey prances about on its hooves.
Autumn enters the silver screen, and dreams cannot be formed. Question: An ancient said, "If one can spit out gold, what can be done with it? What was his meaning?
"What is the essential point? The Master said, "Wearing straw sandals in front of the hall. [The monk] said, "If you set it aside, there is nothing that can be done.

When people come, where do you place them? The Master said, "You shall know in a moment. Evening Sermon: "The eight-fold clouds from Tianxi come; it is difficult to recognize the bend of the riverhead.
In the deep leaves of the mulberry and bamboo grove, one simply knocks on the door-panel. How many people arrive here and forget [the way]?"
The former was lost; the latter is complete illumination. Tonight, I shall open a great skillful means. [He] struck the sounding block and said: "Gourd. [The student] asked:
"What is the pure monastery? The Master said: "To the east of the latrine, on the west side of the street. [The student] asked: "Who is the person within the monastery?"
The Master said, "Call out loudly! [The monk] said, "Picking up one and putting down another is not yet being a masterful hand.

"What then is a masterful hand? The Master said, "The Elder Sun. [Another monk] asked, "What is it like when the skull is smashed to pieces? The Master said, "The monks rank according to their years since ordination (śrāmaṇera-śaikṣa)."
[The Master] addressed the assembly of venerable elders and late-coming practitioners: "If one cannot put even a single word into practice, ten thousand scrolls are but empty vanity.
Let me ask those present before my eyes: how does this compare to the beginning of heaven and earth? He extended his hands and said, "What words are these?
On the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month in the Bingchen year of the Kangxi era, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Next year on this same day, you shall be able to see me elsewhere."
"Is it a peak? Otherwise, you shall not see it. The assembly could not fathom this. When the following spring arrived, he returned to Yuanzhao and again addressed the assembly, saying:
"The Elder Master has presided over Daxiong for nearly three years. All you venerable Chan practitioners, today the retreat ends;
you may go back home. *Du!* Heaven opens the path. Year after year, coming and going amidst the mist and rain; gradually the mist thickens, dampening the swallows."

Foggy and misty, the dawn light obscures the birds and trees. "If the assembly goes on like this, goes on like this," said the patriarch Ciming Yuan with a smile, "it is truly interesting, it is truly interesting.
Grabbing his staff, he set off at once and arrived at Huayan Temple on Mount Wu, where he rested at Lingshan Monastery.
On the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, having completed his painting of the Buddha’s Nirvana, he said to his attendant, "Tomorrow I shall depart.

The assembly wept and entreated him to stay, but the Master replied, "In three days the time will come. He bathed, changed his robes, and again conferred tonsure and the transmission of the dharma-garment upon his disciples.
After receiving his final offerings, he took up a brush and wrote a verse, then passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. His stupa was erected at Yuan.
Zhao Siyou (succeeded by Yulin Xu).
Chan Master Meifa Chun of Ba’en Temple in Huzhou was the son of the Xiong family from Jiangle in Min. By nature, he was exceptionally intelligent and quick-witted.
He was of imposing stature and had studied for the civil service examinations in his youth, though he did not find it a source of joy. Due to the suffering of illness, his worldly thoughts dissolved;
he took Shouchang Qi as his teacher and requested instruction to investigate the Way. His master assigned him to contemplate the saying: "The dog has no Buddha-nature."
For five years he did not let his side touch the seat; then he had an awakening. He wrote a verse, saying: "The expanse within my breast is a small void;
I have ascended directly to the First Peak of Huanglong. The Head Seat asked, "What is the First Peak? The Master remained silent for a long while. The Head Seat said, "Ultimately, what is it?
The Master replied, "The second and third peaks are already finished. From this point on, his dynamic function was fully manifested. [Recorded in] *Chushi*.
He traveled to various regions and visited numerous venerable masters, engaging them in repeated exchanges and inquiries to verify his realization; all of them regarded him as a vessel of the Dharma.
Upon visiting Da’jue Xiu, as soon as he entered, Xiu immediately asked, "Before the Buddha appeared in the world, speak a single word.

The Master replied, "The entire platter is set forth before you. Xiu nodded in approval and appointed him to the position of First Seat, bestowing upon him the transmission of the seal of succession. He then departed.
Having resided at Tianyin in Tingzhou, Tianmu in Lin’an, and Shousheng in Jiaxing, he subsequently took up residence at Ba’en. Ascending the hall, he said:
"By the Xiang River and Longyuan, on Mount Fuyi, for twenty years I attended the Master’s countenance amidst snow and ice. Without cause, I was pushed out into a mess;
with shame covering my face, where can I find rest? Although Xingchun has personally relied upon this old man for over twenty years..."
"You have never studied the Chan of this old man, nor have you ever grasped his words. You were merely subjected to this old man’s scolding until it reached your very bones and marrow.
Your body and mind have become calloused, and you spend all your time in a state of drowsiness; you have not yet dreamed of the Buddha-dharma.
You merely remember a few ancient kōans stored away in your belly, having arranged them for many years. Today, at Baohua Wang..."
Seated upon the dais, he was expounding the ancestral legacy of the Buddhas and illuminating the orthodox eye of humans and devas.
Unbeknownst to him, he had arrived at the mouth of a wildcat’s den; with a single sneeze, it all vanished from his mind. He could not recall a single word.

He saw only the steep precipice of the Golden Wheel, the dense array of myriad trees, the green mountains and azure waters, the crows cawing and insects chirping, and the whistling of the autumn wind.
The autumn rains fall in a gentle drizzle. What is black is black; what is white is white. The bell is the sound of the bell; the drum is the resonance of the drum.

Each and every thing is fully realized; each and every thing is luminously wondrous. Each and every thing awakens the upward-moving faculty for all you brothers; each and every thing turns the Great Dharma Wheel for all you brothers.
Each and every thing flows forth from within one's own breast. This is what is meant by: "I am originally without..."
The mind has its desires and longings, yet now this inexhaustible treasure-trove has arrived spontaneously. Great assembly, that which was before is the mountain gate and the Buddha hall;
that behind is the abbot’s quarters; to the left is the refectory; and to the right is the meditation hall. But tell me, where is this inexhaustible treasure-trove?
(He suddenly strikes the ground with his staff and descends from the seat. Evening Sermon. The ninth month, this very day.

Furthermore, thirteen. The courtyard opens with golden chrysanthemums acting as a compass. Though every head and every object is manifest, if you have not yet awakened, you must still strike at yourself and investigate.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Ten thousand layers of mountains hold the jade of Mount Jing; the people of Yihuang sing the melodies of Jinjiang. The ice-river flames burst forth, crimson as the Brahma-heaven;
in the land of Yan, winter gives birth to bamboo from the land of Min. *Tu!* What thing is this? He suddenly struck.
He held up his whisk and called to the assembly, saying, "Great assembly! When the assembly raised their heads, he threw down the whisk and said:

"The falcon has already passed through the Kingdom of Lapis Lazuli. Evening Inspection: Long rains have not ceased; the rivers and streams run deep, the mountains and forests are pitch black, and the mountain brooks are submerged.
Suddenly, the brilliant red sun surges from the sea, and the entire realm of dust and sand becomes pure gold. *Plopp!*—he struck the floor with his staff.
He said: "There is only the monk’s staff; for years it has been neither dark nor bright. It accords with emptiness in its virtue and accords with heaven and earth in its mind.
Evening Assembly: "The nature of wisdom is perfectly luminous, the source of all dharmas.

Cease attempting to fathom the void of the mind through intellectual understanding. Even if the meditation pillow should laugh aloud, it remains as before, shrouded in the midst of a dream. After a long silence.
Looking to his left and right, he said: "The Great Master Gao Feng is beneath the soles of all of you; each of you, lift your heads and look upward. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The true body is majestic and dignified, like a thousand mirrors reflecting one another's light. To cast aside precious jewels and don tattered rags—how utterly shameful!"
His transformation reached even the grasses and trees; his reliance extended to the myriad regions. The mountains are azure and the waters are vast;

as the peony flowers bloom, the entire courtyard is fragrant. A monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said, "The Xiang River water flows swiftly; the Jingu Peak is high.
[The monk] asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'? The Master said, "A few fragments of cold clouds return to the distant cave."
"A single verse of woodcutter’s song emerges from the green mists. [The monk] asked, "What is meant by 'both person and environment are snatched away'?
The Master said, "In this place there are no mountains; before my eyes there is no disciple. [The monk] asked, "What is meant by 'neither person nor environment are snatched away'?
The Master said, "When one person rejoices, ten thousand nations sing in praise. In the ninth month of the Jiwu year of the Kangxi era, the Master manifested a slight illness. He requested a brush.
He wrote a verse and passed away. His secular age was sixty-three, and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇeraka-vaṣa) was forty. He was interred in a stūpa at his native mountain.
Grand Councilor Wang Gongxi composed the inscription for the stūpa (Yulin Xi succeeded him).
Chan Master Qixian Jia of Daxiong Monastery was a native of the Wang family in Guangyi County, Ruzhou.
At the age of seventeen, he donned the black robes and served as an attendant under Baoen Xiu. One day, upon returning from Jiangnan, Xiu said to him, "Damo did not come to the Eastern Land."
"The Second Patriarch did not remain in the Western Heaven. Why do you come from the east and go to the west? The Master said, "I find no footing.
Xiu said, "I grant that you may walk arm-in-arm with Xuansha. The Master’s monastic age was fifteen; he passed away at thirty-two.
He was interred together with Tuan’an in the same stupa (Yulin Xiu was his successor).
Chan Master Xigou Deren visited Baoen Xiu for instruction. Upon contemplating the "dog" koan, he attained realization.
He often had this verse: "The Dharma takes decline as its prosperity; The assembly takes multiplicity as its excellence. When one raises the 'dog' koan, Not one in a thousand responds.
(Yulin Xiu was his successor.)
Master Qingxi Yunjing went to visit Chan Master Bao’en Xiu. Upon entering the inner quarters, he said, "I have a point of realization.
Xiu asked, "Why does the dog have no Buddha-nature? The Master struck Xiu’s ribs with his fist and said, "Up until now you have been stuck at Zhaozhou's level;
today I have uprooted you right here before the Master. Xiu then pushed him out. The next day, the Master entered again.
Xiu said, "When the entire earth bursts into flames, what samādhi must one attain not to be burned? The Master said, "I have come specifically to spend the summer retreat here.
Xiu then gave a shout. The Master presented this verse: "Perfect as the full moon, vast as the great void;
Throughout history it has had no surname, from antiquity it has been beyond all climbing. Sages and commoners emerge from it; the oceans of lands rest within it at ease. From beginning to end..."
[He was] without change. The location of his touch followed conditions (Yulin Xiu succeeded him).
Chan Master Zudi of Fahaishan on Mount Wan’an was the son of the Liu family from Wen’an in Jinnan.

From childhood, he was upright, composed, firm, and tranquil, possessing the aspiration for world-transcendence. He received the tonsure at Qingjing An in Changping and traveled south to seek instruction, first visiting Tian... [text ends].
Tong practiced with diligent hardship, investigating until he forgot both sleep and food. Suddenly, he attained a realization. He then went to visit Dajue Xiu at Ba’en Temple.
Xiu asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master replied, "Face-to-face, I do not deceive you.
Xiu said, "A skilled Chan guest indeed. The Master said, "Do not defile people. Upon entering the room, Xiu brought up the story of the bamboo stick, and the Master immediately—
He made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat. Xiu asked, "What principle have you seen? The Master said, "This old fellow, what failure could he possibly suffer?
Xiu struck him repeatedly with his staff and drove him out. From that moment, the Master's long-standing internal obstruction was suddenly and completely dissolved like melting ice.

Thereafter, their exchanges were free and unrestrained, their sharp intellects meeting like the points of arrows. Xiu then gave his approval, bestowing upon him the robe and whisk. Consequently, the Master traveled north to visit his mother.
He returned and obtained the old site of Hongjiao Temple on the Western Hills, where he cleared away the thatch to establish a dwelling.
Master Xu was summoned by the edict of Emperor Shizu, the Great Emperor Zhang, and the Master attended him in the Wanshan Hall.
The Emperor inquired about the origins and details of his renunciation, as well as various karmic conditions. The Master’s responses were thorough and incisive, greatly pleasing the Emperor.
He commanded that Hongjiao be renamed Fahai Chan Temple, bestowed upon it a stone plaque with its title, and granted him purple robes.

His Majesty traveled by carriage to visit Fahai, regarding the Master as his legitimate son for repaying his debt of gratitude. Devoted solely to the pursuit of truth, the Emperor’s special regard for him was profound.
During a small-scale assembly (*xiaocan*), he remarked: "Throughout this summer, Cuiyan has spoken here and there for the sake of you brothers;
look—does Cuiyan's eyebrow still exist? Fahai, however, is not like this: throughout this winter, he has not given a single word to the assembly.
The Brothers said: “Do you still know the place where the Dharma Ocean acts for people? If you understand this, your nostrils remain as they were;
if you have not yet realized it, you must truly raise your eyebrows and investigate. In the *Small Assembly* (Xiao Can):

There is a thing, vividly clear, vertically exhausting the three periods of time and horizontally spanning the ten directions. When encountering the noble, it is base; when encountering the base, it is noble. You all—what do you say?
“How do you repay the price? After a long silence, he said: “Explaining the boundless meaning of the spring breeze, branch after branch opens its smiling face.
To the assembly: “When this single breath does not return, where will you find a place to rest? Find a place to rest—take heed of it quickly!”

"Offhand, he breaks through the barrier of the six sense-objects. He even makes empty space laugh and strike the ground. Suddenly calling out to the assembly, he asked, "Do you recognize your original face?
The assembly was speechless. The Master shook his majestic presence and let out a shout.

Addressing the assembly, he raised his staff and said, "Without moving your lips or teeth, try to swallow this. Everyone, try to swallow it! The assembly offered various responses, but [the Master] did not accept them.
Qie. The Master threw down his staff and said, "Today I have suffered a loss. He then returned to his quarters. The Master asked a monk, "All phenomena return to the One;
where does the One return? The monk replied, "The pillar. The Master said, "What did the pillar say to you?
The monk replied, "There is nothing to be attained and nothing to be said. The Master said, "I knew well that you were making your living inside a ghost cave. The Master [then departed].

The Master immediately seized him and said, "Is it when you go out the gate? Is it when you enter the gate? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him with his palm.

In the middle of the eleventh month of the Bingwu year of the Kangxi era, the Master manifested slight illness. He addressed his disciples, saying, "The four elements are but a temporary conglomeration; I shall not remain long.
On the fifth day, he expounded the essentials of the Dharma and again, striking his knee, he chanted: "The golden wind..."
Whispering, yellow leaves fluttered down; the bright moon shone roundly across the nine realms.

With direct and total clarity, he encompassed all existence—what need was there to open one's eyes to vain doubt? He passed away while sitting in meditation. His age was fifty-one, and his years as a monk were twenty-one.
On the day of his cremation, countless *śarīra* relics were obtained. Several days later, some were still found among the grasses.
His stupa was erected before the mountain of his home temple (Yulin Xiu succeeded him).
When Chan Master Yunju Zeng of Qingshan first visited Boshan, he immediately attained a realization. Later, he entered the hall of Tiantong and engaged in intensive inquiry through various methods;
yet his awakening remained incomplete. After eight years of diligent cultivation, he went to visit Xiu at Ba’en Temple. Xiu...
A question was asked: "To cite [a precedent] is to act like a wind-crazed fellow entering the hall; it is licking the calf, and it is falling into the tiger's trap. The Master said:
"The prediction at Vulture Peak has not yet reached such a state. Xiu said: "To travel several li and then doubt this matter is 'yellow-waxwood Chan.'"
"There is another point of excellence. The Master said, "If you wish to exhaust the view for a thousand li, climb yet one more story.

Xiu said, "If you try to hold him back, I strike; if you follow after him, I strike. Is there a discrepancy here? Or is there no discrepancy? The Master said, "Gathering it together and letting it go: this is the birthday of Avalokiteśvara.
As the Master was prostrating, Xiu asked, "The Great Being fundamentally has no death; why then is there [a birthday]?"
[The Master] said, "Today’s prostrations are finished. Xiu said, "I, this mountain monk, cast out a Mount Sumeru from within my sleeves.
The Master said, "No one understands filling the ditches and blocking the ravines; every pore of the Master is Avalokiteśvara. Xiu laughed loudly.
He succeeded [the Master] on the seat at Tianmu. Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddha expounds the Dharma with a single voice, yet sentient beings follow it according to their kind."

"Each attains understanding according to their kind. [The Master] tested the assembly by asking, "What is meant by 'each attaining understanding according to their kind'? The entire assembly offered words of response, but none were in accord.
The Master spoke on their behalf: "Ants understand how to scurry toward places of filth; blue flies fly straight toward the side of stench. (Yulín Xiù was his successor.)
Chan Master Da’xiong Huiji Zhou of Hangzhou was a native of Huai’an. His entire family entered the monastic order together. He went to visit Xiu at Ba’en Temple.
One day, while he was sitting in meditation, Xiu asked, “Who is it that sits? The Master gave a shout. Xiu struck him. The Master rose and prostrated.
Xiu said, “The entire great earth is a fiery pit. What samādhi have you attained such that you are not burned up? The Master—
He then went out. Xiu called him back, saying, "What principle have you seen that you shout like this and run away like this?
The Master said, "There is no principle to be spoken of. When the Abbot asks in such a way, I answer in such a way. Xiu nodded in approval.
Later, when Layman Sun Xiaozhe visited Xiu, Xiu beckoned to him three times and then closed the door behind him. The Layman said:
With one foot, he stepped across the bridge halfway up the mountain. The Master said, "Where is the layman's heels?
The layman looked back. The Master said, "Try to say a single phrase. The layman said, "The Head Seat, heaven and earth share the same root with me.
Where is that root? The Master gave him a slap. The layman said, "Head Seat, you have heels. The Master stopped there. (Yulim Xu was his successor.)
Chan Master Xixin Wei of Huzhou was the son of the Yu family from Jintan. At the time of his birth, he was enveloped in double layers of amniotic membranes, and a white light circled his room.
When he grew up, a man of extraordinary character examined him and said, "This child has the *svastika* marked upon his chest;
he is surely one destined for the Dharma seat. Later, due to domestic calamities, he underwent many hardships. One day, he fell into the waters of the Tao River and cried out, "Da..."
The man’s name was Deju. Supported by a large tree against his armpit, he managed to stand up and made a vow to leave the household life.

When he reached the age of seventeen, he crossed a river by means of trade, but his boat overturned again and he nearly died; a monk rescued him. Suddenly remembering his former vow, he shaved his head and went to Huashan to receive full ordination.
There he studied under Miaofeng Hai, whose gate opened the gradual path. Subsequently, he traveled south, visiting Jia Shan and Jing Shan.
He visited nearly all the famous monasteries of the mountains, such as Tiantong. Later, he went to visit Tianmu Xiu. Xiu asked, "Where is the path you have come by?
The Master remained silent and pointed to his heart. Xiu shouted, "What kind of destination is this? How could it accommodate the path you have come by? The Master had a sudden realization;
he rushed forward, embraced the Buddha’s feet, and Xiu shouted again. The Master then departed. One day, Xiu asked him: "You..."
"Being a Zen monk—where is Zen? The Master said, "The Abbot wants people to cast away sweet peaches and instead seek bitter plums.
Xiu pointed to the bamboo screen at the window and asked, "Do you understand? The Master replied, "I have been beaten into a single piece by the Abbot.
Xiu smiled and nodded, then bestowed upon him the *saṃghāṭī* robe. At that time, the layman Huang Yusheng was practicing cultivation.

He established Ciguang Temple on Mount Huang and invited the Master to preside over its affairs. The Master took charge of the construction with great diligence, expanding the scale while strictly adhering to the architectural regulations of the Pumen Monastery.
After seven years of labor, the work was completed; the halls and buildings were magnificent and radiant, and disciples gathered there daily.

One day, while recording what he had seen within the mountains, he invited Xiu to visit the temple. Xiu replied with a verse and commanded him to serve as the "Knocking-on-Ice" monk (*kōbō*). A monk asked: [The rest of the text follows].
"What is the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena? The Master held up his fan and said, "Which is the principle?

Which is the phenomenon? The monk said, "Master, do not play with empty space. The Master said, "Empty space is shattered to pieces. The monk asked, "What is the non-obstruction between phenomena and phenomena?

The Master threw down the fan and said, "That is neither principle nor phenomenon. The monk gave a shout, and the Master struck him. The monk prostrated and requested a verse; the Master [composed it].

It is said for them: The essence of mind is vast and great; principle and phenomena are without obstruction. Looking up at the autumn sky, there is not a trace of attachment. Pick up a single hair, and a thousand differences and myriad wonders appear.
A horse’s bucket and a donkey’s mouth—each is its own good and its own ruin. Like sparks from flint or a flash of lightning, such is the ten directions of the world.
Earth, water, fire, and wind revolve with swift rapidity. Where did they originally come from? When empty space is pulverized, what is the Dharma?
The realms manifest before one. Then Mahesvara asked:
"How is it that 'one is all' and 'all is one'? The Master said: "One is all; all is one. Where is there a 'one'? One is not empty or quiescent;
it neither perishes nor arises; it is without gain and without loss. The Yellow-Faced One has hands that grasp at emptiness; the White-Handed Thief has a mouth hanging on the wall."
As for the human realm, it is like the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month: hands flailing and feet stumbling; by then, regret is too late. I say:
what benefit is there in merely patching things together from left to right at that moment?

How many clever people clasp their palms and rub their fists in anticipation, only to find, in the end, their two eyes blind and utterly bewildered, not knowing where they are. I ask you: feel your own heart—what more is there to deliberate?
[The Master] said: "What can be said? [The student] asked: 'To enter the gate of the Buddha-dharma, must one still observe dignified deportment? The Master said:

'The three thousand points of dignified deportment and the eighty thousand subtle practices are all merely external forms. From where could one attain ultimate realization through them? Impermanence is swift; recognize this early on.
Before the eyes have time to blink and before the ears have time to listen, see through it and let go. Unstained and unblemished.'"
There are stages. I shall provide you with clear evidence so that you may realize it instantly, cut through it like a blade slicing through two pieces of wood.
A practitioner asked: "The Buddha is in the mind; the mind is the Buddha. Is this Chan? The Master said: "Without birth and without intention, how could there be discrimination?
When the preceding thought does not arise and the succeeding thought does not cease, all is one, and one is all. Mind is Buddha, Buddha is mind; in the end, they return to..."
Quiescent extinction. No Buddha is the Buddha; no mind is the mind. With neither Buddha nor mind, all is vast and naturally pure.
In the winter of the Wuma year of the Kangxi era, the Master visited Guangling to bid farewell to old friends. He was afflicted by a slight illness and announced his passing in advance.

On the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month, he requested water for washing and rinsing. As he was about to enter quiescence, the assembly requested that he leave behind a verse. The Master smiled and said:
Zhaozhou’s "Single-Word Chan" was the word "No. He said, "Even today, it is simply this one word 'No.
The assembly pleaded with him, saying, "The Master has come pure and departed pure; why is there not even a single word? The Master replied, "This mountain monk neither comes nor goes;
why then is there still this one word? The assembly remained silent. The Master stroked his own head with his hand and passed away. (From *Kōzen*)

After Bingfa’s successor had escorted the Master’s reliquary shrine (*śarīra-koṣṭha*) to Zhejiang, the monastics and laypeople of Mount Huang all revered the Master and respectfully requested that his reliquary shrine be enshrined in a stupa at Bagong Cave.
Shi Gong Runzhang, the Court Lecturer, composed the inscription for the stupa (Yulín Xi was the successor).
Chan Master Erzhan Dazun of Shishuang in Liuyang was the son of the Tang family of Ning County in Siming. Having recently emerged from infancy, he turned his heart toward the Triple Gem.
As he grew older, he took no pleasure in the affairs of worldly production; he deeply lamented the impermanence of body and life, frequently giving rise to thoughts of renunciation.
His parents did not permit this, and when they sought to arrange a marriage for him, the Master repeatedly and resolutely refused, whereupon they desisted. One morning...

He rose and went out the door. Beside the house, he saw discarded meditation cushions, precept robes, and various ritual implements. The Master observed them closely and said to himself with joy, "Heaven has granted me these.
He took them with him and entered Mount Fiquan, where he paid his respects to Yuanming and requested ordination. When his father and elder brother arrived to search for him, they found him there.
Seeing that his master’s resolve was firm, he sighed deeply with a sorrowful expression and departed. Ming shaved his hair and beard for him and served him diligently for three years.
He first attended upon the Patriarch Wuzu of Tiantong. Wuzu held up the incense offering and asked, "From where did you obtain this?
The Master replied, "How can you deny it right to my face? Wuzu asked, "What do you mean? As the Master was about to offer further words, Wuzu struck him. That winter, he received full ordination.
He received full ordination in the year of the Yihai cycle of the Chongzhen era (1635), at which time he was already twenty-eight years old.

Having studied under [his teacher] for over a year, he further attended upon the eminent masters Jin-su Seungjeon, Beomsan Seolchong, and Namgeum Munjeong. Later, he went to Dongmyeong-sa, where he met Dunsok Jijeung;

his understanding became perfectly clear upon hearing the master’s words, and he thus resolved to remain in close attendance. During one session by the brazier, Jijeung raised the following koan: "A monk asked Jashan..."
"When the dust is swept away and the Buddha is seen, what then? Shanshan said, "You must brandish the sword. If you do not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in the trees.
"How do you understand this? the Master asked. "It is too much effort," he replied. Shanshan said, "Is it Mountshan who exerts effort, or is it this monk?
The Master said, "Feel free to explain as you wish. Shanshan said, "I knew all along that you would not understand these words. "One."

On that day, Ji again asked, "The ancients said: 'When host and guest are harmonious, it is entirely delusion; when ruler and subject are united, it is precisely heterodoxy. How do you understand this?
The Master said, "'Peace itself was brought about by the generals, yet we do not permit the generals to see the peace.
Ji said, "Even if you understand it thus, how can you attain it? The Master said, "What is your own intention? Ji said, "Why do you not say..."
"The mandarin ducks have been embroidered; you may look at them from afar, but I will not pass the golden needle to anyone. Upon hearing this, the Master attained sudden enlightenment;
his long-standing internal obstruction was instantly dissolved like melting ice. After serving for several years, he received the transmission and seal of approval.

He subsequently resided at Luluo and, in the Bingxu year of the Shunzhi era, emerged to take charge of Shishuang. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The path to Shishuang lies amidst white clouds; it is shallow..."
The venomous snake lurking in the grass spreads its flames fiercely; who has been deceived that they have personally touched it? Blood flows directly, splashing up to the Brahma Heaven.
Sweeping the ancestral stupa of Master Ciming, he personally met Fenyang and extinguished Linji. He gave rise to the fatal illness of Huanglong, leaving harm for future generations.
Even with the "upside-down grasp" mechanism of Shending, what reliance can there be? For a thousand ages, few have gathered [the truth].
In the forest, the eyes are empty and free from all reservations; the entire body enters meditative absorption as the grass grows lushly. There is another exquisite sound that moves heaven and earth.
[The Master] then prostrated himself. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Half of this summer has already passed. How shall this matter be judged? That which has passed is already past;
do not calculate what is yet to come. The present fundamentally has no abiding place; throughout the ten directions, it is utterly cut off. Take whatever comes to hand."
It is not dust. It is the majestic, everyday functioning that shifts according to circumstances; there is no need for further hesitation. You must urgently turn your eyes to look.
[He suddenly threw down his staff and said: "What is this? After thirty years, do not let it be a cause for regretting Shishuang.

Evening Sermon: To seek the ox, one must follow its tracks. In studying the Way, the absence of a deliberate mind is prized. When the tracks are found, the ox is also found; when the mind is absent, the Way is easily realized.
[The Master] sought [the meaning]. The ancients’ occasional expedient means did not issue from emptiness; since they were already without mind, how could one seek them? After a long silence, he said:
"When one reaches the deepest part of the deep mountains, who would know there are no means to avoid royal levies? [This was] the evening instruction.
This morning is the twentieth day of the first month; it is a season of warm sun and gentle breezes. Everywhere the Seal of the Ocean radiates its light.

Why then do you cling to the tethering stake? [The Master] addressed the assembly. A monk asked, "When speech and silence involve transcendence and subtlety, how can one pass through them without transgression?
The Master said, "Junsan pierces through the Lake of Dongting. He then said, "Shishuang has no dharma to speak; he merely pulls out nails and extracts wedges."
He lifted his robe and immediately walked away; he had already been late by eight *kē*. Suddenly picking up his staff, he said, "If you have a staff, I give you a staff;
if you have no staff, I take your staff away. He looked left and right for a long while.

[The Master] let out a shout. Throwing down his staff, he ascended the hall and said: "To break up the Great Tang Empire and find a single person who does not understand the Buddha-dharma is difficult to achieve.
Now tell me, what excellence does such a person who does not understand the Buddha-dharma possess?
Last night, they slept with their arms tucked under their heads; they did not fear anyone coming to steal their pillow. [He then] ascended the hall and said: "The sun may grow cold; the moon may..."
"Hot! No demons can destroy the True Teaching. Do you people wish to know the True Teaching? Stop up your ears and listen clearly! [He] ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddhas appearing in the world is like scraping hair from a tortoise's back. The Patriarchs coming from the West is like cutting off the horns of a rabbit.
The entire Tripitaka is but worn-out paper for wiping sores. When a monk with clear eyes arrives here, his mouth is like—"
The Foundation Stone: All you virtuous practitioners of meditation, how would you deal with this? "Though the road to Jiange is perilous, those traveling at night are even more numerous.
[The Master] ascends the hall. A monk steps forward; the Master strikes him immediately, saying, "Speak! Speak! The monk bows; the Master strikes again and says:
"The Way is the eternal Way; the Dharma is the eternal Dharma. One phrase cuts off the current; ten thousand functions are stilled. Yangqi’s one donkey—" only...
"There are three legs. (He lets out a shout. "Evening session. 'At this very moment, if you would just rest, you would rest;
if you wish to seek the time of completion, there is no time of completion. When the ancients spoke thus, they were already like a doctor treating a dead horse.
What more do you all intend to seek? (With his staff, he drives them away. Opening the furnace, he addresses the assembly: "The various quarters gather..."

The multitude all rely on what comes from without; Shishuang’s dwelling in the mountains is entirely managed from within. When that which is managed from within is impenetrable as water-tight, it cuts off the heels of the monks of the world.
What comes from without is like adding flowers upon brocade; it passes horizontally through the nostrils of the Tathāgata of Fragrant Accumulation.
But as for that which does not involve either the internal or the external—a word that is manifest and without partiality—how do you speak of it? Red.
An iron tortoise burst forth from the furnace; the monk took his leave of the Master. The Master asked, "Where are you going?

The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him across the back with his staff, saying, "This is a ghost guarding an ancient tomb. The monk was at a loss as to what this meant, and the Master drove him out. Another monk came to visit; the Master said:
"I would have given you thirty blows before you even reached here. The monk asked, "How did you see that? The Master struck him. A monk came for an audience.
The Master asked, "When meeting a man who has attained the Way on the road, one does not respond with speech or silence.

With what do you respond? The monk said, "At the peak of Bowel Peak, the waves overflow the heavens. The Master raised his staff. As the monk hesitated, the Master drove him out. A monk came for an audience. The Master... [text ends]
Question: "I have not seen you for a long time. Why is one half of your nostrils missing? The monk hesitated, and the Master shouted him out. Question:
"What is it like when the single breath does not return? The Master said: "Today is as cold as yesterday.
The monk requested further instruction. The Master asked: "Who have you ever met? The monk replied: "I met Master Shi Qi. He said that Xuedou has [it]."
"The staff does not strike me," [the monk] said. The Master then struck him and asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not.

The Master struck him again and said, "In the future, you may well fail Snow窦 (Xuědòu), but do not fail this old monk. Shishuang’s dwelling was dilapidated; the groves were cold and the mountain streams solemn.
Confronted by such a desolate environment, the Master remained composed and at ease, yet disciples flocked to him like the wind, until his sandals filled the space outside his door.

He acted with sincere care for later students; truly, he possessed qualities that far surpassed those of ordinary men. He reconstructed the stupa of the patriarch Yuan and requested Hongjue Mian to compose a record for it.
Upon reading the Master’s *Shichuang Lu* (Stone Creek Record), Mian struck his palm in rhythmic approval and sighed in admiration, saying:

"Among the disciples of the Elder Huan of Longchi, this man is the foremost among the first generation. I shall therefore write a preface and circulate his work. At that time, there was an official of the local administration who...
When construction work on the earthen structures was undertaken, the Master feared it would disturb the local residents and strove to dissuade them;

nevertheless, the monks' hall, the abbot’s quarters, and the refectory were successively restored. All of this relied upon the efforts of his close disciples in planning and execution, while occasional external contributions arose spontaneously rather than through forced effort.
In the *guimao* year of the Kangxi era, he constructed a stupa for himself beside the ancestral stupa.

To his right, as the artisan had just finished the work, the Master fell ill. On the day before his passing, he wrote a final testament by hand, urging only that the ancestral temple be diligently protected and the Great Dharma widely propagated;
not a single word concerned anything else. On the first day of the ninth month, he ceased taking food.

At noon, he again composed a letter, dispatching a monk to bid farewell to Xiaohan Yu and entrust him with his final affairs. At the hour of Hai (9–11 p.m.), he passed away while sitting in the lotus position.
Yu hurriedly prepared his travel gear and arrived on horseback; [the Master] had already been in meditative absorption for seven days, and his countenance remained as if alive.

On the day of the cremation, rain and mist obscured the sky, but when the coffin was raised, it suddenly cleared. After three days, once the collection of the remains was completed, it rained heavily once more. All the assembly...

Filled with awe and wonder, he subsequently enshrined the sacred remains in a stupa on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His worldly age was fifty-six, and his years of monastic seniority were thirty-one.
He has a record of his teachings in two volumes, upper and lower, which circulates in the world. (Sanzhi Jisi).
Chan Master Xuanci Daqian of Huangbo Guangshan was the son of the Lin family of Fujian.
He studied under Dun’ou at Dongming, Nanyue, Nanyuan, and other locations, whereupon he received the seal of mind. He established the Dharma at Guangshan. Ascending the hall, the Master said:
"Today at Guangshan, I wish to meet you all. Is there anyone here who does not shrink from danger? A monk stepped forward; the Master struck him with his staff.
He struck him. The monk’s head split open. The monk said, “I have met the Master. The Master struck him again and said, “Accept it directly!
There are eyes at the tip of the staff. Forged from dull steel, cast from raw iron. When there is spirit, add more spirit;
where there is no elegance, there is elegance nonetheless. Ascending the hall, he said: “Guangshan has a Dharma to speak. All you people...”
Do not say this is a tangle. Guishan has no dharma to speak. Everyone, do not say this is merely plain and ordinary.
Do you know where this mountain monk’s intention lies? After a long silence, he said: "If one is not a true知音 (zhīyīn—'one who knows the sound'), it is in vain to discuss the severity of winter.
A monk asked: "What is the realm of Guishan? The Master said: "The bright moon flows gently; the running water murmurs. The monk said: [The Master replied: "..."
"What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "Ash on the head and dust on the face. [The student] asked, "What is your way of acting for the sake of others?
The Master then struck him. (Shan-ci Ji succeeded him.)
Furthermore, when Chan Master Chuanzi was ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Mount Tai?
The Master said, "The Resting Pavilion beyond Zhaozhou’s Barrier. The monk asked, "Who are the people within that realm? The Master said, "Setting aside myself, everyone is capable."
He then said: "As clear as the bright sun, illumination and function act in concert; killing and giving life are deployed with total freedom, brought forth in response to the moment.
He struck his staff and let out a shout, saying: "The tongs do not move, yet sparks fly; to blink one's eyebrows is to be separated by a vast ocean" (Shanziji’s Succession).
Chan Master Milyan Dagang of Baqing was the son of the Xiao family of Chaling. During his childhood, while wandering at a pine altar, he experienced a realization upon hearing the sound of a bell.
He then investigated the koan, "Who is it that recites the Buddha’s name? One day, encountering someone who struck him, he attained further awakening.
He went to study under Xuan Yin of Mount Nanyue, who asked him about the Dongshan dialogue concerning the eyes, ears, nose, and tongue: "Tell me, do they exist or not?"

The Master replied, "A single arrow brings down two vultures. He then ordained him to leave the secular life and instructed him to go see Lùluójì. Lùluójì’s methods of forging and refining were rigorous and dense;
whenever they met, he would not allow [Yìn] to open his mouth. Yìn consequently exerted himself with fervor day and night. Once, while prostrating himself in the cold, he fell ill.
Examining his past, he found that it was entirely useless; thus, he redoubled his diligent efforts. At that time, two monks were discussing the saying, "Where does this one return?
One said, "This very thing is the lamp. Suddenly, he attained a sudden awakening, as if casting off a burden of hundreds of thousands of catties. Daoyi asked him:
"In daily life, there is nothing that is not this very manifestation. Why is it that everyone sees a snake and is afraid? The Master presented a verse containing the line:

"The cold wind blows fiercely, its chilling power pervading the six directions; the sun of wisdom shines brightly, its radiance universally illuminating the great chiliocosm.
The mechanisms of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are all at once released; the adamantine eye of true insight is opened wide in unison. Nature..."

"How do you untangle this stickiness? Is it being 'majestic and dignified' that constitutes clarifying the mind and reaching the source?

"Where will you go from here, Master? To heaven or to hell? The Master spread his two hands to show him. The layman prostrated.
The Master said, "Take care," and passed away. He was cremated, and countless *śarīra* relics were obtained. A stupa was erected at his own temple (Ji'an Jin succeeded him).
Chan Master Jin Minghuiryan Huijing of Jiaxing once composed a verse on the passage: "That which can be returned is naturally not you;
that which cannot be returned—if it is not you, then who is it? He said: "The ethereal lady’s frame was originally elegant and refined;
She grew weary of applying rouge at the Jade Tower. Her cloud-belt and frost-anklets have all fallen away; Now she is left with nowhere to hide her shame. (Ji’gan Jin succeeded him.)
Chan Master Xing of Tianfeng Peak at Sanjiao in Qizhou was a native of the Wang family of Huangmei; he was a descendant of Lord Zhongxuan. From birth, he was simple and unassuming.

In his youth, he studied the "Green Box" (classical Confucian texts), yet he took delight in the study of transcendental learning. Whenever he read the scriptures of the Buddha, he would do so until daybreak without weariness.

When the world fell into turmoil, he wandered freely in all directions until he reached the Xiaoxi River in Zhejiang, where he paid respects to Master Lang of Jinsha and received the tonsure and precepts.

He practiced diligently for several years. One day, reflecting that the matter of birth and death was of great importance, he went to visit Xuedou Yun and was instructed to investigate the koan of the "original face.
He studied this intensely for many days until an awakening occurred. He composed a verse and presented it to Yun, who nodded his head in approval. Later, he visited Jinming Jin;
as soon as he entered the gate, Jin gave a shout, Jin also shouted, and the Master shouted again. Jin then raised his staff, whereupon the Master said, "Old man, now..."
Jiandui said, "The sun has set. As he stepped forward to strike, the Master said, "I see even less worthiness in you. Jiandui withdrew. On the following day, the Master ascended the seat.
Jiandui came forward and asked, "For many years I have sought a true知音 (zhīyīn—'one who knows my sound'), yet such people are few; now that we have met today, what shall be done?
Jiandui said, "I grant you thirty blows. The Master let out a thunderous shout. Jiandui looked at the assembly and said, "Behold this warrior! The Master then shook his whisk.
He returned to the assembly. In the autumn of the *Yiwei* year of the Shunzhi era, he went to reside at Qingliang Hermitage in Songjiang.
In the *Dingyou* year, he moved to Zhongfu Monastery in Xiaozhen. In the *Wuxu* year, he returned to his hometown. At the request of the assembly, he undertook the restoration of Duoyun Mountain.

In the summer of the *Jiyou* year of the Kangxi era, Gu Xie of Sanjiao passed away; the assembly requested him to preside over the seat. In the *Jiyin* year, the gentry of Huangmei requested him to restore Dong Yongfu.
And at places such as Bodhi, wherever a master arrives, it immediately becomes a monastery. Entering the hall: The standard for practitioners originally has no fixed direction;

movement is like the wind passing through, causing the grass to bow, or water reaching its channel until it is complete. Encountering things, one takes them as the fundamental principle; the perfect sound flows with beauty.
A single phrase encompasses all, cutting off a thousand differences at once. You who have come here must know how to turn [the wheel].
[He takes one step. He picks up his staff and strikes it once. [He descends from the seat. (Meigan Jin-si).
Chan Master Haiyue Tianyan Qi of Guangling, a son of the Mao family of Rugao, gave a small discourse:
"Confucius could not read characters; Bodhidharma did not understand Chan. Yet people do not believe this. Birds as large as mountains; fish as large as the sea. Yet people..."

People do not believe that a father is younger than his son or that a younger brother is older than his elder brother; yet people do not believe in the morning star appearing at noon or the red sun shining at night.
When Haiyue speaks thus, people do not believe him; when people speak thus, [others] do not believe them.
Haichue did not believe; the others did not believe; Haichue did not believe. But tell me: are they the same or different?
After a long silence, he looked to his left and right and said, "Investigate! (Jiagan Jin succeeded him).
At Taicang Wenmeihuan, Chan Master Chen addressed the assembly, noting that he was the son of the Li family of Wulin. He ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "What is the realm of embroidered snow? The Master said, "Twisting paths where moss has gathered many times; deep within the Snow Hall, the bamboo wind is clear."
[The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "Holding a staff, he inspects the falling flowers at leisure;
taking a step, he moves to view the clear, blue water. [The monk] asked, "As for the matter beyond this, how is it? The Master then struck him.
[The Master] ascended the hall and said, "I, this mountain monk, have a phrase that I have long wished to speak to all of you. Because worldly affairs were too busy, I never opened my mouth. Today—"
"I have a moment of leisure. Why not speak in detail? Each of you should listen attentively. He then descended from his seat and addressed the assembly:

"The shade is thick by the courtyard; after long rain, all seem as if intoxicated. By the embankment, the willows hold pearls and spit emerald green. In the pond, the frogs' drums resound like thunder;
beneath the trees, the Chan practitioners nod off to sleep. Hehehe! Do you understand? Or do you not? He struck the meditation staff upon the ground and said: "The sun is high."

The shadows of flowers deepen; the breeze is warm and the birds’ calls shatter the silence. In the spring of the Gui-mao year of the Kangxi era, he returned once more to his old retreat to inquire after the plum blossoms.
He used to say to the assembly, "Time passes with rapidity; you must all urgently attend to the foundation of your feet.

On the twenty-seventh day of the first month of winter, he manifested slight illness. By the evening of the thirtieth, he called for an attendant to bring hot water for a bath. He sat in the lotus posture and passed away.
(Jie’an Jin-si). Master Jibai Xu of Yunmen in Nankang went to visit Jinming Jin. Jin drew a circle on the ground with his staff and said, "Speak a phrase here.
The Master drew a circle with his whisk. Jin struck him. The Master shouted. Jin said, "A reckless shout!"

"What is it? The Master shook his sleeves and departed. He first resided at Wulao Peak on Mount Lu, where he would always engage in discourse with the monastics, and all were delighted and won over by him.
Later, he moved to Yunmen. One day he said to the assembly: "If you can utter a phrase for turning back, there is also the phrase for letting go from the precipice.
If you can utter the phrase for letting go, there is also the final phrase. Try to communicate one."
The assembly was at a loss for words. The Master said, "You do not understand? I shall speak the Dharma myself.
He then sat upright and recited a verse; casting aside his brush, he passed away. (Jiegan Jin succeeded him.)
Chan Master Lanyue Tan of Chengtian Monastery in Quanzhou was the son of the Zheng family from Jinjiang. Once, while observing a game of Go, he gave this small instruction:

"When meeting an opponent at the board, it is difficult to hide one's clumsiness; when composing a poem, it is only upon repeated recitation that its artistry becomes apparent. For those of us who are monks, we must carry our staff and wooden clappers wherever we go."

To achieve victory by adapting to circumstances is also like this game; they are quite similar. When still, the pieces are stationary; when moved, the pieces advance. Illumination and application are one and the same:

moving in tandem through double gates. Affairs and principles both reach their fulfillment: taking a corner and flying diagonally. Deploying troops to provoke a fight—what prevents striking here while attacking there?
A single blade entering directly—the merit lies in being the first to breach the fortifications and ascend. Moving along the flank...
Exerting force at the periphery, how could one hope to invade the main gate? Relying on the corners for survival, how many cities and fortresses have been lost?
The three armies suffer defeat because of being delayed by even half a moment. To break through the encirclement is ultimately like drawing a bow after the enemy has already passed;
to follow others up and down is certainly a flawed strategy. Even if you grant them half a point, you still fall into second place. Thus it is said: "Holding the tally..."
This belongs to the latter [section]. A single move determines victory or defeat;

those who wish to understand the principle of this "single move" must break through the great iron net, overturn the hanging lotus, and attain mastery over both killing and giving life—only then can one be called a master of the game.
Even when scrutinized, the ultimate standard of a monk’s own station still lacks one move. What is this ultimate standard of the monk?
Before black and white were distinguished, the wondrous was difficult to apply; as soon as the patterns appeared, it was but a single game of chess.
Once the nineteen lines across the center were drawn, he was finally able to sit and enjoy the foundation of a peaceful era. At the end of his life, he bathed, recited a verse, and passed away.
Upon cremation, his single sandal remained unburnt and is enshrined for offerings to this day. His stupa is located on Mount Qingyuan (Ji’ān Jìn sì).
Chanshi Sanduo of Donglin Mountain in Luzhou was the son of the Li family of Sangluo.

From birth, he possessed innate wisdom and took no pleasure in the studies for the civil service examinations. He visited Donglin to shave his head and, while reading the *Record of Gaofeng*, he harbored doubts regarding the phrase "dragging a corpse."

He traveled extensively to visit masters throughout the various regions. At the end of his journey, he entered the quarters of Jinming; upon seeing him, they felt as though they had a karmic bond from a previous life, and Jinming immediately lowered his pride before him.
Jinming asked, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing—what is this? The Master replied, "Exposed.
Jinming said, "Yesterday someone spoke like that, and I gave them thirty blows and drove them out. The Master said, "If you were going to hit me, just hit me; do not speak of it."
It was just yesterday. As soon as [the Master] made a sound, [Baizhang] struck him with his palm. Baizhang stepped forward, restrained him, and said, "You blind donkey! Why do you act so recklessly?

As the Master was about to offer a word in reply, Baizhang struck him again. When the Master was about to speak once more, Baizhang struck him yet again. At that moment, the Master attained a sudden realization and enlightenment. Baizhang issued him the seal of the source-lineage.
He went on to reside at Donglin, and subsequently moved to Qi, Hua, Gui, Xiling, and Biyun. [He ascended the hall and preached: "When all is exhausted..."
It is gone! The earth’s axis shifts and the heavens revolve; the dragon roars and mist rises, the tiger howls and wind is born.
At such a time as this, those who habitually ply their hands and feet may, with the single eye of a śramaṇa, seal in place the myriad phenomena of the universe.

Thus they can suck the Western River into their mouths and hide the Northern Dipper within their bodies; they can stir the Yellow River with three inches of tortoise-hair and crush a chestnut burr upon a single leaf.

Splitting open the Flower Treasury World, every single thing manifests the Dharma and every phenomenon reveals its true nature. Like the urine of oxen and the dung of horses, it illuminates the past and shines upon the present;
in every atom and every land, it is preached and discussed. Even a white ox or a stray cat can roar like thunder and flash like lightning.

The patriarchs of Xinghua, Fenyang, and I, Yuanhu—having attained this one point—wield the sword from the royal treasury, employing the mechanisms of killing and giving life to truly uphold the reputation of the Jibei lineage.
Revealing the true eye for humans and devas, this mountain monk today, without begrudging his own possessions, sets forth the whole vessel and casts it before you.

Those who can grasp it as it is thrown into the light will have great cause for enjoyment. On the fifteenth day of the ninth month of the Xinhai year of the Kangxi era, he manifested a slight illness to the assembly and remarked, "There is one who will remember this very day next year.
The entire congregation was struck with wonder and astonishment. At that time, there was...
The monks came forward and asked, "What is your honored intention, Master? The Master said, "The year of the third hundred and eighty-fourth *renzi*, during the first ten days of the seventh month.
He then said to his disciples, "I wish to return to my native village; you should prepare for this quickly. The assembly took this as a routine departure.
He then purchased a donkey to serve as a mount. The Master looked at it and smiled, saying, "My journey is not something a donkey can endure.
From that time on, he earnestly admonished the assembly. On the eighth day of the ninth month, he entered the city to take leave of his lay patrons and the senior monks from various mountains.
He returned to the mountain on the eleventh, and on the twelfth, he ascended the seat to provide instruction. The gist of his discourse was: "After my passing..."

He did not permit the raising of mourning banners or the display of filial piety, nor did he emulate the worldly customs such as the burning of paper money. He further prohibited the construction of stupas;
instead, his remains were to be cast into the rivers to benefit sentient beings, a command that must not be willfully disobeyed.

On the fifteenth day, at the hour of the Dragon (7–9 a.m.), he bathed, burned incense, sat upright, and passed away while reciting a verse. Upon cremation, the recovered bones were found to be pure white, and even his teeth remained intact.

The hall was destroyed. His rosary remained as it had been when he was alive. The Master passed away on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month of the Xinyou year, having reached a worldly age of fifty-two and a monastic seniority of twenty-eight (Ji’ān Jìnsì).
While Master Yan of Ou’an and Zhu’an in Taicang was casually reading the *Noble Total Enlightenment Sūtra*, he came upon the Bodhisattvas’ question:

"Now that the four elements have each departed, where does this illusory body reside? He then struck the desk and sighed deeply, saying, "If people do not clarify this fundamental matter, they merely assume the appearance of monks;
it provides no benefit within their own original allotment. Thereupon, he traveled extensively to seek instruction. One day, he heard...
At the sound of a wooden board, he suddenly attained realization. He went to attend upon Jin Mingjin, serving him for over a year before retiring to Loudong.
Due to illness, he withdrew to reside at Dongguan. On the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the Ding-si year of the Kangxi era, he requested a brush and wrote this verse:

"Throughout my life I have been solitary; I have shut my door to preserve my simplicity. Though my Way may be cold, I rely on the brilliance of future generations. With a shout, he threw down his brush.
He passed away. His stupa was enshrined at the right side of Lotus Temple in Jinsu Town (by Jie’an Jinsi).
Master Xiangxiu Yuan of Baen Monastery at Xiling ascended the hall for formal discourse. He raised the case of Layman Pang;

before he had finished speaking, Lord Wang Hua stepped forward and asked, "Since he was already a perfected Buddha, why did he need to choose? The Master replied, "Dragging the plow and pulling the harrow" (Jie’an).

Chan Master Taisu Suyan, a native of Macheng, ascended the hall and said: "Within the shadows of the multicolored clouds, a divine immortal appears;
holding a red silk fan, he covers his face. You must quickly turn your eyes to look at the immortal; do not look at the fan in the immortal’s hand."
Raising his fan, he said, "This is the fan. Now tell me, where is the immortal? He threw down the fan, bowed, and said, "This is the immortal.
Where is the fan? If you all can fix a single eye upon this point, you may roam freely at will by the waterside or beneath the forest trees.
But if you have not yet attained this, you will only end up biting on a dead tree stump."
The jaw-joints snap shut as life departs; naturally, when the water arrives, the channel is formed. Regarding Dongshan’s “Three *jin* of Hemp,” he said: "What is the Buddha? Three *jin* of hemp.
Twisting it into a rope to bind the mist and clouds. If one casually recognizes the meaning at the tip of the hook, one will laugh the old woman Wang of East Village to death.
He authored the *Jingang jueyi* (Resolving Doubts Concerning the Diamond Sūtra), which circulates in the world. (Ji’ān Jìn succeeded him.)
Chan Master Jianning Puming Yun’an Liang was the son of the Xie family of Ouning. He ascended the hall and said:

"Setting aside for a moment 'three pounds of flax' and 'a dried piece of dung,' let us pass over 'Deshan’s staff' and 'Linji’s shout. Do you all know the claws and fangs of the lion, the head and horns of the fierce dragon?
To cast off the body and sit amidst a single color, one leaves behind a shadow that does not fall into conformity with others."
Manifesting Great Merit: A Small Assembly Talk. When hungry, eat; when weary, sleep. Within the school of the patch-robed monks, there is no need for arduous investigation.
Yet, as the ancient worthy said: "On Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a 'dog-urine day' (a storm).
What matter on this side of reality does this clarify? He further said: "Do not travel the path beneath the mountain," and indeed, one hears the cry of a monkey that breaks the heart.
