[The monk] had not yet raised [the question]. "What is it that is not so? The Master said, "It is not so; it is not so. The monk hesitated, and the Master immediately shouted him out (as recorded in the *Kezheng*).
Chan Master Meishu of Guoqing Mountain on Mount Tiantai was the son of Ma of Liangxi. He ascended the hall and said:

"The livelihood of a practitioner is like water striking a stone. The eyes look toward the southeast, yet the intent lies in the northwest. As soon as one pursues it outward, one has already been robbed by the thief."
Beside the Stone Beam Bridge, five hundred arhats each thought to themselves, "I have realized the fruit; my work is done.
Today at Guoqing, [the Master] intends to grant them the Great while they remain attached to the Small, so that they may together realize the supreme Dharma-gate of the Mind-Ground.

He suddenly held up his whisk and said, "Recognize the source within this single hair-tip, lest you continue to weary yourselves by seeking stillness while rejecting clamor. He then looked to his left and right and said, "It is not so."
Guoqing suppresses and eclipses the former sages. You virtuous ones, you must each take care of your own eyebrows!
(A shout—in Kezhengsi).
Chan Master Qianhua Yu of Mount Yu was the son of the Li family of Huangmei. He studied under Chan Master Ganlu Zheng and investigated the koan of the bamboo stick for two years with great diligence.
One day, hearing a tile jar being smashed against a wall, he attained realization and composed this verse: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
Surrounded on all four sides by treacherous barriers beyond reckoning, there is no path forward and no door to retreat.
With a sudden blow outside the azure heavens, a misstep turns the great earth upside down. The monk asked, "Everyone has a patch of ground beneath their feet;
why is it that they cannot step upon it? The Master shouted, "Who else would you have step upon it? He then presented this verse: "Trampling through the mountain stream..."
The mountain has not a single inch of soil; returning, every affair is peaceful and at ease. If one cannot resolve this within, they will follow along with others;
I dare say it will take them as many years as a donkey’s lifespan to penetrate the essential barrier. *Verse on Deshan’s Carrying the Alms Bowl:* Without cause, he carries his bowl and returns;
This provokes the foul mouth of Yantou to open. Indeed, Deshan remained silent for three years; Like a hound chasing after clods of earth, everyone vied with suspicion and doubt.
He later resided at Sanfeng (Three Peaks), where his quarters contained no superfluous belongings. He maintained a solitary and independent character.
On the day he passed away, a monk asked, "What is the state of your Dharma-body? The Master replied, "The skin and flesh have fallen away entirely; there remains only the single reality.
Thereupon, he entered nirvana (he was succeeded by Kezheng).
Chan Master Zhiguo of Huazang in Wuxi was the son of the Hu family of Wuxi. He studied under Dashi Zheng at Sanfeng and attained a realization.
One day, during the night session, Zheng placed a tile on the ground and asked, "Say it is not a tile;
say it is not a tile. Speak! The Master immediately stepped forward, kicked it with his foot until it shattered, and then walked out. Zheng nodded in approval.
Subsequently, while residing at Huazang, he ascended the hall for the opening of the retreat. He said: "Before the fifteenth day, the Buddhas are born yet unborn.
You people must not depart from within my presence. If you were to depart from within my presence, I would have no hook with which to hook you."
After the fifteenth day, although all Buddhas have entered extinction, they do not truly pass away; yet no person may dwell within my domain.
If you were to dwell within my domain, I would have no awl with which to pierce you. Right now, it is precisely the fifteenth day.
To use a hook is not it; to use an awl is also not it. Tell me, after all, how is it? On this very fifteenth day, the hook.
The awls all come out at once. When he was about to ask further how it was, the Master drove his staff right through his head.
Addressing the assembly: "Every object present here is a family treasure. Why labor your mind to seek elsewhere? Yesterday the sky was clear; today it rains.
The loquats on the tree are all golden. (In Kezheng’s succession.)
Chan Master Zhuyuan of Ruguang Temple in Suzhou, whose secular surname was Li and whose courtesy name was Yao, ascended the hall and said:

"Today is the second day of the fourth lunar month; the commencement of summer falls precisely upon this day. The greens grow deep and the reds thin as the seasons gradually shift; the fragrant breeze arrives here to speak to us.
When it speaks, it speaks in silence; when it is silent, it speaks. The cypress tree before the courtyard shares its age with the moon; its ancient trunk supports new growth."
[The Master] remained silent for a moment. [He said: "If you can understand this, you will attain one peg. After a long while, he said: "The plum fruit turns green atop the tree;
the cherry berries are as red as pearls. In a small *sǎn* (informal sermon), he asked:
"The Dharma-nature is fundamentally formless; from where does this stinking skin-bag come? The Master struck him, saying: "What kind of place is this? The monk bowed, and the Master struck him again.
He said: "Only when you have cast off this skin-sack here will you succeed. He then said: "The Dharma-nature is fundamentally non-existent; green and lush, azure and flowing.
Upon the tips of the hundred grasses, the Great Function is revealed. The Dharma-nature is fundamentally existent; flowers in clusters, brocade in clusters.
Amidst the bustle of the marketplace, the true traces are exposed. If you can realize this, let the sound of metal and jade vibrate at will, and the wind shall sweep across the earth."
Lightning flashes and stars race; as for this stinking skin-bag of supernatural powers and wondrous functions—where will you set it down?
If you do not understand this, you must simply let go of all conditions and press straight ahead.

Be like the Master above who spent five years pounding rice, unmoved by cold or heat, with no interval between thought after thought. Just investigate in this manner; why worry that there will be no awakening?
At the time of the assembly, after a long silence, he said: "When one has traveled until the waters run out and the mountains end, there is naturally a moment to turn around.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If we discuss this matter, it is fundamentally complete and requires no artificial arrangement.
Yet, alas, the gate of emotion is firmly closed and the locks of consciousness are difficult to open. Thus, one's own radiance is, on the contrary, obscured. Today, Master Fan..."
I have no other extraordinary tongs or hammers to forge the ordinary or the holy;
I have only this one ancient koan to present before you all, wishing for each and every one of you to attain realization through and through. Suddenly, he held up his whisk and said:
If you call out to the whisk, it is "contact" (touching). If you do not call out to the whisk, it is "backing away.
You must not speak; you must not remain silent. Speak quickly! Speak quickly! As soon as the monk stepped forth, the Master descended from his seat.

In his later years, while residing at Qiónglóng Niànhuā, as he was about to pass into nirvana, he entered the city to bid farewell to all his old friends and associates. On the way, he said to himself: "I am returning to the mountain. He then composed [a verse].
Within a great circular halo, he placed his body. He then wrote a couplet: "Amidst a thousand mountains and ten thousand peaks / Within a single thought of no-thought.
Having finished speaking, he again let out a long, resonant cry; none were able to fathom its meaning. After returning to the mountain, he manifested a slight illness.
One day, he shaved his hair and requested a bath; then, sitting upright, he passed away. This was on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month in the year of Kāngxī Yimao (1715).
Lifespan: seventy-five (Dingmu Che-si).
Chan Master Foyin Tan of Qionglung was the son of the Wu family of Xishan. He left home at an early age;
upon reading the *Recorded Sayings of Gaofeng*, he attained realization. He went to visit Sanfeng Zang at Jinsu, whereupon Zang saw him and immediately asked, "Who is that?"
Li Ren asked, "The Master speaks of 'original ground' (ben-di). Why, then, does one run away from home? The Master said, "I do not dare to find fault with others.
Li Cang immediately ordered him to attend the meditation hall. Later, he relied upon Rui Guang Che, where he investigated with fierce diligence.

One day, Che asked, "You claim to have recognized the staff that moves freely in all directions; how do you understand this? The Master said, "The waves are treacherous; cease casting your line. "Neng... [The text ends here.]

Long had already recognized the hook. Changche asked, "What is it like after you have recognized it? The Master said, "Even if you were to understand it fundamentally, it would still be but dust in the eye.
Changche approved of this and shared his seat to preach the Dharma. He subsequently went to reside at Nianhua Temple.

Ascending the hall, he held his staff horizontally across his chest and said, "Today, the true command is fully enacted. Should anyone come forward with a question, they shall receive thirty blows of the staff immediately. Long time...

No one came forward. He spoke again: "It is fortunate that you know your own capacity; do not trouble yourselves to gouge out your own flesh. He threw down his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"This mountain monk’s staff sometimes reviles the Buddhas and scolds the Patriarchs; sometimes it distinguishes demons and selects the extraordinary;
sometimes it blends its light with the dust; sometimes it surges from the east and sinks in the west. By what means shall we verify this? With his staff, he struck them all at once.
Chenxia passed away in the autumn of the Gengyin year of the Shunzhi era (1650). A stupa was built at the western foot of the mountain at his own temple (Dingmu Cheshi).
Chan Master Xuyimiao of Taiping Temple in Changzhou asked: "If one calls out to the bamboo staff, it is 'contact';

if one does not call out to the bamboo staff, it is 'contradiction. What do you call it? The Master said: "The red sun shines brightly in the sky. [The Master] asked: "What is the underlying meaning? The Master said: [The same].
"Ha! I shall split your face open! (This was the transmission from Dingmu Cheshi).
Chan Master Meishan Pei of Jiulong, Huai'an, a native of Baoning in Sichuan, addressed the assembly:
"Last night, a tiger on the southern mountain bit a beast. Do you all hear the sound of its agony? After a long silence, he said: "You all are skilled..."
When one is so densely enveloped that even east and west cannot be distinguished, how can there be ears to hear? Looking left and right, he cried out, "Heaven!
Heaven! Addressing the assembly, he said: "In this practice, there is no leakage; it is like water soaking a hemp rope until it becomes tight.
When you reach the point where the tightness cannot go further, suddenly you kick over the pure pitcher. But tell me, what happens after it has been kicked over? You simply pick it back up again."
"Come! Give him a flower to pin in his hair and a willow branch to stick in his hat" (Cheshi points to his own eyes).
Zen Master Daozhao of Konglong Weitang in Suzhou asked, "I do not ask about forging in the great furnace;

how is it with the single phrase of Dangyang? The Master then gave a shout. Daozhao said, "In the depths of the ocean tide, silver waves overturn; amidst the trees of the Jetavana Grove, [the spring] surges forth."
"Bīpō. The Master shouted again. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Henceforth, you must not let me down.
A monk asked, "Zhaozhou’s tea is for people to drink at their leisure; Nanguan’s rice is for anyone to eat until full. I wonder, how does the Master receive guests?
The Master said, "By the fire of split logs, we roast yams. The monk said, "But I have already swallowed it all in one gulp!"
The Master said: "In daily activities, you must also apply yourself with full attention. (From the *Dingmu Cheshi*).
At the evening assembly of Zen Master En of Ichi-ju at Kinzaki Eiran-ji: "Each person’s eyes are like a thousand suns, blazing and radiant;

each person’s ears are like ten thousand valleys, resonant and empty. Within both the mundane and the supramundane, there is not a single thing that can escape their shadow, nor a single sound [that can escape their hearing]."
"It does not enter its orifice; it is most clearly manifest. It is most responsive.
He suddenly took up his staff and said, "Why is it that having eyes, one cannot see here? He struck once and said, "Why is it that having ears, one cannot hear here?
What acts as a barrier? What acts as an obstruction? It is because you, good sirs, yourselves are unwilling to [realize it] directly right here."
He approaches the most accessible point and pushes it away; he merely circles around that which is fundamentally wondrous, lofty, and remote. Again, he raises his hand and says: "Heh! Heh!
The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet it is difficult to behold within those very eyes. It is certainly not the lamp-stand or the lantern; it must be张三 (Zhāng sān) or 李五 (Lǐ wǔ).
If you understand this, you will move with sovereign freedom beyond the conventional; if you do not understand, you will remain sitting inside the drum."
The drumhead is so tightly stretched that it does not allow air to pass; it causes one’s vision to become dizzy and chaotic.

Who would have known that the Buddhas of the three periods of time are not as good as the white ox of the eastern village? Taking water and grass as they come, it partakes of them in measure; dwelling alone upon the solitary peak, it refuses to be ranked with others.
Sometimes its horns are bared to charge the dragon; sometimes its tail-tip strikes the tiger. Suddenly transforming into the Way of Pure Wind, it flies across West Qin and East Qin.
Luzu struck his staff once and said, "I have struck you down with this staff; you are transformed into yellow mud and black earth.
Looking back to his left and right, he asked, "Do you understand? He then rose and said, "Suffering! A monk asked about the "Three Not-sos.
The Master chanted aloud: "Not mind, not Buddha; there is yet another thing that cannot be spoken. If you can speak it—Zhaozhou’s East [Gate]!"
Wall-Mounted Gourd (by Cheshi Dingmu).
Master Jiyun Jun of Meiyin in Suzhou was the son of the Yao family of Xiushui; he was the younger brother of Zhongyu Fan.
Having attended Tiantong for a long time, he next visited Sanfeng Zang and received the "Bamboo Ruler" koan. Following this, he attained peace and stability.

Later, while traveling with Lianzhai Li on the same boat, Li raised the "Bamboo Ruler" koan before finishing his question; the Master immediately shouted. Li said, "When will empty space fall crashing to the ground?
As the Master hesitated, Li raised the bamboo ruler and struck him. At that moment, the Master was suddenly liberated and realized enlightenment, saying:
"The primary source of one's original destiny is right here. [The Master] grabbed him and said, "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The Master then struck him with his palm.
Ascending the hall, he cited Danqiao Lun, who said: "In the mountains of Jing there is jade, but the one who obtains the jade is not in the mountains of Jing.

In the waters of Chi there is a pearl, but the one who acquires the pearl is not in the waters of Chi. A patch-robed monk has the 'True Person of No Rank,' but the one who realizes it is not [found in that rank]."
[The Master] rested his staff horizontally across his face and asked, "Do you understand? A stone man crouches at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou.
The Master said, "Although Duànqiáo has emptied his heart and liver [to explain], he cannot avoid causing people to abandon what is near for what is far.

Today, Ruìguāng does not do so. There is jade in the Jīng Mountains; once the jade is obtained, who looks further at the mountains? There is a pearl in the Vermilion Water; once the pearl is secured..."
Those who have completely forgotten the "Red Water" [will find it]. Zen monks possess the "True Person of No Rank. For those who realize this, it crushes through the gateway of the face.
Then, holding his staff crosswise, he asked, "Do you understand? "From this point on, one does not return; yet if one returns, one shall attain it.

Who can compete for the misty scenery of the Five Lakes? The Master wrote an inscription for the gate of a mountain monastery: "If you wish to practice in that realm, come here to ponder and strike. A monk approached.
The monk said, "In that case, have you arrived home? The Master said, "A lion of Wuzhong roars in Yunjian.
As the monk hesitated, the Master said, "Thirty blows! (Chengduo Cheshi).

Master Sengsen of Cuitang at Tiger Hill in Suzhou ascended the hall and said: "The Buddha-dharma does not reside in the effort expended on meditation cushions or Zen boards, nor does it lie in the closing of eyes and joining of brows.
As the former sages said: 'If you wish to attain the One Vehicle, do not loathe the six sense objects.'"

The six sense-objects are not evil; they are identical to perfect enlightenment. All you virtuous practitioners of dhyāna: if, at the table where wine and meat are set out, you can strike off the tip of your nose, I allow that you have had an audience with Panshan.
If, at the place where the staff strikes the mouth, you can recognize your own face, I allow that you have had an audience with Baoshou.
As for Baguaoshan (Pouch Monk), who spent his whole day waiting at the crossroads—what was he doing?
[The Master] ascends the hall and says: "I cite the Fifth Patriarch, Yuan: 'When an ox passes through a window frame, its head, horns, and four hooves have all passed through;
why can the tail not pass? Now, let us take another analogy: it is like a gnat that is able to build its nest upon a flame.
Why then is there no place for it to settle upon the great land of Jambudvīpa? After a long silence, he says: "One tune, two tunes—there is none..."
People gather. After the rain, the autumn waters are deep in the pond at night (the top of the verse:
Cheshi). Master Yian of Ren’an at Yunju in Hangzhou was Zhang Xiuchu of Wulin.

Having studied under Sanfeng for a long time, he later received the tonsure and became a monk, eventually inheriting the lineage from Xianning. When asked, "Who can reach Yunju in the heavens? the Master replied, "He swings his arms about."
"Come here alone, with no companion. [The student] said, "If that is so, then there is only heaven above, and no mountain to equal it.
The Master said, "Where do the weeping monkeys and soaring cranes return? They remain amidst the thousand roof-tiles and hundred battlements.
[The student] asked, "Suppose National Teacher Zhongfeng were to arrive here; how would you, Master, receive him? The Master said, "This place does not admit fat men."
Furthermore, he was instructed to stand downwind. [The Master] said, "In Wulin, there is only this fellow; he is still somewhat better. The Master replied, "Do not defame others.
The Master first resided at Xianing and finally passed away at Qingyun in Taizhou, north of the Yangtze River.
He authored the *Pihu Lu* (Record of Splitting the Flower). [Compiled by Danyu Hengsi.]
Chan Master Jiaoye of Baima at Mount Xiangshan in Suzhou was the son of the Mao family of Taizhou. At the age of eighteen, he shaved his head and received the precepts.
He was extensively versed in the teachings of the Mahāyāna. Later, he studied under Sanfeng Zang; one day, upon hearing Zang cite the words "the magpie cries atop the tree," he attained awakening.

He remained to serve by Zang’s side. After Zang entered *nirvāṇa*, he split open the stone wall [to reveal the remains] and succeeded him on the seat at Sheng’en Temple, where he relied upon numerous masters for further study.
At the beginning of his tenure, he received formal certification. Upon moving to Xiangshan Baima, he addressed the assembly:
"Zihu’s evil dogs swarm in packs; the venomous snakes of Snowy Ridge obstruct the path; Bimozhi’s long fork impales people; Shigong’s hidden arrows cause havoc.
They stir up chaos throughout the world, leaping everywhere. Last night, the western wind brought word: they have all been gathered and confined within Xiangshan. Now stand ready to await my staff."

"Opening the way and guiding. The assembly, tell me: how does one open the way and guide? [The Master] struck them with his staff to drive them away and returned to the abbot’s quarters for the evening sermon.
Holding up his bamboo pointer, he said: "Bright as the sun, black as lacquer; brought forth in the midst of the assembly, people do not recognize it."
Walking with hands let go atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak; the Unranked True Person is bare-boned and stark. Question:
"Everyone has a shadow that never leaves them for a single step. Why then can one not tread upon it? The Master said: "Your straw sandals lack power.
[The student] asked: "If they did have power, what then? The Master said: "The heels are exposed. Question: "What is it like when every thought-moment does not linger?"
The Master said, "The whole body appears. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when not a single thought arises? The Master said, "Drowned head-first.
[The monk] asked, "Setting aside these two paths, I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "In whose household's hearth is there fire without smoke?
In the eighth month of the Xinchou year of the Shunzhi era, he left behind this verse: "Born in my fifty-seventh year, the Great Matter is now complete. I have toppled..."
Mount Sumeru. He shattered the realm of non-arising and passed away in profound stillness (Pǒshíbìsì).

Recorded by the Thirty-sixth Generation of the Linji School under Mount Nanyue:
Chan Master Zhanting Baiguan of Mount Nanyue ascends the hall. "Majestic is the crimson summer, drawing forth the heat; blazing are the flames."
The sun steams the sky; ten *li* away, lotuses bloom north of the Tiáo River. A stream of flowing water divides the bridge to the east.

On the fragrant grassland, Han Gan’s horses neigh; in the shade of green willows, Dai Song’s oxen lie down. Such a fine scene cannot be fully described at once; for the most part, one must encounter it through discerning appreciation.
It is only a matter of the person themselves casting a lofty eye upon it. Who would say that such intimacy does not allow for the passage of wind? *Duḥ!* (A shout of realization.)

Regarding these words, how many people understand them as a description of external phenomena? Even granting that one does not understand them as a description of external phenomena, what kind of eye do they possess?
[He] planted his staff and said: "Where the level marshes end, there is a green mountain; the traveler stands even beyond the green mountain.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "Ice and snow press upon the cold branches; the void freezes to the very marrow. Throughout the vast and boundless universe, all is silent."
In the Hall of Silent Mountains, a stone tiger sleeps cradling its cubs; a wooden man plays with puppets. Raise your eyebrows and look! All these are your own.

If you harbor doubts like this, there are ten thousand miles of white clouds. He looked at the assembly and said, "Setting aside for a moment the 'ten thousand miles of white clouds,' what is it that is your own?
The assembly was silent. After a long while, he struck the ground with his staff and said, "Look!"
Realize it here! On the day of the midday assembly for the Dragon Boat Festival: the Midday of the Fifth Month, the Festival of Heaven. Regarding that matter, do you all perceive it instantly or not?
At every household throughout the market, mugwort tigers are hung at the gates; realgar is sprinkled on the ground to dispel evil influences.
The ancient story of Qu Yuan reveals the loyalty and integrity of the noble; dragon boats race across the waters of the realm. Step by step, one enters the Treasury of Radiance. Be careful!
Who would not penetrate this thoroughly? (A shout—asked by Seokseung-si.
Master Jeongjeong of Anhwa God Mountain ascends the hall for the opening of the retreat, posting the roster: The bell and wooden board hang high; the one who calls the assembly is the master.
The entire monastic community is his own body. Each of the six gates has its duty, with no deviation; To die together and to live together.
His mind became even more intimate [with the truth]. He then struck the air three times with his whisk, gave a shout, and said: "Remember the words of an ancient:
'Though the Zhou dynasty was old, its mandate was renewed. Again, he gave a shout. *Small Assembly (Xiao-can)*: The Master raised his bamboo pointer.
Looking left and right, he said: "If you all wish to cross the barrier of the Patriarchs, you must exert all your strength to exhaustively investigate the mountain of the five aggregates.
Only by firmly grasping the steel blade and the sharp axe to sever the life-root can you find peace. Again, striking the air with his bamboo staff, he said:
'The meaning of the Patriarch from the West is the cypress tree in the courtyard; the pure Dharma-body is a dry piece of dung. Straighten your spine and investigate this carefully.'"
"Just as a hen’s brooding causes the egg to crack naturally. [Question: "What is the Pure Dharmakāya? [Master:
"If one washes the stains from a vessel with ash and soap, it will still hold its contents without becoming sour or spoiled. [Question: "What is the Perfect Saṃbhogakāya? [Master:
"When true fire is struck from stone, its blazing, fierce flames can never be extinguished. [Question: "What are the thousands and hundreds [of transformation bodies]? [Master: "..."

[The Master] manifested one billion transformation bodies. The Teacher said: "As the ashes fly and the musical tubes signal the arrival of spring at its beginning, the withered mountains across the earth renew themselves day by day.
"How is it the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom? The Teacher said: "When the breath from the nostrils is like thunder, who looks back upon themselves?
"How is it the Wisdom of Equality? The Teacher said: "Welcoming guests and seeing them off—busy at both ends. "How is it the Wisdom of Wondrous Observation? The Teacher said: [He remained silent.]
Returning from delusion to truth, truth itself does not stand. What is the wisdom of accomplished action (*kṛtyānuṣṭhāna-jñāna*)? The Master said:
"The windless deep sea, where the *shen* spirit transforms into a tower. "The Three Bodies and Four Wisdoms have been pointed out by the Master;

what is the matter of the 'total raising' above this? The Master said: "Once the mirror is shattered, one looks at the reflection again; whether one is handsome or ugly, one knows it oneself. (Questioned by Shicheng Si.)
Chan Master Wujin Wengu of Tanzhou ascended the hall. With a unique opening of the vital mechanism, he turns out fresh, cold words.
When the true command is properly executed, old cases are settled anew. "The World-Honored One spoke what was not spoken"—this was originally no more than adding flowers to brocade.
"Kāśyapa heard what was not heard"—this was merely beans popping in the ashes. Let the matter of host and guest be set aside for a moment; as for principle and phenomenon, they are sovereign.
Your servant has no need to labor over further calculations. Suppose someone were to come and press me to expound upon the Buddha-dharma of the "opening the furnace":

the mountain monk’s affairs are many; we shall discuss this in detail tomorrow morning. A small *sǎn* (private instruction): For a patch-robed monk who has utterly transcended the sense bases and their objects, there is no longer any confinement.

For one who has suddenly leaped beyond the cycles of cold and heat, how could the true essence be subject to the passage of time? Within the gate of great liberation, entry and exit are unimpeded. This is the wondrous adornment...

"Clear the paths. What restriction is there on coming and going? If you merely follow sounds and pursue forms, imitating the blind who chase after the deaf, you will not only bury your own spiritual brilliance, but you will also bring shame upon this mountain monk.
You who climb mountains and wade through waters, who till the soil with knives and burn seeds with fire—do not merely tighten the laces of your shoes;
you must further examine the handles of your hoes. Addressing the assembly: "In the deep forest, small birds sing every day."
In spring, the incense burner in the ancient temple emits flames from time to time. Why trouble yourself, mountain monk, to pick it up and present it?

You are merely clogging the way for the high sages. Pointing at the incense burner with his *ruci* (wish-fulfilling jewel), he said: "O assembly, set aside blue, yellow, red, white, and black. Tell me, what color is it?
If you cannot say, then you all have had sand put in your eyes and water poured in your ears by this mountain monk."
[He] struck the incense burner once with his *nyoi* (wish-fulfilling jewel) and entered the hall. The assembly rose all at once. The Master said, "None of you may move;
if you move, disaster will arise. The assembly remained silent. The Master said, "Thirty blows of the staff—wait for another time" (asked by Sekishō Shitsu).
Chan Master Sheng’en Hǒuyá of Suzhou ascended the hall for formal discourse. Having finished citing the four shouts of Great Master Linji, he let out a shout himself and said:
"Is this single shout the Vajra King’s Precious Sword? Is it the lion crouching on the ground? Is it the probing pole and the shadow-grass?
Or is it the case where a single shout is not used as a single shout? If you can, within this single...
"Ha! When one's discernment is precise and appropriate, only then is it fit to untangle the adhesions and remove the bonds for others.
This is called the "Samādhi of Self-Enjoyment. O worthy ones, you must be extremely careful; do not be hasty. If this were just random or reckless shouting, what kind of matter would that be?
After a long silence, he looks to his left and right, then lets out another shout and descends from the seat. Ascending the hall, he strikes the meditation platform once.
The sound is like the great lion’s roar; it compels the Great Spirit to nod his head. He raises two eyebrows over Lake Dongting and opens wide a mouth across Lake Taihu.
Throughout all lands and realms, he speaks with blazing intensity, without ceasing. But tell me: what does he say?
Since ancient times, gazing upon this lake, I have seen nothing different; even now, it remains unchanged from how it was viewed of old.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Now we first see the spring wind arrive; suddenly, spring is already half-way through. Days and months pass like shuttle-cocks; time flies as swiftly as an arrow. For those who truly study the Way, there must be no interval in their every thought.
If you wish to penetrate the barrier of the Patriarchs, it depends on realization at the moment of the critical opportunity. At that moment..."
Turning over, he finally realized his original face; he further exhausted the source of the Dharma. Everywhere he attained mastery and transformation. The incense pillar laughed itself down;
the monk’s hall and the mountain gate rushed into the Buddha hall. Announcing to all people whether they have realized it or not, he let out a shout (Pishi Bi succeeded him).
Master Yunnan Yuehang of Gusu addressed the assembly: "The seven-day period has now come to an end.
Emotions are withered and wisdom exhausted; faith is difficult to penetrate. Suddenly, after a clap of thunder, behold the six dragons dancing in the crimson heavens.
Watch closely; do not pursue the source. The moon rises upon the coral tree, and the tree is red. Addressing the assembly again, he cited Baizhang’s "Opening the Fields": [text follows].
Having finished speaking these words of great meaning, the Master said: "Baizhang was indeed like this, yet he still failed others.
Today, I, this mountain monk, have come to dwell on this mountain; you all have plowed the fields for me, and I shall also explain a word of great meaning for you.
The Master suddenly made the gesture of thrusting a spade into the ground and chanted aloud: "Whipping up the clay ox to plow the stony field, a single furrow turns over—"
Before the turning of the kalpa, the livelihood of the pickaxe was no more than this; it lies only within the realm of ordinary daily life (as transmitted by Poshibi).
Master Xinghua Guyan Li of Jiaoshan ascended the hall and said: "Thread comes and line goes; the jeweled net interlaces.
Weaving brocade and piercing the clouds, Jiaofeng reveals itself directly. The three springs have already passed, and now the nine summers arrive. Tell me, how do you respond to the season?"
A single line: How would you say it? The iron tree blooms with pomegranates, purple mists coalesce; with bare heart and open mind, I answer for you. Ascending the hall, he said:
The brocade trees bloom, their fragrance strikes the nose; branch after branch, hanging leaves reflect the cool clarity.
From this day forth, descendants shall fill the world; the great chiliocosm is but a single meditation seat. (Da-shu [Dadu] was certified as his successor.)
Chan Master Xiang of Baiyun Mountain in Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "The clouds are hidden; the sun is bright.
To till the fields and earn one's rice is the ancient family style. Sometimes west, sometimes east—a single red orb is kicked out from beneath his feet.
His head is held high with eyes like *ākṣīva* seeds; his power lies in meeting conditions without borrowing. (Questioned by Shicheng Si).

Chan Master Wuxi Changtaide was the son of Chen of Jiahe. He addressed the assembly: "The myriad phenomena of the phenomenal world are constantly manifest before us.
Yet, by the time you raise your eyebrows, the sword has long since departed. You who are quick-witted must realize this directly."
"It is already eight *kè* late. If you take your mind to seek the mind, how is this different from asking for Chang'an while inside the Han-yuan Palace?
He then spread out both hands and said, "What bowl are you looking for? He once composed a verse on the Essential Principle (*zongzhi*) which says:
"A pair of stone lions emerges from the wild weeds; A pair of wooden horses enters the chaotic clouds. The moon sets at the third watch and all sounds cease; The clear breeze..."
A chilling roar shakes heaven and earth (revealing the jade wall).
Chan Master Fochuang Hua of Dongshan in Qizhou ascends the hall and says: "One, two, ten thousand, a million—like a swift arrow or a fleeting light, do not let it pass you by.
Before you lift your head, the plants and trees have already blossomed; in the blink of an eye, the ice-flakes have already fallen. Investigate!"
If Chan does not uphold the Prātimokṣa, it is like boiling sand for rice until the bottom of the cauldron breaks. A golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace;
an earthen Buddha does not pass through the water; the True Buddha sits within. On Mount Hua, the flowing waters are springtime for ten thousand years.
Zihu was about to strike Liu Tiemo; he let out a shout and said, "Wrong, wrong, wrong! Friends, tell me: what is wrong? [The text continues below.]
The text is long; it is entrusted for a future day (by Poshibei Si).
Chan Master Cheshi of Qinglian Yifeng in Runzhou was a native of Hezhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The spring light is brilliant and beautiful;
in every instance, Śākyamuni is manifest. The wild scenery is clear and fresh; in every place, Maitreya is fully revealed. As for Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra—"
"It is always entering and exiting the gates of your faces, rising and surging spontaneously, moving freely without obstruction.
He suddenly held up his whisk and asked, "Do you see it? If you can see it, the true does not conceal the false, and the crooked does not hide the straight.
Even so, you must further know that there is a path beyond this. What is this path beyond? He then threw down the whisk and said:
Wearing a straw raincoat, standing askew beyond a thousand peaks; leading water to irrigate vegetables before the Five Elders.
A monk asked, "Transcending mind, intellect, and consciousness—tell me, how does one practice? The Master said, "The stone maiden, paired together, rolls a brocade ball.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Thrown east and west, leaving no trace. A monk asked, "Words cannot unfold the matter; speech does not meet the occasion."
"What do you think? The Master said: "The sun and moon hang from the tip of a rabbit-horn staff; heaven and earth stand upon the point of a tortoise-hair.
(Poushibi succeeded him.)
Zhengzhou Wuzhou Yinguo Shengkeshu Daishi was the son of Guo of Wuxi. In his later years, he attended this mountain monk.
He possessed a "Lion’s Lost Track" teaching method, which I shall now specifically present for you. You must all look closely; do not fail to recognize it right before your eyes.
Suddenly extending a palm, he asked, "What is this? Then, clenching his fist and tucking it into his sleeve, he said:
In the past, while at Li-hui, the Master once extended his hand and asked a monk, "What is this? As soon as the monk hesitated, the Master struck him with his palm.
Later, a monk asked, "I have heard that you, Reverend, possess the device of extending the hand; is this true? The Master said, "It is.
The monk stepped forward and struck him with his palm. The Master held him back, saying, "The true command is actually being exercised by me," and he followed this by striking the monk himself.
On the Double Ninth day of the Yi-si year of the Kangxi era, he passed away.
His remains were cremated, and twenty-seven teeth and jawbones were recovered, remaining uncorrupted and joined together. He was interred at his native mountain (by Prof Shi Bi).
Chan Master Haizang Huan’an Shi of Suzhou was the son of the Wu family of Huishui, Huizhou.
Having renounced his home to study the Way, he relied upon the second seat of Sheng’en Yibei. One day, as Yibei ascended the hall, the Master asked, “The myriad flowers bloom in profusion;
the forest birds warble in harmony. What is the first phrase? Yibei held up his whisk. The Master said, “The wooden boy blows [the flute].”
The Jade Flute: "A stone woman rolls a flower ball. What is the second phrase? Guobian said, "Wait until Mount Xianglu nods its head, and I will tell you.
The Master said, "On the cold crags remain only emaciated stones; on the old trees, only withered branches remain.
"What is the third phrase? Guobian set down his whisk. The Master said, "There is yet another phrase: 'The three realms cannot contain it; the ten directions..."
"How could wisdom possibly encompass it? How would you, Master, proclaim it? Biyu said, "The eye of Mahesvara is set vertically at the crown of the head.
The Master said, "Transcending the thousands of sages, reaching back directly before the August Sovereign. Biyu said, "Thirty blows for you;
take them yourself and depart. He then addressed the assembly: "Each of you must look after your own tongue. By all means, do not seek words from my mouth."
[The Master] said, "The day will come when a great club shall strike you. Do not say that this mountain monk has not revealed it to you.
At that time, a monk just stepped out; the Master struck him and said, "You wild fox spirit! What are you doing here with me?
A monk asked, "What is the matter of the school of the patriarchs? The Master said, "You must realize it for yourself. The monk said, "Is this not the Master himself?"
The monk asked, "How does one dwell as a person? The Master said, "What have I ever said to you? The monk hesitated, and the Master rebuked him, saying, "Go! There is no place for you to rest.
The Master’s teaching in response to opportunities was like the flow of a great river; it allowed no room for disciples to record it.
He passed away in the Xinmao year of the Shunzhi era (1651). His stupa is located on the western mountains of Dengwei (the successor was Poshibi).
Chan Master Wen-shui Tian of Huayan delivers a small *can* (sermon) on New Year’s Eve: The large month has thirty days; the small month has twenty-nine.
