Seeing through it, I realized there is no divergent path—why wait until midday to strike the third watch? The Head Seat received the verse and said, "The verse is right here. As if...
"What is this 'yesterday's' of mine? Master Zuo shouted, "This is yesterday's! The Master said, "Each time it is raised, it is fresh.
Master Zuo said, "But how can it be that Elder Niao still refuses to nod his head?
The Master said, "I grant you a step ahead," and closing the door, he went out. Master Zuo followed him, saying, "How profoundly true! How profoundly true! I dare say, Old Man..."
The elder brother was not yet through [his questioning]. The Master struck him across the face with his palm. The Seat-holder said, "Are you hitting Elder Nest?

The Master said, "Above all, avoid misunderstanding. The Seat-holder then desisted. He ascended the hall. A monk came forward and made the sound of drums and flutes, saying, "I know how to blow the holeless flute;
I request the Master to play the stringless zither. The Master said, "In the presence of those with clear eyes, how would one dare to act so hastily?"
The monk said, "This melody should belong only to the heavens; how many times can it be heard in the human world?
The Master said, "The Yellow River clears itself but once every three thousand years. The monk said, "One might say that when the lion roars, the fragrant grasses turn green;

where the elephant king walks, the falling blossoms turn red. The Master said, "After Ziqi has departed, there are still those who understand the music. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him, saying, "This one..."
"A board is also indispensable. He then said, "If one discusses this matter, it is like the lute, the zither, or the harp:
though they possess exquisite sounds, if there are no skillful fingers, they can never produce them. How could this mountain monk fear the toil of not lending a hand?
He made the gesture of playing the lute and asked, "Do you understand? When the music ends, the person is no longer seen; only the several peaks on the river remain green. (Jugde succeeded to him.)
Chan Master Chengyun Chengyiqing of Taixing was the son of the Shi family of Guazhou. He left home to become a monk under Tianning and paid his respects to Lingyin.
Lingyin instructed him to investigate the koan: "In the state of no dream and no thought, the great function manifests before you.

One day, while Lingyin was on an incense tour, he winked at the Master. The Master said, "At midnight, I have caught a flea. At these words, the Master attained realization. He entered the room and said, "Last night..."
A flea bit him once, and to this day he suffers from the pain without ceasing. Yuanli said, "Right now, where is the flea?
The Master said, "There is nowhere it does not honor. Yuanli said, "In a state of no-dreaming and no-thought, where is the honored one?"
The Master said, "Like a pearl on a tray. He pointed to a monk and said, "Neither touching nor turning away—bring me a phrase!

The monk said, "Empty space has no front or back. The Master said, "In that case, you have already touched and turned away. The monk gave a shout. The Master said, "Do not say there is no front or back.
The monk said, "The black bean has not yet sprouted. The Master said, "You are playing with empty tricks" (Judei Li was his successor).
Chan Master Lingzhao Zeng of Wushan in Xiaoshan was a native of Chu. On the occasion of the dismantling of the old hall, he ascended the dais and, planting his staff upright, said:
"Wushan has a single phrase that resides in the hands of the Elder of Kāśyapa (the Buddha). It penetrates past and present; the times are clear and the Way is prosperous.
Abandon the short for the long; compensate for the clumsy with diligence. He then planted his staff again and said: "The Elder of Kāśyapa..."
There is also one sentence held in the hands of Wushi. Relying on this command, he acts accordingly, bestowing rewards and meting out punishments as the occasion demands;
he compensates for deficiencies and reforms abuses, replacing the old and exalting the new. Even if Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas were to try to avoid it, they could not do so in time;

even if Śakra, Brahmā, and the various devas were to search for it, they would find no way to catch it. But tell me, by what means is it able to be so swift? (He strikes the meditation staff. From before...
Sweating horses go unrecognized; one simply seeks to re-examine epoch-making merit (as in the case of Juede’s succession).
Chan Master Qianminzheng of Lianhua, Quzhou, at his evening discourse: Day after day the sun rises in the east; day after day the sun sets in the west. The staff whistles like a dragon;
the hemp sack conceals the ugly and clumsy. I inform you all: Is it thorough or not? The skull of the patch-robed monk!
Later, Sanjin Tie (具德禮) succeeded [to the Dharma].
Dongyang Faxing went to visit the Great Master Xianjing Chanshi. One day, Tie asked, "What is it like when we meet face-to-face?
The Master said, "Two eyes facing two eyes. Tie asked, "What if someone from among them suddenly arrives?"
Again, [Zhao] asked, "How is it? The Master said, "Letting go, yet not overlooking. Zhao asked, "Before one's parents were born, what is that original face?
The Master said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice. Zhao said, "I have already lowered my voice; how do you speak?
The Master said, "The weather is turning cold; take care, Preceptor. Zhao asked, "Of those few words just now, which one was it?"
[The monk] was polite. The Master said, "Those with eyes see; those with ears hear. [The monk] prostrated and called out in a loud voice, "The Senior Monk still has seeing and hearing!
The Master immediately presented this verse: To scar a healthy flesh with an ulcer, to press down a cow as it grazes— I repent from now on for having endured such delusions in the past.
Casting aside my own inexhaustible treasury, I wander about begging from others. When one is wealthy, do not boast of it to the poor.
He also sweeps. He boils empty space until it is soft and eats his fill in a single meal; he bites down on an entire iron caltrop in one mouthful.
A monk asked, "What excellence does the fierce tiger possess that Sudhana went to study under him? The Master said, "Without undergoing a single matter, one does not grow a single wisdom.
(Jude Li succeeded him.)
Yanguan Zhulin Fu was a Dharma heir of Chan Master Zuo from the Ding family of Tongzhou. He studied under Lingyin Li, who assigned him the koan:
"The master of no dreams and no thoughts. One night, as he lay in bed, a monk on the adjacent mat extended his legs and knocked his pillow to the floor with a loud thud.
At that moment, Fu suddenly saw the place where Gaofeng stood firm. He composed a verse, which begins: "Seven feet of bedding..."

While his sleep was still deep, his pillow fell to the ground and suddenly became a dragon. A flash of lightning brought forth the Vajra-eye, shattering the "thorny burr" (liji pong) that had long obstructed him.
Bowing and seeing this, he said with joy, "This is the first line from the paper and brush;

how is it your own fundamental matter? The Master made a gesture of clapping his hands. The monk bowed and said, "Please do not be too casual. He then entered the Buddha-sun *Jingzintang* (Hall of Diligent Progress). One.
One evening, while mice were fighting over beans, [Zhaozhou] struck them both down with his fly-whisk. Suddenly, he attained great enlightenment. He then composed a verse, saying:
"The original face is manifest in every dust mote; Why use former efforts to seek it outwardly? At midnight, looking directly at the head of my bed, I broke through it:

the mice overturned the salt and beans, filling the sky with stars. Upon reading the verse, [his teacher, Nanquan] summoned him into the room and said, "I am glad that you have settled the great matter."

When he had finished, the Master said, "From where have you obtained this news? Ciming Li replied, "The stolen goods are right here. The Master said, "Thief! Thief! and immediately left the hall. Ciming Li then entered the assembly hall and grabbed the Master, saying, "Just now, did the old monk approve of you or not?

The Master said, "A hawk flies over Silla. Ciming Li said, "I never expected to meet such a monk today," and then addressed the assembly: [The Master] said, "Where have you obtained this news? Ciming Li said, "The stolen goods are right here. The Master said, "Thief! Thief! and then departed.

Ciming Li then entered the hall and seized the Master, saying, "Just now, did the old monk approve of you or not? The Master said, "A hawk flies over Silla. Ciming Li said, "I never expected to meet such a monk today," and then spoke to the assembly:
"Fubo did not practice the Dharma with diligence; he was only able to exert himself for a short time in his life. I have exerted myself many times, which is why I am ten years older than this Elder.
Ascending the hall, he cited the karmic occasion of Lingyun seeing the peach blossoms. Having finished, he said: "The cry of the cuckoo sounds as the tree-tops turn red;
how many wandering travelers have their eyes and minds cleared? Yet they are struck by others who brandish their swords—how can the peach blossoms remain?"
Jiuxiao Chunfeng (Jude Li-si).
Qionglong Ningbang Yuanshi, a Chan Master and son of the Xu family of Tiantu, was asked by a monk: "The mind is not within."
"It is not outside; it is not in between. Ultimately, where is it? The Master said, "The pillar opens the door;
the mortar closes the gate. The monk paused to reflect. The Master asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand.

The Master said, "If you could grasp the message within this, what difficulty would there be in setting the entire platter out before you? A monk asked, "The east wall strikes the west wall; the south mountain bows to the north mountain."
"Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter further above?
The Master said, "The wind-sail hoisted high, passing over Lake Dongting. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, "Before one's eyes, thirty-six thousand qing."
"The moon speaks from the heart of the waves—to whom? (By Jude Li Si).
Chan Master Fuxun Faxiang Lixianxu was the son of the Yu family of Wucheng. Hearing the sound of the wooden board, he suddenly raised his head;
as the meditation curtain brushed against his face, he had a sudden realization. The following day, during the formal assembly, the Master stepped forward and asked: "What is..."
At the place where the student was about to give up his life, Xuedou bowed and threw down his bamboo staff.

The Master picked it up and struck several monks in succession, saying, "You too deserve a blow; you too deserve a blow. He then struck the attendant, saying, "You too shall take a blow on behalf of the Abbot.
Xuedou said, "What about Lixian? The Master tossed the staff back into the assembly. After a short while, Xuedou called for the Master to enter the hall.
The Master said, "What principle have you seen that you dare to act so recklessly? The Teacher replied, "I am at fault.

The Master smiled with joy and addressed the assembly, saying, "It is truly a joy that Li-xi has attained Zen through his practice. He ascended the hall, held up his staff, and called to the assembly, saying, "An ancient said:
'With a knotted staff slung over my shoulder, I heed no one; I go straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. When he arrives..."
"Here! Why do you refuse to stay? He then planted his staff in the ground and said, "For twenty years I have been traveling as a monk, and I have arrived only at this place.
Small Lecture: Last night I composed a verse; I shall not hesitate to present it to the assembly.
"You must all listen with great attention. The assembly all leaned their ears toward him. After a long pause, the Master said: "Take this clearly to heart" (referring to Juede Li’s succession).
Chan Master Suanan Ren of Ruiying Monastery in Songjiang ascended the hall and spoke. He cited Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty, who, upon seeing a monk reading a scripture, asked:
"What scripture are you reading? The monk replied: "The *Renwang Jing* (Benevolent Kings Sutra). The Emperor said: "Since it is my own scripture, why..."
"It is in your hands. The monk was speechless. Later, Xuedou Xian spoke on his behalf, saying:

"Heaven has no partiality; it aids only virtue. The Master said: "Emperor Taizong asked well, and Xuedou answered well. It may be called a perfect union of sovereign and subject, yet there is no one to bear witness.
I have a verse; it will not do to withhold it from you. 'The words of the King are like a fine thread, then like a thick cord; throughout the ten thousand realms, they spread like the wind.'"

"Grasses and trees flourish in spring. Having recognized the movement of the Emperor’s countenance, he prostrated himself like a tiger; from the furthest frontiers, where is there that does not come to be his guest?
He then looked to his left and right and said, "Regarding this assembly today, do not say there is no one to bear witness. (This was the transmission of Juede.)
One day, Chan Master Tanyin of Jingjue in Hangzhou held up a *kumquat* flower and asked a monk, "What is this?
The monk replied, "A *kumquat* flower. The Master set down the flower, then raised his fist and asked, "What do you call this? The monk replied, "A *kumquat* flower.
The Master said, "The former word was not right; the latter word is right. [He] asked: "Yesterday I caught a wind; today my head [aches]."
"When it hurts, what do you do? The Master struck him once with his staff and said, "Take this dose of medicine from me. The monk hesitated;
the Master struck him again and said, "If it is not yet better, take another dose. (Jude Li succeeded him.)

Chan Master Xie Yunji of Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai was a native of Tongzhou. Initially, he relied upon Master Zang at Sanfeng for three years and two summers, after which he attained a profound realization.
Later, when Master Chu of Lingyan took charge of Xiangfu Temple, the Master entered the hall.

There, he raised the kōan concerning the circumstances of Miaoxi’s request for instruction from Foguo regarding "the phrase that has no phrase," and he attained thorough realization beneath the words. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The gown from Qingzhou is heavy; how could it be merely..."
Seven pounds. Though all phenomena return to the One, the essential point does not lie here. Everyone says, "The old man Zhaozhou did not rely on physical strength.
I say that he was a formidable youth; I send word to all quarters: if you wish to remain unassailed by cold and heat, you must cast yourself into this very midst.
The Master traveled on his own, always wearing robes of discarded rags, begging for food every day.
In the city, he stayed overnight at an ancient temple. Someone asked him about his clan, surname, and place of residence. The Master said, "I have forgotten them.

The man asked, "For what reason did you leave home to become a monk? The Master said, "To relieve my hunger. The man asked, "Do you know how to read characters? The Master said, "I returned to this ancient temple last night.

The man asked, "Are you proficient in Chan? The Master said, "I have come all the way from Yandangshan. Those who heard this could not understand it. In the Wuzi year of the Shunzhi era, he was about to—
When his illness became critical, he successively invited his fellow practitioners to bid them farewell before passing away. He was enshrined in a stupa at Guoqing Temple.
His *Wuweiji* (Collection of Fearlessness) circulates in the world. (Recorded by Tuweng Chusi.)
Chan Master Bianyan Guang of Tiantai Nengren was the son of the Jin family of Gusu.
He received the tonsure at Lingyan and invited Chuyu of Guoqing on Mount Tiantai to open the Dharma at his home mountain. While investigating the "Cane" koan, he attained a realization.

One day, as Chuyu served tea to guests and held up a fruit while tossing it about, the Master applied himself with intense resolve to this case. Later, when he saw Chuyu, the Master took a piece of fruit and threw it.
Dizang asked, "At this very moment, is there still any turning toward or away? The Master instantly cast off all that had long been a thorn in his side. Small Assembly Sermon:
The teaching style of Shaoshi leaves not even a hair’s breadth of room for transgression. To take it up with a single thought is like carrying a mountain on one's back;
it is a state of total detachment, leaving nothing upon which to rely. Wait until the peak of Dongshan touches the ground, and I shall explain it all to you. Ascending the Hall:
At Qingming, the snow ceased; at Grain Rain, the frost ended. The blue sky does not grow old; the white sun is naturally busy. With the east wind, flowers bloom profusely like brocade;
the partridges cry until they die as spring days stretch long. Truly, it is better to return home; for how many years has this wanderer failed to go back to his native land?
In the fourth month of the Wuxu year of the Shunzhi era, he manifested a slight illness. He passed away while sitting in the lotus posture. He was interred in a stupa.
Dongshan (Tuiweng Chusì). Master Zhouchou [Muhé] was a native of Huai’an.
He constantly served at Wanfeng, carrying water to provide for the assembly. Sanfeng Zang marveled at his conduct and appointed him to the administrative offices of the monastery.
When Zang was about to pass away, he bestowed a dharma discourse upon him and instructed him to rely on Master Chusì of Jiqi. This was Liaozǐ.
A matter of great importance. One day, while the Master was felling trees, Shu said, "Throughout the entire day you have been hacking east and west;
what happens when you suddenly knock one down? The Master replied, "It will not burn out even in an entire winter. One day, carrying vegetables past [Shu], the Master passed by.
Shu asked, "What is this? The Master replied, "Two years share the same spring. Shu said, "That belongs to the ancients. The Master said, "It is well-suited for use by people of today. Shu [laughed].
[Chushi] said, "When you were at Wanfeng in your youth, what did you see that caused you to immediately accept and agree? The Master smiled and said, "Leftover gruel and stale rice;
it is not fit to offer to the Master. Chushi said, "Can you even spit it all out? The Master said, "Old and decrepit as I am, I cannot let go of this single point.
Chushi gave him his rain hat. On the seventeenth day of the eighth month of the Wuzi year of the Shunzhi era (1648), he fell ill.
He called his attendants to support him up and join their palms; he called out the name of his own teacher, Master Heshang, three times, and then passed away (Tuiweng Chusuo).
Chan Master Sengyanzong of Yongjia Yantoupingtian was a native of Haining. He paid homage to Dharma Master Pingguan and attained realization while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.
He went to visit Lingyan Chu; as soon as he stepped through the gate, Chu immediately asked: "You have studied the *Śūraṅgama*; just as for instance..."
"Whatever can be returned is naturally not you; that which cannot be returned—since it is not you, who else could it be? As the Master hesitated, Shu struck his bamboo pointer once.
The Master attained a sudden, great enlightenment. He went forth to reside at Xinghua on Mount Tiantai.
Entering the hall, he raised up the case where Baiyun addressed the assembly, saying: "First enter the gate of Baiyun; next enter the waves of Baiyun; swallow the thorny *liji* plum."
He ate rice from the *xiān* variety. "If a gentleman were to arrive, look how convenient it would be. The Master said, "The bearing of Baiyun does not fall short of Yunmen’s;
yet his mouth and heart are at odds. Xinghua is not like this: 'Do not enter Xinghua’s gate; you are accustomed to stirring up windless waves.
When the red-finned fish charges through the surf, a shout raises a staff toward the blue heavens. If a gentleman were to arrive, [he would find] it harmonious."

They were so excessively refined in their greetings and yielding to one another. Yanwen (Xuefeng Yicun) cultivated the martial while refining the literary; this has been esteemed alike by both ancient and modern times.
The Master’s nature was fond of cleanliness; he always carried a tea bowl with him wherever he went. Once, his attendant Zan mistakenly took one or two vessels and had already departed from Xinghua.
After traveling more than two hundred li, the Master saw them and rebuked him, saying: "Do you not know cause and effect? Is this right? He immediately [dismissed him].

He ordered [the calligraphy] to be returned, remarking, "Its meticulousness possesses the refined flavor of the ancients. On the first day of the New Year in the Wuxu year of the Shunzhi era (1658), the Master inscribed the characters "Kuai" (Joy) on his gate;
those who saw it could not fathom its meaning. On the eleventh day of the sixth month, he manifested a slight illness.
At the hour of the Rat (midnight), he requested a brush and wrote this verse: "The staff today sets fire; A great, thunderous sound of the poison drum. The True Person of No Rank is lost."
He spoke extensively on the Emptiness of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Then, casting aside his brush and sitting in the lotus posture, he passed away.
He was interred in a stupa at the rear slope of Pingtian Hermitage (by Chu Sisi, known as Tuweng).
Chan Master Taiyu Tao of Tiantai Guoqing Temple was Zhao Taiyu of Wujiang. In the *guwei* year of the Chongzhen era, he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed as the magistrate of Oning.
Due to his excellence in governance, he was promoted to the Ministry of Personnel (*libu*). During the dynastic transition, he shaved his head and received full ordination from Master Xian of Duncun.
While burning incense, he attained a realization. Master Xian asked, "When Mazu gave a single shout, why did Baizhang suffer from deafness for three days? The Master replied, "A rhinoceros..."

Because he had been playing with the moon-pattern, horns grew on him; because the elephant was startled by thunder, flowers entered its tusks. Xian approved of this. Next, he visited Lingyan Chu and asked, "What is the environment?
Chu said, "The bright moon ascends the high mountain. He asked, "What is the person? Chu said, "It is simply this thief. He asked, "What is the Dharma?
Chu said, "In a land there are laws and statutes—the three thousand offenses. At these words, the Master attained realization.
Dawo addressed the assembly: "A pair of straw sandals, an eight-foot rattan cane—wandering all around the mountain, yet no one is there.
One does not know the night of bamboo rain and pine wind; having finished chanting through the autumn mountains, here is this lamp.

What kind of person’s realm is this? After a long silence, he said: "Those with eyes in the entire hall cannot recognize it. I myself clip the *bājiā* leaves to write what sutra? He addressed the assembly once more. Unfinished.
He clarifies the Seal of the Mind-ground. "Difficult to penetrate is the Barrier of the Patriarchs. Holding up his staff, he said, "This is the Seal of the Mind-ground.
Drawing a line, he said, "This is the Barrier of the Patriarchs. Those who have already passed through it simply turn their arms and walk away;
those who have not yet passed through it, let me borrow the seal for a moment—*he gave a shout*—and said, "Do not resent my frequent offenses just now. Since we parted, I have seen you."
In the Xihui year of the Shunzhi era (1651), while accompanying Chu Du across the Yingjing Lake in Wujiang, a great wind capsized their boat.
The Master fell into the water and passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. He was interred at Dengwu Mountain (by his nephew, Chu Sisi).
Chan Master Ying of Yian at Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai ascended the hall and said: "The path is opened; the Old Śākyamuni has arrived. He said:
'This Dharma-seal of mine is for the sake of benefiting all the world. Wherever you travel, do not propagate it recklessly.
The Master gave a shout and said: "Old Śākyamuni, you are far too cautious! The entire assembly of Guoqing are all original [Buddhas]."
The stream of the dhyāna of form flows on; one encounters a fellow traveler head-on, yet it is merely a matter of passing shoulder-to-shoulder in true reality.
One cannot put sand into the eyes, nor can one pour water into the ears. How could this mountain monk bear to gouge a sore upon healthy flesh or drive a stake into empty space?
To speak of the distance of mountains and the breadth of waters is to bring the ancestral traditions into disarray and to betray them.
"Come here, you eyes! He gave a shout and said, "Step aside for a moment. Ascending the hall, he leaped sideways to the mountain peak.
Who comes after, and who comes first? Shattering that which is before one's eyes, the original path is lush with green grass. He struck his staff once and said:
Losing one's footing and yet finding it—this is being a living immortal. Ascending the hall: One is not; two are not. Vimalakīrti manifesting illness has a thorn in his eye.
Sending words to Mañjuśrī, do not act thoughtlessly. Without cause, one blind man leads a crowd of blind men;
their karmic consciousness is vast and boundless, with no foundation to rely upon. Eighty-four thousand lion seats fill the void, acting as they please.
[The Master] acted out a child’s game. He gave a shout and said, "All of this is merely some idle furniture. Ascending the hall, he said: "All day long, one is lost in a vast blur;
that matter is not hindered. Yet as soon as it is pressed upon, it is hidden away in a sack.

O Great Assembly, is that which is hidden away in the sack that very matter, or is it not that matter? After a long silence, he said, "If you have anything to say, come forward; if you have nothing, [depart]."
Stepping back, he ascended the hall. An ancient said, "The Buddha-dharma is not much. He struck his staff once and asked, "Tell me, how much is it?
The assembly was silent. He then descended from the seat. Ascending the hall again, he struck his staff repeatedly and said:
"Cold Mountain, wild Cold Mountain! Principle and phenomena are beyond partiality or perfection. Opening up a path of fire, one goes straight before the Ancient Sovereign. It may be so.
"Pitying Shi-de, he sweeps again and again, his efforts continuous. Furthermore, the old fellow Feng-gan is so talkative he deceives gods and men.
[He] threw down his staff and said: "I announce to all you Chan practitioners: this Way is not like that at all these days. Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"The crimson summer has just passed and autumn has already arrived; the whistling frost-wind reaches the treetops. Since the seasons are so severe, people grow old easily. Manifesting—
The previous few [lines] have already brought the mind to rest. Hasten your gaze; do not be idle.

If you recognize the stability of your own field, you will be elegant even in moments that are not conventionally elegant. Suddenly he calls to the assembly: "What is your own field? The assembly raises their heads.
The Master once dispersed the assembly. On his birthday, he ascended the hall and said: "Guoqing stands alone among ten thousand mountains; I am ashamed to have no ability to succeed my grandfather.
[The Master] ascends the hall. "The entire earth is the single eye of the patch-robed monk. Guoqing has a vow not to scatter sand.

Is there anyone here who can beat the drum upon their eyelashes and gallop a horse through the crevice of their eyebrows? The assembly remains silent. The Master says, "Where is the eye? He ascends the hall. [He] issues a command:
"Long rains have not ceased; the mud beneath one's feet is deep. If a patch-robed monk stirs, he will get his eyes wet."
"Eyes! The farmer clapped his hands. He cut off the passing traveler. But tell me: within the nostrils, is there even a single point to be gained?
*Cough!* Ascending the hall: The frosty wind is fierce, the frosty wind is fierce. The destitute child has no refuge; where shall he stand?"
I urge you to ask the way and return home early; let the storehouses and granaries be filled to overflowing. Do not lean against the wall, do not rest upon the partition;
you will surely be called a thief by the people of this age. (He struck the whisk. "A pity, a pity! Who can contest the ancestral fields?"
"From this point on, if you do not return, you will find it difficult to attain [enlightenment] upon returning. He ascended the hall and said: "The assembly has endured hardship carrying their bowls;
this mountain monk has nothing with which to look after you. I have pulled up some old, rotten vines and dare say: 'Rice is made from grain. (Tuiweng Chusi)
Chan Master Yuyi Chu of Yungai in Tanzhou was a native of Meizhou in Shu. Initially, he studied under Sanfeng Zang and attained a realization;
subsequently, he visited Lingyan Chu for twenty years of winter and summer. Ascending the hall, he struck his staff and said: "Mount Sumeru is shattered into a hundred fragments;
where, then, can one find a place to settle one's body and establish one's life? After a long silence, he said: "Tsk! This..."
A wild fox spirit! With his staff he whirled a whirlwind to scatter it. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The one path that leads upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages.
Disciples of later generations probe to the left and right. After a long silence, he said: "Do not step on the soles of the Cloud Canopy," and then descended from his seat.
(Retu Weng, Successor)
Chan Master Shu of Tiantai Ruiyan Zhifu, a native of the Qin family of Taizhou, ascended the hall and said: "The cup falls to the ground;
the plate shatters into seven pieces. An empty basket is carried back home. I ask you all: do you see it or not?"
Holding up his staff, he asked, "What is this? He struck it once and said, "This serves merely to open a single thread.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When the World-Honored One held up the flower, Kāśyapa smiled. The pillar and the lantern were in harmony at that very moment.
But tell me, from where did the Eye of the True Dharma and the Wondrous Mind of Nirvāṇa come? [Striking the staff] A point is reached, yet it does not arrive."
Question: "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "The moon is like a drawn bow; little rain, much wind. Question: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said:
"Running downhill, one does not stop; such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter again. Question: "How was it both when he saw him and when he had not yet seen him?
The Master said: "A thousand kinds of grass weep at the dew; the pine is the same in its chanting of the wind. Shunzhi Year Yi (1655).
In the month before the winter solstice, he manifested a slight illness and passed away while reciting a verse (as recorded by Tu’eng Ch’u-si).
Zen Master Xuechang Yuan of Shending in Taizhou was a native of Tongzhou in Yangzhou.

During the formal assembly for the examination of monks, he would frequently pose three questions, saying: "The eyebrows and the eyes have never known each other; who is it that provides witness? Furthermore—
[The guest] said, "My family is poor and encountered bandits; I was unable to abandon everything. What remains? He also said, "A family member has become a malevolent spirit, severing my life-root.
Since the thief is a family member, how can I command him? The respondent hesitated for a moment.
The Master then said, "Please step aside (and let Wengchu Sisi pass)."
Chan Master Nanquan Ru Nanchen of Chizhou was a native of Bazhou. On the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and said:

"At Vulture Peak they spoke of the moon; at Caoxi they pointed to the moon. If you look closely, they are both but a single peg. Old Nanquan alone transcends the mundane world, yet he did no more than enjoy the moon for a time.
New Nanquan, however, would never consent to adding a lamp beneath the moon; he too must respond to this moment."
[The Master] strikes a circular gesture with his whisk and says: "Look! Look! This is the first moon. The second moon wanes and then waxes; it waxes and then wanes.
Watch beneath the moon at the third watch; you must guard against this thief Linji! *Shucks!* [He] ascends the hall. "The tiger at the foot of Mount Daxiong;
the turtle-nosed snake of the South Mountain. Their poisonous breath is equally deep; if you wish to avoid them, there is no place to hide."
"No. He drew a line with his staff and said, "If you had not encountered this mountain monk this morning, you would have been certain that the path to Yangqi was cut off.
Is there anyone who can use poison to counteract poison? Come forth and show me your fangs and bare your teeth!
With his staff, he drove them all out at once. (Tuiweng Chusi)
Chan Master Qingyuan Wei of Lingfeng in Hangzhou was the son of the Hu family of Liangxi. A monk asked, "When the great function manifests, there are no fixed rules.
Why then does a square piece of wood not fit through a round hole? The Master said, "No one knows this meaning; it makes me remember Nanquan.
[The monk] asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods sit within the flames and turn the Great Dharma Wheel. [What of] the flames..."
[The Master] was preaching the Dharma for all the Buddhas. Day after day at the hearth door, what did he preach? The Master said:

"When Hanshan meets Shide, they clap their hands and laugh aloud. [The student] asked: "A Buddha expounds the Great Dharma with a single voice, and sentient beings each attain understanding according to their kind.
Regarding these very words, how do you interpret them? The Master said: "The mechanism of a flashing bolt of lightning—mere toil."
Zhusi asked: "Heaven and earth share the same root as I; the myriad things are one body with me.
Why, then, is some long and some short? The Master said: "Because all that is provided for offerings is entirely the reality. (Retu Weng, Successor)
Chan Master Yanzhi of Qianming in Dingshou was Wang Yi of Piling. In his middle years, he went to Lingyan to receive the tonsure under Master Chu.
Through arduous investigation, he attained enlightenment. He was short in stature but vigorous and resolute, bearing the burden of the Dharma with the spirit of Fenyang.
In the hall, he drew a circle (○) with his whisk and said: "This is the essential body and form of all Buddhas. He then stared at it.
Those who have not yet seen it may look and find a share of it; but for those who have once been within it, strip away the body and bring forth a phrase of the Way.
He gave a shout and said: "You all must be among the disciples in the Dharma of Śākyamuni Buddha, the fourth honored one of the Bhadrakalpa."
And thus one attains Buddhahood. [The Master] ascends the hall, suddenly takes up his staff, and calls out, "Wooden Seat-Holder! The latter responds, "Yes. He calls again, "Wooden Seat-Holder!
and the latter responds once more, "Yes, yes. Then, striking the ground with the staff, he says: "It is like a person writing characters in the dark;
though the characters themselves do not take shape, the traces of the brushstrokes are fully manifest. Green appears as green, yellow appears as yellow; that which is neither green nor..."
Yellow. It is made to be neither blue nor yellow. When the Buddha-dharma reaches this point, one must also have unimpeded eyes to see many hundreds of Buddhas and see many thousands of Buddhas.
Everywhere they shall be the foremost, the most excellent, the supreme, the wondrous, the most subtle, the highest, the unsurpassed, the guide, and the teacher.
This cannot be achieved unless one uses a single hand to cleave through the crown of the head at the ten directions.
Above all, everything must be dismantled. One does not see how Linji and Deshan acted as great donors, providing boundless charity, or engaged in beneficial conduct and cooperation;

yet every action they performed never departed from the knowledge of all modes, the knowledge of all-knowledge. It is like written characters and numerical calculations—all are rooted in the alphabet.
When the alphabet is fully realized, there is not the slightest thing that is separate from the alphabet.
He then took his staff and drew a single stroke, saying: "According to the rule, this is a single signature; it is not a mere scribble.
On the day of the Yuanxuan Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "For three hundred years, the ancient practice has been deep;

the lamps in the Cloud Hall have nearly drifted in and out. Today, I strike up the flame of the pearl grove; the wind unfolds the singular heart of the plum blossoms. He gave a shout and said: "All dharmas are..."
Regarding the essence of the Dharma, it is said that it is "mind-only. Yet, failing to see one's own mind, one gives rise to conceptual discrimination.
When a person washes rice and sets it on the fire, and a practitioner boils congee or steams rice—the flavors differ between the upper reaches of the river and the lower reaches;
yet the management of kitchen affairs is the same throughout the world. How can those who have seen their nature and those who have not be distinguished when they arrive at this point?
He gave a shout and said, "A true Zen guest must not sneer behind one's back.
Ascending the hall, a monk stepped forward and said, "Going straight and coming from the side; light meets darkness. The Master struck him across the spine.

Another monk rushed forward in competition, and the Master struck them all back at once, saying, "You are all just people who eat their evening meal by the side of the stove. He then raised the case of a monk asking Xinghua:
"When they come from the four directions and eight corners, how is it? Xinghua said, "Strike the one in the middle. The monk bowed.
Xinghua said, "Yesterday I went to a village feast; midway, I suddenly encountered a sudden wind and torrential rain, so I took shelter inside an ancient temple.
The Master gave a shout and said, "From the four directions and eight corners, fallen petals fall in waves; as for the one in the middle—"
Water and moon flowing; what a fine season! Why did the Son offer but a single prostration? Even he could not bear it.
Furthermore, in an ancient temple, he recited dharanis. To be apprehensive when facing affairs means one need not act as his son of blazing glory.
"Where is the official warrant for this very body? He gave two consecutive shouts and said, "Thieves have no seed!

He ascended the hall, suddenly took up his staff, struck once, and said, "In a single stroke, the hundred wounds and thousand sores of the patriarchs and Buddhas are scraped open, and they are pulled out by the root.
Do you all still cherish them? One group after another!"
A round belly and square garments; his aura and presence are immense.

Wherever he goes to a person's home, he drags them into a soft, padded cocoon, caressing them by day and rubbing them by night—a god among mortals who cannot easily be questioned. Fortunately, Jiufeng has appeared in the world to give you hands and feet:
take off that greasy cap and strip away that stinking shirt. Try to feel for yourself beneath the fur; search for yourself beneath the skin.

"Look for yourself. Is there even a single point [to be found]? He then struck the desk twice and said, "If you can produce a 'note' (a definitive realization) that rivals the Nine Peaks, you may walk shoulder-to-shoulder with the ancestral masters and venerable elders of the past.
A newly ordained monk requested to ascend the hall. [The Master said: "Deshan reviled the Buddhas and cursed the Patriarchs;
Linji slaughtered the Buddhas and extinguished the Patriarchs. These two fellows claimed they had reached the stage of non-doubt."
"Who cares for the wild weeds and deep villages? It is simply rolling. He suddenly struck the meditation platform with his staff and gave a shout, saying:

"Sentient beings are attached everywhere; I lead them so they may emerge [from delusion]. Ascending the hall, before the mallet had even finished its beat, he struck the meditation platform with his staff and said:
"If it were delayed by even a single moment, those with heads like tortoises and heads like turtles would all have deceived you all long ago. Those of inferior capacity and weak intelligence—"
He dropped his breath upon it; a single point of breath fell down. He withdrew with a suppressed sigh and did not bother to contest it.
If one is a true man, who does not possess a deed of ancestral property? Why not spread it out before people instead of hiding it behind one's back, tucked away inside a bowl-bag?
When the spoon is ready to scoop the rice and the chopsticks are ready to pick up the vegetables, this is the universal standard throughout all quarters.
"Please understand this. At the time of the morning and evening meals, one fears being unable to manage them; every mouthful is chewing empty space—can you swallow it all?
Then he struck the table once and said: 'One must not falsely accuse others. (Retu Weng Chusi)
Chan Master Guyi Zhi-xuan of Xilin on Mount Lu was the son of the Wu family from Wujin. He left home to become a monk at the age of twelve and attended upon Master Sanfeng Zang.
Whenever he asked, "Have I attained Chan? Zang would strike him. This happened every time he asked for three years.
One day during a heavy snowfall, Zang rose early in the morning and called him to present a verse. The Master set forth his realization, whereupon Zang ordered him to close [the door].
He applied himself to the investigation of the matter, inscribing the title "Carving Jade" upon his meditation barrier to encourage his own success. At that time, the Master was nineteen years old.
When Master Zang passed away, the Master received orders to attend Master Chu at Lingyan; however, because Chu presided over Tianning Temple, the Master remained at Lingyan.

On the day of the Mid-Autumn Festival, ancestral portraits were hung and offerings were prepared. As the Master entered with the assembly, he suddenly attained great enlightenment as he stepped across the threshold. He was about to—
That which had long been a thorn in my breast was instantly dissolved as ice. I immediately went to Tianning Temple and presented the source of my realization.
Master Chu gave his seal of approval by ascending the hall and, letting out a shout, said: "This is still spoken for those of middling or inferior capacity.

If there is one of superior capacity and sharp intelligence, come forth and display a different standard of conduct! Though you possess the full functioning of your faculties, I shall still strike you with a drum of retreat. If you are one who leans toward...
"A sword avoids an arrow; it is merely intended to preserve one's body and stay far from harm. For now, let this talk spread widely.

In the *dingyou* year of the Shunzhi era, as the Master was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and spoke. He cited the story of Mazu, who one day was unwell. The head of the monastery asked, "How is the Master’s health?
Mazu replied, "The Buddha of the Sun’s Face, the Buddha of the Moon’s Face. The Master said, "When the Great Master reached such a moment, he did not fail his calling."
He was a true disciple who entered the inner chamber of Nanyue, yet it is a pity that he could not fully integrate [the teaching]; he still leaves his head and tail exposed.
Although he indeed outshines those before him and surpasses those after him, how can he avoid making his descendants look here and there in the void?
If Xilin had been willing to leave you a shadow, even today, should someone ask about the Master’s honor—
[The Master] asked, "How is it? He replied, "Just tell him: 'Look after five days. Zhuo leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.
Five days later, the Master indeed passed away. His stupa was enshrined at Xilin. Wen Deyi of the Ministry of Rites composed the inscription for it (by Tuoweng Chusi).
Chan Master Tan Ying Gao of Tiantai Guoqing Temple was the son of the Sun family of Pilin. He ascended the hall and said: "In my bag there is no silk to bind even an ant;

beneath the Shiliang Bridge, jade beads are strung together like pearls. In the kitchen there is not enough rice-gruel to attract a fly; before the summit of Mount Huading, [the scene is vast and empty]."
Shoulders brushing, hubs clashing—staying in the mountain retreats, every word is a word, every step is a step;
all proceed along this very path. Cutting off the head of the direct route, what place is there to evade?

Suddenly, as if heaven and earth were spinning and the great earth became pitch-black lacquer, no one is permitted to cut ahead, nor can anyone fall behind. Even if it were the Venerable Pārśva himself, his emotions and intellect would wither away.
"Exhausted! Elder brother and younger brothers, you have come here treading upon my footsteps; how can you possibly grasp his very essence? He lets out a shout and says:
'If you are a member of this family, I shall speak with you of family matters. As for you lot—standing in the front hall, behind the front eaves, or at the back—is there anything more to deliberate?
He leans on his staff and descends from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "If a person were to live for a hundred years..."
A year passes without grasping the pivot of the Buddhas; it would be better to live for but a single day and attain full understanding.

When a dog runs, it shakes its head; when a monkey worries, it scratches its head. The stars, river, and moon form halos as fish give birth; under the slight breeze of the oak leaves, the deer nourish their new antlers.
He struck the whisk and said, "Enter! He ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One has a secret word; Kāśyapa no longer conceals it.

The talkative old Fenggan has nowhere to hide his shame. Be alert! Be awake! Having spoken, he descended from the seat. He ascended the hall and said: "The flames of the brazier flare up; the ice-moon melts away.
It permeates the three thousand worlds and penetrates metal and leather armor; the calamity reaches all sentient beings. Walking bare-boned through Lu."
Bānkō himself laid out the lines and ink-marks; his body hidden, his shadow exposed—this is a murky muddle. Ancient or modern, who can discern the difference?
Have you not seen how Fǎchāng was utterly solitary on that day? Only those eighteen eminent men stood there with a chilling, majestic presence.
This reveals the very backbone of the teaching: it reduces the "Wall-Gazing" of Mount Song to the ashes of an eon, and extinguishes the "Solely Honored One" of the Imperial House.
That it does not hide even a mosquito or gnat—its fierce flames are truly praiseworthy; that it swallows a tiger whole—it relies entirely upon a mere cricket.
Good brothers, do not compete with fire against fire; do not recklessly cast flame after flame. Together, let us turn toward...
Smokeless fire; a tortoise leaping forth becomes a soft-shelled turtle of its own accord. Entering the hall: A parrot can speak, yet it does not depart from the world of birds;
a gibbon can speak, yet it does not depart from the world of beasts. The old monks of the world do not depart from the staff of Guoqing.
But tell me, what excellence does the staff of Guoqing possess? After a long silence, he raised his voice and said: "From..."

The teaching stands beside the ancient screen; wait to take up the vermilion and green to enter the painted scroll. Entering the Hall: Partiality and perfection, the half and the full—when the mouth opens, it is not upon the tongue.
Form and emptiness, light and darkness—when you lift your eyes, they fall back into the seal-pattern.
At Vulture Peak they spoke of the moon; at Caoxi they pointed to the moon. To grasp the snake’s head is to lose the tortoise’s nose. The Persian from the South Sea—self and other.
It has not been forgotten. Having plucked the coral, every cry is one of grievance. Nevertheless, a carriage should not be pushed sideways; yet, in principle, there must be no unjust judgment.
It is just like those on the south and north sides of the mountain, following their ranks and forming groups.

When Master Li falls drunk before the steps, it is simply because Master Zhang has been drinking wine. But tell me, what samādhi does he possess to be so utterly reckless and unruly? Thereupon, [he] used—
With his whisk, he drew a circle and said: "If it were beneath a covered basin, how could one blame the heavens? Ascending the hall, he was asked: "When you step out the door, it is but grass;
under the hooves of the water buffalo there is no partiality. When ten thousand miles are cloudless, the iron-hearted man honors his whole being with reverence.
Where, then, lies the karmic affinity for your travels? The Master said: "It is easy to distinguish dragons from snakes, but difficult to deceive a patch-robed monk."
The monk said, “The wind and moon on the tip of the staff; the universe within the alms bowl—who lacks these?
The Master said, “Beneath your own feet, do not let this slip away. The monk stamped his foot once and said, “Who knows this meaning? It makes me remember Nanquan. The Master said, “...”
The onlookers laughed and said: "The ten directions have no walls; where are the eyes?
All four sides are bare with no gates; how perilous it is beneath one's heels! Son of the Buddha, the Dharma is not within, not without, and not in between.
Tell me, where does it go? An earthworm suddenly crosses the Eastern Sea—its prior journey has not yet reached its end."
The frog flies up to Lake Dongting; in the end, he goes too far.

Even if one were to have a lantern climb the wall to Mount Tiantai, having been pressed against the face-gate for a lifetime, one would still be leaning on a fence and groping along a wall. If it is not like this at all, then walk until you reach the place where the water ends.
"Sitting and watching the clouds arise; the straw sandals on one's feet cost thirty coins for a single song. Do not misunderstand this! (Retu Weng Chusi).
Chan Master Wanlu Zhang of Nanxiang Wanshou Monastery ascended the hall. A monk asked: "The diamond [mountain] forms its beard, and white silver forms its..."
Before the monk had finished speaking, the Master struck him. Again, a monk asked: "The staff that turns back the surging waves when they have already collapsed, and kills or gives life;
it reveals the sun and moon in the midst of heaven—the very fangs and claws of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Before he had finished speaking, the Master struck him again.
Another monk asked: "Deshan’s staff beats the drum of Heyoshan; Yunmen’s feet roll the snowball of Xuefeng. Before he had finished speaking, the Master likewise struck him. Again—
A monk asked, "What fault was there in those venerable elders just now? The Master struck him with his staff as he spoke.

As the monk prepared to offer a reply, the Master struck him back with another blow and said, "To employ convoluted phrases and sharp verbal displays not only buries the ancestral Dharma, but also laughs the nostrils of the patch-robed monks to pieces.
A person of keen intelligence would have seized it before a single word was uttered."
As soon as he rose, he went off. He was already not clever enough;
how much less so when coming forward in groups of three or two, stepping up to try to find leftover spittle in this mountain monk’s mouth? What business does that accomplish on your own part?
Striking the ground once with his staff, he said: "This Dharma cannot be shown; words and signs are quiescent. Striking again, he said:
"By the power of skillful means, he preached for the five bhikṣus. Let the great assembly say: what did he preach? [The Master] struck the meditation seat once and said:
'Today there is a vegetarian feast at Beibei Temple. [Another time,] he ascended the hall and said: "For those who are non-active and without affairs, having a mouth is fit only for eating rice.
Simply do not strive to analyze or explain; one lifetime’s work is already accomplished. He looked to his left and right and said: "Great!"

The task having already been accomplished, why does one still lack that final blow to the back of the head? It is simply because one is bound by a firm golden lock that one falls into a deep pit from which liberation is difficult.
O worthy ones, from this day forward, if you exert yourselves daily with profuse perspiration, all illnesses will naturally vanish;
you will win a load of pure wind and be fit to roam with elegance wherever you go, like a swan protecting itself from the snow. Old... [text fragment]

[This] example merely increases [the burden]. It is like being imprisoned and bound in a jail. If the regulations set forth can be reformed, well and good; if not, then listen as this mountain monk establishes his teaching.
Ascending the hall, a monk rose to prostrate and prepared to ask a question. The Master said, "Stop! Stop! During this summer retreat, you brothers have spoken here and there;
do you still have these two pieces of skin left? The monk replied, "There is a phrase that is not the fundamental principle; where there is no speech, it is cut off."
The Master said, "Why is it that your heels still do not touch the ground? The monk replied, "At first I followed the fragrant grasses away;
now I am returning, chasing the falling flowers. The Master said, "You are still just a fellow of the weeds. Another monk came forward.
The Master said, "Let everything go until it becomes withered and dull. The monk replied, "I do nothing at all. The Master said, "In every place, there is radiant brilliance."

[The monk] replied, "It has rotted away. The Master said, "How would you dare to keep it in a bag or cover it over? The monk said, "By what cause did it reach such a state? The Master said, "It is your own fault.

The Master continued, "Last night at the third watch, the moon shone through the window. Then another monk came forward. The Master said, "I wish to discuss this with you: both of you have made mistakes.
You must not say hereafter that when you were traveling on pilgrimage in the South, you had already made a mistake. At that moment—
"How is it with the matter at hand now? The monk said, "When walking, one reaches the end of the water; when sitting, one watches the clouds arise.
The Master said, "You may be said not to have spent this summer in vain. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Thirty years hence, do not misrepresent this to others when you meet someone.
Another monk had just stepped out when the Master gave a shout. The Master also shouted. The monk shouted again. The Master said, "I do not value your practice."
"It is simply that you must keep your eyes straight. Now tell me: how many people today have fallen from their positions in the Heaven of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception?
He replied, "I did not come from the realms of humans or devas. The Master said, "Are you not then the one who attained awakening in a single night?
He replied, "I did not go as a wandering monk. The Master said, "In the end, what is it? He replied, "How much wind can the Dragon King endure? The Master struck him with a staff.

He said, "There is no harm in placing a nose beneath the eyes. Another monk came forward, and the Master said, "You must go to a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single blade of grass.
The monk looked up and down, then spread both hands and said, "Look! Look! The Master said, "Why did you not say so sooner?
The monk replied, "To speak it would still be like a lotus flower in the month of December. The Master looked to his left and right and said, "Cook fragrant rice in a separate steamer."
The monk made an offering to the Master. As the monk stepped out, the Master did not look back and said, "It is evident. The Master then gave a shout. The monk also did not look back.
The Master said, "It is evident. The monk also shouted. The Master said, "Do you think you have matched me? The monk pushed over the meditation seat. The Master said:
"Perilous! He then let out a shout, saying: "A thunderclap crashes within empty space!
I open up a living path to release the lives of you all and allow the breath of you all to pass through. Now is precisely the time to stride forth with wide steps;
east, west, south, and north—there is nowhere that is not your own homeland. You must not remain confined here. He then took up his staff.
At one time, [he] was driven down (the succession of Tu’engwǒng fell).
Chan Master Sēngjiànqīng of Sānfēng Qīngliáng was the son of Zhū of Wújiāng. His faculties were sharp and keen;

he could not forget any of the Confucian or Buddhist classics after reading them once. At the age of nineteen, he received full ordination at Língyán. Together with Yìngfāngyuǎn, he participated in a seven-day retreat (*qī*). Yuǎn—

He attained great enlightenment immediately. The Master applied himself with indignant vigor to his studies; before long, while at Tiantong Monastery in Taizhou, he thoroughly realized the nature of mind.

Tuweng Chu appointed him as the Secretary (Jishi), and shortly thereafter commanded him to preside over the ordination platform and wield the whisk. After his formal entry into the monastic world, he successively presided over major monasteries, and his reputation for the Way spread far and wide.
The present Emperor, while on his eastern tour, summoned the Master by special decree for an audience. He bestowed upon him an imperial composition, and the honors and gifts were most generous.

The Master carved this inscription at Lètán Temple on Mount Huá in Sūzhōu, so that it might endure imperishably. [He] ascended the hall. Once seated, he looked to his left and right and said: "Does the assembly understand?
Since the beginning of time, no one has raised the fundamental principles of our school. Even if one were to guide others skillfully according to their capacities, the essence of the school..."

When paths diverge into different directions, one must respond to the world with compassion. When subtle sounds are stalled by competitive debate, discussing the Ultimate and expounding the Wondrous merely results in a dragon painted on a wall.

Analyzing effects and dividing causes—how could this be the elephant that crosses the river? One does not realize that a single word can uproot and elevate, such that every phenomenon completely transcends;
a single phrase encompasses all, such that mind after mind naturally accords. What difference, then, is there between the sages of the past and those of the future?

Regarding the distinction between "total presentation" and "partial presentation": when the forest peaks exude their splendor, one gazes upon them as if they were standing like walls before one’s breast;

when the mountain streams flow through the ravines, those who drink find their innermost organs refreshed with cool clarity. Thus, the gathering of eminent monks from the Five Lakes brings overflowing celebration to the Master’s gate, and the continuation of the true lamp for a thousand years causes the Patriarchal seat to shine brilliantly.
Yet, how can one express that single phrase which does not enter the realm of transformation, but returns directly to the Precious Abode?
The Way. It is already known that there is no second moon in heaven; one may trust that there is but a single monk in the human world.
Small Assembly. Looking left and right, he said: "May I ask about a certain matter? When Bodhidharma crossed the Longqing River in years past, what kind of wind was it on that day?
One must not simply say that it has been forgotten because the years have long passed. Wisdom enters the three periods of time."
There is no coming or going; look clearly at this response. After a long silence, he spoke on behalf of himself: "Half southeast, half northwest. In a small assembly, he asked:
"Venerable one, how long has it been since you set out on your pilgrimage? You have not yet reached the point.

While it is not surprising that you do not grasp the ancestral lineage of discourse, why is it that your own tongue does not know where to land? If you would believe these two pieces of skin before people..."
Opening and closing [the mouth] is extremely difficult. Why not simply keep it shut to eat your rice? In the future, you will avoid having to cry out in grievance and suffering.
Evening Sermon: The single word "knowing" is the gate to all wonders. Do not engage in false imaginings. The single word "knowing."
The gateway to all calamities: let it go! This mountain monk cannot yet spread flowers like patterned brocade from Shu; how could he dare to let snow press down upon the frost of Wu?
He shall cause those of wealth and honor to wash away their precious curiosities, and those in poverty to overturn their narrow-minded isolation.

It is like a skilled physician’s medicine being drawn from the bag of an ordinary practitioner—efficacious enough to cure disease. It is also like an old general leading his troops... [from] the bag of a common soldier.

He was pulled out from the camp of the defeated general; his spirit could have swallowed the barbarians. Thus the Patriarch said: "If you grasp it with a loss of measure, you will surely enter a deviant path;
if you let it be natural, the essence has neither going nor staying. Today, this mountain monk shall once again provide a commentary on these words.
The single word "knowing" involves the dust of the mundane world; to speak further of "non-knowing" merely leaves people sitting in exhaustion.
Those who are not good are the sons of thieves; those who are good at coming as thieves are the true good people. Small-scale Sermon. Question:

Without falling into the eighteen questions of Fenyang, please bring forth the "arrow-point" pivot. Master: "Directly penetrating to the kingdom of Silla. Question: "The guest and host are already clear within the phrase."
The student asked, "What about turning the body around and shooting again? The Master said, "First, do not try to discern it upon the bowstring.
He then said, "In Chan there is nothing to transmit; in the Way there is nothing to speak of. One eats three meals a day and sleeps one stretch at night; how can this be treated as ordinary?
How could one be permitted to seek some other 'primordial subtlety'? If you can truly sever the dualistic mechanisms, the Way will naturally burst forth."
[The Master] opened his heavenly aperture and looked left and right, saying: "If you can step upon it, only then will you know the mountain monk’s foul mouth.
Evening Sermon: Deshan would strike as soon as one entered the gate; a kind intention turned instead into deception. Linji would shout as soon as one entered the gate;
clearly, he was playing with cleverness only to end up clumsy. If you wish to attain immediate resonance, today I shall speak directly: set aside the staff.
Setting aside the shout: as soon as one engages in thought, it becomes further removed from the essential matter. To be able to die and surely live again—who has no fresh blood beneath their skin?
