[The Master] makes a gesture with his whisk as if pouring water and says: "Everyone says that water can wash away dust and grime, but water and grime have always been the gate of non-duality" (Vangxue Zuìsì).

Chan Master Mingqing of East Mountain in Ya’an was the son of the Tang family of Jintang. He studied under Zhaojue for over thirty years until he received the transmission of the Dharma. Later, he resided at East Mountain.

On the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall and spoke, citing the case of Guishan while he was attending Baizhang. As Guishan stood in attendance, Baizhang asked, “Who is there? Guishan replied, “It is I. Baizhang said, “Is there fire in the brazier? Guishan reached into it and found some embers. Baizhang said, “Bring me some fire. Guishan shook the brazier several times but could find no fire. Baizhang then struck him with his staff and said, “The fire is right here before you; why do you look elsewhere? Guishan was suddenly enlightened.

The Master said, “Guishan’s failure to find fire was because he sought it outside himself. If one can see that the fire is right here before oneself, then even if one were to strike the brazier a thousand times, fire would not appear. But if one does not seek it elsewhere, then even without striking, fire will naturally appear. Today, on this Lantern Festival, I shall strike the brazier once for you all—look! He then struck the brazier once and descended from the seat.

Miaoyan brushed it away and said, "There is no fire. Baizhang rose personally and probed deeply until he found some fire; picking it up, he showed it to him and said, "You say there is none, yet here it is!
Because of this, Miaoyan attained awakening. The following day, he went with Baizhang into the mountains to perform manual labor.
Baizhang asked, "Have you brought the fire? Miaoyan replied, "I have. Baizhang asked, "Where is it? Miaoyan picked up a piece of wood.
He blew twice. He passed it to Cháng (丈). Cháng said, "Like a worm resisting [its fate]. I saw the Buddha Dīpaṃkara;
his original radiance and auspicious signs were like this. (Chángxuě Zuìsì).
Chan Master Zhongyan Zhujing Song of Meizhou was the son of the Wang family of Neijiang. Having received formal certification from Zhaojue, he resided at Zhongyan in Meizhou.
On his birthday, he ascended the hall and said: "Throughout the years beyond the mundane world, when have I ever wandered? It is truly remarkable that today marks fifty autumns.
Though I hold a staff as clumsy as a straw rope, the Three Essentials and the Three Principles are gathered all at once. He then struck the ground with his staff.
He said: "Exert yourself once more until you see it directly. At that very moment, when water and mud are blended together, you will recognize the matter beneath your own feet.
Then the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas shall be your peers. Let us set aside the Buddhas for a moment: what is this matter beneath one's feet?
Again, Zuo leaned on his staff and shouted, saying: "You do not even recognize the head of the discourse! Small Assembly (Xiaocan):
The original, single diamond body— When perfected here, one is an awakened immortal. Today, Zhongyan points it out once more:
"The sun and moon in the sky are equal in age. (Zhangxue Zu succeeded him.)
Chan Master Yanguan Jingbuer Gui was the son of the Gao family of Fengxiang. At the age of twenty, he shaved his head and traveled extensively throughout the various regions.
Upon entering Sichuan, he visited Zhaojue; while drawing water, he saw his reflection, let out a shout, and realized, "It has always been right here."

After succeeding to the Dharma, he arrived at Yanjing’s Yanjing Temple. On the eve of the New Year, he ascended the hall and said: "Like a drifting cloud, solitary and vast, I draw near the Polar Star.
By special providence, tonight I encounter the year's end. The private affairs of these patch-robed monks are extraordinary; The biting frost wind fans the Imperial Capital.
Without relying on divine artifice, the exorcists are driven away; The red banner is hoisted high as the laws are first proclaimed. Neither old nor new, there is nothing [to grasp]."
Serving the Han [Dynasty], he relied solely upon his staff as a peach-spirit talisman (taofu). Holding the staff in the gesture of inserting a name tablet, he said:
"Swiftly and urgently, as per the imperial decree! He then descended from the seat. (Zuisi of Zhangxue).
Chan Master Songzhai of Yibin in Western Shu was the son of the Song family of Yibin. His secular name was Yizhang. In his youth, he studied Confucian classics.

In the year of Dingyou, after three unsuccessful attempts to reach the capital as a *xiaolian* (examination graduate), he sighed to himself, "Fame and office are illusory," and immediately went to Zhaojue Temple to shave his head and don the robes of a monk.
Wearing but a single robe through both winter and summer, he remained steadfastly content with himself. He investigated the profound mysteries of the ultimate truth. All...
In this encounter of question and answer, their spiritual arrows met point-blank; one must act with courage and not yield. One day, [Wuzu] asked:

"If all sentient beings in the great earth are already perfectly awakened, why is there delusion and why is there awakening? Wuzu said: "Uniformly beyond contrivance, yet even when face-to-face, they still do not realize it.
The Master asked: "When the sentiments of sage and ordinary are exhausted, what is the matter? Wuzu folded his hands and said: "Have you truly reached such a state?"
"Have you reached this state yet? At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and was subsequently certified by him (the lineage of Chuzi of Zhangxue).

Chan Master Qibaifu of Yuyuan in Meizhou was the son of the Gong family of Meizhou. Having shaved his head and donned the robes at a young age, he went to Zhaojue, where he attained thorough penetration under the master’s hammering and forged training.
He then succeeded him. One day, he ascended the hall and said: "Face-to-face, I open wide the gate of non-duality; both sages and ordinary beings..."
Sentiments are exhausted, severing ties with both kin and strangers. Hooked characters and thorny phrases stir up wind and rain; they block the valleys and fill the ditches—nothing but rotten vines.
Suppose one were to bow high to Śākyamuni and not prostrate before Maitreya: what kind of person is this? After a long silence, he said: "The ninety-day restriction of the feet."
This morning I have finally peeled away the seeds of the coiled peach that grant immortality (by Zhuangxue Zu).
Master Xishengyong of Yueluo Mountain was the son of the Chen family of Anping, Guizhou. In his youth, he studied Confucian classics; his intelligence and insight surpassed those of others.

When the Master sought to leave the household life, his parents would not permit it. He therefore built a hermitage beside their residence, abstained from meat and wine, and grew weary of worldly affairs.

While serving his duties, he encountered the Buddha-Eye (Foyan) while being shown the koan "The myriad dharmas return to the One. Later, while traveling with his father on official business to Zunyi, he visited Taodong Cave and called upon Master Zhangxue Zui.
Their words and expressions were in accord; Zui marveled at him, saying, "This son is a fierce and formidable lion cub. He went to visit Master Minshu Xiang.
As Xiang was about to open his mouth to speak, the Master stepped forward and covered Xiang’s mouth with his hand. The Master then covered his own ears and departed.

The Master said, "A truly sharp instrument. After his parents had passed away, the Master left home and entered the mountains. He then remarked, "The various patriarchs of the past each possessed their own hand-eye;

some used a seal, others a bell, some a staff, and others a whisk. The Master took a piece of wood about five inches long, fashioned it with a rounded head and pointed base, and named it *Deleru* (Joy-Attainment).
He composed a song for the *Deleru* and would daily practice its chanting while wielding the whip. When a monk arrived, the Master—

Brandishing his whip, he cried, "Strike! Strike! For several years like this, no one could understand him. Carrying his staff, he traveled as a cloud-wanderer, traversing famous mountains and great rivers.
He encountered many masters and thoroughly investigated the ultimate source; he would not submit to being beneath others. Eventually, he arrived at Zhaojue.
Chongjian met Zui. Zui said, “It has been a long time since we last met. How are your daily activities? The Master said, “I play music.
Zui said, “Bring me that music. The Master held up his fist. Zui said, “Set that aside. The Master made the gesture of cracking a whip.
Zuì called out repeatedly, "I have attained joy! I have attained joy! At this, the Master attained great enlightenment and subsequently transmitted the Dharma to him (Zhàixuè Zuì was his successor).

Chèyán of Lùmén was a layman named Páng from Jiānīng. While serving as the governor of Yǐzhōu, amidst his efforts to relieve the famine, he would collect his thoughts regarding all conditions and frequently sought out wise masters and patriarchs.
Having heard that Zhàojié Zuì’s teaching style was solitary and rigorous, he went to visit him.
He then entered the mountains to pay his respects and inquire about the essentials of the Dharma. Under a pine tree, they reached a point of mutual understanding.
One day, he went up to Zhaojue and asked, "Han Yu’s visit to Dadian was still but the second encounter; what is the first encounter? Chui said, "Those of the highest capacity do not require a needle.
The scholar said, "Since our capacities and thoughts are of one kind, why did you drive the head seat away? Chui—

The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, do not understand how to engage in such verbal entanglements. The scholar said, "These are words of ultimate truth; I request the Master to verify them for me.
The Master said, "This is precisely where you must let go of body and life. The scholar was thereby relieved of his doubts. The Master then bestowed upon him a Guanyin cap and spoke a verse:
The Avalokiteśvara hat is as large as a leaning parasol; it covers the earth’s quarters and permeates the three realms. Thus has the Dharma lineage been transmitted for a thousand ages.
Before the assembly of humans and devas, [Zhaozhou] freely plays with it (Vangxue Zu was his successor).

The Military Commissioner Kunyu, Layman Zhang, whose name was De-di, was a native of Jingzhao. Having governed Sichuan for many years, he had long been inclined toward the Daoist scriptures and was increasingly devoted to them.
Once, while reading the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, he reached the passage: "Whatever has marks is entirely empty and false."

His mind and spirit were suddenly enlightened. At that time, Master Zuixue was intoxicated with the Dharma in the region south of the Han River; he had long admired Zuixue’s reputation for the Way but regretted never having met him.
During the Renyin year of the Kangxi era, Zuixue took up his staff and returned to Shu, lodging at Taiping in Jinguangcheng (Chengdu).

The local scholar-officials went first to pay their respects and inquire about the Way, finally fulfilling their long-held aspiration. They immediately requested that he establish the Zhaojue Monastery to propagate the essential tenets of the school. One day, he entered [the hall] together with Gai.

Shan asked, "I have come to the mountains specifically to seek instruction; I pray that you, Master, will not withhold the Way from me. Guizhou said, "It is fortunate that you, Minister, bring this up again.
As for the matter of one's own self, even to point it out is difficult. The Scholar asked, "Among the venerable masters of old, were there any laypeople who received the transmission of the lamp?
Guizhou said, "Who would not have a share? The Scholar said, "In that case, do I, your disciple, have a share? Guizhou replied, "Yes."
Suddenly picking up his whisk, he pointed it out and said, "Do you understand? The scholar made a gesture as if seizing it. Chui said, "Take this clearly to heart" (Chui was a successor of Zhangxue).
The lay practitioner Hu Shanyuan of Huan’an was a native of Tushan in Yue province.

Having formerly served as a judicial official in Sichuan, one day while accompanying the provincial governor and various officials to visit Chui at Zhaojue Temple, he set out a table of fruit offerings. The scholar said, "I request that the Master provide a single word; only then will I dare [to accept]."

While drinking tea, Xuanji said, "The weather is cool today; let us not trouble ourselves with further annotations. The scholar said, "Please offer another turn of phrase. Xuanji laid down his chopsticks.
One day, as the scholar was playing the zither, Xuanji said, "You, Layman, can only play that which has strings. Please perform a piece for the stringless one.
The scholar said, "I request a tune for the stringless. Xuanji snapped his fingers. The scholar said, "That still belongs to the realm of 'having'."
Zui said, "If you have doubts, seek instruction elsewhere. He then saw the *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas* and asked, "The names are here;
I do not know where the Dharmakāya resides. Zui called out, "Master Hu! The scholar responded, "Yes? Zui asked, "Do you understand? After the scholar had prostrated himself, Zui spoke again.
They returned to their positions and stood there. Drunkenly, he raised the "Three Sages" koan regarding the offense of "not being tolerated" to test them.
The scholar immediately recited a verse: "The monkeys have been slaughtered; there is no need to search. A thousand-layered iron wall—why labor one's heart over it?

Bringing disaster and inviting calamity is still his own doing. Why must one ask about that monk in the quarters? Drunkenly, he again raised the koan of the "Patriarch’s Mind-Seal" to further examine him.
Shi Lian composed two verses, saying: "Spring arrives and the plum blossoms naturally emit their fragrance; In the river city, the iron flute blows through the waning year.
Seeking plum blossoms amidst the snow, the plum knows nothing of it; Where can the spring light be captured in a painting? He further said: "The great earth is a treasury of radiance;
The wind-swept sails bring laughter unto men. My Master had not a single word; With hands cast loose, he passed through the river city. Thereupon, they were like a needle meeting its eye.

[He] offered [himself as a disciple]; Zhao Liangbi, a lay practitioner (upāsaka) serving as the Judicial Commissioner of Sichuan, heard of the solitary and lofty reputation of Master Zui of Zhaojue Temple upon entering the province and desired to pay his respects.
When he took up his post, Master Zui was staying at Wuzhong Mountain to escape the summer heat, so the layman dispatched a messenger.

Wearing his monastic cap and silk robes, he presented a petition to express his innermost thoughts. At the conclusion, he wrote: "I offer one helmet and one suit of armor; please return quickly to gather the remaining troops.
After reading the letter while intoxicated, he returned to the monastery and prepared a vegetarian feast. When Zui arrived, he saw him at once and brandished his staff as if wielding a spear.
The officer made a gesture of fear. Zui said, "A surrendered general is not executed. The officer replied, "I have long admired..."
"The Master possesses such a capacity; today I have seen it directly. Chui said, "I cannot let this pass either. The scholar leaped for joy and performed a prostration.
Beyond his official duties, he constantly knocked at the gates of Chan meditation. One day he visited Zhaojue and, under Chui’s words, turned over completely.
He was thus certified [as a successor] by Zhangxue Zu (the successor of Zhuzi).
Regarding the layman Nan Zhu Ding Chao: his lineage originates from Jiyang; his ancestors were originally from Haoliang.
He was the son of the Ding family, and because his grandfather traveled for official service, they eventually settled in Shiqiao, the capital market of Yanjing. He was born there...
There was a character inscribed on his hand that read "Kai" (Open). The occipital bone at the back of his head protruded like a crescent moon facing upward.
When he was in his swaddling clothes, if he wept or cried, his nurse would point toward the image of Gautama she had enshrined, and he would immediately stop.

By the time he reached the age of five, when playing with other children, he would sit in the full lotus posture with palms joined and chant the names of the Buddha in a murmuring voice, commanding the children to line up and prostrate before him.
A man wearing a yellow cap passed by his door, saw him, and said in astonishment, "You have come from Mount Song, yet you dwell here?

When you were barely past your teens, you were among the students, pursuing the studies for the civil service examinations. You lived in simplicity and had few friends, finding no harmony with worldly customs.

In your leisure time, you extensively studied the Buddhist scriptures and thoroughly investigated the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*). As you grew older and entered the official registers, you further delved into the essential doctrines of *dharmatā* and *dharma-lakṣaṇa*."

He did not inquire after his family’s affairs or their childbirths. Wherever he went, he would always consult and question his spiritual mentors, offering his wholehearted sincerity to seek instruction.

In his daily life, he occupied himself solely with sweeping his single room; seated upon a rush mat and clad in coarse cotton robes, he sat upright facing the wall, his ribs not even touching the cushion, regardless of cold or heat.

He appeared entirely like an old Chan monk. Previously, he had been contemplating the "Pine Tree in Front of Zhaozhou" koan for seven days and nights, neglecting both sleep and food, yet remaining utterly without attainment;
he even regretted that he did not wish to die. One day, while walking by the edge of a pond, he leaned against the railing and stood for a moment.
Suddenly, a fish leaped with a sharp *pala-la* sound, and he realized that the obstruction which had long weighed upon his chest had dissolved.
The ice then melted away. He composed a verse, saying: "The pond water glistens, clear to its very bottom; Leaning on the railing, I stand alone and watch the fish swim.
Suddenly, with a splash, they break through the surface; This startles me, though I am without intention.
When Master Ding of Pingyan saw this, he laughed and said, "In the future, you shall no longer be deceived by others. Later, he went to Yizhou to pay his respects to Zhaojue Zhangxue Zui.

Intoxicated asked, "Where have you come from? The scholar replied, "From the capital. Intoxicated said, "The road to Shu is more difficult than ascending the blue heavens; how did you manage to reach here?
The scholar replied, "I am well-acquainted with the hoofprints of donkeys by the roadside. Intoxicated said, "Do you recognize this old monk?
The scholar replied, "Before even entering the Jianmen Pass, I have already met the Master. Intoxicated said, "That..."
The Master said, "What you have learned is merely empty verbiage. Yunju said, "To swallow up all the waters of the West River in a single gulp—what difficulty is there in that?
Yunju said, "I do not believe you. The Master said, "What *bi-die-zui* (a type of pastry) is there? Quickly bring it here! Yunju said, "I grant you thirty blows.
The Master said, "Thank you for your offering, Venerable Sir. Yunju deeply approved of this. One day, while serving tea, Yunju...
Huangbo took a single yellow tangerine, split it open with his hand, and passed it to the scholar, saying, "What kind of flavor is this?
The scholar replied, "I am old and decrepit; I do not even know what 'sour' tastes like. Huangbo said, "In recent years, this old monk's teeth have fallen out.
The scholar took a slice and swallowed it whole, saying, "Is this the persimmon of Mt. Miao-shan or the tangerine of Mingzhou? Huangbo said, "Stop showing off your cleverness for a moment. One day...
He went to the Hall of the First Awakened One and beheld the portraits of the two elders, Yuanwu and Poshan, as well as the image of Master Zui.
While gazing up at them, he did not prostrate himself but stood upright, pointing with his hand one by one and saying, "This is so-and-so; this is so-and-so."
Zui said from the side, "For now, rejoice that there is no connection. The Master asked, "What did you say, Monk?
Zui said, "Keep your eyes open. The Master said, "I do not understand; what are the Patriarchs, grandsons, and fathers all huddling together in a circle discussing?
Zui said, "Do you want me to beat the drum so everyone can come and see? The Master said, "You have deceived those looking on. Zui said, "But tell me, old man—"
The monk had several tufts of hair on his eyelids. The layman stepped forward and said, "The weather is bitterly cold;
I pray that you, Venerable Master, remain in good health. Chui then took his leave. One day, Chui ordered the drum to be beaten to assemble the assembly.

He ascended the seat, brought forth the lineage whisk (yuanliu), and earnestly transmitted it [to the monk]. The monk declined repeatedly, but when he could not refuse, he finally bowed and accepted it. The verse says: "Shao..."
Gazing at the bright moon before the Hall of Awakening; the great ocean is emptied with but a single ladle. A bamboo staff soars ninety thousand miles;
one plucks tortoise hair from the back of empty space. (By Chāng-sue Tsui-si)

The Chan master Che Lu Dao renounced his usual life in a chamber of wealth and honor. Observing that the world and the self are impermanent, like a dream or an illusion, he felt only regret at not having encountered a person of clear vision to point the way for him.
Fortuitously moving to Chengdu, he went to visit Zhaojue Temple and paid his respects, saying, "I am fortunate to have this third life;
I hope you, O Monk, will bring me to the ultimate realization. Zhao said, "Today I shall not..."
After some time, he returned on a later day. The scholar asked, "Is there no expedient means? Zui said, "The layman prostrates; the old monk raises his hand. Where is there no expedient means?

He then instructed him to investigate the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature. Without allowing his mind to be divided by wealth, status, children, or women, he investigated with vigor and did not cease.
After a long time, he attained realization. He went up to Zhaojue, where the karmic conditions were met.
He made a formal agreement and bestowed a prediction upon him. A verse says: "Studying Chan until there is no handle— In that very place where there is no handle, one should study.
A bright mirror stands upon its stand as the weather grows still; The Vajra Sword emerges, cold as the Ox and Cow stars. (Zuixue, the drunken successor).
Chan Master Guiyi Chunyujī ascended the hall and said: "The lion exerts its full majesty; even the elephant king finds it difficult to look back.
The mind of the patriarchs of Western India was secretly transmitted here in the Eastern Land. But tell me, what was it that was transmitted? When winter arrives, the plum blossoms emerge."
In spring, trees hang their garments; entering the hall, there is nothing to say. To speak even a single word is already too much. The spring breeze does not speak of the flowers blooming early;
the sun and moon do not speak of their speed, swift as a shuttle. In human life, one must urgently turn back to look:
like a spark struck from stone or a flash of lightning, it is easily consumed. A single piece of ancient brocade contains the image of spring, yet it has been leaked by the Lord of the East.
Question: What is "taking away the person but not taking away the environment"? The Master said: "Frigid frost covers withered trees; the stars and constellations shine upon the Milky Way. Question:
What is "taking away the environment but not taking away the person"? The Master said: "The peak of Jiafu is so high it conceals the Northern Dipper."
A naked child ascends the long street and asks, "What is it when both the person and the environment are simultaneously negated? The Master says, "The true command is being exercised;
Buddhas and patriarchs have no standing. He asks again, "What is it when neither the person nor the environment is negated?
The Master says, "The setting sun stretches to the sea and the mountains; the autumn moon seals the vast sky. (By Zhangxue Zu)
On New Year’s Day, Chan Master Gu’an of Xingfu Monastery at Yaofeng Peak in Suzhou ascended the hall and said: “The king ascends the precious throne;
the village elder sings his song. From within the jade flute, the Dharmakāya is blown forth—possessing both essence and function. Upon the golden zither, the eye of wisdom is plucked open.”
"Both dark and both bright. Among those present, only one who has penetrated the single aperture at the crown of the head is permitted to walk hand-in-hand with me.
After a long silence, he brandished his whisk and said: "One must know that within the tip of a hair, every movement has its source. (Jiqi Chusi)
Chan Master Huang Du Yu of Nantai in Tanzhou addressed the assembly: "The spring breeze blows open the bamboo fence gate;
The waters rise in the Xiang River, submerging old traces. Having exhausted all the verses from my liver and gall at Nantai, I sit beneath the shade of trees to watch the fish swallow [the hook].
Small-scale instruction: Luzu’s wall-gazing is the livelihood of ghosts; Puhua’s shaking of the bell shakes heaven and earth. Sometimes hidden...
"Or perhaps it is revealed through such antics; I dare say you have never even dreamed of the 'uppermost' core. [He] strikes the meditation seat and descends.
**Small Sermon:** "The Buddha’s Zen, the Patriarchs’ intent—have you all realized it yet? [With his hand, he draws two strokes and says:
'When the clouds over Xiangtan have vanished, the evening mountains emerge; when the snow in the Ba Gorges has melted, the spring waters arrive. (Jiqui Chusì)
Chan Master Baiyun Keweng Qian of Le’an, Fuzhou, whose courtesy name was Kuangwei, was the son of the Li family of Liangxi.

In his youth, he studied Confucianism and possessed keen intelligence. After he had married, before long, he suddenly fell gravely ill; with a single thought he turned his light inward and resolved to leave the household life.
He composed thirty verses in rhymed couplets to bid farewell to his wife, then went to Xilin Fufeng to renounce the world and relied upon Yunju Xianyuan.

He was fully equipped [with the necessary provisions]. He did not eat three meals a day; at night he sat only in the long-sitting posture. He traveled extensively through Jiangsu and Zhejiang, yet found no one who accorded with his mind-nature.
Later, while on a boat at Baling, he visited Tuiweng. Upon seeing him, Tuiweng immediately expected great things of him. He then attended upon Tuiweng back at Yaofeng.

One day, as the Master sat in meditation at dawn, he suddenly recalled a line from the *Verses on the Profound and the Essential*: "A single phrase clearly encompasses the myriad phenomena. He reflected to himself:
What kind of phrase is this? How extraordinary! It encompasses and penetrates all phenomena; with robes drawn up to cover the knees, one suddenly feels the obstructions of the chest dissolve.
Spontaneously attaining mastery in every direction, whatever arrangements are made are invariably appropriate. Having served diligently for five years, he appeared in the world to teach the assembly:
"When Yangqi first settled there, the walls of his house were thin; at Ye County, there has never been salt or sauce. I am deeply ashamed that I have come here in secret like a reed.
As for the Way, it simultaneously establishes two standards (the succession of the lineage).
Yantou Jingren Yanche Chan Master was the son of the Lu family of Suzhou. At the age of seven, he took the tonsure under Gubo.

Having received full ordination according to his age, he went to Lingyan Zuyu, where he resided for three years until he attained realization. He presented a verse, saying: "Before the Yellow Crane Tower, the Parrot Isle;
The surging waves of the river have their source. Without needing a fist-blow or a kick, I cause him to chant aloud from the very summit.
He then left to reside at Yantou. Entering the hall, he said: "Rare, rare! The green waters and blue mountains are..."
An uninvited friend—birdsong and the sound of mountain streams—stirring up the very marrow of the Buddhas and Patriarchs without the slightest pretense.

When affairs accord with principle, they strike the cheeks and slap the mouths, setting an example for gods and humans without flaunting their skill. As principle shifts with circumstance, they pluck flowers and gather willows;
thus the golden-colored mendicant broke into a smile. From generation to generation, these great beings of immeasurable capacity have passed this down, manifesting their eccentricity.
To expose one's ugliness: if you wish to be upheld at the highest level, you must strictly avoid looking ahead or behind. As he spoke, he took up his staff, struck it once, and said:
"On the eleventh day of the sixth month in the year of Yimao (1675), at the hour of Shen, I suddenly depart this world.
I am forty-four years old; today my illusory body comes to an end. His attendant requested further instruction, to which the Master replied: "I have no leisure to provide further teaching."
"You have spoken," he said, and tears fell from his eyes. The Master let out a thunderous shout and passed away. His stupa was erected on a southern spur of the mountain, about two li away.
(Jiqi succeeded him.)
Chan Master Yantou Renkui of Ezhou ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to propagate the Great Teaching, you must first ensure that it is as impenetrable as water cannot leak through.
[It is like] steel grit in a bowl or wooden shavings on the edge of a ladle; once you have chewed them until you are full, you can then sing aloud while plucking willow blossoms.
He then looked at the assembly and asked: "Is this a matter concerning the great fundamental principles of the school, or is it something else? [He continued: "Or is it the hundred..."
"The bottom phrase when not thinking. [He] struck the meditation staff and descended from the seat. (Jiqi Chusi).
Master Chengzhang of Qishan on Mount Nanyue ascended the hall and, taking up his staff, said: "The mechanism of a flash of lightning does not rely on verbal elaborations according to circumstances;
for those who linger in thought, how could they be permitted to hide along the walls? It severs the hand at the waters of the Xiang River."
He tried to walk toward Nanyue Shitou and stepped onto a boat at Yueyang; his clever tricks were entirely forgotten.
The waves of Lake Dongting have always been with him, like a bamboo pole used for a performance—how could they ever serve as a stage?

He struck once and said, "If you can realize it right now, you all will not have immeasurable transgressions, nor will Elder Zhang have immeasurable transgressions. Because of illness, the Master retired from the monastery. Eastward...
He returned to Jiufeng to spend the summer retreat. For a total of eight months, although he experienced extreme suffering, he did not show even the slightest sign of illness.
One day, he requested a bath, sat upright upon his meditation platform, let out a great shout, and passed away. He was interred in a stupa at Jiufeng (his successor being Jiqi).
Chan Master Chuyue of Boyan in Guixi, Xinzhou, a native of the Tong family of Longyou, ascended the hall and said:
"On the day of the winter solstice, days are thus short; on the day of the summer solstice, days are thus long. The distinction between long and short cannot be measured by the rulers of Zhou or Han.
In this empty mountain, a single incense burner suffices. (Jiqi Chusi)
Chan Master Zhanyuan Zhong of Langya in Chuzhou held an evening session. He let out a shout. "I have never been satisfied with this," he said.
"Students all regard it as something solemn and weighty, yet they do not realize that this cuts off the life-root of beginningless birth and death.

How could it be attained by merely opening one's mouth in a casual manner? He shouted again and said, "If you can understand this one shout, you might still be slightly ahead; yet he shouted once more."
He gave a shout and said, "Having arrived here, is it so? Only by being able to discern it can one clarify this.
He gave another shout and said, "Even so, has it not been said: 'A hair’s breadth of difference, and heaven and earth lie between'?
As for you all—how is it on your own part? After a long silence, he said, "This old monk is at fault. The evening *can*: On the part of the patch-robed monks...
Originally there was a matter of great significance that did not require this old monk to open his mouth;
had you been able to grasp it and carry it away on one shoulder, it would still have been somewhat better. But by the time you turn your head to look and listen, how much has already been missed!
Is there anyone among you who is such a person? If there is, come forth and receive the staff from my hand. If there is none, for now let us simply...
Beating the drum for the end of the session; this is the evening discourse. Then, picking up his staff, he said:
"To call this thing 'a single object' is the fault of this old monk. To not call it 'a single object'—could one say the fault lies with the staff itself?
But what about at the moment of calling or not calling? After a long silence, he threw down the staff and said: "Fault! Fault! Up.
The Hall Master raised his staff and said: "Not looking back, all distinctions and confusions are severed. If you harbor doubts or engage in deliberation, when will you ever awaken?
Great assembly, you must simply shake out your brilliance and take up this which is no ordinary matter. He gave a shout and said: "Save your eyebrows! (Retu Weng Chusi).
The Complete Works of the Five Lamps, Volume Eighty-Eight.
Compiled by the Monastic Subject (Chao Yong), Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple, Capital City;
and reviewed by the Monastic Subject (Chao Kui), Abbot of Gu Huayan Temple, Capital City. Presented for Imperial Inspection.
A Record of the Lineage of the Linji School,
the Thirty-sixth Generation under Mount Heng.
Chan Master Zong of Yuntai in Guizhou, surnamed Bi of the Gui River, received the tonsure under Wanfeng and was certified by Minshu Xiang.

He ascended the hall and said: "At the summit of Mount Yuntai, far removed from the human world, I shall uphold the ultimate core of the patch-robed monks and reveal the fundamental, essential mechanism of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. He looked left and right and said: "Right at this very moment..."

At that moment, he cuts off all worldly opportunities with the palm of his hand and hangs his precious sword upon the tip of his brow. When the Buddhas of the three periods of time see him, they forget their sharpness and are left tongue-tied;

when the patriarchs of successive generations hear him, they draw in their breath and swallow their voices. His merit surpasses that of a thousand sages; he stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
Now that this very truth is being enacted, he sits in command throughout the ten directions. Only upon reaching this point does one know that there is indeed a path beyond. And so it is said:
The Way. What is this path that leads upward? The front peak rises high beyond the solitary wild geese;
with no one to take his hand, who will walk it with him? (Minshu succeeded him.)
Chengdu Shengshou Zhenru Konggu Cheng Chan Master was the son of Yang Zhongdong of Shu.
While contemplating the koan "The myriad dharmas return to one," he attained a point of awakening. He went to visit Wanfeng, who said, "There is no Buddha-dharma here; what are you doing coming here?
The Master replied, "I do not dwell where there is Buddha-dharma. Wanfeng laughed and said, "Go and perform your duties with the assembly."
Due to the changing times, the Master entered Mount Qixing for eight years. His disciples increased in number daily. Every day, the Master upheld the fundamental teaching.
The assembly said, "If the Master does not transmit the ancestral lamp, what shall we, the multitude, look toward as our hope? Thereupon, the Master returned to Dazhu.
Humen Shu came to the mountain. The Master asked, "Before the Buddha appeared in the world and before the Patriarch came from the West, who was ordinary and who was holy?
Huaiqin said, "The worthy one yourself creates these distinctions. [The Master] asked, "When heaven and earth were not yet divided, where did one establish a dwelling and maintain one's life?

Huaiqin said, "Turn over the lacquer bucket; it is clear and resonant on all eight sides. At these words, the Master’s faculties were in accord with the teaching, and he subsequently received his seal of certification.
Certification: At the request of Prince Shuncheng, the Master resided at the White Pagoda Temple in the capital. He ascended the hall and said:

"When I, this mountain monk, arrive here, there is not a single dharma to be spoken, nor a single thing to be picked up. I can do nothing but recall my time thirty years ago when I lived at Mount Kongwang."
Beneath the shadowless tree while tending cattle, there was a cowherd who sang a song of non-arising.
Today, I shall sing it before this assembly of devas and humans for the great multitude to hear. After a long silence, he said: "Does the assembly understand?
Listen closely, listen closely! (Min Shu Xiang Si).
Chan Master Long of Qinglin in Jingzhou ascended the hall and said: "Master Fu Daoshi said: 'There is a thing prior to heaven and earth; formless, it is fundamentally silent and vast.
It is able to be the lord of the myriad phenomena, yet it does not wither along with the four seasons. Great assembly, do you recognize this thing?
The Buddhas of the three periods attained it and realized perfect enlightenment; the patriarchs of successive generations took it as their standard."
The banner of the Dharma has been erected. Sentient beings are deluded by it and thus undergo the cycle of rebirth; those who awaken to it transcend the ocean of suffering.

If you encounter the Master at every point of contact, this is precisely the time to return home and sit in peace. If this is not yet so, it will ultimately be difficult to utter even a single word. Why?
Because whether it be worldly things or non-worldly things, they fundamentally do not depart from the world. (He lets out a shout.)
(Minju Sasi). Master Cheonbyeok Jeok of Hwanggang Eonyeong Monastery ascends the hall: "That which is seen and that which is heard are inherently present in every person;
each and every one lacks nothing. Yet I require all of you to take another step beyond the hundred-foot pole—to advance until the water ends and the mountains cease."
At the point of exhaustion is the mechanism that ghosts and spirits cannot peer through. At that moment, one realizes that birth and death do not interfere with one another.
(He lets out a shout. Ascending the hall for the funeral of a deceased monk, he says: "Great assembly, where has the deceased monk gone? A monk replies: [He lets out a shout.]
"Up in heaven and down in earth. Another monk said, "Throughout the worlds of the ten directions.

The Master said, "If you say 'up in heaven and down in earth,' you will inevitably sit yourself to death, O *śrāmaṇera*. If you say 'throughout the worlds of the ten directions,' you will inevitably run yourself to death, O *śrāmaṇera*.
Set aside these two extremes; speak a single phrase from the point of intimacy. The two monks hesitated. The Master said, "One coffin, two..."
A Dead Man addresses the assembly. Holding up his staff, he draws a circle and says: "A single glance at the realm of autumn colors: The moon is full in the vast distance.
Pine and cypress leaves fall with a whistling sound; Dewdrops hang like scattered pearls. Flocks of wild geese fly across the shore;
Cicadas embrace the trees deep within the forest. The Zen mind is like the moon upon the river— Where can one seek its hidden source? (Minshu Xiangsi)
Chan Master Xuelin Mei of Jincheng in Wugang was a native of Guixi in Yuzhou. He went to study under Xueshan Shen, who asked him, "What have you come here to do?
The Master replied, "I have come specifically to meet with the Master. Xueshan asked, "With what do you come to see me?"
The Master held up one fist. Shen said, "Where did you get that? The Master then shouted; Shen then struck him with his staff.
One day, while the Master was carrying firewood with the assembly, Shen asked, "Can you carry this? The Master dropped the wood. Shen said, "You cannot carry it?
The Master then picked up the wood and walked away. Ascending the hall, he said: "The staff conceives and gives birth to the brilliant hero; it drags through the mud..."
Carrying water to Jincheng, humans and devas gathered together with no other business than to realize that birth after birth is fundamentally unborn.
[The Master] suddenly held up his staff and said, "All of you, look at this staff: does it have birth, or is it unborn?
A monk said, "All people under heaven share one nostril. The Master struck him on the head with the staff and said, "Jincheng Gate!"
[The Master] descended from his seat. "Rewards and punishments must be clear" (as in the *Yanju shensi*).
Zen Master Zhe of Lingbi at Wenshu Monastery on Shangshan in Southern Dian, a descendant of the Hu family of Linshui in Western Sichuan, ascended the hall and said:
"The Way is utterly ordinary; yet it cannot be realized through mere ordinariness. The Way resides in tiles and rubble—how lowly it is!"
"The Way is present even in excrement and urine. This becomes increasingly clear and more profound [as seen in the *Yanju shensu*].
At Panlong Rushi Monastery in Wugang was Master Xuanxuan, a native of the Wu clan from Guixi in Yuzhou.

Having left the white robe of lay life and received full ordination, he traveled extensively to visit various monastic assemblies. Upon visiting Xueshan Shen, as soon as he entered the gate, Shen immediately raised his staff.
[The Master] said, "Speak! Speak! The Master immediately walked from west to east, extended his staff, and cast it down, saying, "Speak! Speak!

The Master said, "Even if one were to act in such a way, it would already be a failure to hit the mark; how much less can one bear to speak again? He then departed. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said:
"A man of the world who has left the mundane world turns upon being struck, like a fine horse of the world that does not wait for the lash. If the eyes flicker or move, it is like—"
How can one emerge from the fetters of concealment? Treading upon the earth with one's feet and crowning the heavens with one's head—look! The moon and the flowing water arrive at the gate.
If one were always thus, it would completely fill the void so that not even a needle could pierce it.
If one were always thus, one would be scattering sand and earth, calling a jar a bell; this would not only bury the ancestral school but would also be truly regrettable.
"Self. Now tell me: is it thus, or is it not thus? After a long silence, he said:
"When one has few affairs, there are few afflictions; where one knows many people, there is much contention. (Yanju Shen’s Succession)
Chan Master Ruoyu Min of Wugang Yunji was the son of the Wu family of Xin’an. He studied under Xueshan Shen.

Once, when a monk by his side requested further instruction, Shen said, “Delusion has no self-nature; its entire substance is the Truth. It is extinguished right where it is. What do you call a delusive thought?

Upon hearing this, the Master was suddenly freed from his doubts. He ascended the hall and said: “Immediately realizing principle and phenomena, one transcends both the ordinary and the holy. He then wrote: [a verse].

Abiding in perfect interfusion, one transcends birth and death and emerges from the shrouds of delusion. As every faculty responds to its stimulus, how is this any different from cutting off the rushing current of past and present?
It is a pillar of stability amidst ten-thousand-mile surging waves. Having scrubbed away the cataracts of many lifetimes, clear vision suddenly shines forth.
To contract it: the autumn waters and the vast sky are of one color. To let it go: the setting clouds and the solitary wild goose fly together. It is exactly thus.
At that time, [the Master] said, "How do you express this in a single phrase? After a long silence, he said, "The mountains and rivers of West Qin and East Lu differ;
who does not share the same blue sky above their crowns? A monk asked, "Why did [the monk] fall into the body of a wild fox for failing to acknowledge cause and effect?
The Master said, "The man wearing boots eats the meat. [The monk] asked, "Why was he freed from the wild fox body for not being oblivious to cause and effect? The Master said, "The barefoot man..."
**Chentu (Yanju Shensi)** Chan Master Yue of the Yuanfeng Qianan, of Dong’an County in Yongzhou, Hunan, was the son of the local Jiang family.
Upon ascending the hall, after citing the words of Sansheng and Huihua, the Master held up his whisk and said: "Yuanfeng sometimes acts like this—piercing through."
He reversed the nostrils of the Three Sages; sometimes he did not act thus, changing the very eyes of Xinghua.
Although it is so, tell me: is it that which benefits others, or is it that which does not? After a long silence, he rose and said, "You must all avoid boring through tortoises or striking tiles.
He threw down his whisk and descended from the seat. A verse on awakening to the Way upon seeing the stars: On the day of practicing the Way in the Snowy Mountains,
Pobo. To the end of his life for six years, he could do nothing about it. At midnight, when the stars appeared before his door, his eyes protruded like the ancient mountains and rivers.
A Verse on Nanquan’s “Three Is Not”: Heaven and earth, ten thousand miles, are but a single bar of iron;
It presses down upon empty space until its back bleeds. It vexes Vajrapāṇi until his eyes glare in rage; On every mountain, peach and plum blossoms lie in profusion. (Yanju)

Shenshi). Master Yunshan Hunpu Shenchan of Wugang was the son of the Zhao family from Bazhou. He studied under Yunshan Shen, and whenever he asked a question, he invariably received a severe beating and harsh rebukes.
One day, while entering the inner quarters for instruction, Shen said, "Speak the Way regarding that which cannot be categorized as either right or wrong."

"Give me one phrase," the Master said. Shen replied, "Realize it within the midst of right and wrong. Shen then struck him. The Master suddenly attained enlightenment, realizing that all the blows he had received and the insults he had endured in the past were entirely for his sake, down to the very marrow of his bones.
Shen went to Mount Nanyue to sweep the pagoda of the Patriarch Huairang and bestowed upon the Master his robe and whisk.
He instructed [his successor] to take his place and ascend the hall. He raised an ancient saying: "If one can turn things around, one is identical to the Tathāgata.
Holding up his staff, he said: "This here is a thing. How do you turn it?
If you can turn it, then the Buddhas shall not precede you, and sentient beings shall not follow behind you. Nevertheless, even so, the staff of Yunshan refuses to let go at all."
[Zhaozhou] held up his staff and said: "Thirty blows for being turned by things; thirty blows for not being turned by things;
thirty blows for being the same as the Tathāgata; thirty blows for not being the same as the Tathāgata.
He then laughed loudly and said: "How, after all, will you understand this? (Yanju Shen succeeded him.)
Chan Master Yunshu Zhishi of Shengli Temple on Mount Wuyun in Hunan was the son of the Li family of Guizhou. He ascended the hall.

A monk asked, "I have heard it said that you, Reverend, are skilled at lecturing on Zhuangzi and Laozi; is this true? The Master said, "Who told you that? The monk replied, "The Daoist priests of the Wanshou Palace.
The Master held up his whisk to show him. The monk was at a loss. The Master said, "At Mount Wuyun, there is only this."
[The Master] brandishes a *haozhi* whisk. "In the two Yués and three Xiāngs, few know its rarity. He throws down the whisk and descends from his seat.

A monk approaches for an audience. The Master asks, "Where have you come from? The monk replies, "From the foot of the mountain. The Master says, "By the roadside there is a 'Piercing-the-Heart Spring. Have you seen it, or not?
The monk says, "I have long heard that the Master possesses this particular pivot. The Master remains silent for a long while, then says, "I do not understand; please speak, Master."
The Master said: "Donkeys in front, horses behind—Han, get out! The Verses on the Three Barriers say: "What is my hand like the Buddha’s hand?
Picking it up and putting it down myself reveals my own ugliness. Sometimes I seize the Ten-Thousand-Year Cane;

With a single stroke, I cut off the West River so it flows backward. "What are my feet like a donkey’s feet? I have trodden the heavens and earth all the way to Mount Nanyue. Fame and profit—both are gone."
Forgetting all concerns. Beneath the pines, he stretches and contracts as he sleeps. Every person has their own karmic affinity.

The mouth of the alms bowl does not turn outward; it remains round. All year long, it is never covered upon the table. It nurtures the fragrance of jade flowers, which fills the heavens. (By Yanju Shen)
Chan Master Yupu Fu of Mount Gui at Fohui Monastery in Wuyou, Hunan—originally from the Wei’an district of Chongqing in West Shu—ascended the hall and said:
"Opening infinite mouths and extending the broad, long tongue, Mount Gui does not understand. Raising the fist of Guizong and pointing with the finger of Tianlong, Mount Gui does not understand.
Although this is so, tell me: by what means do you act for others? After a long silence, he said:
Before the gate, peach and plum blossoms intermingle red with white, piercing through the first peak of Duliang (by Yanju Shensi).
Chan Master Bingyue Jing of Fenghuang Mountain in Wuhun was the son of the Wu clan of that same prefecture. Upon opening the foundation of the stupa, he ascended the hall and said:
"He splits asunder heaven and earth, overturns the seas and mountains, opens the den of the fierce tiger, and manifests the *stūpa* throughout the dust-motes of the universe."

He took the jewel from the poisonous dragon and emitted auspicious light from the central peak. This is truly what is meant by: "The circle is not yet complete, and the crooked wood has already sprouted.
Nevertheless, there is still one matter to inform you all. After a long silence, he rose and said: "Do not waste your efforts on the hoe and the sickle.
Ascending the hall, as soon as a monk stepped forward, the Master struck him. The monk stepped closer and seized [the Master’s staff].
The monk stood leaning on his staff. The Master said, "I thought you were a beginner of recent training; it turns out you are a true master. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Today Fengshan has lost face," and then descended from the seat. A monk asked, "If one advances, it shatters empty space."
"Not advancing is the livelihood of the ghosts. I do not know whether advancing is it, or whether not advancing is it.
The Master called to a monk; as the monk approached, he bowed. The Master took up his whisk and pointed, saying, "This laughing pillar is not the lantern.
The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Do not deceive yourself, Upāsaka. Even one with three heads and six arms, upon arriving here, would have nothing to grasp."
[The monk] sought a place [to sit]. The monk bowed again. The Master said, "Excessive courtesy is surely deceitful," and struck him (this was the case of Yanju Shen).
At Mount Wuyun in Hunan, Chan Master Shizhu of Bieyun Peak asked a monk: "What is the realm of Yunfeng?
The Master said, "A wooden bird perches on a cliff edge, watching the clouds come and go. The monk asked, "What is the meaning within this realm?"
The monk said, “Within the two eyes of heaven and earth, within an inch of the heart, there are the sun and moon. This is called the phrase of “person and environment.
[The monk] continued, “I have already received your instruction on this. But what did the pillar just say to you, Master? The Master replied, “The ox in the back garden is eating vegetables.
The monk prepared to offer a further remark, but the Master said, “I am busy picking tea today. After the monk prostrated and withdrew, [the record notes: (Yanju Shensi).
Master Mu of Qugu at Shenglin Temple on Mount Wuyue in Hunan ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the coming from the West?
The Master said, "Dwelling on Mount Meiping; tilling with fire and using the axe. The monk said, "That was a statement about dwelling in the mountains.
Please grant me a word for the benefit of others. The Master struck him. The monk said, "I, your disciple, am at fault. The Master did not wait for him to finish.
The monk said, "Master, why is it that today your staff-head lacks the true eye?
The Master struck him again and said, "The compassionate heart of the teacher I studied under was simply Mei-ping. The Master took up his whisk and pointed, saying, "What is this lantern laughing at?
The monk hesitated; the Master threw down the whisk and descended from his seat. (Yanju Shen succeeded him.)
Chan Master Liaozhuo Yuan of Shilian Mountain in Lingling County, Yongzhou, Hunan, was a native of Xin’an. On one occasion, he ascended the hall to give a discourse on a certain matter:
"The skillful can accommodate the clumsy; the winding can conceal the straight. Although this is so, one must still analyze and discern with clarity to be truly worthy of the name of a Dharma vessel.
After a long silence, he looked at the assembly and said: "At this very moment, killing and giving life are both fully manifest."

"A single phrase. Again, how do you say it? "Is it an elephant? Is it a dragon? It does not hinder its leaping about. As for the blind tortoise and the lame turtle, how could they be allowed such madness?
[The Master] struck them all at once with his staff. Question: "What is the great meaning of the West?
The Master picked up a fan and said, "This is a Guangdong palm-leaf fan. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "I shall tell you..."
He said, "This is a rush-leaf fan," and then added, "I do not understand," before striking him (Yanju Shen).
Chan Master Liaoyue Duan of Yunnan Shibo was the son of the Mao family of Jiangjin. He went to study under Zhuo of Zhaojue, who asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "From Huangbo. Zhuo asked, "Who came with you? The Master replied, "Only I myself. Zhuo opened [the door].
On a day when the furnace was being heated, Master [Zhao] asked: "The forge is wide open and the tongs and hammer are fully deployed;
the very lives of the patch-robed monks are all in the hands of the Master. Yizui said, "Do you understand this as 'life'? Master Zhao gave a shout. Yizui struck him.
Later, while residing at Nanming, he ascended the hall and said: "There are worlds where fragrant food constitutes the Buddha-work; there are worlds where sound constitutes the Buddha-work."
There are worlds where silence constitutes the Buddha-work. But tell me: what do I, this mountain monk, take as my Buddha-work here?
[He draws a circle with his staff and asks: "Do you see? [He strikes the ground with his staff and asks: "Do you hear?
Since hearing and seeing are thus clear, what exactly is it? [He lets out a shout. [Ascending the hall: "A dry piece of dung; three pounds of hemp."
"There is no way to penetrate it; it is a dead-end that kills people. Here, cut it in two with a single stroke, and you will not have come to my gate in vain.
If the preceding thought does not cease and the succeeding thought arises again, how will you eradicate them?
[The Master] drew a line with his staff and descended from the seat. (Zui of Zhangxue was the successor.)
Chan Master Ling of Jingming Lanshi in Hanzhong was a native of Zhongzhou. Initially, he visited Xiangya Ting and asked, "When the World-Honored One held up the flower, how do you understand it?
The Master replied, "Two eyes facing two eyes. Ting then gave a shout. Next, he visited Zhaojue.
Zhu raised the kōan concerning Dadian’s dismissal of the head seat and commanded the assembly to offer comments. The Master struck Zhu with his palm. Zhu—
The Master looked up and down. The drunken man said, "This old fellow has his mouth shut! and he went out.
The Master, dragging his staff, pursued him to the Dharma Hall and asked, "Tell me, what was the meaning of my looking up and down? The Master struck the drunkard twice with his palm.
Once he was intoxicated, [the Master] gave him a severe beating. Later, he instructed the Master to succeed him on the seat. Ascending the hall, he raised the following case:
A monk asked Yunmen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still any transgression? Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru. Jingming, however, would not have it so.
If someone were to ask him such a question, he would simply say to them: "The jeweled flower crown upon the head of the Heavenly King. Now tell me, how does this compare to Yunmen’s?
Whether they are the same or different, you will certainly attain them. I, this mountain monk, hand over my staff with both hands.
If you have still not realized it, let this staff deliver a message for the assembly. (Thus he threw down the staff. (Changxue Zu’s Succession Record)
A monk from Dianshui asked Master Cishi, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them?
The Master said, "I have not gone to the hall today. The monk was bewildered. The Master said, "You do not even recognize what is beneath your own feet;
what 'birth and death' are you asking about? (Zuixue Zisi)
Chan Master Dajue Tianji Shun of Dingzhou was the son of the Geng family of Huang'an. He left home to become a monk in his youth and investigated the koan, "Who is it that recites the Buddha's name?
Without gaining understanding, he heard a Zen guest say, "Tiantong only uses the staff and shouts to receive people. The Master packed his bag and went straight up to Taibai Peak.
Entering the abbot’s quarters, he immediately asked, "What is my original face? As soon as [Tiantong] realized his intent, he struck him. The Master prostrated himself.
Wu gave him a blow across the back with his boot. One day, while the Master was carrying sand along the road, he encountered Wu.
The Master set down his load and asked, "When you can neither advance nor retreat, what then? Wu struck him on the head with a staff and said, "I specifically want you to exert yourself like this.
The Master then continued on his way with the load. Later, he received the Dharma from Liangshan Pu and succeeded him on the seat at Da... (Dajue Temple).
Lung ascended the hall and said: "Buddha to Buddha, it is transmitted and received; we value nothing more than the circulation of the True Eye. Patriarch to Patriarch, it is upheld and maintained;

we only raise the single path that transcends all. If there is the mutual interpenetration of host and guest, the alternating deployment of illumination and function, the harmonious union of ruler and minister, or the honoring of father and son as the ancestral source—all of these are merely incidental furnishings.
Here at Dàlóng, there is no dharma to be spoken; I can only address you all..."
"At the crown of the head, he turns the Great Dharma Wheel. He planted his staff and said, "The iron face is heartless and bare-boned;
clearly and directly, it is grandly imposing. (Zhufan Bo succeeded him.)
Chan Master Lianyi Long of Longtan in Liuzhou was the son of the Huang family of Tanzhou.
When he first visited Wanfeng Ming, as soon as he prostrated himself, Ming gave him a kick across the back. The Master said, "This is it; is there anything else? Ming let out a thunderous shout.
The Master made a gesture of fear and then departed. Later, he visited Liangshan Ba, who said, "The chirping of magpies and the cawing of crows are nothing other than [the Buddha-nature]."
“This—how do you understand it? The Master said, “Thirty years ago, it was indeed like this; now it is not.
Wobai said, “Setting aside for a moment that it is not so, tell me a word regarding the countenance before your parents were born.
The Master said, “The mountain mist does not leave the north of the monastery; the sound of the waves is always at the eastern gate of the sea. [He then] ascended the hall.
The Dragon Pool is said to be bottomless; it nurtures golden-scaled fish with crimson tails.
If they wish to soar to the Nine Heavens, thunder crashes, lightning flashes, and the wind rises (the bamboo sail upon the waves).
Chanzher Zhicheng of Zhongyi in Dingzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Tingzhou. He went to Longxiang in Jiangling to shave his head and receive full ordination.
He then visited Liangshan Baoyun; upon entering the hall, he immediately asked, "What is it that does not drown when entering water and does not burn when entering fire?
Baoyun replied, "The very question itself is most intimate. The Master said, "If that is so, then I shall employ it according to my own use."
Pobian shouted. The Master then went up to the hall. He raised the previous case concerning Hong’en of Zhongyi, who had opened the Dharma and bestowed the precepts;
it was here that Yangshan received the precepts. Later, when he came to offer thanks for the precepts, Hong’en clapped his hands on the meditation seat and said, "O-yeh! O-yeh!
Yangshan walked from east to west, from west to east, and then stood in the center before offering his thanks for the precepts. Hong’en—
[Daowu] asked, "Where did you obtain this samādhi? Nanquan Yang replied, "I shaved my head at Caoxi; I learned it from the Seal-Master.
Daowu asked, "Whom do you say you received [the Dharma] from? Nanquan Yang replied, "I received it from Yixiu Jue. Daowu asked, "Where did the Master obtain this samādhi?
Nanquan Yang replied, "I learned it from the Great Master Mazu; there was no seal from which I attained liberation. Daowu said, "The two..."
The Great Old Master’s perspective was so vast and upright that he alone shone through antiquity and vibrated throughout the present. At this time, Xingzhongyi bestowed the precepts;
among those seated below, there was one with the bearing of a king who could not help but come forward to deliver a message (Zhufan Bo succeeded him).
Chan Master Yitianhai of Dongshan in Xiangzhou went to visit Haokong Zheng and immediately asked, "I have long been studying 'the myriad dharmas return to one,' yet I have never had an awakening.
I beg the Master for a skillful means. Zheng said, "The elephant king’s nostrils naturally reach toward the heavens."
The Master said, "Just like this, isn't it? He struck him immediately. One day, Zheng raised the story of Yunmen asking Shushan about the Dharmakāya and questioned the Master about it.
The Master said, "Since the Dharmakāya is all-pervasive, why did Shushan say, 'Venerable sir, do not seek it near the water pitcher'?
"If I had been there that day," [Zheng] said, "I would have kicked it over and left. Zheng added, "You would have kicked over the pitcher..."
"Is it the bottle? Or is it the Dharma-body that has been kicked over? The Master said, "It is entirely up to you to decide. (This was the authentic successor, Lianyue.
Chan Master Chunya Rong of Kaixian Linjiang Gate was the son of the Yu family from Echi in northern Sichuan. He shaved his head and received full ordination.
Having traveled extensively to consult various masters, he later went to visit He-feng Zheng and asked, "Was it true that Nanquan killed the cat?
Zheng replied, "Yes. The Master asked, "Where did you, Reverend, see this? Zheng said, "Eye to eye. The Master asked, "Where does its life reside?
Zheng struck his staff down. The Master said, "Quickly return the life! Zheng then struck him. The Master—
Making the sound of a cat, he stepped out and addressed the assembly: "The primary truth—woodcutters' songs and fishermen's chants—how can they be otherwise?
Thirty blows of the staff! He let out a shout and descended from his seat. (Lianyue was the direct successor.)
Chan Master Xiangrong Chengsheng of Wanzhou was the son of the He family from Huguang. Initially, he visited Shuanggui Ming, who asked, "Have you ever studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*?
The Master replied, "I have. Ming said, "'Knowledge and vision are without seeing; this is itself nirvāṇa.'"

"If you had thoroughly penetrated this matter back then, you would have been fit to receive the old monk’s severe blow. The Master vowed not to disperse the assembly. One evening, upon hearing the sound of the signal bell, he attained realization.
Later, he visited Xingning Wang, who ascended the hall and said: "Heaven and earth have many transformations and nurturings since time immemorial.
If you can understand it at this point, it is neither moving nor still, neither shifting nor changing; you will directly attain the purity of the wind."

The moon is bright; the water is cold, the clouds are frigid. Seeing is cut off, hearing is cut off; one neither knows nor perceives. Although it is thus, there is still a matter that transcends this.
Tell me, what is this matter that transcends? After a long silence, he said: "When the fifty-nine days have ended, one encounters spring.
Do not speak of it in such a way when meeting people. (Xiqu waited for his successor.)
Chan Master Shengjue Miyin of Qianyang was a native of Anshun. Initially, he resided in a hermitage on Mount Guangfu in Chenzhou.
One day, Zizhu Wen happened to visit this place. The Master welcomed Wen and prostrated at his feet, then posed a question: "Zhaozhou pointed to the cypress tree."
Nanquan pointed at a peony and asked, "I do not know, Master, with what will you save people? Wumen gave a shout. Nanquan then fell to the ground and lay there.
Wumen called for a novice to help him up. When the novice arrived, Nanquan rose, circumambulated Wumen once, and departed.
Wumen used this as a seal of certification. Later, someone took up this kōan and said, "The rootless tree has come to life."
A monk said, "Since he is a member of the family, he speaks of family matters" (Lingyin Wen’s successor).
When Chan Master Jihai Zhou of Yuntai at Zhenyuan first visited Longhu Wen, he asked, "What is the patriarchs' mind-seal?
Wen replied, "The bottomless bowl transmitted by the thousand sages. The Master said, "That is still a matter on the side of dharmatā. Wen—
Wen said, "What do you call this 'Dharma-body'? The Master then gave a shout. Wen said, "As for this one shout of yours, what does it amount to?
The Master said, "If that is so, then there is no need for a three-month retreat; you may walk alone through the great square.
Wen shook his head with a powerful shout. The Master said, "A master of the school. Wen said, "Do not slander Huilong. [Later,] he ascended the hall.

To clear away [all obstructions] and penetrate the single aperture above—this the patriarchs of successive generations did not know; it cuts off the crowns of a thousand sages, and the monks as numerous as the sands of the Ganges do not understand.
To speak in such a manner is much like having eyes that look down upon the four seas with total emptiness, acting as if no one else exists. Great assembly!
You must know that within your own being there is a segment of luminosity that is utterly transcendent of cognition and views;
it does not consort with the myriad dharmas, nor does it travel in the company of the thousand sages. It is pure and naked, beyond thought; it is bare and clear, without deviation or compromise.
When lifted up, the myriad dharmas are fully manifest; when set down, not a single speck of dust remains. Now tell me: when neither lifted nor set down, what is it?
"How so? After a long silence, he said: "To have a phrase is not the fundamental principle; to be without words is the true monk.
(From the lineage of Lingyin Wen). *Wudeng Huiyuan*, Volume 88, Supplement.

Recorded by the Chan Master Xiu Guangfa Wuzhuo of Shuchuan, the thirty-sixth generation descendant of the Linji lineage under Nanyue, while presiding at the Pass to instruct the assembly: "To enter this gate there is no interior; to exit..."
This gate has no exterior. Since there is neither interior nor exterior, what is it right now? He let out a shout and said: "Who can cross the wild waters?
The solitary boat drifts freely in all directions. Addressing the assembly: "The primordial source of the primary meaning—lightning strikes and thunder roars within the fire-lotus.
A single blast of the lethal poison shakes heaven and earth; before the pivot, a single arrow pierces the three barriers. (Jiuzhaolang was his successor.)
Chan Master Guting of the Lotus Society at Mount Nanyue ascended the hall and said: The spring breeze and warm sun have just begun to lengthen;
willow catkins and fine rain scent the pond. Fish swim in joy, unstartled by the waves; birds chirp busily, as if intent on urging others on. In this good news, there is no need for acceptance;
the ancestral meaning from the West is perfectly clear. To speak of it makes one’s heart ache with reflection. *Up* (Ascending the Hall)

The Hall Master raised up [the case of] Cuiyan showing the assembly, saying: "Throughout this summer, I have engaged in various conversations with you brothers; let us see if Cuiyan’s eyebrows still remain.

The Master said: "During this summer retreat at the Lotus Society, I have been with my brothers—some ascending Mount Nanyue, some wading through the Xiang River, sitting vigorously or sleeping wearily, burning incense and sweeping the floor—all quite ordinary. There is no need to open one's mouth; each [of you]..."
I know the seasons and recognize the times, yet I do not know whether the eyebrows of the Lotus Society still remain upon their eyes. Let those with discerning eyes examine this for themselves.
Ascending the hall after retiring from the monastery: A single staff brings the vernal colors to the sweet dew; Twice I have seen white lotuses bloom by the pond’s edge.
The old fire awaits its time to warm the purple taros; Lacking the strength to benefit others, I grind the green bricks. The Stone of Three Lives.

"A place where bones may be buried; the ten-thousand-li journey of the Peng bird pauses for a moment to rest its shoulders. Take care, O elders before the mountain; remember only the karmic conditions for a future rebirth.
He held up his staff and descended from the seat. That very day, he ordered a palanquin and retired to Changgui Hall in Hengzhou.

He gave instructions only to have a coffin constructed, yet his movements and conduct remained entirely as usual. On the sixteenth day of the tenth month, he suddenly requested a bath. Having bathed...
He turned onto his right side and lay down. At midnight, he sat up again. The assembly gathered before his couch. The Master picked up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying:
"Throughout forty years, only this one has remained truly sober. Tonight, go back; tomorrow, the moon shall rise upon the treetops.
Having finished speaking, he threw down the staff and passed away. At that time, his disciple Foyuan and others were by his side; they touched the Master’s arm and said, "Chang..."
Master Gui was away on a retreat at Kaifeng and had not yet returned. [The Master] said, "I wish for you, Reverend, to stay for three more days;
do not let us fail our previous agreement. The Master smiled and nodded his head. He opened his eyes and sat in meditation, refusing further food. On the nineteenth day, Chang Gui returned.
That same night, in the middle watch, the Master sat cross-legged and passed away. This was the nineteenth day of the tenth month of the Gui-chou year of the Kangxi era.
This month was the middle of winter. In the winter of the *gengxu* year, the Master spent the New Year at Chang-gye.

During a tea ceremony on the eve of the year’s end, he once turned toward Chang-gye and said with a smile, "In the days to come, when I die, I wish that you, my elder brother, would provide me with a single torch.
Chang-gye responded instantly, raising his hand and saying, "Old brother, take care of your eyebrows! The guests present struck their tables and laughed heartily; this has continued until now.

He served for three years. Thus, the Master’s departure from the Lotus Society for Taiping, as well as his returning and remaining at the very end of his life, were all carried out with a playful air of jesting.
The Master was born in the Jiaxu year of the Chongzhen era of the Ming dynasty;
he was just forty years old when he passed away. (Mìxíng Rěn succeeded him.)
Chan Master Siding (Sìdēng) of Luoyuan Zhongxìng was the son of the Liu family of Jinchuan.
He received the tonsure under Venerable Yanju and relied upon the Elder Master Pogui for many years; he was a successor to Master Mìxíng of Kāifēng.

When Master Xíng traveled through Jinchuan, the fourfold assembly requested him to preach the Dharma at Xìngguó Temple. Under [Master Xíng’s] words, Siding thoroughly penetrated the very source of the Dharma. Master Xíng...
He then spoke a verse to seal this. While residing at Zhongxing Chan Monastery in Luoyuan for the retreat period, the lay practitioner Wang Xuangong requested that he ascend the hall.
A questioner asked, "When Bodhidharma faced the wall and when the Master ascends the seat, are these the same or different? The Master said, "If they were different, they would not be the same;
if they were the same, they would not be different. The questioner continued, "Emperor Wu was sagely and wise; why did he fail to accord with the ultimate meaning? The Master said, "Because..."
"You have heard it by hearsay. Ask your parents before they were born: which one is the student's original face?
The Master struck him, saying, "Blind fellow! Why do you prattle in your sleep? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him out with a succession of blows and said:
"The auspicious breath urges the yellow birds; the bright light turns the green duckweed. If you understand the affairs of today, you will not obscure the person of original nature. Great!
Since the assembly has now clearly understood the matter of today, what is this person who is your original nature? Have you not heard it said:
"Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored"? This is precisely the Original Source of Life (*mìngběn yuánchén*) of the Layman Xuangong today, prior to the birth of his parents.
If you can understand this, then you will understand the Original Source of Life within yourself, and you will understand others.
The original source of human destiny is precisely the meeting with Bodhidharma facing the wall; it is no different from today’s ascending of the seat for the revival of the Dharma.

This is the principle that "where they differ, they are not the same; where they are the same, they do not differ. [The Master] suddenly let out a shout. At the moment of the shout, a monk fell over in shock. The Master said:
How brilliant is this patch-robed monk! With a single push, he turns [the wheel]. (Exiting the seat; Mi Xing Ren’s successor.
A verse by Chan Master Heshang Huijian of Mount Heng in Nan Chu, titled “Not Yet Departing from Tuṣita, Already Descending to the Royal Palace”:
Originally it was but a single level path; In a casual stroll, it suddenly becomes rugged. How much better to return and hide beyond the thousand peaks!
Lying down, I watch the twin wheels turn through the vast void. The verse on "Mind-itself is Buddha" says: Two flaps of skin for lips, A set of bones for teeth;
From Jiangxi’s horse-sieve, A falcon from the distant heavens is released. The verse on Baizhang’s second visit says:
The thunder is great, But there are no drops of rain. Deaf ears and a protruding tongue— An old maid seeing her slave. This is called the River.
The spiritual wind of the Western School—may you not fail to recognize its thousand variations and myriad complexities. A verse on Ling Xingpo’s visit to Fubei:
"Seizing her hair and rushing to the yamen, she brings this upon herself as an enemy. Nanquan and Zhaozhou bear cangues and shackles. (Mi Xingren was his successor.)

Chan Master Wenchuan of Fude in Kaizhou was a native of a neighboring county in Shu. At the age of fourteen, he took leave of his parents and left the white robe for the monastic life at Mount Dongshan in Tóngliáng.
He received the Dharma from Yanyu Shen and resided at Fude in Kaizhou. Upon ascending the hall, he said:

Question: "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said: "News from the northern seas has been cut off; on the southern mountains, spring rains scent the flowers. Question:
"What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'? The Master said: "The setting sun sinks behind the western hills and the mountain light fades;
as the horse's head turns eastward, the inspiration for verse grows thick. Question: "What is 'taking away both person and environment'? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
It is said: "The soul dissolves as the coastal islands are lost and the lone ship is overturned; the bowels break with longing as the mountain passes resound with the neighing of a solitary horse.

It is asked: "What is it to have neither the human realm nor the environment wrested away? The Master replied: "Guests have not yet dispersed within the towers of the singing pavilion; the moon first rises upon the roads of Changgan."
He then said: "Raising an eyebrow is already too late; waving the sleeves is still too slow. Blinking the eyes while walking—both the person and the environment are snatched away.
If this were within the sphere of a patch-robed monk, one might slightly compare it; but as for the matter beyond the patch-robed monk, he looked left and right and said:
"Investigate! (Yanju Shensi).
Chan Master Longzou Pefeng of Jiading was the son of the Yue family of Nanchong and the grandson of the jinshi Menglong.
After traveling extensively to study under various masters, he returned and received verification from Master Huijueyi. He ascended the hall and said: "Śākyamuni spoke what is unspeakable;
the fierce winds of Vairambha blow over the seas and mountains. Kāśyapa heard what is unheard; the green mountains are reduced to mere dust. What remains..."
A Single Turn of Phrase: "The tongue is inside the mouth. Ascending the hall, he said: "The Great Way is broad and level; it neither arises nor falls.
When the true mechanism is proclaimed, what is there to be untied or knotted? Ascending the hall, he lit the incense and took his seat. Suddenly, raising his voice, he said:

"The assembly must not give rise to groundless interpretations. With a single slap across the mouth, he said: "The mouth is the gateway to calamity. He then descended from his seat. (Huijueyi was his successor.)
