Foyu Yuchi of Yuzhou was the son of the Fan family of Jiazhou. At the age of ten, he paid homage to Huijue and donned the white robes of a novice.

Upon contemplating a corpse, he attained a profound realization. In responding to others and engaging in debate, his wit was sharp and swift. He remained by his master’s side with the incense burner and water vessel, never showing even a trace of indolence.
He once showed this verse to a practitioner of Chan: "The clear and distinct words are not obscure; The nose is straight and the brows are arched."

How many have missed it? It is simply because that which is manifest is difficult to discern. Zen practitioners travel across thousands of mountains and ten thousand waters. He composed a poem on plum blossoms:

*With ice-like skin and snow-like bones, long harboring the cinnabar heart;* *It spits forth, causing people to look with close attention.* *Its true nature is not borrowed from peach or apricot;* *A single curtain of shimmering stars upon a jade balustrade.* He took it as his duty to support the monastic communities and attended to his master with filial care.

He was the master Huijueyi. In the autumn of the Gui-chou year of the Kangxi era, Huijueyi passed away while sitting in meditation. [The Master] subsequently grieved so deeply that he became emaciated to the point of being mere skin and bone;
his eating and resting were like those of one in a stupor. On the anniversary of the Buddha’s Enlightenment that same year, he manifested a slight ailment and refused to take medicine.

After seven days had passed, having finished bidding farewell to the assembly and entrusting them with his final instructions, he passed away at noon with his eyes wide open. (Huijueyi was his successor.)
Master Yuan Chan of Sanfengbanshui in Baxian ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "A seven-foot black staff is a turtle-nosed snake;
it soars through the universe and brings auspiciousness to the Three Bas. It wanders far through the marketplace, yet people find it hard to see.

Even if one examines it closely, it has not yet reached home. He dropped the staff and let out a shout. Ascending the hall again, he issued the Yuan for the commencement of the retreat, saying: "This mind is truly..."
Twenty-one days: burning long strands of incense throughout the nine periods of meditation, sitting until dawn and midnight; in such leisure, there is no matter to deliberate upon.
(The Great Roar Transmits the Succession)
Chan Master Huanchu of Huayan in Chongqing ascends the hall on the Buddha’s Birthday: “The World-Honored One carved open the primordial chaos;
Yunmen smelted stones to mend the heavens. Although there was not even a hair’s breadth of leakage, there still remained the strategic artifice of warp and woof.

While it is true that both have achieved great merit like the labor of horses in battle, do you see the Great Peace? For now, let us rejoice that today is free from affairs. (Succeeded by Shengke Yu).
Chan Master Nan-zhi Jing of Huayan, Chongqing, held a small informal discourse (*xiaocan*). Upon the level ground of reality, he picks up a single thread.
Why is it that all people throughout the great earth lose their wits and remain tongue-tied? Tell me, where does the point of benefit or harm lie? Do you understand?
It is as large as a mustard seed and yet as minute as Mount Sumeru; it is as soft as iron and as hard as mud. It does not depart from the four dignified postures.
In the ritual manual: Alas, people do not recognize this! (Sengke yu si).
Master Zhong Hong of Longxing Monastery in Hanzhou ascended the hall and said: "Danxia burned the wooden Buddha simply because the cold had penetrated to his very bones.

The monastery head lost his eyebrows and beard because of a single thought of resentment. This is precisely the moment of shifting the palace and changing the position, where the cold air intermingles."
Furthermore, within the domain of the patch-robed monk, how is it so? After a long silence, he let out a shout and said:
"The hook is in the ground of non-doubt" (Shengkeyu’s successor).
Chan Master Fākōng Zhèng of Lǔzhōu Laifēng ascended the hall. He struck his staff and said: "Conform to the bright side; conform to the dark side.
In the four directions and eight points, act with strategic skill as you will. Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha—what is this thing of joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure?
How many people in the world are like those who wait by the stump? They all withdraw and give up midway. (Succeeding Shèngkěyù).
Chan Master Jia Nanxian of Ciyun in Yucheng composed a verse on the World-Honored One’s first birth, saying: Pointing at heaven, pointing at earth—what does he intend to plot?
He treats others as if they do not exist; his mettle is coarse. It was thought that the whole world was red-bearded, But who knew there were still red-bearded ones with beards?
He composed a verse on the World-Honored One ascending the seat, saying: The one seated above should know the one seated below has come; Originally, there is no contrivance.
He makes a clever arrangement. Among them all, that old Mañjuśrī is truly intolerable; a hundred thousand devas and humans are buried alive.

*Commentary on the National Teacher’s three calls to his attendant:* Three times he called, three times he responded, and then it was over. On land there are carriages and horses; on water there are boats. "Carrying me, carrying you"—exposing the family's disgrace.
This too is "loving one's child so much as not to notice their shame. *Commentary on "The Mind is Not":* The mind is not... [the verse continues].
The Buddha’s wisdom is not the Way, it is said: After the rain at Flower Creek, the mossy stream is slippery; The magpies’ calls linger as the midday dream clears.
Looking in all directions, the white clouds have vanished; The setting sun slants upon several peaks of green. (Sung Ke-yu, successor)
Chan Master Xing of Buhuo at Xiaquan in Hanzhou was a native of the Wang family of Yingshan.

Encountering the chaos of the Shu region, he fled to Chu and received the tonsure under Master Yuan of Dangshan at Xiangyan. He studied with Master Shengke Yuyu, gaining realization upon hearing a single word.
On ordinary occasions, he did not yield when his faculties were tested. One day, Yuyu asked him: "Set aside the 'barbarian speech' and 'Han speech'; what about before your parents were born?"
"Speak a single phrase! The Master then struck him. Yù said, "That was too crude, sir. The Master struck him again. Yù then desisted.
Later, Yìn expressed this in a verse: "The fragrance of the osmanthus has reached even Yáo; Even now there are five scars upon his face. For ten years his resentment has not ceased;
Vengeance is indeed paid by those who harbor a grudge. He returned to Shǔ and resided at Xiàquán in Hànzhōu. Above...
In the Hall, a monk asked, "Before one's parents were born, what is the student’s original face?
The Master said, "The eyes are horizontal and the nose is straight. The monk asked, "Once dead and burned, where are the face and eyes? The Master struck him.
The monk asked, "May I still communicate another message, Master? The Master struck him again and said, "On the ground of green willows and fragrant grass, stroll at leisure as you please."
He looked at the assembly and said, "Do you understand? When some did not understand, he said, "Today I must certainly deliver a separate message to you all.

He dragged his staff down from the seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters. Sitting upright, he passed away. When the assembly went to the refectory and did not see the Master emerge, they entered the quarters and shook him; he was already still.
Only then did the entire assembly realize the meaning of the words, "Today I must certainly deliver a separate message to you all. His stupa was erected at...

Master Wenshi Dian of Yuan Tong Temple in Chongqing (succeeded by Sheng Keyu at the Head Monastery) offered this verse on the World-Honored One’s first birth: Pointing to heaven, pointing to earth, he raised the sword;
How many people still crave such excellence! Even if there were those who transcend the crowd and surpass the norm, The wicked will surely find their own [retribution].
**Grinding the Wicked Man** In praise of a woman entering meditative concentration: An empty valley transmits sound; a vacant hall practices listening.
If you trust it, it exists; if you strike it, it responds. Look at that man of great strength— He does not rely on the orders of a general.
**In Praise of the Old Woman Burning the Hermitage** This old woman is full of fabricated wonders. A clever monk will not let you off so easily. She takes fire and burns [the hermitage].
The hermitage’s followers only fatten themselves; to this day they have incurred a debt that will not be settled for donkey-years (the successor of Shengke Yuyu).
Master Mengchan Bilu of Chonglong in Liyang ascends the hall at the conclusion of the retreat: Snow presses down upon the tips of the pines in stillness;
frost is severe, chilling the old trees. White clouds, with intent, constantly seal them shut; secluded birds, without thought, pass through the passes. Great Chang’an...
The Way: An iron snake lies across the path. Going, one can hardly go; returning, it is not easy to return.
(With his whisk, he draws a circle and then slashes through it, saying: "All you Zen practitioners, examine this carefully! At the end, even straw sandals will be deceived by your feet.
(Shengke Yu was his successor.)
When the lay practitioner Gao Wenying, the Provincial Circuit Intendant, first arrived at Huayan, during a tea break he asked: "An ancient said:

'It is like a person in a tree, whose hands do not grasp the branches and whose feet do not tread upon the branches, yet whose mouth holds a branch of the tree. If one were asked the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West..."

If he had answered, he would have lost his life; if he had not answered, he would have failed the question. How could this be? Baizhang (Yù) pointed with his finger at his own tea bowl, then pointed at the layman’s bowl.
The layman said, “The Master uses his hand as his tongue. Baizhang asked, “What do you, Layman, use as your tongue? The layman replied, “I use my tongue as my tongue.
Baizhang said, “It is none other than you, Layman, who can cast off your body and relinquish your life. The layman said, “There is no body.”
"Life may be abandoned," [Master] Yu said. "The old monk was momentarily blinded by his own eyes," the scholar said. "Blind! Blind! the Master replied.
"In that case, does this become mere frivolous discourse? the scholar asked. "When the benevolent man sees it, he calls it benevolence," Master Yu said.

"I am still like one who uses it daily without knowing it," the scholar replied. Thereupon, he performed a formal bow. Later, the scholar again accompanied Master Yu and the layman Tu to visit the hot springs. The scholar...
As they were about to bathe, while eating some cakes, the butcher said, "Everyone, come for the *tangbing* (noodle soup) feast!

The scholar said, "This place could well be named 'Washing-the-Child Spring. Yu said, "Has the Nine-Dragon yet spat forth its water? The scholar said, "It is a pity it does not emerge from between my ribs."
Juyi picked up his *huánzhū* (prayer beads) and made a cry of pain. The butcher said, "This old man is perverse; he knows how to feign the strange.
Juyi said, "Entering the water to seek a person, two intentions coincide. The nine dragons spout water to bathe the golden body. Do not say it does not emerge from between one's ribs;
the pain pierces through this mountain monk’s single string of beads. Later, he presented the scholar with a stone inkstone and a verse, saying: "An imperial gift, a piece of stone from Yuanchang."
Left behind for one like me, it is like an empty boat. Plucked out from the banks of the Yunxi stream, it transforms fish and dragons into companions in the heavens (Sengke Yuyu, successor).
Chan Master Ying'en Zhan Yiqing of Huichuan was a native of the Wang family from Yongning in southern Sichuan. Having entered Dian, he resided at Huichuan Ying'en. He ascended the hall and said:

"In various quarters, the retreat is established and meditation is settled; at Ying'en, we ascend the hall to perform a dance. This startles the fierce dragons of the four seas and causes the phoenixes of the nine heavens to swoop down.
The followers of the Three Vehicles fold their hands in submission, those of the Ten Stages clasp their fists in reverence, and the myriad phenomena stand in solemn array."
Luo raised his eyebrows and exhaled deeply; the stars and constellations of the heavens shone with brilliant radiance. Microscopic lands surged from the east and submerged in the west;

all wriggling, flying, and moving creatures each manifested their inherent nature. This was neither the wondrous application of supernatural powers (*abhijñā*) nor the natural course of things (*dharmatā*).
He struck the meditation staff and said: "Do you understand? Today, too, the soldiers follow the seal’s turn, and the generals march according to the talisman. This is precisely—
At such a time, how do you express the single phrase for "Wishing the Emperor Longevity" upon opening the furnace? The wild man has nothing with which to repay the imperial virtue;
he shall simply fashion Mount Sumeru into a single stick of incense. (By Ti Zongning)
Master Cāntiānyuàn of Sōngqiū in Zūnyì addressed the assembly: "In the study of Chan, one must be fierce and resolute; do not cease until awakening is attained.
Rouse your spirit and vigor; do not let this opportune moment pass. Cast away all worldly attachments with a heart of total resolve—how could you be bound by years or months?
Only when your footing is firmly established will you no longer be deluded by others. Be willing to endure the bitterest of bitterness; only then can you break through the critical barrier."
Thoroughly! The ancients have already been thus. I am constantly earnest about this; let us become people who stand out from the crowd. One’s conduct must be utterly distinct.
If one can realize the proof within a fixed period, one transcends immediately. Waves surge upon the mountain peak; the seabed stands parched dry.
Even if Maitreya and Śākyamuni were to arrive, they would lose their tongues and be rendered speechless. The three thousand layers of entanglement—every single nest and trap has been eradicated.
Cut off! He intended to ask further how it was, but a white staff struck him right over the head (Liangsheng followed in the lineage).
When Chan Master Huai of Shuanggui ascended the hall, his mouth was like a hanging river; he blew the holeless flute and employed the talisman from behind the elbow before mounting the lion throne.
When the true command is exercised, Buddhas and Patriarchs alike beg for their lives—this is the true mechanism.
The place of manifestation: whether ordinary or holy, all are fused as one. The sage’s arrow pierces the nine layers; frost tints the reeds, all of a single hue.
The sword’s spirit withers the wu-leaves; before the eaves, mortars and pestles pound a thousand peaks. Every thing contains the jade dew; where is there not the golden wind?
This Dharma abides in its own station; the characteristics of the world are eternally present. Do you all recognize this true eternity?
"Mind? After a long silence, he said, "For those who know, there is no need for frequent questioning; the adept should be taught in the dark.

Late evening *can* on the Mid-Autumn Festival: "The nesting place of all Buddhas and the pivotal gate of the patriarchs—before the fifteenth day, I have fully explained them for you until they fill your eyes and ears.
From lamp to lamp, the succession continues until Maitreya descends to be born in the future."
The foundation still remains. After the fifteenth day, when it is precisely the fifteenth, the mountain colors enter the curtains, separated by clouds;
the sound of dripping eaves reaches the ears as the cassia blossoms fall. Everyone sits through the Mid-Autumn moon, sparing their eyes from having sand fall upon them again.
A monk asked, "What is the Patriarch’s Barrier? The Master said, "A beggar holding a broken basket in his hand. The monk [continued].
A question was asked: "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]? The Master said: "Apply the golden whip behind the wooden man's head. (Yunqiao Shui was his successor.
Chan Master Shengfu Yue of Tongren and Xiangshan ascended the hall and said: "A single stroke upon the crown of the head illuminates the ancient and soars through the present.
The halo behind the head shines through all differences. If you are a person of comprehensive understanding, go directly beyond the boundary of Vipaśyin Buddha and overturn it."
To overturn the old molds—how could this be a matter of the present-day gate? Having kicked over all that came before, he struck the meditation seat and said:
"A man of spirit has his own will to soar through the clouds; he does not travel where the Tathāgata has trodden. (Minshu succeeded him.)
Chan Master Sōun Jichēn of Jingzhou gave a small lecture (xiaocan): "Chan does not depend on 'investigating' (can); its application is already perfected.
The Way does not depend on 'learning'; it is inherently round and luminous. One must be such a person before one can speak such words.
Until one reaches such a state, one must undergo a great rest (da-xie). Brothers, do you know the news of this great rest? After a long silence.
It is said: "When you have pushed to the point where the water ends and the mountains exhaust themselves, turn your head and bump into your own father and mother.
(Danzhu Mi’s Successor). Master Lin Xianghengxiu of Kaishua, Yunnan, ascended the hall for formal instruction. A monk asked:
"When Linji was at Huangbo, he asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma three times. Why was he beaten each time? The Master struck him and said: "Under Huangbo..."
He suffered greatly. Why did he go to Daoyu to uproot the very foundation? The Master struck him repeatedly and drove him away, saying:
"To understand such a matter, one must be such a person; if one is such a person, one must be able to handle such a matter.
Thus, fist and kick corresponded, and song and rhythm followed one another. Although this is so, it is easy to see these two elders, but it is difficult to see Jixiang.

This is difficult. Why? Because "having eyes but no ears, one sits by the fire in the sixth month. [On the occasion of] ascending the hall at the conclusion of the retreat, two monks stepped forward together.
The Master said, "One arrow brings down two birds. When the two monks returned to their positions together, the Master said, "The dead are dead;
the living are alive. He then said, "Last winter on this very day, I had a matter of great urgency concerning you all."
Gongfen, do you all understand? If you do understand, I grant you the freedom to pluck the willow blossoms with an open heart.
But if this is not yet the case, then as soon as you step outside the door, it is nothing but weeds. Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring flowers in the imperial garden bloom in succession;
Before the courtyard, the swallows chirp in harmony. If you can comprehend the true message herein, Why need a foreign monk come here on purpose?"
A questioner asked, "A student cannot distinguish between black and white; I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, "Where are your eyes?

On the Mid-Autumn Festival, Chan Master Bai Ningyi of Fuyong in Southern Chu addressed the assembly: "The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet it is difficult to behold within that very presence.
If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, voice, or language. Thus spoke the ancients.
To speak in such a manner is much like hugging a bridge pillar while bathing;

it causes later generations to mistake that which is perfectly round and brilliantly radiant for the ultimate realization, while failing to understand that the Way has no inherent nature. Thus, their pursuit goes astray.
Even if you were to sweep it all away until the azure heavens were bare, this would still be a great ailment of the Dharmakāya.

This evening, I shall not expend the slightest bit of effort, yet I will cause everyone’s constant radiance to manifest before them. Ultimately, what samādhi does one possess? [With his whisk, he draws a circle (○) and says:

Chan Master Huayan Buyan, a native of the Yang clan of Yinjiang, ascended the hall. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the World-Honored One immediately after his birth;

Such is the nature of the Dharma. In short, it is all a blur and lacks true likeness. When I, this mountain monk, reopened Longquan, the monastics and laypeople earnestly requested me to preach the Dharma.

Chan Master Xuehui of Gulaiguo ascended the hall and said: "On the level fields and shallow pastures, the moon is planted and the plow is supported;

This is the ancestral style of the ancient Buddhas—a set of worn-out tools. Today, as I stand before you all, scattering sand and tossing earth, it is much like not knowing good from bad."
However, there is one great matter that you must all take up and carry. Tell me, what is this matter? He then raised the corner of his *kāṣāya* and said:
"The moment a single thread hangs upon the body, one is naturally elegant beyond compare" (Xiao Zongmi was the successor).

The Master’s words were concise. He went to consult with Foyin Miaoxi, who said, "This is not the place for you to cast off your body and life.

The following year, he followed [Miaoxi] in shaving his hair and went to Huangbo Xiyun Qicheng to receive full ordination. Qicheng asked, "From where have you come? The Master replied, "Baolin Temple in Quanzhou."
[The Master] asked, "What do you wish to do? He replied, "I wish to seek the Buddha-dharma. [The Master] said, "In this place of mine, there is not even a single dharma.
The Master said, "This is precisely when you must apply yourself with effort. Qi silently took him to heart. One day, he asked about the story of Nanquan’s killing of the cat.
Before the words had even ceased, he was kicked down by Qi, such that the boundaries of past and future were severed and the obstruction in his chest was instantly dissolved like ice. Great!

He laughed and hurried out. Qí commanded him to lead the assembly in the hall, but the Master declined on the grounds that his merit was meager, wishing instead to carry food to provide for the community.
It happened to be the height of winter; walking through the snow in straw sandals, his feet were all cracked like tortoise shells, yet he felt no sense of weariness or suffering.

Qí was serving as the abbot at Longquan in Changle, so the Master was settled in the West Hall. When the retreat ended, he took his leave and returned to Wenling, where he resided in Zhigong’s Cave for two years. At that time...

When Qiji accepted an invitation to Fusan (Japan), he appointed the Master to succeed him on the seat and bestowed upon him a formal prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*).
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Now that spring has arrived, the scorched earth turns green again. The buds of the myriad trees emerge amidst gentle breezes and bright sunshine."
The eyes of Bodhidharma are brought forth; the nostrils of the Persian are opened wide.
These are all but the original radiance, never having flowed from any other place. Brothers, do you know this moment? If you know it, you will not depart from your seats.

Manifesting all modes of deportment without giving rise to a single thought, he sits and cuts off Mount Sumeru. When one mechanism is penetrated, a thousand mechanisms and ten thousand mechanisms become round and active;

when one place is clear, a thousand places and ten thousand places are bright and pure. Wandering freely in walking, standing, sitting, or reclining amidst the white clouds, he listens from afar to the hundred-tongued warblers chirping on the mountain ahead.
But tell me, what tune is this? (He lets out a shout. Entering the hall: By the murmuring stream.
Frost pearls adorn the precipitous peaks; hoarfrost flowers fall in scattered profusion. As the seasons shift, the yang rises and the yin recedes.
Before a single thought has arisen, the total function is revealed. Where it is expounded upon the tip of a hair, every dharma is presented.
Without the labor of carving, the original body is spontaneously perfected. Still as still water, moving like drifting clouds, one binds empty space into a single staff.
The staff does not reach him. Gathering all sounds into a single shout, he shouts before the other can respond; he holds him fast. A thousand mountains of cold color. He lets go:
eight sides are transparently clear. But tell me, is letting go better, or is holding fast better? Roots and objects are utterly detached, entirely without thingness;
unfolding or rolling up as the occasion demands is entirely free. At that time, the Min Sea region was beset by frequent alarms, and the monastic community was desolate.

The Master led the assembly to personally engage in plowing, exhorting his disciples to forget their bodies for the sake of the Way. He upheld the supreme point of realization, using deep probes and painful pressure;
thus, all students strove to exert themselves, forgetting their hardships and austerities. Those who received the milk of the Dharma were mostly men of high intelligence and brilliance.
In the year Jiachen, he visited his teacher at Guifeng, where the patron Zhou Puyuan, a member of the Ministry of Personnel, served as his benefactor.

He earnestly entreated the Master to remain as abbot. Although the Master reluctantly complied, he had already grown indifferent to worldly affairs; whenever it was time for him to ascend the hall for a small discourse (*xiaocan*), he invariably declined.
In the ninth month, he manifested illness. The assembly sent for physicians to examine him, but the Master ultimately refused them.

When the great assembly went before his bed to seek his final instructions, the Master slapped them and said, "This is the instruction; this is not the instruction. A monk then asked, "What about the final word?"
"Hmm? The Master took up his brush and wrote swiftly: "The final word cannot be spoken; who is the one who knows it? The clear breeze and the bright moon.

He then ordered his attendant to bring hot water for a bath and shaved his head. Sitting in the full lotus posture, he passed away on the sixth day of the tenth month of the Jiachen year of the Kangxi era.
His secular age was fifty, and his monastic seniority was thirty. His entire body was interred at Huangbo.
At the left foot [of the mountain] (Yinyuan Qi’s lineage):
Chan Master Xubai Yuan of Huangbo, Fuzhou, studied under Rong of Jingshan. Rong asked, "Since water has no sinews, why does it flow long and without interruption?
The Master said, "It is simply because its source has a foundation. He then asked about the public cases (gong'an) of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, which were like those in the void.
"A paper kite. Where does one pull back the line? The Master said, "The pulling and tugging depend entirely on the person inside.
He asked about Pengbo Peak and its intersection with Yanzuo Peak; "Tell me, what is being spoken of? The Master said, "One person transmits the empty."
Ten thousand people passed on the news. When asked, "When a great wind fans the vast fields, what kind of form or color does it ultimately take?
the Master said, "It is well to hear its name, but one cannot see its face. When asked, "On the Tower Overlooking the River, you set up your pivot— who is the one who knows this?

the Master said, "A fellow with no face. Later, he visited Huangbo Qi; their minds were in accord within the room, and Huangbo ordered him to succeed him on the seat. He ascended the hall and said: "Fa-chang..."
Moving the Arhats to surround the brazier: when one is poor, one’s wisdom is short. Lingyun attained enlightenment upon seeing peach blossoms; a horse that is thin has long hair.
Although each sees but one side, they cannot avoid being mutually obstructed. Today, as I open the furnace, I shall not employ "how" or "what.
I require only that you all exert some brilliance; were you to falter for even a moment, it would burn through your face.
The skull is shattered to pieces. If the mind is not the Buddha and wisdom is not the Way, then the sword has long since departed;
to mark the boat now is but a futile effort. What then? Do not merely sit beneath the three rafters or before the seven-foot mat; examine it carefully.
Suddenly, if you catch hold of your own nostrils, you will know that [the Way] is not far from you. (He lets out a shout. Question: "Heaven..."
"Last month was the full moon; in the human world, the moon is only half-full. Tell me, what is the true moon?
The Master struck a circle with his whisk and showed it to him, saying, "After the moon has set, how will you see it? The Master said, "Come tomorrow, and I will tell you.
The monk swept his sleeves and left. The Master said, "Look under your feet! He then provided a verse on the character *mi-ba* (the first character of the *Heart Sūtra*) as follows: *A*.
Who can raise these two eyebrows and slantingly insert them into the ancient stone stele facing the sun? The characters do not form [a word], and the eight are not so;
let it be taught that even the Thousand-Eyed One cannot peer therein. (Yinyuan Qi’s Succession)
Master Chan Shi Yi of Xuefeng Shengshou addressed the assembly. He cited the story of the World-Honored One holding up a flower and composed this verse:
“Great or small, Gautama could do nothing about it; He raised the flowering branch, letting it flutter in the wind.
This one great failure few people know of, Until alone was it personally laughed away by Kāśyapa. (Yinyuan Qi succeeded him.)

Master Xian Chan of the Qingsheng Grass Hut in Fujian ascended the hall. He said: "As for preaching the Buddha and preaching the Dharma, yesterday we already ended up in a state of mutual neglect by pointlessly questioning host and guest.
If I were to exclusively exalt the vehicle of the school, it would not avoid the weeds growing deep before the Dharma Hall.
When the ancients reached this point, having no other recourse, they condescended to the times of today by imparting half-verses or single words."
Brandishing the mallet, raising the whisk; rolling the ball, beating the drum; setting the arrow, holding the fork;

or closing the door all day long, facing the wall for years—directly pointing with single-minded focus, the total functioning of the great capacity. Even if one were to examine these matters, they would all belong to the affairs of the gate of construction and transformation.
But as for the ultimate vehicle of the school, how can it be proclaimed? [He] suddenly raises his staff and says: "Who dares to question it? If you do question it—"
"I shall break your waist! [With this, he] ascended the hall. Shishuang said: "Rest! Cease! A single thought for ten thousand years!
Like cold ashes and withered wood! Like an incense burner in an ancient temple! Like a single length of white silk! Yunfeng said: "Do not rest! Do not cease!
A vast expanse of karmic consciousness! Seven topsy-turvy, eight upside-down! A tumultuous clamor at the twelve street corners!"
To sit and lie amidst vast lands of sound and form; to play and roam through villages of three houses where streets and roads are choked with thorns;

to have one’s belly split and heart torn out upon mountains of knives and trees of swords; to have one’s skin flayed and flesh rot away in furnaces of charcoal and cauldrons of boiling water—thus speaks Yunfeng.
Truly, it may be said that "wherever there is water in a thousand rivers, there is the moon. Thus speaks Shishuang: still as before.
Ten thousand *li* of cloudless sky, ten thousand *li* of heaven. If you examine this closely, one person is as if dead and cannot live;
another is as if alive and cannot die. Here in my place, I do not care whether you rest or do not rest, whether you cease or do not cease.
When hungry, go eat your meal; when weary, go sleep in peace; when hot, go seek the cool; when cold...
He immediately went toward the fire. If you can understand it here, then you will understand the realization of the ancients.
Setting aside for a moment the realization of the ancients, what is the realization of Qingcheng? After a long silence, he said: "Do not take this lightly;
do not regard it as something trivial. Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddha taught all dharmas in order to deliver all minds. I have not a single..."
A heart of total sincerity—what use are all dharmas? Old Śākyamuni was far too indiscreet; in forty-nine years he had already leaked it all.
How could it be endured that Bodhidharma came from the West again, turning the direct pointing to the human mind into something circuitous?

From this point on, the five ranks were established with ruler and subject, and ninety-seven types of expressions displayed their ugliness and clumsiness. "Examining" and "Hah! became a single-character barrier, and the mind-consciousness was broken into pieces.
Two stakes. Even if you carry the seven matters with you at all times, you cannot avoid becoming a mere trackway by now.
The ancestral fields are subject to endless contention, until they are torn asunder in every direction—seven parts here and eight there. To cite the present or the past is but to melt mud;
to speak of the wondrous or the primal is but a speck of dust in the eye. At times one blinks or raises an eyebrow; at times one extends a fist or dangles a foot. This is the stirring.
Proclaiming the fundamental tenets and establishing the gates of transformation, everyone vies to take a turtle and certify it as a soft-shelled tortoise.

If a person were to simply accept this right here, I dare say that such a person has not yet reached the ultimate realization. I now use a wedge to drive out a wedge; tell me, is this speaking or is it not speaking?
If you say it is speaking, what is being said? If you say it is not speaking, the speaking does not cease. Whether it is speaking or not speaking—let it be so for now.
Set it aside. I venture to ask the assembly present here: does the mind exist right now, or not? If you have no mind, then I shall desist.
Do not mock this mountain monk for being so loquacious. (Guǎngxìn Mí sì)
Chan Master Ruhu Hong of Xuefeng in Quanzhou was the son of the Liu family from Huian. In his youth, he enrolled in the local school and achieved distinguished renown for his literary talent.
At the age of twenty-seven, he was afflicted with a severe illness; upon reading the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa Sūtra*, he resolved to leave the secular world.

Later, while traveling on the road in Huian, he encountered Huangbo Mi, whose words pierced him like a sharp awl, instantly giving rise to a state of profound doubt. He then applied himself with all his might to the practice of Zen inquiry.

Jiuxiu studied under Baizhang for more than ten years, penetrating deeply into the inner sanctum. One day, Baizhang asked him, "The sound of raindrops falling before the eaves—drop by drop, they do not fall elsewhere;
where, after all, do they fall? The Master replied, "They fall into the nostrils."
Mihu nodded in agreement and ordered him to reside in the West Hall. He composed a verse on the karmic conditions of childbirth in a cave, saying:

"Emaciated for the sake of my husband, I am ashamed before him; Twisting and turning through ten thousand turns, I am loath to leave my bed. A favorable message suddenly arrives, dissolving old resentments; In the morning, facing the mirror, I arrange my rouge and powder.
He also composed a verse on the karmic conditions of Mazu gazing at the moon, saying: "A pair of fine birds perch together, claiming a single branch."
Soaring high with sturdy wings, he alone is called extraordinary. If one were to weigh his words and judge their worth, one would laugh oneself to death at Jiangxi’s Ma Boji.
The verse on the occasion of the Old Mother of the Eastern City says: In her life she never favored Buddha. This mother’s style of conduct truly carries on the lineage.
Between the seams of her ten fingers there is no place of concealment; looking at it, it is still but a flower in the eye. — Evening.
In his later years, he retired to live at Keisui (High Ridge Spring) at the foot of a mountain. He announced the date of his passing in advance and subsequently passed away (succeeded by Jinko).
Chan Master Mingjue Hanpu Cong of Haihui Temple in Beijing was the son of the Lin family of Lian in Shaowu, Southern Min.

While his mother was sitting in the courtyard one night, she saw a star enter her bosom and became pregnant. Later, a red light shone over her room, and the master was born there. At the age of ten...

5. At the age of twenty-five, he went to Chujia Tianwang Temple. Disgusted by the mediocre and uninspiring nature of the monks in his local prefectures and counties, he was moved by a profound sense of resolve to pursue spiritual study.
Consequently, he traveled to Putuo Mountain in the South Sea to receive full ordination. He then proceeded to Pingyao in Wulin, where he met Yongjue Xian.
Xian instructed him to apply himself to the practice of "the myriad dharmas returning to the One. After one year, [his progress] was like that of a mosquito...
The student bit into an iron ox; there was simply no place for his teeth to sink in. Next, he studied under Dongshan Ermu. Suddenly, he attained realization.

In the evening, he went to the abbot’s quarters and reported what he had gained. Ermu nodded in approval. He then traveled to Mount Tiantai, where he engaged in a kōan exchange with the elder Tongxuan Qi that struck the vital point.
He was appointed to the position of *karmadāna*. Later, while chewing rice, he encountered a grain of grit, which triggered a sudden, thorough penetration into the teachings of Dongshan and Xuefeng.
In the "Case of Washing Rice," his doubts were suddenly resolved. He composed a verse to present to the Abbot, who, recognizing its profound depth, gave him his approval.

Subsequently, he visited Bachi Yuan at Changqing and received the transmission of the Dharma. This was during the summer of the Wuzi year of the Shunzhi era. He went forth to reside at Jingshan in Lin’an and Guangfu in Qiantang.
Later, because his influence spread to the Capital (Jintai), the officials and scholars there submitted a formal petition requesting his presence.
The Master resided at Haihui Temple in Nanhai. His fame had reached the imperial court.
In the autumn of the Dingyou year, Emperor Shizu (the Kangxi Emperor) visited Haihui Temple in person.
The Abbot was granted a seat, and the Emperor questioned him on Buddhist kōans. The Master responded accordingly.
The affinity was profound.

He received an imperial decree ordering him to enter Wanshan Hall for the retreat. He was specially granted purple robes, a silver seal, and an imperial edict, with the title "Chan Master Mingjue" conferred upon him.
In the winter of the Jihai year.
By imperial decree, he was ordered to enter the retreat at Minzhong Temple. In the autumn of the gengzi year, he submitted a memorial requesting to return south.

In the eighth month, having received the imperial mandate, he took his leave and departed. In the xinchou year, he entered Min Province. The Prefectural Marquis of Shaowu, Shen Jin, and others invited him to reside at Anguo Temple, where he ascended the hall and, raising his staff, said:
"A net is spread across the heavens, intending to ensnare the golden phoenix soaring through the void. With his staff...
Making a gesture of fishing, he said: "The four seas cast their hooks, intending to catch the brocade carp amidst the surging waves.
Thus, when a master of knowledge leads others, the meaning does not reside in the words. Raising a whisk or striking the meditation seat, they uphold that which lies beyond the threshold.

Deshan saw a monk and immediately struck him, overturning the old dwelling of the numinous serpent. Linji saw a monk and immediately shouted, shattering the black mountains within the ghost cave. Even if one were before words..."
To "attain through recommendation" is still to mistake the shadow for the head; to "turn one's body beneath the phrase" already involves traveling ten thousand miles.

He descended from his seat. He entered the hall for formal discourse: "The sky is cold and the earth frozen; the monks’ hair stands on end with cold. [How can one find warmth?]"
When discussing this in one’s chamber, one immediately falls into a state of indeterminate drowsiness. Therefore, Xuedou said:

With three thousand [blows] upon the crown of his head and eight hundred behind his neck, he possesses the armor to confront the army of birth and death, and the spearhead to battle the ranks of affliction. If there is anyone beneath the skin who still has blood, let them consider this."
Upon hearing this mention, his entire body broke into a sweat; he felt a sense of joy and liberation beyond doubt.

Herein, he sits securely upon the divine platform and the secret treasury, like a solitary *gandharva* guarding an empty stream. I, the mountain monk, have now turned the prow of the boat and shall steer a different course across the misty waves.
Suddenly, he held up his staff and said: "Wooden Seat-Monk, you have just now traveled throughout lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges."

From the earth above, reaching as far as the Heaven of the Thirty-three, down to the water-circle and the limits of space—turning one’s head for a single thought-moment, he sits upon the brows and eyelashes of all people.
Raising his voice, he cries out: "The people of Jambudvīpa have lost their homes to fire!
It brings misery upon the people of Pūrvavideha, who flee in great terror. Fortunately, they encounter Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, who says: 'All of you are [enlightened beings]...'"
“O deluded sentient beings! Why must you give rise to such great terror, crying out and fleeing?

If you can merely still the mind’s false imaginings, the fire of the karma of the three poisons will naturally and instantly be extinguished. Then, they joined their palms and said: “We have encountered the Buddha Vehicle;
it points us toward the gate of liberation. We feel that this is most difficult to encounter. From this day forward, we shall never again retreat or yield.”
He then planted his staff upright and said, "The wooden monk shall serve as your witness. A question was asked: "What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'?
The Master replied: "The birds sing freshly in the woods; human tracks have vanished from the wild paths. The questioner asked:

"What is 'taking away the environment but not the person'? The Master replied: "The falling flowers and flowing water depart; the fisherman picks them up. The questioner asked: "What is... [the third case]...?
"Both person and environment are simultaneously negated. The Master said, "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*; upon this seat there is no old monk.
[The student] asked, "What is it like when neither person nor environment is negated? The Master said, "Where has the white cloud gone? In whose house does the bright moon fall?

The Master resided at Anguo for six years, restoring all that was dilapidated and ruined until it was newly renovated. On the eighth day of the twelfth month of the Bingwu year, his period of precept observance was completed.
The assembly gathered in full, and he entrusted his final instructions to them and distributed his robes and bowl. At noon on the thirteenth day, he took up his brush and wrote this verse:
"This year I am fifty-seven; I have crushed my mother’s nose. Throughout my entire life of experience, there is neither gain nor loss."
Last night, two earthen oxen fought their way into the sea; until this very day, there has been no news. *Ei!* This is the true news.
This morning, the wall of the eastern corridor was knocked down by the western corridor. Pack up the puppets and go home; do not let things fall into such deliberate disorder.
He set down his brush and passed away on his right side. His secular age was fifty-seven; his monastic seniority was thirty-nine. [His] stupa.
To the right of the mountain temple, there are sixteen volumes of his recorded sayings (*yulu*) in circulation (compiled by Bai-chi Yuan-si).
Chan Master Su of Lianfeng at Ximing on Mount Shishan in Xinghua Prefecture was the son of the Ke family of Putian. During his childhood...

Upon seeing the mountains and waters, he immediately gave rise to the aspiration to transcend the mundane. At the age of twenty-seven, he entered the presence of Guohuan and, under the guidance of the reclusive elder, left the white robes of lay life behind.

He once studied the records of Xuefeng; upon reaching the passage where Touzi pointed to a flat stone and said, "All Buddhas of the three periods are entirely contained within this," he investigated it for half a year, yet his state of doubt remained unresolved. He then went up to Caoshan and questioned Baohua Ren. Ren took up [the matter].
“Strike! The Master was enlightened upon being struck once. Later, he visited Yuan of Jinsu at Bai Mountain in Jianzhou; there, the needle met the eye, and he received the seal of transmission.
After taking up residence, he ascended the hall and said: “The Great Way is as straight as a bowstring; the great capacity is as swift as an arrow.

Without moving a single hair’s tip, there are a thousand transformations and ten thousand changes. Originally, there are no people of sharp or dull faculties; one simply requires realization when the opportunity arises. Gao.
The sun hangs in the sky; a fragrant breeze strikes the face. The journey is long and far, yet not separated by so much as a single thread. Two or three notes of birdsong from the branches;
scattered petals of red flowers fall one after another. Ascending the hall on the Buddha’s Birthday: Birth is fundamentally non-birth, yet there is nothing that is not born.
Pointing to heaven, pointing to earth—how most clearly manifest! This episode of elegance in the blue garden must rely upon the feet of descendants.
Descending from the hall, he brandished his whisk and said, "Śākyamuni was born! Does the great assembly see him yet? He threw down the whisk, descended from his seat, and ascended the hall.
"There is one person who eats ten thousand things every day and does not say they are full;

there is another person who, from antiquity until now, has not eaten a single thing and does not say they are hungry. Of these two people, which one deserves to receive the offerings of devas and humans?"
Ascending the hall in autumn, he said: "The pine wind is clear and the mountain stream is crisp. In the eighth month of autumn, where is there heat?

When the heavens are hot, they are cool at times; when humans are hot, there is no respite. If you wish for respite, you must turn your head and see the moon of Mount Ling. This very moon is neither full nor deficient;
it has shone upon the world from antiquity to the present, not waiting until this very night to become bright and pure. He then looked around.
Looking to his left and right, he said, "Do you all see? The assembly was all at a loss. The Master descended from his seat and immediately dispersed them.
A monk asked, "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas; why was he unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi? The Master said, "The official does not permit even a needle.
The monk asked, "Wangming is a Bodhisattva from the lower regions; why was he able to emerge from the woman’s samādhi? The Master said, "The official does not permit even a needle."
The Master said, "Privately passing through with carriage and horse. The monk asked, "As for Mañjuśrī and Wangming, where do gain and loss lie?
The Master struck him and said, "Try to point it out and see! As the monk hesitated, the Master gave a shout. The old monk asked, "When humans and devas meet, both are able to see one another.
But tell me, what is it they see? The Master pinched his nose and said, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "No."

[The Master] said, "For eighty years, my head has been white for nothing. Question: "When ten thousand thoughts arise, from where do they originate? The Master said: "One passes through a thicket of flowers;
not a single petal clings to one's body. Question: "Before a single thought arises, where does it cease?

The Master said: "Nowhere to be grasped. Question: "A fierce tiger does not eat its own offspring; why then does the dragonfly [eat its own]?*" *Note: The final question appears to be an incomplete or metaphorical inquiry regarding the nature of instinctive or karmic continuity.*
"Chewing on one's own tail. The Master said, "Seeking from others is not as good as seeking within oneself" (Baichi Yuan’s succession).
Chan Master Jushan Gumen Zhen of Pucheng was the son of the Pan family of Chaoyang. At the age of nineteen, he entered Daocao Monastery to become a monk.
Initially, he studied under Huangbo Qi, who showed him the koan regarding "throwing down the bannerpole in front of the gate," yet for a long time he made no progress.
While staying there, one day he entered the Abbot’s quarters to seek instruction. Huairang held up his fist and asked, “Do you understand? The Master said, “I do not understand.
Huairang then struck him with his palm. The Master prostrated himself. Huairang said, “When going downhill, one does not run; such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter. The Master was at a loss.
The following year, he returned to Daishan Temple in Zhangzhou. One evening, while outside the mountain gate with his fellow practitioners, the Master brought up the phrase, “Throwing down the gate.”
Before the sound of the preceding *kṣa* (boundary-post) had died away, his fellow practitioner Jiangshi struck him across the face with a single palm. Thereupon, he attained realization.
Later, while relying on Yuan of Jinsu, one evening Yuan descended from the hall to conduct an examination, asking:

"This is a fine assembly of ancient Buddhas; why do they not emit light? The Master let out a shout. Instantly, his entire being was filled with joy and liberation. He then composed this verse: "Under the [囗@力] ground..."
The source of sound has its basis; it is vast and empty, liberated, and utterly without support. With eyes empty of the four seas, one clearly perceives the essential point:
this very splendor is known only by oneself. Afterward, the Master presided over various monasteries, including Mafeng, Jianfu, and Shanzheng;
his recorded sayings from these assemblies circulate in the world. (Baichi Yuan was his successor.)
Chan Master Qianzhiguang of Caoshan Wanshou in Xinghua Prefecture ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he struck it once and called to a monk from the east;
the monk raised his head. He then struck the staff again and called to a monk from the west.

The monk raised his head. [The Master] then cast down his staff and said: "To take this profound mind and offer it to every dust mote and world-system—this is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The source of the Way is not far; the ocean of nature is not distant. He let out a shout and said:
"So it turns out, it is right here! He spoke again: "What is this here? It is Zhaozhou’s 'cypress tree,' and Yangqi’s 'three...'"
[He] kicked the donkey. Again, he let out a shout and said: "When meeting people, do not speak erroneously. Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"A single speck of dust enters right-reception (*samyak-samādhi*); from every speck of dust, samādhi arises. He then struck his whisk once and said:
"This is the single speck of dust. What do you call 'right-reception'? He struck it again and said: "This is right-reception. What do you call 'a single speck of dust'?"
"Do you understand? It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not an object. The meditation board and the sitting mat leap up together! He then let out a shout and said:
"Had I not shouted to arrest you, you would have nearly run right over the Buddhas of the three periods of time. [He ascended the hall: "A thousand explanations, ten thousand explanations..."

"It is not as good as seeing it face-to-face. If you call it a fist, it is 'contact' (touch); if you do not call it a fist, it is 'separation' (back). What thing is this that is neither seen nor unseen?
When the cup falls to the ground, the saucer breaks into seven pieces. Ascending the hall, he said: "When the single principle is sufficient, all matters are complete;
when a single speck of dust arises, the entire great earth is gathered up. He let out a shout and said, "If you can understand this one shout..."
The entire earth is brilliantly clear; there is not a single thing to act as an obstruction or hindrance.
Even so, it causes my descendants to perish. (He lets out another shout. Ascending the hall: Peach blossoms are red, plum blossoms are white;
this is precisely the second month of spring. There is a source, yet no definitive end: a shooting star flies from the land of Silla. It turns out to be North Kuru.
"Beating raw iron on Reed Island. Again, he cited National Teacher Huizhong calling to his attendant; the attendant responded.
Thus he called three times and the attendant responded three times. The National Teacher said, "I thought it was I who had failed you, but it turns out it was you who failed me.
The Master said, "What a magnificent melody! The response is perfectly clear; it is enough to make the mountains and rivers dance and the great earth sing in unison."
Where did the National Teacher fail the Attendant? Where did the Attendant fail the National Teacher? He gave a shout and said:
"The young maiden has already returned to the celestial realms; the simpleton still dwells by the fire. He asked:
"Having eaten the rice of Niu-tou, one sleeps peacefully atop a solitary peak; having drunk the wine of Cao-shan, one is at the crossroads of the city street."
[The monk] lay down on his back. "What kind of person's realm is this? The Master struck him. The monk shouted. The Master struck him again. The monk performed a woman’s bow.
The Master said, "I took you for a man. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Cao Shan?
The Master said, "The ten thousand pines do not change their former appearance. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Those who sit, sit."
Lidili asked, "What is Zhaozhou’s tea? The Master said, "Universal. He asked, "What is Yunmen’s cake? The Master said, "Bitter.
He asked, "When eating both cake and tea together, what then? The Master said, "Poisoned to death, you fellow! (Baichi Yuan was his successor).
Master Yuechuan Jie of Xinghua Shishi Fuhu Rock was a native of Putian. His surname was Zhang and his mother’s was Zhou.
On the eve of the Master’s birth, an extraordinary light filled the room. From childhood, he was exceptionally brilliant and surpassed his peers.

In his youth, he would read esoteric texts by lamplight every night without ceasing, even during wind and rain. He consistently ranked first in all examinations. In the year of Bingxu, he finally renounced the secular arts.
He abandoned his brushes and inkstone and entered Mount Hushan at Nanquan to receive the tonsure. He traveled extensively to consult various monastic centers.
Later, he attained realization with Yuan of Jingu Temple and received his formal entrustment. Upon returning to Putian, he resided at Shuangfengyan on West Mountain, followed by a tenure at Xueyan.
Later, he dwelt in the Stone Chamber at Fuhuyan; opening the furnace, he ascended the hall for forty-nine years.

The yellow leaves used to stop a child’s crying—whether in the Western Heaven or this Eastern Land, people have merely received the echoes and inherited the emptiness. To speak according to reality, there is no ground for the Buddhas or the Patriarchs to open their mouths.
This is precisely the Elder. From what source does he speak of the Great Way? It has been level as the palm of a hand from the beginning;
why need hearths and stoves be separately arranged? Raising his staff, he said: "One cannot help but follow the custom of watching the fire and adding wood.
If it is true gold, its color will not change; let even dull iron be made into fine material. Radiant and brilliant, beyond all doubt—cast it into the eyes of everyone."

[The Master] comes forward, gives a shout, and says: "What is this? You must be careful! He enters the hall, disperses the assembly, snaps his staff in two, claps his hands, and laughs loudly, saying:
"Today I set out small, yet encountered the great. He enters the hall again.

Having traveled the winding paths of the high mountains, he arrives at level ground, yet finds it perilous and suspicious. Do not say that the scenery on other mountains is better; blood is spattered [upon the earth].
The cuckoo calls out, "Not returning! Returning! Returning! and immediately arrives at the fields of one's native village; yet it still lacks that single blow to the crown of the head.
Entering the hall, setting up arrows and banners, brandishing pitchforks and dancing with swords—all these are merely clumsy tricks used to frighten and deceive children.
If one is grand and upright, opening wide like the eight characters, let those who eat congee eat congee, and let those who drink tea drink tea.
At Stone Bridge there is no obstruction; on the Great Road there is no hindrance. All people go straight ahead;
everywhere the green willows can tether the horse, and every house has a road leading to Chang'an. [Ascending the hall: Before it is opened...

Before a word has left the mouth, the Buddha-dharma is already spread across the great earth. Raising a fist or raising a whisk is adding mud upon soil; explaining the essentials or the source is feeling for snow amidst the frost.
How could the Buddhas of the three periods have ever known it? The patriarchs of successive generations have merely labored in vain with their tongues.
Here, one simply tends to the vegetables and weeds the eggplants; how would there be leisure to let a speck of dust fall into the eye? Thereupon, [he] took up the whisk.
[The Master] pinched his own mouth and said, "This old monk’s teeth have broken in his mouth-gate. On the day of his birthday, the Master ascended the hall and said:
"The World-Honored One [attained enlightenment] on the eighth day of the fourth month; this mountain monk [was born] on the eighth day of the tenth month.

Both are the eighth day. One cast gold; one forged iron. One has saved beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; the other cannot even save himself. Why did Śākyamuni say, 'How marvelous! All..."
"All sentient beings possess the wisdom, virtue, and marks of the Tathāgata. [The Master] let out a shout and said: "Let the snow accumulate on Mount Emei as it pleases;
the waters of the Canghai Sea still flow eastward. Ascending the hall, he said: "The western wind blows a fine rain;
fallen leaves fill the empty courtyard. Without a word, the lamp-flower falls; the needle stops, and tears fall of their own accord. Tell me, what matter is so urgent? Let go!"

It cannot be lowered, nor can it be raised; it shines brightly and extends continuously before one's eyes. Those who are sorrowful fear only those who listen to their sorrow—this is the small instruction.
Longtan extinguished the paper candle; Deshan produced light in the darkness. Yanguan sought the rhinoceros horn;
the attendant turned his body and found a path. Although this is merely passing through a borrowed route, one must still provide for oneself. As for capturing the fierce...

For a dragon to seize a fierce tiger is not considered extraordinary; however, if affairs pass and the mind cools, if the scenery shifts and things change, do not blame this mountain monk for his tongue lacking strength.
Addressing the assembly: Since immeasurable kalpas past, you have wandered through birth and death like a wayward son who has left his home, day by day further from it.
When will you ever return? He gave a shout and said: "Who is there to obstruct you?"
Question: "The Buddha-dharma requires those of superior faculties and superior vessels; those of inferior capacity have no share in it. The Master said: "Who does not see the moon atop the tower?
How many pines and winds are there to block one's ears? Question: "What is the家风 (household style) of the Master? The Master said:
"A half-section of bamboo pipe carries the flowing stream; several flecks of idle clouds pass over the distant mountains. [The questioner] said: [Silence].
The Master used the external world to point it out to people. The Teacher said, "I have lost one eye.
Once, while the Teacher was looking at the moon, a monk asked, "The same moon—why is it sometimes bright and sometimes dark, sometimes full and sometimes incomplete?
The Teacher said, "What you ask about is the second moon. The monk asked, "What is the first moon? The Teacher said, "It illuminates heaven and earth."
(Bai Chi Yuan Si). *Wudeng Quanshu*, Volume 89, Supplement.

Chan Master Wude Ning of Yuxiang Longhua in Ningde, Fujian, during a small-scale public address (*xiaochan*) while on a tour: Riding the Fragrant Wind.
Seeking the bright moon, I have traversed the clouds and mists; how extraordinary! Last night at West Rock’s Taibai Peak, light was emitted that shook the earth, and the thousand mountains rejoiced.
But tell me, what did they rejoice in? One person has cause for celebration, and ten thousand people enjoy their work.
Winter Night Small Sermon: The yin wanes and the yang waxes; the cycles of transformation shift. A flower blooms upon a withered tree—this is the livelihood of a man of the Way. Do not...

Studying like one who drills tortoise shells and beats ceramic tiles, one must know the timing and conditions of circumstances. Whether speaking or remaining silent, moving or still, one must act with what is appropriate.

In every gesture and action, one must discern when to adapt and when not to adapt. There are countless people who strike their heads and bump their foreheads [in this pursuit] (Yinyuan Qi was his successor).
Small Assembly by Chan Master Leye of Chao Mountain in Minnan. The thousand peaks rise abruptly; ten thousand trees are lush and verdant.
Outside the gate the rooster crows; before the hall the dog barks. Each and every thing is authentically true, fundamentally free from prohibition.
Being free from prohibition, he opens both eyes wide facing the blue sky—do not nod off during your leisure time! A monk asked: "When one encounters a person who has attained the Way on the road..."
"If you do not respond with speech or silence, I wonder what you will use to respond?
The Master said, "It is either a punch or a kick" (Yinyuan Qi was his successor).
Small Assembly by Chan Master Zhizhi of Shengquan in Fuzhou. In the fifteen days prior, the jade hare and golden crow [the sun and moon] rush like split arrows.
In the fifteen days following, the earthen ox enters the sea with no news. On the fifteenth day itself, every person has eyes askance and a straight nose.
This matter has been fundamentally manifest from the beginning; why need one go out of one's way to seek it? (Yinyuan)
(Qi succeeded him).
At Fúlú Temple in Fújiàn, Master Shíxué Línwáng ascended the hall and said: "This matter has no place for concealment; it is the naked reality of the present moment.

The mountain colors are exquisite in the four directions, and wildflowers bloom anew across the earth. If, thirty years ago, you had taken this as an object of conceptualization... (text fragmentary) ...three...
Ten years later, one realizes that all things are but mind. Reaching this point, do not treat it as something ordinary. Do you understand?
"I have long lamented that the spring light has nowhere to be found; today, I turn toward this mountain. (Seishin Mitsusoku)
Chan Master Zhongmei Kuang of Zhaoqing Temple in Quanzhou, Fujian, was the son of the Cai family of Tong’an.

He addressed the assembly: "The azure sky maddens the sun, spreading a thousand brocades; green willows follow the wind, unfolding ten thousand strands. Everything that meets the eye is a manifest reality;
why need one open one’s mouth to speak of the 'Elegant Spring'? There is not a single thing that does not open for all people the wondrous gate of universal penetration. There is not one...
At that time, he did not reveal the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye for the sake of all people. Why must we wait further for this mountain monk to beat his two pieces of skin?
Even if you were to grasp it and bring it forth, the sword has long since departed. (Guangxin Misu)
