"Who can testify to this Way? He raised his staff and said, "The Oxhead Monk is coming!
He struck the ground once and asked, "What is the road to Caoxi? The Master replied, "East, west, south, north. A monk pointed at the sky and said, "Who can move it?
The Master said, "Bring me the robe from the rack. The monk turned around; the Master said, "He moves! He moves!"

On the second day before the Buddha’s birthday in the Jiachen year of the Kangxi era, the Master manifested a slight ailment. He gathered the assembly and announced his intention to depart for a time.
A lay disciple asked again what the Master’s intent was. The Master said, "I have only one prostration. Having finished speaking, he passed away.

He summoned his attendant, had him support his two feet as he ascended [the seat], and sat down to deliver his discourse. He was then enshrined in a stupa to the east of the monastery (this being the ancient custom).
Chan Master Jian’an Yuan of Qingxiu Monastery in Changyang, Tanzhou, a native of the Liu family of Taoci in Ezhou, ascended the hall and said:
The spring day is bright; the spring birds sing. Throughout the myriad phenomena of the universe, everywhere the absolute truth is revealed.

The ox on open ground suddenly turns its body over. Fragrance wafts from the shadowless tree; flowers bloom upon branches that have not yet sprouted. The Yellow River begins to thaw as warmth first returns;
across ten thousand valleys and a thousand crags, the verdant colors are fresh anew. (In the style of the ancients, by Ran Si.)
Chan Master Lin’an Tianmu Longmen Yinghǒu Zhèn was the son of the Huang family of Lánhuáng in Chǔ.

While traveling to Mount Tiānmù, he passed the old site of Longmén and took a liking to its secluded and remote scenery. He cast his meditation cushion inside an ancient bell and sat in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) for seven days.
Later, when woodcutters and herdsmen entered the mountains, they beheld the Master and were struck with awe. News of this spread far and wide, reaching the local gentlemen of the village.
He revered his teacher’s virtue and character, attending his seat for instruction without a single day of omission. In less than a few years, he had suddenly established a magnificent monastery;
whatever is found in the monastic groves was fully provided there. Ascending the hall, he said: "Since our parting at Vulture Peak many years have passed.
Today we come again to discuss the ancestral barrier. Taking up a single whisk of tortoise-hair, I issue a brand-new decree to be passed down. Now tell me:"
"What is the proof? he asked. Huibei Zhi said: "A single drop from the Cao-Source can bring life to the solitary peak; it shall circulate among humanity for billions of years.
[The Master] then cited the anecdote of Mazu’s "Hiding His Head" (where his head turned black and then white), and composed this verse:
"The cuckoo on the branch calls for spring to return; The rain envies the peach blossoms, staining the mud with blood. Who clearly understands this underlying intent? It still instructs the void..."
Crying toward the fifth watch (a style of ancient verse by Gu Furan Si).

Master Dajian Yuanxiang Qian of Dongchan Temple in Huating addressed the assembly: "This morning happens to coincide with the Double Ninth Festival. Suddenly I recall those guests who climbed the heights and dropped their caps.

One should know that autumn has matured and the chrysanthemums are yellow; they evoke the unceasing sentiment of Yuanming. Investigate!"* *Note: "Yuanming" refers to Tao Yuanming (陶淵明), the famous poet of the Jin dynasty, renowned for his love of chrysanthemums and his famous poem "Drinking Wine. The Master uses this allusion to prompt the assembly to investigate the nature of their own minds.*
Mysterious men, each reflect upon yourselves! Do not bury your heads and become deluded guests. You must urgently exert fierce effort and apply your spirit;
even if you were to bite through a cold-iron scale-weight until it bleeds, you might suddenly encounter that which all know. Ultimately, how shall one make this discernment?
After a long silence, he said: "Autumn leaves are like flowers, red as if soaked in rain; swaying with the wind, they fall into a state of disarray. (This is the style of the ancient masters.
Chan Master Donglian Fayuan Tan of Hangzhou, a native of the Han family from Yaojiang in Yue, gave a small lecture:
"The Buddha-body fills the Dharma-realm, universally manifesting before all sentient beings. By day one sees light; by night one sees darkness. Clouds rise..."
The birds fly; the mountains are green and the waters are azure. Of various species and different kinds—men and women, monks and laypeople—tell me, where is the Buddha?
He then held up his whisk and said: "A single moon rises over the sea; how many families ascend the tower? [This was] the public instruction given during a great snowfall.
The snow is deep and the eaves drip with a *peng-peng* sound; it is reported that the true lineage of Yangqi is being carried forth.

Shattering the void until it is a single color, overturning the great earth so that not a speck of dust remains. Samantabhadra’s strategy failed and his vital mechanism was exposed; Mañjuśrī was terrified and fled in haste.
This has brought trouble upon Samantamukha, who is now in a state of constant agitation, searching secretly from house to house. (Gufeng Ran, the successor).
Chan Master Yeqian Yuan of Sheng’an, Hangzhou, a native of the Yu family of Zhuji, addressed the assembly: “Clusters of flowers, clusters of brocade;

the wind and moon of Gaoteng are ancient, and the household provisions of Half-Mountain are sufficient. When Tao Qian invited friends to join the society, crimson maples carpeted the ground beneath the yellow chrysanthemums.
Revealing that which was before the birth of father and mother—this is the original true face of every person.”
The Master brandished his whisk and said: "I inform you, sirs: you must exert yourselves! The iron walls and silver mountains are all pulverized;
amidst a flash of lightning, a thunderclap resounds. He let out a shout. He then offered a verse on Xinghua’s dismissal of the *vina* (steward):

"Not seeking to strike the grass, yet intending to startle the snake; A ruthless hand belongs only to a veteran master. With a sudden crash of thunder, wind and rain pass by; One may now gaze upon the azure sky."
Blossoming Clear Clouds (in the style of *gufeng* by Ransi).
Chan Master Jie of Gu’an at Shousheng Monastery in Xiuzhou ascends the hall: For a long time I have not ascended the hall, keeping the door closed in stillness;

today, for a special purpose, I manifest my full capacity. Where the flowing water and falling flowers forget one another, does the traveler at the ends of the earth return or not? The plum blossoms...
"When the fruit ripens, the news is good; days grow long, and with nothing to do, one watches the clouds fly.
"Great assembly, if you treat this as a matter for Buddhist doctrine, it is like attaching a handle to a begging bowl. If you treat it as worldly discourse, you bury your own spiritual essence.
But ultimately, how can one attain the perfect state? Listen! He brandished his whisk and said: "The spring colors have no high or low; the flower branches have their short and long. (Quifu Ming-si)
Chan Master Ling of Zhencheng Zu Peak in Shaoxing was the son of the Wang family of Shanyin. He ascended the hall and, holding up his whisk, said:
"If one speaks of this very thing, it is the most honored among those in heaven; it is the most noble among people; it is the sovereign among all dharmas;
it is the greatest among all things. If you can penetrate through to this point, then the Buddhas of the three periods of time..."
All people are non-dual. All people are no different from the Buddhas of the three periods of time; they are without duality and without distinction.
Radiant and brilliant, the myriad phenomena are arrayed within a single palm, completely transcending the ocean of lands of the great trichiliocosm (Xingkong Zhen).
Chan Master Wujianqing of Fusheng Monastery in Lin’an, a native of the Xu family from Lujiang, ascended the hall and said: “A lion cub emerging from its lair lets out a single roar;
foxes, wolves, and jackals all hide away. When the universe is lifted up, there is nothing at all; the mountain colors remain as they have been from of old until now.
Ascending the hall again, he said: “The precious mirror is set upon the stand; the Mohe Moai sword is held in the palm. The meaning within this is particularly—”
To propagate [the Dharma], he raised up the broken sand-basin and restored the old regulations.

He sought to ensure that the single stream of the Hutuo River would have a distant source and a long flow, so that the ancestral style might flourish and the sound of the Dharma resound. In his chamber, mists and clouds constantly shimmered with color;
as he brandished his whisk, flowers rained down like celestial incense. (Gongheng Rensu)
Chan Master Neng of Baiyan at Qizhou Fasheng Monastery was the son of the Gu clan of that same prefecture. He ascended the hall and said: "The wind has just subsided and the rain has newly cleared;
the fishing boat is light amidst the peach-blossom waves. The willow eyes unfurl their golden buds to welcome the green water;

from the lofty trees, the orioles sing in harmony with the clear air. The myriad phenomena are distinct and clearly manifest—what need is there for further repeated pointing out? After a long silence, he said:
Do not fail the mountain monk (Duguang Jingsi). Master Choufeng An of Qixian in Hanyang addressed the assembly:
Autumn leaves fill the mountains and rivers; today we celebrate the Emperor and open the hall. Reeds and flowers drift across both banks;
now is precisely the time to strike the bells and beat the drums. Turn your heads toward the winds of the state of Chu.

Light. Treading the steps into the Dharma-cave of the former masters, the pavilions rise one above another. Ten billion devas dwell amidst the azure mist that embraces the river as the wind sighs faintly.

Behold the five thousand *palm-leaf* scrolls as if they were painted pictures; the boat carries a whole river of wind. Fame and profit clothe men in finery, yet they cannot exhaust the eight-foot space where one sleeps at night.
Turning over and over, dreams pull at the mind, and sleep is not much. Thus it is said: "Within the red dust..."
The Buddha-dharma is preached in every dust mote and in every world-system, proclaimed with fervor day and night without ceasing.
It is not something to be carried upon one's head at a mountain pass; how could it be sought out from Mount Kukkutapāda? (Duguang Jingsi)
Master Chan Li-xianxu of Yushan in Hanyang ascends the hall: "The forge and bellows are spread wide this day; Endlessly chewing rice to feed an infant.
Not knowing who among the seedlings is fit to take up the task— Is it not difficult indeed to perpetuate our lineage?
Ascending the hall: "Spring returns to the great earth; Grasses and trees flourish with renewed luster. The traveler on the road has just plucked the willow; The wanderer in the village..."
A guest explores the fragrant spring. Only the peach buds are about to open. How many can compare to Lingyun (who alone stands supreme among his successors)?
Master Lurzi Ren of the Bamboo Pavilion in Huanggang ascends the hall: "Snow upon snow, the heavens freeze and the earth cracks.
The crow’s beak is flat; it calls out in the cold but cannot reach through. The rock is large if it is large, small if it is small. The pine branch is bald if it is bald."
Pointed bottom, pointed tip. South Mountain and North Mountain strike their foreheads against one another all at once.
I ask you all: what is the underlying principle? Again, he said: "Kuo. Entering the hall, he said: "The gates are wide open. Mountains are mountains; waters are waters. To stay is permissible;
to leave is also permissible. The sack has been untied. Heaven is heaven; earth is earth. To sit is permissible; to lie down is also permissible. Nevertheless—"
Abiding in freedom, moving unimpeded in all directions—yet this mountain monk’s staff refuses to let him off. Why?
It is easy to meet one another, but difficult to dwell together (Du Guanjingsi).
Chan Master Qingliang Juewu Zu, a nun of the Zhao family from Hangzhou, addressed the assembly. She cited the karmic occasion of Nanquan selling himself and said:
"Nanquan only knew how to set the price, but he did not look ahead; although that monk understood how to look ahead..."
He did not understand to look back. If the Venerable Zu had been there at that time, he would have waited for him to say, "I will neither buy it as something noble nor as something base;
how would you buy it? and then have struck him three blows. Why? Because "the heart does not betray the person, and the face shows no shame. Upon leaving the Barrier, he gave a small discourse:
"The one who originally opened the Barrier is the very person who closes it. Each time it is brought forth, it is fresh once more. Eight-sided..."
Linglong is as clear as a mirror; throughout the worlds of the ten directions, his entire body appears. (Xuzhou Xing, successor to [Zhaozhou]).
When Chan Master Tianshi Lun of Tianchi in Huzhou emerged from seclusion, he addressed the assembly: "The wondrous enlightenment is already perfected; once perfected, it is complete."
Small Assembly at Xiangzang Lianan Jing Chan Master’s [Retreat] in Puyuan, Xiuzhou. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, take what is mistaken and proceed with it.
Under the gate of the Patriarchs, one must not let such things pass. A wooden horse chases the western wind; a clay ox’s hooves trample through the earth. Mistake upon mistake!
Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, and the temple master’s eyebrows and whiskers fell off (Zhengwen was a dharma heir of Qian).
Chan Master Xinda of Difan held a small assembly (xiaochan). "To see form and clarify the mind is precisely a blur of the eyes;
to hear sound and awaken to the Way is to betray one's entire life. Aside from these two paths, how is it ultimately? [He] let out a shout.

Returning to the monastery, he ascended the seat: "When departing, the cold plum blossoms had fully broken forth; upon returning, the autumn colors fill the courtyard steps. Meeting again with the elders of the neighboring houses, I rely on..."
"Planting old eyebrows upon the eyes" (Zhengwen Qiansi).
A Minor Sermon by Chan Master Wuman Xun of Chengtian Wanshou Monastery in Wujiang, Suzhou. Regarding the period before the fifteenth day:
Sesame oil within a stone; after the fifteenth day, a fierce fire within the water. Precisely on the fifteenth day, the flower splits heaven and earth;
its body spans the universe. Let it go, and peach blossoms fill the trees; bring it back, and the moon hangs upon the western tower.
Exhausting one’s own mind, one shatters the mouths of others with laughter. Yet, consider this:

when the bamboo staff leaps up to the Brahma Heaven and the walking stick suddenly crosses over the Eastern Sea—tell me, is this letting go, or is it not letting go? (He gave two shouts. In the small assembly:
When joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure have not yet been aroused, it is like the lines of the *I Ching* before they are drawn. When joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure have already been aroused...
It begins. Thus, regarding what has already been drawn and what has not yet been drawn, I know it precedes heaven and earth, yet I lead it back to the beginningless.
Regarding what has already been drawn, I know it follows heaven and earth, yet I push it forward to the endless. This is the broad discourse of the Gate of Sages and the profound talk of Laozi.
As for the realm of a patch-robed monk (*bhikṣu*), how would you analyze it? [He] lets out a shout. Now tell me: is it leading it back to the beginningless?
"Does it have a beginning? Is it endless when one traces it back? He then shouted: "It is easy to distinguish flour from snow, but difficult to discern soot within ink.
(Zhengwen was the successor of Qian.)
Chan Master Huiran Hongyi Juzhan, a native of the Chen family of Huating, ascended the hall and said: "Zen! Zen! The wind tosses the reeds upon the river. Dharma! Dharma!
The moon shifts the shadows of the bamboos across the steps. If you understand, it is revealed in its entirety within your very being;

if you do not understand, you will naturally give rise to affliction. To give rise to affliction—should you attempt to deliberate further or inquire into the profound gate, you will be laughed down by the River."
West Páng’s Old Man’s Small Sermon: The swallow flits across the beam; the gulls play upon the shore.

the sun of wisdom is suspended on high, clearing away the orthodox eye of humans and devas. Truly, the myriad phenomena dance and ten thousand images radiate brilliance;

Chan Master Fensong of Baohua on Mount Duanzhou ascends the hall and says: Hastening and hurrying, not a single step has been moved from beneath one’s heels;
bustling and frantic, not half a person is seen in the midst of the marketplace. There is only he who does not leave his courtyard gate.
"Leaving for Mount Tiantai in the morning, wandering on Mount Nanyue by evening. But tell me, what is the single phrase for returning home? Do you understand? His natural frame is full of spirit;
he does not walk where the Tathāgata has walked. Ascending the hall: "As soon as the precepts were spoken, we have ascended the hall again.
The meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings are not hidden away in the slightest. If you can take them up with your whole being right here—"

Chan Master Longxu Kai-yi-jing was the son of the Zhu family of Wucheng, Zhejiang. Having lost both his father and mother in childhood, he followed his grandfather to receive the scriptures, memorizing several thousand words daily.
By the age of twenty, he was already capable of composing literary works. Suddenly weary of the phenomena of the world, he informed his grandfather of his intention.
He went to Lingrui Temple in Wumen and paid his respects to Master Rongyin, requesting tonsure. Rongyin had him read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and the *Lotus Sūtra*;
as soon as he looked at them, he understood their meaning and had a sudden realization of his past causes. He then took leave of Rongyin and went to visit Master Cheng of Jiaoshan.

Upon seeing him, Cheng recognized his potential and encouraged him by assigning the koan of "the cypress tree in the courtyard. His state of doubt grew daily. Subsequently, he traveled to Mount Lu, where he encountered Master Shengkai of Tientai Temple.

He attained penetration and immediately sought to enter the hall. His efforts were extremely earnest. On the fifth day, he entered the Abbot’s quarters and knelt to ask, "I, your disciple, am practicing *gongfu*;
I pray that the Master will grant me a point of entry. Just then, the wooden board sounded for the morning meal. Yuanzheng said, "The signal has ended; go eat your porridge.
As the Master rose to leave, before he had even stepped through the door, his heart suddenly leaped with joy, like a red sun rolling out from behind the clouds.
On that day, he performed a series of formal prostrations. Cheng said, "What instructions do I have for you? The Master replied, "The Master’s compassionate heart is too eager.
Cheng smiled and struck him with his *ruyi* (ceremonial fly-whisk). From then on, he traveled extensively throughout all quarters, eventually visiting Xiu at Qingyuan.
Xiu asked, "Where have you come from? The Master lifted one foot. Xiu said, "Do not act with empty pretension as a student. The Master replied, "I have never spoken falsely since the beginning.
Xiu said, "You wild-rice-gathering fellow! Go to the meditation hall. He subsequently appointed him to oversee the drafting of official documents. Later, he transmitted the lineage to him.

The fellow monk asked, "What Dharma can one practice to escape this suffering? The monk replied, "To escape this suffering, you must seek transcendence from the world;

He returned to inform his parents of his earnest desire to leave the household life. They sent him to Huishan Temple to receive the tonsure. While reading the records of the ancient worthies, he came upon the lines:

He could not sleep for a single night. On the following day, he set out with his satchel at his waist and left the assembly, traveling directly to Longchi. Upon reaching the mountain gate and looking up, he suddenly beheld the "Morning Clouds" inscription over the gate of Longchi;

How laughable are those who study the Way in various quarters, Forcing themselves to grasp at the hair of a tortoise or the horns of a hare!"
Chui-xun (Weixin) then entered the abbot’s quarters and asked casually, "You have come to the mountain through the rain; what business do you have? The Master said, "The Way is simply unbearable.

Weixin said, "It does not involve the journey. Try to speak of it for me. The Master said, "Why does the Abbot not accept my words? Weixin said, "Cat! The Master said, "I thought as much, I thought as much.
Weixin then struck him. The Master said, "Cat! Weixin struck him again and said: [The text here implies the Master's response was cut off or the narrative concludes with this action.]

Later, Wei-ming appointed the Master as the successor to the Head Seat Jie. The Master did not dare to refuse, having received the transmission of the dharma. He went out to reside at Mount Song in his native district.
Subsequently, he entered the capital and was granted an official title.
The Emperor Shizu Zhang, in his profound and generous grace, commanded that I preach the Dharma for Empress Cishou.
The moon is at its full brightness, yet autumn is already old; beneath the stone steps, the sound of cold crickets is mournful. Why is it that worldly people are so often deluded?

They know only how to break branches for the cassia and climb over flowers. Who is willing to turn the light back upon themselves to reflect within? In a hundred years, there are thirty-six thousand days.
In the mere blink of an eye, it passes away. We who are monks dwelling beneath the forest trees must by all means avoid following his delusions.
Morning attendance and evening inquiry should not be delayed; one must investigate and clarify one’s own matter early.
Hurry to repay the cost of his food; do not wait until King Yama comes to demand it himself. These words of this mountain monk are no trivial matter; they are intended solely for you all.
Self-awakening is good. If you regard these words with indifference, in the end you will only grieve for your own heart and mind.
Evening Assembly: If you speak of two, they do not form a pair; if you speak of one, it does not remain solitary. Two fifty-copper coins, in the final analysis, are one hundred.
The numbers are most distinct; who can discern them? Auspicious snow falls in profusion, mountains and rivers become one color.
To all people, I ask: do you see it or not? Before the slope, wild deer and passing travelers leave clearly one footprint for every step they take.
If one can thoroughly penetrate the source here within, the primary task of study is complete. A monk entered for an audience. The Master asked, "Where have you come from?

A monk visited. The Master asked, "Who dragged this corpse here for you? The monk shouted. The Master said, "After three shouts and four shouts, what then? The monk hesitated.
The Master struck him, saying, "A fellow who dabbles in empty pretenses" (the lineage of Gufan Jie).
Chan Master Fajue Jiemu of Yongjia was the son of the Lin family of Yi County. In his youth, he played with other children.

He delighted in gathering sand to build stupas or sat in meditation with his eyes closed; those who knew him marveled at this. At fifteen, he lost his father and gave rise to the thought of impermanence.
Taking leave of his mother, he sought out Chan Master Jing-an Langxin to undergo the tonsure ceremony. He was directed to visit Dazuo Fatang, who instructed him to contemplate the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.
Upon reaching the passage, "Even seeing is already apart from seeing; seeing cannot reach it," a state of doubt suddenly arose within him, though its full realization had not yet been attained.
However, he studied under various great masters, including Miyin Zhi, Suican Li’an, Fuyan Mingfa, and Tiantong, all of whom had karmic connections with him;
yet, he ultimately could not bring himself to accept their teachings. Upon hearing of the spiritual reputation of Dacho Jie, he sold his cloth robes to seek instruction.
As soon as he stepped onto the Dharma Hall, he said: "I have long heard of the vast, sky-reaching white waves of Dacho; why is it that upon arriving today, they are but mere droplets?"
"No," said Zhe. "Reverend, take good care of the corner of your *kāṣāya*. The Master said, "In that case, there is a place where I may receive your grace.
Zhe struck him and asked, "Tell me, was this a reward or a punishment? The Master said, "I thank the Abbot for his kindness. Zhe said, "Today I have hit half of you. The Master covered his ears.
Zhe then appointed him as the *karmadāna* (Venerable Administrator) and immediately bestowed upon him the robe and fly-whisk. [The Master] departed.
The Abbot, while presiding over the Dharma Hall, ascended the seat and said: "This entire plot of land—the original deed executed before King Ābhāsvara—has already been handed over to all of you.
You may plow deep and sow at will; there is no reason you cannot take advantage of the season to reap the benefits.

It is only because the years have passed so long that things have become empty and neglected. If you turn your heads for a moment and look back, or step back to examine yourselves, you will finally know."
From the very beginning, there has never been the slightest loss. Thus it is said: "It is simply the person of old; they do not change their former way of walking.
Now tell me, who is this person of old? [He] strikes the meditation staff and says: "The pupils in the eyes blow the double-reed whistle;
from within the nostrils, the lion reveals its fierce majesty. At the New Year’s Eve small *sāman*, he raises his whisk and calls to the assembly: "Do you still..."
Do you see? This is the new handle that each person originally possesses; it is the old public case (*gong'an*) that the Buddhas and patriarchs of the past have never yet resolved.
Today, I cannot help but take the head for the tail and turn the tail into the head, so that everyone may know it exists.
He brushes [the whisk] once and says: "If you seek here even the slightest trace of the marks of arising and ceasing, or coming and going, it is still..."
It is like searching for the beginning and end within a revolving wheel, or seeking front and back within empty space.
What more can be said than that this aggregate has just ceased while that aggregate has not yet arisen? Generally speaking, human sentiment involves loss as soon as there is gain;

on the worldly path, there is no going forth that does not involve returning. This is why Fachang invited the Head Seat to drink soup, merely to manifest his family tradition. Thus did Beichan address the monks.
The slaughtering and cooking in the refectory involve excessive toil and expense. If one were to examine this closely, it would all belong to the realm of worldly convention (*saṃvṛti*).
But tell me: here in Fātong’s place, after all, with what will he share the year-end provisions with the assembly? Striking the incense table, he said:
"In a moment, when you hear the drum sound from the hall, go quickly down to the refectory and find out. Four years later, he retired to Huacheng Monastery.
On the twenty-third day of the eighth month of the Gengshen year of the Kangxi era, he manifested illness.

On the twenty-third day of the intercalary eighth month, at the hour of the Dragon (7–9 a.m.), he suddenly took water to bathe, changed his robes, and sat in the full lotus posture. When the assembly requested him to speak a verse, the Master said:

"When conditions gather, birth is manifested; when conditions disperse, departure is manifested. Birth and death are both like dreams and illusions—why should I need to speak a verse again? After a long silence...
He asked, "Is the great assembly gathered? and passed away with a single shout. The Master was born on the seventeenth day of the tenth month in the Bingyin year of the Ming Tianqi era.
His worldly age was fifty-five, and his years as a monk were thirty-seven. He was interred at Huacheng (where Gu Fanze succeeded him).
Chan Master Yì'ān Suì was a native of Yíxīng, Chángzhōu. He addressed the assembly, saying: "The wind sweeps away the lingering clouds;

Upon every mountain, long green moss grows. The sun’s orb stands at its zenith; In ten thousand households, smiles fill their cheeks. I dare ask you all: tell me, what is it they laugh at? The earth is originally made of mud.
His verse on the Buddha’s holding up the flower reads: "The Poisonous Coating at Vulture Peak suddenly struck."
Yet he strikes! He bares his heart and pours out his soul, revealing his claws and fangs. With a single laugh, he eclipses the light of Kāśyapa and tears asunder heaven and earth.
Who can boast of overturning the oceans and toppling the mountains? The Verse on the Woman Emerging from Samādhi says: Entering samādhi and emerging from samādhi, Whetting a brick to make a mirror.
Mañjuśrī and Wuming— A handle for empty space. *Du!* (Meishan Dingsi)

Chan Master Nanfai of Songwan Ting addressed the assembly: "For twenty years I traveled everywhere, calling on masters throughout the land; the potent poison remained deeply hidden within, and I myself had forgotten it.
Had I not this time emptied my belly and purged it, how could I have cleansed this very gut? [He then] ascended the hall.
To plant upside-down in the rootless tree, to hang crosswise a lamp from the bottom of the sea—this is merely ordinary tea and rice.

To turn one’s body within the sea of right and wrong, to walk alone amidst the mountains of self and other—this is still one’s original livelihood. To lose the mountain itself is to ruin one’s own family tradition;
to kick over the pure vase is nothing but playing with a pot. Like the golden phoenix and fragrant elephant seizing what the dragon swallows—who could [resist]?
To dare to look askance [at this]—to possess such majestic virtue and such strategic skill, capable of inheriting the ancestral legacy and flourishing the patriarchal Way;

only then can one not deceive the Sovereign. If, however, one is mired in delusions and trapped within the shell of ignorance, not only will one’s own self be buried and lost, but the ancestral lineage will also be brought to shame.
Is there, at this very moment, any man of transcendent lineage and extraordinary vision? If...
"It exists. The Way does not travel in vain. If it did not exist, this mountain monk would today let out a lion’s roar from atop the crowns of the thousand sages.
With a shout, he descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "His two eyes protrude like the pupils of a snow lion;
how strange and marvelous! The seas and mountains are startled. On level ground, he deceives many scholars; today, all say they have awakened at the morning star."
The Master brandished his whisk and said, "Do you see?
If you can realize it right here, not only will you breathe through the same nostril as the old man Kāśyapa, but you will also walk hand-in-hand with the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
However, if you hesitate or dwell upon it with discursive thought, ten thousand miles of white clouds separate you. He threw down the whisk and said, "To understand this is to be struck down."
"Fall is not another thing; only then does one believe that horizontal and vertical are not dust" (Xianggu Cheshi).
Chan Master Mingbo of Yunju on Mount Fenshan in Shuntian was the son of the Guo family of Guoqing in Weiching, south of the capital.

Among seven brothers, the Master was the fifth. Because his father fell ill, he received a divine warning permitting his son to leave the household life. At the age of seven, he was sent away to enter the monastic order.

At Tiangxian Hermitage, Lì Zhì'ān received the tonsure. The hermitage was originally a branch monastery; in his daily life, he did not differ from worldly customs, which the Master constantly deplored.

He deeply reflected that the matter of birth and death is of great importance, yet there was no one with whom he could consult for resolution. On the twenty-fifth day, he knelt and recited the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
For three years he did not step beyond the threshold of his door. By chance, a Zen guest encouraged him to engage in study, whereupon he received full ordination at Minzhong Temple.
He then went to Tianjin Rulai Hermitage to attend upon Master Daibo Qian and requested lodging. There he applied himself with bitter diligence to his research.
One day, he entered the abbot’s quarters and asked, "What is one's original face? Qian held up his fist. The Master said, "Aside from this, [is there anything else?]"
"Is there such a thing? Qian struck him immediately. From that point on, his state of doubt intensified. Later, he followed [Qian] to Baocheng Temple in Yangcun.
When Qian entered the hall, he said, "There is a sick man in this hall; he owes the world a full body of cold sweat. Hearing this, the Master’s practice became even more earnest.
For four days and nights, his eyes did not close. While taking off his sandals upon ascending to his meditation platform, he suddenly attained realization. Thereupon—
Bai Qian asked, "What is your original face? The Master said, "Six times six is thirty-six. Qian said, "That is not it; speak further.
The Master said, "Nine times nine is eighty-one. Qian gave him a slap and said, "Is this eighty-one, or is it thirty-six?
The Master let out a shout and departed. From that time on, he was truly a man of the occasion.

He did not yield. He served [the Master] for another three years and received his seal of approval (*anujñā*). He maintained a life of stillness at Xiyù Yúnjū for ten years before finally responding to the invitation of Prince Duōluohuì to open the Dharma assembly at Hǎihui.

Since there is neither cultivation nor realization, what was the purpose of his six years of ascetic practice? The Master said:

"Out of pity for a three-foot child, he did not spare his own two eyebrows. He then continued: "Heaven is not high and earth is not thick; benefiting oneself and benefiting others is neither new nor old."

Those who have not yet passed through the barrier have their eye-sight piercing through the four worlds; those who have already passed through the barrier have never, from beginning to end, departed from the nest.
He suddenly called out to the assembly, saying, "Tell me, when the Old Man Śākyamuni beheld the morning star at night, did he still remain within the nest or not?
The assembly was silent. The Master laughed heartily and descended from his seat. New Year’s Eve Small Sermon. The Twelfth Month.
The thirtieth day of the month has arrived. As for the matter beneath the feet of all people, what is it? You must know that everyone possesses it inherently;
each and every one is perfectly accomplished. Therefore it is said: "Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one does not depart from this.
If one departs from this, one passes right by it face-to-face. The Buddhas of the three periods of time are also this; the patriarchs of successive generations are also this.

This is it. All the old masters of the world are also just this. Even down to the scaly, the shelled, the feathered, and the winged, and the grasses, trees, and insects—there are none who do not receive this power of grace. Do you all understand this?
If you do, your eyebrows remain as they were. If it is not yet so, there will be new branches next year; do not disturb the spring.
The wind has not yet ceased. On the anniversary of Guanyin’s birth, he ascends the hall and says: "I was once an ancient Tathāgata, traversing kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
The great earth is entirely pervasive; where, then, is there arising or ceasing? Through the thirty-two transformations, my whole body appears; in every land and every atom, all is revealed.

Falling. "The bright sun circles Mount Sumeru. Entering the hall: "The brilliant sun is right in the midst of the sky;

The Master said: "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*; here there is no old monk. He asked: "What is 'neither seizing the person nor seizing the environment'? The Master said: "Guoqing [Temple]."

"Talented men are noble; when a family is wealthy, children are spoiled. In praise of a woman emerging from meditative concentration, he said: "A solitary green mountain towers high, draped in lofty clouds.

Neither existence nor non-existence is involved; purity leaves no trace. Floating light disperses until autumnal radiance is revealed.
The bright moon, the reeds, and the flowers are all one fresh color. (Dabo Qiansi)
Chan Master Sanhong of Hongguang in Kyoto was the son of the Ge family of Jiading in Suzhou. When his mother was pregnant with him, she had a premonitory dream of swallowing the moon.
As soon as he left the swaddling clothes, his mother passed away. At the age of five, his father sent him to school; he soon became able to recognize characters.

He delighted in reading the texts of the Chan school. As he grew older, he took pleasure in wandering through jade palaces and azure temples; hearing the sound of the *brahman* chants, he was so filled with joy that he forgot to return home.
Consequently, he grew weary of the impermanence of worldly phenomena and informed his father of his intention to leave the household life.

His father did not permit it, and thus time passed until he reached the age of seventeen. Taking advantage of an occasion when his father had gone on a long journey, he finally resolved his will and paid homage to Master Huixin at Nanxiang Baihe Temple.
Having shaved his head, he happened to encounter the elder Master Rong of Mount Jing when the latter arrived at the temple. Rong instructed him to investigate the "Mu" (No) koan of Zhaozhou.
One day, Rong asked, "The white crane has long since flown south; why are you sitting here?
The Master replied instantly, "I am merely waiting for the wind of ninety thousand li to lift me up. Rong smiled and said, "May I assist you? He then struck him a blow. At that moment—
Although he did not know where this blow had landed, a doubt arose within his breast. At the age of twenty-six, he received full ordination from the Vinaya Master Xiangxue of Haizang.
Thereafter, he traveled extensively to visit masters at Fuyan, Lingyin, and Lingyan, gaining many opportunities for spiritual instruction.
In the year of Bingwu, he went to the capital to pay his respects to Panshan Qianyu at the Fangshengchi Pond; there, he received direct oral instructions and was personally nurtured by the master.
After a long time, Hu Xiaozai’s younger brother, Hu Xueyu, invited me to close myself off at Qianmu Garden for six years.
One day, while reading the *Huayan Yuantan*, I reached the section on the tenth profound gate, "The Sea-Seal Where All Phenomena Constantly Abide.

Like one who has awakened from a drunken stupor, I suddenly realized the principle of the inexhaustible, perfect fusion of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), finally coming into accord with the meaning of Master Yongyi’s gesture of opening his palm at Mount Jing.
In the summer of the *renzi* year, he left the Barrier and went to Mount Pan to pay his respects. Yuanzhen asked, "While you were at the Barrier, you must have attained some new realization;
why do you not present it to me for my inspection? The Master said, "What a wonderful news!

Yuanzhen said, "When Lingyun saw the peach blossoms and attained awakening, Xiansha ultimately would not grant him approval. The Master said, "Today I have caught the old fellow red-handed. Yuanzhen then withdrew.

Qian said, "This was originally my shout. The Master said, "One does not pursue a defeated general. Qian laughed heartily.

The Master then departed and received the transmission of the Dharma. He appeared in the world at Haihui Monastery in the capital, where he revived the Perfect Teaching (Yuanjiao), which continues to this day.

"The void is smashed, the lump of dead mud is destroyed; Having gained the ability to turn over, look closely. In every place, one's livelihood is sufficient as it is; Leaning against the sky..."
The sword pressed against him with chilling intensity as he went to visit Tianmu Yulin Xiu. Xiu asked, "What was the underlying meaning when Linji received three blows of the staff from Huangbo?
The Master said, "A precious sword is presented to a hero; red powder is sold to a beautiful woman.
Xiu said, "So it is, so it is" (Jishi Deng succeeded him).
Chan Master Yun Kongyuan of Qingta Monastery ascends the hall for the opening of the retreat. He ties the mouth of his sackcloth bag shut; heaven and earth both lose their luster.
He takes up his staff, strikes once, and says: "It does not emerge outside of this very moment. He lets loose the ox in the open field;
its horns and head are naturally distinct. Again he strikes once and says: "Nor does it emerge outside of this very moment. Let it be taught that with a single inhalation—
The vast ocean dries up; casually, the coral moon is revealed. If you look closely, there is a share for you: he casts out the "grain-thorn" from years past.
Those of the Ten Stages and the Three Vehicles all become cowed with fear—where can one even begin? He lets out two consecutive shouts and says, "The Unranked True Person has been caught!
Now tell me, what kind of words are these? He drags his staff and descends from the seat. New Year’s Eve Small Precept Assembly. *Bao*.
Beyond the southern walls of Zhucheng, the evening smoke lingers; Thousands of gates and ten thousand households bid farewell to the year’s end.

Only the monasteries remain as pure and serene as this; The glow of lamps and the cold plum blossoms are exceptionally beautiful. Children vie with one another in joyful dance; Village elders burn paper money in the night.
Tomorrow morning, I shall lightly compose a "Rhapsody on the Spring Ox," To hang up at Mount Yan as a painted record. In praise of the World-Honored One’s first birth, it is said: He walks alone.
In the hall, he boasts at random: "How much spring color there is—birds singing and flowers blooming!
Even if one could summon the spring back, it would still fall to another's house. A verse on seeing the morning star at night: "A single awakening, and it is already midnight."
The north wind is truly at its coldest; a film clouds the eyes of the morning star. To whom can this desolation be told?
In praise of the Woman Emerging from Samādhi: Seeking the last traces of red among the treetops and beneath them, one petal flies west, another east.
It is but the peach blossom’s greed for fruit that has caused people to resent the wind of the fifth watch. In praise of Nanquan:
Chanzhao said: "Lamenting for the Princess of Xiang upon the Miling River; a tongueless Persian reading Sanskrit texts.
As the three libations are poured, he relies on the refinement of transformation; the funeral shrouds disperse as clouds over the mountains of Chu. (Da Jingmin’s Successor)
Rong Chao-tong, a lay practitioner from Yangtian on the Lushui River, abstained from meat from his youth and always paid respectful homage upon seeing monks.
Reaching middle age, he delighted in discussing matters of transcendence with the monastics of the Chan school.

One day, hearing a monk say that one knows not where one comes from at birth nor where one goes at death, he applied himself with rigorous austerity to investigate this matter. Subsequently, he visited the masters of various lineages, yet only...
He questioned him about this matter. In the early years of the Kangxi era, he went to visit Zhongpan Qian. It happened that Qian was presiding over the assembly when he said:

"If the mind is like wood or stone, what need is there for strenuous effort? If the intent of Chan practice is like cold ashes, there is no need to exhaustively seek the source or the ultimate meaning."
At this point, his doubts were suddenly aroused, and he asked again: "I do not ask about either the path of existence or the path of non-existence;

how is it that the mind is empty and yet one passes the imperial examination? Qian said, "A single idle man between heaven and earth. The scholar said, "One who forgets their home knows the way back upon following the road;
one who is deluded regarding the Patriarch turns around and sees their father. Qian said, "That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure. Furthermore...

The Master asked, "Where have all the ancestral masters of successive generations been? Dajian replied, "South of the mountains, north of the ridges. The Master asked, "Why do they not appear in the world?
Dajian replied, "They strike you right where you are standing; they bump right into you. At this, the Master attained realization. Dajian then tested him with kōans from the past.
The scholar answered each question with perfect accord. On the first day of the tenth month, Qian summoned the scholar into his room and entrusted him with a verse, saying:
"When the iron steamed bun breaks, one forgets all artifice; the root-source of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is entrusted to you. Having served me for many years, there is nothing else to say:
in transmitting methods and dispensing medicine, value the opportune moment. This occurred in the Jisi year of the Kangxi era. At the age of seventy, in the second month of spring...
The second day. On this day, he attended to guests as was his custom. Suddenly, he rose from his seat to bid the guests leave and entered his room.
There, he bathed, changed his robes, and sat in the full lotus posture. He requested a brush and wrote a verse:
"For seventy years I have tended this ox, Roaming freely across eastern hills and western ridges. Now I have recognized the place of true return; The moon reflects upon a thousand [streams]."
"The Yangtze River flows through the ages like autumn. Having cast down his writing brush, he passed away (Da-bo Gan-si).
Chan Master Yuan of Yongfu and Yongqing ascended the hall and said: "This mountain monk has long dwelt in mountain caves; my mouth is clumsy and my tongue is dull.

Yet, urged by various patrons and protectors, I have been pushed onto the seat of the ancestral patriarchs. I feel ashamed before the former masters, but as the matter could not be avoided, I shall now unfasten [the robe]."
The Cloth Bag. He proposed the analogy of a hawk flying over Silla; in the blink of an eye, the skull shatters. Where there are no traces, do not hide yourself;

where a Buddha is present, you cannot set foot. Tell me, how will you understand this? After a long silence, he said: "Do not take your idle scholarly interpretations and bury them within the mind of the Patriarch.
On the day of the Buddha’s Enlightenment, he ascended the hall and pointed at heaven and pointed at earth, proclaiming alone: [the Great Way].
"Venerable One! Furthermore, he studied the gates of meditative concentration in the empty mountains; for six years he knew his error before finally realizing awakening.
One morning, with cold eyes, he bared his two pupils, and forty-nine years became a mere tale of failure. To this day, who can understand how to repay his kindness?
He looked left and right, gave a shout, and said: "To speak with the mouth is like being mute; to see with the eyes is like being blind. (Da Jingmin was his successor.)
Chan Master Weitang of Jingxi Longchi succeeded to the seat at Longchi. Entering the hall for the formal discourse, he said:
"The green mountains are like paintings; the blue waters are like indigo. They adorn heaven and earth, changing with the seasons. Holding up his staff, he called to the assembly, saying:
'Tell me, does this wooden monk have any change or not? He struck the floor once and said: 'On the mountain ridges, white clouds unfurl and then roll back.'"
The bright moon at the edge of heaven departs and returns.
(Compiled by Zhongming Gongsi). *Wudeng Quanshu*, Volume 94.
Compiled by the monk (Chao Yong), Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple in the Capital.
Edited and presented for imperial inspection by the Abbot of Kyoto’s Kokegwan-ji (Subject Monk) Chōkai,
of the Rinzai School.
The Record of Chan Master Yuan of Peian, surnamed Wang, of the Jiangning Wang clan, the thirty-sixth generation descendant of Nanyue. Entering the hall, he said: "Seeing the horn over the wall."
One immediately knows it is an ox. Seeing smoke across a mountain, one immediately knows it is fire.

For what reason, when asked about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, ten out of ten have five pairs who do not understand? After a long silence, he held up his whisk and said: "Precisely because it is so utterly clear, it causes what is attained to be delayed.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A single wheel of red surges forth from the Eastern Sea; the mountains and rivers of the great earth receive this news."
Penetrating. The fruit is right before one's eyes; one must be able to fix the gaze upon it. "Silla originally lies east of Haemun Gate. [He] ascends the hall.
It cannot be clarified, it cannot be described. What follows is a long discourse; leave it for another day. [He] ascends the hall. He cites a monk asking Yunmen:
"What is the house style of you, the Master? The Gatekeeper said, "A scholar is coming outside; someone has come to announce it.
The Master said, "The scholar has arrived to ask about the house style; do not say that this gate is penetrated by the single thread. Serve him a cup of Zhaozhou tea."
Do you still recognize that the flavor is much the same? [Ascending the hall: Today is the fifteenth of the third month. The bell is struck and the drum beaten again;
the pillar of dew breaks into joyful song, and the lantern begins to dance. The entire assembly must not be muddled—count them:
one, two, three, four, five. [Ascending the hall: Langye’s Buddha-dharma is truly great; for these past days it has been nothing but a cold. It cannot be granted to all...
The people deliberated among themselves. Then, with a single cough, he said, "There is still something left; do not trouble yourselves by standing for long.
Ascending the hall, he said, "In essence, it is essence; in function, it is function. Looking around at those on his left and right, he asked, "What is function?
Suddenly seizing his staff, he said, "When the weather is clear, you refuse to walk; you wait only for the rain to soak your head. With that, he dispersed everyone at once. A monk asked, "How is it?"
"This is the meaning of the Patriarchs' intent and the teaching's intent. The Master said: "The melon is straight and blunt; the gourd is curved and bent. A monk asked:
"What was the meaning of Bodhidharma facing the wall? The Master said: "A sick bird perches on the reeds.
A monk asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "A lantern hanging on the wall. A layman asked: "What is your surname, Master? The Master said: "Zhao, Qian, Sun, Li."
The scholar Zhou Wu Zheng Wang said, "Does the Master originally have so many surnames? The Master replied, "Past and present are not separated.
Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "The mountain moon is like silver, stirring the old man's兴致 (xìng—delight/arousal)."
Wandering idly, he did not realize he had passed to the west of the peak (as recorded in the *Gujian Zhangsi*).
Huangmei received Master Luying Yan, a Chan master from the Chen family of Wan’an in Jizhou.

On the fifteenth day of the first month, during a snowfall, he addressed the assembly: "Tonight is the fifteenth of the first month; the snow acts as the Golden Watchmen’s prohibition. The realm of Mañjuśrī is entirely forgotten."

Samantabhadra’s spiritual powers are vast and universal; the starry bridges and iron chains form a heavy barrier. Amidst the fire-trees and silver flowers, nothing can be seen—this is truly a season of Great Peace.
You practitioners of Chan must not be reckless or superficial.

Sitting in meditation upon the Chan platform, chanting by the window, gathering around the brazier to discuss how to transcend the common herd—yet in receiving guests, there are no "three kinds of monks. Suddenly, right before one's head, is Xuansha’s tiger. A-ha!
Hehe. "The sweet melon is sweet to its very stem; the bitter gourd is bitter to its very root" (the sole successor of the lineage).
Master Youzhong Ru, the Abbot of Guangfu at Dongta Monastery in Jiaxing, ascends the hall for the opening of his residence. An old shop has opened anew, with no other merchandise to sell;
merely responding to the needs of the gate, there is only this one thing. He picks up his staff and says: "When it is raised, even Heaven does not..."
[He] strikes the floor once and says: "It can cover all. Put it down! [He] strikes the floor once again and says: "The earth cannot bear its weight. At times its value exceeds that of a city;
at other times it is not worth a single coin. But tell me, how is it when one neither grasps nor lets go? [He] strikes the floor once more and says:
"Only those merchants who travel the great ocean are permitted; those who share the same path should surely know. Addressing the assembly, he cites the case of Xinghua striking [his attendant].
When the Rector had finished speaking, the Master said: "It is said that Kebin was on the verge of completing a nine-cubit-high mound, yet lacked the soil of a single basketful.
This failure implicates Xinghua; his understanding was such that he could be called skilled at assessing affairs, but not skilled at assessing his opponent.
Little did he know that Kebin possessed the strategic art of being gentle yet stern, and majestic yet not fierce."
"Even if one had turned over one's skin at that moment, what 'excellent Ke-bin' would there have been to find? To the assembly:

Having finished citing the story of the old woman burning the hermitage, the Master said: 'In various quarters, people often speculate upon the words and phrases, saying that this monk failed to grasp the old woman, and thus suffered her burning his hut and sending him away.
This can truly be called "those who rely on words perish. Yet they do not realize that the old woman [had already] exhausted [all possibilities]..."
The skill of this child is such that no monk has been able to paint it out; to this day, no one has been able to resolve this public case.

The verse on the woman emerging from samādhi says: "In spring there is orchid, in autumn chrysanthemum; in summer the pomegranate is red. When the plum arrives in winter, the message of fragrance is communicated."
This causes people to ask why his two eyes appear different. Heaven’s timing allows no distinction between east and west.
A monk asked, "Regarding Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout, I wonder: are they the same or different? The Master said, "The moon sifts through pine shadows on trees high and low;

the sun illuminates the heart of the pond, where heaven is reflected above and below. He asked, "When the thirtieth day of the twelfth month arrives, and the Old Man Yama comes to settle the accounts..."
[The monk asked: "How can one settle the bill for the rice? The Master said, "Today I will not answer your questions. [The monk] asked, "Why will you not answer?
The Master said, "I fear you are making your living inside a ghost cave. [Another monk] asked, "What is it like when an ancient mirror has not yet been polished?
The Master said, "It cannot be obscured. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when the ancient mirror has been polished? The Master said, "It cannot be obscured. (Huiyan Xi was his successor.)

Master Chan Yufeng Gang of Ciguang Temple on Mount Huangshan in Xin’an addressed the assembly: “It has been three days since the retreat commenced, yet there is not a single sound from within the hall.
When impermanence and the cycle of birth and death arrive, each of you must exert yourselves with urgency. Do not say that this mountain monk has not spoken;
from the beginning, I have never relied upon the power of another. Take care of the eyebrows above your eyes; take heed not to turn your back on what is right before you.”
Shi Jiezhi ascends the hall: The east wind splashes my face, revealing my rosy cheeks; The mouth of the bag is untied for a moment this morning.

Though those who go depart in such a way, Why should it hinder those who come from coming in such a way? Coming and going, they tread upon the mother-born path; Let them dance the *Santai* wherever they may be.
Addressing the assembly, he cites the story of the Woman Emerging from Samādhi, and says in verse: Pointlessly...
A troop of old world-weary travelers has cheated out both Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti; their滞貨 (stale wares) remain without a place to land even to this day.
It is difficult to sell them in the Eastern Capital, so they are being peddled in the Western Capital. Addressing the assembly: I cite Baizhang’s second visit [to Mazu]. The verse says:
"The face is twisted to test the true master; Rising and falling according to others is not yet praiseworthy. With a single clap of thunder, the whole body is revealed; This time, he pulls it back."
Severing the Old Way of Life: Addressing the Assembly. Citing the National Teacher’s three calls to his attendant and the attendant’s three responses, he offers this verse:
Needless to speak of good matters too often; Keep this harmony to warm the *dantian*. A night of west wind leaves the flowers in disarray; The bees on the full racks can only pity themselves in vain.
Addressing the Assembly. Citing Baizhang’s “Wild Fox,” he offers this verse: Not falling [into the two extremes], one is nonetheless affected.
The wild fox’s entanglement: how could one who is not oblivious ever escape this body?
If you wish to avoid incurring the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma. (Huiyan Xi, the successor)
Small Assembly at Tiantong Chanshi of Wulei Lingshan, Cixi. The Master raised the Way of the First Patriarch:
"Do not let anything go out from within; do not let anything come in from without. Let the mind be like a wall or a fence, and you may enter the Way.

The Master struck his staff and said, "Does the assembly wish to see the Original Patriarch Bodhidharma? To heal the sores before one's eyes, he gouged out the flesh from his own heart. He struck it once more.
Zhuo asked, "If sitting in meditation with the door closed is for those of the highest capacity, what kind of capacity does one have who carries bricks and transports earth?
The Master said, "You are a man from outside the gate. Zhuo asked, "'It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha, it is not a thing.
What is it? The Master called out loudly, "Gourd! Gourd! As the monk hesitated, the Master said, "Zhaozhou’s wall hangs empty on the east side."
While the Master was drinking tea, a monk requested instruction. The Master said, "It happens that I am currently drinking tea.

As the monk hesitated, the Master suddenly splashed the tea over his face. The Dharma Master Qingyi, while observing the summer retreat at Wulei, once said to the Master, "Today I want you to secretly pass through my carriage and horses.
The Master replied, "From the beginning, I have never allowed even a needle to pass through an official's gate."
[The monk] said, "Changqing’s Way says: 'Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. Only when one is personally willing will one be intimate with it.
In the past, I mistakenly sought it along the road; today, looking at it, it is ice within fire. Is this not the contemplation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vipaśyanā*) spoken of by Tiantai?
The Master said, "Wrong. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master waved his fan and said, "A green silk fan is sufficient."
Fengliang said, "You have closed the door again. The Master laughed heartily. Qing asked again, "The wall stands ten thousand fathoms high—what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "A needle cannot pierce it. Qing said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "It drips through the nostrils" (Dabian Quan succeeded him).
Chan Master Liaozhan Jue of Lingyan in Jizhou gave a small-scale sermon on the Spring Equinox. After a long silence, he pressed his staff against the floor and said:
"If you let this one move pass, I shall teach the pestle’s tip to sprout flowers; if you do not let it pass, it will melt like ice and crumble like tiles.
At such a moment, tell me: is it letting pass, or is it not letting pass? Although Lingyan acts in this way—
"The Way. This is also practicing the mandate of spring during winter. What is the phrase that does not violate the seasons? He then struck the meditation seat and said:
"The Weaver of Heaven has another clever arrangement; when pressed, one's own eyes open wide. Having picked up a flower, it blooms upon the pestle’s tip;
forcing others at midnight, it emerges from the yellow plum. Ascending the hall, he said: "Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; above, all grasping is severed."
Looking up. Where there is no Buddha, run past quickly; below, sever your own body. Meeting a person three thousand *li* away, it is none other than yourself;
do not speak of it mistakenly. If you have it, bring it forth—pluck the willow blossoms. When the eyes are free of cataracts, do not scatter sand. The butterflies fly in confusion over the wall;
one knows not whose house the spring colors have fallen upon. Late evening assembly on the Lantern Festival: How excellent!
At that moment, [the Master] said, "If there is anyone among you who recognizes this, please come forward. For a long time no one stepped forth.

The Master spoke again, saying, "Venerable assembly, such a sublime gathering is difficult to encounter; we must not all depart without having spoken. Therefore it is said: 'It is like a treasure in the darkness.'"
"Without a lamp, one cannot see. If the Buddha-dharma is not explained by someone, though one possesses wisdom, one cannot comprehend it.
He then raised his fist and said, "This is the treasure; which is the lamp? He further extended both hands and said, "This is the lamp;
which is the treasure that is seen? "I, this mountain monk, have finished speaking. How do you all understand this? It must be such that—"
There is nothing left uncomprehended. If you attempt to deliberate upon this as a matter of Buddhist doctrine, you will enter hell like a shot arrow.
Addressing the assembly: "The strainer is with outflows; the ladle is without outflows. The small vehicle is a string of coins; the great vehicle is a well-rope. [He] held up his staff and said:
"When the fish swim, the water is turbid; when the bird flies, feathers fall. If you understand, it is wrapped right before your eyes; if you do not understand, you turn away from it face-to-face."
On the Winter Solstice, for a small-scale *sīmān* (private instruction), he said: "The Stone Woman of Huangmei conceives in the night; The Azure Phoenix atop the mountain calls her back.
Suddenly, with one cry, all news is cut off; An iron ox gives birth to a jade kitten. [End of] Small-scale *sīmān* on New Year’s Eve.
Beichan said: "As the year comes to its end, this old monk will cook a white ox from the open field to share with you all for the New Year.

Once everyone has eaten, we shall perform the village dance. Why? So that we may avoid leaning on others' doorways or huddling by others' walls, and not be forced by the people of the age to be called 'Master'.
The Master said: "Righteousness arises in years of plenty; lack of filial piety is born of scarcity. Beichan.
"Those who enter the gate may all behold the splendor. It is not so here at Lingyan. He suddenly raised his staff and said: "Grind three thousand grains of castor oil until they are a pulp;

drain away the five flavors of Chan from every quarter. He then struck the ground once with the staff. On the occasion of the Buddha’s Birthday, he ascended the hall and cited the World-Honored One’s first words upon birth:
"With one finger pointing to heaven and one finger pointing to earth, [he cried], 'In the heavens above and on the earth below, there is only...'"
"I alone am honored. Yunmen said, "Had I seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to a dog, just to ensure peace throughout the world.
The Master said, "The World-Honored One is called 'Honored' because his carriage is not pushed sideways; Yunmen’s administration of the staff follows a principle that allows no crooked judgment.
Yet, if one wishes to see true peace throughout the world, this is still not entirely perfect. He held his staff crosswise and said, "Lingyan..."
Today, I shall press down both the World-Honored One and Yunmen at once. Now listen to the fisherman dancing his oars and the village elder singing his songs.
Why? Is it not because "he who governs through non-action is surely the Sage"? (Sanziyu’s Succession)
Chan Master Shitou Binmu Zhi of Keshan in Yuezhou addressed the assembly: "A small structure on Keshan consists of three rooms; why must one dwell in deep seclusion to envy Damei?
I delight in my own hiding place, concealing my clumsiness and silence; at Shitou, I lie high upon my pillow amidst the clouds.
Addressing the assembly, he cited Master Zhenjing Wen’s ascent to the hall, where he said: "In the past, the World-Honored One, Mahākāśyapa..."
The Way-seeking Sage went from the Tree of Enlightenment to the Deer Park and turned the Wheel of the Four Noble Truths for the five bhikṣus;
it was Kātyāyana alone who first realized the Way. Today, within the cave of Xinfeng, this poor monk merely turns his staff.

He then picked up his staff, gestured toward the left side of the meditation seat, and said: "Is there anyone here who has realized the Way for the first time? After a long silence, he said: "This may truly be called a man."
"From the start, he has had ambitions that pierce the heavens; he does not walk where the Tathāgata walks. The Master said, "The ninefold cinnabar can transform iron into gold;
one might say both are skilled craftsmen, yet they nonetheless lack the marks of a Great Man. Master Zhi is not like this."
Today I do not turn the Wheel of the Four Noble Truths, nor do I turn the staff. Why? Because I dare not slight you. (A shout.
Verse on Deshan Seeing a Monk at the Gate and Striking Him: Langshui, Mengchang, and Chongguo are wealthy;
Kunlun pulls out a single hair and treats it as light. If you wish to know the gallant guest of chivalrous bone, His liver and gall [are revealed].

What words can exhaustively express it? A verse on Zhaozhou’s examination of two hermitages runs as follows: "Hand grasping a three-foot sword of numinous edge, Why need one stir up dust and smoke at the bottom of the sea?
The fisherman cares not for waves that reach the heavens; He lies peacefully amidst the reeds, facing the bright moon.
A verse on the room of Ciming, wherein he placed a basin of water with a sword laid across it, and a pair of straw sandals set beside them: Whenever...
When a monk arrived for an audience, [Tianye] suddenly said, "Look at the sword! As soon as the monk hesitated, he shouted him out, saying:

"To irrigate the waters of the Milky Way and turn them into fields, one relies entirely on eccentricity to defy the immortals. Even in old age, he still indulges in childish play, floating an iron boat upon the briny waves of the Weak Water. (Tianye Zhousi)

Chan Master Tuo Shan Ti of Pujisi in Wujiang was the son of the Xu family of Jiangdu. At the age of twenty, he left the household life at Mount Lu and received full ordination under Master Yuan at Mount Hua.
He first studied under Master Guan of Yangfen and later received the Dharma from Master Yongfu of Tiantong. He subsequently resided at Jiqing in Wujiang and Faguang in the capital.
**Small Lecture:** In the ground of ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), not even a single speck of dust is admitted. This is the realm of Buddha-work.
Within the gate, not a single dharma is abandoned. Great assembly, tell me: which dharma is not abandoned? [He] strikes the meditation staff and says:
"The subsequent text is long; it shall be entrusted to a future day. Small Lecture on the Start of Spring: "Brothers, when the five nines have ended, spring arrives once more.
Grasses and trees vie for beauty as ten thousand plants renew themselves. [He] holds up the meditation staff and says: "Only this Accumulated Blessings Staff has it."
Throughout the year he does not change; his emaciated frame is stark and towering. (A shout. Small Assembly Sermon: Everyone has a shadow that never leaves them for even a single step.
Why then can one not tread upon it? Great Master Gao Feng spoke thus; his tongue has already dragged across the ground.
I, Jiqing, raise this point: tell me, is there still a fault here or not? (He slaps himself with his hand and says: "The mouth is."
The Misfortune Gate: A Small Evening Lecture for the New Year. Dwelling in the waters in solitude, people rarely come; as the years pass and return, I close my door.
Let white mold grow freely upon my lips; too lazy to use idle learning to deceive beginners. A Monk Visits: The Master asks.
The monk said, "Is it ordinary or is it sage? The Master said, "Is it ordinary or is it sage?
As the monk prepared to offer further words, the Master struck him, saying, "You empty-headed fellow! (Yuan’an Fang was his successor).
Chan Master Yingqian Zuigan of Wuxie in Wuzhou ascended the hall and said: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the Way?
Zhaozhou replied, "The one outside the wall. The monk said, "That is not this Way. Zhaozhou asked, "Which Way are you asking about? The monk said, "The Great Way.
Zhaozhou said, "The Great Way leads to Chang'an. The Master said: "Zhaozhou pointed it out clearly; as for that monk..."
To miss it face-to-face is a failure. Wuxie was not like this. Suppose someone were to ask, "What is the Way?
He would say to him: "Yesterday someone came from Pujiang; today he is going to stay in Jiyang. Although this is so, the imprint of the straw sandals cannot be removed. Why?
Because at Wuxie, there is one stream of water, yet there are eighteen crossings at the gate for the traveler.
Observe closely; take care not to get your feet wet. Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "In the past, Old Gautama possessed three kinds of bodies.
I wonder which one benefited sentient beings? The Master replied: "A mud pig, a scabby dog, and a dead cat's head.

The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him with his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "There is jade in Kunshan, but those who obtain it do not come from Kunshan."
Mountains. There are pearls in the red waters, yet those who pick them up do not remain in the red waters.
Lately, among the monastics, there is a "True Person of No Rank," yet those who realize it do not find it at the face-gate. [The Master] suddenly took up his staff, struck it once, and said:
"The Great Assembly has not heard it said: 'At the ferry crossing of Ke-cheng, a stone man squats. He ascended the hall; the summer heat was scorching the sky.
Hot! Three layers of floral patterns, a beak like iron. As he goes to sleep, he seeks out his benefactor’s vexation without end.
Why? Last night, the fan by the bedside was broken for no reason (Lüān Yuèsì).
Chan Master Zhongyan Zheng of Hongshan in Yanjing ascended the hall for formal discourse: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination.
What is red is red, what is white is white. Who would say black beans are red pearls? How could cinnabar powder paint the moon? Water is water, mountains are mountains.
Do not let mist and waves rise upon the mountain peaks, lest you place an ox's head upon its tail. [He ascended the hall.]

the cowherd boy returns to the head of the small bridge. To the Assembly: It is said that a monk once asked Dongshan, "Among the three bodies, which one does not fall into the category of enumeration?

"Where has it gone? The white ox has been let loose and left no trace; one can only hold the iron whip given to the mountain boy.

Xian Si). Late evening instruction by Chan Master Che of Guanyin Bishan in Yanjing. He asked, "What is the realm of Guanyin?
