A monk asked, "The Buddha is the Great Teacher of the Three Realms; why did Yunmen insist on beating him to death with a single blow? The Master said, "The father acts; the son follows.
The monk asked, "If one were to beat him to death with a single blow right now, what would you do, Master? The Master handed him his staff.
The staff-bearer said, “I invite you. As the monk reached out to take it, the Master struck him, saying, “This mountain monk shall now go about with this command inverted!

He then pushed over the meditation seat, shouted to disperse the assembly, and called to them again. When the assembly turned their heads, the Master said, “The World-Honored One’s feet were busy and his hands were in disarray;
his offense is not heavily penalized. Yunmen has no place to set foot; kindness and enmity have their retribution. Today, this mountain monk—”
"I shall personally administer thirty blows of the staff, so that this story may spread far and wide. A monk asked, "What is it like when one goes straight ahead?
The Master said, "Where do you intend to go? The monk hesitated. The Master struck him, saying, "You do not even know where you are going;
why are you wandering about aimlessly? (Daxian succeeded Xuefeng.)
Chan Master Sanming Rui of Jishan in Jinling was the son of the Sun family of Jiading in Suzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The lion roars and the wild jackal howls;
you eminent Chan practitioners, listen with eyes wide open. This single phrase, clearly manifesting the full import of the teaching, is not easily heard unless one has attained universal penetration.
A monk asked, "What is the singular path of the August Heaven? The Master replied, "The sun in the east."

[The Master] said, "Rain falls from the western side. [The student] asked, "Sages and worthies have no dualistic mind, do they? The Master said, "Only those of superior intelligence and the lowest of fools are unchangeable.
[The student] asked, "If that is so, then are sages and worthies each distinct? The Master said, "Yao and Shun were just like other people.
[The student] asked, "What is the Dharma-gate of Bodhidharma? The Master said, "A fine question. [The student] asked, "What is the teaching of the Tathāgata? The Master...
[The student] said, "Please take this clearly to heart. [The student] asked, "Tell me, are the teachings of the school and the doctrine the same or different?
The Master reached out his hand and said, "Gripped, it becomes a fist; extended, it becomes a palm. (Dàxián succeeded him.)
The layman Chen Yin, courtesy name Jinggong and style name Tieseng, was a native of Daxing. He served as an Inner Secretary (Neihan) and was at that time in charge of drafting imperial edicts.
He took a keen interest in the Chan school (Zongcheng), and in all his compositions of poetry, prose, and literary works, he consistently expressed a desire for transcendence from the mundane world.
At that time, Hongjue Muan, Da jue Xiu, and Lingyan Chu all praised him highly. Later, he served as the Governor of Fengyang.
Ling Sima visited Dongshan Xian and was shown the teaching: "When there is no dreaming and no thinking, how is it that the Great Function manifests?

For ten years, the scholar-monk had failed to attain enlightenment. Later, while being exhorted day and night by Bian Xiaozhi, he suddenly reached a silent accord with the words and phrases from his former inquiry.
One day, while on a boat upon the Yangtze River, leaning against the railing as he gazed at the flowing water, because—
He recollected the phrase, "Remembering sensation, one does not know its retribution; knowing its retribution, one does not know sensation," and attained a profound, penetrating realization.
He then composed a verse: "Ten years of drilling and research, the path so long; Laughing, I mistook my own house for another's.
Now, having shattered the window-lattices to look out, I finally believe that the blossoming plum is but the old flower. One day, Qixian asked, "A single grain of rice is as large as Mount Sumeru."

"How was it that you were dragged away by ants? The scholar said, "It covered heaven and covered earth. The Master asked, "How would you say it, Reverend? Xian replied, "Still water does not harbor dragons.
The scholar let out a powerful roar of defiance, and Xian then ceased speaking.

The scholar once associated with the recluse Li Zhongfang, seeking a person for the sake of the Dharma and investigating the study of the *phala* (fruition) stage. He frequently transcribed the great meaning of the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* by hand.

He also studied various sutras such as the *Avataṃsaka*, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, the *Vimalakīrti*, and the *Awakening of Faith*. Regarding the School of Characteristics (*lakṣaṇa-yāna*), he alone penetrated its innermost depths.
He once said to his preceptor: "Characteristics do not arise from characteristics themselves; they are established through the self. The self does not exist as a self in itself;
it is established through characteristics. This was circulated at the lecture hall at that time as a marvelous saying (Da Xian succeeded him).
At Mount Lu, Chan Master Lin Ru Zongjun of Xilin was the son of the Lin family of Min. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Xilin?
The Master said, "In the heartless stupa, old clouds come and go; the guiding pines are tall as spring turns to autumn. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "The hair-piercing sword cuts through the clear breeze; the rattan staff picks up the bright moon."
He returned and asked, "Is there still a place for you to act on behalf of others, or not? The Master said, "One palm, one handful of blood.
The monk shouted. The Master said, "Even if you were to shout until the year of the donkey, Xilin’s staff would still not strike you.
The monk shouted again, and the Master immediately returned to his quarters (Bofan Ke succeeded him).
Chan Master Yisuminquan Xun of Shanghai was the son of the Xiang family of Cixi. His verse on departing this world says: "A lifetime spent only in the ordinary;
At the moment of death, what need for the extraordinary? If you wish to go, lift your robes and go; Dreams, illusions, and empty flowers are naturally resolved.
He further instructed: "After my death, quickly provide a load of firewood; do not delay in preparing the funeral pyre. —From *Xiang* [Record].
In the south at Tan and in the north at Cong, people spoke thus; I say that the green mountains are all suitable for burial.
After one year had passed, his disciples performed the cremation (teapi), and countless śarīra relics were found. The fourfold assembly erected a stupa (Da Yuan Yin succeeded him).
Master Chan Master Zutian Yuzhen of Shitang on Mount Tai ascends the hall for the opening of the retreat.
The entire world of the ten directions is but a single hall of white clouds. Today, all four quarters are to be sealed;
each and every one shall be closed off. You all must seek a way to emerge; if you do not seek a way to emerge, [you will remain trapped].
Thus, all that you see is nothing more than this very heaven and earth, sun and moon; it is nothing more than these mountains, rivers, forests, and marshes.
Your field of vision is not broad, and your breast is not great. Yet, how then shall you seek the path upon which you have emerged?
Be wide awake beneath the three rafter-poles; do not nod off to sleep before the seven-foot mat. —From the *Shang* (Supplement) [of the *Linji Lu*]

The Hall Master said: "White Cloud has never preached the Dharma from the beginning; even the Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of successive generations have all hung their mouths upon the wall.

Maitreya, his teacher kept no superfluous items in his room; there were only several hundred scrolls of ancient books.

Tianxi knows this to be wrong and has cleared it away on your behalf.

Encompassing heaven and earth, both mundane and supramundane dharmas emerge from this. No matter how you expose it to the sun or let it be buffeted by the wind, it only becomes increasingly radiant and magnificent.

the precious blade rests at times as he sits facing the sun. He asked, "What is the intent of the person within the realm? The Master said, [as above].

A single wing flies over the mountain peak. Do not say that Langye has no remaining words; who among you knows the secret meaning within? Evening *can*: It happened to be the time when a dog was barking.

One dharma remains. There is no need for further discussion of this auspicious matter. Let this residual harmony warm the *dantian*.

"Is Nirvana and Bodhi something defiled? After a long silence, he said: "Even if there were such a thing, you must go to the bottom of the great ocean and wash it clean once more before you can attain it.

The matter lies here. But tell me, what is this matter? "Birds flutter through the bamboo leaves as the first frost falls; A man stands before the plum blossoms while the snow is fragrant.

why was he unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi? The Master said, "When it is hot, one is too lazy to seek fire."

The Master said, "Do not slander him. [The monk] asked, "What is 'tranquil and unmoving'?
The Master said, "In the morning one travels to India; in the evening one returns to this land. [The monk] asked, "What is 'being moved and immediately penetrating'? The Master said, "One."

All you people, look with your own eyes! Most certainly do not seek them to the east or west. Is there anyone here who does not seek them to the east or west? A monk stepped forward, and the Master [continued]:

He said: "This is like seeking juice from a sesame cake. On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, the Master ascended the hall. Holding up his incense, he said: "This is the Yellow-Faced Gautama.
Three thousand years ago, atop the peak of the Snowy Mountains, he underwent six years of arduous toil. It was an inextricable tangle of vines that could not be severed.
In the end, for no reason, he buried it shallowly in a deep pit within Mount Kukkuṭapāda. From this point on, it has led [to all manner of complications]."

Climbing vines entangle branches; one knows not how many noble and enlightened monks they have ensnared and killed. Upādhyāya Cheng, being yourself no more than a mediocre fellow, has driven them into this very nest.
Today, I have deliberately uprooted it from its base and cast it into the incense burner, solely to fumigate their nostrils.
Why? Because one who harbors a grudge but does not seek revenge is no gentleman. (On the New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall. This is not [ordinary].
The mind is not the Buddha, nor is it a thing. Ultimately, what is it? Once you see through the iron walls and silver mountains, there is naturally a single path that reaches the heavens.
But tell me, what is this path that reaches the heavens? Let us all bow to one another and celebrate the New Year.
Do not let this once-a-year [opportunity] (the Day of the Heavenly Peak) pass in vain.
Zen Master Mingzhao Hongdu of Wuzhou, a successor of Master Liang, addressed the assembly: "In the three realms there is no dharma; where can one seek the mind?
The four great elements are originally empty; upon what does the Buddha rely to dwell? He then suddenly held up his staff and called to the assembly, saying: "Look! Look! You have a staff."
"I give you this staff; you have no staff. I take away your staff. When the ancients spoke thus, tell me, where did their meaning lie?
[He] threw down the staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters. Evening Assembly: He cited Xuefeng’s instruction to the assembly, which said:
"The entire universe is this gate of liberation. I hold out my hand and pull you, yet you refuse to enter. One.
The monk said, "I cannot help but find the Master strange. Another monk asked, "What is the use of entering?
Xuedou said, "Among these three, there is one who is saved. The Master remarked, "Great indeed was Xuefeng, yet he left his head behind while trailing his tail.
Since the entire universe is this gate of liberation, where else would you drag it? Piteous are those two monks, acting in such a manner."
This is a direct confrontation; it cannot avoid being like Xu Liu’s carrying a single-sided board. Now, as Xuedou said, "Among the three, one person is saved"—tell me, O assembly, which one is it?
[The Master] lets out a thunderous shout. A verse on the story of the wind and the banner: Two armies clash, refusing to cease;
Banners flash and flutter, stirring the people's grief. The General’s single sword settles heaven and earth.
A majestic and awe-inspiring presence throughout the four hundred prefectures. A verse on Zhaozhou’s examination of the two hermits:
"Seizing clouds and grasping mists is their livelihood; Ordinary and sage alike return to the non-dual home. Filling the seas and moving mountains are entirely in their hands;

Master Lianhe of Longquan, a companion of the Yunshan group at Wushan in Huzhou, addressed the assembly: "On a clear spring day, the spring birds sing. Spring...
Layer upon layer of mountains; brimming with spring water. Each and every one has seven openings and eight apertures; clearly visible, they encircle in hundreds of turns and thousands of folds.
This is the seal of the mind, uncarved by calligraphy; it expounds the wondrous gate that cannot be spoken. It simply must not be seen with the eyes nor heard with the ears. Why?
Because as soon as there is even a hair’s breadth of something, it is already dust. Addressing the assembly: It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha. It is...
He extended his hands and said, "Rubbing open both hands, everyone look! Ultimately, what is this that is so clearly manifest?

After a long silence, he said, "Countless are those who receive the empty and echo the sound, yet in the end, the primordial melody remains difficult to transmit. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Every dharma is fully present within oneself;
do not give rise to likes or dislikes. Whenever you take your seat and don your robes, what need is there to speak of 'once in ten thousand years'?"
[The Master] reflects. He lets out a shout. He offers a verse on the World-Honored One not yet having left Tuṣita Heaven: "The needle stops, speechless, suddenly startled by spring.
Incidentally remembering the search for fragrance, the colors compete for novelty. Upon the pillow, thoughts of longing are of a thousand kinds; Having awakened, who is the person within the dream?
He offers a verse on the World-Honored One holding up the flower: "Salt is salty by itself, and honey is sweet by itself. How can one bear this: upon the excrement, once again..."
Adding a point: If you say that picking up a flower was the transmission of the mind-seal, Kāśyapa’s smile now adds even more. (Tian'an Shengsi) Evening Sermon by Chan Master Ruiyan Meishan Mounian:
At the head of the stream where yellow leaves fall, deep within the white clouds, a spring pours down from the secluded cliff and the wind whistles through the high trees.
This is the gate of the Most Supreme; it is true emptiness, abiding nowhere. [The Master] lets out a shout and says: "It is not like this."
Investigating the source to its very root: fallen flowers and flowing water vanish into the profound distance. Evening Sermon. The spring mountains are green and the spring waters are verdant;
with every eye beholding the glory of the season, all things are complete. Willow branches hold the mist, plum blossoms break forth like jade. Listen as I sing a song for you, standing in the wind.
Flying clouds drift slowly out from the pine gate; mountain stream waters murmur through the empty valley.
It is not the *Pusa-man*, nor is it the *Qingping-le*. Striking the ground with his staff once, he said: "Dang-di-du-ding! Bi-ban-bin-bao-bo! **Small Sermon:** "The mind is not the Buddha;
when you arrive, it does not acknowledge you. Wisdom is not the Way; when you acknowledge it, you have not arrived."
The incense burner nods its head in the dark; the lantern laughs aloud in the light. But tell me, what is it that they laugh at?
Last night, the Big Dipper looked southward; to brew tea with a smoothing iron, one need not use a cauldron.
Ascending the hall on the Buddha’s Birthday: If one says that Śākyamuni was born today, you lose an eye. If one says that Śākyamuni was not born today...

he is called Puhua’s donkey, yet he is actually Guishan’s ox. He dwells peacefully within the tiger’s den and dances amidst the palace of demons.
He wields expedient means with reckless abandon, striking the golden bell and rolling the iron drum. As soon as he grasps the blade of Jiyun, he immediately lets it fly."
A crossbow of a thousand *jin* can pierce through ten billion mountains and rivers; the great earth is entirely without a single inch of soil.

Addressing the assembly, he raised the example of Chan Master Fayan’s discourse on ascending the hall, where he said: "Throughout the entire world, all is bright and clear; there is not a single thread of hair.
If there were a single thread of hair, it would be just that—a single thread of hair. Fadeng said: "If there were a single thread of hair, it would not be a single thread [of delusion]."
[The Master] says: "Dafayan, great as he was, was entirely bound to death by a single thread. Dizang was not so;

if there were even a single thread [of attachment], one would enter hell like a shot arrow. He offers this verse on the Ox King’s Dance: "The Ox King laughs and dances, a hidden blade concealed within;
A serpent’s heart in a Buddha’s mouth—his resentment will not fade. A single grain drags the void through the dreams of kalpas; Let him teach..."
A torrential autumn tide pours from the tongue. In praise of the story of Qingyuan’s question to the Sixth Patriarch regarding not falling into stages, [Guanxiu] says:
One step takes Caoxi; the wild beast perishes. From now on, I shall no longer sit upon the White Cloud Seat. Hiding one’s body within the charcoal, one forgets nobility;
Who would recognize that the moss-covered Jade Hall lies in ruin? (Guan’an Dai, the successor)
A Small Assembly Talk by Chan Master Hongzong Yinqiao of Xinzhou: "I have a single phrase that the World-Honored One could not speak and Kāśyapa could not hear.

As for the rest—the forty-seven patriarchs of India and the twenty-three ancestors of the Tang land, down to the great spiritual friends such as Deshan and Linji—they have yet to catch even a glimpse of it in their dreams. Today, as the time has arrived, I cannot help but speak."
He spoke his mind fully, then raised his whisk and said: "Even if you were to see it here, it is still ten thousand miles to Yuzhou. Small Assembly (Xiao Can).
He cited the story of Zhaozhou, who was drawing water on a well-house when he saw Nanquan passing by.
Zhaozhou then embraced a pillar and cried out, "Save me! Save me! Nanquan then struck him with the foot of the ladder, saying, "One, two, three, four, five."
The Governor was slightly taken aback. He then prepared his formal regalia and went to the Abbot’s quarters, saying, "Just now, I thanked the Master for saving me.
The Master said, "One father conceals for his son; one son conceals for his father. To examine it closely, this too is merely airing the family's private disgrace.
If Upādhyāya Yi had been there at that time, when the man said 'save me, save me,' he would have used both hands—"
Raising the momentum of lamentation: Tell me, is this the same as Nanquan, or is it different? Small Assembly (Xiao Can): I cite Deshan’s rule: "No speaking;
thirty blows for those who ask. Here at Foshan, it is not so. Whether you ask or do not ask, I do not strike you.
Why? One dares not scar a good piece of flesh. Upon pure white ground, how could one bear to defile it? *Zhuo*! (The staff strikes the floor.)
[He] leaned on his staff and looked left and right, saying: "The land is vast and the people are few; those who meet [one another] are rare. (Lingyuan should succeed him.
Chan Master Dapò Huán of the Cāotáng Hermitage in Jīngzhào ascended the hall and struck his staff, saying:
"If you can see it here, Śākyamuni does not precede, and Maitreya does not follow. He drives the sages and dispatches the commoners, arranging the past and present, and tramples them down."
Zhongnan Mountain kicks over the Wei River, gouges open Kumārajīva’s eyes, and knocks out Guifeng’s nostrils.
Does the assembly understand? A thousand peaks welcome the beautiful sun; a single stream runs through Chang’an. (He leans on his staff. Descending from the seat, he ascends the hall.
Last night, a Chan practitioner entered my room and asked about the circumstances of the woman entering meditative absorption. This morning, this mountain monk—
Without sparing his lips, he brought it up for the great assembly. If you say he emerged from samādhi, you miss Mañjuśrī; if you say he did not emerge from samādhi, you miss Wǎngmíng. But tell me:
if he does not involve himself with either, you miss the woman. When one reaches this point and does not act in any of these ways, you miss Gautama. After all, what should be done?
He brandished his staff, whirled it like a whirlwind, and dispersed them, saying: "Strike!"
This mountain monk’s transgression: ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. The sun and moon of today are the sun and moon of antiquity;
yet by the time one reaches the twelfth month, their flavors have become distinct. Needlessly, at midnight, a sky full of stars deceived Śākyamuni, causing his eyes to be covered in dust.
In praise of the story of Great Compassion’s diagnosis of the illness: "Spring arrives everywhere with the same redness; why bother to judge it as pale or deep?"
Thick. Waiting for the morning breeze to blow into one’s dream; the yellow oriole sings amidst the green thickets (Lingyuan Yingji).
Zen Master Cheng’an Che of Jingdu Yi-jiao ascended the hall and gave a shout, saying: "It cannot be calculated or measured by the mind;
it is simply as I intend. I do not wish it to be thus; my aim is to cast away the staff and let go of both hands."
The hand moves freely in all directions—seven ways long and eight ways wide—responding to things and following circumstances without any obstruction. Let it be as it may;
even if one were to produce gold at will, I would ultimately not rely upon a single thing. Again, he let out a shout and said:

"Good sons, if you can have such faith and enter in this way, you need not don the three-fold armor of the primary elements nor unfurl the banners of the five positions to sweep away the miasma of heterodoxy and cleanse the calamities of the dark."
The ominous vapors! A chaotic scattering of pearls; ninety-six marks are cast forth all at once. Horizontally grasping the Mohe sword, nineteen gates are opened together.
Should one’s inclinations differ, they will be unable to grasp it directly before the sun. Do not say that this mountain monk is deceiving you—consecutive shouts!
[He] descends from the seat. Ascending the hall: The life-vein of the patch-robed monks, the true essence of Prajñā, is like the pure lunar disc; when it emerges...
Ten thousand waves divide their reflections; like a blade drawn from its scabbard, when it is used, there is no one within a thousand *li* to whom it is not related.
Whether Buddha or Patriarch, who can fathom the sentiments of the holy and the common? Lifting your head to gaze beyond the heavens—who is there who is my equal?
Ascending the hall, he said: "Flowers bloom upon the ridges, willows unfurl by the embankments. Yellow birds tune the lute of Shu Ye; fragrant grasses enter the verses of Lord Xie. What..."
One must see form to clarify the mind and hear sound to awaken; it is not merely seeking bubbles upon the water—it is already like placing grit in one's eyes.
With such a report, I expect that half of those who nod their heads horizontally and half of those who nod their heads vertically will understand.

Setting these aside: the three-legged golden incense burner in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the pair of stone lions at the foot of the Lugou Bridge—these all fall within the realm of "Yes" and "No," or perhaps they remain undecided.
Rather than that, it is better to perform a somersault within the light of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā and, with palms joined, say:
"Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva! Namo Great Compassionate Bodhisattva! Then, open both hands.
Descending from his seat, he ascends the hall and gives a shout, saying: "The man of no dependence is the mother of all Buddhas. Do you all understand? It cannot be named, it cannot be described;
it cannot be grasped, it cannot be relinquished. It is constantly illuminating and constantly manifest.
The Iron Ring Mountains cannot obstruct its radiance; pervading the world and pervading space, the vast heavens cannot cover its essence. It is neither pure nor mixed. Ten thousand...
An elephant cannot conceal its true nature; it neither dwells nor shifts. Worldly afflictions (*kleśa*) cannot disturb its essence.
If you wish to know the definitive point, you must first break out into a cold sweat. [The Master] gave another shout and descended from his seat. (Nan’gang Quan succeeded him.)
Master Yijue Yongchan of Sheng’an Temple in Beijing was the son of the Pan family from Wanping. During his childhood, he dreamed of a deity flashing like a golden serpent streaking through the air;
upon waking, his entire body was drenched in sweat. He subsequently entered Sheng’an Temple to pay respects to Chan Master Yinming, under whom he received the tonsure.

He then followed Dajue Xiu to receive full ordination (*upasampadā*) and was granted instruction on the essential points of *chan* (meditation). However, it was extremely difficult for him to achieve realization. Furthermore...

For days and nights he exhaustively investigated the words and phrases of the ancients, yet he could not penetrate them. One day, as he took paper to light a lamp, he suddenly had an awakening upon seeing the flame;
only then did he realize that his own luminosity was originally not something obtained from without. Later, having received the seal of approval from Píngyáng, he ascended the hall and said:
"The tortoise-hair whisk leaks the springtime radiance; ten thousand purples and thousands of reds are not concealed. I thank all..."

The mountains exerted their utmost strength; Saint An had no ground upon which to stand, overcome with shame and confusion. When the World-Honored One ascended the seat, Mañjuśrī struck the gavel and said:
"Look closely; it would be well to issue a formal indictment. Why? Because the land is vast and the people are few; those who meet one another are rare.

Upon returning to the capital after his audience, he ascended the hall. To those from all quarters, he showed the way: sometimes by raising an eyebrow or blinking an eye, and sometimes by holding up...

Brandishing the whisk or the mallet, or speaking here and there, or with staff and shout exchanged in rapid succession—even if one possesses great compassion, it is difficult to avoid falling into habitual traps.
How much better it is for our old man to remain in a state of silent spontaneity, with a single even-mindedness.

When monks arrive, they have their porridge and rice in abundance; they carry firewood and draw water, following the "Deer-Herd" tradition, picking tea and planting rice, thereby flourishing in the Way.

As for one’s livelihood: if asked about the two characters of "Buddha-Dharma," how could one be willing to draw legs onto a snake? Why? "When the Way prevails, the Son of Heaven need not issue commands;
when times are peaceful, there is no need to sing songs of Great Peace. Addressing the assembly, after concluding the story of the difficult childbirth, the Master said:
"Yangjue tripped on level ground. The World-Honored One administered medicine because of an illness. To examine this thoroughly, it cannot help but provoke laughter."
Pohouen-k’ou (Destroying People’s Mouths). Addressing the assembly, after concluding the story of the World-Honored One’s first birth, the Master said:

“The World-Honored One was skilled at wielding the Great Black Saber, yet he could not avoid wounding his own blade or injuring his hand. Although Yunmen understood the knotted joints [of the sword], he had already fallen into his trap.
As for my judgment thus, tell me: what is its intent? After a long silence, he said: “The battle clouds stretch across the sea; the spearhead is drawn.”
Sword swirling at the Dragon Gate, a small assembly for the appointed time: The Venerable Ancestor Linji established the school of Huangbo by the banks of the Hutuo River;
its thunder was fierce and its momentum swift as the wind. Today, this mountain monk raises high the banner of the Dharma beside the Taiye Pond.

As swift as the wind and as fierce as thunder, the Master brandishes his whisk and says: "The present is the past; the past is the present. Both past and present are swallowed in a single gulp by the *dunlu* (a type of gourd).
If you ask for a verse that clearly distinguishes guest and host, I shall kick out a broken sand-pot from my toes.

He then offers a verse on the "Woman's Determination": "A skilled physician has read every pulse-diagnosis manual; To cure an illness, why need one expend so much medicine? Do not strike the fishing pole too often."
Playing with Cleverness. When the wind comes, waves arise naturally upon the surface of the water (Tianye Zhousi).
Chan Master Yansong of Yantou asked, "What is a phrase that transcends the ordinary?
The master said, "A red fish beneath the water climbs up a tree. The monk paused to reflect. The master said, "On the jeweled pagoda, wind-bells chime and tinkle in broad daylight. The monk...

Upon these words, he suddenly attained realization and said, "I understand! The Master immediately seized him and said, "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! He replied, "In broad daylight, there is a clear ringing;
it is on the precious pagoda’s wind-bells. He then prostrated himself, and the Master let him go. (From *Lüān Yuèsì*)
Chan Master Xianbi Yuan of Kaixian on Mount Lu addressed the assembly. He cited the karmic occasion of Aṅgulimāla’s childbirth difficulties and offered this verse:
"Having mastered the art of piercing the willow leaf, he strikes two vultures with a single arrow at the sound of the string.

As the young gentleman returning from his spring excursion arrives home late, he looks back and sees the snow has vanished from the mountain. Addressing the assembly amidst the snow, he said: "It is enough that the snow melts."
All is exhausted. Naturally, spring arrives. But when the snow has not yet melted, where is the spring? The assembly remained silent.
The Master took up his staff, whirled it like a whirlwind, and dispersed them. Addressing the assembly: "At the head of Zhaoyin Bridge there is a slab of stone.
You all, day after day, carry bricks and transport tiles, haul earth and drag timber. For what reason do you fail to tread upon it? The assembly was speechless.
[The Master] agreed. He raised his staff and said, "Dangerous! On the occasion of the end of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall and said: "The autumn wind is cool; the autumn night is long.
Those who have not yet returned yearn for their hometowns. Let me ask you all: where is your hometown? A monk came forward, prostrated, and returned to the assembly.
The Master said, "A mangy horse tied to a withered post. (Tianye Huizhao was the successor.)

Chan Master Tiefu of Mount Jiao in Jingkou was the son of the Zhang family from Shanyang. Having long served Tianyue Zhouding, he eventually attained the inner sanctum and received the transmission of the Dharma.
Once, while traveling by boat past Jingkou, he took a liking to the secluded seclusion of Mount Jiao and settled there.
He once composed a verse which says: "Songbirds call as I open the door within the woods; A crocodile cries on the riverbank just as I light my lamp. He resided there.
"Who can fully comprehend this mountain scene? A single monk in a thatched cottage of three rafters. He also said:

"This year, with nothing to do, I have come among men; who would say that I am as idle as one amidst the clouds? When the clouds suddenly follow the rain away, my idleness remains all day long upon the green mountains.
Addressing the assembly, after concluding the *Kōan* of Xiangyan Climbing the Tree, the Master said: "Great indeed was Xiangyan!"
To the assembly: "Exerting effort leads to clumsiness. [The Master] raises the story of Luzu facing the wall and offers this verse:
When the beautiful maiden, sixteen years of age, embroiders at her loom, She cannot bear to pause her needle for a moment. On the branch, what bird is grieving for spring?

Just as two by two they arrive, they speak of their longing love. To the assembly: [The Master] raises the case of the Venerable Elder Chen of Muzhou, who, upon seeing a monk preaching, called out to him, "Seat! (Zuo).
The Master said, "Master," and the other assented. The former remarked, "A fellow carrying a wooden board. The Master offered this verse: "Cast out, it requires no lock;
At the moment of encounter, it is like the Iron Ring Mountains. Even with a thousand or ten thousand eyes, One cannot glimpse it here. (Tianyue Zhousu)
The evening *chan* assembly of Master Gaoshan Yu’an of Xiàngtián, Shangyú. He presented his staff, saying, "This staff has leaped forth from the void.
He then threw it to the ground and said, "It seeks to take your very lives. Only those who do not encounter its sharp edge can pass this one barrier.
Even if you pass it, you have still not reached the end. Ultimately, by what principle must you act before you can truly accord with him?"
"Quickly! A monk supported him with a staff and led him across. The Master received it and, with a whirlwind, struck and dispersed them.
He addressed the assembly, citing Zen Master Ying’an: "Seventy monks from thirty-three prefectures, with donkey heads and horse faces, are loathed by all.
Had the various quarters possessed the skill to seize dragons, there would have been no way for me to reach Jingming today. Xiangtian also has a verse; I shall cite it.
Like those people—dozens of monks with iron foreheads and copper heads—who plant fields and trade for their food, free from resentment;
drifting and dazed, they sit together in the hall. With paper wicks and abundant oil, the lamp shines even brighter. A verse on the World-Honored One holding up the flower:

The dhūta practitioner has lost his edge, and the eyes of others grow dim; Yet the ability to laugh remains as intimate as when he first smiled. Had one been able to take charge at that moment, one would have avoided [the cycle].
The Teaching today revives those in the pit. In praise of the World-Honored One’s state before leaving Tuṣita Heaven: "Before leaving Tuṣita, the saving of beings was complete;
I cherished that moment when he was lifted out. The eyebrows of both parties were crossed in an eight-character 'A' shape.
One word exhausts the Way; it is truly real. (Tianyue Zhousi)
Master Xinghua Longzhu’s Small Assembly on the Buddha’s Birthday at the Eighth Day of the Twelfth Month, Entrusting to Master Yazi: "The heavens are cold and the people are cold;
the dripping water freezes solid. The eye-sight pierces through the stars filling the sky—this was originally but a dream born of a feverish mind.
All the ancient masters of the various quarters say that two thousand years ago, Śākyamuni, the Old Man, before Mount Zhengjue, attained enlightenment upon beholding the morning star."

A distant descendant of the Nanman and Gelao tribes of seventy lifetimes ago, I venture to say: awakening is indeed not absent, yet alas, it falls into the second rank. Tell me, assembly, what is the first rank?
(With his staff, he whirled it like a whirlwind and struck them all at once, dispersing them.
He spoke this verse on "The Woman Emerging from Samādhi": Fragrance conceals the heavy gates; the day-drops of the water-clock are sparse. A single branch of lush splendor adorns the painting.
West of the tower: The coquettish birds do not understand the secluded person’s intent; they merely continue to cry out with their intermittent spring songs.
In praise of the dog having no Buddha-nature: The sword leaves the precious sheath; the medicine emerges from the golden flask.
Touch it, strike it—bringing the dead back to life (Senshō Tetsusshi).
Chan Master Xiaozhang Zhizhao of Shouguo Temple in Lishui was the son of the Xu family from Liuan Prefecture.
He ascended the hall and said: "Within heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a single treasure, hidden within the mountain of form.
Great assembly, as you come and go, shoulders bearing the sun and moon, foreheads towering like Mount Sumeru—tell me, where is this treasure? After a long silence, he said: "A kingfisher steps..."
The rain turns over lotus leaves; egrets break through the mist of the bamboo grove. Descending from the monastery to ascend the hall: he presses down the clouds upon the rushing waters.
The Dharma banner stands wherever it may be, establishing the guiding principles. Worn-out straw sandals have trodden the mountain paths by stream;
now they pass again through a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. Grasping his staff, he simply walks away. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master—
It is said: "The *mao* grass sickle is used until it becomes thoroughly worn through. Regarding the ancient worthy eating the pounded rice, the verse says:
"The peach and plum trees speak not; the yellow oriole pays the price. A character passed through three transcriptions—how could *wu* and *an* become *ma*? (Shanziyu succeeded him).
Chan Master Cui Ting Yao of Baoyun Monastery in Shuzhou ascended the hall and said: "The mountains are not pure, and the waters are not elegant.

Yellow earth and stone heads are as much like barbarians as dogs. Brothers, do not run about in confusion. As soon as a monk stepped forward, the Master descended from his seat and ascended the hall again, saying:
"Within the boiling cauldrons and burning coals lies cold ice; within the hells one beholds the Great Dharmakāya. It is vast and long."
The tongue is always within it, turning this true sutra to deliver immeasurable multitudes. At times it appears and disappears, sporting with supernatural powers in samādhi;
according to circumstances and as it pleases, it attains great mastery. Now tell me: what kind of person speaks this Dharma?
He gave a shout and said: "A single cry of a yellow bird outside the green mountains; wherever one goes, one acts as the master with effortless grace. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
"When all things have been extinguished and not even a thread of silk remains, what then? The Master said: "You would die of shame! The monk asked:
"But when putting on clothes and performing formal rites, how is it then? The Master said: "Naked and bare, every limb exposed. Then he said: "The wind whistles..."
The drizzling rain falls pitter-patter. A stone man plants banana trees upon his head. The goose freezes to death; the chicken roasts to death.
Spring marches forth with the ordinances of winter—all in one accord. (He lets out a shout. Entering the hall: Raising an eyebrow, flashing an eye;
facing the wall, shaking a bell—these have long since been missed. Why so? "Many times the solitary boat could not go forward; the partridge cries toward the setting sun."
He then gave a shout (Da Xianxian Si).
This was the informal discourse of Chan Master Hui of Jinling Gu-tan Dumen. If one does not enter the Hall of Flower Treasury, how can one recognize the treasures of Flower Treasury?
Clearly and vividly, the pearl is upon the platter; why need one seek it elsewhere? The assembly of cloud-and-water monks fills the hall, desiring—
What is it? Raising the eyebrows, one misses the mark. The verse on the Woman Emerging from Samādhi says: "Taking up the unperforated flute, who knows the thief’s body is revealed?
At the same place where a finger-snap is made, how many people have been killed by doubt? The verse on the Ancient Virtuous One Eating Oil-Cakes says:
"Walking, he does not leave his door; sitting, he does not lean over the hall. If you know the essential point, the entire world cannot hide it."
(Daoyuan Xynsi). Zen Master Tianhai of Zifu Temple in Longshu composed a verse on Prince Nanda: "Bones returned to the father, flesh returned to the mother;
In his entirety, without dependence, who dares to behold him? Only the mountain flowers continue to bloom, year after year."

Dancing in the Wind. In praise of a woman emerging from meditative absorption (*samādhi*), he said: "Layered peaks of emerald green encircle the solitary crag; The moon rises above the pine treetops, its color intensely deep.
The crane’s tears fall through the vast sky, their sound faint and fine; The monkey cries in the deep valley as the sun is just turning red.
He asked: "What thing in the human world is most precious? The Master replied: "A broken hemp-rope. He asked: "What thing is most base? The Master replied: "Torn straw."
[The monk] asked about shoes: "How is it when one does not fall into the categories of noble or base? The Master said, "The Stone Ganda at the crossroads.

As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him, saying, "Why are you pulling at a tiger's whiskers? A monk asked, "When the vast waves are surging and boundless, how can one cross over without relying on a boat or a rudder?
The Master said, "Ride backward upon Yangqi’s three-legged donkey. The monk was speechless. The Master struck him repeatedly with his staff and drove him out. (Fang’an)
(From the *Yun-si*).
Master Chan Jingxian of Jincheng Dizang addressed the assembly: "If one discusses this matter, there is no principle that can be extended, and no words that can be spoken.
It requires no contrivance; how could it tolerate fabrication? Fabrication and contrivance are difficult to grasp."
Arranged; not contrived. Originally and naturally perfect, bright and radiant. The Great Elephant of Jiazhou has its trunk reaching toward heaven;
the Iron Ox of Shanfu wears horns upon its head. The pines, waters, wind, and moon—few know them; the Persian from the South Sea gives birth to the Baize.
He gave a shout and addressed the assembly: "In the past, when I was in Jinling, I stepped upon an object with my feet as I walked along, and I picked up a thing with my hand.
From the beginning, I have not permitted others to know of it; I have brought it forth here to serve as a joy for entering the gate.
Tell me, everyone, what is it? He threw down his whisk and said, "Do not look at it! If you look, your eyes will be ruined."
Withered. To smell it would split one's brain. The Verse on Baizhang’s Wild Fox:
Baizhang’s wild fox—its words direct and its speech coarse. *Sili sili*, *sulu sulu*. (Lingyuan should succeed.)
Master Lunxu of Lianxi Praying for Auspiciousness addressed the assembly: "Yangqi’s three-legged donkey is also this fierce and malicious.

By chance it tramples the Lu River until it is cut off; bottomlessly clear, there is not a single drop left. Brothers, do not underestimate yourselves; everyone’s nostrils are wide open at the bottom.
In the four directions and eight corners there is no obstruction; one flies ten thousand miles across the edge of the sky."
A Lone Osprey. Entering the hall, [the Master] said: "This very mind is Buddha. Before the crags, the wind sounds through the *lang-zhan* bamboo. "Neither this mind nor that Buddha.

Deep in the woods, the cry of a solitary bird as the last flowers fall. Striking his whisk, he said: "Sharing these high mountains and flowing waters, a single melody is clearly heard by those who know.
Entering the hall, a monk asked: "What is the Buddha-dharma of the deep mountains? The Master said: "A spring."

The sound of the voice hung over the precarious rocks; the sunlight was cool and clear upon the pines. [A monk] said, "If that is so, then there is no dharma outside the mind—everywhere before one's eyes is green mountain.
The Master said, "Do not propagate this recklessly. He then continued, "Bazhang twisted his nostrils out of shape; Lingyun lost his eyesight.
Even if one were to compare this to the single aperture above, it would still not be definitively clear. I dare ask you all: what is it?"
Regarding the "one upper opening," he planted his staff upright and said: "The night monkey cries out a heart-rending sound. A monk came for an audience;
as soon as he spread his sitting mat, he said, "Even before entering the gate, I have already presented myself to you, Master. The Master said, "Why do you thrust your head into the glue-pot again?
The monk paused to reflect, and the Master struck him straight out. He asked, "What is it that all phenomena return to?"

1. The Master said: "The hands are long, but the sleeves of the robe are short. [A monk] asked: "When all have returned to one place, where does it go? The Master said: "The feet are thin, but the straw sandals are wide. Verse on the World-Honored One Holding Up a Flower: The General’s secret command does not allow a breath of wind to pass;
A million heroic troops plot their strategic merit. Who would have known that the city was overturned by a single smile? From the level ground, the weapons of war rise up toward the east and west.

Verse on Nalāta: The Great Nalāta severed his own flesh; His body was born anew from the Dharma-body. He was neither a man nor a god; How could he be categorized as either? The three heads and six arms were originally empty; The four elements and five aggregates are fundamentally non-existent. If you wish to see the true person, Look at the one who has no head.
Zi Xi Gu said: "The milk-crow caws and the jade screen is scattered; One pillow of coolness, a single breeze through the window.
Having woken from sleep, the sound of the flute is nowhere to be found; Moonlight shines amidst the *wú* leaves filling the steps. A verse on Zhaozhou’s “The Dog Has No Buddha-nature”:
"Zhaozhou says the dog has no Buddha-nature; The cuckoo, harboring emotion, calls all night long. With every cry of blood, it weeps, unable to return home."
"Still pitying that the spring colors remain upon the rivers and lakes" (Lingyuan Ying).
Master Huaihaimen Zhun of Longshu, at Quanzhou Nantui, addressed the assembly. Having finished citing the story of the World-Honored One’s birth, the Master said:
Gautama’s eyes bulge out, looking much like a target set up to receive arrows. Although Shaoyang deployed his true command, he was unaware that mud and water had soaked through his entire body.
If one were to view this with the True Eye, it would be laughable—why? Because his father stole the sheep.
And you have realized this yourself. To commemorate the World-Honored One’s awakening upon seeing the stars, he said: "Burying alive on the Snowy Peaks, the cold penetrates to the heart;
Opening his eyes, he immediately boasted of reviving after death. The poor child who has found the treasure need not speak of wealth;
In whose house is there no bright pearl? He asked: "Great Sage of the Four Quarters, why did you appear in Yangzhou? The Master replied: "Flies are biased toward the foul."
Chufei asked, "Is this the place where one lets go of body and life? The Master said, "A stagnant pool does not harbor dragons. (Lingyuan later succeeded him.
Zen Master Tanzhao Ming of Dabeiji, Jiangyin, ascended the hall and said: "To speak for ten feet is not as good as practicing for one foot. One discerns the soil from its sprouts;
one recognizes a person by their words. You brothers who dwell here: the mountain fields provide only coarse grain."
Rice, vegetables, and pale yellow pickles. Not staying here with me, traveling alone without a companion, he waves his hand and departs from Chang’an.
Is there still a place of failure? Or is there no place of failure? Do not seek transformation at the Dragon Gate;
