"I have answered before. Now, when asked, I shall ask; when answered, I shall answer. Question and answer are both complete. Why is there such a vast difference between heaven and earth?
Ten thousand words, however appropriate, are not equal to a single moment of silence. [The Master] ascended the hall and addressed the assembly:

"A flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech. This day is the very moment this mountain monk was born. All you good people should know this. Let the Senior Official Bai examine the assembly!"
They were cooking fragrant food from the Accumulated Merit Hall to prepare an offering. As they placed fire near the cold spot, a great commotion arose.
"Virtuous ones, come forth in a multitude; we pray that you will preach the Dharma for us. This may be called celebrating and praising through a vegetarian feast;

such a favorable opportunity is difficult to encounter. When the mountain monk arrived here, there was no way to retreat; he was left with nothing but his mouth as a carrying pole. At such a time, reflect carefully upon it thoroughly. *Bì*.
In the end, what exactly has been said that would suffice? If one speaks of the Buddha, the Buddha is a provisional name. If one speaks of the Dharma, the Dharma has no fixed characteristics.
If one speaks of where this mountain monk’s own karmic origins lie, my karmic origins are in Rui’an.
Your secular surname is Pan; there is no need to mention it again. If I were to further explain where this mountain monk’s natal *yuanchen* (vital point) resides:
my natal sign belongs to Hai (the Tenth Earthly Branch). Those born under Hai take the form of pigs.
A "mud pig" and a "scabby dog"—these are precisely one's natal *yuanchen*. One's natal *yuanchen* is simply the mud pig and the scabby dog. Speaking thus, do you all, sirs, understand?
Do you have sufficient faith? If you can truly believe this, then even with horns upon your head and fur upon your body, you will have a share in repaying your benefactors.
If this is not yet so, today Minyin has lost his advantage. (He raises his staff, strikes it once, and descends from the seat.
Small Assembly Sermon: He suddenly calls out to the assembly, saying: "The winter is not cold until after the New Year. Today, the tenth month has come to an end; if you move even slightly—
Sweat breaks out all over one's body. Four or five days ago there was thunder; two or three days ago there was rain and hail. Peach and plum blossoms fill the courtyard.
On the grass of the mountain behind, snake skins are shed. Look at the people harvesting grain in the fields;
they still strip off their clothes and bare their shoulders. This is precisely the season when winter is not yet cold. You all will naturally understand this clearly.
Doubtful. As for saying, "Look after the winter solstice," what exactly is one looking at? Is it looking at the plum blossoms? Is it looking at the snow?
Or is it looking at the meaning of Buddha-nature? [The Master] lets out a sudden shout.

If he had not shouted here to arrest you, I fear that even if you looked until the year of the donkey, there would still be no day of rest. Nevertheless, this too is like practicing spring rites during winter. Hehe! [He] returns.
In the summer of the Ding-si year of the Kangxi era, the Abbot fell slightly ill.

On the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month, during the sequence of the assembly’s inquiries after his health, the Master said, "In my life as a mountain monk, I have had no other concerns except for the unfinished entrustment of my late master.
Speaking of it, my eyes suddenly fill with tears. He then wrote a final testament exhorting the assembly that, in observing the period of mourning, they must practice frugality and restraint.

There was no need to perform formal ritual services that would have depleted the monastery’s permanent assets. At the hour of You (5–7 p.m.), the Master took a finger and traced a character for the *gāthā* in the palm of his attendant Mingzheng.
Mingzheng immediately prepared paper and brush; the Master then wrote as follows: "How can one speak of coming from birth and going to death?
In the state of non-action where study has ceased, even half a phrase is too much. To know the ultimate point, look at the opening of the mouth Without moving a single lip."
He suffered from a chronic ailment. Casting aside his writing brush, he passed away with a serene expression. His secular age was fifty-five, and his years as a monk were twenty-nine.
He was cremated according to the Dharma, and his remains were enshrined in a stūpa at the eastern foot of his home mountain, Jilun Yong, who composed an inscription for the pagoda.
Ten volumes of his recorded sayings (*yulu*) circulate in the world. (Succeeded by Fachuangzhi).
Chan Master Duanshu of Baoguang Monastery in Ruian ascended the hall. Holding up his staff and striking it once, he said:
"This very thing is one's original affinity, one's primal destiny and birth-year. It cannot be contained within the five elements; even the most skillful mathematician could not calculate it.

It does not increase when in the state of a sage, nor does it decrease when among the common folk. It fills without being full; it is drawn from without being exhausted. Sit upright and receive [it]."

Offerings. May the donors always be at peace and happy. Even if someone were to investigate and penetrate [the truth] before the matter has been raised, this mountain monk would not decline to see them off with drums and banners.
Why? Because every person possesses the vajra-body; they must directly take it up and meet a master. Small private instruction:
"Seven people, eight grains—seek much fortune for yourself. Give one coin to Rāhula’s son; this is the definitive point.

This year the silkworms and wheat have ripened; on the day of the grain, the spring equinox arrives. Heaven bestows its bounty upon the virtuous; the treasuries are full and the granaries are replete.
That which issues from the gate is the family’s treasure. Thus, the seasons are harmonious and the harvests are bountiful—just like a water buffalo.
Furthermore, how is it? He held up his staff and said: "The plow and the harrow never leave one's person;
they remain only upon the field of one's own home. Each time it is turned over, it is renewed. Small Assembly (Xiao Can): "The moon is full in heaven;
the moon is half-full among men. Everywhere the cloth bags are untied; fire-trees and silver flowers are in profusion. At this very moment, tell me, how do you judge it?"

[The Master] judged [the situation]. Holding his whisk, he drew a circle in the air and said: "The gentleman is harmonious yet not conformist. You monks, look with high resolve at this informal sermon.
On this auspicious festival of Qingming, the peach and plum trees laugh; in the wild fields and deserted graves, there is only sorrow.

For those of us in the monastic community who have not yet clarified the Great Matter, it is as if we had lost our parents—what is there to laugh about? On these long rows of beds, there is rice porridge and rice to eat.
What is there to grieve? Laughter is simply for the white peaches and red apricots. Amidst their layered confusion, flowers do not fail to bloom without the spring breeze;
yet once they have bloomed, they are blown away by the wind. Grief is simply for the desolate graves in the wild fields, where cold smoke drifts vast and thin.
When spring comes, the weeds and thistles grow as before—where can one see grandchildren hanging paper money? Here in this mountain monk’s place...

There is no need for sorrow; there is nothing to laugh at. With three cups of clear tea and a single incense offering, one reaches all the ancestral pagodas of the hundred thousand patriarchs at once.
(He makes a sweeping motion with his whisk. Descent from the seat. Small Sermon: This very morning is indeed this very morning.
Yesterday was already yesterday; in the blink of an eye, it is tomorrow. Time passes as swiftly as a split arrow. Therefore it is said: "The matter of birth and death is great;
impermanence is rapid. To deceive others is calamity; to spare others is blessing. A single thought that turns back to the source is sufficient in every way.
[He] struck his staff and let out a shout, saying: "If they have no sores themselves, there is no need to gouge out their flesh. (Fazhangzhi, successor).
Chan Master Xueji Yuan of Dongbao in Chuzhou ascended the hall and said: "A single phrase cuts off the current; a thousand rivers cease their flow.
The perfect faculty sings alone; ten thousand sages fall silent. Who would dare to meet the edge of the 'blow-off-hair' sword? How could one even bear to listen to the 'poison-painted' drum?
Even if someone were to shout and scatter the mountain peaks, or overturn the very bottom of the great ocean, they still may not move it. Why is this so?"
"Stir it and calamity arises. (He gives a shout. He descends from his seat. Ascending the hall, he plants his staff on the ground and says:
"It can kill and it can give life; it can let loose and it can seize. Sometimes its verification lies with me, yet you do not know.

Sometimes its verification lies with you, yet I, this mountain monk, do not understand. If I were to understand, it would be like branches sprouting outside the joints, bringing laughter to bystanders. You people..."
If you know, you will fall into a pit or drop into a trench, with no hope of raising your head. If you wish to attain freedom from both faults, what must you do to accord with the Way?
[The Master] threw down his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall: Solitary and towering, steep and majestic—this is the orthodox command of Vaiśālī and the custom of Magadha.
At the top of a hundred-foot pole, the path is narrow; on a single-plank bridge, passersby are few. It is all one and the same ancient...
The song has no melody; tell me, how can it be harmonized? Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: In an instant, the springtime light departs and leaves nothing behind;
For a hundred years, the wind-blown trees turn and stir up sorrow. The cuckoo weeps until the third watch of the moon; Blood fills the branches, yet its resentment does not cease.
While traveling through the mountains, an attendant monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma in the depths of ten thousand mountains? The Master said:
The murmuring stream flows like the subtle chanting of pure dharma; the cries of the hidden birds express the wondrous workings of the mind.
When Master Wan visited the Teacher, he asked, "We meet face-to-face; please speak quickly. The Teacher said, "Do not mistake it. Wan said, "I have seen through it."
The Master then gave a shout. During tea, the Master asked, "Hufa, who did you study under before? Wan pointed to his chest and said, "Master Wan.
The Master said, "He is not here at this very moment. Wan said, "I missed him face-to-face. The Master gave another shout. Wan hesitated, and the Master said:
As expected, it was not with General Ji. He encountered the Master at Zhitian, and upon seeing him, he asked immediately, "May I ask whether there is Buddha-dharma within the army?
The Master replied, "There is. Ji asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma within the army?"
The Master stood at his desk, leaning on his staff, and said, "Sweep away the ranks of the myriad demons; turn back to court to pay homage to the Sage Ruler.
Guo Ji said, "If that is so, I shall reward my three armies; I request the Master to determine their ranks. The Master said, "The Five Marquises have exhausted all their lifelong efforts;
from now on, I shall grow weary of looking again at the Odes and Documents. Guo Ji was greatly delighted, prostrated himself, and withdrew. (Fachangzhi was his successor.)

Chan Master Baoyue Jinshan was the son of the Li family of Yongjia. At the age of fifteen, upon seeing a legendary account of the Western Regions being performed, he conceived the aspiration for world-transcendence.
He subsequently paid homage to Baocheng Bi of Meifeng and received the tonsure.

Coinciding with the invitation of Miyin to Snow Peak (Xuedou) Qi to enter retreat, the Master joined the assembly for the seven-day intensive meditation session. When Qi entered the hall, the Master, together with his fellow practitioners, asked about the face of one's original nature.
Master Mu listened from the side and was suddenly enlightened. He immediately presented what he had attained, and Master Qi nodded his head in approval.

After the end of the retreat period, he lived at Mount Lingtian, keeping company with tigers and wolves and befriending the deer; he forgot both cold and heat. At that time, Dashi of Damei returned to Touzi Monastery;
hearing of the Master’s pure integrity, he invited him with a verse. The Master also joyfully left the mountains and fully expounded all that he had harbored throughout his life. Dashi...
He granted all [the requests] and commanded the storekeeper to hand over the keys. He then entrusted the master with a small axe and instructed him to reside on the mountain. A Small Sermon:
It is not the mechanism before one’s eyes, nor is it the dharma before one’s eyes. The eye-sight dazzles the four seas; the tips of the eyebrows stack the five sacred peaks.
There are those who drift aimlessly along, merely scratching at the surface. With his whisk, he drew a line and said, "If you can penetrate this one barrier, even empty space shall be struck down.
He then threw down the whisk and let out a shout. In the winter of the Xinhai year of the Kangxi era, the Master manifested a slight illness.
On the twenty-fourth day, at the hour of the rat, he asked his attendant monk, "What time is it now?"
The monk said, "It is already three watches past. The Master rose, bathed, changed his robes, and asked for a brush to write a verse, saying:

"Severing the spring breeze, I have not reckoned the time; Within the shadows of foam-flowers, the total mechanism is revealed. Last night the iron ox roared amidst the clouds, Announcing that returning home is precisely the right moment.
Having cast down the brush, he passed away. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the foot of the mountain (Fachang).
A Small Private Session by Chan Master Shenmingche of Lohan Temple on Mount Yandang. [The Master] asked: "If there is no self within the phrase, I shall not ask.
What is the guest among guests? The Master said: "One who, having lost their head, recognizes only the reflection. [The student] asked: "What is the host among guests? The Master said...

[The student] asked, "The staff cuts off intimacy and estrangement. [The student] asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said, "Wearing a straw raincoat, girded with a sash, one chants under the moon.
[The student] asked, "What is the host within the host? The Master said, "Killing and living rest with the person. He then said:
"Hardly has the auspicious festival of the New Year passed when we encounter the final three days of spring. Petals of plum blossom fly about; eyes of willow buds protrude from every branch."
This matter is vividly clear; why need one resort to words for inquiry? How could one know the ancestral style of the Buddhas and Patriarchs?
One has missed the news right before one's eyes. Having run into the "True Person of No Rank," one vainly opens a wide mouth to cry out in grievance.
Do not cry out! If you seek it, you will find that it cannot be obtained. (A shout—Fadhangzhi, the successor.)
Chan Master Misheng of Yongjia, whose name means "Secret Seal," ascended the hall and said: "I open the vast furnace and forge both sages and ordinary beings;

I wield the earth-shaking tongs and hammers, swift as wind and thunder. I turn the four great continents into a single grain of rice, while houses, dwellings, cities, and castles remain without the slightest movement of dust.
I take this single grain of rice and encompass ten billion Mount Sumerus, suns, moons, mountains, and rivers."
There is absolutely no obstruction. Thus it is said: "The entire earth is the single eye of the śramaṇa. Wherever one dwells, that is the body of the Buddhas.
Let them go, and they can pervade the six realms; let them be withdrawn, and they are hidden within the profound mystery.

This directly causes even stubborn copper and dull iron to be instantly transformed into refined gold, such that externalists and celestial māras together proclaim this supreme transformation, upholding the succession of the patriarchs.
The Essential Principle: Penetrating the very core of the monk’s nostrils. Now tell me, what samādhi has he attained that allows him such unimpeded mastery?
He draws a circle with his staff, then makes ten marks and says: "Keep your eyes open! [He] ascends the hall; this is for the commencement and conclusion of the retreat.
In the end, it all returns to the old rule: the nostrils stand tall and prominent, unchanged from ancient times to the present.

It simply requires that everyone’s heels be firm and secure, so that each and every one may tread upon their own ground. Why must you seek outward? To do so is, when calculated, a great waste of breath.
"Great man, you must be fierce and sharp! The bright pearl within your robe illuminates the ten thousand directions; do not be like the impoverished son who flees in vain. To the assembly he said:
"Though spoken a thousand times, a myriad times, it is but a single teaching. What is this single teaching? After a long silence, he said:
"With this mouth born of my parents, I shall never part from you. As he spoke, a monk was walking by;
extending both hands before the Master, he said, "What a peaceful and tranquil world! The Master replied, "Since it is a peaceful and tranquil world, why trouble yourself with such haste?"
The monk remained silent. The Master gave him a slap and said, "This fellow who dabbles in empty pretenses! As soon as another monk reached the gate, he asked, "What is the Pure Land?
The Master said, "Every step you take, you tread upon it. He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The price of rice is level this year.
Another monk came for an audience and asked, "I have long heard of the Master; only now do I recognize you. The Master said, "I am but a mountain monk."
"How long are your eyebrows? A monk hesitated. The Master said, "I have recognized you. (This refers to Fachangzhi).
Chan Master Dazhe Li of Chengshan on Mount Xianghu in Xiaoshan addressed the assembly: "I have a single phrase that I simply cannot utter. Why?
If one were to utter it, one's tongue would be scorched to ashes. Is there anyone among you who can utter it?"
A monk came forward to prostrate. The Master said, "Wrong, wrong," and then returned to his quarters. (Cold Hall Lin Si) Chan Master Xuedou Yian Yuan ascended the hall and said:

"To grasp the pivot of the supreme device, to succeed to the precious seat of the Patriarchs, to open the eyes of all sentient beings, and to expand and revitalize the ancient traditions—these are, indeed, the ordinary affairs of a patch-robed monk. However, if..."

He turns the heavens and shifts the mountains; suddenly there is rain, suddenly there is wind. Even Buddhas and Patriarchs have no way to gaze upon him; devas and humans have no ground on which to set their feet.
At times he is atop the highest mountain peak, yet he blends water with mud; at times he is at the bottom of the deepest ocean, yet not a single speck of dust can stand there.
Where not a single speck of dust stands, he is straightforward and free from boundaries; when blending water with mud, he hides his body and remains unmanifest.
There are those who do not know how to proceed or stop; they claim that above there is nothing to grasp at and below there is nothing for their own person to rely upon.
They dig in the earth to seek heaven, laboring in vain through years and months. But tell me, what is the place where Yuan the Elder benefits people?

He planted his staff and said: "A thousand-catty iron mace is lightly brought forth; one must discern the true-bone son of Yangqi. The small *chan* (sermon) on the completion of the seventh period. Long...

This old man does not understand how to preserve virtue; he is habituated to pressing people at their most painful points. Alas, his faculties are dull and his skin is callous; even when pressed, he still does not know the pain.
When he finally returns to the abbot’s quarters, he instead reproaches himself in secret. Do not reproach yourself! You must manifest great function on the spot.
Is there anyone? Is there anyone? After a long silence, he said: "If there is none, I can only do it with a single horse and a solitary spear."
Holding it up alone and playing with it alone, he danced with his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters. Upon retiring from the monastery, he ascended the hall and said:

"In the past, when the ancestral master Baiyun Quan resided at Yuan Tong, upon retiring from the monastery he ascended the hall and said: 'Difficult, difficult, difficult—difficult is the casting off of emotions.

When emotions are exhausted, the perfect luminosity is a single cold pearl. Even using skillful means to cast off emotions is still not it; to further eliminate those skillful means is utterly groundless. Great assembly, what about this?"

"How shall one dispel these emotions? Heh! With this, he gave a shout, descended from his seat, and took up his staff to leave the mountain. Its pure breeze and ancient resonance are to be revered for a thousand autumns.

Today, I, your unworthy distant descendant, have newly assumed the leadership of Xuedou; as my circumstances are similarly fraught, I offer a verse to follow in the tradition of those who came before.
Having received the mandate to serve as abbot for nine months, the hardships and perils have been such that my life has hung by a single thread. [Cui]...
Master Fǎshū of Fēng arrived in person; beating the drum and ascending the hall, he declared his shoulders were relieved (Shānfú Zhèngsì).
On the eighth day of the twelfth month, Chan Master Āngfēng Yǐn of Nánshān in Míngzhōu ascended the hall: "Suddenly beholding the bright star, he sighed, 'How marvelous!'"
He then left the mountain to gather firewood. From that point on, one false rumor spread as a hundred truths, saying he had attained the Way;

even now, people still harbor doubts about this. A monk asked, "From what does nature arise? The Master said, "From what does your question come? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. (Shanfu Zhengsi)

The Chan Master Jingnuo Yue of Wulin Xiongsheng was a daughter of the Lin family of the prefecture. She left home at a young age and studied under Chan Master Xiongsheng Zhi, traveling between him and the gate of Xuedou.
One day, while standing in attendance, Zhi raised the kōan concerning Lopu’s meeting with Jiashan and asked, "How do you understand this?
The Master stepped forward and gave him a slap. Zhi said, "Do not pull the tiger’s whiskers. The Master... [replied].
He said, "O Blue Heaven! O Blue Heaven! One day, while following the assembly into the meditation hall, Yuanzhao Zhi said, "The ancients said:
'Everywhere people possess only the eye of the simultaneous pecking and the egg-breaking, but they do not possess the function of the simultaneous pecking and the egg-breaking.
You all—how do you employ it? How do you understand it? The assembly had no reply. The Master sighed twice. Zhi said, "Not yet. The Master said, "All in harmony, a time of peace."
Song: Ascending the Dais on New Year’s Day. Of the three hundred and sixty days in a year, The swift passage of time is as rapid as lightning.
Following ancient custom, the annual regulations begin; Everyone goes out to celebrate the Imperial Festival. They encounter Maitreya, laughing heartily;
They tread upon a scale, its hammer as hard as iron. Iron! Iron! Iron! Which person in the world knows the true principle? *He!* (A shout)
Drinking Tea and Descending from the Seat (by Weiji Zisi).
Chan Master Hanfeng Ding of Xiufeng in Suzhou, a native of Yixing, ascended the hall and said: "The accumulated snow has not yet melted;
everywhere there are silver walls and iron barriers. When the red sun shines brightly, the green waters and blue mountains remain as they were. When the season arrives, its principle [is revealed]."
Self-manifested. Now tell me, what time is it right now? (He lets out a shout. A verse on Nanquan’s “Selling the Body”:
In poverty, one has no recourse but to worry for the self; Teeth fallen out and eyebrows grown long, yet he knows no shame.
How can this pit of destitution ever be filled? From of old, it has caused people to grieve through the ages. A verse on Zhaozhou’s “Pine Tree”: Filling the valleys... (The text breaks off).
The body of the ravine reveals the truth; why restrict oneself to ancient cypresses in search of a kindred spirit?
This talk has been passed down for a thousand years, drawing out the Han dog to circle the tree in its quest. (Xuoyun Wei, successor).
The lay practitioner Dai Yunyue was a native of Wujiang. He lived in the countryside and did not enter the city for forty years.
Previously, under the guidance of Gounan, he had received the inspiration of a verse-exhortation. Later, he visited Xiufeng Wei and presented him with this verse:
"Birds sing and flowers fall in the twilight of spring; I regret having left the famous mountain nearly ten years ago. The plum fruit is green and about to ripen; Now, how could I not [return]?"
Saliva flowed from his mouth. Wei (Xuoyun Wei) received his certification of realization (Wei succeeded Xuoyun).
Zen Master Dashaen Bin Tie addressed the assembly: "In the early morning, all of you arrive in great numbers;
at midday, all of you disperse quietly. You must know that there is one person who neither comes nor goes—vast and unconfined, like a people without a ruler."
One can name it thus. But tell me, what samādhi has this person realized? After a long silence, he said: "Do not resent his great spirit;
his house has already trodden upon the highest pass. Addressing the assembly, he held up a whisk and said: "Everyone, look! Great is the true nobility.
The guest net spreads across the corner of the hall. What a fine mind of the Patriarchs! Three-legged ancient cauldrons. He asked: "Tell me!"
"If one wishes to behold the Great Life-Sustaining Mountain (Mahāmeru), one must first attain the purification of the five eyes.
What is the fleshly eye? The Master said, "Who does not possess it? "What is the heavenly eye? The Master said, "It illuminates and penetrates the great trichiliocosm.

"What is the wisdom eye? The Master said, "There is nothing it does not see through. "What is the dharma eye? The Master said, "It examines your very bones. "What is... [The question was left unfinished.]
"This is the Buddha-eye. The Master said, "It is empty and void. As the monk prepared to offer a word in response, the Master held up his whisk and asked, "What eye is this?
The monk was speechless. The Master then struck him. (Chongji succeeded to Jun.)
Chan Master Yuanning Hango Yin of Kyoto addressed the assembly: "What is it you seek to investigate? What is it you seek to awaken to? It is vivid and clear;
there is no need for complicated entanglements. To touch upon it is it; to strike against it is it. A majestic qilin has but a single horn.
A layman asked, "What is the mind of the sages? The Master said, "It can kill people; it can bring people to life. The layman said, "If that is so..."
"What is the mind of an ordinary person? The Master said, "That which can praise others and that which can ruin others. The questioner asked, "What is the Supreme Vehicle (Ekayāna)?
The Master said, "From the beginning, there has never been two paths. The questioner asked, "Does this allow a student to tread upon it? The Master said, "Yes."
If you have doubts, seek instruction elsewhere (he attained the local ground and became a successor).
Chan Master Su’ān Yóu of Fǎhǎi in Chùzhōu was the son of the Huáng family of Chángtīng in Mǐn. He ascended the hall and said:
"I have lived at Cùiwēi with my single staff for many years; Lacking talent, I dare not act recklessly. Let others play with tortoise hair and rabbit horns; Fire..."

Sowing with the blade, plowing, and guarding ignorance—O sons of meditation, do you know or not? The fine tea and rice within the bowl and cup are all drops of blood and sweat from the practitioner’s own labor.
Do not fail to cultivate the Way by drumming up right and wrong; though long skirts and tall hats may conceal one’s faults, the Black-Faced Lord of Yama will not let him pass.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the retreat: Two-thirds of the time has already passed; the numinous mind...
Not a single point has been polished away. Greedily clinging to life, they wander aimlessly from day to day; when called back, they cannot turn their heads—what can be done?
O virtuous ones, these are the words of ancient Xuedou addressed to the assembly. Such speech as this has every word resonating like chimes of gold and clashing jade.
It is truly precious and lovely; this is indeed it. Even in the ultimate future, one cannot avoid being without someone [to witness it]. How can it compare to within Zhenshen Temple?

Although the assembly there is not large, it is a joy that beneath each and every person’s heels, the eight characters are displayed in all directions, and atop each person’s crown, the great jewel-light flies forth. I dare ask you all: regarding this extraordinary matter, tell me, by whom is it sustained?
The power of grace: though the lakes and seas may dry up to their very depths, my name shall never be made known to you.

Retiring from the monastery, he ascends the hall and says: For twenty years I have been on a single fishing boat; even where there is no elegance, there is elegance. I have a small cow capable of plowing and sowing;
in the pen there are no more than three or four heads. From this day forth, I return to the mountain temple; with one full meal, ten thousand bundles of hair are satisfied.
The matter concluded. He took up his staff and walked away. Before the stupa of the former master Baozhang, he made an offering.

"In other places one is so poor that there is not even enough ground to plant a锥 (chui—a small awl); at Lion Mountain, one is so poor that there is not even ground for a 锥. The white stones in the bowl; the clear stream in the bell."
"This is my humble sincerity. He stuck incense into the burner and said: "Though there are fine flowers blooming in their prime, one cannot restrain the sorrow that fills Mount Qin.
A monk asked: "I have heard that in the past, when National Teacher Shao resided on this mountain, he would untie the knots and remove the bonds for others.
What about you, Master, today? The Master took up his staff and said: "This iron caltrop of mine can kill."
"A person can also bring a person to life. The monk shouted. The Master struck him. The monk shouted again.

After a long silence, the Master looked toward his attendants and said, "I have been the abbot of Fahai for a long time, yet only now have I met this one man. The monk stepped forward and made a gesture as if listening.
The Master opened both hands to show him. The monk hesitated. The Master said, "After you have prostrated, withdraw. (Recorded by Xuefeng.)
Chan Master Ling Song Ci of Yuanming Monastery in Wujiang was the son of the Wu family of Xiushui. He ascended the hall and said: "Striking stone, the stone rings;
hitting wood, the wood responds. Suddenly, he struck the air once with his fist and said:
"Tell me, what kind of resonance is this? If you listen with your ears, you will go deaf; if you look with your eyes, you will go blind; if you speak with your mouth, you will go mute. If...
He was a man indeed. Upon hearing such an exhortation, he shook his sleeves and departed. Nevertheless, Elder Ci’s staff has not yet granted him passage. Why is that?

The Master said, "Look after your own life! The monk hesitated; the Master said, "Your skull has fallen off! A monk asked, "What is the eye of a good spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)?
The Master said, "Not seeing anything at all. The monk said, "Everyone sees; why is it that a good spiritual friend... [The Master replied: "...does not see anything."
[The student] did not see the Master. The Master said, "You are still outside the gate. [The student] asked, "What is one's original face?

The Master said, "The snow melts and the mountain reveals its bones. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Water dripping wears away stone; fragrance flows" (in the Nan dialect, he said "succession").
Chan Master Xue Chuan-an of Foguo Temple on Mount Jiangshan in Jinling addressed the assembly.

He cited the case where Daowu, upon the arrival of Zhaozhou, donned a leopard-skin loincloth and took up his *jiliao* staff. Standing before the main gate, he saw Zhaozhou approaching and called out with a loud "Nyo!
and stood there. Zhaozhou said, "Be careful in your attendance," and Daowu called out another "Nyo! and departed. The Master said, "This..."
Two men. They are much like a flute without holes meeting a felt clapper. The five notes and six scales are exceedingly clear.
It is a pity that at that time there was no one who could appreciate them. But tell me, is there anyone who can still distinguish them now?
Striking the desk once with his whisk, he said: "Ziqi, Ziqi! (In the Nan dialect, this means "successor.")
The layman Langgong, Wu Xianchang, was a native of Changzhou. Initially, he went to visit Lingyin Li. Li asked him, "What doubts do you have that you have come from so far to pay your respects?
The layman replied, "My wild mind has not yet ceased; when it ceases, that is bodhi. May I ask the Master where this cessation occurs?
Li said, "Let us talk plainly; put away your entanglements. The layman was speechless. He practiced for half a year without making any progress. Later—

While observing the *jinzu* (retreat) at Beian, one night during a period of seated meditation (*zuo xiang*), he had an awakening upon hearing the sound of a tea bowl. He offered this verse on the difficulty of childbirth for Aṅgulimāla:
"Behind the head, white clouds drift idly, slice by slice; At the brow’s edge, the spring colors stretch far and wide.

Not knowing what leisurely furnishings to seek, On level ground, one has needlessly suffered a fall. He also offered this verse on the woman emerging from meditative absorption: "Deep and heavy is the spring sleep..."
The fragrance is still thick; one does not know that the yellow oriole is scolding the east wind. Upon waking, I lift the gauze curtains in vain to look:
through the window screens, fallen red petals lie in disarray. (Impression by Xuanqi)
Master Xiu Shui Yushongying asked: "When Danxia went to visit Master Pang, Lingzhao set down her basket.
What was the meaning of this? The Master said: "A mute conveys the message; the deaf hear it filling their ears. [The student] asked:
"When Danxia asked if Master Pang was at home, Lingzhao took up her basket and left. How would you explain that? The Master said: "In whose family’s secluded courtyard pond does it dwell?"
"A pair of mandarin ducks cannot be painted" (Shangyu Qi).
Master Shengguo Shangsheng Chan asked Duofu Qi to enter his room for instruction. One day, he requested to enter the inner quarters. Qi said, "Above there is not a single tile;
below there is not enough space to plant a single awl. What do you call this 'room'? The Master looked up and gazed around, saying, "The blue heavens, the blue heavens!"

Tianqi said, "Who is crying out in such distress? The Master said, "It is not that the Master is poor and his children suffer; it is simply because the family is wealthy and the young child is spoiled.
Tianqi asked again, "Having lost my kin for many years, today I beg for a coarse fistful [of rice].
Tianqi said, "This old monk has no strength left. The Master said, "Your compassion is truly excessive. Tianqi’s anger flared up, and he said, "You liar! Where have you seen [such a thing]?"
He arrived. The Master said, "I had my morning congee; why are you hungry now? Daokai replied, "You bag of rice, get out!
The Master said, "Go rest, then come back and pay your respects to the Abbot. (Shangyu Qisuo)
When the lay practitioner Zhu Maoyuan of Suzhou was born, his mother dreamed that a bright moon pierced her abdomen; she woke in alarm and immediately gave birth.

Upon reaching adulthood, he placed his faith in the Chan school and traveled to various regions to seek instruction from masters. One day, upon hearing a bell, he attained realization and composed a verse, saying:
"Accidentally lodging east of the Pingjiang Daoist Temple, I joyfully encounter fellow Chan practitioners from all quarters. For ten years I have earnestly sought instruction, [But now]..."
If one personally hears the sound of a single strike of the bell, there is the verse on Danxia burning the wooden Buddha:

"The wooden Buddha was burned to ward off the cold; Why needlessly give rise to grounds for doubt? Pitifully, the temple director was personally struck by poison; He could not help but acknowledge his own loss of beard and eyebrows.
The verse on the World-Honored One’s first birth says: "The young master in brocade robes swings on a swing; He flaunts his elegance and charm."
Displaying youthful vigor, he adds the yellow oriole singing among the green willows; the full splendor of spring is broadcast before all people (Renkechishi).
The nun Dan-tu Zhengjue, Chan Master Fojiyuan, spoke this verse on the bamboo rattle: "Brandishing the 'Blow-off-Body' sword,"
Both Māra and the Buddha tremble with fear. When one hesitates to ask how it is, there is a roar of thunder and a flash of lightning.

The verse on Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman says: "The old woman was thoroughly exposed; The public case has two layers. Mountains crumble and the earth splits open, As the bright sun confronts the sky.
Linji saw a monk enter the gate and immediately shouted. The verse says: "The iron ox tramples the moon upon the clear pool; The stone tiger [roars] from the cliff."
The previous roar did not penetrate; the black-lacquered Kunlun [demon] has nowhere to hide. When the hundred beasts hear it, their brains split open (Zhongpu Ru’s successor).
Shun Tianbao Chengqi Shengren Chan Master ascends the hall: Body lean, face skin yellow—entirely because of being busy with affairs.
Yesterday he personally entered the marketplace; today he again ascends the hall. Intending to sing the Yunmen melody, he still hesitates, fearing it may not be fitting.
[He] struck the meditation platform with his staff and ascended the hall, saying: "Today the furnace is opened; there is neither firewood nor charcoal.
We sweep away spiritual understanding and wash clean the *tathatā*. Originally there are no old acquaintances; how could there be any distinction between kin and stranger?
Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty—this is the true practice. When golden beans burst forth from cold ashes, it will make the Patriarch Xixia [Xuedou] laugh to death."
The Blue-Eyed Barbarian from the West comes to the hall. Speaking straight, speaking indirect;
praising, or disparaging—those who recognize this see it as the finest cream (*amṛta*), while those who do not recognize it see it as poison. Cast aside both the poison and the cream at once.
If you wish to recognize Yangqi’s donkey, it has only three legs. (Succeeded by Gui Changrui.)
Master Zhuo of Qingquan at Huishan, Tongcheng, ascends the hall to break the retreat: To stay is not to use the awl;
to leave is not to use the hook. Neither staying nor leaving—the hook and awl are most sharp. Is there anyone within who knows the sting?
The assembly was speechless. The Master spoke again: "Even if you were to run to the ends of the earth, it would all remain upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff.

(Small Assembly Lecture, early spring. The spring breeze is warm and gentle; days grow long and nights grow short. The green mountains remain as ever green; heaven and earth continue their rotation as before.
Upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff, from ancient times to the present, who has ever been exempt? I respectfully address those who seek the source: the Way is not... [text breaks off].
When people distance themselves from others, they distance themselves from themselves. Zhuo struck his staff once and said, "This place is not [the abode of] the Ten Continents.
Chan Master Deyan of Beidieng, a native of the Zhu family in Changshu, Jiangnan, was born with fragrant light filling his room.
At the age of four, he was already able to sit in the lotus posture and recite the Buddha’s name. At ten, his father passed away. Once, he happened to go to a place west of the city...
Zang saw the forms of the hells depicted on a wall and was struck with terror; he wished to leave the household life, and his mother granted him permission.

Xiang Yougui shaved his head and ordained him. One day, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he reached the passage where Ānanda says, "This is not your mind," and a sudden sense of doubt arose within him.
After three years, he finally attained realization. Later, when Xingfu Ding questioned him using the "host and guest" dialogue, Zang’s understanding deepened further.

He exerted himself in his studies and visited various masters in the Wu region, yet none of them satisfied his fundamental intent. After completing his full ordination, he went to visit his elder brother in Puyi;

on his way through the capital, he suffered a fall, at which point his lingering doubts were completely dissolved. He happened to be staying at Tiefo Temple in the capital when the Master went to visit him.
Ding said, "How many years has it been since we last met? How is this matter going? The Master replied:
The nostrils still hang downward. [Zhaozhou] said, "Where did you see that? The Master said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Abbot.
That evening, the Master related what he had seen and struck him with a severe blow. This happened three times. One day, [Zhaozhou] entered the abbot’s quarters.
As soon as [the monk] opened his mouth, [the Master] struck him. At that moment, it was as if he had cast off a thousand-jin burden. Having paid his respects, he departed.
After receiving the entrustment, he first resided at Poshan on Mount Yu, then entered the capital, and subsequently presided over various monasteries such as Dabeiguan and Guangquan.

While ascending the hall for a formal discourse, he cited a monk who asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard."
The monk said, "Master, do not point to external objects for people. Zhaozhou said, "I am not pointing to external objects for you.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master [Yunmen] said:
"If one says that mind and object are identical, I would gladly bury this monk in a single pit. If one says he simply picked it up at random, he is slandering Zhaozhou."
It is even more so. After all, what is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
“The cypress tree in the courtyard. On a summer day, he ascended the hall and, citing the case of Dongshan, said: A monk asked Dongshan, “When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them?

Dongshan replied, “Why not go to a place where there is neither cold nor heat? The monk asked, “What is the place where there is neither cold nor heat? Dongshan said, “When it is cold, freeze to death.”
"Ācārya! When it is hot, the heat kills the Ācārya! The Master said, "Transforming function to accord with the position; transforming the position to accord with function.

They are harmoniously integrated and subtly in accord, never violating the subtle distinction between separation and union. This is precisely the school tradition of the Dongshan lineage. As for 'when it is cold, the cold kills;

when it is hot, the heat kills,' how do you perform the mutual interpenetration? Have you not seen it said: 'Beneath the gate of the Great Sun, every day is the third autumn month'? (The text ends here).
On the occasion of the Master’s birthday, he ascended the hall before the Moon Hall during the ninth summer. "Heaven and earth share the same root; the myriad things are one body.
How profound these words! You must quickly realize them. He suddenly took up his staff and said, "Since the myriad things are one body, tell me:
is this staff and I one, or are we two? If you say they are one, I am still I."
The staff is the staff. When has it ever been one? If you say it is two, then this mountain monk belongs to the Sheep, but to what does the staff belong?
If you instead call it two, yet can speak with perfect accuracy regarding this point, you may walk hand-in-hand with the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past.
If you cannot speak thus, when you have a staff, I shall give you a staff.
“Staff-bearer! You have no staff. I shall snatch away your staff! Speak quickly, speak quickly!
This was a small-scale informal teaching (*xiao can*). “The entire great earth is a pit of fire. What samādhi must you attain so as not to be burned?
He then looked left and right and said, “Look, look! Every single one’s flesh will burst and their skin will peel away. If you are a true man, simply turn toward the world...”
At this moment, all worldly fame, profit, and sustenance, as well as notions of self and other, right and wrong, and the solid ground of contention—all are shattered by a single blow.
The void is pulverized, and the great earth sinks level. At such a time, tell me: where is the fire pit?
After a long silence, he said: "A second offense will not be tolerated. He ascended the hall and cited the case where two head seats under Linji simultaneously let out a shout.

A monk asked, "Is there still guest and host? Linji replied, "Guest and host are clearly distinct. The Master said: "Both houses need not have shouted; yet guest and host are likewise clearly distinct.
But tell me, who can testify to this? After a long silence, he said: "A second offense will not be tolerated. He then ascended the hall. (End of case.)
Tending to the Eyebrows Ascending the Dharma Hall on the Winter Solstice: At dawn, news was suddenly brought that the first yang has arisen.

In this transient world, who among travelers would not be moved? Only the withered monk remains addicted to his solitude; From of old, he has never been startled by the cold or the heat. Small Private Assembly on New Year’s Eve:
The large month has thirty days; the small month has twenty-nine. From antiquity until now, it is the standard of the calendar masters.
"It is in the house; it is already there. Why not bring it forth and look? At that time, a monk was about to step forward, but the Master called him back, saying, "Wait!
If you do not have the official seal and date-stamp of the Imperial Calendar, it is the same as a private calendar. On the Day of Beginning Spring (Lichun), he ascended the hall:

Ten days have passed since the start of the year; The scenery has finally attained spring. To the dragon-elephant guests at this Dharma assembly, Once again, a new season is seen. A new season, indeed!
The great earth, mountains, and rivers possess twice their usual divine power; do not speak of Old Wang the Elder from the eastern village—his face remains covered in dust.
When one asks, "The Dharma-body fills the vast void," at such a time, where is the response-body?
The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, am right before your eyes, Venerable. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Zhengzhou produces men of the Cao family.
A monk asked, "I do not ask about the great phoenix spreading its wings; what of the matter of being inscribed upon the golden list?

The Master said, "For a long time I have been gazing upward in expectation of you. The monk asked, "What is the rootless tree? The Master said, "Above all, avoid sprouting branches outside the joints. The monk said: [silence].
"What is the ground where there is neither yin nor yang? The Master said, "How many people know when they step upon it?

"How is it that the mountain valley does not echo when called? The Master said, "Moving one's countenance, one reveals the ancient path; one does not fall into the mechanism of silent stillness. (Pinyan Ding succeeded him.)
Chan Master Xing of Longhua Houshan in Ezhou was a native of the Zhang family of Jiangxia. On the occasion of the opening of the retreat, he ascended the hall and said:

"For seven days prior, [the mind] stands like a wall ten thousand fathoms high; one must pursue it to the very tip of a cow's horn, demanding that one let go completely from the edge of a precipice. After seven days..."

"Shatter the lacquer bucket! Sever the life-root! Yet you must also pass through death and return to life. Right now, within these seven days, your lives and souls are entirely in the hands of this mountain monk.
With his staff, he struck them repeatedly, saying: "Quickly save yourselves! He then addressed the assembly: "I possess the single sandal of Bodhidharma;
it has traversed the entire universe, yet it is bottomless. It has been cast off upon a heap of refuse."
[The Master] said: "A thousand sages cannot lift it up. [Question: "What is the essence of prajñā? [Master: "Horizontal three, vertical four.
[Question: "What is the function of prajñā? [Master: "Seven holes, eight apertures. [Question: "What is the oneness of essence and function?
[Master: [He] struck him with his staff. (Sheng’an succeeded to this lineage.)

Chan Master Qingtian Chongsheng Guiyan Song was a native of Putian. In his youth, while visiting a temple with his father, he saw an Arhat who opened his chest with both hands to reveal a Buddha within.
Clapping his hands, the Arhat laughed and said, "How marvelous! There is indeed a Buddha within the heart.
At twenty-four years of age, he went to Longfeng in Changle to receive the tonsure and then crossed the mountain ridges to visit Chongsheng.
Hao. Their karmic conditions were in perfect accord. Later, having received formal authorization (*kṣānti*), he succeeded to the seat and addressed the assembly:

"Upon a single hair-tip stand heaven and earth; ten billion Mount Sumerus encircle the sun and moon. He then held up his whisk and said, "If you can recognize the source here, what tracks will there be for north, south, east, or west?
In a small-scale discourse (*xiǎo-cán*): "The wind is high and the moon is cold; the sea is vast and the sky is open. The howl of the monkey reaches far..."
From the mountain cleft, cranes cry out among the lofty pines. Grasping the very core of the patch-robed monks, he reveals the fundamental principles of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

Rolling up and rolling out with sovereign ease, he is brilliant and penetrating from every side. You must directly cut off the master of the house. Ancient trees, slanting sun—the ridges beyond glow red. Small Sermon:
Ten li for the long pavilion, five li for the short pavilion; when the spirit is spent and the body weary, one pauses briefly to rest. The wind comes.
A sudden gust of wind; the warbling of birds for several moments. Sweat dried and the body refreshed; eyes opened wide and the mind cleared.
From now on, it is good to go home; do not ask how many stages lie ahead on the road. [The questioner] asked, "What is this most sublime realm?

The Master said, "A thousand peaks of emerald green encircle the Zhixi River. [The questioner] asked, "Who is the person within this realm? The Master said, "A gaunt frame, coldly clad in a coarse woolen robe."
Yi asked, "The lantern and the dew-pillar intersecting—what stage of teaching is this? The Master said, "This is the second stage. He asked, "What is the first stage?
The Master said, "The lantern and the dew-pillar intersecting. He asked, "What is the meaning of winter's arrival?
The Master said, "The mountain plum blossoms through the jade. He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A chicken's beak."
Pointed. The duck’s bill is flat. Question: "What is the state of early spring? The Master said: "Where the partridges cry, the flowers of a hundred kinds are fragrant.
(Baiqiao Hao succeeded him.)
Chan Master Guanghui Qimi of Tongzhou addressed the assembly: "Today, recognizing this as the first day, all matters are thereby brought to completion.
In stillness, one hears the mute singing mountain songs; with a smile, one watches the clay oxen fight and kick.
With fists coming and feet going, they display their elegance; they mistakenly give Mount Sumeru a slap, until the Dragon King’s anger knows no end."
"Bringing disgrace upon the two eyes of the asuras; with staff in hand, he perceives injustice from mid-air. Thirty blows each, and they are driven out together.
He strikes the meditation desk with his staff and lets out a shout (Junsui Shis).
Chan Master Xiangweng Zhen of Guanghui in Tongzhou ascended the hall and held up his whisk, saying:
"If you can penetrate this point, you may let go and act in accordance with conditions. But if you hesitate or dwell upon thoughts, you will inevitably miss it right before your own eyes.

I, this mountain monk, shall provide a further commentary: Today, occupying the quarters and ascending the hall once more, the fourfold assembly has gathered like clouds to partake in the joy of the Dharma. It is revealed..."
The pillar lanterns were joined with the incense burner; the myriad phenomena of the universe all paid homage. Not long after the Master appeared in the world, he passed away.
At the moment of his death, he wrote this verse: "I dwelt in this world like a madman for thirty-two years, reviling the Buddhas and scolding the Patriarchs."

Throughout his life, he lived with joy and ease, moving with such carefree elegance that he was free from even the slightest obstruction. He passed away while casting aside his writing brush (his successor was Junsui).
Chan Master Daming Xinghua Duanzhi, who had studied under Yutian Run and received the Dharma, later built a thatched hut ten *li* west of the city of Tianxiong Commandery.
Every night, as he sat in meditation, he saw auspicious light illuminating the heavens; upon investigating its source, he discovered the Lin... [text fragment].
The stupa of the Patriarch Jie was buried amidst rubble and debris. The Master subsequently rebuilt the stone stele and renovated the stupa courtyard.
Tiantong Min, Gunan Men, Ba’en Xian, and Tianmu Xi all contributed funds to assist him.

He further constructed the Xinghua Stupa Temple beside it, which became a flourishing monastic center within three years. This was the primary cause for the restoration of the ancestral temple of the First Patriarch.
"It is no small matter. A monk asked, "Regarding the realm where empty space is pulverized and the great earth sinks level—does one still receive Linji’s painful blows?
The Master said, "The offense shall not be punished with excessive severity. [Another] asked, "An ancient pagoda stands majestic and unmoving."
"Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "Look up at it; gaze up at it. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "It is because of me that you bow to me. (Yutian Ransi)
Chan Master Tianxuan Xu of Mount Zhongfeng in Yushan was the son of the Shi family of Liyang; his secular name was Fan.

By virtue of his noble lineage, he was promoted to the rank of Grand Marshal of the Imperial Guard (Dajinwu). Having led troops to suppress the bandits flowing from Shandong and reporting a victory, he was granted an imperial edict to patrol the borders.

Coinciding with the dynastic transition, he submitted a memorial to the Grand Secretariat (Hongneiyuan) requesting an audience with the Emperor, earnestly expressing his wish to become a monk. He first studied under Tianmu at Fuyan, and later entered Longhua.
The hall was filled to capacity. After being pressed for three months, he attained realization upon hearing the sound of the evening bell while contemplating the "Wild Duck" koan.
He was subsequently appointed as the First Seat (Daisozu). On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, he ascended the hall and held up his whisk, saying: "Śākyamuni Buddha has arrived!
If you can understand it right here, there will be no need to exhaust your body or endure hunger for six years or three years; the morning star will shine brilliantly every night."
"O Celestial One! The boundless virtue and wisdom transmit the orthodox lineage. Is the great assembly present? If not, this mountain monk shall provide a commentary.
He cast down his whisk and said, "Do not let yourselves drift away in a foreign land. (Yunhan Man Si)
Chan Master Muye Zhilin of Yushan was the son of the Yang family of the local district. He ascended the hall and said:

"To say 'this very mind is Buddha' is like a duck listening for thunder; to say 'neither this mind nor Buddha' is like adding legs to a snake. To be free from both 'is' and 'is not' is for a fool to speak of dreams."
This is precisely what is non-being. It is like a short man watching a performance. Within this, there is one phrase:
"It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not an object. Let those with eyes try to discern it. (Yunhan Mansi)
The layman Ge Yitiao of Kunshan, whose given name was Ding and whose style name was Qikong, developed doubts regarding the words and phrases of the ancients at the age of sixteen.

He subsequently sat in meditation throughout the night, casting aside worldly affairs. Encountering the changes of the times, he lived in seclusion to investigate the teachings of the Buddhist vehicle (*śāsana*).
Later, he visited Gu Nanmen Lingyinli, with whom he achieved mutual realization; he then studied under Miaoxi Man, attending him morning and evening.

Qizhi asked one day: "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it—how is this? The Master said: "A dead snake was originally never dead; if you strike it, it will not be born again. He asked:
"How about carrying away a bottomless basket filled with things? The Master said: "If it is bottomless, you can carry it away;
if it has a bottom, it will be emptied to the very last thing. Qiman nodded in agreement. Regarding the verse on "The Old Woman Who Gave Birth to Seven Sons," it says: "From..."
Coming to the great earth, he cuts off all who can understand him; casting it aside, he boasts that his eyes are new.
A pity for the little child drenched in mud and water—letting his six sons grow in majestic power. Riding a cow backward into the Buddha hall, the verse says: "For many kalpas, he has ridden the ox."
It is simply because they fail to reflect. This time, riding backward, one finds a skillful means that far surpasses searching for the ox;
yet, one still fails the Buddha Hall (Yunhan Mansi).
Chan Master Hanyun Ding of Jingkou, a native of the Lu family from Wujin, relied upon Master Long at Lùquán. One day, hearing the song of a yellow oriole, he attained awakening.
He subsequently resided at Wanshou Monastery in Guǎnglíng. Entering the hall, he brandished his whisk and said: "Dharmatrāta left behind a single sandal;
though his descendants fill the earth, none can lift it. Even if one were to act with tenfold likeness," [he would still not be able to do so].
This tilted head makes the mouth crooked; I too laugh at myself for seeking perfection. Seeking a true friend in the south, north, east, and west, who cares whether one meets such a person or not?
Wanshou has laboriously served as the abbot for three years; having exhausted all means of testing, he now seeks a junior master.
In this desolate Way, who is worthy of conversation? [He makes a gesture of gathering his whisk and says: Do not let the needle and thread go to waste.
"Relying on this, gather it up and take it home to wear as your own. He asked, "Is Mount Sumeru ultimately existent or non-existent?
The Master said, "I have already placed it directly before you. (Recorded by Duchi Yong.)
Chan Master Qianshan Jun of Longquan in the Western Mountains of Hongdu asked, "What is the precept?
The Master said, "To sever delusive thoughts is to increase one's illness. He asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "To incline toward True Suchness is also a deviation.
He asked, "What is the meaning of non-transmigration? The Master said, "A bamboo shoot grows crookedly under a stone; a flower blooms upside down on a precipice. He asked, "What about..."
"What is the matter of wandering on pilgrimage? The Master said, "I am going to the village ahead to beg for food; I shall return after washing my bowl by the pond. (Duchi Lang succeeded him.
Chan Master Baizhuo Lun of Jing’an in Hongdu asked, "What kind of medicinal decoction is this 'Dharma Medicine'?
The Master struck him immediately. [The monk] said, "Do not strike me recklessly! The Master struck again. [The monk] cried out, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master said, "A madman crying out."
[The monk] bowed. [The master said,] "Many die and few live. The monk hesitated; the Master struck him straight away and sent him back (Duchi Lang succeeded him).

Only then did he understand the meaning of words. At nine years of age, he passed through Wuxie; there, he paid homage to the Buddha and saw the monks as if they were old acquaintances, whereupon he entered the monastic life.
Later, he went to Shantong, where he was instructed by the Patriarch to investigate the koan: “All dharmas return to one; to what does that one return?

After more than a year, upon hearing the sound of a cat, he attained sudden enlightenment. The Patriarch immediately asked him, “All dharmas return to one; to what does that one return? The Master replied, “A crow.”
The tortoise drilled through the wall; Wù-nǚn nodded in understanding. Finally, he attended upon Lùquán Lóng, with whom he attained accord at first sight.

When Kāihuà took the high seat and ascended the hall, he cited Daguān Yǐng, saying: "In all quarters, the hook is crooked and there is no bait; it is like pressing a gourd down into the bottom of the water.
He then picked up his staff, made a gesture as if fishing, and said: "To catch fish in deep waters is to prolong one's life; I have never used wine."
He made offerings to the River Spirit. Kaehwa, moreover, was not like this. His family trade was a single leaf of a light boat;
drifting south in the morning and north in the evening with the current, he would sing several songs of his heart’s content and idly accompany the sand gulls, forgetting all artifice.
Then, taking up his whisk, he said: "I would rather let the strings break and remain solitary and lofty than bend my hook down for the sake of my gate and courtyard" (Duchi Daeng).
Chan Master Fàngyún Zhì of Lóngshān in Rùnzhōu went to study under Lùquán Nǎng.

While contemplating the saying of Nánquán, "The three 'nots'," he happened to drop his carrying pole for firewood onto the ground, and as it made a sound, he exclaimed, "Aha! Aha! It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing.
If you wish to seek it, you cannot find it; if you wish to avoid it, you cannot avoid it. In a moment of clarity, I have personally seen through it—distinctly so!"
This thief! The verse on the bamboo whisk says: The bamboo whisk has no front or back; Its sharpness is like a blade that shaves hair, brandished in all eight directions.
When a monk encounters it, what happens? It smashes the skull, and fresh blood splatters.
Look at the incense burner swallow the Buddha hall! Longya Shigui’s verse says: The wind blew in the last watch of the night, The rain fell yesterday; Today, I have awakened from my dream.
Furthermore, he saw a ghost. The ghost tugged at his leg, causing him to fall and break his mouth. Reflecting deeply on this, he composed the *Gāthā on the City Gates of Zhaozhou*:
The four gates stand wide open in the city of Zhaozhou; North, south, east, and west, the roads are clearly divided.
Twenty-five strings vibrate beneath the moon at night; A person tipsy in the Jade Tower, amidst the apricot blossoms of the village. (Duchi Langsi)
The Provincial Commander, Layman Kuixuan Zhang Guoxun, was of a distinguished family from Xianfu.

From the beginning, he had spent many years studying under and questioning masters such as Rong’an Tianjing, Yuan’an Yumen, and Chengguo Sheng at Tienjie Monastery. Later, he visited Luquan Daohang and asked, “What is the shortcut to the Way?

Under these words, the Master (Shi) was suddenly enlightened and presented this verse: "The conditions planted here, my Way is entirely the same.
Beneath the bright moon upon the mountain peak, the pine wind speaks of the guiding instructions. (Duchi Lang succeeded him.)

Master Micen of Kunyang Yucang spoke to the assembly: "This Dharma-seal of mine is like a drum smeared with lethal poison;
those who hear it have their life-roots severed instantly. How can you all possibly find a foothold? It is right here, right now. To say 'it is already' is to enter the stages of a ladder.
If you do not act in this way at all, you still fall into the realm of conceptual consciousness. Let a thousand sages come—they are all cast downwind together. You..."

Today, I shall temporarily borrow the worlds of the ten directions to serve as a single meditation hall. I open a deep furnace and pile up blazing coals;

Skin and bone exposed; stripped bare, there is no place to rely. Is there anyone among this assembly who does not undergo this refinement? Holding up his bamboo staff, he said:

The Chan Master Nie Luo Nihui Kong of Siming was a woman of the Wang family from Ning County. At the age of thirty-three, she left secular life to become a nun. Initially, she investigated the koan "Who is it that recites the Buddha's name? but found no point of entry despite her diligent efforts. She subsequently went to visit Master Qi of Tiantong, asking: "A single pearl atop the Panta Rock—neither going nor coming, its trace is not seen. I pray, Master, point directly to it. Qi replied: [He struck her. She immediately attained great enlightenment. She then composed a verse: "A single pearl atop the Panta Rock— Neither going nor coming, its trace is not seen. I pray, Master, point directly to it. Master, you strike me; I suddenly attain great enlightenment. The myriad phenomena are all the Buddha-nature; The ten directions are entirely the True Dharma. The moon shines upon the water without being wetted; The wind passes through the forest without leaving a trace. The three thousand worlds are but a single thought; The eighty-four thousand afflictions are all Bodhi. The ten thousand dharmas are originally empty and still; The six sense objects are fundamentally non-existent. The mind-ground is vast and boundless; The nature of reality is perfectly bright and clear. The Great Matter is settled at once; The Way is realized in a single moment. From now on, I shall roam freely; Wherever I go, I am at ease. She lived for sixty years and passed away in the year of the Water Monkey (1692). Her remains were interred at the West Peak of Mount Tiantong. Her dharma heirs numbered over one hundred. Her biography is recorded in the *Tiantong Jishi*. Her verses are included in the *Jingde Chuandeng Lu*, the *Wudeng Huiyuan*, and the *Zuting Shiyuan*. Her stupa is named "Zhaoxian" (Manifesting the Truth). She was posthumously honored with the title "Chan Master Nie Luo Nihui Kong. Her portrait is enshrined in the Hall of Patriarchs. She is also known as the Nun Nie Luo Nihui Kong. Her secular surname was Wang. She was born in the year of the Wood Rat (1640) and passed away in the year of the Water Monkey (1692). She was seventy-three years old. She was a native of Ning County. On his way back, he encountered an old master who asked, "What is your original face? The old master said, "Who is it that prostrates itself? At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.

"Now I have shattered the face born of my mother; the great earth, mountains, and rivers are unified in peace. He also said: "Fundamentally, one is without mind and things are naturally at ease;
