The layman Li Qian of Zhongfang in Jiangdu was originally from Shanyang in Huai’an, a native of Beizhi.
At the age of twelve, he dreamed of ascending to the Heavenly Emperor, who commanded two monks to transmit to him the phrase: "A dragon emerges from fire; a tiger is born from water."
He informed his parents of this awakening. His parents said, "Before you were born, you were conceived as a result of prayers offered to Lüzu.
The scholar immediately asked, "What was it like before birth? His father was greatly amazed by this. As he grew older, he took pleasure in reading the works of Sun Tzu and Wu Qi.

At the age of twenty-eight, he passed the civil service examination in the Dingchou year of the Chongzhen reign. At thirty-two, he met a strange man who transmitted to him the heart-mind teachings of the Three Teachings.
He subsequently abandoned his official post to seek out teachers, traveling to consult various renowned masters. He visited Shang Zunyuan and asked about the "Three Phrases" of Linji.
Zunyuan shouted, "Do you want me to tell them to you? The practitioner was startled.
He then asked about the kōan concerning Yunmen’s staff leaping about. Zunyuan shouted again, "Do you want me to explain it to you? At these words, the practitioner [attained realization].
The Great Master (Da-sheng) said, "Vimalakīrti’s single silence caused all listening and viewing to vanish completely; the moon set and the crows cried out, while the Milky Way shone brightly.

The Venerable (Zun) said, "From of old, a filial son avoids uttering his father's name. He performed three prostrations according to the rites of a scholar-official, and the Venerable deeply approved of this.

Later, he visited Tianfeng Qing; upon seeing him, Tianfeng granted him approval and specifically ascended the hall for him. He asked: "When meeting a man who has attained the Way, one does not respond with speech or silence."
"What do you have to say in response? The layman said, "That one turn of the autumnal gaze as I depart. Qing said, "Not yet; speak further.
The layman said, "First there was wailing, and then there was laughter. Qing then bestowed upon him the seal of certification (*karmadāna*).

The layman often lived alone at Xingjiao Monastery, preaching the Dharma according to the needs of the occasion and chanting the profound meanings of the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and the *Awakening of Faith*. The world called him "The Great Layman Reborn," and he was ordained as a monk.

Question: Zhaozhou circumambulated the meditation seat once and said, "The turning of the Tripitaka is finished. The Master said, "As soon as he stepped down from the meditation seat, I already knew the sutras had been turned.
[Zhaozhou] asked, "Why did the old woman say he only turned half the Tripitaka?
The Master said, "When an ox passes through a window lattice, its head, feet, and four hooves all pass through; why is it that the tail cannot pass? The monk said, "There is a distinction."
Cases such as these are few (Tianfeng Qingxi).
Master Pujing of Rongfeng at Xinghua Monastery ascended the hall. Having already struck the drum and tolled the bell to proclaim the Dharma, why trouble me to ascend the hall again?
One does not realize that the staff and shout have been fully revealed; they still listen to endless chatter about merits and faults. Thus it is said:
[He] dispersed the assembly and threw down his staff to descend from the seat. Ascending the hall, he held up his whisk and said:
"This alone is the one reality; the other two are not true. He then struck his own mouth and said: "Today, this mountain monk has wrongly provided a commentary for others.
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff and said: "Today, this mountain monk has specially invited Old Wooden Seat to act as your host."
[The Master] leveled his staff and said, "Listen closely, listen closely. A monk asked, "From where does life come?
The Master held up a fire-tongs and said, "This fire-tongs was bought for three copper coins. [The monk] asked, "Where does death go?
The Master said, "A single swipe, and sparks fly. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The main thoroughfare for both land and water. [The monk] said, "No..."
A questioner asked, "What path? The Master said, "What path do you ask about? He replied, "I ask about the Great Path.
The Master said, "North, South, East, West" (Fayin Hengsi).
Chan Master Yilong Pofeng Yi of Jiaxing was the son of the Cao family of Haning. He ascended the hall and said:
"Whether a monastery is large or small, whether the assembly is numerous or few, the great is manifested within the small, and the small is manifested within the great. Have you not heard it said:

'Mañjuśrī rides an elephant within the pore of a lotus fiber'—therein, all traces of communication are utterly absent. The *Hongmeng* dragon beats its wings atop the Northern Ocean; the waves boil and the billows surge."
"Teng" (to soar) refers to the meeting of circumstances. "Obtaining green willows everywhere where one can tether a horse" refers to understanding the principle.
He looked left and right and said, "I only fear it is not jade; were it jade, how truly marvelous! (From *Fayin Jiangsi*).
Chan Master Yuanfeng Zhixuan Tai of Yangzhou was the son of Jiao Shi of Xinghua. He left home at the age of fourteen and relied upon Jianlong Hang.
He studied under him with diligence for many years. One day, Hang asked, "Without falling into the categories of past or present, bring forth a single phrase.
The Master said, "I will not speak. Hang asked, "Why do you not speak? The Master replied, "To speak would again fall into the categories of past and present. Hang then desisted.
**Qu (Going):** A monk asked, "Today we eat congee and rice. The Master said, "Bring me a broken cauldron and I will tell you.
The monk said, "The cauldron is broken. The Master said, "Eat your fill as you please. **Commentary:** Taking up Zhaozhou’s [question on] whether a dog has Buddha-nature or not, I offer this verse:
Why speak of Buddha-nature as having or lacking? The spring colors are at their peak throughout the imperial capital. As for those who plunder empty appearances—there is none.
Dependence. To leave it for my descendants to chant: "Li-luo. The *Song on the Three Barriers of Huanglong* says:
"The donkey’s hoof as the source of conditions, and the Buddha’s hand— Transverse three, vertical four, flaunting the family’s disgrace.
Upon inspection, not worth even half a coin; Yet one still opens a wide mouth before others. (Fayin Hengsi)
Chan Master Fǒngfēng Fǎchāng was the son of the Lǐ family of Xīnghuà. He ascended the hall and said: "The sound of the bell rings out clearly; the drum beats with a lofty resonance.
As this mountain monk takes his seat, the assembly stands on both sides. He gave a shout and said: "This matter is clearly revealed in its entirety;
why need it be proclaimed again and again? The Master once composed a verse on the Three Secrets of Fényáng: The First Secret:

Admitting no deliberation or conjecture, there is no room for verbal distinction. It is perfectly clear that the scale-weight is iron. Seeing the scale-weight, one strikes it with a wedge—this is the second secret.

At Mazu’s Blue Pass, thought was brought to an end. The north wind blows fiercely, the whole world is cold; the great earth, mountains, and rivers are a single expanse of snow—this is the third secret.
At the tips of the hundred grasses, all is revealed and leaked forth: the peach is red, the plum is white, and the willow...
Bestowing his favor: within the cry of the *subing* (cuckoo), it flows as the sound of dripping blood. It is also said: "The Three Secrets of Fenyang" merely create complications;
if you wish to know the point of arrival, cold water and hot fire [are the answer]. A monk asked: "The *Heart Sūtra* says, 'There is no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.'"
"What teaching will you give? The Master remained silent for a long while, then asked a monk, "What was it you were just asking?
As the monk prepared to open his mouth, the Master immediately covered it with his hand (Fayin Jiangjie).
Chan Master Kuan of Weimo, at Jiangu, was the son of the Fang family of Yi County. On the occasion of the Buddha’s Enlightenment Day, he ascended the hall and said:
"The first yang opens the way for prosperity; the myriad phenomena all flourish. The fourfold assembly looks up in reliance as the Buddha-light shines brightly.
But tell me, what principle does Weimo have today? Striking the incense table with his staff, he said: 'O Great Assembly! The entire earth is this very Buddha.'"
"Body! Where have you all gone for your summer retreat? He struck once more and said: "The clay ox roars at the moon and returns to the Eastern Sea;
ten thousand waters flow toward the source, yet there is yet another layer [of the resonant Dharma-sound]."
Chan Master Wenchu Yan of Mount Liuan in the Buddha-land was the son of the Tu family of Taizhou. He ascended the hall and cited the following:

When his own teacher, [Huang]Jie, arrived at Yue’an, he asked, "Is the Abbot there? [Yue’an] replied, "He is not. [Huang]Jie asked, "Where has he gone? [Yue’an] said, "He has gone to the patron’s house.
[Huang]Jie asked, "Was he led away by a water buffalo? [Yue’an] said, "I do not know. [Huang]Jie struck the monk three times and then departed from the hermitage.
The Master returned. The monk recounted the previous conversation. The Hermit said, "The Water Buffalo has been led away by someone; you do not even protect it. He then struck him and expelled him.
Xuedou heard of this and said, "It was a narrow margin of victory. Nevertheless, it was still pressing the ox's head down to make it eat grass.
The Master said, "The more one looks up at it, the higher it seems; the more one drills into it, the firmer it becomes. One looks for it in front, and suddenly it is behind."
"Great assembly! When an old man speaks in this manner, do you know where he is heading?
He is on the verge of completing a mountain nine fathoms high, yet he has not added even a single basket of earth. (A shout—*Fayin Hangsi*).
Chan Master Wanxiangqi of Qingzhou addressed the assembly: "Today I shall briefly open a single thread.

Autumn mountains and autumn waters within a painted scroll—when the red wheel splits asunder, it cleaves the face of you, the *kalyāṇamitra*. To deliberate or reflect is to be separated by ten thousand layers. (Fayin Hengji was his successor.)
Chan Master Fuhai Ji of Daci Nunnery in Zhenzhou ascended the hall and said: "To study the Way, one must first realize the correct cause;
the source of the Way has never been separated by even a single speck of dust. You should know that the realm of all sentient beings is itself the Tathāgata’s true wheel of Dharma."
"Elder Jì has cut out his own tongue! Is there anyone among you who can save him?
He let out a shout and descended from the seat. (Fayin Háng’s Successor)
The layman Jia Longwen of Yunjian, whose given name was Dazhen, lost both his parents at the age of nine. His elder brother, Longmei, raised him.
After he married, he became fond of wine and prone to litigation; he spent ten years in prison. Since the dynastic change, he has been ill-at-ease in all matters.
He often sighed that time is limited and worldly affairs are impermanent. He made a vow to recite the Buddha’s name and provide meals for monks, gradually leaving behind [his former ways].

Xin Benfen consulted Foguo Wentai, Taoming Zong, Sanmo Quan, Jilun Yong, and other venerable Chan masters. For six years he applied his efforts until his realization was nearly as unified as a single piece.
At all times—whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining—it was like the bright moon reflected in a clear pool, pure and devoid of a single speck of impurity.
Yet, when it came to being interrogated, he could not turn himself around. One day, he invited Yong to his residence; after the midday meal, [he said:]
He forced down his lower lip and pressed him with intense pain, asking, "Layman, when this single breath does not return, where will you establish yourself and find your livelihood?
The layman was rendered speechless and unable to respond. He turned and entered the room, straightening his spine.

He cast aside all worldly concerns; before he knew it, cold sweat fell like rain. Suddenly, hearing the sound of the watch-drum, his entire body felt a sense of joy and liberation, as if he had cast off a burden of a thousand catties.
As he came out from attendance, Yong asked, "What news have you received?
The Master let out a thunderous shout. Yong said, "Speak clearly! The Master then struck him with his palm. Yong said, "I do not fear the transgression. The Master said, "Cang! (The sky!)
"O Heaven, O Blue Heaven! He then presented this verse: "The trees wither and the leaves fall, revealing the autumn sky; In total release and total gathering, no trace is left behind.
Man forgets time and the ox vanishes; A single bright orb shines in the azure heavens. Yong said, "I do not believe the Way."
The Master drew a circle and said: "The great earth sinks level, the entire realm is empty; the crown of the head splits open, free to go east or west.

With a single roar, a thousand rivers flow backward; all phenomena are gathered back, transcending difference and sameness. Yong nodded his head in understanding. The next day, he went to Longhua and entered the abbot’s quarters.
Zong said, "If you do not let anything out from within, nor let anything enter from without, how is it that you act?"
Yongshou said, "A single squeeze shatters it to pieces. Zong asked, "Where did you learn that? Yongshou said, "What a fine, discerning head monk!
Zong asked, "And what about your own eyes? Yongshou then gave a shout. Zong raised his staff; Yongshou immediately departed.

He traveled extensively throughout all quarters and later received the dharma-transmission seal from Baoen Chuo. He responded to circumstances as they arose and lived with unrestrained ease until the year Kāngxī Yǐ (1685).
In the twelfth month of winter, he manifested a slight illness and wrote ten points of final instructions to exhort his son, admonishing him not to perform worldly funeral rites.
He prepared a wooden coffin and monastic robes, and composed a verse for sealing the coffin, which said: "I used to love sitting; today I must lie down."
Hitherto I was inclined to sleep; today I love to sit. Attached to neither, with no mutual compromise between the two, there is naturally a single stretch of fine scenery.
Bare and skeletal, I walk alone. The verse for lighting the lamp says: "Jia Longwen! Jia Longwen!"
In the fierce flames of a red furnace, refined gold is long tempered; the foul vapors within the breast are cast off entirely and renewed.
Unchanged by fire, it becomes clear when placed in water. Throwing up a torch, he said: "A single path of brilliance brings infinite joy, replacing the pupils in the eyes of the age.
He then wrote another verse: "This time, it is certain there is no partiality; casting off the hand, it is clearly present in the hour of Xu."
At that time, if one can recognize the meaning within it, the clouds are on the mountain and the moon is in the pond; with a single laugh, one passes away (Foguo Chao succeeded [to this lineage]).
You Ning Luoshan Yanli Min Chan Master was a native of Huining. He studied under Jigan Chan. He asked: "What is..."
Regarding the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, Xuanzhao said, "I will tell you only when the stone tortoise in front of the mountain learns to speak.

As the Master hesitated, Xuanzhao gave a shout. One day, while riding a donkey across a stream, he attained realization. Upon returning, he prostrated and said, "The stone tortoise in front of the mountain nods its head today.
Xuanzhao raised his head; the Master said, "Be careful not to be talkative. Thereupon, Xuanzhao descended from his meditation seat.
The Master pointed and said, "This old fellow’s heels have not yet touched the ground. He presented a verse, saying: "Forgetting meals and abandoning sleep was all for no reason;
In vain, he pinched his mother’s nose until it ached. Before the Small Pagoda Mountain, he suffered a tumble;
Empty space laughs until its tongue goes dry. Chanwei granted him certification (he became the successor of Ji’an Hang).

After failing the imperial examinations, the lay practitioner Liu Weizan of Lishui closed himself in retreat for twenty years. He attained a profound realization and composed commentaries on the sutras and shastras.
He once wrote one hundred poems on mountain life, one of which says: "The daily practice lies at the pickaxe’s tip; Trimming the grass and clearing the brambles, there is no rest.
If someone laughs that I labor in vain, How could this matter be sought elsewhere? [This is] Zen practice.
What use is sitting upon a meditation mat? Exerting effort where there is life while drilling into death. In every matter, follow conditions as they arise; there is nothing that is not so.
Of all manner of flavors, they are all one and the same bitter taste. (By Ji’an Chan, successor to [Master] Yan.)
Chan Master Nanzhu of Fahuashu in Suzhou ascended the hall and said: "One Ding, two Zhuo; white clouds drifting and thinning.
Two fang, three pao; mountain streams murmuring and flowing. Stop! Stop! Even if you borrow the melody of a rooster, it cannot deceive me.
I am not yet willing to let this checkpoint pass in a blur. He struck once with his staff and said, "This is called the checkpoint. How will you all deal with it?"
[The monk] passed by. Just as a monk emerged, the Master struck him repeatedly, saying, "One must not let you off lightly.

He then followed up, saying, "Truly a guest from the gate of Mengchang; let him go once and never return lightly. On the night of the Lantern Festival, at the conclusion of the retreat, he ascended the hall and said:
"Fire seeks dryness; water seeks moisture. Why are thorns curved? Why are pines straight? Those coming from the south go south; those going north go north. Out!"
The grass at the gates spreads vast and wide; along the streets, lanterns cluster thick. One stall, two stalls; three bowls, four bowls.
Six times six is originally thirty-six. Tell this to the monks of today: each and every one shall behold the marvel and be fully satisfied. Addressing the assembly:
"Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored"—this was the first utterance of the World-Honored One. It is the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the wondrous Nirvana.
The mind. This was the final opportunity for the World-Honored One. This story has spread throughout the Western Heavens and pervaded the Eastern Lands;
surely all have understood it thoroughly together. Yet, when lightly probed, most are unable to open their mouths.

If one continues to seek it within words and divine it with the thinking mind, day after day the sun rises in the east and day after day it sets in the west. There will come a day of realization—gold.
The crow flies toward the abyss of the barbarians; the jade hare runs into the valley of the sun. To the assembly: At Hanshan Temple, there is laughter;
at Fahua Monastery, they crowd together. Black beans trade for human eyes; red and crimson lychees are given to people to swallow and chew.
With eyes closed, one eats snails; at whose door are there not several? With eyes open, one eats mouse droppings.
In whose household’s cauldron are there two grains? If you understand, then the shrimp and the tiger, the cat and the mouse, are one;
if you do not understand, then the Tathāgatas of the three periods and the entire Great Canon of Teachings are beneath your feet.

*Chan* (Investigate!). On the seventh day, the Abbot ascends the hall and says: "I have two pivot-pins. Having traveled for thirty years, searching east and west, I have not yet dared to reveal them. Today..."

I have brought forth these "Seven Seals of Peaceful Meditation" for you all. For now, they must serve to cut off the ninety-six kinds of circular signs (*maṇḍala*) of Yangshan and bring one to the ultimate bottom.
Even Śākyamuni and Bodhidharma could not emerge from this place. The Master drew two symbols with his hand, △ and ▽, and said:
"All you practitioners of meditation, if you can penetrate these two characters, it will be like the sun and moon in the sky, shining down upon all."

Throughout the eight directions and the nine provinces, it is as if the earth possesses springs and deep pools; circulating through the five lakes and the four seas, it is like a person possessing eyes.
To examine and verify the monks of the world, tell me: by what means do you verify them? He then held up his whisk and said, "Do you recognize it?"
Again, he lowered his whisk and said: "Do you understand? The mountain monk has already explained the meaning of the characters; the commentary is complete.
If there were a *siddha* guest within this assembly, why would Mañjuśrī need to strike once? On the morning of the spring festival, he ascended the hall and said:
"The peach blossoms are red, the plum blossoms are white—this reveals the eyes of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. The small-leaved willow, the large-leaved poplar—these pierce through the monks."
The patriarch’s nose is broken; the clay ox is shattered. A thousand-year-old tree flourishes anew; the wooden horse is pulled back. Ten thousand miles of long road in an instant.
The yellow oriole emerging from the valley has its feathers naturally dry; the tortoise entering the water has its head not wet.
The wise master has eyes black as lacquer; the person of no rank is bare-boned and stark. *Du du!* Where is there thunderclaps in the spring sunshine?
Addressing the assembly: "Ho! Ho! Ho! Linji, that little fellow, struck the ribs of Dayu so hard that he could not endure three blows and cried out in distress.
When the wind is clear and the moon is bright, how can there be an end? The *subing* bird cries atop the *dujuan* flower; it harbors a long-standing resentment that travelers cannot return home.
They cannot return. But if they return, they shall attain it. The full splendor of spring fills the imperial capital; the young masters of the Five Tombs..."
Lashing his chestnut steed, he lay last night drunk upon the flower-strewn streets. Turning his head, he saw the sun rise and the east turn white.
A scholar asked, "The common people use it daily yet do not know it. If they were to know it, what would that be like? The Master said, "When the wise see it, they call it wisdom;
when the benevolent see it, they call it benevolence. The scholar said, "Please show me the Buddha-dharma. The Master said, "In your own house."
[The Master] did not attend to him. [The monk] asked about his family affairs. [The Master] asked: "What is the other shore? The Master said: "This road. [The monk] said:
"When you ask about water, you answer with water; when you ask about insects, you answer with insects. Why, when the student asks about the other shore, does the Master answer with this road?
The Master said: "This road does not lead there" (Mihe Li succeeded him).
Chan Master Fuhui of Yezhu at Mount Song in Yizhou was the son of the Ye family of Changshou in Yuzhou.

Having encountered civil unrest, his parents fled and dispersed, leaving him alone to seek refuge in the south at Qianzhou. Suddenly, in a single thought, he turned his gaze inward and resolved to leave the white-robed life of a layman.
He went to Dongming to request ordination, and before long, he departed to visit Longmen Huan, who instructed him that all phenomena return to [the source].
For many years he had investigated the question, "Where does each and every thing return? until he finally attained realization and received the seal of transmission from Longmen.
He subsequently went forth to reside at Ciyun in Yunnan, Zhulin in Menghua, Wufu in Shunying, Shuzong Shanfa, Funi Fa Hua, Mili in Chengjiang, and Songshan in Yizhou.
Ascending the hall, he said: "‘This very mind is Buddha’—that is not it either."
"It is not mind, it is not Buddha—this is also not so. It is not mind, it is not Buddha, and it is not an object—this is also not so.
The clay deity laughs and the diamond bone emerges; the local spirit scolds and the temple guardian’s face turns black. If you understand, you are liberated in your entire being;
if you do not, do not stand here in vain for long. Ascending the hall, [he said]: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven—the old man of Yangqi has a tongue!"
A red head. The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. How could even a clever monk recognize this? (He lets out a shout. Entering the hall:
Last year’s spring was at Tianmu; this year’s spring is at Wufu. Yet one must look closely at the cold plum blossoms:
branch after branch pierces through the green of the mountain peaks. Who is pouring wine to offer to the God of Spring? They pay no heed to the cries of the cuckoo.
Blood flowed as he ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What are the Three Jewels? The Master said, "Rice, wheat, and beans. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "At the two meal times, one eats until one is full and satisfied. He then said, "If it were Deshan or Linji, they would have pointed with their staffs and said, 'Stand here for now.
If it were Mañjuśrī or Samantabhadra, they would have pointed with their staffs and said, 'Stand here for now.'"
Standing here, he looked left and right and said, "The Sleeping Dragon would not serve as a footnote for you all. He then descended from his seat and ascended the hall.
With a single cry, he shattered the claim to supremacy; who would have known that Yunmen’s staff was broken? There is yet another "white-thief" old man.
He said, "To speak of what others see is not to distinguish them. He picked up his staff and said, "If one hesitates to sever when it should be severed, one instead invites the thief.
He threw down the staff, laughed loudly, and descended from the seat. Evening *can* on the Mid-Autumn Festival: The green mountains see rain pouring down like buckets day after day;

It is said only that the Palace of Cold Repose is ashamed to show its face. Suddenly the sun breaks through and the sky is washed clean; The clear light remains as before upon the water-weeds of the river. [He] suddenly called out to the assembly.
He said: "At this very moment, is it practicing cultivation? Is it making offerings? Or is it sweeping the sleeves and departing?
The stars follow as the plains stretch wide; the moon surges as the great river flows. At the Small Assembly at Kainan, he held up his whisk and called to the assembly, saying:
"Do you understand? Where Kainan ends is the edge of the world. The bamboo draws in the clear breeze as the sun slants. On my staff there is no money to buy wine."
White wine! Let us pour out a bowl of Zhaozhou’s tea. Those who laugh are as numerous as hemp; those who do not laugh are as numerous as hemp.
Setting it down, he says: *Huṃ phaṭ!* Small Assembly (Xiaocan): To guide disciples and lead the multitude, I exhaust my talent, desiring only that my descendants open their true eye (*zhengyan*).
If one clearly opens this true eye, all sentient beings and all Buddhas shall be buried in a single pit. (He draws a line with his staff.)
Hua said: "Tell me, what is Vairocana? He then drew a line. In a small-scale sermon (xiaochan), he said: "To establish a knowing-seeing within knowing-seeing is the very root of ignorance;
to have no seeing within knowing-seeing is itself nirvana. He suddenly held up his staff and said: "The Śūraṅgama Sūtra!"
"An Lengyan, when did you ever recognize it? Before the rhombus-shaped mirror has reflected anything—[I] address the assembly:
A monk who wears not a single thread and eats not a grain of rice deserves thirty blows of the staff.
Why is this so? Because he only knows how to make a living on pure ground; he does not yet know how to circulate everywhere. Nevertheless, let us reach this point."
Li Zhe addressed the assembly: “If you wish to take it, take it; if you wish to let it go, let it go. But when both taking and letting go are forgotten—how is that?
Within the Great Tang Empire, there is no place to settle him. A monk asked, “What is the countenance before one’s parents were born?
The Master struck him on the mouth with his palm and said, “Is this birth, or is it non-birth? Another asked, “What is the moon in the water?”
The Master said: "I have taught you to search for it, yet you cannot grasp it.
(Shanhui Huan, successor). *Wudeng Quanshu*, Scroll 97, Supplement.
In the thirty-sixth generation of the Linji school under Nanyue, Master Chan Sen of Songyin Boshan recorded these words when asked:
"What is the realm of Songyin? The Master replied: "A bridge spans the flowing water."
As it rises and falls, the pagoda pillar lets the clear breeze pass to and fro. [A monk] asked, "What is one who is within the realm?
The Master said, "The body wears the *kāṣāya*, free from worldly appearances; the mind hangs the ancestral seal, transcending the human world.

[The monk] asked, "What is the essential meaning of the Dharma-king’s decree? The Master said, "You must quickly turn your eyes to look at the immortal; do not look at the fan in the immortal’s hand."
"Param! The Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings are all but yellow leaves used to stop a child's crying.

The seventeen hundred public cases are, for the most part, nothing more than withered vines. Now, toward that place where the Buddhas cannot speak and where the Patriarchs cannot tread, I shall briefly open a single thread so that you may know your home beyond words.
Raising his whisk, he said: "The first opening reveals a new atmosphere; let us sing it together in unison! Ta...
*Pingge* (Flat Song) for the Evening Session: In the midst of myriad conditions, the fifth month of summer; At Songyin, the forest opens a lion’s den.
Each and every one, with mind empty, returns having passed the imperial examination. Dust speaks, lands speak, and they speak with blazing intensity.
This blazing speech continues without intermission. The mountain colors are none other than the pure body; The sounds of the brook are all the broad and long tongue. (Guanmei Huan Si)
Chan Master Tanzhao Gao of Zhihai ascended the hall. "Nanquan’s beheading of the cat lost him two eyes;
Zhaozhou’s prostration won him a pair of straw sandals. To strike locks and beat shackles, to chop nails and cut through iron—this is a matter concerning this mountain monk.
But as for you all, how would you speak of it? After a long silence, he said: "At the center of the crossroads, one..."

Kuai Zhuan ascends the hall. “The *maṇi* jewel people do not recognize; they have personally received it within the *tathāgatagarbha*. [Suddenly] calling out, he says: ‘Great assembly, what is the *maṇi* jewel? What do you call the *tathāgatagarbha*? After a long silence, he points with his finger and says: ‘This monk here is fat; that monk over there is thin. He then descends from his seat. [The Record of] Qingming. however, as soon as he opened a scroll, he would close his eyes and fall asleep. Upon hearing the sound of Buddhist chanting, he would invariably leap for joy.
At twelve years of age, he earnestly requested to leave the household life, but his parents would not permit it. Previously, the Grand Councilor Ruixuan Ding...
Gongwen Sheng served as the Chief Justice in the Central Province. Gong’s son, Governor Taiyan Gong Sikong, was still a young boy with hair hanging down to his forehead.
One night, Gong dreamed of Vemacitra, who said to him, "Your son has come riding upon the wheel of his original vow; he shall attain the civil service examinations and achieve great merit.

However, you must find someone to act on his behalf in shaving his head and donning the robes of a monk, thereby repaying the Buddha's grace. With these words, [Vemacitra] took the mallet from his hand.
Pointing to a boy standing nearby, he said, "This child is a vessel for the Mahāyāna Dharma. Do not let him slip away. The official merely responded with assent.
Upon waking, he told Lady Huang of his dream, and she found that her own dream was identical;

they could not help but marvel at the coincidence. The following day, the official happened to go out. The Master, then fifteen years old, was returning from his school; on the road, they were unable to avoid each other, so he simply bowed.

Standing on the left side of the road, the Duke caught sight of him; he was unmistakably the same boy from his dream. Consequently, the Duke summoned him to his office and asked the boy, "What do you aspire to?
The Master replied, "I wish to leave the household life. The Duke recounted the events of the dream to the boy's father.
The father said, "This is a celestial being; one must not force him. The Duke then provided his official salary for the purpose, and the Master shaved his head and donned the white robes of a novice.
Less than half a year later, he sighed and said, "A renunciant should strive for the great matter of resolving birth and death;
how can one thus waste the food of the faithful and squander one's time in vain? Thereupon, he packed his belongings in a cloth bag, donned a straw hat, and set out alone on pilgrimage.

He visited more than thirty spiritual teachers (*kalyāṇamitra*) and investigated the mind for many years, yet he did not achieve clear realization. Eventually, he arrived at Huguo Temple in Bozhou and called upon Dongshan.
Bai Xuejing was instructed to investigate the saying, "The myriad dharmas return to the One; to what does the One return? He applied himself with great diligence to this inquiry.

One night, while remaining awake until dawn, he suddenly attained realization upon hearing the cock crow. He composed a verse, which said: "The watchtower drum strikes through the long and short watches; The myriad dharmas return to the One."
The lamp is spent and the oil is dry; both eyes stare wide open. With a single, thunderous cry, it announces the dawn. The neighbor’s house is stirred, and the flocks of roosters begin to crow.
The next morning, he presented this to Jingzhao. Jingzhao composed a verse, saying: "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The Master said: "Though gold dust is precious..."
As the dust fell into his eyes, it formed a film over them. Jing said, "Night travel is not permitted, yet you insist on carrying a torch;

you must go straight ahead and show it to people on the road. The Master said, "A swift opportunity is hard to encounter. Jing said, "Thirty years hence, do not fail in your transmission when meeting others.
The Master let out a roar and shouted. Jing said, "By your insight, you are truly a descendant of Linji. Thereupon, [the Master] refined his practice through long-term study.
For twenty years, it has been as if a single day. In the autumn of the Jiashu year of the Kangxi era, I heard that Governor Taiyan had passed away while on duty;

I felt a sense of grief as if I had lost something precious. When the following autumn arrived and the anniversary of his first memorial service drew near, I took up my alms bowl and entered the capital.
There I met Qian Qianshi, who was staying at B保安 (Bao'an). I went to pay my respects and inquire after him. Qian asked, "Where have you come from?"
The Master said, "Baozhou. Wushi asked, "How many stages have you traveled to reach here? The Master said, "Two thousand li. Wushi asked, "By boat or by land?
The Master said, "Every step has a road leading to Chang'an. Wushi picked up his staff and said, "Speak further on this very point."

The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! Xishi then struck him. The Master shook out his sleeves and departed. After a short while, the Master again assumed his full ceremonial dignity and went to the abbot’s quarters to request further instruction.
Xishi said, "Thirty years ago, at Zhaozhou’s hearth, there was a 'no host, no guest' koan that no one has ever brought up.
What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Master, you are advanced in years; please do not..."
[Zhaozhou] wanted noodles to eat. Xuanzhi asked, “Ultimately, what is the ‘no host or guest’ dialogue? Zhaozhou said, “When the crow caws, it is ‘ya ya’; when the magpie calls, it is ‘que’.
Xuanzhi asked, “As for Yuansha hearing this and saying, ‘This old fellow’s heels are still not touching the ground,’ how would you explain that?
Zhaozhou said, “A lion bites a man; a Han-dog chases after a clod of earth. Xuanzhi said, “It shows its head.”
Looking out from beyond the heavens, who is there like me? The Master made a gesture of overturning the meditation seat, whereupon Huishi withdrew.
One day, while Huishi was ascending the hall for formal instruction, the Master stepped forward from the assembly to pay his respects. Huishi said, "A fine warrior of the Dharma-gate you are!"
The Master said, "The Abbot truly possesses the eye of discernment. Tish said, "To deploy strategy within the tent and secure victory a thousand *li* away—of what sort of person is this matter?
The Master said, "Seizing the banner and snatching the drum; occupying the heights and employing the unexpected."
"It is not that there is no *upādhyāya*. To seize the tiger’s head and gather its tail—to clarify the fundamental tenet beneath the first phrase—this still leaves something for me to concede.
Zhishi said, "I have been stretching my neck in expectation of you for a long time. The Master took three steps forward and responded, "Yes, yes.
Zhishi struck him on the head with his staff and said, "Now tell me: was this one blow seizing the tiger’s head, or was it gathering the tiger’s tail? The Master then...
He prostrated and said, "Your great kindness is difficult to repay. Zhi deeply nodded his head in agreement.

Regarding the lineage of the staff, he bestowed a formal certification within the hall, saying in verse: "Having traveled throughout all quarters for many years, The accord between teacher and disciple is fundamentally natural.
Let the staff go forth as a dragon; It shall receive the most eminent of men. (Qianqian succeeded Zhi.)
Chan Master Fayun Banyi of Xuduan ascends the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. At midnight, Gautama beheld the morning star and lost his two mother-born eyes.
He newly attained a certain extraordinary matter: throughout the ten directions of the world, it is entirely his own body.
Entirely his own body—there is no need to seek it. Upon the plum branches, the cold fragrance wafts; on every mountain peak, the white snow crowns them.
Yun ascends the hall. The two head seats of the two halls shout in unison; guest and host are clearly distinguished in that very moment.
Were it not for hands that have long experienced the ranks of battle, this mountain monk would not show such lack of leniency beneath his staff.
Cao Shan’s wine, Niu-tou’s rice, Yunmen’s cake, and Zhaozhou’s tea—these are the ancient styles of the true lineage. Raising both hands and presenting his staff, he says: "The assembly!"
"Do you see? I offer it all upon this platter—many flavors. Once sated, hunger is forgotten; ten thousand matters cease. [The Master] planted his staff and descended from the seat.
While the Master was reading a book, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "One phrase, one circle. The monk asked, "What is 'one phrase, one circle'? The Master said, "What are you asking? [Another] asked about the Great Way.
"It has no form. How can one see its Way? The Master said, "Blue has blue light; yellow has yellow light.
The student asked, "Why do I not see it? The Master said, "Precisely because it is too near. He offered this verse on the Old Lady of Mount Tai:
"The lush greenery is so deep it confuses the returning bird; North and south winds blow, opening the wisteria vines. The wayward son cannot bear to rest and depart; Long..."
The moon hangs in the sky like a white jade disc. In praise of Zhaozhou’s examination of the two hermits, he said: "The military tally is held in hand; one acts as one pleases.
Thunder crashes and roars—wondrous function is marvelous. On the same battlefield, all exert their strength together;
Who knows how to kill or give life at the front line? (Duchi Lang, his successor).
A Small Public Sermon by Chan Master Hanyun Ding of Wanshou Monastery in Guangling. In ancient times, there were no monastic communities for practitioners;
they dwelt in nests and caves, free from all constraints. By day they sought alms in the villages, and with no worries for their families, they were able to cultivate the Way.
Although their movements were like the tracks of clouds, how could they avoid the hardships of wind and rain day and night? Later, those of great wisdom established monasteries.

Wherever the staff and mendicant’s bowl reach, smoke rises from the hearth; elders and youths from all quarters come to take refuge. The forging of talent and capacity begins from here, relying entirely upon the practice of the Dharma by the Master.
Following rules and observing decorum, one maintains order and coherence; the elders are like brothers and the juniors like younger siblings.

Through the four means of attraction and the six principles of harmony, there is neither contention nor pride. One must support the seven essential matters for opening the gate; thus, the path of body and mind is perfected.
Both are fully manifest. One should practice in accordance with what has been explained above. "The staff is insentient, like an iron face.
Entering the hall: "Sound and form are vast and expansive; they are all the Great Way that came from the West. Sentient beings have never been deluded. Sound and form are vast and expansive."
This is not the Great Way that came from the West; the Buddhas have never attained enlightenment.

Knowing thoroughly that delusion and awakening do not interfere with one another, one dwells at ease wherever there are willow alleys and flower streets. Free from both hatred and love, utterly simple and innocent, one acts with spontaneous, unrefined spontaneity.
One knows only that there is rice, so one opens the mouth and eats; what need is there to seek out all the various complexities of the Buddha-dharma?
If you simply proceed in this way, you might think you are failing the noble donors; yet if you do not proceed in this way, after all, with what will you point the way?
He then rose, resting his staff upon his shoulder, and said: "Master Zhi was no ordinary monk; the flower-cutting scissors are on the tip of his staff."
[The Master] was looking at a monk who had come for an interview. The Master said, "Majestic and grand; brilliant and resplendent—what is this? The monk was at a loss.
The Master said, "I thought this was a most exquisite and wonderful phrase; it turns out to be a signboard without any characters. (Recorded by Duchi Lang).
Chan Master Mimi of Mulan in Luzhou held a small *can* (sermon) on New Year’s Eve. Holding up his staff, he said: "On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month last year, there was this very thing;
on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month this year, there is also this very thing. He then raised the staff again and asked, "Do you see it?
If you say you see it or hear it, you are merely chasing after sounds and pursuing forms. With that, he struck the ground once with the staff.
The Master asked, "Did you hear it? "If you say you neither saw nor heard it, then people are merely avoiding form and fleeing from sound.
Ultimately, how is it? He threw down his staff and said, "Receive this color of thawing ice upon the mountain peak. "In the small assembly, we lift our tea bowls together to serve the spring banquet.
A single drop of water from Tiger Spring contains and exhales the ten directions; it is poured directly before one's face, profound and deep."
"A thousand feet. Few know how to repay kindness; it must be poured down upon the head to moisten the field of the mind. Many betray kindness.
Since you possess such supernatural power, why is it dry and parched beneath your feet? When the wind comes, the shadows of the trees move; when the leaves fall, one knows the tree. Question:
"In the state where there is no dream and no thought, where is the Master? The Master said: "A stone tortoise."
"Swallowing the moon. [A monk] asked, "The three realms have no peace; they are like a burning house. How, then, can one find peace?

The Master said, "Why do you tread upon the corner of the permanent brick of the monastery? He offered a verse on Huitang’s raising his fist to show a monk: [Verse omitted as per instructions to provide only the translation.]
Beside the Wuling Stream, emerald peaks and ridges rise; The eyes of the common folk have never been permitted to behold them. Having passed the Six Bridges, the scenery is extraordinary;
Clouds roll on and on, and waters flow on and on. In praise of Deshan’s alms-bowl:

Meeting on a narrow path, the son tests the father; He bows his head in silence—how boundless is that poison! Although he has not yet encountered the hand of Suoyun, He has already caused every person...
Li Lunma (Du Chi Lang Si).
Chan Master Puzhi Guchiyan of Shu Prefecture was the son of Li of Xinghua in Jiangnan. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The green mountains exude their colors; the mountain stream transmits its sound. The monk asked, "How does one maintain this?"
The Master said, "By the water’s edge, beneath the forest trees. The student said, "If that is so, then I shall accept it. The Master struck him and said, "Give me back my rice money!
A student asked, "If one brings nothing at all, do you still allow this student to meet with you?
The Master said, "I do not meet with you. The student asked, "Why do you not meet with me? The Master said, "If you bring nothing at all, what is there to meet?"
The monk gave a shout. The Master said, "I would have broken your donkey’s waist. (This refers to Faying Jie.
Chan Master Zongyuan Pu of Donglin on Mount Lu was a native of Jiangning. He traveled to study under various renowned masters, but found no resonance with them.
Later, he visited Faying Jie at Fenghua. Jie asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Jiangnan. Jie said, "Have you ever seen..."
"Who is this person? the Master asked. [Heng-ji-ke] saw several monks of coarse conduct and raised his fist, saying, "Have you ever seen this?
As the Master was about to offer a reply, [Heng-ji-ke] struck him, saying, "Monk of coarse conduct! One day, [Heng-ji-ke] took up his whisk and said:
"Speak one word here for me now, and I will grant that your studies are complete. The Master rose from his prostrations and stood in his place.
Fayan said, "Try saying something else. The Master shook out his sleeves and departed (Fayin succeeded [Fayan]).
Shishan Sufan Chan Master of Tiger Hill in Suzhou was the son of the Lu family of that same prefecture. He ascended the hall and said: "Secretly shifting one step, he occupies the void;
Expounding the Dharma, he turns to don the formless robe. The iron flute is blown horizontally with a melody beyond the kalpas; The golden bird flies through the heavens at midnight.
A monk asked, "What of the matter of white waves surging to the heavens? The Master said, "Perilous. As the monk prepared to offer further words, [the Master struck him].
The Master said, "Headless and brainless! Who can untie the golden bell on the tiger's neck? The Master said, "A handless person unties it.
[The student] asked, "Since he has no hands, how can he untie it? The Master said, "If you do not understand, how can you blame this old monk? (Fayin Jiang succeeded him.)
Chan Master Chang Yigan of Xinghua Zhengjue was the son of the Zhao family of this very locality. He ascended the hall and said: "The bright moon hangs in the sky, illuminating all;
in the clear pool, there is not a shadow of a tree. The mind is identical to the great void; he manifests a Dharma equal to the void. Great assembly, what is this 'Dharma equal to the void'?
He held up his whisk and said: "There is one more phrase, yet I dare not utter it. If I were to utter it, all Buddhas..."
All the patriarchs stand together beneath the wind. But tell me, which of these is the one? After a long silence, he said: "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not step on it;
take the bottomless basket and carry it home. (This is the lineage of Fayin Hang.)
Chan Master Weizhen Qi of Fayun Monastery in Yangzhou was a native of the Zhang family of that same prefecture.
He ascended the hall and cited Baizhang, who said: "If you have a staff, I give you a staff; if you have no staff, I take away your staff.
Looking at this with the correct eye, it cannot be avoided that he is taking public property to curry favor with people. After all...
How should it be established? I simply instruct you brothers that you may not advance forward, nor may you retreat backward.
Today’s single phrase transcends all precedents; I shall briefly loosen one thread to convey a message. He then struck the meditation desk with his staff and said:
When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present one’s sword; if you are not a poet, do not offer your verse (the successor of Fayin Hang).
Jueweng of Jianlong in Yangzhou had the attendant Ju as his servant; Ju was a son of the Yang clan from Liuhe who had studied under Fayin Hang for the longest time.
One day, while sitting in meditation during the incense period, [Jiexian] asked, "What is your original face? The Master replied, "My legs are numb and my feet ache.
[Jiexian] said, "Do not be mistaken. The Master said, "I am neither aching nor in pain. [Jiexian] asked, "What is the meaning of being neither aching nor in pain?
The Master replied, "A sweet melon is sweet from root to tip; a bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. He then presented this to him.

The verse says: The numbness in the calves and pain in the feet are most distinct; Thoroughly refined elegance bursts open the crown of the head. The sound of the stream at both banks grows fainter as the mountains recede;
Singing a song aloud, one passes through the southern village. New Year’s Eve Small Assembly: When used with intimacy and seen through to the bottom, there is no other teaching to be grasped.
The firecrackers burst forth like thunder; Every sound is a profound and wondrous secret. The Jade Maiden conceives in the night.
T’ai. King Dongcun was forging iron. Striking the incense table with his whisk, he said, “With one blow, I have forgotten where I am;
I shall not add more filings again. He brandished the whisk and descended from his seat. A verse on the Original Face says: In years past we walked hand-in-hand toward the high terrace;
today the vermilion maples cover the wine. When there is entanglement, add more entanglement; when there is a place to linger, linger on.

If you do not act once, you will not understand twice. Half-witted and half-skilled, half a hero. Crimson leaves laugh as the autumn scenery grows old;

Chan Master Huiyuan Falang of Xinghua was the son of the Han family of his native district. At the age of eight, he entered the monastic order under the elder Chesheng at Ludu Temple.
One day, while ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the realm of the Lotus Sutra? The Master said, "Outside the gate, the fragrant grasses are green;
before the steps, the moss is verdant. The monk asked, "Who is the person within this realm? The Master said, "The staff supports heaven and earth."
When the sun and moon shine upon people, it is said that the human realm has already received the Master’s instruction.
Today, as you ascend the seat, what is the matter? The Master said: "One blow, one scar. He then continued: "The ancient monastery is reopened, its colors even more refined;

taking up the white staff, he strikes the blue sky. Today he holds it up for all of you to see: the boat is shattered, yet the moon’s reflection by the stream remains full. O Great Assembly, do you still...?
"Do you understand thoroughly? After a long silence, he struck the meditation seat with his whisk and said: "Drooping willow trees bury the mountain temple;
vast desolate mounds become watered fields. (Fayin Hengji, the successor.)
Chan Master Cheweng Zhao of Huangbo in Jiangxi was a native of Nanchang. On New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall and said:
"Events from several decades past have been cast away into the vast void; today I pick them up once more, and the great road to Chang’an is open.
If you wish to ask about the meaning of the Westward Journey, the sun in the east is already bright red. (Fayin Heng was his successor.)
Chan Master Luan Yuan of Tiantai Huguo was a native of Jiangdu and the son of the Xu family. At the conclusion of the retreat, he gave this small assembly instruction:

"For ninety days we have restricted our feet, and for three months we have dwelt in quietude. We have held fast at the secure barrier, allowing not even a hair’s breadth of deviation, teaching that there is no door for advancing or retreating and no place to hide one's body.
Yet, unable to help it, I must now open a single thread so that everyone may attain a state of total, elegant freedom."
Each and every one has brows arched and a nose straight. Like a dragon finding water, like a tiger relying on a mountain; they move with sovereign ease, wielding life and death with freedom.
Reaching this point, it is acceptable to act thus, and it is also acceptable not to act thus. When the hollow-trunked tree returns to the void, it is unacceptable to act thus at all.
Everywhere one meets Li Babo. Looking left and right, he said: "Return home."
"All these are matters of descendants; the patriarchs have never gone out the door" (Fayin Heng succeeded him).
There was a lay practitioner named Zhu Fengtai of Jingjiang, Changzhou, whose courtesy name was Shenren. He was a jinshi degree holder of the Dinghai year.

Having once traveled with veteran monks and set his mind upon the Great Way, he viewed worldly splendor as being no different from straw dogs. He subsequently went to Longshan under Master Gu to receive the tonsure and become a monk.
