He shook his hand and said, "The Westward Transmission has no fixed intent. [The monk] asked, "What about shaking the hand? The Master struck him (Dayong Zhi succeeded him).
Chan Master Fahai Binya Jian of Xichuan ascended the hall and said: "In the depths of spring, things flourish; the sun is warm and the breeze is harmonious. Swallows rejoice and orioles sing;
the times are clear and the Way is prosperous. Prajñā flows freely, and the Dharma is fundamentally without concealment. He struck the meditation seat and said, "Sound!"

"It is not sound; it is but a vain laboring of the ears. Form is not form; it is difficult to examine and distinguish. Again, he struck the ground with his staff and said: "To weep until the blood flows is of no use;
it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. At the conclusion of the retreat, the Master ascended the hall and held up his staff, saying:
"One does not do half-measures; once begun, one does not stop. A single arrow shot from the distant heavens—turning back the clouds, if you can understand it..."
Some will have a boundless future; others will return home to sit in peace. Among these, there are certain points of confusion, yet I shall never reveal them to others.
Tell me, assembly, where does this confusion lie? He strikes the meditation staff and says: "A mistake! A mistake!"
The auspicious qilin has but one horn. [A questioner] asks: The *Four-Part Vinaya* states that striking a bhikṣu with the hand is a *pāyattika* offense.

For what reason did Deshan strike everyone he encountered? The Master said: "He was training his courage by waiting for a bird to settle, so as to startle it. [The questioner] says: The *Vinaya* states that reviling or scolding an administrator is a *pāyattika* offense.
For what reason did Linji let out a shout the moment he entered the gate? The Master said: [He was] testing the strength of the bowstring before shooting at the tigers.
He said, "A misted leopard, its fur glossy, never stoops to feed. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then a jade tower appears upon a single blade of grass;
a colorful phoenix flies from within a hundred-fold smelting furnace. The Master then struck him. Ascending the hall, he said:

"The lake and sky are calm, a deep azure like lapis lazuli. Eyes protrude; nostrils hang down. Ox-head and He-lan agree to meet for a forehead-to-forehead clash. In the Sangha Hall and the kitchen..."
The treasury laughs in joyful defiance; only the Jewel Stupa at Dangyang, with its Sun-Face and Moon-Face Buddhas, sits majestically atop the highest pass.
A clever fellow says: "I am merely deceiving the ignorant villagers; it is precisely now that one should investigate crosswise and investigate vertically.
I ask the assembly: within these seven days, how many pairs of straw sandals have you worn out? On the Day the Buddha Attained Enlightenment.
Ascending the hall, he asked: "‘This very mind is Buddha’ is too much; ‘neither mind nor Buddha’ is too little.
Setting aside both extremes, I ask you, Master, to speak quickly. The Master said: "A thousand-year field has had eight hundred owners. He then continued:
"The old frozen fellow before Mount Zhengjue spreads a net across the heavens to catch the wind. He deceives countless heroic spirits, who mistakenly identify the mottled leopard."
"Acting as a tiger. Descend from the seat. Entering the hall: To awaken to the Way upon hearing a sound is like digging through the earth to find the sky;

to clarify the mind upon seeing form is like brandishing a staff to strike at the moon. Even if one were to hit the mark a hundred times in a hundred shots, releasing both ends and gathering both ends simultaneously, it would still have no connection whatsoever with the realm of birth and death.
Holding up his staff, he said: "I now guarantee for you that this matter shall never be in vain. *Po*.
This student of Sanskrit laughs the Vajra Deity to a standstill. He hurls down his staff and descends from the seat.
Layman Liu has requested the formal address after shaving his head. Today is the first day of the fourth month; beyond the clouds, the mountains are green and the waters are azure.

To act according to capacity and accord with one's nature is well, yet a flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech. Fear of impermanence is like the light frost; this body and world are as precarious as a fire in an emergency. Do not—
Having reached the profound source of one's own nature, how could birth and death be resisted? If there is resistance, let go of all conditions and cease all seeking.
One day, the alms bowl becomes wet twice. A verse on Prince Nanda’s dismemberment: "Return the bones to the father, return the flesh to the mother;
then manifest your true body to preach the Dharma for your parents. The remaining clouds have vanished, and the mountain light shines forth.
Silence. The autumn moon hangs over the void; the universe is new. After the snow, the cold pines deepen their late-day verdancy. A single cry from a monkey on the green cliffs, call after call.
In praise of the "Cypress Tree Before the Hall": The scholar’s talent is lofty, his art surpasses that of men.

The sharpness of his rhetoric and the power of his brushwork are wondrously divine. He has created a fine landscape of mountains and waters; every stroke and dot is so distinct it seems almost unreal. In praise.
Huangbo’s “Eating Rice Dregs” Verse says: “In the Great Tang Empire there are no Chan masters; Green waters and blue mountains—cease further doubting.
The bamboo staff has transformed into a dragon and departed; The simpleton still has eyes as heavy with sleep. A Verse on Baizhang and the Wild Fox:
“The pearl rolls on the platter, the platter rolls the pearl; Within the Master’s gate, peach amulets are sold. The wild fox leaps in...”
The Golden-Haired Troop. Five hundred lifetimes ago he was not a man of integrity (Yun’uo Xisi).
Chan Master Hanxiu Qian of Fengxue in Ruizhou was the son of the Hu family of Long’an in western Shu. At nineteen, he left the white [robe] for the saffron.

At twenty, he received full ordination and traveled extensively throughout various regions, gaining insights at each location. Later, he went to Shaolin to pay homage to the Patriarch and passed through Fengxue. There he visited Yunge Xi;

their karmic conditions were in accord, and Yunge bestowed upon him a prediction of enlightenment. He subsequently established the Dharma at Xingfu in Jingyang and Xingshan in Chang’an, and later succeeded to the seat of Fengxue.
Ascending the hall, he said: "For twenty autumns I have waded through the weeds and observed the wind; my entire capacity has not..."
With spontaneous faith and ease, he effortlessly ascends the Flower King Throne. Shattering the three primal elements, he connects with the highest stream.

Once the Patriarchal Vehicle is proclaimed, the Three Baskets lose their power to define it. The Ultimate Way is vast and expansive; the ten paths converge on a single track. All currents are cut off;

throughout every dust mote and world-system, all is spontaneously and perfectly encompassed. He wondrously turns the primordial pivot, subsuming both existence and non-existence as he points and bestows his instructions. His radiance transcends...
The sun and moon: wisdom emerges from both the holy and the ordinary; in movement and stillness there is no partiality, and in concealment or manifestation there is no obscurity.

The skull-fragments constantly interact with the world, and the nostrils touch upon the family tradition. Dense and subtle, peaceful and serene, he provisionally opened the five ranks of Dongshan; the dark mechanism is perfectly integrated.
It surpasses the "Three Lives" of Miu and Yang, its single-character barrier exceeds the antiquity of Yunmen, and its doctrine of the six aspects captures the spontaneous realization of Fayan.
It seizes both the environment and the person with directness and vigor; it establishes guest and host as the great function turns like a celestial wheel.

The seal on water, the seal on mud, the seal on space—these are difficult to discern unless one is a master. It is neither mind, nor Buddha, nor a thing; it is known only through thorough realization.
Like the earth universally supporting all, like the sky universally covering all, the true mechanism is revealed and the myriad dharmas are fully manifest.
At such a time, tell me: how would you express the single phrase for the opening of the hall and the offering of longevity to the Emperor? *Geyang the song of the people pounding the earth.*
They forgot the power of the Emperor, as they continued their poetic hymns to celebrate the harmony of the times (Yun’e Xi succeeded them).
Caolun Ruyi (Tàoyuán Rùilín) and Gūyuè Lǎng Chánshī were both sons of the Yang family of Hézhōu.

Having traveled extensively through all quarters, [Gūyuè Lǎng] attained thorough penetration under the guidance of Ruò’ān Wèn and sought certification from Dàngshān Yuǎn. While residing at Caolun Ruyi, he ascended the hall and said: “I wear only straw sandals and do not...”

Using a boat, the matter beneath one's heels becomes increasingly submerged and floating. Now, drinking when thirsty and eating when hungry, it remains uncertain whether the bridge-flow is the flow of water.
Small Assembly (Small Sermon). [The Master] suddenly held up his whisk and said: "This is the foremost point of the upward path;
those who have not yet realized it have no place to rest. He continued: "I entrust this matter to you: chew it slowly, and its flavor will be like that of *ge-ju* (yellow myrobalan). Let it go."
[He brandishes] the whisk and strikes his knee once (Dangshan Yuan’s lineage).
On the occasion of the commencement of the retreat, Chan Master Fú of Jīnsù Huítáng in Xīncǎi ascends the hall: "The root source is direct; how could it fall into stages?
When the great function is fully wielded, no rules or regulations remain. The entire earth is this meditation hall; what distinction can there be between inner and outer?"
The entirety of the ten directions is universally a furnace; right now, all things are melted away. In every place, phenomena are themselves reality.

Throughout the twelve hours of the day, light shines upon heaven and reflects upon earth. Striking the meditation seat with his whisk, he said: "If you can realize it in this way, why seek it elsewhere?
If you have not yet attained this, rouse your spirit and do not slumber; do not let your two eyebrows be scorched away."
Ascending the hall upon the conclusion of the retreat: Breaking through the barrier of deluded emotions, there is nothing at all to obscure or cover.
The True Person of No-Station emerges, attaining great mastery in moving freely in all directions. But tell me: how do you express the single phrase of "transcending the quarters and walking alone"?

"Idle clouds are not struck [by the wind], they unfold as they please; wild cranes are unrestrained, coming and going as they will. Ascending the hall: Everyone says that delusion is caused by awakening.
To dispel [delusion]. Not knowing that awakening is the very root of delusion—though one might forget both delusion and awakening, one still cannot avoid being halfway along the path.
Furthermore, what is the phrase for arriving home? One must advance further on the tip of the pole; let go of the hand without hesitation. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The spring day is bright and mild, the spring birds sing. The spring mountains are layered upon one another, and the waters are overflowing. It is clear."
To leak away the truth of the celestial source—what need is there to seek it elsewhere or look outward? Ascending the hall, he said: The spring mountains are green, the spring waters are lush.
A single awakening has just occurred; the dream is finally complete. Carrying my staff, I follow my companions out through the pine gate;
everywhere, the fragrance of peach blossoms half-pervades the air. This brings to mind the words of Lingyun of old: "For thirty years I sought it nowhere. Now, everyone vies to love it.

Plucking Willow Flowers: The red fragrance has not yet bloomed; spring is still early. Fortunately, we meet an old man from Shangshui, Who seeks the ultimate treasure at Nantang to inquire about the Dharma.
I, this mountain monk, do not begrudge my two eyebrows; Each and every one must be clearly preserved by yourself. Do not casually treat this as a mere observation of words and letters;
Gain and loss, existence and non-existence—sweep them all away at once. [The Master] raised the case of the National Teacher who called his attendant three times.
The verse says: "You owe me, and I owe you; straight as a hook, yet curved as a string. The waters of the thousand rivers rush eastward;
the peaks of the Five Marchmounts are so high they do not touch heaven. This refers to the story of Zhaozhou visiting two hermits. The verse says:
One storm, one clear sky; the spring breeze disturbs the traveler on his way.
Not knowing where his native land may be, he still hears two or three cries of a singing bird. (Yun’uo rejoices in his succession.)

Master Zhen of Longshu’s *Qingyuan Bingjian* offers these verses on Baizhang’s “Wild Fox”: For five hundred lifetimes he has fallen as a wild fox; He knows not where there is such partiality and decay.
When responding to the immediate situation, a pearl is cast into water; Purity and turbidity are both forgotten, and the moon’s reflection stands alone.
He offers these verses on Huanglong’s Three Barriers: “What is my hand like the Buddha’s hand?”—in its application, there is no division.
Beautiful or ugly—strike once and shatter the great void; startled, Mount Sumeru runs backward. "How is my foot like a donkey's foot?
Zhaozhou did not recognize the humble ladle; with a light kick, he topples the pure cauldron, leaving it free to fill the ditches and block the ravines.
Every person has their own karmic affinity; whose hearth has no smoke? Having a mouth is enough for eating rice—who cares about becoming a Buddha?
At the Chengxian Temple (Lushan), on the occasion of the Dharma Hall discourse by Chan Master Jingyun Rui of Taicheng in Siming:
"The yellow oriole sings among the green trees; the white egret plucks grain in the Qingtian marshes.
The intent of the patriarchs of all time is not obscured by the conditions of seeing and hearing. Outside the gate, falling clouds drift slowly; from the roots of the rocks, a stream flows."
The water splashes and flows. Aside from this, there is no other essential point. Where else could there be the Three Mysteries? (He lets out a shout. Entering the hall:
Those who climb a mountain to observe the flooding waters must know the ruggedness of the peaks and the flow of the streams.

Those who enter a forest to play among the tall bamboos must know the density of the grove and the crisscrossing of the stalks. Furthermore, when members of the monastic community have finished eating their present meal...
The tea and rice are prepared; doing nothing is the task. Furthermore, what do you know? Three catties of salt exchange for five sheng of beans;
a bundle of incense costs ten coins. Entering the hall: To speak of this or that is not as good as not speaking at all.
To act in reverse or in accordance with the flow is not as good as not acting at all. Why is this? Because the feet of one who does not act are firm and stable; they have already arrived.
The field of peace and bliss. Without speaking of it, one’s verbal karma is pure, and one attains entry into the Samādhi of Non-contention.

Even if there were such a person, this mountain monk would call him here, rub his head, and bestow upon him a prophecy of enlightenment. Entering the hall, the mountain monk says: "I am too lazy to speak of the fundamental principle."
It grew dark until the sun turned crimson. If someone came to ask about the Dharma, he would plug his ears so they went deaf.
Why was this? Listen! It was simply because he detested being disturbed from his sleep. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A clay statue is not yet finished.
The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "Beyond the reach of words. The monk asked, "What is the Sangha? The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, am not [the Sangha]."
Xie Sanlang asked, "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "He put on his boots and entered the marketplace.
Xie asked, "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "He returned home barefoot. (Yinshan was his predecessor.)
Chan Master Jiànqī Juàn of Dányuán in Jízhōu ascended the hall. A monk came forward, drew a circle (○), and stood with his hands folded.

The Master said, “A talisman drawn in the dark cannot reach its mark. The monk replied, “It is difficult to deceive one who knows. The Master said, “Did you not see the assembly biting their mother’s fingers?
The monk asked, “Who understands this meaning? It makes me remember Fényáng. The Master said, “I only fear it is not so.”
"This is jade. This jade is truly marvelous. The monk prostrated. The Master then brandished his whisk and said: "The bright casts itself into the dark; Ding meets with Yi and Zhuo.
Essence and function are fully encompassed; past and present are no different.

Even if one were a man who exhausts the world’s pivotal mechanisms, who cleaves the barriers and seizes the banners—upon reaching this point, set him aside for a moment. He then drew these symbols with his whisk: [○@(囗@智)] [○@尾] [○@女].
The Master said: "For a thousand or ten thousand years now, the ninety-six kinds of heterodox paths and the eight-armed Nārāyaṇa have been unable to lift it up;
the Thousand-Eyed Great Compassionate One has been unable to peer through it. Stale rice-cakes and moldy pastries—each of these was treated as primary.

Now, at Danyuan’s gate, the old regulations are being re-established and new practices instituted, such that Deshan must fold his hands and Linji swallow his voice; all the old monks throughout the world must step back."
There was a pause. "Is there no one in this assembly who resembles Yangshan? Come forth and meet this mountain monk! He then made this gesture and said, "Look! Look!
If you can understand this, you will not fail to see Danyuan face-to-face today. He threw down his whisk and descended from the seat.
Winter Solstice Small Lecture: "A drop of water, a drop of ice; The horns of a hare and the hair of a tortoise form a great function."

The ox-head sinks and the horse-head turns back; Annam is blocked and the northern roads are steep and lofty. Drinking the official wine and lying upon the official bed, who cares that the capital produces *dàhuáng* (rhubarb)?
As the yin gradually wanes and the yang gradually grows, those with iron brows and copper heads have no skill at all.
Is there anyone among the multitude who can act as the lord of the myriad phenomena, not withering along with the four seasons? Striking the staff, he said: "Look downward."
Long Text: New Year’s Day, Ascending the Dharma Seat. He mounts a three-legged donkey and beats the Dharma drum of the ninefold heavens;
he releases a hairless hawk and raises the spring breeze of the eight directions. In every instance, he manifests his presence, revealing the golden-yellow within the jar;

in every object, he fully displays himself, opening wide the duck-green within the cage. The Three Bodies and Four Wisdoms each present the natural splendor of their own ground; the Five Eyes and Six...
"Penetrating. Together they manifest the wondrous function of True Suchness. O worthy ones, do you understand? The sea is vast and the waves are calm, so the dragon sleeps soundly;
the sky is clear and the clouds are still, so the crane flies high. (Wu-ai Che’s Succession)
Chan Master Yun’ai Zong of Lian’an presented this to the assembly. Having finished citing the story of Deshan’s bowl-carrying, the Master said:
"Regarding this koan, everyone everywhere says it is an 'iron threshold. From the time of the great patriarchs of old until now, no one has been able to provide a definitive critique.
Tell me, where does the crux lie? After a long silence, he said: "Heh! Heh! Heh! [He then drew a circle, a triangle, and a dot.]
Three at the beginning, eleven; nine in the middle, seven at the end. The verse on Master Guishan’s “Having a phrase” and “Lacking a phrase” says:
“Pairs of mandarin ducks roost amidst the reeds; The waters are shallow, the mountains high, and cloud-shadows veil them. At midnight, a black wind blows, yet they remain unmoved;
As dawn breaks, the clear mists disperse. The verse on “All Dharmas Return to One” says: “The sky is full of wind, the colors white upon the marsh of *ping-chen* flowers. [It] cuts off...”
He cuts off the long flow of the Yangtze River so that it runs backward; he directly causes empty space to shatter into dust.
Meeting him is both laughable and sorrowful (the successor of Lufeng).
Chan Master Xue of Yunfeng, a *lohan* at Yanshan in Wenzhou, was a native of Muzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The very mind is Buddha."
Do not discuss it in vain. When the plum ripens, its fragrance is everywhere. I entrust the True Dharma Eye to humans and devas;
who knows who will take up this burden and carry it forth? Is there anyone here who can take it up? He picks up his staff and says:
"One only knows that opening one's mouth is easy; one does not realize how long the tongue is. Question: I do not ask about the supreme patriarchal style; what is one’s original face?
The Master said: "Seven holes and eight openings" (attributed to Huiri Shengsi).
Chan Master Shiye Shizhuo of Quzhou was surnamed Mao of Yiwu. While still a layman, he studied under Jue of Shuanglin, who instructed him to contemplate the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature.
Upon receiving a single shout, he intuitively grasped its essential meaning and immediately presented his realization.
The verse says: Hearing the Master’s single shout, the mountains crumble and the oceans dry up; the dragon of the azure pool is startled awake and brings forth the full moon.
Jiufu said: "It is so, yet it is not yet so. Later, he went to visit Huirui Sheng. Sheng asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Shuanglin.
Sheng asked, "Is there a Great Being (Mahāsattva) there? The Master said, "Yes. Sheng said, "When you came..."
"What did I say to you? The Master stepped forward and said, "I respectfully wish the Abbot ten thousand blessings. Hui-sheng said, "This is but a servant;
what is the master? The Master then departed. (Hui-rìshèng was his successor.)
Chan Master Xian of Yutai Haishi Wild Pass ascended the hall at Chizhou. "The peak of Yutai is high; even flying birds find it difficult to cross.
The forest of lions is deep; there is no room for strange beasts. Each must have a way to emerge. He called out to the assembly in a loud voice, "Is there anyone? Is there anyone?
After a long silence, he cast down his staff and said, "I, this mountain monk, can only go forth with hands cast loose."
Addressing the assembly: White clouds are naturally unique; flowing water is naturally deep. To illuminate and shatter shadows and echoes, one must first eliminate them.
This particular splendor fills the ears and overflows the eyes. Nevertheless, the eighty thousand modes of dignified conduct and the hundred thousand samādhis can only cure oneself;
they cannot benefit others. Now tell me, what is the phrase for benefiting others? He calls to the assembly and says: "Mount Sumeru stands straight."
Polishing the heights, transcending past and present; breaking off blades of grass to measure the heavens—this is a labor spent in vain (the words of Yufeng Shishu).
Stone Creek Chonghua Huideng Chan Master ascended the hall and, raising his whisk, said: "Does the assembly see?
The World-Honored One beheld the morning star before the Mountain of Perfect Enlightenment; Lingyun saw peach blossoms upon the spring breezes of the road. At this—

This can be seen. The Way is not outside of things. After a long silence, he threw down his whisk and said, "Let it be verified as you will. Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind of nirvana is easy to understand;
the wisdom of differentiation is difficult to clarify. If one realizes this wisdom of differentiation, the entire wild expanse is pure gold."
Holding up his staff, he said: "If you call this a 'staff,' I will give you one blow; if you do not call it a 'staff,' I will also give you one blow.
Why? For much emptiness is not as good as a little reality. (Liaowu Neng succeeded him.)
Master Chonghua Fozhou Long ascended the hall for the discourse. "The primary truth (paramārtha-satya) is majestic and eminent;
all phenomena are fully manifest. Sentient and insentient beings alike reveal it at every turn. Holding up his whisk, he said, "Do you see?
Everyone has eyes with pupils; they must surely see. Striking the whisk, he said, "Do you hear? Every person has ears with openings; they must surely..."
This is what is heard. Without waiting for the whisk to be raised or the mallet to be struck, one has already mounted the sound and covered the form (the realization that enables succession).
Master Hongchan of Guangde Jianping Fagu Chuncheng addressed the assembly, citing the story of Linji’s two hall heads simultaneously shouting.
The Master said: "The two head monks each displayed their vast capacities, yet Linji held them fast at the gateway."
Although he was a master of this particular school, how could he avoid being scrutinized and exposed by the assembly? Why is this? Have you not heard it said:
"When the *zhèn* bird descends upon the field, the fish and turtles die; wherever the venomous dragon passes, the grass withers" (Liaowu Nengsi).
Small Assembly Talk by Master Can Hao of Taini, Kuaiji. Outside the railing, the wutong leaves fall frequently; The golden wind reveals its essence, testing the person of now.
A single song of vast resonance fills the autumn light’s stillness; Laughing, I behold the fresh countenance of the chrysanthemums.
(He lets out a shout. The Master asks a newly arrived monk: "Where have you come from? The monk says: "Xiansheng. The Master says: "How far is it from here?"
"How far? He replied, "Ten *li*. The Master asked, "Who was ahead of you when you came? He replied, "I set out after my meal.
The Master said, "It is no mistake that you have come to Xiansheng" (Wu'ai Che was his successor).

Master Quanshiyin of Hengyang held a small assembly for instruction: "The place where it cannot be seen is the marrow of the thousand sages; the place where one cannot reach is the source of the ten thousand spirits.
For the clear-eyed monk, the point of value lies in being ahead of the pivot. If you can grasp this, you will know that there is no back and no front;
even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot fathom its origins, so how could demons or heretics possibly recognize it? Heaven and earth grow and nourish all things by means of this."
All things arise and flourish by means of this. I venture to ask the great assembly: when Xuefeng rolls the ball and Heyan beats the drum, tell me, what matter of realization do they clarify?
[He strikes the whisk and says: "Look beneath your feet" (Mu-pu Yao-si).
Chan Master Hanmulin, a son of the Gu family of Wuchang, gave this informal discourse: "Year after year, the old is exhausted this very night;

When Yu Daozhe was a youth at Lake Shang, Ma Mingxi was a scholar of the district. Orphaned at an early age, his character was broad and unconstrained; he delighted in following his own inclinations.

He had read the *Shi* and *Shu*, and whenever he encountered difficult passages, he would take pleasure in reading them repeatedly. When dealing with worldly affairs, he would only engage in those that he deemed truly beneficial.

Upon seeing others prostrating before Buddhist images or reciting sutras and penitential rites, he would smile and dismiss them as mere "wood and earth" formulas, wondering what purpose such practices could serve.

While living in his hometown, he practiced archery and hunting; he caught fish and shot wild ducks without regard for their lives. Subsequently, fleeing the chaos, he settled at Chazapu, where the fields were peaceful and still.
At the request of Yongquan of Tiantai, he traveled by way of the seashore and stayed at Baziyuan.

It was from this that he acquired the title "King of Ghosts" (*Guishiwang*). Subsequently, he resided at Baozhudong Cave on Mount Xishan.

Xīshān Guǎngquán was originally a member of the Fēng family of Wújiāng; he became a monk at an early age. As a student (*zhūshēng*), he possessed a bold and chivalrous character.

their spiritual affinities were mutually harmonious, and he immediately received the transmission of the Dharma.

In the autumn of the Jiachen year of the Kangxi era, he heard that the heterodox practitioner Zhao Yuanzhen of Baiyun Mountain was wearing monastic robes and spreading delusory teachings, greatly confusing the masses. Fearing that this would bring harm to the orthodox teaching, the Master resolved to rectify the situation.
Jiù traveled directly to Yúguān and, together with the monk Wùzōng, entered the mountains to exhort Zhēn regarding the True Dharma. Zhēn would not comply.

Upon returning to the capital, Jiù composed a treatise titled *Zhàoyāo zhílùn* (A Direct Discourse on Exposing Demons) and presented it to him. Zhēn became enraged and sought to falsely accuse the Master. Having no other choice, the Master informed the authorities.
At that time, the Grand Minister of State submitted a memorial to the throne, which received an imperial decree stating that "Zhào Yuánzhēn uses heterodox teachings to delude the people."

The thirty-sixth generation descendant of Nanyue, Chan Master Xuan Yinsong of Daci Monastery in Hangzhou, was originally a Confucian by profession.
Not yet having clarified the fundamental principles regarding birth and death, he abandoned his family life to become a monk.
He traveled extensively to visit various masters before finally attending upon Master Li of Boshan, where he remained for three years; his conduct and practice were consistently pure and singular.

Whenever he saw those who were poor and destitute, he would invariably give away his own food and clothing to them. Upon seeing those suffering from illness, he would personally attend to their needs.

He often practiced secret conduct, and because his principles were profound, [the Master] held him in high esteem. He would frequently say to the Master: "One who leaves the household life to study the Way must clarify one's own mind.

If one's own mind is not clarified, it will ultimately not be a sharp instrument. Even if you practice for as many kalpas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, you will still be unable to escape the Lord of Death."

The Source of the Dharma is not so; its dwellings are both houses and trees, and its robes are both cassocks and straw raincoats.

Accepting whatever comes by way of one’s lot, each and every person must find peace and joy in their heart. Beating a broken drum at irregular intervals, they sing folk songs from the depths of their hearts. Transverse...
He leaned on his staff and said: "Luo luo li li luo luo. The cause from this day last year; the fruit of this day from last year.
Cause and effect are most distinct; suddenly they become a jeweled place. Though the hall is narrow, the hearts of the assembly are vast. Ten thousand fingers surround the lion throne.
Filling the courtyard, people come bustling from afar—all are those who passed through the single assembly at Vulture Peak. From this point on..."
The source of the Dharma is a new Brahma-abode; it shall serve as a model for a thousand ages to come (by Su Hongli).
Chan Master Shenyun Bian of Yufeng Peak was a native of Suzhou. He left the household life at the age of seven and was filial by nature.
He received the full precepts from Vinaya Master Samadhi and sought instruction on the essentials of Chan under Jingxi. Subsequently, he studied under Su Hongli at Baisan. One...
One day, Ri asked Li, saying, "I have been practicing Chan meditation, but I feel it has become tasteless. It would be better for me to return to studying the Vinaya.
Li said, "If you understand how to practice Chan, you understand how to study the Vinaya; if you comprehend how to study the Vinaya, you comprehend how to practice Chan.

To fully clarify the nature of the mind is the precepts; to thoroughly awaken to the fundamental mind is Chan. Though their names are two, their principle returns to one. People of the present day... [The text ends here.]

The heavens are bright by day. There are many who run along, leaning on fences and feeling their way against walls. This is because they turn their backs on awakening to merge with the dust of the senses, losing themselves in the true to pursue the delusive.
Some do not awaken until the end of their lives; some turn back halfway; some rely on teachers and friends for indirect guidance; others attain understanding upon encountering specific circumstances.
It is like meeting a bright lamp in a dark room, or like a traveler returning to his native home. Such people are merely called...

The first stage is also called the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*). At this point, one must further dissolve one's own present karma and beginningless habitual tendencies, proceeding directly beyond the limit of Venerable Sound (*Vipaśyin*).

At such a time, upholding the precepts is permissible; investigating Zen is permissible; expounding the teachings is permissible; reciting the Buddha’s name is permissible; reviling the Buddhas and cursing the patriarchs is permissible;
and chanting with the wind and playing with the moon are also permissible. All of these are the wondrous functioning of spiritual powers (*ṛddhi-prabhāva*).
In its manifestation, it does not obstruct the three thousand ritual observances; in its concealment, it allows for not a single hair’s breadth of establishment.
One is the infinite, and the infinite is one. Is this not absolute freedom? If you can cast yourself into practice, [you will realize it].

From morning until evening, and from dusk until dawn, he investigated the *huatou* with intense focus. Suddenly, his eyes opened behind his head, and he exclaimed, "I have the right to scold this mountain monk!
Thereupon, for five years, the Master did not loosen his sash nor unfold his mat while sleeping.
One day, hearing the sound of a tiger, he felt the earth tremble; his body and mind became suddenly expansive and clear, like empty space. He went to see Master Li, who...

He consented. One day, he took his leave and requested that his draft manuscripts be recorded and published. Once the carving was completed, he returned and served in the quarters of the Abbot, remaining there until the end of his life (Su Hongli was his successor).
Chan Master Hui Zhang Wenyuji of Hangzhou went to study under Bashi Li. One day, while ascending the latrine, Li saw him and said, "Why do you defecate upon this ground of purity?
The Master replied, "What about the dry dung-stick? Li said, "You have misunderstood quite a bit. The Master asked, "How about you, Preceptor?
Just as Li opened his mouth, the Master said, "You have misunderstood quite a bit. Li then desisted. The Master... [left the hall].
Having served him for several years, I have deeply grasped his essential meaning. Now, as I ascend the hall at Mount Wu, I say: This mountain monk does not understand Chan;

from the start, I have practiced among the heterodox species. I came specifically to visit those of like mind, yet was forcibly seized and placed upon this seat. Thus, I have entered the ranks of the water buffalo.
The plow and rake divide the difficult words; ugly postures cannot be concealed. Fortunately, the nostrils are upright. After a long while, he said: "HŪṂ! To the assembly:
Clouds atop Mount Chao and waters at Tangqi—eyebrows and eyes distinct, a non-dual body. A-he-he! You should understand for yourself:
within the tip of a single hair of all the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, everything is presented face-to-face before the wind. Do you who are present here understand?"
"Not yet. If you do not understand, I shall speak for myself. [The Master] drew his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "A needle from Jiangyou and thread from Hangzhou; northern horses and southern boats—directly, they are infinite.

He made a stroke with his *ruyi* (magic wand) and asked, "Do you understand? After a long silence, he said: "If one is not a true connoisseur, it is in vain to shoot the arrow that pierces the willow leaves. (Suhongli was his successor.)
Master Zhèn of Shàndǒu Hǒushān in Wēnzhōu cited the case of Yūnhú Yòng and Xuěqiáo Xìn while they were gazing at the moon together.
Xìn pointed to the moon and said, "Where has that half gone? Yòng remained silent for a long while and then asked, "Do you understand? Xìn replied:
Yexian said, "I have only obtained half of it. Yun said, "Where has that other half gone? Xian remained silent for a long while. Yun said, "I too have only obtained half.
They both laughed heartily. He then offered this verse: The moon on Mount Emei, half its orb in autumn, Its reflection enters the level river, soaking in, never flowing away.
Tonight let the strings and pipes cease their rhythmic joining; For fear that such romantic sentiment might stir the sorrows of the Jade Pass.
(Recorded by Mengtang Ni Si).

Chan Master Anhua Xiaotang Yu was a native of the Wang clan of Huining. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations, but upon reading the Buddhist scriptures, he conceived the aspiration to transcend the mundane world.
After both his parents passed away in succession, he received the tonsure under Canghai of Yushan and subsequently took formal ordination under Xuanhui Gaofeng.

He was fully equipped [with the necessary conditions]. He took up the koan on the "original face" and practiced for six years without gaining entry. One day, while casually reading the *Prajñāpāramitā*, he reached the passage:

"If one sees me by means of form... and his doubts were suddenly resolved. He studied under Dajue Xiu and met Mingjue Cong at Wanshan Dian, who appointed him as a scribe; there were many such karmic opportunities.
Finally, he called upon Anhua Ze, who held up his staff and said: "Suck it all in with a single gulp."
"Let us set aside the Western River for a moment; try swallowing this staff and see. The Master said, "I am no wild fox spirit.
Baizhang said, "What do you usually eat? The Master said, "A yakṣa’s head and a bodhisattva’s face.

Baizhang said, "Fabricated Chan monk! The Master let out a thunderous shout and gave a *he*. Baizhang said, "The lion’s roar; the jackal’s howl. The Master said, "I still want the Master [to say more]."
As he hesitated and remained attached to his doubt, [the Master] struck him, saying, "Do you know where it fell? When the Master prepared to open his mouth, [the Master] struck him again.

The Master prostrated himself and said, "Had I not personally met the Master, I would have been deceived by those from all quarters. [The Master] approved of this and appointed him to oversee the affairs of the monastery.
Having attended him for five years, his subtle purport became increasingly clear. He was granted a verse of transmission and the seal of succession, and subsequently took the seat at Anhua.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The two gifts—the gift of wealth and the gift of Dharma—are equal and without distinction. The eyes are above, while the eyebrows span across; the tongue is hidden within the mouth. A nun is certainly a woman;
a scale-weight is ultimately made of cast iron. Since it is this clear, what need is there for further words? He then looked at the assembly and said, "To turn..."
Since ancient times, this has been like using an awl to look through a hole or a wedge to drive home a point. On this New Year’s Day, ascending the hall: in the north, wind and frost freeze solid;
in the south, plum and willow vie for spring. In both celestial timing and human affairs, all is peaceful and prosperous.
To realize this is the wondrous essence; why need one establish host and guest? If you further hesitate or engage in discursive thought, it is like facing an iron wall.
He gave a shout and said: "The incense burner burns purple cypress wood as it sings of Yao’s virtue; the court robes of the four seas offer prayers for the Sage’s benevolence.
Addressing the assembly, he held up his whisk and said: "The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet it is difficult to behold even when one stands before it.
If you wish to clarify the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, voice, or language. When the ancients spoke thus, how many people have they brought into trouble?"
To make conjectures amidst sounds and forms is to miss the point. Here in Anhua, when hungry one eats; when weary, one sleeps.
What need is there for so many complications? Brothers, if you can understand it in this way, you may take it that your study of the Way is complete.
Is there anyone else? After a long silence, he struck the whisk and said: "Once the snow has melted, spring will naturally arrive. (Shigao was his successor.)
The Chan Master Jiyuan Jian of Beijing’s Jiaoyuan Temple traveled extensively to visit and consult various venerable elders. In his later years, he met Anhua Ze.
Ze held up a bamboo pointer and said, "Set aside whatever you have attained through study under other masters; tell me, what is this?
The Master replied, "Venerable Sir, do not needlessly create complications. Ze said, "It cannot be touched, nor can it be avoided. Ultimately, how is it?"
"Right away," [Touzi] said. The Master then gave a shout. Touzi said, "That one shout of yours may be acceptable in all other quarters, but here in my presence, I do not yet dare grant it.
As the Master prepared to open his mouth, Touzi struck him. When the Master again prepared to open his mouth, Touzi struck him once more.
The Master nodded his head several times. Touzi said, "On what principle do you see that you nod your head? The Master replied, "I see several learned masters..."
"Your consciousness is like walking through clouds and mist. Today, seeing the Master is like being beneath a clear blue sky and bright sun;
not even a single speck of dust can settle there. He said, "Do you have such a view? Then he struck him again. The Master suddenly attained enlightenment and prostrated himself.
[Zhi]ze nodded his head in approval (and thus succeeded to [Hui]ze).
Chan Master Jing of Hongfuyuan Temple in Beijing was the son of the Feng family of Suzhou. He received the tonsure under Hanshan Guang and received full ordination from Minzhong Bing.
He frequently attended lecture halls and visited Shigao at Anhua, where he was appointed to serve as the *karmadāna* (rector).

This concerns the saying, "Show me your original face. For two years, he had not attained liberation. One day, while wandering on West Mountain, he heard a guest say, "Boundless autumn colors are in the mountains and forests," and he had an awakening. Upon returning, he told Master Ze, who said, "So, you have touched your own nostrils today? The Master replied, "What about the original face? The Master then gave a shout. Ze said, "Without dreams, without thoughts—this is the host. The Master then said, "I grant you thirty blows! Ze then bowed. Later, when Master Ze was about to pass away, he called for the Master; the Master went to him. Ze said, "The Dharma-gate of our school is about to perish. The Master asked, "Why do you say this? "Where does the public person reside? The Master said, "At the top of the feet and at the bottom of the feet. [The questioner] asked, "How can this be seen? The Master said, "Why must you plant eyes upon the eyebrows?
[The questioner] then said, "I understand. Later, the Master bestowed upon him a verse, saying: "The essential doctrine of Che-xi is entrusted to you to circulate.
With a single staff, you shall enlighten humans and devas. (Shi Gao was his successor.)
Master Guang of Beihuilin in Tianjin was the son of the Zhang family of Wuxian.
He entered the monastic order under Master Ze of Anhua, who instructed him to investigate the koan of the "original face. One day, while a monk asked Master Murong, "What is the original face?
Murong replied, "How could a turtle ever run out of a jar? Standing nearby, Master Guang attained realization. He immediately went to the abbot’s quarters and approached Master Ze.
Question: "What is this so-called 'original face'? The Master said: "It cannot be traced; it cannot be painted. The questioner said:
"If that is so, what do you call the original face? The Master let out a thunderous shout. The questioner said:
"You may shout as much as you like, but give me back my original face! The Master said: "At this point, one has a mouth only fit for eating rice. The questioner said: "Three..."
"Ten blows! Wait for tomorrow. He then ordered the secretary to prepare the documents; after ten years of serving as his attendant, he finally received formal certification (*inka*).
He first resided at Fayun on Mount Xishan, then moved to Tianning, and later succeeded to the abbacy of Dabe. Ascending the hall, he gave a shout and said:
"Beyond the realm of Vipaśyin, and even further beyond—right up to the present day, there has been no change. His face and features are clearly manifest."
"This is the channel. Tell everyone to look at it closely. He then asked, "Tell me, who is it that looks? With his whisk, he drew a circle (○) and made a gesture of tossing it away, saying:
"Tossed before the Ancient Sovereign; tomorrow morning, calculate it again. On the day of the commencement of summer, he ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddhas cannot speak of it; the Patriarchs cannot lift it up. Do not touch it; if you touch it, disaster will arise. He then took up his whisk.
The Master drew a single line and said: "Sitting idly at the window of meaning, reading the *I Ching*, I did not know how much time had passed since spring left.
He ascended the hall and said: "Having seen through Zhaozhou’s 'No,' he shattered Yunmen’s 'Universal.

He picked up Shishuang’s staff, struck the drum of Heshan, tossed out Xuefeng’s ball, and seized Yantou’s oar. With a wave of his hand, he departed from Tianjin; even Bodhidharma could not [hold him back]."
This was his ancestral lineage (Shigao being the successor).
Jinghai Puduo Congshixu Chan Master was the son of the Wang family of his native district. In his youth, he practiced martial arts but took no pleasure in them;

he paid homage at Tiantong Monastery, donned the black robes of a monk, and was instructed to investigate the koan: "When one breath does not come back. Consequently, while pulling a stone rope, he tripped and fell.

He had a realization. He presented his understanding at the Gate (the Master’s presence), and the Gate esteemed it. Upon returning home, he visited Dabo Qian; later, he went to see Shigao at Yongquan, with whom he felt a profound resonance.
When Shigao moved to Beici, the Master served him tirelessly through labor for ten years, gradually deepening his grasp of the essential meaning.

During one period of entering the inner quarters, Shigao asked, "Yaoshan has not ascended the seat for a long time; what is the intent behind this? The Master replied, "A solitary moon in the autumn sky."
Lǎng. It is difficult to instruct those below the vast heavens. He said, "When I ascend the seat, the head temple administrator asks, 'And what then?

The Master says, 'A place of profound sorrow—who among you is a true knower? [The administrator] merely nods his head. Addressing the assembly: To open one's mouth is to form a pair of lines; to raise an eyebrow is to fall into two or three.
To point directly still involves partial attachment; to speak further is likewise not so. Since neither is correct, what ultimately is it?"
"How can you attain it immediately? Everyone, try to discern this for yourselves! If you do not understand, it is right beneath your own heels at all times—be careful not to miss it!
[He suddenly struck the meditation staff. "Put it down! [He struck it once more. "Put it down!"
"Unable to let go, take it up and carry it away. [The Master] addressed the assembly, held up his staff, and said: "What a fine message! I only fear that you do not recognize it face-to-face.
If you understand it in this way, your efforts will not have been in vain. If you do not understand, you should set aside body and mind and embrace a *hwadu*.
For the ninety-day period of *jin-zu* (the summer retreat), contemplate with the threefold urgency. Straighten your backbone like a snake boring through a wall. Suddenly—"
Having pierced through the earth, there are worlds like that on the other side. To roam at ease and act with sovereign freedom, wandering as one pleases—how joyful this is!
Is there anyone such? He planted his staff and said: "Holding someone's hand, you cannot make them walk."
"One must personally consent before one can become intimate [with the Way]" (as Shi Gao was the successor).
Chan Master Dan Yuanyuan of the Shifang Monastery in Jining was the son of the Zhang family of that same prefecture.

At the age of seven, he received the tonsure at Lianbai Temple and followed [Master] Tianning to receive the precepts. He was instructed to contemplate the phrase, "Where does it all return? He maintained this inquiry day and night, whether sitting or lying down.
Liuexie was performing a ritual when he entered the hall. The Master asked, "Where does the 'one' return? Liuexie replied, "The triangular fire-wheel roasts within the void.

The Master was so startled that sweat poured from his entire body, and his doubts were instantly dispelled. He immediately presented a verse, saying: "The myriad dharmas return to the One; Where does the One return?

As soon as the precious sword is grasped, Skulls fall strewn upon the ground. Liuexie’s realization was affirmed, and he was appointed to serve as the Secretary (Jishi). Thereafter, he went on to study with other masters.
Bao'en visited Lingyan. Later, he arrived at Mount Yi by the Si River. Upon hearing that Anhuai was there, he went immediately to pay his respects.

Their teacher-disciple relationship was deeply harmonious, and he was entrusted with the affairs of the monastery for several years. He thoroughly mastered the profound essence [of the teachings]. One day, [Anhuai] suddenly summoned him into the room and asked:
"What is the meaning of Xuefeng rolling the ball and Heshan beating the drum? Bao'en replied: "Beating the grass so as to startle the snake. Anhuai then raised his hand like a staff.

Zhe said, "Is it this very function? Is it apart from this function? The Master said, "The thief's identity has been revealed. Zhe said, "The Eye of the True Dharma—why was it extinguished by a blind donkey?
The Master said, "If you know the kindness, you must repay it. He then struck him with his *ruyi* (wish-fulfilling) staff. Zhe then prostrated.
The Master sealed this with a verse and sent him forth to dwell in the ten directions; later he moved to Beici (Shigao was his successor).
Chan Master Nanquan Xin of Shenjing was the son of the Gu family of Wuxi. He traveled to consult various renowned masters;

although he attained moments of awakening and insight, he ultimately remained unable to achieve total liberation. Once, he requested instruction from Anhua Ze, yet still did not understand. Ze repeatedly struck him with severe blows.
He then built a separate room and named it Wénxīng Gé (Hall of the Literary Star). Morning and evening he reproached himself with such intensity that he forgot to sleep or eat.
One night, hearing the sound of a bell, he felt the earth tremble violently; the sound filled the void. Looking back at his own body and mind, he realized there was nothing to be grasped.
When he went to see [Zhìzé], Zhìzé said, "I am glad that today you have caught the thief. The Master replied, "If it were not for the Venerable’s compassion..."

"Nearly in vain have you encountered this sagely age," [Shi Gao] said. "Now I know that I did not deceive you. The Master (Huike) performed three prostrations with great reverence, and [Shi Gao] nodded his head in approval.
(Shi Gao was succeeded by Sengshao.)
Chan Master Anhua Danru Xian of Beijing was the son of the Zhang family of Shanyin. He studied the *Qingxiang* (Green Box) texts and took delight in the language of the Chan school.
Upon arriving at Baixia, he entered the monastic order under Ruojian. He then went to Gulin to receive full ordination and attended upon Lingyin Li, who assigned him the koan of the "Original Face.

Although he applied himself diligently to this investigation, he did not achieve realization. Later, while staying as a guest by a window, he read the *Transmission of the Lamp* and recognized that the great tiger was originally...
Hutuo was suddenly relieved of his doubts and went to pay his respects to Lingyan Chu. Chu held up a bamboo whisk and asked, "What do you call this?
The Master replied, "Su Qing was originally a minister of the Han dynasty. Chu said, "When a single breath does not return, where will you find a foothold?"
The Master said: "Transverse the body beyond the three realms; who is the one who emerges? Shu Qizhi subsequently visited Shi Gao at Anhua.
Upon their first meeting, the karmic affinity was established. He was appointed as the *karmadāna* (rector) for fifteen years, during which time he thoroughly mastered the subtle principles.
One day, he summoned him into his room, struck him on the head, and said, "In this single blow, there is letting go, seizing, killing, and enlivening.
How do you understand it? The Master replied, "Like a dragon obtaining water; like a tiger relying on a mountain. He struck him again, saying, "What about this blow?
The Master said, "I know the Master is truly over-zealous. He said, "Not yet—speak further! The Master then gave him a blow.
Zetuo opened his palm and said, "Do not act in confusion. The Master then prostrated himself, and Zetuo said, "So it is, so it is.
He then bestowed upon him a verse of transmission and formal authorization (Shigao was his successor).
Chan Master Tianlong Cizhong was a native of Pujing in Wuzhou, Zhejiang. He entered the monastic order under Huizong of Huazang.

Delighting in the recitation [of sutras], Huizong instructed him, saying: "To recite the scriptures without penetrating their principle is merely to follow the lines and count the characters; only when you clarify the mind and reach the original source can it be called 'reciting and upholding the scriptures.
The Master requested further instruction, asking: "How is it that this is so? Huizong replied: "You must know it through direct personal experience."
He realized that he had not lost his resolve for the monastic life. The Master then traveled north to Míngzhōng Temple, where he received full ordination and studied the Vinaya.
One day, he suddenly recalled the words of his former teacher and immediately went to visit Lóng'ēn Yuán to investigate the "Mu" (No) kōan. He pursued this inquiry with diligence for several years.

Once, as he was stepping out the door, he heard the sound of someone calling a dog and attained realization. He presented a verse, saying: "The master calls out suddenly; I lift my head and turn around."
Having inhaled some of its poisonous vapor, he bit the people of the world to death. Yuanwei was delighted and asked, "Why does the dog have no Buddha-nature?
The Master said, "Even you, Reverend, must take care. Yuanwei asked, "How then can you say it has it?
The Master said, "When snow presses down on the plum branch, one knows that spring exists elsewhere. Yuanwei said, "Take good care of yourself," and then went again to consult Da Jingmin.
Min said, "For what reason does a dog have no Buddha-nature? The Master said, "The fragrant breeze is cold in the north of the border;
the winter sun is mild in Guangnan. Min said, "Set aside 'is' and 'is not,' and tell me the phrase. The Master said, "Why must one fish at Ziling’s terrace?
Min struck him and said, "You dodging fellow! The Master shook his sleeves and departed. At the evening assembly, Anhua Ze asked, "I hear you understand... [The text ends here].
"Attaining the wordless—does this hold true? The Master said, "Why does the Abbot use a ladle to divine by listening to empty sounds?
[The other] said, "Since it is non-existent, what is there to understand? The Master said, "Tear open the void and squeeze out its marrow. [The other] said, "Not yet; speak further."
The Master said, "Release the soaring falcon that cleaves the heavens; it pierces through the azure void. Zhe said, "For saying that, you shall receive thirty blows.

The Master said, "I have only just arrived today; I do not dare offend the Venerable One. Zhe was thus approved. He attended the Master personally for several years until he had thoroughly clarified the profound principles.
The Master then certified him with a verse and appointed him to reside at Tianlong. Subsequently, he moved to Huazang (Shigao was his successor).
Chan Master Tianran Ding of Beijing paid his respects to Chan Master Ze Chuchen of Anhua, who instructed him to contemplate the "Mu" (無) kōan.
Subsequently, he studied under Gu of Mingbo. One evening, as Gu entered the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying:

"Contemplating the head-word must be intimate and direct, as if standing atop a precipice ten thousand fathoms high; suddenly tumbling to the bottom, one reaches a state where not a single breath remains. Toward...
"Awaken here! Only then will there be a slight degree of correspondence. Before the words had even faded, the Master attained sudden enlightenment;
he rose and prostrated himself. Gu said, "This was merely turned by the force of the wind. The Master then let out a shout. Gu struck him.
The Master shouted twice in succession. Gu said, "Why do you not utter a single word? Why do you shout so recklessly? The Master shouted once more.
He returned to his seat. After the period of silence had ended, Gu called the Master into his room and asked, "Why did you shout at the old monk?
The Master replied, "I saw the Master fall to the bottom of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, so I came specifically to rescue you. Gu clapped his hands and laughed, saying:
A single bean popped in the cold ashes. The Master also clapped his hands and said, "Alive! Alive! From then on, his mental acuity and sharpness became swift and agile.
Later, at Shouzuo, Zhenze asked him, "Do you have a point of entry, or not? The Master replied, "Preceptor, do not heed the idle talk of bystanders.
Zhenze said, "The Sutra says: 'When one person awakens to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions all vanishes.'"

[The Master] fell [into a state of realization]. Then, pointing to what was before him, he said, "Because of this, every single thing manifests. The Master said, "Heaven covers all without partiality; Earth bears all without partiality.
Thereupon, [the Master] entered the abbot’s quarters and closed the door. The Master did not understand the meaning and remained lost in doubt until late at night. Looking up, he saw the moon;
its clear light extended for ten thousand *li*, and everything he had previously possessed vanished completely. The next morning—
He knocked on the door of the Abbot’s quarters. The Abbot asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "Wuanding. The Abbot said, "If you can speak the Way, I shall open the door.

The Master said, "If there were a place where one could open one's mouth, I would not have come to see the Master. Thereupon, the Abbot opened the door and said, "I, this old monk, want you exactly like this.
The Master paid his respects with three bows, saying, "Take care," and the Abbot nodded in approval (Shigao thus became his successor).
Chan Master Zhen of Shenglian Jia-an Temple in Suzhou was a native of the Qian clan of that same prefecture. He traveled north to the capital, where he received the tonsure under Master Ze of Anhua.
There, he investigated the kōan of "The Three Are Not. Later, returning south, he visited Master Fuxi of Jinshu Shigan, presenting his insights on numerous occasions.
Fuyue and Saoke were together one day when they heard a neighboring monk say, "If one has not endured frost and snow, how can one know the heart that withstands the cold of winter?
He attained realization and immediately returned to Huqiu to study under Tiangu Zhen.

Once, while attending him as they walked outside the mountain gate, Zhen asked, "Why did the ancients say that those who can speak [the truth] die beneath the crossbar, and those who cannot speak also die beneath the crossbar? The Master replied, "A fervent heart."
Zhen struck him repeatedly, saying, "For now, look after your life! The Master extended his neck and said, "If you want my head, take it.
Zhen said, "When you meet people, simply speak of this. The Master pointed to Thousand-Man Rock and said, "This is where Dharma Master Sheng preached the Dharma."
Zhenyi asked, "What have you brought back from the South? The Master said, "I went empty-handed; I have come empty-handed.
Zhenyi asked, "What is the phrase for arriving home? The Master said, "The head touches the heavens; the feet tread upon the earth.
Zhenyi said, "Speak a word regarding the space beneath your heels. The Master bowed and said, "Today, once again, I have had the privilege of seeing the Master in person."
Shang nodded his head in agreement. On the full moon day of the second month in the Ren-shen year of the Kangxi era, having finished addressing the assembly, he spoke this verse:
"Coming, it is vast and detached; going, it is detached and vast. But tell me, what is this? Ha!
A solitary falcon soars through ten thousand miles of empty sky. With eyes closed, he passed away (Se-gao then succeeded him).
Zen Master Qingying Run of the Tiantang Zangjingyuan was the son of Cai of Sana. From childhood, he suffered from many ailments;

his parents sent him away to follow the venerable elder Lingyou, under whom he was instructed in ritual recitation. Whenever he read the phrase "This alone is the one reality," he harbored doubts without ceasing.
He went to Qianhua to receive full ordination, where he diligently studied the *vinaya* and aspired to the Chan school, eventually going to seek instruction there.
Tianli Zhen was highly esteemed by Jia Shan. Although he repeatedly received the master’s striking with the staff, he had not yet attained a state of silent realization.

Later, while traveling to Jinmen, he went to visit Anhuai Ze. Ze asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Tianchang. Ze asked, "How long is the sky? Just as the Master was about to answer, he immediately requested to stay.
Ze appointed him as the secretary (jishi) and instructed him to contemplate the koan, "All dharmas return to One. The Master applied himself with such fervor that he broke through his delusions.
Chan. Having no way through, he heard the sound of firecrackers on New Year’s Eve, and his doubts were suddenly dispelled.
He went immediately to the abbot’s quarters and said, “Today is the eve of the New Year; how do you roast the white ox in the open field to share with the assembly for the year?
The Master spread out both hands, and Ze struck him. Ze then placed his hands over his forehead and departed, intuitively grasping the meaning (Shigao was the successor of Ze).
Chan Master Tianbao Jianfengjun of Yinglu was by nature stern and sharp. He traveled extensively to visit various spiritual teachers (*jñānin*), yet none could satisfy his mind.
Hearing that Gubi Wen was solitary and transcendent, he eventually went to Sanjiao. Upon seeing him for the first time, Wen immediately promoted him to the assembly.
One day, Wen raised the case concerning the attendant Kuoluo’s question to Deshan regarding "where the sages of the past have gone," and requested further instruction. Wen then commanded—
The Master thought to himself, "I have arrived at the place where National Teacher Wuzhuo did not break the drum. The inscription read: "Stop! Stop!
If it is thus, then Deshan shall desist. The Master said, "This old fellow has been completely exposed. The inscription read: "And what about you?"
The Master said, "When I arrived here, what excuse could I have made for not prostrating? Wenceng said, "Be careful not to be perfunctory. The Master turned around and went out;
Wenceng closed the door of the abbot’s quarters. Addressing the assembly, he said: "For twenty years I have been traveling on foot; my person is poor and I have no socks to wear.
Though I sit and cut off a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks, I find all the more that there is nowhere to plant my feet. He then spread his two hands and said, "There they are!"
What Dharma? [The Master] ascended the seat for the evening session at the rear of the hall.
"The entire earth is this courtyard; one cannot penetrate it. The entire earth is this self; one has never known it. The entire earth is this almsbowl."
"There is no place to eat; the entire earth is a single site of enlightenment (dharma-cakra). There is no gate through which to exit.
Do you all understand? After a long silence, he said: 'When the great earth is picked up, what is it? No one can grasp it—what then?
The peach blossoms laugh until Lingyun’s eyes burst open. Old Lady Zheng Shisan. Addressing the assembly, he raised the example of *Aṅgulimāla* holding his alms bowl.
The *Inyuan* (Causes and Conditions) says: The elder asked about matters because of certain affairs; the World-Honored One boarded the carriage and struck the carriage.

Aṅgulimāla labored in vain without success. He let out a shout and said: "Today you have mistakenly employed words and names. The verse says: "Lightly or heavily adorned, leaning against the emerald pavilion."

The wind and moon stir melancholy within the inner chambers beyond the curtains; a single cry of the cuckoo passes through the gardens, shattering the dream-tour of Zhuang Zhou’s butterfly. (Gubi Wen Si)
Chan Master Longfeng Tielun Yin of Guangxi ascended the hall and said: "In the blazing heat of the sixth month, ice is born from fire;
in the vast, bright sky, the sun is but a single wheel. When one turns back to look at the ten-thousand-li green mountains, white clouds drift slowly, gathering in swirling mists.
He drew a circle with his whisk and said: "If you can understand this, you shall enter my Dharma; there is no need to distinguish between ordinary and sage, nor to discuss wisdom."
Fools! In all their actions and conduct, they merely follow old decrees.

To claim they have clarified a "separate transmission outside the scriptures" or established entirely new regulations, they cannot avoid merely breathing through the nostrils of Longfeng. (He strikes the whisk once. (Gubi Wen’s Succession)
Chan Master Du Yuan of Sanjiao, Qizhou, was the son of Lu of Xiu-shui. At the age of fifteen, he paid his respects to Bai-lan Cheng and received the tonsure.
He served through manual labor for five years, when he suddenly reflected that the matter of birth and death was of great importance.

He went directly to Fa-chang, who assigned him to contemplate the koan: "When one breath does not come back. Upon reaching the twenty-first day, hearing the startling sound of a firecracker, he leaped down from his mat. Fa-chang approached him...
The Master said, "I am pleased with your news. The teacher prostrated and said, "I have been investigating this matter for three days and nights without closing my eyes;
I perceive that there is no boundary between before and after. Chang said, "Now, I do not want you to practice Chan or study the Way.
I only want you to eat when you are hungry and sleep when you are tired. The teacher thought to himself, "The Buddha-dharma is no small matter," and so he went out to seek it everywhere.
He traveled through Jiangxi and Hubei until he reached Fengshan, where he paid his respects to Dongyan Can. He served as an attendant for six years.
One day, Can called the Master into his room and commanded him to compose a verse on the "original face. The Master said: "The Yellow River winds with its waters curving;
The original face is clear—no need for contemplation. Replace your two eyes and look beyond the heavens; Turn your head, and the stone horse passes over a thousand mountains. Can praised him.
He praised him and subsequently granted his seal of approval. The Master succeeded to the Dharma of Tianfeng Xingyu at Duoyun.

The following year, when Xingyu went to accept an invitation to Sanjiao, he charged the Master to lead the assembly. After seven years had passed, Xingyu received an invitation to Dong Yongfu and charged the Master to succeed him on the seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he inherit? The Master replied: "The full moon over the Double Peak."

He saw through the ice of Lake Li. [The Master asked: "What is the matter that has been transmitted from one to another? The Teacher said: "I have just happened to tread the path through the green forest;

now I have arrived at the very summit. He then said: "Exerting the majesty of a lion crouching on the ground—thousands upon ten thousands of them—their heads and necks burst forth with sparks of fire."
When everything has been exhausted and cleared away, it is like grass bending before the wind. At such a time, the single step that transcends all is like a cliff standing ten thousand fathoms high.
[The Master] suddenly picks up his staff, draws a line, and says: "If you can penetrate and emerge through this point, only then do you have the right to receive a blow of the staff. Why?
Because the momentum of the Dragon Gate cascading downward is such that it overturns mountains and topples valleys, pervading the Five Lakes. (Dongyan Can was the successor.)
Chan Master Chushi Xu of Wushan in Qishui was the son of the Wu family of Hunan. His mother dreamed that a lunar disc fell onto her bed;
startled, she rushed outside the room and he was born. At sixteen, he left home at Chongfa Temple. At nineteen, he visited Luoyue at Yuan Tong.
At twenty-three, he called upon Fachang to receive full ordination. While contemplating the "cane" koan, he attained realization and lived in seclusion at Bai.
One day, while crossing a stream, Yunshan encountered a tiger; his hair stood on end. The Master thought silently to himself, "This is the result of my past karma.

He cast aside all matters of his entire life at once and sat upright by the stream. In a brief moment, the tiger departed. Thereupon, the Master left his hermitage and went into the mountains to visit Huangbo Xiyun.
Later, at Baizhang, he was wounded in a finger by a splitting bamboo splinter, and only then did he penetrate the barrier of the ancients.
*Jian*. In the evening session at Shuanglin, Dongyan Can questioned him: "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Yunju. Can said, "Since you are from Yunju, why have you come here?
The Master replied, "The dragon strides and the tiger gallops. He subsequently attended Can for six years;

his responses to the Master's challenges were so profoundly in accord with Can’s intent that Can remarked of him: "One who can truly succeed and carry on the lineage; his heroic spirit shall flourish through the generations. The Master...

Having received his instructions, he lived in seclusion at the old site of Wushan Temple on Zhusha Rock. For thirty years, he built a thatched hut to discipline himself, never venturing beyond the mountains.
(Dongyan Can was his successor.)
Chan Master Xinzongcheng of Huainan had served Master Fazu at Mount Feng for the longest time. One day, Fazu asked, "There is no water that does not flow toward the east;
why then do you go against the current toward the west? The Master replied, "The great ocean is content; it must flow backward.
Fazu asked, "What about that phrase regarding the backward flow? The Master said, "In that case, one encounters the source from both left and right. Fazu [nodded].
So it was done. In the autumn of the Dingwei year of the Kangxi era, the Master ascended the hall. Holding up his robe and whisk, he said: "Whether in dragon pools or tiger dens, they move with ease;
generally, one must acknowledge their majestic presence. It is not that this mountain monk displays his own clumsy ineptitude; rather, amidst the startling waves, he has captured a fierce dragon.
Master Rangan, whose insight was beyond doubt, had served the old monk for many years. Today, with both hands, I divide [the burden].
Entrusted. Use it freely, turning it upside down or holding it sideways, to glorify the Dharma and its transformation. Master, take care; [he] performs three prostrations (a successor of Zhufeng).
Shimen Tianzhu Jijun Chan Master went to Xianju to visit Gudeng Hongjing. He requested instruction on the essentials of Chan, and Jing instructed him to contemplate the "Mu" (No) koan.
When Jing resided at Qinglian, the Master followed him there as well. During the retreat period, Jing entered the hall and asked the assembly: "Not..."
"Contemplate the good; do not contemplate the evil. At this very moment, is there anyone who can speak? The assembly remained silent. Yuanzheng let out a thunderous shout.

The Master, without realizing it, broke into a sweat all over his body, and his knot of doubt was instantly resolved. He immediately presented a verse, saying: "A single shout causes the void to collapse;
It startles the mud ox from the bottom of the sea. I am driven until my whole body breaks into a sweat, Piercing through to the very bone and marrow."

"Wind-flowing elegance. Jiong nodded in approval and immediately sealed it with a verse: "A single sweat breaks the knot of doubt; With wind-flowing elegance piercing to the bone, the field of vision expands.
I recall again that wordless dialogue of old; It makes one regret, time and again, being without cause [for such realization].

Addressing the assembly, he raised the following case: When Jinming entered for an interview with Yuanhu, as soon as he stepped across the threshold, Yuanhu asked, "What is this? Jinming was about to respond when—

[The Master] said, "Right. He used a thunderous shout of awe, and [the monk] attained sudden and complete enlightenment; he then covered his ears and departed. He offered this verse: Ten thousand layers of silver waves surge at the Yu Gate;
With fins raised and scales stirred, there are whales and sea-monsters. A single clap of thunder startles heaven and earth;
It truly causes wind and thunder to darken the universe. (By Gudeng Hongsi)
Chan Master Daocheng of Leiyin in Suzhou went to visit Gudeng Xiong at Jinming. Xiong asked, "What is your name, Venerable?
The Master replied, "Daocheng. Xiong said, "Since the Way is already accomplished, why have you come here? The Master replied:
“If you do not come, how can one know that the Way is realized? Jiong asked. The Master said, “A turtle shedding its shell flies up into the sky.
Jiong asked, “What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, “Today I have personally seen the Master. Jiong shouted, “Who is it that sees?
As the Master was about to offer a reply, Jiong struck him. The Master said, “Master, do not force others. Jiong—
Xuanjue scolded him, saying, "I was merely restraining you; I will beat you with this staff! The Master said, "I have come specifically to attend upon the Master;
I earnestly beg for your compassion. Xuanjue called the Master forward again. The Master then overturned the meditation seat. Xuanjue said, "You madman!
The Master said, "Just now, it was not appropriate for you to strike me so excessively. Xuanjue said, "Did you take that as being struck? The Master [remained silent].
[The Master] said, "The Abbot must not understand this as a case of madness. Huǐjìng said, "This shows that you have deeply understood the matter of the staff.
The Master then bowed; Huǐjìng approved of him (Guḍēng Tóng was his successor).
Chan Master Chumu Jie of Zhending Ba’en was the son of the Zhong family of Qiantang. He went to Beijing Sanjiao Temple to shave his head and traveled to Anhua to seek the precepts.
He was instructed to investigate the "Mu" (No) koan. Subsequently, he visited various monasteries throughout the forests of Chan without finding entry.
Finally, he sought out Qinglian Hong at Beici Temple in Tianjin; as soon as he stepped across the threshold, Hong gave a shout and said, "There is no place for you here."
As the Master reached the doorway, Yuanzhao pushed him out. After a long while, the Master re-entered; Yuanzhao shouted again. At this, the Master had an awakening.
Just as he was about to prostrate, Yuanzhao shut the door. The next morning, the Master entered the room and prostrated, saying, "Yesterday, you were robbed by a thief and did not even know it.
Yuanzhao said, "Let us set aside yesterday for a moment; how about today? The Master then shouted. Yuanzhao said:
"You clearly understand the events of yesterday. The Master prostrated. Hyong-mun was then appointed to oversee the affairs of the monastery.

Later, he remained in seclusion on Mount Wutai for several years before residing at Baegun-sa. During a small-scale sermon (*saam*), he said: "A single broken sand pot—how joyful it is that everyone supports it!
Every day at mealtime, who can swallow the food filling the entire plate? To say they can swallow it is not impossible; but tell me, what is its flavor? The mountain... [remains silent].
The monk does not begrudge revealing his own verbal faults; he shall disclose them for you all. Rice is indeed made from grain.
Residing at Leiyin Temple in Shengjing, he addressed the assembly: "The various donors within the city of Gu'an laugh at me for sitting in silence all day long.

Suddenly, the thunderous sound of the temple bell roars through the midnight, and the lanterns and the pillar become a missed opportunity. Do not miss it! It is a lump of clay accumulated over kalpas."
Julebo (Clue-Po) resided at Fahua Temple in Xuanfu. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Are the Buddha-dharma of the north and the Buddha-dharma of the south the same or different?
The Master said, "In the northern frontier, it is cold before the frost; in Jiangnan, it is cold after the snow. The monk asked, "Is there still a distinction?
The Master said, "Do not misquote me three thousand *li* away. He then said, "Ten thousand *li*..."

The city walls reach ten thousand *li* into the mountains; when travelers arrive here, all climbing and scaling cease. A single bright moon has shone from antiquity, emerging far beyond the Milky Way this very night.
Only when the beacon fires are removed and the smoke of the wild beasts is extinguished can the people of the four quarters rejoice in peace and security.
The assembly, tell me: by whose power of grace is this received? [He plants his staff] and says: "A seven-foot black cane reaches across the heavens; in a single thought, there is none."
I prostrate ten thousand times for ten thousand years. Entering the hall: Above, there is no Buddha to be realized; below, there are no beings to be delivered.
