With a single stick of incense, close the door and sit in meditation. To act in this manner—do not let it pass you by. He calls to the assembly, saying: "Do you understand?
Along the main road by the Wanquan Barracks, carriages and horses pass. (Gudeng Huijiong’s successor).
The layman Chen Yumen, a native of Changzhou, was nineteen years old when he passed the provincial examination in the Jia-mao year. He was immediately appointed to military duties in Nanjing.
Having experienced numerous perils and hardships, he was moved by a sense of spiritual resonance and resigned his post to return home. Thereupon, he studied the arts of Yuan Gong.

While reading the *Platform Sutra*, he reached the passage concerning "neither thinking of good nor thinking of evil" and harbored a doubt; for a long time, he made no progress. Later, he heard of a monk...
He said, "When one does not deliberate at all upon good or evil, that is the ultimate. He attained realization. Later, together with his friend Huahuiseng, he went to visit Shifan at Cihang.
He asked, "I have personally arrived at the Jewel Mountain; I beg the Master for a reception. Shifan took a cup of tea and splashed it across his face, saying, "Do you understand?
The scholar said, "Fortunately, Zhaozhou has emitted light. Shifan said, "Do not let your eyes deceive you. The scholar gave a shout and then departed.
Shi went out and said to Huihua, "This fellow will stir up wind and waves on another day. At this, Shishuang attained awakening.
Xuedou Yun, upon reaching Songyuan, invited Shishuang to go to Dongchan. Yun asked, "What is the very first step?"
The layman said, "Look beneath your feet. Yun said, "Do not be tripped up by the binding rope. The layman said, "I thank the Master for this instruction.
Yun presented him with a verse, saying: "A single piece of flawless jade, Its entire body is pure inscription. Casually raise your eyes high."
"Having seen through it, what more is there to say? The Imperial Historian Jiang Huchen invited scholars to study together at Dengwu Bi. He instructed them, saying, "Accompany me for seven sessions.

The scholars followed him with great diligence, yet they investigated until dawn without gaining anything. Thereupon, he presented them with this verse: "At the summit of ten thousand peaks, one beholds the King of Emptiness;
A single turn of the pivot illuminates the ten directions. Like beans popping from cold ashes, a red pellet— What need is there for further [explanation]?"

Using this to refine the vajra, Hu suddenly attained awakening. Clapping his hands, he laughed loudly. When Bao’en Xian arrived at his residence, Xian raised his staff and said, "Every person possesses this inherently;
why then can it not be grasped? The scholar said, "It is precisely because it is so exceedingly clear that what is to be attained is delayed.
Xian asked, "Have you attained it yet? The scholar replied, "The Master must also take care of the crown of his head. Xian—

He patted the monk on the back and said, "I cannot deceive you. The monk prostrated himself. He subsequently visited several spiritual teachers (*kishi*), and there was none with whom he did not find resonance.

Later, he went to visit Daebi Hyong. Hyong asked, "I have heard that you have long studied under various masters; where did you gain your strength? The monk replied, "In no place is there any connection.
Hyong struck him and said, "How do you understand this one blow? The monk replied, "Your compassionate heart is most earnest. Hyong—
[Zhao] said, "Do not mistake this for something good. The scholar said, "Who does not do so? [Zhao] said, "In your fundamental state, speak a single word.
The scholar said, "To drink when thirsty and eat when hungry is not an extra effort. Zhao certified him with a verse. The scholar also thanked him with a verse, saying:
"Two strokes from the First Ground; In one morning, the rain and dew are deep. Hanging the Patriarch’s intent before the window, I am glad to have attained the ancients."
Xinhuang said, "So it is, so it is. One day, Master Sanwei came to visit him.
As they discussed ancient kōans, Sanwei asked, "What is it that the layman has realized and attained, yet cannot be defiled? Xinhuang held up one finger.
Xiong said, "When one hides the body, there are no traces; why then do you expose your tail? The Master said, "When there are no traces, one does not hide the body;
only then is one a true adept. Xiong struck him, saying, "You have let it slip quite a bit.
The Master said, "I was seen through by the monk, after all" (Gu-deng Jiong, successor).
Chan Master Huichao Xian of Fengming on Mount Huo went to visit Tianfeng Xing. Xing asked, "What is the fundamental matter of the venerable one?
The Master said, "The tip of my tongue fills my mouth. Xing said, "Not yet; speak further.
The Master said, "I will not speak. Xing asked, "Why do you not speak? The Master said, "I fear it might disturb the Master. Xing raised his eyebrows and said, "Speak! Speak!"
The Master then paid his respects and ascended the hall. He split open a single atom and brought forth the Great Sutra of the Tathāgata.
Holding up his whisk, he said, "Tell me, assembly, what sutra is this? A monk stepped forward; the Master said, "If you try to explain it through intellectual penetration, you are unfit."
He then descended from his seat (Tianfeng Xing’s successor).

Chan Master Xian of Rushi at Chongshou in Jiuyang went to Sanjiao to visit Tianfeng Xing. When the master raised the kōan concerning Lingyun seeing peach blossoms to interrogate him, Xian had an awakening.
He addressed the assembly, citing the words of Nanming Guang of Jingshan as he addressed the assembly: [The text continues with the citation.]

The five peaks stand out with piercing clarity; at the tail of the Double Path, the tip leads the way. At He-shi Rock, [the stone] leaps and bounds; in the Bright Moon Pool, heaven itself is overturned.
The Verse says: In times of great peace and no affairs, the sword is opened from its scabbard; In times of affliction, the blade enters the sheath.
Suddenly hearing the howl of the autumn wind, one hurriedly turns within the deep palace to don the armor. (Tianfeng Xingsi)
Chan Master Sunye Min of Bailong, Huangbo, went to visit Xing of Sanjiao.

Xing asked, "For one who swallows the Buddhas and Patriarchs with their mouths and covers heaven and earth with their eyes, why do you not understand upon reaching this point? The Master said, "That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure.
Xing said, "Why did the ancients go up to Mount Touzi three times and to Dongshan nine times? The Master said, "I thought..."
Tianfeng Xing said, "There is another. What do you do right now? The Master replied, "The king of geese chooses its own milk;
it has never been of the class of ducks. Tianfeng Xing nodded in approval (Tianfeng Xing was his successor).
Master Hanchen Hong of Guangji Helin raised the teaching: "All dharmas should be known thus, seen thus, and believed and understood thus, so that no marks of dharmas arise.
He spoke in verse: Green mountains, green; white clouds, white. The water flows eastward; the stars bow to the North.
Carrying my cup, I drink at night atop the small tower; Drunk, I gaze upon the moon before the peaks—a thousand ages old. (Tianfeng Xingsi)
When Chan Master Yin Xiashu of Huangmei Jiming visited Tianfeng Xingyu at Duoyun, as soon as he stepped across the threshold, Xingyu asked, "What is it?
The Master replied, "I have come to attend upon the Master. Xingyu said, "With what do you attend upon me? The Master said, "Please let the Master judge for yourself.
Xingyu said, "There is no need for even a slight pressure. The Master said, "In that case, am I to pawn my ox at the warehouse?"
Xing nodded his head. The Master (Tianfeng Xing’s successor) prostrated himself.
Chan Master Shizi Heng of Qizhou went to visit Duoyun Xing. Xing held up his staff and said, "Do you recognize this?
The Master gave a shout. Xing struck him. The Master shouted again. Xing struck him again. The Master said, "The Master has attained..."
Tianfeng Xingzao said, "Your nature is so impetuous. Xing said, "Just now you gave me such a fine scolding.
The Master said, "Were it not for Liu Yi transmitting his letter, how could you have reached Lake Dongting? (Tianfeng Xing was a successor of [Zhaozhou]).
Chan Master Zidi Luo of Huanglong in Wuchang studied under Guangjiao Yu. He realized the mind-ground; by nature he was agile and his insight was exceptionally transcendent.
He traveled extensively through various monastic communities (*conglin*), yet none satisfied him. He was close friends with Yunshe Yuan, with whom he stayed for several years.

Upon hearing that Yongfu Xing’s pedagogical methods were like a pair of tongs and a hammer, he went there to seek instruction. At a single word, their spiritual resonance (*jiqu*) was established, whereupon Zidi Luo said, "This is truly my teacher."
The next morning, he took his leave and returned to Huguo. The assembly hailed the Master as the "One-Night Chan Master.

Later, while residing there, he addressed the assembly, citing the karmic connection between the Second Patriarch (Nanzong Yin) and Sanjiao Xi, regarding the occasion when he requested instruction on Zhaozhou’s story of setting down the broom and clapping his hands in great laughter.
Sanjiao struck him twice. Nanzong said, "Did you not grasp it? Sanjiao struck him again. Nanzong said, "Gold..."

"You distinguish not between brass and jade; you cannot tell stone from jade. Zong laughed heartily and went out of the Dharma Hall. One day, Zong heard a monk reciting a verse on wind bells, which said:
"Copper lips and iron tongues, too sharp and new; Hung from the corner of the tower, they do not reckon spring.

Beyond words are hundreds of thousands of samādhi-dharmas; Through the wind, they are spoken to those within. Thereupon, Zong attained realization. He presented his understanding to Jue, who approved it.
The Verse says: The lotus-leaf skirt is cut in one pattern; The lotus-smiling face opens on both sides. Entering straight to the heart of the pond, she cannot be seen;
Yet from the sound of her song, someone must surely be coming. (Tianfeng Xingsi)
The lay practitioner Qin Zhanming of Songjiang visited Master Xingyu at Zhongfu Monastery on Tianfeng Peak.

Xingyu asked, "Clearly manifest at the tip of every blade of grass—clearly manifest is the meaning of the Patriarch. How do you understand this? The layman replied, "When it comes to this point, I simply do not understand.
Xingyu said, "This mountain monk is precisely looking for one who does not understand. The layman asked, "Why does the Master let go of his students?"
However, Xing said, "A thousand soldiers are easy to find, but a single general is hard to seek. Shi bowed (he was the successor of Tianfeng Xing).
At the evening assembly of Chan Master Ju’an Lun of Fuyan in Wuhu, Haiyue asked as soon as he stepped through the door, "What is this?
The Master replied, "I am such-and-such. Haiyue took up his staff and struck him straight out, closing the door behind him. The Master said, "I have long heard of Hai..."
Yue said, "Indeed, the cold light is overwhelming. He opened the door and asked, "Venerable sir, from which demon king’s lair have you come?
The Master slapped him across the cheek. Yue said, "No need; it was simply that I wanted to see if you could hit the mark, Venerable sir."

The mountain monk then desisted. The Master prostrated and said, "If the Master recognizes his debt of gratitude, that is sufficient. He then revealed his profound realization. Renxian Zhe came to visit;
upon seeing him, the Master immediately perceived their karmic affinity. He soon invited him for a meal. Picking up a steamed rice ball, the Master asked, "If you call this a rice ball—"

"Entering hell will be like being struck by an arrow. Zhe said, "The Master’s maternal heart is far too excessive. The Master said, "What do you take for food, a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net?
Zhe said, "I thank the Master for bestowing this meal. The Master then turned his bowl upside down and said, "Tell me, what have you realized?
Zhe said, "I am glad that both material and Dharma gifts have been bestowed. The Master nodded in approval (Tianyan Qi succeeded him).
Chan Master Wan’an Chun of Taizhou ascended the hall for a formal discourse. A monk asked, “The entire Tripitaka is a ‘cutting foot’ (a radical);
I wonder what character it cuts? The Master said, “The Heavenly Sovereign is august; the Earthly Sovereign is august.
The monk asked, “As for Wuzu’s saying, ‘Bolanian,’ what is its meaning? The Master said, “Meeting a blind Persian on the road, his mouth is full of chewing ice.”
Feng. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Repent. The monk asked, "Repent for what? The Master said, "Facing each other yet not recognizing one another—who would not feel shame?
The monk was speechless. The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "Where have all the sages of antiquity gone?
The Master said, "Nowhere but south of the Yangtze, or north of the Yangtze. The monk asked, "Have they come to this place of yours, Master?"
The Master said, "He does not arrive. [The monk] asked, "Why does he not arrive? The Master said, "In this place of mine, I do not allow him to settle.
(Tianyan Qisi) Chan Master Dayuan of Yangzhou raised the case of Tianyan Qisi’s small-scale sermon (*xiaocan*): "Confucius did not know how to read; Bodhidharma did not understand Chan.
People, however, do not believe this. When Haiyue spoke thus, the assembly did not believe him. The assembly [responded], "It is you who are like this!"
Listen. Haicheng did not believe; the others did not believe; Haicheng did not believe. Tell me, are they the same or different? The verse says:
Before the wind, a single song penetrates the subtle and the manifest. From ancient times to the present, no one can sing it in harmony. The immortal rides the dragon back to the azure heavens;
The deluded man still scoops water at the western pond at night. (Tianyan Qisi)

Taicang asked about Chan Master Mei Shunri Gaor, a son of the Feng family from Wumen. In his youth, he studied Confucianism; one day, while reading the poetry of Luo Nian’an, he came across the lines:
"The caged chicken has food, yet the cauldron is near; the wild crane has no grain, yet heaven and earth are vast.

The Master’s heart was moved with compassion, and he immediately went to Xiuxue to pay respects to the official Chen Xiu, requesting tonsure and the precepts. He would often remain silent for an entire day. One day...
He sighed and said, "If one does not clarify the Way, what benefit is there in leaving the household life? He went directly to the Abbot’s quarters to seek instruction.
He served as an attendant for seven years and attained a thorough penetration of the source of the Dharma. When he first resided at Yuanjue Temple, he addressed the assembly:
"In a sandalwood grove and a lion’s den, there is no trace of foxes, wolves, or jackals. Yunmen’s 'One Word' is too coarse; Dongshan’s 'Five Ranks' are too subtle. [What of] the Guiyang [school]?"
The Dharma-eye faces both sides equally; they twist the extraordinary and play with ghosts and spirits, vying for the black lacquer.
Only Linji has a slight edge; meeting people, he is habitually a "white-thief" (a pickpocket). But tell me, how will Upāsaka Gao act? He brandishes his whisk and says:
"Sitting and reclining in an empty room, the spring grasses grow deep; directing the *ruyi* (auspicious wand), heavenly flowers fall. Holding up his bowl, he ascends the hall. "Buddha-dharma..."
Pervading all places, the Great Compassionate One with a thousand eyes gazes upon them without breaking his gaze. The alms bowl opens its mouth and speaks in a babble;
the great earth is gathered up as small as a single grain of rice. Plum blossoms lead the guests to try on their spring garments; three by three and two by two, they form rows of five.
Suddenly he ran into a fighting cock and forgot the Dharma Master Hu of those years (Huan Chen Xiusi).
Chan Master Ziyun of Mount Xi in Suzhou was a native of that same prefecture; he had mastered a vast array of classical texts and traveled extensively through lecture halls.
While listening to the *Lotus Sūtra*, he reached the passage: "This one thing alone is the reality; all else is not true. Having a doubt, he asked, "I do not yet know what this 'one thing' is.
The presiding lecturer hesitated and was unable to answer, saying, "You must seek instruction from a master of the school to understand it.
The Master then went to visit Chen Xiuyu at Wenmei. Xiuyu asked, "Where have you been lately? The Master replied, "The teaching..."

Xiaoxiu asked, "Where are you right now? The Master had no reply. Xiaoxiu laughed loudly, and the Master’s face flushed with shame. Thereupon, he applied himself to intensive study (*mǎngcān*) to the point of forgetting both sleep and food.
One day, upon hearing the sound of the wooden gong, he felt his body and mind become profoundly serene. He hurried to the abbot’s quarters and said:
"Today I am going to beat that old man," said Xiu. Xiu extended his neck and said, "Even if you were to cut off my head, it would not matter.
As the Master hesitated, Xiu struck him a heavy blow and pushed him out. The Master said to himself, "It has always been manifest;
why was I unable to speak? He redoubled his efforts in training. While walking in meditation, a wind suddenly arose, and seeing fallen leaves swirling about, he attained complete enlightenment.
He then entered the room to present his understanding. Xiu said, "So it is, so it is. The Master prostrated [and Chen Xiu conferred the succession].

Gu Shangyu, a *xiaolian* from Taicang and a member of the prominent Wang clan of Loudong, admired the Chan school in his heart. He had previously read the Buddhist scriptures and visited Jinming Jin, but they did not reach a point of accord.
Jin directed him to go and consult Mei Xiu. Xiu asked, "What is your courtesy name, Layman? The man replied, "Shang."
It rained. Xiu said, "Try making a single drop and see. The scholar hesitated. Xiu said, "For now, rejoice; the dense clouds are spreading everywhere. The scholar remained utterly bewildered.
He then spent many days and nights investigating this for a long time. While attending Xiu, he saw a monk making noodles.
The scholar asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Xiu replied, "The rolling-pin for kneading the dough with both hands. The scholar said, "Is there still a Patriarch?"
Huan Chen Xiufu asked, "Do you agree? Shoushu said, "Snowy waves roll with the spring breeze. The scholar nodded his head. Xiufu asked, "What principle have you seen?
The scholar replied, "Where is there that is not elegant? Xiufu approved of this. (Recorded by Huan Chen Xiufu)
Chan Master Jianning Longzhen Jueyuan Yin was the son of the Zhou family of Min County. His mother was of the Shi clan.

She prayed before an image of the Great Being (Avalokiteśvara), and was moved by a white light that illuminated the room as brightly as day. She conceived a child; during her pregnancy, she abstained from meat.

When the Master was a child, whenever he heard the sound of killing, he would wail incessantly. If the creature was released, his grandmother and mother were exceedingly joyful. By the time he was a youth, he would prostrate himself upon seeing a monk.
He never ceased reciting the title of "Mahāsattva. A Brahman monk said to his father, Yu Hu, "This son is no vessel for the mundane world. Yu Hu was surprised that the monk did not speak with him;
as he saw him off at the gate, the monk merely bowed and vanished from sight. Yu Hu was struck with wonder and repented his own shortcomings. When the Master was seventeen, [the monk appeared again].

He possessed the aspiration to transcend the mundane world; however, because his parents did not grant their permission, he became deeply distressed and fell ill. The following year, his parents passed away in succession.
He immediately retired to the wilds of Mount Ke to shave his head and traveled to Mount Gu at the abode of Master Pài to receive full ordination.

There, he requested instruction. Master Pài assigned him the koan: "The state before your parents were born. He subsequently visited all the masters of knowledge throughout the Eight Mins region. Desiring to cross the mountain ridges, he was blocked by military conflict and thus remained there, forming a retreat.
For three years at Maosifeng, he had only a single *huatou* (critical phrase).
Later, when monastics and laypeople invited him to return to Keshan, he frequently manifested spiritual radiance while residing at Ben’an, where he was often inspired by the master’s prodding.

One day, hearing two visiting monks conversing and saying, "The entire universe is this very self," the Master experienced a sudden opening of mind; everything from the past dissolved like melting ice. He went to seek [further instruction].
Zhengtan asked, "What is your face before your parents were born? The Master said, "A snowflake flies from a red furnace. Zhengtan said, "Not yet; speak further.
The Master said, "A brick is thrown in the courtyard. Zhengtan was greatly pleased. When Zhengtan resided at Fengshan, he appointed the Master as the head of the assembly.
They remained there for ten years. One day, while descending into the hall, Zhengtan asked the assembly, "Fengshan..."
"One period. The firewood is very hot. How do you deal with it? The Master said, "It makes the back of the clay ox sweat.
Dan said, "I grant you half of that answer. The Master asked, "What is the other half? Dan raised his staff and struck him.
The Master seized the staff and pushed him away twice. Dan said, "What about that other half? The Master said, "The assembly is the witness. Dan [laughed].
[The Master] said, "Not yet. The Teacher bowed. Tanu nodded his head in approval. In the autumn of the Gengxu year of the Kangxi era, Tanu bestowed upon him a verse.

The following year, he was ordered to share the seat [with the Abbot] at Longzhen Temple. Ascending the hall, he gave a shout and called to the assembly, saying, "Do you understand? The silkworm thread is passed on by Yuanke."

The music played was "The Sentiments of the Lady of Chu. He then looked to his left and right and said, "Alas! Were there not those who understand this music, the sound of the flowing water would have been in vain.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To pluck the 'night-light' [pearl] in the azure sky, one cannot call it a star;

to submerge the 'exquisite blossoms' in the clear stream, one cannot call it the moon. Striking the meditation seat, he asked: "Tell me, is it a star? Is it the moon? Are they the exquisite blossoms? Or is it the night-light?"
"Ya! [He lets out a shout] and says: "If you can discern this here, I grant that your door of awakening remains unbarred; facing the moon, you shall have no delusion. He addresses the assembly:
"What virtue does the divine dragon have toward the myriad things? When it moves, its purpose is to provide rain and moisture.

What resentment does the viper have toward the myriad things? When it moves, its purpose is to inflict poison and harm. Not acting out of either favor or enmity—these qualities exist within all things."
It is seen in the ○. These all exist within it; that which cannot be restrained—○[○@╳]○—is already finished (manifesting at times as Tán-sì).
Chan Master Xi Jue Rui of Kaiyuan Temple in Quanzhou was the son of the Lin family of Jinjiang. His mother was Lady Kang. While she was pregnant with him, she abstained from eating meat.
One day, his father saw from afar a flame shooting up to the sky from atop a house, while white cranes circled and cried out.
He hurried home in haste and found that the Master had been born. With a loud cry, the infant smiled serenely. His father marveled at this. When he grew up, he did not associate with other children.
One day, while playing, he saw a monk holding an alms bowl. Recognizing him as an old acquaintance, he asked, "What are you doing? The monk replied, "I am simply like this; are you not like this too?
The Master could not contain his joy and immediately desired to leave the household life. At the age of fourteen, he forgot both his parents; his grief and exertion nearly brought him to his end.

Upon completing his mourning period, he paid respects at the ordination platform and received the tonsure from Master Chongru Huang. From morning until night, he remained solitary and resolute. There was no...

There is such a possibility. While reading the *Chuan Deng Lu* (Transmission of the Lamp), he reached the passage where Duanqiao Lun instructed Gao Feng to investigate "The myriad dharmas return to one.

At this point, he harbored a doubt. At the age of twenty-two, the monk Fang urged him on; before the Buddha image, the Master vowed that seven days would be his limit, and if he did not attain awakening, he would sever his own arm.
Consequently, he forgot both sleep and food, single-mindedly upholding this one phrase as his koan. On the seventh day...
At dawn, the sound of the bells resonated through heaven and earth, and his entire being was filled with joy and liberation. He then went to visit Master Puhui of Gushan to receive full ordination.

Having traveled to study under various renowned masters, he was acclaimed as a vessel of the Dharma. One day, while sitting in meditative concentration, he heard a neighboring monk say: "Let go at the edge of the precipice."
He accepted it with self-conviction; having passed through death, he was revived. He could not deceive the Master. The Master then suddenly composed a verse.
Later, he heard that Shi Xian had succeeded Tan Kai at Chengtian Monastery. The Master went there to pay his respects; once the formalities were concluded, Tan asked, "Venerable, how old are you?
The Master replied, "I was born at the same time as space. Tan asked, "Do you have anyone to accompany you? The Master replied, "From the beginning, I have never relied on another."
Tanhui said, "What is your own power? The Master suddenly gave him a slap. Tanhui said, "This fellow understands it this way!
He then appointed the Master to lead the assembly. One day, as the Master was about to step through the gate to present his verse, Tanhui asked, "What is that?
The Master presented his verse, saying, "I ask the Abbot to pass judgment. Tanhui took it and immediately threw it to the ground, saying:

"What need is there for such toil? At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. He covered Huitang’s mouth with his hand. Huitang said, "What principle have you seen that you act in this way?
The Master replied, "Today I have seen through you, Preceptor. Huitang said, "Thirty blows! Wait until another time. The Master said, "What do you mean by 'another time'?
If you are going to strike me, strike now! As he spoke, he slapped him. Huitang said, "Again, you act in this way..."
Mona. Later, he commanded the Master to enter the room and asked, "When the world has been swept away and there is neither seeing nor hearing, where do you go?
The Master replied, "A stone tiger crouches in the path. Tan nodded in approval. He then bestowed upon the Master a verse of dharma-transmission. The following year, Tan passed away.
The assembly requested the Master to succeed him on the seat at Chengtian Monastery. Not long after, they further requested him to restore the old site of Chongfu Monastery. Within three [years]...
Upon his passing, he established a monastic community (later succeeded by Tanxi).
Tianjin Xiangdeng Hao Yuegao Chan Master was the son of the Deng family of Bazhou. At the age of seven, he accompanied his father to lecture halls;

he took a fondness for sitting in the lotus posture and studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. When he reached the passage: "The fundamental nature is pure and still; how could mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? [he attained realization].

Feeling a sense of doubt and encountering a time of great hardship, he took the tonsure at Yun’an Monastery in Tianjin and subsequently went to attend upon Master Ciweng Sen. He asked, "The nature of reality is fundamentally pure and still;
how is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? Sen shouted, "Who taught you to speak like that?
The Master also shouted. Sen said, "Moss grows again upon the stone. As the Master hesitated, Sen struck him. He then went to pay his respects to Dajue Xiu.
At Wanshan Hall, the Master asked, "The fundamental nature is pure and still; how is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?
Xiu struck him and said, "What do you call this 'mountains, rivers, and the great earth'? The Master raised his fist and said, "What about this one? Xiu said, "Let it go."
The Master then gave a shout. Xiu said, "A fellow who rolls around with lumps of mud. The Master’s doubts were further intensified. While traveling to Mount Pan, he heard a monk reciting:
"Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all things within the true nature of wondrous function. He attained realization immediately and went to visit Xuezi Jing.
Jing asked, "If it is fundamentally pure and radiant by nature, how did the mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?
The Master said, "On a sunny spring day, the yellow oriole sings. Jing extended one leg and said, "Why does the old monk stand on tiptoe? The Master said, "A poor man thinks of his old debts.
Jing drew a line with his foot and said, "Speak a word here! The Master said, "I ask the Venerable One to withdraw his foot."

Jing said, "Not yet; speak further. The Master then gave a shout. Jing nodded his head in approval. Before long, Jing moved to Yongshou Temple on Mount Xishan and charged the Master with managing the affairs of the monastery.
When Jing passed away, the Master led the assembly in constructing a stupa for him at that same mountain.
The community then invited the Master to succeed him on the seat (as the successor of Xuezi Jing).
Yi Su-yeolrin (義水宜林天) was the son of the Kang family of Hwanggang. He received the tonsure at Anguk-sa in his native district and completed his full ordination (*upasaṃpadā*) at Aengnyan-sa.

Admiring the flourishing of the Southern School, he traveled with his single staff to visit various masters. Initially, he visited Tianjie (天界) in Jinling and, while contemplating the "Three Nots" (*san bushi*), attained a realization.
Upon arriving at Longchi (龍池), he saw the notice posted on the hall which read: "If there is anyone who studies the scriptures..."
Those who practice mindfulness of the Buddha, recite mantras, and perform prostrations reach this point and urgently seek repentance, remaining restless throughout the night.
The next morning, [Zhaozhou] entered the room, held up his fan slightly, and asked, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. He asked, "Why do you not understand?"
The Master said, “This is not within my domain. [The monk] asked, “From where have you come? The Master replied, “Huguang.

[The monk] asked, “How is the Buddha-dharma at Huangmei? The Master replied, “At midnight, it was transmitted to Luoneng; the clay ox returns to the snowy ridge. [The monk] asked, “As for the matter at hand, what is it?
The Master replied, “What did the Master say? [The monk] immediately gave a shout. The Master shook his sleeves and departed. He then went on to Zigai.
Tiantong and Yunmen were both in accord with his spiritual capacity. Finally, he visited Shanguang Mian at Daochang Monastery, where he profoundly grasped the profound essence of the teachings.

Mian appointed him as the head of the assembly. Not long after, however, there was unrest due to rumors of an impending invasion; consequently, he returned to Yishui in Chu Province, where he thatched a hut on Mount Yuqiu.

It happened that Donglin Shanduo was then presiding over the Dharma at Nengren Monastery. The Master went to pay his respects, arriving just as Shanduo was ascending the hall for the discourse. The Master asked:
"When the World-Honored One was first born, he immediately declared, 'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored. What is this matter of being 'alone honored'?
Daiyu said, "I have just encountered the mountain monk ascending the seat. The Master said, "A single branch of the unperforated flute blows forth ten thousand years of joy.
Daiyu said, "Rarely does one encounter a true connoisseur. The Master said, "From now on, walk with high steps upon the peak of Mount Hua; every dharma, every point."
Zhaozhou said, "I do not doubt at all. Daowu asked, "In what way do you have no doubts? The Master replied, "Looking up, I see the sky;

looking down, I see the earth. Daowu said, "Keep this in mind: thirty blows! That winter, he transmitted the robe and the Dharma to the Master, instructing him to ascend the hall as he had done before.
[He spoke of] the *liji* thorn—three leaves, five leaves—and the *vajra* circle—one, two: for the patch-robed monk to swallow or leap over.
[He] attained it. Upon the tip of a single hair, he laid down his weapons; one cannot leap over or swallow this. It would be a betrayal of a lifetime of traveling as a mendicant.
"How, ultimately, do you all proceed? He planted his staff and descended from the seat.

Addressing the assembly, he spoke on the karmic conditions regarding bringing a woman out of meditative concentration, and said in verse: "Holding a jade zither, playing beneath the moon; Careless and intoxicated, leaning against the balustrade. Silently...
The earth calls one back to the frosty night’s dream; azure peaks reach the heavens, mirrored by clear mists (Shandong in the lineage of Sisi).
Dayang, who became renowned as a Chan Master of Mount Shan, was the son of Chen of Qishui. His ancestors were noted for their filial piety.
From birth, he was dignified and grave; worldly pleasures never disturbed his mind. Once, while visiting Mount Pingdeng in Danye, he read the verses of the Seven Buddhas with his own hand.

Unable to bear parting with his books, he eventually went forth to receive the tonsure. He studied the Vinaya with great diligence, abstained from eating after noon, received others with compassion, and spoke in a manner that did not harm living beings.
The world hailed him as an ancient Buddha. While studying under Nengren, he attained the Seal of the Mind.

Addressing the assembly, he cited the karmic conditions of Linji’s three blows of the staff and composed a verse, which says: "When the dragon obtains water, its spirit increases; When the tiger encounters mountain scenery, its vigor grows."
Majestic and fierce! If the Dragon Gate did not send forth wind and thunder, how could one hear the sound of the vast waves for all eternity?
Furthermore, he offered this verse on the Old Woman Burning the Hermitage: Upon the withered tree, silver flowers cluster thick; Amidst the cold crags, auspicious mists layer upon layer.

His livelihood throughout the four seasons leaves his body untethered; Having witnessed the full cycle of heat and cold, he leans against the green pine. Where does he find anyone to provoke a look of anger? The Black Mountain...
Rolling forth the full moon; through iron walls ten thousand fathoms deep, all traces of dust are severed.
The Master composed one hundred volumes of the *Xuehai Yuanzhen* (The Precious Source of the Sea of Learning), which circulate in the world. (Shandong was his successor.)
Chan Master Yun of Shiyuan in Longquan, Huangzhou, was the son of the Zhou family of Macheng. He received the precepts at Xingshan Temple and shaved his head there.

Later, he visited Chan Master Tongshi to receive full ordination (*upasampadā*). Chan Master Tongshi appointed him to oversee the affairs of the monastery. In the Dingyou year of the Shunzhi era, he went to consult with Tianjie Cheng, but they did not reach a point of mutual resonance.
He then traveled south, visiting Hongjue, Gunan, Baoen, Yunmen, and Longchi; he found that they all possessed kōans and pith instructions.

In the year Gengzi, he returned to his hometown and attended Guangjiao Yujou for a long time. Yujou asked him, "If you wish to clarify everything that can be clarified, and to understand everything that can be understood—"
"Why is it that all the sages and worthies distinguish one another by means of the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*)?

The Master said, "You may know that gold and jade are easily distinguished, but how can you discern the heart of King Chu? He asked again, "It is said that when the Great Matter is not yet clarified, one is as if mourning for one's parents; I do not ask about that."
Because the great matter had already been clarified, he treated it as if he were mourning his parents. The Master said, "The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip;
the sweet melon is sweet from stem to end. Yushen Qian agreed with this. He then visited Xiangweng Yun and discussed the five houses of Chan, each having its own specific intent.

Consequently, he harbored doubts regarding Linji’s three blows of the staff and the subsequent remarks about "breaking the summer retreat" and so forth. Later, upon returning to Baitu, while enjoying the cool breeze, [he reflected on these matters].
Upon seeing the bright moon rise, that which had obstructed his chest finally dissolved. That winter, he lived in seclusion at the old site of Folin on Mount Dashi.

In the year Gui-mao, he moved to Huangjing Hermitage at Shimen. The Master compiled the *Wuzong Lianbi* (The Linked Jades of the Five Schools), searching extensively for the collected writings of the various patriarchs.
He then visited Guangjiao Temple, where Tai Fangzhang appointed him to preside over it. In the autumn, he passed through Hua.
Gui stayed at Xiaozhuan Bridge for several days, seeking out the pivotal sayings of the various patriarchs. Xiaozhuan said, "Based on your insight, you possess a capacity that surpasses others.
Wait until next spring, and I will have someone escort you to Jinming; there, surely a relationship between teacher and disciple shall be established."
The Master smiled and said, "If you go to Jinming, you will lose your descendants. Later, when he went to Longxing, the Master built a thatched hut on Mount Baiyun and compiled the *Huilianbi* draft.
In the spring of the Gengxu year, he again visited Longxing; at the conclusion of the retreat, the Master ascended the hall and bestowed upon him a dharma scroll.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Last year on the eighth day of the fourth month, I offered this body and mind to serve the dust-motes of all lands."
The land is utterly exhausted; it brings hardship upon the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. On this year’s fourth month, eighth day, the lanterns and the pillar pillars have all been struck blind at once.
Within the Lumbinī Garden, one is driven mad by the wind; what hands and feet can be used?

The staff, unable to restrain its impatience, manifests a supernatural transformation: leaping up to the Brahma Heaven, it contends forehead-to-forehead with ten billion voids. A fire-serpent swallows—
Turning back the Iron Kunlun, red flags upon the water—thousands, ten thousands, all burned to death at once.

A blow of the staff to the carp of the Eastern Sea, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "On the level fields and shallow grass, the pearl-waves surge.
At the head of Black Stone Ridge, there is a single phrase. Nanyue spoke thus; Mazu spoke thus; Linji also spoke thus."
Thus it is said. Yangqi spoke thus; Jingshan spoke thus; Jingci spoke thus; Chexi spoke thus;
Puming spoke thus; Jinming spoke thus; Donglin spoke thus; and Xin Longxing spoke thus. O assembly, do you understand it in this way? If...
If you understand it thus, you may board a bottomless iron boat and roam at will through the dark heavens and the celestial ponds, hooking those great *kūrmara* fish;

let the long wind pierce straight through. But if you do not understand, this mountain monk shall provide another commentary. (After a long silence, he struck the meditation seat and descended from the seat.
At the Eastern Grove (*Donglin*), during the Great Mourning Period, the Master ascended the hall and said: "That old fellow who hangs a goat's head while selling dog meat—this year..."
Once upon a time, what proof was there? On a raw iron griddle, Buddhas and Patriarchs were boiled alive; on a red sandbank, they ran into the Horse Boy.
This brought misfortune upon many, who were plunged alive into the Avīci Hell, causing the great earth to submerge and the entire world to become invisible.
Even so, tell me: when Dayun of Daini arrives here today, he does not even set foot across the threshold.
Without engaging in the roles of host and guest, how can they meet? Inserting incense into the burner, he said:

"As the purple cypress and yellow sandalwood first curl into fragrant clouds, the cock crows in the nine heavens and the phoenix displays its auspiciousness. (Shan Duo was present at this succession.)
Master Xingfu Degui of Yinglu was a native of Anlu in Chu. He received the tonsure at Hongshan in Ezhou and studied the *Śūraṃgama Sūtra*.
Having long resided in lecture halls, he heard that Master Shandao’s reputation was lofty and thus abandoned his seat to go and attend upon him.

While in the assembly hall, as the master raised the koan of the "Cypress Tree in Front of the Hall," Degui asked: "Master, you have lectured on many kinds of scriptures; from which canon does this saying originate?"
[Zhang] invited him to lecture on [the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*] for the assembly to view. The Master was at a loss. He requested to enter the hall to practice the seven-day retreat (*saptāha*).

When the retreat concluded, [Zhang] called for the Head Lecturer. The Master responded with an "Amen. Zhang asked, "Can you now lecture on the 'Pine Tree'? The Master felt abashed and was about to offer a word when Zhang said, "You have missed it.
He then rose and entered the inner quarters. The Master’s doubts grew even more intense; he read through the scriptures and treatises extensively, yet not a single word could resolve them.

Cuo then entered his quarters and bolted the door, severing all access to water and grain, vowing to remain there until he attained enlightenment. From outside the door, [Zhaozhou] pressed him with increasingly urgent questions.
On the fifth day, upon hearing the sound of the wooden board, Cuo suddenly attained awakening.

He rushed to the Abbot’s quarters, where he danced with both hands and feet, exclaiming, "This time, you cannot deceive me, Master! The Master said, "The Abbot’s kindness exceeds that of my own parents; I seek to enter as your disciple."
On the day he assumed his post and ascended the seat, a monk came forward and asked: "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas;
yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him, and he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood. What is the meaning of this?
Zhaozhou said, "A single idle man between heaven and earth. The Master bowed. Zhaozhou said, "How have you attained such directness and swiftness? The Master [remained silent].
[The Master] said, "Had I known earlier that the dragon was coiled within the deep waters, the overturning of the torrents and the toppling of the mountains would have occurred long ago.
[The Head Seat] said, "Do not soak the old monk's cassock. The Master dragged the Head Seat out and said, "Old man of the hall, today you do not have the advantage."

"Why do you not draw your sword to assist me? As the Head Seat was about to respond, the Master struck him with his palm, saying, "You have already delayed and killed one more," and then shook out his sleeves and returned to the assembly.
Dahui said, "He deserves thirty blows. One day, the Master met Shiyuan Yun;

they both let out a shout at the same time and each returned to their own quarters. A monk raised this matter and asked Dahui, "In the past, under Linji’s assembly, there were two head seats in the two halls..."
At that same time, they both let out a shout. Then a monk asked Linji, "Is there still a distinction between guest and host?
Linji replied, "Guest and host are clearly distinct. [The monk then asked: "Now, these two senior monks shouted at the same time; I wonder, is there still a distinction between guest and host here?
Linji said, "There is none. The monk asked, "Why is there none? Linji said, "It is not the same as with Linji. The monk then desisted. Three days later...
He again requested further instruction on the previous conversation. [Zhao]zhou said, "To truly understand the 'Dragon-Arising' guest-and-host phrase, you must ask the two donkeys in the hall.
A monk asked the Master; the Master said, "I will tell you when you prostrate. The monk prostrated, and the Master struck him. He then asked Yunmen.
Yun said, "Pass me the broom. The monk passed him the broom; Yun struck him as well. As the monk prepared to offer a word, Yun struck him again.
The monk prostrated and said, "What wonderful news! Yun said, "What are you saying, you donkey-headed fellow? If the Head of the Hall knew this..."
This breaks your waist. When the monk arrived at evening, he went secretly to the abbot’s quarters to report what he had obtained. [The Master] ordered an attendant to summon the Master and Yun;
without allowing them to explain, he gave each of them twenty blows of the staff and drove them out. [The Master] ascended the hall at Xingfu Temple.
"The spark struck by flint, the flash of lightning—this has already been cast down past the eyebrows; it has been missed. He struck his staff and descended from the seat. Ren [Year].
On the seventeenth day of the first month of the *xu* year, he manifested a slight illness, wrote a verse, and passed away.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the front ridge of his native mountain (the mountain name is *Duō*, and he succeeded to the lineage).
Chan Master Yushan Yue of Jingxi in Fuzhou was the son of the Xia family of that same prefecture.

Due to the chaos of the times, he went to Jinnazhiping on Mount Lu to leave the household life. He studied under Yonglian Wen and attained keen insight; his brilliance was equal to that of Shansheng and others.

He traveled extensively to visit various masters and lecture halls. Later, he called upon Zaiyuan at Huagui, arriving just as Zai was ascending the hall to give a discourse. The Master asked: "When the pivot turns the tiger..."
The leopard bounds; the jade of the mountains and peaks rolls; the divine whale rushes through the depths of the sea. The laws and commands are brand new—this goes without saying.
As for the fundamental principle of Linji, what is its intent? [Zhaozhou] said: "A flash of lightning bewilders the universe. The Master said: "A master of the school."
Tianran was still there. Zai said, "In how many households do people sorrowfully close their doors in the rain?
The Master prostrated. On another day, he asked, "A single flower in ten billion lands; in each land, one Śākyamuni. What is 'a single flower in ten billion lands'? Zai held up his whisk.
The Master said, "What is 'one Śākyamuni in each land'? Zai struck him with the whisk. The Master said:

The plum reveals its integrity only when weighed down by snow. Who is it that recognizes kindness and knows how to repay it? A man of old said: "Only upon hearing thunder does one realize the gravity of one's filial disobedience.

The Master prostrated himself and addressed the assembly, citing the case of Guăngcān of Jìngshān and Chōngxī of Chēxī. Whenever he heard their instructions, he would shed tears and investigate them with intense focus.

One day, he happened to pick up a scrap of paper which read: "One knows the other only through departure; the departed never returns. Only when one departs can one know the other; yet the one who departs never arrives.
Upon reaching these lines, he had an awakening. He presented his realization to Chong, who certified it. He was immediately appointed as the head of the assembly. The Master composed a verse, saying:
"The River produces the Diagram; the Luo River produces the Book. The Lan-tian mountains produce beautiful jade; the dark waters nurture the mystic pearl. This immortal form is not of human breed;
Hiding within the shell, it serves as food for the imperial kitchen. (Shan-duo succeeded him.)
The nun Zengfu of Qishui, Chan Master Shengzhuodi, had been with him for a very long time. One day she asked, "Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, you had already descended into the royal palace;
before emerging from the womb, you had already finished saving sentient beings. Today, for whom does the Master act?
As she stared at him with wide-open eyes, he said, "I thought you were someone. The Master then covered his ears and left. Di was there.

It is said: "A three-legged frog flies up into the sky. The Master resided in a hermitage to care for his mother; for twenty years he did not leave the mountain (according to the *Shandong*, this refers to his succession).
Chan Master Gulun Yu of Shangfang in Qian'an was a native of the local Zhang clan. He went to Nengren Monastery to shave his head and then entered the assembly for study.

Shandong was present. He illuminated the mind-ground and attended [the Master] for three years. When [the Master] departed for Longxing Temple, he commanded Shandong to succeed him on the seat at Huagui Temple to fulfill the vow of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
A monk asked: "The *Avataṃsaka* robes have been donned and the feast of the thousand Buddhas has opened; all protectors revere and honor you."
“I do not yet understand what serves as proof,” [the student] asked. The Master said, “The plum blossoms open and their fragrance wafts; the three winters are warm.
[The student] said, “If that is so, then you have cut off the tongues of all people under heaven. The Master said, “The spring falls upon the empty cliff; the nine summers are cool.
[The student] said, “At Huafeng, the Dharma rain transcends all; the blue-eyed masses of the great earth are all bathed in its grace. The Master said, “Shut your mouth! (Shandong succeeded him.)
When Chan Master Yan of Donglin on Mount Lu was about to don the black robes of a monk, he went to visit the Fourth Patriarch Xian and attained a realization.
He remained in his service for a very long time and served at Donglin, Nengren, and Longxing monasteries, where he was appointed to oversee the affairs of the monastery.
One day, because a speck of dust entered his eye, he asked: "The entire earth is the single eye of a śramaṇa; why then does it not admit even a single speck of dust? The Master replied:
"Today the Master has suffered a defeat," he said. "This is not within your realm. Thereupon, the Master [Shan-duo] emerged from the abbot’s quarters.
Chan Master Jinming Huaiyue of Jiaxing, whose secular surname was Wang of Qishui, did not eat meat as a child; at the age of seven...

Liwàn Fúxīn (Li Wanshou) had undergone the tonsure and ordination. While serving as an attendant at Mount Shānduó (Mount Huagui), he was instructed to contemplate the koan "The myriad dharmas return to one.

The Master investigated this day and night, finding no peace even in sleep or eating. One evening, hearing a rat gnawing on a glass bead that fell to the floor, he felt his body become like empty space, vast and boundless.
He composed a verse and presented it to Zhàizài (Zhaozhou). Because the Master was young in years, Zhàizài frowned and waited for him [to prove himself].
The Master also did not approve of him. At the age of nineteen, he received full ordination. He did not eat after noon and never sat with his side touching the mat;
he maintained his person with such refined purity that he served as the Master’s attendant for eight years. On one occasion during a formal interview, the Master asked:
"When the cup falls to the ground, the dish shatters into seven pieces—how do you understand this? The Master replied, "Into a hundred fragments. The Master said, "What is the underlying meaning?"
"What? the Master shouted. Zai asked, "Where does that shout fall? The Master said, "It splits open empty space. Zai raised his fist and said, "Can it break this?
As the Master was about to offer a reply, Zai suddenly grabbed him and pressed him down to the ground, saying, "Tell me now, what is this?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! At that moment, the Master was suddenly enlightened and said, "Venerable Master, please let me go."
As Guo was passing by, he immediately stood up. Master [Linji] followed suit and gave him a slap. Guo said, "Is that so? The Master slapped him again.
Guo said, "Do not act recklessly. I have long looked forward to you. The Master performed three prostrations with the words, "I take my leave. Guo said, "So it is, so it is.

One day, while the Master was casually reading the *Linzhi Zhengzong Yuanliu* (The Source and Lineage of the True School of Linji), he reached the passage where Huangbo sticks out his tongue. Suddenly, the Master...
His voice failed him and he cried out, "Agh! Huangbo, the old fellow, acted like this! He hurried abruptly to the abbot’s quarters. Baizhang asked, "What is the matter?
The Master said, "There is indeed a matter, but I fear it might offend you, Reverend. Baizhang raised his staff and struck him.
The Master seized it and shook it twice. Baizhang let out a thunderous shout. The Master nodded his head several times. Baizhang said, "Do you recognize this shout?"

"The great kindness is difficult to repay. The Master joined his palms and performed a woman’s bow, saying, "How constrained! How constrained! Being deeply affirmed, he was granted a verse of transmission.

Thereafter, he traveled south, visiting scholars and masters throughout the regions of Wu and Yue. At the request of the gentry of Jiahe, he took up residence at Jinming Temple. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The wisdom-life of all Buddhas and the mind-seal of the patriarchs are held forth face-to-face; they are to be borne upon one shoulder. Strike the poisonous drum upon the occasion."
Previously, he vibrated the great cosmic pivot before any signs had emerged, manifesting the very core of the patch-robed monks and flinging wide the heavy gate that leads upward.
Yet this was still merely the conduct of the ancients; it does not yet constitute transcending the standard or surmounting the lineage. Do you all understand? He suddenly seized his staff.
Zhuo Yi said, "If you can understand it here, what are Linji’s Three Essentials and Dongshan’s Five Ranks? They are merely trivial accoutrements.
If you wish to restore the noble path and turn back the final age, you must directly kick open the two leaves of the Hongmen Gate, so that auspicious vapors fill the realm in harmonious joy.
Addressing the assembly: "The Great Way of Emptiness and Mystery is fully manifest; in every thing..."
Every single thing is fully revealed. Where the sea moon and lake sky are vast and open, the emerald bamboo stands tall as the slanting sun sets.

Penetrating deeply through a thousand doors and ten thousand households, principle and phenomena are fused into a unity beyond all comparison. O virtuous ones, do not vainly speculate upon this single field of leisure belonging to the Patriarch;
otherwise, your descendants will suffer its lingering calamity for eons. [The Master] takes up his whisk and draws a circle (⊙), saying:
When the great assembly arrives here, you must have sweat pouring down your back before you can succeed. A General Address on the Dragon Boat Festival: Today is the fifth day of the fifth month.

The lunar disc is as large as a bushel; it shines through all five Mount Sumerus. Śunyata runs headlong in confusion, startling the deity of the peach-spirit talisman and smashing open the mouth of Śakra.
[The Master] picks up his staff, twirls it, and says: "O staff! You cannot bear to hold out any longer."
Forbidden. Following the custom, he performs a somersault and shouts, "Stop! Stop! One must not be reckless. He addresses the assembly:
"Before the fifteenth day, smoke mists the ancient ferry; after the fifteenth day, the moon wanes over the clear pool. It is precisely on the fifteenth day."
Green pines harbor white cranes; the azure pond blooms with red lotuses. Does Hanshan know or not? Worldly sentiments perceive warmth and cold;
human faces follow the rise and fall [of fortune]. To the Assembly: The hair atop the teeth parts as the Jade Palace opens;
sitting, one watches the dew-pillar conceive of itself. The child born does not drink the milk of the world; daily it plants numinous fungi upon the rocks. To the Assembly:
If we discuss this matter, I, this mountain monk, truly have no place to set my teeth; I can do nothing but speak it through for you all from the "second gate.
(He shakes his hand. "No, no! Evening Sermon: "The mind is not the Buddha; to act contrived is to deviate. Wisdom is not the Way;
to apply cultivation is still an error. From the Buddhas and Patriarchs of old down to the ancient masters of successive generations, they have spoken of the nature and mind.
To judge the ancients and the present is much like lighting a lamp in broad daylight. Here at Longyuan, it is not that we exhaust the Dharma until there are no subjects left;
rather, it is because those who travel a thousand li to seek a teacher will, if they do not encounter a master, end up as mere discarded vessels.

Those who enter my gate must be made to spit out the drool of the wild foxes and cast off the stinking garments of the hawk. Only when their bones are remodeled and their entrails washed, and they attain even a slight degree of resonance, will they be ready.
"In that case, King Yama does not fear much knowledge or great understanding; do not say he does not speak. [This was] a small-scale sermon (*xiao can*).
A monk came forward, stood with hands joined, and the Master said, "Who made you so topsy-turvy? The monk bowed his head and looked at him.

The Master said, "This old fellow does not even know the iron cangue upon his own neck! Thereupon, the Master returned to his quarters. Addressing the assembly, he raised the example of Chong of Chexi.
[The guest] said, "The world is as vast as this; why is it in the hands of this mountain monk?
The Master said, "Jingshan’s Way, though ten parts complete, does not spare his whole body from mud and water. Since the world is already in your hands, tell me:
where is this old man standing? He then rose and entered the room (Shandong was among those who succeeded him).
Dàbié Wéifànqí Chánshī of Hányáng was the son of the Liu family of Xiàogǎn. He took ordination under the elder monk Yuèlún.
Later, he visited Lóngxīng Zài and, while contemplating the koan of the "Three Not-Sos," he attained realization. He presented this verse: "The Great Mansion of Heaven conceals its form in darkness;
Mountains and rivers suddenly emerge, obstructing the eyes. The twelve jade towers have all been demolished before the pivot."
"Exposed alone is the person of old. Daowu asked, "What is the person of old? The Master then gave a shout.
Daowu said, "A single shout distinguishes guest and host; as for this shout of yours, is it the guest or the host? The Master said, "The Master sits; Benqi stands.
Daowu pointed to a pillar and said, "The ancient Buddha and the pillar intersect—what kind of occasion is that? The Master said, "Today."
He personally visited the Upādhyāya and received his approval. He served the Master for five years and fully mastered the subtle essentials of the teachings.

When the Master passed away, he traveled with Hui, Yue, and Xu to Jinming to see Dongyan Can. He visited famous masters throughout the two provinces of Zhejiang, and there was no one whose realization he did not accord with.
In the spring of the Wu-wu year, he returned to Chu with his staff, blending into the ranks of the untonsured laity, as he did not wish to serve as a model for others.
(Shandong succeeded to the lineage).
Chan Master Shi Hangzong of Puyun in Yingzhou first studied under Qixian Jing, where he received the essential points of the mind.
Later, he visited Longxing Zai and asked, "That which is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing—what is it? Zai struck him and said:
The color of snow stretches across the heavens in darkness; empty flowers carpet the ground. The Master asked, "Ultimately, what is it?
Zai replied, "Old Lady Zhang in front of the village; nun Li with her shaved head. The Master attained a sudden, vast realization and presented this verse:

"It is not mind, it is not Buddha; A raw-iron Kunlun Mountain serves as the universe. With a single squeeze of the whole body, the crown of the head opens through— the myriad phenomena stand in dense array."
Qizhu Wutu held up a bamboo stick vertically and said, "What about this? The Master (Zhaozhou) gave a shout. Qizhu struck him.
The Master snatched the bamboo stick, threw it to the ground, and said, "The Master cannot strike me today. Qizhu said, "Do you believe that I am not deceiving you? The Master prostrated himself.
On the occasion of the first anniversary of the passing of Longxing, the Master ascended the hall. After the Rector had finished striking the gavel, the Master said: "Yet, I have been caught..."
The Upādhyāya’s Way was eminent; he then descended from his seat. He passed away in the Wuma year of the Kangxi era.
His remains were enshrined at the side of the tomb of his preceptor, Longzuo (Shandong was his successor).
Chan Master Ruru of Longxing Dayun Monastery in Xinan was the son of the Yu family. He entered the community at Donglin and received the tonsure from Zai.
One day, he requested instruction, saying, "I wish to practice Chan; may I do so? Zai replied, "You may not. The Master asked, "Who then may do so?
Zai pointed to a pillar and said, "This one may indeed. At these words, the Master attained realization. Later, Zai moved to Neng.

When Renlong was about to rise [to prominence], the Master applied himself to his labors without slackening. When Renlong passed away, Shiyuan Yun succeeded him on the seat; the Master likewise acted as he had done.

When Yun moved to the Second Patriarch’s [seat], he invited the Master to preside over the assembly. The Master said, "What kind of person am I that I would dare to undertake such a great responsibility? Thereupon, [he declined].
He vacated a room of ten feet square to await a worthy guest. When he encountered several years of extraordinary famine, the Master remained serene and did not consider it a hardship.

He would often eat with an empty stomach so that food might be provided for the assembly. Monastics and laypeople from near and far held him in profound reverence. When the assembly requested him to ascend the hall, he recounted the story of a monk visiting He’an.
He’an asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "Mount Song. He’an asked, "Have you ever been to Wuru Peak? He replied, "Yes."
He spent the summer retreat there. A monk asked, "The rock by the side of the 'Listening to the Moon' (Tingyue) Cliff—is it large or small?
The monk had no reply. The Hermit struck him, saying, "When did you ever get there? The Master said, "Do you wish to reach Wuru Peak?
He suddenly held up his whisk and said, "All people throughout the great earth shall see one another here. (Shandong was in his lineage.)
Master Guiyuan Zongrusheng of Huang’an addressed the assembly. He cited the case of Jinming Jin: once, when he was attending Master Fanchu of Zhufeng, Jin held up a whisk.
Fanchu immediately shouted. Jin said, “All Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past have flowed forth from this very place;
do you see it? Fanchu said, “All Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past have come from this very place. The Master [Rusheng] remarked, “Jinming has raised his head.”
The main peak lifts its tail; father and son exchange places—this is truly enough to behold.
Regarding the matter of the ancestral lineage, there are many who merely speculate upon words and phrases, while those who understand it correctly are few. (Shandong was in the succession.)

The lay practitioner Hu Xinwei of Xinan had studied Confucianism since his youth. From birth, he was upright and intelligent. One day, he went to visit Master Zai at Longxing Temple to request instruction.
Master Zai said to him, "That you, a Confucian, have turned toward Buddhism is because the outward forms of Confucianism and Buddhism are difficult to distinguish."
Their Way is one and their minds are the same. When one exhaustively investigates nature and destiny, how could the ultimate principle be anything other than singular?

Now, the mind of those who study Buddhism is this very mind; the mind of those who study Confucianism is this very mind. Yao and Shun were no different from ordinary people, for they likewise possessed this same mind.

It is simply that each was drawn toward what was closest to their own habitual inclinations. Is there truly a superiority or inferiority between Zhu Xi’s veneration of *de-xing* (intrinsic nature) and Lu Xiangshan’s inquiry into learning (*wen-xue*)?
It is merely a matter of each pursuing what was nearest to their own disposition. For the Way, in its totality, is difficult to express in words.
Now you, sir, have set your mind upon the Great Way, yet find no door through which to enter it.

Therefore, it is fitting that you study Buddhism to investigate the principle of nature and destiny (*xingming*), thereby returning to the single thread that runs through all things. However, within this path, one must practice true cultivation and attain genuine awakening;

do not settle for something vague and indistinct, nor mistake the semblance for the reality. Do not be negligent or fail to strive, lest you waste your time in vain. I have often observed people of the world...

In establishing his teachings, he was unsurpassed by sages; yet in his conduct throughout his life, his actions were erratic and perverse. His fault lay in the fact that his four corners had not yet touched the ground.
I have once said to my disciples: "When all phenomena are utterly still, how do you rely upon them? When all phenomena are fully manifest, how do you dissolve them?
When myriad sufferings press upon the body, how do you dispel them? Use this to examine yourself and test your realization.
Only when one becomes such a person can they derive the benefit of daily renewal, come to know the Way of Ultimate Goodness, and penetrate the principle of True Permanence.
I observe that you are diligent and earnest; you are not one of those who study the Way with superficial or shallow understanding, nor is this something that can be discussed with such people.
The scholar had been practicing for two years. One evening, hearing the sound of the drum from the city tower, his body and mind were suddenly struck with awe.
He immediately went to Longxing Temple to present his understanding. Master Linji said, "This is merely the mind’s calculating and measuring.

As for that which is 'neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing'—what is it? The scholar replied, "Eating when hungry and wearing clothes when cold—what is so extraordinary about that? Linji said, "Except for..."
"Having put on your clothes and eaten your meal, how is it then? The Master said, "The bright moon is in the sky. Yunju Zhenai asked, "After the moon has fallen, how will you see one another?
The Master bowed. Yunju Zhenai said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? The Master let out a shout. Yunju Zhenai said: [approval].

Huyu. Once, when a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Huyu said, "The golden wind blows over the embroidered waters;
paulownia leaves fall upon the moss. A scholar commented: "If one were a truly eminent monk, he would know this for himself, as there is a covering upon his brow."
A golden breeze came for one night; the leaves of the *wutong* trees fell upon the steps and pavements. My intention was like an autumn cloud; my mind was like the bright moon.

(Quoting Nanming Guang, who studied under Jingshan Guzhan for a long time. One day, he happened to pick up a scrap of paper containing the lines: "Only by observing the direction does one know where it has gone; that which goes does not arrive at the direction. Upon this, he attained enlightenment and presented his realization to Guzhan. Guzhan confirmed his attainment, and Nanming Guang offered this verse:

The golden breeze comes for one night; The *wutong* leaves fall upon the steps. My intention is like an autumn cloud; My mind is like the bright moon. (Note: This verse is traditionally attributed to Nanming Guang, who was enlightened by the lines on the scrap of paper regarding the movement of a cloud across the sky.)
Suddenly severing all doubt, one probes the profound depths afar; within the void of the kalpa-jar, the wondrous is difficult to describe.
Now, gathered upon the tip of a single hair, a single roll of thunderous sound pervades the great trichiliocosm. (The mountain bell resides in the succession.)
Chan Master Rulin Ru of Suzhou was the son of the Pan family of Shanghai. His mother dreamed of plucking lotus flowers;

shortly thereafter, they bore fruit, and upon waking, she gave birth to the Master. He would not allow meat to enter his mouth. When he reached adulthood, both his parents passed away, whereupon he resolved to leave the household life.
He received the tonsure under Weiyi and studied under Er-yin Mi for a long time, basking in their presence. Subsequently, he visited Xingkong Zhen.
Later, at Fǎlún, he met Zhūān Yǎn at Ōuān; their spiritual capacities were in accord, and he attended him for five years.
While residing at Lianhuá Temple in Jīnshù Town, he ascended the hall on the Double Ninth Festival: "The golden wind rustles as crimson leaves fly;

the chrysanthemums by the hedge defy the frost, exhaling their late fragrance. The Chan practitioners beneath the forest trees willingly embrace their simplicity, laughing at the worldly custom of plucking flowers to wear."
*Evodia* (ju yu). How can it compare to the lotus? It is even more talkative. Adieu! To dredge for the bright moon from the depths of Lake Tai.
Addressing the assembly: The spring colors swirl as flowers fill the branches; The yellow oriole cries piteously as willows droop their threads.

To act with courage when seeing what is right brings forth a noble spirit; Only then does one know the man who transcends the ordinary. Ascending the hall: Today is the fifth day of the fifth month; it is precisely the Dragon Boat Festival.
The Festival of Yang. Chanting mantras over water and writing talismans—red mouths are all extinguished. Apart from mugwort, tigers, and dragon boats, there is nothing more intimate.
As for the lotus flower, there is yet another phrase; I shall not speak it to you. But tell me, what phrase is it? After a long silence, he said: [He remained silent.]
The *jiǎo xǔ* (tassels of millet) are as large as awls; the pomegranate flowers are red as blood (Zhū'ān Yǎnsì).

Chan Master Tiānrǔ of Xīnglóng Monastery in Běijīng was the son of the Sūn family of Suīníng. In his youth, he studied the "Green Box" (classical Confucian texts), harboring a resolve to transcend the mundane world.
He went to Fāngtíng to receive the tonsure and visited Mǐnzhōng to receive full ordination. He traveled extensively among the lecture halls, saying of himself: "In this life..."
At the point of death, he found no place where he could gain strength. He then went to visit Wan’an, who assigned him the koan on the "original face.

He investigated it diligently for three years. One morning, as he rolled up the curtain and saw the sun, he attained realization. Thereupon, he traveled south to seek instruction from thirty-five masters of the Dharma.

Later, he went to attend Miaoyun Xiong at Dabeichan Monastery. Xiong asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From the South. Xiong asked, "How do they discuss the Buddha-dharma in the South? The Master said, "It is no different here from what it is with you, Master. Xiong asked, "What use is that? The Master said, "One must still pass through it. Xiong asked, "Did you reach Yantou? The Master said, "I did. Xiong said, "He said, 'A mother gives birth... [The Master continued,] "...but she does not know her own child. Xiong said, "So it is; so it is. The Master bowed. Xiong said, "In the future, you will be able to hold up the banner of the Way for the sake of all sentient beings. Later, when the Master was traveling through the mountains, he encountered a tiger. He struck the tiger with his staff, and the tiger left. When he returned to the monastery, he told the assembly, "Just now, I encountered a tiger on the mountain path. I struck it with my staff, and it departed. A monk asked, "What did you say when the tiger approached? The Master said, "I said, 'The Buddha-nature is originally complete. "Seven sons—six did not meet with a true connoisseur; even this one was not worth keeping, so he threw him into the water.
What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The poor man regrets that his body is too many. [Xuefeng] asked, "Since ancient times, by what means have the great virtuous ones recognized people?
The Master said, "To kill a person without using a blade. Xuefeng struck him. The Master then shouted. Xuefeng said, "I shall go to the hall for study. He then relied upon the Master for two years.
Recorded: Gradually increasing the profound purport. On the first day of the New Year, ascending the hall: "The new year begins its reign; all things flourish. Birds sing and flowers smile;
mountains are high and waters are deep. Without a written seal, the pattern is manifest; the ancestral intent from the West is accomplished through non-action.
Old Zhao’s tea fragrance calls to guests; Golden Ox’s rice is cooked for the monks. Everywhere it is fully present; every thing..."

From the mind: Xiangyan struck the bamboo; Lingyun saw the flowers. Even up to raising a fist or pointing a finger, or striking the oars and shaking the bells—tell me, what matter of clarity is being revealed?
[He] brandishes the whisk twice and says: "Flakes of plum blossom present auspicious signs;
the sound of firecrackers announces peace. (Miaoyun Xiong’s Succession)

Chan Master Hongliang Tianchi of Dongchang was the son of the Jiang family of Huolou. Having studied Confucianism without completing his studies, he followed Master Wenzong to shave his head and receive the tonsure, and received full ordination from Master Taixu.
He then attended upon Master Shengyi, who instructed him to contemplate the koan of "the original face.

With keen resolve and without slackening, he happened to have an awakening upon seeing a mountain torrent cascading down; he went to pay his respects to Master Fengxue Xiji, who asked, "What will you offer me?"
When the Mountain Monk met him, Master [Huangbo] spread his two hands. Xixi said, "What is this? Master made the gesture of a palm.
Xixi struck him, saying, "Stop making such a fuss. Master shook out his sleeves and departed. Later, he saw Miaoyun Xiong at Dabeishan.
Xiong asked, "Where have you come from? Master pointed at the sky with his hand. Xiong said, "You wild fox spirit! He raised his staff to strike. Master then let out a shout. Xiong—
Linji said, "Linji has four kinds of shouts. Which one of these shouts is yours? The Master replied, "Even the Buddhas of the three periods of time cannot provide an explanation for it.
Xiong said, "I grant you thirty blows! Later, when entering the room, Xiong asked, "What was the meaning of Deshan’s bowl-carrying?
The Master replied, "Out of pity for a child of three feet, he did not spare his own two eyebrows. Xiong said, "Yantou gave him a secret transmission."
"What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The livelihood of a ghost. Xiong asked, "What do you call the 'final word'? The Master said, "A flake of snow falling on a red furnace.
Xiong then appointed him as the head of the assembly. He attended the Master intimately for three years, received his instructions and entrustment, and subsequently went to reside at Hongliang.
At the request of Confucian scholars, he ascended the hall. Holding up his whisk, he said: "The more one looks up at it, the higher it seems; the more one drills into it..."
"It becomes ever more firm. Looking for it, it is ahead; in an instant, it is behind. These are the bequeathed words of the Sage Confucius.

When I, this mountain monk, bring them forth before the assembly, do they suffice as the Buddha-Dharma? To lengthen the ducks and shorten the cranes is not without merit as a skilled hand; to level the mountains and fill the valleys is what truly defines a master.

This is not a matter of competing in cleverness or displaying prowess; the essential point is that Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism are one and the same, and that the monastic and the lay are no different.
Second, let me provide another commentary for you. The more one looks up at it, the higher it seems; one rubs one’s forehead in vain, unable to see its summit.

The more one drills into it, the harder it becomes; axes and hatchets cannot cleave it open. When looked upon as being before one, every step meets the path; when suddenly perceived as being behind, one encounters the source everywhere.
It stands out from its kind and rises above the multitude. Do you understand it thus? He lets out a shout and says: "By means of my..."
"Do you think I have something hidden? I have nothing hidden from you. [The Master] addressed the assembly: "I cite Wuhuan Chong of Mount Jing: A monk asked, 'What is the school of Deva?
Chong replied, 'A single character does not bear a stroke. The monk said, 'I am not asking about that. Chong said, 'A perfect circle does not bear a dot.
The Master said: "The perfect circle is not circled; the single character is not drawn. Demons and Buddhas are difficult to name—this is the patch-robed monk's [domain]."

The monk’s eye is blind; it fills and obstructs all of space. No one can offer a price for it. Suddenly meeting [it], one is thrown into a state of seven ups and eight downs (as recorded in Miaoyun Xiong’s Succession).
Chan Master Xingfu Tiangong Heng was the son of the Wang family of Zhending. In his youth, he followed his father to pay respects to Taixu, where he received the tonsure and ordination.

He then visited Jianmen Qian of Jinling, who assigned him the koan: "Who is it that recites the Buddha’s name? One night, while hearing the sound of rain beating against the window paper, he attained realization.
Just as Qian was dismissing the assembly, he asked the Master, "Who is it that recites the Buddha’s name? The Master walked from east to west.
As he stood there, Xueqian said, "Why are you running about in such disorder? The Master replied, "If one does not climb high to look out, how can one know the vastness of the blue sea?
Xueqian said, "Give me a word from beneath your heels. The Master then gave a shout. Xueqian struck him, saying, "Be careful; proceed slowly.

Because his mother was elderly, the Master returned to his hometown to build a thatched hut. Having long heard of Miaoyun’s eminent reputation as a teacher, he went to visit him. Miaoyun asked, "The wisdom of all Buddhas..."
"Profound! From where did you enter? The Master struck the incense table once. Xiong asked, "The ancients said:
