'First move with concentration, then extract with wisdom. What does this mean? The Master replied, "A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool.
Xiong asked, "If suddenly heaven collapses and the earth cracks, where will you find a place to settle yourself? The Master replied, "The golden incense burner."
Huating Irongonglun asked, "How can one act so as not to touch and yet not to turn one's back? The Master said, "The bamboo shadows sweep the steps, yet the dust does not stir;
the moon pierces the bottom of the pond, yet the water leaves no trace. Huating then desisted. (Miaoyun Xiong was his successor.)
The Chan Master Fupulian of Huangwang in Chu was profoundly adept in the secrets of Laozi and Zhuangzi.

He delighted in associating with monastics and traveled extensively among various monastic centers, possessing an air reminiscent of Lü Yan. Upon arriving at Jiahe, he found great affinity with Xu Huì, Yué Liáng, and Hóngdù, and frequently visited the home of Li Jiāoméng.
People of the time spoke of him as one for whom the Three Teachings had returned to a single source. (Kāngxī Gēn...)
The fifth day. Miaoyun Xiong was staying at Longyuan. Huie Yuexu requested him to ascend the hall. At the conclusion, Xiong said:

"His family naturally possesses golden bones; why need one carve them with sandalwood? The scholar (Shi) had a silent realization and said to Xu, "This old fellow has his tongue trailing on the ground today!
Xu then grabbed the scholar by the chest and said, "What principle have you seen that you say this?"
"What do you say? The Master said, "He naturally possesses golden bones; why must sandalwood be carved with such fine detail?
Xu said, "Try bringing forth those golden bones for me to see. The Master then gave him a slap. Xu pushed him away and said, "Today you have committed the offense of stealing the Dharma."
He reported this to his Dharma-uncle, the Abbot, who said, "I will beat you. He then went together with Jianxiong.
As soon as they entered the gate, the scholar asked, "What is the hidden meaning of the West? Xiong replied, "It is no different from here in our Eastern land.
The scholar asked, "What is the meaning of your being no different? Xiong took up his staff and struck him. The scholar then nodded his head in agreement. Xiong said, "You have seen it."
"What is the principle behind this? he asked, nodding his head. The scholar said, "Water flows back to the sea; the moon descends but never leaves the sky.

Xiong said, "I was almost about to call you a man of the Way (a *daoliu*). The scholar prostrated himself, and Xiong approved of him. Later, at the request of a group of fellow practitioners (*yushi*), [Xiong gave him instruction].
He returned to Lingxian Hermitage at Wutang. At the time of his death, he wrote a verse, saying: "Treading through the void, my whole body feels cold;
This single mass of flesh is as chill as cotton. Who can comprehend such a message? Far from being in the human heart, it is near to Heaven.
He passed away while sitting in the lotus posture (as recorded in *Miaoyun xiong si*).

Chan Master Tianwei De of Shanye Temple in Zhenjiang was a native of Danyang. He traveled extensively, visiting the Dharma seats of the Wu and Yue regions. Later, he went to pay his respects to Master Bei'e Xiong.
Xiong asked, "The 'Poison-Coating' drum resounds through heaven and shakes the earth; for what reason do you have keen ears yet hear nothing? The Master replied:
"One who knows the Dharma is afraid. Xiong said, "The great elephant of Jia Prefecture has been swallowed by a snake—what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "The small goes out and meets the great. Xiong said, "A single grain of rice fills the entire Dharma-realm; even the eight Vajras cannot lift it up."
"Why was it carried off by ants? The Master said, "The thief is a petty person; he who recognizes his error is a gentleman.
Xiong struck him and asked, "Where does this one blow land? The Master said, "The entire great earth returns to spring. Xiong nodded in approval. (Miaoyun Xiong’s Succession Record)
Chan Master Zhen of Guangping Dayunzhao Kong visited Chan Master Bei of Dabeixiong. Bei asked, “Elder, you have come from a thousand li away;
is there anything that does not move? The Master replied, “Presented face-to-face. Bei raised his fist and said, “Do you see this?”
The Master said, "Your compassionate heart is too earnest. Xiong said, "Setting aside seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, try to say something.
The Master said, "When I reach this point, I have a mouth that is only fit to hang on the wall. Xiong said, "I grant you thirty blows" (Miaoyun Xiong’s lineage).
Master Xiu Chan of Juehua Tianyi in Yixing traveled extensively to study under the various elders of Jiangzhe.

He subsequently studied under Dabeixiong, who, upon seeing him, recognized his potential and appointed him as the *karmadāna* (Vina). During a formal interview, Dabeixiong asked: "A person of transcendent capacity strides upon the crown of Vairocana;
where do you usually go about your daily practice? The Master replied: "In the Han-yuan Hall, one does not ask for Chang'an."
Xiong said, "When a lion crouches on the ground, the host of beasts clear the way; why then do you call it a tethering stake for donkeys?
The Master said, "It is to humble the noble and conform to the lowly. Xiong said, "This very person is inherent in everyone; each and every one possesses it. Why do you not recognize it?
The Master said, "Clouds arise from the mountain peaks; the moon descends into the heart of the waves. Xiong struck him. The Master shouted. Xiong—
He struck him again. The Master shouted once more. Xiong asked, "After three shouts and four shouts, what then? The Master shouted twice in succession.

Xiong rose from his prostrations and stood in his place. Xiong nodded in approval. One day, as the Master was taking leave to return south, Xiong said, "When the true mechanism is vast and penetrating, only then can one conceal one's brilliance in the mountains and valleys.
When the sacred embryo is fully matured, only then is one truly called an extraordinary man of the Way. Who says otherwise?"
A slumbering tiger is not to be compared with a crouching lion. When it roars, its sound shakes the universe; when it leaps back, it tears asunder the void.
It is not like the lame tortoise or the blind turtle, nor is it like one who waits by a stump for a rabbit. One day, when wind and clouds meet, [the opportunity shall arise].
At the time when thunder rolls and lightning strikes, one must by no means linger within the pond. Take care (Miaoyun Xiong’s Succession).
Chan Master Muren Chun of Kaiyuan Temple in Suzhou was the son of the Gu family of Kunshan. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations.

He left home for ordination under Xunshi, received the full precepts at Shuangta, and studied under Gudeng Jiong at Jinming, where he was instructed to contemplate the state before his parents were born.
As for the previous dialogue, he neglected both sleep and food. Jiong went down to the hall and said, "In applying oneself to practice, it is essential that the doubt-mind be paramount.
Re-grasp the *huatou* (critical phrase) as if it were a silver wall or an iron barrier; exert all your strength until, suddenly, you topple it over. How much joy and liberation there will be!"

Upon hearing this, the Master’s mind and world became vast and empty. He went out and asked, "As for the collapsing of walls, what is the underlying meaning? Jiong said, "What can one do about the bricks and rubble? The Master said, "I shall return them all to you, Reverend. Jiong said, "What of the original face? The Master said, "The single moon is in the sky; there is nowhere it does not illuminate. Jiong said, "And after the moon has fallen? The Master said, "The light remains. Jiong said, "Who is it that sees the light? The Master said, "It is you yourself. Jiong said, "How is it that you have come to understand this? The Master said, "I have no other way. Jiong said, "If you had not yet understood, how would you have answered? The Master said, "I would have said, 'I am not here. Jiong said, "If you were not here, who would be answering? The Master said, "The answer is already given. Jiong said, "What is the answer? The Master said, "It is not a word. Jiong said, "If you had not yet understood, how would you have answered? The Master said, "I would have said, 'I am not here. Jiong said, "If you were not here, who would be answering? The Master said, "The answer is already given. Jiong said, "What is the answer? The Master said, "It is not a word. Jiong said, "Excellent! Excellent! The Master bowed and withdrew. Jiong said, "I have been deceived by this fellow. Later, when the Master was about to depart, Jiong asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "To the place where there is no place to go. Jiong said, "If there is no place to go, why do you go? The Master said, "Because there is no place to stay. Jiong said, "If there is no place to stay, why do you stay? The Master said, "Because there is no place to leave. Jiong said, "If there is no place to leave, why do you leave? The Master said, "Because there is no place to remain. Jiong said, "If there is no place to remain, why do you remain? The Master said, "Because there is no place to arrive. Jiong said, "If there is no place to arrive, why do you arrive? The Master said, "Because there is no place to depart. Jiong said, "If there is no place to depart, why do you depart? The Master said, "Because there is no place to enter. Jiong said, "If there is no place to enter, why do you enter? The Master said, "Because there is no place to dwell. Jiong said, "If there is no place to dwell, why do you dwell? The Master said, "Because there is no place to be born. Jiong said, "If there is no place to be born, why are you born? The Master said, "Because there is no place to die. Jiong said, "If there is no place to die, why do you die? The Master said, "Because there is no place to live. Jiong said, "If there is no place to live, why do you live? The Master said, "Because there is no place to exist. Jiong said, "If there is no place to exist, why do you exist? The Master said, "Because there is no place to cease. Jiong said, "If there is no place to cease, why do you cease? The Master said, "Because there is no place to continue. Jiong said, "If there is no place to continue, why do you continue? The Master said, "Because there is no place to end. Jiong said, "If there is no place to end, why do you end? The Master said, "Because there is no place to begin. Jiong said, "If there is no place to begin, why do you begin? The Master said, "Because there is no place to conclude. Jiong said, "If there is no place to conclude, why do you conclude? The Master said, "Because there is no place to open. Jiong said, "If there is no place to open, why do you open? The Master said, "Because there is no place to close. Jiong said, "If there is no place to close, why do you close? The Master said, "Because there is no place to manifest. Jiong said, "If there is no place to manifest, why do you manifest? The Master said, "Because there is no place to conceal. Jiong said, "If there is no place to conceal, why do you conceal? The Master said, "Because there is no place to reveal. Jiong said, "If there is no place to reveal, why do you reveal? The Master said, "Because there is no place to hide. Jiong said, "If there is no place to hide, why do you hide? The Master said, "Because there is no place to show. Jiong said, "If there is no place to show, why do you show? The Master said, "Because there is no place to cover. Jiong said, "If there is no place to cover, why do you cover? The Master said, "Because there is no place to uncover. Jiong said, "If there is no place to uncover, why do you uncover? The Master said, "Because there is no place to grasp. Jiong said, "If there is no place to grasp, why do you grasp? The Master said, "Because there is no place to let go. Jiong said, "If there is no place to let go, why do you let go? The Master said, "Because there is no place to hold. Jiong said, "If there is no place to hold, why do you hold? The Master said, "Because there is no place to release. Jiong said, "If there is no place to release, why do you release? The Master said, "Because there is no place to bind. Jiong said, "If there is no place to bind, why do you bind? The Master said, "Because there is no place to untie. Jiong said, "If there is no place to untie, why do you untie? The Master said, "Because there is no place to tie. Jiong said, "If there is no place to tie, why do you tie? The Master said, "Because there is no place to loosen. Jiong said, "If there is no place to loosen, why do you loosen? The Master said, "Because there is no place to tighten. Jiong said, "If there is no place to tighten, why do you tighten? The Master said, "Because there is no place to relax. Jiong said, "If there is no place to relax, why do you relax? The Master said, "Because there is no place to strain. Jiong said, "If there is no place to strain, why do you strain? The Master said, "Because there is no place to rest. Jiong said, "If there is no place to rest, why do you rest? The Master said, "Because there is no place to move. Jiong said, "If there is no place to move, why do you move? The Master said, "Because there is no place to stay still. Jiong said, "If there is no place to stay still, why do you stay still? The Master said, "Because there is no place to change. Jiong said, "If there is no place to change, why do you change? The Master said, "Because there is no place to remain as they are. Jiong said, "If there is no place to remain as they are, why do you remain as they are? The Master said, "Because there is no place to become otherwise. Jiong said, "If there is no place to become otherwise, why do you become otherwise? The Master said, "Because there is no place to be. Jiong said, "If there is no place to be, why are you? The Master said, "I am not. Jiong said, "If you are not, who is it that speaks these words? The Master said, "It is you yourself. Jiong said, "If it is you yourself, why do you say 'it is you yourself'? The Master said, "Because there is no place to say anything else. Jiong said, "Excellent! Excellent! The Master bowed and withdrew. Jiong said, "I have been deceived by this fellow. Later, when the Master was about to depart, Jiong asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "To the place where there is no place to go. Jiong said, "If there is no place to go, why do you go? The Master said, "Because there is no place to stay. Jiong said, "If there is no place to stay, why do you stay? The Master said, "Because there is no place to leave. Jiong said, "If there is no place to leave, why do you leave? The Master said, "Because there is no place to remain. Jiong said, "If there is no place to remain, why do you remain? The Master said, "Because there is no place to arrive. Jiong said, "If there is no place to arrive, why do you
"How is it? The Master was about to open his mouth when he was struck with a sharp, painful blow and driven back.
He said to himself, "I clearly know this kind of matter; why can I not speak it? I have kept it within my breast for fourteen years, never having revealed it to anyone.
Suddenly, hearing that Miaoyun Xiong had arrived at the residence of Layman Chen Yumen to spend the New Year, the Master went to visit him. Their minds met.
Zhongshou said, "Bowing is it; not bowing is it. As the Master was about to open his mouth, Zhongshou struck him across the back.
When the Master again attempted to speak, Zhongshou suddenly covered his mouth. The Master attained sudden enlightenment and immediately prostrated himself.
Zhongshou asked, "What did you see that you prostrate yourself? The Master replied, "Today I am fortunate to have met the Master and seen the Golden [Egg]."
Master Ming stood in his place. Xiong said, "Are you not going to become the successor of Elder Gu?
The Master replied, "If that were so, I would not have come to see the Master in person. Xiong nodded in approval (Miaoyun Xiong was his successor).
Chan Master Fú of Tiānwū in Húzōu went to visit Mìoyún Xióng at Dàbēi. Xióng asked, "Where do you come from, monk?
The Master said, "I am a man from West Zhejiang; what are you saying? Xióng raised his staff and struck him. The Master then let out a shout.
Xiong held his staff upright and said, "Try another shout right here. The Master prostrated and said, "Today I have personally seen the Master.
Xiong nodded in approval. (Recorded by Miaoyun Xiong)

The layman He Dong of Suzhou, style name Chusheng, was a native of that prefecture. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations, yet he took delight in the matters of the Chan school.

Initially, he studied under Lingyan Chu, contemplating the koan "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. One day, Chu asked him, "What is this that is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing?
The layman was at a loss and had no reply. He immediately requested further instruction, saying, "I beg the Master’s guidance."
One day, Xuzhu said, "When I eat my meal, are you also full? The scholar replied, "Is there not some skillful means [to resolve this]?
Xuzhu asked, "How do you apply your mind to this? The scholar said, "I, your disciple, have ultimately no place to apply my mind.

Xuzhu said, "This very state of having no place to apply the mind is precisely where you must exert effort. From then on, his investigation was earnest. He once engaged in a prolonged discussion with Wuzizi.
He encountered the Venerable Sengxiong. Sengxiong asked, "What is your surname? The gentleman replied, "It is He. Sengxiong said, "What is your given name? The gentleman said, "Chusheng.

Sengxiong said, "The Layman is a man of Wu; for what reason are you called Chusheng? The gentleman said, "Venerable Sir, please do not make such distinctions. Sengxiong said: *Note: The term "居士" (jūshì) translates to "layman" or "householder," referring here to the interlocutor.*
"Have you not heard? 'The clouds and moon are the same; the streams and mountains are each different. " The Master said, "I, your disciple, do not speak in such a way.
Fengxue said, "Try to say it for me. The Master said, "The entire great earth is this very self. What is the same? What is different?
Fengxue said, "What about when the Vairambha wind arises and the great earth is consumed by fire? Where is the self then? At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened and prostrated himself.
He paid his respects. Master Xiong took up his staff, intending to strike him. The Layman shook his hand and stopped him, saying, "There is no need.
Xiong asked, "Where do you apply your mind? The Layman replied, "The entire great earth is already occupied by you, Master.
Xiong said, "Where, then, is the Layman? The Layman gave a shout. Xiong approved of him (Miaoyun Xiong was his successor).

Chan Master Xing of Nuo Yan at Longyuan in Jiaxing was the son of the Xia family of Wutang. In his youth, he pursued the study of Confucianism and extensively mastered the *Zi* (Confucian classics) and *Shi* (histories).
Having failed repeatedly in the civil service examinations, at the age of twenty-six, he experienced a miraculous dream and developed a resolve to transcend the mundane world.

While casually reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* in a monastery, before he had even finished half the volume, he set down the scroll and sighed deeply, saying: "If the ultimate truth is not understood, one will labor diligently over mere brushwork."
"What is the use of ink? he asked. Thereupon, he shaved his head in pure devotion and went to Jìngcí Monastery to receive full ordination under Yuányuán. He served him for a long time.

One day, hearing a monk cite the phrase, "One should give rise to the mind that dwells nowhere," he attained awakening. Later, he visited Mèng’ān Jué at Qīnglián Monastery and asked about the final stroke.
Only then did he reach the formidable barrier. He asked, "I do not yet know how to penetrate it; how can one pass through? Jué—

Holding up his staff, he struck [the Master] and said, "I shall not fail to provide you with a single thread of connection. The Master asked, "What is it like after being connected? Jue said, "Seven ways loose, eight ways free.
The Master then gave a shout; Jue struck him again. The Master restrained him, then gave a nod.
Jue threw down his staff and said, "Today I let you get one step ahead. The Master bowed, and Jue nodded in approval. [Later, Jue] ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said:

This is a single patch-robed monk. His radiance surges and his flames blaze; the five eyes find it difficult to perceive his limits. Like a flash of lightning and a clap of thunder, a thousand ears cannot hear his sound.
When he has completely departed, those who encounter him are few. Within this Dragon Abyss, there are times when it is thus.
Rolling back the Milky Way like a thousand fathoms of snow—sometimes it is not thus. Letting loose the myriad layers of light from the Golden Valley—sometimes it is not thus.
Yet within that state of "not thus," it is "thus": flower shadows shift, the moon moves, and fragrant stamens glisten with dew—sometimes, within being "thus," it is "not thus":
willow catkins blown by the wind, not a single speck remains. Within these four lines, there is guest and host; there is illumination.

"It is useful. Is there anyone who can examine it and get to the bottom of it? He planted his staff upright and said, "To cast fragrant bait and catch the golden-scaled fish, he spares no effort with his fishing line, repeatedly lingering in the water" (Master Meng’an Jue’s successor).
Chan Master Litan Li of the Fahuas Temple in Suzhou was a native of the Lu clan of that same prefecture. His father had no heir, so he prayed to the Great Being (Avalokiteśvara) of the South Sea.

Upon reaching Gusong Hermitage, he saw an elderly nun prostrating before the *Lotus Sūtra* (*Fahua*). She appeared as if they were old acquaintances, and when he asked where she was coming from, she replied, "I am seeking an heir.
He asked, "Will there be an heir? She said, "There will be; wait for one year. The father bowed in thanks. After the Lantern Festival of the following year, he saw [her].

When the nun arrived at her father’s house, he asked, "Could this be the venerable master Gusong? As soon as he had finished speaking, she announced that she had given birth to a son. Her father recognized her in silence.
When the master was a child, he delighted in seeing the Buddha. Upon reaching adulthood, he took refuge under Master Buer, shaved his head, and traveled to Mount Wutai to receive full ordination.

He visited more than ten spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). Later, he met Qinglian Jue and questioned him about what he had attained. The teacher said, "I have studied under various elders, but it has not been of any benefit at all.
I specifically beg for your compassion to open my deafness and blindness; if this great matter remains unclarified," [he added].
He vowed to throw himself into the rivers and seas to provide food for fish and turtles; his tears continued to fall like rain.
Yuanjue said, "In my place here, it is not like other quarters that seek to make their gates and courtyards bustling and popular. We only plant fields to earn our rice. You, go and plant fields.
After more than a month, the master went again to the abbot’s quarters. Yuanjue asked, "What about your field? The master pointed to his heart and then drew a circle, saying, "If..."
My teacher did not personally instruct me; for many years my remaining body was nearly swallowed by fish and turtles. Once, there was a monk holding flowers to offer to the Buddha.
Linji pointed at the flowers and asked, "When the flowers open, you see the Buddha. Where is the Buddha? The monk said, "Seeing the flowers is not with the eyes;
what the eyes see is not the flowers. Linji deeply approved. On the occasion of the Buddha-Bathing ceremony, he ascended the hall and said, "Everyone says that Śākyamuni Old Man was born today."
Yet, Śākyamuni the Elder has appeared in this Sahā world seven thousand times. Tell me, on which occasion is he manifesting today?
If you say it is not his manifestation today, yet here the monastics and laypeople request the mountain monk to ascend the seat—this would be like adding a point to an arrowhead.
[He suddenly raises his whisk and says: "Śākyamuni the Elder has manifested!"

"Do you all understand thoroughly? He then took a ladle and scooped up scented water, pouring it over the Buddha’s head and saying, "Even this little ladleful of foul water shall not be spared" (Master Meng’an Jue was his successor).
Chan Master Duanya Jing of Baoen Temple in Suzhou was the son of the Shi family of that same prefecture.

He went to Huayan to receive the tonsure and visited Baoguo Temple to receive full ordination. Initially, he frequented lecture halls; subsequently, he called upon Tiantong Wu, who instructed him to contemplate the phrase, "Who is it that recites the Buddha’s name?

One night, his body and mind both became settled. With a single strike of the incense board, his delusions were suddenly and completely resolved like melting ice. He immediately hastened to the abbot’s quarters; as soon as Wu saw him—
He then asked, "Who is it that recites the Buddha’s name? The Master replied, "When cold comes, one turns toward the fire; when hot, one seeks the shade.
Yuanwu said, "Today, King Yama is settling the account for the rice money. What will you do about it? The Master spread out both hands.
Yuanwu struck him, saying, "There is no need to bring out the stolen goods. The Master gave a shout and departed. Later, he studied under Qixian Qingzi Muyuan. Qing raised [the previous case]:
Ruyi asked, "Is there such a thing as this in Suzhou? The Master said, "Lately the royal decree has become somewhat strict;
it is not permitted to plunder the marketplace. Qing said, "There is no small amount of leakage here. The Master then gave a shout. Qing said, "Where does this one shout fall?

The Master said, "Two eyes facing each other, yet they do not recognize one another. Qing then struck him and appointed him to the position of Secretary (Chamberlain). [End of] the entry for Chan Master Qing.
He interrogated [him] every day without fail. On one clear day, he entrusted him with a verse. Later, he returned to his home village and resided at Baeon-sa (where Ki-hyeon was his successor).
The lay practitioner Yi Gyeong-am of Suui was upright and solemn in his conduct; he would not accept even a single coin of improper gain. Initially, he visited Geummyeong-jae.
He took up the phrase, "Where does one lead the one back to? and investigated it in secret for several years. While attending to his duties, he suddenly attained realization.
Later, after Master Jingjie passed away, he observed the ritual of a disciple under Master Xingkong. Xingkong said, "I and you were fellow disciples of Jinming; how can you have come to this?
The Master replied, "The Old Teacher himself would not allow us to be split into two separate parts. Xingkong said, "The Master is now our former teacher."
"Where? the Master asked. The Layman said, "I do not refuse to reveal it, yet I fear it might become buried.

Xing said, "One must not evade it. The Layman raised his fist and said, "The Old Man of Jinming has arrived! Xing said, "It is buried no small amount. The Layman asked, "And what about you, Master? Xing also raised his fist.
The Layman said, "It is the same kind of fist; why is it that for one there is attainment and for the other there is not?"
Xinghe said, "What place is this? Can you say it or not? The scholar was suddenly enlightened and prostrated himself.
Xinghe said, "Since you have realized this, you must cherish and protect it deeply. At the beginning of the year, the scholar went to visit Xinghe.

Xinghe asked, "How will you spend the New Year? The scholar held up his fist. Xinghe said, "I thought there was something else. The scholar said, "The faculty is alert and complete, with nothing left over."
Yuxing said, "Suppose someone were to ask: 'When Zhang Gong drinks the wine, Li Gong gets drunk. How would you respond?
Yushi bowed respectfully and said, "I humbly wish my teacher ten thousand blessings on the New Year. Yuxing said, "Sit and drink some tea. One day, Yuxing asked:
"Where are the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past now? Layman Shishuang held up one finger. Xing said, "And where are you now? The Layman then drew a circle.
Xing said, "How far apart are you and the Buddhas and Patriarchs? The Layman then gave a shout. Xing said:
The true lion roars well; the gentleman bows in homage. His nature was profoundly receptive, and he was granted a verse-seal (the successor of Kongzhuxing).
Chan Master Qianfu Jun of Puguang Monastery in Jiaxing, a native of the Xiao clan of Jinling, received the tonsure under Master Chunzhan at the age of seventeen.
He visited Master Jiubing of Guyun at Jinsu to receive the precepts and took up the koan "All dharmas return to one," yet for a year he failed to reach realization.
The student was utterly bewildered. Just as he stepped out the door, he encountered the temple steward (zhisu) asking, "Where is the official’s axe?
He replied, "It is still in its original place. At that moment, the master was suddenly relieved. He hurried back to the abbot’s quarters and said, "Now, Master, you can no longer deceive me.
Jian asked, "What is 'the myriad dharmas return to the One'? And where does the One return? The master reached out his hand and said, "Squeeze it! (Nia).
Folding his hands constitutes a fist; extending them constitutes a palm. [Zhaozhou] said, "That is not it yet. The Master then extended his palms. Zhaozhou said, "A fine thirty blows for you!
Finally, he met Master Mugong Jian, with whom there was a karmic affinity between teacher and disciple. He attended him for two years, during which time Jian questioned the Master about his travels.
The next day, the Master presented it to him. After Xuefeng Qian had finished reading it, he asked, "Is there anything more?
The Master replied, "Where could there be any deficiency? Qian said, "It is precisely because there is too much. The Master nodded in sudden realization. Qian then struck him. The Master bowed.
One day, Qian held up his robe and whisk and said, "Clad and seated before Mount Jizu; specifically coming to the head of Mount Dayu. What is the matter today on Mount Ping?"
Having no other choice, I shall annotate and critique this from the beginning. In the past, I obtained its hair from Boshan;

subsequently, I encountered more than thirty venerable masters and obtained its skin and bone; finally, at Jinming, I obtained its marrow. I have no desire to keep it hidden away, but present it whole to you.
Yet, this robe is certainly not something that can be constrained by outward form, nor is it something that can be fathomed by ordinary consciousness. Buddhas and patriarchs—
When he arrived, [the Master] did not dare look at him directly with his eyes. Now there is one whose teeth are like sword-trees and whose mouth is like a blood-basin;
this faceless fellow turns around and approaches his father. Suddenly raising his whisk, he says:
"Set aside what you have attained by studying under various masters elsewhere; tell me a single phrase here! The Master said: "A golden incense burner beneath an iron pillar."
Lun gave a single strike with his whisk. The Master prostrated. Yunquan then bestowed upon him the robe and whisk along with a verse.
He subsequently went forth to reside at Puguang. Entering the hall for the discourse, he said: "The Buddhas appeared in the world, and the Patriarchs descended as traces.

From the picking up of the flower and the wall-gazing, to the severing of the arm and the breaking of the smile—all these were merely transmitting errors through error and taking mistakes for correctness; they had no other purpose than to have you all recognize this."
This very thing. And what is this thing? Listen! Pines and bamboos brush against the Milky Way; Buddhist halls reach into the void. Birds sing and flowers scent;

the wind is pure and the moon is bright. It is manifest in every instance and clear in every object. If you can realize it here, you will naturally see the vast and unobstructed wind of Yao and the radiant, peaceful sun of Shun.
The seas are calm and the rivers clear; the people are healthy and all things flourish. Now tell me, the Dharma assembly is opened once again—what is it?
"One sentence on the initial promulgation of the Dharma-Regulations. Furthermore, how is it? "On a year of plenty, the village elders sing songs of joy;
together they rejoice that the auspicious grain grows with ears joined. Small Assembly: Quoting断桥 (Duangqiao) ascending the hall, he said:
"Deshan lowered his head; Jiaoshan nodded his head; Jueyi held up a finger; Xuansha struck and broke his toe. Raising his staff, he said:

"In the end, nothing emerges beyond the tip of this mountain monk’s staff. How do you see this? [The Master] strikes the ground with his staff and says, "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to the world.
The Master offers a verse: How many painted pavilions and jade towers? How many flower-lined streets and willow alleys?

From beginning to end, I tell the travelers: They are all right here on the Chang'an market. **Small Assembly (Xiao Can):** The Master cites the story of Chong of Chexi. While he was burning firewood...
A monk asked, "What is the self-nature, the true and heavenly Buddha? Chong said, "Bring me a bundle of firewood. When the monk had brought the wood, he asked again.
Chong said, "This slave does not even recognize good from evil," and struck him. The Master composed a verse:
Seeking the spring colors at the mouth of the Peach Blossom Spring, The rustic old man calls out repeatedly, "He is right here! Having wandered through the gardens and groves, one still...
Inquiry: It is not known where he dwells amidst the myriad flowers (by Mu Gong Qian Si).
Chan Master Zhan of Baizhong Cielin in Meizhou was the son of the Hong family of Dahé in Huāi'ān. He shaved his head and received full ordination.
He visited Jia Shan Ba’en, but in all cases he did not find resonance. Finally, while at Xin Kongzhai, he met Ping Shan Qian.

One night, while attending to him, Qian took out some paper and a candle. As soon as the Master reached out to receive them, Qian blew them out. At that moment, the Master attained realization and prostrated himself.
Xuefeng Qian said, "Where have you been? The Master replied, "The Dragon Gate has no guests who stay overnight. Qian asked, "Why do you not stir up waves and create billows?
The Master let out a thunderous shout. Qian struck him, saying, "I cannot let this pass. Later, they were walking through the moonlight.
I happened to arrive at the Duānběntáng Hall. Raising my eyes, I saw the bright moon suspended in the sky; my mind became vast and open, completely forgetting my body and surroundings.

Suddenly, as I stepped on a stone, it made a sound, and my lingering doubts were instantly dispelled. I composed a verse to present to Master Qiān, saying: "The solitary orb, pure and bright, is like a mirror polished against the heavens;
Light flows through above and below, like a pearl rolling upon a tray. Its pervasive elegance is peerless; within the myriad worlds of the great chiliocosm, it leaves no trace."

Qian [Xiaoshan] was profoundly impressed by him. Having personally attended the Master for two years, he thoroughly understood the subtle essence of the teachings. Qian then bestowed upon him a verse.

[The Master] ascended the hall and, citing the occasion when Venerable Piṇḍola Bharadvāja raised his eyebrows while King Aśoka was offering a vegetarian feast to the inner court, concluded the discourse.
The Master said: "When King Yuyang was smeared with filth by Piṇḍola, at that moment [the King] saw him raise his eyebrows and struck him across the face with his palm.

He waited for [Piṇḍola] to say, 'I am also among those invited by the Buddha to the Anavatapta Lake for the midday meal,' but [the King] merely joined his palms and said, 'Thank you, Venerable One, for your instruction.
Watch how he brings it to a conclusion. Small Assembly: The Master raised the case of the Host of Ruiyan.
Master Gu. The verse says: "Spring mountains, piece by piece, five-colored petals fly; Among the cries of the cuckoo, this is most pitiable.
It calls until the setting sun blurs the mountain shadows— How many can truly know this heart? (Master Mu Qian’s successor).
Chan Master Tian Sheng of Huzhou, whose secular surname was Xiang of Jiaxing, was born in the year Wuchen (1052). At the age of sixteen, he developed a resolve to transcend the mundane world.

That same year, while fleeing the chaos of war at Shengxi, he encountered Master Su Hua lecturing on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, through which he attained a profound realization. Later, he paid his respects to Master Yue Xian and received the tonsure.
He studied the teachings and contemplations of the Tiantai school and listened to the lectures of Master Yu’an Yu. Subsequently, he visited Master Yun of Xuedou to investigate the three [mysteries].
He traveled [to various teachers] until Yun entered into stillness; thereupon, he went on a pilgrimage to study under all masters. Later, he visited Bingshan Qian.

Qian struck the incense table with his bamboo staff and asked, "From where does this sound arise? The Master replied, "It arises from the mind. Qian asked, "Where is the mind? The Master replied, "Where is the hearing? Qian then bowed.
One day, while following Qian to visit Jinming Jin, Jin asked, "What practice have you been doing? The Master—
[The Master] said, "There is no 'effort' (kung-fu). [The other] said, "It is not spent in vain. The Master said, "A good son does not spend his father’s money.
[The other] asked, "What is your name? The Master said, "Shi Wang (Master King). [The other] said, "Since you are Master King, why are you being ridden by Mañjuśrī?
The Master said, "Old and decrepit as I am, you speak such words. He then turned to Guqian and said, "To stand out from the crowd, one must be a truly heroic person. The Master [continued].

[The Master] said, "Do not defile others with your likes. As soon as [the monk] stepped forward, the Master struck him. The monk prostrated himself. The following day, Xuefeng Qian bestowed upon him the verse-seal (gāthā-mudrā).
He ascended the hall and raised the case: Linji asked a Dharma master, "What sutras and śāstras have you studied? The master replied, "I have roughly studied the *Śata-dharmaka-vidya-śāstra*.
Linji said, "There is one person who has clearly realized the three vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings; there is another person who, regarding the three vehicles and the ten..."
Regarding the teaching of the two divisions—attainment and non-attainment—as to whether they are the same or different: it is said that attainment is sameness, while non-attainment is difference.
Luopu asked: "What is it here that gives rise to speaking of sameness and difference?
Jiehui asked Luopu: "And what about you? Luopu then shouted. After Jiehui saw the presiding master off, he asked: "Just now, was that your shout, old man?"
Sengna said, "Yes. Puji then struck him. The Master said, "In either case, it was merely passing through by borrowing the road; there was nothing extraordinary about it.
At that time, had you been asked, 'Was it you who shouted at the old monk? you should simply have replied, 'The ancient Buddhas passed away long ago.'"
He disciplined the old man Linji with a different eye, and moreover, provided him with a path for his emergence (as recorded in *Mugong Qian’s Succession Record*).
Layman Luo Shaotang of Xiushui, whose courtesy name was Xuepao, heard at a young age that all natures are empty.

When he discussed Chan with monastics, it was as if it were a long-standing habit. He once asked Master Xing, who said, "This is not something you know. The layman replied, "I, your grandson, have already—"
Xing said, "I know you have attained it. The scholar said, "Try to explain it to me. Xing said, "If one can speak of it like the Patriarchs, that is not true knowledge.
The scholar marveled at this, saying, "From where did you obtain such news? Xing replied, "I obtained it from the realm of the inconceivable.

From then on, he frequently engaged Xing in debate regarding this matter, and his understanding of its profound principles grew day by day. Later, when Xing fell ill, Tiao Shizhen went to inquire after his health.
Next, Xingzhi addressed the Master, saying, "My young grandson has some glimmers of insight regarding his fundamental task.

I beg you to grant him further instruction so that he may advance even further on the tip of the staff, thereby no longer being deceived by others. The Master then asked Huizheng, "How does one progress when at the top of a hundred-foot pole?
Huizheng replied, "One must simply take a single step and tread right to the bottom. The Master said, "But what about..."
"Trample it to the bottom! And what then? Zhen said, "I will tell you once you have turned yourself around and thrown yourself back.
The Master (Shi) then gave a shout. Zhen asked, "Where does this one shout fall? The Master replied, "The void splits asunder. Zhen and Xing laughed heartily.
One day, Zhen said to the Master, "In the past, He Taishou obtained Tian Suanan; after Suanan, he obtained four [others]."
This man’s Dharma-path has spread widely throughout the world. I have received the essential teachings of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* and now wish to entrust them to you, my son.
The scholar said, "Who is Shao Tang? How would I dare to undertake such a responsibility? Xing said, "Based on what I see in you, you possess qualities that surpass those of ordinary men."
"This is a matter within my own lineage; do not decline it. The scholar then prostrated himself. Yan took the name Ji Che and was invested with a verse (Tiao Shiyan succeeded him).
Chan Master Jintian Duoyuan ascended the hall and said: "Within heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a single treasure hidden within the mountain of form.
To speak in such a manner is much like encountering a royal banquet when hungry yet being unable to eat, still passing the days with an empty stomach.
I, this mountain monk, am not so. Within heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a single treasure..."
"Treasure! It is not a mountain of gold or beautiful jade, nor is it a dark pearl from the crimson sea. [The Master] suddenly held up his whisk and said, "Look! Look!
Then he cast it down and said, "The sword has long since departed; you are merely carving marks upon the boat. To the assembly, the Master took up his staff and said:
There is a koan that the Buddhas of the three periods have never spoken of, and the patriarchs of successive generations have never raised.
Today, this mountain monk, unable to restrain his impatience, has specially brought it forth for you all.
(He makes a gesture with his staff as if rowing a boat and calls out: "Do you understand, great assembly? If not, I shall speak of it myself. (He chants aloud:)
He chanted aloud: "From this moment on, there is no returning; once one returns, it is attained. Over the misty waves of the Five Lakes, who would dare to vie?
He then made the gesture of rowing a boat and descended from his seat. (This is from the *Biexuan Huasi*).
Master Song Chan of Maolin in Wu County was the son of the Tang family. His ancestors had followed the Confucian profession, yet he possessed a resolve to transcend the mundane world.

He eventually went to the Great Compassion [Bodhisattva] Hall, where he took the tonsure upon making his prostrations. He investigated the "Patriarchs' Life-Story" kōan for a long time without attaining realization. One day, while prostrating himself on the ground before the Buddha, he...
Zhenze immediately resolved his doubts. Zhenze presented a staff and said, "Do you recognize this? The Master replied, "It is but a piece of furniture.
Zhenze asked, "What was it before your mother was born? The Master replied, "The nostrils still rest upon the upper lip. Zhenze approved.
One day he asked, "The entire world of the ten directions is but a single flower branch; try picking it up and showing it to me. The Master...
Tuo said, "This too begins from the head. Zhen said, "Not yet; speak further. Tuo said, "Does the Master dislike it being too little?
He then struck him with his whisk. Tuo bowed, and Zhen nodded in approval (Anhua Zhen was his successor).
The Chan Master Sulun of Jiuyang Huguo was a native of Henan. He traveled extensively throughout Jiangsu and Hubei, yet he remained unable to attain a state of profound stillness.
He went specifically to call upon Master Xing at Duoyun Monastery; as soon as he entered the gate, Xing asked, "What is it? The Master replied, "I wish for you, Reverend, to have doubts about it.
Xing, with an expression of anger, shouted, "You wild fox spirit! He immediately pushed him out of the room and bolted the door. The Master said, "For a long time I have admired..."
"Venerable Master, out of your compassion, please grant us a skillful means. Xing did not respond. The Master stood in attendance until late in the evening;
just as the attendant in charge of the quarters came out with a lamp, the Master suddenly attained realization. He seized the attendant and cried out, "Venerable Master, come quickly!
I have caught a thief! Xing came out and asked, "Where is the thief? The Master pinched Xing’s shoulder twice.

He said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice. Xing then permitted him to enter the room. One day, he commanded the Master to compose a verse on the occasion of the World-Honored One holding up a flower.
The Master spoke spontaneously: "Before the flower was held up, it already smiled; Once it was held up, who else would laugh at its blooming?
Since the Dhūta first felt shame, It has caused all people of this age to suspect him. Xing said, "After the flower bloomed, what then?"
"How is it? The Master said, "A night of lingering, cold rain; the flowing waters throughout the city are fragrant. Xing nodded in agreement (Duyun Xing was his successor).
Chan Master Dunfeng Rui of Jixian was surnamed Kuang. A native of that prefecture, he failed several times to pass the provincial examinations.

In his frustration, he resolved to leave the mundane world and traveled extensively to visit renowned masters of both Chan and doctrinal Buddhism. His spirit and bearing were outstanding and unrestrained; everyone he met praised him without exception.

Later, he met Master Yuan at Longxing Monastery; their spiritual affinity was such that they were like teacher and disciple. He attended upon him for three years. One day, as Yuan ascended the seat, he raised the following case:
"A monk asked Baofu, 'Throughout his life, what words or phrases did Xuefeng have that could be compared to a wild goat hanging from a tree branch?
Baofu said, 'I cannot act as Xuefeng’s disciple. Yuan then said, "If someone were to ask Biyun, 'Throughout his life, what words or phrases did Jinming have...'"
"What words or phrases could possibly resemble [the state of] 'the deer hanging from its horns'? He simply said to him: "Jinming cannot be my original teacher.
Now tell me, is this the same as what the ancients said, or is it different? Is there anyone who can distinguish between them? Come forward and speak!
As soon as the Master stepped out, he gave a shout. Yuan held up his whisk and said: "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows..."
Hutou said, "Furthermore, tell me: from what does this arise? The Master said, "Today I must not let you, the Abbot, be left disappointed.
Yuan said, "How do you employ it? The Master struck once with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*). Yuan said, "What is it like after having employed it? The Master said:
"Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. Yuan took up the dharma scroll and said, "This talk has been passed down from the Buddhas and Patriarchs until it reaches this mountain monk.
Right now, every one of you, Venerable Ones, is entirely within the bag of this very talk. The Master said, "The prophecy at Vulture Peak had not yet reached such a state.
Yuan handed over the scroll, and the Master then prostrated himself. He subsequently appeared in the world at Jingxi, where his recorded sayings were circulated.
[Se (Baoen Yuan’s successor)].
Chan Master Jiqin Binzhi of Jiulian in Yangzhou first studied under Master Shokui Zhi. While contemplating the "Unborn" koan, he was suddenly enlightened by Zhi’s single kick.
He then presented this verse: "With one kick, I overturned the iron cauldron; The heavy barrier was broken through with a burst of spirit."
Chunrong said, "The void strikes the earth; Mount Sumeru dances. Countless songs and music fill the imperial palace.
Zhizhe asked, "When the void strikes the earth, where do you establish your body and life? The Master said, "At this point, I have a mouth but words will not come forth.
Zhizhe asked, "Why will they not come forth? The Master said, "My tongue has no flesh. Zhizhe said, "A fine three blows for you!"

"Ten blows! Thereafter, he traveled extensively to visit renowned masters, and there was none with whom he did not find resonance. For nearly twenty years, he remained close with Xu, Huì, Yuè, and Yǒu.
When he heard that Xu was residing at Gānlù, the Master crossed the river to visit his old friend. He encountered Xióng returning to Shānběi Dàbēi from the three pagodas of Hé.
The Master said, "I have long admired the Master’s lofty character, yet I have lacked the opportunity for a personal audience. Xióng replied, "Right now..."
"Is this with conditions? Is this without conditions? The Master said, "I am glad you have personally seen the Abbot. Xiong asked, "What is the matter of having personally seen him?
The Master said, "I happened to come here to pay my respects; how would I dare act so hastily? He then struck Xiong directly on the face.
The Master bowed and said, "Truly, his reputation is not spread in vain. Xiong asked, "How do you see it? The Master said, "Be careful," and returned to his place.
Lilongxiong then bestowed upon him a verse and conferred his seal (the successorship of Miaoyun Xiong).
Chen Suohancha, a lay practitioner from Suzhou, was a native of that same prefecture. He was skilled in the medical arts of Qihuang and aspired to the Chan school.
I have been in the company of Master Jinming for over ten years. While investigating the koan "The myriad dharmas return to one," I attained a point of realization.
Once, while I was compounding medicine, Jinming said, "When Mañjuśrī ordered Sudhana to gather medicinal herbs, Sudhana picked up a blade of grass and presented it to Mañjuśrī.
Mañjuśrī said, 'This medicine can both kill people and bring people to life. How do you understand this? The Master replied:
"Only by knowing gratitude can one understand how to repay it. Jiong struck him and said, "What kind of medicine is this? Try to swallow it and spit it out!
The Master then gave a shout. Jiong said, "You must not shout. You must not clench your fists or point your fingers. Speak a single phrase! The Master said:
"The winter cold is severe. Please return to a warm room to deliberate. Jiong took his leave. On the eve of the year of Jiawu, Longyuan Xiong arrived at Duxuelou.
The scholar Huaixiang came to pay his respects; there was a rapport between them like that of water and milk.
Xiong said, "Tonight, Old Yan will settle your bill for the meal. How will you respond? The scholar replied, "The wind blows a flake of snow to patch the plum blossoms."
Xiong asked again, "What is it that 'the myriad dharmas return to the One'? The Master said, "A rooster, cold, climbs a tree. Xiong asked, "Where does the One return?

The Master said, "A duck, cold, dives into the water. Xiong asked, "How about 'leaving the old to welcome the new'? The Master said: The rooster, cold, climbs a tree; The duck, cold, dives into the water. Leaving the old to welcome the new— What else could it be?
"The affairs of the evening are many. Tomorrow I shall offer my felicitations to the Master on his New Year’s Day.

Daowu took up his staff, tossed it to the ground, and said, "The white ox in the open field has turned over. The official then prostrated himself. Daowu nodded in approval and bestowed upon him a verse, saying:

"The heart-lamp of the Buddhas and Patriarchs shines without partiality; Lamp after lamp is transmitted from ancient times to the present. The true source is a single thread, without distinction between black and white; This matter..."
Never deceiving himself (from the *Miaoyun xiongci*):
Chan Master Wenyong Dongyanyao of Yutian was the son of the Wu family of Muye. In his youth, he relied upon Huishan to receive the tonsure.
He received full ordination at Minzhong. Later, he went to attend Dabeizhe. As soon as Zhe saw him, he asked:

"When one has died and been cremated, where does one establish one's dwelling and sustain one's life? The Master replied: "It outshines the past and cuts off the future. Zhe asked: "Ultimately, what benefit do you derive from this? The Master then gave a shout. Zhe said:
"I have thirty blows for you; let us wait for another time. He was then ordered to enter the room. Zhe asked: "The Buddha..."
The Patriarch’s direct transmission: "Ultimately, what has been transmitted? The Master said: "The eyes of the thousand sages are wide open; the radiant light pervades the nine realms.
Zeshao said, "So it is, so it is," and he then bestowed upon him a verse: "The eyes of the thousand sages are wide open; The radiant light pervades the nine realms.
Taken up directly with a trusting hand, It comes from the single stream of Caoxi. (Zeshao was the successor.)
The literatus Layman Liang Hong, courtesy name Chongci, was a native of Yunzhong. At the time of his birth, his mother dreamed that the Three Great Beings entered her chamber.
When he first began to speak, he overheard his grandmother reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "All conditioned phenomena are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows.
Upon hearing this, he attained a realization. He first visited Dabeizhe, who instructed him to investigate the question: "Where does the one return? One night, suddenly...
When subject and object were both forgotten, he could not find them even upon searching. He then presented this verse: "The four elements originally have no form;
where can body and mind rest? The autumn wind stirs the green bamboos; one night, the pillow beside me grows cold. [The Master] approved of this and recorded his realization with a verse.
One day, while crossing a river with a monk, he asked: "The fishing line is a thousand feet long, yet the intent lies in the deep pool. Before the line has even been lowered—"
"How is it now? The monk had no reply. The layman said, "There are no fish in this water. The monk said, "Why do you not pull in your line?
The layman said, "Today is not a favorable day. A fellow student was lecturing on the *I Ching*, saying, "The sixty-four hexagrams do not depart from the Great Ultimate (*taiji*).
The layman asked, "How was it before the Great Ultimate was divided? The student was speechless. The layman said, "It is fortunate that you are speechless; thus you have been saved."
Half asked: "When two dragons struggle over a pearl, who is the one that gets it? The Master said: "Exposed. He spoke in verse: "The full, bright moon is right in the sky;
Its reflections in lakes, seas, rivers, and streams are not the same. Laughing, he takes his jade whip and lashes the stone horse;
With a single roar, he dances in the western wind. Question: "The entire earth is water; tell me, whose nostrils are being submerged?"
[The Master] said, "Rotten. The monk asked, "The entire earth is water; tell me, whose nostrils are not soaked rotten? He then offered this verse:
"A crow within the sun; a hare within the moon. Above heaven and below heaven, the radiance stands alone revealed. (Shigao was thus his successor.)
The lay practitioner Zhang Zhu of Funing, whose courtesy name was Nianyi, initially did not believe in Buddhism.

He generally prohibited the use of characters related to monasteries, stupas, bells, and chimes within his writings. However, upon visiting the Great Compassionate One (Avalokiteśvara), he began to feel remorse.

He then pursued the inquiry into the original face prior to the birth of one’s parents, reflecting on the words from the *Book of Changes*: "In its stillness it does not move; when stimulated, it penetrates all."
Having attained awakening, he once said to a scholar, "If you have a staff, I give you a staff;
if you have no staff, return my staff. The scholar replied, "Thank you for the Master’s profound and compassionate heart.
The Master then asked, "What is the household style of a layman? The scholar said, "Birds fly over bamboo leaves as the first frost falls; a man stands by a plum tree..."
When Huayue was at the height of his influence, Ze said, "I require you to take up this responsibility. Shishi replied, "Everyone has their share.
Ze then confirmed him with a verse (Shige succeeded him).
The layman Liang Hou of Datong, whose courtesy name was Shumin, was one who understood expedient means and mastered adaptability; yet he was simple, reserved, and dignified.

He would often say to others, "To retreat one step is the dharma of peace and happiness. Once, while sitting alone in reflection, he wondered, "In the midst of responding to the world, where is the true host?
Hearing the cry of wild geese in the air, he suddenly attained realization. He went to visit Dabeizhe, who asked him:
The World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa smiled. Ultimately, what was he smiling at? Layman [Shi] said, "You are far too busy.
Mazu Daoyi said, "Where did you get this news? Layman stepped forward, grabbed Mazu by the collar, and Mazu gave him a slap.
Layman then bowed. Mazu sealed him with a verse (Shi Gao was his successor).
The layman Longzhen of Jinmen, whose courtesy name was Dongming, was by nature fond of wine.

He frequently visited the Dabeitong (Great Compassion) Temple, where, amidst the shadows of trees and the reflections of pagodas, he would purchase wine and pour it for himself without restraint. After becoming intoxicated, he would sometimes laugh or cry, and sometimes sing or scold;

many therefore gave him the nickname "The Madman. He would then bestow upon gentlemen "Verses on Ancient Cases: Plucking Pearls" (*Songgu Zhizhu*), which the gentlemen accepted to serve as accompaniment to their wine.

One day, as Wugu read about the causes and conditions of Devadatta’s slander of the Buddha and his subsequent descent into hell, he took a large draught of wine and, drawing out his voice, recited this verse: "The Buddha does not enter hell;
The Mara does not emerge from hell. If the Buddha enters hell, The Mara has already emerged from hell. Without Mara and without Buddha, Where is there a hell? He then presented this to Jueze.

Then [Touzi] let out a great shout, threw his staff before the monk, and returned to the abbot’s quarters. The monk smiled and presented a verse, saying: "Trusting my steps, I enter the empty mountains;
In these empty mountains, an empty fragrance wafts forth. Seeking it out, I reach the roots of the withered plum tree;
From every branch, the bright moon is emitted. Touzi then bestowed upon him a verse (Shigao was the successor of Touzi).
Chan Master Dabeiyuanyin Duoxi of Tianjin was the son of the Liu family from Benwei. As a child, he delighted in sitting in the lotus posture;

his fellow villagers all remarked that he possessed the karmic habituation of a previous life. Upon reaching adulthood, he shaved his head and entered the monastic order. Having received instruction from Chan Master Shigao Ze, he once remained awake throughout the night.
One evening, while walking in meditation along the corridor, he heard the sound of a cat and attained realization. He composed a verse, which begins: "The night is deep, the new moon..."
Illuminating the eaves and pillars, suddenly a cat knows how to meow. Treading through the void, there is no place to cling;
in the midst of the sun, it alone reveals its form from before the kalpas. Zhaozhe asked, "What is your body before the kalpas? The Master said, "The earthen ox bellows at midnight;
the golden crow emerges from the sea gate. Zhaozhe asked, "Once returned, where does one go? The Master said, "Yanling does not require nine."
Huan Dan asked, "When it is said that 'mind, Buddha, and phenomena are all non-existent,' what is it ultimately? The Master said, "A winnowing basket does not have lips. Huan Dan nodded in agreement.
Having personally attended upon the Master for several years, he received this verse: "Puhua shakes his bell and clapper; The perfect sound is transmitted through the ages.
A single drop of Che River water Flows forth before the workings of the mind. (Shigao was thus his successor.)

Jin Shichun, whose courtesy name was Jing’an, was a native of Tielingwei. He had previously studied the records of Chan masters. Upon taking office in Xia County, he would invariably practice seated meditation during his leisure time from administrative duties.
Later, while observing the period of mourning for his father, he resided temporarily in Tianjin. There, he visited Master Zao Bei and requested instruction on the methods of cultivation.
The Master instructed him to contemplate the phrase, "Where does it all return? Jin applied himself with great effort to this investigation. One day, he happened to see a corpse.
I said to him, "Where does this single spirit go? My doubts grew even deeper. Sitting in my study at night, I contemplated the marks of arising and ceasing;
they were all like illusions and dreams. I then composed a verse, saying: "Birth and death are both like dreams and illusions, The single spirit transcends past and present.
It swallows up heaven and earth, being without form; In the void, the bright moon shines alone. When I presented it to Ze, he said, "Swallowing up heaven and earth—the moon!"
"Where is it? Chun snapped his fingers once and said, "Where have you come from, studying such empty-headedness?
Chun replied, "In the Han-yuan Hall, the jade nectar spills like waves. [The Master] asked, "Once returned, where is one? Chun said, "I thank the Master for asking again. [The Master] approved.

Chun stayed with him for two years, intimately attending him, and was finally certified with a verse. He then went to visit Miaoyun Xiong. Xiong said, "I have heard that you, Layman, have attained realization."
"Birth and death are like a dream; is this so? Chun replied, "The earthen ox tramples the moon over a thousand rivers; the wooden horse charges through the clouds of the Five Peaks.
[The Master] said, "That is still a matter of birth and death. Chun said, "Dust upon the head of the Year-Deity. Xiong gave a slap and said, "An Imperial Edict!
Chun then let out a shout (Shigao thus became his successor).
Chan Master Fayun Liaoxinxiang was the son of the Tang family of Suzhou. He visited Miaoyun Xiong at the Nianhua Inn.
Xiong asked, "How does my hand compare to the Buddha’s hand? The Master replied, "Yesterday I heard that the Abbot had arrived here. Xiong said, "..."
“My feet are like those of a donkey,” [Nanquan] said. The Master replied, “Meeting you this morning, I regret it was so late.
Nanquan said, “Everyone has their own karmic affinity (*jìngyuán*); what is the Venerable One’s own karmic affinity? The Master replied, “How would I dare deny it before the Monk?
Nanquan picked up his staff and said, “Why does Staff-Master Ma do not know? The Master replied, “The wind blows the wutian leaves down; where would they not land?”

Autumn was clear. Xiong struck him, saying, "This is exactly when you deserve a beating. The Master prostrated himself. He served as an attendant for half a year, and Xiong sealed his realization with a verse.
One day, Xiong asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "The eyes do not see the nose. Xiong asked, "What is the Dharma?
The Master replied, "The fishing line has dried up the vast ocean. Xiong asked, "What is the Sangha? The Master replied, "The eyebrows are straight, the eyes are [wide]."

Gazing fixedly, he composed a verse on the stone mirror image, saying: "The Three Pure Ones once gazed upon Penglai and Yingzhou; They drained the contents of their gourds, yet their inspiration remained unawakened.
How many times have the seas and sands shifted? They remain utterly oblivious. They sing their drunken songs to the edge of heaven—a melody difficult to continue. (Miaoyun Xiong succeeded him.)
Gulangjing, the abbot of Gao-ting in Jiaxing, was the son of the Lü family of Haiyan.

In his youth, he followed Yun’an Liang to receive the tonsure and received full ordination from Dengwei Bi. He studied under Fuzhen, contemplating the koan of "dragging a corpse. Finding no entry point, he once requested instruction from the layman Lu Tao.
Although he repeatedly received encouragement and exhortation, he was unable to respond. Lu Tao said to him, "For now, you must let go of everything."
Gather your thoughts and extinguish the mind; investigate the question, "Who is it that recites the Buddha's name? Without ceasing day or night, you will naturally find the point of realization.

It was through hearing a lecture on the occasion when the World-Honored One questioned Ānanda, saying, "You should answer my question with a straightforward mind," that he first resolved his doubts and presented his insight.
I (Tao) expressed my joy for him. When I fell ill, the Master came to inquire after me. I said, "Vimalakīrti was ill... (The text ends here).
The Twelve Great Beings asked, "Old man, you are ill. The Master replied, "My intention lies in a place far beyond where the Honored One asks.
Zhaozhou said, "I am not like the Thirty-two Great Beings. He held up his *ruyi* (ceremonial fly-whisk) and asked, "Do you recognize this?
The Master said, "I respectfully wish the Layman ten thousand blessings. Zhaozhou lifted one foot and said, "Speak here! The Master prostrated himself. Zhaozhou nodded in approval. Zhaozhou.
Shu Ruyi said: "You need only deeply cultivate this Way by the waters and beneath the forests. Should there be favorable conditions, you may also enlighten those who come after.
This single matter of mine depends upon you for its transmission and preservation; be careful not to neglect it.
He then sealed [the charge] with the *ruci* (wishing-gem) and a verse (Xuan-du Tao succeeded him).
The lay practitioner Ru Gong Fan Xia of Jiaxing was a native of Xiushui. From childhood, he delighted in seeing the Buddha and aspired to the school of Emptiness (*śūnyatā*).
He first studied under Zhenru Jie, who instructed him in the essentials of Chan. Subsequently, he studied under Ruru Jie, who assigned him the koan "The Three Are Not."

He applied himself with diligent austerity, sitting upright through the night until dawn. Upon hearing the sound of the evening bell, he attained a realization. He composed a verse and presented it to Zhijue, saying:
"Suddenly hearing one strike of the bell, It presses the void so that there is nowhere to hide.
The great earth is level and smooth as a mirror; As before, my very body is revealed in its majestic presence. From then on, he visited renowned masters everywhere. One day, he met Bingshan.
The master and disciple were in profound accord; he immediately sealed it with a verse (Master Mu Qian was his successor).
Zen Master Jien of the Huayan School at Jinling, whose secular surname was Song and who was a native of Yanqing Prefecture, addressed the assembly.
He cited Master Chong of Mount Jing, who said: "The world is so vast and wide; why then is it in the hands of this old monk? The Master [Jien] said: "Mount Jing..."
"Though the mountain path be ten parts complete, one does not mind having one's entire body covered in mud and water. Since the world is already in the palm of your hand, tell me:
where is this old man standing? Question: "When Bodhidharma came from the West, what did he transmit? The Master said: [He transmitted] nothing at all.
[The Master] was tearing up his straw sandals. [A monk] asked, "I have heard that the robe was transmitted to the Second Patriarch; is this true? The Master said, "Believe half of it for now.
The monk said, "Master, do not deceive people. Suddenly, a magpie screeched. The Master said, "When a crow caws, it is 'ya ya'; when a magpie caws, it is 'que que'.
[The monk] asked, "What principle did the ancients see that they simply ceased [seeking]? The Master said, "No one can question him. (Yuzu Jue was his successor.)
Chan Master Duzhen of Ciyun Temple in Tāngyīn Cháoyáng was the son of the Chen family of Yǒngnián.

He received the tonsure under Huìyuè and went to Huáshān to receive full ordination. Having sat in meditation for five summer retreats, he studied the *Vinaya* with great precision. He traveled through various lecture halls, often reflecting to himself:
"The precepts are the foundation for restraining the body, and the teachings are the study of words and meanings; neither is the ultimate principle. Once...

Having heard that the Chan school possesses the essential method for "untying the sticky and casting off the bonds" and for "understanding life and escaping death," he wondered, "Could this be deceiving me?

Thereupon, he packed his belongings and went to attend upon Fengxue Yixuan, who assigned him the koan: "All dharmas return to One. Without collapsing onto his mat, he applied himself with diligent effort and never grew weary.

Suddenly, seeing the sunlight blazing forth, he was instantly released from his previous understanding. He entered the room to present his realization and said with joy, "What is 'the myriad dharmas returning to the One'?
The Master said, "A thicket of mountains at Fengxue. He asked, "Where does the One return?
The Master said, "The moon sets; the long sky is azure. He said, "Not yet—speak further! The Master overturned the meditation seat and departed. Xī said, "This fellow acts recklessly!"

Later, after his father had personally tasted the nectar of awakening, he appointed the Master as Director of the Guest Office. Subsequently, when the awakened father moved to the capital to spread the teachings, the Master managed the affairs of the monastery for nearly two years.
When the father fell gravely ill, he summoned the Master and asked him, "I wish to build a seamless stupa;
try to fashion a model of such a stupa for me. The Master stepped forward, stood with his hands folded, and remained there. The father said, "It resembles it, but it is not it."
"Not yet. The Master asked, "What is the meaning of the Abbot’s intention? Huairang pushed out his meditation pillow. The Master said, "The construction of the stupa is finished.
Huairang asked, "If someone asks you hereafter, 'Can you still capture the true likeness of the Master?
how will you respond? The Master drew a circle with his hand and performed a woman’s bow. Huairang asked, "Is there anything else besides this? The Master replied, "Great kindness."
"It is difficult to repay. Jue said, "So it is, so it is. He then produced his robe, whisk, and dharma verses, and [Yue] was thus certified as his successor (succeeding Master Jue).

In the Shaoxing era, there was the Chan Master Yueguang of the Shengyue Monastery. His secular surname was Ma, and he was a native of that prefecture. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations.

He once sought instruction from the elders San-yi and Shi-yu, deeply investigating the principles of Chan. In his middle years, he went to Dongshan to pay respects to Niguma (Gui-jiao) and received the tonsure.
Upon receiving full ordination, he looked into who it was that recited the Buddha’s name. One morning while washing his face, he heard a monk jokingly say, "Take off your Qizhou cloth robe.
Unconsciously, the Master broke into a sweat that soaked his back. He presented this verse: "Letting go of the external objects of perception, The original nature is pure and still.
Touching my own nostrils, I see That I am not another person at all. [The monk] said, "This is merely a record of the mind and intellect. But tell me, what about the one who recites?"
"Who is this Buddha? the Master asked. Jue replied, "King Yama is originally but a ghost. The Master said, "You must verify this for yourself.
Jue said, "The Master is far too kind-hearted. The Master asked, "How do you see it? Jue replied, "How would I dare deceive the assembly? The Master said, "Then you are deceiving only yourself.
Jue then gave a shout, which the Master praised most highly. Although the Master had attained some realization, he ultimately did not [boast of it].
Kěn followed his teacher northward on a single staff to visit Qīxián Qīng. Their meeting was like the snapping together of a needle and its eye; they were immediately in perfect accord.

Kěn took charge of the affairs of the meditation hall, never shirking labor or service, and his investigations were also rigorous. He often joined others in practicing "dead-work" (intense meditation).

One day, hearing a monk recite the words of Zhaozhou, "Recite the Buddha’s name once, and rinse your mouth for three days," Kěn’s state of doubt became increasingly stifling. At dawn, he heard the sound of a mule-drawn carriage.
Shengzhen had just begun to break free from his doubts and obstructions when he said, "Reciting the Buddha’s name once makes one rinse one's mouth for three days;

though gold dust is precious, if it falls into the eye, it becomes a film. He presented this to Qing, saying, "This is an ancient saying. What about yours? The Master replied, "Boiling raw rice until it becomes cooked porridge.
Qing asked, "What if the cauldron has a leak and the firewood is damp? The Master said, "Today there is no communal labor (pǔqǐng). Qing struck him.
[The interlocutor] said, "To let this pass would be improper. The Master said, "The Abbot possesses the virtue of bringing others to fulfillment.
(This refers to the succession of Xianqing.
*Wudeng Quanshu*, Volume 103, edited by the monk (Chao Yong), Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple in the Capital.
Verified and presented for the Imperial Review by the Abbot (Subject-Monk) Chaokei of Kōkegwan-ji Temple,
Kyoto;
Rinzai School.
The Record of Chan Master Dinglie of Gumei on Mount Gui, in Tanzhou, the thirty-seventh generation descendant of Nanyue.
He was the son of the Wang family of Shaoling. While still young, he frequented the local school, yet he constantly reflected upon the great matter of birth and death.
Thereupon, he shaved his head and received full ordination, relying upon Master Hai at Daguishan. He applied himself to intensive study for fifteen years.
Residing at Guanghua on Mount Furong, he addressed the assembly: "The ox-head disappears; the horse-head returns. Wind and horses, cattle and oxen—none reach one another.
The jade hare hastens; the golden crow rushes. Sun and moon move together without conflict. An arrow is fixed upon a mulberry tree."
Juice flows from the willow tree; he addresses the assembly: "To kill a man, one must see blood. Within the treasury of our King, there is no such blade.
To act for others, one must act with thoroughness. I cannot even attend to my own person, so how could I have leisure to worry about anything else?

He lets out a shout and says: "Stop spreading false rumors! Sea! Retiring to Qixing Rock, he commands his disciple to succeed him on the seat. Entering the hall, he says: "The World-Honored One has a secret word."
All day long it is at your ear; Kāśyapa did not conceal it. All day long it is within your eye. If you understand it in this way, I must ask you:
what have you said? What have you seen? The World-Honored One has a secret teaching; a father conceals [the truth] from his son.
Kāśyapa did not conceal anything, yet his son realized it. Now tell me: what is it that he realized? What is it that was hidden? Evening Sermon:
It is said that when a monk asked Baling, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? Baling replied, "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree."
"The duck, cold, goes down into the water. The Master said, "The rooster, cold, climbs up the tree. With one cry, it falls upon the moon at the tip of the plum branch;

the duck, cold, goes down into the water—its living body treads through the autumn of the Blue Heaven. Looking around at those present, he said, "Even so, to add commentary upon commentary, what ultimately is the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings?
The *Huanglong San guan* (Three Barriers of Huanglong) verses say: "My hand—how is it like the Buddha’s hand? (He pulls [the student] along. ...pulling him along.
Mount Sumeru turns upside down and tumbles over the blue-eyed barbarian monk, needlessly severing one of his elbows.
How ugly! My feet—how can they be like donkey's feet? Leaping and bounding before Parrot Isle, he encounters the fierce King Chu, who has both his feet cut off.
A mistake! Everyone has their own karmic affinity: south of the Yangtze, north of the Yangtze; east of the sea, west of Sichuan. It is all above.
Gaozu (the First Ancestor). Following Xiang Yuanran, his teacher strictly maintained the models of the Vinaya; his Way spread throughout the regions of Jiang and Chu.
He authored six volumes of recorded sayings (*yulu*) which circulate in the world (Huishan Haiji).
Chan Master Fuyong Zhifu of Tanzhou ascended the hall with Chan Master Shangfeng Zhi. "To preach the Dharma without anything attained is called the lion’s roar.
To preach the Dharma with something attained is called the jackal’s howl. When both 'having' and 'not having' are attained, the jackal and the lion are simultaneously struck down.
He struck the meditation staff and said, "Right here, it is like a Wheel-Turning King untying his topknot, utterly cutting off all thought."
Like an elephant king crossing a river, he completely forgets all turning back and shifting about. At such a time as this, is there anyone who can grasp it?
(He lets out a shout. Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Zhaozhou. A monk once asked, "Among the three bodies, which one is the original body?
Zhaozhou said, "None is lacking; none is superfluous. The Master said, "Wielding the tongs and hammer of one's own fundamental portion to guide and lead these hired laborers—how precious!"
Ah! A long-term traveler forgets his home; in the end, one realizes one has been deceiving oneself. If I were asked now, "Among the three bodies, which one is the original body?
I would simply hand him my staff. If he hesitates for even a moment, I would strike him right on the head.
Tell me, how far apart is this from Zhaozhou’s approach? Evening Session: Cooking rice made of iron nails. Stitching...
The teeth stick to the gums; sealing it with white paper, one writes that the empty is much while the real is little. How is this better than partaking of ready-made tea and food?
