When the time comes for distribution, the patterns are brilliantly displayed as one settles matters with venerable masters. If you understand, then things are like a single family, with ritual and music;
if you do not understand, then there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences, yet without faction or partiality. Striking the incense table, he said: "The Master did not..."
"Knowing the characters. Bodhidharma did not understand Chan. The place where his lifelong deception was exposed: a missing tooth before the gate. Question:

"When one who has died the Great Death returns to life, what is it like? The Master said: "Three thousand miles away, all confusion and error are cut off. Question: "When you, Master, dwell in the mountains, what serves as proof? The Master said: "The stone elephant and the clay ox roar throughout the night. A verse on De Shan’s "Resting the Body": * *識字。達磨不會禪。一生敗露處。板齒缺門前* Knowing the characters. Bodhidharma did not understand Chan. The place where his lifelong deception was exposed: a missing tooth before the gate. * *問大死的人。却活時如何。師曰。三千里外絕誵訛。曰和尚住山。以何為驗。師曰。石象泥牛連夜吼* Question: "When one who has died the Great Death returns to life, what is it like? The Master said: "Three thousand miles away, all confusion and error are cut off. Question: "When you, Master, dwell in the mountains, what serves as proof?
The Master said: "The stone elephant and the clay ox roar throughout the night. *A verse on De Shan’s Resting the Body.*
Ba said: "In one gate, rites and music command the heroic; / Gently grasping the palindrome, he strikes it beneath the moon. / Why did he snap the jade strings?
/ In the painted hall, he won the sound of his voice to rise high. The Master traveled through various residences at Guoyuan in Jingzhou, Xichan in Langzhou, Longshan in Shaochuan, and Damingxi.
Ten volumes of his recorded sayings (*yulu*) circulate in the world (his dharma lineage descends from Huisan).
Chan Master Tanmo Wen of Wansong at Bailong in Cixi was the son of the Wang family of Yuyao.

He received the tonsure from Bailong Neng and engaged in rigorous investigation of the "cane" koan. One night while walking in the mountains, he stepped on a stone and injured his foot, which triggered an awakening.
He presented a verse, saying: "How extraordinary is this pine seed! Planted upon a rootless rock. Laughing at its lack of dwelling place, It reveals a single branch."
Zhile came forward and offered a verse, saying: "How do you apply your mind? The Master then shouted. Neng said, "Why do you act so harshly?
The Master replied, "A red sun-wheel bursts forth from the tip of a hair. Neng asked, "What is the essential meaning? The Master said, "The entire earth turns to spring.

Neng nodded in agreement. In a small-scale sermon, [the Master] said: "For a monk, it would be best to simply dwell in the mountains. It was for no reason that you were driven out by such pressing demands."
Shanlai arrived. Who would have known that his merit was so thin as to be difficult to cure? He endured it all with great effort, carrying water and dragging mud.
In the *Small Public Sermon on Planting Pines*: The livelihood of a mountain monk is simply ordinary; Bathed by rain and combed by wind, he relies on no external conditions.

If one can achieve a single state of effort, One may sleep soundly amidst white clouds and green trees. On the first day of the eighth month of the Jiyou year of the Kangxi era, the Master passed away.
The entire body [of the Master] was enshrined in a stupa at the western foot of the temple (by Binghuai Nengsi).
Chan Master Guanghui He of Chongchuan Shizhu ascended the hall and said: "Harmonizing with light, do not mingle with the dust of the world;

exert effort to deeply cultivate the roots beyond the kalpas. If you can penetrate the master who is without dreams within sleep, a thousand flowers will bloom in profusion as birds sing in spring. (Binghuai)
Nengsi. Chan Master Daxie Ding of Kaihua in Wuling, whose secular surname was Xing of Zhaoyang, was asked by a monk:
"What is the phrase for entering the gate? The Master said: "Upon seeing your countenance, one already knows. [The monk] asked: "What is the phrase within the gate? The Master said:
"Planning strategy within the tent to decide victory a thousand *li* away—what is the phrase for being at the gate? The Master said, "The hair-cutting blade must remain unmoving.
"What is the phrase for going out the gate? The Master said, "Carrying the sun and moon upon the tip of the staff;
storing heaven and earth within the sleeves. "What is the phrase for outside the gate? The Master said, "That mountain is high, yet that mountain is even higher. (Binghuai Neng succeeded him.)
Chan Master Gu-yao Zhi of Beishan in Taizhou was a native of Shanghai. At the age of seventeen, he shaved his head and donned the monastic robes.

He traveled extensively to study under various masters of the past, including those at Tiantong, Dashi, Rui Guang, and Jiaoshan. Later, he received the seal of approval from Master Neng of Bailong. Upon ascending the hall for his first formal sermon, he said:
"Ten thousand miles of long, azure sky; heaven and earth are utterly pure. Mountains and rivers form a single expanse—what is there in this matter?"
[He] divided [the teachings]. Having realized this intent, every single thing is entirely spring.
As for the seventeen hundred koans, even if one were to bring them all forward in detail, would they be of the slightest use here?

If they could be used, it would still be like driving a nail into empty space. If they cannot be used, what then? He then pushed over the meditation seat, took up his staff, and drove [the monks] away.
The assembly said, "One must not eat the leftovers from another person's meal. (Binghuai Nengsi).

Zen Master Zuzhang Zongheng of Langya in Chuzhou ascended the hall. He extended his left hand, then extended his right hand, and finally joined his palms and looked at the assembly, saying, "Do you understand?
The assembly remained silent. The Master said, "I have already repeated myself three times," and then returned to his quarters.
Ascending the hall, he pulled his nose with his hand and said: "From the Buddhas and sages down to beasts, mules, and horses, there is not one who does not share this very same nostril.

If you can recognize it, you may play with supernatural powers everywhere—in demon palaces and tiger dens, amidst sword-trees and knife-mountains, within the wombs of mares and mules, and in tea shops and wine taverns—purifying the Buddha-lands. If you cannot..."

Consciousness. Driven by the conditions of karmic consciousness and emotional attachments, one wallows in the cycle of birth and death without any respite. Suddenly, a patch-robed monk comes forth and says:
"Setting aside for a moment whether it is recognized or unrecognized, what about when someone comes forth who has no handle to grasp?"
Dingshan had only one question for him: "Where do you vent your breath? Ascending the hall, he said: "The wondrous existence is not existent; the true emptiness is not empty.
With both ends carried on one shoulder, the moon is bright and the wind is clear. A blow of the staff cannot reach it; from where could a shout even come?
On a fishing boat, one manifests the family style; at night, one rows deep into the reeds. North, south, east, and west—[nowhere to be found]."
[The Master] saw his tracks [and asked]: "Where have you gone? He struck the meditation seat once. [Someone] asked: "For what purpose does a great *kalyāṇamitra* appear in this world?
The Master said: "A lifetime spent addicted to wine, repaying debts to men; three years selling paper, owing money to ghosts. [The questioner] said:
"Why do you, Reverend, suffer so much as to enter this profession? The Master said: "I regret not being careful at the beginning. (Huatang Yan’s lineage)

When Chan Master Baique Kuangbaoqing of Huzhou first visited Lingyin and paid his respects at Tianning, he attained realization through the karmic connection with the "Old Woman by the City Wall" (Chengdong Laomu).
He subsequently presented this verse: "The old woman’s eyes are not a bit dim; On level ground, windless, waves arise of their own accord.
Do not be startled by her ten fingers—they are all Buddhas— For she merely sought to avoid drowning, only to leap back into the river. He then relied upon [Master] Jing...

At Hyeonning-sa, Jiryan presented him with the verses and hymns he had composed over the years. Before Jiryan had finished reading them, he said, "You do not yet have the merit to receive a blow of the staff.
The Master asked, "What is my fault? Jiryan replied, "Wait until the mountain behind me nods its head, and then I shall tell you.
The Master immediately burned the writings and entered the meditation hall. After practicing with intense diligence for a long time, he attained sudden enlightenment upon hearing the "Mu" (dog) kōan.

One day, during a communal work session (*pǔqǐng*), Yánchuí asked, "First, dragging stones; second, carrying earth. To trigger the mechanism, one must have a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt.

What is this crossbow of a thousand jin? The assembly offered various responses, none of which were satisfactory. The Master said, "When it arrives, it does not strike. Yánchuí smiled and nodded in approval.
He then asked, "Who is the person who does not take companionship with the myriad dharmas? The Master said, "The character '十' (ten)."
Liao the Bearded Man of the Streets said, "Why do you say, 'In one gulp, he drinks up the waters of the West River'?
The Master replied, "I am not his equal" (Huatang Yan).
Chan Master Yunan of Linggu at Mount Jingshan in Jinling was the son of the Li family of Taixing.

At the age of eighteen, as his entire family succumbed to an epidemic with no survivors remaining, he resolved to shave his head and don the monastic robes. He requested the precepts from Master Yuning. At that time, Nanping Yan served as the First Seat;

upon meeting him, their spiritual faculties were in accord. He subsequently followed and attended him to resolve his doubts. Later, having received the transmission of the Dharma, he went forth to reside [in a monastery].
At Linggu, the opening of the retreat: The field for selecting Buddhas has opened, and those from the ten directions have gathered.
This mountain monk takes the mind of equality as the furnace and bellows, and uses truthful speech as the tongs and hammer.
Whether it be gold or iron, jade or stone—when struck by water, it becomes a gong of Mount Luofu; when the mountains resound, it becomes a bell of Khotan. Thus, may all who see it...

"How marvelous! Those who hear this are struck with wonder and astonishment. Not only does it establish the value of Mount Jiangshan, but it is also sufficient to enhance the brilliance of the *Zongjing* (Mirror of the Source).
Moreover, by what means does one do so? [The Master] picks up his staff, gives a shout, and says: "The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horns because it gazes at the moon;
the elephant has flowers enter its tusks because it was startled by thunder. During the meal period, the Master said to the attendant of the hall: "Why does the pillar not give [a sermon]?"
[The Master] set aside one portion and said, "This is for him; he does not understand how to eat it. The Master said, "It is precisely for him that this portion should be given.
[The monk] asked, "Why? The Master said, "If he understood, even a single grain of rice would be difficult to digest.

In the second month of the Dingwei year of the Kangxi era, as the Master was about to pass away, the Xidang (Chief Seat) Zhuxian—whom the Master had studied under together with his fellow practitioners—saw that the Master’s illness was grave and that he did not lightly transmit the Dharma. One...
One day, Juefeng gave a formal lecture. Arriving at the point where he shed tears, he said, "If there had not been Nian Fahua on that day, it would have been better to weep until the end of time.
The Master [Huangbo] said, "At that time, Fengxue brought up Nian Fahua; today, it is Dusti Xutang."
He brought this up to Linggu, asking, "Which is upright and which is inverted? Linggu replied, "The intentions of each are different; yet their way of supporting their families is the same.
The Master said, "The words of a parent come from the parent’s own mouth. Linggu said, "I shall borrow Linggu’s toxic breath to repay my karmic debts to Nanping.
The following day, the Master beat the drum and ascended the seat. Addressing the assembly, he requested a brush and wrote a verse, saying: "In coming, there is not a single thing; in departing..."
"Not even a speck. Riding an iron horse backward out of the heavy city, the spring wind of the riverlands rises from the earth.
He then bathed and shaved his head, passing away in serene stillness. He was buried to the west of Master Zhigong’s stupa.
Zhang Youyu, the Grand Minister of Agriculture, composed the inscription for him (Huatang Yan was his successor).
Chan Master Jingci Shunqufang Xiao was a native of the Wang family of Jiangdu. He studied under Nanping Yan at Xianning Temple and joined the assembly for the private interview (入室).

Upon hearing the citation of the *Zhao Lun* (Treatise on Emptiness) regarding "the non-transmigration of things," he attained a realization. He then presented the following verse on "having words and having no words":
"The clash of two blades is like a great mass of fire; As soon as one touches its edge, the skull shatters to pieces. If it does not shatter..."
A clay man pounding ghosts at the spring millstone; Yanke allowed this. Entering the hall, he said: "The entire earth is the single eye of a patch-robed monk.
I, Jingci, have a vow and do not wish to scatter sand. Today, too, it is out of necessity.
Is there anyone who can hoist sails amidst a flash of lightning or gallop a horse within a spark of fire? If you are unable to do so, then simply cut away [the delusions] with resolve."

With heart and gall drained, I present to you all the physical marks and essential nature of the Buddhas, the great intent of the Patriarchs, the hundreds of thousands of samādhis, and the immeasurable Dharma gates.
I hold them up before you, my friends, leaving it entirely to you to arrange them: one upright, two horizontal, three vertical, and four diagonal. (Huatang Yan’s Successor)
Master Chanyuan of Fuyong Peak at Lingping in Zhujia addressed the assembly, citing the kōan of Linji’s passing:
"Do not extinguish my treasury of the true Dharma eye. The Master said: "A man does not eat his family's rice;
a woman does not wear her wedding clothes. When the ancestral fields and gardens are all gone, only then can one go bare-handed to weave a fence. Great!
[The] Assembly: This fence was woven from that place (Huatang Yan Si).
Master Nian’an Hui of Yunnan, a nun of the Yun’an Monastery in Wulin, was the daughter of the Zhuang family of the Prefecture.

One day, while reading the *Record of Sanfeng*, someone asked for instruction regarding the unresolved matter of birth and death. Sanfeng, responding to the voice, struck him with his palm. The Master, at that—

Upon hearing these words, he attained sudden enlightenment and thereupon composed a verse: "For over forty years, I cast aside the consciousness of karma; Suddenly brandishing the precious sword, I displayed my heroic prowess.
With a shout, I bade the Three Thousand Buddhas retreat; The entire great earth is contained within a single hair. Later, he visited Jingci Monastery.
Yan asked, "What is the path to bodhi? The Master said, "Entering hell like an arrow. Yan said, "What is it like when one is not attached to even a single thread?
The Master said, "A person who betrays their own heart grows ever more destitute. Yan asked, "What is discerning wisdom?"
The Master said, "Three times nine is twenty-seven. Yán asked, "Is there still a skillful means? The Master said, "Three times nine is twenty-seven.
Yán then desisted. A verse on Dēshān’s Alms Bowl: A single question at the head—how could it be ordinary?
He shifts the sharp point, hidden in the dark. Father and son each play a different tune; Every cry of the monkey breaks one's heart.
A Verse on Eating Bamboo Shoots: Long hidden in the deep mountains, preserving the sacred embryo; At the first roll of thunder, it emerges with its head.
Peeling away layer after layer, it is steamed for eating; Not failing those who have tasted it once. (Huatang Yan)
Chan Master Keche of Shenshan Baoci Temple ascends the hall: "One does not do it; two does not rest. In the soft and warm place, he cannot be contained.
A *kāṣāya* wrapped around straw sandals—just listen! Within the coarse alms bowl, by the side of the spoon and chopsticks for urinating, do you know his breath?
(He lets out a shout. Ascends the hall: "The spring breeze makes the willows lovely; the spring birds..."
The nightingale warbles; it is a single piece of the Patriarch’s mind, yet it leaks out in two places. When the ancients spoke thus, they split the discourse into two fragments.
Baoci, however, does not say so: "The spring breeze makes the willows lovely; the spring birds warble as the nightingale sings.
How profound! How profoundly profound! What joy! Truly what joy! It is but a single piece, and though it seems to leak, it has never leaked.
Morning attendance. Last night, the autumn colors were fine by the lake; this morning, I shift my oars, departing from the notes of the *gong* and *shang*.
Who can join in the single melody of the "Parting Hook"? Only Xie Lang has cast away his beard and hair. (Claps the desk once—Huiri, like Liangsi.)
Chan Master Xuan Yuxuan of Angji Baofan was the son of the Xu family of Changzhou. He received the tonsure under Vinaya Master Sanmei and completed his full ordination.

He then visited Chai of Ruiwang Monastery, with whom he attained awakening through the catalyst of the staff. Later, when Zhongyu Fan succeeded to the abbacy, he instructed the Master to diligently investigate the "Cane" koan.
The Master felt deeply bewildered and distressed, and said to the Abbot, "I do not understand this 'cane. It is, for example," [and so forth].
He threw beans against the wall; as he tossed them one after another, not a single one found its way inside. Baofeng said, "You should contemplate the saying: 'Before your parents were born.
The Master returned to the hall and practiced with intense focus for a full day and night. At dawn, hearing the song of a yellow oriole, his mind suddenly opened up in a flash of realization.
He hurried to the abbot’s quarters, and just as he was about to speak, Baofeng struck him out. At that time, Yizhu En was serving as the head monk.
Xitang went to see Master En to inquire about the previous conversation. En gave a shout. Xitang also shouted. En shouted again. Xitang’s entire body broke into a sweat;

He placed great emphasis on the matters that transcend the Zen school and devoted himself to their exhaustive investigation for many years.

Although he possessed some degree of understanding and was able to make some progress toward the goal, he could not achieve a direct and total realization. One day, while at Lianhua Temple, he encountered Yuanzhong.
The master asked, "Ultimately, how can one attain clarity regarding the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye? Zhong let out a thunderous shout. The master said, "Apart from this, is there anything else?"
"Is there one? Zhong closed the door. After a long while, he opened it again. As the scholar prepared to ask a question, Zhong covered the scholar’s mouth and said, "Speak!
Speak! At that moment, the scholar attained immediate and thorough enlightenment. He then said, "Had I known earlier that the lamp was fire, how much longer would it have taken for the rice to cook?
He further presented this verse: "The Eye of the True Dharma opens; all phenomena merge as one. As soon as a single mechanism moves, ten thousand mechanisms are unobstructed. The original face..."

"Only now do I see it; it is entirely within meeting conditions without borrowing from them. Zhong nodded in agreement and immediately bestowed upon him a verse, thereby conferring his prediction of enlightenment (Zhong succeeded Jianyuan).
The lay practitioner Lin Wenbo of Linqing, Shandong, whose given name was Xiù, attained the highest rank in the civil service examinations in his youth and served as a high-ranking official.
His family had been virtuous for generations; his father, Zhishan Daoshang, had received the seal of mind-transmission from Doushuai and extensively practiced the six perfections.
Upon reading the Tripitaka, the gentleman attained awakening and, penetrating the profound essentials, exclaimed: "Only today do I know that there is not a single character. He further...
He presented a verse, saying: "The five thousand volumes of the Great Canon revolve according to the mind; when both mind and phenomena are forgotten, one uproots them to the very bottom.
Having personally realized the true face of the original source, whatever is grasped or employed always encounters the fountainhead. Jiaoyuan Zhong then [presented] the Dharma verse of the lineage.
Certified by Jianyuan and Zhongsu.
Compiled by the monk (Chao Yong),
Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple in the Capital, for the *Wudeng Quanshu*, Volume 155.
Verified and presented for the Rinzai School by the Abbot (Subject Monk) Chōkai of Kyoto’s Kokegwan-ji Temple.

The Record of Chan Master Bingtie Zong of Deshan, under the thirty-seventh generation of Nanyue, a native of the Song family in Macheng. A small formal sermon given during a communal labor session for planting rice.
Baizhang raised his hands and said to the assembly, "All of you, help me clear the fields; I will then explain the Great Meaning to you.
When the disciples had finished clearing the fields, they requested the Master to explain the Great Meaning. Baizhang simply extended both hands to show them. The Master [Yunmen] said:
This is indeed so; it still fails to avoid muddying the waters. New Deshan is not like this:

"All of you, help me plant the rice fields, and I will not speak to you of the Great Meaning. Why? Because one must not allow branches to grow old before producing nodes. (Original text: *zhí fù sì*).
Chan Master Mingmin Shihui of Qinshan in Lizhou asked, "What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth?
The Master replied, "I have come from the dharma of the worthy sages; I have never killed a living being. [The monk] asked, "What is the phrase that cuts off all streams?"
The Master said, "I have vowed not to preach the Dharma for those of the Two Vehicles. [A monk] asked, "What is the phrase of 'following the waves and riding the currents'?
The Master said, "It is rare to find a fine horse that will gallop upon seeing only the shadow of the whip. (This was originally attributed to Zhifu Si.)
Chan Master Kuntian Zhenthou of Fuyan on Mount Heng ascended the hall. As soon as a monk stepped forward, the Master said, "What thing comes in such a manner?
The monk replied, "How would I dare speak of it? The Master said, "This belongs to the ancients. The monk said, "Bring forth yours, Reverend, and let us see!
The Master struck him and said, "There is no difference in the soil from the same pit. The Master then added, "Why should it not be spoken of?"
(Original Text: Directly Bestowing upon the Successor).
Zen Master Xuehui of Mount Nanyuan in Guilin ascends the hall and says: "A single peak, steep and precipitous, bears not a trace of moss.
How many people, arriving here, find themselves compelled to retreat? But tell me, how does the new Nanyuan conduct himself? He lets out a shout.
Huangbo said: "Do not walk upon the water of the Eastern Mountain" (originally a direct verse by Sishi).
Master Xuanji Yuan of Taiping in Shuzhou ascended the hall, held up his staff, struck it, and said: "The Dharma follows the practice of the Dharma."
The Dharma banner is established wherever it may be; there is no need for the formal distinction between host and guest or for the frantic exchange of questions and answers.
The subtle and secret functioning of the spiritual mechanism naturally serves as a forge. With a shout, he said: "Tell me, where is that other half of me, Old Man Deshan? Small Assembly (Xiaocan):
When both practice and speech reach the goal, what inscription on a stele is needed? When neither practice nor speech reaches the goal, [it is] white.
Clouds ten thousand miles away. The True Person of No Rank blinks in anger and blinks in joy; he eats a staff of the blue sky. *Rala rala*, a small discourse.
[The Master] raises the koan of Baizhang’s staff and says: "At the tip of that staff—is that something you can manage by merely flaunting your words?
Suppose there were a monk with clear eyes who stepped forward and seized the staff with one hand."
"Son, where else would you place it? (The original text attributes this to Zhi Fu’s successor).
Taicang Qiyuan Yi was a disciple of Master Mingxiu; he was born into the Zhou family of Baoshan in Dian. At the age of sixteen, he shaved his head and received full ordination.
He studied under Jiufeng Fu, who instructed him to contemplate the koan of Linji’s three blows of the staff. Suddenly, upon hearing the bell, he had an awakening.

[The Master] paused and recited a verse: Ten-thousand-fathom peaks towering high, a single path leads through; The wheel and axe have shattered the great void. No one has recognized the merit of past labor on horseback;
I wish only to re-examine this epoch-making achievement. Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind is not the Buddha;
at every turn, lush willows are fit for tethering horses. Wisdom is not the Way; in every house, there is a road leading to Chang'an. He gave a shout.
He said: "Vaguely like falling blossoms in a March rain; indistinctly like the remnants of a dream at the five-watch bell.

Ascending the hall, he said: "This year there are many white waves; planting melons to buy rice is bitter toil. Everyone vies to seek the three stripes [of official rank], yet what benefit is there in binding oneself to them?
He then looked to his left and right and said: "You say that while it has been nothing but wind and rain all day long, you have sat dully and rigidly in this broken hut. Will you take it up?"
The Tathāgata bestowed upon me this samādhi. He let out a shout and said: "In vain you have become a confused mess. (Original text: *zhí fù sì*).
Chan Master Wuyan Kan of Gantulu in Hengzhou was a native of Yongzhou in Chu.

Having studied under Deshan for a long time, he attained a state of rest beneath the master’s staff. Later, he lived in seclusion at Gantulu in Hengzhou. A monk asked: "When all conditions are suddenly stilled..."
"What? the Master asked. [The monk] replied, "The spring breeze of the River Kingdom cannot stir it" (the original text attributes this directly to Sifu).
When Chan Master Ren of Dan Yuan at Tiger Hill first visited Lingyan Chu, he attained a realization. Subsequently, he visited Wanshou Zhang and received his formal transmission and seal of approval.
When the fourfold assembly welcomed him to preside over Ganlu Temple, Chu was delighted and sent him a verse, which begins with these few words: [Short Verse]
Ten *zhang* of verse for my literary grandson; may he strive to repay the kindness of his ancestors on the banks of the Hutuo River. Lowering his hand, he surely knows where the brilliance lies.
Zhangqing Yiru, a Chan Master from Wujiang, was the son of the Jin family of Mount Yu. He ascended the hall and, striking his staff, said:
"This is a monastery. What is 'Perfect Enlightenment' (Yuánjué)? The Buddhas of the three periods have moved mounds and filled valleys;
the monks of the world bind themselves without ropes. Suppose someone were to ask the Master, 'What about it? [The Master] would cast down his staff and say:
'Let you do as you please with your conjectures. (Yuezhang Hengsi)
Chan Master Jiaoheng Mu of Baozhang in Jiangxi ascended the hall and said: "At the tip of every blade of grass, he captures the ancient adept;
from the head of his staff, he presses down upon you, Venerable Ones. Crossing the bridge, he pulls it down; finding the path, he blocks it.
Even if Old Śākyamuni were to come in person, I would first have him step back one pace. Looking left and right, he said, "Do not say this is the new Baozhang!"
This is not in accord with human feeling; it is utterly devoid of flexibility (Yu Qing Gao Si).
Chan Master Can of Bai Zhao at Xiyuan on Mount Nanyue composed a verse titled "Wenshu’s Three Summers of Retreat," which says:

In the evening, drunk, leaning on my staff, I pass through the bamboo village. In several households, remnants of snow cling to the base of the fences. Before the wind, a thousand points of regretful plum blossoms; upon the sand—
"A single crescent of the moon in a sky without people. Mazu was uneasy with this verse, which says: "The face of the sun, the face of the moon; morning and evening they meet.
Reaching out to feel in the dark—what kind of countenance is that? (Yuehan Qiansi).
Chan Master Guyu Xinyi of Pileng, surnamed Jiang of Jingxiang, ascended the hall and said:
"Lei Taijian’s calligraphy improved upon hearing the sound of the river; Wen Yuke’s cursive script flourished after witnessing snakes fighting.
Changqing sat through seven broken cushions of *pútán*; Gaoting beckoned from across the river and walked away sideways. This matter is, indeed, as such."
The joining of the tiger tokens is similar; hereafter, all will be clear. May you not fail me. Addressing the assembly, he said: "One white, two black, three azure, four green.
Looking at the assembly, he said: "There are no Gu Kaizhi or Lu Tanwei among men; this makes me recall the art of painting.
In the autumn of the Renzi year of the Kangxi era, as the Master was approaching his passing, a fellow practitioner asked: "What is the ancestral teaching of Linji? The Master replied: "None."

Renjie asked about this. Tongcan repeated his previous words, whereupon the Master let out a thunderous shout and passed away (Yuehan Qian succeeded him). Changzhao of Jingshan and Yinzai of Xianggu were Dharma heirs of Cansheng.
Born on the shores of Lake Hu by the Huangfu clan, they possessed the reputation of "Righteous Tigers" from their youth.

They were skilled in poetry and prose. Having attended Baoyun Qian, one day amidst a heavy snowfall, they inquired about the karmic conditions of paper and candles, at which point they attained sudden enlightenment.
**Awakening** Lingyun’s verse upon seeing peach blossoms: Lingyun fell headlong into a deep well; Yuansha further pressed down a massive boulder.
What a pity—that one tree of peach blossoms Has bloomed so profusely and in such profusion! **Inscription on a Painting of Vegetables:** Scattered leaves bear the eyes of frogs and insects;
Dotted roots are the flowers of wild greens. If you can truly trust in the flavor within this, it is good indeed.
"It is not so. Thirty years ago, I once severed the life-root of one person. Last night, my bedding was warm; I woke up once and it was already dawn.
[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "If we discuss this matter, it does not hang upon even a single word or character.
Elder Master Lingyan Chu said: 'I do not say there are no words or characters; it is simply that they do not hang [upon it]. Shoushan acted as a lamp in the darkness."
At the perilous place of Lingyan, he acts as a bridge for the crossing. Bai Que Meng Bala also has his own way of speaking;
it is not that he does not hang [his words], but simply that he has no written characters (yuanzi-jiao). Morning Session: I told you about this yesterday—it was like water hitting a stone.
I told you about it the day before yesterday—it was like sand pressing down oil. Today, you must not be so impulsive. Your eyebrows remain as they were.
I return them to your eyes; your nostrils remain as they were, resting upon your lips.
You cannot resent me, nor can I resent you. (Puan Zhisi)
Master Chanyu of Liangxi gave this instruction to the assembly on New Year’s Eve: "In the mountains there are no calendars;

when the cold has ended, one does not know the year. These are merely old clichés. 'Cooking the white ox to celebrate the year' and 'setting aside the staff to pass the year' are but the entanglements of various quarters.
He called a novice, saying: 'Change the water and add incense; today the mountain monk wishes to [give you]..."
"O people, it must accord with the proper occasion. Although it is thus, this is still merely the ordinary livelihood of a monk.
But tell me, how is it when one provides instruction that transcends the conventional? Thereupon, he let out a shout and said: "Suddenly, a thunderous roar bursts forth, shattering all things."

Clouds Ten Thousand Li (Inquiry by Songyuan Si).
Master Fuxiong Zucai of Hengshan in Changzhou was a descendant of the Qian family of Qin River.
At the age of nineteen, he followed Lingyan Chu to receive full ordination. Thereupon, Chu asked him: "What is your original face before your parents were born? The Master—

Terrified and at a loss for words, he then sought instruction with all his might. Later, he visited Master Yun of Xiangfu Monastery. One day, seeing a pomegranate flower in full bloom, his mind was suddenly liberated.
He presented a verse, saying: "The sound of the plum rain never ceases; The pine wind passes through my ears.
Lifting my eyes, I see the pomegranate flower— Both 'two' and 'three' are shattered. Master Yun expressed his joy for him. Subsequently, he relied upon Master Yuan of Taiping. One day, Yuan...
A question was asked: "Having attended upon you for a long time, do you not possess a capacity that transcends the ordinary? The Master said, "To describe it would be inadequate.
He then gave a shout. [The questioner] bowed in submission and received his seal of certification (asked by Songyuan Si).
The Dharma-vehicle arises and sinks; an evening sermon. Holding up a tea cup, he said: "In the past, Zhaozhou offered a single cup of tea to all visiting and resident monks.
Today, it has fallen into the hands of this mountain monk. I wish for you, all you venerable elders, to take a sip together.
Tell me, is there flavor within it? It simply requires that you recognize this tea. Even if...
"Set down the tea cup. Again, where would you go? Listen! He looked left and right and said, "This single flavor alone is possessed by every person.
Who is it that sets it down? (Wanlu Zhang’s Succession)
Changqing Shangyan Dao of Wujiang was a native of Xinghua. Once, ascending the hall, he raised an ancient case:

A monk asked Changqing, "When there is a question and there is an answer, the guest and host are clearly distinguished. But when there is neither question nor answer, what then? Changqing said, "I am afraid it will rot away!"
A monk asked Muzhou, "When there is questioning and answering, the roles of guest and host are clearly defined. But when there is neither question nor answer, what then?
Muzhou said, "Everyone they meet says it is good to retire from office, yet I have never seen a single person beneath the forest trees.

Yuanwu said, "If I were Chongning, when asked, 'When there is questioning and answering, the roles of guest and host are clearly defined; but when there is neither question nor answer, what then? I would reply to him:"

Having secured Annam, he was again anxious about the regions north of the Great Wall. The Master said: "If someone were to ask New Changqing, 'When there is a question and an answer, the roles of host and guest are clearly defined;
but when there is neither question nor answer, what then? you should simply say to him: 'The head is tilted; the eyes stare wide.'"
If he were to deliberate, [the Master] would strike him across the spine with his staff. Why is this? Has it not been said: "Ouyang is still tolerable;
the most painful is Silla" (Master Jianqing was a successor of Xuefeng).
Chan Master Xuanji Xing of Dafosi was the son of Gao from Tianjin. He received full ordination under Minzhong Run.
Upon reaching Zhejiang, he visited Lingyin Li and attained realization while contemplating the koan of the bamboo stick. He later studied under Sanfeng Qing and "lost his sack.
In his teaching hall, he would often test practitioners with three questions, the first of which was: "The World-Honored One’s samādhi—Kāśyapa did not..."
Kāśyapa knew; Ānanda did not know. Since he did not know, why was the golden-brocade *kāṣāya* transmitted from one to another?
One of his contemporaries said: "The aconite of Mianzhou and the ginger of Hanzhou. Another said: "Heaven and earth share the same root as I."
All things and I are one body. For what reason can sand not enter the eye? He provides his own verse in their stead: "A second offense will not be tolerated. One day [a monk] asked:
"In the human world, there is no water that does not flow eastward. For what reason, where the power of Yu did not reach, does the sound of the river flow westward?
He provides his own verse in their stead: "For now, let this one move pass. (Master Jianqing was his successor.)
Master Yelu Zhenhua Xuelu of Yushan ascended the hall for a discourse.
He cited an ancient worthy who said: "Thirty years ago, I once severed the life-root of one person; day and night I am filled with anxiety. How can I avoid this? Yelu [responded]:
"I chew it down to the roots, leaving not a single trace. The Master passed away in the Jiayin year of the Kangxi era after reciting a verse. There is a *qi* tree [at his site].
The *Anji* (Collection of Hermitage Writings) and several volumes of *Jingshan Kehua* (Talks of a Guest from Qing Mountain) were transmitted to the world by Yuehan Qian.
Regarding Chan Master Chao of Zishishuangqiao in Suzhou: he was the son of the Wan family of Hukou in the prefecture. He relied upon Baoyun Qian and investigated the kōan:
"Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion? After a long time, he did not achieve realization and requested to change his line of inquiry.

Qian chided him, saying, "Do you want to change the causal conditions of your practice? The Master was greatly perplexed. One day, hearing the clamor of crows at the treetops, he suddenly attained enlightenment.
[The Master] asked, "What is the meaning of Xiangyan’s 'climbing the tree'? The Master replied, "The ancient hall cannot endure the cold.
He asked, "What is the meaning of Nanquan’s 'beheading the cat'? The Master replied, "The mountains are green and the waters are clear. He said, "..."
"Zhaozhou wears straw sandals on his head. What does this mean? The Master said: "A grove by the corner of the hall, the wind [blows through it].
[The monk] asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "All day long, wind-blown leaves roll in the long corridors.

He asked: "What is the Dharma? The Master said: "His household door is not opened lightly. He asked: "What is the Sangha? The Master said: "If you wish not to incur karma of the Avīci Hell, do not..."
[The Master] said, "To slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma. [The questioner] asked, "Upon what did the ancients rely? [The Master] replied, "Whenever he met someone, he would shout.
[The questioner] asked, "Upon what did the ancients rely? [The Master] replied, "Whenever he met someone, he would strike them with his staff.
[The Master] said, "Even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands could not have rescued him. (Yue-han Qian succeeded him.)
Chan Master Yuanhong of Hanxi and Qiuan was the son of the Qingyang Zhuang family.

He relied upon Baoyun at Meixi and, upon being presented with the kōan of the woman emerging from samādhi, attained sudden enlightenment, saying: "At first, I thought only of the length of the thatch."
The original uneven ground has been burned away; the incense burner of the ancient temple offers this verse:
Accompanying the dragon-and-serpent brush of the Great Antiquity, Cold moonlight and frost never depart. A few wisps of swirling smoke ascend, And the pavilions that appear are naturally wondrous.
The Master’s conduct was lofty and eminent. Having received his dharma-transmission certificate three years prior, he passed away. There is the *Legacy Words of Hanxi*.
Volume One (Monthly Correspondence from Qian).
Chan Master Ruan’an Jiānshù of Wújiāng was the son of the Ni family of Yúcūn in the district. He relied upon Bǎoyún and spent the summer retreat at Shípíng.
One day, as he returned from begging for alms, Qián asked, "What is it like when the wild sheep hang their horns? As the Master was about to open his mouth—
[The Master] spoke. Qian suddenly shouted. The Master was startled. Qian called out, "Jiānshù, come here! Just now I asked you; what did you answer?

As the Master was about to open his mouth, Qian shouted again. At this, the Master attained realization. The following day, he went to the abbot’s quarters and asked, "What is the ultimate principle that does not meet the occasion?
Qian said, "You do not understand how to ask this question. He then uttered a word in response.
When asked, "What is it like when [all things] are exhausted? the Master said, "A thousand-foot length of drifting silk.

In the *ding-si* year of the Kangxi era, as the Master was about to pass away, he secretly prepared for his death by shaving his head, bathing his body, and donning his robes. He struck the bell to bid farewell to the assembly and sat upright until his transformation.

Because the great assembly wailed and lamented, he suddenly opened his eyes and rebuked them. He then ordered the administrative monk to prepare a "feast for the ignorant" and extended the period for seven days.
Day by day he followed the assembly, and after the midday meal, he passed away. His son asked, "What now? The Master said in a stern voice, "Dongshan was like that;
I am not so. Qian said, "I wish to present what is 'not so' for you to see. The Master snapped his fingers once and immediately passed away (Yuehan Qian succeeded him).

Chan Master Huaiyue of Zhanshan held a small *can* (sermon) upon the commencement of the retreat: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time establish jeweled royal lands upon the tip of a single hair;
the ancestral masters of successive generations turn the Great Dharma Wheel within a single mote of dust.
If you attempt to understand this through 'good' talk, have you not heard it said: 'Good things are not as good as having none'? If you engage in false deliberation, how could this be so today?"
Regarding "false and illusory time": if you can take this up and carry it forth here, you may then overturn the meditation seat.
If not yet so, then enter the hall and exert yourself. Question: "What is the path of Bodhi? The Master said: "Greed, anger, and delusion. Question:
"What is the karma of birth and death? The Master said: "Precepts, concentration, and wisdom. Question: "Is there not a great deal of inversion? The Master said: "In your own portion."
"What do you say? he asked. [The monk] replied, "Abandoning greed, hatred, and delusion, one cultivates precepts, concentration, and wisdom.

The Master said, "Your inversions are not few. [The monk] asked, "Does the original nature have arising and ceasing? The Master said, "When it is alert, the myriad dharmas are all born; when it is tranquil, the myriad dharmas are all extinguished."
[The student] said, "Since there is arising and ceasing, there must be change. The Master said, "To transform the myriad things into oneself; to transform oneself into the myriad things.
[The student] asked, "How can there be anything fixed? The Master struck him and said, "Who has been speculating for you? (Ji Xian succeeded him.)
Small Assembly by Chan Master Tong of Yumen, Piyang Shijing: From the beginning, there has been no dharma to be spoken. To unravel paper is merely to look for holes and drive wedges into them.
Solely upholding the lineage of Jibei, this matter is forged with tongs and hammers—nailing down nails and cutting through iron.

If one can seize it and act upon it immediately, what need is there to speak of "melting snow in a red furnace"? There is even more: "drilling through a wall to steal light," and "beating a donkey’s waist until its bones are exposed. This is the report.

"O people! A mere glance—or no glance at all. On the ground of ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), one does not receive a single speck of dust. In a single thought-moment, ten thousand years are fully realized.
At the winter solstice, he addressed the assembly: "One, two, three, four, five. A centipede swallows the tiger of the South Mountain. Five. Four, three, two, one.
A single-horned earthen ox stands upon the surface of the water. The pillar presses painfully upward to Mount Sumeru. Even an iron hammer has no hole."
The Broth. Who would have known that every day is a good day? It is simply because today is the winter solstice. The entire mechanism has been leaked; there is no handle to grasp.
Small Sermon: There is one in Suzhou; there is one in Changzhou. What need is there to speak of facing south to look for the Big Dipper?
Under the shadowless tree, the boat is joined together. Reaching out the hand was originally for the purpose of drawing it back. Looking left and right, he said: "Do you understand?"
"Leaves fall and return to their roots. When he came, he had no mouth (Ji Yan-nian-si).
Chan Master Mingjiang of Beidu Pilu Zhengxin was the son of the Wei clan of Qingyuan, Baoding. His parents died early;
he went to Master Lin of Gui-fang to receive the tonsure and was fully ordained at Guangji. Together with Lin, he constructed Baozhu Temple.
Dong continued the holy legacy; the Master’s contribution was indeed great. He studied under Zhuan’an Yu Shanying and attained realization during a retreat.
The rector asked, "What is your original face before your parents were born? The Master replied, "Vermilion, crimson, black, and white.

The rector said, "And what about after you have died and been cremated? The Master replied, "True gold does not fear being tested by fire. The rector nodded his head in approval. From [this point on].
This person strictly maintained the precepts, eating his rice from a single grain and wearing coarse cloth robes with straw sandals, vowing to himself for the rest of his life.
Next, he visited the ancient master Yunju; entering the "Dry Wood Hall," one day the Master asked him, "The snow covers the thousand mountains—why then is the solitary peak not white?"
The Master said, "He has emerged with a head that stands out from the rest. He asked again, "Regarding the story of Nanquan killing the cat, what is it like?
The Master said, "The verification is right before your eyes. Gu asked, "As for Zhaozhou putting on his straw sandals, how about that? The Master said, "He was eight *ke* late.
He asked again, "To the left is a high precipice; to the right is a great body of water; ahead is a pit ten thousand fathoms deep; behind is a great..."
"The fire comes to press upon you. Tell me, how will you avoid it? The Master said, "The dense bamboo does not hinder the flowing stream; the high mountain does not obstruct the flying white clouds.

The Ancients approved this, and he subsequently received the transmission of the seal of enlightenment. He went forth to reside at Vairocana Temple. Upon entering the monastery for the opening assembly, he ascended the hall and said:
"The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it arises only by relying on conditions. Now, having been reverently invited to preach the Dharma by the An-hu Protector of the Dharma, and furthermore—"
The Way. What can be said? A north wind pierces the bones; a drop of water turns to ice. Amidst the snow, the plum blossoms forth—unclouded throughout antiquity and today.
At times, a single hair swallows the vast ocean; at times, a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. In greatness it does not increase; in smallness it does not decrease.
Beyond the limit of Vairocana, there is neither lack nor excess. At the gateway of the six sense organs, light is emitted and the earth is moved. This must certainly be...
"What is it? Listen! An ancient said: "There is a thing, bright and vivid, black as lacquer; it supports the heavens above and the earth below.
It is ever present amidst movement and function, yet cannot be gathered up within movement and function. Now tell me, what does it mean that it cannot be gathered up? He lets out a shout and says:
"The translucent rabbit-horns span the three periods of time; the brilliant tortoise-hair encircles the nine mounds. (Minggu)
Pasi). Zen Master Jiming Yuantong Mingguang of the Capital ascends the hall: "The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it is born by relying on conditions. The Way does not travel in vain;
it manifests in response to the times. An old shop opens anew; the Compassionate Ferry has long been launched. When movement occurs, there is nowhere [it does not reach]."
It is not manifest. When still, where could it be hidden? He called to the assembly, saying: "Do you understand? Originally there is not a single thing; one merely clings to flowers in the sky.
How could this scatter sand into the eyes of people of the present age? Ascending the hall, he said:

"The first principle is that which the thousand sages have not transmitted. The final phrase is to be realized before words are spoken. The wind blows across the great earth; the bright sun hangs in the heavens. In an ordinary moment, one treads upon the... (Vimalakīrti).

Luding: "The entire body is free of dependence; it is fundamentally natural. (He lets out a shout. Entering the hall, he says: "The constant radiance is uniquely revealed, shining through antiquity and soaring into the present.
The scales of judgment rest with you; cut through the tangles. Transcending alone beyond the mundane world, move freely as you wish.
He strikes the meditation staff and says: "The Great Way is originally without obstruction; one must rely on the feet of its descendants to travel upon it. Dragging his staff, he descends.
The Seat. On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, he ascended the hall and said: "In this season of deep winter, cold as iron, everyone keeps their mouths shut and hides their tongues.

Ice and snow solidify into towering solitary peaks; even beholding the morning star at night, they have still not attained penetration. Great assembly, the World-Honored One beheld the star and attained the Way;
this has been transmitted from antiquity to the present. Why, then, do we say 'not yet penetrated'? After a long silence, he said: "That which was born of one's parents..."
[Silence]. I shall never speak for you [Mingbo Gu Si].

Master Chan Master Jili Sutang’s informal discourse (xiaocan): Words do not unfold the matter; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded.
As for the question regarding the "three pounds of flax" asked by the Venerable just now, I said to him: "I am originally..."
A man from the Eastern Land speaking Western barbarian dialect—tell me, is there any room for deliberation here?
If you say there is, you betray Dongshan; if you say there is not, you betray this monk. The matter is such a matter; the person must be such a person.
What harm is there in asking like clouds gathering? An answer comes like pouring from a jar. Were even a hair’s breadth of conceptual principle to fill one's breast...

In the midst of it all, it hangs between the lips and teeth; here, it flows like water. If, on a later day, you must swallow a hot iron ball, do not resent that I did not break it open for you today, O Senior.
For the sake of the practitioner Ren-an Jue, this small *can* (sermon) is given before the spirit.
Miao-zong let Great Wisdom pass; he grasped the pearl from beneath the chin of the dragon. Ling-xing tested Fu-pei; the golden-winged bird spread its wings.
From splitting the sea with an empty hand, even unto the road to Mount Tai and the side of the starving child’s cauldron, he deployed great mechanisms and issued great commands;

there were none who did not find the talisman behind the elbow efficacious and the eye at the crown of the head active. This group of heroic worthies in headscarves has caused the fragrance of the Dharma Garden to flow from ancient times until this very day.
As for the Great Being Ren’an, for ten years he has returned his faith to the vehicle of the lineage; now, in a single stroke, he stands face-to-face before us.
Acting alone, he upholds the Dharma community and assists his spiritual lineage with a supreme and wondrous resolve that, compared to those of former times, is ten times superior.
He is truly a lion within the lion’s den and sandalwood within the sandalwood forest.

Thus, when his tasks for this lifetime were completed, he suddenly withdrew into the profound mystery; having traveled throughout the *pura-kṣetra* (provisional cities), he did not depart from the *ratna* (jewel).
"Furthermore, how is it with a single phrase? After a long silence, he said: "This very place is named the Garden of Peaceful Nurturing; there is no need to further offer up one's own bright pearl.
Addressing the assembly, he raised the example of the World-Honored One beholding the stars, and spoke in verse: "The young wife within the inner chambers knows not of sorrow;
On a spring day, she applies her makeup and ascends the green pavilion. Suddenly beholding the color of the willows at the roadside, She regrets having sent her husband to seek [the stars]."
Fenghou (Seal of the Marquisate) addresses the assembly. He cites the case of Zhang Zhuo’s visit to Shishuang. Shishuang asked, "Scholar, what is your surname?

He replied, "My surname is Zhang and my name is Zhuo. Shishuang said, "Even 'cleverness' cannot be found; from where does 'clumsiness' come? At these words, Zhuo attained sudden enlightenment and presented a verse.
The Master’s eulogy says: The hand of Shishuang shifts the constellations and replaces the stars; When the character for "cleverness" is brought forth, "clumsiness" is no match for it. This causes...

"The scholar enters the dream completely; it is said this is better than ten years of reading books. Addressing the assembly, after concluding the story of the old woman burning the hermitage, he said:
"The old woman possessed the strategy to open the Hongmen Gate, yet how unfortunate that she smashed the Jade Pitcher.
This monk had the courage to attend the banquet, but could not avoid being constrained by the exigencies of the moment. (Commentary by Sanhong Si)
Master Xue of Ren’an Jíngyè Monastery in Tianjin ascended the hall and said: "The ordinary and the sagely are mutually fused within a single source;

the host and guest are interlaced and brilliantly manifest in dual illumination. The light of the mind is uniquely revealed, and the clarity of awareness is fully displayed. It opens the blue lotus within the burning house and purifies white karma amidst the red dust.
It is worn down yet not diminished, stained yet not defiled; it is cultivated yet remains unstained. When in motion, it engages with phenomena..."
The realm of worldly toil: when still, it is a land of deep stupor and intoxication. When neither moving nor still, how can it be?
A wooden child blows a flute amidst the flames; a stone maiden dances amidst the clouds. Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the retreat: The light of a hundred years is short.
Born in spring and aging again in autumn—one must penetrate the barrier of birth and death. To clarify the Way that transcends [the mundane], one may turn over the great ocean at will;

heaven and earth follow as they rise or fall. When a single thought is clarified and pure, the true nature can be constantly preserved. Whether in the form of a Buddha or the shape of a donkey, [it is all one].
From where do external conditions arise? Tell the wandering traveler: cease your studies and let the weeds grow. Wealth and poverty are like the morning dew; fame and renown vanish in an instant.
Directly beneath you, bring this wild mind to rest; do not seek it within the void. Who shall take off their summer shirt?
"Who will wear this winter robe? Take my words to heart. When you depart, do not be distressed. With a shout, he descended from his seat.
(This concludes the transmission of Sanhong.)
Chan Master Shuntian Yuantong Fatan Zhong was a native of the Li family of Yangqu County in Shanxi Province. His mother, Lady Xu, dreamed of an elderly monk seeking lodging before he was born.
From childhood, the Master delighted in sitting in meditation. At the age of ten, he contracted a chronic illness that resisted all medical treatment;

his parents earnestly prayed to the Buddha, who granted permission for him to leave the household life, whereupon his health gradually improved. At fourteen, he paid homage to the Buddha in his home district.
At the age of twenty, Mao’an Shouzong received the tonsure. He ascended Mount Panshan to receive full ordination from Liaozong Xin.

While participating in a seven-day retreat with the assembly, on the fourth day, he suddenly experienced a profound awakening. His younger brother, Wei Zhu Yuan, encouraged him to travel together to seek instruction elsewhere.

They arrived at Yangzhou, where they first visited Tianning Monastery; however, they did not find resonance there. They subsequently went to Longchi and Tiantong, though they continued to strike against the barriers of their practice.

His practice was intense and without falsehood, yet his realization remained unstable. Later, while staying at Nanjian, he heard the sound of wood being split and attained profound clarity regarding the ultimate truth;
nevertheless, he still felt a lack of total liberation. He subsequently visited Xianxing, Pingyang, and Wulei. While at Zifu, he joined the assembly in going out to the fields.
Upon hearing the sound of a drum, the void suddenly split asunder, and a sense of profound exhilaration suffused his entire being.

He then heard that Huangshan Yufeng Gang’s Dharma reputation was eminent, so he went there specifically to rely upon him. Upon seeing him, he asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Tianmu. Gang asked, "How do they guide people there?
The Master said, "They are accustomed to severing the life-root of others. Gang asked, "For what reason is your own life-root not severed?"
The Master said, "I have no life-root; what is there to cut? Wugang said, "Your former words do not accord with your later speech.
The Master said, "Today I have seen the Master in person. Wugang asked again, "Where is your native place? The Master said, "Shanxi. Wugang said, "..."
"Is Fenyang Zao your fellow villager? The Master said, "I have never known this fellow. Daowei Geng raised his incense board; the Master shook his sleeves and went out.
Geng said, "The phrase for turning back has not yet been presented. The Master turned around and made the gesture of clapping his hands. Geng nodded in approval.

He then received the transmission of the Dharma and served him diligently for two years before taking leave to go to Yanjing. Initially he resided at Zhengjue, and later moved to Yanjing. Subsequently...
Master Zhuzhuyuantong ascended the hall. When he holds fast, the entire world of the ten directions—with its myriad phenomena, great and small, long and short—leaks not even a hair’s breadth.
When he lets go, it is like the Great Peng cleaving the sea, its wings striking the three thousand worlds, or the divine Kunfish circling southward, borne aloft by the whirlwind for ten thousand li.
Only those with such eyes and vision are permitted to stride alone across the great earth. However, if...
Hesitation. Ten thousand miles of white clouds. At the small *sǎn* (sermon) upon the conclusion of the retreat: there is a path before the gate; set down your feet and pass freely.
Once the bag-mouth is opened, the tip of the awl is fully revealed. Every one has a head as lofty as a tiger; every person has feet like a dragon.
There is only one thing I must tell you all: when passing beneath the Black-Lacquered Kunlun Mountains, do not let it be lost.
Two rows of eyebrows. Entering the hall: When it is hot, be affected by the heat; when it is cold, be affected by the cold. That place where neither cold nor heat reaches—what is it?
It is a dried piece of dung. (With his staff, he draws a line and says: Ghosts and spirits cannot extinguish its vision; Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot fathom its essence.
Under the Gate of Perfect Penetration, we discuss the real and not the unreal. Why strive for what is insufficient and yield what is superfluous?
Carrying his staff, he descended from the seat. He offered this verse on Nanquan’s Beheading of the Cat: Half a straw raincoat amidst wind and rain, half a river breeze;
Not fishing for golden scales, I intend to catch a dragon. The stench of raw flesh permeates the whole body, impossible to evade; From this single word, the guiding principle was established.
A monk asked, "In the absence of dreams and thoughts, and without seeing or hearing, where exactly does the true host reside?
The Master said: "Bamboo shadows sweep the steps, yet the dust is unmoved; the moon pierces the bottom of the pond, yet the water leaves no trace. [Another] asked:
"Is the breast milk one has drunk equal to the waters of the four oceans? Are the bones accumulated in this body like Mount Vaipulya? Pray, who is the ultimate [self]?"

At first, when his parents were present, the Master said: "Whether walking, one is attached; whether sitting, one is attached. Later, while the Master was practicing walking meditation (*caṅkrama*), a monk knelt and asked:
"What is the Three Essentials? The Master raised his foot to show him. The monk then asked: "What are the Three Requirements? The Master stamped his foot once.
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning? The Master kicked him over and walked away.
Duhu Fa of Mount Lu asked, "Of the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, how many have already appeared? The Master said, "To miss it right before one's face.

[The monk] asked, "If a member of the monastic community can penetrate this thoroughly, will they be able to realize the fruit and practice well? The Master said, "Do not slander me. [The monk] said, "Two..."
The mud ox fights its way into the sea; even unto this day there is no news of it. What is the essential meaning [of this]? The Master said, "Not a single point can be hidden from him.
[The student] asked, "If one is questioned and does not respond, what kind of principle does that constitute? The Master said, "Its sound resounds like thunder.
Shan-dou then presented a verse on his original face: "Dependent and profound, its wondrousness is difficult to name. Vast..."
Vast and azure, the universe is full. It is in vain to say that the Chan gate is empty of the Dharma-realm; when a single thought is clearly realized, it is immediately one's former life.
The Master also sealed this with a verse (Yu Feng Gangsi).
Chan Master Weizhuyuan of Longquan at Qianshan in Shengjing was the son of the Li family of Yangqu in Shanxi. His mother was surnamed Xu;
she dreamed of a red light entering her chamber before his birth. At the age of three, he fell ill, and his mother promised him ordination. At five, his mother passed away.
At the age of ten, his father sent him to Fumo Hermitage in his native district to receive the tonsure under Master Shouzong. At eighteen, he resolved to travel to study with various masters;
he first visited Hanyi Xian of Pingyang, who showed him the koan, "Who is it that recites the Buddha's name?

He did not yet know where to find the answer. At twenty, he went to Fenyang to receive full ordination. He then traveled north to Yanjing to visit Dajing Min, who held up a single fist to show him. [Min] did not accept his response.
Qia. Malarahan. He entered the hall to engage in investigation, but after half a year he had made no progress. He took his leave and departed, subsequently traveling through various lecture halls.

He subsequently attended Master Puan Yuan at Haihui Monastery, serving him closely. From time to time, the Master would prompt him with inquiries, and he remained awake day and night like one who is demented.
One day, Yuan asked, "What are you investigating? The Master replied, "I am investigating: 'Who is it that recites the Buddha's name? Yuan said:
"Is there a way to enter? The Master said, "There is no place to enter. Yuan said, "I shall go to prostrate before the Buddha in the hall.

As soon as the Master stepped across the threshold, he saw ten thousand rays of rosy light shooting into his eyes. After a short while, countless objects emerged, reflected from the mirror-like light.
At that moment, he stood before the offering table; he did not realize it until dawn had already arrived at the fifth watch, when the hall master opened the door.
He was startled. He asked, "Who is it? The Master said, "It is I. The host asked, "And who are you? At that moment, Yuan suddenly attained realization.
The host asked again; the Master slapped him across the face. The host cried out loudly, "A thief! Yuan said, "Where is the thief? The Master slapped him again.
Yuan said, "So, it turns out you are a house-thief yourself! The Master let out a shout, and Yuan withdrew. The following spring—
Yuan received an invitation from Jinmen. As the Master followed him onto the boat, Yuan saw a fish playing among the wood and said, "When will this come to an end?
The Master replied, "The waves of the lake and sea are vast; let it be as it is, free and easy. Yuan struck him once with his palm, and the Master fell into the water.
As soon as the Master rose, Yuan said, "Speak! Speak! Before the Master had opened his mouth, Yuan struck him again into the water. The Master rose once more.
Dongyuan rose. Dongyuan struck him again. The Master said, "The thread on the tip of the fishing pole is for you to play with; without disturbing the waves, your intent unfolds naturally.
Dongyuan said, "So it is, so it is. When the retreat concluded, the Master bestowed upon him the robe and whisk, thereby conferring his seal of approval.
He subsequently went forth to reside at Pilu in Beijing, Jinfeng in Zunhua, Baoding in Fengrun, Longchi in Wangtian, Qingfeng in Shengjing, and Qian...
At the Shānlóngquán Wànshòu Temple and the various monasteries of Gāizhōu Xīnglóng, [the Master] ascended the hall and said: "Great, yet without exterior; small, yet without interior.
To hold fast and to let go—transcending the crowd and excelling the eminent. Within the flash of lightning, it is precisely the moment to turn the body;
amidst the spark of a flint, each finds its own place. There is no ground that does not proclaim its sovereignty; in every location, there is auspiciousness. He then gave a shout.
He said: "There is another essential word: most certainly avoid nodding off. Small Assembly: "Tonight marks the completion of the seven-day period. The examination is finished.
The roaring lion cub understands emptiness and performs a backward somersault; his nostrils reach toward the heavens, and not even a thousand sages can recognize him.

Is there anyone here who recognizes him to this day? After a long silence, he said: "A single wipe brings the bone out. Evening Assembly: The Master posed a question: "When does winter arrive and spring return?"
All things are brought forth. Now tell me: what is it that is brought forth upon a ground where there is neither yin nor yang?

The assembly’s answers were unsatisfactory, so the Master said: "Chew slowly on a slice of jujube; swallow gently. Move the ancient incense burner aside, and ride from the mountain gate onto the Buddha hall.
(Pai’an Yuan was his successor.)
Chan Master Dazhu Zhizhe of Xinglong Temple in Kyoto was the son of the Yuan family of Danyang in Jiangnan. His father was named Ruruī and his mother, née Wang.
At birth, he was already able to sit upright. At the age of seven, he accompanied his mother to offer incense; seeing the golden hue of the Buddha, he was filled with joy.
Consequently, he sought to leave the household life. At the age of sixteen, his parents both passed away. He then went to Puci Temple and paid respects to Qizhen, receiving the tonsure.
At twenty, he ascended Mount Hua; having completed the full ordination, he climbed the Three Peaks and first visited Master Shokuichi.

One day, while carrying water, he saw that the ground was clear and transparent, whereupon he suddenly awakened to the source of the mind and thoroughly comprehended all phenomena. He then entered the abbot’s quarters, and the Master said:
"You are fetching water. What is this? The Master said, "The carrying pole has transformed into a dragon.
Zhi said, "Where is the pearl? The Master then struck him a slap across the face. Zhi said, "This rustic fellow is easy to beat. The Master said, "You do not even recognize the pearl."
Zhì said, "Not yet. The Master said, "A second offense will not be tolerated. Zhì said, "I may then be called Dàzhū; do not call me Dàfú.
Thereupon, he changed to his present name. He subsequently went to Yángfén to visit Línjī Guān. One day during the evening session, Guān asked, "What is the phrase that is not obtained from others?
The Master said, "The entire great earth is this student; what phrase is there to be sought? Guān—
He struck the staff twice and said, "Tell me, is the old monk within the students, or outside the students? The Master replied, "I deeply appreciate this question.
[The other] observed his nodding. Later, while traveling to Mount Wutai, he arrived at the capital city and passed through Yanjing to visit Shengxin Jue. Their faculties and insights were compatible;
teacher and disciple were in perfect accord. Furthermore, he was...

The Prince of Yushuo, the Yuchin Wang, reverently prepared robes and a whisk, and after repeatedly offering words of encouragement and consolation, he finally received the transmission of the Dharma-seal.

In the year of Bingchen, he succeeded to the seat at Yanjing. Subsequently, while presiding over the Hall at Xinglong, he ascended the dais and said: "The myriad dharmas interpenetrate, and one suddenly perceives the boundless realms of all lands;
the mind is empty and has attained the highest rank, fully manifesting the jade palaces and crystal towers. To such an extent that the clay deities rise of their own accord, and even the rubble..."

Increasing the radiance, it illuminates both past and present; its brilliance encompasses heaven and earth. Pointing to Chang’an as the Land of Ultimate Bliss, he takes the great earth as a monastery.
Launching a bottomless boat, he ferries across both the holy and the ordinary; singing the song of non-arising, he provides sustenance for both the hidden and the manifest.
As for this one phrase—“Today, the Jueyuan Temple is once again radiant”—how would you explain it? [He] suddenly strikes the ground with his staff and says: “The stubborn rock bursts forth!”
Revealing the new face of the Buddha; the Dharma banner stands high for ten thousand years of spring. Entering the Hall: The Dharmakāya is without illness;
even the wondrous medicine of *amṛta* (clarified butter) is but a superfluous teaching. When the eye is free from blemish, though Buddhas and Patriarchs be honored, they are of no account.

Even if one were to realize immeasurable *samādhis*, manifest inexhaustible supernatural powers, abide for immeasurable billions of kalpas, and expound the wondrous principles as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—its meaning [remains beyond reach].
"Endless. This is still a defilement at the edge of pure dharmas; it is in discord with the Way. How can one discern and communicate the message?
After a long silence, he said: "The dripping of water from the eaves is not caused by rain; the crow’s cry at midnight is not sound. He ascended the hall and said:
"When the mind is empty and non-abiding, it is like an ancient mirror without a trace. When everything encountered is seen as true, it is like cold ice being entirely water—clearly so."
One’s own mind is the source of all phenomena. To realize that all phenomena are non-dual with one’s own mind—tell me, where is this mind right now?
He lets out a shout and says: "The lantern enters the pillar" (Shengxin Jue).
Chan Master Yanjing Xiangyun ascended the hall and said: "The first month of the year, when three nines meet; meeting thus, we encounter a most auspicious season.
Raising my eyes, I gaze afar at the vastness of the Dharma-realm; counting on my fingers, I reckon the great and small snows. If you ask what the matter of the Buddha-dharma is like:
the frost is severe, yet the light upon the treetops is bright and pure. The Elephant King holds icicles in his trunk; the Lion..."
Holding raw iron in his mouth, he has attained a clarity that is no ordinary matter. To speak it back, there is no interruption. *He lets out a shout.* He descends from the seat.

The Small Assembly Lecture on the Eighth Day of the Twelfth Month. The World-Honored One said: "Fundamentally, there is nothing original or subtle. When the true command is put into action, illumination and function arrive together.

For six years at the Snowy Mountains, his heart was as pure as ice and his integrity as firm as snow; he hung a spider’s web between his eyebrows. His countenance—*he lets out a shout*. He descends from the seat.
"The magpie nests at the top of the peak; such ascetic practice has persisted until now. Seeing the news of the stars, how can one speak of it?
Looking left and right, he said, "If you are a phoenix chick, you will not seek it there.

He addressed the assembly, having finished recounting the story of the World-Honored One’s first birth, and then said, "This old fellow only knows how to greedily follow the road, unaware that dawn has broken. Although Yunmen..."
To carry out the correct command is like joining bamboo to point at the moon. Examining this closely, I give thirty blows to each. Why is that?
Because one must not broadcast the family’s internal disgrace to the outside world. A verse on the World-Honored One beholding the morning star:
