Xuedou said, "The wind and light are everywhere. Yunmen replied, "Not yet; speak further. Xuedou said, "I thought there was something else. Yunmen then let him go.
The following evening, Yunmen saw him again and asked, "How have things been since your last visit? Xuedou said, "Flutes and pipes play through the moon over a thousand peaks;
pines and bamboos sit empty, locking in the clouds of a single mountain. Yunmen asked, "What about right now? Xuedou said, "As you please."

Guanzhan said, "Look beneath your feet. The Master (Xuedou) then gave a shout. Guanzhan nodded his head and bestowed upon him a prediction of enlightenment. [Someone] asked, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said, "The green bamboo in front of the courtyard grows new shoots. [The questioner] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "It covers the entire world. [The questioner] asked, "And as for the scholar's own portion, what is it?

The Master said: * *Kuan-chan*: To observe and contemplate. * *Cheng*: To receive or inherit. * *Jia-xia*: Beneath one's feet; a metaphor for one's own fundamental state or the ground of reality. * *He*: A shout; a sudden, non-conceptual expression of realization. * *Shou-ken*: To nod the head in agreement or approval. * *Ji-bie*: To record and bestow a prediction of future enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*). * *Chu-shen-chu*: The place of origin or emergence; the source from which all Buddhas appear. * *Yi-zhi*: The underlying intent or essential meaning.

* *Ge-fu-tian-xia*: To cover or encompass the whole world. * *Xue-shi*: A scholar-official; here referring to the practitioner or student. * *Fen-shang*: Within one's own portion or sphere of responsibility. * *Zuo-mo-sheng*: How is it? What is it like? A phrase used to inquire about the nature of reality or one's own realization.
"The ancient Buddhas have long since passed away. Regarding Yunmen’s verse on the fan, he said: "Fluttering spring breezes lightly strike the face;
Wordless, the peach and plum trees naturally form a stream. How can this singular flavor ever be exhausted? In the vast expanse of the universe, how many know it?
Regarding his verse for examining the two hermits, he said: "A lute held askew amidst the misty vines; A single melody of the ancient *Qingping* tune."
Song: The singing poet’s two tongues are fit for laughter; Darkly riding the bright moon, they float upon autumn waves.

(Kai-am Seung-si) On New Year’s Day, the Small Assembly (Sōsan) by Zen Master Gudang Jik, the Record Secretary of Wansu, born of the Wu clan of Wujiang: "Nothing, nothing, nothing; something, something, something.

When asked about his place of birth, he extends his Buddha-hand; A single crackle of firecrackers announces the New Year’s joy. All of you— *Note: The final line "All of you" (Dajia) indicates the verse is addressed to the assembly.*
Wishing for boundless longevity. The mountains are naturally high and the waters naturally deep. What need is there to seek out flowers or inquire after willows?
When spring arrives in Jiangnan, every tree is fragrant. The six-petaled and five-petaled snowflakes alike reveal their secrets.
But tell me: what is this "revealing"? After a long silence, he said: "Yunmen’s rice cake, Zhaozhou’s tea, Xuefeng’s wooden ball, and Zihu’s dog. (Wuan Juecheng was his successor.)
Chan Master Haimi of Chaling addressed the assembly. Having finished citing the story of the bamboo pointer, he said:

"A single piece of black-lacquered bamboo; it stubbornly and falsely produces knots. Held horizontally or grasped vertically according to the occasion, where is there any distinction between 'separation' and 'contact'?
He then held the bamboo pointer across his chest and said, "All you venerable brothers present, try to determine this for yourselves. After a long silence, he said, "Yu..."
Where power does not reach, the river’s sound flows toward the west. In praise of Deshan’s alms-bowl: "Returning with his head bowed, he was already suspect;
How could a secret transmission bear to play such tricks? In a house of venomous insects there is no good flavor;
He loved that idle fellow for gaining the advantage. In praise of the Woman Emerging from Samādhi: "The woman is through and through elegant; the World-Honored One opened [the way]."
The mouth invites calamity. If it were Mañjuśrī or Wuming, they would have long ago exposed the truth for you (as noted by Runkongyuan).

Master Jian Chan of Yian, whose Buddhist affinity lay in Longshu, addressed the assembly. He cited the story of Guquan and Ciming bathing together in the Poisonous Dragon Pool, and having finished, he said:
"To turn over in the midst of the grass thicket, to leap out from the heart of the waves—a single thread of water-vein connects two places."
Chenglong attained thorough penetration here: he stirred up waves without creating ripples; he seized the mist without clutching the clouds.

Had he not realized this, he would have been like a venomous dragon drowned in stagnant water. Regarding the verse on the extinction of the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye at the hands of the blind donkey:
"A lifetime wasted carrying a single plank; how could one allow descendants to inherit it recklessly? At the moment of departure, he overturned [the vessel].
In the country of Vārāṇasī, there is only the whole body with nowhere to hide (Hanshan Yuan’s successor).
Zen Master Liang of the Blue Pagoda ascended the hall: "Lifting my head, I suddenly behold the clouds at the edge of the sky; he fully brings forth a branch of spring beyond the norm.
Its fragrance is rich and pervasive, distinguishing high and low; regardless of those who laugh from the sidelines, it becomes more intimate. If one is truly heroic...
O spiritual practitioners, you must advance from the top of the hundred-foot pole and investigate deeply within the depths of ten thousand peaks.

Far removed from formation and destruction, and utterly transcending awakening and delusion—here, not even a speck of dust can be established, the true eye is difficult to peer into, and the myriad streams are cut off.
"Return home and sit in peace. Is there anyone such as this? He gave a shout and said: "The true mechanism is fundamentally beyond hearing and seeing;
why needlessly scatter sand once again? Addressing the assembly, after finishing the story of Aṅgulimālya’s childbirth crisis, the Master said:
A single point of true mechanism crosses the ancient ferry; cutting off both ends, it is ever-new according to the occasion.
Examining this closely, I fear that mother and child have not yet attained peace. Why? For that which enters through the gate is not the family treasure.
In praise of the Woman Emerging from Samādhi: The pond is shimmering, the green willows fresh; A single petal flies across the waters’ edge. The fish leap at dawn—
Having received the moistening grace at dawn, the young gulls come and go, delighting in the fragrant spring (Yongqing Yuan Si).

The Celestial Immortal and Ancient Cloud Meditation Master, Chan Master Fuxian, addressed the assembly. After the discourse on the World-Honored One ascending the seat was concluded, the Master said: "The World-Honored One raised his eyebrows and blinked;
Mañjuśrī responded to the resonance and inherited the void. Although it is true that like sounds respond to one another, alas, they still fall into the seventh [stage]."
Eight down. If you wish to act according to the command, both old fellows deserve a blow of the staff. Addressing the assembly, he raised his staff and said:
"A single white staff, taken up at hand as it comes; there is gathering in and there is letting go. When let go, it fills the Dharma-realm;
when gathered in, it is upon the tip of a single hair. But tell me, when neither gathering nor letting go—how then? He struck the ground once and said: "Thud!"
"Leave it for your descendants to serve as a model" (Daiyan Guangsi).
Chan Master Longshou Angyun of the Capital ascended the hall and said: "Turn the light back upon itself and reflect; manifest a distinct family style.

The mountains are green and the waters are blue; all eight directions are transparently clear. Outside the mind there are no dharmas; outside dharmas there is no mind. This is the life-vein of all Buddhas, suspended [before us]."
The silk is held in the hand; this is the secret instruction of the Patriarchs. Their nostrils reach the heavens. But tell me, what of the matter today?
He lets out a shout and says: "The bright star appears at midday; the white wheel does not shift in broad daylight.

Ascending the hall, he says: "The cold wind blows through the white clouds; the ancient pines gather deep azure mist. A single heart dwelling in the mountains—the sound of the flowing spring remains unchanged. Suddenly, he raises his staff.
The staff-bearer said: "Do you understand? This seven-foot black cane is of no use; its form vaguely resembles a red-spotted snake.
He threw down the staff and descended from his seat. A verse on Deshan’s Alms Bowl: "The phrase of the open sun seizes the arrow-tip mechanism;
father and son both display their wondrous skills. The handle of the bowl has been stolen away; where there is already no room for doubt, it is even more worthy of suspicion."
The verse on the woman emerging from samādhi says: "Lofty and majestic are the green mountains; vast and expansive is the flowing water. The clear *shang* mode is tuned to the lute of Boya;
a single melody, vast and silent, like the tail-feathers of a cold phoenix. (Shengxin Juesi)

Chan Master Falan Cheng of Ba’en Temple in Jingzhou was a native of the Chen family from Zhijiang in Jingzhou. While residing at Tianwang Monastery, he ascended the hall on the occasion of the Buddha’s birthday.
A monk asked, “What is the realm of Tianwang? The Master said, “The imperial road is as straight as a string.
The monk asked, “What is the person within the realm? The Master said, “Meeting face-to-face, we are intimate. The monk asked, “What is it like when both person and realm are forgotten?”
The Master said, "A single wild goose flies across the heavens. Then he said, "Who among you saw the morning star at night?
Both sages and commoners have been cast down; only the nostrils have nowhere to hide. Their azure ridges shine with brilliant clarity. When the Heavenly King saw this, he pinched him for him;
making a gesture of twisting a nose with his hand, he said, "Śākyamuni, let go! (The Master) followed suit.
I have come. Since it is said that all sentient beings possess the wisdom, virtue, and marks of the Tathāgata, why do you treat this with such great alarm and petty wonder?

Nevertheless, were it not for the path of the woodcutter, how could one reach the home of Ge Hong? Ascending the hall, he said: "Master Xiu’s Northern School has been beyond the reach of right and wrong for a thousand years.
Now that I, this mountain monk, have arrived, my song of snow can hardly match yours in harmony. For now, I shall simply act as a mountain dweller."
Old man! Neither I nor you can fathom this. I report it to all you students traveling for study: tread lightly, lest you step upon the path of the Gateless Barrier (Shuijianhai’s successor).
Chan Master Dizang Han Shike of Yizhen, Yangzhou, was the son of the Fan family of Suzhou. Upon succeeding to the seat, he ascended the hall and said:
"That which enters through the gate is not one's own family treasure. What flows forth from within one’s own breast covers heaven and earth.
Holding up his whisk, he asked, "Do you understand? At any moment, it pierces the mother-born eyes; its boundless splendor leaves no room for laughter to cease. (Shuijian Hai was his successor.)
Chan Master Baogai Benhuai of Chongqing was a native of Bishan County. He studied under Xiqian Jing;

by day he drew water to serve the assembly, and by night he entered the hall for intensive investigation, exhausting himself in diligent labor. Later, he followed Tianwang Hai, residing at Tiefo Monastery in Jingzhou and serving as the attendant to Dizang.
He frequently held key positions. In the year Wushen, he painted a portrait of Hai and returned to Shu. As for Hai—
He was granted a verse. He went to Shu to seek out the tomb of his kinsmen, but no one knew its location; he wept bitterly and wiped away his tears.
Later, while residing at Baogai, his conduct was as pure as ice, and the fourfold assembly looked up to him with reverence. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "You are a slave.
The monk prostrated himself, and the Master shouted at him to leave. In the Jiashu year of the Kangxi era, he resided at Tianwang and subsequently passed away; a stupa was erected for him.

As for Chan Master Xian’an Zhe of Shimen in Yiyang, Changsha (successor of Shuijian Hai of Tiandwang), he was the son of the Chen family of Jiangling. He was thirty-three years old [when he entered the monastic order].

He entered the monastic order under Tiantai Wang Hai and soon thereafter took charge of the monastery’s affairs. He was dignified and fulfilled his duties with distinction; thus, Wang Hai held him in high esteem and faith.
Having shaved his head under Wang, he was subsequently given the name Xian’an by him. He resided at Dizang Monastery in Yizhen and later moved to Shimen.

Upon ascending the hall, he said: “The heavens attain the One and become clear; the earth attains the One and becomes tranquil. But as for this staff—attaining the One, how would you do it? After a long silence, he spoke.
He struck the meditation desk once and said: "Refusing to go while the sky is clear, one must wait until the rain drenches the head; then they are all scattered at once" (*Shuijianhai Si*).
Chan Master Chuan’an Can of Dizang in Yizhen was a native of Zhiyang, Jingzhou. He first resided at Jīnlóng Monastery in Dòngshì, and later moved to Dizang Monastery in Yizhen.
A monk asked, "What is the realm of Dizang? The Master said, "Chūchū bān... (The text here is fragmentary).
In the bamboo grove, a solitary path mists with a whistling sound. [A monk] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The river road in front of my gate leads to Chang'an.
(Shuijianhai was his successor.)
Chan Master Ming of Zhi-an Temple at He-lin in Wu-chang was the son of the Zhou family of Kung-an in Ching-chou. On the anniversary of the Buddha’s birth, he ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, you had already descended into the royal palace; before emerging from the womb, you had already finished saving sentient beings.

What about today's affair? The Master said, "When the mouth opens, it is not on the tip of the tongue. He then said, "Pointing to heaven, pointing to earth... [The text continues with the number seven.]

He paced around in circumambulation; once his horns were exposed, there was nowhere left to hide his body. Nevertheless, before encountering the hand of Yunmen, he caused his descendants to flap their lips.
In the Dingchou year of the Kangxi era, he was appointed to Qixian in Hanyang; five months later, he passed away.
The disciples escorted the reliquary casket back to He-lin Temple and enshrined it in a stupa on the northern slope of Shuangfeng Mountain to the left of the temple (Water Mirror Sea succeeded him).
Chan Master Banfeng Qing of Huanglong in Ezhou was the son of the Wu family of Jingling.
He visited Tianwang Hai at Qixian, who appointed him to oversee the administrative offices of the hall. One day, Hai held up his whisk and said, "Speak a single word here! The Master...

The Master said, "The Way has long since passed. Haikyo said, "It does not matter; please speak again. The Master said, "If I were to speak again, it would be the second phrase. Haikyo nodded his head in agreement.
When fellow practitioners came to visit, they asked, "Do you have any fresh phrases lately? The Master said: "A winding path where no one reaches;
A high mountain where cranes dwell. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Throughout the spring months, flowers bloom at the mouth of the mountain cave; On the north-facing cliffs..."
Clouds veil the horizon; the phrase is clear, yet no one recognizes it. The family style of the Way-farers is leisurely in every matter. Ascending the hall, the Abbot of Tianwang said:
"The single function that points directly upward is naturally and utterly distinct. It stands out prominently before us, unfathomable even to the thousand sages.
Today, this mountain monk receives the imperial decree and carries it out. How can this be described? In an age of Great Peace, there is no need to employ stratagems."
I merely offer this incense of the mind to pray for the Sage’s Radiant Wisdom (Water-Mirror Sea Successor).
Master Dēngmǐn of Jingzhou Tiānwáng Monastery was a filial son of the Zhāng family. At the invitation of Tiānwáng, he addressed the assembly as follows:
This mountain monk strives in mindfulness, dwelling among misty peaks; In my declining years, this idle body endures the cold of the seasons. Today, the official summons has arrived from the heavens;
From now on, right and wrong shall fall upon the human world. [Question: "The World-Honored One possesses an ocean of immeasurable qualities and speaks inconceivable Dharma.
What is this inconceivable Dharma? [Master: "The wind blows through the stone mortar, playing the *Mahā*. [Questioner: "One..."
If phenomena exist, Vairocana falls among the common folk; if the myriad dharmas do not exist, Samantabhadra loses his realm.
Departing from these two paths, I beg the Master to speak quickly. The Master said: "The winter solstice and the Cold Food Festival on the one hundred and fifth day" (Shuijian Hai).
Chan Master Jile Fuzhao Kuan of Jingzhou was the son of the Lei family of Anlu. He addressed the assembly: "The Jile Monastery dwells facing west;

two ponds flank it like mirrors, their ripples shimmering with emerald light. The shade of locust trees covers the ground as horses climb the branches; willow shadows stretch across the pond as fish leap toward the trees.
You people—if you understand this as a description of the scenery at our mountain gate, I dare say you have not yet set foot upon the soil of your own hometown. If...
They hold assemblies on the Dharma-nature of True Suchness; yet these people have not yet reached the principle of perfect penetration.
But tell me, how is it ultimately? "The roses all over the courtyard bloomed last night; my whole body unconsciously became intoxicated by their fragrant soul. (Suijianhai's Successor)
Chan Master Fuyi of Baosheng Temple in Jingnan was a native of the Chen family of his home prefecture. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not an object. What is it? He struck the desk once and said:
"Suddenly snapping the golden lock, one laughs at the peach and plum blossoms by the Changtai Bridge. (His Dharma heir was Hai of Shuijian.)
Nun Yanshou of Jingzhou was originally from Lushan; her secular surname was Jin. She took refuge with Master Hai Tianwang, donned the black robes, and received full ordination.
However, because she could not clarify the "critical phrase" (*huatou*) of her fundamental inquiry, she wept every day. One day, she asked Master Hai:
"What is the one return? Where does it go? Haikai said, "The nun was originally made by you.
The Master then gave a shout. Haikai said, "What about the Qingzhou robe? The Master lifted up his robe and said, "This is a tattered rag.
Haikai then offered this verse: "What is the root of the hundreds of thousands of samādhis? A snap of the fingers opens the gate for those of superior capacity. I rejoice in your eye."
The point where the eyes are truly focused: "A Qingzhou shirt exchanged for tattered rags" (from *Shuijianhai*).
Chan Master Dajiangong of Fanchuan, whose dharma name was Tangdaluangzong, was the son of the Wang family of Wuchang. From his youth, he excelled beyond his peers;

he abandoned Confucianism to follow the Buddhist path and entered the monastic order under Master Deng at Dongying in his native district. He addressed the assembly, saying: "Everywhere it is manifested; every single thing is fully revealed."
Master Ma gave one shout; Baizhang went deaf. Huangbo stuck out his tongue; Linji returned the punch.
Each one of them beat the marrow out of empty space and split open the face-gates of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Then, looking left and right, he said, "Do you see?"
Those near water do not know the place where they suffer from thirst; even a single drop for a person is difficult to digest (Xutang Weisi).
Chan Master Liangzhou of Haihui ascended the hall and said: "Pervading the entire world, it has never been hidden;

clearly and fully manifest, the five petals naturally form a continuous fragrance as the patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another. He spread out both hands and said: "Do not miss it! Do not miss it! Startled.

Small Assembly at the Rising from Songshan, "Breaking the Hearth and Falling" (Pòzào Duò). The Master raised the case of Puhua, who said: "If it comes from the bright side, strike it on the bright side;

if it comes from the dark side, strike it on the dark side; if it comes from empty space, strike it with a continuous flurry; if it comes from the left or right, strike it with a whirlwind. The Master said:
"Puhua employs the 'Iron Ox' mechanism to snatch food from a starving man; he is truly a master. Here at Haihui, there is only one..."
"Flavored iron nails, rice, and wood-apple soup—let you all swallow them sideways or chew them upright as you please.

If you were to chew them through in a single moment, you would naturally experience a sense of total liberation throughout your entire being. Why should this mountain monk trouble himself with further verbosity? [He] took up his bamboo staff and struck everyone down at once.
**Assembling for the Hall upon the Conclusion of the Retreat:** "The clouds follow the dragon; the wind follows the tiger. The phoenix loves to sing; the peacock loves to dance."
How laughable, the donkey prancing its hooves! The spring breeze surges; Yunmen is everywhere. An octagonal millstone flies through the void;
Mount Sumeru is startled into an inverted roar. Today is the seventh nine, sixty-three; Zen monks ride oxen, groping for their noses as they run.
Their straw sandals tread upon the bright moon; Beyond this, there are the eighth nines and the ninth nines— A verse on the Woman.
Emerging from meditation, he said: "The cuckoo cries through the depths of the hundred flowers; The wind plays with flying blossoms, a carpet of gold upon the ground.
Spring’s mandate proceeds as winter; the poor become rich. Amidst the profusion of dense splendor, they wander in vain. (Mingbo Gusì)

Chan Master Mu Chan of Bānshàn in Chǔzhōu composed a verse on an ancient worthy eating oil-cakes, saying:
The flowing water before the mountain plays a jade zither; Having heard it, the fisherman cannot help but laugh.
From antiquity to the present, who within the frosty moon Has run their heels to exhaustion? (Sui’ān Yóu, his successor)
Chan Master Jinglian of Fuan in Chuzhou asked, "What is the realm of Fuan? The Master said, "The Celestial Pond is unfathomably deep.
[The monk] asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Leaning on a staff, watching the clouds fly.

[The monk] said, "I have not realized the Master’s pivot; I beg you to reveal it further. The Master took up his staff, struck once, and said, "It is difficult to deceive one within the cry of a sham chicken."
I am unwilling to let this matter pass by in a muddled fashion (the lineage of Su’an You).
Chan Master Xian, Huiguan of Dongyan in Xuanyang, Chuzhou, asked: “What is the realm of Dongyan? The Master said:
The spring bottom pierces the bright moon; from the mountain peak rises white cloud. [A monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm?

The Master said, "Habituated to sharing fragrant meals amidst frost and snow, the monkeys and birds of the myriad mountains are satiated and silent. The monk performed a woman’s bow and said, "Thank you for the Master’s compassion.
The Master said, "Today at West Rock there is a vegetarian feast" (Sui’an You was his successor).
Chan Master Dayuanjing of Shimen in Qingtian, Chuzhou, asked: "What is the realm of wondrous sound? The Master said: "On the field, the moon is bright;
three feet of waves. At the head of the house, spring has aged; six dynasties of pines. [The monk] asked: "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said:
"The ocean is scooped dry with half a ladle. Pointing toward the setting sun, a staff of *lǐ*. [The monk] said: "A true adept!"
"How was it when you met? The Master said, "Sit and drink tea for now" (Cangshi established his lineage).
Stone Zhu Taiping Gu Yingqian Chan Master ascended the hall and said:
He cited an instance where one day Linji said to Puhua and Ke Fu, "I wish to establish the school of Huangbo here; you two may uphold it."
Three days later, Puhua asked, "What did the Master say three days ago? Linji then struck him.
Three days later, Kefu asked, "Why did the Master strike Puhua three days ago? Linji struck him as well. The Master said:
Look at how Puhua and KeFu unfurled their great banners and drums, raising dust against the wind.

Although Master Linji became a great tree whose shade covers all under heaven, his vision was nonetheless too narrow; wishing to establish the ancestral school, he merely hoped for those two men to bring it to fruition.
I, this mountain monk, am not like that; I also wish to establish it here on a vast scale.
The intent of my compassion is to bring each and every member of this present assembly to full maturity.
If I were to bring them to maturity, it would not wait for three days before or after; from the highest to the lowest, I would have them all receive the painful staff from my own hands.
Why is that? Because the heart bears no grudge, and the face shows no shame. (Qimi Mian succeeded him.)
Chan Master Zongjian Bulun of Doushuai in Yizhou was the son of the Sun family of Qizhou.
At the age of twenty-five, he left the household life under Huituo at Mount Song in Yunnan. He studied the koan "Originally there is not a single thing," yet for three years he attained nothing.
One day, while sitting motionless, he heard a nearby monk let out a shout and had an awakening. When he presented his realization to Huituo, Huituo struck him, saying, "Linji was at Huangbo..."
"Attaining power in the midst of circumstances; attaining power in the midst of great delusion. The Master said, "You have become a laughingstock.
Huì said, "Not yet. Speak further. The Master took up his staff and walked out. One day, Huì asked, "What is the body revealed alone amidst the myriad phenomena?
The Master said, "Bright as the sun; black as lacquer. "What is the nostril of the patch-robed monk? The Master said, "A tile."

The lay practitioner Wanqing of Changzhou, Qian Xuan, was a scholar who professed faith in the Buddha. He served his mother with the utmost filial piety.

His mother, Lady Su, maintained a vegetarian diet, recited the Buddha’s name, and delighted in giving alms to monks. Later, she manifested slight illness and passed away while reciting the Buddha’s name.
The layman was deeply grieved and went to Huayan Yu to inquire how he might investigate the Way and repay his mother’s kindness. Yu said: "Have you not seen that in the past, when..."

He rebuked the Crown Prince, saying: "Break the bones to return them to the father; tear the flesh to return it to the mother. Only then will he manifest his true body to preach the Dharma for his parents.

Within the two eyes of the myriad devas, within the square inch of the heart of the ten thousand nations. He let out a shout (Sui'an You, his successor).

*Verse on the Case of Angulimala’s Difficult Labor:* When the "Startling Insects" arrives, warm breath runs wild;
In the deep forest, flowers and birds announce the spring's haste. The ancient pine knows not how to change with the seasons; Through winter and summer, it remains ever green.
Ying Caotang (Xu Feng Zhao Si).
Yantou Huixiu asked Chan Master Jie, "I have heard it said that the Great Master has been lodging his staff on this mountain for many years; is this true?"
The Master said, “It is so. The monk gave a shout. The Master said, “Yantou is not as good as you, sir. The monk shouted again.
The Master said, “You, sir, are not as good as Yantou. The Master then struck him. The monk withdrew. (Canyong Yi succeeded him.)
Evening *chan* talk upon the inauguration of Master Baicheng Songyun Dai at Yangcun, Wucheng. The Master held up his staff and said:
"Everyone, look! The late Master Baicheng is here, atop the new Baicheng’s staff, emitting great radiance and extending his broad, long tongue.
He has spoken the Dharma and the worldly teachings to his heart's content; now the new Baicheng speaks as well."
"What is this? Since the great assembly is present before us, we must respond to the moment. He struck the meditation table with his staff and said:
"Together let us bring forth the mind of the sages and worthies, and lift up the broken earthenware basin from of old. We simply wish to renew the command for all eternity;
this is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness. Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the fifteenth day of the first month of winter. To celebrate the Emperor, the bells are rung..."
The bell tolls and the drum beats; the mountain monk drags his staff and ascends the hall. The fourfold assembly gathers like a wall of clouds.

While those from all quarters speak of the Way and discuss Chan, they produce nothing but a chaotic muddle. There is no room for deliberation or hesitation; one must directly realize it right before one’s eyes.
Empty space narrows its eyes and raises its brows; the pillar dances before the hall; the Heavenly Kings at the mountain gate nod their heads. The mountain monk has not yet—
"I venture to grant you my consent. Why is it so? "From of old, there have been sagely predecessors who revered the Dharma; yet these days, people treat this Way as if it were common dirt.
He ascended the hall and cited an ancient worthy, saying: "There is a thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth, black as lacquer."
It is always present within movement and activity, yet it cannot be grasped within movement and activity. Tell me, what thing is this? After a long silence, he said:
"The crane is white; the crow is black. The twin precious swords of Fengcheng—both are made of Bin-iron. (Quoting from the lineage of Shengren).
Master Jinchan of Yangtai Xiufeng ascends the hall on the anniversary of the Buddha’s Enlightenment. An event from two thousand six hundred years ago;
today it is picked up once more as something fresh. Although it is like a red-hot iron upon one’s head, it is much like adding another nail to one’s eyes.
It only knows how to teach people to become Buddhas; it does not realize that it has caused many to go astray. The Tathāgata has no...
Artifice. At midnight, beholding the morning star—let one attain realization of the dharma of non-arising, one’s nostrils will still remain tucked over the lips.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the retreat: For ninety days I sat cross-legged on the mountain peak; I have untied the knots of enmity with as many monks as there are sands in the Ganges.
Today, opening the gate, I gaze upon the heavens and the Milky Way; the mountains are naturally green and the waters naturally vast. Fundamentally, it is his very physical frame that is excellent;
even without applying rouge and powder, he is elegant and refined. The Way need not be awakened to; the Buddha need not be sought.
Reflecting on the pure conduct passed down through generations, one does not drink water by the ear-cleansing stream. Small Assembly Sermon. Question: "The Master does not plant [seeds] here."
"One mu of land, not storing a single grain of millet—how will you receive those who come and go? The Master held up his *niyuri* (wish-fulfilling jewel) and said:
"Without planting one mu of land, and without storing a single grain of millet, even if those with copper heads and iron jaws come, they shall have a thousand feet and ten thousand feet.
Why is that? Without planting one mu of land, there is not an inch of soil upon the great earth; without storing a single grain of millet, the world..."
[The Master] rescued a starving man from above. He drew a circle with his *nanyue* (wish-fulfilling) brush and said: "A sword buried in Fengcheng shoots its light toward the Dipper;
clouds in the blue sky, a bottle upon the water. He asked, "What is the realm of Xiufeng? The Master said, "Mist and clouds on both banks welcome the ancient temple;
a stream of flowing water winds around the terrace. He asked, "What is it like for one within that realm? The Master said, "Leisurely holding a scroll of scripture."
Leaning against a pine tree, he stood. He asked the guest, "Where have you come from? (Baizhu Lun’s lineage).

Chan Master Wuyue Hai of Foguo Temple in Liu’an was a native of Shunqing in Western Sichuan. He abandoned his official post to leave the household life and lived in seclusion in the mountains for over ten years, never appearing in the world.
Upon hearing the sound of birds, he attained realization. He traveled extensively throughout various regions and finally went to visit Master Wen.
Chu Yan performed at the Buddha-land [monastery]. Upon seeing him once, their karmic affinity was established; he was entrusted with the succession and took the seat.
Ascending the hall, he suddenly raised his whisk and said: "Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; sweep the pond clean for idle guests. Where there is no Buddha, pass by quickly;
set out the banners and drums to rouse the military camp. If you understand it thus, it will not hinder the earthen ox bellowing at the moon or the wooden horse neighing.
Wind. Should this not be so, even if you exhaust all your supernatural powers, you cannot deceive this mountain monk by a single point.

A lantern may cover its mouth, and a pillar may knit its brows; yet it is merely because there are no flowers to serve as a model that one paints tigers and dragons, deceiving those at the crossroads and making the wine-dregs swallower boast of wonders and marvels, claiming distinctions where paths are the same. This mountain monk has from the beginning never...
I venture to transmit this message at random. This morning, ascending the master’s seat to expound the Master’s Dharma, I could not avoid one more public proclamation.
Why is this so? For fear of failing the assembly gathered here. (Striking the incense table with his whisk, he descends from the seat. (Wenchu Yan-si)
Chan Master Guanyin Ondan Yuan of Macheng, Huguang, ascended the hall. Standing high upon the curved wooden seat, the chrysanthemums by the hedge were in full golden bloom.

"What difference is there between ancient and modern? Let the winds and rains rage as they will. He gave a shout and said, "Everyone, join me in singing a song together; let us enjoy the Double Ninth Festival!
Addressing the assembly, he concluded with the story of the Second Patriarch standing in the snow. The Master said:
Hot blood splatters profusely against the Brahma Heaven; speckled red snow presses upon the tips of the brows.
Although one has indeed won the secret instruction for peace of mind, one cannot avoid the fact that the mother-born back remains incomplete. (A shout—Wenchu Yan’s successor.)
Chan Master Yào Fówén of Dōngchán Monastery in Huángméi was born into the Péng family of Húzhōu. Entering the hall, he suddenly took up his staff and said:

"This one point is difficult for the five eyes to discern; even the six supernormal powers cannot recognize it. The moon is bright and the stars shine; the public case is already established. How? What?
The more you try, the more it becomes unbearable. Addressing the assembly, he cited the story of the National Teacher’s three calls to his attendant.
[The verse] ends. The Master said: "Three calls and three responses—this is the most coquettish sound. Pulling up the wind-sail, one hoists it at a different harbor.
Do not say that the tongue has always been in the mouth; from of old, filial sons have avoided their father’s name. (Wenchu Yan succeeded him.)
Chan Master Renfeng Jie of Lian'an Foguo was a native of the Lin family of Fucheng, Min.
He went to study under Wenchu Yan. Yan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have not come from the human realm or the heavens.
Yan said, "Ultimately, from where have you come? The Master then gave a shout. Yan said, "After that shout, what then? The Master said, "What other bowl do you seek?"
Yanxiu departed. He then received formal approval (*inka*). He asked, "What is the Dharma for going forth? The Master struck him.

He asked, "What is the Dharma for escaping birth and death? The Master struck him again. He asked, "What is the Dharma that does not fall into existence or non-existence? The Master struck him as well. (Wenchu Yan succeeded him.)
Chan Master Pútí Wénhuī Sōng of Mount Hé in Tàhú, Shūzhōu, addressed the assembly: "It is like springtime in a flower—neither separate from it nor identical to it.
It is like a mirror reflecting an image—neither empty nor substantial. When a single thought is pure and true, one lays the foundation for Great Peace.
Moving freely in all directions, one encounters conditions wherever they arise. Now tell me, whose realm is this? After a long silence, he said: "The five turbidities and worldly toil."
One should cultivate weary detachment. The Western Pure Land is the destination for one’s final return. One must simply ensure that the light manifests in every thought-moment;
then, one will behold the blossoming of flowers in the ponds of the seven treasures. (Successor of Gu Chiyen)
Master Jiaotang Lang of Mount He on Lake Tai addressed the assembly. Having cited the story of Deshan’s bowl-carrying, the Master said:
“The poisonous drum thunders, striking the crown of the head; Deshan has nothing but an empty belly and a hungry heart. The handle of the almsbowl makes it difficult to open one’s mouth;
the bright moon is used to hold dregs. With a shout, he descended from his seat. A monk came for an audience; as soon as he had prostrated himself—
The Master then struck him and said, "I have not even asked a question; why do you strike me?
The Master replied, "He who comes to speak of right and wrong is himself a person of right and wrong. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "I am currently discussing non-duality with the mountain monk; look, the new moon hangs from the tip of the pine. (Recorded by Gu-chi Yan-si)
Chan Master Wenfeng of Mount Zhurong Peak at Nanyue ascends the hall during a great snowfall: "Ten thousand mountains, ice and snow, frozen to their very roots;
A single body and mind, thoroughly chilled to the core. Recalling those years of hunger and deprivation— It makes one’s nose involuntarily sting.
(Zongyuan was the successor of Baoshou.)
Chan Master Zihou Chunchen of Taizhou went to consult Jianlong Hang. Hang asked, "What is the fundamental matter?
The Master gave him a punch. Hang said, "If that is so, then it is not the fundamental matter. The Master bowed and departed. Hang said:
This was no longer his fundamental concern. He then presented a verse, saying: "Ten thousand li of clouds and mountains reveal this mind;
I offer this single palm to the Zen grove. I now do not fail the affairs of elegance; On the solitary peak, day after day it is ever new.
He then visited Rong Deyu, who asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Jianlong. Deyu asked, "Is the old man of Jianlong still there?"
The Master said, “I am here. Yuyou asked, “What did you say to me just now? The Master said, “Thirty blows; not even one blow can be spared.
Yuyou said, “This old fellow ruins people’s sons and daughters. As he spoke, the Master gave him a slap with his palm. Yuyou said, “You have not yet attained it;
there are others who arrive before you,” and he struck the Master. (Rong Deyu succeeded him.)
Mingche Shen Daopo of Dongling in Yangzhou went to attend Jianlong Heng. She was practicing the "Original Face" koan.
Upon entering the hall for the seven-day intensive retreat (*qijiu*), one day Heng descended from the hall. Daopo asked, "What is my original face?
Heng struck her. Daopo said, "Is it this striking? Heng replied, "How could there be two? Daopo bowed. Later, she visited Fengxue.
Huìtài visited her. Huìtài asked, "Is the rice harvest finished? The old woman said, "It was finished long ago. Huìtài said, "That is fortunate.
The old woman said, "When hungry, eat; when cold, add clothing. (Fēng succeeded Huìtài.)
Chan Master Zhuan Jishi of Baosheng Temple in Yangzhou was a native of Qingzhou in Shandong. He went to visit Yuquan Qi, who asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "From Yangzhou. Qi asked, "Have you seen the *Qionghua* (Jade Flower)? The Master said, "I have. Qi held up his whisk and asked, "Do you see this?
The Master said, "I see it. Qi asked, "Do you see me, the old monk? The Master then gave him a slap.
[The Master] said, "I cannot see you again. Wanxiang Qi said, "Where did you learn that? The Master shook his sleeves and went out.

Addressing the assembly, he cited the karmic conditions of Baizhang’s second visit and offered this verse: A single shout, bold and majestic before the public eye; Fully upholding the orthodox command, revealing the family style.
The wondrous principle of the mind-source, the dharma of non-arising— Every dharma is none other than the subtle and profound. (Wanxiang Qi, successor to [the lineage]).

The Chan Master Duānlì of Tiānchéng in Jiāngdū went to visit Jiànlóng Hǎng. He was given the koan of "the state before one's parents were born" and received severe blows with the staff each time, yet the Master never attained realization.
One day, he suddenly broke through and composed a verse: "On the tip of the staff there is no retreating; My head is split open and the blood flows crimson.
Because I have received news from Jiangnan, I report it to old Jiànlóng. Later, he visited Wànxiáng Qí, and their karmic resonance harmonized.
He attained the Dharma. A monk asked, "How was the meeting today? The Master said, "Carrying mud and water. (Wan Xiangqi’s lineage.
Chan Master Fuguo Hongfu Guang of Jiangdu, a native of the Lu family of Rugao, was asked by a monk, "Does the Master have any means for benefiting others?
The Master said, "No. The monk said, "Is there no expedient means? The Master said, "If there were expedient means, it would not be [the Way]."
[The Master] said, "How is it ultimately? The Master then struck him, saying, "Do not try to understand this as being 'human'.
(This was the successor Fu Haiji.
Chan Master Che of Daci in Zhenzhou was a native of Jishui in Jiangxi. He addressed the assembly, citing the story of Mañjuśrī’s deliverance at three locations.
The summer retreat concluded. The Master said: "Three rounds of rising and falling—truly a weariness beyond measure. It is laughable that onlookers add further idle chatter.
It is not that I am poor and pity my son’s suffering; it is simply that from time immemorial, children are spoiled when the family is wealthy. (Fuhai Ji)
Chan Master Huacheng Yuanchuan of Changzhou was a native of Taixing and a son of the Chen family. Addressing the assembly, he cited the story of Bodhidharma meeting Emperor Wu and offered this verse:
The magnet attracts the iron; the teeth meet the tusks as they enter the Great Liang. When questioned, he did not recognize [the Emperor]; how shameful and embarrassed!
Pitifully, though he has the goods, no one recognizes them; He can only cross the river in silent desolation. (Hongyue Qingxi)
The Late Evening Teaching of Chan Master Juzhen Jixianwu of Jugong Baozang Temple: On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, how can one discuss the severity of the cold?
Guests, please return to the hall and take care of yourselves beneath your thin robes. [The Master] says: "And what is it that you are taking care of?
After a long silence, he says: "Black. Small Teaching: Cengyin and Dingmao—the fire within the furnace; Gengchen and Xinsi—white.

Wax-gold. Gathering up his meditation cushion, he returned to his seat and said, "Study the 'Shang Daren' [The Great Person] from before. He threw down his whisk and said, "Lower your voices! Lower your voices!
A monk asked, "When wild winds rise on all sides, what is the single path that points south? The Master said, "To leave the gate is already wrong.
The monk asked, "When threading a needle in the dark of night, how can one penetrate the eye of the needle? The Master said, "What would you do in broad daylight? The monk asked, "..."
When two blades clash, how can one distinguish victory from defeat? The Master said, "Someone will laugh at your failure. The monk shouted.
The Master struck him. (Baizhuang Lun succeeded him.)
Chan Master Daliyin of Lanxi went to visit Zhufeng Song. Song asked, "How is it when one studies under a master? The Master gave a shout.
Song said, "What is the phrase for 'the child reaching its mother'? The Master said, "The beggar’s basket is full.
Song said, "What is the phrase for 'constantly honoring and respecting'? The Master said, "I am always earnest about this. Song said, "What is the Cao... [The text here is incomplete].
Shanxiao finished the verse. The Master said, "A ruined *yangmei* plum; the original text is revealed. The seeds of the *gushu* tree cause heartache.
Song said, "Setting aside your own case for a moment, how do you act as a teacher for others? The Master said, "Look at the hole and insert the wedge; see the illness and administer the medicine.
Song nodded in agreement, and the Master sealed it with a verse (Zhufeng Song was his successor).
Chan Master Xiangyan Yirui of Wumen addressed the assembly. He cited the story of the World-Honored One’s first birth and Yunmen’s single blow.
The Master said: "Gautama displayed his brilliance for a time, but it was merely like fiddling with chopsticks after a full meal. Shaoyang’s (Yunmen’s) saying has circulated throughout the world."
This is merely like carrying firewood to extinguish a fire. Again, he composed a verse: Do not say that the stench of flesh attracts flies;
A blade must boast of its fresh whet on the grindstone. When leaves fall from the sparse forest, one can truly look; With mountains piercing the sky, all see the distant peaks turn green.
Regarding the Three Barriers of Huanglong, he said: "Everyone has their own karmic affinity (*jīnyuan*); Its utility is most manifest before us. At midnight, a single window..."
The bright moon; at dawn, green mountains fill the eyes. How does my hand compare to the Buddha’s hand? Scattering earth, scattering sand—all possess it.

Black beans are intended to change one's eyes; in doting on their children, how could one ever perceive their ugliness? How does my foot compare to a donkey’s foot? The bright moon and clear wind are vast and empty.
I knock down the old thief Yangqi; he did not see Zhaozhou’s bridge. One’s karmic affinity lies in the Buddha’s hand.
The donkey’s foot: cut through and threaded all at once. Who is it that has already passed the barrier?
Even Huanglong has not yet dreamed of this (Yupingding-si).

Chan Master Tiyong of Chongning Monastery in the Western Mountains of Kyoto was the son of the Li family from Fenshan. At the age of fifteen, he relied upon Master Lin of Shenggan Temple, serving him for ten years.
He received the tonsure and full ordination, subsequently traveling to visit various masters throughout the land. Finally, he sought out the chamber of Master Faxing;

when the master raised the case of Huangbo’s three blows of the staff, Tiyong attained sudden and perfect realization, whereupon he was granted a formal prediction of enlightenment. Addressing the assembly, he cited a passage from the teachings:
The Way. "If a person with a distracted mind enters a stupa or temple and recites 'Namo Buddha' even once, they have all already attained the Buddha-way.
[The Master] suddenly picked up his staff and said, "When the staff heard this being said, it had long since entered the Dragon’s Vigorous Display Samādhi.
Now tell me, where does Chongning’s acting for others lie? He threw down the staff and said, "Thirty blows!"
"Wait until another time to instruct the assembly. When lifting a foot or taking a step, one falls into duality or falls into triad;
when closing the eyes and hiding the pupils, it is but a vague semblance. If one further attempts to dissolve both movement and stillness, one again falls into the realm of "nothingness.

So, throughout the twenty-four hours of the day, where should one truly walk and practice? He lets out a shout and says: "Severing the paths of a thousand differences, he attains freedom for himself."
The Verse on the Old Woman of Mount Tai says: "From amidst the dust and rubble, a strange ogre arises; A sudden clap of thunder leaves everything cold as ashes.
Had it not been for scooping up the moon from the water, To the very end, one could hardly distinguish charcoal from coal. The Verse on the Wine Stands and Trays before the Spirit says:
"The rivers and seas are dredged dry until not a drop remains; The oysters' embryos are disgorged, all becoming pearls from the black dragon. To this day..."
Within the ashes of the ancient temple, there still remains a lingering radiance that illuminates the great void (Dehan was succeeded by Rang).
While Chan Master Chengxi Faheng was carrying firewood at Baofeng, Baofeng said, "Everyone has a long staff or a short club;
it is very much like catching a thief. An attendant asked, "Where is the thief? The Master pointed to the pole in Baofeng’s hand and said, "The stolen goods!"

Feng said, "This mountain monk will not go. The Master replied, "The notice for the communal work has not yet been withdrawn. The east wind stirs the sharp snow that has just begun to freeze; the warbling of swallows and the singing of orioles startle the embroidered pavilion.
With white eyes, he looks upon the rising mirage; a single branch of willow breathes forth the fragrant spring. (Hongdu Liangsi)
Chan Master Lidang Zhou addressed the assembly. He cited an instance when Xuedou once ascended the hall;

as soon as the assembly had gathered, he said, "There is no need to lower your heads and deliberate," and immediately descended from his seat. The Master remarked, "The old fellow Xuedou was much like one who covers his ears while stealing a bell."

“Stealing the bell” cannot avoid being laughed at by bystanders. At that time, if the Venerable Zhoushan had seen such talk, he would have immediately overturned the meditation seat, brushed his sleeves, and departed.
I ask you, great assembly: tell me, was this bowing the head or was it deliberation?
After a long silence, he struck his own face with his hand and said, “Cat! He addressed the assembly, citing Yunmen: “The Three Vehicles and the Twelve [Divisions of the] Canon...”
*Fen-chiao* (Classifying the Teachings): When Bodhidharma came from the West, it was not permissible to let him pass. Had he not been let pass, a single shout would have sufficed.
The Master spread his two hands and said, "Tell me, was this letting him pass, or was it not? He looked left and right and said, "The Patriarch has arrived!
Verse on the Outsider’s Question: "I ask neither of speech nor of silence. After the World-Honored One remained silent for a long while, [the verse says: "Sweet!"

When the melon is cut through to the core, the stem is sweet; when the bitter gourd is pulled up by the roots, it is bitter throughout. Placing one’s foot [in the path], one immediately soars upward; liver and gall are entirely poured forth.

In praise of the woman emerging from meditative absorption (*samādhi*), she says: Who says that the spirit of a man is ever-far-reaching? Accompanying him, I am accustomed only to plucking the willow blossoms.
Not realizing the body has fallen into deep spring, why must one cover the face when meeting others?
A verse on the pure practitioner not entering nirvana and the precept-breaking bhikṣu not falling into hell: Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed.
When has a single leaf ever gone to soil the dust? In vain do they speak of spring colors having no high or low;
yellow is yellow, and green is green (by Yu Feng’ou Sisi).
At the Huitang Chan Monastery, Master Hong gave a small-scale sermon (xiaochan) at dawn. A monk asked: "On the birthday of Avalokiteśvara, dragons and elephants gather together.
When face-to-face, everything is fully revealed—what is this message? The Master said: "Incense within the burner; candles before the altar. The monk said:

"Ascending high upon the Dharma seat to universally benefit humans and devas, how far apart are you, O Monk, and the Great Being (Avalokiteśvara)? The Master said: "He is on the east side; he is also on the west side."
"Touch it! Touch it! The monks prostrated. The Master then said: "This single staff of pure brightness—neither Buddhas nor Patriarchs can rival it.

Empty space flows with cold sweat; how could humans and devas measure it? He suddenly held up the staff and asked, "Do you understand? He cast it down and said, "Do not touch it! To touch it is thirty blows.
He offered this verse on the World-Honored One holding up a flower: "Spontaneously he held up a flower, emptying both eyes."
How much resentment and how much sorrow! Among the hundreds of thousands of beings in the human and celestial realms, all are clever and talented;
yet only the *dhūta* practitioner lacks one move (Yufeng Sou, successor).
Chan Master Haechon of Hongboksa Temple in Shuzhou explains the "Seven Small Lectures": the opening of the seven-day retreat and the conclusion of the seven-day retreat.
Seven times three is twenty-one. The incense board and the lantern come forth and bow high;
together they sing the *lirō* song. It is simply because it is most clear. Brothers, tell me, what song is this? *Suru suru, siriri siriri.*

The Verse on the Woman Emerging from Samādhi: "If the other has no mind, then I shall simply rest. As soon as thought stirs, it is difficult to respond. Without cause, a single squeeze turns heaven and earth;
It reaches the point where the waters of the Yellow River flow backward. The Verse on the Old Mother East of the City Who Would Not See the Buddha:
"The horse is lean and its coat long—complain of the sparse grass. The whole body is illness; medicine can hardly cure it. It is perfectly clear."
To report this to those who understand: do not discriminate between right and wrong before others (Yufeng Ssu-si).
Layman Fu Wanhong offered this verse: "A great practitioner of the Way should follow the Buddha’s conduct;

why then does he not observe the *vinaya*? He said: "What a fine painting of a beautiful woman! Lightly sketched and delicately shaded, she is even more spirited. Her elegance is displayed in the spring breeze."
Hanging in the Garden Everywhere one climbs the flowers, everywhere there is truth. The entire earth is a pit of fire; what samādhi can be attained that will not be burned by it? [He] said:
"The shade of green trees is thick, the summer days are long; At West Lake, the songs and dances are even more refreshing.
The fragrant breeze does not hinder the traveler’s intoxication; Each time it blows, once again it is fragrant. (Jingyun Ssu)
When Chan Master Huiqian Yun of Pujisi in Yanzhou was traveling on his journey, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master pointed to an ox and said, "The black one is the ox. He then pointed to a sheep and said, "The white one is the sheep. The monk said, "Why do you toy with me?
The Master replied, "What did you just ask? The monk said, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The black one is the ox; the white one... [is the sheep].
This is a sheep. The Assembly has some realization. Evening *can*: The Master raises the case of the Woman Emerging from Samādhi, saying:
"Why could Mañjuśrī not emerge? Because he was that very Mañjuśrī. Why could Wǎngmíng emerge?
Because he was that very Wǎngmíng. He plants his staff in the ground and says: "The World-Honored One, the Woman, Mañjuśrī, and Wǎngmíng—all have been bound together by this mountain monk!"
A bundle. He hurls it before the assembly. "If you can offer a memorial [to this], I shall allow you to walk hand-in-hand with this staff.
When the guest ascends the hall: In this secluded thatched hut, white clouds abound; Along these ancient paths, few travelers have passed in years.
This old monk regrets his own lack of the skill of Foyin; For what reason have you two gentlemen come to this mountain retreat? Therefore it is said: "The elephant roams..."
The Lion’s Cave, the Dragon’s Lodging, and the Phoenix’s Nest—these cannot be entered by one who is not the right person. Now tell me: with what will you entertain them?
He then planted his staff upright and said: "I shall cut a few fragments of mountain rosy clouds; I shall casually brew two or three bowls of lake-moon tea. (Jingyun Rui)
A Verse for the Layman Mao Chengming Yongqian of Shihua Stone Gate, on the Dog’s Buddha-nature Being Non-existent:
“The dog has no Buddha-nature. The fence is pierced and he enters directly; He unfastens the luminous pearl of night. At the third watch, the sun rises red.
A Verse on the Dog’s Buddha-nature Being Existent: “The dog has Buddha-nature. Mad winds and surging waves. A chilling, sharp blade.
Feng. A thousand ages of cold radiance piercing through. Regarding the verse on "Three *jin* of Hemp": "Three *jin* of hemp—no scale can weigh it. Alas, people mostly seek it outwardly.
Even when held up face-to-face, they still do not recognize it; They do not know how to keep their mouths shut as spring draws to a close. (Jingyun Rui)
Master Seng of Yifeng Peak at Shengguo Monastery in Zhenjiang gives a small *can* (sermon) on the Spring Equinox: Spring wind arrives at the edge of the ridge;
plum blossoms manifest amidst the snow. If you wish to clarify the matter of today, you must be one who stands within this circle. But tell me: who is this person within the circle?
[The Master] suddenly held up his whisk and said: "A heart like that of Ziqi, cast from pure gold. **Small Lecture:** "The Great Way is non-action; to direct oneself toward it is to deviate.
The Great Dharma is formless; to pursue it is to err. To neither deviate nor err—this is called Right Awakening. [He gave a shout and said:
"A three-legged donkey prances about on its hooves, trampling the horn atop the head of the black dragon. (Xuling Xian succeeded him.)
Chan Master Zhuoyin Jin of Yuan Tong Temple in Jinling composed a verse on Dadian’s dismissal of the Head Seat, saying:

"He spoke exhaustively of pushing a boat downstream; I say it is about steering against the wind. As for the Buddha-dharma, it belongs to father and son; clearly, where there is error, it is not error.
He also composed a verse on eating oil-cakes at the manor, saying: "Good news does not leave the gate; bad news travels a thousand miles. Two..."
Buried in one pit, sparing future generations from having to deliberate [upon this matter] (the lineage of Yaofeng, Dayu, and his successors).
On the Midsummer Festival, Master Shijin Jin of Guangjiao Temple on Mount Dongshan in Yaojiang ascended the hall and said: "Today the *pú* grass sword reveals its sharp edge;
a hundred monsters and a thousand demons behold their own ruin. A divine talisman shines forth, its light shaking the earth; why do you all not [take heed]?"
Accept it early on. But tell me, what is it that you accept? [Suddenly] he lets out a shout. A verse on the occasion of the "Difficult Labor":
If you understand it, three watches strike at midday; One must know that at midnight the disk is red. Do not doubt the moon in its reflection upon half the courtyard flowers;
The sound of pines filling the entire garden is all but wind. (By Baitang Jingsi)
The Great Master Shishi ascends the hall: “The celestial fragrance is mostly gone; the butchered tree raises ducks.

Shaving the hair of the stone man, feeding the half of Mount Huishan, releasing Zhuang Zhou’s butterfly—meeting on a narrow path, entering the Louzi Stūpa. For the seventh weekly memorial of my late teacher, I offer this small instruction:
Seven times seven is forty-nine. Turning back to look at one's shadow causes the head to run away; fine flesh is gouged to form a sore. The Southern Dipper is taken for the North.
The Dipper. The staff transforms into a dragon; the mouth of the straw sandals is not seen. He lets out a shout (Han Guan Yu Si).
Chan Master Wei Shu Heng of Jingzhou composed a verse on the World-Honored One beholding the stars: "Sitting coldly for six years, there was no binding or killing."

Watching the stars and constellations, they claim the Way is finally accomplished; they have brought much suffering upon countless foolish men and women. By day and under the clear blue sky, they walk groping against the walls.
A verse on the woman emerging from meditative absorption: "The Great Samādhi of the Nāga is beyond all trace; Its coming and going are even, yet the counts do not match.
Having summoned the eastern wind to dye things red and purple, It follows the spring rain across the stream before us. (Hongdu Li Sisi)
Chan Master Jixi of Fushan at Tiantai gave a small public address (*xiaochan*). All myriad thoughts have melted away like ice; a thousand peaks stand forth in stark relief.

Not even an axe or hatchet can cleave them open; neither needle nor awl can penetrate them. He let out a sudden shout and said: "Revealed, vast and grand! Clear and distinct! According to one's lot and conditions, shatter the dust and hit the mark.
What need is there to speak of the twenty-three patriarchs of this land or the forty-seven of the Western Heaven? Even if there were iron..."
When E’-t’ung-t’ou arrives, one must also stand downwind. Again, he lets out a shout (Hongdu Liangsi).
On the Dragon Boat Festival, Master Xi-chan Jing of Xichan Monastery in Guangzhou ascends the hall and says: "On the fifth day of the fifth month at Guifeng, they break the skinless drum;
on the mountain ridges they race dragon boats, and the pines and bamboos all dance together. Does the assembly know? The white goose."
Tansha Jiao. Weicao Changpu Jiao. Shuzhu Jiang Water. Evening Assembly. When the Great Matter is not yet clarified, it is as if one has lost one’s parents.
When the Great Matter has been clarified, it is as if one has lost one’s parents. Thirty years ago, this mountain monk was much like a mute person eating yellow lotus root;
he could neither swallow it nor spit it out. Thirty years later, I have always applied myself to this very point. You people—act!
"How do you understand this? After a long silence, he said: "Heaven! Heaven! Were one not the biological son, how could one weep until the heart breaks?
(Cuiting Yao, the successor).
Chan Master Feitao Zong of Qingliang Fulong in Huzhou, son of the Shen family of Tongxiang County, held a small assembly on the first day of the sixth month.
Everyone must understand this thoroughly: the summer heat gradually begins to invade. You must be diligent; cherish this moment.
Although every time it is raised up, it is ever new, do not vainly rank others as first or second. To rank them as first or second only leads to further alarm.
Tí. How long can the scorching light of the three dog-days last? In an instant, the golden wind suddenly brings a darkening chill. I respectfully inform the Master of the Hall:
please do not stubbornly cling to fixed views. (Zhu Feng Xu, the successor).
Chan Master Tong of Qianchang in Yingzhou offered this verse on the "Three Is Not": "Neither mind, nor Buddha, nor even an object; The blue-eyed barbarian monk has missing teeth.
Ten thousand fathoms of waves, a single drop of spring water— Of ten people, nine will choke.
The Old Woman of East City offered this verse: "To be born with the Buddha, yet not wishing to see him face-to-face; Why must she cover her face with her hands?"
Face. All mechanical devices exhausted, there is no way out. Who realizes that his whole body has already been struck by arrows? A verse on the story of Shushan visiting Xiangyan:

"Dangerous as a mountain of knives, slippery as mud; Sweet as rock honey, poisonous as a jujube pit. Everyone sees the bright construction of the plank road, But few know the secret crossing at Chen’ang.
A verse on the Buddhas of the Sun’s Face and the Moon’s Face: "The Buddha of the Sun’s Face, the Buddha of the Moon’s Face— The sun and moon are both faces; what face does not have them?"
It is said: "The face of the sun and the face of the moon; a flash of lightning in a clear sky. The cup falls to the ground;
the plate shatters into seven pieces. (Xuling Xian’s Succession)
Chan Master Baosheng Yue composed a verse on the butcher Guang'e, saying: "Throughout kalpas there has been no origin; from the very moment, all is empty.
With a lofty and dignified bearing, he manifests the true wind. The correct eye atop his head opens up through the ages; Casting down the butcher’s knife, he enters the Buddha-realm.
(Xu Lingxian was his successor.)
Chan Master Anleji Gao composed a verse on the lifting of the formal session by Master Ciming, which says:

The general rides alone to break through the heavy siege; The golden blade in his hand swings at will. He waits only for the beacon fires of the frontier to cease, Before returning home to finally unfasten his armor.
He also composed a verse on Master Yingshan, which says: Returning to the green mountains, he lies with the tigers; Washing away the mundane bones, he dwells together with...
Wandering Immortals: With a single blow, he shatters the cave of the spirit; he does not allow the Tathāgata’s waves to emerge (Nan-geng Zhen’s successor).
At the Small Assembly of Chan Master Jutang Jian of Guangji, he issues a brand-new set of regulations: all manner of monsters hide their tracks.
His harsh hammering makes even gold lose its luster. For the new Elder to speak thus—this may be called sailing a boat on dry land or painting upon empty space.
The Wedge. If one is a clever monk, they will naturally not be deluded by others. Even with iron eyes and copper pupils, one finds it difficult to peer into or fathom this point.
[He] strikes the whisk and says: "Heaven! Heaven! The true does not conceal the false; the crooked does not hide the straight. Addressing the assembly:
The yellow gate curtains hang down—who transmits the family news? The purple silk curtain is closed, yet pearls are secretly scattered within.
At such a time, there is that which hearing and sight cannot reach, and that which words and explanations cannot attain.
How can one communicate this message? After a long silence, he said: "The dream has ended; the moonlight is faintly dawn, yet it still illuminates the profuse spring before the courtyard.

He ascended the hall. Before a single blade of grass had been planted, the construction of the temple was already complete; before a single word was uttered, the teaching of the Dharma was already ablaze. Furthermore—
The Way. Precisely at such a time, who is the speaker? Who is the listener? Who is the one abiding?
If you can discern this clearly, only then will you see that the assembly on Vulture Peak has not yet dispersed. Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said:
[The Master] was well-provided with clothing and had sufficient food. [A monk] asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "Protecting the noble and restraining the petty.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Sangha? The Master said, "Shining heads shaved clean and bowls washed pure" (Yufeng Sou succeeded him).

The Dharma-body is formless; the Great Way transcends words. It passes through atoms without being cramped; it traverses the realms of sand without being expansive. Upon a single blade of grass, the sixteen-foot golden body appears; within the single true nature, the adamantine essence is revealed. This may still be observed within the gateway of proclamation and guidance.

The Master Chan Shuishai of Shengfeng, Qujing, ascended the hall upon the completion of the Buddha image. "The Dharma-body is without marks; the Great Way is beyond speech. It passes through the realm of atoms without being narrow; it traverses the world-systems of sand without being broad.

Upon a single blade of grass, the sixteen-foot golden body manifests; within the single true nature, the adamantine essence is revealed. Within the gateway of preaching and guidance, this may still be observed."
Guang. If we speak from the standpoint of the fundamental teaching (zongcheng), how could it be limited to three thousand [monks] in the morning and eight hundred in the evening?

In the evening, he took up his staff and said: "There is no need to seek it elsewhere; it can be verified right before one's eyes. Small Assembly (xiaocan): Above is heaven, below is earth, and in between is man.
The Three Powers (Heaven, Earth, and Humanity) are clearly distinct; they do not interfere with or confuse one another. [The Master] held up his whisk and said:
"There is only this. It cannot be placed in heaven; it cannot be situated in the earth; it cannot be established among humanity.
The Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of successive generations cannot fathom its point of origin. He set down the whisk and said: "Stop, stop! To speak for ten feet is not as good as—"
[The Master] walked one chi and addressed the assembly. He raised the case: Once a monk asked Jia Shan, "What is the realm of Jia Shan?

Shan replied, "A monkey carries its young back into the green peaks; a bird carries flowers in its beak before the azure cliffs. Later, Fa Yan said, "For twenty years, I have understood this only as a description of a landscape.
The Master said, "Jia Shan’s words transcend ordinary sentiment; Fa Yan’s understanding is merely clinging to empty space."
Cai. Suppose someone were to ask, "What is the realm of Shengfeng? You would say to him: "Before the gate, the mountain stream has waterfalls a thousand fathoms deep;
behind the house, the pines and cypresses are layered with ten thousand folds of clouds. If Fayan were still here, what would he know?
Even so, though it is thus, it is easy to see Jia Shan, but difficult to see Shengfeng. [The Master] ascended the hall after retiring from his monastery.
He held up his staff to form the shape of a cross (卐). The interlocking patterns of its angles are difficult to perceive. He then formed the shape of ten (十).

Wherever one looks, whether horizontal or vertical, the Way is easy to approach. He then formed this shape [┘*└]. In every place—by stream or mountain—one gains full mastery. He then formed the shape of a circle with the character "ren" (仁) minus the "two" inside it [○@(仁-二)].

From the beginning, it has always been the truth within this very thing. If there is someone who understands these four lines, not only will their unfolding and rolling up follow the same track, but they will furthermore come...

"Departing freely. Whether you have been liberated or not, I, this mountain monk, shall depart myself. With his staff resting on his shoulder, he descended from the seat and walked away (by Yezhu Huisi).
Chan Master Daolin of Longhu delivered a discourse from the high seat: "The school of Śrāvastī has descended to this land; the wisdom-moon of Vulture Peak has long been submerged.
Today, the school's wind begins to stir and the wisdom-moon shines anew. When the Dharma banner is raised, could there not be men of realization?
After a long silence, he looked left and right and said: 'Indeed, in this era of Great Peace, there is nothing to do.'"
All shall enjoy peace and prosperity, and the nation shall be secure. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The rebellious one hears the thunder and no longer doubts;
the red banner flashes, stirring the majesty of Heaven. The dispatch of the letter has not yet reached home—where is it? An ancient road marker lies across the path—who dares to peer at it?
Raising his staff, he said: "Eyebrows planted in the earth, nostrils level with heaven. From antiquity to the present, unchanging and unmoving. All that stirs..."
It is the life-vein of all sentient beings and the excellent foundation for the myriad phenomena of the universe.

Can you understand this point? [The Master] struck the table with his staff and said: "Whether iron or gold, it depends on the forging; whether ordinary or holy, it awaits the call. He asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master replied, "Wind and rain across the mountains. [The student] asked, "Is it not just that? The Master said, "Urgent!"
The monk hesitated to accept the task. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Wrong, wrong. A monk asked, "In the midst of the twelve hours of the day, what do you take as the master?

The Master said, "Set aside the four modes of deportment and ask another question. As the monk hesitated, the Master rebuked him, saying, "Your mental faculties are stilled and your thoughts are focused, yet you have not yet escaped the roots and dust.
Begone! A monk asked, "What is called Prajñā? The Master covered [the monk's mouth] with his hand.
The monk was at a loss for words. The Master then struck him with his palm.
The lay practitioner Tong Mingdaode of Silla came to pay his respects at Renwang Temple in the capital.

After he had been subjected to rigorous questioning and pressing for long, one night at the fourth watch, he suddenly heard the wall collapse. He attained a state of sudden, unobstructed realization and composed this verse: *Suddenly...*
The walls of the earth collapsed; the sound was like a flash of lightning. It startled the Master, who, though he looked with Buddha-eyes, could not see it.
One day, Xu presented a verse. Xu suddenly held up one fist and asked, "Can you see this?
The scholar said, "What need is there to see anything more? Xu said, "What principle have you seen? The scholar said, "Do not let any dust enter the eyes. Xu said, "It is like..."
This resembles it, yet it is not yet it. One day, Xu raised the story of Xinghua beating the *karmadāna* and asked the scholar, "How do you understand this?
The scholar said, "Fire-refined true gold does not change its color. Xu said, "Why is that?

The next day, he again punished him with a meal of rice gruel and expelled him from the monastery. The scholar said, "A sudden thunderclap leaves no time to cover one's ears. Xu then struck him. The scholar said: [The text ends here.]
"Suspecting that you would kill everyone under heaven, I ask: pull open the gate above and see the person of original nature for yourself.
What is this person of original nature? The Master said, "Where did you just come from? He replied, "From home. The Master said, "You have missed it.
[The Master] asked, "All dharmas are neither born nor extinguished. What is this state of being neither born nor extinguished?"
Xiaoxi said, "Master, point to the two oxen in the courtyard and say: 'This one is so large; this one is so small.
[Xiaoxi] replied, 'These are the matters within each person's own mind; only the self alone knows them.
Master [Zhaozhou] patted the ox's back once and said, 'Look at this beast. (Xiaoshan Xu, the successor).
Zhang Mingjian of Laizhou, Shandong, had long admired the Chan school but had no clear direction.
One day he visited Renwang Xu, who instructed him on the saying regarding the "original master. After investigating this repeatedly, he suddenly attained realization and composed a verse, saying:
"Once you recognize the master, who else could there be? Within this, the message is naturally advantageous. The green mountains rely..."
Within the ancient white clouds, though earth and heaven overturn, it remains unmoved. One day, Xu asked, "The World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa smiled. How do you understand this?
The Master said, "It is merely wind and waves upon level ground. Xu asked, "Ultimately, what was the intent behind holding up the flower?
The Master said, "Family secrets have been needlessly exposed in their entirety. Xu let out a thunderous shout.

The Master said, "Generals who surrender are not executed. [The monk] asked, "The Buddha saves all sentient beings; why then do you see someone being killed and not rescue them?

The Master said, "I knew well that you would not be willing to sever the root of your life. [The monk] asked, "A student has given rise to doubt but cannot resolve it; I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master held up his bamboo stick and said, "If you call this a bamboo stick, you will enter hell as fast as a shot arrow. The monk [remained silent].

As he was about to deliberate [on the matter], the Master struck him straight out from the abbot’s quarters. He offered this verse on the story of Yaṅjue’s labor pains: “When the tiger stretches its waist, wind arises in the valley;
When the crane tilts its body, the moon enters the corridor. If there were not the True Eye beneath the eyebrows, One would see only the vast blue sky when turning one’s head.
He offered this verse on Mazu’s teaching of being “beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations”: “Vibrant red, glowing and blazing.”

It does not open; the traveler seeking its fragrance goes and returns. One knows not how much spring has already been leaked away, yet one still speculates at the place where the *shàgū* cries (as transmitted by Biyan Kai).
At Liushui Fengxiangchangzong Laijian Chan Monastery, a monk asked: "When Zengzi said, 'Yes,' and Huangbo had no teacher—tell me, are these one or two?
The Master said: "'The Great Man Above'—is it not clear that he knows propriety? The monk said:
"If that is so, then Confucianism and Buddhism are clearly distinct. The Master said: "The golden wind blows through the jade flute; who is the one who knows the music? (Biyankai was his successor).
Chan Master Dayuan Zhen of Shishuang in Tanzhou attended Shishuang Kewen for the longest period of any of his disciples.

One day, as Kewen entered the meditation hall, he asked, "All you venerable practitioners of Chan, do you see the mountain monk’s heart, liver, and five internal organs? The Master replied, "Those who recognize this kindness are few."
"Those who forget kindness are many. Yunmen said, "Bring me a single phrase from within your own portion of the Way. The Master said, "Even grinding my bones to powder would not suffice to repay you.
Yunmen asked again, "Why did Fengxiang Peak nod its head today? The Master said, "I have thoroughly penetrated it.
Yunmen nodded in approval. A monk asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "The thousand eyes of Great Compassion look on."
[The student] said, "I do not see it. [The Master] asked, "What is the second phrase? The Master said, "Eight-armed Nāṭa cannot speak it.
[The student] asked, "What is the third phrase? The Master said, "The moon shines outside the eaves, a single perfect orb" (Biyankai succeeded him).
A monk asked Chan Master Laiwu of Changsha Shuanghua: "What is the realm of Shuanghua? The Master said:
"One night the thunder moved a pagoda; to this day, where has it not been heard of? The monk asked: "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said:
