"Eight hundred eminent worthies gather their heads together; its fragrance is not confined to the city of the King of Chu alone. The monk asked: "What of the person and the realm?"...

Furthermore, you have received the Master’s extraction [of the essence]. As for that primordial mechanism beyond the categories, what is it like? The Master said: "One must not produce further branches outside the joints. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"The bodies of the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are fundamentally identical. I and all sentient beings share the same life-force and nature."
"The four great oceans within the eye of a gnat—look directly at this! The five Sumeru mountains beneath the feet of a frog—this is truly and clearly so.
He called to the assembly, saying, "Do you understand? I guarantee for you that it shall never be in vain. He let out a shout (Biyan Kai succeeded him).
Liu Yang’s Shishuang Jianyue Lai Ren Chan Master: When Shishuang Kai invited him to serve in the quarters, his deportment and physical bearing were extraordinary.
One day, Kai asked, "You possess the spirit of the ancients; I do not know what your mental practice is like.
The Master replied, "How can you, Reverend, divide it into two separate parts? Kai said, "I must see for myself before I can believe it. Kai... [continued].
He asked again, "Can you pick up this broken sand pot? The Master replied, "To offer this profound mind to all lands of dust is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.
[The Master] then gave a small informal discourse (xiaocan): "The Dharma is the Great Dharma; the Jewel is the Great Jewel."
What is called the Jewel of the Dharma King is not false. You venerable practitioners of meditation, can you see the great treasure of the Dharma King?
If you say you see it, that is not so; if you say you do not see it, that is also not so. Do not bring right and wrong to judge me;
the superficial speculations of this floating life are irrelevant. (Biyankai’s Succession)
At Xingning Caotang, the Buddha said: "The Master Jingce came to the hall for the morning discourse. Having finished citing the story of Baizhang and the Wild Fox, he said:

'The words of a king are like silk; when they emerge, they are like fine cord. Neither falling nor obscured, utterly remote and yet utterly intimate. On every street in the Chang'an market, there is the moon;
in some places there is the sound of pipes and singing, in other places there is the truth. One day, the Master was picking up earth with the assembly."
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A clod of earth on a stone. The monk asked, "What is the intent behind this?
The Master said, "It is blown by the wind and baked by the sun" (from *Xueling Zhong*).
Chan Master Suideng Lai of Fahua Monastery in Yixing addressed the assembly. A monk asked, "What is the scenery of the lake and mountains?
The Master said, "It cannot be painted and cannot be sketched. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the scenery? The Master said, "They cannot be pushed away nor gathered together.
The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma of the lake and mountains? The Master said, "Difficult to proclaim even from the mouth of the sea. He then said, "The lake..."
Those with eyes see within the mountain realm; there, people cannot hide even face-to-face.
Thinking that the Buddha-dharma has something separate from this, they inevitably fall into pits and ditches (as recorded in the *Xueling Zhongsi*).
Chan Master Laisheng of Dayu Monastery in Hanyang addressed the assembly: "Inspring Cloud was struck by peach blossoms, And his two eyes were blinded.
We brothers of this school Should not be turned by external objects. The pines hold the wind, cold at night;
The stream carries the rain, swelling in spring. (Successor of Xueling Zhong)
A monk asked Master Chengbu Yuping Yebun, "When the ten directions are traversed crosswise and lengthwise, what then?

The Master said, "Three thousand blows at dawn; eight hundred blows at dusk. The monk asked, "What is it like when one sits steadily within the hall? The Master said, "I respectfully wish you every blessing in your daily life.
Small Assembly (Xiao Can): [The Master] struck his staff and said: "If you can speak, you die under the staff; if you cannot speak, you die under the staff."
[The master] died. His brothers tried to test his way [of departing], but the assembly did not emerge. The Master said: "To weep until the blood flows is of no use;
it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. He then returned to the abbot’s quarters. (Shi Ling Cui Si)
Master Chan Shi Lai Yong of Beichan in Chengbu addressed the assembly: "The ten directions of the world are the single eye of the śramaṇa.
Now tell me: where are the eyes of the yakṣas, rākṣasas, Kumbhāṇḍīs, and asuras?
If you can discern this here and now, you may be called a monk who has understood the matter. If not yet, it is the fault of this mountain monk. (Shi Ling)
Chui-tou-li (The Point of the Awl is Sharp).
Master Lai-yu of Renwang Temple in Hangzhou addressed the assembly: "The point of the awl is sharp; the head of the chisel is square.
It is clear and distinct, beyond all deliberation. Last night at the third watch, the moon shone upon it. (Succeeded by Zi-yu Xuan).
At Dong’an Fǎngshān, Master Shílái Chéng was asked by a monk: “The entire earth is a pit of fire; what samādhi must one attain so as not to be burned?
The Master said, “One who knows the Dharma is afraid. The monk said, “In that case, a single drop of a lion’s milk scatters ten *hú* of donkey’s milk.
The Master said, “How many people are there in the Great Tang? Addressing the assembly, he said: “Great!”

When the matter is not yet clear, it is as if one were mourning for one’s parents; mountains are not mountains. When the Great Matter is already clear, it is as if one were mourning for one’s parents;
water is not water. The bright moon shines upon the traveler at night; ten thousand miles of rivers and mountains are encompassed within a single mirror. (By Poyou Xuanji)
Master Linlai of Wugang Guanyin addressed the assembly: "When Aṅgulimāla held out his alms bowl and the woman faced the difficulty of childbirth, they met face-to-face;
though struck with the staff, they could not be parted. He addressed the assembly again, striking the meditation staff once and saying, "Does the assembly see?
He then gave a shout and said, "Does the assembly hear? If you clearly see and hear this, there is no need to search eastward."
Western imitation. Should this not yet be so, do not treat what is easily obtained as something trivial (Iron Wheel [Master] Ji).
Chan Master Hugu Decan Yu of Dingzhou composed a verse on "The Woman Emerging from Samādhi," which says:

"When the parrots of Lingnan chatter in confusion, Their value is high and their voices seek out those who know them. Within the ancient melody, the resonance is far-reaching; Who can truly comprehend it?"
Cessation of Thought Only: A Verse on the Gandharva King Playing Music Three or four notes from a secluded bird awaken the dream of a beautiful woman;
Having such intent makes it unbearable to hear, so she quietly plays the strings and bamboo. (Tianji Shunsi)
Chan Master Lengyan Jingcao Shenglín of Yangshan in Dǐngzhōu composed a verse on Dōngshān’s “Three Pounds of Hemp”:
“Such is the Buddha’s three pounds of hemp; How many people have been bound by it as they come and go? Even with the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion,”
To this day, he does not know the fixed point on the scale. The verse for Yunmen’s “One Statement” says: Birdsong in the depths of spring, the cuckoo cries;
A single call sends forth the world of a hundred flowers. Falling petals are hard to retrieve once they touch the ground;
In the dense shade of summer days, even a horse cannot advance. (Zhenshi Cheshi)
Chan Master Jingzhao Qianzhang Jin of Jiaoshan at Jingkou addressed the assembly: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven.
Inverted sentient beings have empty views and consciousness. Seven, six, five, four, three, two, one. The great earth, mountains, and rivers are pitch black.
The numbers herein are most distinct; An eye-opening patch-robed monk must discern them. If you can discern them, a tiger bites a tiger."
A snake swallowing a turtle’s nose—this is for the assembly. Last night at the third watch, my staff swallowed up the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
The mountains, rivers, and great earth are this very staff; this very staff is the mountains, rivers, and great earth.
Where, then, do you all establish yourselves and find your livelihood? (He plants his staff and lets out a shout: "You lacquer buckets! You are not yet sharp!"
Return to the hall and exert yourself; chant the verse on the "Lord of the Self who is without dream or thought," saying:
The long river flows eastward through the ages; Ten thousand miles, cloudless, it seals the azure sky. The night is still, the water cold, and people sleep soundly;
Deep within the reeds, a single lamp glows red. (By Bianhai Yan)
The Complete Works of the Five Lamps, Volume 108;
Supplement to the Complete Works of the Five Lamps, Volume 108:
The Linji School.
Record of the Thirty-Seventh Generation under Nanyue (from Qingshan):
Chan Master Cheng of Shishuang Yewang in Tanzhou ascends the hall and says: "To awaken to the Way by hearing sounds is to receive echoes from emptiness;
to clarify the mind by seeing forms is for golden sand to cloud the eyes. To strike one’s own foot is to have no connection at all; to seize one’s nose is a mistake."
"Having passed away, this faceless fellow is not Shi-sang forcing the noble to become base. Within the armory of our King, there is no such sword.
The Retreat is Concluded; Small Assembly. The retreat has neither binding nor unbinding, yet people themselves give rise to binding and unbinding.
The Way is neither awakening nor delusion; yet people themselves give rise to awakening and delusion. In putting on clothes and eating meals, it is primordially manifest;

in walking, standing, sitting, and reclining, one’s true nature is manifest and majestic. What need is there to glare with bared brows and bulging eyes beneath the three-beamed roof or before the seven-foot mat?

Three times by day and three times by night—what can you possibly endure? When you have reached the point where your skills are exhausted and your strength spent, you will still be lacing your straw sandals as before.
Even if you encounter someone three thousand miles away, do not say that you have come from Shishuang.

Why? It is because you do not know this mountain monk, and this mountain monk does not know you; what connection could there be? Ascending the hall, he said: "The western wind blows fiercely, the osmanthus flowers are fragrant."
The ancestral meaning from the West is beyond concealment. *Tu!* The rabbit’s path is not where the Great Elephant roams;

how could chicken grain be the food of the phoenix? [He] then descended from his seat and addressed the assembly: "The green mountains are green, the white snows are white; One night, the northern wind grows cold.
The boiling water freezes solid to the bottom. Separately, separately! Ten thousand miles of heaven and earth are but a single bar of iron. [Question: "Not in accord with the myriad..."
"Who is the one who takes the Dharma as a companion? The Master said in a stern voice, "Who is that person? The monk prepared to answer, but the Master struck him.
Question: Before the birth of one's parents, what is the student’s own original face?
The Master said: "Green mountains flank the turbulent stream" (Biyan Kai succeeded).
At Zhaozhou’s Ancient Guanyin Monastery, Chan Master Yizhi held the whisk for a small-scale sermon (*xiaochan*). He said: "That time, the fishing weir cut off the myriad currents;
now, borrowing this seat, I extend my fishing hook. If there is a jade-scaled fish among the assembly who can surge through the waves, do not hesitate to come forth and sport."
Yongkan looked around left and right and said, "Is there? Is there? Master Huayanuo asked, "At the ancient Buddha-land of Zhaozhou, the ancestral intent still remains before the courtyard gate;
at the banks of the Hutuo River by Linji, the original wind on the seat is vast and wide.
I ask my Dharma elder: what is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master replied, "Before one's eyes, there is no elder brother. [Yongkan] further asked:
"What is 'seizing the object but not seizing the person'? The Master said, "There is a Zen grove upon the seat. The student asked, "What is 'seizing both person and object'?
The Master said, "The road at Zhaozhou is slippery; it is difficult to set foot upon it. The student asked, "What is 'neither seizing the person nor seizing the object'?
The Master said, "Plum blossoms bloom by the roadside, yet they happen to meet a postal messenger. The student said, "I have already discerned this."
[The questioner] heard the details [of his life]. He asked, "How do you benefit sentient beings? The Master said, "How can one avoid getting one's hands dirty?

[The questioner] further asked, "In that case, 'The rivers and mountains are beautiful on a long day; the flowers and grasses are fragrant in the spring breeze. The Master said, "I rely on you, brother, to bear witness.
Chan Master Shou Shan asked, "I do not ask about a single drop of the Hutuo River; what is the one phrase prior to the triggering of the mechanism? The Master remained silent for a long while.

The Master said, "Do you understand? The student stepped forward and asked, "What is the phrase after the words? The Master said, "Above all, avoid boring through the tortoise shell or striking the roof tiles.
The student said, "Beyond the kalpas, the news is suddenly cut off; among those who know the sound, who else knows beyond the knowing?

The Master said, "Head Monk, you truly are one who upholds the precepts. He then said: "With both eyes piercing through the moon over Qi and Qin, he stands with his single staff remaining in Yan and Zhao."
Yun said: "The teaching of managing the ritual bells is entirely wearying; who would have known that it would strike the great drum of the Chan school?
Suddenly, with his whisk, he drew a circle (○) and said: 'If we speak of this great drum, the Elder in the hall strikes it constantly.
Its tone is pure and elegant, bringing joy to those who hear it. Now, among you brothers present here, there is not one who has not grown accustomed to hearing it. Why, then, wait for more? "
"Venerable Elder, do you intend to continue this tradition today? I shall merely comply with your compassionate command and cannot help but join in the rhythmic beat.
Thereupon, he let out a thunderous shout and said: "This single stroke is not encompassed by the *yuyang* drum; how could it be contained within the *santai* melody?
It requires that each person turn their body from amidst the great mass of fire and plant their feet at the bottom of the thousand-fathom sea. Only then—"
Fully equipped with a complete set [of skills], he possesses the means to rub the itch from the head of a venomous serpent and snatch food from the jaws of a starving tiger;

only then does he dare to strike out before the hall. Not only does this leave those who merely follow words and chase phrases, or who engage in forced interpretation and speculative calculation, with nowhere to hide;
even long-ordained seniors and those of great wisdom and discernment must likewise prick up their ears and listen in awe. *Ei!* A wondrous response!

Setting aside for a moment the various capacities of sentient beings: how is it that one personally receives the prediction of enlightenment? I carefully examine the resonance of this lofty wind on this day;
with my humble self, I feel ashamed yet grateful as I succeed to this fragrant legacy. (He lets out two shouts and descends from the seat. (Xue Shan Xiang’s Successor)
Chan Master Beijng Longquan Xiaoyu was the son of the Cheng family from Dengzhou. He went to Fayan to shave his head and was given the meditation topic (huatou) of "The myriad dharmas return to one.
He traveled to Minzhong Monastery to receive full ordination, but whenever he brought up the huatou, he felt bewildered and had no direction.

Consequently, he packed his belongings and went to the Lounayen Cave. One evening, sitting upright in a state of intense concentration, he forgot everything else; suddenly, he heard the sound of the wind blowing through the pines.
When Fanzhu heard this, sweat flowed so profusely that it soaked his robes; he lost all composure and fled southward.

He eventually reached Dayue Temple in Boshan, Zhejiang, where he finally had an audience with Fayuan Yu. Yu asked, "When Sudhana visited the Universal Worthy (Samantabhadra), why did the black beans not yet sprout?
The Master said, "If they had sprouted, it would have been a disaster. Yu said, "What was the use of traveling south to seek instruction? The Master said, "None."
"Entering into the midst of the great waves—how can one see the man who plays with the tide? Baoyu said, "What business is there in meeting at another peak?
The Master said, "It is very much like planting eyebrows back onto one's eyes. Baoyu said, "I grant you thirty blows! The Master prostrated himself.
He served as an attendant for ten years and thereby attained the subtle purport (Baoyu succeeded him).

Chan Master Nenshan Ren of Fayuan in Dengzhou was the son of the Jiao family of that same prefecture. He received the tonsure under Master Fanyuan Yu. He applied himself to his labors without ceasing;

when at leisure, he would burn incense and perform prostrations. Moved by his devotion, the Great Being (Avalokiteśvara) manifested a vision before him. Yu commanded him to investigate the koan "The myriad dharmas return to one.
One night, seeing the light and flames of a Buddha rising into the sky, he attained realization. He presented this to Yu, who happened to be escorting a deceased monk out at that moment.
Upon his return, [Yuan] asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said, "His nostrils point toward the heavens. Yuan asked, "Why is he upside down?
The Master said, "This is precisely where he has cast off his body and life. Yuan said, "Everyone will burn him into a single pile of ash; where shall we meet?
The Master said, "It is warm in Annam, and cold in the northern reaches of the Great Wall. Yuan was struck with wonder and appointed him to oversee the affairs of the monastery.
It immediately became a flourishing forest. Emperor Yu asked, "Is the merit of this single hall of the Dharma-source completed?

The Master said, "Why need a flake of snow to mark a red furnace? Yu asked, "Is the fruition truly accomplished? The Master said, "When one person has cause for celebration, the myriad people depend upon it."
Baoyu said, "Look at the phrase beneath the heels. The Master replied, "How could I dare trouble Your Reverence? He then prostrated himself.
Baoyu nodded his approval and appointed him to succeed to the Dharma seat at Fayuan (Baoyu was thus the successor).
Yizhen Dizang Juhan Guang Chan Master was the son of the Chen family of Yangzhou. Initially, he visited Xucun Huyu, who instructed him to contemplate the koan:
"Where does one return? Although three years passed, he remained unable to break through his mental blockages.
Subsequently, he went to Ciyun to attend upon Dajue Xiu, and later paid another visit to Xiaotang. While I was in the inner quarters at Anhua, I asked him, "Where does one return? The Master—
I said, "On the high, precipitous summit of the Western Mountain, one looks out over the four directions with no bounds. I planted my staff in the ground and said, "Speak a phrase here!
The Master shouted. I struck him. As the Master hesitated, I struck him again. The Master was suddenly enlightened and prostrated himself. I nodded in approval.
He mentions Chan Master Dongta Yeweng, who visited Tianmu. Tianmu said, "You have reached a state beyond doubt; why fear birth and death?
At these words, Yeweng attained sudden enlightenment. The Master offers this verse: Father and son meet, their conversation long and deep;
The autumn moon shines cool upon people at night. Having exhausted all tales of past hardships, A single thought of sorrow arises once more.
Yi Duanchang (Rixiang Yusi).
[Name obscured] Chan Master was the son of Lu [family] from Yuyao. He received the tonsure under Master Zhixian.
He paid homage at White Horse Monastery (Baima) and received the precepts. He presented the "Cane" koan to the assembly. Later, he traveled to various regions;

while touching a stone, he stumbled and attained realization. Suddenly he exclaimed: "The void shatters into dust, vast and without a trace of clouds; I only regret that my previous path was mistaken.
Today I finally know there is not a single thing; West Village is originally my old neighbor. In the Jiashu year, he paid homage at Mount Tai and reached the capital.
Inside, he went to pay his respects to Xian of Anhua. Xian asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Yang Pass.
Xian said, "What thing comes in such a manner? The Master said, "There is Suzhou; there is Changzhou. Xian said, "Such stagnant goods!
The Master said, "Let us set aside the 'stagnant' for now; I ask the Master to fix the price. Xian said, "Even thirty blows would not be too few. The Master said, "Master..."
"Too much earnestness! He then entered the room. One day Xian asked, "Why was Mañjuśrī, the teacher of the seven Buddhas, unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi?
The Master said, "A single point missed. Xian said, "Wangming is a Bodhisattva of the first stage."
"How did you manage to emerge from the 'Woman's Samādhi'? The Master said, "Upon arriving, I simply did not acknowledge it. Xian called out loudly, "What about the woman?
The Master then performed a woman’s bow and said, "May the Abbot have ten thousand blessings. Xian nodded in approval.
Chan Master Huazang Yaohaiyu of Jinhua was surnamed Jiang and was a native of Putian. He shaved his head under Miaoji at Hushan Hermitage.
Having practiced seated meditation, he traveled north to Tianlong Temple, where he encountered Miaoyun Xiong and requested instruction on the essential methods of Chan practice.
Xiong instructed him to contemplate the saying, "The myriad dharmas return to the One," and said he felt he had attained an entry point into it.
One day, Zhong asked, "What did the Old Man Miaoshan tell you? The Master replied, "When the snow melts away, spring will naturally arrive. Zhong struck him.

Zhaozhou was contemplating the chapters and sections of the *Han* [scriptures], wondering when he might ever reach a full understanding. Master [Linji] said, "Preceptor, do not degrade the noble by treating it as base.
He threw his staff down in the middle of the room and said, "I am not going to hit you; try to speak a phrase that is truly intimate. Zhaozhou said, "I beg the Master to pull me up.
Linji immediately pulled him up, and Zhaozhou gave him a slap. Linji laughed heartily, and Zhaozhou bowed.
Zhongken (courtesy name Zhizhong) was Chan Master Shu’an Ding of Tianjin Shuiyue.
He was the son of the Liu family of Yuyao. He received the tonsure under Master Mojie and went to the capital to receive full ordination at Yanjing Monastery.
Later, he studied under Master Huilin Guang, who instructed him to contemplate the koan “The myriad dharmas return to one. He applied himself with rigorous self-examination.
Having investigated for a long time without entering [the Way], he happened to pass through a village and heard the sound of mortars and pestles; he had an awakening.
Upon returning, he presented his realization to Guang, who asked, "What is 'all phenomena return to one'? The Master said, "Water flows toward the east. Guang asked, "Where does the one return?"
The Master said, "Everyone is right here. Huiguang said, "Speak a word at the point of intimacy. The Master bowed. Huiguang said, "I grant you thirty blows.
In the evening *can*, he suddenly called the Master and asked, "The Three Piṭakas and the Twelve Divisions of the Canon are all the Buddha’s teachings.
Now, suddenly lifting one foot, tell me: who is it that speaks this? The Master said, "Please, Master, show respect."
Guang nodded in approval. Later, he transmitted the gāthā to him (Huilin Guang’s successor).
Chan Master Zhen of Hanzheng, whose courtesy name was Renyin, was the son of the Song family of Tongxiang. He received the tonsure under [Master] Li.
He traveled north to Tianjin to visit Huilin Guang, who directed him at Dabeici to investigate the koan of the "Three Nots. He investigated it intensely, yet found no point of entry.
He entered [the hall]. One night, while walking in meditation (*caṅkrama*), he raised his head and, seeing a shooting star, attained realization.
He rushed to the abbot’s quarters. Master Guang asked, "That which is neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing—what, after all, is it? The Master said, "My staff is seven feet long.
Guang asked, "Where did you get this news? The Master gave a shout; Guang struck him. The Master said, "The Abbot is far too kind-hearted. Guang then withdrew.
Upon entering the room, Guo said, "Yesterday there was wind; today there is rain. What is the meaning of this? The Master replied, "I have pierced through the nostrils of the iron ox.
Guo asked, "Why does the staff swallow up heaven and earth? The Master then gave a shout. Guo struck him, saying:
"Is this one blow? The Master said, "The debt of gratitude is too great to repay. Guang nodded in agreement (Huilin Guangsi).
Chan Master Renshan Zhe of Beiping Cha'eng was the son of Tang of Jinling. From childhood he was exceptionally intelligent and knew there was a matter beyond the mundane;
he took leave of his parents to rely upon Shenggan Yuan, under whom he first shaved his head. He then paid respects to Jueyin to receive full ordination and went to attend upon Duncun.
He was instructed to contemplate the saying, "The state before one's parents were born. Upon hearing the sound of wind breaking a tree, he attained realization.
He entered the room to present his understanding. The Master asked, "What is your original face? The student replied, "The willow by the embankment holds green smoke;
the peach blossoms on the path reflect red in the sun. The Master said, "Not yet—speak further. The student replied, "I remember the place where we first met; turning my head again—"
Seeing the fresh moonlight, he said, "Where has Śikṣānanda come from in his studies? The Master [Zhaozhou] shook his sleeves and departed.
He then went to attend Hongjue Mian at Pingyang. Mian asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "East of the Tiantai River, west of the Zhe River.
Mian said, "Why do you travel two roads? The Master replied, "I want the Abbot to have doubts. Mian said, "I say you did not come from the Tiantai or Zhe rivers. The Master...
[The Master] said, "Please, Preceptor, speak. [Pingyang] said, "You have come from a place where the water curves and the mountain bulges.
The Master said, "Very good. Pingyang asked, "Do you see the tiger? The Master made a gesture of fear. [Pingyang] said, "For now, look after your life.
The Master then made the sound of a tiger. Muan said to the Guest Prefect, "Escort this monk to the hall. He then went to visit Lingji Guan. Guan asked:
In the *Qian-nü-li-hún* (The Soul Departure of the Beautiful Woman), which one is real? The Master then gave a shout. Guàn said, "Where does this one shout land? The Master shouted again.
Guàn struck him, saying, "You cannot do without this stick. Finally, he met Fúyán Lún of Wúhú; the master and disciple were in accord through their spiritual resonance.
He attended him for five years and received his seal of certification. A Small Retreat Sermon: All phenomena are fundamentally at ease.
People create their own turmoil. True wisdom is perfectly luminous; when emotions arise, the fundamental nature becomes obstructed.

If you wish for the source to be clear and penetrating, and the essence of nature to be profound and vast, you must reach the ultimate stillness where light permeates all. Then, naturally, the carriage will fit its tracks. When there is water in a thousand rivers, the stars and moon are reflected in all;

when there are no clouds ten thousand miles away, everything is pure, clear, and free of a single speck. There is nothing to be realized, even realization itself; there is nothing to be attained, even attainment itself.
At this very moment, tell me: how is it so? Then, dragging his staff, he entered the pass and said: "A single orb of the bright sun shines upon the void;
the myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms appear within its reflection. He let out a shout. (Jukan Rin, successor).
Master Langxue of Tàizhōu ascended the hall and said: He cited the small private instruction of Tiānyán Qǐ, who said:
"Confucius could not read characters; Bodhidharma did not understand Chan. Yet people do not believe it. Birds are as large as mountains; fish are as vast as the sea."
People do not believe it when a father is younger than his son, or when a younger brother is older than his elder brother; people do not believe it.

People do not believe it when the morning star appears at noon, or when the red sun shines by night. When Haiyue speaks thus, people do not believe him; when people speak thus, Haiyue does not believe them.
Haiyue does not believe them; people do not believe him. Now tell me: are they the same, or are they different?
He looked to his left and right and said, "In the end, what is it? He spoke again: "Wan’an Chun said: 'The fish swims atop the pine treetops;
the crane roosts amidst the surging waves. Riding an iron horse backward, one ascends straight into the azure heavens; a single song of heroism falls into the profound and mysterious.'"

Hearing with the ears does not lead to understanding; it is only through hearing with the eyes that one attains completeness. If people do not believe this, the moon over the sea will find it difficult to become full.
If the moon over the sea does not believe, then people will sleep soundly. To be born in this present age and yet turn away from the Way of antiquity—how could this possibly be right?

Furthermore, he says: The Master’s verse for "Investigating" runs as follows: "A single mass of glowing red iron, Whirling all around, beyond all climbing or grasping. Cast out along with the smoke..."
Entering beyond the azure heavens, even the Three-Eyed Mahesvara is not permitted to look (Wan’an Chun’s lineage).
Yishui Yuqi Mei Chetie was a native of Nii; he studied under Yilin Neng, who instructed him to contemplate the koan:
"The state before your parents were born. After a long time, one day Neng asked: "What is it like before your parents were born?"
[Zhaozhou] presented his face to him. Master [Nanquan] could not respond; Zhaozhou struck him severely with a staff. The Master said, "I beg the Master to be patient. Zhaozhou asked again;

as the Master prepared to respond, Zhaozhou struck him once more. The Master’s doubts were completely resolved, and he prostrated himself, saying, "The Master’s kindness exceeds that of my own parents.
Zhaozhou asked, "What have you seen that you speak thus? The Master replied, "The eight-spoked staff in Vajrapāṇi’s hand."
Neng said, "Not yet; speak further. The Master then gave a shout. Neng nodded his head. Jue Tianze was able to participate in the teachings of Longchi.
Longchi held up a fan and asked, "Do you understand? Neng said, "I do not understand. Longchi asked, "Why do you not understand?
Neng said, "It is not within my realm. Longchi asked, "Where have you come from? Neng said, "Huguang. Longchi asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma at Huangmei? Neng said, "..."
At midnight, he entrusted [the Dharma] to Lu Neng. "The clay ox returns to the snowy peaks. [Zhaozhou] asked, "What about the matter of right now? Neng said, "What did the Master say?
Wei then gave a shout. Neng said, "An old master! The Master composed a verse: "The spring in the riverlands has ended, the wind-signal is subtle;
The fisherman holds his line at the head of the Qijiang. A single blast of the flute awakens a thousand forests; The golden dragon breaks through the waves."
Scattering scales and snapping hooks (Heaven can thus continue its mandate).
Chan Master Jinzong Qi of Changsha first attained realization while studying under Jiansou; later, he visited Shiyuan Yun at Shimen, where he thoroughly mastered the subtle essentials.
He ascended the hall and, citing the case of Shan Duo being present, asked Jinming: "Is it not so?"
"Mind, Buddha, and dharmas—what are these? They are manifest. Dongshan said, "Yesterday someone spoke thus; I have already chased him out.

Xuedou said, "If you wish to strike, then strike! What need is there to speak of 'yesterday'? As soon as Xuedou finished speaking, Dongshan struck him. Xuedou stepped forward, caught hold of him, and said:
This blind donkey is acting recklessly! When Zai was about to offer a word, Linji struck him. As he again prepared to speak, Linji struck him once more.

At that moment, Zai attained sudden enlightenment. The Master composed a verse: "Having traversed a thousand peaks and ten thousand crags, In the depths of white clouds, the tracks of a chamois are seen.
Turning his body, he ascends straight to the highest summit, Driving thunder with lightning and sending forth distant wild geese. (Shiyuan Yun succeeded him.)

Chan Master Huang An Dushan Weichen Sheng was a native of this locality. Having studied under various venerable masters throughout his career, he later visited Shiyuan Yun at Longxing Temple, where he received the transmission of the Dharma.
In a small-scale sermon (*xiaocan*), he cited the case of Wengu Yin, who asked Nanming Guang:
"If 'delusion is immediately the original emptiness of karmic obstacles,' why was the Venerable Simha beheaded by the King of Kasmira? Guang replied: [The text here indicates the response follows].
[The monk] said, "Fundamentally empty. [Guang] said, "What about the head? [The monk] said, "Fundamentally empty.
[The monk] asked, "Why did the King of Kaśmīra drop one hand to the ground? [Guang] said, "Fundamentally empty. The Master composed a verse:
Willow groves slant against the hermit’s window; Scattered, withered branches accompany the morning river. Precisely where the frosty wind snaps them off, A pair of cold gulls take flight in alarm.
Shuang (Shiyuan Yunsi).
Yinglu Xingfu Yingji Yi Chan Master was a native of Qishui. He received the tonsure and the full precepts under Huangjian Qin.
Regarding the kōan of the Cypress Tree: One day, while chopping firewood, he injured his finger and attained realization. He presented this to Master Qin, who asked, "What about the cypress tree?
The Master replied, "It is dripping with blood. Qin nodded in approval. [The Record] mentions Fǎngshān Bǎo: Whenever a monk entered the room for an interview...
The Master generally held up his whisk and asked, "What is this? If a monk hesitated, he would strike him out directly.
For twenty years, few were able to accord with his spiritual mechanism. Shimen Yun said, "As for the masters and monks who recognize the whisk, what then?"
After a long pause, he snapped his fingers once. Jin Mingxu said, "If one recognizes the whisk, one buys straw sandals to travel the path.

The Master said, "The ancients established their teachings in such a manner; nowadays, people only fear that ants will not understand the scent of meat or that flies will not come to the smell of filth—how can one not sigh at this? (Denghui Qin succeeded him.)
Chan Master Jianxing Zhenru Yule was the son of the Chen family of Jianyang. He received the tonsure under Langyun.
Once, he requested instruction from Yingsu Jian, who said, "To leave the household life and study the Way is not something that those of inferior roots or weak resolve can pursue."
The Master asked, "How is it so? Jian replied, "You need only refrain from calculating any thoughts of good or evil;
simply hold up the word 'Wu' (No), relying on it with your whole being. It is like a Vajra-king sword: if a Buddha comes, cut him down; if a Mara comes, cut him down.
After a long time, it will naturally leave you no room for deception. The Master then applied himself to this investigation, remaining diligent even though his duties were heavy and demanding.

He never let the matter slip. One day, when Huiyue Xu arrived at Puming, he requested the collected writings left behind by his predecessors; the Master sought instruction from him morning and evening.
Xu asked, "Bring me back the meaning of the word 'wu' (no). The Master replied, "There is no source, and thus there is no meaning. Xu said, "Since there is no meaning..."
Someone came to request instruction from Master Xi, who had a realization upon hearing these words and immediately prostrated himself.
Master Xi said, "He is radiant. When Xi Jue was attending Master Rui, he manifested the name Tan. Tan asked, "Venerable sir, how old are you? Rui replied, "I was born at the same time as empty space.
Tan asked, "Is there anyone who accompanies you? Rui replied, "From the beginning, I have never borrowed the power of another. Tan asked, "What is your [true] self?"
"By one's own power, it is sharp and ready to seize. Tán said, "What kind of fellow is this? The Master composed a verse, saying:
"How many years have passed? Born together with the void. Who is there to accompany him? Not borrowing from another's power. Casually nudging it lightly, It cleaves through the wind."
Swift and urgent; his majestic presence was awe-inspiring. Mountains crumbled and the seas stood still (Huiyue Xu Si).
Zen Master Longzhen Tianxiu Run of Pucheng was a native of this province. In his childhood, he paid homage to Longzhen Yin and donned the black robes of the monastic order.
He visited Mount Gu at Xian to receive full ordination. Following [Master] Yin, he went to attend upon Fengshan Tan, who instructed him to contemplate the "Cypress" and "Child" kōans.
One day, while Tan was personally carrying water, the Master prepared to receive it. Tan extended his hand and said, "Give me back the kōan!
The Master replied, "Wait until I have washed my feet, and then I will speak to you, Reverend. Tan asked, "What about the matter right now? The Master then let out a shout.
Dantan said, "What have you studied? The Master shouted again. Dantan reached for his palm to strike him, but the Master took up a pitcher and walked away.
Dantan said, "Yet there is still something of the scent of a monk in you. The Master said, "I also wanted to give the Abbot a start. Dantan held him in high esteem.
Later, Fuyin received the seal of transmission from Tanyue. He was appointed by his master to manage the affairs of Riyuan for twenty years.
While studying the *Lotus Sūtra*, Fuyin asked, "What is this one great matter of causal conditions? The Master said, "The Thousand-Handed Great Compassionate One cannot lift it.
Fuyin asked, "And what about you, Master? The Master made a gesture with both hands as if holding something up. Fuyin said, "You have misunderstood. The Master then gave a shout.
Yin said, "Is there anything further? The Master performed three prostrations, paid his respects, and departed. Yin called for the Superintendent of the Monastery; the Master turned his head.
Yin said, "I, this mountain monk, also have a great matter of karmic connection that I require you to take up.

In the future, from among those who work with the mattock, may you find one or two to continue the Buddha’s wisdom-life, so as not to fail the legacy of our predecessors. I—[the Master]—... [proceeded].
The vow was fulfilled and the transmission was bestowed; this is the seal of the verse (the successor of Jueyuan).
Chan Master Fayun of the Thousand Buddhas Monastery in Beijing, a native of the Yu clan of Jinining, traveled to Huacheng and entered the monastic order under Jingran.

Upon reaching the capital, he visited Yunguang to receive full ordination. He studied the *Chan-deng* (Lamp of Zen) as if it were his former practice, and then went to attend upon Guangsi Gao. [Gao] commanded him...
"Looking at the three [aspects], they are not words. Having investigated this with all his might for many years, one day he heard a monk recite a verse on wind-bells:
"A hundred thousand samādhis beyond words; through the wind, they are spoken to those within. Suddenly, like ice melting, he clearly perceived the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*).
Next, he visited Dabe (Mahākāruṇika). Having deeply received his instructions, he further composed the *Puhui Pu* (The Feast of Universal Wisdom) and commanded the Librarian to preserve it.
One day, the Librarian asked, "What was the meaning behind Huangbo’s striking Linji? The Master said, "Gold is tested by fire.
The Librarian said, "Why did he [Linji] strike back at Dayu’s ribs? The Master said, "To lose money here and pull up the roots there. The Librarian said, "At that time..."
At that time, Daoyou obtained great power. Why did he succeed Huangbo? The Master said, "An enemy has a head;
a debt has an owner. Dayu said, "I grant you thirty blows. The Master prostrated three times. Dayu recognized his realization and bestowed upon him a verse (Dayu succeeded Tianru).
Chan Master Yingqian of Dabeiji Temple in Linqing was the son of the He family of that same prefecture.

He went to Lingjiu to receive the tonsure and requested instruction from Miaoyun Xiong, who directed him toward the essentials of Chan by assigning him the koan "The Three Are Not. Yingqian investigated this diligently day and night without slackening.

One day, while carrying water to irrigate the garden, the wooden band of his bucket suddenly burst and it fell. He experienced a sudden awakening and went to the abbot’s quarters to present his realization.
Yunmen scolded him, saying, "This is merely a temporary direct perception (*pratyakṣa*); it is not the ultimate.

As the Master was about to pose a question, Yunmen struck him out with a flurry of staff blows. Thereupon, he traveled to consult various renowned masters. Finally, he visited Tianchi Shan, who said, "Three days... [he did not finish speaking].
They met face to face. "Do not look at this as something ordinary," [Zhao] Zhen said. "How long are your eyebrows? The Master replied, "They are the same length as the Master’s.
Zhen said, "Is that truly so? The Master let out a thunderous shout. Zhen said, "This shout does not function as a mere shout; how do you understand it?
The Master replied, "The dense bamboo does not hinder the flowing stream from passing through; the high mountain can never obstruct the white clouds from flying."
Tianchi Shan said, "If you understand it like this, how can you possibly attain it? The Master shouted again. Shan struck him and said, "Go to the meditation hall.
He served as an attendant for five years, and Tianchi Shan certified him with a verse. (Tianchi Shan was the successor.)
Chan Master Hong of Yuanyang in Huizhou was a native of Zhenjiang. He ascended the hall and raised the precedent of Fayan, who said:
"When the three beats of the drum have ceased and the crowd has come forward, the Buddha-dharma and human affairs are both fully concluded. Jingju said:
"When the three beats of the drum have ceased and the crowd has come forward, the staff is not here; I shall give you thirty blows with the handle of the broom. The Master said: "These two..."
It is not that the great masters of old did not each manifest their own family style by demarcating boundaries and establishing divisions;
however, as for opening the eyes of people and severing the life-root of men, that was still not yet the ultimate point. Yuan Tong was not like this.

He took up his staff and called to the assembly, saying, "When the three beats of the drum have ceased, you all come crowding forward. Holding the staff upright, he asked, "What kind of whirlwind is this? and struck them all at once.
He scattered [the offerings], threw his staff to the ground, and laughed loudly, "Ha ha! before returning to his quarters (Qianfu was the successor of Jun).
Chan Master Ke Cang of Tianlong in Jingzhou went to visit Puguang Jun. Jun asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied:

"Please, Master, look upon me. Yunmen said, "You potty-urinating ghost! Take this staff! and he struck him. The Master said, "Had I known earlier that the Master possessed such a vital pivot [of teaching], I would have been grateful.
Yunmen struck him again. The Master asked, "Where did my fault lie? Yunmen said, "You have fallen.
The Master was suddenly enlightened and prostrated himself, saying, "Had I not personally met the Master, I would have been deceived by various teachers for the rest of my life."
Junguan took him on as an attendant for several years. Junguan entrusted him with a verse to show the assembly.
Holding up his staff, he said: "This must not be called a staff. If you call it a staff, you will enter hell like a shot arrow.
He then called to the assembly with the staff, saying: "This is truly a staff. If you do not call it a staff, you will enter hell like a shot arrow."
"An arrow shot. He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "Pogong [Wuben] once said:
'For thirty years, I have prepared a single dose of the "Pill of Joy and Freedom from Sorrow. Though this medicine is small, its efficacy is immense.

It does not distinguish between the sickness of the Buddha, the sickness of the Patriarchs, the sickness of the mind, the sickness of Chan, the sickness of the ordinary person, the sickness of the sage, whether it be a sickness or no sickness, or whether it arises in life or death.'"
Regarding illness: apart from one particular malady of the Chan practitioners, there is none who hears of it or sees it who does not find it efficacious.
The Master said: "This 'Pleasant Vitality Powder' is indeed divine and wondrous; yet, it is no more than 'three-year-old mugwort,' which can treat an illness of seven years' duration.
As for a disease as deep-seated as that of the *gāohuáng* (the vital organs), one cannot help but stand by and watch helplessly. Even Tiantong had his own [method].

A single prescription. Requiring no contrivance, its efficacy is unsurpassed. Setting aside for a moment the illnesses of Buddhas and patriarchs, as well as the illnesses of birth and death, this is specifically intended to treat one particular malady of the Chan practitioners: that which causes those who see it or hear it to lose their very lives.
Now tell me, what kind of medicine is this? Listen! Even Shen Nong did not dare to taste it (Qianfu Junsu).

The lay practitioner Wang Quanxin of Kunshan was a native of this very locality. He understood the matters of the Chan school and had long investigated for himself where one comes from when born and where one goes when dying.
Upon encountering the Elder Dun’s instruction in several words, he deeply clarified the principle of the single thread that runs through all things.
One day, he presented a verse for reading to Xuedou, saying: "In the ordinary course of daily life, it is fundamentally not something else;

in every object and every situation, how could one miss the mark? Picking it up with the hand at random, there is no dharma left over; simply by employing this single move, all confusion is settled. After Xuedou had finished reading it, [he said]: *Note: The original text ends with "Xuedou having finished reading," implying the master’s response or the conclusion of the encounter.*
The Master asked, "What is that one point of your daily life? The scholar raised his fist. Du Xue said, "Let it go.
The scholar opened his palm and said, "One must not use cleverness and end up being clumsy. Du Xue said, "Set aside these two paths and speak a single phrase."
The scholar gave a shout. Duzue said, "Shout again and see. The scholar said, "That is merely adding a point to an arrowhead.
Duzue then struck him. From that time on, he was constantly by his side. Duzue inscribed a verse for him, saying: "The Ancestor’s Iron Ox Mechanism—its power lies in being prior to all mechanisms.
I now entrust this to you; let the wind of the school spread throughout the great thousandfold world. (This refers to Duzue Zhangsi.)
Panshan Wei of Jizhou was the son of the Bian family of Wanping. Initially, he visited Master Xinglong, who gave him the "cane" (*zhuhui*) koan.
He investigated it with such intensity that he forgot all weariness. Later, when he studied under Master Daibei Ze, his earnestness was even greater than before.
While passing through Yinghai, he attained realization upon hearing the sound of the tide. Ze asked him, "Zhaozhou said, 'In Qingzhou, I made a hempen robe that weighed seven pounds.'"
"How do you understand this? The Master said, "The Persian chews ice and snow; he does not realize his teeth are cold. [Zhi] then praised him as excellent.
He then ordered him to rely on Ji’an Zhen. Zhen asked, "What is the phrase for entering the gate? The Master said, "It happens exactly when the Golden Guards do not prohibit [passage].
Zhen held up his staff and laid it across [his body], saying, "What can be done about this? The Master said, "The Master’s compassionate heart is too intense."
Zhengshu held up his staff and said, "What about that one phrase for turning back? The Master prostrated himself and said, "I am worthy of receiving the prostration of one who has attained the jewel.
Zhengshu said, "Wait until another time for those thirty blows. The Master grabbed him by the hand and said, "If you want to strike, strike! Why speak of 'another time'?
Zhengshu pushed him away and said, "It is not merely that you have reached such a state. The Master sighed repeatedly.
Sheng served as his attendant for five years, gradually mastering the subtle principles. Later, he received the seal of transmission (the succession of Shenglian Zhen).
Chan Master Wanyuan Fa of Huangmei was a native of Jixian; he shaved his head under Master Congrui and attained realization after seeking instruction at Tianfeng.
Feng again ordered Jian Rui to see him. Every time Rui demonstrated his "tongs and hammer" methods of instruction, the Master showed no sign of difficulty.
One day, Rui ordered the Master into the room and questioned him on the "No-Character" (Wu) koan for thirteen turns of speech, yet Rui did not grant him a word of approval.

The Master said, "Master, do not force a person too much. Rui replied, "I am not saying you do not understand; it is simply that you have too much Chan. The Master paused in thought, nodded, and then—
He prostrated himself. Duìrèn asked, "What principle have you perceived that you act in this way?
The Master said, "The moon in the empty expanse over the ten-thousand-year-old azure pool—only after repeatedly searching for it can one truly know it. Duìrèn approved (Duìrèn succeeded to Dùn fēng).
Chan Master Huanruo Yin of Huangbo Mida was the son of the Wan family of Jingzhou. He followed his father to pay homage to Yungu and received the tonsure;
he received the full precepts at Tianting Monastery in Yangzhou and studied under Ziyuan of Mount Kuang. He traveled extensively to consult various masters, all of whom possessed pithy sayings.
Finally, he arrived at Jinming, where he encountered Chan Master Xu while the latter was carrying bricks. Xu held up a brick and showed it to the assembly, saying: "The Great..."
"The teachings of the Tripitaka speak only of this. The Master stepped forward and also picked up a piece of tile, saying, "The entire Tripitaka does not speak of this.
Xuxu said, "'Speaking' and 'not speaking' are worth no more than a single coin. The Master replied, "It is not worth even half a coin.
Xuxu said, "Today I have lost money on this monk. The Master smiled. Xuxu held him in high esteem and ordered him to serve as an attendant.
He served as the abbot for nine years in total. Geum Myeong-uk succeeded him with a verse of transmission (the *gāthā-mudrā*).
Master Seon Cheon of Ilwi Hermitage in Samheo, Han-yang, was a native of the same province. Having shaved his head at the age of seven, he resolved to aspire to the Chan school.
Yan performed the ritual for receiving full ordination and requested instruction. Yan had him contemplate the "One Return" koan. For three years he practiced with diligent and tireless effort.
During the seventh period of the formal assembly, Yan posed the question: "Where does this 'One Return' go? Yan’s face turned red and he could not answer.
Yan twisted his nose and said, "You beast! After all this time, you still cannot manage it? Yan cried out in pain, and Yan said, "Yet, how excellent!"
[The Master] was kind. Upon hearing this, the teacher broke into a sweat; he felt his body become equal to space and immediately prostrated. Yunyan said, "Why do you not utter a single word?
The master replied, "It is cold and freezing outside; please sit in the warm room, Preceptor. Yunyan then desisted and ordered the master to write a formal document.
Although the master had attained awakening, he remained diligent day and night, investigating with ever-increasing intensity. Yunyan confirmed this for him with a verse, whereupon the master—
Question: "What is it like when one lamp’s flame does not cease as another is lit? Yan said: "It is very much like a blind donkey running in a herd.
The Master said: "Thank you, Teacher, for your answer. Yan struck him seven blows and drove him out. (Donglin Yan was his successor.)
Master Yunfeng Ding of Huang’an was a native of that very locality. Having once heard a monk discuss the principles of Chan, he was filled with such joy that he could not contain himself.
Consequently, he went to visit Dàshèng to receive the precepts; there, he encountered Yǎn and Hú Xīnwéi in conversation.
Suddenly, as if having forgotten and then recalled something, he stepped forward, prostrated himself, and asked, "What were you and the layman discussing, Master? Yǎn replied, "Nothing."
"This is your realm," [Zhao]zhou said. Master [Yuanwu] replied, "It has already been seen through by this student. Yuanwu picked up his bamboo staff and said, "Can you see through this?
Zhaozhou snatched it away, threw it down, and left immediately. Yuanwu said to the attendant, "Does this fellow not practice Chan?"
The scholars among them all acclaimed him as extraordinary. Later, Master Yan summoned Shishuang into his room and asked, "Zeng Can, what realization do you possess?
Shishuang replied, "Great Sage. Yan then brandished his staff and struck him, saying, "You hollow-headed fellow!
Have you come to deceive this old monk? Shishuang said, "In fact, it is this very staff that remembers. Yan then shouted, "This is not the principle! He then commanded—
Regarding the story of the cypress tree: as the Master was about to respond, Donglin Yan struck him and said, "To open your mouth is already an error; get out!
The Master also understood his meaning. Later, Yan sealed this with a verse (Yan was the successor of Donglin).
Chan Master Ninyun Guzong of Puying ascended the hall and said: "The sky is vast and the sea is wide; the moon is bright and the wind is clear.
Everywhere, fishermen and woodcutters dance; in every direction, all species of beings rejoice. How could I, the new Puying, dare to miss the timing or lose the opportunity?
Amidst the thousand differences and myriad distinctions, I cut them off all at once right here. Far removed from all confusion and error, I tread open the crowns of both living beings and Buddhas."
He reveals the cranial cap of Mount Sumeru. The assembly, tell me: is this supernatural power (*abhijñā*) or the natural order of things?

If you can understand it thus, the entire world of the ten directions does not go beyond this very place. Yet, if one were to establish a formal teaching (*menceng shishe*), another hand must be raised.
With his whisk, he draws a circle (○) and says: "The flame of the heart-lamp transmits its fragrance afar; a single point, free from self-interest."
A Small Lecture Penetrating Past and Present: The great bell hangs upon its frame; when struck, it rings. The precious mirror rests upon its stand; when someone approaches, it reflects.
O Great Virtues, each of you possesses a fundamental radiance that is inexhaustible in its application and unfailing in its manifestation.
It is vividly present everywhere, never obscured. There is no difference between the bright mirror and the great bell. It is simply that you have not yet realized it.
This is because one is deluded by the shadows of false attachments, worldly toil, and conceptual discrimination.

Thus, one is submerged in birth and death, drifting and sinking in the sea of suffering, bound and fettered by the sense faculties and their objects, remaining difficult to liberate for many kalpas. You people must understand this directly and right now; what separation could there be?
If you do not do so, then beneath the three rafters and before the seven-foot mat, you must settle and refine your body and mind until they are completely dry and clear.
"Clean and pure. Examine it closely and discern what kind of thing it is. If you can turn yourself around right here, not even a single atom shall deceive you;
only then will you know that I have not deceived you. Is there anyone else? After a long silence, he said: "I cannot take your hand and urge you to walk;
for others, one must personally realize it oneself before it becomes intimate [as precious as a treasure]. (Bao Yuji Siji)
Chan Master Langu Suizhi of Qianshou at Mount Jing composed a verse on the "Qingzhou Cloth Robe": "Skillfully cut and fashioned, it fits the body exactly;
Neither long nor short, it feels most intimate. Usually unwashed by the waters of the spring, Scorched by the sun and buffeted by the wind, how could it ever be stained by dust?
(Wusong Yu was his successor).
Evening Sermon by Chan Master Chongjing of Pujie Temple in Jinling: Beneath Stonehead City, at the head of Swallow Rock, the waves of the Long River surge and the misty rain shrouds all in emptiness.
The pivotal function of the Buddhas and the intent of the Patriarchs are clearly revealed;
from antiquity to the present, they have never undergone change. If you can realize this face-to-face, you may return home and sit in peace. Why need you travel further?
He traveled throughout a hundred cities. What need was there for him to tap the gate with his finger? He suddenly held up his whisk and asked, "Does the assembly see?
He then threw down the whisk and said, "Be careful not to let your eyes be changed! (Qigong Wu succeeded him.)
Chan Master Tianji Che of Fayun Monastery in Anzhou was a native of the Lin family in Quanzhou, Min. At the age of twenty, he shaved his head at Xiangguo Temple in Bianzhou.
He traveled extensively throughout various regions before finally serving under Zhufeng Shan, from whom he received formal certification (inka).

He subsequently occupied the abbot’s seat. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The Dharma has no fixed form; it becomes the source whenever it encounters conditions. The Way is fundamentally wordless, yet it is manifested through words. What [is manifested] is...
Seeking through the three periods of time, nothing is found; examining through the two truths, nothing is known. Without marks and without names, its depth and breadth cannot be measured;
without reliance and without abiding, its traces and footprints cannot be discerned. Reaching this point, you must know there is a path of penetration and liberation before you can succeed.
(He strikes the meditation staff. "Splitting open the Flower Peak Mountains, their beauty reaching to the heavens; releasing the Yellow River!"
"Utterly pure! [He] lets out a shout and addresses the assembly. Holding up his staff, he says:
"This Dharma cannot be understood through thought or discrimination. He strikes the ground with it once and says: "There is only the One Vehicle; there is no second and no third.
If you can penetrate this and understand it clearly, then the entire Tripitaka is nothing but paper used for wiping abscesses and pus. After a long silence, he asks: "Do you understand?"
Ma! A three-legged donkey prances on its hooves; it tramples the universe until not a single inch of earth remains.
This was enshrined in the northern corner of Puzhao Temple (by Zhufeng Shansi).
Chan Master Zhengzong Sheng of Suizhou Shuinan went to visit Zhufeng Shan. Shan asked, “How old are you? The Master replied, “Thirty-six.
Shan asked, “How many water buffaloes do you have? The Master replied, “Two. Shan nodded his head in approval. He then ascended the hall for a discourse.
Many springs have passed since the ancestral hall fell into ruin; though the four boundaries are clearly defined, I have not personally visited them.

An umbrella opens up a new world; a plow and harrow turn over the old heavens and earth. Pointing his staff, he said: "From this moment on, I shall not return; yet were I to return, I would find it here.
Who could vie for the misty scenery of the Five Lakes? (Zhu Feng was his dharma heir).
When Chan Master Lian of Sanhe in Hanyang first visited Huguo, he did not find resonance there.

He subsequently traveled through various monasteries until he finally arrived at Dasheng. As soon as he entered the gate, Dasheng raised his staff, struck once, and said, "The staff leaps and bounds!"
The Master said, "Preceptor, do not poke your head out. Yanguan then struck him. The Master asked, "Where does my fault lie?
Yanguan said, "You do not even recognize good from bad. The Master did not understand. Yanguan set down his staff and said, "Elder, there is no need for such haste.

If you have ever reached a point of true realization, feel free to bring it forward so that I may serve as your witness. The Master then recounted the various kōans and encounters he had attained. Yanguan said:
All such things are merely what the mind and intellect have conjectured and grasped. As for Zhaozhou’s saying “No”—how do you understand it?
The Master was at a loss. Chengyan said, “Go for now; come back another time. As the Master was about to leave the door, Chengyan suddenly called out, “Upādhyāya!
The Master turned his head. Chengyan asked, “What is this? At these words, the Master attained realization and prostrated himself. Chengyan said, “Why did you not speak?”
Dadao said, "A pair of blue and white eyes—why add any more mud and sand? Yan said, "Give me back the word 'wu' (no).
Dadao said, "The official road before Shuangcheng Station—how many travelers have not suffered there? Yan said, "You will run yourself to death, Reverend.
Dadao said, "Step by step, one does not touch the dust. Yan said, "Thirty blows shall wait for another time. Later, this was recorded by Yinzhi.
In verse (as recorded by Yan Si):
Huang An obtained his realization at Yunfeng Ding Chanshi’s hermitage. He was the son of the Cheng family of his native district and received tonsure under Xueju.
He went to the Great Sage to receive the precepts and requested instruction on the methods of practice. Yanming had him contemplate the "one return" koan for two years.
One day, while observing mountains and waters with a torrential cascade and surging waves, he suddenly attained realization. He presented this to Yanming, who asked, "Where is this one return?"
The Master said, "White waves overturn upon the mountain peak; red dust rises from the bottom of the sea. Xianyan said, "If one perceives this or accepts it, it immediately becomes an obstruction.
The Master asked, "How then would it be? Xianyan struck him with a heavy blow of his staff and shut the door.
Standing bolt upright on the steps for half a day, someone suddenly asked, "Where is the ox? A monk replied, "It is right here. The Master heard this.
Suddenly casting aside his previous understanding, he hurried to knock at the abbot’s quarters. Xianyan asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "It is none other.
Xianyan opened the door, and the Master prostrated himself. Xianyan approved of him (according to the *Erguan*, Xianyan was his successor).
Chan Master Weiyun Shili of Jiaxing was the son of the Lu family of Haiyan. He received the tonsure under Xuejie and received full ordination at Santai from Huie Xu.
He was instructed to contemplate the "One Returns" koan. Subsequently, he traveled to Hubei to study under various masters, and later visited Mount Lu, yet found no resonance with them.
Upon returning to see Xu again, Xu interrogated him several times; his responses were quite swift. After some time, Xu...
Xu called to the Master, saying, "The three previous statements were all evasions; you have not yet reached the ground of reality.

Today, quickly and fully confess! Otherwise, I shall beat you to death. The Master, feeling abashed, prepared to respond. Xu struck him immediately. As the Master again prepared to respond, Xu struck him once more.
Dayu struck him again. The Master was at a complete loss. Dayu struck him repeatedly with his staff, saying, "Where does it all return? Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
At that moment, the Master attained sudden realization. He then prostrated and said, "Only today, Qianlin, has he finally come to understand the Master’s single-minded, compassionate heart."
"It would be difficult to repay [his kindness] even by shattering one's body. Xu approved of this. He addressed the assembly, citing the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*:
"All things that can be returned are naturally not you; that which cannot be returned—if it is not you, then who is it? The verse says: "The spring colors in the painted tower are most exquisite."
Exhausting all his elegance with Mo Zhe, he attempts to paint the moon upon the clear waves. His icy countenance cannot rival the excellence of the jade-like face.
In praise of the occasion when Nanquan was cutting thatch grass and a monk asked about the path to Nanquan: "Traversing peaks and climbing clouds, one seeks to learn the way of the immortals;
Yet one does not know that they themselves were already before Ge Hong. He poured out the entire elixir of wondrous medicine, And yet the young child remains as he was."
Questioning Dongtian (Huie Yue): Master Wenben of Jiaxing was the son of the Hong family of his native district.
In his youth, he left the mundane world and received the full precepts from Denglun of Tongcen.
He went to Jinming Temple seeking instruction, where Yue said, "There is fundamentally nothing established; what is there to point out? The Master replied:

"I, your disciple, am foolish and stubborn; I beg for the Master’s compassionate instruction. Xu raised the "Mu" (No) kōan of Zhaozhou and commanded the Master to investigate it without a single day's lapse.

One day, upon hearing the sound of water being drawn from a well, he attained realization. He composed a verse, saying: "Zhaozhou’s single word 'Mu' Pervades the earth and fills the heavens without leakage.
Suddenly shattering empty space, It damns the Yellow River and makes it flow backward. He presented this to Xu, who praised him, saying, "Excellent!"
(Huiyue Xusi). Chan Master Dijing Bao of Zhenjiang was a native of that same prefecture.
Having left the household life, he went into seclusion and studied under Tianning, who assigned him the koan regarding the "story before birth.
After several years, he presented his realization; however, each time he did so, Master Xuguan would sweep it away. The Master became restless in his movements and conduct, and one night—
Sitting upright, he heard the sound of a cannon blast that resonated through heaven and earth; his mind and circumstances became vast and clear.
At dawn, as the sun rose, Yang Xiu asked, "Where does this cannon blast fall right now? The Master gave a shout. Yang Xiu said, "Where does this one shout of yours fall?"
The Master shouted again. Xu said, "Not yet. As the Master rose from his prostration, he gave two consecutive shouts and departed.
Xu nodded in approval. Regarding the verse on the Qingzhou cotton robe, the Master said: "The Qingzhou seven-pound robe, Round and whole, without a seam.
How many people are lost within it? They do not recognize Zhaozhou’s bare bones. (Huiyue Xu succeeded [to the lineage].)
Chan Master Qinglong Fuzai’s Small Assembly Sermon: The Seal of Awakening stands before the hall, transcending the realm of the infinite and the primordial *primal* (xiantian).

Wondrously profound and perfectly luminous, he attains full realization within the midst of worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. He fully upholds the true command, moving with unimpeded freedom in every direction.
He scrapes the hair of a tortoise from its back and cuts off the horns of a hare from a tiger’s head. Displaying great capacity and manifesting great function—how [wondrous it is]!
To conceal the world within the world is to be properly wandering in the vast wilderness of the Great Emptiness (*Gomō*) and roaming at ease in the realm where nothing exists.
Furthermore, what kind of person’s domain is this Way? (A shout. *Small Sermon:* The hollow knows the rain; the nest knows the wind.

Withered flowers have fallen away, and the moon shines upon the void. In every dust mote there is stillness; in every land, all is perfectly interfused. This is the very essence of the Three Vehicles.
Externally, within this vast and solitary seal, the meaning of the Patriarchs is lost to east and west. A clump of mushrooms grows upon the hitching post for donkeys;
on a black-lacquered tray, the sun is a brilliant red. Ascending the hall on the Spring Equinox: The clay ox is whipped to reveal its golden bones.
The vast spring wind scatters across the Five Lakes; Swallowing green and containing red, it holds boundless intent. Behold the landscape as a single painted scroll. Unfold!
The Master asked, "What is this? (Bianhai’s words are his succession). Chan Master Jixian Zong of Puzhi in Yangzhou ascended the hall and said:
"The Way has no front or back; the Dharma transcends seeing and hearing. It is revealed alone in the midst of reality, where ordinary and holy beings do not exist.
Even if one were to seek realization at the tip of a staff or take responsibility under a shout, the arrow has already passed to the west."
The white clouds of heaven stretch ten thousand *li* (as noted by Guwu Zisi).
Chan Master Tianran Shun of Fahua delivers a small-scale discourse (*xiaochan*): upon the stringless lute he plays the five notes and six scales;
from the bottomless bowl he draws forth a hundred flavors of rare delicacies; from the chessboard stone he leaps up to the thirty-third heaven. Wash—
Baoche’s roar entered the vast ocean; Senior Upasena could not restrain his laughter. Arriving here, he reveals the ancestral fields in the open light:
he plows where it has not been plowed and harvests where it has not been gathered. He simply picks them up with his hand as they come.
"Receiving and enjoying it on a single platter. But tell me, how does one receive and enjoy it? Listen! After a long silence, he gave a shout and descended from his seat (Wengu Wusi).

Fu Yun, Layman Xiao Fengyi of Fengtian, was originally a Confucian scholar. Following his father, Guo Lin, who traveled for official service to Guangdong, Beijing, and Shandong, he visited various Chan monasteries and came to know that there was such a matter as this.
Later, when his father passed away, he escorted the coffin back to the capital and went to visit Master Baoru.
Yù visited the Three Great Bodhisattvas Hermitage. Upon hearing a single word of guidance, his heart leaped with joy, and he sought further instruction.

Yù assigned him to contemplate the koan: "The myriad dharmas return to One. Later, upon hearing the sound of the evening drum, he attained realization. He immediately went to see Yù. Yù asked, "What is 'the myriad dharmas returning to One'?
The practitioner replied, "The many stars bowing toward the moon. Yù asked, "Where does the One return? The practitioner replied, "When the moon sets, the sky..."
Kongyu said, "At this very moment, speak a single phrase. The Master said, "Even Buddhas and Patriarchs find it difficult to fathom.

Kongyu said, "Not yet—speak further. The Master then gave a shout. Kongyu nodded his head in approval. The Master had formerly attended Kongyu’s side and deeply received his guidance, thereby gaining entry into the profound and subtle mysteries.
Later, when Kongyu fell ill, after he had finished addressing the assembly, he summoned the Master and entrusted him with a verse, saying: "Entering the room, one knows the hall."
The Master said, "When one leaves the gate, the carriage wheels follow the same ruts; one must overturn the upward barrier and blow the unperforated flute to its end.
The Scholar bowed and accepted this. The Scholar visited a friend at Stone Mountain. Stone asked, "Are you the Layman Xiao? The Scholar said, "A monk must possess the eye before he can recognize me.
Stone said, "I have seen through you already. The Scholar said, "Even if you were to change your eyes, I would still not know you. Stone gave a shout.
Wei let out a single shout. The scholar said, "And you go on like this? Shi said, "So, you are indeed a master. The scholar said, "Why do you defile people?
The scholar went to Tianweng and paid his respects to Miaoyun Xiong. Xiong asked, "What is your honorable surname, layman? The scholar said, "My surname is Xiao.
Xiong said, "The ancients had but a single flute that blew away eight thousand soldiers. Try blowing it for me. The scholar—
He spread his two hands and said, "This is yet another calamity. Xiong said, "Thirty blows; not even one blow can be spared.
Shì said, "Old monk, your staff-head is far too extravagant. Xiong said, "I almost called you a layman. Shì said, "Why does the monk push people into a pit?
Xiong said, "A wild goose flies across the vast sky; its shadow sinks into the autumn [waters]."

[The Master] said, "Water. The scholar said, "If the principle is correct, then I shall comply. Xiong struck him and said, "When meeting people, take care not to misrepresent [the teaching]. The scholar prostrated himself.
(Bao was like jade; he succeeded [to the Dharma]).
When Chan Master Nalan Cheng visited Anhua Zhong, Zhong asked, "What is that wild duck of yours?
The Master said, "Gathered in, no one sees it; let loose, it does not form a flock. Zhong said, "This is not within your capacity."
The Master said, "This is not a matter concerning me. Tell me, whose matter is it? Zhong struck him and said, "Blind! The Master then shouted.
Zhong said, "That is like drawing a bow after a thief has already passed. The Master grabbed him and said, "What can you do?
The stolen goods are right here. Zhong said, "You are being most impolite. The Master prostrated himself and presented a verse. Zhong nodded his head and certified it. (Zhihe)
The middle successor was Chan Master Yuanrong Di of Yongping Tea Pavilion. He was the son of the Shi family of Wuxian. He went to Puming to receive the tonsure and received full ordination at Haihui.
While investigating the koan of "the state before one's parents were born," he suddenly attained realization upon hearing the sound of an incense board falling to the ground.
He went to visit Nanjian Zhen and asked, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said, "A person from the south rows a boat;
a person from the north rides a horse. Zhen said, "Neither end is touched. The Master said, "A millstone rolls through the empty sky. Zhen then struck him.
The Master gave a shout and departed. Later, while serving under Pudu Xu during a period of manual labor, Xu asked, "The pickaxe is in your hand;
who is it that employs it? The Master replied, "Why must one dig in the earth to seek the heavens? Xu said, "Since you do not understand, why do you not ask the mountain monk?
The Master held up the pickaxe and said, "The assembly bears witness. Xu nodded his head in approval (he was thus succeeded by Congshixu).
Chan Master Zhìshànqìnglínghuì of Jīnhuā was the son of the Wú family of Yìwū. He studied under Zhìhé at Ānhuà, where a profound bond of teacher and disciple was formed.
He was appointed to manage the affairs of the monastery, attending upon his master every day without fail. Later, he traveled back to the Zhejiang region and crossed the Qiántáng River.
Suddenly, he lost the one before him. He then went north and presented himself to Mazu. Mazu asked, "How deep is the Qiantang River?

The Master replied, "It is just like the sea. Mazu leaned forward and peered at his face, saying, "Indeed, your nostrils are being soaked rotten! The Master said, "Preceptor, do not let your eyes deceive you."
Zhong said, "For now, it is a joy that your eyebrows are still there. The Master said, "I thank the Master for providing this testimony. Zhong then withdrew and entered the inner quarters.
Zhong asked, "When Nanquan ate the oil-cakes, the village headman came to thank him. Where does the crux lie? The Master said, "It would leave the whole world in doubt.
Zhong said, "Do you recognize Nanquan? The Master said, "Today I have caught this old fellow red-handed. Zhong approved.
He served [the Master] for ten years. During his tenure, he was certified by means of a verse (in the Zhizhong era).
Chan Master Dujī Xiàn of Tàicāng was the son of the Lǐ family of Yùfēng. In his youth, he entered the monastic order under Nánguǎng Yún, who instructed him to contemplate the "One Returns" koan.
He received the full precepts from Zhì of Jiāoshān and investigated the matter day and night without ceasing. Consequently, during a communal work assignment (*pǔqǐng*), while carrying...
While gathering firewood in the snow, he stumbled and attained a realization. He presented a verse, saying: "The clouds are dark, so one knows not whether it is morning or evening;

The snow is deep, making it hard to distinguish the high from the low on the path. In a casual moment, I pierced through the time before Vipaśyin Buddha— It was originally just this face given by my mother. Zhaozhou said: "So it is!"
"But how was it before your mother was born? The Master said, "Even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot see it.
Zhezhi struck him and asked, "Where does this one blow fall? The Master then shouted. Zhezhi approved of him. Later, he attended Baiyu Si at Qinglong.
Si asked, "In what year did you begin traveling to visit masters? The Master said, "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja. Si said, "That was born too late."

The Master said, "Fortunately, I have encountered you, O Monk, living in this world; this is truly extraordinary. He then traveled extensively to consult various elders, all of whom possessed pithy sayings.
Later, he went to Xinzhuang to meet Chen Duoxue. Duoxue asked, "Have you ever planted your heels firmly upon the ground? The Master replied, "The Taihu Lake spans thirty-six thousand acres;
who knows that upon reaching the shore, one need not rely on a boat? Duoxue asked, "What is the phrase for reaching the shore?"
The Master said, "In vain, a scene of sorrow. Xue took up his staff; the Master then gave a shout. Xue said, "What a brilliant monk! The Master shook his sleeves and departed.
He then personally attended [Xue] for several years. Xue sealed him with a verse, saying: "This Dharma has neither 'other' nor 'self';
