This mind transcends past and present. To manifest that which is not-mind is the Dharma; The true mechanism pervades the vast void. (Chen Yumen was his successor.)
Changzhou Huangshan Yaoshi Bushe Tian Chan Master was the son of the Liu family of his native district. He was naturally gifted and possessed keen insight.

When he encountered a point of realization while studying, he would immediately stand up, which his fellow students found extraordinary. At the age of nineteen, having lost both his father and mother, he worked the fields for thirteen years.
One day, he abandoned his wife and children and wandered off to Mount Huang, where he paid homage to Wubai.
An elderly monk had undergone tonsure, and his two sons once relied upon him for instruction. However, the master paid them no heed, so they eventually went to Lingyan to receive full ordination.
He was instructed to contemplate the "Three Is-Nots. Sitting in meditation late at night, he opened the door and saw that the moonlight was vast and boundless;

looking back at his own body, it appeared equal to empty space. He composed a verse and presented it to Tongshuo Hong, saying: "That which is not mind, Buddha, or thing is brilliantly manifest throughout the universe."
He trampled through the barrier above and emerged from the mouth of empty space. Daohong asked, "What do you call the barrier above?
The Master then gave a shout. Daohong esteemed him as a vessel of the Dharma. He then went to study under Mianyun Jishui Guang, who asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Tiantai."
[The Master] asked, "Do you see the Arhat? The Master said, "I see another one. [The Master] said, "Do not mistake him. The Master said, "The thief's true form has been revealed.
[Master] Guang then struck him. The Master caught his hand and sent it flying. Guang called for his attendant; with a single slap, the attendant was dismissed.

In the evening, he personally attended Huìyù Xù at Lóngyuān. As he was about to unfold his sitting mat, Xù said, "That is not it. The Master withdrew the mat. Xù said, "Even more mistaken. The Master—
The Master said, "It is the student who is mistaken; the Abbot is not. Yunxu then struck him. The Master said, "I have long heard that the Dragon Abyss is deep;

indeed, its waves are high. Yunxu said, "This will drown you, Dharma brother. The Master then gave a shout. Later, he went to Gannu Temple for a second interview, where he was appointed head of the assembly.
During a private interview, Yunxu held up his whisk and asked, "Was that of Mazu at that time the same as mine now?"
"No, Master. The Master snatched it away, held it upright, and said, "Please, Preceptor, speak. Xu said, "How would you explain Baizhang’s meaning? The Master threw down the whisk.
Xu let out a thunderous shout. The Master prostrated himself. Subsequently, he certified him with a verse (Huiyue Xu succeeded him).
Chan Master Jiashan Huimin Guxian was the son of the Li family of Jiangning. In his youth, he entered the monastic order under the Vinaya master Hongdu.
At the age of eighteen, he traveled to lecture halls and visited Haihui to receive full ordination. While contemplating the "One Returns" koan, he found no resonance with it.
He then traveled south to visit Master Longyuan Xiong. The Master asked, "What is 'this very mind is Buddha'? He replied, "A lion bites; a common dog chases after it."

[Daowu] Kuei asked, "Master, what is that which is neither mind nor Buddha? The Master said, "The hands are long, but the sleeves of the robe are short; the feet are thin, but the straw sandals are wide.
Daowu hesitated. The Master asked, "How do you understand this? Daowu stood there reflecting. Xiong struck him.

Daowu said, "A long sword leaning against the sky makes people feel cold. Xiong asked, "What about the sword? Daowu let out a shout and returned to the assembly. Thereafter, he traveled extensively to study under various masters; finally—
He visited Huiguo at Mount Xu and asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From the South Sea. The Master asked, "Have you seen the Great Being (Avalokiteśvara)?
The Master said, "When I went there, I met the tide; when I returned, I met the wind. The Master said, "Put down the steamed bun; why is it now a steamed dumpling?"
The Master said, "This too is an ordinary matter. Xù took up his bamboo staff and said, "Since it is an ordinary matter, say something here.
As soon as the Master opened his mouth, Xù struck him. The Master said, "I deeply appreciate the Master’s one blow.
Xù asked, "Where did you understand this? The Master bowed and returned to the assembly; Xù approved of him. Later, he presented a verse: "Every dharma is without form or appearance."
It is neither a thing nor a name; I have personally entrusted it to you. The sound of the bridge flows on without ceasing (Huiyue Xu-si).
Zen Master Er-lun Ming of Zhenru Temple in Jinling was the son of the Lü family of his native district. He left home to follow Master Hongdu and received full ordination under Master Shengguo.
He traveled to Xiansheng Temple to study the principles [of the teachings]. There he asked, "What is that which is your original face? The Master had no reply.
Lil struck him. As the Master was about to open his mouth, Lil struck him again. The Master attained a realization. Not long after, Lil passed away.
The Master went to visit Chao of Qingshan. Chao asked, "What is it? The Master said, "I do not presume to inquire. Chao said, "It seems the Year Star (Taishui) is directly upon you today, Upāsaka.
The Master said, "Fortunately, the Earth Star has entered the Master's destiny. Chao then struck him. The Master then gave a shout. Later, he studied under Ganlu Xu.
There was an agreement that they would gather firewood together and rest by the riverbank. Xu asked, "Since you are one who has attained enlightenment, why are you so short of breath?
The Master replied, "When fish swim, the water becomes turbid. Suddenly seeing a dead fish, Xu pointed at it and said, "Fish take water as their life;
why have they died in the water? The Master replied, "Because its kindness is deep, one does not forget. Xu asked, "What is the point where the kindness is deep? The Master bowed.
Xu said, "The staff is not in my hand; take note of thirty blows. Huaiye followed Xu, and Xu sealed him with a verse (Huaiye succeeded Xu).
Chan Master Shimeng Sheng of Langya in Chuzhou, a native of the Mao clan of Wuchang, lost both parents when he was only ten years old.
At eighteen, he paid respects at Wuzu’s Peak and shaved his head. He practiced asceticism until his full ordination and spent three years contemplating the "Mu" (No) koan under Guang.

Having studied under Master Jiao for several years, he traveled south to Jia Shan, where he stayed at a guest house (*danguo*). There, upon hearing a monk reciting the line, "There is a thing prior to heaven and earth," he attained a realization.
He subsequently built a thatched hut on Mount Jieshan in Chuzhou and remained there for eight years. Later, he left the hermitage and went to visit Master Chun at Baon Temple.
While entering the bathhouse, Chun asked him, "The ancients said one can swallow the waters of the West River in a single gulp; try swallowing the water in this bathhouse and see."
The Master said, "I am not one who holds the views of a wild fox. Chun esteemed him and he traveled extensively to consult various masters, yet he never finally accepted himself as enlightened.
Finally, upon arriving at Ganlu, he stepped across the threshold. Daybreak (Xu) asked, "What is this?

The Master replied, "I have long admired your lofty reputation and have come specifically to pay my respects. Daybreak said, "You are old and decrepit; what reason do you have for coming here? The Master replied, "The ancients..."
"Three times you climbed Mount Touzi and nine times you went up to Dongshan. Was this merely to tour the mountains and rivers, or was there another principle at work?
He replied, "It is like a person drinking water; whether it is cold or warm, they know it for themselves. The Master said, "Ten thousand points of smoke vanish and heaven and earth are pure;
a single expanse of wind and moon is vast and boundless. He asked, "Is this not your own realization? The Master gave a shout. Having attended him intimately for two years, [the disciple] Xuxu...
Seal with a verse (by Huiyue, Xu, and Si).
Chan Master Wuyi Dao of Pujisi in Jiaozhou was the son of the Liu family of Laizhou. He visited Master Faguang of Shishi and applied himself with ever-increasing intensity.
After investigating the Way with great effort for several years, one night he sat alone until dawn. Hearing a sudden clap of thunder and a fierce wind, he became aware of his own body and mind.

Sudden Emptiness. Vast and boundless. He went to present himself to Shishi. Shishi asked, "Where are your features while you are alive? The Master said, "They cannot be hidden throughout the entire world.
Shishi said, "If they cannot be hidden throughout the entire world, where do you establish yourself and find your livelihood?
The Master then gave a shout. Shishi raised his staff. The Master said, "Why does this old fellow get so flustered, with hands and feet in such a mess? He then departed. This is the story of Shigu.
He immediately traveled south, visiting monasteries everywhere. In the evening, he received the nectar-like teaching of Ganlu (Amṛta) and established a karmic affinity between master and disciple.
Ganlu then appointed him as the guest prefect. One day, Ganlu summoned him into his room and asked, "How many new arrivals are there today? The Master replied, "Early this morning, three people."

In the evening, five people arrived. [One] asked, "How many have attained the essence (*tǐ*), and how many have attained the function (*yòng*)? The Master said, "I ask the Venerable One to examine them.
Xu then struck him. The Master said, "This very thing is the function; what is the essence? [Xu] replied, "Where did you see me, monk?"
The Master then bowed. Xu struck him two more times. Later, Yin composed a verse (Huiyue succeeded Xu).
Chan Master Huang An Henghe Yingtong Sheng was a native of the Lu clan in his home district. From birth he abstained from meat and pungent roots; his temperament was serene and simple.

After both his parents had passed away, he paid homage to Weichen to receive the tonsure and ordination. He was instructed to contemplate the koan of "The Three Not-Sos. The Master said: "Since it is already..."

"This mind is the Buddha's property. He asked again, "What else is there to investigate? Chen said, "This is precisely when you must exert effort. He went to visit Dashi Yan to receive full ordination.
Upon entering the seven halls, he had an awakening upon hearing the sound of the incense board. Yan held up the incense board and asked, "What is this?

The Master immediately shouted. Yan said, "A reckless shout! The Master shouted again. Yan struck him. Thereupon, he traveled to various regions to study under different masters, eventually meeting Gantulu Xu in person.

A student asked, "I have come from afar; I beg the Master for a single encounter. Baizhang Xu immediately struck him. The student then took his sitting cloth, drew a circle, and presented it to the Master.
The Master said, "Among the ninety-six types of non-Buddhist paths in India, you are the lowest of the low.

The student replied, "This is essence recognizing essence. Xu struck him out directly. Next, as the student entered the room, Xu held up his staff and asked, "Speak a word that is intimate and direct here."
The Master said, "Waves surge atop Mount Beigù; fire erupts in the heart of the Yangzi River. [The monk] said, "It burns away your eyebrows and drowns your nostrils.
The Master said, "Heaven and earth roam vast and unrestrained; I ride backward upon Mount Sumeru to wander beyond the phenomenal world.

"Last night the western wind suddenly blew; this morning the entire ground is spread with gold. It is utterly bare and unobstructed, revealing—"

Mañjuśrī’s single eye shines through heaven and reflects the earth; it illuminates the past and clarifies the present. Yet it is merely trodden upon by oxen and sheep, and met with the songs of herdsmen and woodcutters.
Tell me, is it within the eye or outside the eye? After a long silence, he said: "A cataract has formed.
He ascended the hall and said: "At the ear is good news: frost strikes the treetops until they turn crimson. At the eye is good news: the sound of bells and drums."
Interpenetration. The gate of perfect penetration is wide open, yet people are unwilling to enter. But tell me, what is this gate of perfect penetration?
[He draws a circle with his whisk and says: "Enter right here. Ascending the hall: Whether by boat or by land, from misty forests to the water's edge, the true mechanism is fully revealed.
On this side or that side, clouds, moon, streams, and mountains, all manifest the wondrous essence. How laughable!
The youth of Southern Inquiry merely boasts of the fifty-three [stations]; do not say that the Bhikṣu Megha-cloud was seen only on a separate peak.
Right now, as one comes and goes across the great earth of mountains and rivers, tell me: where is the *dharmakāya*?
If you had seen it here just now, you would rightly receive thirty blows. Why is that? To distinguish clearly between reward and punishment.
[The questioner] asked: "What is the state of the luminous environment? The Master said: "A stretch of lake and embankment, ten li of mist. He asked: "Who is within the environment? The Master said:
"Crowded together in clusters, with no distinction between the intimate and the distant. He asked: "What is the intent within those people? The Master...
[The student] said, "I love eating white rice, but am too lazy to go work the fields. [The student] asked, "Is there still a way for you to benefit others?
The Master said, "My whisk is frayed and worn; it does not yield its place to others. (Shiyu Fang succeeded him.)
Chan Master Jiukui Jingda of Baofu in Yuezhou was the son of the Liu family from Hengshan in Chu. His mother dreamed that a red sun fell onto her bed when he was born.
At the age of fourteen, he left home to become a monk at Mount Nanyue. After his parents had passed away, the Master grieved for them incessantly.

Shouye instructed him with the "Patriarchs Before Birth" koan, admonishing him: "You must strive with diligent and earnest inquiry. If you attain realization, even the hardships endured over many lifetimes will have been repaid.
The Master received this command. After two years, while hearing a youth reciting the Heart Sūtra, he attained a profound awakening to this principle.
He went to visit Bian Shan Xue at Kongtong, where he gained profound realization. After first receiving full ordination, he relied upon Baoshou, and only then did he receive the mind-seal.
Later, while presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "The wind and rain rage through the night; The new spring stream rushes in its cleansing torrent.

Sentient and insentient beings preach the Dharma together; Yet for the eyes of the patch-robed monk, it is even more chaotic. That insentient beings preach the Dharma—only the Buddhas can understand and hear it."
When the Buddhas preach the Dharma, sentient beings hear it; when sentient beings preach the Dharma, even stubborn rocks nod their heads.

Yet, if you want a handless man to strike with a staff and a tongueless man to understand speech, that is truly difficult. Why is this so? When the rock sleeps, the realm is forgotten and the clouds accompany the host;
only when the moon is high does one recognize the water as the guest. [Ascending the hall: "Good snow falls flake by flake; it does not fall elsewhere."
Ultimately, where does it land? If you can utter a turning word here, Baofu grants you the lifting of the retreat restrictions this morning;
if you cannot, even as you depart there will still be a tethering rope binding your feet.
Nevertheless, as for "building a cart inside the door" and "the tracks fitting when opening the door," what then? Listen to this verse: The trees resound with the cry of autumn; the leaves fall.
The leaves fall; in the wind and moon, they hang from cold branches. Where shall one return when the dream of the swing has grown cold? I ask the fair lady: does she know or not? Ascending the hall:
The spring breeze sweeps softly as trees don their robes; only upon entering the path does one know how well-suited it is to dwell in this world.
Willows are green and flowers are red, vying for our appreciation; the radiant morning sun shines upon this ancient monastery. Do you all understand?
This is the manifestation of the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. What is the realization of the Buddha’s knowledge and vision? After a long silence, he let out a shout and descended from his seat.
On the occasion of the New Year, he ascended the hall: "The lamp is the light of the lamp; the moon is the color of the moon. Lamp and moon shine together; plum blossoms reflect the snow. Suddenly—
Recall Caoshan’s “Three Kinds of Falling. Now tell me: is it he, or is it I? A white ox, a black slave—just so, just so!
Entering the hall: the field for selecting Buddhas is opened; those from the ten directions gather here. Whether you are ordinary or holy, all may enter;
only you must not give rise to thoughts or stir your minds. If you give rise to thoughts or stir your minds, you will be betraying your own spiritual brilliance.
"If you do not give rise to thoughts or stir your mind, you will sink and be buried by the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Apart from these two paths, how would you act? He took up his staff, struck it once, and said, "Study! Question: "What is the fundamental principle of the Cao-Dong school? The Master said:
"The sun sets over the empty mountains, illuminating the distant forests. The Master passed away in the Wushen year of the Kangxi era at the age of fifty-eight. His entire body was enshrined.
The stupa is located to the right of the main hall of the monastery (as recorded by Shi Yu).
Chan Master Jingxing Zixian Jingyang of Hangzhou was the son of the Dai family of Yanguan. On the evening of his birth, his mother dreamed of an elderly monk occupying her bed.
He entered the monastic order at the age of ten and received full ordination under Tiantong. Subsequently, he relied upon Baoshou, where he served him with diligent devotion for a long time.
He then received the seal of transmission. Later, upon ascending the hall, he said: "In the biased realm, nothing is encountered; a single range of peaks is obscured by clouds.
Within the primordial source, nothing is lost; ten-thousand-year-old pine paths are covered in snow. If you can realize this, let the subtle mechanism of spiritual power operate as it will.
Extending the hand, the precious seal of the ultimate is communicated; manifesting clearly, one attains the wondrous amidst the wind. Seated through to the other side of Vimalakīrti’s time."
Profound and deep, the smoke and light fill the eyes; silently illuminating the time before the empty kalpa.
Tranquil and clear, a single jar of wind and moon—here one may freely draw the jade thread to embroider the mandarin ducks, or pull back the golden shuttle to weave ancient brocade.

Although this is still a matter of the realm of construction and transformation, you must know there is yet a phrase where merit is forgotten and achievement is extinguished; only then is it attained. Tell me, how is this so?

This merit forgets its achievement and submerges its traces; not knowing there is a place, one achieves the knowledge that there is. One must believe that Nanquan’s calling it a "cow" is the same as the fellow-disciples arriving.
Ascending the hall, he said: "For ten days the thatched door has been locked layer upon layer; too lazy to employ the spiritual mechanism to cross over to the other peak."
Looking out in all four directions, all is vast emptiness; the human realm is silent. Who can penetrate this single phrase of Dangyang?
There are some fellows who, hearing Jingxing speak thus, claim he has cut off the flow of all streams and lives in seclusion behind closed doors.

If you understand it in such a way, you are just like the spirit of an ancient tomb or a ghost-child from the Black Mountains—what connection could there be? You simply do not realize that when a crane soars through the clouds and mists, its tracks remain.

It does not remain. When the dragon returns to the great ocean, its traces are entirely extinguished. Therefore, at times he sits upright on the peak of a solitary mountain, yet he strides through the crossroads;
at times he strides through the crossroads, yet he sits upright on the peak of a solitary mountain.
This is so, yet it is still speaking from "this side. Do you all know how to speak from "that side"?
Is it so? Fortunately, you have encountered my Dharma brother from Longmen. He has come here with his golden staff; surely he will not begrudge his compassion and will explain it through for you.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Opening wide the gate of liberation, he lets forth the Iron Kunlun.

Shaking his tail and shaking his head, he goes off, soaring and leaping until the seas and mountains are darkened. When the mountain monk has thus proclaimed this, suddenly someone might come forward and say, "The Master..."
To speak in such a manner is precisely the way of one who has lost their home and livelihood. Simply say to him: "I am walking through the wild weeds;
you, moreover, have entered a deep village. In the ninth month of the Bingshen year of the Shunzhi era, he suddenly manifested a slight illness. He wrote a verse and passed away.

He lived to the age of sixty-three. A hall was built for him on a ridge before Goryeosa Temple in Wulin by Seokyu Bangsi. Zen Master Jingcheng (Jingcheng Chan-shi), whose secular surname was Yang and who hailed from Changting in Min, received the tonsure at the age of seven. His posthumous title was Zhengguo (Certification of Fruition). His Dharma name was Xiyong (Western Bell). His lineage was as follows:

At twenty-five, he traveled to Jinling to listen to lectures at the gate of Chao Songruo-mei. Realizing that calculating grains of sand was not the way to resolve the matter of birth and death, he abandoned it.
He went to pay his respects to Master Shigong on Mount Guiyang to study under him. When the Master asked, "You are a man from Min; what are you doing here?

the Master replied, "I am here to listen to lectures on the *Lotus Sūtra*. The Master asked, "The seeds of Buddhahood arise from conditions; how do you understand this? The Master was at a loss and did not know how to respond.
From that time on, he resolved to engage in intensive investigation. He ascended Mount Ehu to receive the full precepts, after which he returned to Mengxi in Qingliu to take up residence there.
He established four vows to fortify his resolve: not to set up a bed or couch, not to eat past midday, not to discuss worldly matters, and not to step into the homes of the laity.
Morning and evening, he shared both joy and hardship with the assembly. At that time, Baoshou was just beginning the retreat at Lingshan.

The Master went to see him, carrying incense in his sleeve. Fang asked, "Where have you been staying lately? The Master replied, "At Dream Brook and Tangerine Mountain. Fang said, "What is the master of Tangerine Mountain?
The Master said, "I rose this morning at the hour of the Tiger (3–5 a.m.). Fang said, "That is merely the understanding of a slave or a servant.
The Master said, "Yet one cannot do without them. Thus, through long service under his forge, the Master was finally able to receive the Dharma.
The Master raised his *ruyi* (fly-whisk) and said, "Do you understand? Within the city of Xiyong, there is one with an iron face and copper eyes;
atop the Dream Brook Peak, he welcomes guests and receives visitors. In the midst of this bustling daily activity, he unimpededly cuts off the flow of all streams;

yet when sitting amidst the white clouds, he again moves with sovereign ease in every direction. He struck the *ruyi* once more and said, "Do you understand? Pairs of clay oxen gallop across the surface of the sea."
Pairs of iron hawks dance before the wind; they stand in the two ranks. Entering the hall: Gold is extracted from the ore; rice is cleared of the husks.
When Hanshan meets Shide, he claps his hands and laughs "he-he. But tell me, what is it that he laughs at?
Beating the drum and playing the lute, the two families meet. The wooden man begins pounding the mortar; the stone woman proceeds to brew tea. Pointing to space...
He said: "Look, look! The spring breeze returns beyond the city walls, and the iron trees all burst into bloom. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The bamboo of the refined gentleman is lush;
the pine of the high official is verdant. When the moon shines upon it, its natural wondrousness is revealed; when the wind comes, the six dragons dance.
Then, holding up his *ruci* (wish-fulfilling gem), he said: "Master Fu has arrived. He says: 'The hair of a tortoise from Puzhou binds the great elephant of Jiazhou. [He then pointed to] Zhenzhou...
"A rabbit's horn! [With these words, he] swallowed the Iron Ox of Shanzhou. When struck by this mountain monk with a single blow across the spine, it was reduced to ruins like ice melting away.
"Do you understand, all you Zen practitioners? After a long silence, he said: "The wind blows the willow catkins as they roll like balls; the rain beats the pear blossoms as the butterflies fly.

Throughout his life, the Master was sincere and steadfast. By nature he was leisurely and refined; his heart was settled in compassion and forbearance, and he harbored no ill will toward any creature.

Regarding the four matters he established, he practiced them with vigor throughout his life without ever wavering. In the summer of the *Renchen* year of the Shunzhi era, he suddenly conceived a desire for world-weariness.
He wrote a letter to take leave of his patrons and supporters. One day, after ordering a bath with fragrant water, he returned to his quarters as the assembly gathered.
At that time, there was a monk from India who said, "The Great Being who came from the West has specifically come to offer you porridge. The Master ate leisurely until finished, then with his hand—
He touched the crown of the Great Being’s head and said, "Will you travel with me? The Great Being replied, "I shall come in a few days.
The Master stroked the Great Being’s beard once and then passed away into stillness. On the seventh day of the seventh month at the hour of the horse (noon), his true likeness was hung up.
Within the portrait, there is an inscription that reads: "Sixty heads emerge from the horns of a rabbit; a golden rope is fashioned from tortoise hair.
Binding the active movement of empty space, he goes with it together to the Land of No-Birth.

This was his verse for departing this world. The Great Being indeed passed away several days later. The Master’s secular age was sixty-two, and his years since ordination were thirty-seven. [His] stupa...

[The stele] for the entirety [of the life of] Chan Master Dazhi Jingding of Baogai Peak in Xinan (succeeded by Shi Yu Fang) is located to the right of the Dharma Hall. He was the son of the Fang family of Xi.
Entering the hall, he said: "What does Heaven say? The four seasons proceed. What does Earth say? The myriad things are nurtured. Only the Nameless Elder remains silent..."
Vast and empty between heaven and earth, seven or eight fragments of cloud atop the ridge. The painter gazes left and right; when the brush is raised, the clouds and the ridge appear first.

Ascending the hall, he concluded the discourse on the saying, "Among the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed," and then offered this verse: Vast and empty between heaven and earth, Seven or eight fragments of cloud atop the ridge. The painter gazes left and right; When the brush is raised, the clouds and the ridge appear first.
The autumn waters form one pool of emerald green; the green mountains open up on all four sides. Old pine seeds hang from the cliffs;

surging waves hasten their flow. Tigers roar as gales howl; dragons fly forth as thunder shakes with fury. Who would have expected that tonight’s moon, pure and expansive, would wash the plum blossoms upon the courtyard?

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the story of Dongshan’s tea conversation with Head Seat Tai. Having finished, he offered this verse: “Deciding victory ten thousand *li* away, sitting still...”
He planned within the tent. The fault lay in his active employment [of means]. He removed the fruit table; he "three times provoked Zhou Yu" and "seven times captured Meng Huo.
With the east wind blowing in his face, Lord Cao was at a loss for what to do. Ascending the hall, he raised his whisk and said: "Do you understand? Medicine and disease treat one another."
Without cause, without cause. The great earth is medicine; the Persian’s eyes are cold. If you intend to question your own self, he slaps your jaw and claps your mouth shut.
The scale-weight floats in the ancient well; the five lakes are dried to the bottom. The Dragon King cries out to the azure heavens—from where does this grievance arise?
[He] struck the whisk and descended from the seat (Sanyiyu).

Master Lingting Jingting Cizun of Jia Shan was the son of the Xue family of Qiantang. Having passed the civil service examination for the Classics (*mingjing*), he renounced it to travel extensively among the monastic assemblies.
While contemplating "the clay ox entering the sea," he took the form of a layman to study under Yunmen Yu. After a long time, he contemplated...
Hao was wearing a coarse cloth loincloth when he heard the words "grape arbor. One day, while walking through the marketplace, he happened to step on a clam shell and suddenly attained awakening.
He went to Yunmen to seek confirmation. Yunmen asked, "At such a time as this, how is it? The Master said, "The moon shines white upon a thousand peaks. Yunmen said: [affirming his realization].
"Recite another phrase," he said. The Master replied, "The lake opens, revealing both shores. Yun’u asked, "Do you remember our meeting at Zonghui Monastery three years ago?
The Master replied, "A jade qilin beneath the peony blossoms. Yun’u nodded in approval. Consequently, he received the transmission of the seal of enlightenment.
At the age of forty-six, having fulfilled his filial duties toward his parents, he left the household life. He first resided at Ciyun and subsequently at Fan.
Receiving [the transmission]. Next, the manifestation of the Holy One ascends the hall: Upside-down and topsy-turvy! Waves surge to the heavens atop the summit of Mount Sumeru.
Red lotuses bloom across the parched earth; great elephants are led by threads of lotus fiber. At midnight, one rides a fish through the marketplace, with a staff piercing both ends.
I laugh at myself; it is truly pitiable that the Persian holds secret mantras while covering his tongue with gold coins. Entering the hall:
Ordinarily, even to utter a single phrase of song-response is no easy matter.

There are certain reckless practitioners of Zen who understand nothing but overturning the Dharma seat and knocking over the meditation platform, taking this to be "not yielding when the opportunity arises. Little do they know that [this is merely] being born together...
Death can be weak, it can be strong; sending forth and drawing back, there is naturally a wondrous subtlety of turning mechanism.
Stop! Stop! Stop! This Dharma-gate of Bodhidharma, I suspect no one understands. The "High Mountains and Flowing Waters" is a melody for a thousand years;
the "White Snow and Yangchun" is a heart for ten thousand ages. Were it not for Yantou and Xuefeng, who else could join in singing this song? He looks left and right.
He said: "Is anyone here? He ascended the hall and said: "Buying low and selling high is already enough to leave people utterly frustrated. Is there anyone?

When the chick pecks and the mother strikes simultaneously, even a 'lacquer bucket' [an expression for a dullard] would not find it agreeable. He ascended the hall and said: "The great garuḍa bird, the golden-winged one, goes straight for the dragon to swallow it;
this too is like being so hungry that one does not choose one's food. As the saying goes: 'Better nothing than something good. A monk asked: "When the Way of Birds is not met with its time..."
"How is it? The Master said, "A silken thread cages a green crane. [The student] asked, "What about after meeting it?
The Master said, "A jade elephant hangs in red clouds. [Someone] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "An eight-cornered yakṣa leads a dog that barks.
[Someone] asked, "As for the matter at hand, how is it? The Master said, "A stone ram gives birth to a milk-tiger. (Sanyiyu succeeded him.)
Chan Master Jingshun of Fusheng Temple in Wulin, a native of the Shen family of Tongxiang, gave a small-scale discourse (*xiaocan*).

Holding his *ruyi* (monk’s staff) and striking it to form the shape of a circle, he said: "A single stroke has not yet appeared; do not say that one hides one's body within the charcoal. Since the two polarities have already been distinguished, how could one be planting one's feet in the snow?
Brothers, if you can see into this, you will know that 'striking' and 'singing' proceed together, and that the 'partial' and the 'correct' are simultaneous."
Interchanging and reversing: taking the waters of West Lake and pouring them into Ye Creek; Ye Creek does not realize it, and moves Stone Umbrella Peak to place it upon Gushan Hill;

Gushan Hill remains unaware. The morning star in the east and the evening star in the west; the seven stars of the Southern Dipper and the six stars of the Northern Dipper. The Patriarch drives the ox out of the pen;
the blind donkey barges into the Buddha hall. The Lantern Festival in the ninth month; the Double Ninth on the fifteenth day of the first month.
When there is darkness, there is light; when there is light, there is darkness. The myriad peaks stand tall and distinct; the Milky Way is silent.
Ten thousand bamboos chime with a *shan-shan* sound; the clear breeze possesses a rhythmic cadence. [The Master] struck the table once and said: "Do you all understand?
The golden ox has iron horns that are sharp; the black dog has silver hooves that are worn smooth. (Siyu Yu Si)
Chan Master Zongjing Meixijingtong of Yuezhou was the son of the Tao family of his native region. He ascended the hall and said: "Clouds drift slowly; waters flow on endlessly.
Chrysanthemums cover the ground, hastening one toward old age. Crimson leaves by the twin streams turn our hair white.
Only Mount Xianglu remains as it was, towering and imposing; Lion Cliff knows neither joy nor sorrow. Where there is room to roam, roam freely."

One does not regret that one’s fur robe is worn out as one passes through the Passes of Qin; one does not rejoice at riding a crane up to Yangzhou. Let the purple swallows chatter on through spring and autumn. Ascending the Dharma Hall on His Birthday:
The past was wrong and the present is right—what comparison can be made? The sun rises over the eastern mountain while the rain falls upon the western.
What difference is there between right now being right and yesterday being wrong? When the moon is full it wanes, and when it wanes it becomes full again.
[The Master] strikes his staff and says: "This celestial mechanism has completely leaked away. It is mostly because teeth have fallen out that one is not concerned with the wind;

at my age of fifty, I am ashamed to speak of it. By the hedge, the yellow chrysanthemums are in full bloom; look, look—already it is the beginning of spring. Several cries of wild geese descend upon the level sands. The moon.

In the cold window, the wind shears the leaves. [The Master] ascends the hall: "For several days past, you have been flapping your lips and stirring your tongues, emptying your bellies and pouring out your guts, lodging grievances against the Buddhas and Patriarchs, and twisting the teachings of all quarters.
This has caused the Heavenly Kings to glare with bared teeth and Vajrapāṇi to clench his fists.

He then recorded this with a *nyoi* (wish-fulfilling jewel) and a verse (*gāthā*). (Third: Yuyu Sisi).
Chan Master Tan-chi Jingyi of Fazang Monastery in Hangzhou gave a small lecture: "Transforming merit into the station; the withered tree and the fragrant thicket."

Shifting positions to manifest function: when the mud ox has but a single horn, both function and position are simultaneously revealed. Temporarily donning tattered rags, one is forcibly named a Buddha;

After all, what can be called "position"? And what can be called "function"? [He spreads his hands and says: "Investigate! (Sanyiyu Si).
Chan Master Zhixuan Jingxin Miaofeng of Yuezhou, a native of the Chen family of Zhuji, ascended the hall and said:
"At the summit of the Wondrous Peak is the kōan of the upward-moving faculty; it fills the void, causing heaven to revolve and earth to turn.

The plum blossoms in the snow and the resonance of the bamboo in the wind have already been revealed to everyone without leaving this hall. Why must I trouble my mouth again this morning? He then ascended the hall once more.
The spring light illuminates the earth; orchids emit their subtle fragrance. Birds chirp among the plum branches; flowers fly throughout the courtyard. Does the assembly understand?
If not, today I shall open for you the gate of skillful means and reveal the true mark. (He lets out a shout and descends from his seat. While residing at Tiantang, he ascended the hall and said:

The filaments. A young gentleman strolls through Lan-ting Park; holding his cup, he walks along with others to view the winding streams.
Yet he recalls Wang Youjun of that time; who knows where he has returned today? The lush forests and tall bamboos remain as they were, but the people are gone, leaving only the old foundations.
He gives a shout and says: "Behold the puppets on the stage performing! He ascends the hall. The lofty mountains rise high.

Xiu! Ever verdant through the four seasons, its winding waters meander as ten thousand streams flow from their source. The sound of the monk’s staff resonates through the mountains, shaking heaven and earth;
the Bowl Peak exhales mist and swallows the clouds. What need is there to speak of everyone’s nostrils reaching toward the heavens and every person’s heels touching the ground?
Let it be so: carrying water and hauling firewood are none other than one’s own glory; plowing fields and digging the earth are all entirely...
"This is a great function. The assembly, tell me: what is this great function? He then descended from his seat.

Question: "What is the single color of the true position? The Master said: "The moon sinks; the golden hall is cold. Question:
"What is the single color of great achievement? The Master said: "A flying egret enters the reeds. Question:
"What is the single color of the present time? The Master said: "Striking the forehead, it is cold" (San Yi Yu).
Chan Master Tongchuan Miaojue Sanli Jingjue was the son of the Liu family of Wanling.

He went to Dongxing Jian to receive the tonsure. At the age of eighteen, he traveled south, visiting many masters for instruction. While reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he came across the passage: "To establish a knowing upon seeing is the very root of ignorance.
He sighed and said: "Those of past and present have read this as a broken sentence; moreover, they have not fully realized its meaning. Why should I remain stuck here?"

He then went to Mount Jing, where he met Yuyi Fengxin. Upon hearing the dialogue regarding "seeing from where life comes," and subsequently encountering the saying, "A hundred years, thirty-six thousand mornings," his nostrils were struck away.
He received full ordination at Tiantong, where he happened upon Yunmen’s opening of the Dharma.

When Master Sanjiang went to visit him, their spiritual capacities met like a lock and key, and he thereby attained the Dharma. Ascending the hall, [he said]: "Steep cliffs and perilous peaks; white clouds..."

Slowly, slowly... the clear deep pool and the emerald pond; the crimson sun blazing on high; the whistling of bamboos and the surging of pines; the sound of spring water and the song of birds—a single scroll of natural painting.
Even were Zhang Sengyou or Wu Daozi here, with all their brushes, they could hardly depict it.
If you, Great Assembly, can realize this, let the dung beetles and ants each display their elegance; let the lame turtles and blind tortoises increase their spirit.
"Why trouble yourself, Elder, by waving your whisk? Why wag your lips and brandish such martial authority? [The Master] remained silent for a long while, then waved his whisk and said:

"Subtly transcending conceptual thought, it is beyond the path of the intellect. How can one act? How can one respond? It is all in vain to labor over looking back."

Pausing. Before this mountain monk has emerged from his quarters, the myriad sages find it suddenly difficult to set foot; once he has emerged from his quarters, all things are further enhanced in their brilliance.
From this, he exerts great potential and manifests great function, causing the dull birds to fly through the sky and the exhausted fish to emerge from the sea.
Those who understand it see the iron ox swallow the moon over a thousand peaks; those who do not understand it hear the stone tiger call back.
"Whether the clouds gather at the Five Peaks or not—how about that? Listen! An old man with a head like a mortar and legs like running dogs; he thunders through the imperial capital.
Ascending the hall, he snapped open the golden lock and shattered the primordial barrier. A wooden horse in the clouds chases the wind; a clay ox at the bottom of the sea bites the moon.
"O worthy ones! The flowers are bright and the waters are clear; the clouds are thin and the sky is vast. The cliff rocks glisten with water."
The *langgan* gems shimmer; where is there that is not the place where one should sacrifice body and life? Why is this?

Because one is ensnared by sounds and forms, and sinks into sights and hearing. Amidst the flowers and thickets of thorns, if one can pass with arms swinging free, one will naturally and suddenly forget both subject and object.
There is no need for cultivation or practice. What more need be said of "pervading the void" or "sweeping across the eight directions"?
Brandishing his fly-whisk, he said, "It can kill; it can give life. After the Master had attained the Dharma, he became increasingly reclusive and concealed.
He lived in seclusion for several years at Mount Dongshan in Tongchuan. Before long, the Baofo Monastery of Miaojue rose majestically there.
Shortly thereafter, he passed away without illness (succeeded by Sanyi Yu).

from the mountain peaks, yellow cranes fly forth all at once. This, indeed, causes people to doubt. (San Yi Yu Si)

Where fresh blood flows profusely from one’s toes, if one has not personally suffered it, one knows no pain. Yunmen praised this verse. Thereupon, master and disciple reached a perfect accord, and he was finally granted formal certification (*kaji*).

Later, while presiding over the assembly, Yunmen ascended the hall and said: "After long rain, the sun comes out; everyone rejoices. Yet when one steps out the gate to travel the road, the very feet that walk..."
Light! Monks especially give rise to afflictions; each one furrows his brow and stares with wide eyes. As for the matter, it is thus; but as for the principle, how is it?
Looking left and right, he said: "Old Wang of East Village speaks clearly:
'The price of rice will certainly be low next year. He gave a shout. Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the first day of the middle winter month. Descended from heaven."
The true news: A fierce wind sweeps up the thatch from the roof; a fine rain wets the stones before the steps. Crows settle upon the eaves of the hall, flying and cawing in flocks;
yellow leaves fall into the empty courtyard, scattered and disordered by the wind. Who is it that does not know how to appreciate this?
Do not let yourself remember it again later. After a long silence, he said: "Do not remember it. The wind has stilled and the black clouds have vanished."
The red wheel spontaneously bursts forth—ascending the hall. Treading through the clouds at ten thousand leagues, one passes through the gates of a thousand households.
Suddenly, when the warhorses are reined in, the spears and shields are forever stilled. The floating clouds of the five aggregates disperse without being blown.
The blazing flames of the three miserable realms are extinguished without being struck; coming and going through birth and death is nothing but a game.

Delusion and awakening, truth and falsehood—all are merely provisional names. Thus, one who reaches the bottom of this matter is like a marvelous falcon seizing the wind, or a fierce tiger with horns upon its head.
Having eaten our fill, we chatter and clamor from east to west. Should one become bewildered, it will be difficult to tie the wandering silken thread to the white sun;

do not let the springtime slip away in its slow passage. Ascending the hall, he said: "The trees are dense and the birds' songs harmonize; the night is clear and the moonlight is fine. The divine light does not come of itself;
facing the wall in vain leads only to regret. If you all understand this, drink a cup of village wine as you please."
A cup. If you cannot comprehend this principle, then after the Immortal of the Curse has departed, those who truly know him will be few.

*He lets out a shout.* Ascending the hall, he said: "The fragrant breeze brings coolness to the palace halls; the bright moon scatters its luster across the courtyard. In the painted pavilion, people sip from golden goblets.
How can one attain such clear and distinct realization before one's eyes? With his hand, he struck his forehead and said: "It turns out it was not far off at all."
Question: "The National Teacher called his attendant three times; what was the meaning of this? The Master said: "I am old and afraid of the cold; I want to wear some socks. Question:
"How is it when the precious sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard? The Master said: "Its radiance shoots toward the Dipper and Ox. Question:

"How is it after it has emerged from the scabbard? The Master said: "One still finds it dull even for slicing vegetables. Question: "What was it like before the Venerable had seen Yunmen? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
"What? the Master said. "The golden goblet has a fine guest. [The monk] asked, "After seeing him, what is it like? The Master said, "The autumn mountains have no old friend.
[The monk] asked, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner? The Master said, "The clear breeze from the northern window penetrates the bones with coolness.

[The monk] asked, "How was it before King [Wang] ascended the throne? The Master said, "Outside the gates of the five courts, the golden horses neigh. [The monk] asked, "How is it? (The Master remained silent).
This is the upward path. The Master said: "The autumn wind blows through the flight of egrets. (Sanniyu’s Successor).
Chan Master Jìng Héng, whose secular surname was Wáng, of the Húishì clan of Lúshān, gave a small assembly talk: "The Way is everywhere; wherever one touches it, it is true.
To blink one's eyebrows is ten thousand miles from Yázhōu. Red trees in a solitary village overflow the eyes."

The light shines; cold geese cry out in lamentation, and the frosty wind pierces the ears. Reaching this point, one must truly make the tip of a cow’s horn nod its head and cause Mount Xianglu Peak to break into dance.
Suddenly, one shatters Zhaozhou’s barrier and kicks through Yunmen’s "All.
What need is there to speak of Xianggu rolling the ball or Heishan beating the drum? At the mountain gate, Maitreya lets out a great laugh—laughing at the Hall of the Patriarchs.
The Arhat Zhongtie: "The present is examined against the past; in total, it does not equal the Venerable Ājñātakauṇḍinya.

[He lets out a shout. Small Assembly Sermon: Holding up his staff, he says: "A withered vine."

Linji personally suffered indignity at the hands of Huangbo; Shao Yang was cast before Xuefeng. Those who gained power on the road ascend straight up ten thousand peaks; those with staffs and wood following their bodies [proceed] accordingly.

He took his seat. Not daring to give rise to arbitrary complications, he struck the ground with his staff to the left and said, "Fully embodying the three mysteries and three essentials of Linji.
He then struck it to the right and said, "Interpenetrating the five ranks of Dongshan’s orthodoxy and deviation.

Finally, striking it repeatedly, he said, "Revealing the essential principles of the Buddhas and Patriarchs of antiquity, and shattering the muddled, heterodox Chan of the present day. Among the assembly, is there anyone who can [respond to] this staff?

(Sanzhiyu Si). Chan Master Linzhe Jingyan of Tianzhang Monastery in Yuezhou was a son of the He family of Jiangyin, Changzhou. From his childhood, he studied the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.

When he reached the passage on "sights being seen and sounds being sought," he encountered a point of doubt. One day, upon hearing the sound of a child calling for its mother, he attained realization.

The Master stepped forward, crossed his hands, and stood facing him. Wu said, "Who is it that drags this corpse along?
The Master said, "Do not treat me with such dullness. Wu raised his staff; the Master said, "Snap this staff, Monk!"
"What do you hold up? Wù replied, "This young man knows his origins very well. Later, the Master left the household life and received full ordination from Tiantong Mǐn.
Subsequently, he visited Yufeng Xìn at Yunmen, who asked, "Do you know me?
The Master said, "I know you; it is simply that I cannot give you a name. Xìn said, "With two clear eyes like pearls, one does not even know one's own name. The Master said, "If..."

He asked, "Regarding Nanquan’s beheading of the cat—was there a transgression or not? The Master said, "A staff strikes a stone man who gasps in surprise;

The Master says, "Flowers blooming red upon the rocks; one branch plucked out for ten thousand people to see.

A pair of solitary wild geese alight upon the sandy islet. The wooden child strikes down the moon at the edge of heaven; the clay ox beneath the water chews the moon as it walks. [He suddenly held up his whisk.]

*Sā*. Squeezing the mouth of the cloth bag, it bursts forth: the flower in the eye, the monkey. One must strictly avoid being as chaotic as hemp.

Chan Master Jingdi of Qingdi Temple in Shanxi, Dongyue, was a son of the Ma family of Kunshan, Suzhou.

He ascended the hall and said: "The frost and dew are as slippery as moss; staff and wooden sounding-blocks follow me wherever I go. When fellow practitioners pass shoulder-to-shoulder, take care not to look back too often.
Amidst crooked streets and narrow alleys, one must beware of the dog of Zihu. If you hurry, you will not catch up; if you walk slowly, you will fall behind."
Later, when you gaze at the wind and part the grass, do not speak recklessly.
Brothers, I have fully entrusted to you the words of the retreat. Yet there is one more vital matter; let us return to the warm room to deliberate. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Before the Yanwei Peak, there are no superfluous words. How shall I bring this forth before the assembly today? Striking the wall, knocking on the fence, and scolding the neighbors!"
Selling divinations on the street, he deceives gods and ghosts; flowers planted upon a rock bloom throughout the night. A boat travels ten thousand miles across dry land—entering the hall:
"Today is the tenth month, a minor spring. The sky is warm, the frost light, and the sun shines even brighter.
Three or four mountain flowers; one or two calls from a cold bird. A cowherd boy on his ox’s back blows a short flute; by the stream, a child..."
Having finished the song and the practice, who cares about you, Daoist Li? Who cares about you, Master Zhang?

Having eaten yellow vegetable soup and coarse millet, everyone simply lets things go as they are, full to the brim. Ascending the hall: Yesterday, while traveling halfway along the road, I heard a village elder speak four phrases.
They are most wondrous, most primal, most intimate, and most direct. If anyone can recognize them, it would be well.
Encompassing both ancient and modern times, and surpassing even the Buddhas and patriarchs—here, the thousand seven hundred cases of entanglement melt away like ice and crumble to dust.
As for the melodies of the thirty-two fascicles, they are truly nothing more than the clatter of hot bowls.
Tell me, what kind of talk is so extraordinary? Gentlemen, do you wish to hear it? After a long silence, he said: "Four nines make thirty-six. Firewood and rice."
Every household has it. In the back garden, they grow mustard greens; a large radish grows there as well. Ascending the hall: Today is the middle of the tenth month.
I shall judge this matter for you. In the morning we ate white congee; the weather was warm and our bodies perspired. Precious robes of honor are not worth half a coin;
worn-out straw sandals cannot be exchanged for gold. Shame on the Tuṣita Palace; take care with the pork platter.
"Mañjuśrī saw the King of Emptiness last night; with a single blow to the head, he was driven out of the monastery. I ask you all: do you recognize him or not?
On the river amidst the reeds, white as cotton wool, the heron flies in and is nowhere to be found. Ascending the hall, he said: "In every place flowers bloom under the warm sun;
in every house the moon is bright and the breeze is clear. There is no need to hang peach branches outside the gate; the spirit sleeps in peace of its own accord."
High on one’s pillow. For those who can let go, left and right, seven strides and eight bounds;
for those who cannot let go, they strike their heads and bump their foreheads, adding rope to their bonds. Brothers, how high is heaven? How level is the earth?
A vast, living path is open for you to walk—why laboriously grope along the walls? One need not worry about Nanquan’s cat, nor fear Zihu’s dog.

"Terrible! To see the strange as not strange, and the strangeness subsides of itself. A radish from Zhenzhou weighs three catties. [The student] asked: "Ultimately, how can one attain resonance? The Master said:
"For days the sky has been overcast with rain; fresh moss covers the ground. [The student] asked:
"When a single mote of dust arises, the whole earth is gathered up. What do you call 'dust'? The Master said: "Heaps of mountains and piled-up peaks. [The student] said: "I do not yet understand."
"How does the Great Earth receive [all things]? The Master said, "If there is much, do not add;
if there is little, do not subtract. "Question: What is the matter beyond the ordinary monk? The Master said, "The warmth on one's chest when facing the fire.
"Question: What is the realm of enlightened awareness? The Master said, "Clouds billow atop Yanwei Peak; waters overflow by the side of Wolong Pond. (Ermi Fu succeeded him.)
Chengrong Guangzi Wenjingyin Chan Master of Yuezhou was the son of the Chen family of Jiyang. Upon entering the retreat, he ascended the hall and said:
"The eye of Mahesvara penetrates through the ten voids; the numinous talisman behind the elbow encompasses the entire dharma-realm.
Having attained the *dhāraṇī* of all Buddhas, one cuts off all news of past and present. Thus, without rising from his seat, he travels throughout the world without leaving a trace."

Without moving the tongue, one may say that throughout the world there is no fault of speech; there is only the constant clarity of the sincere heart, which cuts off the very roots of birth and death.
One must directly attain this state such that it is so in every thought-moment, at every time, in every circumstance, and in every phenomenon.
Only then does one engage in non-action and non-affairs. Like white clouds thousands of miles away, one will never err when meeting people. (He let out a shout.)
The late evening assembly after the lifting of the retreat: The Iron Ox plows the fields of the primordial kalpa; The Stone Tiger sleeps through the night, cradling the moon.
The crane does not pause its flight as peaks vie for beauty; The phoenix has no place to rest as the trees stretch far and high.
If you have a staff, I give you a staff; If you have no staff, I likewise give you a staff. To go together with this is nothing more than severance.

Crossing the bridge over the water, let us follow our companions back to the village of the bright moon. Ascending the hall, he said: "Originally, I am but a lone fisherman on the Xiao River, drifting west and east, north and south.
The clouds have gathered and the mountains grow lean; the autumnal countenance is pale. Now that spring has ended, the coral flames blaze with brilliance."

His elegant and refined spirit reveals no facial expression; he roams through crags and valleys, leaving behind all traces of the mundane. The tips of arrows meet, the lightning-fast mechanism takes precedence;
fragrant vapors float in silver bowls, the snowflakes white. Seizing it up, he blocks the throats of water and clouds; he sweeps away the dark, primordial abode of the Dharma-realm.
Ascending the hall, as soon as a monk stepped forward, the Master struck him with his staff and said: "Standing atop the highest mountain peak."
"Walking at the bottom of the deep sea—how do you understand this? The monk said, "Walking and hiding originally do not belong to another.
The Master said, "Alas, you fellow Meng Babang, you go on like this again! As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. (Ermi Fu succeeded him.)
Chan Master Qinghua Weicen Jingji of Yuezhou was the son of the Zhang family of Jingzhou. His mother dreamed that a blue lotus appeared in her courtyard before he was born.
He lost his father at the age of six and entered Linghu Temple at fifteen to shave his head and receive the precepts. This was the *Renxu* year of the Tianzhi era.
He came to visit Boshan, who showed him the essential points for practicing *chan*. The Master (Xuedou) attended to communal affairs by day and practiced seated meditation at night.

Consequently, he entered the abbot’s quarters to request further instruction; as soon as he stepped across the threshold, he was shouted out by Boshan. The Master became even more resolute. That winter, he received full ordination.
While sitting casually, he had an awakening upon seeing where the incense smoke rose. In the year of Xinwei, he formed a companion and vowed to observe a precept of silence. Just then—
Outside the hall, a bowl was broken. They argued, saying, "You lot only know how to eat the monastery's rice; you do not care for the monastery's affairs.
Upon hearing this, the Master attained awakening and spoke a verse: "Having broken the monastery's bowl, One must seek it back from the monastery.
Meeting yet not recognizing one another, In vain one gives rise to vexation. Tsk! These groundless Chan practitioners, two of them quarreling— They make Zhang Chang in the hall laugh to tears."
Lao went on to study under Bianshan Xue for a long time. He then visited Dongshan Fu at Xiansheng Monastery, where Fu commanded him to enter the room.
Fu asked, "How is it right now? The Master replied, "Wood Seat-Cushion is entirely eyes. Fu asked, "What is Deshan’s final phrase?
The Master replied, "Riding a cow without wearing a hat; crossing water while wearing boots. Fu said:
"Completely without connection," the Master said. "I once mowed thatch in the garden of the South Mountain. With this, he shook his sleeves and departed.

He attained the Dharma in the year *xinsi* (701) and became the abbot of Guseng in *guisi* (713). Subsequently, he presided over several monasteries, including Puzhi on Mount Dongshan and Furong in Jiangyin.
Entering the hall, he said: "Faint mist enshrouds the ancient temple; Mist-colored vapors surge from the mountain peaks. Picking up the tortoise-hair whisk, He sweeps it open..."
In the azure void of heaven, at just such a moment as this, birds warble on every mountain and orioles sing in every place. The true mechanism is revealed in every thing;

He paid money to buy a *hūbǐng* (wheat cake), but when he let go of his hand, it turned out to be a *mántóu* (steamed bun).

After a long silence, he said: "Guests from ancient times who cherish their treasures yet remain lost in their own lands; they toil in vain, seeking only in that other direction. Ascending the hall, he said: "Zhaozhou says, 'Go and drink tea'; Niu-tou carries rice to come.
If you can understand the meaning within this, the primordial barrier and golden lock shall open. There are a certain kind of fellows who recognize only wearing clothes and eating food."
Eating, speaking, talking, remaining silent—taking these as being for oneself—is this not recognizing a thief as one’s son, or taking a servant for one’s master?

[The monk] asked, "What is the matter by the waterside and beneath the forest? The Master said, "Where the clay ox bellows, the autumn light grows old.

In the summer of the Jiachen year of the Kangxi era, the Master passed away without illness at the age of seventy and with fifty years of monastic seniority. His entire body was interred on the rear mountain of Qinghua (successor: Ermifu).

Chan Master Pútán Zìruò Jìngshēn of Gǔháng was the son of the Wáng family of Shānyīn. He ascended the hall and said: "Regarding that supreme point beyond, every single thing manifests it;
within one's sleeves lies a single mechanism, revealed in every instance. Have you not seen the former masters say:

'The crowing of roosters and the barking of dogs all open up perfect penetration; the timely rain and the harmonious winds all suspend wondrous meanings. What need is there for peonies in the courtyard or cypress trees? "
Re-picking up the theme: A red carp and a golden lion ought surely to leap forth. Is there anyone among you who can leap forth? After a long silence, he said:
"When the waves of the third surge grow high, one must pass through quickly; only by retreating from the precipice can one become truly fierce. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The morning star at midnight and the sun appearing at noon—the eyes of Śākyamuni the Old Man have been swapped. The mountains and rivers of the great earth have melted away."
All is unified this morning as we conclude the retreat and each returns to their own land. Those traveling by water or land must look well; they must look well!

I have been fishing for three weeks now; failing to catch a golden-scaled fish, I withdraw my pole. Ashamed that my repayment of the Sage’s grace remains insufficient, I move my boat and cast down another line like that of Lord Ren. My cloud-capped hat moves and my snow-white cloak floats; this ancestral craft is practiced by the public—how could I linger in idleness? With one cry of "kuan-erh," infinite meaning stirs as white gulls fly past the emerald sandbars. Questioning the ancient mirror before it has been polished: [The mirror] is dark and dull, its surface covered in dust. When the bright moon shines upon it, its reflection is not yet clear. Only after being polished does it become bright and pure; when the bright moon shines upon it, its reflection is distinct. Thus, the ancients used the mirror to reflect their own hearts. If the heart is pure, the mirror is bright; if the heart is turbid, the mirror is dark. Therefore, the ancients said: "If you wish to know the person within, look at the mirror outside. This is why the ancients valued the mirror so highly. It is not merely a tool for reflecting images; it is a means of examining one's own mind. If one can maintain the purity of the mirror, then the heart will naturally be upright. This is the way of self-cultivation. Thus, the ancients used the mirror to examine themselves. Chan Master Hongxi Yisheng of Boshan in Xinzhou was the son of the Pan family of Yongfeng. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations.

"Worldly affairs are like flowers blooming and falling; human sentiments are like tides ebbing and flowing. If one practices the Way without reaching the point of ultimate exhaustion, [one remains lost] in the wild grasses."
The shoes still bear green moss. A group of wandering monks are like dung-collecting rakes from the Great Xiangguo Temple in the Eastern Capital;
they have mouths but cannot speak, and eyes but cannot see. Upon hearing this being said, they immediately reply: "The World-Honored One abandoned the imperial palace and entered the Snow Mountains;
for six years he toiled his body, suddenly famished, until on the eighth day of the twelfth month, beholding the morning star, he attained enlightenment."
The Way. Heh! It is vividly clear, it is vividly clear. Why is it that only Gautama’s insight is granted? *Du du!* People, come quickly to the hall!
The Green Emperor has just returned and the news of spring arrives; what indeed does this mountain elder have to do?
Horizontally grasping a single unperforated flute, he carefree beyond the norm blows into it as he pleases. A-he-he! What a fine season! Behold!
The color of the grass is half-tinged with green. Let me ask: has the peach blossom opened yet? The peach blossom has indeed opened; it is not that it does not exist.
It is laughable that Lingyun did not look again. A wordless conclusion: once the snow has melted away, the spring colors naturally reach their full bloom.

Lying weary upon the West River moon, an old crane parts the clouds above the cave. [A monk] asked, "What is the person who does not dwell in the position of centrality?

The grass is green at the edge of the courtyard; the moon’s shadow falls upon the curtain. The borders of the realm have been transformed by virtue, and he returns with songs of victory.

A questioner asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Under the purple *zhijing* flower, the yellow oriole warbles. The questioner asked, "Apart from this, is there still a meaning or not?

The duck swallows the snail. [A monk] asked: "Of all the sutras and precepts, it is said that abstaining from killing is foremost.
When Nanquan slew the cat, where was this precept? The Master said: "You are a man without blood. The Master passed away at the age of forty-two without illness.
A stupa was erected on the left side of Longshan, behind Lianhuafeng Peak (Juelang Sheng was his successor).

Chan Master Dazhi Molì of Qingyuan in Jizhou was the son of the Fang family of Tongcheng; his alternative name was Yuedi. Shouchang ascended the hall and said: "That which points upward is not transmitted;
that which points downward is extensive. Why must one strive when it is unnecessary? How could 'pervading the body' be anything other than 'encompassing the whole person'?
If you treat this as a mere intellectual puzzle, you merely bring shame upon our family tradition. It is just as the Patriarch said: 'The supreme flavor is ghee.'"
It emerges from the milk; if even a drop of water is mixed in, it is no longer so. Have you ever personally passed through this furnace of refinement?
Within thirty blows of the staff, the true eye is opened. When has the mind of the Patriarch ever been transmitted? Entering the hall, he said: "In this way, in this way."
Mud rots the teeth of the lacquered sandals. Not so, not so. Day after day toward the western forest of Denglin.
Within "so," yet not so; within "not so," yet indeed so. The eyes of the stone man do not grow dim. He brandishes his whisk and says: "This matter admits of no proximity;
it is fundamentally free from all circumvention. If you act with deliberate intent or seek to boast of it, you will distance yourself from it ever further. Even if..."
A venomous snake wearing horns; a tigress with wings grown—how increasingly perverse and absurd! What benefit could such things possibly bring?

It would be better not to reach this state than for a sentient being who has first resolved to attain enlightenment to fill the heavens and the earth with a single moment of sincere devotion. As it is said, "The will of even a common man cannot be taken away.

this was the lineage of Juelang Cheng).
Chan Master Qitian Dahaha of Shouchang in Xincheng, a native of the Yang family of Xin’feng in Qianguzhou, had a mother who dreamed of an old man... [text continues].
A monk transformed the site of a house. A woman there was pregnant; when the child was born, he slept soundly. As a youth, he did not enjoy playing. He was quick-witted and insightful in his studies.
He delighted in maintaining a simple, pure life and frequented Buddhist temples. At the age of fifteen, he participated in the regional examinations.

Later, at Xilai Hermitage, he sought ordination under the Dharma Master Fuda. His parents gave their permission. Fuda invited a master of renown to establish a separate residence for him, enabling him to become widely learned.

Regarding the inner and outer scriptures, at the age of eighteen he received full ordination from Baohua and served as his attendant. He subsequently traveled extensively; at twenty-four, he attained the Dharma under Tianjie.

Later, while presiding over the assembly at Xingguo Temple in Wuhu, he ascended the hall and said: "When the Way reaches its limit, it transforms; wondrous responses and spiritual powers follow. When things reach their extreme, they return;
there is no principle that is not fully exhausted. If one were to let loose a single thread of the Path, it would directly cause the ice to melt."
The river sends forth flames while withered trees bloom; he drags away the ancient temples of Mount Zha and stacks them against the gates of Xingguo Mountain.
He sweeps his brush toward thunder and lightning, and his coughs and spits become wind and clouds.

If this is so, then at the beginning of the month of winter solstice not a single thread has been added, and at the end of the month of summer solstice how could even a single strand have been subtracted? Thus, one can condense hundreds of thousands of kalpas into a single instant.
Thus, one can extend a single *kṣaṇa* to penetrate and observe many eons; it is so in every thought-moment, and so in every *kṣaṇa*.
What need is there then to speak of the waxing and waning of the seasons? Nevertheless, today the first line of Yang has begun to stir, and the myriad phenomena manifest their brilliance.
How would you say it? [With the whisk, he makes a dotting gesture and says: "A dot struck upon the high void surpasses the clouds of the imperial examination; it falls precisely on the Xin day."
The First Day of the First Month of the Year of the Rat: Ascending the Hall upon the Conclusion of the Retreat.

In the blink of an eye, the ninety days of the retreat have come to an end. Moss-patterned coins carpet the brocade steps; willow eyes peer out at the fresh green. The great river overflows with spring;

The meal is served. With faith, one entrusts oneself to the Way. As it is truly said: "When the season arrives, its principle manifests of itself.

What must you avoid? Avoid taking the servant for the master. At the request of Yingshouchang, he ascended the hall: "The same human breath extends a thousand miles."

The friendship is profound. Reams of elegant stationery have arrived at Yunlin. Opening my breast, I alone play the *Nanxun* melody; pressing my fingers before the wind, I unfold the jade-like tones. O Great Assembly:

The Master struck him, saying, "Deliver them both at once. The Master passed away on the second day of the ninth month in the autumn of the Jiachen year of the Kangxi era.
